We hope for the opportunity to have you back with us again  should your travels bring you back to the beautiful island of Jeju.
You would believe these rocks are the art work of mother nature until you visit it. We saw heayon (women diver) in action near the cliff. Good place.

you should read the story of this museum.it comes to live cos there is a dream.it has a sharp appearance a vibrant red exterior in jeju when comparing with those surrounding buildings.the art pieces in the museum is nice but i do appreciate the way that the owner makes this museum as an art piece more.To renovate rather than destroy and rebuild keeping the scratches of time and inject the modern art atmosphere into this old building.although you may think the entry free maybe a bit high but it still worth to visit.the cafe and souvenir shop at top floor also nice to stay awhile.

You need to present a copy of your identification before you are allowed into the range. At 35K Won it is not exactly the cheapest range in the world but it is cheaper than Seoul for sure.There are a variety of handguns to choose from and apart from the tacky advertisements on the wall it is actually quite a secure and well maintained range.Weapons are chained to the wall for safety and only the staff can tap you in or out. Good quality 3M earphones are used. There is also a selfie stick attached for you to take your pictures. Unfortunately the staff inside the range does not speak english (only the receptionist does basic english). However they do a pretty good job of demonstrating how to handle the weapon showing you on the screen where your shot have landed after each shot.After the shoot the receptionist will total up your score and pack your score sheet for you to bring it home as a souvenir. The hot tip is to book via Klook or Trazy and hunt for discounts instead of paying for the full price.Overall we enjoyed our shoot very much. Had it been cheaper we would definitely have another go.

You can go underground and experience the cold temperatures close to 12 degrees.. its like walking through an igloo.. Cold air everywhere and some parts are wet due to the precipitation though the soil. Reminder to bring a jacket and good shoes as floor is slippery and area is dark! Very good experience!

Wow a brilliant fun dayloads of pic opportunity for all ages spent ages taking pics just great fun and lots to see and participate inparking easy and we got a taxi very easily afterthere's a go kart place just nextdoorplease visit if in jeju and would be a great place if raining to take the children easy spend an hour or more.

Would have been much fun if you visit this place during warm weather. I havent done any of their tea classes but if you want to take the class make sure to reserve the spot. They have pretty famous tea/souvenir store. Expensive but it will be a great gift for loved ones. If you like green tea flavor try their ice creams! Or they offer ice cream roll cake and other drinks. The museum part was very short where I thought it was bit disappointing. But worth the visit.
Worth visiting and spending a few hours enjoying many artifacts made of glass! Full of suggestions to bring back home for gifts!
Worth to visit  classy  fine art. This is an underrated destination  we do recommend it for adults looking for art and nature
Worth a tour if you're in the area. Fun for couples friends or families. Has a decent restaurant and lots of fun trick art poses.

Woke up early hoping to catch the sunrise. We stayed at a pension just 5 min walk from the entrance to Seongsan ilchulbong. It was a wonderful experience to climb in the darkness of the predawn hour. We were surprised to see so many people waiting the start the climb when we reached?? it was raining the night before so the ground was rather slippery. Thankfully the rain had stopped when we started the climb. According to a local there are 500 steps to the peak. It's  doable though it does require a good amount stamina / more time (we were pressed as we wanted to catch the sunrise). The route is easy to follow - steps all the way; there're toilets along the trail too. It was cloudy on the day we climbed so the sunrise wasn't as we'd hoped but still spectacular regardless. On the way down we took a short detour down a flight of steps to a lagoon-like region where the haenyeon dive for seafood. The view there is spectacular especially before the tide rises in the morning. There is a restaurant that sells seafood caught by the haenyeon that was very yummy  we actually took some really nice pictures there. Would return in a heartbeat just for the refreshing climb!!

With Snoopy Garden’s steep entrance fee it initially didn’t make my itinerary. But the good reviews were consistent and friends also highly recommended the Charles Schulz’s Peanuts themed museum and garden. The indoor museum part was the highlight for me which had explanations about every main Peanuts character and several comic clips that span over Schulz’s 50 years of drawing them. The old newspaper clippings old toys and old books were also cool to look at. There are dozens of great photo spots which can create some major bottlenecks on crowded days. The garden had about half a dozen themed areas (including my favorite Charlie Brown’s baseball field) that are pretty vast and would have been a lot more pleasant to walk around in cooler weather. We skipped the cafe that charged a criminal 8500 won for a lemonade. I’m not sure that the high price of admission is justified but this is a well maintained attraction(which is refreshing considering the high number of run down museums and small theme parks in Jeju) and the quality of the displays are of superb quality. Adults and children both also fans and non-fans of Peanuts both would enjoy the visit here.
With regards as unable to download the recorded clip. Was a fun experience. Located just outside of Famous Love land. A start & end point we clearly shown.

While visiting a friend who works in Jeju my family drove around to visit places casually with a flexible schedule. We planned to visit the temple for half an hour but stayed more than an hour. The name of the temple means medical spring and the flowing water from a 3-dragon-head fountain next to the temple store tasted good and sweet. Although the temple was built for only around 20 years the buildings and layout followed the traditional design. The main building faces exact south that can view the sea. The bell tower is located in the east for sunrise and the drum tower is located in the west for sunset. The main building's first floor wooden windows are beautifully carved with inspiring stories covered by traditional white paper but not glass. There is a traditional Korean painting exhibition of Buddha of Compassion in the basement and it's gorgeous. The best part of our visit was that not many people around. We got the chance to enjoy the quietness and even used the mats inside the temple at the back of the first floor to meditate a short while. There are grapefruit trees in the yards along the way to bathroom.

When we were there they were having a special limited showing of the ancient art of making furniture jewelry boxes etc using shells.  The displays were beautiful and it was interesting to learn how involved the process is.  The museum was nice we went on a rainy day when we needed indoor activities.  The museum is laid out so you walk through different period of history.

When we came it was pouring outside so this place was packed! Even though it was packed we got through the Museum never having to wait in line to take a picture. This Museum has given us some hilarious pictures to share with our friends and families and it was very entertaining to pose in the artworks.

When we arrived there it was already flooded by numbers of tourists so we had a hard time to find a seat and taste the tea sample. Maybe to avoid the bad traffic and buses of tourists you should go early in the morning before the tour buses arrived.Very futuristic design building with the tea plantation across the road perfect for photo session. Don't forget to shop O'sulloc products particularly the green tea.

When in Jeju you can choose to go to Trick Art Museum or Alive Museum. Both are about the same you pose and take funny photos with the exhibits. The Alive Museum is divided into 5 sections Trick Art Object Art Digital Art Sculpture Art and Provence Art. If you follow the route after the first three you will get to the outdoor Sculpture Art. The last section Provence Art is basically a large room with a lot of large-sized stuff dogs in Provence village setting. The dogs are not as cute as the teddy bears at Teseum. I think Alive Museum is more suited for teenagers and youg adults visiting in groups it should be more fun for them.
What I want to know is does anyone go there of their own free will or are all visitors made to go as a part (low point) of a tour?  The tea ain't cheap either.

We've enjoyed looking at the exhibits tasting free samples of tea and bought delicious green tea ice cream (KRW4500). Then we walked over to Innisfree to make our own soap which was so much fun - KRW15000 for one kit that makes three soaps but two people can share the kit so it's a really fun experience! You get to gift-wrap them at the end so they'd make a lovely present. You can naturally buy soap much cheaper but the experience was great and you customise and prettify the soaps as much as you like.Both O'Sulloc and Innisfree can get quite busy - as we were leaving a massive coach party arrived. It's not super-easy to find a table in the O'Sulloc cafe so beware. I saw several couples cruising around desperate to find a table while their ice cream was melting rapidly.The only negative for us was the journey: from the intercity bus terminal in Jeju-Si it took over an hour: the traffic was awful both ways! According to our travel guide it should have been 40 minutes. If you're catching the bus from the bus terminal it's number 755 from platform 10 but beware as the bus leaves before the time stated on the board/your ticket and it's a 50 minute wait for the next one (we've learnt the hard way!)

Went to this as part of a tour. The view from the coach as your ?defying gravity? is of a coach full of people craning their necks not straight ahead which you need to get the perspective. This is something thats maybe worth doing on the way to somewhere else but don?t go out of your way for it.

Went there with the intention to educate my kids on how lava could flow to the sea and came up with beautiful natural shapes such as those seen there. Great to have educational information nearby to explain the formation.  More should be done to explain how small stones also play a part in eroding pitfalls on the rock surfaces It was an easy walk from the carpark.  Some local snacks were sold at the entrance and tickets could be bought via a machine.

Went there as part of a cruise ship itinerary. It is a great walk and views. Avoid if raining or cloudy. The walk to the top of what is known in English as Sunrise Peak is quite strenuous and involves a lot of stairs. There are rest stops along the way. There are no lifts. It can get quite windy so jackets are required. There is a town centre area at the base with restaurants and shops.
Went as part of a day tour with Yeha Tours. This was part of their East tour. Sooo worth all the steps! About 12-20 minutes to top. I slept so well that night.
Went as part of a cruise ship itinerary. It really is like stepping back in time to see houses and the village preserved as it was before technology existed.
Well u can literally find everything here. From live seafood to dried stuff and fresh fruits. We particularly like the night market street food stalls with lots of yummy food

We were taken to the folk village. We originally tried the Jeju Folk Village Museum but that was full of tourists. We were shown around several buildings that we were told were still lived in. Sorry but even primitive people had some form of furniture and cooking facilities. Yes some people may life on site and in other houses. But why show empty and it mean completely empty houses. Show us how you and your past folk lived. Some of the information was interesting until the sales pitch started. The selling of the honey and blackberry cordial which suppose to make you younger and fitter!!! I bought a ship load- not. They took us into a hut with chairs all in rows for a presentation on the value of the juice at $40 a litre bottle. Right next to the village are some restaurants which our guide wanted us to eat in at our expense!!! So I guess the real reason for coming here is their extra bit of money!!!!For most of us on our bus this stop was a complete waste of valuable time.

We were taken to Manjanggul lava Cave as part of a day tour. I've never been in one before and this was pretty neat. Comfy shoes are a must. The feeling under your feet is a slippery one and one of many uneven ridges. The cave is dimly lit which does give it atmosphere but does pose problems if you are unsteady on your feet. The 1km tube takes about 25 mins to walk to the middle of where the volcano erupted. You can't go any further in. We thoroughly enjoy this fab experience and would highly recommend it. It is not suitable for people in wheelchairs or strollers. There are lots of information boards through out the lava tube giving you lots of nformation. The coloured lighting adds to highlight the different textures and forms of the rocks.

We were staying in Seogwipo and had an extra day with nothing to do. So decided to book tickets from Klook on the day of visit. From Days Hotel in Seogwipo we would have to take two buses 201 and then 295?. The first bus is 1 hr 10-15 mins and much more frequent than the second bus which is a 5 mins ride or a 25 mins 2 km walk. Taxis are cheap starting fare of 2800 krw will get you to Aqua Planet from the 201 bus stop but they are a needle in a sack - hard to come by! Other countries??hard to reach facility ir tourist site may provide some form of free shuttle/transport but not here. Once you enter the main facility it would take you a long time to find the toilets - certainly not tourist friendly. Live shows are also all in Korean  albeit with English & Chinese subtitles. The size of this Aquarium is about one third or one quarter of the Okinawa one so we were seriously disappointed with its size and varieties of fishes available. Visit if you have a car or join a local tour or book a taxi. If using public transport like us think twice about going as its 3-4 hrs to and fro Seogwipo.

review: We were recommended Alive Museum by our guide who wasn't so sure what it was all about. The facade is not like any other museums we had visited in South Korea..more like an American building. It actually reminded me of the movie 'Night at the museum'! When we entered we realized that it was all about 'trick art'. We ended up marveling at and trying out almost all the paintings. My whole family really enjoyed the exhibits. The museum is quite big and divided into several sections. There is also a nice spacius cafe there which has fresh delicious egg tarts among other ood and drinks sold. Just outside the cafe is a garden with many interesting sculptures which await you to join in. The museum which I thought would be boring actually gave my family a couple of fun and exhilarating hours!

We were mesmerized with the glass art. Such detailed work! The route made it easier to walk and enjoy all the glass art. Admission fee is 11 000 won. There were also one part of the park that showed glass palace  but we end up walking about 10minutes and no castle was in our sight  quite disappointed. P/S: you can find cute fridge magnet of jeju at the end of the souvenir shop. There were only 1 000 won for one. Very cheap for a fridge magnet I think.

We were looking forward to this museum as a different experience. This museum is amusing but just so expensive in comparison to other museums in South Korea and particularly for the reduced number of exhibits.

We were hoping to climb up to the summit. However we ere told to be there before 9 am. We hiked the Yeangsil Trail instead. It was a great experience. The trail was as per the Trod advisor reviews. Make sure you have the right shoes with the right traction. It was not that hard except for some parts of the trail. We enjoyed it very much. We bought some snacks on the trail but had to carry the trash back to our hotel!! The trail is well kept and marked. Will go back again but before 9 am so we can go to the summit. The views were fantastic . We saw a couple of deer. It was worth the visit. Make sure you arrive before 9 am if you want to go to the summit.

We were here as part of a Yeha Tour. Our guide took us around the village and pointed out some key elements of traditional KKorean living. The Village was small but well kept. We did not go into any of the houses and we did not meet any of the families. Nobody tried to sell us anything. We had free time to walk around and take pictures and then we had lunch on site just outside the gate.

We were brought there by our guide and had no idea what the place was about. We spent over an hour there and had a great time . You need to go there armed with a sense of humor a handphone with a good camera setting  and the ability to use the camera and it?셲 functions for the best results . I would certainly recommend this to anyone with young children  young adults and not so young adults who are young at heart!

We went up at 6am in the morning to see the sunrise. With cold rainy weather the event was less romantic than expected but well worth and good fun for us. We went up with our 3yr old boy. The way up is very well prepared and suitable for children who like walking/climbing a bit. We carried out son partly and party he walked. Well Organised tourist attraction.Entrance fee is only W2000.Have fun!

We went to visit this Dragon Rock and it put a bleak end to our Jeju trip. The rock is a beautiful artwork of nature but people seem to be taking too much advantages of it. The town nearby is full of hotel and other shops for travelers just down the street from the rock. We just couldn?t walk very near to it because the way down there is dangerous and blocked with the fence.

We went to a tee ceremony. A young woman demonstrated the art of green tea for half an hour without uttering a single english Word. Very frustrating The museum is set in beautiful peaceful surroundings but that does not compensate for the lack of english.

We went there with a tour group as part of a package.  It's basically a long walk in the park with a bunch of photo ops.If we had kids with us I would think it was OK.  But not for a couple of retired folks.

We went there by taxi. Only did part of it for about 2.5 hours. Beautiful though it was sleeting and very windy. Enjoyed taking pictures. Would like to come back and spend the whole day. It must very pretty in Autumn.
We went here by bus. We were not allowed to get off the bus. It might be a nice moment but not if you sit in the rear part of the bus.

We went here as part of a shops tour. It was cloudy and rainy so you couldn?t really see anything. Our guide wasn?t very good so he didn?t explain much. I wouldn?t go here again unless it was a clear day

We went down to the second pond in rain and the stairs is quite steep so u gotta be very careful with ur steps. Upon arrival there is a platform where u can take photo of the fall. For dipping experiences u can continue hiking to fall no 1. No 3 is the farthest. U can refer to the map.
We went as part of the Yeha Tour to the west. Bit hurried but ok.Few things are not different from any other good park but the lava cave tunnel is special here.

We walked down to the water for a better view.  Parts of the trek were without steps or handrails and are not for the weak or unsteady.  Saw several women with heels fall when attempting to traverse the rocks.  The best part was the old women divers selling their fresh seafood!

We visited this site on the last week of April when Spring was slowly starting. This place is simply mesmerising!!! The Canola flowers is just so gorgeous and the site of the mountain at the background adds beauty. Perfect for instagram. Worth a visit.
We visited this place and you can see the explanation of the art works while walking to this museum. Can visit for children to see =)

We visited this museum on a rainy day. I didn't expect much but was disappointed by the complete lack of English texts. Pretty much everything is in Korean making it very difficult to learn something. What's left is staring at pictures of cleavage and cultural artifacts that highlight sexuality. Nothing new I'm afraid! As it's also expensive compared to the other things you could visit I'm not sure if I would recommend going here.

We visited this beautiful beach as part of the Western Discovery Tour organized by Yeha Bus tours so we were only given a limited time to experience the beach. We visited during the early days of spring so it was still quite chilly. The views of the beach are undeniably breathtaking. Ten minutes is more than enough to get in those nice shots.

We visited the Tea Museum in a rainy windy day. The place was very crowded with tourists especially the cafe and shop. There were some history and artefacts displayed which I guess was why it's called a museum. I actually expected more from a 'museum'.The goods sold in cafe and shop were the same with other branches in Seoul maybe with a few 'only in Jeju' specials. They were quite pricey but tasted great.

We visited the Manjanggul Cave on a very wet day.  The floor of the cave was wet and the stones slippery. Puddles of water lined the route. It would have been all right if the light was brighter but it was not. The lighting was dim and you can easily twist an ankle if you stepped into one of the many crevasses in the floor. The dim lighting did not make things any easier and you really have to watch where you are going. Wear proper walking shoes if you do not want to slip on the stones. I felt that the lava cone that was our destination was quite dazzling but I wish the authorities had spent a little more care in making the whole walk safer for those who are mobile but who are a little unsteady on their feet like the elderly. The video presentation that we saw after the walk was good. The exhibits were well curated and gave us an idea of other earth formations resulting from volcanic activity in the area.

We visited the Dongmum market in March . It is quite a large market selling all kinds of food items so you can try the local delicacies. Their is a separate fish and seafood area that is quite extensive with a wide variety of local seafood . The is a variety of clothing and souvenir items . It is in the heart of the city around many shopping areas that surround the market . Their is also a Starbucks not too far from the market .
We visited on a particularly beautiful day and took a nice walk to and on the bridge.? There are tours available from the nearby pier and the overall views are wonderful.

We visited on 23rd October. A misfortune happened at about 5.15pm when we were about to leave  our rented car could not start due to no battery. Our baby was temporarily locked in the car so a helpful bystander helped us to opened the door using manual lock and called the car rental company. After a long wait we gotten the staffs at the park to help.the 'gatekeepers' were friendly enough to let us stayed there while awaiting help to arrive. A thin tall lady staff without spectacles came to our help and called the car rental company as we could not understand the options given in Korean. She explained to us and reassured us in English fluently. She also took extra care to follow up and waited til a tow car to help to jump start the rented car. I think by that time her shift is over as few staffs waiting for her too. We are indeed thankful for her and the staffs on that day. Cocomong Ecopark does have a good commendable staff. thank you.Park wise games and design are well thought and worth the entry ticket. The slide down on tire is fun though it looked a bit scary but it is safe. Cafe has got a nice sea view.
We visited Oedolgae as part of our Yeha Bus tour - South Course and it is just another perfect spot to stop and see Jeju's beauty.

We visited in April 2018 and were impressed by the quality and the size of the village. There is a lot of history and culture to be learned here. The exhibits are well maintained they have live gardens and animals to represent the life in the village as well as hands on exhibits for kids and adults to participate in. There are craftspeople and artisans that are making wood work and stoneware that you can purchase. It is very beautiful. Also there is a restaurant on premise near the front gates and gift shop. The living museum and village is wheelchair accessible and worth the price of admission. It will take 2 to 3 hours to see everything. It can easily be a half day experience. Get there early to avoid the crowds. It's popular for students and tourists along with all the major places you should visit while on Jeju.

We visited here as part of a ships tour. The 8 minute film was very interesting. There are three exhibit halls. The first two were the best. You can see the whole thing in less than an hour. I wouldn?t go out of my way to come here
We visited as part of a conference group. It was amazing seeing the size and beauty of the place. It was wet and cold so definitely good shoes and jacket. Well worth a visit.

We truly enjoyed this little tour.  We learned a lot about the Korea of old and life on the island which can be very harsh.  The guide was very nice to our family of four.  We tried their tea and bought some.  This appeared to be their means of support and I was glad to participate.
We took the Yeongsil trail. It is a well laid out path. Only challenge walking on rocks on some parts. Beautiful views. Very cold in the morning. Bring enough clothes.

We took our 27 month old daughter here mostly because she was about to fall asleep on our bike ride and we didn't want to mess up her nap schedule. When you first walk in  they have a walk through of the animals of Africa. Our daughter had a ball naming the animals and learning new ones. We loved the learning experience she got while she stared bright eyed at all the big (and small) animals. She even loved the art and seeing all the different designs (although we admittedly had to go a bit faster than normal through the rest of the museum). For this being an unplanned stop  we were thrilled we did. What a nice addition to our vacation.

We took bus 600 from the World Cup Stadium. This bus is also the Airport Limousine. We got off at Jeju ICC and walked from there towards the sea. The geometrical volcanic rock formation simply took our breath away!  Who cut/shaped the rocks this way? A fantastic work of art created by the Master Craftsman. Another wonder of nature. The geometrical shapes were amazing! This is - must-visit site!

We started at 9am before the busloads Of tourist started arriving. It was a tough hike because the flights of stairs were literally endless. There were many resting areas along the way and I was not shy about just sitting on the stone benches to catch my breathe. Many reviewers shared that they took between 20 to 40 mins to reach the summit. I took 1 full hour. The stairs and tracks were well maintained and most stretches had handrails. The views at mid point and the summit were superb and makes this hike so rewarding! Don?t miss visiting this UNESCO world heritage site!
We spent over 3 hours in the park and exhibition building.Gives you a perfect view on the history and evolution of mother earth. We really enjoyed and learned a lot.
We saw the World Cup Stadium at the start of Olle Trail 7-1. It was very impressive even though we could not enter the stadium. I'm glad we saw it!

We rode most of the Olleh trail routes by bike and it was awesome.  We made a film about it (titled Jeju: A Bicycle Adventure) and met heaps of interesting people to interview.   I'd definitely recommend it as a not-to-miss part of visiting Jeju Island!   I'd like to walk some of the Olleh Trail routes next time to experience it differently and more slowly.
We really enjoyed this part of the weekend. I would even like to return. Superior glass art and plenty of outdoor walking through the facilities. Highly recommend this be on your short list.

We participated in the 2020 Moonlight Walking Tour and it was a really great experience! They prepared a music show and guided us through the whole trail without any issue. The view from the golf course is especially stunning!

We paid for our tickets and got past the entrance when it started pouring. We waited it out for maybe an hour or more  but it didn't stop  only got harder. The lady at the ice cream shop must have felt sorry for us because she gave us chairs to sit on while we waited and even some free chocolates. We asked the ticket counter if we can get a refund since we didn't actually see anything except for the sign  but unfortunately they said no. It seemed like it would have a been a great place if we actually got to go past the front hahaha! At least they made a lot of money selling umbrellas that day.

We only went because it was raining and we needed some indoor attractions. We needed to occupy our young children (ages 9 and 4) so we decided to take a trip to the museum. It was much smaller than we had anticipated. Friendly staff who allowed us to trip some of the more unusual chocolates before we purchased them. We did find the same chocolates at E-Mart that was less expensive. The kids liked the chocolate school but we thought the kit was a bit overpriced as you could do the same thing in your kitchen.

review: We made a short stopover at the Mysterious Road on the way back from the south side of the island - just a quick 20 minute one would suffice. You can start the experience from either lane - there's a marker to demarcate where the Mysterious Road starts and stops.Basic Procedure: 1) Switch on your hazard lights; 2) Slowly come to a complete stop; 3) Prepare your video recording device; 4) Be mildly amused at how something like this can happen!You're done!

We loved looking at the shells collected from all over the world. They were artistically arranged. It was well worth the $6.00 entrance fee and I received pearl stud earrings for free. The gift shop was expensive and bordered on tacky. The few shells for sale were very expensive  $68.00 for a small shell.

We learned a lots about how lava tube was formed and get to experience these natural phenomenon hands on. The kids thoroughly enjoyed the walk as well. Walking inside can be a bit tricky as it?s not flat and some part can be a wet and slippery. Overall a very educational trip for us.

We just visited today. It is winter so maybe the beach looks better in summer time. The sand is covered with a cover and there is much washed up dirt / rubbish on the beach. The view on the city is not specially relaxing.Fun to see black sand but there are other parts of the island where black sand is combined with better views and clean.

We invite you to 'Figure Museum Jeju'  full of fantastic movie figures and statues! There are tons of high quality exhibits! Action figures  movie statues  life size statues  upcycling arts  game statues  etc. Everybody can enjoy and have fun here with figures from movies and games and animations.

We hiked round the coastal route of the mountain in April and took an hour and a half to compete the hike which included stopping at various viewpoints to enjoy the beautiful coastal scenery and sunset.  Weather was good. We started at about 4pm and the place was peaceful with not many people.  We also flew a drone at one of the viewpoints.  The hiking path was well constructed and easy to walk.  You can also ride a horse there.

We hiked down to Jungmun Beach from the Lotto Resort and had a  great time.  The schlep was a little strenuous for a 70 year old especially on the way up.  We went pretty early in the morning on a grey and rainy day at the end of June.  There we no crowds but the water was rough and dangerous for swimming.  This made the whole scene romantic and enjoyable.  The trip was worth the effort but how worth it for you will depend on the weather and the crowds. We walked the beach as part of Olle Trail #8.  We got lost a couple of times.

We have tried black pork in Seogwipo but intended to go to Black Pork Street for the Michelin starred restaurant Dombedon. However by the time we arrived they were already closing (it was close to 11PM at that time) so we went to the restaurant next door called Hwaro Hyang.We ordered 2 portions of black pork ala carte for the both of us although they have a set menu for black pork + abalone. It was not as good as the one we had in Seogwipo but still worth a visit.Will be back for Dombedon next time!

We had to cancel our trip to Udo Island last minute due to heavy rain and because Jeju does not have too many indoor attractions we ended up visiting Aqua Planet. Admission is quite pricey - around USD 130 for a family of four. I am personally not a big fan of aquariums or zoos  but I was glad to learn upon arrival that this aquarium had already released its whale sharks to the ocean. The show was mostly performed by synchronized swimmers and other actors while sea lions and dolphins only played a small part. Kids got to learn some new species from tomato crabs to long-neck turtle and more. Overall it was quite a positive experience.

review: We had some extra time so we thought we would check out Alive Museum thinking it would only take an hour. But it was actually very big. We probably spent 2 1/2 hours there and still didn't go to the outside part. But it was fun
We had a great time! Plenty of fun wall art to get pictures with. It's a little expensive for what you pay for though.

We got the bus to this amazing temple which we found quite easily.  It was one of the most beautiful temples we visited in Korea and one of the few which you are actually allowed to go inside free of charge. There are many parts to this temple which is comprised of several buildings all really interesting and it is set in pretty gardens.  Well worth a visit.

We got here by bus the bus stop is about 20 minutes walk away which was amazing walking all the way up he stream area in the countryside and plenty of opportunities for photos. Very peaceful place there was a few tourists mainly Korean tourists. The water is amazing if your ok walking on some stones etc then give it a go otherwise clogs would be great cause the water feels amazing. But be careful if going in the water as me and my partner walked in quite far when we noticed there was broken glass at the bottom so we tried to walk round it but was a little concerned in case anyone gets cut. This is a beautiful and peaceful place to visit I would recommend staying here a while and just enjoying yourself without rushing.

We engaged a Local private driver to bring us to Yongmeori Coast. He made a call to the Relevant Authority to check the weather and tide condition. Yongmeori Coast is situated beside Mt Sanbangsan.The car park was full that day and fortunately we found one lot. Our driver guided us the walking route to the coast.He was indeed a good private tour guide!We were immense into the nature and its beauty. He skilfully captured many memories into pics for us! This trip was my most memorable part in Jeju.

We drove around Jeju and decided to give this thing a go cos we didn't believe it would be possible. So we reached the road and there were signs that told you that its the starting. So all you have to do is to put your car in neutral gear and release the accelerator at the starting point and watch your friend's jaw drop. Recommended to visit together with Jeju Loveland as its just 3 minutes driave away. Admission at 8000 won per pax. pricey but its a pretty interesting visit XD

We drove along mountainous route 1139 from SEOQWIPO to this place before heading to the airport.  We drove very slowly from the start to finish point and didn't feel the illusion effect.  Some said to see the effect one needs to roll a bottle on the road. I dunno.. i just drove on without stopping. I would however recommend those who drive to drive along route 1139 skirting the mountain and reaching the 1000m height.

We discovered Jeju Mokgwan (the Governors historical admin center) when we drove past it then walked to it from our hotel. Of all the places we visited in Jeju City it was our favorite. Most of the signage included English translations of how Jeju-do was run in the past. The buildings are well restored pieces of art. Very relaxing.  There were also ancient games for children. The venue seemed to be set up mostly for locals for who this venue is free. Foreigners enter for a nominal fee.If you found this rating beneficial please click the helpful button.

We didn't seek to visit Mt. Songak -- our driver just brought us there. Not knowing what to do and since he didn?셳 speak a word of English we just consulted a map near the entrance and decided that the only thing to do there really was walk up to the crater. It's a genuine natural wonder. I?셫 glad we went there because the place was just so beautiful it was worth the effort of climbing. And believe me there was some effort. Unlike other Jeju-do mountains there were rough parts in this mountain without steps or any pavement. Some bits were steep too. If you have mobility issues forget the crater; just walk around. One Korean grandpa lost his footing and scraped his hand on the rocks ??we felt bad for him.There were horses that you can ride briefly for a little bit of money. They were cute and surrounded by fields of flowers. It was like a dream to be there looking at the sky the sea the fields and the horses. Would come back if I have the chance.

We didn't bother with the museum itself. Not my thing.But the Sunday Brunch at the cafe is legendary.Smoothies come in cute glass jars with thick straws and are so full of chunks of fruit that you almost have to chew them as you drink.The brunch itself is a mix of odd elements that I wouldn't normally put together - but they work..... creamy butternut squash soup scrambled eggs mustard coated potato wedges plus a ham/cheese/vegetable panini with salad leaves and balsamic vinegar on the side. Really good food.We sat outside the weather was lovely. Great view of the tea field (part of the museum) and the road. If I come back to Jeju on a trip sometime I'll definitely return for Sunday brunch!

We did this as part of the Yeha Bus Tour East Course tour and they had it timed perfectly for us to arrive and see the Women Diver Show and then after we had enough time to make the beautiful climb up Seongsan Ilchulbong.  We had beautiful weather in October - it was absolutely perfect!  I would definitely recommend tennis shoes and even if the weather seems chilly when you start out - wear a jacket that you can remove.  Lots of beautiful photo opportunities here!
We did this as part of a tour.  It was a good way to end the day. Beautiful natural attraction and lots of interesting information is provided as you walk toward the end of the cave.

We did the yeongsil walk and it was amazing. It was tough in parts of you are not used to hiking but walking all the kids and grandparents doing it lends you the stamina to keep going and gosh is it worth it. Some of the best scenery I have ever seen.
We did it by 7 hours with 1 hour break on the top.We started 9.00a.m. We are o lot of students groups  in the morning and you could't go very fast-be patient. Bring enough water and snacks.

We come here for the lighthouse where Korean drama Iris was filmed. The view is exceptional and didn't disappointed. One unexpected experience is we got to see the women divers. They caught bunch of sea urchins and see their male partners cut it. I wish we could taste it but seeing it is good enough.

We climbed to the top of Mt.  Hallasan via the seongpanak trail. We are in just above average shape and we had no issues getting to the top with not stops in 2hrs 40 mins. There are three rest areas along the way that you can stop at if you need a good break. The last 1.5k to the top is the real shocker. We did not do our homework and went up real early on the morning and it was so windy and cold we did not stay long at the top. It was cloudy at the top anyway so we were not able to see 20 feet off the mountain so we headed back down. There is little to no people climbing the mountain at 6am but I'm out way down there was more people ascending to the top. Overall it was a good trip but I recommend bringing a windbreaker and not starting until around 7 on a clear day.

We came with high hopes of being awed by beautiful camellia Flowers but left disappointed. There was really nothing much except the blooming flowers in the greenhouses. Maybe it was the timing of our visit but we felt cheated. Be prepared to walk a bit to visit the various parts of the park. I will not recommend this park.

We came here on a sunny morning primarily since we had never seen any tea plantations and it seemed like a sufficiently different thing to do on holiday.There is no entrance fee to the actual plantation and parking is plentiful. We started off at the viewing terrace (with a sign halfway up the stairs informing us: 'What a great view') where there were tea plants in view as far as the eye could see. I was a bit disappointed since they really don't look dissimilar from any other bush (not being a gardener myself).The main attraction for us came a bit afterwards when we went into the Innisfree shop. In there you can buy sets for making cosmetic items. We chose to buy two sets of soap making equipment which cost us 10000 won each. You then take the equipment to the craft benches in the shop each of which was equipped with an I-pad showing us in English what we had to do. Our kids (10 and 15 - both girls) just loved it and spent a good 45 minutes happily occupied. We thought it was great - I even borrowed some of their stuff and joined in (very soothing). We thus ended up with some happily entertained girls and two presents to take home to grandparents to accompany the video my husband made of the whole event.After this we ordered some green tea food and drink from the caf챕. Again the atmosphere was lovely - bright and airy. Prices as mentioned elsewhere are quite high but taken in conjunction with the atmosphere felt ok. The food was lovely.Overall we spent a lovely morning here and all came away very pleasantly surprised.

We came here as part of Yeha bus tour - South Course - and my husband and I had a lot of fun with the optical illusion and 3-D photo opportunities!  They do a great job letting you know where you should stand to get a great picture.  We thought this would be a blast for our two teenage girls with lots of Instagram worthy pictures but I think it was an off day for them.

We came here after going to the crater. We wandered around a bit and it was ok just not great- maybe it would have been better if we had purchased an audio tour. If we ever come back to Jeju I wouldn't come back here. They did have some really yummy cactus taffy we purchased though and that was fun. The best part of this place were the old games. I think this place would be better for families with small children.

We came by using GPS to guide us to the National Park. We entered the part called the Healing Forest. Interesting plants on healing the body. Several small huts/cabins are available for those who may like to stay in the forest for healing and relaxation. Do go into the forest for a real feel of the national park. Entrance is free.

We already know its gonna rain the whole day based on the weather forecast that's why we were in this area as it is full of museum...So... We run into this Choc Land after visiting the 'believe it or not museum' & teddy bear museum. Ermm  how to say  you can use part of the entrance ticket to buy chocolate here  and there were many cute & special chocolate displayed... But  that was it  no more no less. So... Unless you don't mind  you may dropby to buy some chocolate & snap some nice picture  rest a bit as there is not much people here. Else you may wanna consider stay longer in the Believe it or not Museum or even the Alive Museum :)

We actually stayed at a hotel right on this beach.  The water is beautiful but there are signs saying no to swimming in some parts of it.  There is a cafe bene right next to it so you can grab a cup of coffee and go sit on the beach.  The only problem is that it is pretty far from anything else like all the museums and nature trails of jeju and it is kind of small which makes me think that in the summer it can get really crowded.

Was? a great refuge from a rainy day. Only one English sign so hard to know what it was all about. Artwork didn't appeal to me- seemed quite juvenile in style. Surrounding area is quite nice- coffee shops and stores.

Was told that its the same operator as Trickart museum but this is larger & newer.  Alive Museum is near the Teseum teddy bear safari.  We did one after another. Lots of trickart to see & interact with to pose for funny photos. Even the adults are having fun. Better value than Teseum unless you're a teddy bear lover.

Was there at about 10ish in the morning lots of (noisy) tourist and you can hardly find a decent seat in the cafe with unruly kids running around. Difficult to take photo at the photo spot cos some particular tourists pose like nobody business and after a long time posing change friend to pose again. I gave up and went outdoors where noise will not be contained and there is more fresh air.Sadly there isn't much nor exciting to see here - yet it is a spot you have read alot before coming. Suggest to just make a brief stop to have a look.I spent more time over at the Innisfree Jeju House instead which was surprisingly very peaceful.

Was not so keen on coming here in the daytime as I wasn?t sure how the glass sculptures will turn out. Was really glad that we came after all. It was really amazing how the artists are able to sculpture glass into so many different sculptures and with colour. Some of them do not even look like glass. The glass was well designed with meandering paths which showcases the sculptures in different settings. Well Worth two hours or more of your itinerary.

Was fun taking photos at Alive museum we visited the museum at night and I guess because of that there were fewer tourists which meant what we could actually interact with the art more and did more funny shots with the art displayed.A great place for families young and old.

Was expecting to see beautiful blossoms of camellia flowers but was disappointed as the blooms were over at that time. I believe if you come at the right time it will be awesome. The only blooming flowers that we saw were in the greenhouses. Park is not small so there's quite a bit of walking to visit the various parts of the park. Would recommend to check on the bloom timing before visiting the park.
Was doing my solo trekking on olle course 7 and of course this is the starting point of the course. Very beautiful cliff and coast line.

Visiting this place remind me such a same road in East Java with the same phenomenon. But I think that this is just an optical illusion created by Korean artist. This is my opinion : the trees and things on both sides was uniquely designed to give an image that the road seem to slope upward though it really slope downward.

Visited the cave cafe only. Due to rain we unable to cover the entire place. Limited choice of drinks: Organic Green Tea Latte Coffee Latte & Americano - Krw6000-8000/cup. Serve only rice cakes with filling (black sesame green beans & red bean) Krw6000/packet. Nicely decorated with luminous lights and some cartoons character.

review: Visited on 19th October 2019.Check before departing because it's often close due to high tide.Unforgettable experience there with stunning spot to take photo.A must visit. Enjoy!!

Visited at mid-day in August.  It was very hot but beautiful.  had a picnic near the carpark and took a stroll along the trail on the east end of the beach. There is a small freshwater spring on the beach at the start of the trail
Visited as part of a day tour. It's quite interesting to understand how Koreans lived in the past. Families still live there though!

Visit this place even if you not interested or lover of sea shells at least to recognise the sheer efforts put in by Ms Myeong Yeon Sook  the director of this museum and owner of this place. This museum which has over 7 800 variety and accounting to more than millions of sea shells originating in Jeju and the world is the brain child of Ms Sook and master Metal craftsman Kwon Oh-Kyun.The beauty of these sea shells are to be seen to be believed. They have been arranged and displayed so artistically that one may easily mistake it as a painting.One may not see much of visitors around  but this really helps as we go around enjoying the magic of nature.Entrance fee is a bit high  but really worth it  considering the efforts put in to bring this huge collection of sea shells under one roof and creating the world's first seashell museum.

Visit if you are free as there are other roads like this in many parts of the world. Objects roll up the slope appearing to go against gravity however its due to an optical illusion. If you visit make sure you try it yourself.
Very well put together with a fantastic collection of music which really compliments the art making it a fully immersive experience. Well worth a visit.

Very pretty and not too taxing walk to add to any outings on Jeju. Our day was a little foggy but the view was still amazing with the Spring growth just starting to show. Lots of other attractions in the near vicinity makes it a good spot to include in a day out. The short but steep hike up to the 'temple in a cave' provides some lovely views on a good day and there are several other attractions at the base of the walk including the Big Golden Buddha temples tea shops the Dutch ship and rock walks. Enjoyable.

Very informative on the formation of Jeju Island with the right mix of information and artifacts. You could also treat this place as an introduction to the places to visits in jeju - the natural part only. Worth about two hours of your time.

Very disappointing. There were a few panels in the entrance hall that had information about chocolate and very poorly kept display boxes  but everything was only in Korean. Downstairs  you can see chocolate packages from different countries  but mostly ordinary products that can be bought in Korean supermarkets. No effort was given to make a proper display with special chocolates. Plus  some chocolates were mislabeled under the wrong countries. There was a station where chocolates in bags could be squeezed into molds. I was not able to participate because the staff panicked when they saw a non-Korean face  despite the fact that I spoke Korean to them. Do yourself a favor and go in the convenience store across the road - there is a better display of chocolate there.
Very cute themepark to while away a good 1-2 hours. Good for summer when it's too hot outside. The rooms are separated into various different themes. Particularly good for silly selfies!!
Very beautiful series of waterfall with each ranging 100 to 200 meters apart from other (3 stages waterfall). Recommended for nature lover and those who love to know the history.
Very beautiful art work on display. Great for all types of groups! Amazing place for photos and for a different appreciation to art. Highly recommend!

Use your 3D imagination and spend a couple of fun hours. Where you can become part of each scenario from hungry dinosaurs to a VanGong painting from an explosive mine to be on a boat in Venice. Great museum best recommendation don't go alone to enjoy it more. Although other tourists are always kind to take some pic for you.

Unfortunately the weather was too windy for us to swim on that particular day in April but I'm sure that it would otherwise be perfect. It's a typical tropical beach with white sand and turquoise water. Hanging around to watch the sunset there is worth it.
UNESCO recognised scenic spot! Most of the part looks more or less similar and the best part is at the last! Better save time for the last part and beware of the slippery floor.

Udo is a beautiful place that we have no regret to visit and spent 3 hours to round the island with rental electric car for KRW35000. Most shop offer KRW20000 for 2 hours and we find it will be a rush that you can?t really enjoy the scenic view of the island. Returned ferry ticket cost KRW8500/person. Rental car is currently not allowed to enter the island as a one year control started Aug 2017 so we parked it at covered parking near the port before we depart to Udo.

Tulips are great. But cherry blossom are ending. The tropical garden is very impressive. If only the other parts of the garden were better maintained. I would have rated this place 5 stars. The caves was very interesting. From hot garden to cold caves. The follow by waterfall. It?s very nice transition. One must spend about 3-4 hours to fully explore this garden and use the guide to walk through the garden. I really enjoyed walking this garden with many different theme. Keep up the good work and hopefully with your increased price you can do better maintenance.

Tr챔s joli petit mus챕e o첫 l'on d챕couvre l?쇕뱔vre de Lee Wal-chong. C'est tr챔s int챕ressant.Le b창timent lui-m챗me a 챕t챕 con챌u par l'artiste  avec trois niveaux plus une terrasse.L'ensemble m'a fait penser 횪 Cesar Manrique 횪 Lanzarote.
Truly heartwarming to see how this cultural heritage is safeguarded and exhibited for us to see. This museum is very informative.

Trip with friends to see underwater animals; sharks star fishes and other tortoise and outside aquarium full happiness with mini korean mart coffee and drinks and if you all like Korean food & beverages terrace

review: Took the longest trail to Mount Hallasan peak (Seongpanak Trail) - 9.6 km - but started a bit late and did not make the cut-off time at the Jindalrae shelter (7km). However it was a great walk and I visited the Saraoream peak on a side tril on the way back.  This was well worth it as there is great view and also a beautiful crater lake.  It is key that you start early and take enough water with you.  Also need good shoes. Although it was August - most of the trail is in the forest - so not so hot.
Took me 11 hrs to complete as I am a amateur. It is important to start in the early morning. Advice to take the seongpanak as it is easier for beginner.

To fully enjoy cultural heritage it is recommended that you spent few hours reading and inspect all the objects that represents it.Even though it was raining during the time I visited I enjoyed the Folk village because they have a very interesting culture and history dated thousands of years.In each places represents how the Koreans house hold systems livelihood and government are highly organized.I also enjoyed the art exhibit and felt honored meeting the National artist.  He even gave me one of his works on display!After roaming around you might want to experience authentic Jeju cuisine by dropping at the Traditional Market inside the Folk village at reasonable price. Oh don't forget to try the Cactus candy!It's just unfortunate that we haven't witness any Korean traditional wedding ceremony that day due to rain.This is much better Folk Village to visit as it is bigger than the other nearby.

To experience something different something unique not know how the car keeps going with the Engine turned off.  We did it on our way over and our way back to the hotel.  It was fun to see all the tourist on the roads waiting to see each car going without the start of the engine.

To be honest we had already sampled the green tea cake ice cream and tea at the O'Sulloc shop and cafe in Insadong Seoul. However this tea garden featured in 'the Kimchi Chronicles' so we had to make a kind of pilgrimage to see it. The overall experience in the shop and cafe was a bit stressful because there are many tourists here at any given time of the day. It is a bit of a shame because this made it difficult to look at the teas properly and then to decide what to purchase. The prices are not cheap - even more so than  eg Fortnum and Masons but the tea is quite unique as it is grown here on the island. I guess it is worth the premium especially if you are buying the tea as a gift.Next door there is the cosmetics side to this enterprise - Innisfree. Once again the products are quite unique eg Jeju volcanic clay pore mask. I think if you are visiting Seoul or any other big city as part of your trip it would be better buying the tea and facial products there but if you are in Jeju also then it is worth popping in to see where it all happens as part of your trip.The teas cake and ice creams at the cafe are really very good but be prepared to pay a lot for it. Just tell yourself you don't do this everyday...

Thought it was gonna be some just rows and rows of teddy bear displays but was pleasantly surprised by the presentation and the whole set-up...the curators really have got a sense of humour!  :)was more like entering an art museum...
Thoroughly enjoyed this gallery. Visually spectacular especially with accompanying music. A very different way to view art.

This was suppose to be one of the 1st museum in the world to exhibit all sorts of teddy bears. Not a very big place but pack with tourists. For the really young at heart or the really young kids this may be a novelty.

This was part of our Yeha Bus Tour and I am really glad it was one of our stops as one of our daughters is a tea lover.  She got some lava cake and a coffee and it was enjoyable just watching her.  It was very busy and we did have to be patient for a table so just keep that in mind.
This was part of our Yeha bus tour - South Course - and it is a beautiful cliff formed by lava.  Such beautiful views!!

This was part of our Yeha bus tour - East Course - that gives you an opportunity to see an old fashioned village showing homes built of thatch roofs and lava rock.  There is a couple that still lives there and explains their way of life and the way things were on Jeju.  We also got to try a tea that apparently tastes differently to people depending on what they have going on in their bodies.  I really enjoyed listening to them and learning about their culture.

This was one of my favourite parts of Jeju! Truly so beautiful!A stunning view and so much history learning about the Haenyeo (or 'Jeju mermaids') who were diving whilst we were there. We also took a ride on the jet boat which leaves from nearby. So much fun!

This was not part of my original plans but I'm so glad this was suggested to me!!! The mountain is gorgeous along with the temples inside. If you walk further down the base of the mountain there are some different food places/cafes. ALSO  at the bottom of the mountain is Yongmeori cliffs!! I had no idea they were there. Such a pleasant surprise. I'm not sure why this place isn't more popular! Gorgeous.

This was just like Legoland in California just on a much smaller scale (no pun intended). It looks like it was once a better place and has gone to the wayside. My first visit was around December then again in June. December was really rundown then June the grass and greenery covered up the poor parts from the winter. Kids will enjoy it you will be wondering why you gave KRW to see it!

This was actually my 2nd 3D museum that I'd been too. While it had different structures and art pieces it's also bigger than the 'trick eye museum' in Hongdae Seoul. This could be good or bad:Good: there's obviously more photo opportunities more of a day out and worth more for your moneyBad: you need to be in the mood to have lots of photos taken turns out multiple photo taking can actually be draining!Don't get me wrong though we had a great time! There's also a go-kart track round the back which you can use for extra money.

This was a tourist trap.No museum to me- just a bit of information about tea on the wall with a tea grousing machine- that?셲 it!Who calls this a museum?The rest of place was for cafe souvenir shop - some observatory deck where you could see the tea field.Honestly Amore Pacific did a great job to let people recognize that Jeju could produce tea that?셲 perfectly linked with their business. Very smart from business perspective- bravo in that sense.

This was a stop of a bus tour through the weestern part of the Island. The so called tea Museum is a building where they sell  tea in all kinds of packaging such as bags and boxes. The word Museum is barely justified by the few pots and cups that are exhibited. You certainly should not come here from Europe because of the tea Museum. For those that never have seen the harvest of tea leaves is worth a stop.

This was a quite pleasant area to avoid people.  Some parts look like the backdrop of a Tim Burton movie in the winter with the leaf-less trees but it was one of the most peaceful spots in Jeju in cold weather

This was a great view. I was able to do it in less than an hour. Its a small descend( you will have to go up these same stairs to leave) to the actual waterfall. There were women selling seafood on the side. You can hear the waterfall when you get in the area. At the entrance there is food. And a 3 minute walk further there is an art museum. The waterfall itself was amazing. There was a lot of water coming down. And you can see it go directly to the ocean. Opposite the waterfall is the ocean.

This village is very well preserved and all the thatched roof houses still live in people with generations down the many 100 of years. The ancient mayor office which is called Gaeksa still remains in the centre of the village and was used to be the place of festivals for the old or parties. Likewise to the castle that was built during the korea ancie dynastiy is still preserved well.

This spectacular waterfall is worth the visit. Parking is easy and there is a small fee to walk down to the bottom of the falls. The bottom is all rocks so it could be difficult to maneuver for some. At the top is a lovely art gallery and cafe.

This really just felt like wasted time on the tour. These optical illusions can be found almost anywhere and is not a part of what I would consider makes Jeju-do a unique place to visit.Do yourself a favor and skip it.

This place will turn u from an adult back to a kid. Not a big place but plenty of Teddy bear and other cartoon figures for u to take pics with. All done up very nicely and photo friendly. But to take a photo is very challenging due to the crowd. About 2 floors and one and half hour is sufficient.

This place was my must visit the first time I came to Jeju and I gladly returned back. You can participate in the tea class which is just another great activity to enjoy at this place. I love that there is both the tea museum and also the Innisfree house both having something different to offer. The only downside is the insane amount of visitors at all time so be ready to wait in line if you want something!

The temple is extremely new as it was built only in 1990s. The outlook was grand and the temple architectural style was reminiscent of the early Korean Joseon Dynasty.  Buddhism in Jeju is unique with its own characteristics and distinctive feature. Unlike the main stream counterpart in mainland Korea Jeju's Buddhism accepts combines and adapt to the local characteristics to form an integrated form of its own. The native folks were staunch followers of Shamanistic beliefs pray to stone deities and attend to superstitious rituals but Buddhism in Jeju embodied the local belief in her Buddhist temples. Behind the Shamanistic gods idols stood the compassionate and tolerant statue of Buddha. Jeju is famous for her natural environment and Jeju's Buddhism takes a natural path towards enlightenment. In fact the repressive Joeson Dynasty suppressed Buddhism but this Buddhist temple incorporated the beauty of the Joseon temple architectural style with Buddhism worship. The compassionate hands of the Buddha practiced acceptance and non-hatred non violence in pursuit of the emancipation of the human soul. I observed that the Buddha statues in the prayer hall were magnificently golden and the grand prayer hall with a height of 28 m was reputed to be the largest in Asia. The ambience here was tranquil and serene. It was a place most suitable for meditation and prayer. I walked around the temple and felt the calmness and peacefulness in the air. From a distance I could hear the dim chanting of the Buddhist prayer. Historically this lovely island of Jeju had suffered tremendously under the repressive hands of the Mongol Empire and also during the Japanese tyrannical rule. But the island survived with the most scenic and gorgeous natural wonders of the world and may this temple bring continual peace to this natural place!.
