The hidden gem in the east of the Jeju island. The best part is to come during sunrise I guess. DOn't miss its traditional ice cream.

The government run museums in Jeju finally opened on a trial basis limiting a number of hourly visitors to 50 with online reservations being required (although it didn?셳 really seem like a must when we arrived).  Considering it's a large complex (which itself looks impressive) Jeju Museum of Art didn't have a whole lot in display other than a temporary exhibition consisting of mostly projected images.  Thorough explanations of the pieces were provided on pamphlets and the display although few in numbers  used the wide spaces well.

The garden starts with a huge glasshouse which is a torture in the summer but we went anyway on carpe diem basis. It's awesome inside and it has little sections. Then outside there are European Japanese and Korean gardens with walkways. Coming from Europe I was not really amazed or entertained by the eurogardens but I guess with Asian perspective they were impressive. The reason I gave 4 is that the entry is expensive and they only sell water at 1 place. Also the toilets are quite dirty

The erotic and exotic art sculptures are interesting and daring but a bit dated.I think the museum has already operated since 20 over years ago based on our driver's comments. It sure is time to undergo an overhaul to spice up the place with digital technology 3D virtual arts and robots.
The Dolhareubong (grandfather rock) collection on the grounds outside the building were my favorite part of the museum.
The caves are a nice break from the blistering heat. Smart to bring a jacket if you get cold easily. Difficult to take pictures cause of dim lighting.

The building looks altogether too expensive aggressive on the outside. The garden is much more welcoming. The oriental poetic flavour of tea culture is missing in spite of the half hearted follies in the garden and the half moon shaped enclosed courtyard. Koreans' wholesale acceptance of western contemporary architecture does not work too well for tea museum. Still not bad for photo taking. We did not find too many affordable items in the store. We were also told by locals that they are not organic and spray herbicide.

The building itself is pretty cool  when we were there the tall grass was in in its full glory and towered over either side of the path into the building. We were given discounted admission because one of the exhibits inside was temporarily closed. It's interesting to walk around inside a bit (there are some nice clean bathrooms in there too) and see the several art exhibits inside. It's very peaceful and relaxing inside the building.

The building is beautifully set into the landscape neither dominating nor subservient to it. Meticulously decorated with timber lattice this is a well designed building on the outside as well as the inside. You first enter into the gallery which brings you along a curve wall into the main sales area which looks out into the surrounding greenery and also into an enclosed courtyard. All in all a very well articulated building.

The building has a good shape good exterior and interior. For the museum itself it is not that special. The interesting part is that you will be explained some kind of tea and they will give you a tester for you to drink. The tea is so good it is worth to buy. And in its cafe they have green tea ice cream and hot gren tea latte which is surprisingly taste really good! Don't forget to buy some :)

The best part of the tea musuem is the cafe. Enjoy a sip of green tea latte pairing it with the green tea ice cream and green tea cake. O'sulloc green tea is different from the japan one and have a unique taste. Musuem is expanding and part of it is under construction. Hopefully it just gets better!

The best part of the tea musuem is the cafe which serve green tea latte ice cream cakes. i never get to try the green tea cheese tiramisu cake at the cafe so i headed to one of the O'sulloc in Myeongdong. It is really good. However the museum is just average. There are only cups and tea pots displayed. I think the BOH tea plantation museum in Malaysa is much better. Just my 2 cents.

The best of all was our retreat leader June Goh. She truly took care of us from her heart and was the kindest sweetest of souls we have ever come across. Thank you so much for making Jeju Island a memorable and wonderful experience!

The bartender look down on you and he is very cocky. Also very poor service I asked for no rock and he puts rock in my glass with whiskey and he told me that that is what I ordered. I would not recommend this place to anyone around the world.

The art is so real and creativity is the most appreciated from this museum. Long walk through the hall with many art picture along side you. At the end there's cozy cafe and beautiful garden. Unfortunately when we visited there it was raining so we can't play and took photo at the garden.

The ?Dragon Hair? rock location is near Jeju airport and a good recommendation if you are trying to burn some time prior to departing Jeju. The location has spacious parking and allows visitors easy access to the actual rock.

thank you so much for lovely detailed explanation of  Jungmun and our museum. If you were teddy bear lover you could stay much longer . we feel so sorry for that. however we exhibit very carefully selected world famous artist's masterpieces and antique bears which have historical value. thank you very much for your visit and have a nice weekend.

thank you for your visit. we exhibited carefully selected teddy bears by the world famous artist and historical value . and there is lovely teddy bear sculpture garden with nice view of Jungmun beach.normally most of people stays about an hour even more at the museum. it's too short 30 minutes  to taste our museum's genuine. have a nice day ^^
thank you for your visit. we exhibited carefully selected teddy bears by the world famous artist and historical value .

thank you for the visit and a comment. each of teddy bears exhibited at the galleries are carefully selected by the world famous artist and historical value etc. and also there is lovely teddy bear sculpture garden where you can take fresh air with nice view of Jungmun beach. please take a time with nice memories of childhood even if you are not a kid. have a nice day.. thank you

Suwolbong peak is a part of the tuff ring which was formed due to hydro Volcanic explosion caused due to molten lava coming in contact with water. One can see the tuff formation layer by layer formed continuously throughout the cliff. Suwolbong also has a observatory tower to monitor the weather.

Sunrise Peak. Sunset PeakWe travelled as part of a tour and on arriving were given the usual coach departure time. 1hour in this instance! Not sure of the entrance fee as it was included in our tourNot hanging around we set off immediately for the top with several good rests in between. The pathway is steep in places but in good order with plenty of resting/passing places. Separate paths up and down. Quite a climb but well worth it. Half way up is a little stall/shop for soft drinks and snacks (they have to manhandle everything up!)Once at the top there are plenty of viewing spots. Really worth the climb. We witnessed a superb sunset over the island and took some wonderful photosOn the path down there is a WC.We made the round journey just about in time with 15mins at the peak and a wander around the cliff edge on the way downFrom what I?ve heard the sunset is equally as breathtaking as the sunrise but not as crowded. Sunset was at approx 7.30 and on the way down the path is fairly well lit

Suitable for anyone who can walk without aid as there were steep stairs leading in/out of cave. Floors were uneven as can be expected. We entered just after the rain so the place was literally dripping from the ceiling. One way in and out from the same entrance. Midpoint (the deepest part of the cave) was a formation that was supposedly the highlight. Lighting was sufficient to find your way around but not for taking pictures unless you are equipt with an SLR and a tripod. My 10yr old couldn't wait to get out as he was rather bored. No thanks to his father(me) who was busy taking pictures with long exposure :-)

Strictly for adults this open air museum has many stone sculptures of male and female in various positions. There is also an indoor museum with miniature clay figurines a souvenir shop and a food stall within the compound. Admission fee 12.000 won. Suggest you combine this place with the nearby Nexon Computer Museum.Transport tip: From the airport take bus 331 332 465 466 at airport bus stand 6 between gates 4 & 5. Alight at Jeju Museum of Art walk 400m. Bus fare is 1150 won journey about 30 mins.

Strictly for 18 years old and up. Could be better if they have a place where you can leave the underage to be entertained while waiting for the old ones. How they portray different sex positions and private parts are funny yet artistic.

Stop by Alive museum on the way to visit other places spend an hour inside the optical illusion museum and play kart outside.  Karing part is fun with the two seater. (Kids can sit next to parent) and it is 4 times faster than the ones in Disney.
Starting the beautiful day with sunrise on top of Hallasan Mountain. Refresh and restore yourself. Worth to hike~~^^

Started trekking early in the morning. May be very cold in the morning but no need to wear too much as you warm up as you trek further. Quite an experience. A little slippery but everyone should try at least once.

Started our trek at around 5:50am for the 6:50am sunrise and we reached the peak at around 6:20am. So many steps... for a person who hasn't been jogging often this climb was tiring! There are wet wooden bleachers at the peak for folks to sit on and await the sun to rise. Many locals head up and will exclaim when the rising red sun appears.The descend starts getting tiring again near later half of route... very peaceful and wonderful view of Jeju at the top.

Started our hike as early as 5.30 am because we took only less than 5 minutes to walk from the guesthouse we stayed. So lucky to be able to have a perfect spot to stand and sit to enjoy our sunrise even though the place was very crowded. The view was spectacular and definitely worth the effort of hiking up to the peak!

Spent half day on Udo Island walking around different spot by tourist bus! The bus tour is highly recommended to visitors without driving liscence since you can get on any bus of the same company with the ticket. Each stop has its uniqueness but still highly recommend the first stop! Simply stopby and enjoy Jimmy's Icecream along the seaside... guarentee this to be the most memorable part of the trip! The beach is also highly recommended since you feel like visiting Maldive with the clear water and blue sky. Try to arrive the ferry terminal to avoid overcrowding!
So-so place which was also offered to us as part of the tour package. The place consisted of 3 floors but was pretty small to begin with. 1 hour should suffice at a casual pace.

Some people may think this place is cheezy or stupid but I think we had a lot of goofy laughs while taking pictures here.  The place has a bunch of 3D or interactive paintings to take your picture with to make you look like you're a part of the place.  I think it was worth the hour or so to come by and get some memorable pics.

So many choices of tea particularly green tea. Bought different variety of green tea concoction in time for Christmas. I thought the tea capsules which you put in a sports bottle and shake is interesting and convenient.  I shall test it on my next biking exercise.

Sitting prominently on a hillside there is no missing this huge Temple and it is one of the largest in the East.There is a bit of steep walk from the carpark to the Temple complex and we rewarded ourselves with a drink from the spring well on one side of the grounds.Consisting of a main hall with a Deities sculptured side walls of Buddha a large bell a separate Pagoda Monks quarters and three or four floors upstairs that can be accessed by visitors. These floors have many donations of precious metal statues and from up here there are excellent views of the main hall.It is prudent not to use the main entry into the big hall as there are clear warnings in many languages not to so out of respect. Also shoes must be taken off before using the side entries on either side of the main doors. A group of hapless visitors ignored these signs and were promptly told off and hustled out to use the side doors.Money donations are accepted either for the upkeep of the Temple or for incense and candles.While we were there we had three or four Monks chanting and offering up to Buddha and it was very serene to hear it from upstairs while overlooking the main hall.The grounds are well maintained with a couple of restrooms around the complex a cafeteria and Temple stays are available too.Enjoy your visit!
Simply amazing. From the moment you start the climb up till you reach the submit the views wqs just out of this world. Once on top it is just wow all the way. A must do.
Should be able to take a slow walk at this place and enjoy even more of its scenery and mother nature's art pieces.

Shinhwa Theme Park is unique in many ways.  First it tries to make its own characters seems as popular as Mickey Mouse and Spider Man - it doesn’t work but it’s great fun just trying to figure out who is who.  Second everything seems brand new - so it’s spotless and at the same standards as a Disneyland or Universal Studios.  Third - the rides are small but oh so knock out fun.  And there is rarely anyone there.  I don’t know if they sell a fast pass but there is no need for one because i don’t ever imagine it getting that crowded.  The food was quite delicious too - great offerings at multiple locations.  You can easily do this park in a half day and not feel like your exhausted or missing anything.  Like everything in Jeju I think they think they are expanding but who knows..  and as i remember the entry price is super affordable.  So this is really a great time for anyone with kids or who enjoys theme parks.  Don’t go in thinking it’s Disneyland though and get picky - just enjoy it for what it is...a bold effort to start something special and first class and doing very well right from the start.  It was a great day for me and my daughter and her two cousins.  Enjoy!
Seri World is a super basic theme park. To me  the only thing fun to do was ride the Go Karts  which was a good time  but expensive and pretty small. I wouldn't return.

Seashell and coral art in their fascinating and natural colors. The seashells' mysterious world under the sea-- as designed by several artists. (is this a title. If not keep original sentence) With a collection of 7 800 species  hundreds of millions of beautiful shells and corals from all around the world joined by metal craft and copper  present the world's first 'Museum of Seashell Art'

Samyang Beach was the only beach in Jeju that took down contact info for all visitors and even had visitors put on temperature sensitive stickers.  The swimming area is quite small and most visitors were there for surfing/windsurfing lessons which most of the beach area was allocated for.  We liked the shaded areas near the water and were able to hang out without having to pay for a parasol or a cabana.  It's not a particularly picturesque beach but it's one of the few in the city.

Run by a tea company that touts itself to be a premium tea brand the tea museum is nothing more than a small exhibition of some historical earthern ware and the owner's/ company statement about bringing back Korean tea culture to modern society.It has a tea shop (their tangerine and Camellia teas are good) cafe (very crowded but has really good green tea sets  for two consisting of ice cream a drink and green tea Swiss roll) and a tea workshop area called the Tea Stone situated in a garden. There's also a tea plantation where you can score some good photos or just simply take a quiet peaceful stroll through the greenery.Nearby is the innisfree Jeju House which also has a cafe selling some of their beauty products. The selection isn't great and they don't  give you free samples though you could score some Jeju only products. I find going to Myeongdong for your K beauty haul much more satisfying and easier on the wallet. Or if you just wanna stop by for their DIY soap making activity (they also sell the kit at the store so you can do it on your own) it seems like a peaceful way to escape the hustle and bustle of the city.
rockbig stonevery good art jobthere are artficila lake made by bronzewow~
rock formation. nothing particularly special about it. visit if along the way or have time to do so.

Really beautiful views from the peak of the tallest mountain in Korea! My friend and I are of above average fitness meaning we exercise with weights and cardio about five times a week. We made it up the mountain in three hours and down the mountain in three hours.  We took two separate 15 minute breaks on the way up and the way down.There will be a lot of people around nine and 10 AM! You should take the first bus in the morning to arrive before the crowds. We Took the 6:10 AM Bus from Jeju city intercity bus terminal and arrived at Seongpanak national park entrance at 6:40am to start our hike. The morning was a bit chilly but by 11:00am it was warm! We hiked in shorts with tshirts and a fleece. We had removed the fleece by 11. Bring water (2-3 bottles) and food as there isn't anyplace to but it once you leave the entrance to the park.If you don't make it to the final check point by 12:00 then they won't let you proceed to the peak. It would be really disappointing. There is an much to see for most of the hike as you're covered by trees but as you get close to the peak you can start getting the breathtaking views of Jeju.

read reviews on this place and thought should visit and ee all the hype. To start of with there is an entrance fee of 12000 KW its not worth it for the exhibits and it was all in Korean so really didn't get it at all. Anyways since I was already there just make the most of it. nothing so special so you can give this a miss if you have spare time enjoy the beach view is much better than wasting time here.
Quite an eyeopening day with many great art installations to explore and view. Would not recommend this for prudish people! Most of the art is outside remember to pack a jacket/umbrella.
Quite a good place with plenty of art work. But I missed the experiential glass making. I do think it is a good experience.

Pyoseon Beach is just the opposite of Jeju Folk Village.So after visited the Village  we came here.The beach is pretty large with wide white sands.It is the perfect place for families to spend some time relaxing  particularly at low tide with its lake-like pools.It has abundant parking space  public toilet (with shower) and cam-ground around the square.Near the beach  there is white lighthouse near the shore.This lighthouse is where the last scene in Kdrama Iris (2009) was film.

Purchased both museum & go karting which provided a fun morning. More fun pictures than I expected & certainly took many photos!! Make sure have plenty of battery as think get better with photos as you go.
Pretty to kewl to check out what they did with glass. Still fascinating to see them make glass art work right in front of you.  Got to see numerous glass art work from different countries...
Possibly the asia only waterfall which falls directly into the sea.. sad part is you cannot swim here.. pretty scenic
plus: the concept about 3D art is very good me and my wife very excited. if you like art and like to take a photo. you must visit this museum.minus: nothing

Please note that one has to charter a taxi to this place otherwise you would face a problem to get back from where you come from as this place is very far. Extremely difficult to get a taxi as most of them thee are chartered.

Personally I find this place to be one of the most undervalued sights in Jeju. Mokwana represents the historic administrative center in the oldest part of Jeju City. The place is not large yet has a lot to show with stories at every corner. It takes only about half an hour from the airport and it took us about an hour to get around once inside. They have nominal admission fee (~ 1.4USD) and it was worth. The only complaint is that some of the labels for exhibits were provided only in Korean.

Perhaps it was too early in the morning (0900) and the food stalls are just starting. Didn't end up eating any snacks which I originally was planning for breakfast.Nice authentic place for local marketing.
Party party
Parts were cute but pretty lame. I only went because they were open later than other museums around.
Part of the full day tour Well worth the visit.Interesting to see how life was many centuries ago and how tough life would have been.
Part of a tour I took. I enjoyed the presentation and the chance to see and learn some of the history of Jeju.
Part of a package trip. Probably wouldn't have gone on our own but nice tour fun foot bath and nice selection of green tea products
address: 제주 제주시 조천읍 선교로 266-4 캐릭파크 내
입력주소: 제주 제주시 조천읍 선교로 266-4 캐릭파크 내

review: Part museum  part art gallery and totally worth a visit. The shells are wonderfully displayed in a variety of artistic designs that enhance the viewing experience. Absolutely worth a visit.

Our two children loved this one. Easy to interact with and you leave with lots of funny pictures to bring home. Pizza at the restaurant was really yummy too. Nice break before you go out to the statue park in the back of the museum. Didn't seem to be well promoted - it's new and the first museum as you start on the road to the Jungmun Resort area. We took a cab from the Hyatt Regency (long uphill walk and potential rain) - less than 5000 won for the cab.

Our last destination for our first day in Jeju is this temple. Before arriving to the worship place near the parking area you will find vendors selling various souvenir items. Upon entrance we walk through the garden where we saw trees with oranges (mandarin in their place). It was last week of March when we visited this place we were lucky to see trees beautiful big oranges. Continuing the path we pass big rocks display with signage written in Korean which I don't understand. We then continue to walk farther and took the stairs until we reached the temple. Just like other places for workship you are not allowed to bring your shoes inside the place. Near the temple is a fountain they say if you drink water in the fountain it will bring good health and good luck to the person.

Our guide added this on to our tour as we had a bit of time free and it proved to be very interesting and informative. You wouldn't need a lot of time to visit so maybe an hour or 90 mins would do but proved to be a lovely insight into Korean life. We particularly liked the story behind the number of wooden logs the put across their front gates whe the villagers go out ask your guide!

Osulloc tea is known as one of the more famous and reliable brand in Jeju...most of the tea is expensive too. Thus it is not uncommon for travel agencies to include the Osulloc green tea museum into its itinerary. A walk around the museum shows you a little background of tea in particular. You can also be able to see tea cups from different countries on display. I tried the green tea ice cream and it was yummy. We were told that if we spend more than 30000 won we can get a tax refund at the airport. So we really spent more than 30000 won on tea :) I wandered alone out of the tea museum and saw Innisfree!!! They were conducting some soap making lesson when I walked in. The deco is very different from what I saw in the malls. And of course I ended up buying stuffs....some facial masks that I wasn't able to find in Singapore.

One of the interesting tourist object in Jeju Island. But I don't understand why they call castle which for me it's a park with many kind of glasses art.  Anyway it's fun &  we can pretend like in wonderland.

One of the highlight of our trip as we wanted to visit tea plantation and try the green tea products. Plantation is ok and is a good spot to take pictures. Observatory facing the plantation and museum is so so only. We tried their happy green tea green tea swiss roll and green tea ice cream. Happy green tea with a citrus taste was refreshing. Swiss roll was yummy (a must try!) and my partner loved her green tea ice cream. A great place to have our afternoon teabreak!
One of the bigger and more popular beached around the island - hence the amount of people. The waves were quite big at this part of the island so there were also some windsurfers around.

One of the advantages of Covid is that it reduces the number of people using certain facilities and the pleasantly low number of people within the Theme Park was testament to this. Only a few of the rides were open. This led me to ponder how some rides can be more Covid friendly than others. But the conclusion I came to was that there is no Covid-difference between the rides but instead it is all just one big excuse to provide half-hearted service and blame Covid. The rides on offer were fun thought the roller coaster was a tad over before it was started. The staff seemed to be depressed. I do not know if this is because it was quiet or because they were having to work there on such a pleasant day. I think families with kids in the range 8 to 14 will like this the best. It's an enjoyable couple of hours and the models and designs in the park are fun.

One of my family's favorite attractions on jeju although we had to drive more than an hour from seogwipo.The enclosures were made such that you could literally be so close to the sea creatures. We were especially awed by seeing the walrus so close up. Food at aqua terrace was also decent. Animal show was better than the synchronized swimming one. Loved the place both adults and children. They did some parts better than the aquariums in Singapore Melbourne etc.

review: One of my best spot in Jeju. We went in July end and the climate was very very hot. We were sweating like anything and in the mid way my wife said lets go back but i was like we have to go. But when we reached at the top it was so beautiful around. I forgot the stairs and all our exertion was gone. The view is so astonishing and it definitely looks like a world heritage.Tip: Do keep lot of water if visiting in summer.This peak has lot of stairs (not advisable old person or for heart patient).

One can take a slow walk inside the cave and enjoy the art form by mother nature. It maybe one in a life time to walk on cool off lava where the surface is not smooth but rather come in difference shapes.

Onc e you are on the south coast you might as well stop at the highest temple of Jeju. Unfortunately all the new temples look artififial and are lacking atmosphere. Do not miss the building belkow with some 500 small Buddha statues and the the 2 Stone statues called Dolharubang.

On month of June 2019 I booked 4 logs on 2 days dive plan. I went to Jeju for solo travel from Jakarta-Indonesia. Really appreciated all of GD expert Dive Masters who really assisted me to adapt on Korea water harsh condition. Even during strong currents the DMs assisted us to enjoy the dive itself it's amazing for me really excellent DMs service in the world ! If you have any plan to dive at Jeju-Korea we welcome you to the best DC in Jeju is Good Diver Jeju. Bravo GD Jeju ??????????????

Okay this is pretty common on Jeju I guess. There are lots of museums that copy each other and it confuses tourists. This listing is an example of that. The reviews for this listing is a mix for the Museum of Sex and Health and for Loveland there is no actual listing on here for Loveland. We did our research first to decide which one to go to and Loveland looked like the more fun one - a lot of the pictures of outdoor sculptures on this listing are actually from Loveland not the Museum of Sex and Health). I'm not even if they both have the outdoor sculptures. Loveland is mostly outdoors but it does have an indoor section too with a shop and a diorama exhibit (if you're strapped for time you can probably skip the indoor part it's not very long and the exhibits inside are mostly in Korean so if you can't read it you have to extrapolate things for yourself). The park is fun a lot of it is very silly (they even designed the bathrooms in the spirit of the park - have a look at the door handles).
Oh wow. Clean. All is delicately placed to delight the eyes of the buyer. You can find fresh fish- delicious citrus fruits among others- sweets ( chocolates- cookies- jelly candies) and artisan work.
Now they have a kart there! Amazing! My kids just loved it! They renewed all the miniatures and now it looks much better.

Nothing much just by telling u some stories about the village peoples than later wanted you to buy thier products and are expensive too. Village are just some old houses and a waste of time. We have no choice coz it's part of the group tour...if u can avoid this place dun go.
Nothing much in this cave except it was very cold for me.. would suggest to go in with shoes. And iz a 1000m walk from the start till the end
Not that Jeju Museum of Art was a disappointment just that it was a small place to see limited collection.
nice place for hiking but must start as early as possible. it's about 1950 metres high. no more entry to the national park after 2.30pm

Nice place for a short stroll from the pier to the bridge and over to Saeseom Island. We took quite a number of photos of the sea  bridge  and looking inland to Seogwipo Port. We enjoyed the sea breeze  the view of the clear waters and the displays of acrobatic jumping fish in the port. Locals stroll the area and it is a picturesque place to relax for a while. If you're into nature walks you can follow the trail around the island  which is probably small enough for you to complete in an hour or so.You can also take the submarine tour nearby at Seogwipo Port - but do check the weather conditions  our guide told us that the currents and weather play a big part in whether you'll be able to see lots of marine life during your dive.

Nice hiking and walk for the great views. We managed to complete the hiking route round the mountain in about 2 hours.Also a good idea is to stop and walk slightly before the mountain as there are also nice scenery of the beach and sea.Beware that the buses out of the area are very irregular and it would be good to start the hike early in the morning and leave before noon as the buses seem to run more regularly early in the morning.We waited an hour for the bus out and gave up walking to the next town to get a cab.
Nice experience. You will require to stop the car and change the gear to N and you will feel the car start moving slowly even though is sloop.

Never would have guessed but there's shopping  eating  a water park and movie theater at the world stadium. Jeju triathlon was headquartered here so I did that business. You can put on Hanboks (Korean clothing) and take pictures as well  that's all free.
Never been to such museum before so it was a very fun experience. Spent about 2 hours here taking tonnes of pictures. Feel like i'm 15 yrs old again. A must visit for the young at heart!

Need something to do with your family and don't want to break the bank? This is the place for you. For $10 per person you can go into the Trick Eye museum which is designed for you to take some amazing pictures using some perceptive and trick camera angle techniques. Everyone will have a great time being immersed in some cool paintings and pictures. There is also a GoKart race track on the premises (extra fee) and a few snack bars to grab something quick.

My wife and I had a great time.  There was no sales trap that some people mention here (maybe because we weren't part of a tour group..)Highlights: Gorgeous flowers everywhere Female drummers performance Dressing up in traditional outfits seeing traditional houses.

My review is a little late but it's better late than never. We've visited this place when I was four months pregnant and I was able to hike up to the summit. This place is serene. It's breathtaking to see the wonderful view when you've reach the top. The kids love the lush greens at the hilly part of this place. It's very well-maintained. There are souvenir shops located at the entrance of the park.

My rating is based on my love of caves.  This one is quite long. Part of the cave you walk right on the cave ground itself/ there are also some walkways.  Explanations are also in English. It is cold inside so bring a sweater. Down the street is a Maze ( which I didn?t see)

My most favourite place in Jeju with neatly built stairs and hand rails starting from the ground to the uppermost area. My group members are mixture of adults and elderly. All of us could manage to visit the top of this mountain!

My friend had completed the maze shorter time by instinct and not following the map.  Me and my partner collected all the marking stamp but takes a longer time to end.  But it was a great fun. Worth visit!

My family took the Eorimok Trail and the path is well maintained.  Remember to bring food and water along.  Recommend to start early morning as it gets hot at noon and early afternoon. It is worth the effort and a must see if you go to Jeju.

My family and I chose the Alive Museum over the Trick Eye Museum because the former is larger and has more art pieces. Furthermore we chose to go in the evening after dinner so that we don?셳 have to jostle with the daytime crowd. However the disadvantage of the night visit is that the karting (carting) activities were already closed at 5 pm. Moreover it was too dark to take any photographs with the outdoor sculptures in the French themed garden. But it?셲 okay because our primary objective was to have a good time inside the Museum which we did. Getting there and Fees: We drove to the Alive Museum (GPS coordinate/code 8050888) and reached there at about 7pm 2.5 hours before Museum closing time of 9:30pm. Parking is free at the huge car park. Entrance fees to the Alive Museum is 10000 won for adults 9000 won for teenagers and 8000 won for children. If you rent a car check whether there are available discounts on the entrance fees and karting on the discount booklet (we used those from the Hertz discount book).The Museum:  Depending on your time spent at each art piece and the number of visitors present (who would jostle with you for the right to pose and take photos) you would need at least 2 hours to ?쐏articipate??in all the art pieces inside the Museum. It is very easy to become so engross that you lose track of time! And don?셳 worry about how to pose because there?셱e instructions and explanations written in Korean Mandarin (Chinese) English and Japanese on how to pose. If you are going by yourself I recommend you bring a tripod along or you could take selfies (although most photos have to be taken beyond the selfie distance) or you could keep asking other visitors to take your photos.We leisurely spent a lively 2.5 hours (7-9:30 pm) inside the Alive Museum which was just enough to view and take photographs and selfies of most of the art pieces. I say ?쐌ost??because there are a few paintings of adult themes which are not suitable for my children. Anyway we almost had the entire museum to ourselves except for 6 other visitors! So we unreservedly and hilariously pose at most of the 3-D art and paintings without feeling shy and without anyone looking at us. As a result we were among the last to leave the Museum.Of the 4 categories of art inside the museum ??trick art digital art objet art and Provence art (sculpture art is outside the museum) ??my favourite are those in the trick art section. Trick art is a perspective technique which makes use of optical illusions so as to enable visitors to interactively ?쐃nter??as the main character into seemingly three-dimensional realistic paintings and artworks with the visitors eventually having a good laugh at their ?쏿dventure??  I particularly liked the 3-D illusions of the parachute standing on the bridge over the molten lava and the hanging onto a nail at the side of the building. We also enjoyed the Provence art section which is a pastel-coloured fairy tale village with bears and dogs donning period costumes.We had a truly unforgettable experience with plenty of amazing photographs and fun with optical illusions. So could you!

My 9 and 7 year old boy loved it and wanted to go back the next day.  Pleasantly surprised that there was go-karts to ride as an option to add to our purchase with the museum tickets. We paid extra and it was worth it. Fast carts!

Must visit if you are traveling with kids. It's in the southern part of Jeju. Site is interesting and educational. Taxi fare from main city is around 35KRW one way. There also other interesting sites around the place.

Most heartwarming and helpful driver in Jeju!
Mere words cannot express how beautiful Jeju Island is and Oedolgae is particularly lovely. A huge rock pool where you can dive and swim - it's great!

Located on the eastern part of Jeju lies Ilchul Land  a cultural spot that showcases Jeju's ecology which consists of the Micheon Cave  Subyeon Park  Folk Village  Wild Flower Bonsai Garden  and Cactus Greenhouse etc??For fans of Running Man (?곕떇留?  this is one place to visit as the team actually filmed here before: various signboards showcasing certain place scenes (at certain corners) that occurred during the filming of Running Man; bringing you a step closer to your favorite Running Man characters! The first stop was Micheon Cave  a cave that is a designated Natural Monument and one of the representative lava tubes of Jeju. Within this cave lie beautifully landscaped and manicured gardens which include a pond (Chumsung Dae).After we were done with the Micheon Cave  it was off to visit the Folk Village with a little yummy ice-cream of a snack on the way. The village was a replica of what would have been in the past with a millstone and buildings with commentary. There were even ?쁫ive??black pigs which were as long as my golden retriever! *Black pork is apparently a famous product of Jeju.For more on my experience and photos  please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/03/ilchul-land-micheon-cave-folk-village.html

Like the beaches that surround beautiful Jeju Island this pedestrian-friendly shopping zone is constantly evolving?쫉ifferent almost with each new day.Once frequented by students the area was reborn in 2011 as Bao Jian Street to mark the arrival of nearly 12000 Chinese tourists who were given a vacation trip to Jeju Island by their employer.  The street?셲 new checkerboard pattern now showcases fountains with colored lights outdoor seating areas Korean-style bonsai landscaping statues brightly colored neon street lights and oh yes  a TROVE of shops.  Specialties include cosmetics trekking shoes and clothes golf-specialty shops hair and nail salons jewelry (including a Korean jade store) local souvenirs a handmade-leather-goods shop restaurants cafes bars and boutique hotels.  Just off the main street one can find bakeries more restaurants bars (including the locally brewed Jespi Beer) and more shops?쫛ne could spend an entire evening or longer just checking everything out.While most of the coffee shops and some stores are open during the day this is a place that really comes to life in the evening. All the colored lights sort of draw you in and along.  And note that while most of the street is closed to vehicles there are a couple of active cross streets so do look both ways before entering those intersections.Depending on when you visit you may get treated to an outdoor concert.  In 2014 the local Culture and Art Division sponsored a street music fest during late summer and early fall.  (For information about future festivals or events call 82-064-728-2714).  Although it can?셳 compare with say the night markets of Taipei or other larger cities Bao Jian Street does provide a bit of balance to all the hiking and climbing many tourists do during the day.  You can definitely find some dinner and a few brews there so check it out.  Interesting photo ops.

Jeju Folk Village Museum as it appears on map for Jeju is on the coast and is a must do for history and culture buffs. There is also a restaurant on premise.The Jeju Folk Village attracts students from all over Korea as well as tourists from other countries. I highly recommend the park. Nearby the entrance  there is a display ?쏥lass Worldwide??and the countries that produced glass are mentioned here - China  Italy  Czech Republic  Arab and Japan. I have seen many Korean Markets in the course of my 18 days in korea. To be honest  no market have truly captured my attention. You can go to any traditional market in any state of S.K and you wouldn't be missing out. My advice for any Korean Traditional Market in general:- Go to any market that is decently sized that is convenient to travel to from your accomodation. - Take note that they do not have rubbish bins there most of the time and you'd have to return your trash to the store which you have bought the food from. - Be very clear in the number of portions you order as I had a rather awful experience ordering one portion and receiving three person quantity since I had three people.- Go in the morning/day time since most markets will be closing shop by 6pm- The fishcake skewers and the broth are great to enjoy on a cold day. You grab a cup from the stall to get the broth and start eating the oden. Payment will come after you return the sticks to the owner.Lastly  enjoy yourselves in Korea. Learn some basic Korean before you come as you will definitely elevate your experience in Korea. Koreans will always treat you better if they see you making an effort to speak some Korean as all other countries.

I had a great time doing this pheasant hunt and afterwards ate Pheasant Shabu Shabu. However there were some struggles in doing this trip which first of all - you must schedule an appointment with them at least 2 days prior to the day that you want to hunt it's quite pricey compared to other hunting opportunities that I've done (make sure you have a friend or you'll get charged the minimum of 2 people) it cannot rain a lot nor be really windy on the day of your hunt and lastly you have to at least have someone who speaks Korean well to get it scheduled. This last aspect is very important almost everywhere in Jeju as the people don't speak other languages - kind of like when my friend and I went fishing and scuba diving elsewhere on the island.So what happens on the day of the hunt? Well make sure you bring your passport and money to get the initial part out of the way. After that you start off with some shotgun practice (if you've never shot before then at least you get some warming up) then you jump on an ATV where you'll cruise to the hunting grounds and then head off to an area where it's setup like a Pheasant tower shoot except it's on the ground. I originally thought that we would have a hunting dog and walk around tracking down pheasants but that was not the case. They said that only happens during November-February when it's not hot. The shooting was very quick and we got all of our pheasants easily since I've hunted before and my friend and I have shotgunned before. Bring earplugs to the hunting grounds! They didn't provide any and I had a feeling that they wouldn't.Once we were done we took the ATVs back and went into the restaurant where they had everything setup for us minus the pheasant meat which they had to process. After boiling the broth for several minutes the meat came out and our server explained how to cook the meat which was great. You cannot beat fresh meat served to the dinner table like we did! It was so good that we skipped dinner because we ate a lot!Overall though I enjoyed it a lot because I was with my friend who had never hunted before. You must understand that there are a lot of people locals and tourists on the island of Jeju so it's not exactly the most open area out there for the best hunting and/or shooting opportunities available. They don't really openly market towards foreigners to show up but if more clients did show up then maybe they make some changes for the positive side. Pigs? Deer? Never know.This is a good place to take friends to enjoy something different especially for those who have never shot guns nor hunted before.

Other than that  touring the museum and picking the tangerines were free.We went to look around the tangerine museum but came out quite disappointed and upset. It was uninteresting waste of time. The museum also felt quite old and outdated  and would recommend you just skip going in (thank god it was for free) and go straight ahead to pick tangerines (which is also free!)I only managed to find the tangerine plantation after walking through a huge tangerine plant-house that only allows you to walk one-way. It was also an uninteresting and non-fulfilling walk with all the tangerine plants looking exactly the same despite what the markers on the ground tell you otherwise. It was a long walk despite all the plants having minimal diversity to showcase. We were properly led to the tangerine plantation only after I found a worker there and pointed out to him the description for the tangerine picking activity on the brochure I picked up at the entrance.The tangerine picking was wonderful. They gave us gardening pliers (2 only for a family of 7) and allowed us to pick a maximum of 3 tangerines. We went a little overboard and picked more than we should have. There was someone there to keep a lookout  but he kind of just turned a blind eye to what we were doing. This place really isn't that worth checking out if you ask me. There is little help available and you can technically pick tangerines all over Jeju (a souvenir store in the museum sold a box of tangerines for S$50) because the island is filled with tangerine trees. But I couldn't really expect much from a place that did not take our money. But if you want to pick tangerines the proper way and not risk the locals chastising you for picking tangerines off the street then feel free to come here.

Husband and I had been to the one in Seoul so we decided to stop by this one as well. I?셫 glad we did. They had completely different props and we had a great time. They have go carts in the back that we paid separately for. The instructors let my husband and I go early while they explained the rules in Korean which we do not speak.

Hiked up from Yeongsil trail. The trail is amazing and full of surprises. The trail starts out as a forested path then opens up to a breathtaking and liberating view of the surrounding. Can see as far as Seowipo city in the south of Jeju. The hike up is long and can be challenging for elderly visitors. There are sufficient rest areas along the way. Cater around 4 to 5 hrs for a return trip.

Hi got Mr Kim as our tour guide for a day at Jeju. He came to hotel half an hour earlier than the designated time. He bring us to eat pork noodles before we start our tour. He is very accommodative with our request. Especially is a raining day and he still being us to outdoor tour site. If you are in Jeju for a tour pls get Kim. He able to speak little English and little Chinese. But for a Korean is consider very good.

Having arrived in Jeju eager to see as much as possible in a short time frame - the art work was top on my hit list. I stumbled across the website for the Museum of Contemporary Art and was very excited to go (as there are so many museums to choose from!)I would recommend a whole morning to visit Jeoji as there is more than just this Museum there. The first Gallery I went to showed a lovely exhibiton on the Sound of Nature this gallery was on the left hand side of the road and was a free two floor exhibition. I then walked along the road to the Museum of Contemporary Art on the right. The Museum had 4 big rooms of Art - all of which had a meaningful message behind the artist's work in both Korean and English! The receptionists were very helpful when directing me as to where to go and I finished my self-guided tour with a visit to the Art shop which was outside in the sculpture garden. A lovely morning well spent taking in the delights of Korean art.

Have you been to a road where cars move on it's own? This is my first experience. It's so cool and the car just move along the stretch of flat road. What could be the reason? Our guide said that it could be the magnetic effect from the earth. It's something that you can only find it here. Well!! At least for me it's the only one of this kind so far until I discover more. Regret no photos taken here coz it was raining when we were here for this experience.

Has serene garden  $3 entrance fee. They preserved the deceased artists study which was interesting. The photos had a rare spiritual feel to them. Out of the way  took almost an hour to get there from our hotel in seoguipo  be careful not to speed above posted speed limit - there were about 20 traffic cameras along the way and even saw two impromptu mobile speed camera setups.

Hallasan the 2nd highest mountain in South Korea is a fantastic hiking place!! You can choose to hike from two different easy routes to enjoy different scenery. If this is your first hike after a long hiatus do be mindful that it's better to take the easy route. Cos at some points it's huge boulders that require some stamina to step up.Take the first bus from the bus interchange cos it's advisable for tourists to reach midpoint by noon so that you have adequate time to trek back and catch the last bus from the bus stop which is still 20 min from the start of trekking point. Alternatively there's taxi if you are a group or pair. There's only a hut at midpoint which sells cup noodles which is not cheap.  Thus advisable to bring along dry food and plenty of water for recovery. Along the way you would meet seasoned hikers and some are so friendly that they offer you a ginseng sweet if they see you resting.  There's a water point and the water taste so good! The viewing points offer such fantastic view and it's so breezy that we forgot ourselves!  Definitely a place to visit.

Hallasan is the climax of our trip to Jeju. Jeju would be non existense if not because of Hallasan. So we made it a point to spend one day out of our limited time in Jeju hiking the tallest mountain in the country.We took Eorimok trail to ascend and descend via Yongsil trail. Both are beautiful in their own way. Eorimok's view started with tall shady trees and later an open space with mountains and oerums (parasite mountains) as far as the eyes can see. Yeongsil on the other hand displayed a canvas of rocky mountain with autumn leaves colouring the picture. The steps at Yeongsil trail were endless and steep - we were glad we took the trail to descend and not ascend.I enjoy being at Hallasan. Hopefully I'll get the chance to take the other trails leading up to the peak in the future.

Halla Mountain is the tallest mountain in South Korea and dominates Jeju Island.  It is an old shield volcano and is snow capped.  The part of the national park that we went walking in was swathed in fog the day that we were there.  The fog gave the national park an eerie ethereal feel as you never knew what interesting things would come up ahead.  Had a great time.

Haha worst museum i have ever visited. For non-Korean speakers  95% of the displays are in Hangul  ?쒓?. The museum is comprised of 3-4 large rooms of tacky semi-chocolate related items  the chcolate displayed is random chocolate primarily bought from Korean supermarkets... some are just empty boxes. The owner seems to be a Liverpool F.C. fan and for some odd reason there was a compilation of Gerrard goals and a signed England shirt; easily the best part.

review: Great to hang out with a scooter. Many scenic views and nice small restaurants and artist. It is really young place that I didn't expect at the beginning.

Great scenic spot with narrow shelf or rock at the base of cliffs which were part of an old volcano.  We visited on a day of high wind and rough seas and the site was closed as the path was too dangerous.  was able to visit the climate exhibition centre and see the model of the Dutch Ship De Sperwer  wrecked hundreds of years ago.  Also took the walk up the hill to the beacon tower.
Great place to visit on Jeju. We loved the path 2 at the village part. But actually  all of it was amazing.
Great hiking trails.   We did #7 along the coast by Oedolgae rock.    Check to see which particular route best fits your needs.

Great hiking adventure! A must do in Jeju! We took Yeongsil Trail and it was breathtaking. If you are have a chance take a different trail going down like. Also if you are heading to the summit make sure to have an early morning start.

Great day tour at small price with small group We did the east course tour. There were eight passengers plus one driver in a car for nine persons (i.e. very small). The driver was very friendly. He gave us some basic explanations but apart from that we were on our own (as advertised I have to say). We were sometimes in a rush but overall we saw a lot and appreciated it. There is lunch included. We liked the tour.

Good to visit this place for an understanding of why it's happening. Optical illusion of the Dokkaebi road and the story behind its discovery. Short road distance about 150m from start to the ending point.
Good collection of artefacts and little describing in details about the items on the display. Liked it.

Generally a fun and interesting exhibition due to the interactivity of the exhibits/3D photos. However if you are expecting a large variety of interaction you will be slightly disappointed. About halfway through the museum most exhibits start to feel similar. More enjoyable for teenagers-like crowds. Recommend about 1-1.5 hours for the whole museum.
Gardens were not well maintained (except bonsai garden good) but it broke my heart to see the conditions of the animals in captivity. Completely turned me off.
Fun walk through the lava tubes. We did this as part of an east side tour that included a beach and Sunrise Point and an English speaking guide

Friend and I visited this museum on our first trip to Korea (while on the island of Jeju) and was pleasantly surprised by a great live performance of traditional African dances and drum beats/riddim. The artifacts are also very interesting and place was so big (3 floors) that we didn't have time to view everything.

Found that there was a lot of explicit trick art etc which I would not recommend for children to attend. More of a friends (adults) and couples outing. Fun for those who love to take interesting photos. Massive place as it also has an outdoor area with sculptures.

For those who can get up early and it's amazing.  The local tourism board also arrange an annual 2-day party on 31 Dec and 1 Jan where you find interesting booths for travellers of all ages which I happened to be there 2 years ago.

For seashell lovers  this is a must visit museum with small entrance fee^^. They have the most exquisite collections of the world of seashells created into masterpieces of art collections. There are 2 storeys of them and a little cozy cafe on the ground floor to relax over a cup of coffee.

For a museum of tea I was disappointed to sample only one type of tea. I had more to taste when I went to a department store than the actual museum.It does have the green tea farm and displays that look beautiful but I found the whole experience disappointing...

Firstly do not travel here for the sole purpose of this attraction otherwise you will be disappointed. Was around the area as I went to Loveland. The Korean GPS number gives you the wrong coordinates so follow my direction. When you exit Loveland turn left and it will be ~100m down. You need to drive further up past the point where it says start and make a U-turn in order to start the experience.

First obtain the Olle walking trails book from tourist information counter near the central bus station. From there you can ask for recommendations. I chose the scenic routes and it required walking up slopes which allowed paranomic view of scenery and also along the coastal area which was slippery due to rain. Some routes bring you directly to the beach whereby you can enjoy Jeju famous mandarin oranges and buy souvenirs such as their honeyed tea and famous chocolates! Do ask for discount like for all tourist attractions and at times the lady boss will throw in more pieces of the chocolate.You can also take partial route but check for the correct bus and you need to check which stop to alight. Unfortunately despite being a popular tourism attraction bus drivers can't communicate in English. Good luck if you encounter locals who can speak English.

First my lower rating for this aquarium comes partly from expectations that were not met.  This aquarium used to have whale sharks but does NOT anymore.  They couldn't properly take care of them one died and they released the other back into the ocean.  Second this aquarium has been advertised as the largest in Asia which is not true.  It has the largest viewing window in East Asia.  Those misconceptions out of the way this is still a great aquarium.  Interesting sea life some of which I had never seen before.  Great displays and a show that is entertaining if you understand Korean at least somewhat.

review: first advise don't travel juju alone ... tour and tour buses become a necessity ... as i was travelling by public bus it took almost more then an hour to reach there .... was already a bit tired by the time we reached ... After going in was a bit excited at how beautiful the place is .... but its so huge that we got bored watching trees after trees at such heat ..... exciting part was the lava cave.... where it was also coooollll.... there are many places to take pictures .... a very good picnic spot .... will enjoy with family

Fabulous collection of contemporary art. Interesting installations and sculptures. Worth visiting. Some important artists shown. I love that Sth Korea has really good contemporary art to view. There are also other exhibition spaces included in the ticket. Amazing really.

Exotic Jeju Island is known for many things: the majestic Hallasan--the massive shield volcano that formed the island and the highest point in South Korea; its mandarin groves; persimmon-dyed galot fashions; the sturdy Jeju ma horses  descended from the ponies of Mongol invaders; tasty black pork; and the iconic haenyeo women divers. But most visitors would not expect to find a Museum of African Art there. And  it's pretty darn good! Located in a massive structure modeled after the mud-brick Great Mosque of Djenne  the museum offers photo-ops galore in its Safari section  although the animals are of the stuffed variety. Very popular with children and couples. The upper floors house a respectable collection of African artifacts and photographs by Kim Jung Man. There is also a great gift shop. But  I have saved the best for last...the live performance of African folk music and dance. The group  Zalia from Senegal  featured lots of drumming  and audience members also got a drumming lesson and a chance to play along on one song. All in all  a quality experience...and a surprising one.

Even though I am not a tea person I enjoyed this beautiful tea museum. Not only is it educational and beautiful but there are plenty of activities for everyone to participate. I learned alot about tea and tea making process and lots of things to drink and eat as well.

Don't go here expecting to be impressed. It's a bit underwhelming. But if you like oddities this is one place to see the major structures of the world in miniature. As well as some other odd ball photo opportunities. This was one of the more expensive places considering how tired it looks and slowing falling apart. I'd skip this one even though it could draw you in from the vastness. Move on... if they lower the price to like 4000-5000won it might be worth it but not at 9000won per person.

Don?t ever lie to our face. Please improve your command in english. If you cannot converse properly all you can do is look me in the eye and properly say sorry. I didn?t come to immigration or custom office. Sometimes I wonder why young teens fall into this kind of business capitalizing in idolizing artists

Do try to catch the sunrise. The view is awesome and the tour groups will start coming in around 9am onwards. Please check with your hotel staff the night before for sunrise timing. Do try to reach there at least 45mins before it rise. My friend and i overslept and had to literally run up in order not to miss the sunrise.

did a slight detour this place  before returing to airport. the road was pretty empty except for one or 2 cars that were already. Did a u turn to face up the slope from where we got in. Followed the sign where to start and put it to Neutral and experience the pull up the slope. It was over with about 200-300m stretch and turned into the carpark beside the shop. Didn't really feel anything strange or excited about it.

Defintely a must see the pictures were artfully created and its great to pose with them.I think i may have paid 20000 won ($20 U.S.) but if you have teenage or below always look for the student (high school) price which was maybe 13000. Have a passport or student id ready.

Decided to hike Hallasan via the Eorimok trail. Went there early in the morning and it was cold. Almost decided not to hike but started seeing people going into. It was a steep hike and nothing prepared me for what I was about to see. Here are some of the photos I took...Oh yeah I made it to the top of Eorimok trail.

Dec 2019 My husband and I (in our 40s) went on a free & easy to Jeju Island in Dec 2019 and engaged Mr Kim Choong Kun for 4 days from 14th to 17th. We touch base with him via what's app and listed the activities & food we wished to try and places of interest we wished to visit prior to our travelling. He could text in English converse in Mandarin & English. He planned our itinerary in an organised manner which ensured travelling time efficiency. He did such a good job in planning our itinerary that we could visit so many places of interest plus completing all our intended activities such as horse riding shooting Go karting and catching a NANTA show. Mr Kim not only drives us to destinations he was knowledgable and could enlighten us with historic information to the various places of interest. This was a big bonus to us as he served as a good tour guide and doubled up in helping us take photographs. He brought us to places for meals which are patronised by locals (not touristy places) for instance we had a yummy authentic ginseng chicken soup pork knuckles sashimi and other Korean local dishes. If you are willing he is able to join in for meals and personally we liked the arrangement as he was able to communicate on our behalf when placing ordersand even suggested to us which food goes well with which sauces. His sensitivity and personality made dining together very comfortable. He is patient and accommodating to our preferences and needs. He is friendly and we enjoyed conversations with him along our rides. He is also sensitive hence for travellers who are introverts I am sure he is able to gauge his involvement in conversations accordingly. He definitely made our stay in Jeju enjoyable and memorable. These are his info/ contact: Mr Kim Choong Kun Taxi licence plate: 2984 +82-10-63425688 Highly recommended. Good Value.

Coming from India this doesn't look much of a village. Yes there are huts but it's all too neat and clean . Some huts have split ACs too. It's a nice setting but I would have preferred seeing another beach or a natural site vs a man made artificial village .

Chocolate land  is an interesting place to visit  it is close to Teddy Bear museum  they charge 3000 won for enterance  & give you coupon for the same amount  so when you buy chocolates the amount is deducted. It consists of 2 floors  the lower level has workshop where I saw people experimenting with chocolates  I did not because the did not know english.They have exhibition where chocolates from all parts of the world shown.They have samples on both levels to taste & then decide which flavor to buy. The upper level has cubicles with history of chocolates  & nice statues made of chocolates.The upper level has coffee shop where you can rest & have hot or cold drinks  icecream & chocolates.

Chilsungro Shopping Street consists of 2 sections. One section is the covered arcade with shops selling international and boutique stuff. This stretch is much quieter. Perpendicular to it is the open space section much more human traffic with shops in the lower to mid tier ranges such as New Balance ABC Mart etc.Suggest to visit this section in the evenings. The shops lightings plus the music add to the shopping ambience in Jeju. You can also visit the nearby Dongmun market Jungang underground shopping centre and the black pork street.

Caught sunrise at the peak after 40 minutes hike.  I do not exercise regularly and the mini hike up the endless flights of steps was a little strenuous.  Nonetheless the sight of the sunrise was rewarding and worth waking up in the wee hours of the morning and taking an 1 hr odd drive in the dark.  I stayed behind a little after the sunrise with most of the crowd gone to enjoy the fresh air and the serenity of the peak while looking out to the horizon. It is one of the most memorable part of my trip to Jeju.

Black Pork Street was recommended to us by our Hotel when I asked about where is the best place to eat the famous Black Pork on the Island. We were quite disappointed as we walked down the street there were hustlers from each of the restaurants approaching you trying to sell you on their restaurant which we found odd. Almost every restaurant required you to buy two orders of Black Pork and my Wife had her heart set on kimchee stew. 3/4 of the way down the street we found a restaurant that didnt require two servings so we ate there. I excitedly took pictures of the pork to find out later that it it wasnt black pork. My advice is find a local and ask where they take their family to have Black Pork and you will truely be able to enjoy their Island delicacy.
Besides being fun place to visit it  has better lighting than Trick art museum It looks newer too.  There are outdoor sculptures which are interesting.

being a glass museum  it really contains everything glass. i love the art pieces and how intricate the details are and all  but if youre short on time  this place is worth a skip unless youre REALLY into glass. i would recommend however  trying the glass making pendant pieces though. its worth the price and experience.

Before starting the Hallasan hike I checked out the Gwaneumsa Temple near the entrance to the trails.  It?s in a secluded area and visited by mostly locals and not really a tourist spot.  The big Buddha statues along with a few rows of small Buddhas are quite impressive although the main halls are not.

Before flying to Jeju-do (island) many of my friends suggested me to do a one day jeju tour that completes the island in one day. But I'm the type of person to enjoy my vacation slowly. Although the island is not that big I wanted to enjoy every bit and detail of the island. I choose to focus on one area at a time. Three months before my trip I researched top 5 beaches in Jeju. After researching I decided my hotel and location place where to spend my vacation. I choose Seogwipo end of Jeju.  The hotel I stayed in was Grand Mer Hotel. I stayed 3 nights there it was a new hotel and the best part was it was across the ocean. You can wake up to the view of the Jungmun beach. Which was listed top beach in Jeju. It's a little far out so you'll need to rent a car. Shopping and museums and hiking was 10 mins drive away. But the view was spectacular and my morning walk was so refreshing. If your ever in Seogwipo you have to try Hawaiian Shrimp restaurant which was 15 mins away from my hotel

Been there last late autumn. Temperature around 10 in the morning. The beach was deserted with only a couple strolling on the beach. The beach is covered with beautifully covered with fine white sand interrupted only by some black rocks. Surround this beach is a park where several human size bronze artworks are erected. Nearby are several eateries and convenience stores.
Beautiful waterfall with nice view.Kids love them n lots of pics taken.Tired part is to climb up the stairs n big step..

Be careful what you do. Just kidding  fret not for breaking anything. The biggest chance of you breaking anything here would be in the souvenir shop. A beautiful museum to go to  to see everything created out of glass pieces. How a simple  yet breakable piece of glass can turn into an artpiece which seems as strong as the pillars of a temple.I like the glass tulips best  a great number of them around this museum. It really shows Korea being a Tulip country  as I get to see these lovely  brightly coloured flowers everywhere. There's a little cafe in there which I thought was a very beautiful cafe  made out of glass. The table you use  the chairs you sit are all made out of glass  added with colour.Surprisingly  the thing you should be checking out is the stand alone toilets  one for female  the other for male. Yes  it's made of glass and from the inside  you can actually see through to the outside! Don't worry  your privacy is intact while answering nature's call  because it's tainted black from the outside and people cannot actually see anything inside! So don't be surprised to see people taking a look at their reflections and doing funny poses while you are doing your business in the toilet. Have a good laugh instead!
Be a kid. Imagine yourself in different parts of the world as you capture memories with iconic buildings from around the world.

At there if you looking for almost all kind of cloth and cosmetic there you will love it! Because some brand name is there and almost is a fashion cloths there! For cosmetic is so many brand there start from Korea product will go to almost every brand in the world  and the area is just next from dongmon market ...and don't forget you are shopping at underground shopping centre not in a big mall because I will experience some poor service...have a great shopping
At first we got warm welcome and free explanation from the villager. I'm happy to see black pig here. After this they will trap you in the room and start to sell.

At first  i thought it was another museum but i was amazed by all the detail and display of all the artwork. Great for families  couples  and all. I recommend buying tickets in advance online as i have found all the museums in jeju island to be at least 2000 won cheaper.

As the Chocolate Land is within 10 minutes??walk from the Teddy Bear Museum in the Jungmun Resort area ??just follow the direction on the sign-posts ??my family and I had no hesitation to visit it on a rainy Sunday.Getting there and fees: First and foremost  you have to note that Chocolate Land is different from Chocolate Museum. Chocolate Land is in the south central part of Jeju while Chocolate Museum is in the south west Jeju. We didn't need the GPS coordinate/code for Chocolate Land but it's 7381197 for anyone who's driving there directly. The entrance fee for adults is 3000 won and 2000 won for children. A voucher was given back for every purchased ticket which can be redeemed at the gift shop or the caf챕 or the Chocolate School.The Museum/Attraction: After going past the ticketing counter  you then turn right. The section on the left is a caf챕 and photograph/selfie stops of different types of Korean houses and benches with toy bears. There's even a figurine of Santa Claus in front of one house  which was interesting considering Christmas is still some 6 months away. The section on the right is the exhibits on the history of chocolates  with the words written only in Korean. We went down the stairways to the level below in which there's a Chocolate School which teaches chocolate making at 120 000 won with lessons starting every hour from 10am to 6pm (I think the children would be more interested than adults). We didn't go into the School; instead  we walked past M&M figurines and a Christmas tree (again interesting) and reached the chocolate shop where there are interesting exhibits of chocolates (behind glass) from America  Europe and Asia. The gift shop has an extensive selection of chocolates (I think slightly more than outside). The prices of the Jeju chocolates of the same brand at the gift shop were slightly more expensive compared to those selling outside Chocolate Land. However  the Chocolate Land chocolates became slightly cheaper than those outside when we utilised the discount vouchers. Unique local Jeju chocolates are those with pink cactus flowers  mandarin oranges and hallabong fillings. We couldn't wait till Christmas?쫤e ate some of the chocolates before we left Jeju  and these were yummy!There is a small observation area (Chocolate Garden) outside the building where the view looks towards the sea. There's also a statue of Willy Wonka from the 1971 movie ?쁗illy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory??where you could take a photograph and selfie with. But we couldn't go outside because it's raining.I recommend visiting the Chocolate Land if you have the time and if you have an appreciation of chocolates. Otherwise  I think you wouldn't miss much if you decide to skip it.

As part of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour we were given some time to go around O'sulloc Green Tea's fields museum and cafe; as well as shop around in Innisfree's Jeju House.Queues tend to be long for both the O'sulloc Green Tea and Innisfree so it's best to prioritize one over the other if you're working with a limited amount of time. O'sulloc Green Tea displays its wide array of teas packaged in gorgeous boxes and tin cans. These are perfect as gifts for loved ones.They also house a cafe in the store where you eat and drink tea-infused items. Fortunately we were able to visit its branch in Seoul already (and bought our fare share of their tea boxes) so we focused our time in Innisfree instead.Innisfree has numerous branches in Seoul; however it's best to look out for the Jeju-exclusive items available in the Jeju house. Similar to O'sulloc Innisfree also has its own cafe which serves its own selection of drinks and food; for those not interested in its beauty products.
as my view that was just a traditional temple. seem not too much local at here but part of trekking point on it. the cave Buddha also not special but ok to visit

As a rule I try not to visit places that do animal shows and keep animals in small confined places. However I came here as a part of a group and enjoyed the portion of the show with dancers and divers. One male diver in particular was very impressive for a small waterpark show. The show was all in Korean so I was unable to understand the informational portions although some parts did have subtitles. There are also animal shows with sea lions and dolphins but as mentioned previously I do not enjoy these.

review: As a resident of Jeju  I enjoy walking through this park every week. It is a great and safe place to take kids or walk dogs. There are two parts to the park: north of the road and south of the road. In the southern part  there are interesting ponds and pathways.I would not recommend this place to tourists only because there is so much else to see in Jeju Island that is far more impressive than this park. However  it is only a five minute walk from the city Center (Jungang Rotary) to the northern part so it is not far at all.

Art is the expression of an idea. Good art is a clear expression of of hopefully a strong idea. I love how both present themselves in the context of apparently underwhelming repurposed setting. Please come visit and give it enough time!

Arrived an hour and a half before closing. The trails starts with a relatively step decent and the walk thru the lava tube is a 1km walk in and 1 km walk back. The lava tube cave is spectacular. Signs were available to help us learn about the the lava tube. An easy walk but need to be careful on certain section of the party as we were walking on wet lava rock. Well worth the drive there!!!

Aqua Planet was a last minute improvised of plans as the wind was exceptionally cold that day.However for the price we pay i am a tad disappointed. Yes the place is huge but the animals that were displayed weren't much. We've seen more and bigger arapaima sharks and stingray elsewhere.Theshow was half synchronized swimming and half animal show. The synchronized swimming wss just okay a bit too lengthy that it turned a little boring.Displays could have been more informative. It wasnt stated smaller shows like feeding times etc. We took our time wandering through the science part but overall there just isn't much.Not recommended.
