The bus journey about 30 minutes and cost less than 2000won one way. The bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly (Although I did not see Jungmun Tourist Complex on the TV screen, therefore I used GPS to locate instead. You can press the bell to alight. For my other bus trip, the stops were announced correctly and was reliable). We actually stopped that Jungmun Tourist Complex to go the the Teddy bear museum and Cheonjeyeon Falls before proceeding to the beach. Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. We needed to change bus 702 (opposite the tourist infrmation counter) to Hyeojae beach. It cost 3300 won. The journey on the bus we great as you will pass by paddy field, wind mills and wild flower fields. You will see a beautiful beach 1st ( I think it is Geumneung Beach) but don?t get down, get down at Hyeopjae beach as the view is nicer (about 2 stops away). You can walk down the stretch later (There is a public toilet down the stretch if you need). The weather then (April 26) was 12 to 17 degree Celcius and remember to buy a jacket and windbreaker as it was very windy when we were there. We so blessed that the sky cleared up to reveal one of the most beautiful turquoise beaches I have been. The beach was wide and the colours of the water clear and blue. There are many caf챕 where you can buy a hot drink from. Noted that the caf챕 only allow you to use the toilet if you buy a drink (the receipt will print the password to get into the toilet). You can always use the public toilet. We decide to walk along the orange and blue ribbon trail (Jeju Olle Route 14) and it was one of the best trail for me. We complete only part of the the trail where we walk through the villages to the fishing port. The route will bring you to a serene path with light house and the wind mills. The the path became rocky nearing the windmills, and we decided to walk out through the rocky back alley of a shellfish place (away from the orange/blue ribbon) and landed at a bus stop. We took bus 702 back to seogwipo. It was a must go beach but only on a clear blue day where the magnificent of the beach will show up.

We stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal and took bus 110 from Jungang Rotary bus stop to Jungmun Tourist Complex. The bus journey about 30 minutes and cost less than 2000won one way. The bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly (Although I did not see Jungmun Tourist Complex on the TV screen, therefore I used GPS to locate instead. For my other bus trip, the stops were annoucne correctly and was reliable). You can press the bell to alight. Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. The Teddy bear museum is a small two storey museum. The famous personnel, movie and cartoon characters were dressed in bears to make those bears special. You can expected toy bears moving their limps as some bears were mechanically  wired. There is also a small outdoor park with some display of bears. There anShort 5 to 10 minutes elvis show at level 2 theatre. 30 minutes would be sufficient to finish the entire museum. The ground floor has a large souvenir shop where you can purchase teddy bear. A small palm size teddy key chain about SGD$15. A 10? bear cost about SGD$50. As I am not a bear fan, I rated 3 stars as I personally feel that SGD$12.50 for the entrance fee was a little pricy. However, I am sure the teddy bears fan would love this place and rated 4 stars and above. Anyway, the museum is close too many other attraction that is walking distance (Eg: Cheonjeyeon Falls). If not, you could also take a bus 702 to many other attractions like the Hyeopjae Beach. If not, you can take bus 782 or 110 back to seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal.

We started with Yongsil Hiking trail passing through: Byeongpung Rock, Witse Oreum till the South Wall Folk and then to go down we followed the Donnaeko Hiking Trail. The way up is ok, the way down is quite difficult, ai recommend proper shoes.

We started with Yeongsil Trail and down with Eorimok Trail which took about 2.5 hour each way up and down. The view of Hallasan were so beautiful at 1700 meters, somehow i regret that i didn't make it to the top of the mountain due to tight schedule. Definitely, It makes me want to go again to conquer Hallasan ! Top of the Mountain !

We started with a speedboat tour around the island. This was so much fun, because it's in an inflatable boat, and it goes super fast! My husband is Korean and told me to hold on with both hands. I am a Floridian so I thought I have done this before, but no! Hold on with both hands! The water are very rough there. You got to see the dragon head rock formation, the elephant rock formation, and the moon cave. He stops briefly to let you take pictures but I suggest a water proof camera with a strap so it does fly away or get wet.Then we went to look at all the restaurants. We took a bus to the middle of the island so we could hike to the light house. The hike was awesome the lighthouse was eh, okay. But the sights along the way we're really cool. The nature, and the ocean below was beautiful

We started our climb at 9am by which time the tour buses had arrived. Eventhough it was crowded it was a safe climbing environment because the paths were well paved with grab railings. The elderly and young could stop at rest points along the way. The view of the crater at the summit, the scenic coastline up and down the paths is worth the climb. Give yourself at least an hour to enjoy this amazing Unesco site.

We started at 8.30 at Yeongsil and exited at 1 pm from Eorimok . Lovely walking and climbing experience. Fresh air, lot of greenery, lot of birds. Just us and nature and fellow hikers. It was fun. Very exhausting but refreshing.One must have good pair of shoes. It has lot of rocky patches.Carry water and some snacks. Sunhat is must. The trail is well guided with sign boards and emergency numbers. It becomes windy on top so a jacket is useful.Must visit place.

We start our journey from Hotel Fine at 5 am in the morning and manage to arrived there at 6 am. Please bear in mind that you are required to climb a high numbers of stairs so at least make sure you had a breakfast first. The effort of climbing the numerous stairs is really worth it as once you reached the top, the scenery are breathtaking and amazed me on each second I blink my eyes. This is a must visit place when you are at Jeju.

We spent more than an hour walking to and back from the beach. The place can get crowded and you can walk farther too but we stopped because of the huge waves. Nice photo location!The stairs can get quite challenging for older folks because it's uneven and slippery even, so have to be careful. There is also some distance of walking from the car park.

We spent a very nice day at the beach. Nice white sand, warm water. There is a place to rent lifejackets and floating articles. Not too much people in september.A lot of pkaces to eat/have a drink nearby.

We selected yeongsil trail since we rarely hike in own country and it is recommended for beginner. We started our hike at 9:30am and it took us 3 hours to reach the shelter while 2 hours to come down. We used back same route to come down since we drove there. The cup noodle shop was closed when we reached the shelter, grateful we brought some biscuit and roti else we will starving after long hike hours. We didn?t expect still having ice on mountain since it is turning spring. This get bit challenging especially to me as my shoes a bit tough to walk on the ice. But luckily a korean lady offered her stick to me and hold my hand to cross the ice path. It really make a different with the stick support. It is really recommended to get prepare self well with good hiking shoes, enough water and food.

we saw a signage stating 'can speak mandarin' with some car parking space outside so we went down, apparently is a very small 'display village' which the 'guide' explained some of the history & activities. didn't manage to see live black pigs. the 'guide' saw we cannot enter the actual village as was occupied with people (which I am not sure how true it is). and they started selling us product in the end... however we manage to see folk village which we think should be the 'real / correct' one when we left and go straight down the road and see walls surrounding with flag & a big map (which too bad we can't understand)

We rent a bicycle and just cycling along the sea coast. It's very windy and we even spotted the hanyeo picking up the seaweed! If you visit the island at the right timing. U can see lots of canola flower! We saw partial here and there still very pretty. If you are being lazy, you can just rent the ATV bike (which most of the people do so). If you plan to have lunch there. Give yourself 4-5 hours to explore this island (take photo, had an ice cream etc etc). Note: we didn't walk all the way up to light house as it is already mid noon and we can see something similar @ seopjikoji so we let go this one :)

We really enjoyed our hike up Hallasan.  From the tropical, palm-tree lined streets at the bottom to the barren, snow coated, rocky pathways at the top - at times it felt like we had wandered into Narnia.  After reading some of the previous reviews on this website and following a stern warning from the concierge at the Lotte Hotel, we almost opted out of our plan to take the more challenging Seongpanak trail to the peak and Gwaneumsa path back down.  In the end we decided to give it a go and turn around if it became too challenging.  For people who have hiked up mountains previously, the difficulty is actually fairly reasonable (mostly steps and handrails etc).  We did not have crampons, walking sticks or colourful walking gear like our Korean accomplices, yet somehow we made it to the top and back anyway.  It took us 3 hours up and 3 hours down (starting at 8am).  I suspect the time of year largely will determine the difficulty so check the weather on the mountain carefully before you go.  And avoid the toilets.  Trust me.

We reached the ferry terminal at 11am and waited for a short while for the ferry. The ferry depart quite frequently so there is no worry for that. As mentioned by other people, you will need to bring your passport to purchase a ticket. If you intend to rent a motorised vehicle in Udo, you will need to bring along your international driving permit. We rented a covered motorised scooter for 3h at KRW40,000. The scooter has doors and can seat 2 people. It took us less than 2.5h to cover the whole island, we even took 45min lunch break in between. The entire island is around 17km, so if you intend to make stopovers for photo taking, renting for 2h will be good enough. Just follow the coastline and you won't get lost. I highly recommend travellers to opt for the motorised scooter for a relaxing trip around Udo island. It will take you just half day. There are not many cars on the road but there are many scooters and bicycles which share the same path. There are many tourists and they might not observe the driving rules very well, so do be careful when driving on the roads. However, if you intend to see some of the other sights on Udo, they are not accessible for these transportation as you will need to take a separate ferry to go there. There seems to be many people taking the shuttle bus in Udo, so I don't really recommend people to do so if you have an international driving permit.

We reached Seongsan around 5am, few peoples has started climbing. Trail quite dark all the way up. City view in the dawn during climbing is pretty. Reached to the top and sun has started to rise. Good facilities provided for the guest to view the sunrise.

We paid for the VIP seats, KW10,000 more than the standard seats. When we entered, noticed that VIP seats were in red right in the centre of stage, while standard seats were on both left n right sides of the VIP seats. Worth paying the extra to be at the centre. They also choose guest from the VIP seats for participation on the stage. Show was hilarious, enjoyed by both young and old. Even my 4 year old child was laughing all the way to the end. It lasted 100 mins, try to catch evening show instead of night show during winter a the hall would be freezing at night.If you have not seen this, include this show in either Jeju or Seoul.

We only went here to escape from the unrelenting rain, but were glad we went. They've resisted the temptation to over-commercialise or trivialise, so only minimal lighting, natural rock footpath underfoot, no intrusive commentary or redundant health and safety notices. All that allows you just to take in the majesty of the space and lava formations in the hushed atmosphere, reminiscent of a great cathedral. 1km from start to finish then 1km back.

We love this place!!! It is so so so so so so so beautiful! Travelled with my hubby and 2 kids and took the earliest ferry to Udo. The ferry we took is those that doesnt come with seats and we have to sit on the floor like the Koreans do. Rented 2 scooters and rode the around the entire island for 2 hours with our kids sitting behind us. It is really safe to ride but you need to make sure you have your international driver license with you before you can rent a scooter. My hubby doesnt know how to ride a scooter, but no worries, simple instructions and quick lessons were given and within 10 mins we were off to our adventure. Though it was winter when we visited, the wind did not stop us from visiting every checkpoint to take photo and of coz, eating the famous peanut icecream. I really felt like I had jumped into a K-drama, especially when I have my Oppa with me, haahaa! It was quite cold so we din manage to get into the water. But already we had spent like 4 hours just wondering around the island. The fun part was to get lost into some residents farms and got directed to get onto the right path. The sceneries are breathtaking! I cant describe better. Really beautiful. Definitely highly recommended, even for people with young kids!

We love Jeju and we loved Nanta!  The theatre in Jeju is spacious as i think compared to other Nanta Theatre.  This is a must show for everybody who visit Jeju!  Here is some dos & dont's when you plan watching NantaDo's1.  Please be on time as it really starts on time.  2.  Arrive 10 to 15 minutes ahead of the show performance.3.  Go to the toilet before the show starts 'coz you need to be focused during the show.4.  Hire a car since the location is a little bit far from the city centre. Allocate 30mins or so for travelling time not unless you are staying at Nanta Hotel.5.  Do choose good seats.  You can sign up from their website to avail discounts for shows.6.  Do search for Nanta Hotel in the GPS or Starlight World Park instead of Nanta Theatre.  Do not attempt to input the number if you are unsure.  Dont's1.  Do not, i repeat DO NOT use the google address mentioned for Nanta Theatre otherwise you will be lost! (It happens to us so don't be a victim)2. Do not refer to Nanta Theatre's contact number from the Visit Korea site as it is wrong.  The picture is wrong but when we checked with the Nanta Hotel, the address is correct.Address:  56-26, Seondolmokdong-gil, Jeju-si, Jeju-do二쇳밸＿?移＿? 二쇱 ＿?紐⑸湲 56-26 (ㅻ깅)I cannot think of anything else but do enjoy the show! This is a fantastic mix of traditional korean drum techniques and a great and funny non-verbal script!

We like to hike.  Our idea of hiking is day trips and not super remote.  A 4-6 hour hike in a California Redwood state park is a good example.We took about 6 of the 20+ trails on the south and east coasts.  Every one was different and interesting in its own way.  We stayed in Jung-Mun on the south side.  Terrific little town with hole in wall places with tasty, healthy, cheap food and good bus transportation.These hikes were a little different from our standard in that they often took more than 6 hours. They also could dip in and out of populated areas. We liked that because we might trip across a restaurant run by old lady divers or an archery club doing target practice.  Most trails were not at all crowded. The worst was part of a trail where a Korean soap opera was filmed. It is hard to describe the Korean style of friendliness. They are very direct.  Example was a man at a bus stop who figured we were going to have difficulty getting to our destination. So he flagged a taxi, allegedly for himself, and invited us to hop on.  When we figured out what he was doing, we insisted on paying.  He refused. We got out, gave the driver money, he grabbed it and gave it back. We tossed the money into the window. He grabbed it again, tossed it back on the street and had the driver zip off.  There we were, picking up our money off the pavement. Anybody who has watched Koreans fight over who gets to pay the bill at a restaurant knows what I am saying. To Americans it looks like a hot argument when in fact it's best friends being best friends.  My advice is enjoy it but don't always loose the argument - sometimes you have to win and pay the bill.  This time we really tried but he was too clever for us;-)

We just came back from the Manjanggul Cave this afternoon. There is an entrance fee of 2000 won per adult. It is quite a distance from the main road. We had rented a car so it was easy for us to go there with the GPS.The cave. It was dark, wet and slippery. It was really difficult to walk, not the whole path cos certain parts have raised platform, but generally the stones/ rocks are at their natural state which is not even. I do agree with an earlier posting that you have to watch your steps cos you may end up walking into puddles of water. You will walk 1 km in and the same route out, making it a total of 2km.The experience is however, - awesome. You are standing / walking where lave once flows. You have to go there to see how big the lave tubes are. The lave shelves, the staglamites, staglatites and many more of the geographic terms fully explained at the appropriate juncture in the caves. You have to take your time to read and understand the structures found there.

We initially came here the day after a typhoon, and when we arrived, all the trails were closed due to wind damage. It was unfortunate, but we got some BEAUTIFUL pictures on the road along the way back of the fog hanging in the trees in stuff. It was sort of a spooky, peaceful atmosphere and we barely saw another car. So even if it's kind of a crummy, foggy day, you might get some really pretty photos. We came back the next day (after confirming the trails were reopened) and decided to do the Yeongsil trail. It's not terribly strenuous, and a lot of it is on wooden stairs/walkways. The worst part is going up all the stairs about halfway through the hike (which is basically the rest of the hike), but if you're like us, you will probably be stopping frequently to take pictures. Bring lots of sunscreen/protective clothing because a good chunk of the hike (maybe even half of it) is completely exposed with no shade. We stopped and had some obligatory ramen at the top (along with some mochi cakes that were kinda like protein bars we bought at the market that morning), then hiked back down the same trail, because that's where our car was. I wore my heavy-duty hiking boots for this, but if it's nice out you can probably do it in a pair of Keens (or similar), or even a decent pair of sneakers with a good tread (there are some parts that are slippery and rocky, so something like Converse sneakers or flip-flops are probably a bad idea. I say this as an experience flip-flop hiker, lol). Go as early as you can, because there will likely be lots of people out. I think we started around 9:30 -10AM and there were a fair few people, but not so much that it was blocking or slowing down traffic on the way up or down.

We hiked up to the peak for Sunrise with our boys age 6&8. We started at the bottom around 4.45am. There were many people along the trail and everyone walk in the dark. Surprisingly, torchlight or headlamps are not required. With some rest on the benches along the way, we reached at 515am. The sun started to rise around 5.30am. It was truly beautifully.

We hiked up the Yeongsil trail. The trail is very well maintained. The views are amazing. However, if you expect to see the crater lake, you should consider one of the other trails. Start early because hiking is very popular in Korea. On our way down, we encountered a steady stream of hikers.

We hiked up on a cloudy day. I really recommend choosing the day for hiking according to the weather forecast. The hike itself and the views and people on the path made it an unforgettable experience, but after like 2,5 hours of hiking on a really quick pace we made it to the top and couldn't see anything. The crater was filled with mist and it was so windy that staying up there would have been quite uncomfortable. It doesn't necessarily take 4,5hours to get up and 4,5 hours to get down, if you don't stop every two hundred meters. But make sure to get to the last milestone (the place to take a break and buy ramen) in time to be able to start the climb to the top.I can only imagine what the trip and the scenery would be like on a clear sunny day.

We hiked to the top of the volcano. The walk was pretty easy but long. Lots of information signs make it really easy to manage. The first part is in the wood, which means no view but shadows. The last quarter of the ascension is out of the woods but was really crowded what made the walk boring.The volcano is nice, but i think it may be overrated dut to the fact that it is the highest mountain of Korea.Anyway, it is a must do if you go to Jeju

We hiked this in December in the snow.  We started from the Yeongsil entrance, and just went up to the Shelter as we started pretty late.  The hike is tough for those who are out of shape but perfectly doable for regular hikers.  It took us about 2 hours up and about 1.5 hours down - the snow making it much slower than we would normally take (and more scenic, but very slippery in places).I would recommend good hiking shoes as the rocks are tough and slippery in places - I saw some people wearing what I would consider to be bedroom slippers and they were really struggling!  Those mini-crampons were also a godsend in the snow (the shop at the bottom sells them).Great views on the way up and from the top.  As we had a car, we had to go back the way we came but next time we will come when the plants are green and do a loop hike.  Can't wait.

We hiked the Eorimok (up) and Yeongsil (down) trails. *If you're hiking in winter, you definitely need crampons.*These trails were stunning. On the Eorimok, we experienced surreal forest setting shrouded in misty clouds and stunning landscapes. At the top of the trail, there's a great place to snag some cup Ramen and Choco-pies. Bring a few cheons and you'll be fine. Two-thirds of this trail was in the forest and the last third was along a large plain created by a lava field. Expect to be amazed by vast skies.The Yeongsil trail was just as satisfying. There are sheer drops and exposed cliff faces. Most of this trail was composed of wooden stairs. If you're planning to bus in and out, make sure you start early. The buses fill up fast and the last bus back to Jeju-si from Yeongsil runs at 16:15 during the winter (until March). Also, if you're not exhausted, the walk to the bus stop from the trail is not too far (maybe 2km at max). Don't waste you money on shuttle service.

We heard and saw this on TV and view to visit when we get the chance so of course we had to see for ourselves. We had impression very crowded road but there were only a few cars. It was about 4pm. We were able to follow another car uphill turn around, follow to the start point.We put car on neutral then let it drive us. Very strange. It just move slow motion like haunted road feel.We stop by at a mart for coffee. There is a cafe too. A few people cos winter not nany tourists strangely, we saw a van and a bus doing same thing, just gliding down.It was just nice finally seeing and experiencing this in jeju.

We have visited this place, Sunrise mountain during Rains. It was raining heavily. While entering we bought raincoats and started tracking. View was so amazing at that time, you just want to keep looking for hours. Rains + Fog has made this place much beautiful. We have got many amazing pics of this place and will remember the same.

We have visited many caves in various countries. More or less they are quite similar. Dark, quiet, mysterious, cold, etc.As with every cave, it's not well litted & its quite dark in certain sections of the cave. Being a natural formation, the ground is usually uneven. Particularly for this cave , the unevenness is very bad. And rocky in certain parts. We spent the most of the time in the cave focussing on the rough/uneven ground rather than the place - in order not to slip or fall. One can easily slip or fall on the widespread/rocky uneveness here & darkness if you looked up rather than down ;& get sprained ankles or worse injuries if you fall.Do not recommend children, elderly or physically disadvantaged people to visit this cave or any caves.Frankly, we were not keen to see yet another cave but since it was part of our paid day tour, why waste it?

We have no idea that such place exist until we drove along the Hallasan range from North to the southern part of the island. Spotted the beauty along the road, we saw a parking space opposite the 1100 Altitude Wetland, decided to stop and take a look. There is a 1-km boardwalk which we stroll along the peaceful woods and admire the trees, stones, frozen stream, mountain range. As it is winter, we could not spot any birds, or wildlife.However, we are pleased with a little surprise that we have added a new destination of the day to our itinerary.

We had quite an adventure that could have ended disastrously for us but for the amazing kindness of a family that stopped to help us and the team of park rangers who helped us down and refused to take a penny from us. The trail we chose to climb was supposed to be the easiest route up to the crater lake and indeed, the trail was well laid. The different parts of the trail were graded based on steepness of the gradient. There were rails on either side most of the way and steps as well. The toughest part of the trail for us were 2 boulder fields that we had to cross. My husband got careless when we got to the easiest part of the trail, slipped & twisted his ankle. Unfortunately, this was close to the end of the trail, less than 1 km from the crater lake. We had to turn back and our daughter tried to help him get back down - another 2 hours when one is fit! It was soon evident that we needed help & soon. The sun would set in another hour, we had forgotten to pack food or water, warm clothes. All along the trail our signs with emergency phone number & a number to indicate location. But we had not coverage & knew no Korean to communicate. Just as we had begun to despair, a party of 3 ladies, a father & a daughter stopped to help us. The 3 ladies told us that they would alert the rangers when they got down. The father & daughter stayed with us, helped my husband lie down on a mat they had brought, elevated his foot, called the emergency number. I had some alleve with me & they gave us some water. The rest & the alleve brought down the swelling some & they helped us proceed   a little more down the mountain till the park rangers (a team of 5) met us. The park rangers iced my husband's foot, sprayed pain medicine and bandaged it. A pair of them supported him down the mountain. The father and daughter stayed with us & climbed down with us. We could not have managed without these incredibly generous, compassionate people. The park rangers would not accept any compensation. They told us 'it is our job'. Regarding the trail itself, the route is absolutely stunning beautiful - rhododendrons were in bloom, one could see virtually the whole of Jeju island and the small islands beyond. Well laid out & marked trail with railings & emergency signs, warning signs everywhere. Our accident was due to our own carelessness.

We had high expectations of Udo, having read many great reviews. It turned out to be very touristy - lots of commercial establishments and activities (e.g. hipster cafes, rental bikes, women divers, boat/submarine rides). We enjoyed the quieter parts of Udo (e.g. Udobong Peak trail), away from the crowds. Please note that drivers of the mini-buses spoke only Korean which posed some challenge in communication. The traffic can also be quite chaotic at certain parts, with the mini-buses having to navigate through the many cyclists/bikers and tourists on the roads.

We had an hour and 30mins here, part of a tour we took,we were really too exhausted to reach the very top but there is a viewing deck somewhere up there and the views were magnificent. The view of the sunrise peak was also beautiful from the bottom. REally worth the visit!!

We had a short very informative visit at this village as part of a day tour. There are many old-style buildings. Very interesting. A very friendly local man explained us the houses, the surroundings and the past way of living there. We tasted some fermented tea. It was very nice. They sell the tea at 40000 KRW. We would have bought a smaller quantity for maybe 10000 if offered, but they had only the large units at 40000.

We had a lovely half hour drive from Jeju city to the trail head of the Eorimok trail. As we neared the mountain, the temperatures dropped and more and more snow could be seen. Roads were clear though and no snow chains were needed.We reached the carpark around 8 am and it was mostly empty (less than 10 cars). It cost us a 1000 won to enter the carpark. The entrance to the Eorimok trail can easily be found by the signage around the carpark.The trail started off easily then there were the stairs. The hardened snow made it harder than it was to climb up and down those stairs. Do remember to wear crampons if you are planning the climb when there?s snow because we only had on our hiking boots and it would have definitely been easier with the crampons.We took a rest and a toilet break at the Witsaeoreum shelter. Do bring your own food and drink as there are no food and water sold at the shelter. There are also no dustbins there so whatever trash you have must be brought back with you.Enjoy the walk and take in all the scenery and fresh air while you?re there and have a great time!

We had a hard time locating the exact spot and drove around a few times. It was also a foggy day which made it worse. When we finally reached the sign that shows the start point, we tried to see if the car would defy gravity but it didn't. We tried twice. It was really a short stretch of road and we gave up. Sad. Perhaps we should go with a guide next time.

We had a guided tour of the compound by a rather fun employee of the place. She was rather animated and injected a lot of humour into her narration. The buildings were authentic and so I think might be actual conserved 'wealthy main house', servants' quarters, pig sty and commode toilet etcPart of the tour included a persuasive sell of their produce (grounded horse bone tablets, honey).

We found this museum in our travel guide and it sounded fun to visit. However, it was quite disappointing starting with the price which was much more expensive than all other museums. It only had a few rooms with teddy bear representations that got repetitive and monotonous after the first. On the other hand there was a nice outdoor park with fun sculptures to take pictures next to. Overall might be good for children but not so worth it for adults.

We found the reviews here very useful for preparing ourselves for the ascent so I'm contributing my own, hoping that others will find it equally helpful!   I'd say that it's a simple ascent for those already used to hill walks and there's no way one can lose the path, as it's between ropes or handrails all the way.  The path surface is mainly made of railway sleeper type large wooden beams and rocks which provide good terrain when dry.  However, for our descent it was raining and slippery and we were constantly bracing ourselves for a slip caused by the crowds - beware those with spikey walking poles! - descending more quickly than we were!  Our ascent to the peak took a leisurely 3 1/4 hours so we were delighted, although we weren't rewarded with any views but the sense of achievement and relief was great!  Our descent took 3 3/4 hours and sometimes my pace felt a little faster than comfortable, as had to concentrate so hard on each footstep placing. It looked as if some sections of the path near the summit have been replaced fairly recently, as we found it to be in good condition and not like the experience of other reviewers - and that was a relief!  I'm very glad that I wore my walking boots to protect my ankles, as the rocks are uneven and a few are slightly unstable.  So, short, if you're fit and used to hill-walking, you have nothing to fear but if you're not usually very active, then give yourself a plan B e.g. opting for the side-path to Sara Oreum if you realise, by the junction with the path off to that (round trip 40mins) that you're struggling.  That would mean that you'd still have the great satisfaction of a spectacular view from Korea's highest mountain but without the stress of having had to climb - and descend! - the 1200 metres from the bus stop to the peak!  Make sure you have enough layers of clothes and a good hat and gloves for the summit and descent, as, at this time of year, you'll definitely need them.  Oh, and if you're looking at the frequent posts with figures on alongside the path and which start with a '1' at the bottom which then progress to '2' etc, the peak is '36'.  Hoping you find this as helpful as we found other reviews!

We followed the Seongpanak Trail to reach the top. It is hard to say that there is a   road   in many parts of the walk, merely some volcano rocks placed irregularly on the ground :) Although we were exhausted when we reach the top, we were amazed by the great view from there, which was a good return for all the efforts we made.

We enjoyed a family visit ( 3 generations ) on a glorious sunny day. This is definitely a place to visit on a dry dayThere are some beautiful gardens and in one area a very impressive display of bonsai trees.The grandchildren particularly enjoyed the area displaying snakes, lizards , tortoises and parrotsThere is also a very good section of caves to walk through

We engaged a Jeju Korean driver at 180,000 won per day for 2 full days to bring the 9 of us around for sightseeing in Jeju. On the first day, the guide headed to the attractions in the north and east of Jeju and on the second day, he covered attractions in the south and west of the island. Oedolgae was located at the southern part of Jeju at Seougwipo city. We came to view Oedolgae on the second day afternoon. It was free entrance. From the car park where we alighted from our van, there was a signboard that indicated Oedolgae was 250 m away from the car park. As we strolled our way to the cliff area, I noticed that this attraction was crowded with many tourists and everyone was trying to take good photos by standing at the barricaded area overlooking the azure seawater with the 20 m tall Oedolgae rock as the background. The scenery was amazing. Our guide spoke good Mandarin and he told us of the mystical tragic sorrowful legend of a saddened wife who feared the death of her beloved husband jumped into her death on seeing the body of her husband flushed to the coast. The Oedolgae rock was the embodiment of the wife who had committed suicide and the base of the rock represented the body of her husband. The sad story dampened my spirit momentarily but the awesome view of the stunning rock blended seamlessly with the azure sea and the clear blue sky. The fresh cooling sea breeze that caressed my face lifted my spirits and the next moment I found myself squeezing among the crowd to take good pictures with my group members against the picturesque backdrop. As we strolled along the weaving coastline, we viewed the Oedolgae from different perspective and each angle projected a captivating scenery. At one point was a big board depicting the picture of popular Korean drama show Dae Jang Geum (Jewel in the Palace) and of the famous Korean actress Lee Young-ae who acted as the great Palace female physician during the Joseon Dynasty. This place was the filming location of this popular traditional korean drama.  I really like this place. It is so picturesque and I was totally immersed in the magnificent scenery appreciating that rhythmic splashing of the seawater against the high cliff. That short juncture, the clock stood still and I just could not believe my eyes that I was standing and facing such a fairy like breathtaking natural attraction.

We drove to Udo Island by taking the ferry from Seongsanpo Port.  We had to pay ferry charges for the car and the number of persons going to the island. We spent about  6 to 7 hours on the island. While we drove around the island, my daughter & friend rented each a bike when we reached Udo.  Scenery and the beaches in Udo Island are not as nice as in Jeju itself.  The fun parts were riding the e-scooter or bike around the small island, stopping by for the famous peanut ice cream and hiking the udobong peak.

We drove over to Sunrise Peak on a rainy, windy day in October and knew that we would be back the following day when the rain was supposed to be gone. Thank goodness, we came back, it would have been a miserable and somewhat dangerous hike in the rain. The ticket for the hike was less than $4 USD for two adults. The hike is full of stone stairs, and if you follow the signs (please follow the signs, don't be that person) there are plenty of places to stop, rest, and enjoy the view. At the halfway point, there is even a small shop with drinks and a souvenir stand that will char a wood sign for you with your name. When we got to the top, and enjoyed the clear, clean skies (so different from Seoul) we could watch the fishing boats and could even see some of the Women Divers of Jeju at the bottom. My suggestion is to get there early, the trails opened at 0730 and enjoy your hike. The bus tours and most other Korean tourists won't be out that early. Wear good shoes and comfortable clothing and bring your camera. It was a lovely sight in October. By the time we came back down after enjoying the views and watching the divers, the parking lot was starting to fill up with many bus tours. This place would still be gorgeous, but not as fun, if we would have had to share the stone stairs with 3,000 of our closest tourists.

We drove our car over to Udo Island via a ferry. It was a great experience. A tip for drivers to head for the parking at the jetty as you have to fill in a form with your particulars (car number, drivers details) to purchase a ticket at the tour office. It only takes 15 mins to cross the island and thereafter we drove around. There are no maps so we went one round. It was very crowded being a Saturday so try to go on weekdays. There are a lot of interesting cafes, 4 beautiful beaches, lighthouses, lots of lovely spots for sightseeing and great photos opp. You can also take a speedboat at the black beach or visit the caves. We took the seafood pot with instant noodles for lunch in a local small restaurant. The last ferry was at 6.00pm but maybe earlier on weekdays. Overall, it was a very interesting day trip and we enjoyed ourselves.

We drove here using waze , got to start from the signage point beside the road , try to put the gear to neutral and it does move.  It's a short drive like 1 -2 minute here . Then we park our car near the 7 eleven and use the restroom .

We divided into 2 teams, my brother teamed up with mom, while my little nephew teamed up with me. So 2 teams started at different starting points & then compete to finish point. As I can see the bell (finish point) at the centre of the maze, my nephew & I finished it in less than 5 mnt. While my brother & mom took just a little longer. It was good for a quick fun though.

We did this hike by end of March 2014. The first part is indeed a kind of forest walk. Half way we were indeed surprised to see some snow on the hills and later on lots of snow on the path, Since we did not have those clampons it was pretty tough. At the 2nd shelter we did indeed buy those clampons whereafter the hike was more easy to do. The view from top was not that good due to the upcoming mist. We were amazed though to see so many RAVENS waiting for food.

We did this as part of Yeha bus tour - South Course - we were in the back of the bus, so it was really hard for us to see, but apparently, you put your vehicle in neutral and it rolls the opposite of what you would expect.  I'm sure the experience would be better in a car.

We did the Yeongsil trail hike in early April as one of our must do activities in Jeju.  Weather was perfect on the day of our hike. It took us about 5 hours (2 ways) at a leisurely pace to complete the hike. We enjoyed the lovely scenery along the way.  Most parts of the trail have proper steps but some parts are rocky and the steps are uneven.  It is helpful to use hiking sticks for the hike. We drove to the starting point of the trail and started the hike at about 11am. If you are driving, do not park at the car park after the car park payment kiosk.  You need to drive another 2 km up the slope to reach the starting point of Yeongsil trail.  Although the hike was challenging but we felt a sense of accomplishment after completing the hike.

We did the sunrise peak climb as part of our tour of Jeju with Yeha bus tours - it wasnt at sunrise, but it was pretty pleasant nevertheless.We started off by watching the women divers at the bottom of the cliff. After this, it is an easy 20 - 25 minute climb up - with gorgeous views over the sea and island. Unfortunately, part of the peak was fenced off because of some maintenance work . We had a nice  walk down, enjoying the views .Tips:There are clean restrooms midway down.Try the peanut and orange ice cream at the base of the cliff - oth are yummy.

We did the Seongpanak walk to the summit. I am of average fitness and found the first half relatively easy going, although the rocky path and stairs after the last rest station were a little harder. It took just under 2 hours up and about the same going down again, with a couple of very brief rest stops.The views from the top are pretty good if there are no clouds. There's not much to see on the way up though, as you're in the tree line and there is little variation.The track is well marked and easy to follow. Most of the track is volcanic rock, although there are sections of board walk as well and the last 1km is wooden stairs. I didn't think that the distance markers were that accurate.The paths get very crowded - most of the walkers are dressed and equipped like they are attempting to summit Everest, but realistically all you need is good shoes and plenty of water. Most people were using walking poles as well, which became extremely frustrating as they tended to block the paths. The only people I saw fall were using these poles, they really are not required.It would be difficult to do this track in the rain, as it would get quite slippery in places. My advice would be to go early to avoid the majority of the crowds - the car park fills with tour buses by mid-morning. We started at 0700 and it was still relatively busy then. You need to be at the last rest station by 1230 to be able to continue to the summit and leave the summit by 1430.Overall - I wouldn't do it again, but if you had a free day on Jeju, it's a good way to burn off a few calories.

We did the seongpanak trail. Check the weather the day before embarking, and make sure you have proper hiking shoes as the climb is rocky and some parts are pretty steep. Stretch your muscles before the climb or you'll end up sore the next day (or you can tote along some muscle rub)! Bug spray is also recommended, for those prone to mosquito bites. Try to get an early start if you can; as you have to pass the second rest stop before 1.00pm if you want to make it to the summit, otherwise the staff will not allow you to proceed. On average you would take 7-8 hours to hike to the summit and back, depending on the number of rest stops you make. There are 2 rest shelters along the way (one selling food like cup noodles and choco pie, pocari sweat and bottled water). There are toilets at both rest stops, but no water; no washing hands or flushing systems. Generally, the climb path is divided into thirds - beginning (relatively easy, mostly uneven but flat ground) - first rest stop - second leg (rocky ground, with some portions made up of many steps) - second rest stop - final leg (fair warning it gets really tough for beginners, as the terrain gets pretty rocky and steep) - summit!

We did the Seongpanak trail which is about 9.7km one way. The trek is pretty straightforward with clear markers. Not too difficult to summit at 1950m as the climb is gradual. Took us just under 6.5hrs to complete the 19.4km course including an hour for lunch and photos at the summit.  For the first 7km, you will be trekking under the forest canopy. The view will open up as you push for the final summit to the crater. Great view on a clear day. Path is very rocky so do have at least a sneaker on to have a good grip, especially after a rainfall, which is pretty frequent in Jeju. Buses plow the route so it's easy to get to start point from most part of Jeju. (Do take note that you have to reach the 2nd checkpoint by 1pm during summer or 12pm during winter to be allowed to continue to the summit.)

We did the hike up the Summit via the 8.7km Gwaneumsa Trail and down via the 9.6km Seongpanak Trail. Though parts of the Trail are marked deceptively yellow and green (  easy  ), we couldn't feel our legs for 3 days thereafter. Very rocky/uneven terrain at most parts of the Trail - challenging without the aid of hiking poles. Good hiking boots is a definite must. Please note there is a specific cut-off time at each Trail checkpoint (which may differ depending on season) and also a specific cut-off time to descend from the Summit. Hence, it is recommended to start as early as possible. We started at 8am and completed around 7.30pm (which was getting really dark by then). Though tiring, the hike is still the highlight of our Jeju trip and memorable for many reasons. The feeling of walking above the clouds (at 1,950m) and having accomplished such a challenging hike is priceless.

We did the Gwaneumsa trail up Mount Hallasan to the peak and back is over 18 miles round trip, over 3500 feet of climbing and then descending it. But it's worth it. I offer only a few points of advice. It is tougher, 800m longer, but more scenic than the Seongpanak trail. To find the Gwanmeusa trail entrance parking lot, plug in the number for the Unesco Hallasa Gwaneumsa Office: +82-64-756-9950 (you only need the last 7 digits on Jeju GPS systems if driving).1) Be prepared with good hiking and walking shoes. We saw two shoes blow out, one about 2.5 hours in. The poor guy had to walk back. There is no rescue if this happens. Also, a girl's shoe blew out on the way down about 3/4 way down, it still nearly 1.5 hours to the end depending on how slow you go. I will discuss in #3 why good shoes are so important.2) Go early, and go slow if you are not in shape or do not do activities often. Hallasan is definitely attainable by nearly anyone but it is tough, very tough because of the steep steps. Unless you are in shape and do many physical activities all the time, I recommend starting at 6AM. You MUST be at Samgakbong shelter by 12:30PM otherwise they will turn you around. It is 3/4 way up the climb. From here it is another 2 hours to the peak of the Halla.3. The volcanic stone paths and the stairs will make your legs very very tired and your feet sore. I believe they made Gwanmeusa trail challenging with rocks on purpose. These are not small rocks, they are big ones that challenge each step. Walking sticks are highly recommended. The stones seem pretty and authentic until halfway up then they are tough. Then on the way down, each step seems like a sadistic joke played by the planners. Eventually you will be relieved to make it to the bottom to your car or bus.4. Be prepared for wind. We got lucky and it was warm the day we went... in fact low warm temperatures will seem even warmer due to humidity about 1/2 the time up the mountain and back. It is a little cooler and windier at the top. Wear light, polyester clothing in layers. long sleeve tech shirt, with light jacket and light rain cover. You should be OK. Gloves and hat or scarves during cooler time. Very light during summer due to heat and humidity.After you get down on Gwanmeusa trail, there is a small restaurant with Korean snacks like pajeon and gimbap, as well as a 7/11 next door. Drink some local mokkoli or soju with with the hot snacks/food! We had a great time. Only 20 minutes out Jeju City when there is no traffic. However with rush hour traffic, or busy time it takes about 45 minutes to get back into Jeju City.

We did Olle Trail 1 (15kms) starting in Siheung and finishing in Gwanchiji Beach. Trail started next to Siheung elementary school and it was very well signposted all the way. The information center 1km up the road has no info in English and the gentleman didn't speak It either, although it's not really needed to follow the trail.The first 5-6kms are beautiful as you go up a hill, from where you can see the coast (including Seongsan Ilchulbong) on one side and the plains and Hallasan on the other, and you're surrounded by forest.Once down the hill, trail gets very boring for 8-9kms as it's on paved trails next to main roads. Final part from Seongsan to Gwanchiji is nice again as you walk next to the beach/sea.

We did not had a chance to really walk around the village due to the on-going construction. Only manage to explore the front part of the village. There are students who volunteer themselves to walk you through the history of the village. Quite an interesting one. At the end of the sharing, they also do some selling.

We did a day trip covering Sunrise Peak and the Manjanggul Lava Tubes. It was a long drive though from the south. It was quite interesting to experience the vastness inside these tubes, imagining all these form by lava thousands of years ago. It was dark indeed and photography or videoing seemed very difficult. It was cool and moist, dark of course, not suitable for those in dress shoes or high heels. Be prepared to come along with proper walking shoes with good grip and some areas are wet.  Not a suitable site for family with young children. The end of the walk was a constructed steel walkway to see the   turtle  . Not something to wow at, but just knowing that , that is the farthest you can go. Being a tourist attraction, food was easily availble.

We did 3 Jeju Olle Route 1, 6 & 7 and 14-1. We did not complete all the Olle route but every one of the route was breath-taking and worth the walk. All the route were doable by public transport and car rental was not needed.Jeju Olle Route 1We did not do the entire route 1 as we wanted to visit seongsan 1st plus we started late. As we stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal, we took bus 701 to Seongsan ilchulbong. The bus journey took more than 1.5hours and cost about 3300won one way and the bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly.  The TV screen will flash seongsan-ri entrance and you can press the bell to alight (photo attached). Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. I have car sickness but it was still bearable for me. We alighted and headed to the black beach along Seongsan. It was called the black beach as the sand was black. Not sure why we need not need to pay for the entrance fee to Seongsan that day (25th April) but we were happy as the temperature was about 17 degree Celsius. We wore T-shirt with a windbreaker only as the sun kept us warm. A windbreaker will be good as it can be quite windy especially if you walk along the beach. There were 2 track at Seongsan. One track led to the peak of Seongsan which consist about 10 flights of stairs (Pretty doable even with poor fitness ? just take as many rest breaks as needed). At the peak, you will be able to have a panoramic view of the city and the surrounding water bodies. The other track is along the coast area with pretty wild purple (I think is Lunaria annua)  and yellow canola wild flower and volcanic stacked rocks.After Seongsan, you can continue to the Jeju Olle Route 1 to Al Oreum along the ocean area. The Jeju Olle Route 1 will pass by canola flower patches for photo taking, a nice ocean view with beaches for scenic viewing, a new hotel named as The Cloud, the ferry terminal, along many beautiful seashore. We stopped at one of the seashore where we witness locals harvesting gastropod, sword razor clams and cockles using simple equipment. We were friendly and allowed us to take photo of how they harvest sword razor clams. If you are interesting in harvesting, remember to bring a good jacket as the wind was strong in April. Putting on waterproof boots will be good too. We continued to walk along the coast where cuttlefish were being dried along the coast. There were many restaurants along the way too. As we continued the walk, we noted that there was no bus stop along the walk after the fish port/market (there was a Ojo Haenyeo House bus stop). The next bus stop was at Jongdal Elementary school which was quite a distance away.After walking through the coastal area, you will walk through a village for a short period before reaching the expressway. The walk towards Al Oreum required you to cross an expressway and the route up the Al Oreum seemed alittle deserted with trees but there was still a road up. You will contine to see the orange/blue ribbons that were well spaced. However, we started the walk at 1pm and took too many stops for picture taking. Therefore, we were unable to finish the walk to Al Oreum.We decided to back track  and took bus 701 from the Jongdal Elementary school stop at about 5.30 pm back to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal (we take on the side nearer to the expressway, not the opposite). Therefore, make sure you start the Olle route earlier if you want to reach the top of Al Oreum where you will have a bird-eye view of the paddy field and coastal area. The bus journey took about 2 hours to reach Seogwipo-si.Jeju Olle Route 6 & 7 We did not do the entire 6 & 7 trail but we visited Chilshimni Poetry Park, Hwangwooji coast, Oedolgae observatory and Oedolgae. This was a scenic trail and I highly recommend. We stayed at a hotel along Jungang-ro road, that was near the Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market. From our hotel, it was a 10 minutes walk to Geolmae Eco Park. The park led us along Seohong-ro road to Taepyeong-to road (where we passed by Hotel Yeon) where we were able to see the Saeyeong Bridge. After the bridge was in sight, we followed our instinct to the Bridge. There was an ice-cream stall that serve grape soft-serve that was delicious. We made our way onto the bridge to view the pristine bluish-green coastline and headed to Saeseom Island. Saeseom Island was a short 20 to 30 minutes trail that brought us to a rocky coastline where you can view two lighthouses (red and white). You could walk to the white lighthouse on the rocks but at your own risk. There were many locals fishing along the rocky areas too. In short, the trail along the Saeyeongyo Bridge was fairly easy yet scenic enough. We were there on the 22nd of April and the weather was about 15 degree Celsius in the day. A light jacket with windbreak will be sufficient. Afterwhich we headed to Chilshimni Poetry Park (which you can view Cheonjiyeon Falls for free) as there was a stairway along the left side of main exit road (where all the tour buses parked, pedestrian walkway path with brown wood). The stairway seemed to indicate going up a temple. However, we landed in Chilshimni Poetry Park. We took pictures of the waterfall and left Chilshimni Poetry Park to follow the orange/blue Jeju Olle ribbon to Hwangwooji coast and Oedolgae. The orange/blue Jeju Olle ribbon were along the park main road (Namseongjung-ro road where Park Sunshine hotel was). Then, You need to turn in to Namseong-ro road and you will see a brick wall painted dark blue with pinnochio seated on a bench (photo attached) you will passed by a ?hip?몃媛?? Hostel (the hostel name is in Korean as I cannot find the English name online - photo attached). u will then past by Poong Gyung Hotel in Jeju (not the one u can find online - photo attached) before arriving at Hwangwooji coast. I love Hwangwooji coast bcos it was like a private pool. There were only a few Korean that day, playing, swimming and hunting of sea creatures in the private pool. It also has a good view of the Saeyeongyo Bridge from a far.  After-which we head to Oedolgae and walked till Dombenang-gil Road. We decided to head back as I needed the toilet. At the entrance to Oedolgae, there was a public toilet acorss the road. The toilet were will keep with toilet paper provided. You can watch the sunset if you have time. However, we decided to walk back to our hotel as we were tire. Jeju Olle Route 14 ? 1If you love beaches, this is a must walk route (at least it was really breathe-taking for me). We stayed at Seowipo, we took bus 110 from Jungang Rotary bus stop to Jungmun Tourist Complex. The bus journey about 30 minutes and cost less than 2000won one way. The bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly (Although I did not see Jungmun Tourist Complex on the TV screen, therefore I used GPS to locate instead. You can press the bell to alight. For my other bus trip, the stops were announced correctly and was reliable). We actually stopped that Jungmun Tourist Complex to go the the Teddy bear museum and Cheonjeyeon Falls before proceeding to the beach. Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. We needed to change bus 702 (opposite the tourist infrmation counter) to Hyeojae beach. It cost 3300 won. The journey on the bus we great as you will pass by paddy field, wind mills and wild flower fields (photo attached). You will see a beautiful beach 1st (Geumneung Beach) but don?t get down, get down at Hyeopjae beach as the view is nicer (about 2 stops away). You can walk down to Geumneung Beach later as it was part of olle route 14-1 (There is a public toilet down the stretch if you need). The weather then (April 26) was 12 to 17 degree Celcius and remember to buy a jacket and windbreaker as it was very windy when we were there. We so blessed that the sky cleared up to reveal one of the most beautiful turquoise beaches I have been. The beach was wide and the colours of the water clear and blue. There are many caf챕 where you can buy a hot drink from. Noted that the caf챕 only allow you to use the toilet if you buy a drink (the receipt will print the password to get into the toilet). You can always use the public toilet. We decide to walk along the orange and blue ribbon trail (Jeju Olle Route 14) and it was one of the best trail for me. We complete only part of the the trail where we walk through the villages to the fishing port. The route will bring you to a serene path with light house and the wind mills. The the path became rocky nearing the windmills, and we decided to walk out through the rocky back alley of a shellfish place (away from the orange/blue ribbon) and landed at a bus stop. We took bus 702 back to seogwipo. It was a must go beach but only on a clear blue day where the magnificent of the beach will show up. In Summary, I always thought that you would need to rent a car around jeju. However, during my 4 days trip (even Hallasan was done using public transport ? can look at my post at tripadvisor), all our travelling was done throuh public transport. We were able to view those usual scenic places that ple usually go too! The good thing about walking was that we could stop at anytime we want to take picture or do something we did not plan for (Eg: watch how the local harvest shellfish). However, we were the kind that love to walk and could spend 7 hours walking. Therefore, we could travel in jeju with a budget using their public transport.

We decided to visit one of JeJu?s famous attractions Hallim park. We took bus 100 from the Jeju intercity bus station and had a relaxing journey to the west side of the island passing through countryside and the coast line. The bus stops at the Hallim park bus stop and you still have a little walk along the road and through the car park until you come to the entrance.(entrance fee 10,000 won) we were lucky because the weather was good for June , sunny but not too hot as you do spend alot of time walking around. On entering you will see a large map of the park with all its attractions numbered, there is also a very good gift shop which has a large range of items from T.shirts to natural products made into soaps and teas. Then you start the walk of around 10 different attractions including water garden, bird garden, subtropical garden and ofcourse the attraction most people come to see the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves.Jeju is famous for its volcanic larva tubes and caves and if you haven?t visited any then this is a good time as its alot more convenient than doing another trip to the other caves. The park is actually quite big and you do need to spend a good 2 hours to see it all, so if your going to visit the nearby beaches allow yourself enough time.There are also some restaurants and washroom facilities.

We decided to go up  the Eorimok Trail and then down the Yeongsil trail and then catch a taxi back to the Eorimok car park.    I had been told it was a gentle incline to the top (from where you can see the summit of Hallasan) but this is far from the truth unless you are super fit.    If you are like me and generally unfit, it is a steep climb (it's very well done with wooden steps but they are steep!) Towards the end of the trail as you near the cafe and rest area it does level out.   Fortunately there are lots of benches on the way up for frequent stops and it took us 3 hours to the top.  About 5km long?The Yeongsil trail is shorter - about 3.7km I believe - but quite tricky in some parts as the steps are a mixture of wood and rock and you have to watch your step going down.   The scenery is fantastic - especially on the Yeongsil trail - and if the azaleas had been out it would have been even more amazing.   The whole trip took us 5 hours and then the taxi ride took about 20 minutes and cost KRW 20,000.   At the time I said it was unlikely I would ever do this hike again but now I have recovered I think I would in the Autumn to see the colours and also maybe in May to see the azaleas.   Maybe next time we will try the other way round......  Tips - lots of water, snacks, walking poles might be useful. good walking boots and a coolish day.

We could not have gotten to so many attractions on our own in one day, so great time taking the bus tour from Yeha.  Wish we had booked more days in Jeju to explore other parts of the island such as Seowipo.  The cave is 1km long and a nice attraction to check out, especially for families.  Cold inside!  Bring an extra layer...

We climbed the Eorimok track on the way up and Yeongsik track on the way down. I must say Yeongsik is SUPER SCARY, because the snow is so deep the safety rails were buried under snow, so parts of the trail we had to walk on snow steps next to the cliff.... For totally unexperienced climber like me, it was quite intimidating. If you go in winter, and are not very confident in your skills (like me!) make sure you have crampons and hiking sticks. The convenient store at the entrance sells crampons (around 7USD). My friends were totally fine with those simpler crampons, but I prefer the wire-net style one (the one my friend lent me was from Columbia brand).Hiking sticks are helpful because where it's supposed to be stairs would turn into slides because of the snow -_-Good luck and enjoy!Amazing view. Must note the bus timetable, as we missed the last bus (around 5pm) and had to take taxi (at Yeongsik trail entrance there's an office which can help you find taxis. But it took >1 hour for ours to come...)

We climbed Halla via Yeongsil Trail on Christmas. Really worth the hiked, yet when we reached the view point on top it was covered by the clouds.Be sure you wear layers of clothes, sweater and jackets as it?s really cold up there with the wind gust blowing so hard in winter.Despite of the clouds on top, we can still take so many pictures on our way up.3.5 hours with many stops for photo session and 1.15 for went down.We travelled from Seogwipo - Vistacay world cup hotel, took the 282 blue bus around 9.30am in the bus stop across the eMart, and dropped at Jungmun Elementary School (We should?ve start earlier actually).From there we went to the other bus stop (it?s near the junction) and took bus 240 straight to Yeongsil Ticket Office and walked about 2 km to the Yeongsil Entrance. There?re small store where you can buy some food and hot drinks as well as hiking equipments like Crampons, Hike stick, gloves etc.Notice that i think in winter the crampons is a Mandatory (except you come with a full hiking equipments) as we?re not allowed to enter the trail only with our bare sneakers.So we bought two pairs of crampons cost 70.000 Won (pick your size carefully as it can squeezed hard your feet if it to small).

We chose the   short   hike up the mountain (volcano) and it was all up. We are Coloradoans and hike quite a bit and this one was a bit of a challenge. The first part was through an oak forest and it was hot and humid. We sweat like crazy and things got better once we got out of the oaks and into the pines. It took us 2+ hrs to get to the rest station and a bowl of noodles and a chocolate bar. The hike was amazing, though with strange vegetation and a miniature deer, the only wildlife we saw along with many butterflies. We did not go to the top since it was in the clouds and starting to rain, but the views of the ocean and Jeju-si were as advertised. This is a must see place and there is an easier hike than ours, but takes much longer we were told.

We chance upon this on our drive from Seogwipo to Hyeopjae.  The pink building is big and visible from the highway. They should have repainted it as it looks washout and faded pink. But once I step in, it?s totally new! Infact it is even newer than Sanrio Puroland which I visited in Tokyo and bigger than there! I am a true blue HK fan since 40 years ago. Once HK fan steps in, I am sure you will be transformed to a little princess at heart and you?ll be so excited again! There are a lot of Instagram worthy area to take photos. As others pointed out, it has a section that talks about the evolution of HK from 1970s till now.  There are HK rooms, dining room, bus, living room, wardrobe, dressing room etc. Even the toilets are so pretty! Level 2 offers some purikura area, a restaurant and some other HK displays.  There is a 3D dancing room too. On the 3rd floor, there is a open air rooftop HK small maze. On level 1, you go through the souvenirs shop to exit and a notice states that once u exit, u can?t go in again. So it?s best that u buy yr souvenirs when u are ready to leave. I swear I could stay there for 3 hours but as my husband is with me, it only took us about 1.5 hrs to complete our visit. Overall this place is small and not much for non Kitty fans. For us Kitty fans, it is definitely a must visit.

We caught the Nanta show in Jeju and it was such a fun night for the family. It is a combination of comedy, musical, martial art and drums. Though a Korean production with a Korean context but the storyline was kept simple and easy to understand. For a show that ran an hour and a half long, the performers were really awesome with great stamina! They kept their energy high up until the end, without missing a beat. Nanta is also known for its audience participation and without giving the plot away, this was done with a delightful, surprising twist. One that you should experience yourself if you ever get the chance to catch the show.

we can enjoy this place with family and toddler or young kids,  not recommend for gentlemen. but very educative for children. located inside the Jungmun Tourist Complex, you can get anythink you need in this tourist complex like various restaurant, hotels , 3D art museum, Belive it or not. Kpop Museum , Conventionl Centre , Waterfall Etc

We came here as part of a tour from Hong Kong and no one else went to climb up to the top, but me and my boyfriend did. It's about a 30 minute walk - you can take it slowly and take photos along the way, but it can be a bit steep. However, the views are great (on a clear day) and you get a good workout (after sitting on a bus for so long). The ascent/descent paths are clearly marked and separated, so it's quite well organised and the path/fence is very well maintained. At the top, you can overlook the big crater, which is now overgrown with lots of lush grass and trees - quite beautiful. You can also overlook the water and the town below etc. The way down has lots of stairs, so watch out if you have bad knees.

We came down here because like anyone and everyone who visits Jeju, they're told to go try black pork at one of the restaurants at Black Pork street in Jeju City. So we were in town (stayed in Seogwipo) and decided to go.However me and my partner both thought that the food is over hyped and isn't as great as it's made out to be. I even go on to think that majority of the pork they serve is from regular pork... for anyone that thinks they'll be able to tell the difference is lying. Much prefer traditional Korean BBQ with beef cuts as I much prefer beef as the pork is quite fatty.Still visit for the experience but wouldn't go again if I was to go back to Jeju.

We booked a tour with Mr Jang for two days, exploring the east and southern parts of Jeju island. He was extremely kind and went the extra mile to make our visit to Jeju enjoyable. 10/10 would recommend!

We agreed that visiting the Jeju Stone Park in the snow was one of the most enjoyable experiences we have had in Korea. The stones, sculptures, houses and other artefacts, as well as the lovely walks are beautiful in the snow. It also meant only a few people were visiting, so it was very peaceful and serene. The museum was excellent, very educational, and we really appreciated how the different lava types were displayed as sculptures. They are beautiful, nature?s art!

We ( mostly) enjoyed our hike up Hallasan. It is a moderate climb despite being the highest peak in S. Korea. Important to note that you still need crampons to climb right now. Our hotel went and told us we didn?t need them as there was no snow left...well they were wrong! The steepest slopes on the trail are still sheer ice and it is quite treacherous without the crampons to help you grip! Other than that it was a good hike. Crater at the top is pretty cool. Also note that even on a clear day it was really hazy in the distance so the view from the top wasn?t as expected. Still worth it though. I recommend starting very early, get the first bus in the morning. The trail becomes quite crowded later on.

Waterfalls are very accessible in Jeju. Jeongbang is the most unique as we seldom see a waterfall that goes straight to the sea. Going by public bus is easy and the path towards the falls are already paved except for the rocky part near the falls itself. I suggest you take your time in sitting on one of the rocks and just enjoy the relaxing view. If you're patient, you can wait for 10-20 mins for tourists to leave and you can have the view all by yourself.  For photography enthusiasts, have a wide angle lens ready =D

Watching the sunrise at Seongsan Ilchulbong was definitely the highlight of my stay at Jeju. We had reserved a hotel right next to the attraction (Hotel Aroha), which was a very wise decision as all we had to do at 5 am in the morning was to get up, get ready and get going. There were hardly any people when we had started our ascent roughly 45 mins to an hour before sunrise. The hike itself is ~30 mins or less, but it can be a bit tiring because of the steep steps. We stopped a few times to catch our breaths and also interact with the locals. We had close to 10 mins before the sunrise by the time we were at the peak. The view from the sunrise is gorgeous, and even amidst so many people around you, it is still not chaotic but calm and serene. We stayed at the top for over 2 hours, taking pictures, resting, and even listening to some folk music being played by local artists. Great experience overall!The descent isn't tiring, so we took our time taking pictures and taking in the gorgeous views. At the base, we had freshly squeezed orange juice from Jeju oranges, which are again a must try!

Was on YEHA bus tour (which is really great), but this particular place is not that special. Do not spend any time going here unless it is included in some tour package. Basically a road where stuff kind-a sort-a roll upwards but not really.I was more interested of the over-priced street food and the pig statues down the road.

Was here for dinner across two nights.  Managed to compare Dombedon (without knowing it's Michelin rated) and Hwaro Hyang (on our 1st night). Comparing the two restaurants, I'm wondering what's the big deal about Dombedon. For a start Dombedon seemed to be mass producing with the intent to get us through our meals asap while those at HH treated their meats with respect.  E.g. HH doesn't cook all their meats at one time while Dombedon just dumped all the meats at one time, resulting in charred meat, spoiling the experience.  I am not even sure if I was eating black pork, insignificant as it may be.  At HH, it was odd at first to see abalone being baked along with black pork, but it was a pleasure to see the shellfish curled up as it cooked.  In HH, they bothered to sprinkle salt on their pork to bring out the flavour, but Dombedon disappointedly didn't. Prices are really almost the  same anyway.  My recommendation would have been HH, though we haven't really tried the rest.(The 2nd pic is from HH and the 1st pic is from Dombedon.)

Want to do a bush walk with nice scenery ?  Eorimok Trail & Yeongsil Trail in Hallasan National Park in Mt Halla will be a good choice when you visit Jeju Island in South Korea. Be sure to take a bush hat, sun screen lotion and bottles of water. Along the trails, there are a couple of water refill spots for refilling water from the mountain. The cheapest way is to take a bus No. 740 from the Jeju City Outer Bus Terminal if you stay at Jeju city.  Get off at the stop for the entrance to Eorimok Trail. From there, it will be uphill passing nice vegetation & trees until you reach Yeongsil Trail. Follow this Yeongsil Trail, you may be lucky to see Mt Halla deer. Once you start walking downhill on the Yeongsil Trail, you will see beautiful mountain scene. At the exit of Yeongsil Trail, you will need to walk a couple of Km downhill along the road to reach the Yeongsil Entrance to get the bus 740 back to Jeju City Outer Bus Terminal. Bus 740 travels between Jeju City and Seogwipo-si and uses the same bus stop at Yeongsil Entrance. When you get onto the bus, be sure it is going back to Jeju City Outer Bus, not the bus going to Seogwipo-si.[ The walk on Eorimok Trail & Yeongsil Trail will easily takes 5 hours plus.   Air brushes are available at the entrance / exit of the trails ]

Walk down to the falls is quiet and serene. A couple of local women were offering the fresh seafood they have just caught for sale. One just need to pay small amount and the woman will cut up the seafood and serve it with some sauce. People will just eat it fresh like sashimi.To get bearer to the fall, one need to navigate through rocks. Care should be taken else one may fall or drop your camera of smartphone. We were lucky to spot a rainbow at the place where the water splashed on the rocks! This is real rare and definitely made our day.

Visually, the road is seen to be an uphill road. But when the bus driver turned off the engine and release the brakes, it starts to move forward. Quite interesting. But don't purposely go there unless it's part of the journey. Not worth.

Visiting Jeju ? Do it if you have at least4 days or more ! All the tourist attractions are in different corners of the island and they are far from each other .There are daily bus tours , running in one direction , starting at 9am coming back at 6 pm . Not every spot is so interesting , probably many of travellers have seen some similar somewhere else . The same is reg. this small beach . There are plenty of such beaches or even nicer around the world

Visited Yongduam Rock as a part of my Olle walk. Pretty views, peacefull sea, a place to sit and contemplate, but be wary of mass tourism as busses pull in all day long bringing hords of people. Follow the Olle Trail to see more scenic views around.

Visited this place as part of a tour package. Its horrible. Phototaking opportunities are limited. The guide there spent 10mins running through various aspects of the village and the other 30mins hard-selling their honey, horse oil and supplements. Horrible experience and an utter waste of time.

Visited this place as part of a tour group, and spent slightly under an hour at this place There are a total of 3floors to explore, starting with a history tour to the current entertainment scene today. Several interactive booths and kiosks allow you to experience things such as singing, makeups and dancingAnd of course you can take photos of all these experiences

Visited the Glass Museum and I enjoyed every minute of it! It was fascinating to see how different coloured glass of different shapes and sizes were used to form different pieces of art. They ranged from different type of flowers  to a maze  to a   tunnel   and many other forms of objects!This is certainly a place for the family as well if you're visiting and I'm sure everyone will have loads of fun!

Visited the cave as a part of a bus tour. We entered through the 2nd section and were given 40 mins to walk to end of the cave and back.
