When we were there, the weather was cool and nice and we really had a good time walking around admiring the stones. It is a park that combines nature and art.  We like it a lot.

This place is great, fresh seafood sold at the coast, seeing the sea ladies in action (we were lucky and saw her catching an octopus with a fork like stick) and beautiful scenery of the coast, sea and land. It's a short boat ride over from the main island, then one could choose to take their bus at a fee, which will stop by 4 or 5 stops near the beach, cliff, etc  then bring u back to the starting point. Alternatively, you could rent a motorbike or four wheel drive. For the latter, one needs an international driving licence. One thing that's everywhere is their peanut ice cream, basically soft serve with peanut powder. Also, there's grilled cuttlefish everywhere.

This place is essentially a tourist trap to sell you exotic sounding herbs and products at ridiculously expensive prices. When we arrive, we were given a short tour of the village by a guide. After about 10 mins, we were ushered into a room and that's when the product pushing started. In short, the products were pitched as having miracle medicinal qualities, and as such, the prices were exorbitant to match. According to the guide, those products were only available from the village. Hmm, if the products were so good, why limit the distribution to only the village? Politely declined and made a beeline out of there.

This place is a must-see if you're a fan of teddy bears, but it's not just for the rabid fans.  I don't count myself as a particular fan one way or another, but I don't dislike them.  The bears here are displayed as various characters and in a variety of situations.  They're cute and can be interesting, but if you're not really into this kind of thing then you'd be bored.  I'm sure children would enjoy it.  For myself, I enjoyed it but I've seen it once and wouldn't go back.

This mystery road is just a small portion of a long road with many undulating slopes. There is sign broad showing the start of the mystery. Both sides of the road has plantation indicating the road is up slope.  Vehicles with engine killed will moves slowly from the start point with the plantation effect. At the ending point when out from the vehicle, looking at the road as if you are on the top of the small gradient.According to academic research, it is actually down slope but due to side plantation causing people to view wrongly.

This museum is one of the attraction at Jungmun Resort. It consists of teddy bear exhibition from several country, the history, the art, life size teddy bear & of course souvenir store. If you're Princess Hours lovers (Kdrama) this place is perfect for you. You can't bring you belonging inside, so placed you belonging into a free locker on the entrance of the museum.

This museum is intended for tourists who love to take photos. Most of the artworks housed in the museum are modified versions of original paintings so that you can integrate with the painting. Hence bringing a camera or a smartphone is a must! A companion is also a must since taking a   selfie   to achieve the desired effect might prove to be impossible.This is one of the two 3D interactive museums in Jeju Island. The other one Trick Art Museum is located farther in the eastern part of the island. We went to this place as it is nearer to the Jungmun Area where most hotels (Hyatt Regency Shilla Hotel Lotte Hotel etc.) are located.Aside from the in-house artworks there is also a park with sculptures and play sets that will be appreciated by kids. Tips: avoid flash photography to get the desired effect; bring a jacket w/ hoodie (can be used in some of the artworks); and black pants make people blend better with the background.Admission costs KRW 8000 per person. The entire area is air-conditioned and wifi access is offered for free. Other extras include lockers to deposit your bags as this may hamper your experience.This is a fun destination for couples families or small groups.

This museum is 90% in Korean but as they say some things are easier to understand. In the beginning the museum starts out with some interesting if broad sex-positive history. It's sex and HEALTH however so there's info about AIDS as well as misconceptions about sex and sexual health. Towards the middle of the museum it starts to go off the rails a little bit. The   Fantasy   section is a lot of chintzy garbage and mannequins in lewd/bizarre positions and tableaus. It doesn't add anything it moreso detracts from the legitimacy established in the first half. Only go if you're stuck with a rainy day. Otherwise you'd be better off enjoying Jeju's natural wonders.

This mountain (aka Sunrise Peak) is located to the eastern seaboard of the island and is not accessible easily if you are staying in one of the hotels in Jeju-ri (city area) in the north. You need to take public transport which can take you more than 1 hr (Blue intercity bus, flat rate 1200 W) or 50+ min by express bus (Red, flat rate 2000 W). It is advisable to put up overnight in one of the many hotels or guest houses in Seongsan itself so that you can wake up early and start your ascend to watch the sunrise.This will take about 25-40 min to climb up the well laid out steps if you do not stop along the way to take pictures. However it is advisable to stop along the numerous rest areas and take your own time to ascend. Certain parts can be quite steep so come with a good pair of canvas sneakers or hiking shoes, sunglasses, sun screen, bottles of water. The climb up is worth the effort as you will be rewarded with the fantastic views from the peak. Going down is much easier and you can stop at the foothill to watch the women divers putting up a demo at 1.30 pm and 3 pm. At the foothill is a public toilet and a McDonald and cafe apart from stalls selling souvenirs and cold drinks.

This mistery road is about half kilometer long. Stop you?re vehicle at the start of this road, put the gear in neutral, and turn off the engine. Your car slowly climbs up a pretty steep slope. At least what it looks like upward slope. It is really hard to believe that the upward slope is an optical illusion and it in reality slopes down. I have seen magnetic hill in Moncton, Canada and they have a road like this. But there is just below a mountain slope and the optical illusion is very understandable there but here there is no such thing, just a plain stretch of road. I really could not figure out how your eyes are deceiving your brain. Not a big deal,but worth experiencing it if you are in Jeju.
This might not be for everyone, though if you like stained glass you'll love this place! Lots of stained glass and other glass art. Very pretty and playful.

This market was near our hotel so we came by here a few times in the evenings (and a couple times in the day time). Mostly because we were trying to find this fried chicken restaurant that never seemed to be open and we kept going back to try to find it. Don't come here expecting a night market extravaganza like other parts of Asia. This is more strictly a   market   market, though there are lots of restaurants that have take-out. There are a few street food stalls, so you can get your fix in a couple spots. Definitely make sure you try the orange juice from one of the sellers here, Jeju has amazing oranges (and tangerines). There are some souvenir type places here, but nothing special. We bought some of the chocolates because they were dirt cheap and wanted to try them, but when we got home and ate them they were just waxy and artificial tatsing (you'll see which chocolates I mean when you get there. EVERY souvenir seller has them. Even in the airport). We bought some dried mandarins from the same vendor, and they were pretty good. We also bought a bunch of oranges to bring around with us as snacks while we were driving. If you've been to markets in Asia before, this will be nothing special. But if you're looking for something to do, it's probably worth visit - wouldn't go out of my way for it though.

This Lave cave is long, dark, cold and wet and the ground uneven due to the Lava deposits.  My partner did it as he is physically fit.  I needed help because of the uneven ground and the dark and wet ground.  If you are fit then it is a good experience.

This lava tube is huge.  The part open to the public is a bit over half a mile in although the entire system is much larger.  The natural formations are fascinating and beautiful in their own way.  The place is   other worldly   and so different from life on the surface. Be aware that there are many steps (some steep) down and up.

This island is 15min away from seongsan ferry terminal. You just have to fill in the passenger particular and show yourpassport. The island is full of atv for rent, do look out for the bus as the road are quite tight.  I shipped my car over at the price of 21000wonDo try their seafood ramen and peanut ice cream!

This is your typically local market where you can get fresh product here.  I will NOT say this place offers the cheapest price but rather there are varieties for you to choose from.  The market has many entrance and each entrance leads to you to a particular section where they sell the same stuff ranging from clothes, fruits and to live seafood.  We picked up some Jeju tangerines and sweets here which were pretty good.  Discount?  Most shops are priced the same so its hard to get discount. Best time to come is about 2pm where there are lesser crowd.  Its also a short walk to the underground shopping mall so if you are here, do take the chance to visit the underground mall altogether.

This is your typical open air market. In the west we call it a Farmers Market. It has just about everything you might need. You will be exposed to the Korean Culture there.  The shop keepers are usually older so there isn't a lot of English spoken but, if you  want to buy something they will understand and act accordantly. Don't be afraid to barter a little.It is crowed  most the time so I shy away from going there but, if you like to rub butts with the general public and need to pick up something for the home, garden, something new to wear or something special for dinner this is the place for you.

This is the sort of cave one would visit on a tour , decend down into the bowls of the earth , in fact it's not too far down , but be prepared to walk for some 2 km there and back , this is in fact a Lave Tube run then an underground river , all along one can see the water line marks that have cut into the lava ;The floor is VERY uneven , bit slippery if not careful , you are in effect in a huge underground tunnel , rather dark , somewhat damp and water is dripping from the roof all of the time , not sure how wide or tall it was but, shall we say huge . At the end of the tunnel there is a spiral of volcanic rock that has shot through the earth and been frozen by water ( I suppose ) One of UNESCO World heritage attractions in Korea , To be honest I think one has to like this sort of visit to enjoy it , whilst I somewhat enjoyed the visit , I have seen better in France ; however if you have travelled this far around the world and find yourself in Jeju Island then make the effort to visit , entrance fee is 2000 won

This is the second time my family and I have visited Gapado Island since we had a good experience during our first visit back in November of last year. Unfortunately, our image of Gapado overall is now completely ruined due to an extremely unpleasant experience at the restaurant named “Gapado Yonggung House” (가파도 용궁정식&민박)?Upon arriving at the port at Gapado, we saw many restaurant advertisement posters. We found one restaurant poster with nice food images, so I called the restaurant to get directions. The owner (male) who answered the phone was quite unfriendly and told me bluntly to just look them up on naver map and find our way. He said that even if they give me directions, I wouldn’t know they are located. So my family and I found our own way to the restaurant after a 20 minute walk. It turned out that this restaurant was located furthest away in Gapado Island.?We ordered our meal and started to set our own plastic ware. Due to Covid-19 sensitive period, we always bring our own disposable chopsticks, spoon and paper cups to restaurants. The owner (lady) out of the blue bluntly asked us if we bought our own cups in a rather accusing manner. We said yes we brought these cups and asked “why do you ask?”, to which she said “Oh, we have some cups in our kitchen and wondered if you took them” I found this question to be rather offensive as I feel she was insinuating or implying that we just took (or stole) them from their kitchen without their knowledge. However, we overlooked her strange question and went about eating our meal.?We then wanted to order soft drinks. However, I could see that all staffs, owners included looked quite busy. Therefore, in my attempt to be helpful, I went to the fridge and removed two soft drinks from the fridge while at the same time informing the owners of my action of taking the 2 drinks, to which they acknowledged. To be perfectly clear, I was telling them to charge me for the 2 soft drinks I was taking.?However, only a few minutes after this action, I overhear the lady owner speak to her employee in a very loud voice to not stock up the fridge with so many soft drinks because people keep taking them from the fridge, while she herself was removing half the stock from the fridge and putting them away in the back storage. At that moment, I felt she was saying this intentionally to let me hear her, as her way of telling me that she was not pleased with the fact that I have removed the 2 soft drinks directly from the fridge. So at that point, I told the lady owner that I wanted to clarify that when I took the drinks from the fridge, I was telling her to charge me for it and that it didn’t feel nice to hear her make that comment so intentionally.?This is when we have experienced the most horrifying and unnatural turn of events. The lady owner got extremely angry at me and started yelling and shouting at me saying that she wasn’t talking about me, that she was talking about her other guests, etc. She could have very easily cleared up my mis-understanding in one nice sentence. Rather, she was ready to bite my head off and was talking (more like yelling, shouting) at me ten times louder than my voice.?I was so shocked by her behavior that I said I just wanted to clarify any potential mis-understanding about my taking the soft drinks, which I was telling them to charge me for, and that I actually did that as a gesture to be helpful since they looked so busy (obviously a huge mis-judgement on my part). ?The lady owner would not let this go and kept on yelling and arguing with me, her voice escalating louder and louder every second. I told the owner that we took the time to visit their restaurant and did not appreciate being treated like this. To this comment, the male owner jumped in and said that fact has nothing to do with this matter. Neither the lady nor the male owner offered one single word of apology nor made any attempts to provide explanation for their rude behavior, nor try to rectify this intense situation. The lady owner having her say just ran off and hid in her room after having her furious tantrum with us.?Although extremely disturbed by what just happened, as we have never experienced such rudeness ever in our entire lives, we still managed to complete the remainder of the meal in silence, all the while feeling ill at ease and uncomfortable. (FYI, my entire family and I suffered from indigestion later this same day due to this incident). After the meal, I paid for it at the counter and left the restaurant with my family, and not one single person at the restaurant acknowledged that we were leaving their restaurant, and no one (owners, staffs) even bothered to say a simple “thank you or goodbye”.?I am a firm believer that the most important part of any meal at any restaurant is quality of service. However, the level of horrible service we have experienced from this restaurant is completely unacceptable. From the many restaurants we could have chosen from at Gapado Island, I certainly feel choosing this restaurant is the one mistake I will live to regret. This unpleasant and rude encounter was bad enough to leave a bad image of the entire Gapado Island for us, while at the same time ruined a perfectly peaceful and happy family trip. All in all, it was a very unpleasant experience from beginning till the end at this restaurant, and I strongly do not recommend this restaurant to anyone visiting Gapado Island.

This is the longest lava tube in the world.  It's 7kms long and only 1km is open to the public.  It's rather spectacular to be in it, to appreciate the wonders of Nature.  For the cynics, you would probably ask yourself why you want to part with money to walk in almost darkness, through a wet and uneven surface, just to affirm yourself that you are visiting one of the UNESCO's accredited natural wonders of the world.  For me, it's a been there, done that experience.  Enough said!

This is the local traditional market. You can buy the local products here as souvenir such as keychain (Many designs of Dol hareubang),chocolates products, tangerines chocolates, tangerines tart and etc. Most of the stall owner didn't speak English but some can speak in Chinese (Full of people). Multi level car park available here.

This is the kind of park where family with young children will enjoy at least half a day here. The maze is not that simple to fulfill from start to finish, but its a good practice of what a tram work means to the kids and how they should appreciate good team performance. Before and after the entrance of the park, there are scenic attractions where phototaking venues and selfie booth are made available. With kuds runnung around and getting more attracted to the children's playground which I think is a very well thought strategy and well kept, it is hard for parents to concentrate and take a decent picture although the scenery and amenities are so tempting to be utilised.

this is the easiest waterfall among all in jeju in terms of access.we walked for about 15 minutes before reaching the waterfall.however,to reach the waters,u have to go through slippery rocks-definitely not for kids or elderly.wear comfortable walking shoes.however,the view from the upper part of the waterfall(before descending down the many stairs) was already breathtaking.there were also foodstalls selling snacks-we had the ice cream and the grilled squid.super delicious.do try it.oh and don't forget the orange juice (hallabong).the freshest i have ever tasted.good snack,superb juice to wash it down,beautiful scenery-i could not ask for more.do visit if you are in jeju.preferably early morning before the crowd.

This is the best stone exhibit on Jeju island.  And the best part of that is the museum itself.  There are many, many very interesting stones shapes, all collected from Jeju (I think).  If you like geology, there's a great explanation of lava types, stone formations, lava tubes, etc.  Also there is a nice drift-wood display with very unusual, artistic shapes.  Outside, there are many carved stone artifacts used by Jeju islanders from ages past.  The Obaek Jang-Goon Gallery has a nice drift-wood display in the basement.  Park is big, but except for the museums, just a walk-through is enough.  I spent 2 hours in the museums -- the best part!

This is super easy to do... From Jeju city go to Jeju Bus Terminal and the lady at the desk will tell you which bus to get. In this case, 740. This takes you to a ticket office and car park. From there you can get a taxi or walk 2.5km to the start of the trail. We walked and it took about half an hour (but it is all uphill). I would say there are about 3 sections to this walk:1. Through the forest - stream nearby and wildlife (I saw a deer). This is relatively flat until the end when you have to climb some stairs. 2. The hard part- walking along the ridge of the mountain going up the stairs. This is tough on the knees but there are loads of places to stop and absorb the view. 3. Along the top- relatively flat through a forest part and then open until you get to the rest stop. It is the easiest hike and does not go to the top of Hallasan, but it is beautiful and gave you stunning views of the top of Hallasan (which you would not get if you were actually on it). Make sure you bring water, snacks and hand wipes. The rest stop at the top sells only instant noodles and has no running water.
This is really the heaven for antique car fans like us. Grandpa was enjoying the old days by seeing these old pals, and kids enjoyed the fun ride of kiddy kart surrounding the museum.
address: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관

review: This is quite a climb in places and in winter time will need crampons, but it will reward you with amazing views on a clear day and even in cloudy weather is really worth the trek. Choose your route by the least fit member of your group and remember to take food and especially water with you.There is a cut off point which you need to reach by 13:00 if you are going right to the top, so that means an early start.

This is purely an activity you should do if you actually enjoy adventures! The guides say to get to the peak it will take 4.5 hours, 8-9.5km depending on which trail you take. We took the popular one, seongpanak because there is a direct bus route from the Jeju intercity terminal (number 781). Here's my itinerary for the day:08.45: arrived at seongpanak trail start09.45: arrived at Sokbat shelter11.10: arrived at Jindallaebat shelter12.30: arrived at peakSo in total 3.45 hours including breaks. I had around 1 hour at the top to sit, eat, take photos, luckily we chose such a clear day so everything was so visible!At 13.30, you have to head down, staff will tell you to move. We decided to take the Eorimok route (8.7km) down and made it to the bottom at 18.00. Things to note:- you have to reach Jindallaebat by 12pm or you are not allowed to the peak. - there are no trash cans, so you have to carry all rubbish. - on the seongpanak route, there is also the Saraoreum Observatory (extra 40 minute walk) which is supposed to have great views!- hiking boots or sturdy shoes are needed!I exercise everyday and managed it fine. My friend who does no exercise made it eventually and was super proud of herself!

This is our last stop of our 2nd day in Jeju Island and was worthy for the line Save the Best for last. If you are into caves and lavas then this is the right place for you. Since this is our last stop, we went there around 5PM, we were in a hurry to reach the entrance of the site. Get ready to walk on dark and cold pavements. Although it was cold we manage to take photos inside the cave (which needed editing) and was mesmerized with the unique beauty the cave has to offer. It entails walking so get ready to walk and prepare the right shoes. Plus, inside the cave is really cold, colder than the other sites so be ready with your jackets. You may also explore the park and the cafe located outside the cave. The entire place is relaxing and worth the visit. This must be part of your itinerary once you happen to visit Jeju Island.

This is one of the most remarkable scenic attractions of Jeju. Our Korean driver brought us here. We told him we are not interested in arts museums or teddy bear or maze park. We only wanted to see the natural sites and wonders in Jeju and he brought us here and we thanked him for that. There was a Buddha Park directly at the car park where we alighted. I could see the golden face of the Buddha from the highland opposite the park. From the car park,  the panoramic view of the beach was amazing; the lush green vegetation studded with autumn foliage with long stretch of gorgeous coastline and natural cliff view and the azure sea horizon. It was nature's master-piece presented in so marvelous and harmonious form that I could not find better words to describe this stunning, breathtaking and jaw dropping scenery. For a moment, a sensation of joy and happiness flooded and filled my heart. As the gentle sea breeze blew on my face, I found tranquility, calmness and serenity in this beautiful land. I immediately dashed down the flight of stairs to embrace this beautiful and spectacular piece of natural wonder. I roamed and wandered around the scenic landscape and found myself singing the Happy Wanderer lyrics: `I like to go a wandering up the mountain track  And as I go, I love to sing, My knapsack on my back. Val-deri,Val-dera, Val-deri,..'  There was the Hamel Castaway Memorial and the vessel Hamel that drifted to this place in 1653. I stood near the replicated Hamel vessel to admire the European naval architectural of that time and I saw the rangers tendered to the horses in the range. From the coast, I could see the majestic Mt Sanbangsan loomed at the site of the Buddha Park and I could vividly see some of my group members were resting and relaxing at a pavilion below the car park enjoying the gentle sea breeze.You must pardon me for my excitement and exhilaration as I came from a city with urbanized concrete jungle with little natural scenery. Jeju is full of natural wonders and Mt Sanbangsan and Yongmeori beach are exceptionally gorgeous gems that deserved a good lengthy exploration.

This is one of the highlights of Jeju Island. If you're ever there, you MUST go on this trail, unless outdoor activities aren't your type of activity. We took the Seongpanak trail up and down via Gwaneumsa. The pathway up was well constructed with wooden planks and shades for about 3 quarters of the journey. The rest of the path was quite stony. As the Gwaneumsa trail is relatively newer, it is not as well covered with wooden planks and a bit more slippery when you hike on the rocky trails. Both trails are as spectacular and offer different sceneries. On the way down, I encountered a deer sighting!Do bring along a wind wall as the winds can get very strong as you progress towards the peak. Also, it's best to start off as early as possible (we started at 6am) to enjoy the nature scenery as much as possible.

This is NOT something to do on your own. Going with a small group is best because you will need someone to take photos of you/your friends interacting with all of the   art  . It's a silly good time with lots of themed rooms each one with loads of photos or interactive displays. Watch the floor for markers of where to stand to get the best angle for the optical illusions!

This is not really part of our tour in Jeju but since I researched on how to enjoy the tour with 30+ friends, I chanced upon this garden maze near Manjanggul lava tubes site (as in 500m away only).I really recommend this to friends and families who'd like to solve a mystery together and have fun doing it. The price in finishing the maze is a banner and the right to be the first to ring the bell.Please try the ice cream at the exit. You'll enjoy it after an exhilirating yet fun game (30 minutes estimated)

This is not a common attraction but it's a place where we can follow the path and walk around the crater. Though pitifully there is no more water in the crater, it's still an interesting place to visit. The walk just take around 30 minutes. Apart from the crater, it's also a good place to overlook the plains and farmlands.The only offset of this site is its accessibility and limited car park. There is no public transport to go to this place. We drove by ourselves. After we drove off the main road, we entered a small road to the peak. The path is so narrow that only one car can go through, but it is for two-way traffic.

This is my first time visiting a cave and this is an extraordinary cave where this is actually a LAVE Tube which was formed 1million years ago. The open to public is only a section of its 5km length as a protection to its other natural environment and that is why it is labelled as the UNESCO Natural Heritage. The entrance to the 1km tube is a 100m long flight of stairs. Upon entering, the internal is wet and cold when visiting at this season (starting of spring). Other days would be still wet but temperature would be around 10-20degree C. The length of the tube excursion is just nice for family of elderly and young. My family (Mum, brother, wife and me) had a nice time inside the tube and although it is quite hard to take beautiful pictures, the experience is definitely immense.However, most of the time my mum is trying to avoid the water on the floor (do not worry it is not as slippery but it is on some areas), she did not notice much of the natural formation of the lava flow and lava stalagmites. The tube is well lit but it is recommend to bring torchlight to shone on areas above to see properly. Beware of the top water flowing down, that is why there is water on the floor. Overall, i feel that it is educational for the young and good walk for the elderly. To tour the place, i recommend to wear tracking shoe or covered shoe to prevent water or slipping. Else you will not enjoy the beauty of the tube. We had lunch at the nearby restaurant and it is a hearty meal. Lastly, i really enjoy the visit and definitely visit again in future, i hope you too!

This is it, even though its FULL of stairs and exhausting to climb up (with lots of   take 5   in between the climb. The view is magnificent and too beautiful to behold.Consider this the best part of JEJU.

This is interesting place located in Joongmun tourist complex and definitely worth visiting.You can take tones of interesting photos and illusion is   wow  I probably took more than 100 photos.Also they sell Egg Tart(??) in the cafeteria and was very tasty.

This is an underground shopping center which is just around the corner of Orange Tree  Cafe & Hotel. This is just the normal shopping center which you would see in most of the subways thru out Seoul, however, the good thing about this underground shopping mall is that each of the exits leads to different streets which has more shops....eg. Uniqlo, ABC Mart, Daiso, and also various cafes.....and also to the Dongmun Market and also to the Black Pork Street.

This is an icon of Jeju, so it is hard to imagine coming to the island without seeing it, and see it you should! But try to go in the early morning or late evening, if you want to avoid the tourist crowds. We went after lunch at about 1pm on an overcast day with showers and it was still pretty crowded..it does take something away from the beauty of the place. Tickets are sold, 2000 won per person, at the base of the crater. It is mainly stairs all the way up and takes 50 minutes return trip according to the sign at the ticket counter. We found this to be accurate. There are beautiful views down to the town and coast from the top. The crater itself, my partner and I, actually found more interesting from the bottom. There are many vendors and eateries around the base for snacking/meals before or after your climb. There are also restrooms at the base and 2 others we saw on the trail.

This is an excellent museum featuring contemporary art as well as traditional art. The buildings themselves, which were designed by Tadao Ando, were amazing. It was great just walking around inside while perusing the exhibits & or going for a stroll outside. My favorite part was the sculpture garden, which featured 3 pieces. You can go on the rooftop as well to see another sculpture as well as a great view of Jeju. I was also fortunate to have an opportunity to see Yayoi Kusama's Pumpkin & Infinity Mirrored Room. I don't know if it was because I went during off-season, but the museum wasn't crowded at all, so I was able to take my time. I would definitely come back here again if I had a chance

This is an awesome place to go with street sights and photography in mind, with all the locals and tourist here collectively, lots of items to see, and nearby jungang underground market. Visiting both, seems to be the smart thing to do. Interesting place but of course it is still a market.

This is an authentic market which embodies local life on the island. It has so much to offer... There is an entire section devoted to the economy of the elderly, selling their goods and calling sweet encouragements to passerbys. There are regional fruits and veggies, artisan crafters, cloth and clothing sellers, seafood and fresh meats, animals, and a multitude of food trucks/stalls.This is the ideal market for immersing yourself in Jeju and Korean culture. It's open every day ending in 2 or 7: 2, 7, 12, 17, 22, 27thPictured: a pressure cooker used for puffing rice and corn, cooking beans, etc...

This is all about geology.... How lava tubes are formed during volcanic eruptions and the rock formations produced. It's something different from what most resort islands offer. A journey to the center of the earth.... cut short to about 1 km. Yes 1 km. So, if you aren't into walking for 1 km in and 1 km out, this is not the place for you. Especially so since the temperature drops significantly as you descend down the steps. It was the month of May, with outside temperatures ranging from 25-28 degrees Celsius, but as you walk into the cave, the chill can get to you. The ground is uneven and wet, with water dripping from the cave ceiling. Be prepared for all this.

This is a weak but personal reason to visit this bridge, that is to say, it featured in the first Korean Drama series I ever watched. To put it in a nutshell, the guy followed the girl all the way to Jeju-do in order to convince her he was the one for her. The bridge scene featured just after they landed on the island, so it was just nice to see it in person as part of our stay here. There's not much more to say - I guess other people would have other reasons to visit. As a bonus we spotted women divers going out in their gear so that was some cultural aspect to the visit.

This is a UNESCO World Heritage listed site. It is indeed one of the largest lava cave/tube I have ever seen. It is awesome, dark, wet and huge. Its floor uneven, wet and slippery. Artificial lighting is minimal and don't attempt to take photos as it is too high to be lit by ordinary flash lights. You need to watch where you are going. The result of a fall can be serious. Minor twist ankle is common. The experience is well worth the trip. Do not forget to take extra clothes and be prepared to have a thorough shampoo and shower that night as it drips everywhere.
This is a strange wonderful mystical place. A work of art on a grand scale, a hommage to the volcanic, mineral nature of this island, and also to its ancient gods.

This is a small stretch of road. The GPS setting is 7126988 ( which is for Loveland) but you turn off just before it. The stretch is about 50 m. There is a start and stop sign. At the start sign, set gear to neutral and off the brakes and watch your car go uphill. It is quite fun because of the optical illusion. No fun if you don't drive.

This is a lovely spot to visit. You can wander around the artists village enjoy the outdoor sculptures (kids will like the brightly coloured animals near the art shop/cafe) and then have a good look at the exhibitions inside.  There is a permanent one and a temporary one. The temporary one at present is about marine plastics and pollution. The work was really good especially the video work and created   man   by a young female Korean artist. Most impressive.The last Wednesday of the month entry is free but it's only 2000 won anyway I think. They have an English brochure and the lady at reception was very pleasant.

This is a lived-in Village.  Locals are still living their lives as how they used to live centuries ago.  That being said, modernity started to encroach into the lives here with satellite dishes being placed outside their residences and that villagers explained that theft & burglary are starting to become a nuisance, most possibly caused by tourists that came to their village.  Here, you got to learn about sustainability measures that were used before and we have to ask ourselves why such tradition isn't continuing.  That being said, there are certain customs that are gone for good measures such as the black pigs that are raised there.  In the olden days, the pigs would be fed faeces by humans and then, their meat would be consumed by humans (recycling)!  Anyhow, this is only applicable if you are genuinely curious about Jeju way of life, which is VERY different from the mainland.

This is a greatt museum and more traditional compared to most of the Jeju ones which can be rather quirky. The Haenyeo museum is well resourced in English, has some lovely photos and details a really important part of Jeju's history. Definitely worth a visit

This is a glass art theme park featuring an exhibition hall, garden and models all made entirely out of glass. These are six themed model parks jn which over 250 models are exhibited. These include glass qrt masterpieces by international famous artist from Italy, the Czech Republic, Japan and more.At least one hour explore the entire exhibitation garden. Visit at night as the place is well litted and less tourist.

This is a fun place to visit. I wouldnt get out of my way to see it, but if you are in Jungmun and have an hour, its a fun place to see. The part I liked best are the Teddy Bears in   historical situations  . Like the first moon landing,  the discovery of the Terracotta Army, the fall of the Wall in Berlin etc.
This is a fun place to visit, as apart from the waterfalls you can walk around the area and see many different attractions.

This is a fun and interactive show that would be great for families with members of all ages.The VIP seats are more expensive, but you have the chance of being picked to participate in segments of the show. If this is not important to you, choose the regular seats as the theater is not very large anyway. You can get a 5,000 won discount if you reserve tickets through YEHA Tours. Then pick up the tickets on the day of the show.Instead of an intermission in the middle, a cast member does some interactive clapping and stomping with the audience.The City Hall downtown area is a 15-minute walk away from the theater. You can find restaurants and shops there.

This is a facility that houses multiple attractions  and they are all basically geared toward separating the tourist from his or her money. Notwithstanding this  our family had a great time spending a couple of hours here. The main attraction appears to be the indoor cart racing track. It's not cheap  around KRW 40 000 for a package that includes 10 minutes on the track and a ticket to the   unique objects   museum. We actually found the items in the museum quite entertaining - objects that trick your eye  weird inventions. The go cart driving was a bit disconcerting (no helmets  no apparent real concern for safety) but in the end it was fun. I was glad I was on the track with just another father-son pair. On the way out  my kid bought carrots for horses that were in a corral  and the guy there was nice enough to take my kid around a lap on the horse (again  no safety gear). My kid was fine but I was glad when both the go cart ride and the horseride finished without any problems.If you are desperate to kill a couple of ours and the weather is bad  this may be a good place to go with tweens or teens. They also offered a   Survival Game   attraction which looked like it was done with laser-tag type guns (not paintball).

This is a cave formed by molten lava melting the rock layers away over a very very long time. So expect a huge dimly-lit tunnel with uneven walking surface. The small museum does a good job of explaining the geological aspect of the cave. The 2 km round trip into the cave is not difficult but wear a pair good walking shoes and if you need, bring a small torch. This cave is located on the eastern part of the island so best to visit nearby attractions like the Ichulbong, Phoenix Island etc.Another tip: if you hated Geography in school, give this place a miss. LOL!

This is a beauty to behold. The site is really breathtaking! We visited the site after our lunch, it was a sunny day yet it was very cold due to the wind. The site is famous destinations, many tourists come and flock to the cliff, that is why patience is very important if you want to have  good solo and group photos. My Jeju visit was complete due to this wonderful, amazing and lovely cliff. The blue sea is just so enticing. The sound of the waves was mesmerizing and the arrangement of the stones in a unique and beautiful shapes are indeed a beauty to behold. This must be part of the bucketlist for every tourist who will come to Jeju.

This is a beautiful waterfall that empties directly into the sea. Once at the bottom the mist was very refreshing on a hot day. There are places where kids can wade but I'd recommend water shoes. I saw an adult sandal get swept into the sea. I brought my two kids (age 8 and 4). At the bottom of the stairs there were some very big rocks that were difficult for my 4 year old to navigate, had to carry him part of the way. My 8 year old did just fine. We didn't have water shoes and even though they had fun, they would have been a lot more comfortable with better foot protection. Good site, family friendly with some caution due to big rocks/slippery, not good for toddlers or smaller.

This is a beautiful volcanic crater well worth visiting. It doesn?t take too long to reach the top from the entrance (despite the sometimes steep stairs). The views are magnificent as you ascend, from the summit, as well as when you descend. Plus there are various volcanic rock formations that you can appreciate along the way, both ascending and descending (the two paths are different). The crater is full of trees and grass of a very unique shade of green (I?ve seen this shade of green only in the vegetation of other extinct volcanic craters such as the ones in Tanzania). There are platforms to sit on at the summit from where you can appreciate the view. After descending, make sure to visit the cove where you can meet the Haenyeo or the traditional fisher women of Jejudo. The way to the cove is clearly marked with signboards and it?s only a couple of staircases down to the beach. The Haenyeo put up a performance twice a day, which is very touristy but interesting nevertheless. You can buy all kinds of fresh seafood from them and ask them to prepare it for you to eat at the restaurant. But it?s mostly eaten raw / semi-raw with various sauces and the typical side dishes. The sea weed is particularly good, which you get as a side dish. There is unfortunately no English menu. If you don?t want to eat raw seafood, after picking your seafood portion at the entrance, take it to the counter inside the restaurant and ask that it be stir-fried (?pokkum? in Korean). Beware that even when it?s stir-fried, it?ll still be more on the raw side than the fried side. The black sand beach in the cove is also a treat. If you look closely and attentively, you?ll find all sorts of marine life among the rocks, in the pools and on the sides of the mini cliffs facing the beach.

This hike round trip, if stopping at the witseoreum shelter is about 5.8 miles round trip.  But a better way is to go up Eorimok trail (2.9 miles) and come back down via Yeongsil trail from Witseoreum Shelter (2.3 miles) Constant uphill to the top, good views of the mountains and the city below after halfway mark, and clean fresh air make this hike very worthwhile.  the hike up Eorimok trail consists alternating thick square studded steps, Boardwalk, and grave bedded large stones.    The first half is rather boring.  You hike up through the forest and have a recurring doubt about the trail you have chosen.  However, once you leave the trees, the view opens up and while it isn't majestic, it is a very pretty view to soak in during the remainder of the trail.    There is a lookout post that provides a sweeping view of the city below, and if there are low clouds you will be above it giving you an even more amazing view.   At the shelter you can use the restroom and buy cup noodle soup at around 11am and then start the descend down Yeongsil Trail.  This trail provides a view of the opposite side of the mountain and also has a lookout post that is rather awesome, especially when clouds are speeding past you.  Since we had friends drop us off at the Eorimok trail and pick us up at the Yeongsil trail, transportation wasn't a problem.  But at the Yeongsil trailhead we saw plenty of taxis waiting for business.

This Hallasan Fried Rice is a must have, must Go, must try, if you are in Udo Island. It is available at the 'Pungwon' restaurant. It is about 20mins walking from the harbour. If you are driving, key in the Tel no. 7841894 in your GPS device.First you will have to order either Black pork or cuttlefish according to your preference. There is a minimum number of portions to order based on the number of pax. There were 4 of us and we order 2 Pork and 1 Cuttlefish. We will begin by BBQ the meat. Until we are about halfway through, you can order the rice from the staff. The staff will put aside some meat and start by cooking the rice. The whole idea of Hallasan Fried Rice is that the staff will tell you the story about Mount Hallasan and the islands nearby; all these while making the rice into the shape of a mountain. He will then pour in the egg mixture and meat and cheese... and after numerous of flipping the rice, it's done. Fret not if you don't understand Korean, they have Chinese staff who can do the story telling in Mandarin. The process of hearing about the story is very interesting coupled with the visual of the staff cooking the rice. Not to mention, it tastes damn good too!

this form part of our family trip (winter korea trip end November - December 2013), which the view so so nice, so do the weather...1 thing must try, which we missed.. go to the bottom near to the side which there are so may fresh seafood available which the foods are so to fresh, straight from the sea!

This crater is unlike the others seen on the island because it didn't form much of a surrounding cone due to its quick explosion without spewing much lava around. It is the only such kind of volcano seen in Korea.Apart from the special crater, there are miscanthus (the purple reed) and eulalia in different seasons. Very leisure walk around.We spent an hour inside, including a nap under the tree on a wooden swing.

this cave is huge and takes some time to walk it from start to end. it's cold and damp inside and smells fresh and foresty. You can see layers or larva formations on the walls as you walk.  I enjoyed this place, and have recommended my friends to visit too. It's worth the drive out from the touristy hotel beach areas.  But be careful to wear comfortable and waterproof shoes, it gets slippery and a bit wet in some places.  A must for nature lovers.

this beautiful mountain is located in the east side of island , from centre of jeju to mountain is around more than an hour . entrance ticket is 2 dollar and your journey will start from bottom of mountain , korean made easy stairs which really don't bother u that much . i visited mountain on evening so like sunrise which is famous , sunset can be too . this is a must so go n enjoy it .

This beach, East of Jeju city, on the North coast, is a real gem. Our favourite part is the smaller bay to the East of the main beach. You can rent a static caravan right on the beach there, with an unbeatable, uninterrupted view of the sea. Great snorkelling around the rocks to the right and you can walk up the small oreum further to the right. The main beach has a good eatery that sells Western food and Stella Artois!

This beach is surrounded by cafes, seafood, and one amazing restaurant in particular -   Arepa Grill!   At the end of the main strip facing the water, this place offers the most amazing Venezuelan food and ice cold beer They have a delicious vegetarian arepa that they can make vegan upon request. It's a nice change from the cafes that are all quite similar. I did, however, enjoy the bean bags at   Woodstock.

This beach is a great place for tourists! Upon arriving there are lots of vendors with delicious food and things you might need for the beach (towels, hats, beach mats, swim suits, booze, etc). The main beach is usually very crowded (understandably). I like to go to the beach to the right, it's just a 5 minute walk on the sidewalk, clearly visible with a clear understanding it's leading to another beach. This part of the beach seems to be less crowded with all of the same benefits! Great place to relax, enjoy the sun, and swim in the water!

This attraction consists of a beautiful and natural   sculpture by the sea  . This formation occurred long ago as part of volcanic activity in the area. You get to experience amazing scenery and photo ops at this very special place. As you enter, you walk through a gorgeously landscaped park and continue on with an easy walk to the observation platform overlooking the formations by the sea. You will not see anything like this anywhere else in the world. They also offer a nice snack bar and gift shop specializing in local fare. A really enjoyable way to spend a couple of hours!

This 6 KM (one-way) hike begins steeply, with nicely laid-out stairs climbing up through a beautiful, dense forest of oaks and maples.  It is very peaceful here, and our early (8 AM) start put us on the trail ahead of the crowds that showed up later in the day.  Most of the elevation gain -- total about 700M -- is accomplished in the first third of the hike.  The reward is a lovely stroll with some ups and downs through open meadows for the remainder of the hike to the Witse Oreum shelter.  Two springs are available if you need water on the way (but fill your water bottle directly:  I saw people drinking from the dippers hanging by one of the springs).  Views of the Halla crater wall and sweeping views downslope, of other parasitic cones and the sea, can be spectacular here on a clear day.  We went back down the Eorimok trail to our rental car, but other hikers we met recommended a one-way hike up the Yeongsil Trail (not so long) and then down the Eorimok (but then you have to take a bus or have two cars to do a shuttle).  Neither trail goes to the top of the crater, those areas being closed for extensive restoration.  However, the views were fantastic and I don't feel that I missed out on anything except a hard climb.

They have everything here from hiking, go karts, horseback riding, sky diving to airsoft. Buses traverse every half hour in one of the safest highways all over the world amidst a back drop of awesome scenic views.

There's no variety at all, looks like... Only the exoensive overrated oranges of Jeju. don't get me wrong, they are good, but I would NEVER pay so much money for fruit! Yes, fruit is REALLY expensive in Korea, but 50k is over the top... So: Harabongs, the other oranges in sweets like tartlets and chocolates, black pork jobal, seafood, souvinirs and fruit. That's what you can buy in the market. It was nice to see and the taste some stuff, but i wouldn't visit there again

There's basically nothing here except for the black rock that is sculpted by nature to look like a dragon head.  However, the sea view is pretty. Doesn't need to spend a lot of time here.  Maybe about 10 mins max. There's also a souvenir soup nearby which sells Korean gifts. The shop is not huge but you can find stuffs that typical souvenir shops will sell. eg. keychain, pen, towels, mugs, socks (yes, for some reasons, Koreans are really fond of cute socks with cartoons)..etc.Saw the Roll Hotto snack.  In Singapore, we call this flakey flour pastry as prata. In this case, they rolled the prata with egg and ham complete with vege. Kindda cool.The ice cream they are selling at this attraction is interesting.  I chose 2 flavors: Vanilla and Strawberry. Price is KRW3,000 or RMB20. It's kind of interesting to note that RMB is accepted in Korea as a form of payment. Nonetheless, the ice cream is yummy!More photos available onhttp://i-wanna-travel.blogspot.sg/2015/03/korea-jeju-17-mar-2014.html.

There's an entrance fee, that's one . It's very far away from where we stayed (Gujwa-eup), that's two . Transportation is quite a pain.... when you stay outside the city area ...we had to hire a cab everytime we go out and see places, although, they were very kind enough to ask and offer to wait for us until we finished our tour.I think the place is great for kids and teenagers and those who love modern art and colors. It's quite a huge place with lots of interesting collections... just follow the trails so you won't miss any of the displays. At the end of it, there is a shop wherein you can buy some souvenirs...i find it quite expensive though. ⓒ

There's a starting point and ending point, that shows this mysterious road's gravitational force. Many went with tour buses but it's best to experience this in your own rented car! Switch to neutral and let the mystery begin!

There's a lot to try and absorb in this open air museum. Maybe too much for your average tourist. I mean the somewhat authentic reproductions were cool for the first three or four structures. I enjoyed having a window into what life was like for peasants 100 - 300 years ago and/or the actors who currently play them in historical television dramas. However the minutia became simply overwhelming especially since there was a tendency to focus on the details as if everyone lived and breathed Korean archaeology. There was also a fairly obvious and persistent attempt to commercialize on cheesy trinkets. Some of the   traditional wares   were okay but I think you can get better quality at lower prices elsewhere. The same can be said for the food. The reenactments of wedding ceremonies and shaman rituals were entertaining and the kids could ride ponies. All in all I was glad to end my tour of this facility. It was a rather pricey way to spend an hour or two. If you were in the area or you have a passion for such things maybe give it a try. However I think there are far better ways to spend your time on Jeju. *You can catch bus 720 at the Bus Terminal for 3300 Won. The trip takes a little over an hour:http://www.rome2rio.com/s/Jeju-si/Jeju-Folk-Village-Museum*Here's a Jeju Weekly piece that might give you a better idea of what this place is all about:http://www.jejuweekly.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=4196

There were many themes in this park, and even though I had thought this wouldn't be very interesting initially, my family and I ended up really enjoying the place.In particular, my mum liked the hydrangeas display, my kids liked the birds display (peacocks, especially), my wife liked the bonsai garden and I liked the caves! In all, we spent almost 4 hours there!!! And we didn't complete the park, because we were too hungry and wanted to go the Jeju-si for dinner :)

There were a lot carter in jeju island, one of them is sangamburi.We went there by rent a car, from our hotel around 1 hour. The place is calm and nature. With mountain view, savana and trees all around.If you like nature, this place is one of your choice. One of korean movie was made there.When we entered the place, there's a garden, walked inside there's line of trees, in the middle, there's savana.Going further, you will find mountain view.

There is not much to see on the way to the top. Remember it's a 19k hiking and you need to use your time wisely in a day. We went on a cloudy day. It wasn't too hot but the hiking was difficult with rocks covering most of the roads. So get yourself a real pair of hiking shoes! My feet got hurt and it was slippery after rain. Some parts have stairs, which are highly appreciated... The top view was great but maybe it was dry, we did not see water in the crate. Spring and Fall might have more to see. My friend and my legs have been hurting since we accomplished it...

There is a start sign & stop sign. Upon reaching the start sign, switch to neutral gear, on hazard light, and keep your car engine on. It will start to move forward on a uphill slope. Very slowly. Of course, do be alert and keep your eye infront and foot hover on brake if necessary.It is a one lane traffic, so not all cars are stopping to be wow by this nature forces, you might be honked by other drivers for slowing down and doing this anti-gravity act. Well... just ignore them. They will move on by cutting your lane.There is a convenient shop next to it and car park. You can park your car there and come down to try it with a half-filled water bottle. It will perform the same too, rolling up on a up-slope.However, beware of cars. There is still on-coming traffic.

There is a start point specified on the road. I stopped my car, put car to neutral and released the brakes - the car started to move slowly forward and up slope! From inside the car, the road is up slope, yet the car is like rolling down slope on neutral gear. Fascinating! A must try if you are self-driving.

There is a secret bunker at on Jeju Island, which once housed old national communication facility and had remained unknown to the public for a long time. This large structure is covered with soil and trees, thus disguised to look like a mountain. This old national facility will be reborn as “Bunker de Lumieres”, a media art exhibition hall that will become Jeju's new landmark for culture and art.

There is a reason that this place was packed.  The museum is located in a super modern building set amongst impeccably groomed grounds and a green tea plantation.  The   museum   part takes 5 minutes to get through but the caf챕 and market is buzzing with tourists enjoying an assortment of green tea treats.  I found lots more tea options at this store than any other in Korea (and there are many!)  But the bonus is the Innisfree store adjacent to the Museum on the same grounds.  Here you can make your own mask concoctions customize soap and find lots high quality unique gifts with Jeju logo on them.  I spent at least an hour here alone.  They also have a caf챕.  Definitely a must stop on Jeju!

There is a place for hand-made soap. If you buy a pack of raw material for making soap, you are able to sit down and design your own soap right away. The package is ~15,000 won which includes the material of making 3 pieces of soap and the final product wrapping stuff as well. It is a very good experience for ladies apart from shopping.

There is a lot more than meets the eye here. People first wonder but then realize they are glad to visit The Glass Castle. It is a museum and park of glass works by local artisans and crafts people and the collection is vast, so vast it takes a while to see everything. There is a diverse array of glass work in gardens, themes, and museum displays of varying quality and rarity around the park.This includes large outdoor sculptures such as the yellow submarine at the entrance or crystal skulls, and glass displays around the park. We were impressed by the size of the park and diverse collection of work. They also have workshops here and some hands on experiences.I would recommend this place as a worthy place to visit while on Jeju, near the O'Sulluc Tea Museum and Plantation which only 5 minutes away.

There is a bus from Jeju bus terminal that takes 1hours and a half min and you have to take a Ferry that costs 5,500won.If you dont know how to plan one day travel I would like to recommend you to go Udo and  Seongsan Ilchulbong that is closer to each other If you start your day early you will probably have more time thoughTo see all island it takes 3~4hours by bus that there is Tour bus which costs 5,000wonHowever i would like to recommend you to ride a bike for some partIt is beautiful to ride around the sea and you can feel relaxed.There is 3 beaches that you can visit and those are all different atmosphereespecially there is Coral beach that are exists only 3palce on the world Please go towards the end where people are not crowdedYou will see more pretty coralUdo is famouse for peanut that if you like plz try only small amount since it is a bit expensiveI am not sure if there is famouse food for foreginer but street food is okay As my memory Udo is one of the best part in Jeju island I will recommend for my friends

There are two main reasons for which I cannot rate this park a full 5/5. One being that although the park is supposed to be a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and a World Heritage Site, it allows an absurd number of treacherous hikers (most of whom will be waving or dragging their useless trekking poles around, so watch your eyeballs) onto the trail each day. I do not believe that there is a limit to how many people can start the trek, which makes for a very busy and quite honestly annoying trail. Don't expect to be one with nature on this hike. Secondly, the hike itself is not a technically difficult course, but I cannot for the life of me understand why the trail is set with awkwardly placed and downright dangerous rocks. It would have been much better to leave the path completely untouched in my opinion.HOWEVER, the view from the top is well worth the rolled ankles and the gouged eye sockets to which you may subject yourself on this trek.I ascended via Seongpanak Trail (＿?깊 - 9.6km) and descended via Gwaneumsa Trail (愿???  - 8.7km) in late autumn, 2014. Having read that the hike is beautiful in every different season, I originally thought of trekking the mountain at least once per season as I'll be here for a year. I can't, however imagine - no fathom - surviving the brutal heat, humidity and mosquitoes during the summer months. There are a few different ways of reaching the summit of Hallasan and they are apparently not always open. There are also checkpoints that you need to reach before certain times during the year so make sure to get an early morning start and to do your research before attempting this hike.

There are two kinds of people in the world: those who like their beaches to be overrun with screaming, writhing masses of tourists, and those who think being happy is important. And sure, this could be just another one of those jaded reviews written by a bitter old troll who has no other outlet for his vitriol than to misinform random strangers on the Internet, but it's not. I'm here to vehemently disabuse anyone who is thinking of having a quiet day at Hyeopjae beach out of a sense of civic duty. Yes, the beach itself is a soft sand frame for spectacular sunsets punctuated by occasionally clear blue-green waters, but it's also a growing epicenter for the worst kind of overbooked tourism. Pros: The beach itself is broad, and the area in front of the main beach lends itself to a safe experience for attended children: there is a large, open region of sand at low tide and shallow water at high tide for kids to play in.  The view is nice, and the sunsets are extravagant. There is camping nearby with good tree cover, adequate facilities for showering, stores for trinkets and swimming paraphernalia, and places to buy food and drink. There is also a small but growing night life near the beach that has a distinctly island feel, far from the thumping of your standard Korean club scene. Cons: The swimming area is unbelievably small, so not only does everyone get to experience a sardine style of   swimming   in water that rarely goes past the hips of an adult, the water is also full of sand and debris due to the high person-per-square-meter ratio. Visibility underwater is often zero, so don't expect to see fish on a busy day - which is pretty much the entire high season. There is garbage everywhere, both in the water, and in large, reeking piles near the parking lot. The noise is unbelievable (just like the parking) and the local restaurants - with only one or two exceptions - cater to the lowest common denominator for quality.  Hyeopjae is being targeted by packaged family tours, and yet there is a laughably inadequate infrastructure in place to ensure a safe, organized experience for children. The beautiful volcanic rocks along the sides of the beach and in some parts of the water are playgrounds of minor and major injury. The often unattended children that race up and down the beach are in no way warned about or protected from these hazards. The forest of beach umbrellas tightly packed on the   main beach   is both uncomfortably crowded and poorly organized for parents to keep an eye on their kids, and for kids to find their parents when they get lost. The lifeguards are simultaneously overworked and overzealous. They are simply too busy whistling at people to keep them safe from the dangers of hip-deep water (a strange and annoying tradition amongst Jeju lifeguards) to effectively keep an eye out for people - especially children - who are may be in real trouble.Bottom Line: If you've never had the chance to explore Jeju, you won?t know just how bad Hyeopjae is. Moreover, as I said in the beginning, some people actually enjoy the mass market appeal of tourist traps, and I don't begrudge them their tastes. All I'm saying is Jeju has an embarrassment of better beaches with better food and better facilities. In fact, you only have to travel up or down the road for 15 minutes in either direction to find beautiful, secluded areas where you lavish on an empty beach and swim in truly pristine waters. Q.E.D.

There are some fictional characters that you and me adore and love during our childhood and yet still relish even though we have become adults. Hello Kitty is certainly one of them, and is a favourite of one of my children. However, the good part is not every visitor to Jeju and the locals are a fan of Hello Kitty, so the Hello Kitty Island Museum is not on the itinerary of most tour companies, and hence it?s not crowded.Getting there and fees: Hello Kitty Island Museum, opened in late 2013, is located in the south west part of Jeju (GPS code/coordinate 7926114).  Not to worry if you cannot find space in the small open-air car park outside the Museum because there?s another huge open air car park below the small one. Parking is free. Entrance fee to the Museum is 12,000 won for adult, 11,000 won for teenagers and 10,000Won for children. However, my family and I made use of the discount coupon for entrance fees from the Hertz car rental discount booklet.The Museum/Attraction: when we entered, we were immediately greeted by a large hall where there?s a circular cone of Hello Kitty toys, a photo-taking stop with the entire Hello Kitty family and Hello Kitty?s house where she?s standing at the balcony welcoming you and beckoning you to enter the door into the various exhibition halls. There are 3 levels with the exhibition halls on the first and second level, the gift shop on the first level, the Hello Kitty Caf챕 on the second level and the 3D theatre and an outdoor gallery on the third level. To cover everything, including a meal at the Hello Kitty Caf챕, would easily take about 2-3 hours. In the true sense, this Hello Kitty Museum is a museum ? there are exhibits of anything related to the adorable Hello Kitty. There are several themed exhibition halls on the first and second level e.g. History Hall, Art Education Hall, Music Education Hall, World Gallery Hall, Hello Kitty Room, Constellation Education Hall, amongst others.So we took plenty of photographs and selfies. I particularly like the exhibit of Hello Kitty represented by 26 countries (I found my own country) as well as the huge room containing the huge Hello Kitty bed where one of my children got the Hello Kitty toy snatched away by a toddler.At the Hello Kitty Caf챕 ? with Hello Kitty ribbon windows, Hello Kitty-themed sofas and Hello Kitty engraved tables ? you have to try the Hello Kitty Waffle Set, green tea latte, coffee or  hot chocolate (the 3 hot drinks have a profile of Hello Kitty on the surface), Hello Kitty Strawberry Cake and Cheesecake. Really yummy stuff!Whether you are a fan or not of Hello Kitty, I think this Museum is a fun attraction to visit and be acquainted with Hello Kitty. However, be prepared to ?share? the premises with many joyful and lively children and teenagers. But if you are not a fan and if you have limited time in Jeju, then I suppose you could spend that 2-3 hours elsewhere.

There are so few places in the world which offer this columnar basalt formation, and even fewer in such a scenic location. This is the best spot to view these gorgeous formations along the stretch of coast and nothing bets watching the surging ocean smash against the rocks - it's hard to believe this is simply the result of rapidly cooled magma and not some otherworldly creation. My heart still tells me mermaids have something to do with it! Make sure to take a snack and just sit and be humbled, it can get a bit crowded on the viewing platform but everyone is in such a hurry if you just sit back and take it all in you will find you have this wonder of the natural world to yourself in no time!! An absolute must do!!

There are sign posts to mark the start and end of the 100 metres stretch of the Mysterious Road.  Pretty fun to play   magic   with family and friends. Put your car to neutral gear, release your foot off the accelerator and notice the car moving   uphill   on the road.  Recreate the same effect with a bottle or ball rolling uphill.  The Mysterious Road is actually a gravity hill i.e. a place where a slight downhill slope appears to be an uphill slope due to higher surroundings, creating the natural illusion that water flows uphill or that a car left out of gear rolls uphill.  Worth a fun stop if you self-drive!

There are several things to visit and see inside the Hailim Park.  This botanical garden includes bonsai artwork and garden, a Jeju stone, a Jaeam Folk Village, an underground Hyeopjae & Sangyong Cave, and a zoo.  Well worth a visit.  Best time to visit is in the spring especially during the cherry blossom season.
There are pretty parts to the garden, but it's definitely not worth the 9,000 won entrance. It's very stereotyped. Hallim Park is far better for a half-day trip and a similar price.

There are only 2 trails that lead to the peak of Hallasan. Gwaneumsa and seongpanak trail. We took the seongpanak trail up and gwaneumsa trail down. It was no easy hike for sure. It took us 10 hours to hike up and back down ( late 20's, amateur!). We thought we give it a go and hike all the way to the peak since we were there. The scenery was breathtaking and definitely worth the hike. autumn foliage was amazing (but our leg muscles were aching real bad the next day). tons of people though. best to start the hike early about 6.30am if you wish to reach the top and if you are an amateur hiker with not-so-active lifestyle. be well prepared with adequate clothing, proper shoes and snacks

there are many kinds of artworks such as glass flowers,trees,music instrument,toilet,etcworld artist from japan,usa,italy, their works displayed.you can make something like glass cup if you want.it will be memorable while you are in jeju.

There are a few spots that feature the renowned Jeju women divers. However, this museum is a good place for one to be more acquainted on this tradition and the dwindling of this important part of Jeju history.

There are 5 trails, we took the shortest but most challenging one since we started after lunch. Steep but scenic view. 3 hrs going up (with several rests in between) and took us 2 hours going down. I almost gave up but it is rewarding once you reach the top and can touch the clouds!

There are 5 trails up to Mt Hallasan. I took the shortest trail, Yeongsil Trail 3.7KM. The Koreans told me this is the most beautiful trail up to Mount Hallasan, but this trail doesn't lead you to the crater. The landscape changes at as you hike up. Super stunning and beautiful. You must reach the   stop area   by 12pm if not they will not let you go till the end of trail and continue to descend with Eorimok trail. Start early, it's a tough hike but it's worth it! A must to visit!

There are 3 memorial towers, one of Kim Man Duk, civil uprising volunteers, and one of patriot at the end of Joseon dynasty. There is Kim Man Duk's grave stone, original one which moved here because of road construction in its original place. This is located in Sara-bong(hill) park. It is very low hi,, but you can enjoy beautiful sunrise on the top of hill. Even day time, I could enjoy nice view toward Jeju international port. I recommend walk around the hill first then visit Mochungsa afterwards, The Sarabong walk path is part of Olle #18. There are many locals who work out here. You can feel like a local!

The Yongmeori coastline was not on my list of places to see/go when I first planned my taxi tour itinerary, but I was persuaded to go by my guide, Mr Lee Hong Min. I am so glad that he brought us here as it turned out to be the highlight of the tour for me.There are 2 ways to access the coast - and you'll either begin or end up at the very impressive looking stone   stairway  . To walk the coastline, you don't need to be superfit as it's not a tough hike, but some might find the rocks to be uneven and slippery so do watch your step even as you take in the beautiful scenery. The round trip takes about 30 mins for the superfit and about an hour for families.The scenery of Yongmeori is breath-taking, especially for someone who's never seen such rocky formations before. Turning every corner drew exclamations of awe from us and we took dozens of pictures throughout. You can really see where the sea has eroded away the cliff, leaving craggy sights that vaguely remind me of the Grand Canyon. You can even see the inhabitants of the sea that were left 'stranded' at low tide, waiting for the high tide to return - small fish, oysters and mussels, and some weird cockroach like crustaceans scurry along the rocks. Haenyeo or women divers set up stall along the coast so if you fancy a fresh seafood snack, you can feast on the rocks for a unique experience unlike any other.Tip: There are no toilets once you pass the small stalls set-up before the attraction entrance as this is natural scenery attraction so do make sure all in your party go first before you enter.

The world's largest nutmeg forest can be found on Jeju Island, South Korea.  A beautiful, old growth forest with a gigantic nutmeg tree as the central attraction, this forest offers quiet beauty to stroll through in a relaxed and rejuvenating atmosphere. The smell of nutmeg is distinct immediately upon entering.  Parts of the forest have beautiful red crushed stone walking paths and other parts have very well maintained wooden pathways.  To do the whole forest takes about 60 minutes at a comfortable pace.  Picture opportunities abound, and you'll likely be able to see wedding couples posing for their formal pictures amidst the beauty of the forest surroundings.  A great break from the hustle-bustle of other attractions, this forest offers the opportunity to enjoy nature in a very unique way.

The women divers of jeju are famous for their free diving culture of gathering food from the bottom of the sea such as sea cucumber, sea weed, and various shellfish. They are so dedicated to this that It is said that they will start their diving three days after giving birth. They also form unions to govern their way of life and culture. The purpose of this museum also serves to preserve their culture as less and less women are taking up this trade.

The whole way from the car park to the falls itself was scenic. At the start was a pond with mandarin ducks and a bridge. There were various representative statues of Jeju. There were also souvenir shops if you want to buy some snacks or souvenirs. I liked the different types of trees grown, even though it is not autumn, the maple trees still looked very pretty. All along the way is a river, you go to the falls on one side and you can return on the other side of the river. There were plenty of explanation signs on the falls, the mottled eels and the rock face etc. The falls themselves don?t look very impressive but I still like the whole place. On the way back there is a nice flower display and large sculpture as well a stone auditorium.

The whole trip up and down including breaks took us 8 hours.  19.2 km (to and back) at 1200 meters elevation.  Most of the trail is covered with volcanic rocks, big and small so it's not so easy to walk.  Lots of steps which is not typical in Europe or the Rockies.  It was cloudy the day we hiked up.  At the peak it was windy, cold and foggy so we couldn't really see much and didn't want to stay longer.  I have done many trails in other parts of the world and this is not one I would want to do again.

The whole trail takes about 45 mins to an hour to complete. It was truly interesting to be inside a lava tube and during the walk, there were informational signs to explain parts of the tubes! I would recommend bringing a hoodie and water proof shoes as it is very wet and slippery inside :) The dampness will make you feel cool even in the summer.

The walking trail at Yongmeori Coast is just a few hundred meters (~700 m) long, but the layered sedimentary structures made from rocks and volcanic ashes, and dramatic shapes created by erosion from hard ocean-waves and wind make it breathtaking art of nature and truly resembles Geopark. It is known that the site is indeed designated as one of the nine Jeju sites certified by the Global Geopark Network in 2010. Personally, this is one of my best scenic places in Jeju in the view of both geology and photography lover.The part of these cliffs appeared stretched out from nearby Sanbangsan Mountain. The meaning of Yongmeori in Korean is Dragon Head. Interestingly, the rough surface of rocks and dramatic shapes formed by rocks due to erosions make it look like a dragon's head going underwater.This part of Jeju is also famous for women sea-drivers. During our visit, we have got an opportunity to try out a few fresh kinds of seafood sold by Korean grandmothers along the coastline. Another attraction near this cliff is the huge shipwreck which is actually a reproduction built as the Hamel Castaway Memorial to commemorate a Dutch sailor (Hendrick Hamel). It is said that he was drifted to the shore of Jeju by a typhoon in 1653. He then wrote a book providing the West some insights into Joseon Korea for the first time. All together this place is very impressive and must not be missed.

The volcano look really scenic when looking from far away. This is also a part of UNESCO world heritage site too. There are about 500 steps to the peak of volcano which is not that tired though because step are well built. The view from the top also worth climbing. The weather is great even it was winter, it is not too cold, about 5c.
The visit to Eco land was part of a tour, we liked the train ride the best, there were some nice spots to get off and take pictures of but other than that there was not much to do.

The view was stunning and the crater is large and definitely a great place to take photos. Before you start hiking, i advice you should bring a bottle of drinking water, because there's no stores that sell one near the peak. A windbreaker or double layer clothes are useful, coz the wind was pretty strong. I sweated a lot. But reaching the top will pay all physical efforts!Last but not least, Keep your trash to yourself.
