Trash disposal bins are very rare. i Highly recommend this place.!

The view of the so-called Dragon Head Rock will be impressive for some and disappointing for other. My friends and I definitely felt the latter. After a whole day of exploring Jeju, we decided to stop by this attraction to look at the sunset.However, we were greatly disappointed by the attraction as all 4 of us felt that the rock wasn't as impressive as the other attractions we have seen around Jeju. Not to mention the amount of tour buses at this particular attraction was ridiculous. The price of the items and food around the area was also very expensive. I would not recommend this place unless you have a lot of extra time at Jeju. I rather you spend that time on the Olle Trails which provides better view of the coast.

The trip up and down the 1.95km tall mountain took me the entire day but experience and view was really worth it. It would have been better if I had been properly equipped as I was in normal walking shoes and a small bottle of water while everyone else had their trekking shoes and stick with them which made going up and down more quickly and safe. There are alot of routes but not all the routes will lead you to the peak. Spoke to a few people on my way up and they shared that this is most tedious route as its the longest. There is only one way up and down which makes trekking easy for solo traveller like me.It'd be good if you can bring some food and lots of water with you where you can picnic with many korean families when you reach the peak. Do prepare to start early as you will have to reach a certain checkpoint before they allow you to continue your way up the peak. It was a heartwarming experience for me when all the korean people who walked past me would encourage me to press on and they would share they food around at the peak. Korean families usually do this as a family activity where the grandmother, grandfather, parents and kids would climb leisurely. If a grandparent can do it, so can you. Thats all :)

The trip ti Mt Halla is great and do not miss it. Youu really should start early, and it takes a little less than recommended times, about one hour less if you walk clow but continuously.We walked three 15, 30 and 55, two males - my son and me and one female accompanied us.We traveled by bus from Seogwipo, busses go every 15-30 minutes since early morning to Seongpanak - busstop.Back we walked to Gwaneumsa and there is no direct bus connection, but take a taxi (for 5 thous WON) or walk about 5 km. We finaly shared taxi with very kind Korean directly to Seogwipo, thank again to the kind man. It was good and exhausting and we slept nicely after all. The next day we were ready to walk again. Unfortunatelly was very cloudy and walked upon clouds finally, however it was June, it was not too hot. There are two springs along the way - one up and nexd on the way down. Recommended to every who travels with teenagers:) Normal hiking shoes like trainers were OK, dont worry.

The trek and the views from the mountain were beautiful and I am glad to have spent some time there but I think I may have some had some disillusions/overly high expectations caused in part by Jeju Islands (with Mt. Halla as one of the focal attractions) recent media attention created by its addition to the 'new 7 natural wonders of the world' I found Mt. Halla to be an awesome area but not offering exceptionally greater views than  the many 'mountains' all across mainland South Korea. The trails and park area receive a constant flow of tour bus groups from China, Japan and around Korea year round so if your looking for some seclusion in a natural setting you may want to look elsewhere.  (although it is interesting to see throngs of people decked out head to toe in the latest and most expensive trekking gear unnecessarily)I am working in South Korea so for me the travel costs were rather low and thus my vacation to Jeju Island and trip up Mt. Halla was worth it but I think if I had come from anywhere that doesn't offer a direct flight to Jeju Island (China/Japan/Korea) I would have been a little disappointed.

The trail system in Jeju is quite extensive and well mapped out. Our hotel was right on Olle 7 so one day we went tracking. What started on a normal surface road became a rough surface hiking trail through bushes, up and down a rocky coastline. The trail is indicated by ribbons, from what I understand different colors for different olles. when in Jeju hiking should definitely be on the to do list.

The tourist industry is creative. So they discovered a sandy patch on the Island and made it a highlight for an excursion to the Western part of the Island. After one picture you can leave. The sand is nice, however. I took a sample

The teddy bear musuem is filled with a vast variety of teddy bears in different sections. These teddy bears were build to replicate a safari zoo, an aquarium, a palace, an art gallery and many more. There is side information of history of teddy bear and a gallery with ancient greek gods. Try to spot the most expensive teddy bear in the world! Apart from that, its located beside an expressway. Travelling to there might need a bus or taxi ride. Its worth a visit, but not interesting enough for me to come back again. There is too some eateries around there to settle your hunger needs. The musuem requires some entrance fee.

The teddy bear museum is exactly what it's title states.  It's teddy bears in every shape and size.  The first area has historical teddy bears, dating back as far as the turn of the century (1900's).  The second section is works of art redone with teddy bears and finally, there is an outdoor exhibit including a 9 meter tall teddy bear that makes a showing every hour on the hour.  Young kids that like teddy bears and such will have a great time visiting here.  My daughter adored everything.  It is a little pricey, but if you rent a car to get around they often give you a book with coupons for the various attractions on the island or you can book in advance online at a discount price.
The Teddy bear museum has pictures of different famous arts and history. Examples (the mona lesa, WWII, THE KISS)

The tea museum is located on the western side of the island and represents the showpiece of the O'Sulloc tea   empire   in South Korea.  There are a number of O'Sulloc tea cafes all over South Korea which specialize in green tea and also sell sweets as well.  There is a large parking area to accommodate a number of cars and visitors.The tea museum consisted of four   features   from what I could surmise.  First you get a decent view of the western part of the island by walking up the stairs to the roof of the museum itself.  The views aren't that interesting but you do get a good view of the surrounding area.  Second the museum itself describes the tea growing/making/serving process.  Third the cafe/gift shop inside seems to attract the most number of visitors.  You can buy teas and other desserts like you would at any other O'Sulloc cafes.  However it does sell many other items - various teas and more.  Finally another attraction is the tea plantation itself.  O'Sulloc seemingly has a small portion of their plantation on-site that you can walk through (note there may be snakes in the plantation) to get a sense of how the green tea leaves are grown.There is also an Innisfree store right next to the tea museum but we did not visit it.The tea museum is worth a trip though I wouldn't go out of the way to visit it as you can always partake in O'Sulloc teas in various locations in South Korea.

The sun was shining though not really hot this time (last time 9 years ago was rainy).  I wasn't sure how far up I wanted to climb but started off with the family anyway.  Personally I preferred slopes to stairs.  I saw these signs which showed the distance to the peak (caldera): 274m, 180m, etc. I almost decided to turn back because I thought I would be late if I continued to the top when suddenly I reached the top.   Turned out that those were distance markers and not altitude markers.  The view at the top was really good.  The grass in the crater was lush green.  No steam here.  The walk back down was very manageable, and had some good photo spots.  Towards the bottom, the vast patches of perfect green grass were really pretty.

The stairs down into the cave system are steep and plentiful, so if you have trouble with stairs then you should skip it.  Also, if you don't like walking on uneven ground then you should skip it, because most of the cave floor is natural stone, so it's rough and uneven in many places.  There's also small standing pools of water in places, so watch where you step.  You don't have to walk the whole cave length, since it's very long indeed, so you can just do what we do and walk part of the way and then back again.  But you do need appropriate footwear, and no, high heels are NOT appropriate footwear.And remember, this is a natural cave system, not a fun park, so don't go expecting anything beyond what it is.

The Spirited Garden is a great pastime to spend with friends, the garden is beautiful! There is so much plant life to see with a rich cultural and historical story behind each part of the garden! Plenty of great photo-ops here for your social media or if you are big fan of botany you will definitely enjoy it.

The spirited garden has a unique and impressive collection of beautiful bonsai trees, stone artwork, and tranquil ponds. Its a great place to spend a couple of hours while visiting Jeju and offers some great photo opportunities. The staff were very kind and helpful.

The small village seemed to be tended by a couple who actually live in the village.  I believe the village is government subsidized as well, but perhaps the couple who lives there gets additional money from selling some products (more on that later).A lady who lives there gave us a tour of the houses at the village.  She started off with where she lives - which is traditional on the outside, but seemed to have all the modern features on the inside.  We then got a small explanation of the milling device there as well and a water collecting jar.  We were also allowed to put one of the water jars on our backs.  A little pig pen and outhouse were shown as well.Unfortunately, the final destination for the tour was a small room where our tour guide could give us a hard sell on some products - mainly some horse cream or something like that...  That sort of ruined the tour, but I could imagine that this could be the tour guide's main source of income.  And she was kind when we said no to the hard sell.The tour was informative in many ways as the tour guide provided a lot of information and stories of the hardship and struggles of the native Jeju people.

The site was the best part of an all day trip covering the eastern end of Jeju Island. Such places are always fascinating. As soon as you enter, the temperature drops to the lower double digits C.There is a one kilometer stretch you can walk. I like that it has not been jazzed up with a rainbow of colours. The floor is naturally uneven with some sectors covered in wood. The cave is 18 meters as its widest and  23 meters as its tallest. At the far end is located the world tallest lava column at 7.6 meters. When you appreciate the force of Mother Nature to cause such formations, it only adds to the visit.

The show is very entertaining and the performers are professional. There's some audience participation and it's nice. The theater seats are comfy, just relax and enjoy this entertaining show. Good show!

The Seongpanak trail that goes to the summit is curentlyclose, until July 31st. I went all the way to the start of Seongpanak  trail and had to take 2 buses to go Gwaneumsa trail.The hike was nice but difficult. The first part was nice, 3,1km of normal hiking, until we reached the hard part, very steep, with stairs and rock. The climb fromSamgakbong shelter to the summit was not too hard, but a bit warm because of the sun. It as very humid, so be sure to pack a lot of waterand food as there are no vendors on the trail. It easy to reachthe trail by bus, but we took a taxi back to our hotel as we were too tired. A very good exercice and a good hike. I would doit again! ;)

The Seongpanak Trail is the easiest, though the longest trail to hike up Mount Hallasan (bit over 9km). It's a beautiful path with a gradual ascent and some steep sections. The difficulty in this trail is the surface, as the majority of the time you are walking on volcanic rocks that make your footing uneven and it does wear you out. I hiked in Chaco sandals and was ok, but I'm used to it. I highly recommend wearing comfortable shoes. I also suggest getting an early start, before 8am. Because it's the most gradual ascent, this is also a busy trail with hikers constantly going both directions. Bring snacks and plenty of water. There is a re-filling spring water station a bit more than half way to the peak. Highly recommend if you are an outdoorsy person and can handle long walks/hikes.

The Seongeup Folk Village was a walled-in village in the southeast of the island where stone homes showed the construction, culture and lifestyle of the island?s people long ago.Obviously, Jeju wants to maintain some type of historical reference to the old lifestyle.  Our tour guide made it interesting by talking about some practical aspects of the design of the huts (how it was heated, how it was built, etc), but this just wasn't my thing.  In fact, several families that help with the upkeep of the huts actually live in other huts in the community.  That said, those huts have modern adjustments like windows, electric power, etc so even they have moved beyond the   old ways  .  The village had a few shops and a restroom and outside the village was a convenience store with drinks available and another restroom. For me, the bottom line was - I would have preferred to spend the time at a natural landmark (waterfall, cave, hiking trail, etc) instead of doing this, but it was part of an all day tour.  There are simply too many other options to see in Jeju for this to make it to the top of the list, unless it is your   thing  .

The Seongeup Folk Village is huge.  The main entrance has a big car park and a side entrance where you can drive your car in.  Besides the car park, there are many restaurants, two public toilets and a few shops.From the main entrance, you can take a stroll and check out some of the conserved buildings which are open to public.  Information is available in English and you can learn about the earlier settlers and buildings of Jeju Island.  There are also some shops and restaurants inside the folk village.You can easily spend 1-2 hours inside the village and having lunch either in the restaurants inside or besides the car park.  We had delicious black pork bbq at Nammun restaurant (787 2432) located in the area besides the car park.Tip:There are other entrances to the village as well.  I was at one of these prior to finding the main entrance, and there are sales people trying to get us to into houses outside the gate and market horse oil cream and other products.  Avoid these.  While I can't verify whether the products are authentic, it definitely felt like a scam.  Seemed that some reviewers thought this is part of the folk village.

The rocks surrounded by the island have different size and have eroded for years. But the most interesting thing is that rocks are eroded into different levels of cylinders, so it is worth to spend a couple of minutes there taking photos and have a look. Moreover, there are paths for visitors to walk around the edges of the island to have different look of the rocks. It is the margin of Jeju, so when the wave flaps the cliffs, it creates a huge noise. At first, I thought it was something like weapons exposed, my heart pumped faster than normal. After I recognize it is only the wave hits the cliffs, I can clearly experience that how the level of power that the nature can be. It was an unforgettable experience.So, if you have an iPhone which contains the program of Live Photo, try to open it before you take photos. It is because you can record the energetic movement of wave in your photo.

The road was called mysterious road as it seem to be a up slope but your vehicle can move slowly up like going down slope. The area is less crowded at around 7-9am until the tour bus came, where many people actually went down to crowd around this road. The tour bus would stop at the start of the slope and off its Engine and slowly moved up to the end and turn into the car park where the tourists would come down and see cars moving up. Some of them would pour water to show that the water went up instead of down. It is quite mind boggling. But actual fact that this road is due to the surrounding which makes you have the perception thinking it is a up slope but actually it is down.Way to get there is by Car or Bus. It is close to Jeju LoveLand and it is down the same road, so it is not too difficult to find.

The queue was long starting from midnight. The tag was given starting 2:30am. The limit was for 1300 first come first served. The waiting was in 2 celcius temperature. The trek up started at 5:30am in an orderly manner in a hushed procession like atmosphere. At the top of the plateau there were decks facing the direction of the sunrise. All was ready for the first sunrise of 2020. Unfortunately it did not happen. The clouds was too thick and we headed back an hour after the sunrise time. Was I disappointed? Not really. The whole experience was exhilarating, the wait, the trek, the anticipation of the sunrise. It was a memorable experience which I hope to repeat one day.

The products they sell are overpriced compared to the innisfree stores in Busan, Daegu and Seoul so don't bother buying from them. There really isn't much to see apart from the fact that it is rather close to the O?셲ulloc Tea Museum.TLDR: Not worth your time, Jeju is so beautiful go somewhere else!

The principal purpose of the bridge is to provide a walkway to Saeseom Island. The area close by is great for photography - clean water, interesting rock formations, local flora etc. The circuit of the island is also very pleasant, particularly in good weather.

The place itself is huge. We went before lunch and it was a good time because the sun was up. Being a glass museum, most of the art are made of glass and having the sun at its brightest made the art look even more amazing. It's nice to look at the reflections made. There are different signs in Korean, Japanese, and English. They also have shop where they sell little glass artwork. You can bargain with the sellers too. They're nice and friendly.

The place is breathtaking, starting from the parking lot with all the old ladies selling the traditional stuff, the park is amazing with the clear water and swimming ducks & fish, the sakora tree is more than beautiful, then the waterfall i can?t even describe its beauty....and the ticket cost only 2000 Korean won . Inside the park there is a clean toilet and services alsoIf you go to jeju you must visit it

The Peace Park is very spacious and beautifully laid out.  (Shouldn't compare but it reminded us of  a smaller version of the National Memorial Arboretum in Staffordshire, UK.)  They were still working on some landscaping while we were there.   We were lucky enough to catch the excellent art exhibition that is on at the moment and the museum display is very well laid out and informative - lots of English  so we learnt a lot about the Jeju's history around 1948.   We were there about 1.5 hours but could have stayed longer.
the park planting many flowers and plants outside traditional housing. Very refreshing, we can teach our sister too who start to love Korean culture about traditional village.

The park is the mystical legend of how three gods arrived in Jeju-do and started to develop the island. The place is a great escape from the busy city of Jeju, surrounded with trees and pavilion of traditional Korean architecture. You can also sit in for a 15 minutes long animation, available both in English and Korean  describing the origins of Jeju.

The park is quite large. Access to the cave is via two flight of stairs downwards into the earth. The temperature inside is colder than the outdoors, with the pathway often wet with water dripping from above the cave. Lighting is limited, and one has to use flash to take pictures, though a little tweaking of the camera could bring pretty good results without using the flash. There are written explanations regarding the lava layers. Because of time constraints, we were not able to finish exploring the cave to its end.

The park is divided to theme gardens from different areas (China, Japan, Italy, ...) Huge greenhouse has tropical fruit in glass domes so yo can learn how cocoa and bananas grow. There are also glass-fibre dinosaurs and crocodiles hiding in some of the more jungle-like parts. From the viewing platform you can see all the gardens and surroundings. Place was a must-do for schools trippers, who were plenty when I visited. A relaxing stroll in beautiful surrounding.

The park is a it run down and not well maintained. Although the park is big, but there is nothing really big and great. There was a signboard (even on the brochure) stating there is white peacock but we see none. Flowers are dying (perhaps it's because of winter starting soon?) Feel a bit disappointed. I would advice you to plan this in your itinerary if you really have a lot of time as it take quite sometime to go to this park and entrance fees is not cheap.

The park covers a vast area. One has to decide how far you wish to explore and watch your time. A map is given at the ticket counter and we did not expect it to be so big. We went according to the numbered stops. The view was spectacular for some parts of the park that we spent so much time on taking pictures. We tried to move quicker however, in the end, we did not even complete Course 1 (there are 3 different routes). It was enjoyable for some walk & laughter. There are scripts on stones to tell you about the legendary story of this stone park. You may decide, whether you want to keep walking and cover the whole park (I am not sure whether this is even possible in a day) or would you just want to have a feel of this peaceful and beautiful park.

The musueum is dedicated to the Haenyeo - female divers who traditionally fish for molluscs and octopuses etc. without using oxygen masks.  UNESCO has declared the Haenyeo part of humankind's intangible cultural heritage.  We visited the museum shortly after having seen a group of Haenyeo sing their traditional song before heading out into the sea to fish.  Having just witnessed the women fist hand added an extra element of interest.  The museum is well set out, informative and interesting.  Its models, life stories of individuals and displays of clothes and tools  really bring home how tough the life of the Haenyeo was in the past (and it's not easy today).  There is also a short movie explaining the history and traditions of the Haenyeo.  Well worth a visit!

The museum was very very hard to find. The employees were rude and unpleasant. The glass   art   is just a pile of glorified junk. I regeret wasting my time there with my boyfriend. The entrance fee is a joke  please Do NOT go there

The museum was ok, computers and computer games are not my kind of thing but it was interactive so really kept me engaged.The keyboard-shaped waffles in the cafe with four side sauces/cream/ice-cream in the cafe in the basement are awesome. Go for them!Walkable from Nohyung Lotte Mart.

The museum is located next to a please area of town with multiple artists in various media as well as tea/coffee shops - which is how we found the location.? There is a small entrance fee (1000 Won per adult at the time).? In addition to the small, but nice collection of paintings and sculpture, there is a great view of the city and see from the 3rd floor.? If art is your thing, then definitely go.? Otherwise go only as weather or your schedule dictates.

The mountain is extremely busy with tons of people and older koreans are not always very friendly toward foreigners, but the rude people are exceptions. In general the hike is wonderful, just very long. There is beautiful scenery and forests to enjoy. Take a jacket for the top as its cold and start early.

The mountain is beautiful viewed from any side. We started with the 1100m stop early one morning, there was a light dusting of snow from the previous night so the place really pretty. We spent a short time here, about 20 minutes as the fog started to appear. We then drove to the other sides, nice scenic drive.

The Moon Light Walking Tour at Jungmun Golf Club was pleasant and relaxing. The walking tour started and end at the same golf course with optimum safety rules for ongoing corona-19 spreading. The distance was shorter than expected, about 1.5 km which took only about 30 min. Walking was fun due to the group of new friends. During the walking, the sunset was very beautiful. Also, the scenery of the ocean view seen from the golf course was amazing. After walking for 30 minutes, we enjoyed an evening

The market mainly consists of two parts: a fruit market (mostly for visitors) and a fish market (mostly for local, as visitors basically can?t do anything with the raw fishes). In night time, there is also food stalls near Gate 8 but the number is limited (I think there?s about 20) so the queue is often long - mostly Korean youngsters. My Korean friend told me that Jeju is unique with its rice cake (similar to Japanese mochi) and orange that even Koreans ?have to? purchase as gifts when visiting Jeju thus their prices are not cheap.

The market is 60% local 40% tailored to tourist, hence depending on what you are after you can choose the part that suits your expectation.It is the local fresh meat , fish and vegetable market--fresh goodies are sold at a very reasonable price and exceptional quality. The touristic part is nice also-- lot of old aunties promoting the snacks, personally i dont think that's the most authentic souvenir so we decided to go to the pottery shop and ending up buying soup copper pot and stone pot back (though it's heavy) as it did remind us a lot more about the trip.The fresh snack stands are very busy and people are elbow to elbows. Food was yum but probably you don't wonna spend more than 2 hours there. Btw, there is a night food market outside after 5 pm and it's worth grabbing a snack or two.

The marker for Routes 13, 14 and 14-1 are located in one spot. We got confused at first that we ended up completing abour 2-3km of Trail 14 until we got to another marker that we realized we were following the wrong path. We went back to the spot and started looking for the 14-1 trail. We spent the first half of the day doing Trail 14.When we headed to Trail 14-1 which was the intial plan, it was past noon already so the sun was up and it was hot (we did the trail on a summer day). It was a cool experience because the trail will bring you to the peak where you get a great 360 degree view of Jeju! It will take you inside a forest. You might even meet some horses along the way. By the time you'll get to the midpoint, which is the Osulloc Museum, you will realize how much you miss civilization and strangers. The trail will connect you to nature. You'll even find yourself in a dense forest! There are a lot of blue/orange ribbons so you won't be lost. This trail taught me to simply trust and find the blue/orange ribbons and enjoy/embrace nature wherever the trail (or life in general) may take you. Haha. This is definitely off the beaten path but it makes your Jeju tour even more special and truly your own. I would want to do more of the Olleh Trails in the future :)

The Manjanggul Lava Cave was a very large lava tube cave.  A 1km section in the middle of the 7.5km lava cave was open for groups to tour.  We found it an amazing place to visit, and an outstanding example of a lava cave, but since it is a lava tube cave, visitors should expect the following when visiting this attraction:1) unlike limestone caves, generally created by water over long periods of time, lava caves do not usually have the stunning formations (ie ? stalactites, stalagmites, etc).  They have their own unique, highlights, but are not as colorful.  Such is the case with this lava cave.2) the cave is very softly lit (not brightly lit) and has a very uneven floor, so walking takes attention and concentration.  Anyone with mobility problems should be very sure they can handle all the steps, uneven ground, and low lighting.3) the cave is cold and damp and the ceiling drips constantly.  The amount of dripping is directly related to the recent rain amounts received.  Since lava rock is very porous, the rain drips through the rock into the cave.4) the cave lists that it is ?restricted? access.  I don?t know what that means but I recommend finding out if you are trying to visit it on your own.  We were the first group to arrive that day and we had the cave to ourselves for about 30 min before other groups started showing up.  It made our experience even better, but it is possible that only groups with pre-purchased tickets have access?5) aside from the sheer size of the cave (again, huge for a lava tube cave), the coolest feature for us was the large lava column at the far end of the cave.  The dark hole in the ceiling, where the lava flowed into the cave and made the large column was quite impressive.We visited this cave as part of a cruise ship tour.  For those looking at things to do from a ship, there are 2 cruise ports on the island, one in the south port and one in the north port.  Where you port could determine your itinerary since various and impressive sights are available close to either town/port.  This lava tube cave is in the north-east part of the island, and is listed as   restricted   so, again, before you try to visit on your own, you might want to make sure you will be able to get into it.Jeju Island has so much to offer ? large lava tunnel caves, waterfalls, craters, mountains, cliffs, black sand beaches, incredible fresh seafood, and more but they are spread throughout the island, so it is impossible to see all of them in one area or in a short amount of time.  Also, some of the attractions are restricted, so they might require group access to enter.  We concentrated on the east end of the island during our visit and found it to be similar to Hawaii in many ways other than the temperature, which was quite a bit cooler than Hawaii during our visit at the end of March (55 deg F was our high temp).

The Manjanggul cave was worth going to see, but there really isn't much to actually see in there. As one of the longest lava tubes in the world, it's sheer size is impressive, and the information boards about the particular features of the cave are informative (albeit in strange English translations) and interesting. Once you've reached the end of the tunnel, there's not much to actually see except the lava column (largest known in the world apparently), and then you just walk back the way you came. The horrible coloured lighting makes it all look a bit tacky though, and the museum on site is geared towards younger school children. Worth popping in for a quick visit on your way to somewhere else though.

The main part of this beach is full of kids and you will need to pay to sit on the beach...(there are table services). Also, the area is restricted. You can only go to a certain area. Instead, if you go to another part, which is 10mins by walk, you can enjoy more and free to sit... This beach does not have many waves.

The main attraction is just a short walk from the car park. Tickets can be bought from a machine so you don?t have to queue. The walk takes one through lovely art structures like dolphins, boats and conch shell. There were canola flowers just before the entrance of the walkway. It has to be the right season or you will not see them. The cliffs themselves are amazing. They look like sculptures done by the hand of an artist. A row was cube like, another was like honeycomb. At the other end were corrugated pillars. Be careful not to sit on the parapets as the wind is super strong and there are large crowds, you may fall to your death if you are not careful. Hold tight to your umbrella or headwear. Best not to use any. Young children and old folks will be able to handle this attraction, the walkway is constructed well and not hard to climb up or down. It is also very short. Good view of the ocean and pines.

The Ma Park was one of the best theme parks I've ever been to.  We started off with horse riding, which was led by a friendly staff along a route for about 15 minutes.  I was surprised that he spoke English quite well!  We then headed for the go karts.  The venue was very spacious and the karts were very easy to handle.  I had a lot of fun.  After that, we watched the spectacular show which was performed by around 50 elite Mongolian riders.  Before the show started, we were able to feed the horses with carrots, sold at 1000 korean won each.  I had a blast at the Ma Park and I strongly recommend families to visit.

The lava tubes are very interesting and quite large - especially compared to those in other parts of the world. The only word of caution is to bring a raincoat and sneakers if it has been raining, as the water will trickle down through the rock and will drip considerably as you walk through. Definitely worth a stop.

The lava cave was dark and spooky but then, that is part of the fun and adventure.  I took the long walk in the dark cave, looking at the various lava formations and reading the information that was provided about them. The cave is not completely dark, subtle lighting from lanterns are provided to show us the way into the cave. Some areas are brighter than others. The floor is very uneven, wet and rocky so you have to wear sensible flat shoes.  I got to see the Turtle Rock (Lava Raft), Lava flowstones and the 7.6 meter lava column at the end of the cave which is the highlight of our subterranean adventure. I saw a couple with flashlights and wondered why I had not thought of bringing one. I will definitely bring one next time.  It was a lovely adventurous experience at the Mangangul lava tube. I recommend it to visitors to Jeju Island because it is not every day that you get to see a geological wonder like this  UNESCO World Heritage site.

The lack of literature on the Seongeup Folk village was compensated by the cheerful caretaker who gave informative, colourful and refreshing description of their well preserved ancient village.The village revealed a period of time when peace and security were prevailing, and privacy was highly respected. No one would enter the village when the two horizontal portable poles placed across the main entrance were not removed.Visitors would learn about the social structure of the days gone by, when men were out-numbered by women, when men stayed home and were pampered, while the women became the   work-horses   of the family.  Apart from becoming skilled divers, many womenfolk had to travel long distance daily, carrying heavy loads of water supply or agricultural products back to their homes.One would be surprised to learn that rudimentary recycling system was already being practiced. The caretaker must be congratulated for so cleverly circumvented the description the   grand father   stone status, which was in the shape of a male organ.  She described the statue as a god that offered protection against the demons, and promoted fertility for the living.

The Jeongbang Waterfall is one of the   Big Three   on Jeju. This one is particularly stunning as the water falls down over the cliffs to the beach below. You can get very close to the water (your camera will get wet) and get some stunning photos. There are good facilities at the top and the walk down isn't too strenuous.

The Jeju Olle Trail is an island-wide wooden path that takes you to the hills, rivers, beaches, and into the woods of Jeju. This is the perfect break from the busy urban jungle or if you want a break from the treadmill. Once on top of a hill, you will be offered a great view of the island.I took route 8 and connected to another route. I jogged some parts of the path and walked some (as some parts of the path are composed of stairs). It may be safer to walk since some parts of the path have no railing.Bonuses:There are huts and platforms that serve as resting areas. I encountered a local doing yoga in one of the huts.The river-side path has toilets and emergency rescue equipment ( life buoy, life vest, rope). Tips: Bring a camera, some sights are worth capturing; wear running shoes; and bring a phone, your GPS can be helpful in estimating your location.The path goes through or into private properties so be mindful not to trespass.

The Jeju Glass Castle was part of the itinerary of the group tour that I was part of. We spent more than an hour in the premises. We visited at daytime?I noticed that there a good number of spotlights so the Jeju Glass Castle must have a different ambience at night.I have mixed feelings about the Jeju Glass Castle.THE GOODThe Jeju Glass Castle is picturesque and very instagrammable. There are numerous displays that one can pose with. Many of the displays are quite feminine, though?very floral and colorful?girly, even. Most of the displays are outdoors including a small glass maze. Our trip was in December so it was cold but manageable. I liked the international glass displays?the Murano glass, especially because it reminded me of my aunt who had a significant number of pieces of this type of glass. THE BADFirst and foremost, I expected to see a palace or at least a castle straight out of a fairy tale. The Jeju Glass Castle is nowhere near a castle or palace. The buildings were plain and very utilitarian. The gardens were manicured but not palatial. It was more of a museum and a park, rather than a castle. Secondly, aside from signage that are in Korean or that mention the name of the place, there is nothing in the museum that shouts, ?I am in Jeju!? or ?I am in Korea!? for that matter. There is nothing in the museum that is intrinsically exclusive to the Jeju Glass Castle.Lastly, I was looking forward to try the glass comfort but the lock inside was broken and the door won?t keep closed. THE VERDICTI was able to take good photos of the displays?like I said, they were very instagrammable. Nevertheless, I do not see myself going back here just for the sake of it. It gets boring eventually, with little to do except to look at beautiful glass.

The idea is cool. I mean, yes, it's a cave formed from lava. But there's not really anything to see. It's cold and dark, and you walk for about 25 minutes to get to one end and then you turn around and walk back to the other end.The formation thing at the end is certainly the coolest part, but it wasn't worth the long taxi drive (or long walk from the bus stop - it's about 2.5km from the nearest bus stop) or the freezing wet environment. It had rained a lot on Jeju before we visited, so you definitely needed an umbrella inside the caves, or else you were going to get wet. We also really needed jackets. It was freeeeezing inside.

The hot springs have a good reputation and are very popular amongst Koreans. There is a large indoor area, separated of course for male and female, and then an outdoor area with 4 small pools the size of a hot tub and one larger lap pool which has cold spring water. Out of the 4 smaller pools 3 have hot water, 1 has cold water.The overall condition of the outdoor pools is quite shocking actually and I was surprised. In Korea almost everything is well maintained and in good condition, at these hot springs the paint coating came off at the pools, the pool furniture was old and falling apart, just very surprised to see it in this poor condition. It was busy nevertheless. There is a mix of couples and families, kids running around, people talking loudly, so it is not really serene and peaceful as a hot spring should be. The bathing experience was good, very relaxing, no doubt, but the overall experience was mediocre.

The history facts in this memorial hall recalled me of the one in Oswiecim, Poland... This memorial hall will help you to understand Jeju people's local history. Whenever I visit war related museum or places, we should stop fighting for nothing but losing the precious lives. I was even cried when I read 2 young men who could not enter the military school due to the wrong record of this tragic incident. I read all of explanation in Korean and English. I skipped some clips but I tried to watch 2 or 3 min's clips. Very well prepared in English and Korean. One of best museum. It is FREE. Only I concerned, there is no chairs to take a rest from time to time. And there was a decent with 15ish people, her voice was too much loud to make big echo in the hall area! I think they have to pay attention with other visitors who look into all scripts! I was a bit mad because she was too passionate to proceed her job. I think you do not need a docent because all of exhibits are perfectly translated in English. There are many heart breaking stories, but when I entered into the cave Darangshi(?), I could keep saying   oh my god..   I feel very sorry for all deceased, and their family members who survived at the same time witnesses. I strongly recommend this museum if you are interested local history, and history buff. It is a must. In fact, there is no restaurant, there is a coffee shop only. If you rent a car, within 10 min's drive, there are some. The bus #343, or #344 go to 4.3 Peace Park. From this park, Jeju Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest is 5 min's drive away, and 20 min's walk on foot. This Forest is wonderful. I recommend to combine these 2 places to visit at once. History and Nature are very good combination! The last stop of 343 &344 is this forest.

The hiking trail is well designed and fellow hikers are courteous. There are multiple trails with varying levels of difficulty. Some parts are fairly steep. Stairs are installed in most parts of the trail that we climbed on, though I am not sure if this is the case with all trails. The midway station includes food and water facilities. There are no garbage cans anywhere on the trail, nor indeed even at the entrance to the trail. Make sure you do not bring too many things that require disposal when you climb.

The hike was awesome. Very scenic and nature at its best. There are a few different routes to the top. ( summit is out of bounds though) At the top, you can find a shelter with washroom and a small shop selling cup noodles. We drove there, so had to take the same route down. There are taxis waiting at the start points when we finished our walk(around noon time)

The hike up Hallasan is fairly easy though a good portion of the hike is on rocky/basalt boulders.  There are long sections of boardwalks especially near the summit where there are a fair number of stairs.  Most of the trail is well shaded except for the last kilometer or so.  There are locations to purchase food and drinks along the way.  I saw families with young kids as young as six hiking thee trail.  It can get dairly crowded at times, but if you are fast people will kindly let you buy.  If you are an experiencex trail runner its a fun and slightlytechnical run.  Time up is about two and a half to three and a half hours, while time down is one and a quarter to two and a half hours depending on ability.  At the summit you will see a large crater.  Unfortunately you are not allowed to circumnavigate the crater.  Fun hike overall though a bit crowded.

The Hallasan National Park, South Korea?s tallest mountain, is a place that is definitely worth visiting on a trip Jejudo. There are 5 trails up the Halla Mountain, but only two can lead you to the summit where the Crater Lake is. Some sections are quite steep and takes some effort and time but the view at the top is definitely worthwhile. Start the climb as early in the day as possible to avoid crowds as well as to ensure that you have plenty of time to hike up and down the mountain. The hike has to be done in one go since there are no overnight shelters available. The best descending route is the Yeongshil trail, which is the most scenic of the 5 routes. The view is just MAGNIFICENT and it is a relatively easy descent. On a clear day you could see right down to Seogwipo on your way down. You?ll also be able to see the numerous parasitic cones located around Hallasan. The terrain changes as the altitude changes and it can get chilly at the top even on a summer day. So dress in layers accordingly. Make sure to check the weather in advance and set out on a sunny day since it will be very difficult to climb in rainy or foggy weather. You will not be allowed to summit anyway under such weather conditions (or if you arrive late). There are buses which bring you to the trailheads from both Jeju city and Seogwipo. So it?s not hard to reach by public transport.
The Glass Castle offers many interesting pieces of art for one to view, I recommend this destination to anyone visiting Jeju.

The gardens were reasonably well tended and we liked the indoor themed zones spreading out in a cartwheel from the main atrium. Outside there are a series of larger themed gardens. Some better than others, but it is a South Korean take on these different countries garden styles. For example the fountains in the Italianate garden were quite impressive and it was good to stroll in the sunshine. We did like the many sculptures placed within the various indoor spaces and this has lifted our score from 'average' to 'very good'.

The garden is huge and beautiful. Unfortunately, it was a rainy day when we visited the garden. Different variety of plants from different part of the world are collected in a dome. A full tour throughout the dome takes around 90 minutes. There is also an observatory above the dome for people to overlook the Jungmun Tourism Complex. Though the garden is huge, I found most of the plants are not native to Korea. It is a pity that foreign tourists can not know more native plants? by visiting this garden.

The floor is uneven and the lighting is dim, not for those with walking issues. Nice place to see the strange wall formation due to lava. Only 1 km and mostly even.  The tourists can be a bit noisy, hope the bats in the other parts are not too disturbed

The filming location of a period Korean drama series, this place is reputed a well preserved village with part of the original city walls, official houses and commoners houses still intact. Several families still live here to maintain the place. Worth the trip if you are into this kind of things.

The experience is new and the music is nice. However, I go bored after some time because I am not a art person and do not quite grasp what the artists are trying to express. Driving through narrow road to get there.

The entrance fee is very expensive. From 10,000 won now increased to 11,000 won. It's not really worth it to visit during early spring as most trees and flowers are not in full bloom yet. Some parts are closed and only during certain months so suggest to visit when the trees and flowers are in full bloom. Hyeopjae Beach is nearby, nice to visit.

The entrance fee is 11000 won . Worth a visit if you are in the vicinity . I particularly like the salmon Swimming upstream , the glass flower garden and the Pinocchio like town in the dark room. The glass forest panel is also unique . This place will look fantastic if visited at night.

The drive there was pleasant as you passed through many scenic places. Saw some homes with unique design.As we were at the start of Mysterious Road, our taxi driver switch off the engine and let the car just roll ?up the road?. Was wondering how could this happen!!! We witness some other vehicles doing the same. Our taxi driver took a bottle of waterAnd pour it in the middle of the road, the water didn?t flow backward. A group of Chinese tourist ,were doing the same thing, the guide say it?s a scam.  But the truth is ?Optic Illusion ?Nice backdrop of mount hallasan

The dragon head rock is in North part of Jeju, close to the airport. It is a rock that looks like a dragon head on the coast. The Seogwipo coast line like the Jusanjeolli Cliff or the Odelgae Rock are much more interesting than this. However, if you do not have time to visit the Jungmun/Seogwipo area, this is an alternative to see the rocky coastline. The sunset here is nice, but the place is packed with tourists fighting to get photos, so it's not all that romantic. I think a beach sunset at a more remote beach on the West side would be nicer and a calmer experience.
the destination is built by legend about dragon who fall from the earth, as tourist object not much to see. it's nature rock, beach and on autum the weather is nice. no need much time

The day I visited Jusangjeolli Cliff, the place was crowded with group tours particularly students on education trip, so had to virtually jostle for a good spot to get some views of the cliffs, which were really a classic example of Mother Natures numerous works bringing us all her beauty.

The coral sand beach was really nice! Not much to see or do beyond that, and another two beaches - one very crowded white sand beach, and another black sand beach that nobody seemed to care about other than for a walk. The reviews make it seem like it's some kind of paradise, we just found it crowded, full of concrete and terrain that is parted for construction, not much vegetation. There are a few lighthouses and it looks like people could venture out on the rocks by the beach if they felt like it. What saved our trip was a little place called Chocolate Castle by the Sea, a burger restaurant that had amazing burgers and a great homey feel inside. We biked the whole island in 3 hours, with stops.

The collection of teddy bears is good and very nicely organized according to themes. I especially loved the collections of very old teddy bears and the stories behind them and their owners that really touched a soft spot in my heart. There were also very vintage Winnie the Pooh bears that were really an eye-opener, as well as bears wearing traditional korean costumes depicting scenes of ancient korean life that I liked. The outdoors section of the exhibits were however not very impressive and when my friend and I visited the museum in June, the museum was very warm indoors. We were sweating profusely as we looked at the exhibits and in fact found it a joy to go outdoors into the sun, which turned out to be cooler. This prevented me from giving the attraction a four star rating. However, the collection is really a must-see for teddy bear lovers and it will undoubtedly be a more enjoyable place to visit in other months of the year.

The climb up to the crater of this old volcanic cone is not for the faint of heart, but it is worth it!  At the top you get a 360 degree view of the coast, along with the bragging rights for the climb.  Beware, though of the summertime crowds.  I climbed on a weekend in November and it still felt a bit on the crowded side.  The stairs are in good shape and sturdy, as are the lower, ramped sections.

The climb to the top is tough, but totally worth it as the view from top is breathtaking. You will continue to enjoy the view from different angles as you descending through the clearly demarcated paths.  A huge and beautiful patch of grass awaits you at the bottom of the hill as you recover from the climb (so don't waste too much time below before you even start climbing.  There are a lot of drivers of tour bus that rest at the bottom of the hill and will even offer their assistance to take photographs for you. I totally enjoyed this place.

The Cheonjeyeon Falls was a memorable last stop of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour. The size of the entire park the falls are situated in is generally small, but it's loaded with so many sights to see. In the entrance, you're immediately greeted with a beautiful pagoda and lush well-kept gardens. There's also a wishing fountain called the Fountain of Five Blessings that's worthy of your participation as the coins tossed inside the fountain are donated to Korea's underprivileged. Entering the site, one has to cross an intricately beautiful bridge which is elegant and regal in its own right. After that, the trek to the falls; sites begins. The entire trek is paved with concrete steps which make it more convenient and safer for visitors, especially as the trek requires ascend and decline quite a lot. Although, be prepared for a light workout as the number of steps do add up if you complete the entire trek (there are quick detours to the exit for those who don't wish to complete the entire trek or those grappling with a fear of heights).Shoutout to our amazing tour guide from Yeha Bus Tour for going the extra mile in making our entire tour enjoyable!

The cave is very big, stairs at the entrance is quite steep, you might be a little bit out of breath here, but once inside it is manageable. The cave is spacious and well maintained, there is clear line for people to walk, there isn't much to see, after walking around 1km you will reach the end of the accessible part of the cave, people take pictures here and then walk back to the entrance.  It is a great place to explore a cave for the first time, my children loved it here. The temperature drop inside the cave, so bring warm jacket

The cave is a mysterious wonder that Mother Earth presented to us. This cave is a long lava tube in which once lava flowed many years ago. You could guessed the history and patterns of how lava had flowed from the lines, colors and patterns on the wall of the cave. If only the whole 4km could have been opened to public instead of just the 1km. I believe that they are more wonders along the rest of the tube. I would spend the whole day here if I could.

The bus driver has completely stopped the engine at the starting point of Jeju Mysterious road and once he release the break the bus moves eventhough it is an upward slope...Why? The answer we got from the tour guide is that, it is an optical illusion - that actually it is a downward slope. Well it doesnt look like that at the time and even now I couldnt believe it is a downward instead of an upward slope - believe it or not!!

The bridge itself is a landmark of Seogwipo, which leads to a small island that offers a short 20-25 mins walk. Not the most exotic part of the city, but nice indeed. My favourite place here however are rocks on the edge of the island, which is off the track, but if you are careful while walking out to the rocks (they are pretty flat and not dangerous at all), it is the best place to relax and enjoy the sea and view.

The Botanical gardens is set up in to different gardens and a large doom/ indoor area set up into zones. The plants on show were very nice but I have seen a lot better. This could be because of the South Korea climate. Look at the surface and it's well kept then you notice dirty water in the ponds. What I did enjoy was watching some of the workers weed some of the areas they are so methodical. As we were part of a day tour this was just one of our many stops and our time was limited. Perhaps I would have enjoyed it more if I didn't have such a tight schedule. I would rate this attraction as Good but there isn't a good rating and average would do it a disjustice. I thought the entrance fee to be very high considering the country it's in. You don't pay much more to go in Kew Gardens, London's Botanical garden that can actually take you days to get round.

The best time to go is early in the morning, to see the sun rise. I had gone a little after the sunrise and many people were already on their way down. The views are spectacular and the way up is very safe, and good for all ages. This was probably the most memorable part of Jeju Island.
the best theater ever!!!!...it's full with fun, funny, comical, martial art, music, etc.....just like they said, it a combination of every little thing that u like...suitable for the whole family!!!

The best parts about this tour were the walk from the main road where you can admire the cherry blossom on both sides of the road and the newly opened Angel-In-Us coffee house. If not for the springtime cherry blossoms, there doesn't seem to be much else to see.

The best part of this is all the nature surrounding you while on the train (which takes you everywhere) , the river, just the pretty landscape. I'm a teen and I definitely wouldn't go there again, it was boring for me except for the nice pictures of the landscape tbh. There's a windmill, a big pirate ship, picnic side. If you have kids they are gonna love it, trust me. I went with other families with kids and they completely enjoyed it. If you want to have a picnic, I suggest this place also cause even when it's crowded the picnic side is literally huge so you have all the space you need anyway.
The best part of my entire trip, this attraction was so beautiful, calming, and overrall an amazing site. The view was amazing, and it wasn't overly crowded.

The beach itself could do with some TLC from the council.   There is a lot of debris which washes up daily onto the beach and along the coastal walk. Most of it travels in from China and for the most part seems to be from fishing boats.  The coastal walk is good, good paths and I have seen everything from flying fish, the women Abalone divers, wild cats, cute puppies to feed and dogs kept on short leads and some I'd say rarely fed (I feed them too). The selfie people are many along this walk it's quite comical to watch them all.

The area of the beach is nice but the sandy part and the open water space is soooo small... You cannot even go for a swim here. The water was dirty and full of water plants. I honestly thinking every beach in Europe is way more attractive than this. Italy, Greece, Croatia....Have they actually seen clear azure waters?! If this is jejus prettiest beach then im really sorry for koreans

The actual Hyeopjae beach, at the north end of town can get very crowded, but is close to the cafes on the main street. Personally we prefer the Geunmung beach end which is to the south, just past the Hallim park entrance.Both beaches are stunning with turquoise water and great views out to the island. The beaches shelve very gently which makes them great for kids. Geunmung particularly is awesome for the kids as it has little bays and rock pools too.

Thanks to Korea Tourism Organization (KTO) and Jeju Olle walking Festival,  we got an opportunity to participate in the Jeju Olle Walking festival 2020 despite there was a limitation on the number of the participant due to spread of Covid-19. This year, the festival is held in a new and unique way with the slogan ?Walk Apart, Finish Together?. All participants have to register online in advance; only up to 15 participants accepted for each of 23 routes for 23 days. Also, all the participants were given Clean Kit set that includes face masks, sanitizers, and others needed for personal hygiene.Since we had just one day to participate in the walking festival, Route 10 was chosen for our team. Route 10 start from Hwasun Golden sand beach, then passes through major touristic attractions Sanbangsan Mountain, Yongmeori Coast, Songaksan Mountain, Altteureu Airfield, Victims Memorials, and finally Hamo beach which is close to the endpoint. The total distance is 15.6 km with a maximum elevation of around 60 m.The walking experience in this route was amazing. We pass various landscapes, from beaches to forest, coastal walk to mountain hiking, and finally to radish and potato farms at Altteureu Airfield site. The various volcanic and sedimentary rock structures at Sanbangsan Mountain foothills and Yongmeori Coast were amazingly gorgeous. Walking along the perimeter of volcanic mountain Songaksan was a unique experience. The cliffs of the mountain close to sea were spectacular and walking along the top of those cliffs was just amusing. This type of walking, I think, gives the opportunity to explore the hidden natural beauty of Jeju Island and its traditional cultures which we could miss if visited by other means. Thus, the Jeju Olle Trails is highly recommended for those who love hiking or walking and want to explore hidden natural beauties while enjoying local customs and local foods. I, personally, wish to complete all the Olle walking trails and get the certificate of completion from the organizer.

thank you for the visit. well , first of all we are so afraid of you were not so feel good at the teddy bear museum. however our museum consist of two main theme galleries. the history and the art.  and also there are extra gallery, Elvis concert theater and out door garden. we will take an effort to present visitor more exciting display and exhibition . thank you again and have a good day ^^
Teddy Bears dressed up in art and history, what's not to love? Museum isn't big, exhibition are on two levels. Elvis show is entertaining.

Teddy Bear Museum in Jeju opened in 2001 and boasts for owning the largest collection of teddy bears.  What differentiates this museum from the rest is that Korea's history was told using the bears.  It was cute and a not so serious approach that would cater to the children.The museum consists of 2 Exhibition halls namely the hall of history and the hall of art.  This museum serves as the home for as many as 1,500 bears that includes the luxurious Louis Vuitton bear.

Taxi took us here as part of a few hours tour.  It's a pretty waterfall, but I thought Cheonjiyeon Falls was more impressive with 3 layers so if you are nearby, it's worth going, however, if you only have time to go to one, I'd choose the latter :).  Both have small entrance fees per person.

TAKE NOTE: If you are not healthy and dont usually do cardio, the step up will be absolute hell for you. The only way you can circumvent the hellish experience is if you wake up extra early and take your own sweet time to traverse to the top.We woke up at 6am after checking sunrise at 7:20am, and was living in a hotel 2 minutes away. As we want to experience the whole sunrise, we rush up the rising path. Big mistake. By the time we're halfway up, I had visions of my 42km route march in 1.5 days during my army stint, and had to take frequent rest stops on the way up.Once you reach the top, you'll see nothing but the sea in front of you and while you're tired, you're also excited to witness the sunrise.Which you COULD... if it was a cloudless morning. The clouds will ruin your day. We didn't get to see anything in the end, as it was so cloudy and drizzling a bit, but after staying for an hour after sunrise, we did get to see a few peeks of sunrays.It only cost 2000 won so well worth the price, but definitely check the weather forecast first. It feels terrible to have almost burst your heart only to see nothing but clouds. I do imagine the sunrise is heavenly if you actually get to see it though.

Surprisingly, despite standing tall at 1950m, Hallasan was a relatively easier climb than other mountains such as Seoraksan, Bukhansan and Dobongsan, the trio that busted my thighs and made me swear off hiking for months. Youngsil trail was indeed picturesque, with small streams, autumn foliage and sweeping visages of the sloping hills and multiple arboretums that dot the island. The trail was mainly covered with boardwalks to protect the soil from human footsteps. Some parts were difficult to maneuver due to the uneven volcanic rocks so do wear proper hiking boots (the only investment I made for hiking).Visit my travel blog for more information and pictures on Jejuhttps://honjatravel.wordpress.com/2015/07/24/top-5-favourite-places-in-jeju/

Sunrise was at 5:58AM April 19th, 2018. We woke up ans started walking to the crater at 5:15 AM and had ample time to get up and witness what may be the only Unesco protected sunrise. We walked from the Co-op City Hotel and took about 10-15 minutes to get to the start of the path. It took another 20 minutes to climb to the lip of the crater. It can be challenging for some  but is is fine for anyone of average active health.Breathtaking views.

Sunrise Peak is the nickname - I was sadly not able to see the sunrise because the weather, but it was still a beautiful lookout. The hike isn't too bad - I did have to catch my breath a few times because some parts are steep, but it was worth it. The path is lit, so you don't need a flashlight. Get there early because the good seats will be taken!The ferry to Udo Island is also close to here. You can find a path outside the town that leads to the ferry terminal. The path also provides great picture taking for Seongsan.

Sunrise peak in English, this volcanic cone is 182 metres high. That works out to about 25 stories which is roughly how high you have to climb to get there.And to get there early enough to get a good position, you need to get up pretty early. We woke at 4am for a 4.30 start (this after a 60km bike ride the day before and another 60 to come on the day. We went up rather more briskly than we had planned (exuberance?) and were one of the first to arrive.First, let me acknowledge the impressive steps, in stone and wood, that have been built to help people get to the top (and the separate staircase that leads you down). Kudos to the engineers and builders. They even thought of rest stops which also work well as photo opportunity spots.The amphitheater-style seats at the top are well-thought out too and provide a good view.Sunrise was scheduled for about 5.30 and a fair crowd had gathered by then.Unfortunately, the sky was overcast and we could only glimpse the sun as it occasionally peeped through the clouds. But it was spectacular nonetheless.There was no admission charge as we were up and down before the ticket booth opened at 7am.It is still worthwhile visiting even if you don't want to watch the sunrise.

Suggest to start early, before 7am. We started at 7am, and managed to reach the summit before 1pm, but had to descend before 1.30pm. Took a total of 10 hours, up and down. If I can do the hike, anybody else can too, for a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Remember to do proper warm-up before starting and bring along enough water to hydrate yourself. Proper hiking shoes are important and hiking sticks are definitely helpful.

Such a beautiful place where I experienced peace of mind and heart. Reading how Bunjae and our lives are quite parallel really made me think twice about nature and how we should cherish it as if it was our own lives. The quote that I will keep with me forever is   Potted plants wither when their roots are not trimmed, and people age when they do not change their ways of thinking  . Thank you for providing a space for people to learn and reflect on life amongst nature. God bless.

Stop by this place right after visiting Manjang Cave. Since we were really walking was a good pit stop to grab some Korean snack.The main attraction is of course the maze itself. It look rather simple and there were a lot of family with young kids about so being a bunch of young adult we thought that this would literally be a walk in the park.We grab a map and the self appointed maze expert started to lead the way through the maze. Took some picture and had real fun arguing over the route with our   expert  . The turns can be deceiving and hidden but our   expert   was so confident that nothing could stop, as he was so convince we were reaching the end. Just as we were the last turn we we were anticipating a finish line only to discover that we were back at the starting point! At that point it become a race who could exit the maze faster. It was so much fun racing among each other and when we ended up split from the   expert  . It was really funny trying to contain our giggle when we found a breakthrough route so others would not realize our current position. All in all it was great fun with a good picture session when you reach the end on an elevated platform. Probably not suitable for individual traveler, elders and traveler looking for something more serene. For family with young kids and group of traveling friend this can be really fun. The appeal comes from the traveling group itself. My experience with the maze   expert   still makes good conversation on how not to solve a problemVisited February 2012

Staying in Seogwipo, I was advised to take bus 780, with the first bus leaving about 6:30am or 7am & getting to Seongpanak around 7:30 or 8am. I thought about taking a taxi to get there earlier, but I found later in the day it wasn't necessary. I believe it's the same bus from Jeju City.There's a small carpark at the entrance and a little store with a few drinks and snacks on sale. Apart from the lunch hut near the summit (which only offered noodles with hot water & bottles of cold water), this was the only place to buy anything. So carry some food and water with you, enough to last 4 hours or so.It's a fairly pleasant walk. Most of the time you will be walking on ground or planks of wood, and at times there will be nothing but big rocks, although most people were walking. I think I was the only person with hiking boots.Yes it can be very steep at times but is by no means difficult, nothing more than a series of steps. Just take lots of rest breaks and you'll be fine. It should take anywhere from 2.5 to 3 hours to reach the cut-off mark (see next paragraph) then another 1 hour to the top, so as long as you leave before 9am or 10am it should be alright.Coming down can take anywhere from 2.5 to 3.5 hours in total.I thought the cut-off point was strange, having a man in an office stopping people trying to reach the summit after 1pm, especially when the sun doesn't go down until about 7pm. I would've thought that was plenty of time to get up and back. That's just Korea and their over-sensitive rules...Not a lot of scenery along the way, but it's nice to enjoy being surrounded by trees for most of the way. For the most part it will be quiet, although some of the locals spoke loudly or even had their phones out playing music which I thought was weird.A lot of Koreans seem to be on a mission to get it done as quickly as possible, and they certainly have the stamina to do it, so keep in mind at times you may have to deal with people almost pushing you aside to get past.The view from the top is worth the hike. You'll be extremely lucky to see the bottom (climb Seongnam if you want a nice view), but you're here to see the crater lake, which is quite lovely to see when the cloud clears.

Spent more time looking at the ground......., watching out for puddle of water than looking at the cave/tunnel. Do be careful if going with elderly and children as some parts are quite difficult to walk . It's quite dim and chilly inside. Nothing much to see....

Spent an hour exploring the cave first thing in the morning - very beautiful, unique and wasn't crowded. It started to get very crowded on the way out since the tour buses started arriving making walking a little difficult because it's dark and the path is uneven. Arrived in Jeju by cruise ship and this was the first stop of our 8 hour private taxi tour which I highly recommend. Saw the lava tube as well as 5 other attractions (Sunrise Peak, Seongup Folk Village, Haenyo Museum, and Jeongbang Waterfall). Our driver Mr. Kim Choong Kun (nytaxi5445@hanmail.net) was very pleasant, patient, spoke English, informative, and even took pictures of us.

Sorry, guys if i am a bit skeptical for this kind of attraction.  For me, and perhaps for some others, it is just an optical illusion.  No surprise on that....lol.I watched closely the power lines running alongside the street and the top of the trees alignment you might be able to see that the street is actually going down and not up, giving an impression that the bottle is rolling upwards....  As the old saying states,   the law of gravity still applies everywhere on earth  .  It was quite crowded when i was there, and needed to be a bit careful when people were trying to walk backwards whilst buses and cars were trying to pass by on that narrow street.  There are few food stalls as well.

Someone told me Udo is beautiful, so it's in my wish list when I visit Jejudo. I went there on Saturday (7.5.2016). At the harbour, there are many different type of transportation vehicles for rent to travel Udo, so, basically the narrow road at Udo is full of vehicles, no matter is two wheel, three wheel or four wheel. I did the Olle trail 1.1, travel on foot, it was frustrated and irritating when need to walk together with so many types of vehicles, noisy and crowded. But, luckily the trail does divert some part of the trekking route which is away from the vehicle road, hiking up to the light house hill and also farm house and farming area.

some people say this road again the earth gravitation, but some said it's cause the magnet field is big at that area. if see with eyes the street look uphill but the car stop and  engine stop can forward till some point.

So, one might think that this is a great place to see artifacts or historic pieces, but as far as we saw, everything was a replica. To include the replica lava tube entrances. Sigh. They couldn't even be bothered to completely thatch a straw hut- they had concrete roofs with thatch done at the top and edges. They do have quite the array of carefully placed rocks and replica stone statues, but seeing as how none of it was real (the whole thing was built on the site of a landfill) there are more real things to go do on Jeju. The price is cheap. Spend it looking at the columnar basalt on the beach. At least that is real.

So I read a review that the hike up Hallasan was not very difficult so I thought I could do it in my Asics running shoes...well, I don't recommend that you do the hike up Hallasan without proper hiking gear.  Pack lots of water and food so that you can replenish yourself on the long hike up.  We went in early October and it was warm so dressing in layers was a godsend.  The route we took was to take Seongpanak up to the summit and then take Gwaneumsa trail down.  Taking Seongpanak to the summit took approximately 4.5 hours with 1 lunch break at the 3rd resting place before the summit. The resting place had washrooms and also a snack bar.  I saw people with cup ramen etc. Be prepared for the washrooms to be stinky.  It's the nature friendly kind.  The last stretch up to the summit on the Seongpanak trail is quite steep and some parts very rocky.  But the view makes up for it all!  Instead of hiking down the same trail, we came down the Gwaneumsa trail and wow, the views were breathtaking.  There were times when I had to stop and just take in the view just a bit longer because it was so beautiful.  T he Gwaneumsa trail doesn't have as many resting places so use the washroom when you can.  It took us a total of 9.5 hours to hike up and down Hallasan and I would do it again the next time I am in Jejudo Island!!

So happy we took the time to make the climb.  It's a lot of stairs to the top, so I would suggest you take along some water, and possibly some snacks, so you can take a rest part way up.There is one way up, and another down, which keeps things moving quickly.

smaller than what i thought. But a lot of bear with different characters inside. For a hurry visitor, you would just need no longer than 1 hour to finish all part of the museum. The elvis bear show was nice but quite short and not really worth to see, thats why it is free.

Slapstick, cheesy humour so just relax into it and join in the fun of the show. It's entertaining as the predictable story unfolds - beware, there is a little bit of audience participation - just go with it! The performers are professional and their drumming is excellent. The story is told with very few words but is very easy to follow. There are strobe lights at one point. The theatre is out in the middle of nowhere so eat before going or book into the NANTA hotel next door to eat. The planetarium is across the road so you could go to an early NANTA performance the on to do some star gazing.

Skip this and head for Dodubong Peak, especially if you're on the Jeju Golden Bus day tour. This place is unremarkable and is honestly one of the dirtiest parts of the area; I attempted to have my photo taken and a rat scurried out from between the rocks. If you walk up the road (away from the site) about a half mile, maybe less, the photo ops are much nicer. The area near Dodubong Peak is also nicer and you can see great views of of Jeju from the summit.

Should go and visit this museum as it forms part of the culture of Korea especially the women divers of this island is very brave to dive into the sea for food. In the past, they wore normal hand made diving clothes and dive in to get food. They did the same thing when it is winter time and imagine the water is freezing cold. Right now, they wear normal diving suits but the tradition still lives on.
Should be rather pretty when all leaves turned brown and golden. However, colors had just started to change slowly at the end of Oct.

Seongsan Ilchulbong, or Sunrise Peak, gives you a sweeping view of Seogwipo City so don't forget to stop at different points to witness this. I love it being a tuff cone and all (even if I'm not that into geology). It's also a UNESCO World Heritage site.They say it's best to climb to the peak during sunrise (hence, the name). But it rained at dawn when I was there, so I just started out around 10 AM. The occasional drizzle did not dampen my experience. Wherever you look you'll see, breathe, and smell nature. :D There are stairs for climbing. It's a short trail. The place can become crowded, but there's a place for everyone. Take a side trip to the beach area at the bottom. The haenyeo, or Jeju women divers, perform there in the afternoon.

Seongsan Ilchulbong provides a great view of the city, and ocean especially if you reach the peak.It's 180m up, and steep, so if you don't have the right condition it may be hard for you to climb up.The place is also famous for the women divers performance. It starts at 1:30pm and 3:00pm if I am not mistaken.There are also nearby shops in the area you won't get hungry or thirsty.If you collect city Starbucks mugs, there's a Starbucks nearby that offer Jeju mugs, cups and tumblers.

Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak is the most eastern part of Jeju Island and has the same terrain as Punchball. When you stand at Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak, you can see the beautiful sea and clear sky endlessly, and when you stand at Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak with a cool breeze, you feel good. Also, there are many tourist attractions nearby, so it is convenient to move around. In addition, there are many restaurants that cook braised kingtail fish and roast caught in Jeju, and there are many unique and delicious restaurants around. I recommend that you visit Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak with your family at least once.

Seongsan Ilchulbong or sunrise peak is one of the most visited spots in Jeju. We took a public bus here from port after visiting Udo Island. Lucky it is near the port as it was already late afternoon when we reached here.  The parking lot was crowded with tour coaches and and you could see the crowd climbing up and down the peak.
