review: My family and I visited this UNESCO World Heritage and South Korea National Monument cave on a late afternoon for 2 hours. There were not many visitors and we didn?t find any tour buses when we reached here.   Getting there & fees: Manjanggul Cave is located in the north western part of Jeju-do. To get (drive) to Manjanggul Cave, key in GPS coordinate 7834818. There is no parking fee at the huge car park. Entrance fee is 2,000 won for adults and 1,000 won for teenagers and children.Manjanggul Cave Museum: Upon climbing up the stairs from the car park, you will reach the Museum and a cafeteria/restaurant on its right. You could go in and have a look at the interesting exhibits, including how the Manjanggul Cave was formed from the volcanic activities.Manjanggul Cave: To get to the underground Cave, we followed the sign-posts ? it?s within 5 minutes? walk from the Manjanggul Cave Museum. Trek the entire 1 km stretch that?s opened to public and you will end with a colourful lit lava column - created from the dripping of lava from a hole in the ceiling ? which at about 8 meters high, is the tallest lava column on Earth. Nevertheless, there are a few things you have to take note while you are in the Cave:(1) The entrance to the Manjanggul Cave is also the exit ? there?s no exit at the end of the 1 km trail, which means you are walking 2 km return (2) Make sure you bring and wear a jacket or sweater with you because it?s freezing cold and chilly inside the cave. (3) Wear a cap or the jacket or sweater can be waterproof because you get water ocassioanlly dripping from the cave top onto you (4) The surface (floor) of the Cave is full of solidified lava flow terrain (i.e. extremely uneven surface) and water puddles, so you have to wear a pair of good walking shoes and walk carefully. Hold on to the railings of the stairs.(5) You probably don?t need a torchlight because the Cave is illuminated just enough by ground lightings. Some parts of the cave even have colourful lights shining at the dome shaped ceiling (cupola) (6) If you would like to take photographs inside the cave, you would need a tripod and switch to manual mode for long exposure (I used 4 seconds to 10 seconds exposure on my digital SLR).   There are displays at certain parts of the cave in English explaining the geology of the cave and the formation of the interesting structures (e.g. stalactites). In particular, there?s one structure ? ?Stone Turtle? ? in which the shape looks like Jeju-do Island, and which you could reach in about 30 minutes of one-way walking as it?s about 400m from the entrance. Along the Manjanggul Cave wall, we saw varied patterns of lava flow lines, some are straight while some are wavy. Really interesting! I have been to over 10 limestone caves around the world, but this is my first visit in a lava tunnel cave or lava tube cave (and Asia?s longest lava tube cave for that matter). You have to experience being transported to another world in this ?out of this world? cave for yourself ? don?t miss it!

My family and I visited this attraction on a sunny Monday mid-afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli ?? Jeongbang Falls ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Falls itinerary. ?Oedolgae? means ?Lonely Rock?. Oedolgae Rock has its origin from a volcanic eruption.Getting there & fees:  The GPS coordinate (code) for Oedolgae is 7328027.We parked our car under the trees at the large car park. Entry to the attraction is free and the only fee we paid was 1000 won to the parking attendant.The Rock/Attraction: We looked for a blue signboard with a picture of Odedolgae Rock and an arrow pointing left saying ?250m?. It?s then an easy walk of steps and path that?s abundantly shaded by the trees. So you don?t need an umbrella or a cap. After 5 minutes, we came to a large viewing platform from which this amazing and unusual 20-metre high solitary grey basalt pillar rock that juts out from the sea with a few trees growing at its top can be seen. From a certain angle, the Rock looks like a woman?s face with little hair.Compared to another 20-metre lone-standing limestone rock, Ko Tapu, at Thailand?s James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan), I find the Oedolgae rock slightly more interesting in terms of geographical origin and features. You could better appreciate the other face of this Rock as well as getting to a large poster of the popular Korean TV drama ?Dae Jang Geum? (Jewel in the Palace) by walking further onto another path, which we didn?t venture.  Despite the Oedolgae?s attractiveness and beauty as well as free admission, somehow I didn?t see busloads of tourists here. This means the attraction is not crowded. Maybe the thinking is they could spend their time at other tourist attractions where there are more things to see rather than just a solidary rock.  Nevertheless, for me, I recommend a visit to this amazing rock as part of the southern Jeju itinerary. It only takes up at most 1.5 hours.

My family and I spent about 45 minutes at this attraction on an early Monday afternoon, as our first stop of a Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliffs ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary. It is designated a Natural Monument and is part of the Global Geopark Network. Getting there & fees: When I keyed in GPS code of 7351000 and 7381521, it brought us confusingly to the Convention Centre and the car park of the Seaes Resort respectively. Thanks to the helpful staff of the Seaes resort, we followed the advice and drove past the Convention Centre and then looked out for a signage that indicated taking a right turn to a road that leads to the destination. Once there, we parked the car in the car park which charged a parking fee pf 1000 won. The entrance fee is 2000 won for adults & 1000 won for teenagers (youth) and children, and we used one of the lockers for free to keep our stuff.The Cliffs/Attraction: After paying the entrance fees, we walked past figurines of dolphins and a huge rock surrounded by the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac. We then took the pathway of wooden platform steps that brought us to the bird-eye view of the beautiful blue sea and the rocky cliffs containing the awesome columnar joints that are typically at the base of the cliff. The platform only showcases a section of the 2 km stretch of these rocky cliffs. Along the platform, there is a display in English and Korean that educate you about the origin of the rocks. It would be good if another display would be able to pictorially illustrate the geography and formation. According to the information, the columnar joints were formed from the lava flows from the Nokhajiak scoria cone from 140,000 to 250,000 years ago. During cooling of the molten lava, contraction occurred and split the basaltic rocks into polygonal columns. We saw mainly tetragonal (4 sided), pentagonal (5-sided) and hexagonal (6-sided) columns. Because the origin of the columnar joints and rocks is volcanic, these are black. Throughout the time, I stood there simply awestruck by what I saw ? it?s like a divine being had creatively sculptured these columnar joints to perfection. And why only at this 2km stretch and not at other coastal areas in Jeju since the volcanic molten lava flowed everywhere?  It?s a pity the waves that crashed onto the joints and rocks were not huge; otherwise I think it would be an even more awesome sight. There are several pointers to take note:(1) You could appreciate this attraction in less than 1 hour (including photo and selfie-taking)(2) As the attraction is outdoors, be prepared for what the weather will throw at you. Carry an umbrella or wear a cap or sunglasses or put on sunscreen on a sunny day(3) To see these rocks better, I suggest bringing along a pair of binoculars or zooming closer using your camera telephoto lens or your handphone(4) Take plenty of photographs but do not climb over or lean over too much the platform ?railings?We ranked Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff as one of the top 3 attractions in Jeju. For sure, this Nature?s awesome masterpiece is not to be missed!

My family and I liked this waterfall simply because of the coolness that sweeps away the afternoon heat. We visited this attraction on a Monday late afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary.Getting there & fees: The GPS coordinate/code for Jeongbang Waterfall is 7331530. It is located on the south central part of Jeju (Seogwipo). We parked our car for free at the car park. Entrance fee to the Waterfall is 1000 won for adults and 500 won for teenagers and children. The Waterfall/Attraction: Because the waterfall is so close to the sea, it gives the impression that the fresh water falls directly into the sea. The water actually falls 23 metres into a plunge-pool in a sheltered cove comprising of mainly black lava rocks and then flows to the sea. After the ticket booth, an approximately 5 minutes? descent on the sturdy steps of the wooden stairway took us to the bottom but still quite a distance from the waterfall. Even then, we were already ?bathed? by the cool water mist from the impact of the waterfall plunging onto the pond. We had to step on the rocks and boulders to get nearer to the base of the waterfall, and this was where we had to be very careful, very slow, very nimble and very sure-footed in negotiating the uneven rocks or boulders of different sizes and shapes as well as the slippery surface of the wet rocks. This is also where you have to wear good walking shoes and I don?t recommend slippers. Nevertheless, as more and more water mist and droplets landed onto our tired bodies as we approached closer and closer to the waterfall, we just felt refreshed and energised!  Because of the persistent mist and fine water droplets, it?s difficult to take selfies and photographs for that ?I was here at Jeongbang Waterfall? moment without these landing on your devices? lens and blurring the image. So you have to wipe off the water and be quick with the photograph taking.We spent about 30 minutes relaxing and soaking the ambience of the waterfall. During this time, we counted no less than 7 waterfall ?mini-streams? and only 20 visitors (not crowded). As the first 쩌 part of the descent path will not be walked again during the ascent, I would recommend taking photographs and selfies of the panorama during the initial stretch. In fact, the lookout point just after the ticket booth has this ?landmark? lone tree that faithfully watches over the waterfall, and you could include it to frame your photograph.If I could come again, I would do so in the cool morning with the sun shining on the waterfall. Anyway, this is one majestic waterfall that you wouldn?t want to miss!

My family and I drove to this awesome natural attraction and walked along the layered rocks and cliffs produced as a result of a volcanic eruption on a beautiful non-windy and sunny morning. Safety concerns: Yeongmeori (Dragon's Head) Coast is opened from 8 am to 6:30 pm from May to September. It will be closed when the weather changes in a way that impacts people?s safety (e.g. high tidal waves, strong winds), so it is better to call to check before going. Also a rainy day means that the rocks and coast will become slippery and you may have problems taking photographs. in any case, you definitely need a good pair of walking shoes.2 walking trails: You have to take note that there are 2 trails and entrances to Yeongmeori Coast. Both trails meet each other but are not connected due to safety issue, which means you have to pay separate entrance fees. However, I saw a white bridge is presently being constructed that links the 2 trails, but it remains unclear as to when it will be opened. Between the 2 trails ? Trail 1 and Trail 2 (described below) ? I found Trail 2 to be  safer for walking and has more spectacular sandstone rock formations and cliffs, and because of that my family and I spent about 3 hours admiring the attraction and taking photographs.  Trail 1: This trail is where the tourists go, and starts after the Hamel Castaway Memorial and the Hamel vessel. You park your car (along with the tour coaches) at a car park that?s next to a mini theme park (with the Viking amongst others). You then walk along the seaside promenade next to sandstone layered rocks along the sea, which takes about 1.5 to 3 hours return after the ticket booth (1,000 won for adults & 500 won for teenagers & children). Since certain stretches of the promenade are narrow, you have to walk carefully so as not to fall into the sea and onto the rocks.Trail 2:  This is a shorter trail that in theory should only take about 30-60 minutes return after the ticket booth. You park your car just beneath the temple. Parking is free. Cross the road and look for 3 bronze circular structures with inscriptions of ?Jeju Island Geopark?, ?Global Geopark Networks? and ?New 7 Wonders of Nature? and a green signage ?Yongmeori Coast Entrance -> 300m? From there, you just walk down the steps and follow the path which will take you past several shops. After about 10 minutes? walk, you will reach a ticket booth. After buying the tickets (1,000 won for adults & 500 won for teenagers & children), turn left and you would come to the top of a narrow and steep passageway to the coast. Take your time to carefully choose the big rocks as your steps for your descent (and then I realised what the term ?stepping stone? means). There are no handrails. Once you reached the bottom after about 6 minutes (longer when there are many people), turn around and look up at the challenging and difficult passageway and appreciate your achievement! Looking across the sea, we saw Mount Hallasan. Instead of going left, I recommend you go to the right and once through a archway or hole in a rock wall, and you will soon encounter the spectacular irregular layered and wavy sandstone cliffs that often contain ?pot-holes?. The rock formation at certain places was carved out by  a blade that cut itself into the layered rocks, creating v-shaped clefts. And when the waves crashed into the rocks, it sounds like roaring thunder ? awesome!  There?s a short cement bridge where standing on it allows you to take a superb photograph of the rock formation and the narrow stretch of turquoise-coloured sea. It is also around this same spot that you can take another superb photograph of the cliffs with Mount Sanbangsan in the background. There were 2 ladies (I didn?t think they were the famed ?Haenyeo? sea-divers) at the shoreline with 3 basins of sea animals - sea snail (sora), sea squirt (myeonggye) and sea cucumber (haesam) ? who would be happy to enable you  to experience Korean culture of eating raw seafood by the shoreline. I didn?t like to eat raw seafood so I didn?t try.Overall, my family and I think that Yeongmeori Coast is one attraction in Jeju that ranks it as among the top 3 attractions in Jeju. Don?t miss it! It will blow your mind away!

My boyfriend and I were excited to visit the Maze Park and it really did not disappoint! The maze itself was really good and it took us an embarrassingly long time to finish, :-) This is really for people of all ages! Everybody was laughing and having such a good time that the whole atmosphere was so nice. The workers were very nice, and one man who I assume is the manager had a wonderful conversation with us while we waited for the taxi they had called for us! His English is PERFECT and he can tell you all about his interesting travels. We were lucky enough to see Mr. Dustin himself, the owner. They have loads of cats inside and outside that are well taken care of. This was one of our favorite parts of Jeju! You definitely should go here!

Must visit this place if you are in Jeju.  This is the place where you can also watch women divers performance and taking the horse ride too. If you want to catch the Sunrise at the peak, start to climb at least 30 mins before the sunrise. Please check the weather first. If you are not that fit, start to climb 1 hour before the sunrise. Take note: Stairs all the way from the bottom to the top. A lot of resting area along the way.  Alternatively, from the entrance, walk towards the ocean on the left.  You can catch the sunrise from there too if you are too lazy to climb.  The view around the mountain is fantastic.  Many eateries, shops nearby.  It will be very crowded from 9am onwards with many tour buses.  Many parking lots nearby if you are unable to get any parking at the mountain carpark.

Must see place in east part of island.Wonderful atmosphere is there. The trail takes about 1 hour.It's possible to reach from west Seogwipo by bus.Choose airport limousine 600,get off in stop   World cup stadium  .Then find intercity bus terminal-about 50m to the right-there is tourist info also. Then get in a bus 701-journey lasts about 1.5 hour-get off in  Seongsan Ilchulbong park entrance  -and here you are.I added sunrise schedule.

Must do if you enjoy hiking! We climbed to the peak of Mt Hallasan, South Korea's highest mountain.  Took us 3.5 hours up and 2 hrs down at a reasonable pace hike.  Beautiful autumn/fall leaves starting to changing colour (we hiked on the 13th Oct).  Despite what is advertised, there is a water station on the way up so you don't have to overload on water.

Mt Halla is known as Korea's jewel. It is its highest peak. And well worth the trip to Jeju. We left Seagwipo very early (around 7 am) and took bus 182 (181 also goes there) to Seongpanak because we wanted to climb up to the peak. We got to the mountain around 7:45 and started the hike. The weather was super nice when we left, and we planned it that way, because we wanted to at least get some nice views of the city, and while at the summit. This is a long day of hiking, so be prepared. Bring snacks (and a trash bag, because you have to carry everything back down), and water. There are 2 checkpoints along the way that have bathrooms. The last checkpoint sells ramen for about 1500w with hot water. This is the checkpoint you have to get to before 12:30. We made it there around 11, and up to the summit before noon On the Seongpanak trail, there is also a lake with an observatory that's worth the detour.The last part of the hike up to the summit is pretty steep and rocky, so watch your footing, especially because you might be tired from walking up. Wear adequate footwear, make sure they are sturdy and comfy!Unfortunately, we didn't get that lucky with the weather as it because overcast as we were getting up there. I guess it really depends on your luck (the next day, it was super clear! Damn you Mt Halla!!) hahaha.We took the same trail down (from the summit, there is another trail, but no buses stop there. And this is where your comfy shoes are a must. The hike up was not bad, but the hike down, was torture! Our feet kept hitting the front of our hiking shoes, so we were bruised and hurt by the time the hike was done. We were also sore for the next 2 days (and we're pretty sporty, but we rarely walk for 8 hours) Overall, it's a great hike. The trail up is covered by trees, so it is cooler than it seems, but there are still some great views, especially with the fall foliage. We'd be surprised at the range of people walking the trail, old and young love to hike up this trail, and we understand why!

Mr Kim, also affectionately known to us as Samchoon was introduced to us by a friend. Even before we arrived in Jeju, he was so ever helpful whenever I had questions about planning the day. He would offer the best ideas and try to accommodate to your requests as much as possible so that your day would be a breeze and convenient. He didn?셳 mind that we stayed almost an hour away from Jeju city and arrives early at our hotel to make sure our day starts off well. He actually does research and make calls for you and made sure that attractions and restaurants are open when you get there. He really goes to the extra mile to put a smile on your face! Not to mention showering our family with little treats and souvenirs. He also made sure my mum who wasn?셳 feeling well is okay and offered to get us some medicine. That really warmed our hearts. He?셲 very familiar with the places and routes in Jeju and knows the best restaurants for quality and value. He drives safely and makes the ride really comfortable. I have to say, most drivers would just drive and drop you at places but he went with us and explain how do we enjoy the best out of the attraction. As a bonus, he?셲 always ready to take the best photos for you without you asking! At the end of the trip, Mr Kim really felt like a family friend to us.You won?셳 regret hiring his taxi tour service when you?셱e in Jeju :??

Mountain HallasanIt was a fanatic walk ever, friendly people all around. Unfortunate in Jeju island, English is not a common language, road signs, information boards are all in Korean, mainly people speak Korean, surprisingly, you might find people speak Japanese and mandarin. There are a few entrances from around the Moutain, make sure you do your research.I believe there are more than 4 entrances. Due to limited time, I have chosen the easiest and fastest trail (Eorimok). You could take public transport or driving. There is parking 17mins walk, and payable parking 1000won, save your time. Be prepared below- Go toilet, do the necessity before you start - Go to visitor centre get a map and find out more. ( e.g. if the convenient store is open?) - 2-3 hours walk one way, the washroom only available in the destination. Choose the hiking shoes. (Bad experience, my sport shoes are ruined) - Best to start your journey at 8 or 9 in the morning, as early as you could. If you are doing other trails, allow more than 8 hours. Eorimok entrance, it took me 5hours, I took a slow walk. - Be warned after certain time (14:30, not certain), you may not be allowed to go in. - Bring a lot of water, or bring enough cash (drinkable water is not enough to supply to public), bring your own food if you don't want to end up eating spicy instant noodle.- Store only sell, instant noodle(super spicy), and spring water. (Limited to 2 portions of instant noodle per person) price: 1000won for instant noodle, 1000won for a bottle of water- Bring extra clothe to change, bring a light weight jacket. (It is a bit chilling on top)- Bring insects repellent spray or lotion- Bring wet tissue and normal tissue- Bring a bag for rubbish, smoking and littering are not allowed.The place is well protected, please respect :)  Voila! Happy Journey!

Mount Halasan is located in the southern most tip of the Korean Peninsula. The height is 1950 m, a young volcanic mountain. The scenery is lovely and unique. The climbing route is interesting and versatile. Stones, rocks, wooden planks, concrete and steps is what makes the path up to the peak Baengnokdam. It takes 4 hours one way to reach the peak and about the same time for descent. Only one canteen is available where we can get coffee, chocopie and noodle boxes. The vivid autumn colors brought joy to the heart. Thoroughly enjoyed climbing this mountain

Might not be very tall at 1950m but it's no walk in the park. The best part though is that the path is clear and generally easy to walk especially when there are planks. Otherwise walking on volcanic rock and boulders are not so comfortable for the feet. Great views at the top and as we went in spring, flowers are in bloom.

Marado Island is remote, largely barren, and is   nearly   empty. There is a small population of island residents. There is a small oddly shaped church, a Buddhist temple, and a lighthouse. As far as buildings go, there is little of interest. The primary feature of Marado is the rugged coastline, typical of Jeju-do. Doesn't sound that appealing? Yet, I did enjoy my visit here because it is nice to see a part of Jeju that is largely unaffected by tourism, small museums, resorts, golf, or honeymooners. The ferry does not depart too frequently. Once you arrive on Marado, you really can only do one thing, walk around the entire island, which only takes 2 hours. If the weather is nice (May-August), you should be able to get some pretty pictures of the rugged coast, bright green grass, and some of the lonely buildings on the island.Some of these small island communities are such a contrast to our (foreigners) perception of Korea, that a visit in itself helps creates a more broad image of the country. A worthy experience, that I would recommend if you have plenty of time on Jeju Island.

Many tours include this spot for tourists.  I personally find it over-rated.  It is an illusionary experience where the environs surrounding the particular stretch of road gives one the impression that it is not what it is supposed to be.  Some guides would even spill water on the road to experiment.  Interesting - yes, but I would not include it as part of a tour itinerary.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the top ten lava tubes to visit that was formed about 200,000-300,000 years ago. It is one of 7 Geomunoreum lava tubes of Jeju Island and located in the North East area.The visit can be done using either bus (another 30 mins or 2.7km walk to the entrance) or car. I'd suggest to rent a car while in Jeju because it will make it super easy to get around the island. If you drive, the number you want to input into the GPS is 7107903 :-).It was really windy and cold on the day we went to the cave. We walked for about 5 minutes from the free car park to the ticket booth but the temperature inside of the cave was very comfortable.The first lava related item that we saw was the lava column cascade. It would be there on the way to entrance, to greet everyone who came to visit the Manjanggul Cave.?The entrance started with two flights of stone stairs that might get a bit slippery during the rainy or winter period. Even though you wear non-slip shoes with you, it's definitely worthwhile to hold on to the railing when going down and up the stairs.The cave was definitely not wheelchair friendly since the stony surface is always wet, rocky and covered with puddles. Water will occasionally drop from the ceiling of the cave but it didn't really bother us. We saw that some people carried an umbrella with them or wore the plastic rain poncho but since you'll be walking a lot, it would be too warm if you wear the poncho. Another suggestion is just to wear a hat/ baseball cap in summer and stick to your winter jacket in the winter time.I tried to take some photos inside but it was pretty hard because the cave was quite dark. It was a really enjoyable walk and we got to learn about how the lava stream formed the lines on the cave, stalactites and stalagmites.There were a lot of rocks around our path and we learnt later on that big and fragmented rocks fell from the ceiling during or after the formation of the lava tubes! There were a lot of lava columns as well that was formed when lava flowed from the ceiling to the floor of the lava tube.Manjanggul Cave closes on the first Wednesday of each month. Their opening hours is from 9 AM to 6 PM with last admission at 5:10 PM.

Manjanggul cave is a 7.4km long lava tube, although it is only possible to walk for the first kilometer. It takes about an hour. Manjanggul cave is said to be one of the largest lava tube in the world. During the walk, one can really feel the size. There are open spaces here and there that are indeed pretty large and spacious. I appreciated the nice selection of several lava formations that was available, each of them being in general accompanied by few pieces of information. In particular, one should not miss the locally-famous 'turtle' rock (an accretion of lava around a fallen rock that has a turtle shape) and the tallest lava column in the world (7.6 meters high, see the picture I uploaded).There is an entrance fee, but it is very reasonable (about 2 USD).Overall, the visit is worthy but one must be ready about what Manjanggul Cave is: a dark and humid cave with a few stones and lava formations.

Manjang Cave is one of the finest lava tunnels in the world and it is a designated as a natural monument.Not an easy walk as lots of even walkway,  slippery and dark. Take a slow walk to enjoy the surrounding and was cooling as you walk. You will be able to see the trace of the lava that flow through the cave. I saw some who rush all their way in and out.With young children do note of their safety, for older people who having legs problem do not try. Partly, you need to walk down the stairs which is not easy and when you finished you need to walk up again.We really enjoyed the nature of this cave.

Manjang Cave is near the northeast portion of Jeju, therefore if you are staying on the touristy south side of the island it will take over an hour to get here.The cave is part of a cave system that extends for kilometers that has been given some sort of UNESCO title (kind of like every natural sight on the island it seems). While the cave is indeed interesting, the allure of the cave stops once you descend down the stairs from the entrance and realize that you should have come more prepared.If you decide to embark to the cave, come with hiking boots or waterproof shoes and leave your Toms or Tori Burch shoes in the car because 95% of the cave is unimproved meaning walking along uneven surfaces filed with cracks and cold water puddles that may cause sprained ankles or ending up with cold and dirty feet is more than likely to occur.Also, the cave is dimly lit so unless you are Bruce Wayne or a vampire, you can't really see diddly-squat. So bring a flashlight or come hardcore prepared with a headlamp.Lastly bring a sweater or jacket because the cave is really cold. It's like being inside a commercial freezer but with cold wet feet. Not cool... I mean too cool LOL.As for the cave itself, it is impressive, but gets really repetitive and unlike the photos on the signs and pamphlets, the lighting is so bad you can't really see anything. Aside from   turtle rock   and lava stalactites, everything started to look the same. Would I return? Methinks not.The cost is 2000 won per adult, which seems to be the standard fare of most touristy spots on the island including the waterfalls and Sunrise Peak.

Manjang cave is impressive! One of our party has arthritic feet, but even she managed to navigate the uneven surfaces by taking great care. The entry/exit includes steep stairs and be aware the handrail is slippery. There are two sections with ropelike lava walkways (one worse than the other) - these are by far the most difficult and uneven terrain to walk. The lava tube itself is pretty much on plane... no significant inclines or decents. Be aware that at the end you retrace your steps to the entrance.

Lovely peaceful spot , nice statue at the start then all the buddas on the walk up to the temple offset by the lanterns. The temple is nice take a good look at the food and painting but the golden Buddha at the side is worth a look. Nice cafe and shop on site well priced.

Loved this island off Jeju Island!  If you're staying in the Jungmun area, this requires about an hour taxi or car ride to the port where you catch a ferry (15 minute ride) the island. Best to buy a return ticket at the ticket office (the taxi driver helped us to do this, lucky for us as you need to show your ID or passport to buy tickets!).  The sun came out for us and the island was in all its glory - blue skies and blue sea - absolutely worth the trip.  Can easily spend half to one day here. Not sure how it works with the bus options though if you hire a cabin to stay along the bus route.When you arrive at U-Do, there are various bicycles/cars that you can hire (if you bring your driving licence), however, you can easily buy a hop on hop off bus ticket.  The bus driver talks for some of the way during the bus tour but if you don't understand what's going on, it's just as easy to enjoy the view from the window.  Nature is all around.Apart from the surrounding sea and boats, you can see horses and women divers (next to their orange buoys) in the sea.   We also enjoyed a black pork burger, mandarin juice at our first stop and also a peanut ice-cream from Jimmy's.This visit was another one of the many highlights to our trip and I would love to come again!  Pre-teen kids also enjoyed the beautiful breathtaking scenery.

Love love love. Everything was beautiful. If you like just seeing different glass art works this is the place for you. It was between $11-12 for entry but of the   museums   in korea  this one is my favorite (lived in korea for 4 years). The jungle walk through that starts with some dinosaurs is kind of long but very gorgeous

Located next to   Loveland   this museum is small modern place with beautiful outdoor features such as a reflecting pool sculptures and a small surrounding forest. There was a little bit of everything from an exhibit about a famous national artist who lived for decades on Jeju to an interesting video and poetry collaboration of Korean rappers talking about social issues. The upstairs is currently showcasing drawings and sculptures made by Korean schoolchildren in a surprisingly cheeky cheerful exhibit. Much of the museum was in English but others were only in Korean. The price of admission was only 1000 won well worth it for the experience. There were several pieces that didn't wow me and some outdoor floorboards that need repairs but all in all this is a nice little museum. Make sure to drop by the cafe on the way out for a lovely view of the reflecting pool outside as you sip your coffee!

Located in the north eastern part of the island.  Took us an hour from hotel.  The cave temperature is 5-10C lower than outside, so suggest to bring a jacket and don't wear your Jimmy Choos.  Is wet and slippery with uneven grounds.  (Not suggest for elderly)The open part in 2017 is the 2nd section.  which is about 1km from start to end. First you walk down a steep stairs 3 floors down and you start walking. When you reach the large platform at the end and see the huge lava rocks, take photo and then you walk back .Spent about 2 hours there.

Located in the middle of the Jeju island, it's a very beautiful and well managed National Park. Unfortunately, we were too late for hiking to the Hallasan and back. We decided to hike to the top of a directly opposite and much lower peak. It was easier and we were almost alone on the whole trail as well as at the peak. In the end, we had a nice picknick at the tourist and information center. If you really want to hike to the Hallasan itself, arrive and start as early as possible, be prepared with enough water, some food/snacks and other important hiking utensils.

Located in the middle of Jungmun Resort right across from a Ripley's Believe it or Not museum, I would only recommend this kitsch and cheese-tastic museum to visitors on a bleak and rainy day. The idea is cute, at best - history and art through the ages represented by teddy bears (My Fair Lady, Princess Diana and Prince Charles get married, the falling of the Berlin War, the Beatles, Mona Lisa, the Creation of Adam, etc.), but I would expect a museum in an expensive resort complex to at least have descriptions in English and other tourist languages (Japanese, Mandarin, Cantonese). The entrance fee of 8000 won is a little steep for what you are able to see. Not surprisingly, there is an entire floor dedicated to a pricey gift shop. The most impressive parts of the museum are the architecture of the glass pyramidal shaped building and the views from the garden to the rear. Overall, it's an alright way to kill an hour or so, but definitely not a must-see for me.

Located in Seogwipo. What makes this waterfall unique compared to the rest of waterfalls in Asia is ? this one falls directly into the ocean. The view is very dramatic and I can guarantee that you will say 'wow' the moment you see it from the distance.This waterfall is 23 meter / 75 feet high. It was written in a legend that a holy dragon lived underneath it. Due to it, it was said that the water can cure disease and bring rain during drought season.It costs KRW 10,000 to enter this area, same price as Cheonjiyeon waterfall entrance fee. The comparison that I can make between these two waterfalls is ? Cheonjiyeon has beautiful landscape compared to Jeongbang. But Jeongbang has the dramatic factor compared to relaxing, calming Cheonjiyeon waterfall.You will go through a simple, quaint little path before you reach the waterfall gate entrance. No man made sculptures or attempt to make this road appear to be more touristy. However, the pink wild flowers blooms along this little path captures my heart. If you pay very close attention, you will see spider (s) hanging in the bushes alongside the road too. And if you not scared of it, you can check it out and test your macro skill with your camera. Remember : look but don't touch!Note: There are lots of spiders in Jeju Island. They are every where.I was unable to get too close to the falls because 1) it was cold windy day 2) I easily suffocate with water mist 3) I don't have water protection cover for my camera. So, if you plan to come here, please make sure to bring water proof camera protection if you really care of your expensive camera.Ah, one more thing ? shoes. Please wear sensible, flat, good grip kind of shoes / sport shoes.

Located 25mins from Seogwipo, at the Jungmun area, this is a dramatic stretch of coast with hexagonal rock columns. They result from the rapid cooling and contraction of lava once it has met the water of the sea.There is a viewing platform right behind the Jeju ICC (convention centre), from where to admire the coast and the formations in particular.To access the platform, park the rental car at the designated park (KRW 1000) and buy the access tickets (KRW 2000). The platform is always busy and with all the selfies going on, one struggles to look at the rock formations.

Living in Hong Kong we're pretty used to tough hikes - this one is a little difficult but manageable for anyone who is reasonably fit or has some hiking experience. Whilst the incline on this hike is never that steep and the first part of the trail is easy with paved walkways, the terrain for the second half is pretty hard going with lots of rocks and boulders. We managed in trainers but hiking boots with a sturdy sole would probably be better, and some may feel more comfortable with poles. But it's ABSOLUTELY worth the effort for the view. The crater lake is quite impressive but more stunning is if you look back on Jeju from above the clouds. Took us about 6.5 hours up and down but bring plenty of snacks as there is only one point where you can buy water and some dubious looking packet noodles. Oh and there are no bins so bring a bag for your rubbish. If you are in Jeju and like hiking, you must do this as it's a great sense of achievement when you can say you've hiked S Korea's highest peak!

Living in a country where there is no chance the snow will fall, we are so excited to experience snow even though by that time it is nearly end of March. The view is amazing, though I cannot go for the hike as I went there with my mom. Will definitely go again and bring my hiking partner next time.

Let's first get this out of the way: If you're not a teddy bear fan, if you're an over-serious person, or basically, if you had a fun-less childhood, don't bother visiting this place. Because then it would be pretty much a tourist ripoff kind of place, with nothing really worth seeing.But, if you do like bears, and regardless of how cheesy or a ripoff this place can be, you just want to have some fun, then by all means, check it out!Admittedly, I quite like teddy bears myself, and right from the moment I stepped in, I was constantly tickled by all the teddy bears modeled in the form of famous people, famous artworks, and even historical events. It can be sometimes strange to see the head of a bear in the place of what should've been a human one, but toss the strangeness aside and you'll realize there is so much to see and chuckle over. Having teddy bears in place of humans in the exhibits add a touch of innocent cuteness to everything.Do note that there's both an indoor and outdoor exhibit, so if you're on a schedule yet really want to see everything, make sure you plan your time well!

Lee Jung-Seob Art Gallery, like most government run museums in Korea, had a low display items to museum area ratio.? It is dedicated to Lee who spent the last few years of his life in Seogwipo after being raised in present-day North Korea and spending a significant part of his life in Japan.? In a three floor building it was just one room with about 20 pieces of artifacts.? Fortunately the few artifacts which consisted of postcards Lee sent his wife, his earlier sketches, letters to his children, and his palette donated by his wife were all interesting to check out.

LEE Joong Seop Street is lovely and there are some art shops where you can do window shopping. Then this small street lead you to the house where Lee's family lived for certain period, in a 4.6m2 room for 4 family member. You will be stunned to see how small it is!! But they loved this place where they could hug all the time, kids, and the couple. Behind those free zone, the art museum is located. Admission is 1,500 KRW(1.10 USD, 0.80 Euro). You can request docent on the spot. Korean is always ready, for English, better to call in advance when you will visit. At the end of the street, there is small traditional market where you can get some street food and fresh fruits. Strongly recommend to visit to feel the artist' spirits who lived miserable period. He made lots of work for 6 years before he died, age of 40's. It looks like Van Gogh did lots of works during short period. Good to visit 3rd floor to enjoy the view toward south part of Ocean.

Korean women divers are called haenyeo. They dive in the ocean without any special tools to gather abalone, clams or seaweed. Wearing a lead weighted  vested and goggles, they plunge into 20 meter depths and stay underwater holding their breaths for two to three minutes.  Once they come up to the surface, they make a whistling sound, which is their unique way of breathing out carbon dioxide and breathing in fresh oxygen. The museum is in a four story building and housed many exhibits.  Gallery 1 on the first floor depicts the haenyeo's way of life. On the second floor at Gallery 2, you can see haenyeo's working life.  On the third floor at the observation area you can get a view overlooking the sea.  Gallery 3 displays exhibits of the sea around Jeju.  Outside the museum there is a lawn with statues, including one honoring the haenyeo. You can also admire the architecture of the museum. Further down, we chanced upon the haenyeo who were starting their show by singing a song. We were indeed lucky on that Tuesday afternoon as we managed to watch the show which started at 1.30.

Kim Tschang-Yeul museum had a stylish exterior designed by Tadao Ando.? Featuring the namesake artist Kim’s sculptures and paintings, the museum is very chic for a government run museum. Kim’s trademark is the water drop, which is added to what would otherwise look like rather plain patterns painted on canvas.? The sculptures mostly contained large glass water drops.? Some of the outdoor sculptures complement Ando’s architecture very nicely.? This was an unexpectedly cool visit.

Just got back and it was cool. Not been down caves before but nothing scary here. You do need a decent pair of walking shoes (preferably water resistant or water proof).. The odd splash of water won't hurt you but solid footwear is a smart move (read that as flip-flops and high heels are a big no). I liked the experience, there are a few steps to go down which are easy at the start of the walk but if you walk to the end and back, those steps are a killer at the end. All-in-all, I loved it, nice little solo adventure; loads of couples down there (but well behaved) and it is cheap as chips for the entrance fee of just over 짙1.GBP. Easy to reach by taxi or bus and taxi shouldn't cost more than 20,000WUN at the most from most central places.. go along and view for yourself though if you have small children, it is taxing on their little feet cos the floor is very uneven (as to be expected on a lava field).
Just a short stretch of road where it   appears   to defy gravity. Kill the engine where the START signs indicate and feel the car moving uphill on its own.

Jungmun-Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff is beautiful place where, look at huge waves crashing against volcanic rocks, one can experience the power of nature. With so much to do and so much to see, the Jeju island is certainly one of the most prominent tourist places in the world. Just about an hour's flight from Seoul, it's a paradise for nature-lovers and surfers. There are countless world class museums offering education and entertainment based on themes like Glass, Ice Sculptures, Trick Art, Folk Lore, Health and Sex, War, Art - the list is endless. Best way to explore the Island is to take taxi tours with a driver who speaks and understands little English. They ask for W150,000 for 8 hours, however, you may beat them down to W115,000 or so. For sightseeing, 5-6 days should be enough.

Joined the 2016 Walking Festival to walk the olle trails & it was a fantastic experience. Yes it rained (which was unusual in October but with global warming!) & was initially disappointing as the scheduled performances were cancelled. Nonetheless it was amazing to see so many people walking together. After the Walking Festival which covered trail 1 & 2 I did trail 1-1, 5,6, 8 & 10. Each of the trails were different and beautiful. I was fortunate to get the assistance of Jim Saunders who gave me information on line & Ms Han at the Tourist Information Centre located next to Seogwipo Bus Terminal & e Mart who spoke good English.Ms Han helped me by writing in korean the bus stops & landmarks for the different trails so that I could show the bus drivers my destination  when I boarded using the T-money transport card. She even took the trouble to show me the different landmarks using satellite pictures on her computer in locating the Starting Point of each trail. The Olle Guide Book in English (which I obtained at the Olle Trail counter at the airport)was also very useful & well written.I enjoyed every trail & got to see Jeju on foot. It was also fun meeting locals walking the trails. I plan to return to walk the other olle trails.

Jeju stone park was rated A by Korea Ministry of Culture and Tourism, in recognition that this park is excellent in term of its specialization in the theme of stone, differentiation from other facilities, and characteristics relating to mythology and the life of the people in the region.Get the map at the entrance and follow guided park course. Don't miss out the Jeju stone museum to know how the formation of Jeju Island. After a short nice walk from the entrance,the museum is just located in the basement of a building opposite the Sky Pond. Follow the map to look for Jeju traditional village with thatched roof houses. Before at the end of course, drop by the unique Gallery in the park which you may find artworks of domestic and foreign artists.It is indeed best travel Korea during Autum because even though it was sunny day, but the breeze was so cooling and the air was very refreshing. It is a museum as well as an ecological park. It is a very remarkable cultural park which sublimating nature in art ,really very fantastic.
Jeju Stone Park is interesting. There are lots of great spots for photos and there are also lots of stone exhibits which infuses some aspects of history, culture and art.

Jeju Stone Park exceeded our expectations.  So much space and everything well laid out.  The museum was particularly interesting with some absolutely amazing pieces of lava, and microscopes set-up, which my 9-year old Daughter loved.  They also had an interesting photography exhibition (temporary).  If you are a geologist and/or simply interested in volcanoes and rocks, then you will probably spend all day here.  Appreciated the water machines everywhere but the restaurant was closed (just in case you are hungry).  We all enjoyed it immensely.  Children less than 12 are free and adults are KRW 5000 (very reasonable).

Jeju Olle Trail is completely round the island broken up into 21 different routes.In total we walked about 13km, about 3.5 to 4 hours time taken. Photography time included.We started our walk from Hyatt Jeju along the Jungmun Beach (we did Route 8 going eastwards) heading towards the Daepo Pego (port) and ended our walk at the Yakcheon Temple.Ensure that you look out for arrows (blue&orange) along the ground and olle trail ribbons (blue & orange as well) tying on trees along the way. Terrain is very varied, from easy tarmac lanes to quite difficult lava rocks along the bays. Suggest you wear proper walking shoes. Bring along your own water & snacks. Jeju is rather large and most of the sights are quite far apart. It can take an hour to 2 hours to get to the various sights. Jeju is not only beaches and shopping malls, but has also a really interesting history ! Jeju is full of great natural wonders - Seongsan IIchulbong Peak, Manjanggul Cave, Cheonjiyeon Falls, Hallasan Mountain, Jeongbang Falls, Yongduam Rock, Jungmun Beach, Oedolgae, Jusangjeoli Cliffs; each and every of these world class attractions is Nature's well-carved masterpiece. Jusangjeoli Cliffs is one of those gorgeous and stunning attractions that I favored. While it does not have the sentimental legend that back-up Oedolgae or the auspiciousness of the dragon like Yong-duam rock, the sight of the crashing torrential sea waves rhythmically crashing against the set of blackish, rock pillars and columns was so beautiful a sight that I was totally immersed in the picturesque scene. The turquoise azure sea water contrasted magnificently with the black cliffs and produced one of those awesome scenery that one could hardly imagine it existed on Earth. I was mesmerized by what I saw and my ears drowned by the thundering waves. For one short moment, my mind went into a meditative state despite the presence of the squeezing and noisy crowd. I like to thank our Korean guide, Mr Won, who drove us in his van around Jeju to visit all these beautiful nature's wonders.

Jeju is a volcanic island and the black lava that erupted from Mount Hallasan few thousands years ago are found almost every where. When we visited this attraction at Yongdam which is about 20 minutes drive from the Jeju airport, we could see the sea rocks and soils were black in color. The Yongdam rock was probably a volcanic rock that erupted and eroded down Mount Hallasan and over the years sculptured by natural forces of strong wind and rain and powerful sea waves into a structure of a `dragon head' . But the invisible hands of nature did not leave a distinctively well carved aesthetic product that deserved our admiration and appreciation. I really could not figure out the `dragon head' from the rock until my guide pointed out it to me. But black dragon in traditional Chinese folklore was supposed to symbolize bravery and auspicious luck and good fortunes to the people and visiting this attraction assumingly bring good luck and prosperity.Nevertheless, Jeju is exceptionally natural beauty and boasts of so many awesome and stunning natural scenic attractions which are so fascinating so lovely so magnificent that make me wondered if this was paradise on Earth. The air is fresh and you hardly find heavy machineries and factories with thick polluted smoke emitting out from the chimneys or the methane smell of diesel and petrol from vehicular emissions that is so typical in crowded cities. Jeju impressed me what nature is all about. From Yongmeori seashore, manjanggul caves, cheongjiyeon waterfalls to Hallasan National Park and Oedolgae Cliffs and this Yongdu-am dragon head rock, the physical geographical lessons appear no ending and I found intense pleasure in enjoying nature's silent whispers.

I've climbed Hallasan twice now, once in December and once in early March, and both times I took this route. This route is slightly longer than Gwaneumsa, but it's also a gradual incline with several easy portions. I took this route primarily because there is not a lot of public transportation available to/from the Gwaneumsa trail, plus I'm not sure I can do a steep incline the entire way up to the summit. For Seongpanak, you have about 5 km that are easy, 2.5 km that get harder, and then a pretty brutal last 2 km. Regardless, know that there are other hiking trails around the island and even around the volcano, but only the two mentioned above will lead you all the way up to the summit.Given some of the reviews I saw that are either inaccurate or not very helpful, I hope to compile a quick list to help you decide if this is something you want to do and if so, what you will need:1) It's definitely going to be an all-day kind of thing. You will be tired afterward, so you likely won't want to schedule too many other activities for the evening. Also, it's likely that you will be sore and tired the next day or two. 2) You need to start climbing no later than 8:30 AM. As several people have mentioned, you will not be allowed to access the last chunk of the way if you're not at the second shelter by 12:30 PM (this is winter time, so the schedule varies slightly from season to season... always check the Korean tourism sites).3) Even if it's sunny, there's a chance you might need crampons. In the winter months you will need them for sure, but even last weekend people were sliding down and falling repeatedly without them. I hear that it's even worse on the Gwaneumsa trail since it's a lot more shielded from the sunshine. 4) Bring food and water! The only place you can buy something is at the very beginning of the trail, and even then the options aren't fantastic. A little protein or fruit will go a long way whenever you're starting to feel tired, and it'll help you push through. Please make sure you do not leave any of your trash along the way; there are zero trashcans, so if you carry something particularly messy, you might want to pack a bag for the waste.5) Do not use the toilet in the first shelter! It's the worst smelling bathroom ever, which is rare for Korea since things are usually so clean... I suppose it's the septic system. I suggest using the toilets at the parking lot and at the last shelter (there are two). The first one is seriously a nightmare. 6) It's not an easy hike, but it's doable even for people who don't exercise strenuously. I've seen people carrying babies all the way to the top, and I've seen small children and old people make it, too. Definitely wear the right clothing, though, and especially the right shoes. If you're hiking at a time without snow, you will spend hours circumventing rocks of all sizes and ankle support will be extremely helpful for this. Anyway, thanks for reading, I hope you have a fantastic hike!

You see the striped walls indicating different levels of the flow, each stripe has a bit different color. Glossy lava sinters, black, dark red and orange. Fantastic landscape of big and small stalactites and stalagmites. It's a shame, only a small part of the lava tube is opened for public. And the trail is arranged pretty dull. Nothing (except the natural beauty of the cave) would take your breath away and make you come again.There are many tunnels that branches from the main tube and go further and further after the end of the main trail. With a proper lighting and clever management it could be a fantastic place that would attract plenty of tourists and make them come again and again to explore this place.

It's for kids.  Good to take pictures at a distance, but when watching closely, I got the feeling that things are not that clean and new.  The cafe is particularly messy with no one clearing up the food leftover or liquid on the floor, table sticky.

it's definitely a unique place to visit but you should wear proper shoes as the 2km walk to and from the entrance has lots of rocky areas...the cave was dark,cold and wet but worth the visit if it's part of your tour.

Its big, full of trees, nice view for taking pictures. Dont go there during holidays, lots of people, long queue for the service train that will bring you around. It's an extremely demanding 'hike' for most average people. We read about it but didnt expect it to be that difficult. We went up the Seongpanak trail, starting at 7.30am, did a short detour to see the lake and crater and eventually reaching the summit at around 1pm. We descended the gwaneumsa trail and only managed to reach the base at around 6.30pm. We aren't considered extremely fit and so the climb was considered challenging for us. Our legs hurt for the next few days. The view down was amazing, but the climb was also steeper. Many parts of the trail were rocks so that made it a little difficult to climb as well. There are many cabs waiting at the base of Gwaneumsa trail to take you back to Seongpanak where we parked our car. The cab fare was about 15000won and took about 15 minutes. Overall the hike was fulfilling albeit tiring. But the views were a good return for our efforts!

It's a nice looking waterfall that falls directly into the ocean which is great but there are literally hundreds of people here at a time. The rocks are not particularly dangerous by themselves but add a huge crowd of tourists and school kids to the mix and it's a little risky. I think the fact that it was the scene of a Korean drama tv show may be part of the reason for it's popularity. The ladies selling seafood on the rocks so affectionately mentioned by others are not genuine haenyon, they just sell seafood at exorbitant prices. Buy your lunch elsewhere.

It's a nice bridge, and takes you across to the little island on the other side. Not really a lot to see apart from passing through the quaint port and adjacent coastline. Would suit you if you just wanted to go out for a relaxing walk along a peaceful area.

It's a must do to spend some time at this museum. Located in a relatively new building right on the coast, it tells the story of these amazing women divers who work 52 weeks of the year diving for a abalone, conch and other sea products. How they managed in the winter time without wet suits astonishes me. These women also played a vital part of the resistance movement in World War II against the invading Japanese Army. Add this visit as part of your Jeju Island tour - best idea it to hire a taxi driver for a day (approx A$100). They turn out to be your tour guide, photographer and restaurant selector - fantastic value! Enjoy :)

It's a great honour to be able to admire Mr Sung's Spirited Garden! It's absolutely a must visit whenever you are in Jeju! The garden is a real Paradise on Earth! It's a unique place that teaches you many important things! The garden features many outstanding examples of bonsai trees, beautifully shaped stones, a waterfall, a restaurant and a souvenir shop. It's easily accessible by car or by bus, and will be a worthy place for everyone, especially the nature and art admirers. I highly advise everyone to visit this incredible place!!!

I thought a 10:30 arrival was more than enough time to reach the summit and back before dark, but apparently when it is rainy, there is fog, so if you don't reach the highest checkpoint by 13:00, they won't let you summit. It was my first hiking trip and I decided to take the Seongpanak trail (9.6km one way) so that I can reach the summit. The hike is long and steep at certain stages. Very rocky road and proper hiking shoe is strongly recommended. The hike starts from visitor center is at 750m. At 1500m, there's a Jindalrae shelter where you can take a break for hot instant noodle and refill your drinks. The hike is tough for me (someone who jog/cycle once or twice a week). Walking stick is my best friend to support me all the way. Reaching the submit at 1950m is breathtaking. You will see the beautiful Baengnokdam lake. On the way down, at 1324m we hike to see Saraoreum Lake too. The whole trail with break took me almost 10 hrs (9.15am till 7pm). It's seems to be an easy hike for the Koreans, including the elderly but to me is a lot of determination and perseverance. Will definately hike at the other trails if I have the chance to go back to Jeju. ** I saw deer **

It was just an OK place to visit as it was part of our Tour Package. The old fashioned village homes were probably the only thing which was interesting to me. It was just amazing. Though the path way is well maintained but  it might be tough for some foreigners because of its slope but for Koreans it seems to be an easy task. It was interesting how they recreated real-life historical events and famous works of art with teddy bears.  There are two main exhibit halls.   Of course there is a gift shop where you can purchase teddy bears.  My wife and I enjoyed it and took lots of pictures.  I think you will enjoy this place, even if you don't have a thing for teddy bears. Bonus:  there is a really nice Starbucks right across the street.

It was felt like exercising when walking down to the see the waterfall. But just about ten steps down the stairs, the scene reveal the hidden stunning waterfall. So beautiful. It was a very hot day yesterday, July 31st 2018, and I got sunburn the day before so in 33 degree heat and me didn't match. It was a rainy and foggy day when I visited. It was very hard to drive, but went there anyway. It was a good experience for me family with 2 children as they enjoyed ut the most. Weather as a bit chilly even during autumn, so bring extra layers with you so that you can get confortable. The train ride at the start of the trip really feels like the highlight of the trip, although you can board the train on and off later to get from one garden to another. There are 5 stops for you to stroll around, toilets, cafes and other facilities are available and very much well taken care off. We had a great time all in all. It took about 10 minutes to travel on a ferry to visit Udo (thanks to G map)!I decided to walked around the coastline after lunch on arrival.An interesting island with some public arts and you wouldn?t stop taking photos!It worth spending some time walking around! It took a little over 2 hours by bus to get here. I feel conflicted with it, as a part of me liked the place but another part of me thought there was (yet again!) nothing special here. Plus the journey to get there was already exhausting so probably my feet were already asleep halfway into my walk.So only go if you can rent a car, it will take much less time to get here. All in all a relaxing place to take a stroll or read in.

It is probably a bad idea to go round island with the 5000 KRW tour bus - all the 4 stopovers were swarmed with tourists, but with just 2-3 hours to spare, we did not have much choice. First stop was at Udo-bong leading towards the Udo Lighthouse. Next was the Geommeolle Beach with black sand and rocks. The other two were beaches. At the last stop it was a little confusing as to which tour bus to board (to end the tour) as there were apparently 2 ferry terminals, and each terminal would sell tour bus with different docket colours.If we were to come again, we might do the 1.1 Olle Trail, perhaps by bicycle. At some parts of the island it was really picturesque coastline and we saw the haenyeo divers.Sans the big turnout of tourists, Udo will get a better rating definitely.
It is part of an Olle trail and well known as a filming location, so it is a bit crowded. But the trail after, is beautiful.

It is only mildly interesting as part of a tour package which include this as a drive-through attraction.Plenty of cars & coaches stop & have their engines turned off to experience the   rolling uphill   mysterious effect.It is quite interesting to see how this phenomenon and the perception of the surrounding environment to the naked eyes has come so far to give birth to a tourist attraction. It could also double as a quick pit-stop to grab some snacks & skewers at the food store along the road.Hint: Get there, spend 5-10min walking one way forward, and then walking backward, or lay a half filled water bottle on the road, to crack this mystery.

It is no wonder why Spirited Garden is one of the top-rated tourist attractions on Jeju Island. I found it one of the best garden I have visited so far. It is basically a Bonsai tree-themed Garden decorated with many waterfalls and beautiful ponds full of colorful koi carps. Hundreds of artistic bonsai trees can be seen planted on small to large flower pots and on the ground. The bonsai trees of fruits, especially Jeju mandarin (or orange), apples are very impressive. It has seven small gardens with beautiful exotic gates, one of which is called Secret Garden and exclusively use for national and international MICE events (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions). It appears that the garden is very famous in China and other neighboring countries. The information boards show that the garden has been visited by many honored public figures notably former premiers of China, Japan, Indonesia, and others. Also, the garden has been awarded many decorations such as ?KOREA Unique Venue?, ?Green MICE Venue?, etc.

It is my first hiking ever, I do feel some kind of relaxation after the experience. At first, I wonder how can those people climb up to reach the top, it takes more than a thousand stairs to be on the top, I was pretty scared. But when I was first stepping on the environment, I can feel the natural beauty of the nature. It enhances me to have a greater heart to finish the journey. There also some strangely shaped stones while I was climbing up the stairs, I learned the history behind the stones and took several selfies with the special stones. About 20 minutes, we reached the highest point of the mountain. The mountain was naturally a dead volcano, which build up with lots of grasses and trees, and is no longer a crater. The view is like a green-sea. I had never been such relaxed before. It is a great experience to me and is memorable.The overall journey took us about 1 hour, if you are a fan of hiking, you must enjoy it as the view is priceless. **Remember to buy a bottle of water before you go, there are shops for you to buy some snacks and drinks in the beginning of the path.
It is just a street; however, I was surprised when I put down my Evian bottle water n it started to roll by it self (fast enough) even though it was put on a flat street.

It is great to visit in Autumn. I went there in the middle of October and it was sunny. No rain, not too much wind. You can see the field of silver grass which might capture your mind and heart (if it is your style). Great over all. Its near the forest trail so you can visit there too.

It is an interesting showcase of lifesize and all sizes of teddy bears being used to personify famous art pieces, fables, fairy tales and etc.  There are many interesting photo opportunities.  The Koreans are very creative in coming up with such a museum dedicated to teddy bear lovers, but I would not return a second time.

It is an archetypal tuff cone formed by hydrovolcanic eruptions upon a shallow seabed about five thousand years ago.  Situated on the eastern seaboard of Jeju Island and resembles a gigantic ancient castle, this tuff cone is 182 meters high, has a preserved bowl-like crater. There are two hiking trails to reach the peak , take the white path uphill and the orange path downhill. You just follow the crowd and the signages along the trail. During May and the coming summer, you do not need a jacket or pullover as it will be  hot and you will sweat a lot on the climb up. Wear covered sports shoes and  a cap / hat. The first part of the hike is the easiest and the least steep.  The rest of the path comprises steps of varying steepness. The final stretch gets very steep. Along the hiking trail, there are benches and pavilions to rest. Take a sip of water, rest your aching legs before proceeding . Toilets are available along the way. From the peak, you can see beautiful landscapes of Jeju island and do take a photo with the signage saying you are at Sunrise Peak. It took us 30 minutes to reach the top. The downhill walk was much easier, just follow the wooden stairs meandering its way down.  At the bottom, you can go for drinks at the cafetarias.

It is a must visit place and I enjoyed it though I didn't spend as much time as I wanted.  It is damp and so a jacket is needed to keep you warm.  The ground is unlevel so walking with a good pair of grip shoes is a must as some parts are wet.I have been to the Shenandoh Caves in Virginia and though I must say it is more 'commercialised', I prefer the concept they have where you are brough down to the caves by their own 'cave guides'.  The guides would point out more interesting rock formations and though we did have our own personal guides, I think the ones by the cave operators would make it more interesting.It needs to be better lit as certain parts were very dark and there are minimal hand rails.  When we were in the Shenandoh Caves, the elderly were always upfront so that the other visitors could help them or watch out for them (mind you we were not from one tour group but individual members visting the cave) and one of them actually fell despite that.  That came to mind when I was in the caves too, that there was little light, a little brighter would have been ideal.  It was brighter lit nearer the entrance but not as you proceed further in.

It is a museum showing the history of Korea, the emotions and aesthetics of Koreans. Lee joong seop died at a young age and did not leave much work. However, the well-maintained birthplace, street and cafes and crowds around them show how this artist is popularly loved by Koreans.

It is a lava tunnel. It's interesting to see but not a must-see. There were some stairs to descent into the tunnel at the entry and it gets pretty dark inside. Your eyes will need to adjust, and there isn't any place to grip along the wall. Please wear comfortable shoes and some layers since it gets wet and chilly inside. Walking paths are uneven on some areas, and most are not well-lit. The tunnel is purposely not well-lit to preserve the natural habitat of its resident animals. A round trip from the entrance will take about 30-40 mins if you're strolling through the tunnel. We visited this cave as part of Yeha East course tour. If you have interest in geological formation, stalagmite, and nature, you may find it interesting.

It has always been something i try to do everytime i go for a holiday, is to go trekking in the mountains or forest. I went in late December and took a cab up to the start of yeongsil trail, and went down Eorimok trail. It was near a six hours journey, with a 20 mins lunch break. As i went during late december, the drive up the mountain area was really foggy and the visibility is only like 5 metres in front of us which is kinda scary because there were many windy roads. but as soon as we are nearing the trail, the fog seems to have been lifted due to the heights. Good info to know: Yeongsil trail have many flights of steps. Depending on what you prefer, manmade steps means relatively safe walkway but it is up most of the time.Eorimok trail has more stones steps and is more natural. But it could mean that it is more tedious, really depends on your preference.Lunch is ramen noodle at the shelter, they sell small snacks and drinks too. PS: As i went during the winter, the timing to enter certain trail is really strict because the sun sets really early like 5ish in the afternoon. So it is definitely a thing to take note of especially if you are not fast paced. Also during winter, along the trail, there will be snow left from the night before, and it IS really Slippery!! I nearly slipped many times because i was wearing a normal sneaker and not trekking shoe. And a really helpful thing to have is a walking stick! Other than that, enjoy your time with nature there!

It featured the women divers as the spirit of Jeju, displaying the culture and past of the people; clothes worn then, agricultural tools, even dishes and at one time, a wall with proverbs stemming from these women. It's a two floor museum only though, but holds alot of artifact

is kind of pricey. there are only 2 levels of bears being exhibits and it is all behind the glass. The bears are just being display in different themes and costumes. we were impressed at the beginning but started to get bored a moment later. Overall, it is still worth a visit.

Interesting, many different types of local food and daily items.  We had fresh seafood hotpot at one of the local eatery stalls.  30,000 wons, enough for three people.  The fresh fish slices are, in particular, very delicious.

Interesting waterfalls with a park. Lighted up at night. We came by at 8pm.  The clear and deep water of Cheonjiyeon Falls is designated as Natural Monument No. 27 and is renowned as a habitat for Mutae eels. Take a walk around the beautiful park. You can also take photos with the props such as 'Summer', hearts etc.

interesting shapes of rocks and lovely blue water.not too difficult, short walk along the trail. there are 2 different trails starting from different car park. both trails are not connected at the moment due to safety issue so make sure you visit the right one.by the look of it no.2 may not available or can be very wet @ low tide.i like the both but personally like no.1 trail little more.

Innisfree Jeju House is just next to O'Sulloc Tea Museum, so is great to visit both the places. Innisfree is just one floor in a glass house.Besides selling Innisfree products like facial care, there is also many other things to explore.There is a big space for soap making area, visitor can purchase a bag of soap making set at the counter, and do it at the available place. The staff will guide you on the soap making. A self making post card corner for visitor to bring back (free but with limited, per card per person).Nice cozy clean comfortable cafe. Don't forget to try the black pork hot dog. It is so delicious. I bought a soap making set for my son to enjoy the art work, while I enjoy my facial product shopping. Initially I wasn't sure if I would go to see this as I'd already gone to Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak the day before, but it was definitely worth it! It was a cloudy June day which made the setting even more mysterious. Very simple but nicely kept grounds of rolling hills and volcanic rock walls. The crater itself was one of the more bizarre and intriguing natural landscapes I've seen. If you've seen the movie   The Mummy Returns,   it's like the end of that! The surrounding grounds are lovely and you have a great view of the mountains all around you. Would be a very romantic place as well, if you're with your partner. Great place for a picnic or just a long stroll! However, if you're looking for activities and souvenirs and snacks and other touristy things, you'll have to go elsewhere. Fortunately there is a bus stop right outside to go to Jeju City.

In the summer heat, Manjanggul is the perfect place to escape the heat. It's quite cold inside, and water drips from the ceiling. I changed into jeans and a light sweater before going in, which was perfect. The texture of the cave is fascinating! There are good informational English placards that explain how the cave formed. The floor of the cave is quite bumpy, so take care not to trip.It's a popular destination but getting there and leaving can be time-consuming unless you are with a tour. I took a bus from the Bijarim Forest to get to the cave, which dropped us off right at the cave. The bus leaving right from Manjanggul only leaves once an hour, so I recommend checking the bus departure times before you go into the cave and plan your stay accordingly. Otherwise, there are taxis but the drivers are rudely persistent, charge a non-negotiable flat price, and refuse to go by the meter. They kept pestering us the entire hour we waited for the bus, even after we rejected many times and had begun ignoring them.

In previous trips to Seoul, i had passed by the theatre in Myeongdong many times but never thought of seeing the show.Then a friend who saw it recommended it highly.And I'm glad I did.It was very entertaining and tge skills on show were awesome. I doubt if anyone in the crowd did not have a good time.The performers interacted well with the audience and the lucky patrons who were chosen to participate looked like they thoroughly enjoyed themselves.Tickets are reasonably priced and there are often discounts to be had if you look hard.Treat yourself to this if you get the chance.The show has been to more than 50 countries around the world.

It is windy up top so you might not stay atvthe summit for more than 30 mins but the views are breathtaking. This is not a boring hike as some may say. It is a classic in these parts

I'm from Hawaii, but this cave was very impressive, not to mention a welcome reprieve from the heat and humidity!Walking on wet lava rock is not for the faint-of-heart, so wear a good pair of tennis shoes that can provide some traction, because it is slippery!

I'm an American living in South Korea. On the west coast of the United States there are many hikes and every weekend I was on a trail. So, when I saw Hallasan I thought it would be a peice of cake. I was very wrong. It doens't look hard but the trail is cut straight up, (no switch backs). After reaching the top you know that you climbed a mountain and it feels good.
