I'll start by saying I love caves, they've always fascinated me and this one doesn't disappoint. The Cave is a couple thousand year old lava tube with a really neat walking path through it. The tube itself is 7 km long, but the tourist portion is 1 km in length. The cave itself is a bit dark, but it also sets the mood of the cave. I went in the summer and the cave was at least 5 degrees C cooler than the outside and had some condensation (closed toed shoes a must). The only downside would be the crowds, but still didn't take too much away from the experience. Very much recommended if you visit Jeju Island!

Ilchubong has a dramatic history of formation. Some parts of the areas had been submerged underwater and lifted up while others sunk underwater over millions of years ago due to earth movements and volcanic activities. Even though the lower part slopes gently and make relatively fairly easy to climb the upper part is slightly steeper. Generally there are so many steps to reach the top,climbing can be pretty challengingfor the less fit. However, the view from the top is rewarding.

Il faut vraiment etre un connaisseur de l'histoire coreenne pour venir ici. Mais meme sans l'etre c'est interessant, en particulier si on s’interesse a la calligraphie chinoise. .L'acces est gratuit.Peu d'explication en anglais.

If you've never been to a traditional Korean market, the Jeju Five Day Market is a wonderful introduction, and if you are an old hand at these sort of things, then you will enjoy Jeju's style. Pros: Roughly the size of a football field, there's a little of everything at this market. And every market is a little different too, so it stays interesting even over multiple visits (seasonal goods are fantastic here). Fruits, vegetables, herbs, roots, jams, honey, traditional medicines, gardening supplies (including seedlings); clothing, shoes, traditional crafts, a sprinkling of electronics now and then, kitchenware, furniture, rugs, and a whole host of things you won't recognize. It's truly a bizarre bazaar, and I am hopelessly in love with the sights, sounds, and smells of this style of capitalism that hearkens back to a time of more hooves and mouths than credit cards and smartphones. Go! Try everything! Buy everything! You'll love it!Cons: Sensory overload. Severe introverts should farm their energy for at least a day prior to going to this market. Expect to be shoved, bumped into, pushed, and in every other possible way have your personal space invaded. The shouting can be persistent, and the din is incredible. Trying to park your car can induce migraine headaches, and the traffic jams that lead up to the parking can be even worse. People here are generally honest, but I urge you to be extra vigilant when you buy perishables. More than once I've gone home with a great deal, only to have it go bad the same night. Also, check around for prices. Often you will buy something and then find a better version at a lower cost just a meter away. And finally, don't hesitate to haggle: the   foreigner price   rule is definitely in effect at this market.

If you've never been to a Korean public bath then there are some things you should know. First go in and pay - currently it's 6000 Won for the baths (segregated by gender) and 8000 Won for both the bathes and the   jimjilbang   (which is a unisex area filled with different hot rooms to enjoy a sweat lodge style experience). You can stay as long as you want and even sleep there. I would never suggest doing so however since even though this is a standard option for most Korean baths and they are arguably the cheapest place to sleep in Korea they are also loud sometimes crowded and generally pretty damned uncomfortable for sleeping. You will be given a set of shorts and a shirt. If you are large like me you can expect to have to cram yourself into them. Use the key provided to find a locker in your respective undressing area. Don't worry even though it doesn't seem like you should be naked in this area it's okay.From here you will go into the showering/bathing area. DO NOT get into any of the pools without first scrubbing yourself down. Soap is provided as well as some abrasive washcloths but you will need your own shampoo which you can buy in the changing area. Once you are clean you can enjoy a variety of different temperature pools and sauna options ranging from the almost freezing to the almost boiling. After you are finished soaking you can either shower again and leave or put on the shorts provided and go to the jimjilbang common area. Here you will find several different hot rooms including a traditional mud hut style outside that looks like a giant wasps nest. Some of these rooms are intense so work your way up to the higher temperatures don't stay in for too long and remember to drink lots of water. Food and beverages will be available in the common area so remember to stash some cash in your shorts before going to the jimjilbang. You can also relax on the floors in the common area watching some bad TV or just snooze. There are a few other nooks and crannies you can explore but this is a basic sketch of what you can expect. Once you're done at the jimjilbang you can go back for another shower and soak dry off enjoy some complimentary personal hygiene products (although I urge caution with their aftershave) get dressed and go home.  Yongduamhaesu Land is a decent example of a Korean bath. It's fairly clean and has some nice facilities. It's also pretty busy so expect high volumes of people especially tourists. Oh and for all you   foreigners   out there of non-Asian decent please expect an awkward amount of interest in your body especially those regions that you'd rather not have a room full of Koreans staring at. I know this is weird and to be perfectly blunt I wish they could be more circumspect with their curiosity but they don't really mean any harm. It's an unspoken obsession amongst humans - particularly men and especially Korean men - to compare genitals. Koreans just tend to be more obvious about it in ways that might signal either sexual interest or a punch in the mouth in non-Korean cultures. Have patience.

If you're into nature, love moderate hiking and stairs climbing, love to see sea and city thru the bird eye view, taking plenty of photos of nature formations and also selfies (or wefies), then wjy don't you go to Seongsan Ilchubong, Jeju Island, South Korea. Designated as Unesco World Heritage site, this mountain is one the best place that you can hike and feels the wind blows your hair or maybe yourself too. The combination of flat lands and also the hike to the peak gives you an unforgetable memories. With each steps you take to climb to the peak, you will encounter several break spots or photo viewing for you to stops and take photos. Half way thru to the peak, you can see the entire city below you and starting to see the seas too. Hike to the peak, you can the see majestic view of the Seongsan Ilchubong itself. To your front is wide sea and the flat land (heard that it's actually a death volcano, correct me if i'm wrong) and to your behind is the view of the city and their surrounding. Don't forget to take photo at the peak's signboard. The formation of the clouds and the sun may give you the awe moments to you, especially when it reflects to the sea surfaces. When you go down from the peak, try to look at your right. You may see people going down to feels the sea water. Mind you, sometimes the wind blows a bit strong.  You need to pay for entrance and you don't like to hike to the peak, the ground is enough for you. Me and my friend, went there on Nov'15. Do try to enjoy nature at their best.

If you're into exploration and discovering a destination's unique treasures, this is one place on Jeju Island, South Korea not to miss.  Located in a beautiful park-like setting, Manjanggul Cave permits you to descend hundreds of feet below the surface in a cave system that was created by lava flows from a now-extinct volcano.  The cave system constitutes the largest lava tube in the world and is accessible by foot.  Wear comfortable shoes that have good traction (like hikers or sneakers) and expect to get a little wet as the interior has water dripping from the ceilings in places that are unavoidable.  Nevertheless, this experience is a must-do for anyone who likes adventure.  The floor of the cave can be wet (necessitating the need for footwear with good traction) and the temperature in the cave is approximately 55* year-round.  Dress accordingly.  There are many interesting features to see and experience in Manjanggul Cave.  Allow about 90 minutes (minimum) to walk the entire length and be able to see all that it has to offer.  Although you don't get to experience total darkness as in some cave systems, this cave is more than intriguing with the lava formations that remain and the expansiveness of the interior areas.  You might also encounter some inhabitants of the cave.  Anyone who enjoys nature would find this place particularly appealing.

If you?re driving around Jeju Island, this place is a must. It took me a while to figure out what was the big deal (mysterious) about this road but after I figured out the way it was described to be, it was definitely cool and somewhat mysterious. So here it goes: you drive upto the starting point of mysterious road and put the car in neutral gear. The road certainly looks like and uphill, however the car drives forward until 100m to the end of the mysterious road. Anti-gravity huh? I?m not sure of the scientific explanation for this phenomenon, but I recommend you experience this if you?re driving around Jeju Island. Takes only 15 minutes and certainly worth the time and experience!
If you want to see something colorful glass art work, you don't want to miss this spot. There are many nice glass art sculpture all around the park. Good chance to take a memorable picture in there.

If you plan to go to Udo, spend at least a day here. Enjoy every part of Udo : Udo Olle Trail, Udo lighthouse, Beach. Trying the popular Halasan Fried Rice and peanut ice cream, so yummy. Really enjoy my time in Udo, fresh air, clear blue water, white sand, warm local people, beautiful scenery. This is what I picture Jeju in my mind. Everything in Udo are beautiful for me. I will regret if I didn't come here, this is my favourite part in Jeju.

If you need a good work out, this forest in Jeju is worth paying a visit. The autumn 10C air is perfect, although the leaves were only starting to blend with the sun, you can imagine the shades of red, orange and yellow if it's at its peak!  The old nutmeg trees provided good photo opportunities for those with a passion for nature.

If you love Hello Kitty, I think you will really like it. That being said, though, I think it is better for adult fans than for kids. For the most part, it is a Hello Kitty museum with displays for looking at. There's not really much for kids to do, other than look. The cafe was good, and cute. The gift shop had some cool stuff I hadn't seen elsewhere, but it is pricey. All in all, I would say that I am really glad I saw it, because it was super cute, but it wouldn't warrant a return visit.

If you live on Jeju you have to do it at least once. I'm from the West where the mountains are huge so, when I saw Hallasan it looked like a piece of cake. How wrong I was. Mountain trails in the West take you up by switchbacks but the tail up Hallasan goes straight up  and straight down. There are no switchbacks. Only about a million steps to climb. I'm not saying that there is anything wrong with that......just be prepared. Start early and take water.When I went up I thought I was going to die. It didn't help that there was this grandpa in flip-flops who passed me on the way up and then he passed me again as I was still on my way up and he was coming down and then he passed me again going up as I was still on my way up. How embarrassing was that?????? Very embarrassing!As far as the climb went, it was great. I felt like two cent going up but once on top I felt like a million bucks. Clean air and blue sky. Views of the whole island.One good thing about going down is that it's all down hill. I do a lot of complaining about it but I've been up there five times now so  there must be something I love about it.If you do go up and you see that grandpa tell him hi from me. He passed me so many times I feel like I know him. ;)

If you like caves, then you have to visit Manjunggul Cave. It is simply fascinating! It is an extremely cheap entry fee and an easy kilometer walk inside the lava tube. Though the weather outside was rainy and wet, we thought the cave would be drippy and wet as well. It was quite dry. The interior is spacious and equipped with fairly good lighting along the guided route. For kids learning about volcanoes and the structures of the earth, this is a great field trip.

If you like cave, do not miss out.my partner pick this one as a highlight in Korea. It's very huge cave.only open 1/3 ish though, you can walk on actual lava stones all the way.* MUST bring jacket or something to warm you up and wear proper shoes. its quite cool inside and wet.
If you like bonsai, tulips and great landscaping, this botanic garden is for you. I particularly loved the hundred year old bonsai trees delicately nurtured to inspire visitors of its natural beauty.

If you go to Jeju Island, this is a good place to go. There is a Kitty Cafe inside, it is the same as those in Seoul. Apart from the Cafe, there is also an souvenir shop, you can buy those limited edition products there. If you drive there, you may need to wait for the parking space during peak hours.
if you go by walk don't bother to go there, you can't notice anything apart from cars driving very slow

If you find yourself in Jeju (May to June preferably) Halla is something that must be done. As the island is so small you can see the mountain no matter where you are. It sits there calling to you to climb it and you should. It is not one the most difficult climbs I have ever had, the end was a bit bad because there had be a storm that had damaged parts of the path. It is absolutely picturesque especially for the colour changes you see. I would suggest going up the easy path and going down the easy path for those who have trouble managing such large mountains, but no matter which you choose just go. The canteen at the halfway point was only serving instant noodles, so bring your own grub to be safe. Also have your pickup scheduled accordingly as transportation on the bottom parts of certain paths are almost non-existant.

If you enjoy nature, hiking one of the olle trails is a must-do while you're in jeju. It will not be an easy hike and not all parts of the trail are scenic but there are sufficient sights to blow you away and be left in awe of nature. This is also the best way to experience jeju's natural beauty (after all this is what its most famous for and not for teddy bears). It is also arguably the least touristy thing to do during your trip here. You can do as long or as short of the trails as you like; there are trails passing through hot tourist destinations where you'll see many tourist buses, local villages, rice fields, even resorts. You'll walk on sand, on rocks by the ocean, and if you time it correctly you'll be able to catch a gorgeous sunset along jeju's coastline. Be sure not to get stuck in a remote area after sunset as it can be difficult to get out. If you're doing a multi-day hike, there are many pensions located along the olle routes and you can just pop in for a night.Suggest to go with at least one other person in case you get lost (there are some places where the markings are not so visible/well maintained). If you rented a car, dont drive. Wear comfortable shoes and bring lots of water and snacks!

If you are into rocks, earth and geology thing, then this place is for you. The visit costs you less than 5000won and would probably take you an hour to finish the entire route.Take your time to read all the usefull information and appreciate the wonders of nature

If you are intending to go for the sunrise climb, please bring your own torchlight as lighting is minimal. About 2/3 of the climb comprise of a steep ascend. Not for the weak-hearted or those with circulation problems. It's physically challenging on the heart, not so much on the legs.Personally, a day climb (rather than a dawn climb) is better as you can see the view from the various heights. At the top, there are benches to sit and appreciate the view. Coming down was the easy bit as the stairs are well designed for the descend.

If you are in the Seogwipo-city area and only a short time in Je-Ju this is a great find. A traditional house, a story of a great S. Korean artist, a nicely designed park and a street of small arty shops.

If you are going with little kids, definitely go. But otherwise it's just OK though I would say worth a visit if you are bored. Pretty much all the information is in Korean, but then again doesn't take much to identify the teddy bear version of Steve Jobs or Albert Einstein ;) The place has two floors of teddy bears, and I must say after about 25 teddies they all start looking the same. This was close to our hotel and it was raining so we paid a visit. I would advise the museum to put more info in English as Jeju is becoming more internationlised in terms of tourists.

If you are fanatic about nature then you would probably really like this park. However if you enjoy nature but are more swept away by breath-taking scenery then in my opinion you will be really disappointed. We did the Seogwipo trail and for the effort involved the reward was just not enough. The trail took around two hours each way, and part of that was over some extremely difficult terrain. It's not that step, but walking over really large stones and boulders for over an hour can get really tiring, especially when there is no view to distract you, you are just surrounded by trees, There is nothing to see at all for the most part! At the end of the trail, the mountain lake and view of the valley is nice, but nothing that special or amazing. We were there in low season and even then it was extremely crowded, so you never have the feeling that you are really hiking a mountain. I wouldn't do it again.

If you are ever in Jeju-do, you have to make a day trip to Udo... Udo means   Cow Island   - so named because the shape of the island looks like a cow lying down... but try as I might, the island on a map doesn't look like a cow to me, but I guess the ancients who named it looked at things differently from me...  :PYou can drive your Jeju rental car onto the Udo ferry for a fuss free 15min journey over to this lovely island. Once there, you can tour the island by car! There are many beaches you can choose to hangout at, my favourite is Hagosudong beach for it's crystal clear waters and fine white sand. however Koreans aren't really into bikini culture, the Korean women go to the beach in long sleeved t-shirts, hats and umbrellas... So if you wanna sunbathe, you have all that white sand to choose your fav. spot! there are many cafes on Udo for you to grab a burger or sandwich for lunch if you are into western fare and also many restaurants that serve seafood Korean style. The seafood comes from the   Hae-nyo   sea-women who dives around Udo to haul in fresh Abalone, sea-urchin, octopus and the like for our enjoyment. As you tour around the island, you will be able to see these sea-women in action in various parts of the sea. My family and I love the relaxed vibe of this little island. In Udo, you can also take a speedboat tour of the natural caverns dotting the cliffs and coasts. the speedboat drives all the way into these caverns for you to observe up close the cave formations. This is my second visit to Udo and I recommend it to any nature loving, beach going traveller.... :)

If you are a UNESCO World Heritage Site ticker, this is on the list. I?m not a cave fan, so walking into the lava tube, taking a u-turn and walking the same way out in the damp and dark, jostled by rude kids on a field trip wasn?t one of the highlights of my trip. In any case, no regrets going there because it would be weird not to go at all -- it?s a Jeju landmark, and I would have wondered what I missed if I didn?t come here.If you?re checking out the Seongsan Ilchubong, it's pretty close by (if you're in a car). You should allot another hour for this. It?s not too far from the Jeju airport, too.The thing is, once is enough ? if I were to come back to Jeju and my friends insist that we go here, I would let them go ahead and hang out somewhere else.Like the title says, it's a cave.------Tip for parents:I tried to warn a family with a baby that it?s not the best place if you have little kids, but they ignored me. Hello, it?s dark, with water dripping and the terrain is uneven rock. You have to walk down some steep stairs for about half a minute to start your tour. There are a lot of people, and sometimes they bump into you because they can't see well in the dark. That family was going to take a baby stroller into this cave. Wah, suit yourself. It was so insane. If they trip in the dark, the baby could be hurt.

If this place was in Europe I am sure the entrance fee would be double or triple, and it would have a giant shop at the end. This place is full of hard to believe facts, artsy stuff and little experiments. To be honest, I would really like to see a little shop at the and, so that I could send a postcard or add a pencil to my collection if not buying a few sciencey gifts. Definitely spare some time for this place, you will enjoy!

If possible, I would recommend visiting this garden on a cloudy day or partly sunny. There is something peaceful about the weather and the garden that makes you want to stay forever. All the bonsai trees are beautiful and wonderfully taken care of. You can see how much great care was given to these trees. The plants, the rock artworks, and the people all create a very peaceful and very unified picture. This place is fitting for people of all ages. I would recommend everyone visiting this place.

If it’s springtime?or even summer or fall-- that means it’s also time to think about visiting beautiful Gapado, or Gapa Island, which sits just off the southwestern tip of the Korean resort island of Jeju. ? Located some 5.5 km (3.42 mi.) offshore, Gapado is a quick ferry run from the port village of Moseulpo (maybe 20 min.)Gapado nearly got the distinction of being South Korea’s southern-most point, but that title went to nearby Marado.? Some tourists want to go there just to say they’ve been, but Gapado is noteworthy in its own right.? Gapada is home on its .84 sq. km? to about 250 residents.? The island has a picturesque school, a church and a Buddhist temple.? There are a couple Korean restaurants and small stores.? But, it’s a good idea to take bottled water and snacks with you, particularly if you plan to hike or bike all the way around the island.? You can bring your own bike, or perhaps rent one there.? Walking (Gapado has a 5k hiking trail that is part of Jeju’s famous Olle Course) or biking/electric scooter likely will be your only transportation choices, as there are no fossil-fueled vehicles on Gapado… But more about that in a bit.What makes it so special there?? Gapado offers spectacular views of the iconic mountain peaks or “sans” back to the north on Jeju, including Sanbangsan, Gunsan, Songaksan, Gogeunsan, Dansan and the Big Daddy of All Sans, Halla…the massive, central shield volcano that formed Jeju Island and the highest peak in South Korea.Equally impressive are Gapado’s golden-green barley fields, surrounded by traditional “batdam” stone agricultural walls.? The crop begins sprouting in late winter and reaches its full glory in late spring.? Gapado’s tradition of barley cultivation dates back to the 1840s and is celebrated annually with the Gapa Green Barley Festival. (Dates for 2015 are April 18- May 10.)Back to that transportation thing…well, barley is not the only thing green about Gapado.? Wind turbines, solar panels and other renewable, sustainable forms of energy are now being used on the island as part of a plan to make it one of the world’s first carbon-free islands, maybe THE first…. Summing up:? Good points:? outstanding natural beauty and photo ops in all directions; fresh air; clear aqua-hued seas that reveal black lava rocks; abundant hiking; colorful neighborhoods festooned with murals, recycled art and traditional Korean cultural artifacts;? site of annual Gapa Green Barley Festival? (April 18-May 10, 2015)Be sure to have on hand:? bottled water and small snacks; comfortable shoes; sunblock;? sunglasses; and a hat that won’t blow off easily; a stroller for very young children, layered clothing for coolish days.? There is little shade on the island, so be on guard against dehydration or sunburn on those hot or even excessively windy days.? Getting there:? Take an Intercity Bus from most points on Jeju Island to Seogwipo Main Terminal, and from there, a local bus to Moseulpo .? There is a short walk to the ferry from the busstop.? Ferries generally run twice a day, but as schedules and fares can change, it’s probably best to check for specifics through the Korean Travel Hotline: dial 1330 in country or outside Korea: +82-2-1330 or 1339 (Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese)

I'd highly recommend visiting 9.81 Park on your next trip to Jeju. This place is a lot of fun. The karts are in excellent condition, the course offers some amazing sea views and the staff are very professional and helpful. Definitely worth a visit.
Ice sculpture, Trick art, VR and 5D experience

I’ve visited Jeju in mid-April with my friend and we’ve gotten John to bring us around in Jeju. It was a great experience, John was punctual and well-articulated(telling us fun facts/history) along the tour. Also, he took initiatives to show us more spots throughout the tour for “instagram worthy” photos! We will definitely get John as our tour guide if we come back to Jeju again!

I would die to visit Udo again, it's a tiny island and can be covered in one day with a scooter which can be rented once you're off the ferry but I'd love to stay a few day next time so I can really enjoy the island.  Everything here is like straight out of a book, the beaches, the hiking trails, the lighthouses, the food, OMG the food.  Anyone visiting this island, I recommend starting early morning and renting a bicycle, a scooter if you're good with directions or pay for a bus ticket that with have drop off locations as well as pick up so you can explore at leisure and when you're ready to go to your next location, just stop by one of their pick up locations and you're ready to go.

I woke up really early to get ready for this hike. I took the first bus 281 from the old bus terminal in Seogwipo leaving at 6am. We arrived at Seongpanak trail entrance about half an hour later. I did this trail mid January and you need crampon for this. Personally, I don?t like slippery surface so crampons really give me the confidence. But I saw people on the hike didn?t have crampons. Some other people hiked in their running shoes. Snow was thick but you basically walked on top so I guess You don?t necessarily need hiking boots. Unless you go off trail, the snow will be knee deep. It was such a nice feeling to see everybody get up and early to start the hike when it?s still dark out. The hike up was not very challenging and it took me about 4.5 hours. I?m an extremely slow walker. Keep in mind that there is cut off time. If you start too late and couldn?t get up to the last shelter on Seongpanak trail before 12pm, you are not allowed to go to the summit. The view at the top was so beautiful. It was very windy though. I took Gwaneumsa trail down since I wanted to change views. That was challenging. My knees hurt so bad even though I already wore knee braces. It?s shorter than Seongpanak trail but it took me almost the same amount of time. There was one part quite steep and I didn?t notice the rope which you can hold on to, I slid down and broke my trekking pole. Apart from being slippery, the trail is quite rocky and by the end of the day, after a beautiful sunny day, the snow started melting and made the trail very slushy. There was time I almost gave up, my whole body hurt and I started to get blister on my toes. When I got to the entrance of the trail, I took bus 475 for 10 mins to a university entrance station then changed to bus 281 to go back to Seogwipo. I guess you can take 281 directly from Gwaneumsa to Seogwipo but I didn?t know where it was so I followed the crowd. I totally recommend this hike.

I went to this museum just because a friend has suggested. Despite I am not a big fan of teddy bears this museum is really amazing! You will see the major events from the world history, famous singers and artists, as well as some scientists! I better don't tell everything not to ruin the surprise! There happens an Elvis Show at every hour or so. If you have time, definitely give it a go.

I went to jeju island to see some view like this and i can say this Park was beautiful one . I suggest everybody to visit jeju island in fall season because u can see colours and feel great weather . Park is actually for hiking but if u don't wanna go till top u can enjoy forest before getting top , take some snacks and drink with ureself because there is not many mart nearby just one small and limit one down of park .

I went there with my family members in a cloudy day. This place is composed with several parts of themes. Lake, play ground, short hiking with spa, and snack bars.My kids(9, 5yrs) really enjoyed the place with running, taking pictures, and eating.Even I visited in Jeju more than 10 times, this place is the most memorable place to visit. Because kids didn?t have any bother others.Additionally, there were packed with people and very noise when I waited for tour train. Then please be sure to keep you eyes on your kids. I visited there at the last of tour then I couldn't have enough time to hiking.However, I recommend you to take a walk at the picnic garden station (2nd stop).There are kids town and eco-land at Picnic garden station

I went early in the morning before the admission desk was opened and saw many walking up with torchlights. I went again in the afternoon and this time there was an admission charge and wad very crowded. There are restrooms at the foot of the rock and another on the way up. The toughest part would be the starting and it gets easier soon. It is a short walk up so pace yourself. The views and wind at the top was amazing. On the way down, look out for the diver women show which is at 1pm & 3.30pm. Look out for the rock resembling an eagle beak and the korean ironman

I went at July... quite a few steps down from entrance to cave and the floor is slippery with water...  You can feel the chill at entry, I suggest you remain in motion to avoid get cold..Walking around can be a challenge for some (especially for the elderly) since the floor is very rough and uneven, this is exacerbated by poor lighting in most parts throughout the cave.. a lot people used torches from phones to get around...It?s annoying for a inquisitive person as the half of the sign and info are Korean only... The interior of the space is pretty featureless... only two noticeable Lime stone caves are a lot more pretty, but it?s worth going if you are in the area and never been in a Lava Cave

I wasn't really keen on dropping by Teddy Bear Museum; but since our tour dropoff destination was literally across it, we decided to just check out the museum. I never expected that I'd enjoy it as much as I did. The museum is relatively small, but its attention to detail is amazing. Exhibits range from historical events, famous movies/characters (Titanic, Snow White, Disney), notable figures (Steve Jobs, Michael Jackson, Audrey Hepburn), famous works of art (Mona Lisa, The Thinker) among so many others. Highlights would be its Louis Vuitton bear as well as its immensely groovy Elvis Presley bear who would serenade you with the King's greatest hits.

I was there to lead a Sacred Circle Dance event in memory of the 4-3 Massacre, which was the most touching and powerful experience of group dance and solidarity. The following day I witnessed an amazing dance performance (Kim's troupe) as part of one of the services offered that week.- also touching. The level of art is very high. The architecture of the buildings speak loud and clear. Not to be missed - approach with reverence, and you too will be deeply moved.

I was really impressed by this museum, designed by the famous Japanese architet Tadao Ando. The architecture of the building and the beautiful garden make this place worth a visit, but the collection is also really interesting. I really loved the collection artefacts from the late Joseon period an the special exhibition 'Carriage to Heaven' that shows sangyeo (traditional funeral bier) and kkokdu (small statues used as decoration for the sangjyeo). The joyous artwork of Japanese artist Yayoi Kusama were a nice extra on top of all that.Not to be missed when visiting Jeju.

I was on tour with my parents thus the title. The art itself is pretty good. You have different artists interpreting sex in different ways. Just like a typical museum with labels this has one too. Don't miss out on reading what their art are called. It's pretty hilarious. There's a shop where you can buy   stuff   as well. The whole place is open to 18 year olds and above only.

I was hesitating to climb the mountain in the winter, but it is definitely a must do! It was so amazing with the snow. The path itself was 'easy' to walk and to follow. Tip: buy crampons at the start of the trail (12,000 krw (I think) for the cheap ones).

I was here with my family. Thinking what is so mysterious about this road? Its just a road, with nature on the sides. It?s just another ?normal? road. Sigh, a total waste of time.Until I reach the place, I was blown away! Not because of the strong wind (I was there when it was raining heavily with strong winds), but the mysterious part of this road. I was told to stay in the car, to witness the mystery of this road. The engine got turned off, hand brake was let gone, brakes were let gone too, the car automatically went up the slope by itself!It is a new experience here for me in Jeju, a totally worth of time to visit!

I was clearly the wrong age, the wrong gender, and the wrong nationality to visit this place. Despite that, I enjoyed it somewhat.  Even though I had never heard of any of these artists, aside from Psy, it was fun to see some of the exhibits.  The hologram concert was pretty well done.If I had a Korean teenage daughter who loved to take selfies with celebrities, it would have been the highlight of her trip to Jeju.

I walked Routes 6 and 7 on 23rd-24th Oct 2017. The distance was 15km and 18km respectively.The weather was perfect - sunshine and cool breezes. These 2 routes are reputed to be the more beautiful ones. There are a couple of picture-perfect waterfalls and breath-taking shorelines along the way. 2,000Won per entry is charged for the waterfall. Along the way are small fishing ports where one can get to taste local seafood. There are small cafe along the way too, where one can sit, relax and taking in the beautiful scenery. Coffee is +/-4,000won. As I was staying at the starting point, from the finishing point I took taxi back It costs about 8kWon. Oh yes, there are clean restrooms every 5km or so. Just a little minus point, the blue & red ribbon is not easy to be found in urban area. So try looking for the blue line on the tar road.

I visited this sight with my brother yesterday and it was so cool! The lava tube was pretty intense. The walls were wide and the ceilings were tall. There were also lava shelves, balconies, etc, made from lava flows. It felt so cool to walk on the hardened lava, knowing that it flowed once as a bright and burning river of melted, hot hot hot rock!Stairs wind down from the entrance (an awesome gaping hole of an entrance), and it leads you down to the lave tube...It was about a 1 km long walk. Only 1 km out of the whole 7 km long lava tube was available to the public. Still, it was, an exciting walk. There are also signs along the way that describe the parts of the lava tube and brief you on how they came to be. I recommend you check it out whenever you visit Jeju Island! Thanks for reading my review!P.S. There is an admission fee, but it's inexpensive and affordable!

I visited this as part of an inclusive tour so I cant comment on the value of the entrance fee.  This is a   musuem   of pictures and exhibits that enable you to have amusing photos taken of yourself.  It would be little fun on your own.  You need a friend to take photos of you and if you have several it becomes quite hilarious.  In the Jungmun Resort area.

I visited Seongeup Folk Village as part of the tour package to Jeju Island that was provided as free gift by a company that I need not mentioned here. As an Asian and having extensively travelled throughout Asia. I am familiar have experience all sorts of tricks and gimmicks. The first tip that this was another hard sell stop is that there is no time limit for the stop. Prior to this stop, we visited the famous Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak, they insisted that we returned to the bus by 1 hour which is not enough to really enjoy the place. However, we were told we can take all the time we need at Seongeup. Then a nice looking old lady who can speak Mandarin were waiting to greet us and give us a tour of the place. I was curios why no such tour guide were organised for Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak. The whole tour of the village was short 15 minutes, most of the info she provided I can easily find out from internet, then we were ushered into a room in one 'village building' where she proceed to let taste and test their natural products and tell us how miraculous is the products, the tea, the honey, horse bones and horse cream. The whole presentation took twice as long as the village tour. Then she went on and on and on about how healthy are the people and it is due to the miracles of horse bones. I mean come on. There are horses the world over. Surely if horse bones are the key to living longer and younger,.Someone other than the Jeju people would have known about it. Then next she talks about pricing which I almost fell out of my chair. Korean Won 190,000 or USD 185 for horse bones pellet? I am not sure how many fools are there in the world that bought into this ludicrous claims. Right there and then I wanted to leave. She then changes tack and describe how they money will help preserve the village, fund village children education healthcare etc etc. I heard that before in almost all my travel. Apparently, some of my fellow tour travellers are interested, so they stayed in the room while I explored the 'village'. The area is very small, most of the 'buildings' are similar to the one that I was in and there are various product demo sessions going on in other 'buldings'. In the end, we spend a total a 2 hour there and the organizer waited until everyone got onto the bus. It so different from the Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak stop where they chased back onto the bus and even went into the washroom to look for missing passengers. Just for non-asian travellers tour organiser gets sales commissions if the tour groups buy something. So they benefit if when they spend more types at such places rather then the actual sight that you wanted to see.

I visited Hallasan in early March, some parts of the trail were still covered in snow. At the lower area I had some difficulties because of the melting snow. It's doable without crampons or walking sticks, but be careful. Past Witseoreum shelter, it's recommended to have walking gear. I have an average condition and I did the Yeongsil trail up in 2h15 and the Eorimok trail down in less then 2h. I think it's better to do the opposite. Yes, Yeongsil trail is longer, but easier. The Eorimok trail is covered with rocks, and if you don't watch out, it is easy to twist your ankle when coming down.

I visit the place with the tour I bought in Jeju city. The place is higher than expectation. There are several parts of the park including the real underground lava tube which is amazing. The folk village also decorated really nice. When I visit the place, it is about 5 degree c so theres not many flowers in that time. Theres also a small zoo inside as well!

I took the eorimok trail which took about 2.5 hours to get to the top with the rest rooms, the first part of the trek is hard work and quite strenuous. After reaching the top I took the yeongsil trail back down which had some of the most stunning views along the way. As I came by bus the walk down from the yeongsil trail to the yeongsil ticket office where the bus stop is located takes another 40minuts or so depending on the pace. I Would highly recommend visiting this area and trying the trails.

I took bus 281 from Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal at 6.24am and get off at Seongpanak stop. Start hiking at 7.30am. It took me about 4 hours to reach the top. It was hot at top. I brought 1 liter of water and some buns and it was okay for me.I walked down the Gwaneumsa Trail. It took another 4 hours. If you want to go back to Jeju Intercity bus terminal take bus 475 from Gwaneumsa to Shancheondan Altar and switch to bus 281 to the Jeju Intercity bus Terminal.Every bus fare is 1,200 won.

I thought this place was mainly for kids before coming, but I was wrong. The artworks inside are very imaginative and historical. There are artworks mimic historical figures (e.g. Einstein); reflect a certain historical period, or historical events. Highly recommended!

i thought the museum sounded stupid but it was actually really cute!!! there were so many scenes set up with stuffed animals on the first floor.  they were so creative!  then you can you to the second floor and take pictures.  there's the rock band set up, the proposal bear, and many more.  there are also famous works of art re-done with teddy bears. finally there's the gift shop.  everything is over priced but you can't expect anything else...

I think this will be a fun experience for the family especially with small kids. I am not young anymore but it was rather interesting and fun for me as well. Not as easy as I thought and it took me 30mins to navigate through...for price of 3300won, it is a pretty economical way to spend a few light hearted hours after all the serious geographical sights in Jeju.

I studied the seoqwipo bus route and decided to bring my family for a day trip to Udo Island. I stayed in Jungmun Resort vicinity. It was easy to catch bus 282 from here and made a transfer for direct bus to Udo Passenger Terminal. Upon arrival, after filling up the necessary details and proof of passports竊we went to the cruise Departure point. Luckily we chosen a weekday for this trip. The queue was short. In the cruise ship, we could find seats. A 15 min ride and we were greeted by several e-scooters and shop houses. Here, you could settle for lunch. But if it was too early for you, several sightseeing spots come with line of restaurants. We took the circular bus (white color van) which we thought was the best choice. Every stop you were  required to queue to abroad. This bus went to most attractions including black sand & Udo lighthouse. The bus route was also the route for E-scooters /car. Do be careful for safety sake. Returning from Udo Island was amazing : we could not find a bus stop that for the same bus number  supposed to bring us back to Seoqwipo! Nevertheless, luckily we had alternative plan ! we took a bus that brought us to Gimpo Airport. Got a decent dinner and then took limo bus 600 directly to our accomodation, alighting at bus stop named Jungmun Resort Entrance. This DIY by public transport comes in cheap!This trip you need a whole day.

I stayed 4 night in Hamdeok Beach. If you are visiting Jeju for the very first time, you might want to move around because Jeju is quite big. Hamdeok is a great location to start your trip. It takes 20 mins by car, 30~40 mins by bus from Jeju International airport. It has many bus lines which offers you easy access to Airprot, Mountain Halla, Jeju city centre and even Seogwipo. I love the beach itself, but also there are lots of place to eat and chill. If you like to camp, there is a camping & caravan park at the end of beach. I loved it !!

I started off by lowering my expectations for this tourist stop.  The building is a little outdated from the outside and I wasn't sure how good it could be.  The whole family was pleasantly surprised.  We learned about the fun character and her family and friends.  Everything was well done and there was more to the museum than expected.  My daughter and son both had smiles from ear to ear, making for a great day.

I started from Eorimok Trail and came down by Yeongsil Trail. Eorimok trail starts off with steps then followed by wooden walk way before you reach Witseoreum Shelter. Shelter is a basic one with just toilets and resting rooms. We took around 2hrs to reach the shelter. Yeongsil trails starts off (from shelter) with wooden walk way then followed by countless stairs. You are like literally hiking on the edge of the mountain up/down. We took 1.5hrs to descend.Definitely recommend going down by Yeongsil trail rather than heading up due to the countless number of stairs. Both trails offer truly beautiful scenery and great for photos. I cant forget the view which the horizon mixed with the sea level that you can differentiate. Stunning!Advice:Bring food like energy bar, fruits etcBring water enough to reach water points. There are a couple of water points for you to refill along Eorimok trail. Else 1.5 litres for 2 pax is enough.Bring jacket and wear hiking shoes. Sports shoe is possible like what most korean did but be v careful as you will be walking on uneven rocks at times. Probably suggest ankle guard to go with sports shoe.For those who want to scale the mountain but doesn't wish to try the 9-10hrs climb to summit, i would really recommend this 2 trails.

I start my trekking 8.00AM at Gwanneumsa entrance and reach the summit around 12.30 and down to Seongpanak at 3.00PMPros : Magnificent various views(uphill), very easy downhillCons : No Hallasan view during uphillat this period, The weather is not so cold and the snow is still thick but robes and signs are intact. Good equipment is needed

I saw the review and decided to give it a try if I ever manage to find this location from the Korea GPS (we rent a car).Lucky enough we discover this road when we were heading to Love Lands. It's just right after it! So we drove to the starting point and off the engine and yes, it is moving! (Even the road is up hill a bit).Then we park the car aside and walk towards Love Land, but we saw many people were trying to walk in a backward manner up the road (which you suppose to feel hard/difficult bcos it is up hill), and backward manner down the road (which then strangely you felt like something is pulling you back even you are walking down hill) So I would say this is a very good experience and I'm glad that I experience this! But my friend didn't really feels anything when she tried the walk, so I guess it also depends on individual's physical sensitivity towards this mysterious road...

I really liked this part of the trip. We hiked up to the top, and I am a five month pregnant lady so you can do it too! The view of the city below is the most interesting view you are going to get from the top of the crater. The top of the crater itself isn't that spectacular. It was very pretty and fun! Also we happened to be there around the same time as the lady divers so we watched that and it was pretty interesting. When we were there in December they were doing shows around 1:30 and 3:30. You should definitely come here. There are also little restaurants and shops at the bottom if you are hungry!

I really enjoyed wandering through Hallasan National Park. I spent 4 days here, and was quietly impressed. At times there were way too many hikers, as they often come by the bus load, but mostly you were alone with your thoughts and the environment. The trails were well marked out, and easy to follow (even for people who don't read Korean). There was plentiful assistance if you get lost, but you felt like you were alone. The other tourists were polite, interested and friendly, definietly great for conversation. Jeju would have to be one of the highlights of this particular trip to South Korea. Would definietly makee the trip again.
I really enjoyed looking at the different waterfalls. It's a pity we're not allowed to swim as the warning sign said and I quote   You'll be died of heart attack  .

I read a few reviews saying how it?s just a park with trees and birds but I love this place! The greenery is beautiful, the air is fresh with a cool breeze and the cave system is entrancing. Being from a concrete city means all this is actually quite a refreshing change of environment for me. I don?t particularly care for the animals and birds being kept in too small enclosures though. But the scenery alone is enough to give it 4*.

I only went up this trail for 1.5 hours then came back as that was all I wanted to do.  I took my time and because I did that I saw deer which many people just walked by not noticing.  The trail is quite rocky.  You need good boots and cotton gear as you get quite hot. (All the Koreans dress up in this synthetic mountain looking gear and my husband who went all the way up said they were all nearly passed out on the side of the track from over heating!) Some people had these HUGE packs on their backs.  God knows what they were carrying! I had 2 bottles of water and dried octapus for sustenance and that was enough.  My husband who went all the way up used 7 bottles.  You can buy water at various places up the trail so you don't have to carry it all. There are a lot of people who do this ...or try...so it's best to start at 6am to beat the crowds.  There is also a train of sorts that you can pay for to take you most of the way up.  Not sure how much that costs.  There's a restaurant at the bottom surprisingly that's all in Korean,  no English, no pictures, which is odd for such a big tourist area. They have a beef soup, sushi rolls Kim bap and other stuff.  I'll upload a pic of the menu so you can get a translation before you go there.I'm not sure if you have to pay a fee to climb this track as we just walked up but on my return I did see a ticket box so maybe you do...

I moved to the U.S. (from Korea) 26 years ago when I was 15. I have been coming back to visit almost every year in the past 15 years or so and visited Jeju five times thus far. I don't get to take long weeks off from work, so I always try to pack as many activities into any given trip, so I squeezed this one in on my way back from a day trip to Udo (which is my favorite place in Korea). My 16-year-old kid, who almost never bothers to read through anything at museums, was taking photos and reading through the exhibits, which I found impressive.My appreciation for the island (and its residents) grew tenfold after the visit to this memorial hall. I made the climb on 22.11.2013 but few days before my climb, I have been keeping my eye on the weather on the mountain. The first snowstorm hit the mountain top a few days earlier and I know that my hike will be much difficult with the snow along the path to the top of the mountain. I chose to ascend from Gwanuemsa trail and descend from Seogpanak trail and I know that I have made the right choice. Starting from Gwanuemsa trail was much tougher, with the rocky pathways in the beginning to the steep climb in the middle of the trail and snowy trail all the way up to the mountain top. Along the way, there is no food on sale but there is a shelter for people to fill up their water, at the Samgakbong Shelter. The total length of Gwanuemsa Trail is about 8.7km and Samgakbong shelter is about 6km from the starting point. To make it here will take about 2 hrs of normal walk. There is also a toilet available here but the you wouldn't want to spend more time at this toilet. The trail after Samgaokbong SHetlter has obviously been much tougher, with a lot of steep steps, or even no steps at all (all covered by thick snow) and at some point, the is a need to pull the rope along the trail to move upwards. The efforts are all worthwhile upon reaching the top of the mountain. It is good to come on a clear day because the view along Gwanuemsa trail especially upon approcahing the mountain top is spectacular.At the top of the mountain, the wind can be really strong. Be prepared with the chill and wear enough layer to prevent from getting cold. As mentioned, I descend from Seogpanak trail and this is somehow a boring trail. The total length is about 9.5km but all I can see is trees along the way. There is nothing much to see but it was quite a flat trail that make it the choice among many hikers. There are food on sale at the Samgakbong Shelter, and also a big toilet there. A good stop for hikers to build up their energy before continuing their hike. Crampon also on sale for 5000 won. Overall, it was a fresh and good place for first time traveller. If there is a chance to come back to Hallasan, I will sure try the other 2 trails on the western side of the mountain.

I loved this seemingly unassuming place that I would have never really thought of visiting.  It was one of the most interesting and beautiful places I visited in Jejudo Island.  It is definitely a   must do  , as they say in Disney World!  We would have loved to spend more time there.  It's not just a park with a bunch of rocks so don't miss out!  It's like a natural museum/art gallery of indigenous Jejudo volcanic rocks with a splash of the island's history.  Highly recommended to spend a minimum of 3-4 hours here!!

I loved this place!!! Maybe because I love teddy bears and collect them. But objectively, I think they did a wonderful job to dress the bears up in adorable costumes and arrange them in all sorts of different themed settings. You start at the 3rd floor and walk down to the 1st. My favourite was the 2nd floor - even though the exhibits are encased in glass, I could put my own little bears (yes, I brought my own bears with me on this trip) on the glass and take pictures with them (no flash allowed). Some of the bears have even moving parts and some are life-sized. There is a scheduled musical and dance performance by Elvis bear and friends, which my parents enjoyed. At the outdoors area, you can take photos with life-sized bears in interesting poses and themed settings and there is even a clock that chimes hourly and is accompanied by bears dancing with the chimes. There is a cafe and a souvenir shop in the ground level and you can take pictures with panda bears (not real of course) and other cute bears, and buy a souvenir bear home (but price is quite ex).

I loved my hike in Hallasan. We were a couple and we decided to take the 'most challenging trial' - Gwaneumsatrail (8.7 km).  There are four Hallasan trails on and around the mountain, but only two of these trails will take you all the way up to the volcano?s crater lip ? theGwaneneumsa trail is one of these, theSeongpanaktrail is the other one. It is important that you check beforehand which trial is open, because it depends on the weather forecast. In my case all the 4 trials were partially open which meant that the crater lip was not accessible unfortunately. There is a website you  check (in Korean) or you can simply do what I did and ask the staff at the reception of the hotel. Each trials is easily accessible by bus, however the buses are not that frequent - for example 1 every hour for the Gwaneneumsa train, so you might need a bit of planning. Our trail was accesible for 6 out of the 8.7 km and took us to the first shelter (1500m elevation) the hike took us.6 hours back/forth including a quick lunch break; the pace wasn't that high but we weren't that slow either. If you want to access the crater lip, one think that you need to bear in mind is that you need to make it to the first shelter by 12-13 depending on the season (November was 12.00pm).Another thing to remember is that there is no convenience store or food vendor available during the hike, so you want to pack some food (kimbap is a good option) and water. As the hike itself, I really enjoyed it, you will feel immerse in the nature and you will enjoy a nice variety of vegetation depending on the altitude.

I loved Hamdeok Beach. We live in China and visited during Golden Week, assuming the rest of China would follow us to Jeju (as is typical during ANY holiday traveling in China) and we were pleasantly surprised to find that there were little to no Chinese tourists, or really any tourists in the neighborhood. It was quiet, clean and so peaceful! I would return again in a heartbeat.

I love visiting botanical gardens whenever i travel.? Unfortunately this is one of the poorer ones and I feel compelled to warn others!? With an entry charge of 7000 won per person, the value is low.Let's start with the greenhouse, it was just ok, nothing exciting.? During sunny days, the greenhouse is like a toasty oven as the ventilation is poor.? There is a variety of plants but they are not well organised or well kept.? Moreover, if you live in tropical parts of Asia, you would have seen most of the fruit trees and plants in neighbourhood backyards, which makes visiting it less exciting.Besides the greenhouse, there are themed areas - e.g. Korean garden, Chinese garden, French garden etc.? I was excited to see these options but after seeing what there was at the Korean and Chinese gardens, i just gave up on the rest.? I don't have the confidence the others will be worth the time.Management of the garden needs to be improved.? When I was there, they were renovating the entrance to the greenhouse.? As a result, the smell from the paint, varnish or whatever that toxic smelling thing is, is overwhelming.? Also, there was lots of noise.? Garden management would have better managed the renovation or at least inform visitors there is renovation going on.? I tried to offer feedback to the folks at the ticket counter on my way out but they didn't seem to care.In summary, there is nothing much to see and the garden is not well taken care of (even if there is no renovation going on, I would have rated it 'Poor').? Go to this place only if you have nothing else to do.The only plus I can think of is ... parking at free!

I love this place. If you are teddy bear lover like me, this is   the place   you have to visit. The Museum have all kind of teddy bear with theme or famous people such as Marilyn monroe or Charlie chaplin and more. Best part of all, you can buy one or a set of teddy bear for souvenir. A highly recommended place for Teddy bear lover or stuffed animal lover!

I like the view of the nature that surrounds this beautiful sunrise peak. The lush grass and the crashing waves against the cliff. The walkway was well built. What I didnt like was that as we had to start the climb quite early, it was pitch black and I was afraid of the darkness. So be sure to bring a torch and a jacket as it was raining and windy when I went in the morning.

I like the structure and set-up (the wooden boardwalk and handrails) and it looks majestic when I step past the ticket entrance. In the wide open space, it feels you have so much freedom to run around! If I had came earlier, I would have joined the Jeju Woman Diver performance (1.30pm and 3pm daily). No regrets since I headed to Udo before coming over and that was even more amazing! It requires certain level of stamina to climb up the flight of steps but fret not! There are stone chairs along the way, not many though, for you to sit and rest.The young kids and senior citizens are surprisingly the more consistent climbers up the stairs!Despite rating 4/5 due to my liking for the crater and natural structure, my actual experience there is only 2/5. There were large crowds of extremely rowdy and unruly chinese tour groups who spoke loudly at the top of their lungs, their tour guides shouting several times for them to gather and start moving down with no avail, zero consideration for other visitors who also paid the same ticket price to see this UNESCO World Heritage site. No way you can enjoy a peaceful moment and respect the site. They stood around various areas of the steps and took ages to complete their group photo. I have seen many tour groups before but the ones I encountered were horrible. It would have been good if the owner or caretaker of this site can do something to regulate and not spoil every visitor's experience at this place...

I learnt a lot about the brave women divers of Jeju by visiting this museum. I had hired a driver/tour guide for sightseeing in Jeju Island and got to visit some of my ?must see? attractions that were not close to my hotel. My tour guide was good so I had a great time. We visited this museum as part of our itinerary for the day, and I was glad we did. The museum charges a small entrance fee. I got to see a very interesting video about the history and lives of the women divers. There also a lot of painting, sculptures that is centered on the lives of these brave women. The museum is small but I liked it a lot. I came out more knowledgeable about the women and Jeju Island as a whole.

I kindly suggest this trail!!! We started the hiking from Gwaneumsa Temple, probably the most challenging trail. The entire trail is organized and you can't choose the wrong street. It is not impossible to reach the top of the mountain but it is better to start early because after 1-2 pm they close the top of the mountain. We started at 8.30 and we reached the top in about 5 hours. Climbing down was more difficult due to the pain of knee and leg muscle but the environment and the mountain were wonderful. I have the dream to repeat the hiking again in another season, possibly easter or summer.

I initially booked 2 days of private touring with Core Travel for my family and me (two adults and three children aged 5-12). The email communications before departure were excellent, and June very helpfully advised postponing the tour by a couple of days when she saw that the weather forecast for the planned days was bad. This flexibility was highly appreciated. We also decided to add an extra day to the tour, making 3 days in total, and June was able to accommodate that change at very short notice, which again we very much appreciated.

I hiked up the Seongpanak trail, which was easily accessible from Jeju-si. It took only ~45 minutes to get to Seongpanak station on the 780 bus. It was crowded, but it was still a very nice hike (and luckily the weather was pretty good!). You have to reach the Jindallaebat Station by 1 pm in order to be allowed to climb to the summit. Then, you have to start your descent by 2:30 pm. Please note, the time may change depending on the season, but I?m not sure (I climbed late April). It?s a big hike, and I definitely recommend wearing good hiking boots and wearing a proper backpack. Bring lots of water. If you forget to pack food, there is some available at the Jindallaebat Station. The summit is breathtaking! I hiked back down the Seongpanak trail since the bus to get back to Jeju-si seemed more frequent than the other one. During the descent, I took a side-trip to the Sara Oreum and scenic view. It was just a good 30 minute detour, and well worth it! Once at the bottom, it was easy to catch the 780 bus back to Jeju-si.

I hiked up Mt. Halla in the winter of 2007. It was my first hike up a mountain and relatively easy getting up to the first summit as a beginner. Unfortunately, I dont remember exactly what trail and how many hours it took but it was a day trip (up and returning down). The only downside with visiting during winter was that the snow and ice made it a bit challenging in some parts, since I didnt have proper footwear. My body ached a bit the next day, but spending the day at the spa made it all worth it!

I hiked up Hallasan via Seongpanak trail and went down the Gwaneumsa trail. The hiking was almost torturous, for a person who does only some jogging as preparation to hike Halla, but it indeed worth every step towards the peak because of the heavenly view of Jeju from there. Expect rocky trails, crazy steep staircases and trails. Bring at least 2 litres of water (you can refill your bottles at fresh water springs along Seongpanak and after the bridge in Gwaneumsa trail). There's a small shop selling hot noodles, drinking water and hot coffee at Jindallae Bat shelter. Toilets are available at Sokbat and Jindallabaet and a few more somewhere along Gwaneumsa. Start early to complete the hike early. Be sure to bring your camera. Get walking sticks too if you can, I didn't but I could still do the hike :D I went to Jeju on a solo trip and did the hike alone, but a lot of other hikers were very kind giving me words of encouragement and even waited for me along Gwaneumsa trail. A must do if you get to Jeju! No entrance fee! :D

I hiked up Hallasan during Spring March 2013. It was my first time scaling such mountains and i found it relatively tough. (20yo M) I would say its a very satisfying hike, as its really mind over body for my case. The mountain is roughly 1960m, and I started with the Seongpanak course at 700+m. It took roughly 4 hours to get up and slightly more to get down. Descend is more generally difficult as you have to take note of the ice and snow which gets very dangerous even with proper hiking equipment.Just some points to take note of.Hiking during Winter would provide very nice views but very dangerous.Remember to be well preparedIt takes around 10 hours round trip for a first time beginner

I hiked Mount Halla in mid-March 2017 with my wife. We hiked up on the Yeongsil Trail and hiked down on the Eorimok Trail. The whole hike was roughly 5 hours excluding lunch break. It was quite tough but enjoyable. The view was great from the top. Some parts of the Eorimok trail was slippery because of the snow there. We brought our own lunch because we read that the only dish sold at the top is cup noodle (this is correct!).Distances from the bus stops to the trail entrances were quite far and the signs were not clear or even non-existent. The lady at the information counter was unable to speak English although she tried her best to help us locate the bus stop.There was no garbage bin anywhere in the area. If I understand the signs correctly, we are expected to bring back all garbage.

I hiked for 14 hours (amateur hiker) because I'm slow and also have not been doing any exercise for years... It was raining and windy quarterway through. Then it was sunny on the hike back. Since it was misty at the peak, so I didn't see the lake. Go prepared with water and food. Two bottles of water to last you to the top. When you come down, refill water at portable water spot. When I said food, like actual kimbap, bento or even cup noodles. In fact, bring all three. If one of the guy I bumped into did not give me his kimbap, I'd have starved for sure cause all I brought was three bananas and protein bar. Some people even offered me mini chocolate bars and tangerines. Bring isotonic drink if you want to. Bring Hiking stick(s) if you're uncoordinated like me. Bring windbreaker for sure and make sure it's waterproof. Get a good hiking shoes tha can grip because I slipped a lot on the way down. Because of my lack of preparation, I've suffered for sure coupled with my lack of exercise lol. So really, go prepared. And if you're like me with determination, and don't mind 14 hours hike, please go early like 5am. Though they do have transportation to bring you down should you really need it. I just missed it...

I highly recommend visiting Manjanggul cave while visiting Jeju island. It's a very interesting piece of nature that I was very impressed with. It's basically a lava tube formed from molten lava of volcano that pierced the earth surface and now is a long cave. It's very well maintained and open to public for about 1.5 km walk one way. When you enter the cave, you'll realize it's pretty   cool   as well as   cold  . Definitely recommend bringing a light jacked if visiting during summer hours. Inside, pathway is quite rough to walk, however it's easily doable for adults while if your traveling with kids below 3, this might not be an ideal place to visit. Inside, you'll also find lot of information about the type of volcanic rocks formed that will refresh your high school geography or you might learn new information, if you've had not already. The whole walk can be done in 30-60 minutes.

I highly recommend this service, and hiring Mr John Sheen in particular. Friendly, on time, courteous. I have nothing but positive things to say. Simply put: book a private driver with Jeju Taxi Tour and you'll be very happy .

I heard from the owner of our guesthouse that this place isn?t always open because of the tides and weather, so if you have the chance to go, take it. It?s an amazing rock formation, but unlike the ones that you can see at a distance, like Oedolgae and the Jungmun Daepo, you can actually walk on it. That rocks. It took us a while ? was it an hour? ? to walk along the perimeter of this massive rock. The terrain is not smooth ? think of desert sands except that the undulating surface is made of rock instead of sand, so wear study shoes that won?t split because of the damp. It looks like a movie set -- for an alien planet. Really, I didn?t know such a place existed on earth.If I were taking someone around Jeju, I?d recommend this place and I would definitely come back so we can exclaim together.Where: Seogwipo west coast

I have to say it was nothing special for me. The good news is that the museum is located in the jungmun complex, where other interesting attractions available, like trickart museum, jusangjeoli cliff, pacific land, etc. So if you have time, why not visit it as the entrance fee is not that expensive. But it's not a must visit attraction in my opinion

I have quite mixed feelings about the NANTA show, but the criticism is not with the show itself but with the overall experience. This review is for the show in Jeju-do.Positives:It was very easy to book tickets on line even from abroad. Once you create an account and log in, you are able to see ticket availability, choose your seats and pay for them. An online confirmation serves as your ticket until you turn up at the theatre on the day and get physical tickets. They send you a reminder via email before the show, and you can cancel up to a day before the show.The show is very funny and our whole family laughed a lot.My dad commented that the seats are more comfortable than the theatre seats in London.There is a parking lot if you are driving in.Negatives:The location in Jeju-si means that if you are staying in Seogwipo-si (as we were) then it takes over an hour to get to the theatre. And over an hour to get back home to your hotel after that.The show is catered to tourists as it doesn't use any Korean language to communicate its humour. As such, you will be surrounded by people who talk throughout the show. There's nothing you can do about this, they are really having a fun time, but you need to be aware about it. Or you can just join in and make loud comments too.There are no catering facilities at the venue so if you are driving in you need to think about where you are eating before or after the show. Fortunately just opposite the car park, across the road, there is a row of restaurants - just pick the one that you like.The toilets were filthy on the day we visited, and this was even before the show started. Since we were there for the early session at 5pm, I just don't know how the toilets can be be in such a disgusting state, unless they were not cleaned from the night before.Finally:If you are visiting Seoul, you can watch the NANTA show there too at several locations in the city. That might be a better option if you are not staying in Jeju-si itself, as the driving was just too tiring from Seogwipo-si.

I have just come back from Udo and i am happy i decided to go there.originaly it was  not in my plan. Based in Jeju-si I took bus710 (3300짜) to Seogsan port,1h20min drive. Then ferry (return ticket 5500짜) 20min. I rent bicycle (8000짜/3hours) and start Udo tour around the cost. It is 18km around island so if you are in hurry it is possible to make it much faster 1.5h enough. I also made a couple of detours inside island to see how people live. Everything is small and cute there:roads,houses,fields,fences made of stones.I recommend to climb Udo hill -nice view from there and climb is easy. It was sunny day and i get sunburned so please do not forget sunblock cream. It is windy island and one doesn't  feel is being sunburned.

I have been to many caves but this is the first volcanic cave. There are explanations in both korean and English with pictures and the light shine on the park of the rocks to show you which part is mentioned. It is a 1km walk which is quite relaxing. I took bus 201 from the old bus terminal in Seogwipo City and it took about 2 hours to get to the Manjaggul cave entrance station. From the station, you?ll need to walk for 2 km to the park. During your walk to the cave, you will see a Maze Park. I didn?t visit this park but from what I observed from other people, they seem to have a lot of fun. The cave is quite straight forward. You pay the entrance ticket and get in and just walk and learn all the information along the way. When I left the park, I noticed there is a bus station so I checked it out and realized that I can take bus 711-1 to go back to the Main Street where the Manjaggul cave entrance bus stop is. From there, I can take 201 back to Seogwipo.

I have always wanted to climb Hallasan so when I got the chance to visit Jeju, I included it on my itinerary. As I wasn't an expert hiker, I have opted to start my ascent at the Seongpanak trail. I wasn't disappointed. It was only a moderately steep climb for most of the trip. You will only have a more difficulty from the rest stop. The scenery wasn't as good as Gwaneumsa but if you want a more relaxing climb, I'd suggest to take this trail.

I have a deep love and appreciation for the artist Lee Jung Seob. The museum itself? and the neighboring art-walk is a great tribute to the artist, but the exhibition itself does not do the artist that much justice. They have a great selection of his smaller works from the earlier periods but they do not house his bigger, dynamic paintings that he is known for. This visit would be a great place to take the family as the entrance fee is very manageable. The museum offers a closer look at the artists' context and life story rather than a display of his most prominent works. In short, a brilliant artist but not the best exhibition space/display method.

I had a lot of fun riding the carts but also enjoying the beauty of Jeju. It's situated in such a beautiful location where you can view the ocean and take Instagram photos! The interior of the building was also cool. It was futuristic and very clean. The staff were friendly and helpful! I didn't play indoor games but there were many indoor games as well, so it seems like a place that you can have fun in any season. I will definitely recommend this place for any ages!? I will go back in a heartbeat when I visit Jeju next time!!

I guess if you've been inside a really spectacular cave before this won't be much to you but for someone who doesn't go into caves that often, like me, this is a cool experience. the cave is nice and cool so it is refreshing on a hot day. It's also good to visit during a rainy day as it is underground. It's dimly lit and has a spooky ambiance. part of the walls look like they're melting chocolate. I would recommend it as it is one of the highlights of the island.

I got to visit this museum as part of an inclusive tour so I can't comment on the value of the entrance fee, but I loved this museum.  I haven't laughed so much in ages.  I am not sure if it is meant to be so delightfully funny!  It is famous in S Korea for a TV series   about a Princess that was filmed there.What you get is several galleries of teddy bears dressed up as historical figures, famous art works, and scenes from history or of S Korean culture.  There are several large bears around the place suitable for having your photo with eg Charlie Chaplin, Michael Jackson.  Outside there are several bears enjoying the gardens again suitable for being photographed with.  There is a cafe and a gift shop.  The cafe was closed when we visited late afternoon. There is a short running show of an automaton Elvis-Bear again hilarious!  I would definitely go back.  This museum is located in the Jungmun resort area on the Bus Route 600.  Get off at PlayKpop stop - its just next door.

I found the volcanic caves here interesting but apart from that it was just another botanic garden. We went when the rapeseed and cherry blossoms were in bloom which was very pretty and a good photo opportunity. However, the same flowers are everywhere in Jeju at that time of year and don't cost anything to take a photo.

I found out about Love Land on Google during our cruise to Asia.  So when we landed my husband and I took a taxi cab there.  It was right next door to the Museum of Modern Art so we checked that out first.  And then we walked over to Love Land.  It could also be called   Happy Land   as we would every now and then hear an eruption of laughter from other visitors.  We were certainly laughing too.The sculptures in various poses of love were whimsical and clever.  It was a nice walk that took us about an hour and a half.  At the end we went into the shop where there were small dioramas and objects for sale.Volcanoes and waterfalls I have seen before.  But I had never seen a place like Love Land.  When we returned to our cruise ship fellow cruisers said   Why didn't you tell us?!  We would have gone.

I flow to Jeju just to walk up this mountain.  You have to apply to the  Hallasan National Park visitor management system for the QR code admission ticket. My ticket was for the Gwaneumsa Course, time slot 5-30am - 8-00am.   I started my walk at 7-50am,  It was perfect walking weather, overcased so not too warm.  There is a 500 hiker per day limit on this route to the top, on the other easier route there is a 1000 hiker per day limit. The first few kms is easy going and you think to yourself this walk is going to be a piece of cake.  After around 4 kms you reach the first of two public toilets on the route.  From there the walk becomes a uphill slot with countless wooden steps. On the way up there is two downhill's with maybe a couple of hundred steps to walk down before walking uphill again.  After the second public W.C.  the route is a never ending series of wooden staircases until at last it flattens  out and the top of the mountain.  When I did it there was maybe a hundred or more walkers queuing to get a photo next to the summit stone.    I just gave my phone to a person and asked them to take a photo with the stone in the background.
