Whilst I'm giving the Teddy Bear Museum just 2 stars for quality, value for money, class of exhibits, and any actual worth as a proper   museum  , I have to admit that my visit made me laugh. I'm not sure though that derisive snorting sarcasm was what they were looking for.This museum is a pile of pants, masquerading as teddy bears.. The   attractions   are about 15 to 20 poor quality adult-human-sized bears, dressed in various outfits of clothing, with a challenge to guess   who   they are dressed as. Military uniform and two medals apparently is enough for a bear to resemble Prince William, for example - and a grey wig and   E=mc2   to represent Einstein.Then there are the bear portraits. Frames containing bears dressed to vaguely resemble famous portraits. Mona Lisa teddy bear, anyone?There's no   history   of the teddy bear, no collection of historical bears, no pictures / video clips of teddy bears being made, no maps showing where different types of teddy bears originated from - nothing educational whatsoever. There are no audio tours, no leaflets or signs to show the visitor around, and certainly no staff available to talk to about any   exhibits  , whether you are Korean, English, American or anything else.The gift shop on the lowest floor contained the largest number of bears - none of them particularly special, all just your usual cheap mass-produced bears, but at slightly hiked up prices.By far the worst part of the visit was the funniest. Your ticket includes entry to the   Elvis Stage Show  . Oh dear Lord, where on earth do I start? The show is on every 15 minutes. In a room with about 12 benches in it. There is a curtain at the far end, hiding the   stage  . On the quarter hour, the announcement is made -   The King of Rock and Roll, Elvis, is in the house!   The curtains open, and there it is. The Elvis Presley Show. Six, sad, lonely looking teddy bears, dressed in stage show outfits, rocking gently on their animatronic sticks. The three backing singers sway gently on the right, the drummer's arms flail up and down towards the drums, the guitarist's arm moves.Elvis meanwhile gyrate and swivels his hips, the crowd goes wild. Oh, no, sorry, that last sentence was a lie. Elvis sways and looks like he almost falls several times.Worst animatronic puppetry in the world. Hilarious. Hilariously BAD. Less than two minutes later, the curtains shut, and   Elvis has left the building   - until the next showing in approximately 12 or 13 minutes' time....Don't go to the Teddy Bear Museum thinking you'll have an interesting visit. Go to see the absolutely bizarre vision that South Koreans have of   entertainment  .

If you like teddy bears then it is a museum for you as there are alot of cute displays and exhibits that memorialize past events in history.  Kinda cool but not my thing.  I enjoyed the outdoor park area more.  You can take pictures with cute bear statues and sit and enjoy the greenery.  There is a cafe that sells Taiwanese pearl drinks and a nice gift shop.

We went to see waterfall at 12PM, there were loads of people, nevertheless view was stunning, waterfall is huge. I'd say better go in day time as when sun is starting to set you'd get weird shadows on your pics and it just won't be the same. Bear in mind you'll have to walk on huge rocks so it's not very safe for toddlers and those carrying their babies, not suitable for those with walking difficulties. Better wear sports clothes which would cover legs in case you fall, to prevent scratches or whatever other injuries. It says no swimming but we took off our shoes and walked in shallow water. It was cold but fun. We also sat on rocks in close proximity to waterfall and splashes from it made us quite wet. But it was spectacular. Such a unique place! Tickets are 1,000 for 16-24 year olds, they require ID. For adults it's 2,000.

We went in, looked around the first 5 minutes and then left. I like teddy bears, I'm actually a bit of a big kid, but this was all a bit boring. Lots and lots of bears dressed in little outfits. Maybe good if it's raining but if the sun is shining outside I'd advise you to try other things. It was crowded too, so you couldn't easily see the displays anyway.

We visited this just because it was rainy, and realized that it would be great to visit otherwise.  It was interesting because of the theme-based teddy bears in thousands, spread across 3 floors.  Loved the Gandhi bear, Times square scene, Mother teresa bears, Charlie Chaplin bears, most expensive teddy bears (Louis Vuitton) and so on.Do visit if you can fit it in your schedule!

We visited the museum a bit reluctantly and only because we had dragged our two children (10 and 15) round two scenic waterfalls and an archery practice place in the hours before. Our youngest daughter was definitely keen to do something that she chose. When we got there our suspicions seemed to be confirmed with a relatively high entrance fee (I think it was 6,000 won per adult) for what seemed to be a small place.However, once we got into the diorama room, both kids couldn't stop themselves from oohing and aahing the whole time. You really felt that somebody had fun putting it all together. It was in all the little touches (like adding little German flags to the 'storming of the Berlin wall' display) and the set ups such as the 'Bearacotta Army). As previous reviewers have mentioned, all of these are in glass cases so my husband (who is a very keen photographer with decent equipment) didn't deign to take any photos - our teenage daughter took over instead. Having just completed our photobook, I can only say that we had plenty of good shots, I could easily have filled 20 rather than 4 pages with good shots.We didn't miss any English explanations - the teddies really spoke for themselves. We also didn't approach it as a museum but rather as a fun place to look around. The re-enactments of historical events from the 20th century were also fairly self-explanatory.The shop was probably the only really boring bit since the selection was not particularly big and the prices, given the location, quite high.Overall, don't go if you want to learn anything about teddy bears but do go in with kids (or adults who appreciate the cuteness).

We visited in the Teddy Bear Museum in Jeju around late Nov 2017, and it was quite empty when we visited.  The entry charges was pricey considering the only activity was to look at teddy bears in glass casings.  The glass casings made it difficult to take nice photos, as there were lots of reflections.  However, the kids enjoyed the place very much.  There is also an outdoor area (don't miss it, very nice place to take photos).  Overall, an above-average place to visit, but it is indoors so if the weather is bad, this is a place you can drop by.

We took ride on bus no. 282 from Arang Joeul Street to visit Teddy Bear Museum jeju which is nearby to Jungmun  tourist resort. Bus fare cost us only KRW 1150 per pax. The visit to Teddy bear museum was fantastic especially for my sister, teddy bear lover. It was amazing to see many collection of teddy bears from all over the world with different themes and events globally.  There were three sections of the teddy bear museum; starting from the history, artwork and forest of teddy bear. There was a garden outside of the museum with the construction of enormous teddy bear. We can get a glimpse of the LV and Swarvosky teddy bear. The most nostalgic teddy bear was the Princess Hour theme teddy bear. The most great thing to watch was the Elvis Presley show. However, the teddy bear sold there was expensive. It was worth to visit this place.

We stopped at Jungmun tourist complex to visit teddy bear museum by taking bus no. 282 from Arang Joeul Street in Seogwipo.  It was 6 minutes walk to Cheonjeyeon waterfall. Do not confuse this waterfall with Cheonjiyeon waterfall. The admission fee was KRW2,000 per pax. You can kill two birds with one stone. You get to see two attractions the famous Seonimgyo bridge with seven nymphs carves (fairy bridge) and the three-tiered waterfall. We did not go for the third waterfall as the trail was quite steep. We only went to the pond of fairy and the second waterfall.

We stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal and took bus 110 from Jungang Rotary bus stop to Jungmun Tourist Complex. The bus journey about 30 minutes and cost less than 2000won one way. The bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly (Although I did not see Jungmun Tourist Complex on the TV screen, therefore I used GPS to locate instead. You can press the bell to alight. For my other bus trip, the stops were announced correctly and was reliable). We actually stopped that Jungmun Tourist Complex to go the the Teddy bear museum and Cheonjeyeon Falls before proceeding to the beach. Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. We needed to change bus 702 (opposite the tourist infrmation counter) to Hyeojae beach. It cost 3300 won. The journey on the bus we great as you will pass by paddy field, wind mills and wild flower fields. You will see a beautiful beach 1st ( I think it is Geumneung Beach) but don?t get down, get down at Hyeopjae beach as the view is nicer (about 2 stops away). You can walk down the stretch later (There is a public toilet down the stretch if you need). The weather then (April 26) was 12 to 17 degree Celcius and remember to buy a jacket and windbreaker as it was very windy when we were there. We so blessed that the sky cleared up to reveal one of the most beautiful turquoise beaches I have been. The beach was wide and the colours of the water clear and blue. There are many caf챕 where you can buy a hot drink from. Noted that the caf챕 only allow you to use the toilet if you buy a drink (the receipt will print the password to get into the toilet). You can always use the public toilet. We decide to walk along the orange and blue ribbon trail (Jeju Olle Route 14) and it was one of the best trail for me. We complete only part of the the trail where we walk through the villages to the fishing port. The route will bring you to a serene path with light house and the wind mills. The the path became rocky nearing the windmills, and we decided to walk out through the rocky back alley of a shellfish place (away from the orange/blue ribbon) and landed at a bus stop. We took bus 702 back to seogwipo. It was a must go beach but only on a clear blue day where the magnificent of the beach will show up.

We start our journey from Hotel Fine at 5 am in the morning and manage to arrived there at 6 am. Please bear in mind that you are required to climb a high numbers of stairs so at least make sure you had a breakfast first. The effort of climbing the numerous stairs is really worth it as once you reached the top, the scenery are breathtaking and amazed me on each second I blink my eyes. This is a must visit place when you are at Jeju.
We spent only about 30 minutes in here, there was nothing much to see.  Full of bears in different settings, like The Beatles, or during the war, or circus.

We had an afternoon to kill and it was too hot for any outdoor activity so we decided to visit the museum. It had a fairly interesting display of teddy bears - displayed by era and themes. Highlight was the most expensive teddy bear in the world - the Louis Vutton teddy bear. If you had limited time on Jeju, this is not a must-see, but I'd like us you had an extra day, then, this is worth going on a hot or rainy day.

We go in the end of June , basically it is hot outside, but inside the cave is cold and a bit freezing, take along taxi ride from Soegwipo area, cause we travel in 5, 1 senior over 75 , 1 teenager ,1 children of 7,  so we decide to book taxi for 8 hours to explore Jeju it is more convenient and save time  than using bus , but a little pricey 120.000 krw for whole day, After reaching the cave and go down to look inside , my wife and mother in law surrender, cause it is to exhaust to walk 2 kilometer ( in and out )for senior and a bit dim,   Cave is big , but there is no living creatures like bats or others, I my self do not really excited at first,  but my 7 years son and my teenagers daughter really like to explore the cave, so we are not prepared and just go. A bit chilling but still bearable, no toilet inside so prepared your self , the light is dim but still able to see around, there is water dropping from ceiling but not too often ,the water clean and no smell, the pathway is not level and bumpy ,watery here and there in a few area the but still manageable and walkable ,  don't have to worry,  if my 7 years old can do it so can others , at last this is a pleasant and unique experience, a bit exhausting walk , but worth a try

We found this museum in our travel guide and it sounded fun to visit. However, it was quite disappointing starting with the price which was much more expensive than all other museums. It only had a few rooms with teddy bear representations that got repetitive and monotonous after the first. On the other hand there was a nice outdoor park with fun sculptures to take pictures next to. Overall might be good for children but not so worth it for adults.
We enjoyed this museum thoroughly.  Thousands of teddy bears with a multitude of poses, extremely creative. Very good history of teddy bears.

We did 3 Jeju Olle Route 1, 6 & 7 and 14-1. We did not complete all the Olle route but every one of the route was breath-taking and worth the walk. All the route were doable by public transport and car rental was not needed.Jeju Olle Route 1We did not do the entire route 1 as we wanted to visit seongsan 1st plus we started late. As we stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal, we took bus 701 to Seongsan ilchulbong. The bus journey took more than 1.5hours and cost about 3300won one way and the bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly.  The TV screen will flash seongsan-ri entrance and you can press the bell to alight (photo attached). Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. I have car sickness but it was still bearable for me. We alighted and headed to the black beach along Seongsan. It was called the black beach as the sand was black. Not sure why we need not need to pay for the entrance fee to Seongsan that day (25th April) but we were happy as the temperature was about 17 degree Celsius. We wore T-shirt with a windbreaker only as the sun kept us warm. A windbreaker will be good as it can be quite windy especially if you walk along the beach. There were 2 track at Seongsan. One track led to the peak of Seongsan which consist about 10 flights of stairs (Pretty doable even with poor fitness ? just take as many rest breaks as needed). At the peak, you will be able to have a panoramic view of the city and the surrounding water bodies. The other track is along the coast area with pretty wild purple (I think is Lunaria annua)  and yellow canola wild flower and volcanic stacked rocks.After Seongsan, you can continue to the Jeju Olle Route 1 to Al Oreum along the ocean area. The Jeju Olle Route 1 will pass by canola flower patches for photo taking, a nice ocean view with beaches for scenic viewing, a new hotel named as The Cloud, the ferry terminal, along many beautiful seashore. We stopped at one of the seashore where we witness locals harvesting gastropod, sword razor clams and cockles using simple equipment. We were friendly and allowed us to take photo of how they harvest sword razor clams. If you are interesting in harvesting, remember to bring a good jacket as the wind was strong in April. Putting on waterproof boots will be good too. We continued to walk along the coast where cuttlefish were being dried along the coast. There were many restaurants along the way too. As we continued the walk, we noted that there was no bus stop along the walk after the fish port/market (there was a Ojo Haenyeo House bus stop). The next bus stop was at Jongdal Elementary school which was quite a distance away.After walking through the coastal area, you will walk through a village for a short period before reaching the expressway. The walk towards Al Oreum required you to cross an expressway and the route up the Al Oreum seemed alittle deserted with trees but there was still a road up. You will contine to see the orange/blue ribbons that were well spaced. However, we started the walk at 1pm and took too many stops for picture taking. Therefore, we were unable to finish the walk to Al Oreum.We decided to back track  and took bus 701 from the Jongdal Elementary school stop at about 5.30 pm back to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal (we take on the side nearer to the expressway, not the opposite). Therefore, make sure you start the Olle route earlier if you want to reach the top of Al Oreum where you will have a bird-eye view of the paddy field and coastal area. The bus journey took about 2 hours to reach Seogwipo-si.Jeju Olle Route 6 & 7 We did not do the entire 6 & 7 trail but we visited Chilshimni Poetry Park, Hwangwooji coast, Oedolgae observatory and Oedolgae. This was a scenic trail and I highly recommend. We stayed at a hotel along Jungang-ro road, that was near the Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market. From our hotel, it was a 10 minutes walk to Geolmae Eco Park. The park led us along Seohong-ro road to Taepyeong-to road (where we passed by Hotel Yeon) where we were able to see the Saeyeong Bridge. After the bridge was in sight, we followed our instinct to the Bridge. There was an ice-cream stall that serve grape soft-serve that was delicious. We made our way onto the bridge to view the pristine bluish-green coastline and headed to Saeseom Island. Saeseom Island was a short 20 to 30 minutes trail that brought us to a rocky coastline where you can view two lighthouses (red and white). You could walk to the white lighthouse on the rocks but at your own risk. There were many locals fishing along the rocky areas too. In short, the trail along the Saeyeongyo Bridge was fairly easy yet scenic enough. We were there on the 22nd of April and the weather was about 15 degree Celsius in the day. A light jacket with windbreak will be sufficient. Afterwhich we headed to Chilshimni Poetry Park (which you can view Cheonjiyeon Falls for free) as there was a stairway along the left side of main exit road (where all the tour buses parked, pedestrian walkway path with brown wood). The stairway seemed to indicate going up a temple. However, we landed in Chilshimni Poetry Park. We took pictures of the waterfall and left Chilshimni Poetry Park to follow the orange/blue Jeju Olle ribbon to Hwangwooji coast and Oedolgae. The orange/blue Jeju Olle ribbon were along the park main road (Namseongjung-ro road where Park Sunshine hotel was). Then, You need to turn in to Namseong-ro road and you will see a brick wall painted dark blue with pinnochio seated on a bench (photo attached) you will passed by a ?hip?몃媛?? Hostel (the hostel name is in Korean as I cannot find the English name online - photo attached). u will then past by Poong Gyung Hotel in Jeju (not the one u can find online - photo attached) before arriving at Hwangwooji coast. I love Hwangwooji coast bcos it was like a private pool. There were only a few Korean that day, playing, swimming and hunting of sea creatures in the private pool. It also has a good view of the Saeyeongyo Bridge from a far.  After-which we head to Oedolgae and walked till Dombenang-gil Road. We decided to head back as I needed the toilet. At the entrance to Oedolgae, there was a public toilet acorss the road. The toilet were will keep with toilet paper provided. You can watch the sunset if you have time. We decided to include this in our tour after feeling a bit tired from all the hiking up mountains and paths. It's an easy couple of hours, especially if you have kids, whom seemed to be entertained with every variation of dressed up bear. There is also an extensive gift shop, with, you've guessed it, lots of bears and cuddlies. The prices aren't exactly cheap, but the quality seemed good. It's a good way to slow the pace down if you are in need of a rest.. Nice afternoon out.

Was recommended to this place by a friend. Entry wasnt cheap at around 10k won. I was initially disappointed when inside the building. But upon stepping outside the building, i thought the displays were beautiful when the teddy bear displays are placed with nice scenery.

Was here during the winter, winter clothes sold at value. You can get a whole set here, from undies to mittens at a discount price.  Place is well maintained, underground so you're warm.  Not too many restaurants but the space is sprawling and windy, you can get lost. Thankfully there are maps, just remember your entry point to keep your bearings.  Toilets all around, with no bidet.  Things sold were all more or less the same as you spend a bit of time browsing.

Walk down to the falls is quiet and serene. A couple of local women were offering the fresh seafood they have just caught for sale. One just need to pay small amount and the woman will cut up the seafood and serve it with some sauce. People will just eat it fresh like sashimi.To get bearer to the fall, one need to navigate through rocks. Care should be taken else one may fall or drop your camera of smartphone. We were lucky to spot a rainbow at the place where the water splashed on the rocks! This is real rare and definitely made our day.

Visited this place 4 years ago, this place is full of different teddy bears, each with lots of different types of size and different types of theme. Although the place is quite packed, but we really enjoyed our trip there and took lots of photographs as memo, as this is a good place for photography. A place not to be missed in JeJu!!! Thumbs Up!!!

Visited this museum with my kids.  There were hundreds of Teddy bears displayed over 3 floors. We saw Teddy bears in all sizes,  different era and occasions, celebrity characters dress up, themes etc.   Kids were excited to watch the free performance theatre with teddy bears dressed up as Elvis and his supporting singers singing. Every floor has different group of bears on display.   Entrance also allowed visitors to venture out to the back garden which boosted more Teddy bear statues.   Garden was well maintained and worth a visit.  Near the main entrance,  it also had a 2 storey high wooden Teddy bear which is a real attraction for the kids. The entry ticket is not cheap,  unless you are a real Teddy bear fan,  in my view,  it is not a must see destination.

Very interesting display of modern and old teddy bears. Take the time to see the Elvis Presley gig in the theatre! A bit pricey and as most museums on Jeju is quite small, but worth it on a rainy day.
Very entertaining and cute. Nothing much to see other than bears, but all were made perfectly for each scene represented.

Very cute and tons of displays.  Many different themes and ages of bears.  Very good place for couples and children.  The lifelike bears were very sturdy so you dont need to worry about them falling on kids, even with posing with them.  They have an outdoor display section, but it was raining for our trip so we didn't get the full experience.  Nice store at the end but was a bit over priced as anticipated.  Very good for any rainy or sunny day.
Very create teddy bear. You can find terry bear verson of Mona Lisa, Vincent Van Gogoh, Tera-Cotta Warrior, Terry Bear at folk village, etc

Unlike Hello Kitty, I think most of us have cuddled or have in possession a toy teddy bear at a certain stage of our lives. So it is no wonder that the Teddy Bear Museum has such a wide appeal and which surely be included as a ?compulsory? destination on the itinerary of the independent travellers (especially those with children) and tour companies alike.Getting there and fees: We visited Teddy Bear Museum (GPS coordinate/code 7387600) on a rainy day, which was appropriate since the exhibits are predominantly indoor, except for the Teddy Bear Garden and Park where there?re a few teddy bear figurines outside and a park with great views of the sea.  The admission charges are 10,000 won for adults won, 9,000 won for teens and 8,000 won for children.The Museum/Attraction:  This Teddy Bear Museum is the first and largest teddy bear museum in South Korea. Once you enter, you are greeted by this huge teddy bear, who gives you a ?grand? welcome to further explore the five sections spread over 3 levels: The History Hall, The Art Hall and The Project Exhibition Hall, Gift Shop (all indoors) and an outdoor Teddy Bear Garden and Park. There?s also a caf챕/restaurant. Be prepared to spend at least 1 hour looking and taking photographs/selfies at all the interesting exhibits. The History Hall comprised of the history of bear manufacturing and some of the earliest toy bears, many of which are antique and rare. It also showcases milestones in human history, with the bears enacting several famous (human) historical scenes from different eras. This is indeed a refreshing concept for a museum! I particularly liked the teddy bears enacting the Titanic, landings on the moon and the iconic celebrities like the Beatles and Gandhi.In the Art Hall, you could see the world-famous artworks and designs in an art gallery form as well as animation characters beloved by children. I liked the Mona Lisa and two of the most expensive bears in the world - the Louis Vuitton teddy bear and the Diamond Bear. In the Project Exhibition Hall, you would meet teddy bears grouped to suit the theme of each exhibition. Not forgetting the large Gift Shop on the first level. While it offers plenty of gifts, these are nonetheless pricey. Nevertheless, you could take photos with Michael Jackson bear, Steve Jobs bear and a wedding couple bear amongst others. There?s also a mother panda with her baby pandas on display too.  We certainly enjoyed the wonderful experience of the Museum bringing out the child in each of us, and making us feel young again. Despite the pricey entrance fees, I still think the Teddy Bear Museum is worth visiting, and to me, once would be sufficient. But if you don?t like teddy bears at all, then it would be prudent to skip this attraction.

Unless you really really love Teddy Bears, this place is rather overpriced. At 8,000KRW per person, it gets expensive if you're in a group. And, they won't let you enter the gift shop without paying for a ticket. In the end, we found their gift shop not terribly different from the Safari Teseum (7,000KRW per person, but you can go directly to the gift shop). The Safari Teseum gift shop actually had more options (aka other animals for those who don't like stuffed bears).Still, if you really love Teddy Bears, you can make a day of it between the two places.

Unless you really love Teddy Bears, this place is not worth it. The place has two floors of teddy bears, It is full of history with all the teddy bears from all over the world. All of the ancient teddy bears is well preserved but with relatively minimal background story. Some of the information are written only in Korean, so there isn't many interactive attraction here.My advise is SKIP this place if you're not Teddy Bear lovers.

Udo is a beautiful island by itself but due to the time constrain we had, we didn't had time to digest the beaches and scenic views. We had always wanted to rent an ATV there and even applied for international driving license as advised by many reviewers, however, we were greatly disappointed as the rental places only rent ATV to holders of Korean driving license. IDL are not accepted so don't waste money to apply for one. We rented electric bike in the end but had a dispute with the rental store nearest to the udo habour. One of our electric bike tyre went burst as the tyres were already old and the store owner wanted us to pay. We had an disagreement as the tyres when rented to us were already worn out. I must attribute to miscommunication as the people at udo are not conversant in English nor mandarin. We beared half the cost only after calling udo police to mediate the situation. But not much help from the police who told us to   go home  . Quite a memorable experience for us though.
Two floors of teddy bears for display and one floor for selling them. Outdoor park is nice to walk around. But due to hot weather, we only go out for a short while and hide indoors.

True to the museum title, there?s quite a number of precious collections, including the first generation of Winnie the Pooh, Carebear and other well known bears. A number of bears dressed up as historical figures placed throughout the building provide good selfie opportunities. Worth it if you are a bear lover and in the Jungmun area.

Though am not craving for Teddy Bear, still find it ok to stop by if you have time.  You may know the history of teddy bear via this museum.  Only too bad, we can't find Mr. Bean best friend, Teddy in it.  However, you will find Elvis Presley, The Beatles & many others.

Thoroughly enjoyed the visit to the Museum. Awesome show featuring the Elvis Presley bear. So many bears with such exquisite costume designs, special thematic showcases. From celebrity bears to Disney bears. You name it, they have it. I was completely mesmerized. Don't miss the bear shows.

This was pretty entertaining. I had no idea what would be in a Teddy Bear museum... PLEASE go though. There are tons of bears from every period imaginable, wearing period and geographical clothing to match. Everyone is represented and it was actually a lot better than I thought when I hear   we are going to the Teddy Bear Museum  .... don't let that fool you! There is also an outside where you can walk around and see life-sized teddy bears. The gift shop is at the very end, and you WILL want something from it. Class Act, and a welcomed surprise!

This teddy bear museum is one of a few around the world.  Located in Jungmun tourist complex in Jeju, Korea, is this tiny museum for teddy bear fans alike.  For 8000 KRW you have unlimited day access to 3 floors of teddy bear exhibits and the outside grounds.  This museum carries interesting themed bears like the Mona Lisa bear, the Leonardo Da Vinci bear, a Marilyn Monroe bear, and so many others.  Currently they are displaying the Elvis bear.  On the ground floor there is even a really nice restaurant if you get hungry.  Not much choice in  terms of breakfast, they do offer mostly burgers and different types of coffees.  Also there is a gift shop if you are interested in taking home one of the really cute teddy bear souvenirs.Well worth the visit and few hours for both teddy bear fans and those with just a passing interest.  Remember to use the lockers next to the admission counter.  We didn't and carried all our jackets and bags for the entire exhibit,  It will make the visit a whole lot lighter and more fun.  Enjoy!

This place was really unexpected. Through the Yeha Bus tour this was one of the stops and I am glad we visited this place. A lot of mini exhibits with bears dressed up according to the theme and the gift shop is great as well. For teddy bear lovers and lovers of all things cute, we recommend this place.
This place was pretty kool, and it's great to take the kids there. I wouldn't say it would be a lost if you didn't have time to go here. Unless you really want to see teddy bears...

This place starting to get famous in my country when Korean drama 'Princess Hour' was aired, never thought that someday I will visit this place. If you're a Teddy fans, take your time ^^ to enjoy the dioramas and various Teddy collection. They also have garden that full of teddy bear statues.

This place is really worth a visit. Very creative teddy bear figures that show well known people from the past, e.g. van Gogh with one ear, Ghandhi, Elvis, Marilyn etc. My wife has made Teddy bears at home and we know what a lot of work and material is required

This place is reallly cute.. There are a lot of teddy bear. There is the story of teddy bear and also teddy bear in children story like Snow white. It?s recommended to bring your children or go just with your friends in here. They also have cafe and teddy bear store in here if you like to buy something as a souvenir. For the wrapping or plastic bag, you should pay more for it.

this place is only teddy bear doll. nothing interesting for me as an adult, but very recomended if you bring your kids here. The souvenir is expensive but the entry ticket is cheap enough. We went here by rent car i'm not sure what public transportshould we use to get here.

This place is highly recommended! Not only the kids are attracted to the beautiful diplay of teddy bears,the adults too will be fascinated by what this place can offer. It's truly a great attraction for all ages!

This place is going to be boring if obviously you do not have an interest to look at teddy bears because this is what the place is all about, various themes of teddy bears on display. It also depends on some children, they may or may not like this place. My family love this place (including my parents) so it's not only for children if one have the interest. I even bought a teddy bear wearing a hanbok as a souvenir for myself. There was also a free Elvis teddy bear mini performance which is so cute. Only consider adding this location to your itinerary if you do have the interest, don't waste your time if you don't.
This place is filled with teddy bears. Visited the place with 3 different age group. Only the kids love it the most, not for adults and senior citizen.
This place is best for teddy bear fans, it's had many collection from the beginning till the y generation now.

This place is a must-see if you're a fan of teddy bears, but it's not just for the rabid fans.  I don't count myself as a particular fan one way or another, but I don't dislike them.  The bears here are displayed as various characters and in a variety of situations.  They're cute and can be interesting, but if you're not really into this kind of thing then you'd be bored.  I'm sure children would enjoy it.  For myself, I enjoyed it but I've seen it once and wouldn't go back.
This place has variety of teddy bear. Upon entering, they have a zoo theme on the 1st floor. They have many zoo animals made of stuff toys. The 2nd floor is more of a theme section.

This museum, like most of Jeju's other similar attractions, is but an excuse to get you to the gift shop. You can finish it in one hour, because they want to get you there fast! As opposed to most other museums in this resort island, this one is cute and amusing. It consists mostly of tableaus or displays with teddy bears re-enacting some important historical or popular culture event. Some may frown at the   Gandhi   teddy bear as perhaps not quite tasteful, but must surely enjoy the   Beatles   teddy bears, the   Chinatown   teddy bears, etc. You get the picture. Oh, yes the gift shop! It works; I bought a little cute bear as most everybody else seems to have done. Not that expensive and well-made. In other words, if you are going to see at least one of these museums that dot the south of the island, you may want to give this one a try. It's enjoyable.

This museum is one of the attraction at Jungmun Resort. It consists of teddy bear exhibition from several country, the history, the art, life size teddy bear & of course souvenir store. If you're Princess Hours lovers (Kdrama) this place is perfect for you. You can't bring you belonging inside, so placed you belonging into a free locker on the entrance of the museum.

This museum is all about Teddy Bear. All the display from old to the newest Teddy Bear is here. Teddy Bear in Louis Vuitton, Teddy Bear in Hong Kong and even MJ Teddy Bear will make you smile. You can also buy Teddy Bear for souvenirs.

This museum is a lot bigger than expected, and housed so many different teddy bears in fun settings that it made even adults excited. Would highly recommend if you have little kids, as they would love being able to touch the bears and taking photos with them.
This landmark is very well maintained with beautiful structures. Very instagram friendly. Location is also pretty near many places like teddy bear museum, several waterfalls and casino resorts.
This is the place you can hug, kiss and take photos with teddy bear. Jeju Teseum is Korea's first and largest teddy bear museum. If you likes Teddy bear this is the place must visit in Jeju Island.
This is quite an interesting place, even I'm not really a teddy bear fans, I quite enjoyed the visit because there are many different   styles   of teddy bear!

This is one of the most remarkable scenic attractions of Jeju. Our Korean driver brought us here. We told him we are not interested in arts museums or teddy bear or maze park. We only wanted to see the natural sites and wonders in Jeju and he brought us here and we thanked him for that. There was a Buddha Park directly at the car park where we alighted. I could see the golden face of the Buddha from the highland opposite the park. From the car park,  the panoramic view of the beach was amazing; the lush green vegetation studded with autumn foliage with long stretch of gorgeous coastline and natural cliff view and the azure sea horizon. It was nature's master-piece presented in so marvelous and harmonious form that I could not find better words to describe this stunning, breathtaking and jaw dropping scenery. For a moment, a sensation of joy and happiness flooded and filled my heart. As the gentle sea breeze blew on my face, I found tranquility, calmness and serenity in this beautiful land. I immediately dashed down the flight of stairs to embrace this beautiful and spectacular piece of natural wonder. I roamed and wandered around the scenic landscape and found myself singing the Happy Wanderer lyrics: `I like to go a wandering up the mountain track  And as I go, I love to sing, My knapsack on my back. Val-deri,Val-dera, Val-deri,..'  There was the Hamel Castaway Memorial and the vessel Hamel that drifted to this place in 1653. I stood near the replicated Hamel vessel to admire the European naval architectural of that time and I saw the rangers tendered to the horses in the range. From the coast, I could see the majestic Mt Sanbangsan loomed at the site of the Buddha Park and I could vividly see some of my group members were resting and relaxing at a pavilion below the car park enjoying the gentle sea breeze.You must pardon me for my excitement and exhilaration as I came from a city with urbanized concrete jungle with little natural scenery. Jeju is full of natural wonders and Mt Sanbangsan and Yongmeori beach are exceptionally gorgeous gems that deserved a good lengthy exploration.
This is heaven for teddy bear lovers!Bear dressed in different clothings and cosplaying different iconic persons like Steve jobs, MJ and etcGreat place for a date or photos :)

This is definitely a place for kids & ladies. Sorry guys. It is bear, bear, bear & more bear wherever you turn your head. Thank goodness photography is allowed in here. Most of the bears are small, about the height of your palm. I guess that makes them all the cuter. There is a giantic bear in front of the souvenir shop. Do take a few shots with it. Considering the number of bears on display, the number of teddy bear related memorabilia is quite limited,. I wonder why.

This is a Teddy Bear Museum that all inside about the Teddy Bear.  They have so many Theme of Teddy Bear.  Near the exit they also have many stuff for us to buy and bring home, such as doll, key chain, cloth, jacket, sweater, etc..  This Museum is more suitable for the children, but for adult if you are bored you can wait near the exit there are some coffe shop.

This is a straight-up collection of really adorable teddies all in different themes and characters!Some are the classic teddy bears that we grew up lovingSome are teddies dressed up as music icons, roman gods/goddesses, characters from movies, etcIf you need your fill of cute things, this place is loaded with itIt's nice if you ask meAnd it doesn't hurt that we even got free teddies after the visit! yay!

This is a must place if you come visit to Jeju island. So many type of teddy bear collection inside a protected glass, enlarged version for photograph. You will fulfill your child dream and can take photo with a   human   size teddy bear!

This is a great place for young children, with so many teddy bears to see and to play with. Even my husband and I were kept fully entertained. Inside you can see teddy bears in many different settings, all very cuddly and well presented. What I loved most is the outside area - I could spend hours just watching kids play, and it'll be great to have a picnic in the garden with all the nice surrounding, and with teddy bears of course.

This is a fun place to visit. I wouldnt get out of my way to see it, but if you are in Jungmun and have an hour, its a fun place to see. The part I liked best are the Teddy Bears in   historical situations  . Like the first moon landing,  the discovery of the Terracotta Army, the fall of the Wall in Berlin etc.

This is a cute collection of teddybears and other stuffed animals in a variety of settings (a castle, a safari, etc.), but it's not what I was expecting with the name   Teseum   (teddy+museum).  There's a very small display of older teddybears (mostly photographs), but the main attraction is the displays you can see in the pictures.  There must be thousands here, ranging in size from one inch or shorter to probably eight feet tall. I imagine kids would be in hog heaven, but some of the older people in our tour group said it was a waste of time.  My favorites were the safari and the teddybear versions of old paintings.
This beach is one of the most beariful beaches in Jeju, with its white sand and really good restaurants and coffeeshops nearby. Really recomendable to go!

They have my favourite teddy bears in different shapes and different theme. If you are a soft toy lover like me, this is definitely a place for you. A lot of photoshoot spots. They also have huge teddy bears, twice the size of you.

There's two Teddy Bear Museum in Jeju Island. One is Safari Theme that has an entrance fee of KRW 8,500 (Php 369) for adults. This has a safari theme great for pictures but on the second floor, there are more which has a variety of themes. The other Teddy Bear Museum where the most expensive Teddy Bear is on display wearing a Louis Vuitton outfit costs KRW 8,000 (Php 347). This one is better because it has so many display that you will be amazed, famous scene, characters, celebrities from different industries. Very nice! This is also the museum where Princess Hour was shot, a Korean novela. I will go back!
There were so many characters of teddy bear, very cute and lovely. Heaven for teddy bear lovers. Girls and kids will love it.

There were bears of every color and design imaginable: there was an Elvis bear, Marilyn bear, Mona Lisa bear, Chinese bears, countryside bears and even Goong (the Korean drama) bears! It really was a bear wonderland. The only problem was that the commentary was all in Korean, it would have been better if there was English translation as well. The other problem was that most of the exhibits were housed in glass cases which made taking photos challenging as the reflections were very prominent. Besides viewing the bears, there is an in-store souvenir shop that has all sorts of bear items (e.g. keychains, stuffed bears, bags etc...). But if you love bears, than it should be worth a visit.For more on my experience and photos, please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/03/an-impromptu-visit-to-teddy-bear-museum.html

There are many many many uncountable (which may count but hei! not necessary man~) teddy bears inside and a lots of other animals dolls like brown bears, sheeps, monkeys, elephants, snakes, lions, tigers, etc. Me and my siblings are having a great photo time inside there. I feel lovely and joyful for all interior design which teddy bear had placed. Love this place much! Worth to visit once in lifetime.

There are lots of teddy bears in different dressing inside the museum. It cost KRW10,000 per entry but my opinion is it doesn't worth this amount of money as this museum majors in displaying teddy bear collections in the display box, numerous of human size teddy bears satisfy your photo shooting desires. As compare to KRW10,000 spent in the Jeju Village Folk where cultural living of Jeju residents in the earlier century can be experienced, it's more worthy. Desire to enter this museum was due to the Korea drama series   若モ?, and I expected to have the display of the human size teddy bears in different room with different theme enable for photo session (something like Madame Tussaud's Wax museum) but it is not the way. All the theme teddy are inside the display box. You can just sight seeing it people collection.

There are a few attractions within the same area. The teddy bear museum has 3 floors,with teddy bear exhibits and also it's history. There where some with themes and also resembles idols and famous people  and some that moves. There is also an elvis show with teddy bear on level 2 theatre. The outdoor photo taking area has a few exhibits too.

There are 3 teddy bear museums in Jeju Island, but this is the only one you could touch and hug, that?s why it?s called safari, while the teddy bears in the other two are kept in the glass box. Although I am not a big fans of soft toys, it?s still cute to see them.

There are 3 levels to the place. All 3 levels showcase bears of different ages and make. Many are modelled after heroes of the present and future, there's Disney bears, Korean culture bears, Moon bears etc. There's even a Steve Jobs bear on level 1 (within the shopping area). There's quite a fair bit of 100+ year old bears and i find these more fascinating than the rest. Sadly, the most crowded place is the shopping area on level 1 where tourist buys all sorts of momento bears.

There are 2 teddy bear museums in Jeju. I don't have the address of the one that I went to, but it's not the one in Jungmun, which is the older one and where you'll only see teddy bears in glass cases. The newer teddy bear museum has teddy bears that are displayed according to themes, where you can pose together  with the teddy bears, and even touch and hug them. This is definitely more interactive than the ones in glass cases.

There are 2 major teddy bear themed attractions in Jeju, One is the Teddy Bear Museum and the other is Jeju Teseum. The Teddy Bear Museum is for mohair connoisseurs, but the bears there are all boxed up in glass exhibits. That is why given the limited amount of time we had in Jeju, we chose to visit Teseum. There are a lot of photo opportunities where we and especially our kids can pose with the many cuddly large-sized teddys at Teseum. The keyword here is interaction.

The title summed it all up. I love stuffed toys, but even I found the place overpriced and boring. The ones that held my interest were those actual historical bears. But that's the end it. The elvis show was terrible too. We left the place within the hour.  Take your money and time else where. Jeju has more to offer than this!

The teddy bears in many styles, very funny and complete! We can also do the interactive pose in the stage and take some picture there, ex: go hunting with teddy, being proposed by teddy (!), sing along with teddies band, etc.

The teddy bear musuem is filled with a vast variety of teddy bears in different sections. These teddy bears were build to replicate a safari zoo, an aquarium, a palace, an art gallery and many more. There is side information of history of teddy bear and a gallery with ancient greek gods. Try to spot the most expensive teddy bear in the world! Apart from that, its located beside an expressway. Travelling to there might need a bus or taxi ride. Its worth a visit, but not interesting enough for me to come back again. There is too some eateries around there to settle your hunger needs. The musuem requires some entrance fee.

The Teddy Bear Museum is quite a fun attraction to visit if you like teddy bears! There's soooo many teddy bears around! With different themes, different era and even teddy bears of very popular characters! (something like the teddy bear version of Madame Tussauds)Full review: http://wanderer.summeree.com/travel/korea/jeju/teddy-bear-museum/

The Teddy Bear museum is near other attractions in Seogwipo.  Opposite is the Believe it or Not Museum.  If you have watched the korean drama Goong (The Palace or Princess Hours) , this place place is probably something you would like to visit.  I like teddy bears and it's fun to look into all those dressed up teddy bears.

The teddy bear museum is exactly what it's title states.  It's teddy bears in every shape and size.  The first area has historical teddy bears, dating back as far as the turn of the century (1900's).  The second section is works of art redone with teddy bears and finally, there is an outdoor exhibit including a 9 meter tall teddy bear that makes a showing every hour on the hour.  Young kids that like teddy bears and such will have a great time visiting here.  My daughter adored everything.  It is a little pricey, but if you rent a car to get around they often give you a book with coupons for the various attractions on the island or you can book in advance online at a discount price.

The Teddy Bear Museum is a pleasant surprise. The museum is very close to The Lotte Hotel and just across the street from Ripley?s Believe it or Not in Jungmun.  The exterior is nice. I wonder if the Louvre Museum was an inspiration for the conical architectural design of the museum.  The exhibitions consisted of many famous pictures and major events in human history. The difference is that in this museum, the teddy bears have taken over. So you will see Teddy Bear versions of Neil Armstrong on the moon, Michael Jordan dunking a basket ball, Elvis Presley rocking a guitar, Psy showing us Gangnam Style, and Marilyn Monroe, etc.  It is interesting, cute and amusing.  I am really glad I visited this museum and you should visit it too even if it is just for the laughs. It is adorable.

The Teddy Bear museum is a fun stop. There are many displays of teddy bears in various historical, cinematic, and pop-culture type settings. Take your camera and visit each floor. The gift shop at the end is full of fun teddy bear treasures as well. Definitely a good stop for anyone. We went on a rainy day, but it would also be fun on a hot day if you are looking to get out of the heat. Fairly easy to find, it's located in a popular tourist area.
The Teddy bear museum has pictures of different famous arts and history. Examples (the mona lesa, WWII, THE KISS)

The place was rather quiet when we visited (it was on a Sunday morning) despite the heavy traffic from Seoul the day before. We were given pamphlets in English, while most of the displays were in Korean language. There are many teddy bears in display and most have been displayed/posed in accordance with certain themes (like Hollywood, Snow White, landing on the moon etc). It was interesting.There was an Elvis show, with teddy bears swaying their hips to Elvis's concert in Hawaii (if I'm correct) and that was entertaining for the kids.Outdoors is a small park with human size teddy figures, great for picture taking. Remember to take pictures with large teddy outside.There is also a cafe but we did not stop by since we had breakfast earlier. In the pamphlet, we saw a train ride but we couldn't locate it anywhere. May have missed it.There was one floor for shopping and there is a large selection of teddy bears to bring home. Maybe pricey but the quality is quite good.The place is convenient for families with small children (the kids were not terrified) and stroller friendly as there is an elevator available. There is also free parking outside.As usual, for Korean tourist attractions, there are discount vouchers available. Just have to know where to get it :)

The museum was so awful and pathetic, smell dust and you can meet creepy and gloomy teddybear inside. We had lots of fun with my friends because we decided to laugh at the situation instead of being angry for spending 9000 wons at this place... Please note that if you want to wear drama disguise you'll be charge 5000 wons more...

The museum is not too big, you'll be finished around 30min.  The teddy bears collections are awesome, and for kdrama mania, there is a spot dedicated to the famous Princess Hours drama.  There are other museums nearby so you can plan the visit together with other nearby attractions,  most of the attractions close by 18.00 so plan accordingly

The museum is interesting and probably really fun with children. It is a little strange as there are bears dressed up as princesses, maybe even British royalty and whole safaris. It was interesting to say the least, but I would rather spend my time outside.

The museum has a vast collection of very cute and adorable exotic bears. Bears made to look like Van Gogh, Steve Jobs and even Michael Jackson. Entrance fee is reasonable and includes both the indoor and the outdoor portions of the museum. Outdoor has limited exhibits.

The museum has a lot of teddy bears (e.g.   Goong   or   Princess hours   teddy bears, etc) well protected in a glass boxes. A total of 3 levels in the building, displaying different kind of teddys and you can buy some souvenirs from the ground level. At the grond level, there are also teddys which you can take picture with (e.g. Steve Jobs, Psy, etc).Outside the building, there are some other teddys which you can also take pictures with. It would be fun if you love teddys but if you are not, it would be quite boring. Nothing much you can do, other than taking pictures and buying souvenirs. However, it still worth a go if you are curious about the variety of teddy bears being displayed inside. The admission fee is around 8,000 won (if i didn't remember wrongly).

The interior was nice with teddy bears as the main characters. The costumes the bear was wearing was splendid. Other than bears there?s a mini safari displaying animals such as lions, bears, tigers etc. Overall, for adults you can finish visiting the place within 20 mins.

The history of teddy bears is interesting and there are some examples of early teddy bears.  There are also teddy bears dressed up in various outfits, including as astronauts landing on the moon and a fashion show.  Don't miss the Elvis Teddy bears, including the singing Elvis.

The entrance fee was quite high, but it was a very fun family outing.  Our son loves teddy bears so this was great.  There were a lot of displays of bears in various famous places and dressed as famous people in history - cool.
The entrance fee was quite expensive. Bear was so cute. I like the history of Teddy bear. And it was impressive to see the first teddy bear in the world !! Near this museum, it was Chocolate factory.

The description at each stop was brief brief brief. I wonder why we came here...What took the longest amount of time??? The darn sales pitch conducted by a Korean auntie who claimed to be a BIG star just because she acted once in a local drama. The sales pitch was held inside a shabby shack. As it was winter the stuffiness was still bearable. Can you imagine if you came in summer??? With her broken Chinese (she turned to our tour guide for any sentences containing slightly more complex grammar) she enthusiastically tried to sell us this & that especially her biggest profit spinner - honey. She did not let her lack of fluency in Chinese stop her from making big bucks out of tourists. Not only that she even tried to sell us the many   benefits   of her empty honey glass bottle! Namely what we could do with it after we had finished eating the honey - Coin bank kitchen container blah blah blah & blah blah blah. Yakkity yakkity yak. She gave those who wanted to try a tiny teaspoon of her honey. And at the end of her sales pitch instead of letting tourists approached her if they were interested in buying she walked to each & every one of us while we were still seated (!) to ask if we wanted to buy. I think this must be because she knew that we would all walk out without buying anything if she just stand there & wait for people to come to her. So she took the more aggressive approach. Unfortunately I fell for her aggressive sales tactic & had to fork out a hefty sum for her   unique   honey. I say 'hefty' sum because when we were at the airport waiting to transfer for our flight to Seoul we saw a souvenir shop selling the SAME honey at a price which was 10000 won LESSER than what the darn old woman sold us!!! Oh man we were all so pissed! We had been cheated!!! Warning to tourists: Do NOT buy honey at this village museum!!!

The collection of teddy bears is good and very nicely organized according to themes. I especially loved the collections of very old teddy bears and the stories behind them and their owners that really touched a soft spot in my heart. There were also very vintage Winnie the Pooh bears that were really an eye-opener, as well as bears wearing traditional korean costumes depicting scenes of ancient korean life that I liked. The outdoors section of the exhibits were however not very impressive and when my friend and I visited the museum in June, the museum was very warm indoors. We were sweating profusely as we looked at the exhibits and in fact found it a joy to go outdoors into the sun, which turned out to be cooler. This prevented me from giving the attraction a four star rating. However, the collection is really a must-see for teddy bear lovers and it will undoubtedly be a more enjoyable place to visit in other months of the year.
The bears are adorable! It is also a 10 min walk from the cheonjeyeon waterfalls, alive museum and 3100w away from the cliffs!

The admission fee is 10000 won per pax, so it's probably the most expensive admission ticket you'll pay in Jeju.If you're a fan of bears, though, this is photo heaven =](And maybe shopping heaven! The prices of the bears are really exorbitant though.)

thank your for coming and your comment as well. as you said it's a perfect place to the teddy bear lover ,family and also anyone who wants to memorize their childhood. thank again have a nice weekend ^^
thank you so much. you must be a teddy bear lover, right? ^^

thank you so much for visiting.At the museum, there are two main galleries, gallery extra, souvenir shop, cafe, Elvis theater and outdoor garden. you might had wonderful time with lovely teddy bears at the museum, we believe. thank for the review and have a good day ^^
thank you so much for visiting , we are so afraid to hear you haven't taken your time long at the garden .  however we believe that you had wonerful time at the teddy bear museum. have a nice day ^^
thank you so much for the visit. in the museum , lots of teddy bears are exhibited by various interesting concept. have a wonderful day ^^

Thank you for your visit. you seem to be a Korean drama lover,too. we exhibit the goong teddy bears which were presented at the drama. you probably notice that already, right?  again appreciate you comment and have a nice day^^

thank you for the visit. well , first of all we are so afraid of you were not so feel good at the teddy bear museum. however our museum consist of two main theme galleries. the history and the art.  and also there are extra gallery, Elvis concert theater and out door garden. we will take an effort to present visitor more exciting display and exhibition . thank you again and have a good day ^^
Teddy Bears dressed up in art and history, what's not to love? Museum isn't big, exhibition are on two levels. Elvis show is entertaining.

Teddy bears comically arranged to recreate different points in history. I must give credit for the details of the handiwork, including teeny-weeny plates and swords. A must-see for teddy bear afficionados... if you happen to stumble into it, you may be like WTF.

Teddy Bear Safari is the world?s first exhibition theme park with various real life-sized wildlife and marine stuffed animals and teddy bears. Moreover, you will also meet our teddy bears dressed in traditional clothes of countries around the world and as gods from Greek mythology. Lastly, some of our teddy bears will be dressed up as Korean celebrities whom you may be well aware of.

Teddy bear museum located at Jungmun resort at Jeju. It's easy to reach the resort by Airport Limousine 600 from Grace hotel bus stop or others. So many teddy bear with different characters and customs. We can take a photo with big Teddy bear like Einstein, Steve Jobs, Van Gogh etc.There's a garden with many teddy bear statues. So cute!

Teddy Bear Museum in Jeju opened in 2001 and boasts for owning the largest collection of teddy bears.  What differentiates this museum from the rest is that Korea's history was told using the bears.  It was cute and a not so serious approach that would cater to the children.The museum consists of 2 Exhibition halls namely the hall of history and the hall of art.  This museum serves as the home for as many as 1,500 bears that includes the luxurious Louis Vuitton bear.

Sounds odd that it is actually my favourite attraction.. I love teddy bears. This place does not require much trekking like the sunrise peak, manjanggul cave, waterfall etc but it is a fantastic place to spend one or two hours just staring at the teddy bear exhibits with some even moving and each exhibit with a different theme. You get to see Elvis teddy bear performing   live   with his friends too. First time seeing teddy bear moving, wow experience for me. The souvenir shop is expensive though... nonetheless do give it a visit if you are a teddy lover! There is a Steve Jobs teddy, Einstein Teddy, quite creative and a twist to the usual brooding teddy we see.
Some of the bears on display are quite old and dusty. Generally, give it a try if you have not been to other teddy bear museum.

So, perhaps this comparison is unfair, but if you have to choose between the two: the Teddy Bear Museum and this Teseum, I would personally choose this Teseum because the Teseum is slightly cheaper, closer to Jeju City, and way less pretentious (that may sound weird, but that's more or less what the difference was). Teseum was laid back, a bit more interactive, and generally understanding of that a visit to see Teddy bears would mean visiting the childish side on all of us. The Teddy Bear museum was more like an anthropological study of teddy bears or something, aka, less fun, a bit more uptight.For those in the group who were not as interested in the actual display, they could opt out and still purchase teddy bears. The gift shop was conveniently open to everyone visiting and there were a few convenience stores and such around.

smaller than what i thought. But a lot of bear with different characters inside. For a hurry visitor, you would just need no longer than 1 hour to finish all part of the museum. The elvis bear show was nice but quite short and not really worth to see, thats why it is free.

Since their official website is unclear about opening hours in June, I called the 1330 Korea Travel Hotline and was informed that the museum was indeed open late under summer hours. So after spending 45 minutes in and 30,000+ ?? on a taxi to visit the area with my girlfriend, who absolutely loves teddy bears, we arrived at 6:10pm. With doors still open and people still inside, we were told the museum closed at 6pm. Self-Drive Holiday in Jeju:Everyone loves going on holidays and I believe a great percentage of these do so on guided tours. Guided tours are fine where convenience is concerned; hotels, meals, itineraries, transport, flights, places of interests to visit, entrance fees etc. etc. are all taken care of by the tour company. As I had discovered decades ago, despite all the conveniences of a guided tour, there are drawbacks that would put one off such tours completely; not being able to sleep-in and wake up as and when you want, having limited time to enjoy the various places of interests or enjoy your lunch while taking in the magnificent scenery from a mountain top restaurant , having to put up with other travellers who simply cannot or are not bothered to be on time, not being able to visit or enjoy other interesting places that are rarely included in tour itineraries, to list a few. Ever since my first guided tour holiday overseas, I have opted for a self-drive holiday and I am very sure there are many out there who would love to do so too,  but refrained from doing so because of a lack of information and perhaps, apprehensive about what it would entail to do a self-drive holiday in a foreign land. This guide is to help dispel those apprehensions and provide the necessary information for you to successfully make that first self-drive holiday in the Honeymoon Island of Jeju, and hopefully, many more thereafter in other destinations of your dreams.Preparation:Many experts would advise, and rightly so, that you should first read up all the necessary information on driving at the destination that you will be holidaying in. However, in my opinion, what is more important is having the self-confidence to drive in a foreign land. Sometimes, things can go wrong, road and weather conditions can change to the extent that no pre-reading or preparation can help, but, with that very important self-confidence, it will see you through. You must also have a flexible mind set and be ready to accommodate changes when necessary ? only then will you be able to thoroughly enjoy your self-drive holiday. Having said that, I must say that driving in Jeju is a walk-in-the-park, quite unlike, for example, driving through the mountain pass between Sun Moon Lake and Hualien County in Taiwan ? that is a drive I would never recommend to the feint hearted.International Driving Permit ? you will need to obtain an International Driving Permit to be able to rent a car in Jeju, and for that matter, in most other countries. It can be easily obtained at AAS and it costs only $20.00 and is valid for one year. You would also want to search for information on all the places of interests and decide on which of those to visit during your stay in Jeju. This is to help you plan and minimize travelling time. These can be had at the Korea Tourism Centre at Samsung CentreChoice of Hotel ? There are many hotels catering to different needs and budgets to choose from. The one most often asked question is the location ? to stay in Jeju-si or Seogwipo-si? My experience tells me that it makes no difference ? it is just a matter of choice. If you are arriving in Jeju late at night, then, perhaps, you may wish to stay in a hotel that is near the airport, to minimize your night driving had you decided on a hotel in Seogwipo-si. We landed in Jeju at 2000 hrs, collected our car at 2100 hrs and drove to Seogwipo-si where our hotel was situated. It was a pleasant forty-five minute drive with guidance from the GPS unit.Car Rental Company:There are many car rental companies in Jeju, but you will most likely come across only a handful if you search the internet ? Kumho, AJ Rentals (AVIS), SIXT, Donga and Jeju Rent-a-Car. Do note, though, that there are more than a dozen of competing rental companies at the airport to choose from if you prefer to shop around for the best rates and cars upon your arrival. I book mine through AJ Rentals, not only because of the brand name, but it also provided the best rates among the others on the net and it did not require me to pay in advance upon confirmation of my reservation. To rent the car, you will need to have an International Driving Permit (obtain it from AAS), your local driving license and passport. You can pay either in cash or credit card. Type of Car:The type of car you choose is totally dependent on your preference and budget ? luxury or basic. However, do consider the available boot space that will be needed to accommodate your luggage. As a guide, the boot of a KIA K3 can accommodate only three large suitcases with no space for a smaller, fourth piece. In a situation where there are four adults, the smaller, fourth suitcase will have to share estate space in the back seat with two other passengers. The cost of rental is dependent on the type of car, number of days and the period of travel. As a guide, a KIA K3 cost approximately S$60.00 per day for 5 days during the holiday season in November. The rate includes insurance, CDW and the use of a English language GPS, with collection and return at the airport. The rates of the other rental companies that I surveyed were cheaper, however, I cannot vouch for their quality nor service support. You decide at your own risk. The overall condition of the car was good. The only ?defect? was the slight steering alignment problem but it was not something that would put us in danger at any time. Maps:Do you need a map when it is very likely that you will be relying on the GPS? YES! A map is necessary for planning your routes and selecting the places of interests to visit.You can easily obtain a detailed map of Jeju Island, with all the major highways and feeder routes from your local Korean Tourism office. You can also obtain these from the car-rental companies when you collect your car in Jeju. You can use it to plan your route, estimate the travel time and locate other possible places of interests that you don?t find on the standard tourist trail. You can use this same map to write down the telephone numbers of the places of interests that you plan to visit. You will need these numbers for keying into the GPS system to guide you to your destination. I made it a point to re-confirm that the telephone numbers are current by asking the hotel staff to extract the numbers from their computer system. This proved to be very useful. Collecting Your Car At The Airport:After clearing immigration and customs, proceed to gate 5 of the arrival terminal. Opposite the gate, there is a green, covered walk-way with a sign that says ?Car Rentals?; it will lead you to a building where there are a lot of car-rental companies. If you had pre-booked your car, look for the car-rental company in the building. However, do take note that this building houses the local car rental companies. For the international brands such as Avis, Hertz and the other bigger local companies, they are housed in another location outside the airport. You will need to check with them when you are doing the booking or email them for the information. If the collection centre of the car rental company that you booked with is located outside the airport, wait for their shuttle bus at Gate 5. You will recognize their shuttle bus by their brand name boldly emblazoned on the sides of the bus. Since I booked my car through Avis, I took the ?AJ? shuttle bus to their rental office on the outskirts of the airport. The shuttle bus runs on a regular schedule. Arriving at the front of the office, you take a queue ticket. If you had made reservations, it takes just a few seconds to call up your reservation after presenting your passport, driver's licence and International Driving Permit. You will be shown the rental agreement with all the details pertaining to the type, class, number of days of rental, total costs and any other relevant information. With Avis, the GPS is included in the rental, whereas for other rental companies that I had enquired with, the GPS is charged separately. After you have signed the rental agreement, you will be shown your car. You then drive it off to the inspection building where they will go through the car with you to identify any minor damages, scratches, dents etc. They will also have you verify that the fuel tank is full and instruct you on the use of the GPS before getting you to sign off the acknowledgement form. Do ensure that the GPS is an English language version. Keep the documents safely in the glove-compartment and be sure to get the telephone number of the station that you will return the car to. You will need this number to key into the GPS system to guide you back. You then proceed on your way, presumably, to your hotel for a much needed rest after the long flight to Jeju.When returning the car, you just need to drive back to the same depot from where you had collected it. Just key the given number into the GPS. Upon arrival, follow the sign, ?Car Return? and head for an available lot. The attendant there will check the car with you and when all is in order, he hands you a form to sign after you have returned the key to him. You then take the shuttle bus that will take you to the departure hall at the airport.The use of the GPS:Different makes and models operate slightly differently from one another, however, the common function that generalizes all of them is the use of the telephone number of a particular hotel, attraction or establishment to program the location into the GPS. For example, the telephone number of our hotel, Ocean Palace Hotel, Jeju, is 064 - 7305800. To navigate to the hotel from the airport, I just had to key in the number 7305800 and simply touch the 'Navigate' button and voila, it calculates the shortest route and starts the voice navigation system in a jiffy - it's as simple as that. From then on, just follow the voice navigation to get you to your hotel. If you make a wrong turn or pass a junction where you were supposed to turn, do not panic. Just relax and drive on ? it will re-direct you back to the planned route or at times, provide you with a new course. In fact, we had a lot of fun and discovered many new places of interest by intentionally turning off to smaller but interesting-looking roads just to see what lies ahead and where it will eventually lead us to ? that is the beauty of a self-drive holiday. Driving in Jeju:Jeju has a coastal ring road of approximately 181 km, not counting the connecting highways linking the North-South-East ?West regions. The coastal scene is a sight to behold! It is left-hand driving in Jeju.To those who have never driven on the left side of the road, it takes a little getting used to, physically as well as in your mind. It gets a little more confusing when turning at traffic junctions, especially when driving through ? stopping gives you an opportunity to orientate yourself and prepare in your mind the lane to take when turning. To minimize this confusion, always try to follow a car in front of you which is turning in the same direction as you. It is also helpful to remember that when turning, the roadside kerb will always be on the right of the driver. The roads, save for the highways, are slightly narrower than the roads we are used to in Singapore.Generally, the speed limits are:30 Km / hr within 100 m of school zones50 Km / hr in town areas60 Km / hr in the outskirts of town70 Km / hr along highwaysThe speed limits change quite frequently, so it is advisable to keep a look-out for the change in speed limits. There are speed-cameras practically everywhere, usually positioned up on traffic lights, lamp-posts and in some places, hidden behind 'boxes' manned by a policeman. So, if you wish to spend your money supporting the policemen, speed on at your own risk.The local drivers can, at times, be quite reckless. Just like we have hell-drivers here, there are hell-drivers in Jeju too, but not too many. Just stay alert and always be on the look-out using your wing and rearview mirrors all the time. Except for the main areas of Jeju-si and Seogwipo-si, most of the roads around the island are quite free of traffic.  To estimate the time needed to travel any distances, take an average speed of 45 km/hr.Parking:Generally free parking along kerb-sides and paid parking in some buildings and are generally available easily. Most hotels have free parking for their guests ? do check with the hotel management that you have booked with. Petrol cost: As at Nov 2014: Krw 1750 / ltrPlanning Your Routes:Planning your routes is totally at your own whim and fancy, depending on the places of interest as well as the available time you have on the island. If you have a few days ( I would recommend a minimum of five days), perhaps you may wish to consider the following suggestion:1. Day 1 ? Arrival and check into hotel. This sample itinerary is on the assumption that your hotel is in Seogwipo. 2. Day 2 ? Explore the west scenic coastal drive (Route 1132) of Sagye, Gosan-Ilwa, Hagwi-Aewol and visit the places of interest along this route ( Mt Sangkaksan / Songkaksan / Yongmeori). There are many cafes (especially along the Coastal Cafe Road) and bbq restaurants for stops of aromatic coffee and grilled black pig meat. Explore Jeju-si city (underground shopping mall) and return via highway 1131 where the famous ?Forest Tunnel? is located. After dinner, take a drive to the Lotte World Resort for some very beautiful night scenery of the giant windmills.3. Day 3 ? Go East this time along the Pyeoson, Sehwa-Jongdal and Gimyeong ? Haengwon coastal routes. Stopover at Seongsan Ilchubong (Sunrise Peak). Have dinner in Jeju-si before doing a night drive back to Seogwipo. 4. Day 4 ? Alternative 1Drive to Seongsan Port in the north-east via the eastern coastal route and park your car there. Purchase your ferry tickets to Udo Island and spend a very interesting day there. You can tour the island by buying the hop-off-on bus tickets or for the adventurers, you can hire the quad-bikes or scooters. Alternative 2 ? visit the popular tourist spots such as the Trick-art museum, teddy bear museum, waterfalls, submarine tours, Green Tea museum, Geomun Oreum, Citrus fruit farms, mysterious road, etc etc....5. Day 5 ? Check out of hotel for catch your flight back home.Have a safe and enjoyable holiday!Telephone Numbers of Attractions For GPS:Citrus Fruit Museum - 732 2114Geomun Oreum - 7108981Joongang Underground Mall - 723 1510Jusenggeolli Cliffs - 7381521Lotte Hotel - 731 1000Alive Museum - 805 0888Trick Art Museum - 787 8774Seongeup Folk Village - 787 1179Traditional 5 day market (Jeju-si) - 7435985Seongsan Harbour (Ferry to Udo Island) - 782 5671Seongsan Ilchubong - 783 0959Cheongyejeong Waterfall - 760 6331Cheongjiyeong Waterfall - 733 1528Jeongbang Waterfall - 733 1530Teddy Bear Museum - 738 7600Jeju Folk Village - 787 4501Jeju Sea-World - 784 2333Aqua Planet Jeju - 780 0900Manjanggul Cave - 710 7903Oedolgae - 760 3033
