If you enjoy nature, hiking one of the olle trails is a must-do while you're in jeju. It will not be an easy hike and not all parts of the trail are scenic but there are sufficient sights to blow you away and be left in awe of nature. This is also the best way to experience jeju's natural beauty (after all this is what its most famous for and not for teddy bears). It is also arguably the least touristy thing to do during your trip here. You can do as long or as short of the trails as you like; there are trails passing through hot tourist destinations where you'll see many tourist buses, local villages, rice fields, even resorts. You'll walk on sand, on rocks by the ocean, and if you time it correctly you'll be able to catch a gorgeous sunset along jeju's coastline. Be sure not to get stuck in a remote area after sunset as it can be difficult to get out. If you're doing a multi-day hike, there are many pensions located along the olle routes and you can just pop in for a night.Suggest to go with at least one other person in case you get lost (there are some places where the markings are not so visible/well maintained). If you rented a car, dont drive. Wear comfortable shoes and bring lots of water and snacks!

I loved my hike in Hallasan. We were a couple and we decided to take the 'most challenging trial' - Gwaneumsatrail (8.7 km).  There are four Hallasan trails on and around the mountain, but only two of these trails will take you all the way up to the volcano?s crater lip ? theGwaneneumsa trail is one of these, theSeongpanaktrail is the other one. It is important that you check beforehand which trial is open, because it depends on the weather forecast. In my case all the 4 trials were partially open which meant that the crater lip was not accessible unfortunately. There is a website you  check (in Korean) or you can simply do what I did and ask the staff at the reception of the hotel. Each trials is easily accessible by bus, however the buses are not that frequent - for example 1 every hour for the Gwaneneumsa train, so you might need a bit of planning. Our trail was accesible for 6 out of the 8.7 km and took us to the first shelter (1500m elevation) the hike took us.6 hours back/forth including a quick lunch break; the pace wasn't that high but we weren't that slow either. If you want to access the crater lip, one think that you need to bear in mind is that you need to make it to the first shelter by 12-13 depending on the season (November was 12.00pm).Another thing to remember is that there is no convenience store or food vendor available during the hike, so you want to pack some food (kimbap is a good option) and water. As the hike itself, I really enjoyed it, you will feel immerse in the nature and you will enjoy a nice variety of vegetation depending on the altitude.

I didn't reach the summit but hiking the Eorimok and Yeongsil trails didn't provide amazing views as far as I was concerned, but it's definitely worth doing.Take the 740 bus from City Bus Terminal to Eorimok (krw1800, 45 min) or Yeongsil Ticket Office (krw 2800, 60 min). Bus leaves CBT at 07:00, 08:00, 09:00, 10:00. You don?t want to set off after 10:00 as you won?t get back! Last returns are 17:36 (Yeongsil) and 17:55 (Eorimok) April through October.I took the Eorimok trail up (there?s an easy 1km walk from the bus stop to the trailhead) and reached the Witseoreum shelter in 2 hours, including stops. The first 2.4km are quite tough but it gets much easier the further you go. If you?re worried about your ankles then wear hiking boots but trail shoes are fine. The descent down via Yeongsil was a leisurely 90 mins but it feels like it would be a slightly tougher climb compared to Eorimok. There?s also a 2.5km downhill walk from the trailhead to the bus stop, so bear that in mind if you decide to start from Yeongsil. The scenery is much better on Yeongsil, although those with vertigo may find it tough, even with the very good safety barriers on the route. Eorimok doesn?t have those problems but the first 2km is under forest cover, with little scenery to admire for most of the climb.If you want to hike to the summit start very early, which probably means you'll need a car in case you miss the last bus back.There are clean, normal toilets at both entrances and at the Witseoreum stop. You will have to carry all trash back down as there are no bins anywhere on the mountain. You can buy hot instant noodles at the Witseoreum but you?ll have to carry it back down. I bought several buns and pastries at Paris Baguette for my hike.

Great location with beautiful sightseeing...Jeju Island, also known as the   Island of the Gods,   is a popular vacation spot for Koreans and foreigners. Despite attempts to market the island as   the Hawaii of Korea,   climatologically and geographically it bears little in similarity to the Hawaiian Islands in the U.S. The island offers visitors a wide range of activities: hiking on Halla-san (South Korea's highest peak) or Olle-gil(routes), catching sunrises and sunsets over the ocean, riding horses, touring all the locales from a favorite television K-drama, or just lying around on the sandy beaches. Although tourism is one of the main industries on the island, many of the hotels and other tourist areas are run by mainland companies, so much of the income never gets put back into the local economy. Also, since the attractions are geared towards tourists, many of the entrance fees can be hefty (although the locally owned and operated ones tend to be cheaper). Back in the days of yore --  how far back, no one can be certain --  three demigods came forth from three holes in the ground located near the northern coast of an island to the south of Korea.  These three demigods lived as hunter-gatherers until a ship arrived bearing three princesses, domesticated farm animals and seeds for growing grain. The princesses married with the demigods, and the Tamna Kingdom was born. Today, we know Tamna, which ended in 1404 with the coming of the Joseon Kings -- Korea's last imperial dynasty -- as Jejudo or Jeju Island.  We know that beloved and mystical site as Samseonghyeol (  sam   means three in Korean). It is a special place and, particularly for history buffs, a   must-see   in Jeju.  The holes, which likely were once active thermal vents on this volcanic isle, are surrounded by a protective Stonehenge-like ring and a mini-forest/park of lush and majestic, mature trees and flowers.  It is quite pleasant, and on a warm summer's day, a cool respite from the city that has grown around it.  There's a small museum showing a film about the founding of Tamna.  The film is in Korean, but if you look at the exhibits there before watching the film, you will understand it much better.  It is not readily possible to actually photograph the holes unless you have a ladder, a drone, a long selfie stick or happen to be about 8 feet tall...this would be my one disappointment about the site.  But there is an official photo mounted nearby.  If you have the time, plan to spend 1-1.5 hours there, to take in the walking trails, museum, movie and various historic buildings.  You will also be greeted by some of the original 18th century dolhareubangs (protective   stone grandfathers  ) remaining on the island.  It's a good outing for singles, couples, friends and families.  Even young children can enjoy the birds, flowers, stones and many benches located throughout the park.  Admission is quite nominal...2,500 KRW adults, 1,700 teens; 1,000 children 7-12.

But quite overpriced 10,000won for a key chain teddy, 35,000won for a palm size teddy. I don't even dare to look at how much the larger bear cost.

10,000 KRW per person. When you enter, pay for admission, and start in third floor, go down floors in order. In the basement, theres gift shop, cafe, and theres few more exhibits to see. Perfect for kids, fun for adults. Wish there could be more exhibitions of teddy bears. But if was nice!
You travel to get different experiences and this was definitely one of those. Close to Jeju city and free car park. Definitely an adults only/couple only museum.

You definitely need more than 5-6hrs to explore this beautiful island. Last ferry which leaves back from Udo is 6pm so kindly plan your day accordingly. We were there only for 2 hrs so took a bicycle to explore this little paradise.  Views and trails on this island are amazing with a lot of food options available. My recommendation is to rent the little car to drive around if you are short on time and its easier to go up the slopes in the car . The ferry ride is also not very expensive up and down from Udo.

You can get right up to the falls even as it empties into the sea. Where sneaks that day because there are a lot of rocks. Be careful and take lots of pictures. A taxi or bike ride is preferable but you can easily walk to the entrance it is just out of the way of the town
You can access it by ferry. Rent a scooter at the Island. With little kids I would recommend to take the car with on the ferry. Nice sights and views!

Yes! I love this place for its natural scene and beautiful environment. It is really quiet and peaceful except at the base where there are plenty of tourists. Note there are several hiking trails of different distance and demands. Be sure to read to it and do note the closing time in different seasons. Some closes as early as 1330hr in winter due to early sun set. Most charged entries for vehicles into the car park. Small car (Kia Morning) which I rented from rentalcar.com was charged 1000 won (peanut) Put on right shoes and gear. There are air blower (See pic) available to dust off the mud or dirt from your shoes before u step into your car. Love that. Enjoy the beauty.
Yes u car still moving even free gear (N)...u all can plan come here while ontwy to MOUNTAIN HALLASAN it same road..
Yeongsil trail said to have the best autumn views. Be prepared to walk 2.5km(along the road) from car ticket office ( No 740 Bus-stop ) or catch a taxi up to trail entrance.

Yakcheonsa Temple is a famous Buddhist Templet located in Jeju island south of mainland Korea. The temple was built in 1981 by a Buddhist monk . It has three floors  It has a large Buddhist prayer hall. It is also famous for housing 80000 Buddhas all located on the second floor encased in glass.  It also has smaller statue of Buddha surrounded by lotus flowers under a pair of intricately carved protective dragons. The view from the top floor is veryy beaytiful facing the sea
With 20-30 Wind Power Plants on both sides of the road. It is supposed to be an enclosed private areas  but it is not fenced. Can only go with a car or rented cab.

While visiting a friend who works in Jeju my family drove around to visit places casually with a flexible schedule. We planned to visit the temple for half an hour but stayed more than an hour. The name of the temple means medical spring and the flowing water from a 3-dragon-head fountain next to the temple store tasted good and sweet. Although the temple was built for only around 20 years the buildings and layout followed the traditional design. The main building faces exact south that can view the sea. The bell tower is located in the east for sunrise and the drum tower is located in the west for sunset. The main building's first floor wooden windows are beautifully carved with inspiring stories covered by traditional white paper but not glass. There is a traditional Korean painting exhibition of Buddha of Compassion in the basement and it's gorgeous. The best part of our visit was that not many people around. We got the chance to enjoy the quietness and even used the mats inside the temple at the back of the first floor to meditate a short while. There are grapefruit trees in the yards along the way to bathroom.

While learning about the life of Jeju folk village we enjoyed the gardens farms and orchards. They are beautiful and being taken care well. It was our first time that we saw cabbage with flowers.During our visit it was almost toward the end of closing time and probably that's the reason there're not many visitors.

When I was planning my trip to Jeju  I found this museum has got half positive and half negative comments from travelers. Well ??I decided to have a look by myself. When our car got near to the place  there was a strong smell. I was then told that there is a piggery farm nearby which stinks out the whole place. The ticket was not cheap but it included a cup of coffee plus a discount in the shop. The appearance of the building is interesting with an open courtyard. The first impression was not so bad.However when I got inside  it was quite disappointing. I think the management should consider a renovation  or at least a deep cleaning and some maintenance. I just felt I was in a dusty old weird mansion. Maybe those exhibits are precious and rare  but they are not well presented. For example  they put lots of chocolate boxes from all over the world in the same window display without proper descriptions. How can the people think that those boxes are precious when they are packed in a glass cabinet? The lighting on the second floor was horrible. The rooms were so dark adding horrific ambiance to the museum.

review: When I hear bbq I think of Kansas City and Texas sauces.  No such thing in the East.  Bbq means grilling.  But this was delicious with some chili powderesque dipping spice.  They also offered a liquid dipping sauce which I did not care for as it tasted very fishy.  Each bite of the pork cost about $1.50.  Do it is very expensive.  But worth it for the experience if not for the delicious tastes.

Went there with the intention to educate my kids on how lava could flow to the sea and came up with beautiful natural shapes such as those seen there. Great to have educational information nearby to explain the formation.  More should be done to explain how small stones also play a part in eroding pitfalls on the rock surfaces It was an easy walk from the carpark.  Some local snacks were sold at the entrance and tickets could be bought via a machine.

Went there with my friend.. We took a bus from Halla hospital (?쒕씪蹂묒썝) bus stop and took bus no. 755 and alighted at the bus stop right in front of O'Sulloc Tea Museum. The entrance is free and there is a gift shop and a cafe.. You can buy different types of teas and other products made from tea in the shop (e.g. tea packs skin care products etc). You can buy green tea ice cream green tea roll cake and beverages etc from the cafe.. The cost of the products are reasonable while some are more expensive.Opposite the road there is a big Tea farm of the tea museum. You can take pictures there but must beware of snakes (諭�議곗떖) as warned with a sign board on the tea plant.Beside the museum there is Innisfree Jejuhouse (just walking distance). There is a sign board showing the direction and the Innisfree Jejuhouse is on the left hand side of the Tea Museum. If you like Tea this is a must visit place.
Went there Sunday mid-morning. Car park was crowded with locals after /preparing for morning walk. Take a slow stroll to soak up nature's beauty. Boardwalk wide enough for wheelchair access.

Went there a few days after Xmas and the weather was cold and hence made the climb easier. If we had came during summer I would never have wanted to make the climb. As it is with the cold weather and strong winds we made the climb with 2 or 3 stops in between to catch breath and take photos of the magnificent views. If you have kids or old folks to take care I wouldn't recommend the climb.

well. this fashion street was near with my hotel & i've walked here quite many times in a week. not so special for me as i don't do shopping but i ate 2times in this street that was impressivefirst time i reached here at 1st day no any breakfast shop near around*(they are opened at 9-10am at least) quite hungry & finally i stepped in one of traditional shop that only served 3 types of food all was hangover soup ha. seem that for drunken. price not so expensive(but not cheap) and quite many stuffs. tasty but full. lady boss also quite nice although she can't well communicate with meanother times with fds that was in a quiet corridor seem quite expensive restaurant with old & korean deco. however price was acceptable & serve sausage stew. well we ate traditional sausage stew in korean style house(boss always walk out from his room & overall style was house instead of restaurant). he was quite concern do we know how to eat & taking care of our table. maybe it has no many tourist but only korean or japanese while we having dinner moment.

Well this place was big. Need to prepare to walk if you're going at non-peak hours. Why? due to the train not moving. This place features Korean village cultural show donkey / house riding costume trying & a beautiful setting to get some nice pictures. We enjoyed solid 1-2hours walking. But having to travel with small kids its quite tiring. Anyway the replicas of houses & setting was great. Enjoyed buying some quality souvenir at the gift shops. My kids just love the small maze park. I don't op for a tour guide but a head set was just enough for us to make us understand the place.One thing for sure they're snakes wandering around the place. While walking we come across 2 snakes (small). My kids was terrified! So need to be extra careful for those who bring little kids. Another set back was the small shop selling fast food. I know there's a barrier problem in language but they seem to ignore foreign tourist due to the fact we cant communicate well with each other. Very hard to buy stuff. Water! walking makes you thirsty. Pro's :- The head set helps to understand the place even-though not so many point haves explanation. Perhaps its an area for improvement.Con's :- Snakes? YikesOverall the place was ok. But will not come again..

Well is rather a unique Lava rock by the sea shore but to me it looks more like a Horse head. You may find people selling seafood by the side of the rock under simple canopy. Just be careful as you walk down to the sea because the rocks are hard .

We were staying in Seogwipo and had an extra day with nothing to do. So decided to book tickets from Klook on the day of visit. From Days Hotel in Seogwipo we would have to take two buses 201 and then 295?. The first bus is 1 hr 10-15 mins and much more frequent than the second bus which is a 5 mins ride or a 25 mins 2 km walk. Taxis are cheap starting fare of 2800 krw will get you to Aqua Planet from the 201 bus stop but they are a needle in a sack - hard to come by! Other countries??hard to reach facility ir tourist site may provide some form of free shuttle/transport but not here. Once you enter the main facility it would take you a long time to find the toilets - certainly not tourist friendly. Live shows are also all in Korean  albeit with English & Chinese subtitles. The size of this Aquarium is about one third or one quarter of the Okinawa one so we were seriously disappointed with its size and varieties of fishes available. Visit if you have a car or join a local tour or book a taxi. If using public transport like us think twice about going as its 3-4 hrs to and fro Seogwipo.

review: We were hoping to climb up to the summit. However we ere told to be there before 9 am. We hiked the Yeangsil Trail instead. It was a great experience. The trail was as per the Trod advisor reviews. Make sure you have the right shoes with the right traction. It was not that hard except for some parts of the trail. We enjoyed it very much. We bought some snacks on the trail but had to carry the trash back to our hotel!! The trail is well kept and marked. Will go back again but before 9 am so we can go to the summit. The views were fantastic . We saw a couple of deer. It was worth the visit. Make sure you arrive before 9 am if you want to go to the summit.

We were asked to put our car in neutral gear and be amazed! The road appeared to be flat but what transpired next had us in transfixed.We were figuring out the science behind it.It was all over quickly but was fun while it lasted......just like a magic show!

We went up at 6am in the morning to see the sunrise. With cold rainy weather the event was less romantic than expected but well worth and good fun for us. We went up with our 3yr old boy. The way up is very well prepared and suitable for children who like walking/climbing a bit. We carried out son partly and party he walked. Well Organised tourist attraction.Entrance fee is only W2000.Have fun!

We went to the memorial hall to see the exhibition on Kim Manduk after we visited a recreation of her travellers' in that is about 150m away.I have always admired Korea's efforts to recreate buildings and scenes fron the past that are both infirmative and interesting.The exhibit at the hall added to what we had learnt at the inn.What comes across from the information cards and exhibits was a woman dedicated to the service of others.Profit was never her main motive. Nor self-aggrandizement.We need more people like her today.

We went there on our way back after a day of sightseeing. It is good to just drive pass that stretch. But not worth if it is not on the way. You could just spend a brief less than 5mins there while staying in the car.
We went on a wet and rainy afternoon. The cliff was dull and unspectacular in such weather conditions. We parked at The Seas resort carparked and strolled through their beautiful landscaped grounds.

We went down to the second pond in rain and the stairs is quite steep so u gotta be very careful with ur steps. Upon arrival there is a platform where u can take photo of the fall. For dipping experiences u can continue hiking to fall no 1. No 3 is the farthest. U can refer to the map.

We visited Udo in our recent visit to jeju island. We couldn't see the whole island due to rainy weather. One thing the visitor should be careful about the renting of battery bike or other types of two wheelers. The store owner will ask U something unethical rate for rent and the behaviour of them are really very very bad. They behave with us very rudely.

We visited the Manjanggul Cave on a very wet day.  The floor of the cave was wet and the stones slippery. Puddles of water lined the route. It would have been all right if the light was brighter but it was not. The lighting was dim and you can easily twist an ankle if you stepped into one of the many crevasses in the floor. The dim lighting did not make things any easier and you really have to watch where you are going. Wear proper walking shoes if you do not want to slip on the stones. I felt that the lava cone that was our destination was quite dazzling but I wish the authorities had spent a little more care in making the whole walk safer for those who are mobile but who are a little unsteady on their feet like the elderly. The video presentation that we saw after the walk was good. The exhibits were well curated and gave us an idea of other earth formations resulting from volcanic activity in the area.

We visited on 23rd October. A misfortune happened at about 5.15pm when we were about to leave  our rented car could not start due to no battery. Our baby was temporarily locked in the car so a helpful bystander helped us to opened the door using manual lock and called the car rental company. After a long wait we gotten the staffs at the park to help.the 'gatekeepers' were friendly enough to let us stayed there while awaiting help to arrive. A thin tall lady staff without spectacles came to our help and called the car rental company as we could not understand the options given in Korean. She explained to us and reassured us in English fluently. She also took extra care to follow up and waited til a tow car to help to jump start the rented car. I think by that time her shift is over as few staffs waiting for her too. We are indeed thankful for her and the staffs on that day. Cocomong Ecopark does have a good commendable staff. thank you.Park wise games and design are well thought and worth the entry ticket. The slide down on tire is fun though it looked a bit scary but it is safe. Cafe has got a nice sea view.

We travelled here by bus and got completely soaking wet walking the 20 minutes from the main road to the cave. Unfortunately it wasn't worth the soaking! It was pretty boring and after 30 minutes walk up and down we were out in the ran again.I would only recommended visiting if you have a thing for geology or if you have a car and happen to be passing by.

We took one walk here. Vertical rise of about 200m through nature. A couple of hours of hiking & stopping to view the plants & birds. Great view of the crater from the top. Worth the trek. Carry lots of water if it hot!
We took a car passenger ferry to to Udo island from Jeju. This a small but beautiful island. We drove around the island and try some fresh seafood.

We stumbled upon this place whilst walking about but didn't regret it.I would be careful if you are accompanying very young children or old people as the stairs are made of rock and quite difficult to negotiate. Our 5 year old made it ok but required assistance.A nice place to visit but not much in the way of a waterfall when we were there. Perhaps they take the water in during the day? (that was a joke by the way!)
We stop here on the way to the airport. It's quiet interesting experience when the car moves. Can't help laughing inside the car as the power is off but it still moves.

We spent some days in Jeju and also visited the Manjanggul Cave. It is easy to find with car. Few parking places are available. Entrance fee is 2000 Won for adult and 1000 Won for child. We have seen much better caves but this cave was aslo somehow interesting. The cave is 1000 meter long. Walking through is easy but you shall watch your steps. It is quite dark inside and also wet. So bring flash light and some rain jacket if you want. We went without and suvived. Unfortunately a lot of people were there and noise level was high. However it is worth a visit.

We rented a car. We reached the Tea Museum just after 12 noon. The car park was already full and we had to park by the side road. The museum is more of an exhibition of tea cups with write-ups on a brief history of tea and the origins of the Osulloc tea. Easy reading for a morning activity. There is a tea merchandise section and a cafe.We ordered the green tea ice-cream and black tea ice-cream. Both were good. The tea was very intense on both the ice cream. The green tea roll was just passable for us. Drop by if you are on the way. I think at certain times of the day there maybe some demonstration on tea but nothing was written in English so not sure of the timing.
We rented a car in jeju and decided to experience the mysterious road. It was amazing how your car rolls backwards when it looks like an uphill road. A must visit place if you are in jeju.

We rent a car in jeju and drove to this place.  We were pleasantly surprised and really enjoyed ourselves. If you're the sort who likes taking photos that stimulate the senses don't miss.  Quite a big museum and there are many fun and interesting spots to take photos.
We really enjoyed visiting this place! I recommend you to bring your car with you. but any way you will enjoy there

We passed by and stopped there to have a look.Displaying on how tea are being grow till harvested and what it is to be done!We bought some bottles of tea spread which is widely known for its yummies!Then we went to see the tea fields too! Took some photos and proceeded back to our car to another destination.

We hiked the trail at Seogwipo Recreation Area.   The cost is 1.00 US per person and 2.00 per car.The trails are very well marked in english with plenty of stopping stops along the way.   There are also a number of bathroom faculties along the way.   be sure to get the trail map when paying admission.

We heard about this and immediately thought that we should come by to see it for ourselves. Initially we took a bottle thinking to place it on the road as we were too shy to drive in our car. But the bottle was too light and the wind actually was moving it instead. We saw ppl just came and did what was suggested. Just put the car to neutral and do not step on the accelerator - the car will move forward despite it?s an uphill road. We did that twice as there?s not much car around. :-)

We have tried black pork in Seogwipo but intended to go to Black Pork Street for the Michelin starred restaurant Dombedon. However by the time we arrived they were already closing (it was close to 11PM at that time) so we went to the restaurant next door called Hwaro Hyang.We ordered 2 portions of black pork ala carte for the both of us although they have a set menu for black pork + abalone. It was not as good as the one we had in Seogwipo but still worth a visit.Will be back for Dombedon next time!

We had two rounds of tea tasting - the signature green tea and another caramile version. Both are good but not great. It's more of a Cafe than museum we had a great time buying tea for our family. The sales people speaks good English and is always ready to help.Cafe is a bit crowded but the turnover is fast and it did not take long to buy our drinks and get a seat. The back garden is connected to Innisfree Cafe so don't miss that too.Parking is a pain however so remember to be aggressive. Parking is not restricted to what's marked on the ground in Jeju.
We had good time playing in this maze. It is well-maintained the owner/ caretaker is accommodating and they also have several cats who will welcome and waiting to be cuddled.

We got here by bus the bus stop is about 20 minutes walk away which was amazing walking all the way up he stream area in the countryside and plenty of opportunities for photos. Very peaceful place there was a few tourists mainly Korean tourists. The water is amazing if your ok walking on some stones etc then give it a go otherwise clogs would be great cause the water feels amazing. But be careful if going in the water as me and my partner walked in quite far when we noticed there was broken glass at the bottom so we tried to walk round it but was a little concerned in case anyone gets cut. This is a beautiful and peaceful place to visit I would recommend staying here a while and just enjoying yourself without rushing.

We engaged a Local private driver to bring us to Yongmeori Coast. He made a call to the Relevant Authority to check the weather and tide condition. Yongmeori Coast is situated beside Mt Sanbangsan.The car park was full that day and fortunately we found one lot. Our driver guided us the walking route to the coast.He was indeed a good private tour guide!We were immense into the nature and its beauty. He skilfully captured many memories into pics for us! This trip was my most memorable part in Jeju.
We drove there since we have a rental car.Indeed the vehicle moves uphill on its own when in neutral.Interesting.Need to figure why though!

We drove past it on another parallel road and didnt realise how fun it was! So we made it a point to visit it and try it out before we returned the rental car. The speed went up to almost 20km/h! We didnt encounter any local motorists though there were some tourists placing water bottles to see them roll up the hill :)

We drove around Jeju and decided to give this thing a go cos we didn't believe it would be possible. So we reached the road and there were signs that told you that its the starting. So all you have to do is to put your car in neutral gear and release the accelerator at the starting point and watch your friend's jaw drop. Recommended to visit together with Jeju Loveland as its just 3 minutes driave away. Admission at 8000 won per pax. pricey but its a pretty interesting visit XD

We decided to take the ferry to Udo at the last minute. We could have taken the rented car but decided not to. That was a right decision in my view. We took the hop on hop off bus and visited most of the tourist attraction. Be mindful of the bus schedule. Most people don't understand or speak English so one has to be patient. The scenery was lovely and the island unadulterated. I recommend to spend half a day here - just relax. The island is well known for peanuts which I find quite expensive. We had seafood ramen and abalone porridge. Yummy!

We climbed up Yeongsil and down Eorimok trail. Needed 5hours from Yeongsil ticket office to Eorimok ticket office. We made couple of short stops to enjoy amazing views and one longer at Witseoreum shelter for eating. Hallasan was covered by plenty of flowers it looked like pink carpet. Very beautiful. Pity that this season is dry so we could not see waterfalls at Yeongsil trail.  Next time i want to make Gwaneumsa - Seongpanak trail because those lead to summit so crater lake can be seen only from there. Nevertheless Eorimok and mainly Yeongsil trail is worth to go.

We came here but it was very hot and the sun intensity was very high. Its a long walk from the parking lot but worth it when you reach.We didn't go in the water because it was quite crowded when we went. It can be a bit tricky to climb and walk on the rocks so be careful.
We brought our hire car on the ferry over and stayed for about 3 hours. There is some nice scenery however it wasn't enough to justify staying for an entire day.

We are glad that we have our wonderful tour guide was with us thus we were able to gain better understanding n knowledge about the green tea n it's plantation.The museum itself actually showcase the different type of green tea products (including facial products) so it's a shopping paradise for some.  There are free sampling of the green tea however we like the cafe most. Though a little pricey but the green tea yogurt ice cream n also the green tea milk ice cream is yummy (it has strong green tea taste).As it was crowded when we were there the cafe seemed to be under stocked for the crowd.  A friend managed to get herself green tea macaron n said it taste superb.A good stop over for some retail therapy n tea break n photo taking.

We also went to Jeju Stone Park. Easy to find and approach with car. Parking places are available but during peak season the earliy bird .....Entrance fee with 5000 Won for adult and 2000 Won for child. It is a nice walking area with a lot of big and small stones. Dont forget your camera to bring. Inside there is also a huge museum with history of vulcano eruptions and of course with history of Jeju. Mainly in Korean but it it is definetly worth to visit. It is a very nice place and we would come back again.
Was fascinating to watch cars and buses stop and roll uphill. A skateboard would gave been useful. My insect repellent definitely rolled uphill for a bit.

Was excited to see the tea museum but disappointed as it was only a 5 minute tour. We drove for about 1.5 hours to visit this museum from the other end of Jeju City.  The treats at the museum shop was a nice respite against the summer heat though. There is also the tea plantations just across the museum and Innisfree (Korean Skincare) beauty shop about 2 minutes walk away. I would recommend to go for the Stoner Tea museum tour to make this trip more worthwhile. However there are certain timings for it and we didnt manage to join.

Walking along the sides of the mountain next to the open sea was quite thrilling for us seniors to say the least.  We had to be careful of our steps in the uneven stone/rocks which were wet.  But it all paved for a good adventure with lovely views photo opportunity and a chance to take some great photos standing up on the rocks.  We enjoyed the visit.

Visited the cave cafe only. Due to rain we unable to cover the entire place. Limited choice of drinks: Organic Green Tea Latte Coffee Latte & Americano - Krw6000-8000/cup. Serve only rice cakes with filling (black sesame green beans & red bean) Krw6000/packet. Nicely decorated with luminous lights and some cartoons character.

review: Visited at mid-day in August.  It was very hot but beautiful.  had a picnic near the carpark and took a stroll along the trail on the east end of the beach. There is a small freshwater spring on the beach at the start of the trail

Very tasteful and informative. We were hesitant at first but figured we might as well take advantage of seeing what a sexually suppressed country could teach us :)The gift shop was a little lacking on museum related material and seemed to carry just local touristy items.
Very peaceful and quiet. Hardly see any cars around. Very nice place to stroll and chill by the beach. Few cafes along the beach
Very interseting to see our car moves uphill with the engine off. My tour guide explained the reason behind this but I still don't understand XD. Try to pour the water and the same thing happened.
Very interesting Mother Nature Creation.It is cold in the cave so bring extra clothing along.Be careful of the uneven ground.Experience the creation yourself.. =D
Very informative but ofcourse the internet can tell us about those things. There are some display that scared me as im all alone when i visited the place. Overall i find it entertaining.

Very educational and interesting. How the cave was formed and the type of formation. It was nice and cool there. Be careful not to slip as the rocks can be wet and slippery. Some stairs with no wheelchair access.

very amazed by the korean ladies they were so brave to do the ziplines by themselvesit was a fun short activitythe instructors were nice and professional helping my young child not as scary as initially thought

review: Variety of skin care products
Unusual phenomena as our stationery car that was on neutral could roll upwards by itself. Other than that nothing to shout about
Unless you are passing in a car it seems pointless to search out this road. Even then I did not see many cars staying more than a couple of minutes and most people seemed bemused

UNESCO heritage site in Jeju. Location near the restaurant that sells live abalone and woman diver. It's crowded with holidaymakers but well worth the view. There are some cafe and restaurant at the car park. Didn't catch the sunrise as we were staying at the other side of the island.

Understand that the day we went weather was harsh as there?셲 typhoon warning ; the parking escort/attendant wasn?셳 helpful at all is was raining and very windy we were traveling with a 2yr old baby  ask him nicely to let us ?쁃rop off??only but he insisted that we go to the other carpark to park our cars (the carpark has open lots and a few cars are coming out) ; I don?셳 know his against foreign or what but after we parked our car Far far away carrying the baby  pram  umbrella diaper bag we saw he letting the locals go in and park . We were so piss ; and it ruin our trip in jeju as my toddler felt sick after. His now down with flu thanks to them and I still got 12 more days in Korea . Very disappointed  will not recommend any of my friends and family period

Udo is a beautiful place that we have no regret to visit and spent 3 hours to round the island with rental electric car for KRW35000. Most shop offer KRW20000 for 2 hours and we find it will be a rush that you can?t really enjoy the scenic view of the island. Returned ferry ticket cost KRW8500/person. Rental car is currently not allowed to enter the island as a one year control started Aug 2017 so we parked it at covered parking near the port before we depart to Udo.

tried the hot green tea latte green tea ice cream and green tea swiss roll at the cafe and they are fantastic! nice place to sit down and rest/chill for a while before moving on to other attractions. you can also buy green tea products over here eg tea leaves tea in powder form and green tea skin care products (innisfree).

Travelled by ferry from Seongsan habour (price 5500W two way). Upon reaching the island turn right to the carpark to purchase bus tickets (price 5000W). Bought the red tickets (you can only board the red buses with the red tickets and blue bus for the blue tickets). The bus is a hop on hop off bus (can only go forward not backward); you'll have to hold on to your ticket to board the bus for the next stop. Buses come every 20-30 mins. First stop was udobong peak - we had peanut ice cream (must try!!! Albeit a little sweet. Udo is known for the peanuts). The climb up is a little slippery so I won't recommend it on a rainy day. Requires some fitness to make it to the top but it is not too difficult. Otherwise a very relaxing climb that my family and I enjoyed very much! Stopped also at the Beacon mound (second stop on red bus) which was a nice selfie spot and then headed to the beaches before catching the ferry back to the mainland (last ferry back to jeju 5.30pm). The island is quite touristy though; expect things to be a bit more expensive.
Tourist flock in by the bus load to see cars (in neutral gear) roll mysteriously uphill

Today I hired a car and drove to Hallasan National Park. Only 1000 won to enter and park.Plenty of clean toilets. An excellent Visitor center who gave me an informative map. I did not have time to do Eorimok Trail today but will do tomorrow.I climbed the Eoseungsaengak Trail which is only 1.3km and has wooden steps all the way up so no problem with any fitness level.30 minutes up to the top. Great 360 deg.view of the surrounding mountains and a small Japanese bunker to see too. Friendly Jackdoor birds wanting a scrap of food..

To reach the place  need to walk along not properly paved route with long bushes  initially thought the guide had taken us to wrong place. Quiet place with nice coastal view. Unfortunately  we didn't manage to go to the church as there's sudden downpour  left us no choice but to end the visit. I saw horse carriage and shuttle bus service that can bring you around.

To experience something different something unique not know how the car keeps going with the Engine turned off.  We did it on our way over and our way back to the hotel.  It was fun to see all the tourist on the roads waiting to see each car going without the start of the engine.
To arrive in jeju misterious road you can go by bus or private car. If you use private car you can try how misterious that road. If you go by bus you need to walk to arrive in jeju misterious road.
Thought I was in the Carribean. The beach is segmented into small sections but beautiful nonetheless.

This was my favorite amongst all the waterfalls I have been to as you can get pretty close to it. You can even wade in the pool if you want to as it's quite shallow. Very nice place to take photos. Took a short trek to Sojeongbang waterfall from the same parking area. For those driving you can enter the phone number 7331530 into the gps. Admission fee is 2000 won for adults. Make use of your youth ID card if you are below 24 years old! It's half the price and can save you a lot if you go to many attractions. Closes at 6pm though so plan your itinerary properly!

This was a great way to spend an hour!  It would have been more fun had I been able to navigate alone.  My friend was not interested in using the map and just wanted to finish for the photo op as quickly as possible.  We did go back into the maze to each of the six stations and stamped our cards.

This so-called museum is really a sales outlet for O'Sulloc teas.  The grounds above the tea plantation is just beautiful to walk around.  The Innis Free Jeju House on the grounds is another sales outlet for Innis Free skin care products.  They offered a hands -on activity to make your own soap.  Lunch here was great.  They pride themselves in locally sources produce. I had the rice balls and soup.  We shared the mungwork steamed buns with red beans - not much to look at but very tasty. The shaved ices are a treat not to be missed

This place will turn u from an adult back to a kid. Not a big place but plenty of Teddy bear and other cartoon figures for u to take pics with. All done up very nicely and photo friendly. But to take a photo is very challenging due to the crowd. About 2 floors and one and half hour is sufficient.

This place was a little bit out of the way but we had a rental car so it didn?셳 really matter. The aquarium itself was very clean and well organized but I agree with the others that it is a bit overpriced. The touch tank like others said was unmanned and I can only imagine what those poor creatures go through with all the handsy kids that were around. The main tank was neat and they had a lot of variety.

review: This place still exists as of April 2019. It's an amazing place for kids and they have so many toys and so much equipment. If your kids know about Tayo the little bus the place is magic and if they don't well it is still a pretty good kids play cafe. There's a cafe selling drinks and food. While as noted in the previous review the staffs English isn't good but is sufficient and they try to help. We have been to this Tayo cafe and some in Seoul as well. This one is much bigger and has more and better play equipment overall. It was also way less busy than the ones in Seoul and slightly cheaper @ 12k won per child and 3k won per adult compared to 15kw won per child and 5k won per adult in Seoul. Note: Visits are capped at 2 hours (or I'm sure the kids can play there all day)Tip: Ask the staff about riding the Tayo car ride as they are not always on but when you request a staff member will assist with it. Also the pork cutlet and rice were pretty decent for the kids (and adults) to eat.

This place is rather far from where stayed (it would take about an hour from Jeju city/Seogwipo) and if you have a car you can enjoy the scenic route passing by horse farms and ATV parks and occasionally some towns. Make sure your car has enough petrol/gas as we didn't note much stations during our drive.It is located at a bay by the sea which has a good view (after you are done with the aquarium). There is a parking lot available but we were there on a super busy day despite being a Monday (we just thought that maybe it was the school holidays?) and we were lucky to get a lot.Place is stroller friendly but be mindful if the place is quite full. Everyone can get mesmerised by the display and you may just knocked by a stroller or two.The displays are quite entertaining. There are some attractions such as otter/pelicans feeding. You can check the time of these attractions at their website and you can time your visit there. There is a underwater tunnel and the manta rays will just swim pass.There was a huge aquarium display and unfortunately for us we were not able to the see the whale shark they were housing as it had been released back into the sea for research purpose. At certain times there will be a feeding session by scuba divers. The penguin display had some fake penguins in between and for some reason they look pretty realistic beside a real one when the real ones don't move. Have fun figuring out which is which!There was a show featuring synchronized swimming diving from high places. The show was about pirates and fairies. Everyone enjoyed the show (all in Korean with English displayed on the screen) and we were just clapping without really understanding what's going on but you will sort of understand the story. After about 20 minutes or so there was a seal show followed by a dolphin show. Again in Korean and you just shout and clap whenever the locals do. (For the language: it is the same in all other countries. Just be don't care and enjoy the show!) The show was about 45 minutes long and there is a stand outside selling popcorn and peanut butter roasted squid (a must try!) so get some and enjoy the show.On another wing there is a small science museum and a 3D theater. You can skip the museum and head outdoors (as most are in Korean) but there is a holographic display of the whale shark inside that is really cool. Attraction is free. For the 3D theater not sure if we had to pay an additional sum but it was featuring a shark show and we reckoned the kids would be terrified.There is a cafeteria downstairs and the food is pretty good. You will need to pay at a counter which they will give you a device which beeps when the food is ready for collection. If can get quite crowded as there's limited space. During your walk there will be pop up stands selling food so you don't have worry about getting hungry while walking around.After it all head outside for the scenic view and some outdoor picture taking. We were there on a gloomy day and wind was pretty strong.

review: this place is quite hard to be accessed. the best way to reach this place is rent a car or bike if you have international driver license. you need strong stamina to explore whole and some area need climbed up.
This place is huge. And the walk til the end is a very long walk. It's very dark and very cold. I was all prepared with sneaker and jacket with scarf.

This place is extremely beautifully especially during sunset. The rocks are carved by water to different shapes. Nice view of the ocean with a well maintained garden. It is 5 mins walk from international convention centre.

This place is an entertainment on its own. Be sure u bring and extra memory card if needed =P Expect to take loads of photos here and by photos I'm not talking about plain boring ones here everyone can be like a child again. The art in this museum are done to look 3D as if you yourselves are part of it. I really had a great time here I would say u need at least 2 hours in here as there are so many funny and amazing art to play around with. Let your imagination go wild here and be creative as there is so many poses you can do with the art. While I was there I've been skydiving escaping a hippo rock climbing creating art falling all buildings got my head chopped off...and many more X3

this place is a two story building tuck far away from anything however there are carnivals outside with loads of kiddie stuff. you will be greeted by man-sized teddy bears every great picture taking all the time had a fabulous time there.however if u are in korea for a party pumping time. skip this place.

This park is relatively new and a haven for kids. Within the park there are play areas for toddlers and young kids. There is a sandpit  a tube slide  an outdoor playground  swings  car and train rides  flying fox  indoor playground etc. The train and car rides are available at extra charges.There is a baby changing room  makes it convenient for parents with babies. Flying fox is for kids above 100cm but they have the mini version for kids below that height. Indoor playground is a rather big area which is toddler friendly. There are seats for parents to wait while the kids play their fill in the indoor playground. There is also a restaurant within the park with amazing sea views. My daughter had an amazing time as the park was not crowded when we visited. Overall its a nice park to visit if u have kids below age of 7.
This park have what kids like: dinosaurs. They need a good painting job that I noticed but kids don't care about it. So if you have children this place is nice for them

This museum is one of the most popular of the 50+ on Jeju Island and the carpark was packed with tour buses when we arrived. But if you can manage to get a slot on one of the formal tea ceremonies it really takes you out of the bustling tourist crowds and takes you to another place altogether. The time and care taken for all the preparations was amazing and could not have been more different to having a casual cuppa at home! I am not sure they do them in English - our host spoke in Korean but our little group had an interpreter to help us out. The venue used for this ceremony is also amazing. Beautiful minimal stone and wood shaped furniture in a sunlight-filled pavilion looking out onto the lawns of the museum. We also had a glimpse into the underground tea cellar area and a quick tour round the tourist shop. The collection of tea cups from different countries and eras was fascinating too in the area next to the shop.

This mountain is definitely worth a visit. I recommend a nice espresso and carrot juice at the bottom at Lazy Place Cafe - cool place with great views. It takes a little effort to get up to the cave with the water falling from the ceiling but well worth it especially if you?셱e a spiritual person. The other temples are serene. It is an UNESCO site of outstanding natural beauty with an historical layer at the coast below. A Dutchman was shipwrecked here in the C17th and wrote the first description of the Kingdom of Korea published in the West. I had a wonderful time with my girlfriend. Close place to stay is Mirabil.

This island is only about 10 mins away by ferry from Jeju Island. The environment is very clean and very beautiful. You can either take your own car or hire a scooter to go around the island. It only takes less than 2hrs to complete a full circle. I seriously recommend you to spend a least a day or two.

this is the only white sand blue water beach in Korea. So i was pretty excited to see it. Its quite shallow and you can easily play around. Its well maintained just like alll other beaches in korea. there is life guard always on duty. Careful while walking near the stones.
This is the must place to visit in Jeju island.Beautiful cave with very cold inside.The floor of this cave are total wet so when you walk please be careful
This is really amazing. I loved the view. The place is well taken care of. The walk is of moderate intensity. We had wonderful weather. Recommend this place

This is no Caribbean beach so don't expect warm turquoise waters and endless stretches of fine white sand. Considering the area however it is a decent beach and worth checking out if you are in the area. It is located within the Jungmun Resort complex in Seogwipo but there is no charge so anyone can visit.Here's what to expect: yellow/orange rough sand with lots of bits of shell; water that gets deep quite quickly; STRONG undertow on stormy days. The resort restricts people from swimming during certain months (wintertime I think) because of the risk of undertow.  I mention the last point because the beach is actually quite beautiful to watch on a windy day as the waves crash into the volcanic rock.Quite often on weekends foreigners gather to play rounds of volleyball.There are spots to get food near the beach and in the resort but be ready for sky-high prices.

This is my fisrt experience to ridding horse. It was amazing memory to me. I feel like ridding the cloud. And now i know horse is not dangerous animail.They are so lovely. That's why i would like to raise horse in my home. lol.I heard that Korean proverb show that Jeju Island is an good place for raising horses from jeju people.And local people said that original jeju horses are smaller than others. I don't know why.Give it a try and you guys must love it  if you are not scared about horses.The fee is quite expensive.

This is located in the southwest quadrant of the island and can be a chore to get to without a car. The highlight of the building is the tea drinking experience that you need to make a reservation for(I'm pretty sure) that is entirely in Korean though so bear that in mind. There are tea fields in different directions for quite a ways the ones next to the museum are setup for visitors and picture but the further away fields aren't meant for tourists. We arrived around 10:30 and it wasnt busy at all but when we were getting ready to leave at 12:30 it was quite full.

This is actually my second time here and this time without a guide as we go by car ourself. You need a guide to actually understand the history of these traditional houses. I went there around 3pm and the whole village seems like a ghost town. Very quiet. Only 2 families of tourist sighted. We took a nice walk around the village but our main reason for visiting is to eat the black pork meat cooked in spicy flavour. It was my best meal 11 years ago when I visited and best meal in Korea this time too.

This is a well maintained natural forest. You can walk here after visiting the Roe Deer Observation Centre or take the Jeju City bus.  There are many trails and a fair amount of visitors. Entrance fee is payable and a car park is available at the entrance.

This is a very spectacular waterfall plummeting down into the ocean. The boulders add to the fun of the attraction clambering over them to see the waterfall more directly .Very well organised walk from car park down to waterfall area. Some interesting stalls at the entrance. Again very cheap to visit.
This is a interesting road drive whereby even the engine is off the car will even go upslope. It is worth to go there for an experience.

This is a great volcanic cave with very interesting information cards dotted around to teach the novice geologist more about how it was formed and the story of the cave. Its a bit out the way but you can get the 101 circle route to nearby then one of the 7xx buses up to it

This is a farm for Green Tea. First and foremost it is near the Glass park 5 mins drive away. So if you are planning to visit this place and have no budget constraints and have lots of time you can consider to spend 30mins at the glass park as well.The Tea farm sells tea (of course) and remember to try the green tea ice cream in the building. You can walk around the farm but be careful of the snakes. We seen one there.Nice place to visit whether alone in a group or with your family and kids.
This is a big temple with lots to see.  There are a couple of large budda statues and many small ones.  It also has a nice gift shop.It is far from downtown and a bit hard to get without a car.
This is a beautiful and large temple. I love it the moment i step out of the car. Must visit place at Jeju.
These rocks are truly remarkable and will make you feel grounded and very in touch with nature. Be careful of the tide!

There's not really much museum. I thought I turned a wrong corner but had actually walked through the whole thing. Just one wall of tea cups and pots and basically no English signage. But it's free and you really go for the tea shop and cafe.Nice teas for sale (spendy but tasty!) and there are often free samples in the tea shop. Then move to the cafe for some green tea flavored sweets. I recommend the softserve ice cream twisted with yogurt. If you're here take time to climb to the 3rd floor observatory for some nice views. If you have a little extra time it's worth two other stops:1) just through the garden path walk up hill to the natural skin care center where you can smell local essences and make your own natural soap (for a fee). They have nice sandwiches and snacks for sale.2) Climb the oreum (small mountain) just north of O'Sulloc. Walk along the road past the tea fields until you see a concrete paved walk in toward the hill. Follow paths or bushwack until you see the path entrance. You can walk to the top in less than an hour from O'Sulloc. There's a nice viewing platform with views toward Seogwipo from the top.

There wasn't much to look and read (all in Korean) but caring and friendly staff made our day.For one of the most visited city or area for foreign tourists  it's hard to believe that the most of the places do not have English speaking staff.We were having hard time finding good place to go and dine  recommendations by the staff at the Chocolate Land were very very helpful. Also  the chocolates we purchased with his help turned out very good.If you are in Jung Moon tour sector  need a little break for a free coffee (it's free with a coupon you get when you pay an admission) and some help from an English and Chinese speaking staffs.

There is a parking lot for self park and that was handy. Luckily we found a spot as someone was leaving. Hiked up to the top for fabulous views. Came back down and had lunch at a local place just down the road since the car was parked in the lot we didn't want to try parking somewhere else. The local place was very good. Definitely have to go to this tourist destination if you go to Jeju

There is a fee at the entrance. It takes only 10 minutes to climb down the steps to the waterfall. There is no proper footpath so you have to walk on jagged rocks and stones to go near the waterfall. Wear proper shoes and tread carefully. It's really a majestic waterfall and you could get really close which adds to the experience. We sat down in the shade and enjoyed the cool mist and sounds of the waters. Took a lot of photos of course. A sight not to be missed!

There are spacious parking area provided for a visitor which is very convenient to whom that driving a car here. You need to buy a ticket for entrance bit it is not that pricey. The cave requires you to have a long walk with a majestic view inside the cave. Highly recommended and a must visit place when you are at Jeju Island.

There are many stone carvings statues in the garden. They make the place looks cool as well as creepy at night. There?셲 not much to see and do here anyway though the stones look funny. But the staff can?셳 speak English.

There are a lot of food choices in the market  especially a lot of shops selling the Jeju oranges and Jeju orange juice. You can easily get souvenirs from the market. Most of the shop keepers can speak English/Mandarin. There is a free car park just 1 min on foot from the market  another one with charge right inside the market.

The Yeongsil trail is beautiful. But wouldn't suggest eurimok. Very rocky and didn't see much. Apparently there were supposed to be flowers blooming. It was also very hard coming down.. Better to stick to Yeongsil going up and down. We went up Yeongsil and came down eurimok and took taxi back to Yeongsil pick up the car.
The view on Udo myeon is excellent where can take a look of half of the island. But you better rent a car and drive there.

The usual suspects (green tea roll matcha soft serve etc) are good of course but I also had a delicious cup of Houjicha Latte. It was perfect for a cool spring day sitting out in the O'sulloc back garden. Definitely deserves a repeat order.The O'sulloc shop here has many varieties of tea as well as skincare. Bought a pack of jeju green tea bags - when I opened the packet a most delicious aroma of roasted tea leaves greeted me.

The trick worked for the car but not for other objects that we kept on the road. Not worth the trip unless on your way. There are a few cafes around that place so can be a stopover. Was not very crowded.

The trail is relatively easy and is one of the shorter trails that takes you up Hallasan. The views along the trail are amazing and very well maintained. There are plentiful rest stops along the trail with excellent views of the surroundings. There are 2 carparks here. Do wait a little or arrive early to gain access to the car park nearer to the trail. The outer carpark requires a 2 km walk. Parking is very limited and controlled vehicle entrance to the car park near to the trail. Cater around 4 to 5 hours for a return trip from the nearer car park. Definitely worth a visit.

The temple is located on olle 8 trail and there is a bus that takes you directly there from Seogwipo (bus 140).At the entrance someone might aak you to give 10 000 won to buy a bag of rice but you dont need to pay ... You can make a small donation instead. They alow you to take photos inside this temple (which is rare in Korea).  Outside is a small souvenir store where you can get cheap postcards and even a bowl of cooked ramen (not cup!) for 3000 won.
The routes to the top can be hard one route with lots of steps up is very steep most of the way. Both routes are uneven and it does take 5/6 hours to do. Make sure you carry water.

The road to this temple is a single carriage way and you drive carefully.  Parking is free. Before I reached the temple I can hear the chanting and is was so soothing.  It just calm a city travellers. I didn't take any pictures inside the temple only the surrounding. It would be great to have a audio or a translator/guide to explain more of this historical and majestic temple.  The sea view from the temple is stunning. Do check out the temple second floor.

The place is relatively small and when I was there there where a lot of people. The beach is with black sand nice. I had a very nice Mandarin Orange icecream and that was worthwhile. From there I walked along the beach maybe 5 kilometers until I came to a little fishing port. From there a very nice person took me along in the car... there was a bus stop but the busses only come at a long interval...it would have been possible to wark until Seogwipo but that would have been another 3 or so kilometers. A long but really beautiful walk...the stones are all vulcanic and black. If you have the time and inclination I recommend

The place is lovely in a postcard sort of way. I wouldn?셳 insist on going here and really I didn?셳 know about it before our trip; we just followed the suggestion of the guesthouse owner and the driver.Love water? You get two kinds when you visit this place ??a beach to swim in and a river to canoe in (there?셲 a whirlpool in the river that people row to just to see). We did neither since we were on a taxi tour in cold spring weather and didn?셳 have any swim gear. We were constrained to just take some pictures here and tick it off the bucket list. Might not come back since there are plenty of nice places in Jeju-do. Once is enough.

The person in charge of the company is really nice and caring. The date of my tour are having a typhoon and he send me notification to postpone the trip and even share with me the dos and donts during typhoon. He also recommend a nice restaurant for me to try out. The service is really nice and awesome.

The parking is 1000w. Don?t stop right after the entrance keep driving or you?ll end up walking very far. The trail is well marked no chance of getting lost. I got there about 0900 and it wasn?t busy. When I was heading back to the entrance at 1200 it was getting very crowded. The ?peak? wasn?t much of a peak. It was a flat staging area with the rock slab marking the elevation. There is a trail that leads off left of the seating area and one behind the rock slab. I followed it about 1 hour before I decided to turn back. I wasn?t sure where the path led and my car was at one end. Beautiful but easy hike. Little to no shade to wear sunscreen or hats.

The O쨈Sulloc Tea Museum and tea field is a treat!  It쨈s easy to get to by the airport bus we got to it by taking the Yeha West Tour.Be prepared for crowds in the cafe.  However if you go across the road to the tea fields it쨈s easy to walk along the tea plants and be alone in a field of green tea.The museum is interesting and explains the tea picking and fermentation process.The real fun is the cafe and shopping for tea!  It쨈s a bit overwhelming but fascinating to think that so many types of tea can be produced with one leaf!O쨈Sulloc also sells a cosmetic line I haven쨈t tried any of those products so I can쨈t comment on their cosmetics versus all the other great stuff that Korea has for skin care. The cafe offers the most delicious green tea ice cream.  I쨈m dying to try the cakes but can쨈t get pass the ice cream.  There is also a brown roasted tea ice cream but I prefer the green tea one.  It isn쨈t sweet and has a distinctive green tea flavor left on your palate as you get ready for the next bite.Recommendation--I got the Cold Green Sticks which are perfect for a bottle of water.  The other teas you definitely need a strainer otherwise get the tea in teabags.Oh and O짢Sulloc has a cafe in the Nampo area in Busan if you need your green tea ice cream fix. Other cafes have green tea ice cream but OSulloc is yummy and my favorite.O쨈Sulloc seems to be branding itself as a high end tea so you just can쨈t purchase it in a grocery store nor do the hotels have it as complimentary tea a shame since it is a Korean brand. So stock up and enjoy.

The museum is quite small and expensive....there are 2 floors with old teddy bears and teddy bear versions of famous painting and famous people. If you are nearby you can go but I would not specifically go there. My 3 years old son was little scared by the giant bears in display! Koreans seem to like it more

The museum can be improved with more English explanation. Go to the open air top for the best 360 view of the area and plantation. There are signs at the plantation warning of snakes but none spotted during our visit. There is a crowd at the cafe and shop but the turnover is quick as most of them followed a group tour and hence can't linger that long. You can get a seat if you are not in a rush. The stuff are expensive but it won't deter a green tea fan. Do be extra careful when crossing the roads to the opposite car parks. The cars and trucks are speed demons.

The garden starts with a huge glasshouse which is a torture in the summer but we went anyway on carpe diem basis. It's awesome inside and it has little sections. Then outside there are European Japanese and Korean gardens with walkways. Coming from Europe I was not really amazed or entertained by the eurogardens but I guess with Asian perspective they were impressive. The reason I gave 4 is that the entry is expensive and they only sell water at 1 place. Also the toilets are quite dirty

The food (for the tummy and the face) is pricey. Overheard one visitor saying she could get the same skincare products cheaper online back in her home country. Pays to know your home price before you buy.

The folk museum is a huge cultural town-like place located at the south-east portion of Jeju Island. It is easily accessible by car. For those who are self-driving like I did fear not there is an abundant number of parking lots to park your car and it's completely free.The admission fee for an adult cost around 10000 won. Considering the size of the museum it's a rather reasonable price. The museum is divided into many different sections showcasing different cultural aspects of Korea's rich history.If you get tired from walking or can bear the scorching sun the museum provides a tram service that brings you around the museum stopping at different attractions. There are also many different restaurants and snack booths selling traditional Korean meals as well as snacks. If you have never been to Jeju before do take the opportunity to visit this place at least once! Ideal for all ages.
The female lead taking care of our tour group is very funny and lively. She made our visit at Seongeup Folk Village a fun trip!

the engine of the bus I am in was switch-off and yet it continue to move upwards.. only a stretch of about 250m of road.... a bottle of mineral water seems to roll upwards too...most puzzling was a bus moves up faster than a sedan car...simply strange...

The drive from jeju airport area to aqua planet is around 1 hour 10 minutes passing by many small towns. The entry tickets were quite costly and I used klook to get some discounts with the tickets. Upon parking the rented car outside the vicinity of aqua planet then picked up a number from the machine next to the ticket counter. Waited for the number and redeemed my wristbands without much hassle. Kids under 3 can enter for free.There are plenty to see and we were in time to watch fish feeding a seal and dolphin show. Outside the facilities has really good view and many people were taking photos.Food in the food court was not too bad and similar like incheon airport have to be ordered and paid at the cashier counter and picked up from the individual sections when the device buzzes.Overall experience was great and worth every cent spent.

review: Sitting prominently on a hillside there is no missing this huge Temple and it is one of the largest in the East.There is a bit of steep walk from the carpark to the Temple complex and we rewarded ourselves with a drink from the spring well on one side of the grounds.Consisting of a main hall with a Deities sculptured side walls of Buddha a large bell a separate Pagoda Monks quarters and three or four floors upstairs that can be accessed by visitors. These floors have many donations of precious metal statues and from up here there are excellent views of the main hall.It is prudent not to use the main entry into the big hall as there are clear warnings in many languages not to so out of respect. Also shoes must be taken off before using the side entries on either side of the main doors. A group of hapless visitors ignored these signs and were promptly told off and hustled out to use the side doors.Money donations are accepted either for the upkeep of the Temple or for incense and candles.While we were there we had three or four Monks chanting and offering up to Buddha and it was very serene to hear it from upstairs while overlooking the main hall.The grounds are well maintained with a couple of restrooms around the complex a cafeteria and Temple stays are available too.Enjoy your visit!

The arboretum is home to 6000 camellia trees of 500 different species including species that are known to produce the world?셲 largest and earliest blossoms. The place is drop-dead gorgeous and I would of spent a whole day adoring the different flowers if I wasn't rushing to maximise my day in Jeju.We were lucky to catch the early blooms of the Cherry Blossoms which was a major highlight of the trip for us. Towards the end of the trail is a small shop that should desserts coffee and souvenirs like postcards and cosmetics. I loved their postcard selection and went a little crazy on those souvenirs but no regrets. My brother enjoyed his homemade strawberry ice cream as it was packed full of flavour!

I recommend finnishing it with a horse ride by the ajoshi at the exit for man won and a cold jeju tangerine juice.

Really beautiful views from the peak of the tallest mountain in Korea! My friend and I are of above average fitness meaning we exercise with weights and cardio about five times a week. We made it up the mountain in three hours and down the mountain in three hours.  We took two separate 15 minute breaks on the way up and the way down.There will be a lot of people around nine and 10 AM! You should take the first bus in the morning to arrive before the crowds. We Took the 6:10 AM Bus from Jeju city intercity bus terminal and arrived at Seongpanak national park entrance at 6:40am to start our hike. The morning was a bit chilly but by 11:00am it was warm! We hiked in shorts with tshirts and a fleece. We had removed the fleece by 11. Bring water (2-3 bottles) and food as there isn't anyplace to but it once you leave the entrance to the park.If you don't make it to the final check point by 12:00 then they won't let you proceed to the peak. It would be really disappointing. There is an much to see for most of the hike as you're covered by trees but as you get close to the peak you can start getting the breathtaking views of Jeju.

My family and I chose the Alive Museum over the Trick Eye Museum because the former is larger and has more art pieces. Furthermore we chose to go in the evening after dinner so that we don?셳 have to jostle with the daytime crowd. However the disadvantage of the night visit is that the karting (carting) activities were already closed at 5 pm. Moreover it was too dark to take any photographs with the outdoor sculptures in the French themed garden. But it?셲 okay because our primary objective was to have a good time inside the Museum which we did. Getting there and Fees: We drove to the Alive Museum (GPS coordinate/code 8050888) and reached there at about 7pm 2.5 hours before Museum closing time of 9:30pm. Parking is free at the huge car park. Entrance fees to the Alive Museum is 10000 won for adults 9000 won for teenagers and 8000 won for children. If you rent a car check whether there are available discounts on the entrance fees and karting on the discount booklet (we used those from the Hertz discount book).The Museum:  Depending on your time spent at each art piece and the number of visitors present (who would jostle with you for the right to pose and take photos) you would need at least 2 hours to ?쐏articipate??in all the art pieces inside the Museum. It is very easy to become so engross that you lose track of time! And don?셳 worry about how to pose because there?셱e instructions and explanations written in Korean Mandarin (Chinese) English and Japanese on how to pose. If you are going by yourself I recommend you bring a tripod along or you could take selfies (although most photos have to be taken beyond the selfie distance) or you could keep asking other visitors to take your photos.We leisurely spent a lively 2.5 hours (7-9:30 pm) inside the Alive Museum which was just enough to view and take photographs and selfies of most of the art pieces. I say ?쐌ost??because there are a few paintings of adult themes which are not suitable for my children. Anyway we almost had the entire museum to ourselves except for 6 other visitors! So we unreservedly and hilariously pose at most of the 3-D art and paintings without feeling shy and without anyone looking at us. As a result we were among the last to leave the Museum.Of the 4 categories of art inside the museum ??trick art digital art objet art and Provence art (sculpture art is outside the museum) ??my favourite are those in the trick art section. Trick art is a perspective technique which makes use of optical illusions so as to enable visitors to interactively ?쐃nter??as the main character into seemingly three-dimensional realistic paintings and artworks with the visitors eventually having a good laugh at their ?쏿dventure??  I particularly liked the 3-D illusions of the parachute standing on the bridge over the molten lava and the hanging onto a nail at the side of the building. We also enjoyed the Provence art section which is a pastel-coloured fairy tale village with bears and dogs donning period costumes.We had a truly unforgettable experience with plenty of amazing photographs and fun with optical illusions. So could you!
