review: It felt spooky from the fog as it was really cold inside. Do bring a jacket if you visit this place. You could see firsthand how the lava affected the rock formations in this cave and it is interesting to watch for first-timers. The floor is quite uneven due to the natural rock formations so do be careful and wear proper shoes. It is about 1km walk to the end and you have to u-turn back to exit as there's only one entrance which is also the exit.

It a pleasant place to visit: Lots of visitors n cars maybe was a weekendThe walk is not too difficult  you will enjoy if you take it slowly n see the view from different angle n height Need food shoes n the slope is pretty steep n may need to hold the rope/railing at certain height Feel good n nice when reach the top
Is just a short road to be amazed.  Not worth to travel so far.  Saw people trying to roll water bottle on the road and ignoring oncoming cars.

is a place where you will spend at least 3hours there. you must get prepare SD card with memory space & extra battery for your camera. you must catch the right angle if order to get the interesting result from the photo. stand at the photo point to take photo to catch the right angle.

Irion (magma) carved the small valley. This is the place where the magma carved the valley long long ago. The small valley meet the sea here. You can enjoy transparent canoe and see under water(not always).  Scenery is exotic.  It is also good for you to walk along here.

Interesting optical illusion. Most busses and car will stop at this stretch (near to 100m - 200m) to demonstrate this trick. However i felt it is quite unsafe as alot tourist are standing beside the road and some will try trick on their own like rolling bottle in the middle of road. Just around 5 mins walk to Loveland and around 20 mins taxi ride from jeju city.
IncredibleSeems to go uphill ... but in fact go downhill.Pure optical illusion.To be seen once. Car at neutral point.. and see what is happening.

In the 'Tea Stone' building you can try their tea workshops. They explained the history of Tea in Jeju and how all the elements in nature affect the taste.During the class we were not allowed to take pictures which made us focus on the experience and just relax smell the aroma of the wet tea and even make tea for our friends! The desserts they served were also very nice! I drink tea a lot but this workshop proved there is much more to enjoy when you brew and prepare the tea!Personally I devour a cup of tea in seconds but this class made me realize the pleasure I can get if I put effort into making it.There was also a decent cafe with various options all using green tea.If you like makeup and skin-care the famous Korean brand Innisfree also has a branch there which is quite different from the shops in Seoul.

In Jeju  we had the opportunity to visit the Jeju Art Museum & Glass Castle  which is a theme park featuring an exhibition hall  garden and models made entirely of glass. One must spent at least two hours or more to walk around the indoor and outdoor areas. Nearby the entrance  there is a display ?쏥lass Worldwide??and the countries that produced glass are mentioned here - China  Italy  Czech Republic  Arab and Japan. Once you step indoor  a large glass beanstalk from the fairytale ?쏪ack & the Beanstalk??will greet visitors.The world's largest all-glass labyrinth  glass ball  glass diamond  a glass stonewall  mirror lake and a glass bridge are found in the model parks here. In one part of the outdoor theme park are Cinderella's glass slippers and a glass carriage. One will be held in awe at the marvellous pieces of art  all made entirely out of glass! Truly an eye opening experience!

if you want to really see power of nature at its best do visit this cave. you can understand how lava caves are and how they were formed over the years. Make sure you carry rain coat or umbrella and have some warm clothese if you are not used to cold. The caves  has water dripping at place and its very cold even during the hot sun outside. We went there after noon and it was quite cold. Be careful while walking inside the cave and its slippery. Do read the story as you go through its. there is restaurant which server good korean food just outside the entrance which we felt was very good.
If you have chance to travel here. Please careful about strong wind and rain. I ran to the bus because of wind and cold!! You can have seafood for dinner there too.
If you have a chance you must  visit this place. The tea is amazing and the caf챕 at the top serves a superb Carrot soup.

If you are the fan of Korean tea you should go to this place and try yourself. They offer some tester so you can before you buy. Besides tea there are some products such as green tea milk spread cosmetic skin care etc that the main ingredient is tea are also available here. Besides the indoor museum or shop you can walk around at the tea plantation outside and take a nice camera shot.

If you are near by or driving around the island this is definitely one of the places to check. It's not the place to stay longer than 2 hours since the place is small. I would recommend to get off the car and take a walk around the water enjoying the scenic view for about 1/2~an hour. My family were there in May when it was not too busy. There were only a few locals jogging and walking so we enjoyed the quiet peaceful and almost mystic moment there. The kayaks are no longer operating for the sake of environmental conservation. It definitely would have been amazing to have that clear water beneath when you paddle but I am glad that they've prohibited them. The place is amazing as it is. I would come back next time.

If you are looking for some exercise and mountain climbing that is manageable and has good view (no blockage). I think this place is good to visitThe footpaths are properly laid but there are some steps that are pretty steep. So be careful. Parking is free at the venueLots of food around the location as well.

If you are big fan of the Korean variety show Running Man (?곕떇留?  you will enjoy walking around Ilchul Land. Serious fans (like myself) will remember that the cast visited this attraction in 2012  episode 89  featuring the Alice in Wonderland theme. Ilchul Land is quick to play up on the connection for fans as there are various signboards placed around the attraction showing you exactly where certain scenes took place. Great for taking photos to show that you have been there!For regular visitors/tourists  Ilchul Land is more of like a very well maintained outdoor park  with lush and verdant landscaped scenery including bonsai plants  palm trees and even miniature waterfalls. However  the highlight for me was the natural underground cave/tunnel  which you can explore - do go all the way to the end (until you reach the roped off area) and mind your head as it is a bit low in parts. There are some carvings and statues placed inside the caves  whereas I would have preferred that it was left in its natural state. If I remember correctly  it was about a 10mins stroll all the way in. Other areas of interest within Ilchul Land would be the mock-up of a Korean village where you can see the famous Jeju black pig.All in all  you can probably spend about an hour at this attraction or less if you do a quick run through.

If I hadn't done this myself I don't think I would have believed it.  You look like you are ascending up this road when the car is in neutral you actually roll down it! It's a MUST DO if you come to Jeju.

I went with a group of fellow Taekwondo practitioners. The cave is an amazing example of this type of geology. Need to be careful as floor a little uneven due to the natural rock formation but well worth a visit if your in the area. We all did a little Taekwondo practice whilst down there so it made the visit even more memorable.

I went traveling to Jeju from Shanghai and my friend helped me booked the Discovery diving trip at good diver. We chose this dive shop because it's PADI certified and the location is convenient. And they have English website with very useful information compared with many local dive shops with information only in Korean. It was such an amazing experience doing discovery dive with them and it went beyond what I expected. I felt I was in good hand because the instructor was very experienced and he knew how to make beginner at ease with a good sense of humor. His calm and caring presence also helped a lot. Traveling and diving at Mun island which is a small island to the south of Jeju in the morning is a very refreshing experience. The scenery is beautiful and we saw a good amount of soft coral and school of fishes. Jen another instructor is also very helpful and it was fun chatting with her along the way. She gave me a ride and dropped me off at a local restaurant for lunch and the pork noodle she recommended was very delicious.

I went there in Nov. This is a small island but need to rent a mini car/motorcycle/cycle for travelling around the whole island.  We chose to take the tour minibus with total of 8 stops in different part of the Udo.  THe ticket can be bought near the pier. There are some beaches which all looks gorgerous! However its autumn time which we cant swim there.

I was told this lava tube is about 9 km long but only 1 km is accessible right now. It's really huge but kinda dark so you can't really appreciate the tube except in some parts where a spotlight is placed - I guess that's where the authenticity lies. Anyways wear comfortable shoes and be careful since it gets wet and slippery.

I was there watching a child put a can on the road at the entrance to the car park and the can rolled uphill.I then put my car in the same place in neutral and filmed it rolling UPHILL.I can only assume that the road appears to be uphill but must be sloping down.Unless there is some other scientific answer.It is worth the effort to see it for yourself.Bottles did not work like an empty can.There is an Archery range there so you can practice some archery as well.

I was not expecting a lot when I drove into the car park but I was very pleasantly surprised with it visit. It only cost 2000 won entry and I spent about 1.25 hours.Firstly the guide will set up the video for you and it is pretty gruesome with the brutality of war shown. Then you walk through the exhibition area which has good information about the tunnel system and how Jeju was included in Imperial Japan's last stand at the end of the Pacific War plus weapons and memorabilia. All with English explanations. Then you walk up the hill and go into the tunnel system. When you come out you can follow the less used path and go to the top of the hill for good views.  Lastly there is a tank you can climb into just before you leave. Absolutelyrecommended for all ages.

I was here last week with my wife and we enjoyed the walk around this part of the coast. On a light drizzly morning the walk took on a determined bent but we were certainly not alone. There were loads of people when we were there. The backdrop is fairly dramatic looking and there is a small entrance fee. The view from the top at the carpark is quite beautiful too.

I visited this aquarium with my family on New Year?셲. I had high hopes for it since it was rated as one of the top 10 world?셲 best aquariums in the world. I was impressed with the way the animals were kept and could tell that they put a lot of effort into maintaining this aquarium. The only complaint I had was with their Touch Tanks. It had starfish and sharks but there was no staff to guard it and guide people how to handle the animals. I saw a lot of kids grabbing the sharks by the tail grabbing them out of the water to carry them across the room and throw them into another tank. I was disappointed that such a conservation-based aquarium did not place staff at the touch tanks to make sure the visitors learn how to respectfully handle animals. However besides that a great place to learn about marine life and support Jeju tourism & conservation.

review: I visited on a tour from Yeha Bus Tours. It was such an awesome experience that I would have never seen if it wasn't for being part of that tour. The buildings were really neat and the restaurant was delicious. I was there on a rainy day but it was still pleasant. The mist contributed to the mysterious and dreamy vibe that this place had. I recommend carrying a small umbrella. I needed it throughout my 2 week stay in South Korea.

I visited here to experience the power of the waves as well as Korea's first surfing spot. As expected there were many people because it was a famous place but there were so many tourist attractions nearby that I could stay in nearby accommodations and experience various things. I was not good at surfing so I couldn't figure out when the waves were strong. However I was exiting bout surfing bcuz the instructor gave me delicate care so that I could safely surf. Their board was purple color and I liked it because it was the symbol color of BTS. Right after surfing I could enjoy a freezing beer at the marvelous pub at the entrance of the beach.

I visited Hallim Park confined in a wheelchair. Some ways are not appropiate for a wheelchair. I love gardens and seen a lot. This garden had beautiful displays although some were needing care. The park takes several hours to see. It has different plants from many parts of the word. The Bonsai collection was excellent and one of the best I seen in a botanical garden. Again this particular area was needing help with the trees. They have so many bonsais and only two workers to trim them. And the specimens available were very old.The caves are unique because I do not know any other part in the world you can see a volcanical and calcareal cave together and they have one in here. I had to use crutches to see them and I am not dissapointed of the effort.The local village moved into the park is nice and realistic (we visited a folk village the day before). The animal collection was above average. For kids they have an area to feed love birds and parakeets. Excellent fun. My youngest daughter is 25 and she was a child again in here.

I took the PADI Open Water Diver course at Good Diver. Fast response on requests taken care of reservations and formalities everyday pick up nice dinner great English Instructors (even some German ;-)) and above all great diving at different sites! If you are a foreigner (or not) this is the place to go for diving in Korea.

I really enjoyed this place for a short visit. Things genuinely appear to roll uphill which is something I have never seen before. It's a little crowded but we had no problem rolling our car up the hill and rolling some bottles up the hill once parked. Definitely worth stopping for if you are in the area or passing through.

I love this place. Lots of variety of tea and we bought the tangerine green tea which is only available there. The Innisfree also carry some clay masks that you can only get there. Took pictures with the tea farm. Pretty.

I have spent years reading about WW2 history so it's a sobering experience to walk the same places as the men and women who fought and died in that conflict. Altteureu Airfield was a WW2 Japanese airbase that sits in a strategic corner of Jeju Island  midway between China and Japan. In the 1930s bombing missions were launched from here to Shanghai  later it was a training base. There are 19 remaining concrete hardened shelters sized for a Zero fighter and Jeju has done a good job with preserving the site (even though most of it is active farmland)  adding a large parking lot and bathroom  and placards to explain the history and locate the structures. It's right on the Olle trail so there are many hikers passing through and it's easy to find from the shore road by car.

I go here every day to walk up the steep hill to the right of the beach for exercise.  It's the start of the No. 19 Olle Trail.  I usually always see bride and grooms having their photos taken on the beach and in the fields of rapeseed.  Views from the top of the hill are amazing.  Sometimes if there are horses around I'll pick grass and feed them in exchange for a little pat and nuzzle from them.  If you look carefully there are quite a few different flowers around.  If you pick a green rapeseed that hasn't yet flowered and peel the stalk you can eat the stalk.  It tastes like sweet brocalli.  The cherry blossoms are lovely there too if you happen to be there in early April.  The water is clear.  I like to feed and water some of the stray dogs.  It kills me that I can't give them a home.  They appreciate a bit of a cuddle too but you can see their priority is getting food.  There are some very good restaurants in Hamdeok as well.  Ive put a pic of one of the ones on the main street of Hamdeok. .its a local one that serves a set menu at lunch time and its very good.  The sunsets are spectacular.

I found the second part of the drive more interesting and mysterious. The second part is having the car on neutral and it mysteriously reversing. You have to experience it for yourself! Doesn't take too much time of your day.
I felt the whole mini structures in the land have been long not taken good care and most of the painting had faded.

I don't think anyone is taking care of the vanue well enough. Everything seems to be dirty so the glass is not shiny. You really have to be into glass to enjoy it. Kitsch is the king here. Not worth the ticket (11.000 won)

We spent more time here than we planned (about 30 minutes) since we made our way down from the temple to the fields covered in canola flowers. There were paths to run in it! There were cherry blossoms and tangerines. It was a beautiful place and I would come back if I have the chance.

Has serene garden  $3 entrance fee. They preserved the deceased artists study which was interesting. The photos had a rare spiritual feel to them. Halla-san is the highest mountain in South Korea and the middle of Jeju Island.  There are two trails that go to the summit of the mountain.  There are a few other trails on Halla-san but they don't go to the top.  It is about 9KM from one side of the mountain to the top and about 10 KM on the other trail to the top.  There are water sources on the mountain so you don't need to carry much drinking water.  It took me between 2 to 2.5 hours to reach the summit and about the same time to go back to where I had parked my car.  The trail is fairly rocky and vertical.  On a clear day you can see all of Jeju Island and the sea below from the summit.  There is also a small pond in the middle of the summit of the dormant volcano that is Halla-san.

Gwangchigi Beach is a beach near Seongsan Ilchulbong.We park our rental car on the side road.There are a few cars & tourist bus park along the road.We can see beautiful view of Seongsan Ilchulbong from this beach. The beach is long and it has black sand.The beach is unique to it own because of the green stone/rock at the shore.It produce picturesque photo because the green stone contrast with the blue sea.This beach appears on drama Warm & Cozy starred by Kang Sora and Yoo Yeonseok.
great place to go on a hot day as it is nice and cool inside and it is amazing to see how lava carved it's way through the rocks

Good scenery location for photo taking & trail walk. Area are clean and windy. They are free parking area that i just realized after finished my activity here and my rent car parked in the paying area! Paid 2000 won to old man already waiting next to my car as i went to toilet.

Good place to visit. We joined YEHA's East Course tour and this is one of the stops. A 20-25 mins walk up the slope to the tip of the peak. Nice to do this at end Nov where weather is cool. You can get a good view when you reach the top. You can visit Woman Drivers taking their dip at the base. There are many shops at the base where all buses and cars park.
Good experience. Pull over your car once arrived in the road and enjoy the experience.  On your way to loveland you will pasd over the road.

getting to the jetty might be an issue unless you take a cab. Fun activity to warm up and dry off after  visiting the lava caves. The perimeter hedge symbolises the coastline of Jeju and care has been taken to maintain the maze as close to nature as possible. Shouldn't take more than 20 minutes to complete.

For those who loves nature.. This is where you can see plants you've never seen before. The area was so huge but it did not deter us from walking and exploring. They kids also loved the exotic plants and were excited to see the carnivorous plants that were indoors.
For 10$ you can visit 2 museums nearby. Very scary museum it obsesses me for a while. If yo no fan of scary things do not come. Go to teddy bear museum or something.

First my lower rating for this aquarium comes partly from expectations that were not met.  This aquarium used to have whale sharks but does NOT anymore.  They couldn't properly take care of them one died and they released the other back into the ocean.  Second this aquarium has been advertised as the largest in Asia which is not true.  It has the largest viewing window in East Asia.  Those misconceptions out of the way this is still a great aquarium.  Interesting sea life some of which I had never seen before.  Great displays and a show that is entertaining if you understand Korean at least somewhat.

review: Fascinating 100m. Our car rolled  down when on Neutral and the road is flat... Bottle of water rolling backward. Same goes when water was poured on the ground...
Experience the car to move backward even though you are not reversing the car. My kids and I enjoyed the experience.Worth it.
excellent for people interested in such. wear comfortable shoes and carry a torch if you need though it is pretty much well lit. carry a good camera to get good pictures in the dark.
even though the cave quite far but worth to visit. even though we came in a rainy day but the visitors still a lot. inside the cave it self pretty interesting and not scary at all.

Even I am not a great fan of cars ... this place have a great collection and is in good condition .? Looking at the different model and time it was produced ...? very educational. ? The outdoor display was very appreciate as you can touch and get in it for the kids.

review: Enjoyed the visitVery informativewas able to make purchase of productsGood car parking facilities

did a slight detour this place  before returing to airport. the road was pretty empty except for one or 2 cars that were already. Did a u turn to face up the slope from where we got in. Followed the sign where to start and put it to Neutral and experience the pull up the slope. It was over with about 200-300m stretch and turned into the carpark beside the shop. Didn't really feel anything strange or excited about it.
Definitely worth a trip if you have time. Your car moves forward while in neutral. We got there at night with our rental car and there were 8 other cars doing the same thing.

Cool nice underground cave cafe ... paid about KWR4000 each pax entrance to the cafe and have a choice of 1 hot or drink or green tea ice cream with that ticket.The green tea ice cream is the best I ever tasted in Korea the green tea latte as well.Cool quiet environment..As for the other attraction outside the cafe there are some miniature world famous buldings near to the green tea field. But they looks run down  which is left untaken care of for sometime.Green tea field is a little small scale  not so impressive as those in Boseung.

review: Cool experience. Not too hard to figure out the mystery but fun! We had a taxi hired and she drove us to the spot and turned off the engine and the car was rolling uphill! I loved it when she did it backwards. Pretty trippy. wouldn't go out of the way to see it but Loveland is literally right next to it so you might as well!

Car parking near the beach is a nightmare... too many cars... cars parked improperly...  but at least it was free.I really like this beach as it was very clean... although there were a lot of people the beach can easy absorb them due to its size... lots of cafe and coffee shop nearby I arrived at low tide and it wasn?t suitable for swimmers as the deepest point (next to shark nets) was only up to my thighs. So I was disappointed by that.. maybe it?s a lot better during high tide....Another negative is you have to pay to use the SHOWERS.. 3000w for adult and 2000w child.... shower gel and shampoo is available... for a price

Car park is free . Entrance fee was 12000W. The maze was great fun because of the music and also the sprinklers sprayed out a fun mist so you did not feel so hot in the maze . There was also a magical spot where they had lights hanging above and the photos turned out real nice . Best of all was the foot spa at the end . Best cold water ever . The viewing observatory was great with a lift that brings you up three stories that gave an aerial view of the area . A most enjoyable experience.

Car move uphill automatically when in neutral gear. Water don't flow down but up. Pretty interesting when you are in a car experiencing so. Suggest to come here if you are going to Love Land else skip it. Suggest to spend maximum 15mins here.
Car is going backward at down slope road. Mysterious! Interesting. Can incorporate into your itinerary. The place is not very big. Nothing much other than the road.

Came here just to try the tea but not visit the museum. The cafe offers a good variety of nice tea. I enjoy the cakes and ice cream too. There are gifts that you can buy for friends here. Things such as green tea chocolate biscuits and facial products. It?셲 quite a walk from the carpark for my tourist bus to the museum itself.

C1 ( 2016.07.15 ) I visited this museum for appreciating collection about liquor. I was surprised because of many collection and well-management. In museum  there was many collection related in liquor  bottle  glass  local soju  and many liquor in the world. Though the entrance fee was a little high  I didn't care because of my satisfactory. There was true museum by collector  I think.
Bring half full water bottle and try to experience the car is moving uphill without engine running! Don't forget to give hazard signal when you try this experiment ;)

Before flying to Jeju-do (island) many of my friends suggested me to do a one day jeju tour that completes the island in one day. But I'm the type of person to enjoy my vacation slowly. Although the island is not that big I wanted to enjoy every bit and detail of the island. I choose to focus on one area at a time. Three months before my trip I researched top 5 beaches in Jeju. After researching I decided my hotel and location place where to spend my vacation. I choose Seogwipo end of Jeju.  The hotel I stayed in was Grand Mer Hotel. I stayed 3 nights there it was a new hotel and the best part was it was across the ocean. You can wake up to the view of the Jungmun beach. Which was listed top beach in Jeju. It's a little far out so you'll need to rent a car. Shopping and museums and hiking was 10 mins drive away. But the view was spectacular and my morning walk was so refreshing. If your ever in Seogwipo you have to try Hawaiian Shrimp restaurant which was 15 mins away from my hotel

Be careful what you do. Just kidding  fret not for breaking anything. The biggest chance of you breaking anything here would be in the souvenir shop. A beautiful museum to go to  to see everything created out of glass pieces. How a simple  yet breakable piece of glass can turn into an artpiece which seems as strong as the pillars of a temple.I like the glass tulips best  a great number of them around this museum. It really shows Korea being a Tulip country  as I get to see these lovely  brightly coloured flowers everywhere. There's a little cafe in there which I thought was a very beautiful cafe  made out of glass. The table you use  the chairs you sit are all made out of glass  added with colour.Surprisingly  the thing you should be checking out is the stand alone toilets  one for female  the other for male. Yes  it's made of glass and from the inside  you can actually see through to the outside! Don't worry  your privacy is intact while answering nature's call  because it's tainted black from the outside and people cannot actually see anything inside! So don't be surprised to see people taking a look at their reflections and doing funny poses while you are doing your business in the toilet. Have a good laugh instead!

As an American when I think beach I think sand water sand castles a boardwalk and a place to grab a drink. This beach has the sand and water but that is absolutely it. Sand water then a huge hill. You have to have a car to get here. There is a parking lot a 1/4 to 1/2 mile away. At the lot there is some minor touristy things. Think about 5 minutes of time to see it all. You then walk down a steep road and are at the beach. The pros: one of the few spots on the south side with sand and not just boulders. There are bathrooms and a place to wash off. The cons: it's a beach and nothing else. Since our hotel is about 4 miles up the coast and right on the beach that is solid rock we will drive here for the kids. But this is certainly not a reason to come here.

Arrived and saw many tourist came by bus just to check out the road. We tried with our car and it really goes up the hill with free gear. A place shouldn't be missed if driving from jeju city to seogwipo.

Arrived an hour and a half before closing. The trails starts with a relatively step decent and the walk thru the lava tube is a 1km walk in and 1 km walk back. The lava tube cave is spectacular. Signs were available to help us learn about the the lava tube. An easy walk but need to be careful on certain section of the party as we were walking on wet lava rock. Well worth the drive there!!!

An interesting place to visit though there is nothing much except for the short stretch of road.. It's amazing to see that the bus really glide uphill.. Some cars are not able to do a good job and the driver ended up starting their engine and start driving
an interesting place to pop by for a short while to see the mysterious road for yourself. experience it in a car with the engine off or roll an empty bottle down the road.

Although a little hard to get to unless you have a car or come with a tour group this museum is kinda cute with a great cafe  AND an InnisFree cosmetics shop.  The O'Sulloc Museum and InnisFree natural cosmetics brand are both owned by the same Korean company.  Bought lots of teas there AND attended a class on tea-making/Korean tea ceremony.  This museum is also located close to the KIS boarding school and not terribly far from Raon Town.
Agree with many of reviewers is pathed very well with many stairs but was worth the visit. Close to the bus stop provided great access & has large car park.
after we arrived in mysterious road we tested with this way .the car engine is off and the road is up hill but the car is going up not going down.amazing
Actually the road has a huge magnet inside well we do not know is it natural or human does it....still mysterious....but we had the sensation when the engine stopped the car is moving

Actually I really want to visit this place after watching korean tv show : 2 days 1 night because I see canola flowers field that really beautiful. Actually it?s quite hard to communication here as a foreigner because not many people can speak english. But they are so kind and helpful even though we need some effort if want to say something by using some gestures. You must try peanut ice cream and Hallabong fresh Juice (tangerine) that really sweet and delicious! You also can find peanut soju here if you want to try.You can also buy a round trip ticket bus there to see this island around or rent a electric car for 2 people.

Across the street from the museum is a green tea patch where people can take touristy pictures and just walk around. The day I was there it was way too hot to even attempt to take photos. Inside the building isn't really a museum but a tea shop that has a lot of variations of teas. There's also a little cafe that serves hot and cold tea drinks along with simple snacks to have with you tea. Out back there is a walkway for people so that they can see the open landscape. There is also a Innisfree Jeju Island shop that has make-up and it was interesting to see some of the main ingredients in their skincare line out on display. The Innisfree shop also had it's own separate cafe with beverages and food.

According t the map the falls were 400m from my hotel - so tried to walk.  Reched the park above the falls easily but could not find a path down.  Turns out only way to access to to go 1km downstream and walk down to the car park and in the official entrance. From entrance it is a 500m walk back upstream to the falls. many people all queuing to take photos.On the way out saw a musical performance near the entrance.
A small beach with black volcanic lava stones. Almost the whole beach has a carpet of mat and sand bags to slow the process of beach erosion. There are better beaches around Jeju.
A short walk from the parking lot. This waterfall is also connected to one of the Olle trails which you can explore from the car park area. It gets quite crowded though.

A really cool place to hang out for half day. Take a return ferry from Port.  If staying near beach in jeju then walk to sanho beach. Stay for few hours and then come back to ferry point. Now take a bike or electric car... for merely 40000 krw. But it's only for 3 hours max (after bargain). But need an international I'd.  I visited with my wife n 3 year son. Took electric car. Stopped at breathtaking  points where bus does not take you. So driving in own vehicle a must for best time.

A place can stopover to visit where not far from the airport. We rent a car and took us few minutes to here. We spent around 30 minutes to look around and photos. A place for discoverer and those who love nature.

A nice stroll along a coastline that is inspiring. Take the time to enjoy this place - don?t just blow past it.  Look at the years of nature carvings and imagine what it was like when first inhabited.

A must stop during our busy vacation here in Jeju! They have free parasols that we used during the sunny day and it made the garden a lot nicer to enjoy. We bumped into the Director that created the garden and he was very kind. I highly recommend buying his book from the store and he even gave us an autographed copy:)) You can tell that each bonsai tree in the garden has a lot of love invested. There are koi fish in the water flowing through the garden and they are well fed and taken care of. There is also a cafe in the garden that has fancy drip coffee. We went in early October and the weather was perfect.
A little scary and very dark inside the cave and the ground is uneven making walking rather tiring and it was a long walk but overall a good experience for me.

A good place. It is very near to jeju love land and it just looks like any other normal road but when you go there you will see the mystery of your car moving by itself without the external and engine force. Also there is a very scenic view around road. Had nice fun.

A geographical wonder and respite from the heat in high summer. Fascinating to see how lava carved out this cave which represents how the whole island (and many like it in the world) were formed. Recommended but also suggest you take a sweater or light jacket. It is cold and clammy!

A beautiful tiny island that is definitely worth a visit!Prepare a full day there. And get your International driving license ready to rent the mini scooters there which is a totally different experience!We ditch our rented car and never regretted. But do note that each scooter can probably take up to 2adults and a toddler max if u have kids. Bicycles are an alternative too.Start your morning early as it?s probably some drive to the port.

A beautiful scenic walk along the coast and the path was well taken care of. We walked to the right first and walked most of the path up until it started to inclined towards the end and then turned around and walked down the left path all the way to the parking lot. Definitely recommend walking both paths since you see different rock formations and the walk is not too difficult or long.
2nd time here but still not convinced about the mystery...only thing is that the car can move on its own without stepping on the accelerator

200 or more exhibits directly carried from ItalyIf it is not the Da vinci museum in jeju  you will have to go all the way to Italy!Meet Leonardo da vinci's scientific ideas brilliant inventions  and paintings at Da Vinci Museum.Docent program10am  11am  12am  13pm 14pm 15pm 16pm 17pm

Your Eyes will tell you one thing. Your experience will tell you another. All in less than 10 minutes.An this is not part of 'Alive' or 'Trick Art Museum'.Although this peculiar stretch of road in Jeju is only about 100 metres long, it really does draw in the crowds.  I arrived there as a skeptic. My wife have read the brochures and blogs about that place. But I was persuaded to be there. Following the instructions:1. drive car to start point, indicated by a stone pillar on the side of the road.2. engage Neutral Gear3. switch off engine4. disengage all brakes (foot and hand brakes)5. sit and relax as you feel your car roll UPHILL!Outside you you will see tour-leaders and other disbelievers coming out with all kinds of theories and proofs. They have their   spirit-levels   (as contactors carry) and cans of soft drinks to, without external force, roll uphill.All this in 5-10 mins.  Figure out HOW for yourself.
You will not believe your eyes.  We started at the   Start   sign, put the car in Neutral, and coasted up hill.  Unbelievable.

You will have to try it youself to experience it! Tried it with a water bottle but it doesn't work. Tried it with a car and shifted to neutral, the car will ascend the inclining road. Quite interesting but will be bored after 5 minutes.
You put your car gear on neutral without stepping on the accelerator, the car will move by itself even though the road is flat. There is 7-11 next to it. Within 5 minutes walk is The Loveland.

You need to purchase a ticket at 2000won each and then take 130 steps down a flight of stairs to get to the waterfall. Comfortable shoes are recommended if you want to get closer to the waterfall. It is advisable to use your feet to check for the stability of the rocks before stepping on them as there were some loose and moving ones amongst the pile of rocks. The rocks nearer to the waterfall are wet so be careful if you want to get even closer to the fall. The waves crashing on the shore are also rather strong, so be more cautious if you?re moving nearer towards the shore.

You need to pay an entrance fee which doesn't include the train ride (which is an additional small fee if you opt to use it). The train can take you on a short ride to view the gardens. Inside the greenhouse, it's quite warm and you can climb up some stairs to view Jeju Island from the top. There was some renovation being carried out in the lifts.? Can spend 1-2 hours here if you're not a garden fanatic!? It's located next door to the Cheonyijeon Waterfall.

You have to walk on a ramp in order to get into the museum because car cannot drive into the area of exhibitions. The venue is separated into indoor and outdoor. For outdoor exhibitions, you should be aware of the weather. If it rains, the ramp would be slippery, so visitors are recommended to wear water-resistant shoes for unusual events. There are plenty of cars exhibited, including antique cars and modern cars. There are descriptions beside every single car including where they produce, which car firm belongs to and when it is first produced. There are many limited-edition cars and some of them are even the only one in the world. There is also a shop located besides the entry of the museum, selling different car models and peripherals. I bought a wheel like key chain, it costs 10k KWD, which is relatively cheap compare to the models of cars.So, if you are a car fan or you want to have some souvenirs about cars, you are recommended to go to the car museum to buy your favorites.

review: You have to walk a little distance from the car/coach park, but the path is flat and well paved.  The falls themselves were, however, disappointing with little water flowing.  I?m sure the falls would be more impressive after heavy rainfall.

you can skip it unless you really love glasses. the entrance fee is quite pricey for the content. we took quite fast to finish the exhibitions, there's indoors and outdoors, one with a punmpkin like carriage for Cinderella. there's also a park where glasses are scattered around purposefully. I like the quietness of the park rather than finding where are the glasses.
You can see there so well cared garden. There is also many different snakes, birds, turtles etc. The caves and botanic garden makes me happy too. Take time and relax. Eeva A

You can reach Ilchulbong by bus from the Intercity bus Terminal in Jeju-Si. It takes around 1h30 to reach it. You don't really care if it is an express or intercity bus you are taking, they more or less all go at the same speed... which is quite fast. You can't really miss the stop which is quite close to the crater. Dozens of buses parked in front of the mountain kind of spoil the nice atmosphere of the place but remember you are a tourist as well...  Left to the entrance, their is a nice small temple, worth the look. The climbing to the top is all made of wooden stairs and doesn't take too long (don't remember exactly, around 30 min). We did it with kids (youngest is 6) and she could do it easily. The view from the top is nice. It is a bit disappointing not to be allowed to walk around the crater. You can just see it from a platform. Before (or after) climbing, don't forget to take a look at the beach on the left of Ilchulbong specially between 13:00 and 15:00 when the old women divers are fishing.

You can imagine: blue sky, strong wind and black shore.  Lots of shops and restaurants around the small island.  Locals can hire a small motorcar but for foreigners without local driving licence, bicycles seem to be the only choice.  It takes about 3 hours to finish the round-island cycling with adequate sightseeing.

Yes, you will able to see water bottle accend up the road without any force applied to it and when you switch off your car engine or shift to Neutral, your car still able to accend the inclining road. But after 10 minutes, you will be bored and it's only work a certain stretch of road only.

Wow. Just wow. We're beginners climbing up Seongpanak trail (longest trail, 9.6km). I thought I was never going to make it! But the people going down were very encouraging. Try to go early, as the carpark will be full by 9. Entrance is free, but you have to pay for the parking. Take note - you gotta reach the peak by 1.30. They'll start chasing people down by then, because you don't want to get stuck up there in the dark (trek takes approximately 4.5 hours one way) Oh, the weather was really good; it was sunny and not a cloud to be seen. It gets pretty hot up there so wear sunscreen. The lake was quite dry though.

Wow! I'm glad I saw this before leaving! Jeju is full of surprises and this is one of them. We were extremely lucky this was a foggy day because seeing this place in fog was really special.  The amazing display of wood carvings etc at the wood exhibition place was amazing as we're all the large insects carved out of cedar wood. It's a 20 min drive from Jeju City. Apparently in summer you have to protect your lunch from the crows! A nice easy walk and an oreum (hill) trail if you want something a bit harder. There are lots of carved statues all along the way and one of those stone paths which you can walk on with your shoes off.  I manage about 2 feet, too hard for me! Haha!

Worth paying for. There are so many teddies in various costumes and postures. There are elvis, the paddington bear, bear at the markets. For those who loves teddy bears, you can also see the evolution of teddy bears . My personal favourite is the teddy bears as featured in Princess Hours and also few diorama of korean culture; the women's diver, korean traditional wedding. Dont forget to take the picture at the park too! My take on the souveniers, as expected is a bit pricey, but if you want to have a momento, maybe you should buy the postcards.

Wondered how we would with a Korean map, but no need to worry. The path is crystal clear, bounded by rope all the way, and very clearly signed. Much of the path is either wooden planked or hessian carpeted (I jest not !). Starting at 750m it?s a tough 1200m to the top, but a mainlybgentle ascent over 9.6km. The last 150m is a little tougher, but the views of the volcanic basin when you get there make it all worthwhile. Much of the climb amongst trees, and very popular with the locals so busy even on an early Monday start. We took 7 hours including half an hour at the top, very stiff calves this morning...
Witnessing at the scene, I could not believe my eyes that car's engine is switched off and empty bottle can rolled uphill.  Something that I cannot explain.  This is really mysterious.

With a few different trails to choose from, climbing Hallasan is an experience I'd recommend to anyone visiting Jeju and wanting a close experience with its nature. Careful preparation of equipment is still necessary, as the easy trail was quite slippery even while wearing winter shoes. The change in scenery when ascending the mountain was magnificent, even though the snowstorm at the top prevented us from seeing the scenery at apparently one of the best sightseeing spots in all of Jeju.

While in Seogwipo, we don't need our car because most of the things are within short distance.First time we walked around the outside of the waterfall park along the traffic to find restaurants. The next day day we took a taxi uphill from our seaside hotel. We were quite bewildered why he dropped us just opposite the Twosome coffee complex, which wasn't the suggested stop by the hotel front desk. Nevertheless, we got off anyway because we saw the cashier booth.Taxi tips: later after the walk uphill, we realized we could have insisted the taxi to go a little further to the big parking area which was the main entrance. That way we would be walking downhill to see the waterfalls, and could exit at the mid hill exit near the temple, just opposite the Twosome Square. If desired, you can also continue downhill to the third waterfall.Photo tip: don't wear aqua or turquoise colors, or green or blue etc. as the the waterfall, although not big, is aqua and turquoise in colors in a sunny day. Is possible, should also go on a sunny day to see the colors, which I think are not so spectacular on a rainy or cloudy day.

When you visit JEJU island, UDO is a must-visit spot, especially in summer.UDO is a small island next to Jeju island.You can go to UDO by taking a ferry.It takes about 20 minutes and you can load your rent car on a ferry as well.A ferry back and forth between jeju and UDO frequently.The best thing in UDO is to enjoy the swimming in the shell beach.Instead of sand, the beach in UDO has  small stone and shell. Due to the small, round stone and small shell particles, the color of the sea is wonderful.Also you can rent a bike or small 4-wheel motorcycle and enjoy the scene around the island.I visited UDO twice and it was always above my expectation.

When you reach the place you bet your life that the road goes uphill. The driver stopped the engine and switched to neutral. To our big surprise the car picked up speed and rolled downhill. your eyes were cheated by the bushes, trees and surroundings.

When you land in Jeju Island, You can start your tour at Dragon Head Rock called   Yongduam  . It takes only 3 minutes by car to get there. Like the name, it really looks drag on head rock and it seems the dragon is ready to go up to the sky.In front of photo zone, if you take a picture, you will realize your trip in Jeju Island started.

When me and my friend tried to look for a car rent with a driver who can guide us, we chose Hi Jeju Taxi Tour, at first because the term of payment is really easy (We can pay cash directly to the driver), and we can customize the places we love to visit.
When car stops the engine, it goes on its own. Other than this, nothing special. However, we have tried to use wheelchair to see whether any similar effect, its not working.

What's interesting is that you really, actually get to see cars/buses with their engines obviously off, rolling up the slope. Expect to see a number of tour buses. Some tour guides will demonstrate the mysteriousness of the road even further by pouring water on the ground. The water will flow upwards. 10mins is enough time to spend here. Recommended to visit once for the experience.

What a fun little island! Exploring the island on a motorized bike/trike was an awesome experience. To rent the trikes an international class A drivers license is needed (US Military living in Korea can use your ID card and Korean drivers license). No license is needed for the motorized 2-wheeled bikes. This is the easiest way to travel the island making frequent stops to see the scenery or stop at one of the many cafes or restaurants. We saw tour busses, and a few regular cars, but seems like the majority of visitors chose the motorized trike to see the island. The ferry from Seongsan Port on Jeju to  Cheonjin Port on Udo runs every 30 minutes and the ride was about 15 minutes. There was an air-conditioned room on the upper deck but it was floor seating only. It is possible to see the whole island in a few hours.

Went up and down seongpanak. Went with my parents who are in their early 50s. The way up gets a little tough after the 12:30 point. We started at 6:30 and got to that area by 11:00. On the way down gets very boring. Bring lots of water and wear shoes. You'll see old Korean people wearing stuff you'd wear to summit some crazy mountain but just good shoes with good grip (not converse) will be good for the hike. Of course hiking boots would help. Things to bring: hand sanitizer, water, sunscreen, gatorade/pocari sweat if it's very hot. Bring some food and bags for trash as you have to take it all with you. Overall probably 4/5 experience but nice to experience with family. Probably not good for young kids - people with health problems die each year per locals.

Went to hyeopjae beach just to try swimming while i was in Jeju. Rented a car and drove there, thought that parking was gonna be a challenge but managed to get one in mere minutes. Mum didnt swim, so we rented an umbrella + mat for her to wait at. Cost us 15K won. Not sure if it was cheap or expensive. They guy attending to the rental didn't speak english, thank God for a local young chap who helped us translate.Loved the vibe of the beach, everyone there was enjoying the waves. Where I'm from, our sea is not as rough. so it was really different to see everyone in their floaties waiting for waves to hit them.

Went there to watch sunrise with Sunrise Peak background and foreground with water and rock.? The beach is large and we could find a spot without disturbance of others.? However, there is no official car park space.

Went there to catch sunrise, but was disappointed. Couldn't see the sun peek out over the horizon as it was cloudy.Went at about 5+ in the morning, it was freezing with the winds blowing. Its autumn. Be prepared to bring your thick windproof parkas and scarves. The walk up to the peak is about 30 minutes. For someone who doesn't exercise, I must say its quite a challenge going up. Take your time. Once up there, the view is gorgeous. Take lots of pictures.From Seogwipo-shi, we drove about 1 hour to get there. So do plan your time correctly to catch the sunrise.

went there after breakfast and was a good time to start if you didn't care too much of sunrise view. Even though it was windy and chilly, got up to the top sweaty and hot. you see see pretty ckear view from the top; Udo island, the wind turbines in the east, Seopjikoji in the south.

Went on a day hike up and down the Seongpanak trail! It was a gorgeous day, about 18C and I couldn't have asked for better weather. It took about 10 hours round trip. Started around 8:30am and made it down by 6:30pm. Luckily the sun didn't go down until 7:15ish so I had plenty of light to guide me.Now, I am not a hiker by any means and this was one of the toughest hikes I've been on. To be honest, it wasn't because the trails were all that difficult - it was actually quite pleasant through the woods and there were 2 rest stops along the way. The first stop is basically a bathroom break and the 2nd had some food available before heading up the last (somewhat steeper) trail to the lake up top. Oh, by   food   I mean some cup ramen and snacks. They also sold water and sports drinks. It would be helpful for you to bring food of your own. They also have no garbage cans so you need to carry and dispose of your own trash once you get back down.The reason why this trail was difficult for me was because I simply wasn't ready for a 20km hike! By the last 5km of the descent, I felt my feet and legs were going to fall off or give in to becoming jelly due to all the stairs and rocks. Make sure you have proper shoes! All in all, I'm glad I did this hike - it was worth it when I got to the top and was able to experience amazing views and clean air. And the flowers!! It was simply beautiful. Just expect to have sore calves for a few days following :)

Well, they call it the mysterious roadBut it's more like optical illusion!Yes it may look fascinating that your car, though in neutral seems to be moving up a slopeBut as people say, it's optical illusion!It can be considered as a stop as there are snacks sold on site as well and if you're there during spring, cherry trees and fields of canola are everywhereVery colorful and pretty

Well worth the trip! The museum is very well presented and organized. So cute! So pink! Lots of kids and laughter about. You can opt to pay for extras, like buttons, passport stamp collecting and heart shaped tag to write on and lock onto the balcony. Some furniture is a bit run down but overall it is really well cared for. The staff is very friendly and helpful. You can also get small food and drink from the cafe and there is a jungle gym are for children to play. They have a short movie and photo station on the roof at the end. The gift shop had lots to choose from and prices were pretty good compared to official merchandise sold elsewhere online. Spent almost the whole day there and I loved every second of it. The museum is incredibly interactive, it would be hard not to have fun. Brought my boyfriend and even he couldn't believe how fun it was :)
Well its just a small steep road but the thing is when driver turn off the engine, the car kept going,    quite excited, but you won't feel mystery .

Well it's a big cave and you are surrounded by lava rocks- which are basically... Rocks.So if you like caves or rocks you will love this!It was very quiet.. Just a few people walked past us... Very different from Ichulbong..You don't need walking shoes or even a torch really, but do care where you walk..It is about 2km from the main road if you take a bus that drops you off on the main road.. Taxis often wait in the main road and charge 4000 one way to the caves..I think entry to the caves was just 1500..The Maze garden is a few hundred metres away too but I didn't go

We where on the way to the Love Park, then suddenly our driver passed it by some 20 metres. He stopped the car with the 5 of us in it, we were facing up hill, he turned of the engine, took the handbrake off, put the car in neutral and I kid you not we rolled UP the hill???I am told it's obvious its an optical illusion but amazed us!! It's free by the way, it's just a normal road

We were very impressed with what happened, and it was really an eye-opener for us! After we drove down the mysterious road, our guide let us get off to watch the other cars in action, and it was really interesting!

We were very excited to visit Manjanggul Cave, and it did not disappoint.It is quite a large cave, and if you walk slowly and look around at the cave carefully, you can see the changes of the lava formation colours and shapes.Make sure you walk the entire length to check out the lava tube, I mean - when will you get another chance? Also make sure you wear comfortable shoes, as my recommendation of walking slowly is not just to check out the different sections, it also means you won't trip, as the ground is pretty uneven and the cave is quite dimly lit!

We were tired in the carpark and considered sleeping but decided to go in. So glad we did, walking through the garden was a deep feeling of peace and felt refreshed. Would definitely come back. A must do in Jeju Island!

We were on a tour bus when we passed by the road. There were quite a lot of people so we couldn't really go down and take pictures. It was literally a 5 minute driveby. Luckily, I was near the front so I had a view of the road and it's optical illusions. I recommend coming with a rented car or taxi, not with a big group. Then you get to really appreciate why it's called the Mysterious Road. I heard from our tour guide that some golf ranges in the area have the same effect to. Golfers should ask around so you can play there.

We were on a mountain holiday.  OUr goal was to walk up the highest mountain in each country.  Korea's Hallam Mountain was our first country and our first mountain. Be prepared if you have not hiked in Korea before to be the dowdiest dresser on the mountain!  Our Korean friends are the snappiest dressed walkers on earth.  Oh, and don't think you will ever be alone.  On the day of our walk it was slow raining,misty and miserable.  Early in the morning, getting off the bus and thinking no-one else would be silly enough to walk on such a miserable day, we were so surprised to see great crowds of Korean tourists all decked out to walk up Halla.  We  packed lunch before we left but there is a good restaurant to the right of the car/bus park where you can get a good breakfast for a fixed price and also order lunch to take with you up the mountain.  Halla proved to be a challenge even though it is the lowest altitude moiuntain  of the countries we will visit.  The access track is very long and because traffic is regulated in both directions you must keep up a steady pace to get to the check points on time.  This is the most critical advice we can provide.  Check locally  and carefully what times you can climb up, and what times you need to come down the mountain.  Finally enjoy.  We were constantly overtaken by our Korean climbers who relished the speed of their ascent and descent, but in the end we both arrived together since they always found time to have a snack and a drink along the way.  Great fun, go slow, enjoy!  Oh, and avoid the snow and ice patches that were still plenty in late April - take/rent walking poles.

We were lucky with the weather to visit the place, and it is important because during the rain it might not be so attractive.The nature is very beautiful, you will take good pictures for sure.We took a small electric car (for 2 people), but it was comparatively expensive for only 2,5 hours. It is possible to go around the island during that time but only without staying at all tourist points. Moreover, you cannot really enjoy the trip because of being in hurry.All Korean suggested to try peanut and mandarin ice-cream, that we did. Again the price was high, and mandarin one was so sweet that make us to put it in trash right away.People in the island are friendly, and even offer to pick us up to some places by car and shown the shortest way.Taking a boat to see caves was the best experience during the whole travel. For only 10 000 won you will have a lot of fun as the boat goes so fast, and definetly amazing view on the island.

We were lucky to start the hike with a beautiful warm Autumn day and clear skies. We started around 7 in the morning at the Gwamneumba campsite, getting a taxi ride from Jeju city was easy and cheap - about 10500 won gets you right in front of the gate. We chose to go Gwamneumsa - Seongpanak, as research suggests that most people who did it preferred to avoid masses of people.. Gwamneumsa also boasts the best views, and it sure lived up to it.The Gwamneumsa trail was lovely at first, most tranquil. But then shortly afterwards, it started getting quite difficult having to balance hopping between and stepping up uneven surfaces of lava rocks..Great views came 2/3's in and at the very last part of the trail.. There's also drinking water available at a small fountain in front of a bridge 2/3 way in. The bathrooms on this trail were pretty gross, one of those toilets that pile waste at the bottom - only that the bottom wasn't very far down.. I would say the bottom was less than a metre, many outdoor bathrooms have their toilets down 20m!.. But consider oneself to be lucky to have bathrooms!We reached the summit around 1pm, having taken countless 2 minute breaks along the way. We were quite slow and took it easy. The lake at the top looked much like a drying pond, I think views would probably have looked better in the Spring. There's nothing much else there, a resting area, a helipad and a wifi tower.Next - Climbing down Seongpanak trail.. The first check point on the Seongpanak trail sells FOOD! We didn't know that, as many sources state there are no food stalls on the mountain.. There's 2 minute noodles, chocolate, bottled water, pocari sweat, tissues, etc. Then on the checkpoint after that you have a small fountain of drinking water.The rest of the trail was a nightmare. We didn't have the correct hiking gear and very underprepared trekking in sneakers and boots. Many say that Seongpanak is easier because its a slope, but having to balance each step as we walked on lava rocks was most tiresome. 99% of the time you're just looking down at your feet making sure it lands on a rock, and you're doing it in a hurry because you're trying to reach the end before the sun sets! And you'd probably be doing that for about 6km.It would have been much easier to go up Seongpanak and down Gwamneumsa, as it is much easier to go down by steps rather than on a slope with uneven rocky terrain.Make sure you have the correct hiking gear - sticks and shoes. Our legs ached! Mostly caused by keeping our balance on the uneven, rocky terrain. My partner ended up with a crook knee, micro ligament tear. We reached the exit gate at 5:30pm! Taxi ride back to Jeju city was about 15000 won.I give this 3 stars because a lot of effort is involved for minimal reward. Yes it is a mountain, and I have hiked other incredible mountains with magnificent views like huangshan and wulingyuan. My expectations were very high as well, the most you get are views of the city, mountain fauna ( though very beautiful), and the drying lake. Do it for the enjoyment of experience and go the other direction, climbing down Gwamneumsa would be so much easier as there are better stairs, not just kilometres of rocks on a slope! And with the right gear! ;)Enjoy!

We were greeted by the only English speaking guide of the village. He must have encountered many tourists and picked up a bit of foreign languages. He was able to greet us in our national language. Further more, he explained that there are no beggars, thieves and gates in Jeju. The villagers live in thatched roof houses with stone walls , black volcanic lava  stones as fence and poles serving as gates. There are three long poles, if one pole is up, it means the owner is away for a few minutes and will be back soon; when two poles are up is an indication that the owner will be away for the whole day; whereas when three poles are up , the. Owner will be away for quite a long time.  Just beside the poles gate will be stone statues of grandfather and Jeju woman carrying a water jug .  Long time ago, Jeju men were treated like kings as due to volcanic eruptions lots of males died and those that have survived had been involved with war activities.  So in the end, there were very few men left and they were thus treated like kings, no need to work, only rest at home, drink wine and enjoy. However, the Jeju women had to do all the household chores, take care of the children and do other work like as divers hunting for shellfish. There was no piped water source then and the women had to carry jars of water on their back from a water source which is usually situated quite a distance away. My sympathies to the Jeju women of yesteryears. And these women had devised an ingenious water filtering system by placing water jars next to nettle trees. There are nettle leaves tied to the tree branch by a straw. The straw cleans the rainwater coming down from the leaves to the container.  One can also see a pig pen attached to a toilet.. In the olden days, the black pigs used to feed on the human feces  that passed down from the toilet. Nowadays, the pigs do not feed on feces anymore but normal pig food and Jeju is famous for barbecued black pork pig,  very succulent and tender. After the tour, our guide told us the village was the shooting location for the famous Korean drama Dae Jang Geum and we were directed into a mini hall where the guide introduced us to Jeju products - black omija tea, honey and horse cream. Howerver, we were not obligated to buy

We were dropped by a taxi at the beginning of the Seongpanak trail (a little way up the volcano), but you can catch the bus there if you prefer and there is a bus stop right near the entrance. The track is 9.6km (19.2km return), and took us about 6 hours return walking at a medium pace, including breaks at Sokbat shelter (4.1kms up - toilet facilities only) and at Jindallaebat shelter (7.3kms up - toilet and small kiosk). We had initially wanted to walk up the Gwaneumsa trail and then down the Seongpanak one, but were too tired to get up before 6am to achieve it in one day. Walking the Seongpanak trail up and down was a great experience in itself, even though it is apparently not as scenic as others. But, because it's one of the easier ones, it is packed with tourists, most of whom are not seasoned walkers, so be prepared for being held up a fair bit (and witnessing some pretty avoidable but hilarious injuries!).The trail is quite an easy one in comparison to other hikes we have done - no really steep bits or actual climbing - more of a gentle incline, with boardwalks in parts, dirt paths and as you get higher, rough rocky paths. The only strenuous thing about the trail is that it is long? It will take you all day, and you have to start early so you reach the Jindallaebat shelter before a certain hour (changes depending on the season, but in September it was 12:30pm) or the ranger won't let you continue - for obvious reasons, there's no lighting at night to climb back down, so he doesn't want to come and find stupidly lost tourists! You can check the times on the official Hallasan website. You don't really need proper hiking boots/other equipment for this hike (we did it in light walking shoes), but if you have weak ankles I would probably recommend wearing hiking boots with ankle support, especially for the walk back down the rocky paths. Take plenty of water and snacks - don't rely on the shelters like the Koreans do, they may sell out/be extremely busy, and you have to get to Jindallaebat by 12:30! We just bought some muesli bars, fruit, WATER and energy drinks like gatorade/powerade at a 7/11 before we left Jeju city in the morning, and were almost the only ones who had thought ahead! On the way back down, the Jindallaebat shelter will be quieter, so it's the perfect opportunity to then buy some of their hot ramen noodles or a chocolate bar. I would also recommend bringing a light rain jacket, and a waterproof backpack/cover for your backpack - it showers sporadically within the fog. I also took a plastic bag to put my camera in to keep it dry.When we began our walk, it was quite chilly at the entrance and the local walkers laughed at us wearing shorts - but by the time you get a few kilometres in, you'll be stripping off layers of clothing, so totally wear shorts if you want to - it's quite warm in the sun on the summit, so everyone will be peeling off their layers anyway! There was a thick fog hanging low over the volcano for about 2/3 of the walk, so it's a bit muggy, but the side of the mountain is lush and green, an eerily quiet forest. As you get higher, suddenly you notice you're climbing above the fog - feels like you've popped out above the clouds, on top of the world! The last part of the track is quite windy, and you can see how the wind has beaten its wooden steps, which are strewn everywhere. Be careful in the last part and beware pushy tourists! But, once you get to the summit, at Dongneung Peak (no facilities on the summit, by the way), the view is breathtakingly beautiful - like nothing I've ever seen before! The crater when we were there was overgrown with vegetation, with a small crater lake. Such a wonderful experience, and most definitely a highlight of our trip to South Korea! You must hike Hallasan during your stay at Jeju-do!

We were coming from Hamdeok Beach to the Jeongbang water falls and happened to directly pass by this place on the highway and I remembered it was one of the top places to visit in Jeju so we decided to pull over and enter.  We're very glad we did.  We spent about an hour there but you could easily spend more time.  It was awesome to see all the man made stone statues and their significance or their meaning, one of the main ones  being the mother who had 500 sons.  The museums were pretty cool as well and you could learn a ton of geography.  The setting was very picturesque with Mt. Halla in the background and the surroundings looking like you were sort of in a savanah.  We took some awesome photographs and learned a lot of information.  I think if you're able to rent a car and drive there it's a must see in Jeju.

We went to udo island in ferry with our car inside the ferry. That was a good experience. Island is nice, but the attractions are not so breathtaking as explained. Can visit once. Beach was good. And the electric small 2-seater rental car was nice.

We went to the market wanted to try some fresh octopus. We bought an octopus from a stall and the nice lady told us in broken English that we can have it prepared at the nearby restaurant. So we went into that restaurant just opposite the seafood stall. None of them can't speak English, even a little bit. So went back to the seafood stall and asked the nice lady to help us. So we seated in the restaurant waiting just for our octopus to be prepared. Then they bring out the cutlery.. we were quite puzzled... why does one octopus need so many cutlery.. then they took out the big steamboat with all the seafood in it! We keep using sign language to say show we don't want the steamboat and just want our octopus prepare... after a while we gave in. and our octopus came out serve in a plate, fully chopped into tiny bits like being blended in a food processor :(we have had enough seafood steamboat over the past few days in Jeju and this is not the time we want to eat the steamboat again. oh well, all because of language barrier and luckily we still have enough cash to pay for the meal as they don't accept credit card.Besides the story, local products sell in this market are quite interesting.

We went to see waterfall at 12PM, there were loads of people, nevertheless view was stunning, waterfall is huge. I'd say better go in day time as when sun is starting to set you'd get weird shadows on your pics and it just won't be the same. Bear in mind you'll have to walk on huge rocks so it's not very safe for toddlers and those carrying their babies, not suitable for those with walking difficulties. Better wear sports clothes which would cover legs in case you fall, to prevent scratches or whatever other injuries. It says no swimming but we took off our shoes and walked in shallow water. It was cold but fun. We also sat on rocks in close proximity to waterfall and splashes from it made us quite wet. But it was spectacular. Such a unique place! Tickets are 1,000 for 16-24 year olds, they require ID. For adults it's 2,000.

We went to Hallasan with my brother: the hiking is just wonderful, this is a must-do if you love nature & trekking. The weather was ok, a lot of wind nonetheless, be careful when going. If you have the opportunity, you should definitely go to the summit!

We went to Eorimok trial thinking that we can go up with normal tracking boots. To our surprise, there was snow even though it was in the middle of spring. Due to the snow, we cannot go up the mountain without crampons. We still enjoyed ourselves at the carpark area as it was beautiful.

We went there with a local guy who show us the mystery. We were in a group of friends and found it quite funny that our car rolled downhill why it looked impossible. I think it can be boring when go along. It's just a short stretch of road, nothing spectacular, just for fun. Visit if you are in the area, but I would not make a trip just to go for this specific attraction.

We went there with a bus group, they organized a lot of activities and Mysterious road was one of these. We found out it's too crowded and there's nothing to see and to do, it's normal street, they said that the cars will move without a driver, but you can't see it or feel it, just the driver feels that. overall don't go there if specially for the street if it's on your way or you are with a group it's okay.

We went there twice on the same day as it is within walking distance to our Seaes Resort.First we went during the general time when other tourists all come the same time, which was still ok for us because we somehow could find a good spot for taking photos.Tips: don't wear black or dark grey or another other dark colors if you want to pose in the photo, unless you want to disguise as a rock formation yourself.After checking out the place we decide the best time is to return at around 6pm to tke the sunset view which was truly amazing. We visited Ireland and the Giant Causeway in Iceland before and must say the sunset here in Jeju is much more likely because of the weather, and is so much easier to visit (although the scale is smaller).More tips: When we arrived at 6pm, one would be intimidated by the tourist crowds at that time but hang on to it and stay longer if you can. The crowds probably were restricted by their guide and car, just quickly left just BEFORE SUNSET ( tours!), or some individual visitors also left right away, leaving the spot empty for a truly memorable experience.  I did my yoga there freely in the sunset until the door guard finally swept us away, about 20 min after sunset

We went there for lunch. It is next to O  Sulloc Tea Museum. There is a car park next to it, if it's is full, can park opposite next to the tea plantation. They serve Bing su (shaved ice) as well. Tried the tangerine shave ice. Average, don't waste your money. Menu limited an pricey. Can purchase Innisfree products as well. Price same as Seoul. Nice place to relax. There is soap making class, where by one cAn purchase the ingredients and make a personalize soap. There is a tea plantation next to it.

We went there directly from the airport via bus (because it was too early for us to check in at our booked hotel).  At the place, the lockers were not available, unfortunately, and we cannot leave our bags somewhere. So we had to carry our things up to see the Seongsan Ilchulbong. We did not attempt to climb up to the peak due to our heavy bags. Instead, we opted to see the observatory at the side of the mountain (it was free... the side going to the peak has an entrance fee) and has a nice view of the sea and the mountain. Can even go down to the sea shore if you like (we didn't). The view from the observatory was breathtaking vast ocean, blue sky and cool green mountain. Will definitely go back someday to see the peak! Also, we tried the Hallabong softcone (ice cream) just near the entrance road to the place, and it was so delicious!!

We went there by ferry, it takes around 1 hour, small but really nice island, must visit if you are in Jeju, it is the southern area of south Korea, population is only 90 , no cars aloud on the island you can make the whole tour by foot in 1 hour and a lot of beautiful scenery to see so prepare camera

We went there by car that we brought from jeju. It's really beautiful nevertheless. 1 day is enough to tour all of it. If you want to try horseriding, there's some that offer price 5000 won per ride, while others 10k won. There's many place that offer horseriding, so if you want to save your budget without sacrifing the experience, walk some more to find cheaper ones.Try the Hallasan fried rice! It's really worth it!

We went on the shortest trail as it was really hot when we traveled here. But the scenery is beautiful. The trail was not difficult and all the people we passed were very friendly! Would definitely recommend checking it out, but just be careful of the heat.

We went on a cloudy day and the driver drove us all the way to the entrance at Yeongsil.  Having a hot afternoon the day before, we thought it would be warmer thN the day before as we Han to walk uphill. The driver saw us in our thin layer, offered me a rain and wind breaker and a pair of gloves. I reluctantly accepted them out of courtesy but later genuinely thanked him after four hours.On a windy and cloudy October morning, the temperature actually dropped as we ascended. Two hours later it got even much colder with strong gusts, as we approached near to split of the main road to either continue uphil to the top, or to go downhill to the other parking lot. I had to use my gloves and another layer there. My husband regretted not bring his hat on a cloudy day to protect his cold ears (anyway later I found his nose sunburnt even on a cloudy day)We used our walking sticks and wore our hiking shoes, which I found very helpful. We saw some people who really had difficulty completing the loop.  I suggest tourists first decide whether you physically can complete the four hour trip (adults) to the other parking lot. If not, better discuss with your driver (if using one) to meet in the starting point, or decide where to park your car, if not taking the bus.Pack your bag reasonably and don't take any unnecessary items. Some snacks are helpful though as there are no snack bar at all. I suggest also try to bring your garbage downhill as I don't think there will be regular cleaner everyday up/downhill for hours'hike.

We went here to get the experience for the gravity feels, and its totally worth it. Our car moves on its own without using any human forces. One of the interesting place for tourists spot and attraction.

We went as a family with young children (age 8-16) and they enjoyed this park. It has a few mazes to choose- all with a different configuration and theme. Just be careful to go in the maze when it's not too dark, or you just might get 'lost'! Overall, quite a fun and challenging adventure - especially for the kids!
