We had a rental car which was nice to be able to retreat back to air conditioning. But the line for the ferry was so long that it took about 2 hours to get on the ferry. Once on the island our first stop was for lunch at Haha Hoho. We were lucky in that they didn't sell out of burgers by the time we got there at 1:50. Buy by the time our burgers were ready 2:40 they were sold out and not taking any more orders. So get there early for lunch. The drive around the island was nice  and picturesque. The first beach we stopped at was a disappointment. The water was green with algae and smelled. There was also quite a bit of trash. With the number of people there I would expect more maintenance. We stayed only briefly hoping for better beaches down the road. The next stop was a black sand beach nestled in a cool looking cove. But again there was trash everywhere. We didn't stay long. The first two beaches were a   bust.    The third was the   coral beach.   It was clean but the water still green with algae and seaweed. The beach was rough under our feet but the kids had fun. It was pretty crowded and the water became deep quickly so not much space to play for new swimmers. The views from the island were great, especially at sunset. Overall we were underwhelmed and felt we probably should have stayed on Jeju and just visited the northern beaches.

We climbed the Eorimok track on the way up and Yeongsik track on the way down. I must say Yeongsik is SUPER SCARY, because the snow is so deep the safety rails were buried under snow, so parts of the trail we had to walk on snow steps next to the cliff.... For totally unexperienced climber like me, it was quite intimidating. If you go in winter, and are not very confident in your skills (like me!) make sure you have crampons and hiking sticks. The convenient store at the entrance sells crampons (around 7USD). My friends were totally fine with those simpler crampons, but I prefer the wire-net style one (the one my friend lent me was from Columbia brand).Hiking sticks are helpful because where it's supposed to be stairs would turn into slides because of the snow -_-Good luck and enjoy!Amazing view. Must note the bus timetable, as we missed the last bus (around 5pm) and had to take taxi (at Yeongsik trail entrance there's an office which can help you find taxis. But it took >1 hour for ours to come...)

We climbed Seongpanak Trail on the Saturday of a 3-day weekend and it was crowded as hell. On the way up it didn't feel like a hike but more like a line of people marching. It was not a huge deal for me. I've never seen a mountain for hiking so well equipped. There were 2 rest areas, one about a fourth of the way up and another 3/4 of the way up. The one 3/4 of the way up is where many people have their lunch and can buy snacks/ramen (less windy). The toilets are horrendous and I had to tie a scarf around my face but it was so strong. About halfway up a mountain you can take a left and for a 20 min walk in & out you can see a nice lake (it may be foggy).This was DEFINITELY a worthwhile experience. The hike was quite easy because there were many man made walkways. When you are approaching the summit it can be very windy. I had to grab the rope a few times to prevent myself from being blown away (I am only about 50kg). We went in October so it may be less windy and cold in the summer months. The clouds move quickly so we were able to see and take many great pictures. Please do this if you enjoy hiking and want to stand among the clouds!

We climbed Halla via Yeongsil Trail on Christmas. Really worth the hiked, yet when we reached the view point on top it was covered by the clouds.Be sure you wear layers of clothes, sweater and jackets as it?s really cold up there with the wind gust blowing so hard in winter.Despite of the clouds on top, we can still take so many pictures on our way up.3.5 hours with many stops for photo session and 1.15 for went down.We travelled from Seogwipo - Vistacay world cup hotel, took the 282 blue bus around 9.30am in the bus stop across the eMart, and dropped at Jungmun Elementary School (We should?ve start earlier actually).From there we went to the other bus stop (it?s near the junction) and took bus 240 straight to Yeongsil Ticket Office and walked about 2 km to the Yeongsil Entrance. There?re small store where you can buy some food and hot drinks as well as hiking equipments like Crampons, Hike stick, gloves etc.Notice that i think in winter the crampons is a Mandatory (except you come with a full hiking equipments) as we?re not allowed to enter the trail only with our bare sneakers.So we bought two pairs of crampons cost 70.000 Won (pick your size carefully as it can squeezed hard your feet if it to small).

We choose a day with the best weather forecast, during our visit to Jeju island, to take a walk to the peak of Hallasan. We choose west trail ? it doesn't lead to the peak, but is much shorter. It took us 3h to get to the highest point of the trail and 2h to get back to the next bus stop. Everything was very exotic, as we are used to hike in Alps or Carpathians. It is worth to remember, that the temperature drops about 1째C/200m, so it should be 10째C colder on the peak than on the sea level. And it was. More surprising was that there are no possibility to buy food or drink in the park. Fortunately we took lot of water and some fruits and sweets (old habit from   real   mountains). The trail was very   civilised   ?mostly steps, easy and very safe (however with ice or snow it's for sure not a pice of cake). More walking than climbing. Not so much people (May seems to be off season), but we were not alone. The view from the trail and the peak just beautiful. In my opinion it's worth to spent half a day on Jeju to see it.

We caught the 7:30 am ferry from Seongshan Port to Udo.  The ferry left a bit early so we actually arrived at the island by 7:35.  The ferry ride should be about 15 minutes.  Cost was 17,000 kwr for 2 adults for round-trip tickets.  We struggled with whether we should have brought our car on board and immediately regretted not doing so once we landed.  Seems it is off season so not busy at all.  The first place we stopped at was the mango shop, where they also have a shop In the back for vehicle rentals.  Stopped there and tried to rent a mini-car/scooter but the staff said no rentals today because of the festival (seems it is the seashell festival).  Anyway, with no other option, we just took the hop-on and hop-off bus (5000 krw per person).  It?s about 21,000 krw round trip for a small car.  First stop was the lighthouse, got there at 7:45 and went back down to catch the next bus at 8:30.  The next stop after was the black sand beach.  Then to the other lighthouse on the northern tip of the island.  We concluded our trip at the stop after that which is the other ferry port.  We caught the 10 am ferry.  We skipped the white sand beach which is probably the most popular site as a lot of Korean dramas were shot there.  Some tips:- bring your car if you have one so you can visit the island on your own schedule - try the peanut ice cream at Jimmy?s Natural Ice Cream- most of the food places may be closed on a Sunday

We came here on 11 January 2015. We hiked up the Eorimok trail and came down on the Youngsil trail. According to the signs, the Eorimok trail are divided into three sections of differing difficulties - it begins difficult and gets easier as you hike up. I found the first half of Eorimok exhausting for a casual hiker because it is quite steep, and also slippery with snow. On the day it was also very foggy, resulting in low visibility. As we walked up to 1700m, we came across a store selling cup noodles. The cup noodles aren't very good and the environment of the eating area is poor; however, it is sensible to say that one shouldn't expect too much from a little mountain store. After eating you have to take the cabbage with you and bring it down to the mountain.Next, the Youngsil trail, which is THE BIGGEST NIGHTMARE. After walking for half an hour down we realised that most of the fences are covered in snow, meaning that we were walking in a mountain unfenced! Given the steep and slippery (snow) nature of the trail, it poses significant risks of fatal falls. In some situations we were (and also some other hikers) so scared that we had to sit down and slid slowly rather than walking. Sometimes it is so steep and slippery that it's not possible to stand up without tripping over, so we slid as though it's slippery dip. Make sure you wear crampon and bring trekking pole. Without them it is almost impossible to hike in Mt Halla in winter.

We came here after the Manjungal caves. The maze is challenging enough and took us about 35min to solve, but it was fun and worth the entrance price. It was a hot day so take a bottle of water with you to stay hydrated. Also, whilst in the maze we noticed some pretty large spider webs with some fairly big spiders, so careful of those. All in all, its a great family activity. There's also some lovely cats in the park that are friendly and you can pet them.

We booked one day tour, but had the best time with Andy so we decided to book one more day. We really think Andy is the best tour guide available in Jeju. Not only professional but he is very caring and very kind.He recommended the best destinations and kindly tried his best to find restaurants for us (we are vegans so it’s quite hard). It was our first time to Jeju and we felt safe traveling with him. You really want him to guide you for your Jeju trip!

We are a relatively fit family, but were not properly prepared for hiking Halla Mountain.  We made it as far as the Observatory (approx. 6 hours round trip). Since it rained days before, the summit was closed due to poor trail conditions.  Although some portions of the hiking trail are level & nicely paved (w/ wooden planks), the majority of the trail is very steep & rough (comprised of large, uneven volcanic rocks). Unfortunately, we wore Nike running shoes & Converse tennis shoes which did not provide adequate support & protection needed on the feet.  Since the incline & steps are uneven, you need to be careful where you step in order to prevent ankle or knee strains/sprains.  We saw some people fall on the jagged volcanic rocks & get scrapped pretty badly.  We found wood branches along the way to use as hiking sticks for balance.  This hike is alot tougher than the hike to the upper falls of Yosemite.  So we recommend that you come prepared:- sturdy hiking shoes and hiking poles- at least 2 bottles of water per person (there are 2 drinking wells w/ a communal drinking cup; we drank it & had no stomach probs)- bug repellent (we were there in the humid summer)- cooling scarf (to wet & wrap around neck)- energy food (power bars, fruit/nuts)- backpack (carry out your trash)- small first aid kitTip: There is a parking fee to park in front of the entrance.  All of the parking spots are usually taken very early.  Otherwise, if you park on the street or arrive by taxi/bus, there is no fee to enter the park.

Was in the area, so decided to have a look at this phenomenon.Turns out to be optical illusion.Tourists were trying to get their cars rolling   up   the slope, children were trying to get bottles rolling, and local drivers were getting annoyed making more aggressive manoeuvers than usual
Was in car driving through this path.Similar roads can be found in mainland China places too,  but children may like.

Walk down to the falls is quiet and serene. A couple of local women were offering the fresh seafood they have just caught for sale. One just need to pay small amount and the woman will cut up the seafood and serve it with some sauce. People will just eat it fresh like sashimi.To get bearer to the fall, one need to navigate through rocks. Care should be taken else one may fall or drop your camera of smartphone. We were lucky to spot a rainbow at the place where the water splashed on the rocks! This is real rare and definitely made our day.

Visiting this caves/tubes you can walk trough the geology! A huge tunnel made by lava rivers 300 thousands years ago, now accessible and well explained. A lot of lava stalactites and stalagmites and huge lava stones felt down from the ceiling. It is unbelievable how   untouched   their rest through the millenni. Nice job by the administrators of the park. It costs only 2000 won.You can also enjoy a free car parking and a small restaurant.

Visiting Manjanggul Cave is one of the main reason I visited Jeju. I and my family were not disappointed at all. We visited during late June 2015. The cave is a little bit cooler inside even in a hot summer day so remember to bring a jacket especially for kids. There was rain before our visit so the cave inside was a little bit wet but we could go inside and visit. There is a steep stair in the beginning of the tunnel/cave so one must walk very carefully. After entering the cave, there is no more stair and on flat level mainly.The whole cave is well lit so you should be able to see inside without bringing your own flashlight torches. (You can still bring it if you want to see everything in detail!)Only 1km of the cave is accessible by visitors. You go inside and walk to the end of the tunnel and then walk back the same way you go in. I suggest you riding a taxi to this place since public bus is not easily accessible to this tourist spot. There is a bathroom outside the cave only. So if you need to go to bathroom, you have to go before entering the cave.

Visiting Hallasan was one of the best experience when we were in South Korea in July. Weather was absolutely gorgeous there! So we thought we well prepared for the one-day hiking event, wearing normal running trainners was a big NO, it was okay for the first few hours, then our feet were felt like being on those painful foot massage non-stop for the next 5 hours. So wear walking boots if you want to hike all the way up to the top! Tips: * If you get there by public transport (bus 781), be aware the bus back to the bus terminal is 782... it seems strange, but anyway bus 782 opposite the hallasan park entrance will take you back to the city centre.* Bring enough snacks and water, and take a proper rucksack with chest strip. you can get instant noodle at 2nd shelter, but its also your responsibility to bring the empty plastic noodle bowl and some left soup down, It could be a bit pain to carry the noodle bowl with some oily soup with you all the way back.* walking boots! !* For girls, take a pack of tissue/napkins with you

Visited over Thanksgiving weekend and were surprised by all the snow! We had a rental car (with chains and GPS) ... 1139 was blocked off first attempt so we took 1131 and viewed the snow from Seongpanak Rest Area and we knew we wanted to hike the next day but didn't have enough time for the long trek so we approached from the other side on 1139. Arrived to Yeongsil Hiking Trail at 7:50 a.m. and had no problem parking at the entrance. Hiked/walked the 1 hour of 2 we had and reached the temple and entrance to the next 40 minute hike which would have taken us to Witse Oreum - fellow hikers informed us crampons were required from there and I don't doubt it, wish we had hiking sticks too, definitely not to be done in the snow with anything other than proper boots. It was a more difficult walk than we thought it would be, fairly steep toward the end and we were all down to long sleeved shirts even though the temp was freezing. Kids (9, 12 & 15) loved it, lots of stops to throw snowballs, etc. As we headed back down at 9:00 we started passing big crowds ... so glad we got out early and enjoyed the tranquil quiet of the snow covered forest! The road was just about cleared when we were leaving so it seems you can drive and/or take a taxi to the temple then do the 40 min hike to the final stop on a day when the roads are clear. Cars were parked for over 1 mile toward the access road so again, hit it early!  Mt. Halla was visible when we approached the top - the first we had seen of the crater in 3 days there, absolutely gorgeous.

Visited on my self drive with my 60+ old parents, wife and 2 & 4 yo kids. Easy to find on GPS,  plenty of parking. Those who don't fancy the hike up can choose to take a scenic path that's still pretty good (wheelchair accessible). We did the suicidal and hiked up baby carrying our kids. Wife and mum thighs are still aching after 3 days lol. It's quite a hike up multiple flight of stairs to get to the top but boy it was worth it! Great views of the crater and the city around, with a nice viewing area to park our tired bums. Mum almost gave up halfway though. Recommended for relatively fit people, think hard if you have old or young in your group.

Visited Manjang Cave in the month of June, which is Summer in South Korea. Entrance fee is nominal - 2,000 won per adult and it should be half price for kids.Temperature within the cave was 21 Degrees Celsius to around 11 Degrees Celsius, a good respite from the summer heat. Humidity is high within the cave, with dripping waters (natural) and wet grounds. Be prepared and carry with you a windbreaker, cap and good covered walking shoes. The entire walk is around 2km. Not entirely suitable for young toddlers, but kids above the age of 7 should do fine. Interesting rock formations within the cave, and a giant lava column at the end the walk. If you have not visited any lava caves before, this UNESCO site is a must-go when in Jeju!

Visited in on 31 Dec  2013 with my Cousin. There was a carnival going on and a stage was built for the new year count down that night. So there were lots of activities and music going on when we were there. It took us about 30mins to slowly climb up the stairs to reach the peak. The higher we go, the prettier the view was and we stopped along the way go take some selfies.  By the time we reach the peak, we had taken off our sweaters and left with only our tshirt on although it's supposed to be winter. It was a good exercise but not advisable for those with knee problems.  Would like to visit again in spring or autumn.

Visited here as part of my tour package. There is a ferry that can transport cars and people to the island. Upon reaching the island, we took a bus tour n brings us to a few locations. The most memorable one will be the hike up to the lighthouse. Tiring but fun and you can see the great ocean around. Took slightly more than a half day of tour in this island and it's fun :)

Visited Hamdeok Beach (⑤댁) with my boyfriend. We took a walk around the beach. It was really windy and cold. The wind was strong. The beach is very clean and beautiful. The waters are clear. We took some pictures there and we happened to see couple having wedding photoshoot (with the beautiful scenery).Many people from various age groups visited this beach. It is a nice place to take a walk and chill out. There are hotels, shops, convenience stores, cafes and restaurants nearby the beach. There is also public toilet nearby the beach (near the carpark). We drove there. It is very convenient and we can get some snacks while chilling out there.

Visited at about 4pm, 2 hours before its closing time, however everything was still available. We tried out the DIY soap making and bath bomb making, which cost 15 000 won each. Do remember to bring along your passport, as you can get a tax refund too. The DIY sessions were very fun, and a great experience for children.The Innisfree House was although small, it is very well-maintained and therapeutic. It sells a range of Innisfree products, mostly for face and skin care. The cafe drinks and desserts were great as well, and definitely worth a shot if you?셱e there for tea break.

Very scenic place to see a pretty high waterfall flow directly into the sea!! There is an admission fee of $2000 Korean won entrance fees per Adult. Short walk from the ticket booth with steps reaching downwards to the waterfall. Interestingly if time permits, one can walk to the end of the big car park in front of the ticket office and there is an Olle trail near the sea that leads to a Castle of Shell and a smaller waterfall!

Very lovely island. But travelling is an issue if you do not have international license to rent the atv. The roads were pretty narrow hence, a little scary to ride bicycle around. Hence the best would be by feeder bus.The seafood noodle, peanut makgeolli and peanut yogurt were fantastic and must try!
Very interesting road that the car or bus or water bottle can walk by themself without anything, very weird

Very interesting road on the way from Jeju City to Hallasan. Haven?t quite figure out why at a certain stretch the car actually rolls upwards on a neutral gear and without brakes. Probably an optical illusion but I didn?t stay to figure out - better just take it as a mysterious road, it?s more interesting. There?s some statues of pigs nearby, symbolizing prosperity and many children. Take a picture, touch the pig?s head.

Very interesting for the first time. The local guide told us they name this road as   monster road   cos locals belive there is a invisible monster playing with the cars that's why the car move forward when uphill even stop engine. Great experience

Very enjoyable trek down the stairs and to the end of the cave and back but be careful when walking because the   ground   is not even as you'd imagine.Very cool inside.Great experience if you haven't done this before

Very cool trip and 2km walk underground in the lava tube. Largest in the world. It is dark, cool and damp. The walking surface is cooled lava, so I'd recommend appropriate footwear. The lighting is respectful for the nature of the cave and energy efficient. Plenty of photo opportunities, for the low entrance price I was very pleased!!I wouldn't recommend any strollers or children who are learning to walk unless you plan to carry them the entire cave visit.

Very big market. Combination of a wet and dry market. Interesting cos they sell many live seafood, vegetables, fruits, sourvenir.The seafood seems expensive when i convert but it could be cos more for tourists. A fish can be $50. We enjoy eating the local food like cuttle fish, fish cake, fish ball, crab stick. About $4 to $7. Just immerse in local culture. The colouful array of oranges and by oroducts. 15 boxes orange chocolate for 10k won. Looks alot but one box only 8 pcs candies so bulky to carry.There is a store sells korean sourvenir like keychain, clipper, magnet, etc $3 to 5 a piece.Bought a sweatpants 5k won so less than $10.Did not dare buy hallabong oranges cos too heavy to carry home. More for local tourists.Overall we do enjoy this market. Near to the underground shopping and fashion street too.

Udo, which means cow island because of its shape, has been a popular island trip from the island of Jeju.  Taking about three to four hour to circle on an electric bike, it?s a great day trip (there are plenty of lodgings for those who want to stay longer).  With only a handful of full size cars on its road, it?s a fantastic place to ride a bike around.  Also, for a small island, the amount of dining and cafe options are impressive. Just going around to sample some cafes and restaurants can easily fill up a full day on Udo.  As the island is famous for peanuts, there are lots of peanut flavored products available ranging from ice cream to makgeolli (Korean traditional wine).

Udo- we went early, were there before 9am. Spent roughly 3 hours on the key spots.1. Ferry to Udo- Our jumbo taxi driver drove us over. Needed to fill out all personal details plus showing our passports when purchasing tickets. Return trip for 5 of us plus driver plus jumbo taxi return was KRW70,000. No queues, not crowded. We went there on 2 Jun 2017 Friday. Just a 15-min ride, need to leave the car diring the trip. Have a good view of Sunrise Peak from the ferry.2. Peak- For a good view of Jeju and Udo, walk up to the peak. Be alert that the track along the coastline uphill is not an easy one for people who don't exercise a lot.  Useful to have hiking stick with you for this short track.3. Geommeollae Beach- Absolutely gorgeous scenery.  A must go place. That's where the famous peanut icecream shops are. There are two.  We tried one and it tasted well.4. Beaches- We went to two. Unforgettable colour and tranquility.  Must go as well.

Udo isn't for everyone and I actually wish that a lot fewer people would visit because the island can get crowded with tourists in cars or on ATVs and scooters. I have lived in Korea 2.5 years and travelled extensively during my time here. I will be going back for my 4th visit next week, each visit for no less than 2 nights. The snorkelling is great especially in places that most Koreans deem   too dangerous   simply because the water is deep. There is one of the best raw fish restaurants in Korea on this little island. The sea surrounds you and the sights are lovely in every direction. There really isn't a lot to do on the island which is exactly why I love it. Sea. Seafood. Sights. It is all amazing.

Udo Island, a small volcanic island 10 minutes by ferry from Jeju Island. A day out on this island can be a bore to those who have no affinity to the outdoors, particularly that of the sea.But if you love the care-free life of roaming from one sandy beach to another rocky one. In between with lots of coastal features to be awed by, then this is the little paradise on earth.Udo is an island which allows you to go the entire distance around the coastal roads, in under 4 hours, including stops for pictures, strolls, ice-cream, desserts and of course a whole host of meals.  There are rugged, rocky coastlines and little stretches of sandy beaches with emerald waters.Getting from point to point on the island is very easy, either on bicycles, rental motorbikes and scooters. Mainlainders can ferry in their car for their own pleasure. We rented a motor-scooter for 25, 000 Won for just over 4 hours. The rental is for 2 hours (Won 25000)

Udo island offers push bike and motorised bike hire for a small fee at both of the docking locations. You can also drive your car onto the ferry and just drive. I used the push bike so I could enjoy the feel of the coast roads without rushing past but you'll still see everything (without the muscle pain) with the other options. There are several little eatery places scattered along the road that offer very fresh and yummy food. I spent about 3-4 hours riding around the coastal road stopping for freshly squeezed juice, lunch, the local peanut ice cream and peanut rice wine. If your looking for adventure this isn't for you but if a quiet relaxing back to nature is what your looking for be sure to stop by.

Udo Island is what I imagined Jeju to be..beautiful coast line beside grassy fields. A relaxing day trip soaking up the amazing scenery. Well worth the (little) effort if you are in the area, and consider a day trip if you aren't!The port is about a 15 minute walk from Sunrise Peak. You buy ferry tickets in a white dome building; start by going to one of the desks with pens and boarding cards. Fill out 2 boarding slips EXACTLY the same (one collected on your trip to Udo and the other collected on your way back). For example, we were a party of two, and on BOTH slips we wrote BOTH our names and details. When you have completed the slips, go to one of the ticket windows and present the slips with your PASSPORT (for international travellers), and if like me, you don't know any Korean at all, just smile and say   Udo  . The lady will ask you if you are returning the same day and issue you return tickets costing 5500 won each. She will also tell you the last ferry time coming back from the island, in our case (November) it was 5pm.Off we went! The ride is about 15 minutes and you get lovely views of Sunrise Peak on the way. When we disembarked, we were immediately greeted (sold to) by various venders renting out pedal bikes or motorised vehicles. We chose the   old fashioned   bikes and had a wonderful time. It costs 10000 each bike, for the whole day. We took 2-3 hours biking around the coast (map provided) taking breaks to admire the scenery and have lunch. If you didn't make any breaks, our vendor thought it would take 1-1.5 hours around. My partner and I are healthy late-20-somethings that don't bike often, but we felt the trip was pretty easy and relaxing as its mostly flat. There are not many cars either, and other motorised rental vehicles zipping by, are small scooters/2-3 seaters, so biking around feels very safe. There are numerous eateries and toilet facilities all around the island. We stumbled upon a cart selling home made pies (Bulgogi, Spicy Chicken, Red Bean and Apple) and they were delicious! I wish I knew the name of it, but if you happen to see it and feel like pies..these are yum!Fit in a trip to Udo if you can..Its a beautiful place to spend some time..

Udo island in jeju is a must see attraction. From jeju have to take ferry to get there, you can take your car or you can go there and take either ATV or Motorbike to tour the island. We had took our rented car since we had bags and baby stuffs. There are many photo spots, beaches , light house etc., across the circumference of the island. A must go place if visited jeju.

Udo is an amazing place We took our car in the ferry ... Costs only 22000 KRW for return trip plus 6000 KRW for each person. We stopped at so many places and took pictures every where. You could also rent a scooter or electric car, but it you have a car, I would recommend taking your own car esp if you are a group unless you like to enjoy on bike. But be ready to face high wind.Though people recommend a few hours only, this place is worth full day spend.

Udo is a small island to the east of Jeju Island - about 1 hour bus from the Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal to Cheng Shan Port and take another 15 mins on a ferry to Udo.  Udo offers a beachside road around the island.  If you have an international driving license, you can rent a small electri car to drive around the island, if not, you can still rent a eletri bicycle or use local bus.  There are many restaurant and cafes along the beachside road.  Sometime you can see a small white sand beach between those dark volcano rocks.

Udo is a really small island, you can go around by bicycle in several hours. Udo is a volcanic island, so it has several nice beaches with white and black sand, impressing lava rock formations, caves etc. We went there several times, every time for 2-3 days, and every time it was just wonderful. You should go and spend a few days there if you want to relax in a quite and peaceful atmosphere with no nightlife, co crowds, no big attractions but with beautiful nature. Still, if you want to get in touch with the rest of the world - no problem here, our Korean mobiles were working fine, Internet was available right in the   arrival hall   of the port and in many   minbaks   (small Korean-style hotels).You can get there easily from Seongsan port  (＿?깆??고) of Jeju island by ferry in just 10-15 minutes. Ferries depart every hour from 08.00 till 17.30 or 18.00 depending on season. Most accommodations are found on on the White Coral Beach (Seo-bin-baek-sa, ＿?鍮諛깆?? or  Sanhosa, ??고몄?? ), 10 minutes walk from the port. They are all small 1-2 floor buildings located directly on the beach with seaview (Pensions, Minbaks). We never booked anything in advance, but found a room on site, but we went in May and October - not highest season. The rooms were always nice and big, also with kitchen and all the necessary kitchenware. Also there are small shops with snacks and some Korean restaurants.So, what to do in there?- swim in the pure emerald water of White coral beach, see the special kind of sand, it really feels like you are in tropics ^^- rent a bike and go around the islandThe road goes nicely along the shore, there were almost no cars except on the busier Jeju-facing side, and we enjoyed the scenery very much!  - Geommeolle Beach (寃?硫?)This is a black sand beach with very beautiful and unusual rock formations and caves, and we spent a very good time there. You can go in caves and see small rocks piled up on each other. And once a year they have a symphony concert in the caves!!Also, if you are a diver with a certificate, there is a diver center there. We tried to do it, but we did not have a PADI certificate so they refused, they do not do fun dives.And  we took a motor boat (10 000W/person) to see farther caves with a spectacular view of Udo cliffs (Hu-hae-seok-byeok, ＿?댁＿?踰). If you are lucky, you can also see a peculiar site called Ju-gan-myeong-weol - sun reflecting at the ceiling of a cave giving a   moon shape  . We also went up the hill, nice view of both Udo and Jeju!!What problems you can encounter in Udo?- languageLocal people are friendly and try to help, but they do not understand English!!So if you do not speak Korean, print out Korean names of what you want to visit and some basic Korean phrases (preferably in Korean, not transcriptions, because pronunciation may be tricky). BUT! the owner of the LOG-house speaks English very good!- foodThere is no Western restaurants on the island, only Korean!! The shops on the beach only sell snacks like Ramen, but there is a bigger mart inland called Hana-ro Mart with fruits, vegetables, milk, etc. (??濡 留, try to ask locals for directions and go there by bike, you will find it, there is no place to get lost ^^). And it could be a good idea to bring some food with you from Jeju, especially if you want something like cheese, wine etc.

Udo is a beautiful island but I would recommend a day trip as Jeju island has a lot more to offer. My friends and I climbed Seongsan Ilchulbong in the morning and then hopped on a boat to Udo, the port is very close and boats go regularly. If you have a car I would recommend leaving it behind as the queue for cars was extremely long. Once we got there we boarded one of the shuttle buses, while they're restricted in where they go it only costs 1,000 won for a single trip, versus renting an electric car that cost about 40,000 but only last 2 hours. The beach we went was not nice, the water was dirty and full of rubbish but the locals didn't seem to mind.Overall it's a nice island but the beaches on Jeju are a lot nicer and cleaner, a day trip is all I would recommend.

Udo feels like more of an island than Jeju itself, because it is much smaller and rural. You can hire a car, golf buggy, cycle or simply walk around this scenic little island. Very short and cheap ferry ride from Seongsan, so add this into your trip to Sunrise Peak.

Turn off your engine, it will push your car uphill.The speed was fast, it is not magic, it is a real thing.You have to see it in person to believe it. If you go there after sun set, it will give you a chill.Must see place on Jeju island. I believe if you a tour, you will get a chance to experience it.

Turn off the car engine, release the brakes and the car moves by itself. Up the tiny slope. It is something very unique which you do not normally experience. Nothing fanciful but definately interesting.We were at night with minimal cars so our driver being a fun guy did it with the car facing front, then backwards.

True to the museum title, there?s quite a number of precious collections, including the first generation of Winnie the Pooh, Carebear and other well known bears. Transportation: There are several buses that make stops at this destination, but just like everything in Jeju, rental car is the recommended mode of travel. Food: the lava tubes does have a restaurant colocated but I did not eat. There are also some snacks you can purchase here but you are not allowed to bring them down into the lava tubes. The stairs were slippery, so be cautious when descending. Don?t worry if you have claustrophobia, The tube is about 25ft across and 20 feet high! There are no tour guides, so you won?t have anybody explaining the history or the geology of the tubes, but there are educational signs posted about every 100 feet. There was also a great museum on sit I recommend visiting prior to going into the lava tubes. Great place to visit, and it took us about 1 hour and 15 minutes.

Transportation to the island: rent a car to drive there, or get 4 people to share a cab (costs around 50,000 won from jeju city). There's also the bus option but I wouldn't recommend as its not the easiest to navigate around the ferry pier. Then take the ferry which leaves every one hour, costs around 5500 won. The ferry is a short ride, only ten mins away! Transportation within the island: the shuttle bus costs only 5000 won, pretty convenient, and it'll take you to the main 4 spots. There's also option of ATV and car rental, which id recommend ATV since its mostly single-lane roads on the island. Food: everyone wanna try the peanut flavored ice cream but I found it's extremely mediocre. It's not 'peanut flavored' but just normal ice cream with peanut powder sprinkled. Save your stomach for the seafood pot! Although not the cheapest I've had, but still pretty worth a try! Get the option with octopus cook on the table if you can stomach the scene (I know lots of my friends can't). A lot of light walking you can do around the island, the weather was still quite cold so we couldn't get into the water. I love that you can go hill climbing at one spot and the dip your toes into the (chilly) ocean the next.

Took the Seonpanak trail, one of the 2 only trails that will lead to the summit. It is a longer route compared to the other but was supposely less challenging. Well, still a very tough hike to me. Much of the path and climbs are big rocks so good hiking shoes and walking stick will be very helpful. No water along the way though one sign mentioned there is one, which was WRONG and not updated. My son believed in that signboard and finsihed his water way before half into the hike. Big mistake!Not much to see along the way, except if you take a detour to view sara oreum. Took about 3.5hrs to reach Jindalrae office/ shelter (which is 1500m high) and after much thought, decided to turn back due to lack of drinking water.Descending is much tougher for me and took longer time. Deers and boars were spotted.Do go early so that you do not have to park too far from the park entrance as the carpark gets filled up fast and you will need to park along the roadside. Go during weekdays if possible to avoid the crowds.Take note there is time limit to reach Jindalrae so that you can continue to the summit.

Took a taxi to the cave from Jungmun. It took 1hr 20 minutes going inland. It was a rainy day and we were looking for undercover activities. The Lava tunnel is 9km long, but the area you can walk in is a 1 km stretch. It is a 2 km return if you walk all the way to the end and then back. The cave is dimly lit, with a few areas better lit to highlight different features. As you would expect, it is cool inside the cave. It is an uneven and rocky surface for most of the walk, although there are a few areas of boardwalk in the more slippery, or rocky places.  The wet surfaces can also make it a little slippery, so care is needed and it is not recommended for the very elderly or for people who would find it hard to walk 1km on rocky surfaces. It is not accessible for people in a wheelchair.Our 4 yr old and 7 yr old loved exploring the tunnel and the walk was no problem for them as they were busy looking for the Lava Monster from the Moana Movie.Signs are posted in Korean, English, and I think Japanese. there is a convenience store and a Korean restaurant located near the cave entrance.Entry fee was 5000 won for our family (The 4yr old was free).If you are looking for a place to stop on the drive, we visited a chocolate factory where we were given a tour and samples. They have a chocolate store on sight. not worth a trip on its own, but a good place to stop when headed elsewhere on the inland route.

Too dark to actually take any nice photos inside. The paths are quite moist and therefore slippery, so have to take extra care when walking. The scariest part was the path down from the entrance as it was pretty steep, so have to be careful of your footing.

Too crowded.  Trail very rough - they   improved   it by adding very large rocks that make it difficult to traverse.
