To make sure hikers are able to return to base before sundown, you have to enter the trail no later than noon and must reach the final section of the approach by 12:30.  Gwaneumsa trail was about 8.7 km long taking about five hours at a leisurely pace.  Most of the hike was in a shaded area which would make it comfortable even during summer.   The first 3 kilometers were just a stroll with nicely laid out boardwalks for some stretches.  There are railings parallel to the trails in case an injured person needs to be transported from higher elevation, which made it extra reassuring for me.  Although steep, it was still a relatively easy hike and I made it through the last section without much problems.  From about 1600 m above and onwards, the trails were covered in ice and snow which slowed me down a bit as I didn?t even think about carrying crampons in late March.  As I got a late start the summit area was a little crowded with hikers having lunch or taking breaks.  Luckily, the Baekrokdam peak is a crater and there was a relatively wide area for people to sit around at the summit.  Unlike the Baekdusan Cheonji Lake, Baekrokdam is devoid of any water except a small patch of water that looks like a small puddle from the top.  While not particularly scenic, it is nice to stand at the highest point in the country.  Because of the strong winds, I didn?t stay long and started to head down the less steep Seongpanak Trail which was about 9.7 km to the parking lot.  Few kilometers from the summit was easy with boardwalk paths and steps.  There was a three kilometer stretch of snow covered trails that made the descent quite stressful though.  Once the snow covered area was cleared, it was a long but relatively flat walk rest of the way which my knees were thankful for.  The entire round trip took about nine hours total without much rest.  Having crampons would have shaved at least an hour off of that time.

TLDR:Long hike, not that easy if you're not fit. 8-9 hours, 19.6km in total.Bring at least 3L of water each. They do sell water at the checkpoint, though only in 600ml bottles.Wear shoes with good sole and ankle protectionConsider taking a small towel (or two) to wipe away sweatBring a warm jumper and possibly a clean, dry shirt. Even in summer it's cold at the topStart the hike before 8.30am if you want to reach the peak because if you don't make it past the checkpoint at around 7km in, before 12.30pm, you won't be allowed to go to the peak.Bring a plastic bag for your rubbish because there are no bins at all on the hikeFor those who want moreRemember that this hike is longer than an average work day and you will need to replace water lost through sweat. Pack around 3L of water per person. Also pack some protein and carbohydrate heavy snacks such as nuts and dried fruits to keep up your energy levels. If you sweat a lot, consider bringing an electrolyte drink sachet to use halfway (or buy a can of Pocari sweat at the checkpoint). At the checkpoint, you can buy instant noodles, 600mL water bottles and Pocari sweat. If you don't want noodles for lunch, bring lunch. But keep in mind it's cold at the top so some warm noodles can be perfect. The noodles are a bit spicy though, so if you don't like spicy food, maybe bring your own lunch. There are absolutely 0 facilities for heating or preparing food. They won't even give you hot water for any noodles you don't purchase from them. Also there are no rubbish bins on the entire hike so you'll need to bring a plastic bag to carry out your own rubbish. The toilets are pretty gross and may or may not have toilet paper so consider bringing tissues. Also the toilets generally have no sinks, so bring some hand sanitiser gel.A small towel or two to wipe away your sweat wouldn't go astray, and a warm coat/jacket and clean, dry shirt will make your time at the peak much more comfortable (addressed in a later section).We took the 781 bus from Jeju city hall at around 6.55am. We arrived at the Seongpanak stop around 7.25am.Make sure you give yourself enough time to get to the Jindallae Shelter (checkpoint around 7km into the hike) before 12.30pm. If you don't make it to the shelter before 12.30pm you will not be allowed to continue up to the peak. It's very disappointing, I'm sure, to hike for 7km, hoping to see the peak and then be told you can't go because you missed the 12.30 deadline. I can't stress this enough. At the shelter, we heard some Americans complaining that they had missed the deadline by 24 minutes (they had started the hike at 10.30am) and that there was no information available on the trail or online about this rule. They were wrong on two counts- there are at least 5 signs along the trail up to the shelter stating that you need to pass by 12.30pm (in English). Also there are a number of blogs about this hike online which also talk about the rule. Now we started at around 7.30am and made it to the shelter by 10am, but we didn't stop to rest at all before the shelter. The walk up to the shelter is 90% easy level with gentle slopes and a few short harsher sections. If you are fit enough to contemplate doing a 19.4km hike then this section should be fine for you. If you start the hike around 8.30am, you will have no issues making it to the checkpoint in time and you should make it back to the bottom by 6/6.30pm. Earlier if you don't rest too long and are relatively fit.Note: there are several places that you can stop to rest just after the shelter. If you are running close to the 12.30pm deadline, just get past the shelter and then stop to rest once you've gone past. Just make sure you don't rest too long because you've probably got another 5-6 hours before you get back to the end of the trail including the rest of the walk to the peak, and you don't want it to get dark or have to rush on the way down.The next section after the shelter is graded as 'normal' by the signs along the route. This section does have a few challenging sections but also some easier stretches as well. If you have regular short rests then it's manageable for people of minimal to moderate fitness with some huffing and puffing.The last 1-1.5km of the walk to the peak is where it starts to get difficult. By this stage you've already hiked uphill around 8km and for probably 3-3.5 hours. The way to the peak is hundreds and hundreds of stairs often with many oddly shaped rocks to navigate around whilst traversing increasingly steep steps. If you're not super fit then you will struggle on this section. At one point we were setting ourselves goals to make it up 3 sets of staircases before we would rest for 1 minute then start again. But the important point is you are so close to the top now, so just keep pushing.The top can be quite crowded. We made it by around 11.30am and hung around for about 30mins to take photos and admire the view. My next piece of advice is- bring a warm jumper because the wind is cold up there and if you're anything like me, you will be sweaty which makes the wind even colder. Another point: if you're a sweaty person, consider bringing an extra dry/warm shirt (or two) with you to change into at the top (and possibly on the way back down). If you're prone to sweat a lot, this can make a huge difference to your enjoyment at the peak because you will by dry and warm. Your photos won't look so sweaty either. Make sure you take a picture of all members of your party with the peak stone marker or the crater to prove that you reached the top.Keep in mind that the way back down can take longer than the way up because you are now passing many people on their way up and going down is very hard on your already exhausted legs and feet. It can take 4-5 hours to get back down from the peak. We started going down at 12pm and made it to the bottom by 4pm, but we stopped several times.The path is quite narrow so on your way down, you will have to stop to let people pass in the other direction many times (unless it's significantly past the 12.30pm deadline, in which case everyone will be going down). The section between the peak and the checkpoint is very hard on your feet and legs. It will feel like forever but just remember that the track gets gradually easier and gentler the closer you are to the end. Stop at the checkpoint for lunch if you haven't already had it, or you feel like some hot noodles to warm you up.Keep on all the way down, being very careful not to slip. There are many rocks and if they are slightly wet, they are very slippery. Eventually you'll make it to the bottom. Then you can take your photographic evidence of reaching the peak to the little tourist office and for 1000 won each, you'll get a certificate saying that you reached the 1950m summit of Mt Hallasan. Congratulations!Sore feet and legs and weary bodies, you can catch the 782 bus back to Jeju city for a well earned rest.

Tips & things to take note:- Bring LOTS of water. On average 2litres per pax.- Bring sufficient food - basically breakfast,lunch,dinner.- Got to reach the checkpoint by 1pm to be allowed to attempt summit- Got to start descent from summit by 2.30pm- Gets cold and windy at the peak so bring a windbreaker.- You have to carry your own trash down. No bins on the mountain at all.We took 11hours and took the Seongpanak trail up and Gwaneumsa trail down. Seongpanak is easiest as its gentler but its the longest trail. Gwaneumsa is much more scenic. We were beginner hikers and hence probably took longer. The tourist  centre told us it would take ~9hrs. Spotted a deer on our way down on the Gwaneumsa trail. It was pretty scary though, we walked for 1hr+ without spotting a single human. (probably cause we were slow)My legs ached for 4 days straight but I have no regrets. My knees and ankles were insanely sore by the end of the hike. If you've even the slightest knee/leg issues, please think THRICE before you attempt Hallasan.Also, toilets are only available at the bottom (before the hike) and at the checkpoint. The toilets are GROSS. I couldn't do it no matter how hard I tried. Toilet was damp and stinky and lots of flies. No water system & its a squat system for ladies. Basically peeing into a hole filled with other people's waste. Saw another lady peeing in the woods instead...Also, all the announcements are in Korean, though signboards are in English.Aim to start hiking by 7am-8am. Any later, you may not reach checkpoint/summit in time unless you have a good enough stamina.Hiking sticks and shoes would help tremedously. Though we did it with regular sneakers. LOTS OF BUGS. Bring insect repellent though again, we didn't have one.Overall, its worth it and wouldn't do it again but have no regrets.

Tip: when you are on that road uphill, please put the car into NEUTRAL gear & switch OFF your engine. That's the only way to test. You will then see that the car is indeed going uphill when gravity tells you that you should be descending downhill on that slope.Having the engine on would offset the effect.Try it.

This works better for coaches, small cars might not see the   magic   so obvious. We tried using water bottles and it worked. Quite fun and it's really amazing. But it only takes 10 mins to view this attraction, nothing much.

This waterfall lies in the southern part of the island, specifically in Seogwipo. Pay an entry fee of 2000 KRW and you can experience it up close for some photo-opportunity but just remember to wear a good air of shoes and be very careful when walking around or climbing over large rocks for a closer feel of the cool breeze. It's worth the trip.

This waterfall is not very big as compare to other but the view is breath-taking as the water falls into the edge of the cliff at the sea front. One can feel the mist of the water fall spraying onto the face as one walk closer to the cliff of the water fall. However, be very careful while walking on the rock towards the waterfall as the rock gets more slippery as one get nearer to the waterfall. But it is definitely worth the risk and the slow walk as the pictures that comes out from the shot is gorgeous!
This waterfall is amazing, but be careful, it's almost dry in summer!! Only negative point: we need to pay to access to it.

This was the same village that Dae Jang Geum (鸚㏝룝) was filmed. It looked like a huge place in the show but in actual fact is that this place is really tiny! It should not take anyone more than 10 mins to complete. We were shown how water was collected from the rain by wrapping a rope on the tree that links into the water pots. The tourguide said that in those days, women in Jeju island work while the men stay at home. The lady touring us in the area carried the water trout to show us how Jeju women in the past used to carry water. There is one small house that according to the lady, is still inhabited. We were not allowed to enter but we can take pictures from outside the house. The house smells of the aroma of freshly cooked rice. We were told that someone is actually cooking. After touring the small compound comes the main part of the program - promoting honey. It seems like there are many version of how real honey should be. For this version, the honey doesn't melt in water. One can see the hives when it's placed in water and swirled around. We were given different honey to try: Pure honey, lingzhi and 5 flavors. For some reasons, they also sell handcream made of horse oil. It smells quite nice though. But I still have a whole box of lanolin cream at home so decided not to buy. They are not cheap either.

This was the last stop on our vacation. Unfortunately it was also the only grey/cloudy/cold day. The island was still a must see for us. The ferry ticketing area can be very confusing, so be prepared if you don't know any Korean. We figured it out after about 5 minutes of standing around, staring in confusion. Once we reached the island, we rented an electric car (from Gulliver's Travels) with side-by-side seating for 占35,000 for 2.5 hours and cruised around the island following the path. The beaches were incredible. White sand, crystal clear water at the shore, turning into turquoise water a little farther out. Even with the grey sky, it still looked amazing. We didn't climb out to the lighthouse (if you climb to the top of Hallasan on your visit, you'll understand why. Ow.) but we got some great photos of it. Peanut ice cream is way overrated in my opinion, but it was still a must since we were on Udo! My husband got the hallabong ice cream. We liked that one more, but the stuff they put on it tastes like mashed up hallabong peel, so it was bitter and we just scraped it off. There is a restaurant that serves (I forget the name, I am guessing) Hallasan fried rice. They make it look like a volcano! We really wanted to go, but needed to catch the ferry back. Overall, if it had been warmer and the we could actually see the sun, it would have been much more enjoyable. We talk about going back and spending a night on the island so we have the time to walk around it, instead of having to drive/rent a bike.

This was the first time I'd ever been to a lava tube so it was a really new experience. It's basically a geology lesson on the impact of lava flows. It was interesting though perhaps a little too academic for non-geologists like me. It's dark though and you have to be careful where you step as this is, after all, a cave not a paved walkway. On the whole, it was a unique experience and it gave me a different view of the beauty of Jeju.

This was the first place to visit before we headed to other place in Jeju Island.O?셎ulloc Tea Museum is also located here and we just stopped by there for lunch and check out the products at Innisfree Jeju House. The lunch was not cheap , it's organic, There were also some visitors who were learning how to make soap, I think we need to pay for that course. I just bought a box of mini masks and move on to other places.Not too bad for a short lunch time and for photos maybe. To go about Jeju Island is best with to rent a car as it's more convenient to go for one places to another unlike in Seoul or Busan where subway are available.

This was one of the most exciting UNESCO sites I travelled to while in Jeju. The cave is a true demonstration of the power of nature. The walls are beautifully scarred by the movements of lava. It is definitely a place to visit for any geologist out there as well as any layperson. Not to mention, it was nice and cold down there, which is a blessing in the summer heat!

this was one of  the most memorable places i visited in jeju. the coast was not an easy walk through, there were 2 entrances/exits for the coast. we took the one with large rocks we had to climb down through. (would recommend taking the other entrance which was behind a large ship) it was scary and there were a lot of sea roaches scurrying around. the VIEW AND WALK around the coast was worth everything though. the coast right infront of sabangsan mountain was filled with canola flowers.

This was my best experience in Jeju. I went in October 2013 and we went up Yeongsil and down by Eorimok. The hike was not the most difficult, but can be quite crowded. We arrived by car around 8am and there was a queue to the carpark. Note that there are two carparks, one on the lower level (where buses drop you off) and one at the start of the trail. We waited about 45 mins to get into the first carpark, and when we saw that there was another queue to go up, we just parked at the lower carpark and started our hike from there. This is a good idea if you plan to go down by Eorimok - you won't have to climb up to get your car after taking to bus from Eorimok to Yeongsil.The hike in autumn was wonderful, the foliage was awesome and the weather was perfect. There is a rest area between both trails where you can buy cup noodles and chocolate bars. It took us around 4 hours to go up and down.

This was a really enjoyable hike up the highest mountain in South Korea @ 1950m, and I recommend it as a great experience of the outdoors and physical activity.  However I saw a lot of people (both locals and foreigners) struggling with various aspects so please take note of the following points:WEATHER:  If you have the flexibility of several days from which to select, review the weather in advance and aim to choose the best day.....otherwise for example you may have no views when you emerge from the trees and at the summit.TIME, PACE & TIME-LIMITS:  This is a long hike, 19.2km round trip to be exact or about 12 miles, but is a relatively gentle incline.  The general consensus in many reviews is that it should take 10 hours total including breaks and lunch.  I would consider myself slightly above average fitness and took 6 hours total, however being solo it makes a difference because I could walk at my own brisk pace and take breaks (typically quite short 5-10 mins) when I wanted.  There are 2 shelters (with toilets) on the route located at approx 4km and 7km, and it's very important to note that for safety reasons they do not allow anyone past the second shelter (which is 2.3km from the summit) AFTER 13-00 HRS, no exceptions.  Furthermore everyone must depart the summit to start descending by 14-30 HRS latest.  I did come across quite people between the 2 shelters who appeared to be rushing to make the 13-00 deadline.  This is not recommended because either you could push yourself too hard and get exhausted, or get injured walking on the rocks, or simply miss the deadline.  FOOTWEAR:  At minimum bring sturdy training or trekking shoes, preferably hiking boots to provide ankle support. Some sections of the hike are on hessian mats and wooden walk ways which of course are very nice to walk on, however probably 30% or more is on large volcanic rocks which are not comfortable to walk on and requires some focus and concentration (especially descending when your legs are tired).  I was surprised to see some walking in sandals and they suffered.  A walking stick can be helpful but is not essential.DAYPACK:  Bring a small daypack to carry water, snacks, clothes etc and to keep your hands free.  Even in summer bring a light jacket or sweater because it can get cool at the top with the wind and elevation.  In Winter I'm sure it's really cold at the summit.PROTECTION:  Bring a hat for the higher elevations (when not in the forest), sun cream and lip balm.HYDRATION/SNACKS:  There is reportedly a source of mountain water half way up but personally I did not see it near the sign, and staff at one of the shelters advised me that no water is available.  Hence suggest that you bring at least 3-4 bottles of water or isotonic drink in your day pack per person (maybe 1.5 to 2 litres), and be sure to conserve it wisely because you'll need some on the way down.  I encountered some people on the way up who had no water left.  Muesli bars, chocolate and fruit are good sources of energy.  As well as fruit, the locals tend to pack rice & meat lunches and have communal picnics at the summit.TRANSPORT:  I used a rental car and got there early, before 8am.  The car park was already full and people started parking on both sides of the main road, which is allowed.  The bus stops are right there beside the car park for those using public transport.CERTIFICATE:   There is small office hidden away near the Seongpanak car park which will print your name on a nice certificate for 1000 Won. (US$1).IN SUMMARY: Please take the time to prepare properly and get there reasonably early so that you can enjoy the hike at your own pace.  During the walk I saw several deer, lots of beautiful butterflies and other insects and loved the great views ....Jeju is covered in 300+ volcanic cones so its amazing to see all of these.  HAVE A GREAT DAY ON HALLASAN!

This was a part of our Yeha bus tour - East Course - and felt it was worth seeing.  It is a lava tunnel/cave, which makes it kind of unique.  Visitors are limited to how far you can explore, which is fine as you do need to watch carefully where you walk - it is a lava tube and the floor is very uneven.  It is known for   Stone Turtle   because it is shaped like Jeju island.  Be sure to have a light jacket.

This was a nice place in Jeju to take the kids, preferably in cooler weather because we went in July, and we were dying.  Besides the weather, everything else was nice.  There's a train that will take you to different stations.  We only stopped at stations 2 and 3 because we brought our boys ages 5 and 7, and those stations had more stuff for them to enjoy.  We probably could have stopped at all stations, but it really was just so hot!  There were lots of places for photo ops, whether all cute or nature-like.  The restaurant at the main building was very limited in the food that they sell.  We ended up eating light food at station 2's cafe and also got drinks at station 3.  All the staff there were very friendly and seemed to enjoy their work.  Overall, nice place to visit.  Oh one warning though, our rental car's GPS brought us to different places even though we entered the correct phone number and even when we asked someone for help and they entered it in Korean.  Just make sure you research how to get there because it was very frustrating for us.

This was a nice little excursion from the main island. Gotta take a ferry which means you need to head over to Udo early and be prepared to come back in the early evening as the ferry schedule will dictate your movement. There used to be a nice coffee shop halfway up at the base of the stairs to the lighthouse exhibits (October 2013). They had the cutest dog too but they were closed when we went back in December 2013. We took our car on the ferry. But you can also walk onto the ferry and then rent mopeds or four wheelers once you get to Udo so you can get around. I was thankful for the GPS in the car though because the roads are very winding, narrow, confusing, and I don't think are marked with names.

This was a great visit!  There is a hidden gem that people didn't seem to know about or decide to see (I'll mention later in the review).  The entrance fee is nominal and you get to see so much.  Even from the top, you get an awesome view and picture with sort of a bonzai tree at the top of the stairs.  Then walk a little further down and there is an alternate path you can choose to walk on large stones and there's some locals selling fresh seafood.  We didn't partake but a lot of other people were purchasing and eating the fresh seafood.  Then we walked all the way down to the falls using the stone path.  Be very careful if you choose to do this as the stones can be slippery.  Once we got down to the base of the waterfalls, you could feel the mist from the waterfalls and just hang out there to take pictures.  It was pretty cool to know this is one of the few waterfalls in the world that fall straight into the sea/ocean.  We walked back up after relaxing a bit near the waterfalls and we saw a path to the Castle of Shell near the edge of the parking lot.  You should take time to walk through this and visit the Castle of Shell.  It's free and you get a very picturesque view from the 2nd floor inside the castle.  Ok it's not really a castle but a small house but it's still very neat to see and just relax on the 2nd floor with the breeze and the nice views.  Then go around the house and there's a relatively unknown path leading down to smaller waterfalls and another great view of stone beach and cliffs around the corner.  I actually liked these falls the same as the main falls.  Smaller but more greenery and there were small little ponds you could soak your feet into.  We took some wonderful photos there and spent a long time wondering why very few people knew about coming here.  There were a ton of people at the main falls but we were at these smaller falls around the Castle of Shells for a good hour and literally saw just 2 other groups of people at the smaller falls.  Take a look at the pics.  It's worth the extra walk!

This was a beautiful climb, but let me tell you, it's a climb. Granted we seemed to go on a particularly hot day at like 1:00 pm so that didn't help.I recommend taking water with you, but if you don't feel like carrying it, there is a store about half way up that you can get water and snacks. There are also lots of souvenir stores and restaurants at the base to stock up on supplies before heading up. I also recommend sunscreen and bug spray.There was a short line to pay about $2.00 for an entry fee. You received a ticket stub with a pretty picture of the volcanic crater on it. The trail is one-way: meaning there is one trail that goes up to the peak and one that returns down. This cuts down on congestion and ensures a scenic route the entire way. There are lots of places to take pictures and rest along the way. The time it takes to complete the trail all depends on your fitness level, but it is advertised as a 50-minute round-trip experience. At the peak, there are numerous places to sit and relax. You can see a beautiful 360-degree view of Jeju and Udo. Other items of interest: Horseback riding is available here and you can see the famous female divers of Jeju.

This transport & tour service is one of the best I’ve ever come across. Mr. Kang himself is very kind and reliable. His recommendations were also some of the best spot we went to throughout our trip. The cars we used were very comfy and clean. The in-car wifi runs pretty fast and, trust me, it’s a convenience you didn’t know you need. My friends and I highly recommend using this transportation service. Thank you Mr. Kang!!

This teddy bear museum is one of a few around the world.  Located in Jungmun tourist complex in Jeju, Korea, is this tiny museum for teddy bear fans alike.  For 8000 KRW you have unlimited day access to 3 floors of teddy bear exhibits and the outside grounds.  This museum carries interesting themed bears like the Mona Lisa bear, the Leonardo Da Vinci bear, a Marilyn Monroe bear, and so many others.  Currently they are displaying the Elvis bear.  On the ground floor there is even a really nice restaurant if you get hungry.  Not much choice in  terms of breakfast, they do offer mostly burgers and different types of coffees.  Also there is a gift shop if you are interested in taking home one of the really cute teddy bear souvenirs.Well worth the visit and few hours for both teddy bear fans and those with just a passing interest.  Remember to use the lockers next to the admission counter.  We didn't and carried all our jackets and bags for the entire exhibit,  It will make the visit a whole lot lighter and more fun.  Enjoy!

This small gallery is tucked away on the southeastern side of the island  but if you're planning on going to a folk village  it's can be easily placed into your itinerary and is a nice break from all of the tourist attractions around the island. The gallery is really just two halls of one guy  KimYoungGap's  work. The photographer  now deceased  only photographed Jeju during his career and it was interesting to see the different landscapes of the island - landscapes that most of us don't see simply because we're so busy checking off all the tourist   must-sees?? This was the only place that our driver  a Jeju native  ran into friends and it was fascinating to note that they could name practically every hill in each picture because each hill (to the natives) was so distinct.The whole visit  including the garden entrance  takes thirty minutes or so. Admissions was 4 000 KRW  but they give you a nice postcard (well  basically  they force you to buy a postcard). Still  the place is well kept  including their bathroom  and we enjoyed our visit enough to buy a photo book. Note that the parking lot is across the street and that you can't enter with beverages or big bags. You have to leave them at the front.

This site is just around the corner from Love Land, so if you're in the area or need a restroom, stop. Otherwise, don't waste your time and gas just to drive here.When you see a bunch of cars with their hazards on, moving very slowly next to the 7-Eleven, you know you've arrived. Put your car into Neutral and watch as you slowly appear to roll up hill.

This shop is located along Chilsung Fashion Street, just a short 5 min walk from Dongmun Market. There is a range of souvenirs that are affordable and not found at the typical tourist shops, e.g. scented candles, dolls, organic socks, brooches, postcards, handmade key chains of fabric horse, notebooks, tote bags and posters. The quality of products are better here.

This roads' mysteriousness can only be seen by placing things that roll on the road because these things will roll the opposite direction it's supposed to!Bring a toy car and take a video, just look out for other free rolling things like cars and buses.

This road is really a mystery, Indeed am intrigued by this stretch of the road as your car on free gear can move by itself. definitely worth to try this road out if you have a car just for the fun of it.

This road is have trick optical, whick look like up hill but actually down hill. All the bus and car turn off their engine in the down, but the car n bus can move to the top of the road like climb without machine, but that acttualy just optical trick. Many place like this in the world, but Jeju goverment use that as a attraction, very good idea.
This road defy the law of gravity. When a car is on neutral gear and foot off the accelerator, cars can actually go ?uphill? on this road!

This review will be written from the point of view of a middle aged woman of average fitness, not someone for whom a 20 km trek is a walk in the park.Mount Hallasan is the highest peak in South Korea and if you are on Jeju island it's definitely worth visiting. We took the Seongpanak trail, a scenic , easy route which reaches the summit. Plan on one day for the trek up and down. Here are some tips:1. It goes like this - You take a bus or taxi to the Seongpanak trail, and start climbing. It's a mix of  some steps and an easy trail. After a while you reach the first stop - I forget the name - where you can use  the restroom. There's a small shelter where we had our packed sandwiches. After this, the trail becomes a little steeper, and you reach the next stage - the jindeballat rest stop.( Times by which you must reach the Jindeballat stop and when you must start your descent are posted on the trail). There are restrooms here - but inspie of information to the contrary , there was no food for sale. After this the climb becomes a little tricky , and you need around 2 hours to reach the summit . The views are amazing from the summit. The Koreans hiking the mountain were not only super fit, they were the sweetest people I've met. When I became tired near the summit, so many encouraged me with words like   Fighting!     Turn around and see how far you have come.  Tips :1. Wear good hiking shoes - at points , the trail is slippery, and good shoes with ankle support are helpful.2. Carry a stick. You can get your own hiking stick or buy one from the store at the bottom.3. Carry plenty of water and snacks.4. Take a selfie at the summit and you can get a certificate at the bottom stating you have completed the climb ( costs 1000 won)5. You do need a certain degree of cardiovascular fitness to make the climb comfortably. But apart from that, the uneven  rocks and boulders are a little tough to climb, so make sure you do some core and lower body exercises too. 6. If you climb down slowly, it gets a little dark by the time you reach the base. Carry a head lamp.

This review was told to me by my awesome afternoon English class student.  I love Korea; especially because I have great students.  It is very beautiful island. Next time I will go to U-do Island with Diisha.You should visit the ocean.  There are many nice beaches.  I didn't like the lighthouse because it was scary.  I liked the lunch. The noodles were delicious/very good. The smell was good. You can see everything in one day.  I was there for four hours.  (Monica/Sing hae).
This really is a great beach, one of the best on the island, a fantastic place to camp or hire one of the caravans there.

This post is about logistics and what to expect from the hike. My partner and I hit Hallasan around 6:45 in the morning on a Saturday to avoid the crowds. We drove to Seongpanak parking lot (free and was filling up quickly. A tour bus with dozens of hikers was already there) which was about a 30-minute drive from Seogwipo. From there we took a $15.00 taxi ride to the Gwaneumsa parking lot. As this was not a loop trail, we wanted to take the steeper/harder route in and have gentler descent (easier on our knees) back to our car. Turns out, doing it this way we avoided what felt like hundreds of people ascending when we were heading back later in the day. The Gwaneumsa parking lot has a fee. (Sorry TA fans, I didn't get the amount since we took a cab --- I am sure it is nominal, like all fees in RoK:) People are allowed to camp at the Gwaneumsa section of the park and I saw a few people starting their day as we marched to the trailhead. We were under tree cover and walked along a dry river bed for the first couple of miles. At this time of day, we only ran into seven other hikers on this trail. After you cross the river via bridge, the hike starts to get a little steeper. About two hours in, you hit a large, modern shelter and toilets. Good time to take a break and snack. Or keep carrying-on as you will get a chance to sit, eat and gaze at another resting place. After the shelter, you will cross a much larger, newer suspension bridge. Fresh water available here. The climb will get a bit harder for next half quarter mile. Continue past the foundation of the destroyed shelter. After you ascend the 18-22 inch tall stone steps, you will reach a ridge which is the other good stop.  No shelters (in fall you should opt for the shelter), but a nice wooden platform from which to gaze at how far you've come. Crows will land in search of scraps. At this point you are very near the top, only a couple more hundred feet to go.The crater was dry when we visited (first weekend in October), but still a wondrous site. The seasoned, local hikers brought burners and ramen and were happily chowing down near the crater. Darn! That would have been nice. The  t-shirt, fleece jacket and windbreaker I was wearing barely sustained me, so the hot ramen sounded freakin' great.The hike down Seongpanak was not nearly as enjoyable since we were bombarded by the late starters heading up. At one point, the hikers coming up were in a jam ? seriously, no one could move, there were so many people. There?s a large shelter a third of the way down. As another reviewer noted, be sure to wear supportive shoes with rigid shanks as you're constantly stepping on uneven rock.  I had on trail runners, which was fine going in, but heading down, my feet were pretty battered. The boardwalk was a nice breather when we could get it.*Seongpanak gentler ascent, (and descent) but be prepared to share the trail with dozens and dozens of other people.*Free parking at Seongpanak -- fills up quickly as early as 7am on weekends.*Toilets available on trail.*Take bimbimbap for a nutritious, affordable, and portable snack. Mandoo is another good one -- good balance of carbs and fat.*Listen and look Nuthatches, Wrens, Great T*ts, and other winter birds on the Gwaneumsa trail.*The park states you must hit the summit by noon. I think this is why so many people were rushing to hit the peak at the same time.

This place was gorgeous! It is a Korean beach so it is crowded please keep that in mind. I am a Floridian and we have some of the best and most peaceful beaches on earth. But this, even for me, was truly an experience. One the amount of people was impressive but less crowded than Busan beach. Try to get here early and pay the money for the umbrella spot. They all cost the same, but you wanna be in the first row so you can see the water.The water is truly beautiful. The color is very different than floridan green blue waters. The ocean here is the deepest darkest blue I've ever seen, and the part that meets the beach is a light bright crystal blue. There are many families and watching the kids is really cute. We spent a lot of time floating around. Next time I would bring a float so we could inner tube around like the locals did.You can order food and the vendors or restaurants will bring them to your umbrella.Fried chicken is a must for Koreans on the beach. We actually were super hungry before going (next time we will do it differently) so we went to Korean food chain Mom's Touch that serves amazing crispy fried chicken in bbq glaze with pickled radishes. So on the beach we got ice cream and fresh fruits.Warning for travelers: more of a cultural heads up. There are showers- like beaches in America have...you do have to pay to use them, but there are no private changing rooms or showers it's all a show for anyone to see. Now it is gender separated, but don't be shocked to find you'll have to strip down in front of strangers. My husband is Korean and didn't warn me, but it was too late once I walked in, plus he already paid for my shower and I really needed a shower. But here's the thing you'll notice that no one cares about you, and no one looks at anyone. Just shower off, do your thing and you'll be outta there in no time. If this is too much for you to handle...then skip the shower and head back to your place to shower in your comfort level.

This place seems to be a lowkey secret place for the local. I went there early autumn so? maybe that's why it's so surreal and empty and looks like I had the whole   pools   for myself. Water's still not cold yet and don't forget to bring mask to see so many tiny fishes down under. Mother-nature created 3-4   pools   and amazingly, it happened to be different depth levels too so to make sure it safe, you can let your kids swim in the most shallow one, just be careful of the sharp rocks (hey it's all natural). Great view with the ocean and beautiful color on a sunny day!
This place near Sex Land, our chauffeur driver show us (by turning off the machine) that the car still able to move even the machine is completely off.

This place is small but surprisingly occupied us half a day. Largely it?s because of the photo moment and also the activities it has to occupy the kids. These activities are drawing, taking self portrait, kids playground, and watching cartoon etc. There is a small cafe to rest your feet while your kids spend sometime at the indoor playground.

This place is really so pretty and peaceful! The assortment of various trees and flowers was so nice, especially in the fall as you could see all the different citrus fruits almost fully ripe. The waterfalls were so nice too and the big coi carps could be the sole reason for the visit!  A bit smaller than I expected but still worth it :)

this place is only teddy bear doll. nothing interesting for me as an adult, but very recomended if you bring your kids here. The souvenir is expensive but the entry ticket is cheap enough. We went here by rent car i'm not sure what public transportshould we use to get here.

This place is only about 8 km from Jeju downtown.  Worth a quick visit to see for yourself the   supposedly   optical illusion where things (water, cars, etc) seem to roll uphill, instead of downhill....

This place is just so amazing! All the displaying items were made by glass, the butterfly, the chairs, benches, pumpkin car, etc..... Not just clear colour and its colourful! I think they have done the check frequently because I can't find any defects, broken part from the displaying items. Best visit for lovers, family with elderly or kids...

This place is an epitome of beauty, beautiful rock formation, beautiful sea, beautiful waves, beautiful clouds, it is amazingly beautiful. Here you enjoy both worlds of rock formation and beautiful sea. Definitely this place is super windy and you might get wet with huge waves hitting against the rock formation. The scenery of the place couple with the beautiful sound of waves for me makes any visit to Jeju complete. Be careful in walking and exploring place, there are areas that are slippery and rough.  If you are an instagram addict this place is the best for you. You can choose to have those lovely rock formation as background or the beautiful blue sea with the huge waves and or both the lovely rock formation and waves.

This place is amazing! I expected to find something of this quality in the US or Europe, not on a vacation island in Korea. The cars on display were absolutely amazing and gorgeous. Classic cars for me are better than modern machines as they have more unique designs and just invoke a more awe inspiring feeling within. Absolutely love it!

review: This place is a must-visit not only because of its UNESCO status, but also because it's really fun!!  Entrance fee was around 2000KRW.  It took me for around 60minutes to have a round trip between the entrance and the lava tube, while browsing and looking at some of the information lined scarcely within the cave.  If you have children or elderly, it'll take longer (I won't really recommend people with walking difficulties to go).  It's quite a walk and be sure to wear comfortable and non-slip shoes.  This is very, very important because there's water puddles on the floor, and the rocks on the floor are actually quite smooth and can get very slippery when wet.  The lighting was very dim but it makes it more fun, but do be careful.  For those who might be wondering, I don't know whether it's allowed, but you definitely cannot use a baby stroller in the bumpy walkway in the cave.  Little tip:  At the information centre (near the bathroom/toilets), there's a photo-booth that costs around 1000-1500KRW for a photo that can allow you to take photos with backgrounds of different attractions (including the Manjanggul cave) within Jeju.  Given that you ought not to take photos inside the cave, why not give the photo-booth a go?  It's not only quite cheap and easy to operate, it's actually a lot of fun!

This place is a must-visit if you visit Jeju. It was a pretty long walk from one end to another end. Inside the cave, it was quite dark and you have to be extremely careful while inside as the floor might be slippery. It was a magnificient cave and if you are a nature/cave lover, you will definitely love it!

This park is on the mountain above the Jeju main ship port.The way up can be done with a car, then the entrance to the park is near the large white lighthouse with a great view over the coastline.you'll have their wide green areas. good for to chilling out but can be skip after the lighthouse.
This nature island was very nice & the Day trip here was very good option, Biking around was memorable. It's a bit to book ferry round trip & need to check carefully if you don't want to miss it!

This Mysterious Road is nothing very special actually, but it can explain by the Physics explanation why we see downhill road but the car can climb up without engine on.. hehe.. so there nothing spooky here..

This museum boasts its huge variety of old computer related exhibitions to a new one. You may enjoy the old memories of punch card, MS-DOS, APPLE I~II, to VR, motion recognition, etc. The only point you should consider is entrance fee. I was ok because I can get Jeju resident discount. But most of visitors from outside of Jeju island should try to discount chances such as Naver booking, etc.

This mistery road is about half kilometer long. Stop you?re vehicle at the start of this road, put the gear in neutral, and turn off the engine. Your car slowly climbs up a pretty steep slope. At least what it looks like upward slope. It is really hard to believe that the upward slope is an optical illusion and it in reality slopes down. I have seen magnetic hill in Moncton, Canada and they have a road like this. But there is just below a mountain slope and the optical illusion is very understandable there but here there is no such thing, just a plain stretch of road. I really could not figure out how your eyes are deceiving your brain. Not a big deal,but worth experiencing it if you are in Jeju.

This might be one of the best beaches of Korea like some say, I wouldn't know, but that tells you more about beaches in Korea rather than about the quality of this one. It is an ok beach super crowded. It cannot be compared to southeast Asian beaches, or Caribbean. It's fine if you are here, but I was def deceived by some ultra glowing reviews of this beach that I felt are completely unjustified. Another thing that puts me off is the fact that many Koreans choose to bathe fully clothed and that they cannot take their eyes off you if you are western.

This market sells many products either fashionable clothes and branded cosmetics. There're many food shops available with reasonable place too. If you are seeking for sport shoes or toys.You can also find here. Some shops will give you the tax refund and some not.You need to check carefully. The famous cosmetic shops like ETUDE and skin food, some of famous items may not available. There're 11 gates which the even gate no. will locate on the right whereas the odd ones are on the left. It's not complicated and easy to walk. There's restroom available too.If you don't buy the well known brand, you will also find the local Korean cosmetic brand which is very cheap. I buy 12 hand creams with 10,000 won prize and can get the complimentary mask for 10 sheets. It's very good price. The souvenir shop also available here.I would also recommend to come as the choice of your shopping since it's not too crowded like duty free building and you don't need to buy a lot of same items in pack like duty free. As most of Korean cosmetics in duty free would be sold in pack of more than 2 pieces which sometimes you don't need that much.

This looks like any regular road.  However, due to an optical illusion, your car without any power will seemingly roll uphill.  This was discovered by a taxi driver by accident.  If you?re there, why not stop by.  It only takes a few minutes.  You?ll see other cars as well testing it out.  This was the first stop of our taxi tour that day and it only takes a few minutes.   There?s an English sign explaining the road.  If on the way, why not. A bit of fun!

This island is not in your usual tourist-package because you really need 1 day to cover the whole quaint island. But it is worth it. The whole place had lots of walls made up of volcanic rocks, making it look almost Irish. And the scenery around the island is just quite breath-taking. We drove and put the car in the ferry as well. Only complaint is that instructions were all in Korean at the ticket office, so hard to figure out what to do. Also, what would happen if one misses the last ferry back to the main island???

This island is 15min away from seongsan ferry terminal. You just have to fill in the passenger particular and show yourpassport. The island is full of atv for rent, do look out for the bus as the road are quite tight.  I shipped my car over at the price of 21000wonDo try their seafood ramen and peanut ice cream!

This is W10,000 per adult.  Lots of car parking.  There are different areas to see at this park including 3 long lava caves, an area with bonsai (my favouite), an area of flowers, a water area, a stone area, old JeJu houses and my least favourite...caged birds some in dubious conditions! I took lots of photos.  Plenty of places to get snacks and drinks but chicken a la flies is not my cup of tea!  A nice place to take a picnic.  There are lots of buses there but they all follow a route...if you go left you have a reasonable amount of quiet time from the hoards of yellow hat people and all the selfie photographer's.

This is the sort of cave one would visit on a tour , decend down into the bowls of the earth , in fact it's not too far down , but be prepared to walk for some 2 km there and back , this is in fact a Lave Tube run then an underground river , all along one can see the water line marks that have cut into the lava ;The floor is VERY uneven , bit slippery if not careful , you are in effect in a huge underground tunnel , rather dark , somewhat damp and water is dripping from the roof all of the time , not sure how wide or tall it was but, shall we say huge . At the end of the tunnel there is a spiral of volcanic rock that has shot through the earth and been frozen by water ( I suppose ) One of UNESCO World heritage attractions in Korea , To be honest I think one has to like this sort of visit to enjoy it , whilst I somewhat enjoyed the visit , I have seen better in France ; however if you have travelled this far around the world and find yourself in Jeju Island then make the effort to visit , entrance fee is 2000 won

This is the only waterfall in Asia which falls directly into the ocean. Admission fee is 2000 won. You'll need to climb over quite a number of rocks to get nearer to the waterfall. Be careful of the slippery rocks if you go after raining. In my opinion, Jeongbang Waterfall is worth to visit than any other waterfalls in Jeju.

This is the local traditional market. You can buy the local products here as souvenir such as keychain (Many designs of Dol hareubang),chocolates products, tangerines chocolates, tangerines tart and etc. Most of the stall owner didn't speak English but some can speak in Chinese (Full of people). Multi level car park available here.

This is the first UNESCO world heritage that we visited in Korea. Walking distance about 1km, so be prepared to wear the comfort shoe. Some area a bit dark so be careful. Overall nice experience to visit this nature cave.

This is the first tourism that I visited during staying in Jeju Island. I went there around last October. At the same time  I went there since this island is one of the seven wonder. This lava tube actually make me very curious since it has so many education things. I went there with my mom which was 70 years old. Eventually we arrive in this place, this lava tube is wet and slippery so be careful when you go along with elderly. At the same time, you should wear proper shoes and mind your steps.So many interesting knowledge you will get inside this lava cave, beside you can visit museum close to this place.

This is the climb for the unfit too. It is relatively easy compared to Hallasan or Elephant Mountain in Taipei (not even half as difficult) and the views all the way up and down is amazing. We did the sunrise climb as we stayed overnight at Illchubong Hotel. From the hotel, it is about 20mins walk to the base - we had a car. There are many public buses that come to this spot. If you have 4of you, you can cheaply get a taxi to the spot for the morning climb.At the top, we did not see the amazing postcard view (aerial view?). If you wanted to take the sunrise with the illchubong Seongsan, you actually do not have to climb up the mountain. There is a huge area to view it as you drive up the highway.There are public buses to the entrance/ base of the mountain. There are 2 women divers performance which we missed due to the timing. It's 11 and 1 or 3pm. You can probably go to Udo island and be back for the late performance.Highly recommended to visit.

This is the best stone exhibit on Jeju island.  And the best part of that is the museum itself.  There are many, many very interesting stones shapes, all collected from Jeju (I think).  If you like geology, there's a great explanation of lava types, stone formations, lava tubes, etc.  Also there is a nice drift-wood display with very unusual, artistic shapes.  Outside, there are many carved stone artifacts used by Jeju islanders from ages past.  The Obaek Jang-Goon Gallery has a nice drift-wood display in the basement.  Park is big, but except for the museums, just a walk-through is enough.  I spent 2 hours in the museums -- the best part!

This is super easy to do... From Jeju city go to Jeju Bus Terminal and the lady at the desk will tell you which bus to get. In this case, 740. This takes you to a ticket office and car park. From there you can get a taxi or walk 2.5km to the start of the trail. We walked and it took about half an hour (but it is all uphill). I would say there are about 3 sections to this walk:1. Through the forest - stream nearby and wildlife (I saw a deer). This is relatively flat until the end when you have to climb some stairs. 2. The hard part- walking along the ridge of the mountain going up the stairs. This is tough on the knees but there are loads of places to stop and absorb the view. 3. Along the top- relatively flat through a forest part and then open until you get to the rest stop. It is the easiest hike and does not go to the top of Hallasan, but it is beautiful and gave you stunning views of the top of Hallasan (which you would not get if you were actually on it). Make sure you bring water, snacks and hand wipes. The rest stop at the top sells only instant noodles and has no running water.

This is such a great place!Even if you don't have enough time, you can see a lot.There are few stages and different   yards   to go to.Really peacefull place if you climb few stages up.After going up you can see beautiful view of the coast as well.And the helpful thing is that they have a small shop in front of the temple (downstairs) so after climbing all mountains and the temple place you can get nice drink or ice cream. Also, they have a car parking place.

This is similar to Dongdaemun market concept in Seoul though this time around so many oranges, Jeju oranges. They are all of the same price, you got your numbers, there is no need to go further. The famous Jeju oranges looked fresher here though I think more expensive than those sold at the Dragon cliff site ? another friend had bought hers there. I am assuming that all other things go the same way here at Dongmun market, so we didn?t venture further in. Parking is a hassle if you are driving a rented car, I saw yellow lines everywhere and cars parked almost everywhere.
This is really the heaven for antique car fans like us. Grandpa was enjoying the old days by seeing these old pals, and kids enjoyed the fun ride of kiddy kart surrounding the museum.
address: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관

review: This is quite a long, dark cave with uneven rough ground surface so it's a bit dangerous. One must be careful with every step. However, inside is a treasure of lava tubes & our guide told us that each one represents a volcanic activity. At the far end is a unique rock formation or a stalactite shaped like a mother & child. Really amazing!

This is purely an activity you should do if you actually enjoy adventures! The guides say to get to the peak it will take 4.5 hours, 8-9.5km depending on which trail you take. We took the popular one, seongpanak because there is a direct bus route from the Jeju intercity terminal (number 781). Here's my itinerary for the day:08.45: arrived at seongpanak trail start09.45: arrived at Sokbat shelter11.10: arrived at Jindallaebat shelter12.30: arrived at peakSo in total 3.45 hours including breaks. I had around 1 hour at the top to sit, eat, take photos, luckily we chose such a clear day so everything was so visible!At 13.30, you have to head down, staff will tell you to move. We decided to take the Eorimok route (8.7km) down and made it to the bottom at 18.00. Things to note:- you have to reach Jindallaebat by 12pm or you are not allowed to the peak. - there are no trash cans, so you have to carry all rubbish. - on the seongpanak route, there is also the Saraoreum Observatory (extra 40 minute walk) which is supposed to have great views!- hiking boots or sturdy shoes are needed!I exercise everyday and managed it fine. My friend who does no exercise made it eventually and was super proud of herself!

This is probably my first 1-star review on TA. Much regretted visit and the only saving grace is that this place is right next to the Osulloc Tea Museum. We were drawn to this place after very good experience at the Innifree Green Cafe at Myongdong and we expected the same (if not better) at this concept store.Product - any Innisfree shops in myeongdong or duty free can offer you a better range at much better price. As Jeju was the last leg of my trip, I was planning to make most of my innisfree purchase in this store but they don?셳 carry much range here. I don?셳 remember there was onsite tourist refund as well (like how it is in Myeongdong) - another reason not to plan your shopping here.Food - I ordered a 18000krw main dish (named herdsman?) with some cold sausages, potato mash, rice balls and orange. The presentation was really pretty but it tasted nothing special. If you are looking for good looking food and great taste at the same time, you have better chance at Myongdong innisfree Green cafe. The other two pretty drinks we ordered were not worth a mention as well. Service - We were there at 450pm and all the soap making stations were occupied. We were told by a staff the soap making would only take 15mins and the place would close at 6pm. so we decided to wait at the cafe and return when the crowd lessen. At 525pm, a staff stopped me at the cashier when I tried to purchase the soap making set. She said that they have closed the soap making station at 520pm. And then another staff came by and said the station was closed at 5pm (?!). I am not sure exactly what time the station closed as there was no sign in the store and the staff were telling different things. The store closed at 6pm sharp and the staff can?셳 wait to have all the guests out by then - this I am sure. This place is a sad contrast to the Osulloc Tea Museum next door.

This is perfect for solo and family travelers that are vacationing in Jeju. Adult admission is 5,000 KW and is well worth it. The hike takes about 30 minutes to an hour and can be  fairly steep in some areas. There are many shops, cafes, and restaurants around the area once you are done with the hike to the top. If you time it right, you will be able to see the famous Women Divers of JeJu who perform at 1:30 PM. The heritage behind it is very unique since it has been carried one for generations.

this is one of those strange Jeju adventures that's worth a quick check.  yes, just like they describe, it's a road which, when you walk down it, it feels like you're going up - and vice versus.  be careful, so you don't get hit by a car - but on your way to something else to do in Jeju, give it a go.  BTW, I  m sure kids won't get it - this is an adult thing, and I don't think I'd want my toddler walking down an active road.

This is one of the must see in Jeju. The most beautiful rocky beach in Jeju. Hamel ship (copy) is on beachside. You can check some pics on TripAdvisor. Spring season is high season.  Summer season is also high season, but check if typhoon is near. Check the typhoon, you cannot go close beach if there is typhoon. It is not normal beach, waves carved this beach for long time, hundreds of thousands of years.

This is one of the most remarkable scenic attractions of Jeju. Our Korean driver brought us here. We told him we are not interested in arts museums or teddy bear or maze park. We only wanted to see the natural sites and wonders in Jeju and he brought us here and we thanked him for that. There was a Buddha Park directly at the car park where we alighted. I could see the golden face of the Buddha from the highland opposite the park. From the car park,  the panoramic view of the beach was amazing; the lush green vegetation studded with autumn foliage with long stretch of gorgeous coastline and natural cliff view and the azure sea horizon. It was nature's master-piece presented in so marvelous and harmonious form that I could not find better words to describe this stunning, breathtaking and jaw dropping scenery. For a moment, a sensation of joy and happiness flooded and filled my heart. As the gentle sea breeze blew on my face, I found tranquility, calmness and serenity in this beautiful land. I immediately dashed down the flight of stairs to embrace this beautiful and spectacular piece of natural wonder. I roamed and wandered around the scenic landscape and found myself singing the Happy Wanderer lyrics: `I like to go a wandering up the mountain track  And as I go, I love to sing, My knapsack on my back. Val-deri,Val-dera, Val-deri,..'  There was the Hamel Castaway Memorial and the vessel Hamel that drifted to this place in 1653. I stood near the replicated Hamel vessel to admire the European naval architectural of that time and I saw the rangers tendered to the horses in the range. From the coast, I could see the majestic Mt Sanbangsan loomed at the site of the Buddha Park and I could vividly see some of my group members were resting and relaxing at a pavilion below the car park enjoying the gentle sea breeze.You must pardon me for my excitement and exhilaration as I came from a city with urbanized concrete jungle with little natural scenery. Jeju is full of natural wonders and Mt Sanbangsan and Yongmeori beach are exceptionally gorgeous gems that deserved a good lengthy exploration.

This is one of the best scenic spots on Jeju Island and we intentionally chose to stay in Seongsan for that reason. Admission fee of ??2000 was lifted in the month of April so there was free entry. Parking, free at all times, is plentiful in the area close to the UNESCO World Heritage entrance. The climb up the tuff cone was gradual along well-marked and well-laid pathways and steps in spite of the throngs of tourists. Do stop occasionally along the route to catch your breath and to catch the surrounding views from various altitudes. On a perfect day, one can see the blue skies against the blue seas and the township of Seongsan below. As a bonus, take the side trail to the Haenyeo or Women Divers? House, to taste the fresh seafood like abalone and other shellfish, sliced and diced before your very eyes and served with kimchi and seaweed. To finish, take a peek at the Dong Am Sa Temple near the car-park. With such a majestic location, the temple is fortunately understated and does not stick out to compete with the volcano backdrop. What an incredible place to spend half a day!

This is not a common attraction but it's a place where we can follow the path and walk around the crater. Though pitifully there is no more water in the crater, it's still an interesting place to visit. The walk just take around 30 minutes. Apart from the crater, it's also a good place to overlook the plains and farmlands.The only offset of this site is its accessibility and limited car park. There is no public transport to go to this place. We drove by ourselves. After we drove off the main road, we entered a small road to the peak. The path is so narrow that only one car can go through, but it is for two-way traffic.

This is like a must-see attraction according to the reviews and the crowds there.... so despite there is nothing much to see when you reach the summit.... just some balding green on a small concave patch of land  .. it is probably still worth the 20 odd minutes climb up , for health sake.. .   Some cardio exercise is always good after all the black pig meals ! If you arrive at the right time at the foot of the hill, you may be lucky to  catch some women divers performing there..

This is just ANOTHER UNESCO Heritage site on Jeju Island. The designation doesn't seem to count for anything special. You probably will not see what you have seen in brochures or website photos because those pictures were taken with much better lighting than is presently available.It is cool but not cold. Like any underground area it is stable temperature all year round. Yes it is wet inside. There is some dripping and there are puddles. A good pair of sneakers will do fine. The ground is uneven most of the time. There are a few wooden walkways over the worst areas but most of it is in its natural state. There is no need for great physical ability to do the walk as long as you allow time to go carefully.It took us just under an hour to walk the length of the tube and back to the beginning including stops for pictures. I can't say that it was very interesting and the walk out was even less interesting since we had seen it all on the way in. The concept of it being a lava tube was interesting and the size of it was impressive. For this, I would say if you are in the area already pay the small fee and just go down the stairs into the tube. No need to do the whole walk. If you aren't in the area...don't make the trip.

This is just another roadside attraction where you stop your car on a road and if you're lucky and the wind is blowing your car will seem to roll up hill. You might think that the world is about to end or that little green men have finally arrived but, it is just an optical illusion. The lay of the land and the slope of the road is all it is. If you're driving past it wouldn't hurt to stop and check it out. Just a few minutes is all you need. If you stop by keep an open mind and don't expect too much. It might help if you have a few drinks before you go, (but no drinking and driving).What is a mystery to me is who discovered it and how and why?

This is free, no entrance fee needed. But if you go by car, you need to pay the parking, about 2k Won as fas as I can remember.They have a path to walk along. You will enjoy the walk along the ocean, actually it is a quite long track, you can choose to walk from one end to another end. but during my time, we have a short time, so we just go and see the rock, took pictures, and go back. There will be a lot of people selling tangerines(oranges), their tangerines is so sweet, and it is only for 1k Won for 1 bag. and in their culture, after you eat the oranges, you can just throw it away to the ground, as it is organic, so return it back to the nature. you dont have to wait until you find the dustbins to throw it. you can throw the plastic in the dustbins but not the orange skin.

This is for the female Merchant who saved people in Jeju island 17,18 Century, Joseon dynasty. Very carefully and beautifully made. However, it is limited for 3rd floor. 2nd floor is for kids' experience museum. 1st floor is for some special exposition from time to time. It is FREE, worth to visit for an hour. It is located near by Jeju coastal international port and Dongmun traditional market. Actually from this market, exit/entrance #3, it is just 500 m away. In those times, people in Jeju island could not get out of the island, however, since she saved whole population in the island, The King Jungjo wanted to give a awards but she refused. Instead, she asked him she would love to visit the peninsular once, and wanted to travel in Diamond mountain(located in North Korea now). So she could get the chance to meet the King and travel inland. Under the Patriarchal system, it must be very hard for her to work as a merchant, but became the most rich person in Jeju, then when there was big famine, she released whole rice and food for free to Jeju people. Any way, it was great fun to enjoy each section from her birth to death. All explanation are in English and in Korean both.

This is by far the easiest rock formation to see on the island. It?s within a stroll from the carpark and very accessible, no Long trials or multiple flights of stairs to climb. Expect bus loads of tourist though. Good views of the coast from the viewing deck.

This is a very well maintained mountain park as expected of any Unesco World Heritage site. My wife and I visited on a Monday and it was packed with people. We climbed up from Yeongsil and climbed down to Eorimok. It's impossible to lose your way. The hike is moderate and you don't have to be very fit to do it. Trainers or tennis shoes are adequate in May. You can do it at a leisurely pace or try to break a speed record. Hot noodles is available at the top (this is not the summit trail) or you can pack your own lunch and there are also a couple of water stations along the way on the Eorimok trail. The view from around the top is expansive but hardly breathtaking. Overall it's a pleasant and enjoyable hike.If you park at Yeongsil and return at Eorimok or vice versa, you can take a taxi back to your car for 20,000 wons.

This is a very interesting place to visit. Our driver put his car in neutral gear, turned off the engine and put his keys on the dashboard, and the car rolled uphill! We got off and watched other people put bottles of water on the road and they rolled uphill as well! It is actually an optical illusion, but still a strange sight to behold. You don't have to stay here for long - maybe 30 minutes will do.

this is a very good island in jeju, just about 10min from the pier to there and meanwhile you can see many seagulls follow the boat, just for asking the snack in your hand~the island is a good place for a walk, or you can rent a bike, motorbike or electric car(these 2 types needa an international car license) just nearby the pier.and please remember to bring your passport to there cos you needa show your passport when you buy the boat ticket.

This is a very easy climb, you can take the bus from the city in Jeju and go all the way until the car park there the path is well marked and you just have to follow the trail it is an easy ascend to the summit then you can com back the other way (west ascend and east descend) and just follow the way back from the east, it is very easy and well marked all the way back, at the bottom yuo can take the bus back to jeju again.

This is a small stretch of road. The GPS setting is 7126988 ( which is for Loveland) but you turn off just before it. The stretch is about 50 m. There is a start and stop sign. At the start sign, set gear to neutral and off the brakes and watch your car go uphill. It is quite fun because of the optical illusion. No fun if you don't drive.

This is a small and nice village that re-animates the life of the Koreans in the past. There are many things to see and learn to know how the people lived in the old days. The tour guide also told us about some interesting agriculture methods. However, there are many ginseng and healthcare products from many companies are located in this place that was a great annoy.

This is a really cool place to visit, one of the best activities in the Island.  Inside the cave it can be a bit cool so do not forget to bring a jacket or a sweater. We went inside the lava tunnel all the way to the end, at least to the section where you are allowed to walk. It will take you about 45 minutes walking, then we came back running, it was fun and a good exercise but you have to be careful as the floor is uneven.  Some of the views are quite spectacular.  The whole experience will give you a sense of peace and adventure.

This is a park for all seasons. It is beautiful any time of the year. We were there in autumn and although the colours were not significant yet, there were plenty of flowers to please any nature lover. The only set back is the cave. It can be quite wet inside and one has to be careful.

This is a nice place to have some scenic shot. The natural volcanic formation is indeed unique. The walk from the carpark to the scenic view is just a short 10 Min slow stroll. There are amble carpark but there are many tourists too. If you don?t stay at the cliff to absorb the nature then the entire place can be done in just 45mins. So if you are here, don?t rush so that you can enjoy the wind and listen the waves hitting into the cliff!

This is a lava tunnel, NOT a stalactite cave. There is one huge stalactite at the end of the tunnel, but if you are planning to see many stalactite formations, you would be very disappointed. Nonetheless, there are many interesting rock formations here. The horizontal and vertical lava flow marks on the cave walls and dimmed lighting give an aura of an alien tunnel. There is also a stone that looks like a stone turtle. :-) The air is slightly chilly and damp with occasional water dripping from the cave ceiling. I would recommend a light sweater or a light scarf to make experience enjoyable. And wear comfortable walking shoes, since the ground is very uneven(but interesting).
This is a huge park and we go around by trains. Not much to see other than natural scenes, but good to walk around. Access is not convenient, you need cars.

This is a great show reenacting the life of Genghis Khan. The horsemanship and acrobatics are amazing and the riders, I believe, are all horsemen/women from Mongolia. There is also horse riding, but the guide maintains control of the reins.  The show is narrated in Korean and some Mandarin, but the action speaks for itself. It is a little out of the way, but if you rent a car or have some form of transportation I highly recommend it!

This is a fun place to stop and spend about a half hour or so.  The road in this section appears to defy gravity.  Not sure of the reason why, but is very interesting to see the car go backwards while facing downhill.  There are some interesting exhibits and statues, along with shops, nearby.

This is a facility that houses multiple attractions  and they are all basically geared toward separating the tourist from his or her money. Notwithstanding this  our family had a great time spending a couple of hours here. The main attraction appears to be the indoor cart racing track. It's not cheap  around KRW 40 000 for a package that includes 10 minutes on the track and a ticket to the   unique objects   museum. We actually found the items in the museum quite entertaining - objects that trick your eye  weird inventions. The go cart driving was a bit disconcerting (no helmets  no apparent real concern for safety) but in the end it was fun. I was glad I was on the track with just another father-son pair. On the way out  my kid bought carrots for horses that were in a corral  and the guy there was nice enough to take my kid around a lap on the horse (again  no safety gear). My kid was fine but I was glad when both the go cart ride and the horseride finished without any problems.If you are desperate to kill a couple of ours and the weather is bad  this may be a good place to go with tweens or teens. They also offered a   Survival Game   attraction which looked like it was done with laser-tag type guns (not paintball).

This is a difficult review to write - the vegetation and environment at Hallim Park is great but my visit was ruined by seeing the way that the animals of the park were being treated.Firstly the Macaw House, an extra 1000krw to enter a large, hot greenhouse full of gorgeous birds in tiny wire cages with no vegetation or shade from the scorching heat.  There was a small black skinned pig in a cage less than 1m long.  Some animals were showing clear signs of distress and in two cases I was seriously concerned that animals were suffering severe heatstroke in a room that was exceedingly hot (34C outside and hotter in the house).The 'Beautiful Bird Garden' is a similar story - birds in cages with little shade, clear mite infections and stress related loss of plumage.  There were a few lucky peacocks able to roam freely but most were in tiny pens (10-15 per pen).  The facilities were not well maintained and the lack of shade is shocking given the heat of the Jeju summer.This was the most depressing experience I've had in a park - I've seen better cared for animals in developing nations.  The conditions at this park bring shame on Jeju and the nation when it appears that plants are treated better than animals.  To make any claims the Hallim Park is an ecological park is rubbish based upon this!If you care for the welfare of animals I would strongly urge you to avoid and express you anger to the local government.

This is a big area in the outskirts of Jeju city, need to car to get there. There are many stone formations around the park and there is story of an old grandmother who had 500 kids and was finally cooked in the porridge and the kids ate her as they didnt know. There is a nice stone museum that explains how rock formation on Jeju is formed and all about volcanic activities and some weird looking rocks. Educational place for kids!

This is a beautiful waterfall that empties directly into the sea. Once at the bottom the mist was very refreshing on a hot day. There are places where kids can wade but I'd recommend water shoes. I saw an adult sandal get swept into the sea. I brought my two kids (age 8 and 4). At the bottom of the stairs there were some very big rocks that were difficult for my 4 year old to navigate, had to carry him part of the way. My 8 year old did just fine. We didn't have water shoes and even though they had fun, they would have been a lot more comfortable with better foot protection. Good site, family friendly with some caution due to big rocks/slippery, not good for toddlers or smaller.

This huge place has many shops and stalls selling household items, fish and seafood.   And there is also the food street selling all kinds of local food.   Just be careful and remember which gate/entrance you enter or else you may find yourself lost and spend time trying to find your way out.

This forest is peaceful, gorgeous, and sit you shouldn't skip. You can get here by car (if you brought one) taxi, or by taking several buses. You can take a map with you but you shouldn't get lost its all marked and one loooooong path. This takes a whole day if you plan to make it to the end. We didn't because we came in the afternoon and didn't want to be in the dark trying to find our way back.
