It is humid so dress light in summer, and bring water.Don't forget to bring a camera as there are beautiful natural rock formations and plant life, as well as bridges to pose on and if you are lucky you'll see Jeju deer frolicking around. We were super lucky and saw 4! There are little   rest stops   along the way but they are like camping ground logs to sit on and Korean squatter outhouses. The only problem I had was the bathrooms....I just couldn't bring myself to go because one they were smelly, two they were dark, three filled with various spiders and I was too terrified to go. If you are brave enough bring tissue paper you wipe with and to toss into the trash. (Tip many bathrooms in Korea don't have toilet paper in the stall. You have to grab it by the sinks before you head in. Many Koreans carry tissues in their purses or bags in case a bathroom is out of tissue. Be wise. Carry tissue. It can save you from an embarrassing episode)We want to go again so we can at least get to the prehistoric volcanic rock formation that we hear have lush plant life all around it!

this cave is huge and takes some time to walk it from start to end. it's cold and damp inside and smells fresh and foresty. You can see layers or larva formations on the walls as you walk.  I enjoyed this place, and have recommended my friends to visit too. It's worth the drive out from the touristy hotel beach areas.  But be careful to wear comfortable and waterproof shoes, it gets slippery and a bit wet in some places.  A must for nature lovers.

This beach, East of Jeju city, on the North coast, is a real gem. Our favourite part is the smaller bay to the East of the main beach. You can rent a static caravan right on the beach there, with an unbeatable, uninterrupted view of the sea. Great snorkelling around the rocks to the right and you can walk up the small oreum further to the right. The main beach has a good eatery that sells Western food and Stella Artois!

This attraction was quite an adventure and somewhat scary at the same time. Throughout the long walk to the end of the cave, it was very dark, wet, slippery and bumpy. Make sure that you wear sturdy shoes(no sandals, flip flops), carry a light/flashlight, and something to cover yourself/head (jacket w/ hood, hat). The entire trek (roundtrip) took about let's say 45 min. to an hour- depending on your pace. Also, it's difficult to take a good picture due to the lack of light and darkness - FYI

This attraction is one of the three UNESCO World Heritage sites on Jeju Island. We drove here in our rental car from Seongsan without any navigational issues. Admission fee of ??2000 was lifted in the month of April so there was free entry. Parking, free at all times, is plentiful in the area. The climb down into the cave entrance is via a large stairway and the surroundings get dimmer as you venture deeper. Only 1 km of this vast network of tunnels is open for public viewing. Take a walk through the cathedral-like cave to view spectacular rock formations, and weird and wonderful shapes of the stalagmites and stalactites, all formed from volcanic lava activity. These are not like the usual delicate works in limestone caves, but more rugged and robust. There are heaps of notices along the way which provides all the geographical descriptions and technical details for those who love the information overload. Conditions in the cave can be a little damp and cool, so watch your step and bring a jumper!

This 6 KM (one-way) hike begins steeply, with nicely laid-out stairs climbing up through a beautiful, dense forest of oaks and maples.  It is very peaceful here, and our early (8 AM) start put us on the trail ahead of the crowds that showed up later in the day.  Most of the elevation gain -- total about 700M -- is accomplished in the first third of the hike.  The reward is a lovely stroll with some ups and downs through open meadows for the remainder of the hike to the Witse Oreum shelter.  Two springs are available if you need water on the way (but fill your water bottle directly:  I saw people drinking from the dippers hanging by one of the springs).  Views of the Halla crater wall and sweeping views downslope, of other parasitic cones and the sea, can be spectacular here on a clear day.  We went back down the Eorimok trail to our rental car, but other hikers we met recommended a one-way hike up the Yeongsil Trail (not so long) and then down the Eorimok (but then you have to take a bus or have two cars to do a shuttle).  Neither trail goes to the top of the crater, those areas being closed for extensive restoration.  However, the views were fantastic and I don't feel that I missed out on anything except a hard climb.

They are selling variety of products ranging from skin care, hair care, body care and even food and beverage. Their skin care products are popular in Korea and well known. Besides, if you have times try to buy a hand made soap pack and try to make the soap yourself. It might take time around 1 to 2 hours as there are 3 pieces of soap inside the pack. I would strongly recommend you to try this as this is only available in Jeju island not at other's innisfree branch.

There's basically nothing here except for the black rock that is sculpted by nature to look like a dragon head.  However, the sea view is pretty. Doesn't need to spend a lot of time here.  Maybe about 10 mins max. There's also a souvenir soup nearby which sells Korean gifts. The shop is not huge but you can find stuffs that typical souvenir shops will sell. eg. keychain, pen, towels, mugs, socks (yes, for some reasons, Koreans are really fond of cute socks with cartoons)..etc.Saw the Roll Hotto snack.  In Singapore, we call this flakey flour pastry as prata. In this case, they rolled the prata with egg and ham complete with vege. Kindda cool.The ice cream they are selling at this attraction is interesting.  I chose 2 flavors: Vanilla and Strawberry. Price is KRW3,000 or RMB20. It's kind of interesting to note that RMB is accepted in Korea as a form of payment. Nonetheless, the ice cream is yummy!More photos available onhttp://i-wanna-travel.blogspot.sg/2015/03/korea-jeju-17-mar-2014.html.

There's a starting point and ending point, that shows this mysterious road's gravitational force. Many went with tour buses but it's best to experience this in your own rented car! Switch to neutral and let the mystery begin!

There's a car park round the corner from the market. Came down by the lifts to the middle of the market. There's fresh sea food, vegetables, fruit and a lot of locally produced chocolates and pies. Stopped at one of the hole in the wall eateries because of the freshly shucked oysters (KRW 5,000) and sat down for seafood stew (KRW 12,000). Scrumptious lunch!

There were a lot carter in jeju island, one of them is sangamburi.We went there by rent a car, from our hotel around 1 hour. The place is calm and nature. With mountain view, savana and trees all around.If you like nature, this place is one of your choice. One of korean movie was made there.When we entered the place, there's a garden, walked inside there's line of trees, in the middle, there's savana.Going further, you will find mountain view.

There was so much to see and do, and the actual burning of the hill is spectacular. I spent half a day there and hadn?t seen everything. The thing to be aware of is the time it can take to get out of the car park afterwards, but totally worth it !

There was a tour group with a guide when we visited. We saw his demonstration of water flowing upstream and a water bottle that roll upstream too. very interesting, when you switch off the car engine and witness the car rolling upwards.

There lies 3 waterfall spots in Seogwipo, south of Jeju. I have went to all 3. But this Cheonjeyeon (not to be confused with Cheonjiyeon waterfall) itself has 3 waterfalls around the area. So in fact, there are 5 waterfalls in Seogwipo. The ticket is more expensive compared to the others but it is worth it as you can visit 3 falls and an arching bridge with nymphs (angels) carvings on the side. I prefer this place to Cheonjiyeon Falls.

There is a start sign & stop sign. Upon reaching the start sign, switch to neutral gear, on hazard light, and keep your car engine on. It will start to move forward on a uphill slope. Very slowly. Of course, do be alert and keep your eye infront and foot hover on brake if necessary.It is a one lane traffic, so not all cars are stopping to be wow by this nature forces, you might be honked by other drivers for slowing down and doing this anti-gravity act. Well... just ignore them. They will move on by cutting your lane.There is a convenient shop next to it and car park. You can park your car there and come down to try it with a half-filled water bottle. It will perform the same too, rolling up on a up-slope.However, beware of cars. There is still on-coming traffic.

There is a start point specified on the road. I stopped my car, put car to neutral and released the brakes - the car started to move slowly forward and up slope! From inside the car, the road is up slope, yet the car is like rolling down slope on neutral gear. Fascinating! A must try if you are self-driving.

There are some fictional characters that you and me adore and love during our childhood and yet still relish even though we have become adults. Hello Kitty is certainly one of them, and is a favourite of one of my children. However, the good part is not every visitor to Jeju and the locals are a fan of Hello Kitty, so the Hello Kitty Island Museum is not on the itinerary of most tour companies, and hence it?s not crowded.Getting there and fees: Hello Kitty Island Museum, opened in late 2013, is located in the south west part of Jeju (GPS code/coordinate 7926114).  Not to worry if you cannot find space in the small open-air car park outside the Museum because there?s another huge open air car park below the small one. Parking is free. Entrance fee to the Museum is 12,000 won for adult, 11,000 won for teenagers and 10,000Won for children. However, my family and I made use of the discount coupon for entrance fees from the Hertz car rental discount booklet.The Museum/Attraction: when we entered, we were immediately greeted by a large hall where there?s a circular cone of Hello Kitty toys, a photo-taking stop with the entire Hello Kitty family and Hello Kitty?s house where she?s standing at the balcony welcoming you and beckoning you to enter the door into the various exhibition halls. There are 3 levels with the exhibition halls on the first and second level, the gift shop on the first level, the Hello Kitty Caf챕 on the second level and the 3D theatre and an outdoor gallery on the third level. To cover everything, including a meal at the Hello Kitty Caf챕, would easily take about 2-3 hours. In the true sense, this Hello Kitty Museum is a museum ? there are exhibits of anything related to the adorable Hello Kitty. There are several themed exhibition halls on the first and second level e.g. History Hall, Art Education Hall, Music Education Hall, World Gallery Hall, Hello Kitty Room, Constellation Education Hall, amongst others.So we took plenty of photographs and selfies. I particularly like the exhibit of Hello Kitty represented by 26 countries (I found my own country) as well as the huge room containing the huge Hello Kitty bed where one of my children got the Hello Kitty toy snatched away by a toddler.At the Hello Kitty Caf챕 ? with Hello Kitty ribbon windows, Hello Kitty-themed sofas and Hello Kitty engraved tables ? you have to try the Hello Kitty Waffle Set, green tea latte, coffee or  hot chocolate (the 3 hot drinks have a profile of Hello Kitty on the surface), Hello Kitty Strawberry Cake and Cheesecake. Really yummy stuff!Whether you are a fan or not of Hello Kitty, I think this Museum is a fun attraction to visit and be acquainted with Hello Kitty. However, be prepared to ?share? the premises with many joyful and lively children and teenagers. But if you are not a fan and if you have limited time in Jeju, then I suppose you could spend that 2-3 hours elsewhere.

There are sign posts to mark the start and end of the 100 metres stretch of the Mysterious Road.  Pretty fun to play   magic   with family and friends. Put your car to neutral gear, release your foot off the accelerator and notice the car moving   uphill   on the road.  Recreate the same effect with a bottle or ball rolling uphill.  The Mysterious Road is actually a gravity hill i.e. a place where a slight downhill slope appears to be an uphill slope due to higher surroundings, creating the natural illusion that water flows uphill or that a car left out of gear rolls uphill.  Worth a fun stop if you self-drive!

There are several trails to various peaks of Hallasan. Travelling with family and limited time, we only hiked one of the shorter trails i.e. Eorimok. The 1.3 km trail begins where the car park is. From the car park, it is only a 300 meter hike uphill and you are at the top (the lower peak). Being December, there is already snow (or frost?) at the peak. Magical... Oh, and we took a public bus from Jeju bus terminal which costs us less than KRW 2,000 per person, and the park entrance is free. You only pay for parking if you drive there

There are several beautiful beaches on Udo, but we preferred the  popcorn  beach above the others. Cristal clear water and white popcorn like beach sand. you can rent snorkel gear from the cafes near the beach. We went there after watching the sunrise from sunrise peak. Ferry was W35000 for a return including our car. Do take your own snacks and drinks.

There are outdoor and indoor exhibits of glass sculptures and trinkets. There's a princessy area with giant diamond rings, a Cinderella glass carriage, showcase of glass slippers, etc. The girls liked this place. The adults found it boring. And overall, the place feels dated. Go only if you have young girls who might like the pretty glass exhibits.

There are a lot of negative reviews basically saying this waterfall is just average. It may not have that 'wow' factor but one should not visit if they are expecting the niagra falls. The one valid complaint are the stairs, slightly steep, and the rocks that need to be traversed to get closer to the falls. One has to be careful when hopping and stepping from rock to rock. Also, it can be a bit crowded with picture taking tourists.I found Jeongbang to be a modest waterfall, but nonetheless very charming. Great pictures can be taken on approach and up close, right next to the pool where you can feel the freshwater spray. Turn your back to the waterfall and a nice ocean view greets you, with two small mountain isles off in the distance. For the more adventurous, there are rocks of all sorts to be found closer to the sea. Most visitors snap a few pics and leave, but hanging out by the sea for a spell was also quite enjoyable.  While the rocks won't be confused with the rainbow, it was fun to pick out unique looking rocks from the saltwater, but watch out for the waves!

There are a few waterfalls in Jeju but Jeongbang waterfall stands out as it is the only waterfall in which the water falls directly into the ocean. The rest of the waterfalls are within ponds. An entrance fee of 2k won is needed. Walk down straight ahead and you can see Ahjumahs selling raw seafood. You can buy and eat it on the spot. The rocks around/near the bottom of the waterfall made it hard to walk. Walk carefully and you are good to go. I nearly fell into the water due to the slippery rocks. Otherwise, its a great experience.

The whole way from the car park to the falls itself was scenic. At the start was a pond with mandarin ducks and a bridge. There were various representative statues of Jeju. There were also souvenir shops if you want to buy some snacks or souvenirs. I liked the different types of trees grown, even though it is not autumn, the maple trees still looked very pretty. All along the way is a river, you go to the falls on one side and you can return on the other side of the river. There were plenty of explanation signs on the falls, the mottled eels and the rock face etc. The falls themselves don?t look very impressive but I still like the whole place. On the way back there is a nice flower display and large sculpture as well a stone auditorium.

The well-landscape beautiful environment surrounding the entrance to the   Manjanggul Lava Tube   enticed us into the cave which can be described as a hole in the ground.  As we descended the steps, we realized it was quite dark and the ground was not level.  Walking has to be slow otherwise we may slip and fall on the damp and watery walkway.  We also have to be careful that we will not be drenched by the dripping waters from the top of the cave.There were two or three highlights of the walk, one is a giant-shaped lingzhi (or mushroom) and the other is at the apparent end of the 'tube', two intertwined stalagmites growing to a hole at the top.The good thing about the cave is the cool temperate and although we were sweating from the walk, we liked it. So for those who fear the cold, take a sweater and also a cap!

The waterfall is not so large when we came, so we can walk up near to it to take some pictures. It is only a short walk down from the entrance, but be careful when walking on the stones as it can be very slippery and very crowded at times. The falls itself is very unique as it flows straight to the ocean and it cost only 2000 won to enter.

The walk in the cave is about 1km, which is pretty long. Please be careful as the cave is long, dark and slippery. In fact I think I spent more time looking on the ground than at the actual cave walls. But safety always comes first, and you can always stop at certain junctures to take a good look at the walls/ceilings.Nonetheless, the lava shelves and cave features were a wonderful sight to behold, especially for someone who appreciates geography/geology like me :) I have went to this attraction twice, and both times I have found the visit worthwhile.

The volcano is an impressive sight from the car-park. Get ready for the steps up 180 metres to the top. Be prepared to climb, climb, climb!As you ascend, the view is the best reward, and from the top you have a commanding panorama.Time it at sunrise or at sunset if you can - we went at sunset: it was remarkable and very moving to see the sun disappear behind the mountains.

The visit to the lava tube is interesting, but the way leading there is not good, and might definitely be dangerous under certain weather circunstances. Lightning is precarious and there are only few explanatory boards. definitely not adequate for people with walking restrictions of any kind

the view of the waterfall is great! however, many will get closer to the waterfall by walking through the very rocky area from the stairway. kids and elderly need to be careful and also to secure your belongings, if things were to drop into the rocks, may be hard to retrieve. ensure you wear proper footwear!

The trails to the sight were well marked and easy to walk. There is no entrance fee and the view at the end is spectacular. It?s totally worthwhile. Be wary of the elderly gentlemen at the car park collecting a parking fee of 2000Won, it?s not legit because the sign at the carpark says it?s free parking. I wonder why the local authorities have not acted on this.

The three days of touring were really excellent. We saw so much, way more than we could have achieved if we just hired a car and drove ourselves. June was a very friendly and knowledgeable guide, and she continued to maintain a flexible approach throughout the tour, adjusting itineraries according to how we felt and how our kids were doing. She also chose some great lunch restaurants for us, based on our tastes, and we really enjoyed those lunch experiences in Korean restaurants with her.

The teddy bear museum is exactly what it's title states.  It's teddy bears in every shape and size.  The first area has historical teddy bears, dating back as far as the turn of the century (1900's).  The second section is works of art redone with teddy bears and finally, there is an outdoor exhibit including a 9 meter tall teddy bear that makes a showing every hour on the hour.  Young kids that like teddy bears and such will have a great time visiting here.  My daughter adored everything.  It is a little pricey, but if you rent a car to get around they often give you a book with coupons for the various attractions on the island or you can book in advance online at a discount price.

The tea museum is located on the western side of the island and represents the showpiece of the O'Sulloc tea   empire   in South Korea.  There are a number of O'Sulloc tea cafes all over South Korea which specialize in green tea and also sell sweets as well.  There is a large parking area to accommodate a number of cars and visitors.The tea museum consisted of four   features   from what I could surmise.  First you get a decent view of the western part of the island by walking up the stairs to the roof of the museum itself.  The views aren't that interesting but you do get a good view of the surrounding area.  Second the museum itself describes the tea growing/making/serving process.  Third the cafe/gift shop inside seems to attract the most number of visitors.  You can buy teas and other desserts like you would at any other O'Sulloc cafes.  However it does sell many other items - various teas and more.  Finally another attraction is the tea plantation itself.  O'Sulloc seemingly has a small portion of their plantation on-site that you can walk through (note there may be snakes in the plantation) to get a sense of how the green tea leaves are grown.There is also an Innisfree store right next to the tea museum but we did not visit it.The tea museum is worth a trip though I wouldn't go out of the way to visit it as you can always partake in O'Sulloc teas in various locations in South Korea.

The taxi driver showed me this while I was headed to Love Land (nearby).  He put the car in neutral near the convenience store area, and even though it slopes downward, the car will roll backward.  It was cool, free, and quick.  I would not divert from an itinerary to experience this, however if you want a free thrill, check it out.
The sight was really intersting - the car really moves up the hill. Though, the place was a bit crowded.

The Seongsan Sunrise Peak is a crater with views from the overlook at the top edge of the crater, and a paved stairway/walkway up to the crater's edge.  A ticket is required to hike up the hundreds of steps to the overlook on the ridge of the crater, but if you are up to it, the view from the top is wonderful.  The crater is accessible from a causeway connected to the main island, but is itself surrounded by water everywhere except along the causeway, which adds to the view of the clear water below.  Parking is available at the crater, along with rest rooms at numerous places near the parking lot and shops, and one more restroom on the path, near where the uphill and downhill paths cross.  I always recommend carrying some toilet paper and hand towelettes in case they restrooms don't have them.The women abalone divers perform a couple of times in the afternoon on most days, so that might help determine your schedule.  Also, the smog was fairly thick the day we were there, so it limited a lot of the view of the island from the top of the crater.  The view nearby was still beautiful.  On a side note, we visited on a tour from a cruise ship.  There are 2 cruise ports on the island, one in the south port and one in the north port.  Where you port could determine your itinerary since various and impressive sights are available close to either town/port.The island has so much to offer ? large lava tunnel caves, waterfalls, craters, mountains, cliffs, black sand beaches, incredible fresh seafood, and more but they are spread throughout the island, so it is  impossible to see all of them in one area or in a short amount of time.  Also, some of the attractions are restricted, so they might require group access, or have other requirements to enter.  This attraction had a ticket kiosk near the entrance, so it didn't look like it had any restrictions for individuals to either enter or buy tickets.  We concentrated on the east end of the island during our visit and found it to be similar to Hawaii in many ways other than the temperature, which was quite a bit cooler than Hawaii during our visit at the end of March (55 deg F was our high temp).  Even this crater reminded us of Diamond Head, in Honolulu.

The Seongeup Folk Village is huge.  The main entrance has a big car park and a side entrance where you can drive your car in.  Besides the car park, there are many restaurants, two public toilets and a few shops.From the main entrance, you can take a stroll and check out some of the conserved buildings which are open to public.  Information is available in English and you can learn about the earlier settlers and buildings of Jeju Island.  There are also some shops and restaurants inside the folk village.You can easily spend 1-2 hours inside the village and having lunch either in the restaurants inside or besides the car park.  We had delicious black pork bbq at Nammun restaurant (787 2432) located in the area besides the car park.Tip:There are other entrances to the village as well.  I was at one of these prior to finding the main entrance, and there are sales people trying to get us to into houses outside the gate and market horse oil cream and other products.  Avoid these.  While I can't verify whether the products are authentic, it definitely felt like a scam.  Seemed that some reviewers thought this is part of the folk village.

The route of the tunnel is 1km one way, and then the same way back.  Its an interesting environment - dark and very cool.  Its quite interesting to see how the lava flow carved this tunnel and the size of it.  Its definitely something that is memorable and unusual.

The rock itself isn't very impressive. Yes, it looks like a dragon and you can take pictures but that isn't the only thing you can do there. If you go down the steps and cross a quite rocky and unstable path (be careful), there are some fishermen who sell fresh seafood like octopus, oysters, and sea cucumber. You can eat them fresh and raw. Food adventurers will definitely love the place. There's a stall near the toilets where they grill the catch too.

The road was called mysterious road as it seem to be a up slope but your vehicle can move slowly up like going down slope. The area is less crowded at around 7-9am until the tour bus came, where many people actually went down to crowd around this road. The tour bus would stop at the start of the slope and off its Engine and slowly moved up to the end and turn into the car park where the tourists would come down and see cars moving up. Some of them would pour water to show that the water went up instead of down. It is quite mind boggling. But actual fact that this road is due to the surrounding which makes you have the perception thinking it is a up slope but actually it is down.Way to get there is by Car or Bus. It is close to Jeju LoveLand and it is down the same road, so it is not too difficult to find.

The place was filled with cars, buses and people at about 10.30am when we were there but we had no difficulty finding a parking lot. We were too lazy to wake up early to watch the sunrise which should be spectacular. Signs were well posted as to the route to climb up. It was a tiring climb but we were rewarded with spectacular view of the surrounding. After getting down from the peak, we headed towards the shore where Haenyo woman divers sell their catch of the day. To get there, it was another flight of stairs up and down but again it was an experience to be near the shore and watching people eating raw stuff.

The place is good only for families with little children.Kids will be excited about the fact that a  car(or bottle) seems to go up on downhill. However, for adults? Not really...If u have plenty of time to spend on the road.

The period I went was very windy, the surrounding was very refreshing with patches of green. Very relaxing, peaceful  and is a good place for photography. A typical k-drama filming location for kfans to visit! Once you reach the highest point, you will see endless of   green    and can even spot mountains that is far away. You can actually relax and enjoy this view by sitting at this cute wooden swing. Very nice place which you probably won't want to miss it.However, to visit this place, you need an entrance fee of  6,000won, But if you booked a experience tour driver with your own group of friends, he can help you bargain it to a even cheaper price which is like 3,000won per person! So, afterall, it was pretty worth it for both the price and this exquisite experience! Recommended to rent a car there, inaccessible by public transport!

The Park is quite a distance away from other major sights but it is different in that the star attraction are those   grandfather stone sculptures  .Be prepared for lots of walking on easy trails.  There are small pebbles everywhere so do watch the kids and carefully navigate those wheelchairs and baby strollers.The underground museum near next to the water reservoir/water sculpture is definitely for those interested in geology.  It is a good place to take a break and use the restrooms as there is another set of lavatories near the car park.

The Mysterious road is really mysterious to me! As my friend and I booked a taxi for the day, we still had time on our hands before the day ends, so the taxi driver took us to this road and off his engine. Next thing we know, the car was moving on its on up the slope. Talk about creepy. Can't know what scientific explanation there could be behind this. If you are travelling by car and will pass by here, by all means, experience the wonder.

The Mysterious Road is one where the road appears to go uphill, but it's actually downhill.  So cars go there, turn off their motors and   coast uphill.    It's actually more fun to watch the faces of the tourists than to watch the vehicles.  My advice: take a long lens, and quietly record the looks of awe.  Makes for some great shots.

The most common way to get to Udo is by ferry. Just a reminder to bring your passport to get the ferry tickets. You may take your car on the ferry but I think it is unnecessary. There are a lot of tourists heading to Udo every day, you can rent a small car, electronic bikes or just bikes to get around the island. Our family went around, took some photos, ate peanut ice cream and ate more peanut ice cream. You can take really nice photos here but to be honest there is not really too much to do.

The main attraction is just a short walk from the car park. Tickets can be bought from a machine so you don?t have to queue. The walk takes one through lovely art structures like dolphins, boats and conch shell. There were canola flowers just before the entrance of the walkway. It has to be the right season or you will not see them. The cliffs themselves are amazing. They look like sculptures done by the hand of an artist. A row was cube like, another was like honeycomb. At the other end were corrugated pillars. Be careful not to sit on the parapets as the wind is super strong and there are large crowds, you may fall to your death if you are not careful. Hold tight to your umbrella or headwear. Best not to use any. Young children and old folks will be able to handle this attraction, the walkway is constructed well and not hard to climb up or down. It is also very short. Good view of the ocean and pines.

The Ma Park was one of the best theme parks I've ever been to.  We started off with horse riding, which was led by a friendly staff along a route for about 15 minutes.  I was surprised that he spoke English quite well!  We then headed for the go karts.  The venue was very spacious and the karts were very easy to handle.  I had a lot of fun.  After that, we watched the spectacular show which was performed by around 50 elite Mongolian riders.  Before the show started, we were able to feed the horses with carrots, sold at 1000 korean won each.  I had a blast at the Ma Park and I strongly recommend families to visit.

The longest lava tunnel in the world and designated as a natural monument.  Plan to spend a couple of hours here and wear study shoes with traction. Also bring a flashlight.  Walking in and out, over a mile distance.  Some light provided in the interior of the cave, but fairly dim.  The floor of the cave is rippled, uneven, sharp and unpaved, with occasional stepping stones placed in areas.  May cause injury, if you stumble, so you need to walk carefully the entire way in and out of the cave.  The entrance of  the cave requires you to walk down about 3 flights of stairs, which you will have to climb up to exit the cave.  Not reccommended for elderly, frail people and young children.  See some different lava formation along the way.

The lava cave is like a small adventure if you are keen at exploring. Bring a torchlight or make sure you have one installed in your handphone as the cave floor is uneven and slippery. Wear good shoes and a warm jacket with hoodie or wear a cap as water occasionally drips from the top. There is a short trek up a flight of stairs to reach the cave entrance. Lockers available near toilets. Set aside one and a half hours to finish the cave and return as it is slippery at certain sections. Wear good shoes and walk slowly and carefully. I was apalled at how some kids manage to walk pretty fast without their parents holding on to them. In summary, I do not find this cave spectecular, not much for photography too. Just a straight tunnel like structure. We were tired out by the time we went to the cave as we climbed seongsan ilchubong in the morning. Not recommended to combine the cave with other trekking activities in a day. Imo, I find the cave interesting but not a must visit.

The lack of literature on the Seongeup Folk village was compensated by the cheerful caretaker who gave informative, colourful and refreshing description of their well preserved ancient village.The village revealed a period of time when peace and security were prevailing, and privacy was highly respected. No one would enter the village when the two horizontal portable poles placed across the main entrance were not removed.Visitors would learn about the social structure of the days gone by, when men were out-numbered by women, when men stayed home and were pampered, while the women became the   work-horses   of the family.  Apart from becoming skilled divers, many womenfolk had to travel long distance daily, carrying heavy loads of water supply or agricultural products back to their homes.One would be surprised to learn that rudimentary recycling system was already being practiced. The caretaker must be congratulated for so cleverly circumvented the description the   grand father   stone status, which was in the shape of a male organ.  She described the statue as a god that offered protection against the demons, and promoted fertility for the living.
The kids enjoyed this place, lots for them to see and do.? Although, for smaller children some exhibits are a bit gruesome and scary. The shrunken heads were a fascination for them.

The journey up from the car park to the peak took 20mins.  A bit strenuous for some people and the path near the car park is not even ground. Advise to bring torch lights, check for the sunrise time and cater more time to get to the peak. Absolutely worth the time to catch the sunrise.

The Jeju Fire Festival (now renamed the Field Burning festival) takes place every year and is a huge celebration, with music, dance, enormous quantities of food from many different places. It is on The last evening that the Oreum (hill) is set fire to.Allow plenty of time to get in and park (shuttle buses from Jeju city are probably a better idea, as it can also take an hour or more to get out with your car afterwards.

The island is beautiful but difficult to get around with out renting a motorbike. However, motorbike only fits two people and you need an international driver's permit. The wind was too strong to walk around or bike in. There were a total of 3 of us that went and it would have been worth it to drive the car over from Jeju island because it cost the same as a tourist bus for all three of us.Other than figuring out transportation, it's a beautiful island to chill at and enjoy nature.

The history facts in this memorial hall recalled me of the one in Oswiecim, Poland... This memorial hall will help you to understand Jeju people's local history. Whenever I visit war related museum or places, we should stop fighting for nothing but losing the precious lives. I was even cried when I read 2 young men who could not enter the military school due to the wrong record of this tragic incident. I read all of explanation in Korean and English. I skipped some clips but I tried to watch 2 or 3 min's clips. Very well prepared in English and Korean. One of best museum. It is FREE. Only I concerned, there is no chairs to take a rest from time to time. And there was a decent with 15ish people, her voice was too much loud to make big echo in the hall area! I think they have to pay attention with other visitors who look into all scripts! I was a bit mad because she was too passionate to proceed her job. I think you do not need a docent because all of exhibits are perfectly translated in English. There are many heart breaking stories, but when I entered into the cave Darangshi(?), I could keep saying   oh my god..   I feel very sorry for all deceased, and their family members who survived at the same time witnesses. I strongly recommend this museum if you are interested local history, and history buff. It is a must. In fact, there is no restaurant, there is a coffee shop only. If you rent a car, within 10 min's drive, there are some. The bus #343, or #344 go to 4.3 Peace Park. From this park, Jeju Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest is 5 min's drive away, and 20 min's walk on foot. This Forest is wonderful. I recommend to combine these 2 places to visit at once. History and Nature are very good combination! The last stop of 343 &344 is this forest.

The hike was an easy one with stairs. Less than one hour slow pace hiking up. My brother brought his baby as well in baby carrier. There are a lot of souvenir shops nearby. In my experience, the souvenir sold there is much cheaper than the one in Jeju City.

The hike id quite steep, but only takes about 25 minutes if you take a few breaks. Entrance is 占2,000. The path is all wooden and carved rock stairs. It's a great view! We came here right before Chuseok and stayed on the beach across from Seongsan. We wanted to watch the sunrise over the cone, but the sun was behind the cone from where we were. Make sure you hike the mountain or go to the park to watch the sunrise!
The highlight of this place is the lone rock, where there is a lookout near the car park. Go past the lookout to see a different aspect of the rock. We were glad we did that.

The highlight of my trip to Jeju was visiting Udo, which is small enough to be traversed by bike in a matter of hours. My girlfriend and I were glad to chose the pedal-bikes over the motorbikes and car tours because, with all the different little coffee shops and sites to explore, you'll want to take your time. While you may not find much in the way of   impressive historical sites   compared to other places in Korea or the rest of Asia, this is a beautiful place if you're just looking to relax, meandering the coast with friends or a loved one, and enjoying some local treats. It's also very scenic, so super easy to capture scenic photos. The people were also super-friendly in helping you get around, even despite the language barrier. I'd love to return again.

The guard told me I should've called to the office before heading for there. The snow made cars are stuck in the road. I could clearly see with my bare eyes. Even if today's weather was so perfect and wonderful, it is a forest under tremendously tall trees so lots of shadow made them ice. Maybe next week might be OK to visit inside but please call beforehand if it is allowed to get in. Even at the entrance, I could see beautiful scenery from a distance.

The grounds are HUGE! It felt like a nature forest walk, a geography and history field trip all rolled into one.I don't know if it's windy there all the time, but when we were there, it was freezing when the wind blew when we were in the shade.We had a tour guide who explained the various rock features and how/why people carved the stones for use in the past. But honestly, I was bored after awhile. This place had rocks/stones galore. Considering that there are so many other things to see/do in Jeju, I would give this place a miss.
The GPS lead us to a wrong car park and that's a 20mom walk to the cliff, when there's another carpark just a few minutes away from the cliff. View is aweson but very crowded in the afternoon.

The gardens were reasonably well tended and we liked the indoor themed zones spreading out in a cartwheel from the main atrium. Outside there are a series of larger themed gardens. Some better than others, but it is a South Korean take on these different countries garden styles. For example the fountains in the Italianate garden were quite impressive and it was good to stroll in the sunshine. We did like the many sculptures placed within the various indoor spaces and this has lifted our score from 'average' to 'very good'.

The food at the cafe is DELICIOUS. We ate out of convenience but would make tris a destination meal. Plus, it isn't everyday you can buy quality Korean skin care products. Loved that it connects to O'Sulloc tea farm.

The entrance fee was 2000 W per head and 1000W per car . After buying the tickets , you descend about 5-6 flights of stairs onto the base of the waterfall . There you can clammer on the rocks for better photos of the waterfall or catch the sea waves crashing upon the rocks . After which you climb back up and then one can see stalls selling iced water with ice .The stalls also sold orange juice and ice-cream. Overall expect to spend about 45!minutes here .

The entrance fee is a little pricey, but if you consider the maintence for each car, it's understandable. If you're into classic cars, this is the place to be.? The style and uniqueness of each car was awesome. Would like a few other classics in there. But they had a Bentley and a Chevvy so I'm more than happy.
address: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관

review: The driver dropped us there on a rainy evening. It was a nice experience because it makes you wonder why would the vehicle move 'upwards' after the driver has killed off the car engine. Due to communication barrier (a Korean driver), she could not explain it well to us. However, it is still interesting.

The drive there was pleasant as you passed through many scenic places. Saw some homes with unique design.As we were at the start of Mysterious Road, our taxi driver switch off the engine and let the car just roll ?up the road?. Was wondering how could this happen!!! We witness some other vehicles doing the same. Our taxi driver took a bottle of waterAnd pour it in the middle of the road, the water didn?t flow backward. A group of Chinese tourist ,were doing the same thing, the guide say it?s a scam.  But the truth is ?Optic Illusion ?Nice backdrop of mount hallasan

The coral sand beach was really nice! Not much to see or do beyond that, and another two beaches - one very crowded white sand beach, and another black sand beach that nobody seemed to care about other than for a walk. The reviews make it seem like it's some kind of paradise, we just found it crowded, full of concrete and terrain that is parted for construction, not much vegetation. There are a few lighthouses and it looks like people could venture out on the rocks by the beach if they felt like it. What saved our trip was a little place called Chocolate Castle by the Sea, a burger restaurant that had amazing burgers and a great homey feel inside. We biked the whole island in 3 hours, with stops.

The coastline along the bottom of Jeju-do, near Seogwipo is truly beautiful. Such clear blue waters and jagged, unusually shaped rocks and little rock pools everywhere - they look as though they were made for people to swim in! Oedolgae is found along this coastline, and while it is really only mildly interesting (it is just a strange-shaped rock sticking out of the water - apparently once scared off invading Mongolians), it is worth seeking out just to walk along the paths in the park near it. The rock pools along the coast line here would be perfect to swim in, in hot weather.

The cherry blomsson at its carpark in April 18 was wonderful - one long row of beautiful sakura trees.Do not expect to see much inside (basically you walk 5 min into the park and you saw crater on your side. It will not look like crater, only valley). Rather it is the 360 degree view of the horizon that counts. The air is fresh and the mood will be lifted when you can see very far into the horizon dotted with mountains. It really look like you are in Europe or NZ. Go there for sunset as there will be no shelter from the sun above your head.

The cave/ lava tube was interesting with many learning points The walk inside was about 1 km in semi darkness and wetness. Please wear the right footwear. I was using hiking boots so it was not an issue for me. If you are taking public transport bus 700 stops way too far from the cave about a walk of 3km or more...(after kimnyeong maze park, walk a further 500m) please be mentally prepared for a long, cold and uneventful walk (nothing to see along the way...maybe because it was winter). Cave was value for money though though you have to walk back 1km out of the cave from the same way you came in. Total 8km of walking if you take public transport. Take a cab or rent a car for greater convenience.
The cave is dark and cold especially nearing winter. If you are into cave exploration, then be sure to bring along a flashlight to brighten up. Be careful walking in the cave.

The bus ride from the bus terminal is near an hour and the bus stop you alight at looks like a bus stop in the middle of a highway. From the bus stop, walk 2km to Manjanggul cave. It's a very long walk and not if you are on a solo trip (my mistake as i thought there would be shops and things to see along the way!) as it can get quite scary. Cave is very dark, not well-lit, cold and vey wet. The floor and stairs/steps are very uneven with puddles of water so will suggest covered shoes. Will need a jacket or shawl as the cave gets colder as you walk further in. The lava/cave formation is amazing but I couldn't properly enjoy the sights as I have to keep watching out for puddles of water and the uneven floor to avoid tripping.Will only suggest this if you like to see lava formations, have a group of friends to go with and have transportation to bring you to and fro.

The bridge itself is a landmark of Seogwipo, which leads to a small island that offers a short 20-25 mins walk. Not the most exotic part of the city, but nice indeed. My favourite place here however are rocks on the edge of the island, which is off the track, but if you are careful while walking out to the rocks (they are pretty flat and not dangerous at all), it is the best place to relax and enjoy the sea and view.

The 5 day market is named because it opens every 5 days only. There are other 5 day markets in Jeju but this market is said to be the largest in Jeju with 1,000 over stalls. This market opens on the 17th and plus / minus 5 days before and after.Fret not if you missed the opening of this market. Because apparently the other 5 day markets are operate by the same stall owners. They rotate among the different markets and hence will be back to the same market after every 5 days.We went there on a morning and expected to spend the whole day there. But we were out in 2 hours.There are indeed many stalls in the market but many of them are carrying the same stuff. Clothings, household products, fruits and vegetables, kimchi, cooked food and of course Jeju mandarin oranges which are famous. Interestingly, pet dogs are sold alongside with fresh chickens. And ironically, there are stalls selling dog meat at the other end of the market.Same animal but different fate.We bought the famous mandarin oranges here although these are available at other places in Jeju as well. There are many similar-priced stalls selling this famous product in this market. We chose one of the varieties on display after sampling. It has a sweet aftertaste after the first tinge of sourness. The one we purchased is the 2nd most expensive type at $25,000 Won per 5 kg. There are other varieties at $30,000 Won per 5 kg and $15,000 Won per 10 kg etc.It?s a nice experience after all and I would say it?s worth a visit if you are in Jeju.

Tested on the car that we rented~N Gear and the car really move up slope~Tried it with water too, but did not see the effect~Not too sure if it cos the sky is dark~ Go at night if you rent a car~ Can reverse the car as many times as you want~

Taking ferry to the island with a car is a little bit pricy, so it's better to get and ATV and go around the island. One hour or two chill hours are enough to go around the whole island.Hey!If you are searching for something cheap but decent, then I would recommend hostel called Galaxy in Seogwipo. I was planning to stay there for one night, as I thought it's yet just another cheap hostel, but ended up staying there for 2 nights. There are some beautiful beaches and food places, so you might want to take it easy..If you want some more information on what you can find on the island, you can check out this video: http://youtu.be/X2RwSnOMgYk?list=UUYEqXBrHobdnJF591_o-vcg

Take your time and enjoy the views. After rain, the waterfall is very pretty and worth the walk from the car parking area. Vendors sell drinks and traditional snacks at various spots and there are many photo spots.

TAKE NOTE: If you are not healthy and dont usually do cardio, the step up will be absolute hell for you. The only way you can circumvent the hellish experience is if you wake up extra early and take your own sweet time to traverse to the top.We woke up at 6am after checking sunrise at 7:20am, and was living in a hotel 2 minutes away. As we want to experience the whole sunrise, we rush up the rising path. Big mistake. By the time we're halfway up, I had visions of my 42km route march in 1.5 days during my army stint, and had to take frequent rest stops on the way up.Once you reach the top, you'll see nothing but the sea in front of you and while you're tired, you're also excited to witness the sunrise.Which you COULD... if it was a cloudless morning. The clouds will ruin your day. We didn't get to see anything in the end, as it was so cloudy and drizzling a bit, but after staying for an hour after sunrise, we did get to see a few peeks of sunrays.It only cost 2000 won so well worth the price, but definitely check the weather forecast first. It feels terrible to have almost burst your heart only to see nothing but clouds. I do imagine the sunrise is heavenly if you actually get to see it though.

Take a boat is convenient from Jeju to Udo (we were driving , the boat is able to carry the car) only 30 minutes boat, then arrive at Udo. We drive along the coste road, stopped by the hill, it is a 30 mins climbing, once reach the top you can have a overview of this Island  We literally turned around the island by car. Tried sea food abalone and some shellfish. It was very good experience. We star at 11.30am boat to Udo and finished at 4pm to take boat back to Jeju main land. It can be a 3-4 hours visit.

Sunrise is at 615 am . The entrance fee is free if you arrive before 7 am . Free Car park to the viewing points a short  8-10 minutes walk away , very doable and you get one of the most memorable sunrise sights . A most do except the getting there so early in the morning is hard .

Suffering from Avascular Necrosis bilateral hip, hiking up the mountain was not only a challenge but also proof of the fact that with perseverance, one can overcome any obstacles... Would recommend people with disabilities to try hiking up Yeongsil trail (thanks to a lovely couple who took us up from the ticket office to the Yeongsil entrance) for the breathtaking views and to hike down Eorimok Trail which is easier with not so much beautiful views...as when we came down it was 6pm, there was no bus and we were stuck.. thanks to Hyun Seung, a caring park management personnel, we were able to head back to our hotel with ease. Hyun Seung not only called for us a taxi, he even waited in the cold with us for our taxi so that we wouldn?t miss it. Overall, our experience at Hallasan was amazing and complete thanks to Hyun Seung!
Stumbled on this shop while hiding from the rain. Very   girly   and cutesy style things for sale. Great place if you like to buy postcards or items with the travel location name though!

Steps down to the waterfall are well constructed and have seats along the way. It is mostly shaded on the way down if it is hot like when I went. You can see women selling abalone on the rock shore, I have tried it, because when in Rome, but I don't like the texture.There are little shops selling souvenirs, and drinks etc. There is also a tourist information point near the car park exit, and they are very helpful. You can walk to the harbour, or to the other waterfalls in the area in around 30 minutes along the seashore and there are a few gardens along the route.

Staying in Seogwipo, I was advised to take bus 780, with the first bus leaving about 6:30am or 7am & getting to Seongpanak around 7:30 or 8am. I thought about taking a taxi to get there earlier, but I found later in the day it wasn't necessary. I believe it's the same bus from Jeju City.There's a small carpark at the entrance and a little store with a few drinks and snacks on sale. Apart from the lunch hut near the summit (which only offered noodles with hot water & bottles of cold water), this was the only place to buy anything. So carry some food and water with you, enough to last 4 hours or so.It's a fairly pleasant walk. Most of the time you will be walking on ground or planks of wood, and at times there will be nothing but big rocks, although most people were walking. I think I was the only person with hiking boots.Yes it can be very steep at times but is by no means difficult, nothing more than a series of steps. Just take lots of rest breaks and you'll be fine. It should take anywhere from 2.5 to 3 hours to reach the cut-off mark (see next paragraph) then another 1 hour to the top, so as long as you leave before 9am or 10am it should be alright.Coming down can take anywhere from 2.5 to 3.5 hours in total.I thought the cut-off point was strange, having a man in an office stopping people trying to reach the summit after 1pm, especially when the sun doesn't go down until about 7pm. I would've thought that was plenty of time to get up and back. That's just Korea and their over-sensitive rules...Not a lot of scenery along the way, but it's nice to enjoy being surrounded by trees for most of the way. For the most part it will be quiet, although some of the locals spoke loudly or even had their phones out playing music which I thought was weird.A lot of Koreans seem to be on a mission to get it done as quickly as possible, and they certainly have the stamina to do it, so keep in mind at times you may have to deal with people almost pushing you aside to get past.The view from the top is worth the hike. You'll be extremely lucky to see the bottom (climb Seongnam if you want a nice view), but you're here to see the crater lake, which is quite lovely to see when the cloud clears.

Stayed by Hyeopjae beach two nights, wish we stayed longer.Lovely place with a real local feeling, many caf챕s and restaurants around.Large and free car park.Don?t miss the beer battered chicken with beer by the walk down to the beach, opposite to the foot cleaning bath

Spent more time looking at the ground......., watching out for puddle of water than looking at the cave/tunnel. Do be careful if going with elderly and children as some parts are quite difficult to walk . It's quite dim and chilly inside. Nothing much to see....

spent a long day in Udo - so idyllic and relaxing.  There are endless seaside beaches, cliffs, cafes, ...  Just drive your own car there (via car ferry - costed us 32k Won) for a small car and 2 pax, or rent one of the bikes, motor tricycles (very cute), and just drive and stop anywhere (almost) you like and take photos, drink coffee, or just doing nothing and daydreaming. Excellent scenery, food- freshest seafood, burgers, ..... How nice to spend a day.

Spectacular views from the bottom, the side, the peak and everywhere else. I couldn't put down my camera. After two rainy, cloudy days at Jeju, the morning of our visit to Sunrise Peak we were blessed with blue skies.The ticket booth (2000 won for adults, 1000 for youth) listed the roundtrip time as 50 minutes, but we spent 2+ hours climbing and descending the tuff cone, followed by checking out the 1:30 p.m. Haenyo woman diver performance. (There is a second performance at 3:00 p.m.)The tuff cone at the peak is something else, and the climb itself is not that bad, especially if you take it slow. The descent is arguably just as good, with cooling breezes and more picture opportunities. One Con: It can get fairly crowded. Dozens of tour buses are parked at the base, carrying mainly Chinese tourists. It get can a bit competitive at times waiting out the best picture spots, but luckily they like taking pictures by signs. Overall it's not that bad, though it was funny watching the korean couples' responses to the crowds, with the girl posing for the picture and giving the side eye while the guy patiently crouched several feet away.But hey, it's a UNESCO heritage site and definitely worth a trip!

Sorry, guys if i am a bit skeptical for this kind of attraction.  For me, and perhaps for some others, it is just an optical illusion.  No surprise on that....lol.I watched closely the power lines running alongside the street and the top of the trees alignment you might be able to see that the street is actually going down and not up, giving an impression that the bottle is rolling upwards.... It was quite crowded when i was there, and needed to be a bit careful when people were trying to walk backwards whilst buses and cars were trying to pass by on that narrow street.  There are few food stalls as well.

some people say this road again the earth gravitation, but some said it's cause the magnet field is big at that area. if see with eyes the street look uphill but the car stop and  engine stop can forward till some point.

Solo traveling in Jeju Island is not that scary:) Koreans living nearby this tourist spot can speak English. So I am not worried about it.It was raining that day when I reach the place. Nevertheless, still can see the view at the top.The wind blowing my hair together with the greenery grasses and leaves of trees surrounding the peak.The place is accessible by public buses so I don't have difficulty in reaching this site. Though you have to walk a few distance to reach the entrance gate.There are educational boards installed for all the tourists to read and understand the history of it.It's worth visiting this place. Entrance fee is also cheap:)I visited Unesco World Heritage!

So, one might think that this is a great place to see artifacts or historic pieces, but as far as we saw, everything was a replica. To include the replica lava tube entrances. Sigh. They couldn't even be bothered to completely thatch a straw hut- they had concrete roofs with thatch done at the top and edges. They do have quite the array of carefully placed rocks and replica stone statues, but seeing as how none of it was real (the whole thing was built on the site of a landfill) there are more real things to go do on Jeju. The price is cheap. Spend it looking at the columnar basalt on the beach. At least that is real.

So we are sat in the car, put on neutral mode and the car actually moved! This is a really cool experience and it only takes a minute to do- I have seen mysterious roads on the travel channel before but this was my first time doing it- if you find yourself on Jeju island check it out!

Since Jeju is best travelled by car, the mysterious road (it's actual name) is definitely worth checking out. Putting the car on the apparent downslope in neutral gear will make the car move backwards and vice-versa...freaked us out until we discovered the optical illusion behind it. Be careful of all the other cars trying it out as well as pedestrians attempting something similar by pouring water onto the road surface.

Seongsan Ilchulbong/Sunrise Peak (＿?깆??곗쇱遊). Seongsan Ilchulbong, as with all natural formations on Jeju, was formed by hydrovolcanic eruptions about 5,000 years ago. Its volcanic cone is 600-meters wide and 90 meters tall, and its crated lined with 99 rocky spires that resemble a crown. In addition to its appearance, or rather, because of its appearance, it was name as one of the 7 wonders of nature in the world in 2011 (UNESCO Natural World Heritage). So needless to say, it would not be a surprise to see busloads of tourists at the carpark planning to make their way up to the peak.There are 2 suggested paths to reach the peak, where the view is said to be magnificent. I can?t remember which path we took, but the trail leading up to the peak was well maintained and quite manageable with proper steps to lead us along our way.However, despite there being steps, they were still steep, but at least the path was one of the most even paths that we had walked that day (e.g. no rocky paths nor muddy roads). The path uphill to Seongsan Ilchulbong comprises steps of varying steepness.For more photos and about my experience, please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/seongsan-ilchulbongsunrise-peak.html

Seongsan Ilchulbong, also known as ?Sunrise Peak?, is a UNESCO World Heritage site. The peak is 182 metres (600 ft) above sea level. It is around 30 - 40 minutes walk/hike to reach the top. Make sure you are fit enough because the weather is cold and windy in the morning. I've been there in early March recently and it was 4째c. To reach this place, you may drive by rent a car or take a bus from Seogwipo or Jeju City. The journey takes approximately an hour and half. Starbucks is just nearby the carpark to enjoy a cup of coffee.

Seongsan Ilchulbong is certainly the top scenic spot in Jeju island. It?s basically a crater formed from volcanic eruptions, so it?s definitely has geological phenomena associated on top of being scenic. We drove from Jeju city to Seongsan for about an hour. There?s ample parking spots and entry fee is only 2000 KRW. Hiking involves climbing lot of stairs and takes about an hour to the top. We had a 2 year old with us and we could easily pick her and go to the top. I recommend carrying water and small snack items for energy. View from the top is very beautiful and obviously you see the crater when you reach the top. I think it?s top 3 spots to visit in Jeju Island and definitely a must if the weather is nice. Bonus if you during sunrise or sunset!! There are coffee shops (starbucks, McDonald, Paris Baguette etc.) and some local souvenir shop at the entrance. Enjoy

Seongsan Ilchulbong - one of the main attraction in Jeju. Suitable for those who love sightseeing. Definitely worth a visit because of the view was extremely stunning. I went here in Feb, weekday..but surprisingly this place still packed with people, mostly local..but who cares..the more the merrier rite? :P

Self-Drive Holiday in Jeju:Everyone loves going on holidays and I believe a great percentage of these do so on guided tours. Guided tours are fine where convenience is concerned; hotels, meals, itineraries, transport, flights, places of interests to visit, entrance fees etc. etc. are all taken care of by the tour company. As I had discovered decades ago, despite all the conveniences of a guided tour, there are drawbacks that would put one off such tours completely; not being able to sleep-in and wake up as and when you want, having limited time to enjoy the various places of interests or enjoy your lunch while taking in the magnificent scenery from a mountain top restaurant , having to put up with other travellers who simply cannot or are not bothered to be on time, not being able to visit or enjoy other interesting places that are rarely included in tour itineraries, to list a few. Ever since my first guided tour holiday overseas, I have opted for a self-drive holiday and I am very sure there are many out there who would love to do so too,  but refrained from doing so because of a lack of information and perhaps, apprehensive about what it would entail to do a self-drive holiday in a foreign land. This guide is to help dispel those apprehensions and provide the necessary information for you to successfully make that first self-drive holiday in the Honeymoon Island of Jeju, and hopefully, many more thereafter in other destinations of your dreams.Preparation:Many experts would advise, and rightly so, that you should first read up all the necessary information on driving at the destination that you will be holidaying in. However, in my opinion, what is more important is having the self-confidence to drive in a foreign land. Sometimes, things can go wrong, road and weather conditions can change to the extent that no pre-reading or preparation can help, but, with that very important self-confidence, it will see you through. You must also have a flexible mind set and be ready to accommodate changes when necessary ? only then will you be able to thoroughly enjoy your self-drive holiday. Having said that, I must say that driving in Jeju is a walk-in-the-park, quite unlike, for example, driving through the mountain pass between Sun Moon Lake and Hualien County in Taiwan ? that is a drive I would never recommend to the feint hearted.International Driving Permit ? you will need to obtain an International Driving Permit to be able to rent a car in Jeju, and for that matter, in most other countries. It can be easily obtained at AAS and it costs only $20.00 and is valid for one year. You would also want to search for information on all the places of interests and decide on which of those to visit during your stay in Jeju. This is to help you plan and minimize travelling time. These can be had at the Korea Tourism Centre at Samsung CentreChoice of Hotel ? There are many hotels catering to different needs and budgets to choose from. The one most often asked question is the location ? to stay in Jeju-si or Seogwipo-si? My experience tells me that it makes no difference ? it is just a matter of choice. If you are arriving in Jeju late at night, then, perhaps, you may wish to stay in a hotel that is near the airport, to minimize your night driving had you decided on a hotel in Seogwipo-si. We landed in Jeju at 2000 hrs, collected our car at 2100 hrs and drove to Seogwipo-si where our hotel was situated. It was a pleasant forty-five minute drive with guidance from the GPS unit.Car Rental Company:There are many car rental companies in Jeju, but you will most likely come across only a handful if you search the internet ? Kumho, AJ Rentals (AVIS), SIXT, Donga and Jeju Rent-a-Car. Do note, though, that there are more than a dozen of competing rental companies at the airport to choose from if you prefer to shop around for the best rates and cars upon your arrival. I book mine through AJ Rentals, not only because of the brand name, but it also provided the best rates among the others on the net and it did not require me to pay in advance upon confirmation of my reservation. To rent the car, you will need to have an International Driving Permit (obtain it from AAS), your local driving license and passport. You can pay either in cash or credit card. Type of Car:The type of car you choose is totally dependent on your preference and budget ? luxury or basic. However, do consider the available boot space that will be needed to accommodate your luggage. As a guide, the boot of a KIA K3 can accommodate only three large suitcases with no space for a smaller, fourth piece. In a situation where there are four adults, the smaller, fourth suitcase will have to share estate space in the back seat with two other passengers. The cost of rental is dependent on the type of car, number of days and the period of travel. As a guide, a KIA K3 cost approximately S$60.00 per day for 5 days during the holiday season in November. The rate includes insurance, CDW and the use of a English language GPS, with collection and return at the airport. The rates of the other rental companies that I surveyed were cheaper, however, I cannot vouch for their quality nor service support. You decide at your own risk. The overall condition of the car was good. The only ?defect? was the slight steering alignment problem but it was not something that would put us in danger at any time. Maps:Do you need a map when it is very likely that you will be relying on the GPS? YES! A map is necessary for planning your routes and selecting the places of interests to visit.You can easily obtain a detailed map of Jeju Island, with all the major highways and feeder routes from your local Korean Tourism office. You can also obtain these from the car-rental companies when you collect your car in Jeju. You can use it to plan your route, estimate the travel time and locate other possible places of interests that you don?t find on the standard tourist trail. You can use this same map to write down the telephone numbers of the places of interests that you plan to visit. You will need these numbers for keying into the GPS system to guide you to your destination. I made it a point to re-confirm that the telephone numbers are current by asking the hotel staff to extract the numbers from their computer system. This proved to be very useful. Collecting Your Car At The Airport:After clearing immigration and customs, proceed to gate 5 of the arrival terminal. Opposite the gate, there is a green, covered walk-way with a sign that says ?Car Rentals?; it will lead you to a building where there are a lot of car-rental companies. If you had pre-booked your car, look for the car-rental company in the building. However, do take note that this building houses the local car rental companies. For the international brands such as Avis, Hertz and the other bigger local companies, they are housed in another location outside the airport. You will need to check with them when you are doing the booking or email them for the information. If the collection centre of the car rental company that you booked with is located outside the airport, wait for their shuttle bus at Gate 5. You will recognize their shuttle bus by their brand name boldly emblazoned on the sides of the bus. Since I booked my car through Avis, I took the ?AJ? shuttle bus to their rental office on the outskirts of the airport. The shuttle bus runs on a regular schedule. Arriving at the front of the office, you take a queue ticket. If you had made reservations, it takes just a few seconds to call up your reservation after presenting your passport, driver's licence and International Driving Permit. You will be shown the rental agreement with all the details pertaining to the type, class, number of days of rental, total costs and any other relevant information. With Avis, the GPS is included in the rental, whereas for other rental companies that I had enquired with, the GPS is charged separately. After you have signed the rental agreement, you will be shown your car. You then drive it off to the inspection building where they will go through the car with you to identify any minor damages, scratches, dents etc. They will also have you verify that the fuel tank is full and instruct you on the use of the GPS before getting you to sign off the acknowledgement form. Do ensure that the GPS is an English language version. Keep the documents safely in the glove-compartment and be sure to get the telephone number of the station that you will return the car to. You will need this number to key into the GPS system to guide you back. You then proceed on your way, presumably, to your hotel for a much needed rest after the long flight to Jeju.When returning the car, you just need to drive back to the same depot from where you had collected it. Just key the given number into the GPS. Upon arrival, follow the sign, ?Car Return? and head for an available lot. The attendant there will check the car with you and when all is in order, he hands you a form to sign after you have returned the key to him. You then take the shuttle bus that will take you to the departure hall at the airport.The use of the GPS:Different makes and models operate slightly differently from one another, however, the common function that generalizes all of them is the use of the telephone number of a particular hotel, attraction or establishment to program the location into the GPS. For example, the telephone number of our hotel, Ocean Palace Hotel, Jeju, is 064 - 7305800. To navigate to the hotel from the airport, I just had to key in the number 7305800 and simply touch the 'Navigate' button and voila, it calculates the shortest route and starts the voice navigation system in a jiffy - it's as simple as that. From then on, just follow the voice navigation to get you to your hotel. If you make a wrong turn or pass a junction where you were supposed to turn, do not panic. Just relax and drive on ? it will re-direct you back to the planned route or at times, provide you with a new course. In fact, we had a lot of fun and discovered many new places of interest by intentionally turning off to smaller but interesting-looking roads just to see what lies ahead and where it will eventually lead us to ? that is the beauty of a self-drive holiday. Driving in Jeju:Jeju has a coastal ring road of approximately 181 km, not counting the connecting highways linking the North-South-East ?West regions. The coastal scene is a sight to behold! It is left-hand driving in Jeju.To those who have never driven on the left side of the road, it takes a little getting used to, physically as well as in your mind. It gets a little more confusing when turning at traffic junctions, especially when driving through ? stopping gives you an opportunity to orientate yourself and prepare in your mind the lane to take when turning. To minimize this confusion, always try to follow a car in front of you which is turning in the same direction as you. It is also helpful to remember that when turning, the roadside kerb will always be on the right of the driver. The roads, save for the highways, are slightly narrower than the roads we are used to in Singapore.Generally, the speed limits are:30 Km / hr within 100 m of school zones50 Km / hr in town areas60 Km / hr in the outskirts of town70 Km / hr along highwaysThe speed limits change quite frequently, so it is advisable to keep a look-out for the change in speed limits. There are speed-cameras practically everywhere, usually positioned up on traffic lights, lamp-posts and in some places, hidden behind 'boxes' manned by a policeman. So, if you wish to spend your money supporting the policemen, speed on at your own risk.The local drivers can, at times, be quite reckless. Just like we have hell-drivers here, there are hell-drivers in Jeju too, but not too many. Just stay alert and always be on the look-out using your wing and rearview mirrors all the time. Except for the main areas of Jeju-si and Seogwipo-si, most of the roads around the island are quite free of traffic.  To estimate the time needed to travel any distances, take an average speed of 45 km/hr.Parking:Generally free parking along kerb-sides and paid parking in some buildings and are generally available easily. Most hotels have free parking for their guests ? do check with the hotel management that you have booked with. Petrol cost: As at Nov 2014: Krw 1750 / ltrPlanning Your Routes:Planning your routes is totally at your own whim and fancy, depending on the places of interest as well as the available time you have on the island. If you have a few days ( I would recommend a minimum of five days), perhaps you may wish to consider the following suggestion:1. Day 1 ? Arrival and check into hotel. This sample itinerary is on the assumption that your hotel is in Seogwipo. 2. Day 2 ? Explore the west scenic coastal drive (Route 1132) of Sagye, Gosan-Ilwa, Hagwi-Aewol and visit the places of interest along this route ( Mt Sangkaksan / Songkaksan / Yongmeori). There are many cafes (especially along the Coastal Cafe Road) and bbq restaurants for stops of aromatic coffee and grilled black pig meat. Explore Jeju-si city (underground shopping mall) and return via highway 1131 where the famous ?Forest Tunnel? is located. After dinner, take a drive to the Lotte World Resort for some very beautiful night scenery of the giant windmills.3. Day 3 ? Go East this time along the Pyeoson, Sehwa-Jongdal and Gimyeong ? Haengwon coastal routes. Stopover at Seongsan Ilchubong (Sunrise Peak). Have dinner in Jeju-si before doing a night drive back to Seogwipo. 4. Day 4 ? Alternative 1Drive to Seongsan Port in the north-east via the eastern coastal route and park your car there. Purchase your ferry tickets to Udo Island and spend a very interesting day there. You can tour the island by buying the hop-off-on bus tickets or for the adventurers, you can hire the quad-bikes or scooters. Alternative 2 ? visit the popular tourist spots such as the Trick-art museum, teddy bear museum, waterfalls, submarine tours, Green Tea museum, Geomun Oreum, Citrus fruit farms, mysterious road, etc etc....5. Day 5 ? Check out of hotel for catch your flight back home.Have a safe and enjoyable holiday!Telephone Numbers of Attractions For GPS:Citrus Fruit Museum - 732 2114Geomun Oreum - 7108981Joongang Underground Mall - 723 1510Jusenggeolli Cliffs - 7381521Lotte Hotel - 731 1000Alive Museum - 805 0888Trick Art Museum - 787 8774Seongeup Folk Village - 787 1179Traditional 5 day market (Jeju-si) - 7435985Seongsan Harbour (Ferry to Udo Island) - 782 5671Seongsan Ilchubong - 783 0959Cheongyejeong Waterfall - 760 6331Cheongjiyeong Waterfall - 733 1528Jeongbang Waterfall - 733 1530Teddy Bear Museum - 738 7600Jeju Folk Village - 787 4501Jeju Sea-World - 784 2333Aqua Planet Jeju - 780 0900Manjanggul Cave - 710 7903Oedolgae - 760 3033
