review: My husband, 17 month old son, and I visited the caves and had a nice time. It was different from caves I'd seen before because of the lava that formed this one. The walk is 1 km of uneven pathways in dim lighting, but there didn't seem to be a problem for any of the elderly or very young we saw. My husband carried our son on his back in a carrier. Be prepared for the cool air though. We regret not packing light jackets, so we rushed actually rushed through to avoid our son getting sick. We would have loved to examine the structures more. Nice experience overall!

My husband loves hiking and the great outdoors. Me? Not so much, but when he told me about the opportunity to climb a very old volcano in a day, I couldn't say no. We chose to do the Gwaneusma trail (8.7kms one way) which is considered steeper of the 2 trails (that reach the summit). I was initially worried that I wouldn't make it to the top because of my poor fitness level, but we did it with zero meltdowns from me. For those who are concerned about the difficulty, ask yourself if you can climb stairs for about 2-3 hours continuously. It was definitely a challenge but I've come to love the mindfulness that comes with hiking. Although, my muscles screamed on the way up, I found it easier to climb up than climb down. The reason for this was because a lot of the path is lined with uneven rocks, so you have to have pretty strong ankles and good foot placement. I managed to roll my ankle 2kms into the descent. Fortunately, I could still walk on it (just!) and we made the very slow climb down. We watched as many people just seemed to fly past with their walking sticks and strong ankles (I'm so jealous!). Moral of the story is, it's a wonderful hike, but be careful!!

My husband had a great time switching to neutral gear and switching off the car engine... haha,,,we went back and forth 3x before he had enough fun.. that was after i said i think we should GOOOO... we tried with empty bottles and pouring water.. but it didn't work.. I think the bottles need to be filled before it can roll upwards...If ur in a tour bus it's probably no fun.. but when u are the driver of the car and experiencing phenomena, it is indeed great fun!!! we made the car roll backwards btw >.<

My husband and I took our elderly parents to Jeju for a holiday and we decided to visit the falls. When we arrived, we realised that there were a lot of steps to be taken to reach to the bottom and there was no pathway at the bottom to walk to the falls. Basically you have to hike through the boulders to get to the falls. Clearly, our parents wouldn't be able to visit the falls.So, we just settled for viewing the falls from the car park level, just past the ticket office. The staff was so angry with us and adamant that we pay the entrance fees although we were just viewing the falls 5 steps past the ticket office. They stood right next to us and kept trying to push us back out even after we explained our situation to them. I found that absolutely ridiculous. They could clearly see for themselves that our parents were elderly and required some assistance just walking on flat road! Walking down those steps and hiking those boulders were completely out of the question.How appalling! No words can describe how utterly disgusted we felt at the attitude of the park staff.

My husband and I made the mistake of 1. Going there at 11am instead of bright and early 2. Not driving all the way up to the entrance of the trail. There are in total 4 trails and we took the one that was located south west of the island. We had to hike 2.5km from the car to the entrance before we even begin the trail. The hike is tiring and if you are doing it leisurely like I was, I will suggest good hiking shoes, hiking sticks and lots of water. We did not reach the crater and turned back after reaching the rocks. The view was still wonderful and the weather was great but I do not encourage beginners like me to go all the way. Do what you can and enjoy the view. Its better that way.

My husband and I consider ourselves pretty fit people, we regularly run and ski seasonally but we were impressed at the older Korean folks who visited the same track we did!We visited the Eorimok Trail which was advertised as a 3 hour walk one way. This time estimate is definitely accurate especially if it's consistent walking (which we did with very little breaks) if you take a 10 min breaks every so often, it would take you longer. Definitely allocate a full day for this walk and start early in winter as day time is shorter and sun sets early. We started around 10am and made it down by 4.30pm with about an 30-45 min break at the top of the trail. Remember to bring your rubbish down with you, there are no bins at the top!This trail is definitely not pram or wheelchair friendly. If you have had any leg or hip surgery recently I would also not recommend. Even though this is an 'easier' trail the walkway access is not well paved, there are large rocks and very uneven surfaces much of the way up the trail. Near the end of the day, my husband and I witnessed at least half a dozen people needing assistance down the mountain on their 'conveyor belt pulley' which was supposed to only be used for stock to be transported up and down the mountain, but in these cases of emergency some elderly and struggling walkers were transported two at a time, down the mountain. I also witnessed an old man cramping up on his way down, but lucky he was with a walking group, so they managed to organise for him to go down safely.Like many reviews say, there are consistent reminders around noon for walkers to start making their way down the mountain for your safety.This walk was beautiful and we definitely will be back to attempt another trail of this mountain! We were lucky with the weather and there was no cloud cover when we went up, but got really windy when we descended the mountain.If you are driving to Eorimok trail by rental car and are using their rental gps, the telephone number for Eorimok trail for input into the gps is: 7139950 or 7139953, definitely go early if you can, otherwise like us we arrived around 10am and had to park at the trail driveway entrance and hiked up to the full car park :)

My friends and I visited this museum in Jeju as our ode to one of our fave korean dram Goong. So we looked for the bears used in the drama like Alfred and the rest of the bears featured in the drama and we were quite excited seeing them in the flesh although a bit disappointed as it was not for sale.The museum features also life sized bears, bears resembling famous celebrities like michael jordan, elvis presley, the beatles,superman or bear?,old bears like old winnie the pooh, bears in hanboks, drewsed like emperors in  joseon dynasty,astronauts,a vampirebear, a Ronin bear, a Leonardo da  Vinci bear,A bear in LV get up,paddington bear,care bears,polar bears,there were bears in the outside depicting picnic, inside a telephone booth,fishing and even a bear taking a leak....one will enjoy if you are a bear lover. they also have a souvenir shop to buy of course different kinds of bears

My friends and I pirposely went to this theme park as we are fans of the Bae Yong Jun drama- The Legend, when we planned this trip, we asked the tour agency to include this on our itinerary. The facade was like a fortress from the Joseon dynasty except for the cars in the parking lot, the ticket booth and te posters saying this place was the location for the drama    The Legend   with a big picture of BYJ. We feel like we travelled back in time, the entrance is the main village with the bridge and man-made lake, the houses are surreal as you can see inside its like 3D not only the facade of the house then as you turn right you will see the village for common people , its more hanok styles, there is a market place with plastic meats, beefs but lloked real and the center of the village has a big traditional bar , it has second fllor where you can go up and see the view of the rest of the village, there were chairs and tables with some traditional glasses and wine bottles where you can do some photoshoots, there were tradional rickshaw downstairs, and a well with water, then there's a big gambling house with tables, some traditional games, with a big wheel with numbers you can bet on it, then a high ranking official house where you can go inside, there were furnitures, a fire place, there's living room, bed rooms and a TV where the drama is being shown, they really used this for the drama, thenat the center if the whole theme park was the big palace, as there were big gates leading to the palace with the whole field with cobbled stones, the palace is just so surral, you can enter it, you can see receiving rooms for the royalties, the emperor's chair, the rooms for the royalties with huge bed, books made of bamboo so it looked like window blinds, then there' s a roomfilled with hanboks where you can wear them and take pictures with it, there were mannequins of the characters in the drama, there's a dungeon too where they filmed the slaves or criminals being? punished, there were other rooms as well like the dining room with huge and long dining table, ere's a garden too with waterfalls, whoa! its really like the whole Joseon dynasty vibe! We took a lot of time taking pictures of the whole place with every nook and cranny of this place, its really a place for those who are fans of the drama or BYJ or even if you are curious how they live during those times, its like we time travelled back to those kings, emperors, slaves, scholars. the entrance fee to the park is USD10 and you can stay as long as you like. We used a private car courtesy of our tour guide but its quite far from the city as I remember we travelled for at least an hour from our hotel Shilla,but its worth it.

My friends and I drove up to the visitor centre (attitude of 950 meters on the mountain) and started the hike at 5.30am on the Seongpanak Trail. It was really cold so early in the morning. The trail was clearly marked out and easy to follow. It got tiring and cold really easily so it is best if you travel as a group to motivate each other. The trail is made up of sections of large stones, forest ground and wooden blocks. Some parts are steep so hikers must practise caution especially during the descent.There are two toilet points along the trail but I heard from my friends that they were really gross. There is a checkpoint near the middle of the trail which hikers must pass by a certain time (was 1.30 pm for the month of May). At that checkpoint, there is a small shop selling essentials such as drinks and food.The ending part of the trail was the most scenic as there are few trees to block the views. However, it was very cold here and I was not dressed according. I am not sure if it was due to the season (end of spring) or the attitude.We reached the top of the mountain after hiking and resting for almost 6 hours. At the top (attitude of 1950 meters), many koreans had there mini picnics while I had to take a long break to recover from the monstrous hike. There is a crater lake at the top of the mountain but it seemed like it was drying up. Remember to take photos at the summit as it is really an achievement to complete the seemingly impossible hikers for urban dwellers like us.We took the same way down as we needed to get to the car. However, if you are not driving, you can try to take the Gwaneumsa Trail down as recommended by some people online. One must be careful on the way down, especially in sections which are steeper. Do not be shy to take breaks if you are really tired. We took nearly 4 hours to get down the mountain to the car from the top.

My friends and I didn't expect much when we headed out here. We thought it would be a short hike but we were in for a surprise. From the moment we got out of our car, the view of the ilchulbong was breathtaking. After a short 10-20? minute hike, we took a pause at the peak to take in the grand view in front of us. I believe this is the #1 attraction of Jeju island.

My friend and I took the 781-1 bus there from Jeju intercity terminal at 6.40am, cost 1800W. Get off at the Seongpanak stop, approx 30-40mins. We were happy to find that the walking is free and we got a good map (incl english) from the counter where you pay for parking (which we didnt need to pay for given we got the bus). It took us 4 hours (incl breaks) to get to the top. It's well sign posted and there is some food and drink at the stop before the top. I'm usually a solo female traveller and it would be totally fine to do on your own as it's so busy and we'll marked. Footwear ranged from Converse (!!!) to sneakers to full on tramping boots. We wore sneakers and were fine but if you have weak ankles, sensitive feet, or its wet then I'd wear boots. Take a wind breaker as the summit has a cold wind, otherwise casual walking gear was sufficient for us in Oct. We walked down the Gwaneumsa track which was great as there were hardly any people and much better views, it's also 1km shorter. On sat/sun/public holidays there is bus from Gwaneumsa every 50 mins (the timetable is in korean on the side of the parking lot entrance pay station booth) but as we were there mid week, we just walked 3.7km to the nearest bus stop (facing the road/with your back to the track exit, turn right on the main road and just follow the road to the main junction then turn left to the nearest bus stop). This was ok as we had already walked so far, it was only another few km, and it is all downhill, the only dodgy part is that you're walking along a road with not much of a shoulder to walk on when cars fly past. But, don't be afraid of Gwaneumsa! Bus from there to Jeju is 1200W. A long and tiring day but definitely worth it.

My friend and I loved this place. We drove in to Udo, boarding the ferry in our car (quite an experience in itself!), and only had 4 hours to explore. Jump shots at the various beaches, hiking up to the tallest part of Udo, trying Hallasan fried rice at the Pungwon restaurant, and having peanut and tangerine ice-cream at Jimmy's ice-cream were all memorable experiences. Driving around, and many a times through one-way lanes between low stone-walls that Udo is known for, was exciting as well. Udo is a must-go!

My family with two boys 10 & 12 hiked up the Yeongsil trail to Witseoreum and back down by visitor center near Eoseungsaengak trail. We made a mistake of getting dropped off at the ticketing office by Yeongsil trail and not at the entrance of the trailhead.  It added another hour to 4 hour hike. But the walk was nice nevertheless and we saw a snake and a giant snail to compensate for it.         Trails were very well maintained and clean. But be prepared for ankle twisters and knee pains. I sure wished I had my walking sticks with me. I had to drink some Hite(Korean pale beer) afterward to relieve some pain on my knees. My two boys had no problem for them being young and all.  A little one did the whole trail on sandals but I don't recommend it as there are sections of trails made up with volcanic rocks. One wrong fall and one can easily get a nasty scrape.  Oh yeah, don't forget to bring, snacks, bug repellent, bandaids, medical tapes for your toes and heels.          I enjoyed the cupnoodle at the Witsoreum.  It was only $1.50. I think coffee was $0.50 or 0.60. There are few other snacks offered at incredibly low price considering the location. They give you a plastic bag to carry all our garbage down the mountain.         One thing I really love about this place is the variety of landscapes. It felt like going to several different national parks at once.         Few things...there are no bathrooms between trailheads and Witsoreum.  Be sure to use airgun a the trailheads to blow away the ticks and other insects off your body and clothes.

My family went to Dombedon because it was given a Michelin Star.  We were very, very disappointed with this restaurant. The food was just average, except for the stir fried rice which was spicy and delicious and the service was terrible.  My mother didn?t want the pork, rather just the noodles.  However, the server forced us to purchase the pork for her and added the noodles as a side dish, inflating the cost of our dinner.  When we asked to speak to the owner about this, we found out that she was the owner and basically yelled at us.I think because this restaurant is on the corner of Black Pork Street, they get many tourists and they don?t care about the quality of the food and service knowing tourists aren?t likely to be returning.  Shame on them!!

My family was holiday in Jeju on 12 Dec 2011.  One of the tourists spots where we visited is the Mysterious road.  It really amazed us after we had seen in our own eyes and sitting in the car.  The driver took us to place near to our our hotel Ocean Suite Hotel.  He then switched off the engine of the car and of course, there is a spot where there is a sign show   start here  .  There it goes the moment he let off his brake, 5 of us including the driver were siting in the car and the car just move up the a slight steep slove (about 5 degrees) and the distance it travelled is about 50m.  After that he U turn and took us to the same spot where we can witnessed other cars, including buses and coaches also did the same thing.  What a wonderful and awesome sight I have seen.  So when you are in Jeju, please do not miss this.

My family and I visited this UNESCO World Heritage and South Korea National Monument cave on a late afternoon for 2 hours. There were not many visitors and we didn?t find any tour buses when we reached here.   Getting there & fees: Manjanggul Cave is located in the north western part of Jeju-do. To get (drive) to Manjanggul Cave, key in GPS coordinate 7834818. There is no parking fee at the huge car park. Entrance fee is 2,000 won for adults and 1,000 won for teenagers and children.Manjanggul Cave Museum: Upon climbing up the stairs from the car park, you will reach the Museum and a cafeteria/restaurant on its right. You could go in and have a look at the interesting exhibits, including how the Manjanggul Cave was formed from the volcanic activities.Manjanggul Cave: To get to the underground Cave, we followed the sign-posts ? it?s within 5 minutes? walk from the Manjanggul Cave Museum. Trek the entire 1 km stretch that?s opened to public and you will end with a colourful lit lava column - created from the dripping of lava from a hole in the ceiling ? which at about 8 meters high, is the tallest lava column on Earth. Nevertheless, there are a few things you have to take note while you are in the Cave:(1) The entrance to the Manjanggul Cave is also the exit ? there?s no exit at the end of the 1 km trail, which means you are walking 2 km return (2) Make sure you bring and wear a jacket or sweater with you because it?s freezing cold and chilly inside the cave. (3) Wear a cap or the jacket or sweater can be waterproof because you get water ocassioanlly dripping from the cave top onto you (4) The surface (floor) of the Cave is full of solidified lava flow terrain (i.e. extremely uneven surface) and water puddles, so you have to wear a pair of good walking shoes and walk carefully. Hold on to the railings of the stairs.(5) You probably don?t need a torchlight because the Cave is illuminated just enough by ground lightings. Some parts of the cave even have colourful lights shining at the dome shaped ceiling (cupola) (6) If you would like to take photographs inside the cave, you would need a tripod and switch to manual mode for long exposure (I used 4 seconds to 10 seconds exposure on my digital SLR).   There are displays at certain parts of the cave in English explaining the geology of the cave and the formation of the interesting structures (e.g. stalactites). In particular, there?s one structure ? ?Stone Turtle? ? in which the shape looks like Jeju-do Island, and which you could reach in about 30 minutes of one-way walking as it?s about 400m from the entrance. Along the Manjanggul Cave wall, we saw varied patterns of lava flow lines, some are straight while some are wavy. Really interesting! I have been to over 10 limestone caves around the world, but this is my first visit in a lava tunnel cave or lava tube cave (and Asia?s longest lava tube cave for that matter). You have to experience being transported to another world in this ?out of this world? cave for yourself ? don?t miss it!

My family and I visited this attraction on a sunny Monday mid-afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli ?? Jeongbang Falls ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Falls itinerary. ?Oedolgae? means ?Lonely Rock?. Oedolgae Rock has its origin from a volcanic eruption.Getting there & fees:  The GPS coordinate (code) for Oedolgae is 7328027.We parked our car under the trees at the large car park. Entry to the attraction is free and the only fee we paid was 1000 won to the parking attendant.The Rock/Attraction: We looked for a blue signboard with a picture of Odedolgae Rock and an arrow pointing left saying ?250m?. It?s then an easy walk of steps and path that?s abundantly shaded by the trees. So you don?t need an umbrella or a cap. After 5 minutes, we came to a large viewing platform from which this amazing and unusual 20-metre high solitary grey basalt pillar rock that juts out from the sea with a few trees growing at its top can be seen. From a certain angle, the Rock looks like a woman?s face with little hair.Compared to another 20-metre lone-standing limestone rock, Ko Tapu, at Thailand?s James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan), I find the Oedolgae rock slightly more interesting in terms of geographical origin and features. You could better appreciate the other face of this Rock as well as getting to a large poster of the popular Korean TV drama ?Dae Jang Geum? (Jewel in the Palace) by walking further onto another path, which we didn?t venture.  Despite the Oedolgae?s attractiveness and beauty as well as free admission, somehow I didn?t see busloads of tourists here. This means the attraction is not crowded. Maybe the thinking is they could spend their time at other tourist attractions where there are more things to see rather than just a solidary rock.  Nevertheless, for me, I recommend a visit to this amazing rock as part of the southern Jeju itinerary. It only takes up at most 1.5 hours.

My family and I spent about 45 minutes at this attraction on an early Monday afternoon, as our first stop of a Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliffs ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary. It is designated a Natural Monument and is part of the Global Geopark Network. Getting there & fees: When I keyed in GPS code of 7351000 and 7381521, it brought us confusingly to the Convention Centre and the car park of the Seaes Resort respectively. Thanks to the helpful staff of the Seaes resort, we followed the advice and drove past the Convention Centre and then looked out for a signage that indicated taking a right turn to a road that leads to the destination. Once there, we parked the car in the car park which charged a parking fee pf 1000 won. The entrance fee is 2000 won for adults & 1000 won for teenagers (youth) and children, and we used one of the lockers for free to keep our stuff.The Cliffs/Attraction: After paying the entrance fees, we walked past figurines of dolphins and a huge rock surrounded by the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac. We then took the pathway of wooden platform steps that brought us to the bird-eye view of the beautiful blue sea and the rocky cliffs containing the awesome columnar joints that are typically at the base of the cliff. The platform only showcases a section of the 2 km stretch of these rocky cliffs. Along the platform, there is a display in English and Korean that educate you about the origin of the rocks. It would be good if another display would be able to pictorially illustrate the geography and formation. According to the information, the columnar joints were formed from the lava flows from the Nokhajiak scoria cone from 140,000 to 250,000 years ago. During cooling of the molten lava, contraction occurred and split the basaltic rocks into polygonal columns. We saw mainly tetragonal (4 sided), pentagonal (5-sided) and hexagonal (6-sided) columns. Because the origin of the columnar joints and rocks is volcanic, these are black. Throughout the time, I stood there simply awestruck by what I saw ? it?s like a divine being had creatively sculptured these columnar joints to perfection. And why only at this 2km stretch and not at other coastal areas in Jeju since the volcanic molten lava flowed everywhere?  It?s a pity the waves that crashed onto the joints and rocks were not huge; otherwise I think it would be an even more awesome sight. There are several pointers to take note:(1) You could appreciate this attraction in less than 1 hour (including photo and selfie-taking)(2) As the attraction is outdoors, be prepared for what the weather will throw at you. Carry an umbrella or wear a cap or sunglasses or put on sunscreen on a sunny day(3) To see these rocks better, I suggest bringing along a pair of binoculars or zooming closer using your camera telephoto lens or your handphone(4) Take plenty of photographs but do not climb over or lean over too much the platform ?railings?We ranked Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff as one of the top 3 attractions in Jeju. For sure, this Nature?s awesome masterpiece is not to be missed!

My family and I liked this waterfall simply because of the coolness that sweeps away the afternoon heat. We visited this attraction on a Monday late afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary.Getting there & fees: The GPS coordinate/code for Jeongbang Waterfall is 7331530. It is located on the south central part of Jeju (Seogwipo). We parked our car for free at the car park. Entrance fee to the Waterfall is 1000 won for adults and 500 won for teenagers and children. The Waterfall/Attraction: Because the waterfall is so close to the sea, it gives the impression that the fresh water falls directly into the sea. The water actually falls 23 metres into a plunge-pool in a sheltered cove comprising of mainly black lava rocks and then flows to the sea. After the ticket booth, an approximately 5 minutes? descent on the sturdy steps of the wooden stairway took us to the bottom but still quite a distance from the waterfall. Even then, we were already ?bathed? by the cool water mist from the impact of the waterfall plunging onto the pond. We had to step on the rocks and boulders to get nearer to the base of the waterfall, and this was where we had to be very careful, very slow, very nimble and very sure-footed in negotiating the uneven rocks or boulders of different sizes and shapes as well as the slippery surface of the wet rocks. This is also where you have to wear good walking shoes and I don?t recommend slippers. Nevertheless, as more and more water mist and droplets landed onto our tired bodies as we approached closer and closer to the waterfall, we just felt refreshed and energised!  Because of the persistent mist and fine water droplets, it?s difficult to take selfies and photographs for that ?I was here at Jeongbang Waterfall? moment without these landing on your devices? lens and blurring the image. So you have to wipe off the water and be quick with the photograph taking.We spent about 30 minutes relaxing and soaking the ambience of the waterfall. During this time, we counted no less than 7 waterfall ?mini-streams? and only 20 visitors (not crowded). As the first 쩌 part of the descent path will not be walked again during the ascent, I would recommend taking photographs and selfies of the panorama during the initial stretch. In fact, the lookout point just after the ticket booth has this ?landmark? lone tree that faithfully watches over the waterfall, and you could include it to frame your photograph.If I could come again, I would do so in the cool morning with the sun shining on the waterfall. Anyway, this is one majestic waterfall that you wouldn?t want to miss!

My family and I drove to this awesome natural attraction and walked along the layered rocks and cliffs produced as a result of a volcanic eruption on a beautiful non-windy and sunny morning. Safety concerns: Yeongmeori (Dragon's Head) Coast is opened from 8 am to 6:30 pm from May to September. It will be closed when the weather changes in a way that impacts people?s safety (e.g. high tidal waves, strong winds), so it is better to call to check before going. Also a rainy day means that the rocks and coast will become slippery and you may have problems taking photographs. in any case, you definitely need a good pair of walking shoes.2 walking trails: You have to take note that there are 2 trails and entrances to Yeongmeori Coast. Both trails meet each other but are not connected due to safety issue, which means you have to pay separate entrance fees. However, I saw a white bridge is presently being constructed that links the 2 trails, but it remains unclear as to when it will be opened. Between the 2 trails ? Trail 1 and Trail 2 (described below) ? I found Trail 2 to be  safer for walking and has more spectacular sandstone rock formations and cliffs, and because of that my family and I spent about 3 hours admiring the attraction and taking photographs.  Trail 1: This trail is where the tourists go, and starts after the Hamel Castaway Memorial and the Hamel vessel. You park your car (along with the tour coaches) at a car park that?s next to a mini theme park (with the Viking amongst others). You then walk along the seaside promenade next to sandstone layered rocks along the sea, which takes about 1.5 to 3 hours return after the ticket booth (1,000 won for adults & 500 won for teenagers & children). Since certain stretches of the promenade are narrow, you have to walk carefully so as not to fall into the sea and onto the rocks.Trail 2:  This is a shorter trail that in theory should only take about 30-60 minutes return after the ticket booth. You park your car just beneath the temple. Parking is free. Cross the road and look for 3 bronze circular structures with inscriptions of ?Jeju Island Geopark?, ?Global Geopark Networks? and ?New 7 Wonders of Nature? and a green signage ?Yongmeori Coast Entrance -> 300m? From there, you just walk down the steps and follow the path which will take you past several shops. After about 10 minutes? walk, you will reach a ticket booth. After buying the tickets (1,000 won for adults & 500 won for teenagers & children), turn left and you would come to the top of a narrow and steep passageway to the coast. Take your time to carefully choose the big rocks as your steps for your descent (and then I realised what the term ?stepping stone? means). There are no handrails. Once you reached the bottom after about 6 minutes (longer when there are many people), turn around and look up at the challenging and difficult passageway and appreciate your achievement! Looking across the sea, we saw Mount Hallasan. Instead of going left, I recommend you go to the right and once through a archway or hole in a rock wall, and you will soon encounter the spectacular irregular layered and wavy sandstone cliffs that often contain ?pot-holes?. The rock formation at certain places was carved out by  a blade that cut itself into the layered rocks, creating v-shaped clefts. And when the waves crashed into the rocks, it sounds like roaring thunder ? awesome!  There?s a short cement bridge where standing on it allows you to take a superb photograph of the rock formation and the narrow stretch of turquoise-coloured sea. It is also around this same spot that you can take another superb photograph of the cliffs with Mount Sanbangsan in the background. There were 2 ladies (I didn?t think they were the famed ?Haenyeo? sea-divers) at the shoreline with 3 basins of sea animals - sea snail (sora), sea squirt (myeonggye) and sea cucumber (haesam) ? who would be happy to enable you  to experience Korean culture of eating raw seafood by the shoreline. I didn?t like to eat raw seafood so I didn?t try.Overall, my family and I think that Yeongmeori Coast is one attraction in Jeju that ranks it as among the top 3 attractions in Jeju. Don?t miss it! It will blow your mind away!

My family (including 1 years old and 4 years old kid) visited this place. The experience is very good.If you plan to stay 2 nights at Seogwipo, i suggest you to arrange to go on the 1st day itself, cause the weather is very difficult to predict.Get the help of your hotel reception to 760-6321 and confirm the opening time (might close due to high tide or bad weather)Free parking space available. Spend 3 hours there.Suggest to go for a toilet break before going thru the entrance.Bring baby carriers, cause the road is uneven. Have to be extra careful especially going with kids.There are 2 entrance. (follow the counter clock wise direction, where the entrance is situated behind the huge ship)Enjoy the scenery, watchout for the waves too.Their is a canola flower field where you can take some instagram photos too (need to pay to enter)

My comment to my wife after touring the O'Sulloc tea museum:   It's more of a fun cafe and tea shop than a museum or   plantation   for tea enthusiasts.  It's a nice stop if you're staying closer to that side of Jeju - we traveled about 15 min. by car to reach it.  Really enjoyed the green tea cake and latte and bought some fresh tea for souvenir.  However this is not a   must see   aspect of a trip to Jeju.There is also a Innisfree cosmetics shop on the site which has a lot of products; we made a few purchases there too.  Nice little add-on for the Jeju tourist.

My boyfriend and I were excited to visit the Maze Park and it really did not disappoint! The maze itself was really good and it took us an embarrassingly long time to finish, :-) This is really for people of all ages! Everybody was laughing and having such a good time that the whole atmosphere was so nice. The workers were very nice, and one man who I assume is the manager had a wonderful conversation with us while we waited for the taxi they had called for us! His English is PERFECT and he can tell you all about his interesting travels. We were lucky enough to see Mr. Dustin himself, the owner. They have loads of cats inside and outside that are well taken care of. This was one of our favorite parts of Jeju! You definitely should go here!

Must visit this place if you are in Jeju.  This is the place where you can also watch women divers performance and taking the horse ride too. If you want to catch the Sunrise at the peak, start to climb at least 30 mins before the sunrise. Please check the weather first. If you are not that fit, start to climb 1 hour before the sunrise. Take note: Stairs all the way from the bottom to the top. A lot of resting area along the way.  Alternatively, from the entrance, walk towards the ocean on the left.  You can catch the sunrise from there too if you are too lazy to climb.  The view around the mountain is fantastic.  Many eateries, shops nearby.  It will be very crowded from 9am onwards with many tour buses.  Many parking lots nearby if you are unable to get any parking at the mountain carpark.

Mt Halla is known as Korea's jewel. It is its highest peak. And well worth the trip to Jeju. We left Seagwipo very early (around 7 am) and took bus 182 (181 also goes there) to Seongpanak because we wanted to climb up to the peak. We got to the mountain around 7:45 and started the hike. The weather was super nice when we left, and we planned it that way, because we wanted to at least get some nice views of the city, and while at the summit. This is a long day of hiking, so be prepared. Bring snacks (and a trash bag, because you have to carry everything back down), and water. There are 2 checkpoints along the way that have bathrooms. The last checkpoint sells ramen for about 1500w with hot water. This is the checkpoint you have to get to before 12:30. We made it there around 11, and up to the summit before noon On the Seongpanak trail, there is also a lake with an observatory that's worth the detour.The last part of the hike up to the summit is pretty steep and rocky, so watch your footing, especially because you might be tired from walking up. Wear adequate footwear, make sure they are sturdy and comfy!Unfortunately, we didn't get that lucky with the weather as it because overcast as we were getting up there. I guess it really depends on your luck (the next day, it was super clear! Damn you Mt Halla!!) hahaha.We took the same trail down (from the summit, there is another trail, but no buses stop there. And this is where your comfy shoes are a must. The hike up was not bad, but the hike down, was torture! Our feet kept hitting the front of our hiking shoes, so we were bruised and hurt by the time the hike was done. We were also sore for the next 2 days (and we're pretty sporty, but we rarely walk for 8 hours) Overall, it's a great hike. The trail up is covered by trees, so it is cooler than it seems, but there are still some great views, especially with the fall foliage. We'd be surprised at the range of people walking the trail, old and young love to hike up this trail, and we understand why!

Mr.Jang is really helpful. From the moment we arrived at the airport, he let Mr.Lee to fetch us and dropped us in our lodging. His Starex Van is really comfy. We visited many spots and he recommended the most beautiful spots among the places we've chosen to visit. It's a hassle-free travel. We're so happy we didn't rent a car. It's a great vacation with Mr.Jang and his team.

Mr. Lee was an excellent tour guide! On time for both full day tours, patient and takes great pictures! As a solo traveler this was a wonderful experience in Jeju island mostly because of Mr. Lee. I did both East and West coast tours with him. Car is comfortable and very clean! He was very flexible with the itinerary and squeezed in his favorite waterfall in Jeju my last day! He was awesome and I highly recommend this tour to explore Jeju!

Most of the park is outdoors, and we went when it was raining, so that wasn't that good. But the place is beautiful, with trees and stones lined up. There's also a museum about volcanoes as well as statues of historical figures. Very nice place although it is only accessible by car and very difficult to get a cab.

Meet them, watch them and read about them here, at their own museum( which even has electric car charging points) Given there are so many museum to celebrate the dead and gone, this one for the living, is special with moving exhibits

Me and my family went to this place on a rainy day but it is still a good place to go. the nature in the area is very nice and during that time, it was quite windy yet cool at the same time. The only disadvantage is that this place is a bit far so you definitely need a car to get there.

Many of the paths are laid with big rocks, better to have a trekking pole (or even a pair) with you to keep your balance and to aid your walking up and downhill. It is not an easy trail but the view up on the mountain is rewarding. If lucky enough, can see sea of cloud hanging near the mountain, it's beautiful. The spring water is fresh and pure, and is a good source to refill your bottle before going downhill. It is really amazing to see the locals, many of them middle-aged, walking so fast and can carry so many food up to the mountain. At the rest point, it was a feast for the eyes to see the food they brought up for hiking - kimbap, jokbal (pork knuckle),...and many more.

Manjanggul is a must see when in Jeju. It is easy to get (near) there from the main bus terminal in Jeju City, just take bus 701. It drops at the highway at the crossroad (there is an audible announcement in English on the bus as well as written on the screen) in about an hour's time, or just under. From there you can walk (under two KM) or take a cab (about 1000 Won per person). There is also a large parking lot if you have your own car or take a taxi.The entrance fee is 2000 Won and once you have your entrance ticket you follow the crowds of people down the steep set of stairs (be careful - it can be a bit slippery) and into the cave itself. The floor of the lava tube can be difficult for some (elderly, disabled, children) as it is rather uneven and tends to be rather wet. With proper shoes one should be able to navigate the 1 kilometer tube with no issues. It isn't very lighted inside so take care and watch your step.It's a pretty cool (in every sense of the word) experience and definitely looks very different from a   normal cave   in that it is one long tube with high ceilings and lacking the traditional stalagmites/stalactites.if you have a tendency to get chilly, do take a sweater or light jacket as the temperature inside is cooler than the outside, regardless of the time of year.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the top ten lava tubes to visit that was formed about 200,000-300,000 years ago. It is one of 7 Geomunoreum lava tubes of Jeju Island and located in the North East area.The visit can be done using either bus (another 30 mins or 2.7km walk to the entrance) or car. I'd suggest to rent a car while in Jeju because it will make it super easy to get around the island. If you drive, the number you want to input into the GPS is 7107903 :-).It was really windy and cold on the day we went to the cave. We walked for about 5 minutes from the free car park to the ticket booth but the temperature inside of the cave was very comfortable.The first lava related item that we saw was the lava column cascade. It would be there on the way to entrance, to greet everyone who came to visit the Manjanggul Cave.?The entrance started with two flights of stone stairs that might get a bit slippery during the rainy or winter period. Even though you wear non-slip shoes with you, it's definitely worthwhile to hold on to the railing when going down and up the stairs.The cave was definitely not wheelchair friendly since the stony surface is always wet, rocky and covered with puddles. Water will occasionally drop from the ceiling of the cave but it didn't really bother us. We saw that some people carried an umbrella with them or wore the plastic rain poncho but since you'll be walking a lot, it would be too warm if you wear the poncho. Another suggestion is just to wear a hat/ baseball cap in summer and stick to your winter jacket in the winter time.I tried to take some photos inside but it was pretty hard because the cave was quite dark. It was a really enjoyable walk and we got to learn about how the lava stream formed the lines on the cave, stalactites and stalagmites.There were a lot of rocks around our path and we learnt later on that big and fragmented rocks fell from the ceiling during or after the formation of the lava tubes! There were a lot of lava columns as well that was formed when lava flowed from the ceiling to the floor of the lava tube.Manjanggul Cave closes on the first Wednesday of each month. Their opening hours is from 9 AM to 6 PM with last admission at 5:10 PM.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the finest lava tunnels in the world and is designated natural monument. Only 1km of the 13,422m Manjanggul Cave is open to public, be prepared for a good & non slippery shoes, walking stick (for elderly fit), raincoat and torchlight. Inside the tunnel is a little dim with light, water puddle every way and water dripping from the cave top. Lava stalactites and lava stalagmites, lava columns, lava flowstone, lava helictites, lava blisters, cave coral, benches, lava rafts, lava bridges, lava shelves, grooved lava striations, and ropy lava are well-preserved. Among them, a lava column of 7.6m is the largest known in the world. This attraction is located in Gimnyeong-ri, this place closed at 6pm, be there early as you will take approximately 1hr to 2hr to have a stroll inside the tunnels (dont forget, is to and fro). This is not a wheelchair place as it needs a lot of walking and 2 flight of stairs down to the entrance of the tunnelIt is a very good experience for children and adults to understand the natural at work.For those who driving, key in 7834818 for the location. There is free carpark outside the park which is just 5 mins away. Another attraction close by Lava Cave is Gimnyeong Maze Park.

Manjang Cave is near the northeast portion of Jeju, therefore if you are staying on the touristy south side of the island it will take over an hour to get here.The cave is part of a cave system that extends for kilometers that has been given some sort of UNESCO title (kind of like every natural sight on the island it seems). While the cave is indeed interesting, the allure of the cave stops once you descend down the stairs from the entrance and realize that you should have come more prepared.If you decide to embark to the cave, come with hiking boots or waterproof shoes and leave your Toms or Tori Burch shoes in the car because 95% of the cave is unimproved meaning walking along uneven surfaces filed with cracks and cold water puddles that may cause sprained ankles or ending up with cold and dirty feet is more than likely to occur.Also, the cave is dimly lit so unless you are Bruce Wayne or a vampire, you can't really see diddly-squat. So bring a flashlight or come hardcore prepared with a headlamp.Lastly bring a sweater or jacket because the cave is really cold. It's like being inside a commercial freezer but with cold wet feet. Not cool... I mean too cool LOL.As for the cave itself, it is impressive, but gets really repetitive and unlike the photos on the signs and pamphlets, the lighting is so bad you can't really see anything. Aside from   turtle rock   and lava stalactites, everything started to look the same. Would I return? Methinks not.The cost is 2000 won per adult, which seems to be the standard fare of most touristy spots on the island including the waterfalls and Sunrise Peak.

Manjang cave is impressive! One of our party has arthritic feet, but even she managed to navigate the uneven surfaces by taking great care. The entry/exit includes steep stairs and be aware the handrail is slippery. There are two sections with ropelike lava walkways (one worse than the other) - these are by far the most difficult and uneven terrain to walk. The lava tube itself is pretty much on plane... no significant inclines or decents. Be aware that at the end you retrace your steps to the entrance.

Manjamg cave is located on the north-east of Jeju, away from most of the hotels. In order to get to it, you will need to take a car, tour bus, or private taxi tour.The cave is massive and long, but not too interesting compared to real adventure caving. It is basically an uncomfortable walk in a cold and dark tunnel.Overall verdict: If you happen to go here on a tour, drive past, or have never been in a cave, go andcheck it out, otherwise don't waste your time.

Main target is the teddy bear in Goong drama  but just one section there..a lot of cute, handsome, pretty teddy bears are gathered in this farm..you should spend hours here as the farm is huge! easy to park your car and enjoy your fairytales day there!!
Lovely view.  However u need to clinb endless stairs, which was horrible for me as I was using a babycarrier.  Nonetheless, everyone should visit, lovely views.

Loved this island off Jeju Island!  If you're staying in the Jungmun area, this requires about an hour taxi or car ride to the port where you catch a ferry (15 minute ride) the island. Best to buy a return ticket at the ticket office (the taxi driver helped us to do this, lucky for us as you need to show your ID or passport to buy tickets!).  The sun came out for us and the island was in all its glory - blue skies and blue sea - absolutely worth the trip.  Can easily spend half to one day here. Not sure how it works with the bus options though if you hire a cabin to stay along the bus route.When you arrive at U-Do, there are various bicycles/cars that you can hire (if you bring your driving licence), however, you can easily buy a hop on hop off bus ticket.  The bus driver talks for some of the way during the bus tour but if you don't understand what's going on, it's just as easy to enjoy the view from the window.  Nature is all around.Apart from the surrounding sea and boats, you can see horses and women divers (next to their orange buoys) in the sea.   We also enjoyed a black pork burger, mandarin juice at our first stop and also a peanut ice-cream from Jimmy's.This visit was another one of the many highlights to our trip and I would love to come again!  Pre-teen kids also enjoyed the beautiful breathtaking scenery.

Lots of various beauty shops and shoppers crowded around those shops. You can buy some good Korean made health care products, and a lot of Chinese and various types of Asians. It claims to be a tax free zone, and the prices are more than reasonable. Also, the free wifi hotspots are good, as well as very clean bathrooms. Good place for shopping.

Lots of steps but there are plenty of places to rest along the way. Probably prettier to visit in Spring or Fall. It was a cold, gray and windy day, though the sun did come thru a little.  The Haenyeo, lady divers performance at 13:30 and 15:00 is very good and we enjoyed eating some of their very fresh catch! Easy to get to by public transportation but takes a long time. Easier if you have a car.

Located in Seogwipo. What makes this waterfall unique compared to the rest of waterfalls in Asia is ? this one falls directly into the ocean. The view is very dramatic and I can guarantee that you will say 'wow' the moment you see it from the distance.This waterfall is 23 meter / 75 feet high. It was written in a legend that a holy dragon lived underneath it. Due to it, it was said that the water can cure disease and bring rain during drought season.It costs KRW 10,000 to enter this area, same price as Cheonjiyeon waterfall entrance fee. The comparison that I can make between these two waterfalls is ? Cheonjiyeon has beautiful landscape compared to Jeongbang. But Jeongbang has the dramatic factor compared to relaxing, calming Cheonjiyeon waterfall.You will go through a simple, quaint little path before you reach the waterfall gate entrance. No man made sculptures or attempt to make this road appear to be more touristy. However, the pink wild flowers blooms along this little path captures my heart. If you pay very close attention, you will see spider (s) hanging in the bushes alongside the road too. And if you not scared of it, you can check it out and test your macro skill with your camera. Remember : look but don't touch!Note: There are lots of spiders in Jeju Island. They are every where.I was unable to get too close to the falls because 1) it was cold windy day 2) I easily suffocate with water mist 3) I don't have water protection cover for my camera. So, if you plan to come here, please make sure to bring water proof camera protection if you really care of your expensive camera.Ah, one more thing ? shoes. Please wear sensible, flat, good grip kind of shoes / sport shoes.

Located in Jungangro of downtown Jeju this underground shopping mall was the perfect spot to take in some local shopping due to the rain on the day we visited.  Most of the 280 shop locations were open but quite a few locations were in the process of or still had yet to open.  Most shops here sold shoes, clothing, and cosmetics.  We found several shops for children apparel and a few shops of general items and a couple of places to eat (which we tried - very good).  Of the shops there we didn't really find anything to our liking but the shopping experience was pleasant.  The shops varied in what they accepted for payment.  Most accepted Wans and several Credit Cards.  If any, tenants spoke very little English.

Located beside O'sulloc tea museum. When I told the taxi driver he seem don't know the place but when I said O'sulloc he just get it. Outside you can see green tea plant. Inside you can buy innisfree products, make your own soap here and in the corner you can design your own postcard for free with the stamp that have been provided. For me it's closed so early on 6 pm and since I been there too late, many menu already sold out and trying the Tangerine Shave Ice which is nothing special but after all it's a nice cafe.

Located at the eastern end of Jeju Island. It will be about 1hr - 1.5 hrs drive if you stay at the city centre to this stunning place. Advisable to travel early in the morning if you want to avoid the tourists. I drove from Yeha Guesthouse around 7am and arrived in Seongsan Ilchulbong about 8.10am. The area was still empty with only those coming with their cars and still lots of parking lots. However if you arrived around 10am onward, rest assured the parking space will be a challenge. The entrance fee is KW2000 per adult. If you intend to hike until to the top, please wear proper shoes as the stairs can be pretty challenging and steep on the way down. The hike will take about 50 minutes if you walk slow and steady. Can be shorter if you climb faster. During the winter season, you are lucky if you can watch the sunrise. When we were there, it was cloudy and the sun is rising behind the cloud, but still the view up there is beautiful. If you don't want to climb up to the top, you can still enjoy the beautiful scenery around the area. If the time permits, you can also catch the Jeju Woman Diver (Haenyo) in action on your way down from the Seongsan Ilchulbong performing at two timing 1.30pm and 3.00pm respectively. There is a separate trail that leads down to where the action is. I wasn't able to watch it as we are rushing to go to Udo Island.There are Starbucks & Dunkin Donut for you to stop for a cup of coffee while enjoying the views and few shops that sells souvenirs. However the price may be a bit expensive as compared to Dongmun Market.Return visit : A must...for a sunrise views!

Located at 2nd floor of hotel. Ample space, perhaps it's because there's hardly anyone playing. Limited number of types of games available. Eg 2 roulette tables, no poker of any sort? mostly baccarat and blackjack.
address: 제주 제주시 탑동로 66 라마다 프라자 제주호텔
입력주소: 제주 제주시 탑동로 66 라마다 프라자 제주호텔

review: Located 25mins from Seogwipo, at the Jungmun area, this is a dramatic stretch of coast with hexagonal rock columns. They result from the rapid cooling and contraction of lava once it has met the water of the sea.There is a viewing platform right behind the Jeju ICC (convention centre), from where to admire the coast and the formations in particular.To access the platform, park the rental car at the designated park (KRW 1000) and buy the access tickets (KRW 2000). The platform is always busy and with all the selfies going on, one struggles to look at the rock formations.

Lee Jung-Seob Art Gallery, like most government run museums in Korea, had a low display items to museum area ratio.? It is dedicated to Lee who spent the last few years of his life in Seogwipo after being raised in present-day North Korea and spending a significant part of his life in Japan.? In a three floor building it was just one room with about 20 pieces of artifacts.? Fortunately the few artifacts which consisted of postcards Lee sent his wife, his earlier sketches, letters to his children, and his palette donated by his wife were all interesting to check out.

Lava tubes are different all over - so these have their own special yet similar features. The overall experience was well worth it and I certainly recommend the visit. The trail is reasonable well developed with stairs down into the tubes. Though basically light, I thought the selected illuminations added to the features and overall feel of the caves. It is not overly spectacular in showing off the various formations and features, but it still gives a good view of the tube walls. Be careful of the path as it does have rough spots and puddles. Moist, cool and over 2 kms of walking, I enjoyed the visit, although not the most impressive caves I have visited.

Korean women divers are called haenyeo. They dive in the ocean without any special tools to gather abalone, clams or seaweed. Wearing a lead weighted  vested and goggles, they plunge into 20 meter depths and stay underwater holding their breaths for two to three minutes.  Once they come up to the surface, they make a whistling sound, which is their unique way of breathing out carbon dioxide and breathing in fresh oxygen. The museum is in a four story building and housed many exhibits.  Gallery 1 on the first floor depicts the haenyeo's way of life. On the second floor at Gallery 2, you can see haenyeo's working life.  On the third floor at the observation area you can get a view overlooking the sea.  Gallery 3 displays exhibits of the sea around Jeju.  Outside the museum there is a lawn with statues, including one honoring the haenyeo. You can also admire the architecture of the museum. Further down, we chanced upon the haenyeo who were starting their show by singing a song. We were indeed lucky on that Tuesday afternoon as we managed to watch the show which started at 1.30.

Kids may enjoy posing with Cinderella's carriage & shoe collection and running around the grounds.  As I was not however, although a few glass sculptures were interesting, I did not think it was worth the time or effort (& of course the entrance fee) to go.  Agree with the comments of previous reviewers who rated   poor  .  The  fish lunch I had at the restaurant next door however, was enjoyable. On the plus side, the place is wheelchair accessible.

Keep in mind, the founder, Paek Uncheol, is quoted   ?Visiting the park is intended to be a journey through the mythology of the island, entering through the ear of Seolmundae*, progressing through the body and exiting at the feet. It represents the journey of life and death.? Taking a journey that ends in death, even if it is a metaphoric (mythical, mystical, mind-boggling) death, may not appeal to everyone, but it could be transformative if you're open to it. Allow for hours of contemplating stones, thousands, tens of thousands, of stones, natural, carved, authentic, replicas - millstones, mortars, volcanic bombs, boundary markers, 2000 ceramic jars, fossilized tree roots - locals thought its creator, who collected these stones for forty years, had gone mad. Three courses to follow, each taking one to two hours. *Seolmundae Halmang, the grandmother of Jeju Island.

Just like everyone already mentioned, the road is indeed mysterious as the car would really move uphill on its own. However, it is only a very short stretch of the road. But I would still recommend it if you are self-driving and it's your first time in Jeju. Definitely, something you have to experience.You can also head to the museums that is nearby too after going to this road.

Just got back and it was cool. Not been down caves before but nothing scary here. You do need a decent pair of walking shoes (preferably water resistant or water proof).. The odd splash of water won't hurt you but solid footwear is a smart move (read that as flip-flops and high heels are a big no). I liked the experience, there are a few steps to go down which are easy at the start of the walk but if you walk to the end and back, those steps are a killer at the end. All-in-all, I loved it, nice little solo adventure; loads of couples down there (but well behaved) and it is cheap as chips for the entrance fee of just over 짙1.GBP. Easy to reach by taxi or bus and taxi shouldn't cost more than 20,000WUN at the most from most central places.. go along and view for yourself though if you have small children, it is taxing on their little feet cos the floor is very uneven (as to be expected on a lava field).

Just did the hike on 30 March.Trail: seongpanak up and gwaneumsa down. Goes to summit. (highly recommend to do this trail Cos going up by gweumusa is really steep though the view is nicer for gweumusa) Time taken: 4.5hrs up and 4hrs down (please go early and check the time that you need the reach the shelter and summit by.  Think should be by 1230 reach shelter and by 2 to leave summit) Weather: good.  Cold in the morning but as you hike,  you will perspire and definitely need minimum sweaters. I was only wearing teeshirt and windbreaker. In the end only tee-shirt cos it's getting warmer and you climb and when the sun is out. Need crampons?  Yes!!! It helped alot especially at the icy areas both going up and down. Not too sure where you can buy it but I managed to rent it from my hostel. Though I did see people without it,  and they did just fine.  I was wearing track shoes kind. So crampons helped alot!  How to get there: I went there from Jeju city and took bus 281 from bus terminal to seongpanak bus stop. Coming back from gwaneumsa trail: took bus 475 back to jeju  national university and change bus 360 to Jeju city.  Please check with bus driver or use kakao map/bus to help as Google Map doesn't seem to help much with he routes. Bus 475 have some timings going back. You can always find out from the visitors center at the gweumusa base. It is situated at the left side as you make your way down passing through the car park.  Shelters and food: not sure if I did miss it..  But I didn't see any food vendors, drinks stall as I hiked up and down. So I was really thirsty as the end of the trail. There's a small restaurant and a convenience store at gwaneumsa trail end. So please bring ALOT of water like at least 1.5L. Bring along food to eat up there and also plastic bag to put your trash and there are no rubbish bins around.

Just an ordinary road but countless of tourist buses and vans parked along it. Explore the mystery personally to appreciate the magical side of it. We'd done all tricks - stopped the car engine and let it roll uphill, poured water on road and see the trail running upward, closed our eyes and walked both ways where we found the gravity is totally against us !! Great fun ~!
Just a short stretch of road where it   appears   to defy gravity. Kill the engine where the START signs indicate and feel the car moving uphill on its own.

Just a rock formation that looks more like a bunny than a dragon.  Nothing much.  FOC entry but if you're driving, parking is paid when you exit the carpark.  Payment is to an attendant.  Highly touristy area and can be quite packed when the tour buses arrive.  This attraction is open 24hrs.

Joined the 2016 Walking Festival to walk the olle trails & it was a fantastic experience. Yes it rained (which was unusual in October but with global warming!) & was initially disappointing as the scheduled performances were cancelled. Nonetheless it was amazing to see so many people walking together. After the Walking Festival which covered trail 1 & 2 I did trail 1-1, 5,6, 8 & 10. Each of the trails were different and beautiful. I was fortunate to get the assistance of Jim Saunders who gave me information on line & Ms Han at the Tourist Information Centre located next to Seogwipo Bus Terminal & e Mart who spoke good English.Ms Han helped me by writing in korean the bus stops & landmarks for the different trails so that I could show the bus drivers my destination  when I boarded using the T-money transport card. She even took the trouble to show me the different landmarks using satellite pictures on her computer in locating the Starting Point of each trail. The Olle Guide Book in English (which I obtained at the Olle Trail counter at the airport)was also very useful & well written.I enjoyed every trail & got to see Jeju on foot. It was also fun meeting locals walking the trails. I plan to return to walk the other olle trails.

Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest, walking through these wood is believed to enhance cardiovascular function and to prevent asthma and tuberculosis. This is the most famous forest on Jeju island and here you can taste mineral water that is thought to relieve muscle and gastrointestinal problem

Jeju-do best attraction, the Mysterious Road (Dokkaebi Road) or Goblin road as folk story say, it was the goblins who does the trick.. sound interesting. Young and old will find this place fun and mysterious. All you have to do is just stop your car at the designation point, on the double sign(emergency light), off the engine, release the hand brake and let the car move up the hill by itself, 'Yes.. roll up the hill'.The best is, this attraction is free of charge. Along the Mysterious Road, have a few food stall, try out the grilled black pork sausage and many delicious food. For those driving, key in the number 7126988 (yup.. heading to Loveland, you will reach Mysterious Road first), most people stop by here on the way to airport.

Jeju is full of great natural wonders - Seongsan IIchulbong Peak, Manjanggul Cave, Cheonjiyeon Falls, Hallasan Mountain, Jeongbang Falls, Yongduam Rock, Jungmun Beach, Oedolgae, Jusangjeoli Cliffs; each and every of these world class attractions is Nature's well-carved masterpiece. Jusangjeoli Cliffs is one of those gorgeous and stunning attractions that I favored. While it does not have the sentimental legend that back-up Oedolgae or the auspiciousness of the dragon like Yong-duam rock, the sight of the crashing torrential sea waves rhythmically crashing against the set of blackish, rock pillars and columns was so beautiful a sight that I was totally immersed in the picturesque scene. The turquoise azure sea water contrasted magnificently with the black cliffs and produced one of those awesome scenery that one could hardly imagine it existed on Earth. I was mesmerized by what I saw and my ears drowned by the thundering waves. For one short moment, my mind went into a meditative state despite the presence of the squeezing and noisy crowd. I like to thank our Korean guide, Mr Won, who drove us in his van around Jeju to visit all these beautiful nature's wonders.

Jeju is a volcanic island and the black lava that erupted from Mount Hallasan few thousands years ago are found almost every where. When we visited this attraction at Yongdam which is about 20 minutes drive from the Jeju airport, we could see the sea rocks and soils were black in color. The Yongdam rock was probably a volcanic rock that erupted and eroded down Mount Hallasan and over the years sculptured by natural forces of strong wind and rain and powerful sea waves into a structure of a `dragon head' . But the invisible hands of nature did not leave a distinctively well carved aesthetic product that deserved our admiration and appreciation. I really could not figure out the `dragon head' from the rock until my guide pointed out it to me. But black dragon in traditional Chinese folklore was supposed to symbolize bravery and auspicious luck and good fortunes to the people and visiting this attraction assumingly bring good luck and prosperity.Nevertheless, Jeju is exceptionally natural beauty and boasts of so many awesome and stunning natural scenic attractions which are so fascinating so lovely so magnificent that make me wondered if this was paradise on Earth. The air is fresh and you hardly find heavy machineries and factories with thick polluted smoke emitting out from the chimneys or the methane smell of diesel and petrol from vehicular emissions that is so typical in crowded cities. Jeju impressed me what nature is all about. From Yongmeori seashore, manjanggul caves, cheongjiyeon waterfalls to Hallasan National Park and Oedolgae Cliffs and this Yongdu-am dragon head rock, the physical geographical lessons appear no ending and I found intense pleasure in enjoying nature's silent whispers.

Jeju had a volcano that erupted long time ago, its lava flowed thru the Manjang cave leaving a lava tube that is about 4 kilometers long, The part open to public is about 1 kilometer with three entrances. Although lighted, it is still dark, wet and cold inside. Although it is an experience to go in, but be careful as it is wet and dark, the floor are not level, especially in the inner portion where there is almost no road. For the adventurous, bring along flashlight and wear rubber shoes. As for me, I just walk part of the way to feel it, as it's not worth the risk to go thru the whole cave. Again, it may help if there are better lighting showing important landmark within the cave like other caves in asia. Underground cave of Palawan, stalagtite cave in Halong Bay for example.
