I've done the hike from the trail head at Seongpanak parking lot to the summit of Halla-san 14 times.  The hike is about 9 KM to the top.  The trail is very rocky and vertical.  There are a few drinking water sources on the way to the summit.  As you get near the top, the trail becomes a series of wooden stairs.  The trail becomes seriously vertical about 7KM from the trail head.  It took me between 2 and 2.5 hours to go up and about the same amount of time to return to my car.

I've climbed Hallasan twice now, once in December and once in early March, and both times I took this route. This route is slightly longer than Gwaneumsa, but it's also a gradual incline with several easy portions. I took this route primarily because there is not a lot of public transportation available to/from the Gwaneumsa trail, plus I'm not sure I can do a steep incline the entire way up to the summit. For Seongpanak, you have about 5 km that are easy, 2.5 km that get harder, and then a pretty brutal last 2 km. Regardless, know that there are other hiking trails around the island and even around the volcano, but only the two mentioned above will lead you all the way up to the summit.Given some of the reviews I saw that are either inaccurate or not very helpful, I hope to compile a quick list to help you decide if this is something you want to do and if so, what you will need:1) It's definitely going to be an all-day kind of thing. You will be tired afterward, so you likely won't want to schedule too many other activities for the evening. Also, it's likely that you will be sore and tired the next day or two. 2) You need to start climbing no later than 8:30 AM. As several people have mentioned, you will not be allowed to access the last chunk of the way if you're not at the second shelter by 12:30 PM (this is winter time, so the schedule varies slightly from season to season... always check the Korean tourism sites).3) Even if it's sunny, there's a chance you might need crampons. In the winter months you will need them for sure, but even last weekend people were sliding down and falling repeatedly without them. I hear that it's even worse on the Gwaneumsa trail since it's a lot more shielded from the sunshine. 4) Bring food and water! The only place you can buy something is at the very beginning of the trail, and even then the options aren't fantastic. A little protein or fruit will go a long way whenever you're starting to feel tired, and it'll help you push through. Please make sure you do not leave any of your trash along the way; there are zero trashcans, so if you carry something particularly messy, you might want to pack a bag for the waste.5) Do not use the toilet in the first shelter! It's the worst smelling bathroom ever, which is rare for Korea since things are usually so clean... I suppose it's the septic system. I suggest using the toilets at the parking lot and at the last shelter (there are two). The first one is seriously a nightmare. 6) It's not an easy hike, but it's doable even for people who don't exercise strenuously. I've seen people carrying babies all the way to the top, and I've seen small children and old people make it, too. Definitely wear the right clothing, though, and especially the right shoes. If you're hiking at a time without snow, you will spend hours circumventing rocks of all sizes and ankle support will be extremely helpful for this. Anyway, thanks for reading, I hope you have a fantastic hike!

Its worth it to climb up there. such a beautiful and breath taking view from the top. its a must visit place if you come to Jeju. entrance fee is just 2000krw per person. we actually drove there from our pension. many parking space. other than climbing the peak, you can also catch a Haenyo Diver Women performance at the bottom of mountain right beside it. its amazing to watch those elderly women  holding their breath for several minutes without any oxygen mask! overall its awesome! for those muslims, there's fast food restaurant Lotteria for you to grab your lunch or dinner since they have shrimp burger available. its located on your left when exit the car park area.
It's very near to Loveland. Interesting to see the car roll forward upslope. Start on the south, towards Jeju city. Length of the road is quite short, maybe 50m?
It's really mysterious, we put the gear to   N   and the car will go uphill on it own! weird right?! Yous should try your own!
Its quite a good time for walking in the lava tube. There are several announcement, so you can read and understand whats that.Its quite slippery, just be careful or hold ur friends hand (better).

It's pretty difficult using public transportation in Jeju to getting around expect using car. But this one is ok because there is bus stop in the highway, but you need to take a taxi or walking 3km from bus stop to get this place
it's only an eye perspective view. when we see the car slowly run up while the machine off, the road actually go down. Nothing special

It's my second time to this place. I remember few years ago there were bicycles for visitors to experience the mysterious by ourselves. However this time I don't see any bicycle there for the tourist. You can feel it better when you are riding the bicycle. Just need to be caution, there will be many cars passing by.

It's just a stadium with some architectural appeal but the shape tells a story  which is interesting. Try telling any football aficionado that it just a stadium and you will get howls of protest!From the 2002 FIFA World Cup it is designed around   the mouth of a volcano    and its roof in the shape of nets of traditional fishing boats in Jeju.So looking at it in that respect makes it more interesting.It was not open when we visited as of course there are no games here at the moment (although open during the summer months) so it was like looking into a fish bowl without the fish.Outside the stadium are many stone crafted 'dol hareubangs ' carved from porous basalt (volcanic rock).The statues' faces feature grinning expressions and bulging eyes without pupils  a long  broad nose  and slight smile and their hands rest on their bellies.These are quite common throughout Jeju and can be quite comic and a little suggestive!Have a peek here if in the area just to have at look at the stadium design and also the rock statues.Enjoy your visit!

It's honestly just a really cool cave. Not much to see here and I wouldn't highly recommend taking kids here as they *might* not enjoy it that much. It was my 23rd birthday and I had the entire day to myself (my mother had a business meeting) so I thought I'd kill some time getting lost in Jeju and decided to visit this cave instead.The way to the cave was honestly an adventure on its own; it took 2 bus rides from my hotel, the Orange Tree hotel (I would advise downloading a map of Jeju island) to reach the destination and I was the only tourist on the second bus that dropped me off the entrance of the cave. I was using a transportation card (like an oyster card) so I wasn't able to keep track of how much the fares were.Not a lot of people when I came to visit (which is ideal for me) and I only paid 2000 won for the entrance. I stayed for like an hour here just walking about and sitting down staring at the trees and sky. Not everyone's cup of tea but I enjoyed myself immensely and loved the sound of the birds just chirping. Wasn't able to take any pictures of the cave as it isn't well-lit enough for my camera phone.

Its definitely a worthwhile trip to make and just walking through the Lava Tube is quite an experience.  It is not everyday one has the opportunity to walk through and see the various formations, the caves formed, columns, the different textures formed, etc.One needs to be relatively fit to do the walk with comfortable shoes as the location tends to be wet. Elderly should have a walking stick which will help and carry a torchlight.  Its a few degrees lower underground.

It's basically an optical illusion, where it appears to be upslope, but it's actually going downhill. All the drivers there will switch off the engine an let the car run down the road by itself. It's only worth seeing if you so happen to pass by this road.

It's an incredible lava cave! We spent half day in this sight seeing and my daughters loved! (2 teenagers) It's very difficult to do sight seeing in Jeju without a rental car! We took almost an hour to arrive there, and the same to come back!!

It's an extremely demanding 'hike' for most average people. We read about it but didnt expect it to be that difficult. We went up the Seongpanak trail, starting at 7.30am, did a short detour to see the lake and crater and eventually reaching the summit at around 1pm. We descended the gwaneumsa trail and only managed to reach the base at around 6.30pm. We aren't considered extremely fit and so the climb was considered challenging for us. Our legs hurt for the next few days. The view down was amazing, but the climb was also steeper. Many parts of the trail were rocks so that made it a little difficult to climb as well. There are many cabs waiting at the base of Gwaneumsa trail to take you back to Seongpanak where we parked our car. The cab fare was about 15000won and took about 15 minutes. Overall the hike was fulfilling albeit tiring. But the views were a good return for our efforts!

It's all about glass, place for pictures. But do not try their macaron ice cream please. Taste awful and hard. I believed it's been a while no one buy not fresh at all. Yucky. But overall we enjoy picture everywhere.

It's a waterfall that goes directly to the see. Not many like that so you should visited it at least once. The road after the stairs was rocky, so you have to be careful. There's a woman diver, so there' s some people that ate her catch near the waterfall.

It's a stone throw away from the Lava Tube. There are a lot of cats lying around the park. The maze is quite easy but to collect all the stamp to accomplish the mission, it takes more time. However, the grass/plant at the maze seem not well taken care as you can see a lot of holes along the plant fences of the maze.

It's a place that is almost carbon-free. Electric cars, wind and solar panels are used for energy. It's small enough to travel around on foot or rent a bicycle. A ferry from Jeju takes about 20 minutes. Nice local restaurants to try.

It's a natural wonder.  Amazing how lava can create a tunnel as large as this. Must visit when in Jeju.  Wear a pair of walking shoes and an autumn jacket as temperature falls to around 15 inside the tube. It'll take you at least 30 minutes to walk 1km in and then another 30 minutes out.  So,  it's pretty chilly if you are without a jacket. Floor is wet therefore walk carefully & enjoy the unusual sights especially the walls & ceiling of the tube. Walk until the end as there's a lava column in there, the only one.

It's a mixed review.  The ticket price is 10,000KRW per adult and since other natural attractions are around 2,000KRW, this park should be well worth it.  Highs: The caves are really cool as well as the Bansai and Stone Garden. The park is easy to walk and has shops and toilets easily available.  Transportation is also easy as it's just the 702 bus from the Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal for 1 hour. Lows: The park is dated, like late 90s with its signage and information cards.  The bird exhibit, stone exhibit and flower garden are average at best.  While the park trail is easy to walk, you do walk through gift shops for the next exhibits (so a bit too tourist-y). Overall, it makes for a decent easy afternoon, especially with kids or elderly.  The park needs some updating to be worth the ticket price, but it is close to the beach (just 5 mins walking).
It's a lava cave, national herritage. Nothing special in there, it was dark and only rocks along the way. You need to be careful because the floor was wet and slippery.

It's a hedge maze straight out of the movies, except with nothing popping up to scare you. It is only the hedge.  It takes about 20 minutes to find your way out and costs 3,300 for an adult. It's 500m down the road from Manjanggul cave, so if you're going to the cave you could stop by, but not worth the trip otherwise.

It's a great honour to be able to admire Mr Sung's Spirited Garden! It's absolutely a must visit whenever you are in Jeju! The garden is a real Paradise on Earth! It's a unique place that teaches you many important things! The garden features many outstanding examples of bonsai trees, beautifully shaped stones, a waterfall, a restaurant and a souvenir shop. It's easily accessible by car or by bus, and will be a worthy place for everyone, especially the nature and art admirers. I highly advise everyone to visit this incredible place!!!
It's a bit dark here and u hardly can see your way, so u need to be careful when u go inside. Every lava section is quite different that makes it quite special and memorable.

It's a beautiful waterfall. As described by another reviewer, there is a flight of stairs you have to descend to reach the waterfall. At the bottom of the stairs, you will have to carefully traverse across rocks if you want to get nearer to the waterfall to take a good photo with it in the background. Be sure to get good shoes to avoid injury as the rocks can be slippery. Not recommended for pregnant ladies or old folks, especially so when the rocks are wet from rain.

It's a beautiful island just 15mins ferry ride away from Jeju Island. Rented cars are not allowed to travel over so we parked our car at the terminal port in Seongsan. Upon arrival at the port in Udo, you will see a few shops just right infront of the port start promoting their offering on bike rentals. Standard rental is 2hrs (KRW 10,000 per pax) for a standard bicycle. So great to tour around and have the best seafood pot ever along the coastal. Peanut ice-cream is a must have, it is so good! We did not manage to visit any of the recommended sightseeing places due to short of time but we had a great time cycling around taking pictures, along with the beautiful weather. Definitely will return again.

It's a 100m road whereby majority of the tourists are fascinated by this mysterious road. A short stop is given and you can have a good photo shoot over there. Most of the tour guide will tell you the truth behind this mysterious road and you will realise that    Things really cannot be judge by it's appearance.   Beside the Mysterious Road, there are a few stall selling some snacks. You must go to the first stall which is near to the ending point of the mysterious road, and try their strawberries. It's the most fresh strawberry i have ever seen and eat! It's a must to try.

It worth a look just to see the beautiful coastline of the Island.Most of the rocks come in various heights and sizes shaped like hexagons and if you look at certain angles, they can take on various animals etc.The black lava colour offsets against the outstanding sea and coastline.These cliffs are very similar to the Giants Causeway in Ireland with a pancake rock system but on a much smaller scale.It was crowded the day were there and we assume it is the same most days in the summer months. So a lot of people were snaking along this narrow path around the cliffs and we needed to wait our turn to see over the barriers.There are a few stallholders near the carpark (fee charged) selling fruit, souvenirs and the local home made confectionary similar to nougat.On the way out you can go to a park with some gardens and perhaps a museum type building.The hours vary seasonally however it is the standard KRW 2,000 entry fee for most monuments around the Island.Place it on your ?must see? places to visit here just for the dramatic coastline and on a rough day you may get some blow hole situations with the force of the water.Enjoy your visit!

It will take about 30 to 40 minutes to hike up the mountain which involves lots of stairs. View is superb, especially during sunrise because you will be facing east. There are quite a number of shops and restaurants down there, perfect for breakfast after morning hike. Spacious carparks. p/s: I read somewhere that there will be entrance fees (KRW2000-3000). However when we went there, the ticket booth was closed, perhaps because we went there at dawn.

It wasn't very clear from the guide books. The spot is basically a volcanic rock formation that is concave. I'm not sure that you can actually have a good view of the formation with its lush green centre from any walkable vantage point (like you get from travel books). So on nearing the spot, stop on the highway shoulder to get a distant photograph first.After you arrive, note that the car park is basically one way. Miss a turn and you have to exit the carpark and come back from the entrance. Be prepared to walk / hike as the areas open to public are quite steep. You can get a good open view of the city or the ocean. Refreshing scenery.
It was very weired and interesting. If you are going there, try to turn off your car and test it if the road tricks you! You will be very surprised!

It was very cooling in the cave, you can feel the temperature difference at the entrance of the cave. It was dark and slippery, be careful! It was really amazing to see the insides of this cave, definitely eye-opening experience~

It was the easier but longest route to the summit of Mt. Halla. Longest day of my life but it was so worth the aches and pain and sun-burns. Couldn't have done it without the constant encouragement of my partner. Reached the peak before lunch time and saw the beautiful lake and summit. Any later, the haze will start to come in and will ruin your pictures. Bring water and snacks and lunches while hiking. there is only one point where u can get drinking water. Pack light but sensible. Be prepared to spend a whole day for this climb and the next 3 days for aching thighs. So. worth. it. There are stalls selling food, drinks and ice-creams at the park. You can refresh yourself after the climb. Best to rent a car and start early.

It was really pretty and there are horses which you can ride at the bottom. Climbing up includes of climbing up many flights of steep stairs which might be difficult for the elderly or the unfit(like me). It takes about 50 mins to go up and down. The view on top was nice but when i was there, there were some construction works on going and they chased us away if we were to stand at the peak to take pictures. Imagine climbing up all the way to the top just to get chased away. Not a gd feeling.At the bottom near to the sea, there is also the performance of the women divers at 1.30pm and 3.30pm. It was interesting to watch even though we were flooded by many china tourist. Be careful when walking on the rocks as it can be very slippery. There was also a small pile of shells that you can choose from and to bring home. You can also buy the seafood caught by the women divers and enjoy them at the cafe just beside.

It was pretty crowded when we got there at about 3pm on a weekday. From the parking area, It was a short walk down some stairs to the observation decks where you get good views of the unique (column) rock formations by the coast.However, we had difficulties getting photos of us with the rock formation because there were just too many people on the observation decks. As we exited the observation deck area, we saw a guy selling postcards of the photos he himself took of various scenic Jeju attractions and we bought some to support him.I am not sure what else there is to explore in that area because we were hurried off to the next destination on our guided tour.If you are into Geography, love cliffs by the sea and rock formations, I highly recommend this place! I loved it!

It was nice experience when suddenly u find these kinds of roads... Some kind of mysterious nature behaviour that able to control your vehicles to suddenly runs on its own... Probably kind of magnetic field...Well, u can also enjoy a small view of grassfield and view restaurants around... I took a nice picture here with my travel friends, used a large stone (its carved with korean words) as background... Interesting experience... ;)

It was like being in another world! The cave is enormous and there are interesting rock formations, along with information about them along the way. It's very cold (10-15C), which is a welcome break from the Jeju heat! But maybe bring a sweater. The only problem is that it's very hard to get to if you don't have a car. From the main road, only a special bus goes to the cave entrance, and it comes once an hour. There are no taxis in the area. It's a 20 minute walk with no buildings/trees to shelter from the heat. So keep this in mind when going, as you may want to arrange for a taxi beforehand.

It was just amazing. Though the path way is well maintained but  it might be tough for some foreigners because of its slope but for Koreans it seems to be an easy task. But once you go uphill it looks so beautiful, not to be described in words rather to be felt by heart. As usual in Korea, I saw that every traveler keep the way neat and clean from waste food materials and carrying poly bags.

It was great to see the vehicle moving while turned off. I recommend whoever visiting this place to read the scientific explanation to add a benefit to enjoyment. On the other hand, I was told that there are other mysterious roads in other countries that make the cars move faster and harder. If it is near to a place you're already going then I think you should have a look, it won't take much time.
It was freezing in the tube! There were puddles of water everywhere so be careful when walking. The stones were interesting and do walk all the way in. You've already paid,so why not?

It was felt like exercising when walking down to the see the waterfall. But just about ten steps down the stairs, the scene reveal the hidden stunning waterfall. So beautiful.  A dozen shoots were never felt enough to capture its beauty. I would recommend to spend a sufficient time just to enjoy the scenery.Please take be careful when walking in between stones near and around  the waterfalls. They are so slippery, so chose a flat surface stones as you walk? or not at all. A friend had her camera and mobile phone slipped down into water when she struggled to stand still on a stone. I was slightly more fortunate to be able to keep those gadgets of mine dry?. but not my shoes. While the water was refreshing, but I do not think you would like getting your shoes wet, particularly when you have only a pair for the whole Jeju island exploration. A wet trousers could spoil your whole day trip around the island.

It was around a 20 minute walk into the cave and another 20 minutes going out... Path was dark and wet, so you must be careful walking inside the cave... It was a good experience with a little workout.

It was a very hot day yesterday, July 31st 2018, and I got sunburn the day before so in 33 degree heat and me didn't match. I didn't go up to the top but I did go up to the first viewing platform, which i think most people would be able to manage slowly, not matter your age. It is well paved, and the views are incredible. It was a very windy day too, so there was no show by the women divers, Haenyo, but you could see where they went out and to be honest the roughness of the seas showed how tough the women must have always been. There are a few shops near the bottom and one part way up, so you can purchase drinks and trinkets if you wish. There is a Starbucks and a Dunkin' Donuts and i think a McDonald's near the car park, as well as multiple Korean restaurants. Well worth a visit, even if you can't ascend to the peak.

It was a short drive from Seogwipo where I stayed with my son In late Dec. The trip was highly recommended by the Shilla hotel staff and I could understand why after having spent an hour on its rugged coastline. Awesome selfie spots at every turn! Another highlight was the women divers selling their harvest (sea cucumbers) on the coastline. It was a stimulating walk, with crystal clear waters lapping at our feet. We went when the tide was receding as advised by the hotel staff. So do check before venturing down. 2nd tip: go well bundled up as it can get very cold in winter. As a reward, we headed to the Hiddink cafe at the end of the trail (next to car park) for a hot cuppa. It felt like we had stepped into a Dutch village, replete with tulips and clogs. As you can probably guess, Korea is still besotted with the Dutch football coach.

It was a rainy morning that my friend and I visited this cave. We were greeted with a flight of stairs entering the cave. The temperature in the cave was so much lower, approximately 10 degrees celsius. It was dark and slippery too. The further we walked in, the colder it gets. The pathways are actual lava that hardened over the years therefore, it was not a smooth walk. A lot of locals enjoyed their walk, some strolling while youngsters brisk walk, talking and laughing along the way, making the whole cave not too scary. It was a nice morning walk looking through the structure left behind by the once active volcano forming rocks, mini wells naturally. The work of nature. Beautiful!

It was a great visit! My hubby is a car lover and he enjoyed this attraction very much. We even bought car models for our new house at the store. To get into this attraction you pay a minimal fee, additionally, there's an outdoor area where you can feed rabbits and goats, do pick up the carrot sticks from the shop!

review: It was a good experience for me family with 2 children as they enjoyed ut the most. Weather as a bit chilly even during autumn, so bring extra layers with you so that you can get confortable. The train ride at the start of the trip really feels like the highlight of the trip, although you can board the train on and off later to get from one garden to another. There are 5 stops for you to stroll around, toilets, cafes and other facilities are available and very much well taken care off. We had a great time all in all. Highly recommended to friends and families.

It was 15-min walking from our hotel, and admission was 2,000won for adults, and 1,000won for teenages (up to age 24). You purchase at ticket box, but don't throw or put tickets away, as they check for them close to the entrance.  It was an easy walk, not too many steps down to the sea level.  Nice waterfall, where you can get close to it should you choose! If low tide, there is a pebble/sand pit area revealed, where you can get to by carefully climbing over some rocks...but could be slippery...so weigh the risk carefully!  However, pictures taken from this angle - with the waterfall as the backdrop - was breathtaking!

It took me a long time to get there. All those folks with cars would have no problems. But I am on a budget, and I am bussing it all the way. I came here from the Seongsan Ilchulbong crater thing, and I took the 701 bus to the stop that said it was for the cave. Then I walked 2.5km to the cave. The cave was gloriously cold inside, as I was a hot sweaty mess by then (Korean people staring at the fat, sweaty American haah!). I took my time through the cave, it was nice and worth the trip for me, even though it took me almost 2 hours to get back after I was finished. I think you could take a cab for a reasonable price... but I am cheap.

It took a little over 2 hours by bus to get here. I feel conflicted with it, as a part of me liked the place but another part of me thought there was (yet again!) nothing special here. Plus the journey to get there was already exhausting so probably my feet were already asleep halfway into my walk.So only go if you can rent a car, it will take much less time to get here. All in all a relaxing place to take a stroll or read in.

It takes 10 min tops to actually enjoy the rock.  Its unique and pretty but that's all folks!  You have to pay for parking (500 won every 30 min) and believe me, it doesn't even take that long to see all there is to see.  We had extra time before rental car needed to be returned so we stopped.  But I wouldn't have otherwise gone out of my way to see this rock formation.

It smells so good as soon as you get off the car and pass the entrance. After a short walk, you get to the Forest.  It is also easily accessible for baby strollers as they put some straw mats alone the forest so the whole family can enjoy a wonderful walk in the forest.  Not sure if wheelchairs can roll easily on those mats though but I saw quite some baby strollers.We took a detour after Sangumburi crater (about 20 min away), and spent about an hour in the forest but didn't complete it. Then in another 20-30 min, we arrived at a Five Day Market, which is about 10 min from the Haeyeo (Women Divers) museum.So this was how we planned our route to and from the forest.
it memorable experience in my life, seeing things all made from glass, and get to see glass roses, glass the ring,cinderella shoes, and carriage.. a special moment in my life
It is very nearby the airport, you can stop by once you have your rental car picked up. We did a quick stop for some photos only, we did paid for the parking. There is not much to see.
It is really a mysterious road!!! It is a upslope. However when u off engine, the car will move dwn by itself

It is only mildly interesting as part of a tour package which include this as a drive-through attraction.Plenty of cars & coaches stop & have their engines turned off to experience the   rolling uphill   mysterious effect.It is quite interesting to see how this phenomenon and the perception of the surrounding environment to the naked eyes has come so far to give birth to a tourist attraction. It could also double as a quick pit-stop to grab some snacks & skewers at the food store along the road.Hint: Get there, spend 5-10min walking one way forward, and then walking backward, or lay a half filled water bottle on the road, to crack this mystery.

It is no wonder why Spirited Garden is one of the top-rated tourist attractions on Jeju Island. I found it one of the best garden I have visited so far. It is basically a Bonsai tree-themed Garden decorated with many waterfalls and beautiful ponds full of colorful koi carps. Hundreds of artistic bonsai trees can be seen planted on small to large flower pots and on the ground. The bonsai trees of fruits, especially Jeju mandarin (or orange), apples are very impressive. It has seven small gardens with beautiful exotic gates, one of which is called Secret Garden and exclusively use for national and international MICE events (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions). It appears that the garden is very famous in China and other neighboring countries. The information boards show that the garden has been visited by many honored public figures notably former premiers of China, Japan, Indonesia, and others. Also, the garden has been awarded many decorations such as ?KOREA Unique Venue?, ?Green MICE Venue?, etc.

It is my first hiking ever, I do feel some kind of relaxation after the experience. At first, I wonder how can those people climb up to reach the top, it takes more than a thousand stairs to be on the top, I was pretty scared. But when I was first stepping on the environment, I can feel the natural beauty of the nature. It enhances me to have a greater heart to finish the journey. There also some strangely shaped stones while I was climbing up the stairs, I learned the history behind the stones and took several selfies with the special stones. About 20 minutes, we reached the highest point of the mountain. The mountain was naturally a dead volcano, which build up with lots of grasses and trees, and is no longer a crater. The view is like a green-sea. I had never been such relaxed before. It is a great experience to me and is memorable.The overall journey took us about 1 hour, if you are a fan of hiking, you must enjoy it as the view is priceless. **Remember to buy a bottle of water before you go, there are shops for you to buy some snacks and drinks in the beginning of the path.

It is located just beside O'Sulloc Tea Museum. To get there, just take bus no.755 from any bus stop bound for Pyonghwa-ro global education and alight at O'Sulloc Tea Museum station.They sell cosmetics, skin care products, stationaries, D.I.Y soap, etc..There are also cafe which sells bingsu, beverages and food. Tried the 珥덉퐫荑좏궎?먯씠?? (choco cookie shake), it costs 6000 won and tastes good but I think the portion is a little small (for me). Nice to visit if you are visiting O'Sulloc Tea Museum since it is just beside it. There is a big tea farm beside Innisfree Jejuhouse.. you can take some pics there, but it was raining when i visited the place so i didn't manage to take a lot of pictures.

It is just a vision trick. The road appears going up when it is really going down, so cars and buses can glide down when put in neutral. The way the trees at the side of the road is planted tricks your vision. Coming from Canada, we have seen it similar to the one in Moncton, New Brunswick.

It is interesting but not quite a must-see in Jeju. If you miss it, it is still no grave regret unless you love geology. An extremely long volcanic lava tube but due to the number of tourists, I believe the condition of the cave is not as well preserved as the caverns in Europe. Careful walking in the first 100 metres... can easily twist one's ankles.

It is indeed mysterious as to why this spot is named as mysterious road and promoted as such (there are road signs giving directions to the spot in the city).  I think the road is not steep enough so that when the car is put to neutral, it goes too slow to create an impressive illusion.

It is definitely an important piece of gem showing the massive power of lava flow.We were excited to see the marks on the wall, the tall lava column and the Stalactites in the forming.  However, I echo the other reviewers their caution:1. It is poorly lite to protect the rock formation.  Bring a torch so that you can appreciate the mark of the flow.2. Ground is uneven and slippery (worst than the cobble road of medieval towns).  Old people and children have to take care.3. It is cooler than ground level and there is water dropping from above.  Recommend to bring along water jacket with hood.4. Its a fairly long walk (exit point is same as entrance).  Total walking time is more than an hour if you want to see the lava column.If you are not big fan of rock formation, you can pass.

It is definitely a park full of stones, but it is actually quite interesting.  There is also a museum in the park which is worth checking out.  It shows some of the history of the island and the different types of volcanic rocks that can be found on the island. If you aren't interested in parks or rocks this probably isn't a place you would enjoy, but my husband and I really enjoyed it.  Naturally shaped rock sculptures, carved rock sculptures, stacked rock sculptures, etc.

It is dark inside so you need a good camera if you are planning to take some pictures. It is also cold so you might want to wear more layers of clothing. Through the tube, there are signboards that explain certain geological formations and structures (in several languages). Around 2km of the tube is opened for visitors and at the end, there is a lava column that is well lit for photo opportunity.Becareful inside as it is slippery, cold and a bit dark despite the lamps at an interval from each other.

It is beautiful,  seeing nature transformed.  Wear comfortable shoes with traction,  closed toes. It can be slippery and the rocks can be slick. Bring a light jacket bc it is cool down there. There are about 75 to 100 steps of stairs.There is a delicious restaurant on site. They do take credit cards. There is also a mini convenience store. Restrooms are clean and well maintained.

It is an UNESCO World Heritage site.  The Manjanggul Cave Tunnel formed by the lave, is one of the longest tunnels of the world.   The tunnel is 8-9 kms long but only 1 km is opened to tourists.  So, be prepared to walk 2 kms (return trip) on a lave based surface which is very uneven and wet.  It is cold inside and water keeps on dripping from the top; be careful. Carry a torch which comes very handy in the dark though some light is provided throughout the tunnel.  Various structure formed by the lave will fascinate you.  Opening timing 0900-1800 hrs; last admission by 1700 hrs.  Entry fee: Won 2000.  Recommended while in Jeju Island.

It is an old village that show us the homes for the people of Jeju in the past few hundred years. We have been guided through the village by a lady, who speaks very good Chinese's Mandarin. After the tour, they try to sell their products. Some of those are quite expensive. The thing that made us a little unhappy is   I think they have been trying too hard to make us buy something   so we end-up to select the cheapest product but then it became worst when the price was 10X different from what was being offered. It was already nicely packed and we did not want to make her unhappy so we just swipe the card.Anyway, it could be a communication error but both of us are Chinese and heard the same thing. It is a nice place but just be a little careful when you purchase those items.
It is an interesting road and we had a car so we can do it a few times. I would say that if you are not going in that direction, there is no need to drive there specially for it.

It is amazing to see nature?s wonder , a must go in Jeju. Will not take much of your time as just 1km of the cave is open to public. Must go till the end of the tunnel to see nature?s wonder. Be careful while walking as the rocks formed after lava formation is uneven.

It is a small island. we took the boat from Jeju. In a lobby full of Korean people, speak no English or Chinese. It was a bit challenge for me. ;) helpful enough, when I tried to talk to the ticket officer, she spoke a little Chinese. The boat took around 15 min. it is a pretty simple boat, with both people, and cars. with 30 min. time interval.Landing on Udo, we chose the red bus tour. 4 stops. the first stop is the best place I should say. Brilliant view! sea with sea wind. And there are some bars and restraunts where you could take a seat and rest.The rest of the 2-3 stops, are normal. On the bus, the driver were saying in Korean languange, which we do not understand at all. But we heard laugh from time to time, which we believe everyone else enjoyed the drivers speech.It is a good short stay. sun shine is strong, get prepare with some protections.

It has always been something i try to do everytime i go for a holiday, is to go trekking in the mountains or forest. I went in late December and took a cab up to the start of yeongsil trail, and went down Eorimok trail. It was near a six hours journey, with a 20 mins lunch break. As i went during late december, the drive up the mountain area was really foggy and the visibility is only like 5 metres in front of us which is kinda scary because there were many windy roads. but as soon as we are nearing the trail, the fog seems to have been lifted due to the heights. Good info to know: Yeongsil trail have many flights of steps. Depending on what you prefer, manmade steps means relatively safe walkway but it is up most of the time.Eorimok trail has more stones steps and is more natural. But it could mean that it is more tedious, really depends on your preference.Lunch is ramen noodle at the shelter, they sell small snacks and drinks too. PS: As i went during the winter, the timing to enter certain trail is really strict because the sun sets really early like 5ish in the afternoon. So it is definitely a thing to take note of especially if you are not fast paced. Also during winter, along the trail, there will be snow left from the night before, and it IS really Slippery!! I nearly slipped many times because i was wearing a normal sneaker and not trekking shoe. And a really helpful thing to have is a walking stick! Other than that, enjoy your time with nature there!

It felt pretty surreal to walk through the caves, and I mean it in a good way! Definitely worth the visit.Just one advice - grab a cardigan when you go: even in hot summer days it is pretty cold in the cave! and also a torch can be useful so you can see better the shapes of the lava walls.

Island best explored by driving, ATV or bike rental. Ferry across from mainland Jeju also carries vehicles. Road kinda narrow so one need to be careful, I blew a tyre when my right wheel rammed into a rock or kerb :-(  Lots of climbing if you really wanna explore in-depth. Many small eateries on the island. Very scenic island with lots of photo opportunity. Be wary of last ferry back or you would be stuck there overnight

Is worth going if u have young kids and a husband/wife who enjoyed looking at vintage cars instead of young woman (:p). My kids enjoyed driving the cars and they were issued a license with photo after the 10mins ride. Although they say no phototaking but trust me, phototaking opportunity are plenty once u r out of their sight. Read that there's an outdoor area where we can feed the deer. Unfortunately it was raining shortly after we were there. Hence didn't manage to do there. This place is very near to the ossulloc green tea museum. Easy to swing over after the visit to ossulloc. But beware to check weather. There's a unsheltered slope uphill from the entrance area (remb to bring enough umbrella for whole family in case it rains). My hubby only brought 1 from the car hence he needs to go bk to the car and climb uphill again just to pass us the ponchos and umbrellas). :P
address: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관

review: Interesting way they hide it from free view, but a  nice drop and fall into the ocean.  Careful clambering over the cobbles and boulders to get your shot.  Looks like local vendors selling raw oysters of sashimi down by the shore.  Other souvenir shops align the entrance and exit.

interesting shapes of rocks and lovely blue water.not too difficult, short walk along the trail. there are 2 different trails starting from different car park. both trails are not connected at the moment due to safety issue so make sure you visit the right one.by the look of it no.2 may not available or can be very wet @ low tide.i like the both but personally like no.1 trail little more.

Interesting facts about the formation of the lava tube. Malaysia has no such thing so i was definitely eager to learn more and to experience it. Walking into the lava tube really exciting as i step on to the solid harden lava ...beautiful formation of harden lava, adores the lava pattern ... careful stepping onto the path as it is uneven and can be challenging to some ... just take your time walking in. As i adores nature, i really enjoy exploring the lava tube...as you go deeper into the tube it gets warmer than the windy cool air outside of the tube. Enjoy it, a must.

Interesting experience  as we we pull to neutral gear, release the accerator, the car just go forward, upwards. The mysterious road is short, we made a few rounds. There is a car park where you turn in to go a few rounds if you wanted to. We tried the  same stretch to road after the end point. The car just go backward on the upward facing slope.

Innisfree Jeju House is just next to O'Sulloc Tea Museum, so is great to visit both the places. Innisfree is just one floor in a glass house.Besides selling Innisfree products like facial care, there is also many other things to explore.There is a big space for soap making area, visitor can purchase a bag of soap making set at the counter, and do it at the available place. The staff will guide you on the soap making. A self making post card corner for visitor to bring back (free but with limited, per card per person).Nice cozy clean comfortable cafe. Don't forget to try the black pork hot dog. It is so delicious. I bought a soap making set for my son to enjoy the art work, while I enjoy my facial product shopping. My husband and mother where having a good time at the cafe.

Initially, we were only planning on staying here for a few minutes to take some pictures because the reviews were so mediocre. We rented a car and drove to the entrance our GPS took us to (FYI if you rent a car and don't read Korean, make sure you get a GPS with it, Google maps/Apple maps/etc doesn't work in Korea, only Naver). I think it was some kind kind of back entrance, off the road, because no buses or anything were parked there. There wasn't even really a parking lot. When we walked through the village, to the other side, we saw the big parking lot and all the cheesy buildings and shops and stuff. But from the back side, it was just lots of nice little houses (some I think still had people living there) and pretty, walled-off yards. We were there in the morning and the are we were in had almost no one around, except for a few Chinese ladies who had decided to leave their tour and were having fun (we saw them rejoin with their tour later, so I didn't pull that out of thin air, lol). The main front entrance area is way more touristy and that's probably all people getting off the bus see, hence the bad reviews. If you keep walking through the whole town and take your time (if you can), it's actually pretty and peaceful. I think we spent a couple hours here.

Initially we had wanted to walk here from Seogwipo but gave up and took a taxi up the hill, the road was quite crowded with taxis and the car park filled with tour buses and cars. It is a very touristy place, there is ample reason. This is the place where Jewel of the Palace (Daejanggeum 鸚㏝룝) was filmed - one of the first Korean dramas popular all over asia. There is a cut-out of Janggeum where you can put your face and take a photo.More importantly, the scenery is lovely and dramatic. The rock column rises out of the beautiful blue sea. We left the path and tourists behind and walked around the rocks to the edge. We even came to a point where we could see Saeyeongyo Bridge in Seogwipo. We came across a blue rock thrush and a nice little coffee house before grabbing a cab on the main road. There is a bus running but we did not want to wait for it... it is about 6-8 min drive to seogwipo town

In the summer heat, Manjanggul is the perfect place to escape the heat. It's quite cold inside, and water drips from the ceiling. I changed into jeans and a light sweater before going in, which was perfect. The texture of the cave is fascinating! There are good informational English placards that explain how the cave formed. The floor of the cave is quite bumpy, so take care not to trip.It's a popular destination but getting there and leaving can be time-consuming unless you are with a tour. I took a bus from the Bijarim Forest to get to the cave, which dropped us off right at the cave. The bus leaving right from Manjanggul only leaves once an hour, so I recommend checking the bus departure times before you go into the cave and plan your stay accordingly. Otherwise, there are taxis but the drivers are rudely persistent, charge a non-negotiable flat price, and refuse to go by the meter. They kept pestering us the entire hour we waited for the bus, even after we rejected many times and had begun ignoring them.
in summertime be careful, there must be enough water.we found no waterfall at all, so maybe next traveler more luck ;-)
In short, you will be walking/driving with chaotic buses, motor cycles, bicycles, walkers & rental cars in single lane. Terrible visit.

In order to reach the waterfall, you need to walk down many stairs and using the same way back. But worth it as the view is beautiful as it directly flows to the ocean. But be careful since the area is rocky.

Ilchulbong is a huge rock/volcano/crater on the North East of Jeju Island. At first it seems a little daunting when you pull into the carpark as it looks really huge and steep. Yes, there are a lot of steps, but there are plenty of places to pause or sit for a rest and once you get to the top there's a great sitting/viewing platform. The views are really spectacular in all directions and you can see all over the mountain. It's really worth a visit if ou are going to Jeju.

If you've never been to a traditional Korean market, the Jeju Five Day Market is a wonderful introduction, and if you are an old hand at these sort of things, then you will enjoy Jeju's style. Pros: Roughly the size of a football field, there's a little of everything at this market. And every market is a little different too, so it stays interesting even over multiple visits (seasonal goods are fantastic here). Fruits, vegetables, herbs, roots, jams, honey, traditional medicines, gardening supplies (including seedlings); clothing, shoes, traditional crafts, a sprinkling of electronics now and then, kitchenware, furniture, rugs, and a whole host of things you won't recognize. It's truly a bizarre bazaar, and I am hopelessly in love with the sights, sounds, and smells of this style of capitalism that hearkens back to a time of more hooves and mouths than credit cards and smartphones. Go! Try everything! Buy everything! You'll love it!Cons: Sensory overload. Severe introverts should farm their energy for at least a day prior to going to this market. Expect to be shoved, bumped into, pushed, and in every other possible way have your personal space invaded. The shouting can be persistent, and the din is incredible. Trying to park your car can induce migraine headaches, and the traffic jams that lead up to the parking can be even worse. People here are generally honest, but I urge you to be extra vigilant when you buy perishables. More than once I've gone home with a great deal, only to have it go bad the same night. Also, check around for prices. Often you will buy something and then find a better version at a lower cost just a meter away. And finally, don't hesitate to haggle: the   foreigner price   rule is definitely in effect at this market.

If you?re driving around Jeju Island, this place is a must. It took me a while to figure out what was the big deal (mysterious) about this road but after I figured out the way it was described to be, it was definitely cool and somewhat mysterious. So here it goes: you drive upto the starting point of mysterious road and put the car in neutral gear. The road certainly looks like and uphill, however the car drives forward until 100m to the end of the mysterious road. Anti-gravity huh? I?m not sure of the scientific explanation for this phenomenon, but I recommend you experience this if you?re driving around Jeju Island. Takes only 15 minutes and certainly worth the time and experience!

If you want a good workout, take this adventure on. I'm in average shape and it took me just around two and 1/2 hours to climb the Seongpanak Trail (9.6KM) going non-stop. The trail is definitely steep in sections and please use caution on the way down. I learned the hard way that tired legs don't descend as well as normal legs and took a pretty good fall.  Fortunately I was able to careen into the bushes on the side of the trail much to the suprise of all the hikers around me. There are stairs...lots and lots of stairs. There is an trolley car too hidden off to the side that they use to resupply the shops at the two shelters and maybe for medical evacuation if needed.

If you visit Jeju, this volcanic mountain should be on your shortlist! It has excellent hiking trails which are well maintained. Trails are all well documented and give explanation about the distance, altitude and rest areas along the trail. At the top you have an amazing 360 degrees panorama view on the complete island. Plan your hike carefully. Check the weather before you leave. Bring along some warm clothing and rain protective clothing. Climbing 100 meters means a temperature drop of 1 degrees Celsius. It can get cold and humid up there!

If you love the sea, sand, mountain and great scenery, you will need to make a day trip to Udo!  You can take a ferry to Udo from Seongsan Harbour.  I highly recommend that you rent a car in Jeju and drive that over to Udo as there are so much to see and do in a single day.  You can drive your car up onto the ferry to Udo.

If you have seen any of the large dramatic water falls around the world then you will be disappointed by this tiny cascade. Barely 60/70 ft tall and about 20/25 ft wide. A small stream tumbles directly into the ocean. The tourist brochures make this more dramatic than what it actually is. Have uploaded pictures of the falls from the top (from the platform adjacent to the ticketing office and entry barriers) and from the bridge over the stream just before it tumbles down. Would give you some idea of the size.But having said all of that, this a pleasant enough area. Pay Won 2000 for entry (entry hours 8am - 6pm/7pm, depending on summer/winter) and leisurely climb down about 60 odd feet i.e. equivalent of climbing down about 6 stories. You will arrive at a rocky area. Clambering over about 1/5th mile (300 odd mts) of large rocks to where the water falls, isn't for the aged like me! But it would be nice to get to the water's edge if you can.Not a bad idea to carry sandwiches and beer and sit on the rocks, moments of peace and quiet, isolated from bustling Segwipo all around.You wouldn't miss anything if you haven't been here. But it would be a shame to miss it if you are on Jeju.
If you have been to Niagara, don't bother to visit this one. It's not a roaring high waterfall. Also when it's crowded, you have to be careful, climbing up the wooden steps.

If you have an opportunity to visit these lava tubes, then make sure you do!   We have lava caves in New Zealand and I have seen the lava tubes on Hawaii, but these are giants in comparrison.  The grounds of Manjang Caves are well kept.From the carpark it is only a 3 or 4 minute walk along a concrete path to the entrance of the caves.   We were expecting big, but these caves are huge!There are a number of steps leading down into the mouth of the cave and then you are inside this amazing formation.   It was quite an eerie feeling as we ventured deeper and deeper inside the tube which measures approx 5meters wide and up to 10 meters high.   The temperature is quite pleasant inside the caves and it is a little damp.   Even though we all had good walking shoes on, we still had to be quite careful of where we walked on the uneven, slippery  floor.   It is true that there is not a lot of light inside the cave, but we felt that the dim lighting added to the atmosphere.   In hindsight, a torch might have been helpful.All in all, definitely well worth the visit and would highly recommend to all. I would recommend that this is probably not a safe place for the elderly and very young children.  My elderly parents waited for us at the main building where there was a restaurant, shop and toilets.

If you have a tight schedule and cannot afford a whole day climbing the Hallasan Mountain, or some of your group physically can't do Hallanshan, this is a good option, because it is closer to other sight seeing places so you don't need a whole day, also because it is a much easier climb compared to Hallasan.The day we visited this was not crowded at all because everybody went to Udo Island on the opposite, after a two day close of the ferry service due to weather. If there was a helicopter service i(not sure), it must be very spectacular from an aerial view.  From the ground level,  if you didn't see the photo from the Internet, nor post cards, you probably don't realize it is a flat volcanic crater.Anyway, it would be quite a nice walk close by other sightseeing places, but might look more impressive from opposite Udo, or from a plane or helicopter
if you go by walk don't bother to go there, you can't notice anything apart from cars driving very slow

If you enjoy nature, hiking one of the olle trails is a must-do while you're in jeju. It will not be an easy hike and not all parts of the trail are scenic but there are sufficient sights to blow you away and be left in awe of nature. This is also the best way to experience jeju's natural beauty (after all this is what its most famous for and not for teddy bears). It is also arguably the least touristy thing to do during your trip here. You can do as long or as short of the trails as you like; there are trails passing through hot tourist destinations where you'll see many tourist buses, local villages, rice fields, even resorts. You'll walk on sand, on rocks by the ocean, and if you time it correctly you'll be able to catch a gorgeous sunset along jeju's coastline. Be sure not to get stuck in a remote area after sunset as it can be difficult to get out. If you're doing a multi-day hike, there are many pensions located along the olle routes and you can just pop in for a night.Suggest to go with at least one other person in case you get lost (there are some places where the markings are not so visible/well maintained). If you rented a car, dont drive. Wear comfortable shoes and bring lots of water and snacks!

If you book a car to travel around, probably you can consider to drive pass this mysterious road which took less than 20min when you're on the way to other attraction. This mysterious road is quite interesting, it is about rolling up this   Down slope  .  You can try it, just by asking the driver to off the engine of your car, and let it roll freely. I also tested it out with my water bottle, it was quite funny, the bottle actually roll up. At first, i thought this was due to law of gravity, but i realize is just optical illusion caused by the surrounding that cause this illusion of   down looking slope  . Fun place with interesting facts.

If you are travelling with small kids, i suggest to drive a car into the island. (They allow car to enter the island if having kids below 6 years old), really regret that we park our car at the multi storey parking, with all the high hope to rent a electric scooter (the one with 3 wheels)The electric scooter is strictly for 2 person only (they dont allow 2 adult + 1 baby too)Only those with Class A international license allow to rent the electric scooter (i am a Class B international license holder (allowed to drive car only)If you plan to travel the island by bus, it will waste lots of time on queueing and waiting for the bus. The bus driver will not explain any tourist spot in english, so you will have a hard time to decide which is the good spot to get down from the bus.Overall the island has nothing special with we are not allow to ride the electric scooter and generally the island is too crowded with tourist.

If you are traveling alone, not planning to ride a bicycle or rent a car on the island, you can buy a local tour bus ticket. The price varies as they are several bus company. The local tour bus stops at several highlights of the island. The bus driver will introduce and talk about the island (in Korean). The scenery is excellent, a must-visit-place in Jeju. You need to spare at least 4 hours for U-do Island.

If you are planning to visit the Hello Kitty Island, beware: there is a specific audience that his place caters to; it is not recommended for everyone. Our tour group went here in lieu of the Trick Eye Museum.Little girls and Hello Kitty fans would love this place. Hello Kitty merchandise are displayed everywhere. There is also a room that narrates the history of how Sanrio characters came about.  There is a Hello Kitty Caf챕 at the 2nd floor. On the 3rd floor, there is an auditorium that plays a Hello Kitty-themed show. Outside is an open-air Hello Kitty-themed miniature garden maze. The view of the landscape from here is wonderful. For me, it was meh. I am not among those that this place was built for.On the plus side, there a postcards available at the souvenir shop, which you pass through as you exit the building. I also liked the stamping stations spread around the place, which are reminiscent of postmarks.

If you are into local stuff, you need to visit this market. We rented a car and it is equipped with gps, hence we drove around. There is a parking space  Earby,  just watch out for P sign. The market has plenty of fresh, live abalone freshly dugged korean ginseng, banchan, salted fish, seafood, home ware, snacks, and little eateries. It is very clean and also if you are looking at those orange chocolates or even souvenirs they have it here aa well. We manage to buy some yummy vegetable chips which cost 10000krw per pack with vegetables that you like such as chillies, apples, seaweed, and etc. Spent 1 1/2 hours here before heading back to the airport.

If you are interested in the history and culture of Jeju island, and of Korea, then I would recommend spending an hour or two at this park. If you aren't, or are expecting something more exciting, skip it. For me, who lives in Korea and is already familiar with much of Korean history, I wish I had gone elsewhere. True to previous reviews, it was beautiful, but so is most of Jeju, and there are many other places more beautiful than the park itself. Overall: if you don't care about the history behind the park, it's 2 hours of looking at rocks.

If you are ever in Jeju-do, you have to make a day trip to Udo... Udo means   Cow Island   - so named because the shape of the island looks like a cow lying down... but try as I might, the island on a map doesn't look like a cow to me, but I guess the ancients who named it looked at things differently from me...  :PYou can drive your Jeju rental car onto the Udo ferry for a fuss free 15min journey over to this lovely island. Once there, you can tour the island by car! There are many beaches you can choose to hangout at, my favourite is Hagosudong beach for it's crystal clear waters and fine white sand. however Koreans aren't really into bikini culture, the Korean women go to the beach in long sleeved t-shirts, hats and umbrellas... So if you wanna sunbathe, you have all that white sand to choose your fav. spot! there are many cafes on Udo for you to grab a burger or sandwich for lunch if you are into western fare and also many restaurants that serve seafood Korean style. The seafood comes from the   Hae-nyo   sea-women who dives around Udo to haul in fresh Abalone, sea-urchin, octopus and the like for our enjoyment. As you tour around the island, you will be able to see these sea-women in action in various parts of the sea. My family and I love the relaxed vibe of this little island. In Udo, you can also take a speedboat tour of the natural caverns dotting the cliffs and coasts. the speedboat drives all the way into these caverns for you to observe up close the cave formations. This is my second visit to Udo and I recommend it to any nature loving, beach going traveller.... :)

If you are driving, I recommend you visit Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak first at around 7am to catch the sunrise at around 8:00am something.For me it's better seeing the Seongsan Ilchulbong in a far away place rather than hiking it for 30mins. So before reaching the gps route you would notice a lot of cars parked at the road side. Stop for a while and from there you would see a crowd of people waiting for the sunrise at the seashore and infront is the mountain touching the sun.If you like, you can still proceed with the peak 1km away from the stopover and hike a bit at the stairs to see the peak.After that a few kms away is the Seongsan Port going to Udo Island.Gps to Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak 710-7923Gps to Seongsan Port 7825671Upon reaching Udo island in a 15min ferry ride for 5500won, you can either walk, cycle or rent a scooter. You need an international drivers license to rent a scooter for 25000won for 2 hours, which i think is really short. Circling the whole island with a bit of stop over would already take you 2 hours. Not much to see in the island, a bit of flowery patches, mermaid statues and lighthouse and that's it.

If you are a UNESCO World Heritage Site ticker, this is on the list. I?m not a cave fan, so walking into the lava tube, taking a u-turn and walking the same way out in the damp and dark, jostled by rude kids on a field trip wasn?t one of the highlights of my trip. In any case, no regrets going there because it would be weird not to go at all -- it?s a Jeju landmark, and I would have wondered what I missed if I didn?t come here.If you?re checking out the Seongsan Ilchubong, it's pretty close by (if you're in a car). You should allot another hour for this. It?s not too far from the Jeju airport, too.The thing is, once is enough ? if I were to come back to Jeju and my friends insist that we go here, I would let them go ahead and hang out somewhere else.Like the title says, it's a cave.------Tip for parents:I tried to warn a family with a baby that it?s not the best place if you have little kids, but they ignored me. Hello, it?s dark, with water dripping and the terrain is uneven rock. You have to walk down some steep stairs for about half a minute to start your tour. There are a lot of people, and sometimes they bump into you because they can't see well in the dark. That family was going to take a baby stroller into this cave. Wah, suit yourself. It was so insane. If they trip in the dark, the baby could be hurt.

If you are a teddy bear fanatic, you can give it a visit. I personally like teddy bear and was exciting to visit this place but after the first level, it was overall the same bear with different costume and theme showcase in the window and it's all in KOREAN! So U don't get to read the history of what being showcased. Only those with pictured like lady Diana's wedding, Roosevelt, Marilyn monroe are some examples. And the bear not that cute compare with some other bear I have seen before. It's very pricy too for you to get the bear. Paying for a premium but the quality is not that good. I ended buying a bear key chain as a remembrance n there is not hand carry bags for it. They charge KRW500.I was just wondering if I were to buy the bigger sized bear, so I still need to pay for the hand carry bag? After all, visitor pay for the entrance fees and it's much more than the KRW500.
If you are a car enthusiast, this is a great place to visit. They have a broad range of cars and an area where kids can drive a car around a track.
