review: If this place was in Europe I am sure the entrance fee would be double or triple, and it would have a giant shop at the end. This place is full of hard to believe facts, artsy stuff and little experiments. To be honest, I would really like to see a little shop at the and, so that I could send a postcard or add a pencil to my collection if not buying a few sciencey gifts. Definitely spare some time for this place, you will enjoy!

If possible, I would recommend visiting this garden on a cloudy day or partly sunny. There is something peaceful about the weather and the garden that makes you want to stay forever. All the bonsai trees are beautiful and wonderfully taken care of. You can see how much great care was given to these trees. The plants, the rock artworks, and the people all create a very peaceful and very unified picture. This place is fitting for people of all ages. I would recommend everyone visiting this place.

If it's your first time visit, definitely take the path to Oedolgae. If you have time, from the main entrance, take a left and it will take you along a path along the ocean. Go about 1/2 mi walk along the path and you'll see off on your right a smaller path. Take this and it will take you down to the ocean. Many locals take this down and it's a small watering hole where locals go to swim and fish. Once you get to the bottom, the navigation along the rocky formations can be challenging but very much worth it. It's not a beach but you're right next to the waves as they come in. It's absolutely beautiful. Just for context, I took my 8 year old daughter and 6 year old son. They had to be careful navigating, but was able to do so with adult supervision. Many others have come to appreciate this but they have been leaving their trash behind and it's quite saddening to see such a beautiful place littered with garbage. If you do go down, please respect the beauty and take your garbage with you.

If it’s springtime?or even summer or fall-- that means it’s also time to think about visiting beautiful Gapado, or Gapa Island, which sits just off the southwestern tip of the Korean resort island of Jeju. ? Located some 5.5 km (3.42 mi.) offshore, Gapado is a quick ferry run from the port village of Moseulpo (maybe 20 min.)Gapado nearly got the distinction of being South Korea’s southern-most point, but that title went to nearby Marado.? Some tourists want to go there just to say they’ve been, but Gapado is noteworthy in its own right.? Gapada is home on its .84 sq. km? to about 250 residents.? The island has a picturesque school, a church and a Buddhist temple.? There are a couple Korean restaurants and small stores.? But, it’s a good idea to take bottled water and snacks with you, particularly if you plan to hike or bike all the way around the island.? You can bring your own bike, or perhaps rent one there.? Walking (Gapado has a 5k hiking trail that is part of Jeju’s famous Olle Course) or biking/electric scooter likely will be your only transportation choices, as there are no fossil-fueled vehicles on Gapado… But more about that in a bit.What makes it so special there?? Gapado offers spectacular views of the iconic mountain peaks or “sans” back to the north on Jeju, including Sanbangsan, Gunsan, Songaksan, Gogeunsan, Dansan and the Big Daddy of All Sans, Halla…the massive, central shield volcano that formed Jeju Island and the highest peak in South Korea.Equally impressive are Gapado’s golden-green barley fields, surrounded by traditional “batdam” stone agricultural walls.? The crop begins sprouting in late winter and reaches its full glory in late spring.? Gapado’s tradition of barley cultivation dates back to the 1840s and is celebrated annually with the Gapa Green Barley Festival. (Dates for 2015 are April 18- May 10.)Back to that transportation thing…well, barley is not the only thing green about Gapado.? Wind turbines, solar panels and other renewable, sustainable forms of energy are now being used on the island as part of a plan to make it one of the world’s first carbon-free islands, maybe THE first…. Summing up:? Good points:? outstanding natural beauty and photo ops in all directions; fresh air; clear aqua-hued seas that reveal black lava rocks; abundant hiking; colorful neighborhoods festooned with murals, recycled art and traditional Korean cultural artifacts;? site of annual Gapa Green Barley Festival? (April 18-May 10, 2015)Be sure to have on hand:? bottled water and small snacks; comfortable shoes; sunblock;? sunglasses; and a hat that won’t blow off easily; a stroller for very young children, layered clothing for coolish days.? There is little shade on the island, so be on guard against dehydration or sunburn on those hot or even excessively windy days.? Getting there:? Take an Intercity Bus from most points on Jeju Island to Seogwipo Main Terminal, and from there, a local bus to Moseulpo .? There is a short walk to the ferry from the busstop.? Ferries generally run twice a day, but as schedules and fares can change, it’s probably best to check for specifics through the Korean Travel Hotline: dial 1330 in country or outside Korea: +82-2-1330 or 1339 (Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese)

I?ve never been this near to the base of a waterfall before.  No railings, just the raw power of a thunderous fall.  And a rainbow!  The kids loved jumping from rock to rock.  This may be a little precarious on a wet day, but we were lucky with the weather during our visit.You do get some splashes.  So if you have very expensive camera equipment, you may want to protect it?  The walk up was a little tiring, but not overly so.Absolutely love it.  A must see!

I wouldn't say this is a must visit attraction. Our driver took some time to show us this place since we were passing thru. The kids found it somewhat interesting, we spent about 10 mins trying out the optical illusion in the car.

I would say that this waterfall is higher and have better view than cheonjaeyeon waterfall althought cheonjaeyeon waterfall is close by from teddy bear museum, we take taxi in the afternoon from teddy bear museum to jeongbang waterfall and it cost around 25-30 usd, and the street is almost empty. The road down to the waterfall is much nearer and easier than cheonjaeyeon waterfall. When you take pictures, off course you would like to get closer to the waterfall, but be carefull of the rocks, they were quite slippery, we spend an hour to take pictures and sitting in the rock. The admission fee on nov 2014 is still 2,000 won per adult about $2. On winter it opens from 08.00 to 18.00

I would highly recommend this place for an extremely hot or wet day.  Being covered and large enough, it was an enjoyable walk.  There was adequate lighting and enough fellow tourists not to make the cave walk too scary.  Despite the unevenness of the terrain - they are dried lava and so quite uneven, most people would be able to walk comfortably.It's certainly a nice change from limestone caves although some people may miss seeing amazing rock formations like the stalactites and stalagmites in limestone caves.  In fact, I was not overly impressed with the gigantic lava mass on display at the end of the walk.  For me, the enjoyable walk was good enough.

i won't repeat what others have mentioned.personally i love this place.i went during spring in april 2017,weather was perfect.food was presented beautifully,the latte i had was delicious.the garnishing is really insta-worthy!my friends and i had breakfast at the outdoor area,overlooking the tea plantation.some of the skincare product sold was exclusive to this outlet,glad i bought a few.would surely return if i happen to visit jeju again.

I went to Udo with the ferry, the queues were super long to buy the tickets but it was quite fast. The island was very crowded. I got a normal bike for 10000 won. Go to the shop on your far right. the shop straight ahead when you inboard the ferry is super crowded with Korean tourists who look for a 3 wheel scooter. These scooters are everywhere. You need to be super careful as no-one really knows how to drive them. The island is super popular among locals. Thousands of scooters and selfie-hungry teenagers looking for the best pose next to the lighthouses. Moreover prices are high and the island is full of plastic rubbish (bottles, cups, bags). I would only recommend to go during low season. But most probably the rubbish will still be there as some piles looked already quite old. The peanut ice cream is nice but not worth the money.

I went Thursday morning with my girlfriend and it was quiet enough. Nice walk, but be prepared for stairs and bring water! The bridge you can cross is exquisite and crazily steep (so be careful in the winter). The views are outstanding on a clear day.I really enjoyed this site; the wooden walkways, the history behind the irrigation channels and of course the waterfalls really kept my interest.Would recommend!Shane & Jill

I went there because I have never been to a volcanic cave before. It was interesting, with lighted signs describing different rock formations, but overall, the experience is average. The cave gets colder the deeper you walk into it. It is about 750m one direction, a total of about 1.5km walking. The cave is cold and damp, so be prepared with a jacket and good walking shoes. Water drips from the top of the cave, and there are also puddles of water, so take care while walking in there, and wear a pair of good shoes that has good grip.There is no public transport that goes directly to the caves. We took a public bus, but after alighting, we had to catch a taxi for a ride to the entrance of the attraction. If you are going to visit Jeju, know that the attractions are all over the island, and it is not easy to get around on public buses. Most people join a tour, or get a taxi to bring them around for the whole day.

I wasn?t expecting much but the displays were certainly fun and interesting. Can see that?s lots of care have gone into it. Great for photographs with the missus and if u have kids, this is heaven for them. Around an hour to walk the whole museum.

I was very excited to visit Jeju; and this probably one of the most accessible place by Bus. There's actually public transport to this place (Yongduam Rock) from my accommodation. However, when I reached this place , i was busy looking for this legendary dragon head rock. Much to my disappointment, the rock doesn't seem to look like dragon head, you must really view it from the other side with your imagination.However, in order to reach to the other side, you need to climb all the way down the stairs, Not recommended for elderly. And if you notice carefully, you will spot alot of cockroach crawling around the rock, that totally freak me out!! Very big turn off if you spot the cockroach.the period I went was very crowded, probably around 5-6pm, This timing was quite a good timing for me, as I manage to catch a sunset. The sunset there was relatively awesome with the endless view of sea. If you can walk all the way down to those seafood stores, whereby you can enjoy fresh seafood hot pot + splendid view of sunset & sea!
I was very excited to see that road, but when you are in the car the feeling is not as obvious as you may imagine. Worth visiting but nothing spectacular

I was traveling solo via public transportation, I arrived there 30 mins early before it opened for public that day. For it's 1st month of Spring (April), most of natural attractions were free admission. Good thing it was free, though I appreciate it, it's not really astounding as I though (well, as per my perspective).From downtown of Jeju, take bus 701 (East Route). You can ask your hotel reception of the bus stop. It would be easier if you have private car (especially for group traveler). Alight at Manjanggul Entrance, walk about 25mins, you'll pass by Gimnyeong Maze Park (roughly 15mins walk from bus stop). Not for a person who's kinda frightened to walk alone in a road of unknown :) You can wait for bus 990 the only bus that passes through Manjanggul Cave yet it isn't frequent.Just follow your path way back, if you're lucky enough, a taxi would offer you a ride for a certain price roughly KW3,000. You can negotiate the cost. In my case, I negotiated for KW2,000 which I think is reasonable enough. Yet when I'm about to pay, I only have KW50,000, the driver doesn't have any loose change, so he asked only KW1,000, I still have none, instead he just took the last coins I have, KW700.

I was really impressed by this museum, designed by the famous Japanese architet Tadao Ando. The architecture of the building and the beautiful garden make this place worth a visit, but the collection is also really interesting. I really loved the collection artefacts from the late Joseon period an the special exhibition 'Carriage to Heaven' that shows sangyeo (traditional funeral bier) and kkokdu (small statues used as decoration for the sangjyeo). The joyous artwork of Japanese artist Yayoi Kusama were a nice extra on top of all that.Not to be missed when visiting Jeju.

i was quite amazed to this natural wonder and i had not seen any falls which ends directly to the sea. its very close the segwipo city. You need to walk down around 100 step to reach the bottom of the falls. Careful near the bottom the stones r slippery and if its raining better be watchful for the waves. Its a delight to watch the gorge. We went to this place when it had rained a bit so the water fall was in full flow. Due to heavy wind and cyclone in china the sea was rough which added to the fun!!! one of the most memorable place i visited in jeju,highly recommend it.

I was in awe of the waves and how high we stood on the cliff against the shore. It was a little scary as at some point, I wasnt sure if we might fall. But it was a great place to look at the sea and take a stroll there.

I was here with my family. Thinking what is so mysterious about this road? Its just a road, with nature on the sides. It?s just another ?normal? road. Sigh, a total waste of time.Until I reach the place, I was blown away! Not because of the strong wind (I was there when it was raining heavily with strong winds), but the mysterious part of this road. I was told to stay in the car, to witness the mystery of this road. The engine got turned off, hand brake was let gone, brakes were let gone too, the car automatically went up the slope by itself!It is a new experience here for me in Jeju, a totally worth of time to visit!

I visited Seongeup Folk Village as part of the tour package to Jeju Island that was provided as free gift by a company that I need not mentioned here. As an Asian and having extensively travelled throughout Asia. I am familiar have experience all sorts of tricks and gimmicks. The first tip that this was another hard sell stop is that there is no time limit for the stop. Prior to this stop, we visited the famous Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak, they insisted that we returned to the bus by 1 hour which is not enough to really enjoy the place. However, we were told we can take all the time we need at Seongeup. Then a nice looking old lady who can speak Mandarin were waiting to greet us and give us a tour of the place. I was curios why no such tour guide were organised for Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak. The whole tour of the village was short 15 minutes, most of the info she provided I can easily find out from internet, then we were ushered into a room in one 'village building' where she proceed to let taste and test their natural products and tell us how miraculous is the products, the tea, the honey, horse bones and horse cream. The whole presentation took twice as long as the village tour. Then she went on and on and on about how healthy are the people and it is due to the miracles of horse bones. I mean come on. There are horses the world over. Surely if horse bones are the key to living longer and younger,.Someone other than the Jeju people would have known about it. Then next she talks about pricing which I almost fell out of my chair. Korean Won 190,000 or USD 185 for horse bones pellet? I am not sure how many fools are there in the world that bought into this ludicrous claims. Right there and then I wanted to leave. She then changes tack and describe how they money will help preserve the village, fund village children education healthcare etc etc. I heard that before in almost all my travel. Apparently, some of my fellow tour travellers are interested, so they stayed in the room while I explored the 'village'. The area is very small, most of the 'buildings' are similar to the one that I was in and there are various product demo sessions going on in other 'buldings'. In the end, we spend a total a 2 hour there and the organizer waited until everyone got onto the bus. It so different from the Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak stop where they chased back onto the bus and even went into the washroom to look for missing passengers. Just for non-asian travellers tour organiser gets sales commissions if the tour groups buy something. So they benefit if when they spend more types at such places rather then the actual sight that you wanted to see.

I visited here with several work colleagues.  We had a great time and laughed so much trying to make our way through this maze.  Built by a westerner and former professor over a number of years, the time, planning and care that went into making the park are all quite easy to see and appreciate.  It is beautiful there, very green and clean, and close to Manjang Caves, another iconic Jeju attraction.  Negotiating the maze took us about 45 minutes...longer than we thought...but we laughed our way through it.  Once you make it to the center, you can climb up to a platform and ring the   finder's bell.    Great for photo ops.  They also have some traditional Korean games just outside the end of the maze...fun to play if you never have.  At the snack bars, they offer delicious Jeju-brand ice-cream.  And as a BIG added bonus for my fellow cat-lovers, LOTS AND LOTS of mascot cats, belonging to the mazepark builder.  He is now a retired gentleman, known for his affinity for cats; journalists and business persons who go to meet with him in his office are likely to find both his desk and his person draped with one or more of his uniquely colored cats...black, orange, brown, white and grey.  A GREAT activity for families (although very young children may tire unless you take them in a stroller); couples; and colleagues...good team-building exercise:  Who can lead us OUT of here?  LOL  You'll enjoy it.

I visited here with my family, so we drived our rental car. But if you don't have an international license, then rent a bike or motorcycle.You can rent it in a reasonable price.There are 5 bus stations here and those are nice sights.There is a beach in two sights and one of them is a popular site for jet boat.And the other one is popular for water leports.And whole Island is a heaven for riders.If you love mountian bike or road bike, then take your bike to this island.This is a perfect place for cycling.And there are many nice restaurant and dessert cafe, so enjoy yourself here.

I visited Hallasan in early March, some parts of the trail were still covered in snow. At the lower area I had some difficulties because of the melting snow. It's doable without crampons or walking sticks, but be careful. Past Witseoreum shelter, it's recommended to have walking gear. I have an average condition and I did the Yeongsil trail up in 2h15 and the Eorimok trail down in less then 2h. I think it's better to do the opposite. Yes, Yeongsil trail is longer, but easier. The Eorimok trail is covered with rocks, and if you don't watch out, it is easy to twist your ankle when coming down.

I visit play kpop by taking bus 600 from sogwipo harbour. It was very exciting experience. Even though it is a hologram concert, it feels like a live concert and my wife won the card selection and my wife?s hologram was on stage and yonghwa singing for her. I never seen this technology and appearance anywhere else. Play kpop need to improve the 360 3d cinema because it makes visitor feel dizzy and to improve the sound system. Anything else is okay but need to pay every single shots with the celebrity. Overall i give 5 stars for the experience. Thanks Play Kpop!
I tried walking and rolling in car to feel the effects of such claims... no luck, felt cheated... at least the kids had fun.

I thoroughly enjoyed myself. It was so entertaining and fun to watch. Definitely worth going to see!! Ours was the blue team. I booked and paid direct from their website. It was very simple. Just sign up for a membership, pick the theatre, the date, time and the type of discount. Please read-up on their terms and conditions for each discount. Payment was done via credit card. I managed to get my VIP tickets for 45000KRW each and sat at D17, 18. The seats were just nice, not too far and not too close. Although maybe E would've been a better bet. Different locations have different discounts and it varies according to the different months, so just check out their website.Jeju NANTA theatre is a bit run down and the toilet wasn't very well-kept... Also, be prepared to be surrounded by bus loads of tourists from China (as with most tourist spots in Jeju.... )

I studied the seoqwipo bus route and decided to bring my family for a day trip to Udo Island. I stayed in Jungmun Resort vicinity. It was easy to catch bus 282 from here and made a transfer for direct bus to Udo Passenger Terminal. Upon arrival, after filling up the necessary details and proof of passports竊we went to the cruise Departure point. Luckily we chosen a weekday for this trip. The queue was short. In the cruise ship, we could find seats. A 15 min ride and we were greeted by several e-scooters and shop houses. Here, you could settle for lunch. But if it was too early for you, several sightseeing spots come with line of restaurants. We took the circular bus (white color van) which we thought was the best choice. Every stop you were  required to queue to abroad. This bus went to most attractions including black sand & Udo lighthouse. The bus route was also the route for E-scooters /car. Do be careful for safety sake. Returning from Udo Island was amazing : we could not find a bus stop that for the same bus number  supposed to bring us back to Seoqwipo! Nevertheless, luckily we had alternative plan ! we took a bus that brought us to Gimpo Airport. Got a decent dinner and then took limo bus 600 directly to our accomodation, alighting at bus stop named Jungmun Resort Entrance. This DIY by public transport comes in cheap!This trip you need a whole day.

I stayed 4 night in Hamdeok Beach. If you are visiting Jeju for the very first time, you might want to move around because Jeju is quite big. Hamdeok is a great location to start your trip. It takes 20 mins by car, 30~40 mins by bus from Jeju International airport. It has many bus lines which offers you easy access to Airprot, Mountain Halla, Jeju city centre and even Seogwipo. I love the beach itself, but also there are lots of place to eat and chill. If you like to camp, there is a camping & caravan park at the end of beach. I loved it !!

I started from Eorimok Trail and came down by Yeongsil Trail. Eorimok trail starts off with steps then followed by wooden walk way before you reach Witseoreum Shelter. Shelter is a basic one with just toilets and resting rooms. We took around 2hrs to reach the shelter. Yeongsil trails starts off (from shelter) with wooden walk way then followed by countless stairs. You are like literally hiking on the edge of the mountain up/down. We took 1.5hrs to descend.Definitely recommend going down by Yeongsil trail rather than heading up due to the countless number of stairs. Both trails offer truly beautiful scenery and great for photos. I cant forget the view which the horizon mixed with the sea level that you can differentiate. Stunning!Advice:Bring food like energy bar, fruits etcBring water enough to reach water points. There are a couple of water points for you to refill along Eorimok trail. Else 1.5 litres for 2 pax is enough.Bring jacket and wear hiking shoes. Sports shoe is possible like what most korean did but be v careful as you will be walking on uneven rocks at times. Probably suggest ankle guard to go with sports shoe.For those who want to scale the mountain but doesn't wish to try the 9-10hrs climb to summit, i would really recommend this 2 trails.

I specifically spend half a day here during my trip at Jeju and has no regret. We rented a electric scooter with KRW30k for 2 hrs, do note that you need International Driving License to rent it. We had burger at HahaHoho cafe and the Pork burger is delicious. The landscape and view is so pretty. The road is narrow so I don't recommend you to drive rented car there. Udo island trip is definitely one of the highlight of our trip to Jeju!

I simply love this place! It's so peaceful and so beautiful. When you arrive the island, u are spoilt for choices in getting around the island. U can travel via car, atv, bike, bicycle or tour buses. I will suggest bicycle. It is really very threaupitic to cycle the whole island which is about 16km. You definitely need more than 4 hours so go as early as you can. The beaches are so beautiful. Water is crystal clear. There arent much shower areas near the beach tho so do think twice if u wana swim at the the beach. Do check out the lighthouse at the top of the mountain too. Udo is famous for their peanut icecream. If you are a fan of peanuts, do go try it.

I saw the review and decided to give it a try if I ever manage to find this location from the Korea GPS (we rent a car).Lucky enough we discover this road when we were heading to Love Lands. It's just right after it! So we drove to the starting point and off the engine and yes, it is moving! (Even the road is up hill a bit).Then we park the car aside and walk towards Love Land, but we saw many people were trying to walk in a backward manner up the road (which you suppose to feel hard/difficult bcos it is up hill), and backward manner down the road (which then strangely you felt like something is pulling you back even you are walking down hill) So I would say this is a very good experience and I'm glad that I experience this! But my friend didn't really feels anything when she tried the walk, so I guess it also depends on individual's physical sensitivity towards this mysterious road...
I recommend you this place if you have a rent-a-car. It?sa very long cave, and registered as a UNESCO heritage.

I really loved this waterfall. Just the way you can chill on the rocks and look out to the ocean or the waterfall itself. You can also get close to it also which is nice (unlike Cheonjiyeon Waterfall which in my opinion pales in comparison). It costs 2,000 KRW to get in and my advice is set aside a few hours to just chill. It's really wonderful. There is also wifi so you can video call your mates and show them how much their lives suck compared to yours. I got the 781 bus from Jeju bus terminal (3,000 KRW and 50 mins) and got off just as you get into Seogwipo (best use an offline map with gps). I wandered towards it and it's actually not that easy to find. The waterfall is on the west side but you want to get to the east side to view it. If you can't find it, there's a Buddhist arch/gate thing you can see from the main road. This marks the correct path and takes you in front of Seobok temple (Seobok temple should now be on your right and some well kept walled gardens on your left). Keep walking and you'll see the entrance. Note: as you walk on this path you'll be on a bridge at some point. If you carefully tread over the side garden you can look over the wall and see the top of the waterfall, it's not that spectacular but might as well grab a look.

I really love this place, sooo much. You can reach this place by bus number 710 from Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal directly, trip around 90 minutes & pay for bus fare by T-Money. This bus route passing some attraction in Jeju, so please stop at the attraction you wants to visit. You can rent a car too. From bus stop at Seongsan Ilchulbong, you must walking around 300 meters. What i loved about this place is, so many seafood restaurants (because it really close with ocean) & some Korean cosmetics shop too. Don't forget to bring jacket, umbrella and of course mineral water. If you have strength, you can climbs the hill (around 500 meters). But so much fog when i'm there, i can't see clearly the basin. You will met some elderly people here, at the peak. Fresh air & green vegetation will makes your eyes & breath feels relieve. You can buy some souvenirs when you get back to the foothills.

I really enjoyed my visit here. I've never visit a volcanic cave before but its an very cool place (literally!). The temperature in the cave is much cooler than outside, although be careful, because they keep it quite dark so it can be difficult to walk on without good shoes.

I read many negative review about this place from other travellers but for me, it was quite an interesting place with strange phenomena going on. My taxi driver brought me here on the way to Seongsan and he show me what is so mysterious about this road and it was indeed very strange. He stop the car at one end of the road and the car will automatically move up towards the slope (even when the car engine is not on). It was just an experience and one will not spend more than 10 minutes here. A good short trip before going to other places.

I read a few reviews saying how it?s just a park with trees and birds but I love this place! The greenery is beautiful, the air is fresh with a cool breeze and the cave system is entrancing. Being from a concrete city means all this is actually quite a refreshing change of environment for me. I don?t particularly care for the animals and birds being kept in too small enclosures though. But the scenery alone is enough to give it 4*.

I reached Jeju around 1pm and planned to go to Hyeopjae beach for the sunset, since Hallim parknis just 5minute walk away, we decided to go there while waiting for the sunset. Entrance fee is 10,000??. My personal opinion, I don't feel it's worth it. I came with my friends on a budget trip, and we are from the tropical side of the world. There's nothing much to see for us. The birds, The tropical Garden, The palm trees, The water park, there's nothing much there to impress us. Unless you have a lot of time to spare in Jeju (unlike us), or you plan to sit down and relax (because it's a nice place to relax and enjoy nature), you can skip this place. To be fair, I did enjoy the cave walk and tye bonsai.To go there: take bus #702 from Jeju intercity bus terminal, before you board, tell the driver you're going to Hallim Park and swipe your T-Money card. It took around 1hour for us to reach there.

I only went up this trail for 1.5 hours then came back as that was all I wanted to do.  I took my time and because I did that I saw deer which many people just walked by not noticing.  The trail is quite rocky.  You need good boots and cotton gear as you get quite hot. (All the Koreans dress up in this synthetic mountain looking gear and my husband who went all the way up said they were all nearly passed out on the side of the track from over heating!) Some people had these HUGE packs on their backs.  God knows what they were carrying! I had 2 bottles of water and dried octapus for sustenance and that was enough.  My husband who went all the way up used 7 bottles.  You can buy water at various places up the trail so you don't have to carry it all. There are a lot of people who do this ...or try...so it's best to start at 6am to beat the crowds.  There is also a train of sorts that you can pay for to take you most of the way up.  Not sure how much that costs.  There's a restaurant at the bottom surprisingly that's all in Korean,  no English, no pictures, which is odd for such a big tourist area. They have a beef soup, sushi rolls Kim bap and other stuff.  I'll upload a pic of the menu so you can get a translation before you go there.I'm not sure if you have to pay a fee to climb this track as we just walked up but on my return I did see a ticket box so maybe you do...

I love visiting botanical gardens whenever i travel.? Unfortunately this is one of the poorer ones and I feel compelled to warn others!? With an entry charge of 7000 won per person, the value is low.Let's start with the greenhouse, it was just ok, nothing exciting.? During sunny days, the greenhouse is like a toasty oven as the ventilation is poor.? There is a variety of plants but they are not well organised or well kept.? Moreover, if you live in tropical parts of Asia, you would have seen most of the fruit trees and plants in neighbourhood backyards, which makes visiting it less exciting.Besides the greenhouse, there are themed areas - e.g. Korean garden, Chinese garden, French garden etc.? I was excited to see these options but after seeing what there was at the Korean and Chinese gardens, i just gave up on the rest.? I don't have the confidence the others will be worth the time.Management of the garden needs to be improved.? When I was there, they were renovating the entrance to the greenhouse.? As a result, the smell from the paint, varnish or whatever that toxic smelling thing is, is overwhelming.? Also, there was lots of noise.? Garden management would have better managed the renovation or at least inform visitors there is renovation going on.? I tried to offer feedback to the folks at the ticket counter on my way out but they didn't seem to care.In summary, there is nothing much to see and the garden is not well taken care of (even if there is no renovation going on, I would have rated it 'Poor').? Go to this place only if you have nothing else to do.The only plus I can think of is ... parking at free!

I love the atmosphere in the cafe as there was not many people when in was there in the morning. Enjoyed view of the field and the food by the fireplace and it was really cosy. The black pork sausage was not bad. If this place had been full of people, then maybe I wouldn't fancy it as much...Heard that there is also the DIY soap making activity but I didn't go for it. As for products, I didn't purchase any as the price is the same as Seoul and there was no deals. So it didn't make sense to carry all the way until my final city.

I love hallasan so much, this is definetly the camp, although it was winter when we got there, but really its very beautifull .... I cant imagine , hallasan when spring ... For get in here, there is bus station 15 minutes walk from the foothills, but dont know exactly the number of the bus, because we hire rental car for only 20.000 won !!! Its amazing right ?? But sadly hallasan didnt have any restaurant or proper rest area for us to enjoy the view, or it because the winter season, i dont know ...

i like this waterfall that connect to the beach but i dont understand why they have to take entry fee for that because its really close to car park.other than that, all good. beautiful and huge waterfall cool you down.

I like the structure and set-up (the wooden boardwalk and handrails) and it looks majestic when I step past the ticket entrance. In the wide open space, it feels you have so much freedom to run around! If I had came earlier, I would have joined the Jeju Woman Diver performance (1.30pm and 3pm daily). No regrets since I headed to Udo before coming over and that was even more amazing! It requires certain level of stamina to climb up the flight of steps but fret not! There are stone chairs along the way, not many though, for you to sit and rest.The young kids and senior citizens are surprisingly the more consistent climbers up the stairs!Despite rating 4/5 due to my liking for the crater and natural structure, my actual experience there is only 2/5. There were large crowds of extremely rowdy and unruly chinese tour groups who spoke loudly at the top of their lungs, their tour guides shouting several times for them to gather and start moving down with no avail, zero consideration for other visitors who also paid the same ticket price to see this UNESCO World Heritage site. No way you can enjoy a peaceful moment and respect the site. They stood around various areas of the steps and took ages to complete their group photo. I have seen many tour groups before but the ones I encountered were horrible. It would have been good if the owner or caretaker of this site can do something to regulate and not spoil every visitor's experience at this place...

I highly recommend a visit here! My friends who came to visit said it was their favorite experience on Jeju.The sandstone cliffs have been intricately carved by wind and water over the years. They are stunning up close, and most days you can see crustaceans, interesting bugs, and other life in the tide pools. Check out the gorgeous bright-blue water. And possibly see some women collecting shellfish and sea urchins to eat and sell!Be sure you walk all the way around the point. It's easy to think you can't, but the narrow path hugs the rocks to make a loop. Beautiful and totally worth it!

I have visited Sunrise Peak (Seongsan Ilchulbong) for sunrise hikes on three occasions this year. Each was very different, but all pleasant. Things to consider:- The hike is all steps, but only takes about 20 minutes for a moderately fit person.- The top is always windy. If it's already windy at the base, make sure everything you carry is tied/contained, because it can be very windy at the top.- It costs a small fee to enter when the ticket booth is open. If you get there really early, they might not be open yet!- No bathrooms after you leave the parking lot (and no secluded places), so plan accordingly!- Nothing at the base will be open before a sunrise hike, but you should be able to grab coffee/donuts after!- It's nice to carry up a picnic breakfast and sit at the top to eat and watch the other tourists.- Check the weather before you go if you really want a good view. We had a couple cloudy days that were less spectacular, but still always a refreshing hike, beautiful mountain and cool views over the ocean.We usually pair our trip with a trip out to Udo Island or to some of the other east-coast attractions like Manjangul Caves.There's a lovely motel paired with a seafood restaurant about 10 minutes walk from the entrance to the peak hike. Follow the beach sidewalk almost to the edge of town. Views from the in-room balconies over the beach. Big rooms and nice folks, even if they don't speak any English.

I have read many Super review of Mr Kang being a good driver. I decided to use his service. Diana and 2 others took a 2 day taxi tour with Mr Kang on 14-15 Jan 2020. Mr Kang, though English is limited, we did not have any difficulty in our conversation. He arrived at our place on time. He was very friendly and a careful driver. He was very flexible as we changed our itinerary last minutes. He also suggested some nice places to visit, and good and cheap resturant to eat. The food was sumptuous. He took photos for us every places we visited and they were so well taken. He also helped us to carry our luggages up to our new location, 3-storey, without lift. He had done beyond his duties. We were much appreciated for his great help and service.We enjoyed our 2 day tour with Mr Kang. Will highly recommend him to my friends.Thanks Mr Kang, who made our journey so comfortable and pleasant.

I have quite mixed feelings about the NANTA show, but the criticism is not with the show itself but with the overall experience. This review is for the show in Jeju-do.Positives:It was very easy to book tickets on line even from abroad. Once you create an account and log in, you are able to see ticket availability, choose your seats and pay for them. An online confirmation serves as your ticket until you turn up at the theatre on the day and get physical tickets. They send you a reminder via email before the show, and you can cancel up to a day before the show.The show is very funny and our whole family laughed a lot.My dad commented that the seats are more comfortable than the theatre seats in London.There is a parking lot if you are driving in.Negatives:The location in Jeju-si means that if you are staying in Seogwipo-si (as we were) then it takes over an hour to get to the theatre. And over an hour to get back home to your hotel after that.The show is catered to tourists as it doesn't use any Korean language to communicate its humour. As such, you will be surrounded by people who talk throughout the show. There's nothing you can do about this, they are really having a fun time, but you need to be aware about it. Or you can just join in and make loud comments too.There are no catering facilities at the venue so if you are driving in you need to think about where you are eating before or after the show. Fortunately just opposite the car park, across the road, there is a row of restaurants - just pick the one that you like.The toilets were filthy on the day we visited, and this was even before the show started. Since we were there for the early session at 5pm, I just don't know how the toilets can be be in such a disgusting state, unless they were not cleaned from the night before.Finally:If you are visiting Seoul, you can watch the NANTA show there too at several locations in the city. That might be a better option if you are not staying in Jeju-si itself, as the driving was just too tiring from Seogwipo-si.

I have climbed Mt Bogong in Australia, Mt Kinabalu in Malaysia, which were both taller than Mt Hallasan, but I find climbing Hallasan most challenging! We took the bus to Seongpanak. The path is all uneven as it was paved with lava rocks, all the way to the top! My poor feet were quite sore the next day. Make sure you have proper hiking shoes. Definitely not recommended for children or people with knee problems. It was raining and quite foggy when we reached the top, so we couldn't see the crater unfortunately. We were pleasantly surprised at the half way mark where that is a little shop selling instant noodles for 1500won. You can also buy mineral water for 1000won, which is the same price as in the shop in the city. I would have thought they would sell it for twice the price! They are strict about the timing of your climb. It was summer, so the cut off time at the halfway mark was 13.30hrs. If you couldn't make it there by that time, they would not allow you to further climb up to the peak, which is fair enough. We wanted to hike down Gwaneumsa but it closed due to falling rocks, so we had to hike down the same way we came up. Before you leave, you can always pay 1000won for a certificate with your name printed on it (at the foot of the mountain, there is an office near the toilet areas, where they usually collect payments for climbers that come by cars. If you take the bus, you do not need to pay any parking fees). You'll have to show a selfie photo at the top of Hallasan, in order to have the certificate. The person manning the office is not very good with computer. He took forever to type out names. Overall, it was an interesting experience.

I happened to notice a separate entrance desk that had pictures of SCUBA divers on it. I asked an attendant nearby in simple English sentences if they had any SCUBA diving and how much was it? It was only 119000 KWon and they happened to have availability right away! I've dove in other aquariums but this was the cheapest and didn't even require a reservation on a busy day! Note: I had to present my cert card.I was taken to a back area above the large exhibit where I was given a 5/7 wetsuit (the water was a little chilly) Meres booties a weight belt and weights mask regulator ScubaPro fins and BCD.There was a shower room for women with two open shower stalls. They do not allow you to wear anything under your wetsuit. I was given a small basket to store my clothes but it was difficult to keep them totally dry. I recommend giving them to someone or renting a locker out in the lobby for delicate items. After donning all my gear I got to check out the fish   hospital   above the aquarium where sick fish are kept separate until they are healthier. There was even a sea turtle!Each guest diver was assigned a guide but mine let me wander freely once he observed I could dive. There was only one other guest in the tank so that was nice. Otherwise it was just me and LOTS of sea life. In the tank there were lots of sharks: black tip nurse leopard small hammerheads. There were lots of large sting rays and schools of fish too. It was fun to interact with the guests too! I'd swim up to the glass and wave at the kids. They loved it!I still had to pay the separate entrance fee for the aquarium (about $40 but I received a 20% off coupon at the airport) but it was worth it. The exhibits were very well done there was lots of food to eat while wondering around and great picture taking opportunities. Would definitely go back.Note: A lot of the aquarium features the image of a whale shark. Apparently they had two a few years ago but one died and they released the other one so they are no longer there.

I flow to Jeju just to walk up this mountain.  You have to apply to the  Hallasan National Park visitor management system for the QR code admission ticket. My ticket was for the Gwaneumsa Course, time slot 5-30am - 8-00am.   I started my walk at 7-50am,  It was perfect walking weather, overcased so not too warm.  There is a 500 hiker per day limit on this route to the top, on the other easier route there is a 1000 hiker per day limit. The first few kms is easy going and you think to yourself this walk is going to be a piece of cake.  After around 4 kms you reach the first of two public toilets on the route.  From there the walk becomes a uphill slot with countless wooden steps. On the way up there is two downhill's with maybe a couple of hundred steps to walk down before walking uphill again.  After the second public W.C.  the route is a never ending series of wooden staircases until at last it flattens  out and the top of the mountain.  When I did it there was maybe a hundred or more walkers queuing to get a photo next to the summit stone.    I just gave my phone to a person and asked them to take a photo with the stone in the background. Within minutes I was on my way back down.The reason why you need a photo with you and the summit stone (even if it over your shoulder in the distance) is to claim your Certificate of climbing Mt, Hallasan. On the Gwaneumsa Course you can self print your certificate at a booth just past the QR-cord booth at the trail head  If like me you are clueless with mobile phones you can go the manned QR code booth and them to do it for you.  There have a printer in the booth and was very happy to do it for me.   It costs 1000 won (around 1 us$) Facts and figures, I am a 73 year old Englishman on an extended holiday in Korea.  Start time 7-50am, summited at 11-05am.   Started down at 11-15 and back to the trailhead at 12-55pm. Yes I do class myself as a bit of a mountain walker so these times  are maybe a little faster then average, but mountain walking is about enjoying yourselves and not about how fast you can get up and down. I took a litre of liquid, in hindsight I should have taken more and I did finish it off when I was within sight of the carpark. There is a shop across the road from the carpark.   Food, I took no food just a few sweets and a couple of chocolate bars.  So the bottom line is you have to take all the food and drink with you.  It does say that you can get drinking water at the second WC (shelter) but I could not find any so don't depend on it. Getting back to Jeju City.   There was no buses so I started walking the 8 miles back to my hotel on the seafront. Pleased to say that  I did manage to flag down a taxi after around a mile.  All in all a very enjoyable day out on the mountain.

I first saw this falls on the local map I received. I investigated and stopped there using the airport limousine bus route no 600. I find this cave beautiful as it is made by nature. It is just 1km long, it is good for a short trip. The place is cold, that's why Koreans go here in the summer. I didn't reach the summit but hiking the Eorimok and Yeongsil trails didn't provide amazing views as far as I was concerned, but it's definitely worth doing.Take the 740 bus from City Bus Terminal to Eorimok (krw1800, 45 min) or Yeongsil Ticket Office (krw 2800, 60 min). Bus leaves CBT at 07:00, 08:00, 09:00, 10:00. You don?t want to set off after 10:00 as you won?t get back! Last returns are 17:36 (Yeongsil) and 17:55 (Eorimok) April through October.I took the Eorimok trail up (there?s an easy 1km walk from the bus stop to the trailhead) and reached the Witseoreum shelter in 2 hours, including stops. The first 2.4km are quite tough but it gets much easier the further you go. If you?re worried about your ankles then wear hiking boots but trail shoes are fine. The descent down via Yeongsil was a leisurely 90 mins but it feels like it would be a slightly tougher climb compared to Eorimok. There?s also a 2.5km downhill walk from the trailhead to the bus stop, so bear that in mind if you decide to start from Yeongsil. The scenery is much better on Yeongsil, although those with vertigo may find it tough, even with the very good safety barriers on the route. Eorimok doesn?t have those problems but the first 2km is under forest cover, with little scenery to admire for most of the climb.If you want to hike to the summit start very early, which probably means you'll need a car in case you miss the last bus back.There are clean, normal toilets at both entrances and at the Witseoreum stop. You will have to carry all trash back down as there are no bins anywhere on the mountain. You can buy hot instant noodles at the Witseoreum but you?ll have to carry it back down. I bought several buns and pastries at Paris Baguette for my hike.

I decided to see two waterfalls down south at Seogwipo! Jeongbang fall is one going into the sea.A bit rocky if you would like to have a photo been taken in front of it as close as possible. There are always many people down there, be careful of your steps when taking a nice photo!I like the fall as it?s open to the sea!
