I couldn?t resist visiting this place on our way from Jeju city to Seogwipo. It made me giddy as a child. Entry fee is now 14,000 won per adult, and either 11,000 or 13,000 for children. This place has optional guided tours and accepts credit cards. Small room of Hello Kitty history and how her image has evolved since 1976. Original design merch on display. Lots of interactive rooms for kids and 3 floors to play. As an adult I still had fun and enjoyed a Hello Kitty hot chocolate (her face is in the cream), and Hello Kitty-shaped strawberry mousse cake in the cafe. You?re paying for the experience, here, so if you or your child is not a Hello Kitty fan, don?t waste your time. The maze on the roof is shaped like Hello Kitty from an aerial view and is strictly for children?the maze walls are only about 2 feet tall. My favorite part was the art exhibit (2nd floor) and all the small, unexpectedly perfect details (heart shaped straws, Hello Kitty toilet paper!). Souvenir shop: a mechanical pencil costs 7,700 won (more than $6)?I guess this is slightly more than American Sanrio store prices. But, if you?re willing to visit this museum, you?re probably also willing to pay for a momento of your experience.

I completed every single course over a period of a year so the following comments are just my opinions. If you are staying for a short period of time in Jeju courses 6 and 7 are the most popular and will probably get the most from. Both are very scenic and you will get to see some of the major sights. If you start at one of the information sites, you can pick up a Jeju Olle guide which has maps and information of the trails, guides for the Buses, to get to and from the starting points. Also I'd recommend downloading Kakao Maps app on your phone and you can zoom in and see the actual trail that you are following when you are on it. It comes in handy especially for me when I made a wrong turn on my trips. If your doing the entire course I'd recommend buying a jeju Olle Passport. Carry it with you and get it stamped at the starting points and halfway way points of the trails. I was living near jeju city and caught most of Buses from the Jeju inter city bus centre. The 101/201 express buses will take you to/ or near a lot of the starting points but I'd recommend picking up the Olle Guide first and the info in that is invaluable.Most of the Starting points are close to the roads unless you are going to one of the 3 islands. I used booking.com most of the time to book places to stay overnight as I don't speak Korean. Jeju has a lot of places to stay and there would be abundant places to stay except for maybe a couple of the more remote locations on the trail. There are offical Olle trail Hostels throughout the trails to which are very nice. If planning for no Korean speakers just check before hand that you are not traveling on a Jeju holiday as a lot of paces close down and might be harder to find a place to stay. Of course take plenty of water and there's usually 7/11 of CV's around the place where you can get snacks to eat.The trails themselves are very beautiful , Different scenes ranging from Black volcanic rock on the coastlines, Forest trails, Beautiful beaches, Hill sides, a lot of Oreums (Jeju extinct volcanoes) small towns with a chance to see wildlife and a lot of friendly people. For myself my favourite trails were routes 11, 18-1 Chuja-Do island), 1-1 (Udo island), 7. For me the stronger trails were on the southern eastern point of the island starting from route 6 through to 15.Getting to the supporting islands it you might take note you will need your Passport to catch the ferry to Udo. You must show it when buying a ticket. There are a lot of ferries going most of the day to Udo. They have a very nice Peanut ice cream there. The smaller island Gapado at the time I went there were only 2 ferries in the day and its not the most reliable service and the ferries can be cancelled due to bad weather can be cancelled due to bad weather so check beforehand if you can. Chuja-Do island was one of my favourites. When I done it they had 2 ferries a day and you can not do the whole trail in time to catch the next ferry back so be prepared to stay over night. I have heard of instances when the weather turned bad and people had to stay a couple of nights on the island because the ferries were cancelled so just plan for that just in case. it is a beautiful Island though and one of my favourites.I would also recommend going and joining the Olle Walkers Facebook group. They take guided walks along certain courses and have great information about weather and so forth. all you need to do is contribute to the group from time to time.

I chanced upon this wonderful beach along Ilchul-ro Road while my family and I were on our way to Breeze Bay Hotel. I returned to the beach in the late afternoon and my family and I went to the same spot again the next day early afternoon. On both occasions, I parked our car at a car park that’s got just a few cars. Gwangchigi Beach is very long and the spot that I was at was near to a erected stone put up by the Rotary International. The good part was that there were very few people on this secluded beach. The better part was that Gwangchigi Beach is a black sand beach (yes, we finally experienced a black sand beach). The best part was the beach offers a marvellous view of the south-western face of Seongsan Ilchulbong. Using a pair of binoculars or a telephoto camera lens, you could see visitors climbing the stairways as well as the summit of Seongsan Ilchulbong.Moreover, walk along the beach and you will find unusual rocks and rock terrain just beyond the black sand. I believe the rocks arose from the explosion of an underwater volcano long time again that created the Seongsan Ilchulbong. During the late afternoon or sunset, the sunlight produced a beautiful array of black, brown, orange and green (algae-covered) colours of these rocks. Because late afternoon is where low tide occurs, the sea water was trapped within the rocks as ‘ponds’ ? and there were beautiful reflections of Seongsan Ilchulbong on the still water. Alternatively, you could walk on the rough brown ‘mat’ (not sure what’s the material) that was laid on the grass. It was along this mat path that I saw a horse that was tied to a pole. I guessed the horse was used for horse-riding but I didn’t see such activity as it was already past 5 o’clock in the afternoon.Gwangchigi Beach is one beach in Jeju that is under-rated and not well known. It warrants being among the top 10 beaches in Jeju. Anyway, I recommend visiting it as part of the Seongsan Ilchulbong experience.

I came here expecting mundane rock formations. Ohh how wrong I was. This is one of the most beautiful places in Jeju. The rock formations are gigantic and so artfully formed. Be careful when walking as you're walking beside the water and it can get slippery. We even sampled some fresh raw seafood like sea squirt, sea cucumber, sea snails and octopus with rocks as table and small children chair as our seat! No soju for us as we're driving!You park at the base of Sanbangsan and walk across the road to reach Yongmeori Beach. Entrance fee varies depending which location you want to visit.

I came here by bus .. so I waited for the bus and cars to go on neutral and watch them drive up he hill hands free.Some people poured water while other rolled a water bottle.Since this attaction takes less than 15 minutes, i would suggest also going the Jeju Art Museum next door :)

I arrived that place on a sunny afternoon.When I entered the cave, I immediately felt very chilling and refreshing!I was really amazed, beautiful formation from the lava, 'elephant toes' 'cupola' etc.The floor is wet and uneven, so be careful.

I am sorry to say it but it was a boring place to visit. It would be interesting if we didn't have internet to get to know the world. By the way, my 8 year-old son was scared on the second floor to see all the torture instruments.
I am not sure I will tell others that this is a MUST GO place.  We spent 5 mins taking few photos of the rock, enjoyed the breeze before going back into the car.

I am interested in world heritage and Manjang Cave is included in sites of Jeju's world heritage so I went there. I had never walked inside a cave before, so it was an interesting experience. And I appreciate the carving in the walls and the shapes of rocks that were formed by volcanic activities.The temperature inside the cave is colder than the temperature outside, so it's better to bring a jacket.

I am a huge fan of Udo.  I have been numerous times and I never get tired of exploring a new road or a new cafe.At times it is soooo overrun by tourists that it can be a little overwhelming, but if you are smart and plan your trip during quiet times of the year, it is really rewarding.  The roads are quieter, the stores less busy.  There are numerous ways you can tour the island:I usually take my car.  I have heard that NO rental cars are allowed on Udo anymore.  so be aware of that.But once off the ferry there are so many scooter and electric bike shops* around.  *Foriegners be aware that you do need a license to rent these!ProTip:  I absolutely recommend you get off the beaten path and go explore the inner part of the island. So many cute cafes and splendid views!

How they get the cars, coaches etc up the hill with the engine switched off is a bit of a mystery,I thought some kind of electro-magnetic set up under the road, then if that's the case when people poured water onto the middle of the road surface, why did the water go uphill and not downhill. Do not think it is an optical illusion as it certainly was a hill that went up and down, I walked it !.

Hiked up to the summit via the Seongpanak trail. A 35 minute ride on the 5.16 bus from the Jeju main bus terminal drops you off right at the entrance to the trail. Great hike up. Took me a little under 4 hours including a 30 minute detour which breaks off from the trail to go see the Saraureom. This trail is mostly wooden steps. Both the Saraoreum and summit crater lake were dry, but still beautiful. I do not recommend relying on the   store   at the Jinderaebal shelter. They do have hot water if you want to bring your own instant noodle mix. Bring your own food and be prepared to bag your garbage and carry it. walked down via the Gwaneumsa trail which is a bit shorter. I defenitely recommend this since the trail also has a different type of scenery, including a beautiful bridge crossing. Not sure if there is a bus back to the city from the bottom of the Gwaneumsa trail, but by the time I made it down (3 hours) I was ready to take a taxi, one of many which are available which cost me 15,000 Won (about $ 15) back to the city. Certainly worth it. Overall, a beautiful and amazing experience.One last recommendation would be NOT to attempt this hike with less than proper hiking shoes.

Hiked to the top of Hallasan yesterday morning through the Gwanmeusan Trail - started at about 7:10am and were back in our car at 2:30pm - so this start and finish time includes breaks, and you'll need them even if you are in okay or good shape. It was a bit disappointing to see the majority of water bodies in the mountain are dry at the moment - just a few ponds on the early parts of the trail, and the crater lake at the summit, which we expected would be much deeper. The trail has a combination of dirt, rocks, and steps/bridges. I wish the steps and parts of the trail didn't include so many sharp rocks - your feet WILL feel them! We did the hike in running shoes because we don't have hiking boots here. I can see the climb being a lot easier with hiking shoes. Some parts of the trail are very steep so if you have serious knee problems, I don't think this is the trail for you. Do bring lots of water and snacks - we had two liters of water for each of us and I still think my husband got dehydrated rather badly. There is really nothing to eat on the trails so bring snacks. Visibility yesterday wasn't great - pollution has been pretty high in Jeju the past couple of days - but it's still a GREAT, BEAUTIFUL view from the top. I loved all the flowers you see growing in the rocky sides of the mountain in the last third of the trail. Very happy I did it and it's a great hike, but there is not a lot to see before you get to the top. We went down the same trail, so a total of 17.4kms. It'd be interesting to see what the other trails are like, but I don't think I need to summit again.

Highest mountain in Korea.  Beautiful area.  The wife and I went in midweek hoping to beat the crowds.  Forget it.  masses of cars, buses and people.  At 10 am on a weekday we sat in a line of cars for approx. 80 minutes just to get a place to park.  Once in, the hike was pretty strenuous.  Bring a hat and sunscreen.  We got approx. 2/3 of the way up (in a horde of people) before the park employees turned everyone back saying there was a   big wind coming  .  It was a nice sunny day and no visible weather to be seen.  Oh well.  I will probably try again when I come back.  But I will be sure and get here at daybreak and try to beat the crowds.

Hi all!, we visited this place on 1 July, 2017. It is indeed a good place. when you are almost fatigued with seeing big big places such as Seopjikoji, Seongsan sunrise peak, you can visit this place while returning to Jeju si. the entrance is really amazing. Lots of tall and large stones will welcome you. We took lots of pictures there.  There are different carvings of stones of different types. There is a gallray of stone-made sculptures. We also noticed a nice water reservior type of thing. Really nice place.

Hexagonal shaped rock formations jutting out of the ocean that reminds me of the kryptonite crystals I once saw in an early Superman movie. Unusual and definitely 1 of the places to see if you are in Jeju. Entrance is KRW2000, 50% off if you are below 24 ? foreign ID accepted. Unfortunately, since the best view is only through a series of stairs which ends at a platform, weekend crowds in bus loads can be a nuisance for that desired background photos effect or even a selfie. And I was continuously concern about the strength of the viewing platform to hold so many people at any one time. I got there in a rented car and discovered fields of canola flowers up front for good picture taking.

Here is the best was to try the experience of climbing up the hill Come from the loveland (from the north) and stop at what seems to the bottom of the hill (there will be a sign on the other sign of the road)Stop your car, go in neutral put you warning signals on.Make sure there is no pedestrian and car behind you and release the break The car will start climbing the hill in reverse mode It is a bit dangerous as there are lot of pedestrian and potential drivers that dont understand what you are doing but really the best way to experience the illusion

Having visited limestone caves in other countries before, what was different about this experience was the stalactite or staglamite looking structures were not made of limestone but lava.  The walking surface was very interestingly grooved unlike limestone caves but called for very careful walking at parts. The lava stack at the end of the section open to public was pretty awesome and is helpfully bathed in lights so one can see.What I wanted to point out is that we happened to visit at a time when many Korean schools send their students out on educational trips (we visited in early April).  So the lava tube was full of noisy teenagers who seemed more interested in shouting out to each other and seeing who could run through the tube fastest than in appreciating one of nature's wonders.  Seems like Korean teenagers are just like teenagers everywhere else!  So if you are going in early April, be warned.  If it is going to bother you then better give this a miss because you will be in a dark confined space where sounds are magnified.

Having never seen a lava tube cave before, we were very keen to go here. We live on Jeju Island so it wasn't a terribly long trek to get there. Not exactly on the beaten path, but not too far off either. Once you arrive, there's a small information center that explains the history, science, and mythology surrounding the cave. There's also a restaurant on site, which we didn't use, and then there's the short walk to the cave entrance. Here's the only reason I didn't give this a rating of 5. I have some minor mobility issues stemming from multiple knee surgeries and the entrance to the cave is a fairly lengthy and sometimes steep set of stairs that can be wet and slippery. Once you're in the cave, however, it's not too bad to traverse unless you have much more significant mobility issues. There are a few places where you have to go up ramps or small sets of stairs, all of which are industrially produced. The cave itself is quite dark and damp, and I'd recommend long sleeves if you're prone to feeling cold. Definitely wear good walking/hiking shoes as the cave does not have a full walkway installed. You're walking over ground that is solidified lava. It's about a 1km walk to the end of tourist access where there is an impressive lava column, which they claim is the largest in the world. There's an observation deck approaching it, but you cannot go past and actually touch the column. Along the way, there are decent informational placards in multiple languages, including English. The explanations are reasonable for most people, including children, to understand. Our kids, ages 7 and 5, enjoyed the experience, particularly because you could get right up beside the cave walls and touch them, along with other artifacts inside the cave. For anyone interested in geology or volcanos, it's a great experience. Price is reasonable too. We paid 12,000 won, which is currently a little over $10 US, for four people. Supposedly children under 7 are free with ID, but we didn't ask about that for our younger one.

Having never been to a lava cave before,  this was definitely a new and cool(literally,  because it is a few degrees colder than the outside temperature in the cave) experience for us. There's quite a bit of walking involved-about 1 km in almost darkness. There are a number of different formations such as stalactites, etc marked along the way, until you finally reach the lava column. If you don't have a car, getting here is quite difficult since the bus stop is almost 2 km away-the walk was very beautiful though, along one of the oreums.

Having been to the sex museum in China near Shanghai I was somewhat disappointed by this one mostly because I found it more biased and sexist than I would expect a museum to be.  It started out good with a fairly progressive and balanced presentation albeit almost entirely in Korean talking about sexual freedom and equity.  But the vast majority of displays were very...vanilla and heteronormative.  There was very little depiction or discussion of anything besides sex between one man and one woman.  Furthermore the depictions of women and closeups of vaginas far outnumbered depictions of the male form with many showing women in very submissive poses such as on all fours and wearing a leash!  There were even a few instances where the English text accompanying a display used rather judgmental language describing certain sex acts as   abnormal   or   depraved   which I found very shocking.  I think it's great that Korea which is typically very conservative has a museum about sex at all.  But to a more sexually progressive westerner it will probably seem outdated and disappointing.  It's also hard to get to if you don't have a car.

Having always wanted to see the cliffs off of Northern Ireland, it was a pleasant surprise to see these interesting hexagonal basalt column shapes on the coastline of Jeju Island!  There is a wooden walkway/stairway with informational signs along the way.Restrooms are near the entrance/ticket booth.  There are typically cart/street vendors hawking various foods/fruits/veggies and other items here and there throughout.  There was a local photographer with his work (varying in size from postcards to poster-size photographs) which were of breathtakingly beautiful scenery around Jeju Island.I would definitely recommend this as a stop on your trip around Jeju Island.

Hamdeok beach is just so beautiful. It offers you black rocks, white sand, and breathtaking views. It was our first destination for the day after we landed in Jeju. I found the beach quite peaceful and calm. It is very near to Hallim park. Just took us about 2 mins to reach the park by a car. I wish we could spend some more time at the beach but we had to rush to our next destination. Good place to stop by and click some nice pics. Good luck!!! :)

Hallim Park is quite a beautiful park. There are so many things to see, and the flora is really quite spectacular; however, the living conditions of the animals in the park killed the whole experience for us. The turtles are in aquariums that are much too small, and the aquariums don't contain any kind of natural vegetation for the turtles. In fact, only a few turtles had only a single rock in their containers. If that wasn't depressing enough, the living conditions of the peacocks were, quite simply, inhumane. Although some lucky peacocks got to roam around in an area that was relatively open, most of the peacocks were living in small enclosures and sharing those enclosures with up to 13 other peacocks. There was hardly enough room for them to move around, and the birds seemed to be living in quite stressful conditions.  Then, there were the ostriches. All of the ostriches we saw had a terrible looking skin condition, and most of them were going bald. Compared to the flora in the park, it just seemed like the park put no effort into properly caring for the animals at all. If Hallim Park would put a little more effort into making sure their animals are properly cared for and provide better living conditions for the animals, I would recommend going to this place. However, with the current living conditions of the animals, I absolutely cannot recommend anyone go to this place.

Hallim park is part botanical garden, mini zoo, and culture center. The majority of Hallim is mediocre, but the jewel of the park is its rich bonsai collection. There's an extensive range of bonsai trees at display, some of them are over 300 years old. To those unfamiliar with bonsai trees, they may just be miniature trees; but to those who know the value of these works of art, these bonsai trees are literally priceless. In fact, it's almost unbelievable how openly accessible these trees are to the guests, considering their value and need for extreme care.If you're planning on visiting, briefly study the artistry before your trip to enhance the enjoyment. This is a one-of-a-kind collection.

Hallim park is huge from the inside. You will need a lot of time to cover the entire park. We took almost 2 hours to cover it. But it contains beauty at its best. We went there in the month of May and there was so much greenery all over the place. It has so much to offer inside which includes flower garden, bonsai garden, bird garden, water garden, botanical garden, caves and so much more. You can get yourself clicked with the beautiful backgrounds everywhere. Its completely outdoor so do not forget to carry your shades and a hat or a cap on a sunny day. Also, do not forget to wear comfortable walking shoes as there is so much of a walking. They have marked the directions inside for every attraction so it was super easy for us to follow them and cover the entire park. All in all, a very good park and a must visit if you are going to jeju.Good luck!!! :) :)

Hallasan is Jeju?s massive mountain, and was once a volcano. It peaks at 2000 meters, and from 700 meters up, the only way up is by foot, and you?ll have to drop your car at a designated area to begin the climb. The best place to start the trek is Seongpanak, on the East side of the mountain. Going up takes about 4 hours, at a normal pace, this trek will take all day. There are two checkpoints that you much reach before a certain time of the day to be allowed to go all the way up (and come back down before sunset). This means that you absolutely have to go there early. I was at the foot of the mountain at 9am, and I wouldn?t advise anyone to start climbing after 9:30 if you don?t want to be turned down. Also, since this can be exhausting, pack beverages and food before going up. There is a small shop at Seongpanak and another one at the 1500 meter checkpoint, but they have very limited choice. Just stop at a convenience store in the city before going up and you should be good for the day. The climb is relatively uneventful for the first 2/3rd of the way, with fairly little to see because you?ll be surrounded by vegetation. But once you reach an altitude of about 1600 or 1700 meters, you?ll start getting a great look at the top of the mountain and more importantly at the rest of the island.  Once you reach the top, the view will be amazing. The volcano?s caldera feels like being on the moon, and you can also see Jeju?s coastline as well as its major cities, Jeju and Seogwipo. Absolutely breathtaking! Make sure to check the weather if you plan to go there, because the tall mountain tends to attract clouds, which could completely ruin the awesome view you?d get on a clear day.

Halla Mountain or Hallasan is one sadistic hike. For the month of May 2018, Gwaneumsa Trail is the only trail open that summits Halla. Seongpanak is having maintenance done.We did Gwaneumsa Trail... with one slow hiker... we got to parking at about 7:30am and we were walking by 8:06am. It is beautiful and green, especially in Spring. There is one restroom stop about 1/4 way and another 3/4 way at Samgakbong shelter. There was no other support. Take water, take food, take toilet paper just in case.READ: There is only one potable water stop. It is after Samgakbong about 3.5 hours into the hike at the last downhill before the bridge and start of final red part of trail. There is a hose at the corner at bottom os stairs before the bridge. Fill up here both going up and down.Also wear good walking or hiking shoes. We witnessed two people's shoes rip up and one guy had to walk back 2.5 hours with no shoe. There is no rescue for small issues. There is a supply cart that goes up once or twice a day but only for serious rescue. There is AED in Samgakbong shelter too. No food for sale when we went in April 2018.The reason for the difficulty is the climb and distance... mostly on volcanic rocks... large ones... and lots of stairs of wood and of stone.We left at 8:06 and back in the parking lot at about 5:30. All day event. 9.5 hours going slow up Gwaneumsa Trail.

Haenyeo literally means, 'Women of the Sea' and this museum pays tribute to the historical significance of this dying profession.  Solely carried on the backs of women on this island, these incredible ladies have carried their over 400 year old craft into the 21st century where instrumentally built the economic foundation for many of the Jeju natives.  Mothers who passed on their skills and knowledge of the sea to their daughters ensured that this lineage would endure the centuries of time.  However, as the world faces rapid changes and economies - the Haenyeo divers are slowly becoming a ghost of the past.  Recently recognized as an UNESCO intangible Cultural Heritage in 2016, tremendous efforts are in place to preserve this historical tradition.  A bonus of a visit to this museum is a trip to Sunrise Peak where there is a traditional Haenyeo performance.  (admission fee required)However - enroute to Sunrise Peak is the opportunity to meet a handful of Haenyeo divers!  What a thrill to visit with them in their modern 'bulteok' - warming huts.  Of all the sights of Jeju - this is perhaps the one that represents the very backbone of this amazing culture!This is definitely a 'must see'

Had a lot fun going through this maze. Don't use the map because it will spoil the experience. We kept on running into the other tourists that had the same look on their faces because we couldnt find the exit. But you could tell they were also having fun no translation needed. Took us about 45 minutes to finish the maze. Only problem was getting there. The nearest bus stop is a bit far and taxis are few and far in between.We took a cab going to the bus stop and planned on splitting the cab fare with other tourists. Turns out the driver wasnt using the meter and asked us to pay 2000 won each. We didn't argue too much with the driver because we were trying to catch the bus plus he didnt speak English. Just be careful because this might also happen to you. This was the only bad experience we had in Jeju (the cab ride, not the maze).

Guide is good explaining about the village and oldtime Jeju. We came here by chartered car, not really sure how to come here by public transport. For me this place not very special, it's just different with typical hanok house that you ever see in Seoul or Jeonju.

Great visit for the curious or those interested in nature and/or rocks. Nimble feet required. Numerous formations and lava sights to see and learn about.We took a taxi from Jeju city, around 22,000 won one-way. Very inexpensive entry fee though!The lava tube is more than 7 km long and 1 km is open to the public. There is modest lighting throughout though the footing is uneven at times. But hey, you're in a cave. We saw some Korean tourists carrying their infants to and fro inside! It took us more than an hour total to explore the whole thing.It gets really cool (temperature-wise) down there, so those sensitive to cold should bring an extra layer.

Great Views, Must Go, Wear to walking shoes, Not Baby friendly for Strollers as you will have to climb a lots of stairs. If you have child?s on stroller make sure you carry Baby Pouches/Bags for carrying the baby. Drink the Tap Water - Very Springy & Natural.

Great day out doors. Many options of travel within the island (drive from mainland, rent bicycles, various motorized vehicles) making it really easy.Roads are narrow so personally would avoid driving. Further the ferries can only hold that many cars which means expect long wait times during peak periods.Many nice small eateries for coffee or ice cream along the way. Beaches are really pretty too and water clear though I didn't see anyone swimming in dec (winter).Only thing that I didn't quite like was the rentals were pricey at 70000 won for 3 hrs (two motorized bicycles and one two seater). And that was after some bargaining . The guy mentioned that it takes 45 min to go around the island without stops
Good to walk , and watch local food and ingridients...specially seafood, and souvenirs. Dont forget to pick up  ginseng to carry home.
Good place to have a relaxing walk in a natural forest. It's not a long hike, about an hour, and there are flat trails. Check out the cafe that has nice tea beside the car park.

Good driving views.  You will be blown away. Should visit this place in the morning before 9am to avoid the crowd especially during weekend. There are so many trails.  Please ensure you know which trail you are taking as the mountain is so huge.  Must wear proper trekking clothes and shoes. If you are driving, please ensure you go down the same way as you climb up or else, you need to get a cab to bring you back to your car. Bring water, snacks and plastic bag to throw your rubbish. You must bring down your rubbish with you.

Go with an unknowing mind.You can easily find the explanation for this phenomenom but don't! I didn't, so when my car rolled up slope in neutral, I was thrilled! But it lasted at most 5 minutes so not for people with an already packed schedule. An interesting side trip for those who have time though.

Getting here was tricky, as you must take a bus from either Jeju or Segowipo and even then the bus stop is 2km from the entrance so usually taxis cruise past and you can do them a deal. It is pricey to reach and has an entrance fee (half price for youths under 25 with valid passport) but has full facilities such as restaurant, shop, toilets, lockers etc, It is a little cold underground so recommended to bring a jumper or warm clothing. It is incredible to be underground in a volcanoe and there are numerous info signs in various languages along the route as you walk underground to the cone. It's a little dark for photos but if your camera can be adjusted there can be some great shots. You must walk quiet far and it can be wet on the ground so proper shoes recommended and flip-flops/sandals avoided. I saw plenty of kids but obviously it is dark so may be a little scary, plus it's quite a fair walk so think through if you want to walk about a mile to the cone or just have a quick look. An interesting trip for sure!

Getting close to the waterfalls looks easier than it seems. However, that adds to the thrill of getting nearer to mother nature. It is tricky manuvering around the wet, slippery & sometimes unstable rocks & boulders in cold weather. Many a times, you find yourself balancing precariously on the boulders or have your feet stuck between the rocks as you slip or slide from the smooth rocks. You will also find visitors around you lending you a hand to help you get back on your feet. Such spontaneous camaraderie !  For the young & agile, it is fun watching them jumping from rock to rock, like Tarzan in action.  It is a thrilling on the rocks experience not to be missed !  And you get rewarded by the beautiful sight & sound of a great waterfall!

Generally, a great place to shop for mask, body care, face care products with great prices. Do beware of some shops do actually give a kind of face/attitude if you touch or even asked for prices ( please note that, most shops dont include a price tag) after you  decided not to buy.
Full of antique cars, if you are a car lover, definitely worth to visit this museum! But most of the explanation is in Korean.
address: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관

review: From the Jejusi bus terminal we took bus 201 to Udo. It took about 1 1/2 hours. Definitely download the app Naver to navigate your way around the island, as Google Maps does not have any results for public transportation. We spent 4 hours on the island. Ferry ride from the port is only about 15 minutes each way. Buying a ticket can be a little chaotic as there are no signs in English but we just held up 2 fingers for two passengers and were given 2 round-trip tickets. Upon arrival in Udo expect to be bombarded with shop owners yelling at you to rent bicycles, ebikes, motorcycles, or 3-wheeled cars (for 2 people). 2 people renting 2 ebikes for 4 hours cost us 40,000 won. Need int?l drivers license for the latter 2. I definitely recommend the ebike over the bicycle unless you really want to get strenuous exercise. Lots of hills and 11.4 km of trail to follow. Lots of little mini-towns where you can buy food, have coffee or peanut ice cream (recommend). Tons of photo opps so take your time. We finished in 3 hours, 40 mins (and my hubby wanted to stop A. LOT. Last ferry back to Jeju is at at 5 pm this time of year. Plan accordingly.

From our recent experience and what our driver/guide told us:(1) rental cars: totally not allowed in busy summer. We visited in October so his car was allowed to take us onto the island, and still it was very crowded with the scooters and the bus, after a two day closure due to the wind(2) bring your passports (or other ID): although we had a rental car and were not going to rent any scooter, we were still asked for the passports before we boarded the ferry(3) when you plan your itinerary, if Udo is a must for your trip, be ready to make flexible rearrangements due to weather. We had to change our hiking in Hallashan due to a two day closure of the ferry service because of the wind. Check your weather forecasts as you get close to your Udo visit. If you plan to stay there overnight, also ask for cancellation or delay policy.(4) snacks not to be missed: peanut ice cream and peanut rice wine (although I should say it's a snack!) peanuts are local on Udo Island(5) reserve a whole day or most of the day if you want to fully enjoy Udo.  Even we had a car, we found it quite rush with some time wasted on the traffic (and it was only October, not the busy summer!)(6) romantic?? The reviews below were quite right about the beep,beep, beep.......of the scooters and the bus so I guess if you really want a Romantic Udo, it's better to stay overnight and after all the day visitors are gone, I think you should be able to enjoy a serene starry sky (but we didn't stay I could only imagine....)Enjoy Udo!

From Jeju city it?s quite easy to reach by car. I had rented a car so no problems with public transportation or finding cabs.Going to the caves with a cab won?t be the problem. Unless you have instructed your driver to stay, you will get a problem to find a taxi.The cave can be a bit wet and slippery, so don?t go there thinking you are going to the beach. Dress accordingly is the advice.I found it quite interesting and definitely a must see when you are staying in Jeju.

Friends, my husband and I rented ATV's, Scooters and a Golf Cart to check out this island. It was so much fun touring around and stopping at the beaches and different view points. We even saw the diving ladies who dive by only holding their breath! This wasn't the most spectacular views of Jeju we saw but the adventure was a lot of fun!

Friendly staff: worked hard to communicate with me in English as best they could.  We took the B course for horse riding.  The leader allowed me to guide my own horse as I am an experienced rider, which I appreciated.  The leader guided my daughter's horse.  Horses were well trained with kind temperaments.  The horse show was well rehearsed and the riders and horses were skilled.  My daughter is 8, and she loved the show.  After the show, we fed carrots to the horses for 1000KWN a piece.  I would recommend buying a horse riding ticket as soon as you arrive because there was a 95 minute wait for use to ride.
Free stamping art in paper , handmade soap you have to pay , No make up for sale here , only mask , perfume , hand creams, skin care . Love the view outside from this cafe .

Free carpark. There?s a replica fountain of the real lava column which is found at the end of the tunnel. Entrance costs 1000 won. Descent about 80 steep steps into the tunnel. Temp change can be felt immediately. Floors are damp from the rain and the water drippings from the ceilings. Best to have a hoodie and raincoat or an umbrella. The tunnels are very dark and damp. Go slowly and let the eyes adjust to the dim conditions.  There is a marking at 850metres which is great as it is difficult to gauge the distance while walking in the dark. Then you will have 150 metres more to go before reaching the end of the tunnel open to public. The world?s largest lava column, 7.6m in height is located at the end. Advise: wear sensible shoes with good grip as the floors are damp and slippery ; warm clothing; carry a torch- or use your phone?s flashlight. It makes the trek so much easier. Lastly, restrooms located at the surface level are decent though damp and a bit stinky.
Forget Lotte Duty Free, You can find almost every Korean Skin Care Brand here, TheFaceShop, Etude, Isoi, Banilla , Nature Republic, etc, all with cheap price and lots of bonus.
For you who look for car rent and and experienced driver in Jeju, I highly recommend Hi Jeju Taxi Tour as your option.

For visitors arriving by bus: Take Bus 201 from Jeju Intercity Bus terminal and get off at the Manjanggul Cave Entrance Stop. At the same stop, wait for Bus 711-2 to reach the actual Manjanggul Cave site entrance (transfer at KWR 0 cost if using T-money or CashBee card).Note: It's a 2.5km distance from the Manjanggul Cave Entrance Stop. Being a UNESCO Heritage site, we had expected a much better set up for the cave site. Overall lighting could be improved; brighter lighting for better visibility of the rugged paths and water puddles along the 1km lava tube (reduce risks of slipping or tripping as a fall could be quite fatal).The temperature underground can get chilly so be sure to wear warm jackets/coate and proper shoes with good traction (saw some visitors in flip-flops and sneakers, and they ended up almost slipping).

For us it was a bit of a disappointment that we would need international driver's licence to rent 50-125cc scooter/motorbikes/small car like vehicles on the island. So it is a good thing that they have the electronic scooters, which don't require the licence. They are way cooler to cruise around the island with.It was a clear sunny day, and we spent 2 hours driving around the island, stopping every now and then to enjoy the scenery. There are a few places to visit on the tour so no need to rush around the place. Be sure to make it to the last boat back to the mainland in time (for us it was 5:30pm, but people kept coming there late so it left just before 6pm). From the boat we were able to enjoy the setting sun, which was a great finish for the trip. The boat ride there and back was reasonably priced, and the scooters we got were 25,000KRW for 2 hours. We went there a bit late so the only minus was that the place available for us was with no insurance for the scooters. Still, if you visit Jeju and have extra time on the east side of the island, be sure to visit udo!

For those that love fish, this market is a place to visit. Very interesting but not for me. You can also shop for shoes, clothes, chocolate, souvenirs and fruit. I found it a little on the dirty side but it might be because I don't care for fish much.

For someone with bad stamina like me, it would take about 2.5 hours to reach the end of the trail.The tip is, to go there early in the morning, then you can take some leisure time to rest from time to time. When we're going down to trail at about 10p.m., there are lots of people coming up the trail and it is quite packed with people.For person with knees or legs or ankle problems, must be really careful as I fell down several times due to rocky trails at certain places. However, the view along the trail were awesome and it feels really worth it! The warm ramyeon at the shelter was the climax!I went in April 2016. The wind is super strong on top. So make sure you're ready for that. Hotpack, jackets, windbreaker or whichever deems to keep you warm. You may not need them in the beginning of the trail but you might need it in the end of the trail.

For only $10 (10,000 KW) you can spend an afternoon wandering around a carefully manicured small park that exhibits outdoor glass work. As you walk in there is a place to watch professional glass blowers blow bottles in the traditional way, and if you are taking a school group there, the kids can have ago at making something, and then return the next day to pick up their handiwork. After that you follow the path around the exhibits until you get to the other end.In this mainly outdoor museum, there are glass plants, flowers, and an eclectic collection of glass made curiosities that make a very pleasant way to spend a couple of hours. There is a small cafe in the middle of the exhibition, and the gift shop just before you exit. The bathrooms are at the entrance exit, so go before you start!

For most people, this place is kind of hard to reach because the public transportation in Jeju is not really comfortable. But if you rent a car, you really need to visit this place.You need to take ferry from the east part of Jeju Island. Inside of the island, you can borrow a bicycle to travel around the Udo Island. Don't miss the authentic ice cream of this island (see the pictures).

for me there is nothing special about this cave. the only thing we can do is just walking straight through the cave almost 1km (cmiww). and after we arrive to the end of the tunnel , we just see a small stage and some pic as i remembered. if you traveling with child , pls be carefull when you step the floor. because its really slipper..

For 1st time hikers climbing Mount Hallasan, take note of the different hike trails AND the closing time for each trail. This is especially if you drove on your own and parked at 1 of the 5 (one of the locals told me there are 5 different car parks at different foot of the mountain)If you are climbing Mt Hallasan to reach Baengnokdam (the crater top), do not take the Eorimok trail as it does not lead there. I made the 1st mistake taking this trail and the trail ended 3 quarters way up the mountain and you only get to see the side of the mountain top. I made the 2nd mistake not watching my time and could not descend Hallasan from the trail (Eorimok) where I came as apparently it closes at 2pm, and there was a park warden stopping me from taking the trail back and kept ushering me to take the other way (towards Donnaeko trail) to descend. The descend took 4 hours and the trail was treacherously full of rocks. You could tell that it was a trail less taken as there were over-grown bushes covering parts of the trail. Your only guidance of where to go was a      thin cord string tied from tree to tree and red strips of cloth tied on the string. If you weren't too careful and lost sight of the guiding string, you may actually go off tangent of the trail. There are no lights, very few signage and are all in Korean, so if you are like me with no understanding of Korean, good luck. And that wasn't the end. Donnaeko trail actually ends up at Donnaeko cemetery. So when I got to the foot of Hallasan, it was pitch dark (6pm+ and no street lamps), by myself, and I had to walk for 1 hour through the cemetery to get to Donnaeko car park (which was 30 mins driving distance away from Eorimok car park where my car was T-T).

First, the name was really eye-catching. Everyone wouldn't deny that. The road was short, doesn't even reach 1km. Although we have read the explaination on how come everything that were put on the road will be rolling upside the hill, not downwards (this is the mystery), we were really excited as we turned our gear to neutral, and the car keep going upward by itself. It was fun :)We also drip by walnut pie cafe just beside the road. It was delicious!!

First time in a cave, so I really enjoyed the experience and learning about the history of the formation of the cave and Jeju island itself. Its a UNESCO site also, which gives the site a more special reason to visit. Be careful as the surface can be slippery, but in general the walk can take about over an hour.

First some people said it is   Mystic   supranatural thing but actually it's only a trick eyes illusions that twisted out logical thinking. The road looks like going uphill and makes the car or bus like climbing moving forward againts the gravity. When we saw from the end of the road, yes the road is going downhill not the opposite around. Well, still it's amazing thing to experience!

Few hundred feet of road that makes you feel like your rolling uphill with the car in neutral.  Best is to begin at the start point from a full stop place the car in neutral and release the brake, the car will begin to roll very slowly and it appears that you are going up a slight incline.   I would not go out of my way for this... although I did.  If you have plenty of time or nothing to do because of rain then why not.

Everything rolls backwards on that 50m of road! We tried it with our car without its engine, and then with a bottle of water.. It works all the same! Takes about 10 mins to experience it.. Seeing is Believing!

Even though my family and I stayed in Breeze Bay Hotel which is within 3 minutes? drive to the Seongsan Ilchulbong (Sunrise Peak) car park, we couldn?t wake up so early to hike up to the summit to catch the sunrise. Eventually, we were at the base of the Seongsan Ilchulbong at 10am, together with hordes of tourists and locals?nd the sunny weather.Getting there and fees: GPS coordinate/code for this UNESCO World Heritage and South Korea National Monument site/attraction located in the east Jeju is 7830959. As the parking lots are limited, I suggest you drive (arrive) there early (before 9am). Parking is free.  The entrance fees are 2,000 won for adults and 1,000 won for teenagers and children.The attraction: A non-stop no-rest ascent for a fit person takes about 30 minutes, but with my young children and with stairs-climbing not part of our daily routine, we took about 1 hour to make complete the 182 metres climb to the summit. There are several pointers that you may want to take note:(1)
address: If you can, go on a weekday. We were there on a Wednesday mid-morning and already it was quite crowded, so I cannot imagine what the weekend would bring(2)
입력주소: Wear a pair of good-sole and comfortable walking shoes and bring enough water to hydrate yourself (you could still buy water at only one place during the ascent)(3)
X: On a sunny day, you could bring an umbrella or wear sunglasses or a cap and preferably put on sunscreen lotion(4)
Y: Take note that the ascending trail or route is different from the descending trail or route, so do take lots of photos and selfies along the way. (5)
CLSS: Hike at your comfortable pace (although I understand that may not be possible when the tour guide requires you to be back at the bus within a certain timing) and do rest at the benches and the viewpoints or points of interest (e.g. huge rocks) whenever you are out of breath (give you an excuse to take photos and selfies)(6)
PNU: There is no need to bring a jacket or sweater unless the weather becomes chilly or windy or cold (e.g. winter) or you are hiking in the wee hours of the morning to catch the sunrise. In fact, it was scorching hot when we reached the crater summit at around 11am(7)
주소구분: When you reach the summit, remember to pose with the signage says ‘Top of Seongsan Ilchulbong 180m’We started the climb after the 4 bronze round inscriptions (one of them is ‘New 7 Wonders of Nature’) on the uneven rocky or bumpy uphill sloped path. After a certain distance, this sloped ascending path became one that comprises of proper (stairway) steps. Look for the signage “Ascending Trail” and continue your ascent. Somehow the last stretch is a steep climb on continuous stairway steps and with so many people behind you, you simply cannot stop to rest. But once you reach the top, before you have time to catch your breath, your breath will be immediately taken away by the breath-taking panoramic views! You could see the flora-covered 600-meters diameter crater with 99 jagged rocky spires that resemble a crown, in addition to the Seongsan town (village), Seongsanpo-hang harbour, Cheju Haehyop (Cheju Strait), Mount Hallasan and others. It amazed me when I considered the almost symmetrical tuff cone crater was created by the explosion of an underwater volcano thousands of years ago. Due to the barriers, all visitors cannot walk into the tuff cone crater.Of course, the descent was relatively easier along wider wooden stairways with railings. When near the bottom, there are two directions to take. Going to the left, you could ride a Jeju pony (Jorangmal), which we didn’t go. Going to the right (signage “Women Diver Performance”), you would come to a black basalt rock cliff and also to a place to see the famous female divers (Haenyeo). To the right too, you would come to a lookout point for Udo Island (South Korea’s second largest island)Comparing with the only other tuff cone crater that I have climbed ? Diamond Head in Honolulu ? I find the Seongsan Ilchulbong more challenging to climb but it offers more breath-taking scenery.  So don’t miss Seongsan Ilchulbong on your Jeju itinerary! Start the ascent early to avoid the crowd.
표준구주소: If you can, go on a weekday. We were there on a Wednesday mid-morning and already it was quite crowded, so I cannot imagine what the weekend would bring(2)

review: Even though it is only 180m in height, but to climb the stairs (no lifts or cable car) all the way up to the crater takes a strong determination and some stops in between. The view from the top is amazing. You can view the Seongsan town and its connecting roads which are surrounded by sea. It is very windy at the top, so make sure you have a scarf or a beanie with you. Wear comfortable shoes though I managed with sandals and no socks (applicable to early autumn).

Eorimok trail ends at Witse Oreum, at about 1700m up Hallasan. From carpark to the hut and back, including half an hour for noodles at the top is close to 4.5 hours. This includes photo times. Like everything on Jeju, this is a tourist walk, for pretty much anyone who can put one foot in front of the other up a very well marked or board-walked track. That notwithstanding, the walk is pleasant and the area itself is nice. In early Feb you will still likely have snow (we had snow from carpark to hut) and will require some small walking crampons to ensure grip. These are 5000W from the small shop at the carpark, beside the toilets and are pretty good actually. If you have some full mountaineering fangs it would almost be worth taking them for a laugh. We were the only westerners on the trail from perhaps 3-400 people and it would have only added to everyone's curiosity. Taxi from Jeju city will set you back about 20 000W and you can easily get a cab from the carpark taxi stand for your return trip. Hallasan is definitely the best, and some would say only real, attraction on Jeju and if you have half a day, then this is the track for you.

Eokimok trail up and Yongsil trail down, I really enjoyed the well taken care off hiking trails and all of the signs in various languages. You meet people all the time so no worries if you are alone. Must do on Jeju island!

Entertaining Mongolian horse show. We caught a taxi here as it's not easy to get to by other public transport. Impressive expert performance by the young horse riders who did some amazing acrobatics on horses. The Park's website is in Korean and the show was all in Korean but we managed to follow what was going on!  The horse show is on 3 times a day. After the show, kids can have fun riding a horse or driving a swing car (7 minute ride) or go kart (not sure of the minimum age for that).  Need to pay additional fees for each activity.  Worth spending a couple of hours or half a day here.
Easy visit - gps to car park, down steps and the rock's there.   Its pretty enough for a quick visit.  Some shops, snack places in the area.  Parking was free for a short stay

Due to the bad weather and rain, my friends and I just managed to experience the mysterious road inside our tour guide's car. The car is moving upward when our pretty tour guide turn off the car engine and the car keep moving up... If you have the chance, experience yourself!!!

Due to lack of time, I decided to take a blue/ yellow tour bus (5000KRW for 4 destinations). For those, I prefer the 2nd one which I can enjoy peanut ice cream.The weather was so much hot, which made me tired quite fast.If you wanna rent scooters or cars, international driving licenses are required.Peanut ice cream was not that delicious, but you know, what they sell is creativity, not ice cream.

Drove to this portion of road after Mount Hallasan.  There is a sign that says   start of Mysterious Road  , but it neglects to tell you to put your car in neutral at that point.  We didn't do it and were wondering what the big deal was.  After having waited in a slowdown of cars we decided that we didn't want to try again.  Had a great laugh!

drove there via ferry car ferrying services. Was a little confused on where to purchase the tickets but just follow the crowd. Paid about 30000 won for car and 2 paxs to get across the island. When I arrived at the island, it was very windy and it really felt cold! However, I enjoyed the fresh air and flower fields there!

Drive yourself to the 100m stretch of road. When see the   start   marker, put your gear to neutral and you will notice that the car is moving forward even as you are going uphill without engaging any gear. Pretty interesting short experience.

Don't talk, just feel yourself on the walk way to clim to the top. Open your eyes and record the scene to your soul. It will treat your mind, very well. Don't forget your water bottle. Be careful when taking your selfie.

Don't make a special trip to see this place,  Only interesting if you pass by.  I mean, it's only a piece of road where you turn off the engine on the incline and watch the car roll for a few yards.  We've got more interesting mystery spot in Santa Cruz, Calif.

Don't forget to drive past the ticket booths to the real start of the trail, we some some poor gits having to hike up the twisty road which takes 5 - 10 minutes in a car.  Wear layers as it gets cool up high.  First part is through bush trail, we had a roe deer come across 10 m. away.  Then trails steepens to get to ridgeline, a little tough.  Nice views and steps on the ridge, then another transition to a boardwalk through a tundra like alpine area.  Go past WitseOreum to the 1700m. junction where there's a toilet and snack bar, hot cup noodles are the best.  You can go another 2 km closer to the crater but why bother? Pack out your garbage.  The man made plank trail is kind of artificial but keeps the humans on a defined path and generally keeps them out of trouble, all in all a good way to get the masses of all ages into the outdoors.

Don't bother if you honestly hoped to gain much knowledge in green tea / tea by coming here. The   museum   per se is a small area probably 20 steps from end to end with around 30-40 exhibits I guess.Main attractions are the many tea they sold and the cafe selling green tea products. I have yet to try those tea leafs yet so I can't commend on the taste (but it was mentioned in the museum that Jeju had the most fitting environment for producing green tea) I also bought 3 slices of swiss roll a green tea roll with cheese inside a black roll with vanilla inside and another caramel roll with i think green tea inside. The roll were soft and sweet but not overtly sweet. My cousins bought their green tea ice cream but it was very milky.Still worth a visit for their products if you are in Jeju.

Dongmun market is close to Jeju airport. It is huge and so many allies for so many different stores. I had a rental car so used a public parking lot which was cheap. We had a great time exploring almost all allies, but the parking lot was a bit too tight and small. Don't forget to try out some   Omegi   rice cake which is a very authentic, famous, and delicious rice cake in Jeju.

Do you like cold, dark, dripping lava caves? Then this is for you! Just be warned - WEAR PROPER WATERPROOF SHOES! Or at least, bring an extra pair of shoes and socks cause your feet are going to get soaked in the many puddles. Better still, bring an umbrella or wear a poncho. The roof constantly drips, and there?s no way to avoid getting soaked. It would have been better if:- More lights could be installed. Some places were way too dim, and we had to use our handphone lights. - There was the option of tour guides. We wished someone could have walked us through and explained things a bit more!- Sone portions of the cave needed levelling. We were very worried about twisting our ankles at some points because the floor was VERY uneven! On the bright side:- Entrance fee is very cheap.- It?s a rare experience to walk around a lava tube. So just do it! :D (But be careful and walk slowly!)
Do not ask why, but it is happened. Car can move without engine on. The car uphill. Engine is off. The car still move up.

Do check on the sunrise timing before heading up. We took about 45-60mins to climb up, taking short breaks in between. The place can be quite dark at 430am, so do bring along a portable torchlight. The torchlight mode from Smartphones just isnt bright enough. If you enter before 7am, there is no admission fee. Or rather, the admission office starts at 7am. So, lucky for us.The stone stairs are well maintained, im amazed, especially this is a popular spot for sunrise.We went during late March, transition period to Spring and the temperature was about 12-14 degree celcius in the wee morning. Although it might be chilly in the morning, pls do not wear thick clothing or heattech, as you will start to swear & feel hot after climbing up the stairs. So just like the locals, just don something light and with a windbreaker. If you scare you still might feel chilly, have a heatpack to warm your hands. It is important to carry light.However, i didnt get to see the sunrise. ): it was way too cloudy. Oh well..

Dived back to those nostalgic childhood moments when teddy bears once played as friends in your life. This Teddy Bear Museum has a wide array of collection of teddy bears, dressed beautifully in different costumes. The most popular bear will probably be the one dressed in Louis Vuitton clothes.What particularly caught my attention was the exhibition which actually used famous paintings such as the Mona Lisa, and the Teddy Bear was dressed to depict her. A creative way to carry out this exhibition. However, those expect to see a wide range of   depiction  .Overall, I felt that this was only an average stop-over, but will be good for families traveling with their young children. There's a souvenir shop on site too, where I'll be expecting young children to be bugging their parents to get them a teddy bear each!

Despite the temperature being around 17 degrees Celsius Springtime end of March, we were nearly blown away the minute we got out of our car. It was super windy & cold at the base! Had to put on extra layers, wind breakers etc. However the climb up is via long, steep stairs (my nemesis!!) so had to take off some layers halfway as I wheezed & panted my way up! View from top was just okay, wasn't as green as the photos we saw. Maybe because it was early spring. On the way down, we took a detour to the Diving Women's museum / hut / restaurant just by the rocky beach. Owing to the weather, no diving woman worth her salt, was going to do a performance in the sea. We had to contend with a couple of squirmy sea creatures in tanks, which the diving women chopped up with precision & served to us with soya sauce. The abalone, octopus & shell-fish were as fresh as you could get and tough as erasers. But we did it more for the experience than the cuisine or taste. You can pick up more tasty fare at the shops near the carpark if you're hungry.
Definitely go there if you've got a car. We went there when it was snowing and sleeting, still a perfect view. Wish I could spend more time there - definitely go on a good day!
Definitely a tourist trap, not a lot to do here. The illusion of the car rolling uphill isn't that big of a deal. Plenty of other pretty roads to drive along that are worth more of your time.

Decent trip for the price. A little outdated as the show hasn't air in years, but for something to do with our spending a lot this is a good place to go. For those with little ones the electric chair showcase may be a little scary. I had seen multiple children cry going past it.

Couldn't believe that a car museum of such excellence would be found on Jeju Island in South Korea.the large number of cars covered all makes, types and brands and we just loved all the old advertising posters around the museum.The displays outside were also a delight and the museum was not hard to get to by public transport.? We stopped off to watch some of the races on the way back and that is also worth a visit.? They use descendants of the Mongolian ponies, and with their colourful jockeys they made a wonderful display.? The extensive grounds have lots to entertain children as well as a mini golf course in the centre of the race track.? Would definately recommend both destinations.

review: Couldn't believe eyes when the car started to go   uphill   even though the engine has been turned off. My son and nephews put a water bottle on the road and it rolled   uphill  . Very unique

Considering this is a FOC attraction, its not too bad at all.  Basically, you start at the stone pillar (which say start point).  Engage to neutral gear and lift off the pedals.  Your car will gradually roll forward, even though the gradient seems to be be positive.  This   attraction   should take no longer than 10 minutes.

Communication barrier is not a problem for us to shop here. Yes, they don't really speak English. But, we still had a good time to shop and bargain. If you want to shop korean fashion (but not the designer label or branded one), clothing, accessories, bags, cosmetic, skin care, this is the place. One place for everything so that you don't have to walk more. Innisfree, Nature Republic, The Saem, Skin Food, you name it. All are here.
Close to the Jeju Loveland Park and worth the stop. Mind boggling how a car moves up a hill, merely a trick of the eye.

Climbing Mt Hallasan was absolutely amazing, and I would recommend anyone going to Jeju to attempt a climb. If you?re a bit unsure, make sure to research the trails before-hand and start walking in the morning ? many trails close at 2-3pm.Bring lots of water and snacks (although in typical Korean fashion, there is a 'restaurant' at the 'top', where all the lower trails intersect. Do your research, take a car or taxi to the start of the trail (buses will drop you off much further down the mountain, and you'll have to spend time and energy walking up along a road before you can even start the trail). The views must usually be stunning, but on the day we went, it was covered in cloud/fog. Even so, I would 100% recommend it and I would definitely go again if I went back to Jeju.

Cheonjeyeon Waterfalls consists of 3 waterfalls. Such a nice turquoise water. There is an entrance fee to enter this place. Make sure you have some energy because you need to climb stairs to reach each point. There is a bridge called 'Seonimgyo Bridge', meaning 7 nymphs as there has an arch carved on the side. This place open from 8am to 6pm. We came here late in the evening in a rainy day but the admin staff were so nice to allowed us to enter but with time restrictions.

Certainly my first experience entering a natural geological occurrence like this one. A nice walk on a seasoned path, although some parts were slippery, it was safe for most people. Senior citizens must take extra care as the uneven path were dimly lit. Here were many features to be amazed by and the information centre gave visitors a better understanding of the geological occurrence. Worthy visit.

Cars and buses usually demonstrate this seemingly mysterious trick. They have their engines turned off at the beginning of the road stretch (there's an indicated sign). And while the engines are off, it seemingly feels and looks like there's this   mysterious force   pulling the vehicles towards the end of the road. Civilians also use a water bottle and place it on the road surface. Mimicking the vehicles, it too would roll towards the end of the road. Just like the saying goes, looks can be deceiving. Optical illusion is what it is.

Carpark available. It was a lovely walk in the forest. Wear comfortable shoes and a light jacket. We went during autumn. I have sinus.. but minute we walked into the forest, my nose magically cleared up. The air was fresh and the sounds in the forest was beautiful. Wish i could record it. They have created a path to walk so its easy. No food allowed though. Took about an hour to walk.

careful of when walking in the cave, very uneven and wet grounds. The cave is very far from the city, the public bus does not go direct and takes 45min with many stops in between. When arriving at the destination, its about 2.4km walk to the entrance of the cave. If you are lucky to get a taxi when u alight from the bus, they will charge u 4000won to drive u to the cave entrance to purchase your ticket to the cave

Came here by using waze , there's parking , entrance fee 2000 won for adults , 1000 won for youth , walk down the stairs leading to the rocky waterfalls , got to be careful when walking around the rocks .

C1 ( 2016.07.12 ) This museum was more many car than I think. I didn't expect this museum, but various car was exhibits. Especially, the car about 30 years ago was very good to me. There was a various car in the museum and outside. For children, the experience facility was good.
