review: But too overcrowded by visitors even at September! :)Possible to rent bicycle or scooter (electric or usual) or quadro-unit and make your trip around the island (but you need actual international driver license with correct category!).It's big enough for walkers.Very small and narrow road all around island - be very, very, very careful as main part of drivers are young people with very little experience of driving and winds in their heads (sorry, but true!) :)

Built on a reclaimed land-fill site, this vast area of pathways, statues, displays, museums and traditional villages is very worth a visit if on Jeju. From the impressive stone structures and flat basalt 'floor' at the entrance of the park, I was blown away by the vast array of statues that are displayed, explained and on show in this area. There is ample car parking that is only a short walk form the entry way. A small fee is required and then you are free to wander the area that included a massive and spectacular 2 store (below ground) museum that outlines the geographic development of Jeju along with many interactive displays, a short film with subtitles, examples and galleries of 'stone art'. A gift shop of course, provided a range of traditional and specific items and there are amenities spread throughout the part. Water features, a traditional village, an art gallery and a vast array of stone sculpture will give you hours of things to view and read as you wander through the park In my humble opinion, not to be missed!!!

Bring your swimming gear along, it has a sea swimming pool during low tides, basically daytime. Seeing ppl drives and swimming. There is life-jacket rental available for snorkelling. No entrance ticket required. But the carpark attendance charged us W2K which seem only W1K per hour. No proper carpark control. See ppl park along road side.

Bought the tickets online to enjoy a discount. We arrived early to be amongst the first cars within the car park. Thus, we had a fuss free horse riding experience for the kids. The 50mins performance was also enjoyed by the kids. Unfortunately, the go karting wasn?t available due to rain a few hours before.

Borrowing the words from our innkeeper,   don't give up   until you have reached the peak. The 180m high volcano gives a full panoramic view of the sea and the eastern coastline. Stairs are available all the way, but gets narrower as it approaches the peak. At intervals, there are magnificent viewpoints for postcard-worthy shots, even with a phone camera (which I have uploaded). Not to worry if you aren't that physically fit, you can always take a timeout at these points and take in the scenery. Highly recommended to go during pre-winter when the air is cooler for a comfortable trek. For those who are less fond of the cold, recommend to bring a light jacket/coat as the wind can be pretty chilly during this time.

Bijarim Forest holds about 2,800 nutmeg trees between 500 and 800 years old and is supposedly the largest nutmeg grove in the world. A 813 years old   Ancestor tree of Bijia tree  , also dubbed the   New Millennium Nutmeg   (#0001 tree) sits in the middle of the forest. Local residents hope the spiritual power of this noble tree will bring happiness, prosperity, and health to all in the coming millennium.The trees emit phytoncide, said to strengthen one's immunity system and enhances natural healing of the human body. Japanese and Koreans advocate forest bathing, aka shinrin-yoku or 汝役 and sanlimyok ??곕┝ respectively.  Essentially this is a short, leisurely visit to absorb the forest atmosphere and was developed in Japan during the 1980s as part of preventive health care and healing.  So do walk slowly, breathe deeply, open all your senses in the revitalising woods to calm, rejuvenate and restore your body.  Truly pleasant stroll for nature lovers and family outing.Note: Despite its charm, Bijarim Forest is more popular with locals than foreign tourists due to public transportation and lack of awareness. Cover this place as part of  Manjanggul caves/Sangumburi crater tour. The woods can get mud-logged after rainfall.

Best way is to go to the starting point (where it's steepest and most deceptive).  Make sure that there's no car or people behind you, put car in N, then release your brake too, to see you and your car going backwards UP the hill.

Besides the short walk up to the Buddhist cave, there is a lovely temple and huge golden Buddha just up from the carpark. It does cost money to get in but being able to get up close to the Buddha was excellent. And there are nice views of the coast too.

Believed to be formed about 2,00,000 ? 3,00,000 years ago, this UNESCO protected heritage centre, the Manjjanggul Lava tube tunnels said to be one of the longest ( around 7.5 km) and well maintained Lava tube tunnels in the world. Though there would not be much to see around, the sheer excitement one experiences just walking into the dark ,rocky ,slippery tunnel is worth the money paid for.Important things to remember.-Those who are having difficulty in walking should avoid getting down the tunnel as the floor is rocky,slippery and uneven.-A good pair of shoes is a must. No high heeled footwear please.-Carry or wear warm clothes as the inside temperature would be much lower than outside.-Wearing a cap/hat would be also good as water would be dripping on your head as you walk.-The Tunnel is open for 1 KM for the Public and with minimal lighting. Carrying a low intensity torch would be best.

Before, people usually visited there for watching trees, feeling energy from the forest and healing. But these days there are more and more people to take photos for wedding. Wedding couples turned into one of the enjoyments of the forest. You can go there with your family and any kind of carrier will be fine.

Before you want to take a ferry to Udo island, please take note that you need to bring along your passport to purchase a ticket. You will be given 2 tickets, 1 for departure & 1 for arrival (you have to keep this and pass to the boatman at Udo when you want to return to main island). A tip is to get the korean map together with your language?s map because they have more details of the island as compared to other languages. The ferry comes every 15 minutes so you do not have to worry if you miss it. Inside the ferry, there are flooring with thermal and you have to take your shoes off before stepping into the resting platforms. Otherwise, you may choose to stand outside those rooms and there are some outdoor seats at the top of the ferry. Please also take note that there are 2 ports at Udo, so your ferry might stop at either one.Once you reach the island, you will be greeted by tons of shop assistants trying to get you to rent bikes to you. You will need an international driver license to be able to drive any motorise vehicles. Upon confirmation which is the vehicle you want, you have to leave your passport with the register counter. They will provide you with a map to go around the island. We were informed that the whole cycling trip takes an hour. However, here comes the challenging part. There were no proper division of the road for those driving trucks, buses, cars, motorcycles & bicycles. You can be riding your bicycle and have a full speed bus chasing behind you and pressing the horn at you. Cars and trucks from the opposite direction also travel at fast speed towards you, which we had to stop many times to give way to these fast moving vehicles. After getting to the first beach, which was really beautiful, the rest of the trip towards the next beach was tough as there were many upward slopes and split roads which have no proper signages to tell you which way to go. We had to go in to random houses and ask in broken korean for which way to go. However, when we reach the lighthouse area, we managed to locate Jimmy?s icecream shop as suggested by our Jeju driver. I tried the mandarin orange ice cream while my friend tried the apple mango ice cream. Everything tasted natural and yummy so I would recommend it to tourist who visit the place. However, from the road before this ice cream place onwards to the last 5 mins of the ride, it was all upwards riding.We took almost 3 hours to finish cycling around the whole island (We have done quite a few rides in Singapore so I don?t think we were slow in cycling around the island). So for those who have no license or feel that you?re not up to 2-3 hours of cycling, I would advise you to take the tour bus to get from places to places on the island.

Before you visit this attraction, be sure to be appropriately dressed and have the essential gear.  Hiking boots are highly recommended as the ground is uneven and mostly rock.  Sun hat and shades will also be very useful when nearing the peak as the area there is more barren without much trees.  Trekking pole will also be useful for those with knee problems.You will have to start your day early as they will disallow entry to the final stretch (at the 2nd rest point).  There are 2 rest points, both with toilets.  The 2nd rest point (higher up) sells drinks and instant bowl noodles.  Rubbish will have to be brought down and thrown when you leave the park.  I climbed in early June and there were many many many bugs and wasps at the last leg and the peak.  For those climbing during spring, please prepare some bug balm.  These are the tips;1) Start early, reach the 2nd rest stop before 12pm.  2) Have the proper gear3) If possible, have your noodles etc after you finish the peak (if you're descending via the same trail), that way, you won't have to carry your trash up the peak4) If you're driving, reach there early (before 730).  Carpark fills up pretty quick5) A mineral spring can be found along the way for cool refreshing water!

Before traveling to Jeju I was unaware that there was a horse show.  Our guide asked us if we wanted to see a horse show and we said ?sure?.  We had no idea what to expect.  It appears that this show caters towards Korean tourists and the show is only in Korean.  However, there was a pamphlet available in English.  I didn?t see any other foreigners in the audience.  The show takes place in a large arena and lasted about an hour.  The seats are covered in case of rain.  The show is supposed to take place during the Mongol invasions of Korea during the 1200s.  They had mock battles, displayed archery skills, performed equestrian vaulting, and a variety of other skills.  I thought that the show was entertaining, well performed, and the Mongolian riders were very talented.  My 3 year old, was a bit scared by the battles.  The horses appeared to be well cared for and healthy.  At the beginning and end of the show you can purchase a carrot to feed to the horses.  I believe that the cost of the show was 18,000 won, but our guide was able to get us a discount.  Overall, I thought that it was fun and would go back.

Been there during last autumn. This place is also known as Sunrise Peak. To reach the peak, you need to ascend 600 steps. The 1st 400 over steps seems easy but be more careful after that as the steps become steeper and more rugged. Also mind the autumn chilly strong wind which can blow your bags off (personal experience). Get there to the top for the panoramic view of the peak. Also, if you are in time, you can also watch the pearl diver women in action.

Beautiful, serene and breathtaking views. A mid-level challenge to hike up and carrying extra water was mandatory in the heat. It is the highest peak in South Korea and the geographical centre of Jeju. A most worthwhile wander.

Beautiful scenery at the top with breathtaking surrounding views of Jeju. Well maintained stairs, although uneven at first because they use the volcanic rocks, Many resting places as you go up. There is a lady at the top who explains the origins of the peak in English, which was a pleasant surprise. Large carpark area, fast food stores and souvenir shops.

Beautiful place to take a nice walk around the shore line. Can imagine it would get a bit busy in the summer, but it was empty when we visited as it was a snowy winter day which by all accounts added to the experience. Be careful though it can become a wee bit slippery when the rocks get wet.

beautiful place & good for take 1day visit if you have time in jeju. we take off bus stop prior to entrance and take many picture at the outside of Seongsan Ilchulbong. it has a beautiful beach & flower and horses etc... after that, went inside the hill. we went to the end of cliff that has a show for haenyeo starting time was 1330 & 1530. that has a dance & sing a song before go inside the sea. first time to close view their hard duty as actually jeju still getting many haenyeo woman as i viewed that carrying the orange ball inside the sea. some near coastal and some in the middle of ocean. seem take a long time duty such a hard duty.after that we went to hill of Seongsan. good view but the summit just a half & not easy to identify. but overall view & trail was enjoyable. must see

Beautiful hike, I went up the Seongpanak trail and down Gwaneumsa. Hardly anyone around on the way down, was nice and peaceful. Contrary to what some info says online there is a public bus to/from Gwaneumsa during the week - the 475. The column in red of the picture below are the times to depart on this bus from the trail car park.

Basically, this is just an eye illumination. You see a uphill road but actually it's a downhill road and vice versa. What you have to do is just let your car in N mode, then you will see the magic. Or you can get down from your car, and put a bottle on the road in a laying position. It's quite interesting because you can hardly find this kind of natural eye illumination.

Basically this place is formed when lava flows through the land on its way to the ocean. Understand that this cave (or tube)!is 6.4m long but only 1m is accessible as the rest are closed for various reasons. It?s about 11degrees at the deepest end so for those who are not used to this, please bring along your sweaters. Also the path is uneven and wet so don?t come in your shopping shoes. Otherwise it?s a very educational tour. Signages are posted at strategic points to explain the event. Oh yes. The steps down to the cave is very high so hold on to the railing tight or be very careful where you plant your feet.

Basically nothing much here. The road seemed to be uphill and when the engine of the vehicle is switched off, it will   roll uphill  . However, it is a natural optical illusion, and the road is actually downhill. Spend not more than 15mins here if you drive as the road is just about 50 metres. Also, the   rolling down   phenomenon only works on large vehicles like buses or truck. Small saloon cars will not encounter the   rolling uphill   effect.

Basicallu it's a small island, so we can walk / rent bicycle - motorcycle - small car / hop on bus to get around. Almost no activities. Just stop by here n there to take picture, buy ice cream, dine, etc. If you just want to relax and embrace the beautiful nature around, this is a good place. Our family rent bicycle 10.000 won per bicycle. It took us 4 hours to go around the island slowly.

Bangju Church is a picturesque little church that?s unmissable on the way to Bonte Museum.  It?s the unique ark-shaped exterior along with the surrounding water that makes it photogenic and there isn?t much inside (which is off limits most of the time anyway).  Despite being a short stop, there were always a half dozen cars in the parking lot with people busy taking photos around the church.
Awesome! 2 km total by walking, cold place inside, we are so amazed by how the nature creates it. When you come in rainy season please be careful with your steps. Not recomended for the elder.

At this place you need to walk, climb a little. Be very careful when climbing on and over rocks at the bottom of the fall to take pics. Some rocks are very slippery. You can see the water go straight into the ocean which is quite different to the other two waterfalls. It is a lovely sight!

At the entrance of this huge garden layout is lush, green plants  there is a bonsai garden, herb gardens, an array of flowers, a subtropical garden, water garden and a stone display as you travel along a palm garden road. There is a fair amount of walking.This display of trees, plants and gardens is a wonderful experience although its the caves, limestone tube-shaped structures growing downward from the ceiling of the cave and stalagmites that grow from the floor up. Structures are formed  containing calcium-bicarbonate. Fossilized seashells, frozen lava, and numerous other structures which enhanced our walk through the caves.  Visit the stone exhibition hall, see the parrots and the various species of birds. A must see attraction.

At KRW2000 this was well worth the money.  Don't forget to wear a jacket or a warm Cardy though, I forgot and found it very cold.  Lots of people do this it's very popular.  We tried the restaurant there which was good enough.

As with many cars that went there, my taxi stopped, turned off the engine, switched to Neutral gear and yes, the car started rolling uphill......But interestingly, the road is also called the demon road there. Look around the place, and you will see some cute little   devils   around the place.Nothing much there else, expect that you need to be there and say you done that.

As we stayed in Seogwipo, we followed part of Jeju Olle Route 6 and  7  from Chilshimni Poetry Park to Oedolgae. We started our personal trail from Saeyeongyo Bridge and went up to Chilshimni Poetry Park through a wooden stairway. The wooden stairway was located along the road where a lot of tourist buses parked (towards the end where there was a brown building beside) away from Saeyeongyo Bridge. When we reached Chilshimni Poetry Park (is just beside Park Sunshine hotel), we were lucky to catch a view of  the Cheonjiyeon Falls from the top. There was also a resting shelter with table and benches if you want to enjoy the view of the waterfall while having snacks or lunch. Afterwhich, we left the park to the main road (where Park Sunshine hotel was) and headed to Namseong-ro road which was indicated by the blue/orange ribbons for Oedolgae. Along the way, you will pass by몃媛?? Hostel (the hostel name is in Korean as I cannot find the English name online) before reaching Hwangwooji coast first (it is a very beautiful coast with a private emerald green pool. Then there was a trail to Oedolgae where was a cliff top that you can view the Saeyeongyo bridge. Oedolgae trail is  free 1 to 2 hours trail and it is not a difficult trail, it is pretty gentle with lots of benches for rest breaks as needed. It has pretty nice coast view. There were fruits and snack sold along the trail where you just need to place 1000won at the basket where you take the fruits/snacks from (there is not one attending to the store). It is based on trust. There were rest rooms outside the trails if needed with food stalls near the free public toilet with toilet paper provided. We need all the trail by foot and there is really no need for a car.

As we stayed in Seogwipo, we followed Jeju Olle Route 6 from Chilshimni Poetry Park (to see the Cheonjiyeon Falls from the top) to Oedolgae and happened to see this Hwangwooji coast (probably part of olle route 6) which was my favourite spot of the day. You will walk along Namseong-ro road and passed by 외돌개나라 Hostel (the hostel name is in Korean as I cannot find the English name online). I love the place bcos it was like a private pool and it is free. There were only a few Korean that day, playing, swimming and hunting of sea creatures in the private pool. It also has a good view of the Saeyeongyo Bridge from a far.? After-which we head to Oedolgae.You can walk there and you do not need a car. Probably a 15 minutes walk from the main road (Namseongjung-ro road where Poong Gyung Hotel or Park sunshine hotel jeju is) and walk in to Namseong-ro road where? 외돌개나라 Hostel is.

As someone who loves walking on rocky surfaces (yes it does sound weird when I type it like that), I really enjoyed walking down to the base of the waterfall. You don't have to walk the rocky part to get you to the waterfall though - the steps from the carpark down to the base will take you close enough. Someone the rocks are slippery so be careful. Along the way I think there were haenyeon with their very freshly caught seafood. Loved this place; would come back in a heartbeat.

As part of the tour, we had a short stop at dragon head rock, where you can see the head of a dragon naturally carved on a big rock. There is also a small mermaid sculptured on a rock for photo opportunity. This is more of a photo stop. Jeju as an island attraction have plenty of rock formation, volcanic rocks, and shoreline with plenty of rock. Again like all part of Jeju, the place has good breeze and quite comfortable.

As our tour guide said nest stop is the beach... i was wondering how can any beach rival Philippine beaches? But as we get nearer i saw it,,, a hill with a small island... really shaped like an oriental dragon serpent just starting to submerge into the water. It was a sight to behold! so we went down the trail and enter the coastline path... it was so beautiful! the coastline is carved by ancient volcanic eruptions and was smoothened by the waves. it was a 30min walk around the coast line and as we were walking the view just gets better and better. when we turned a corner around 14 minutes in the walk. The best view suddenly came out. no amount of words can describe the rock formations we saw. we felt small beside it. Along the way were many old ladies selling seashells and sea urchins and sea cucumbers for us to taste as sashimi (raw fish) to be downed together with soju(rice wine).These ladies were the famous jeju island deepsea divers. They dive without oxygen tanks. After the walk we were all tongue tied at the beauty of the past 30 minutes. Yongmeori means dragon head coast. and it really took a dragon size breath away from me. Entrance only 6000won (6us$)
As mysterious & strange as its name. Drive the car there, stop the car, take out the car keys & leave the brakes...the car really move forward by itself!

As mentioned this place does not get a lot of attention. Today while we were there, were surprised to see a lot of local Korean tourists. From Seogwipo bus terminal (the one near Jeju World Cup Stadium) take bus 702. There is announcement in English. Alight at Sanbangsan. This place is truly nature at it's mightiest, the wind/sea carved walls/cliffs are very different from the rest of Jeju's natural beauty. Entrance fee is 2000 won for adult and 1000 won for child. Take time to enjoy the wind, sunshine and views as you strolled. Along the way, there are old ladies selling fresh seafood and soju. There is a mini theme park next to one of the entrances. There is Viking, trampoline.. A number of stalls selling bbq squids/seafood, mandarin juice, chocolates and mini cakes. Good for the kids to take a few rides. All in all, a good half day spent in nature.

As lava caves go, this one is pretty good. It is approximately 2 kms long, wet, cold and dark although well lite for the tourists. Car parking is available and you can also take a local bus close to the area - you ned to walk the final distance. Payment is made at the booth prior to the entry stairs and from there the path is pretty well developed. Having visited many lava tunnels/caves in other countries, this one was basically what I expected but had its own unique sights. The path is rough and rocky in places and you need to wear sensible walking shoes and have a coat - visit in winter and you need o really rug up. Signage is both Korean and English and prior to the cave entry there is a selection of Korean restaurants and food shops. Some pretty park areas are also worth a look.

As I rented a car to explore Jeju (highly recommended), we came here a couple of times to enjoy the experience putting the gear at N position and realizing how the car went up the hill.We also tried on the road with a can of beer that also was rolling hill up apparently. It is maybe an optical illusion but when you are there it looks clearly and without any doubt that cars and things go up the road. The kids were amazed and really enjoyed as we also did.Try to avoid the afternoons, as most of the guided tours are here at that time with many buses horning in hurry to repeat the experience several times and many pedestrians around. In the morning the day after it was almost empty !

As I didn't have access to a car and was traveling alone whilst in Jeju I caught the city bus to the national park. This was pretty simple and the bus from the main bus terminal leaves every hour between 9 and 4 (during summer) the journey coat 3100 won. The bus stops at the end of 2 trails to the west of the mountain. (Eorimok Trail, Yeongsil Trail) . Both trails meet in the same place on the mountain and both give a varied, pretty and pleasant  walk up Mt Hallasan . There are toilets and facilities at each of the trail tickets offices which are well maintained. The paths are a mix of steps and decking to help mark the trail clearly. You get great views of the different Oreum's (small volcanoes) these trails do not lead to the summit like the longer trails that start on the east. Ensure you have snacks and plenty of water

As all caves are, the interior is dark. But there is lighting along the way that is sufficient to show the wall and ground.The ground is not even, but one just need to be careful and pay attention when walking. A touch will help (I carried one). Wear sports shoes for easy and safe walking.We walk for about 30 minutes to reach the end, with stops to read the explanation posted along the way.

As a family of 3 it took us 11hrs round trip to do Seongpanak trail which reaches the summit. it can be done in 9 hours if u are a fast moving, experienced hiker with great gear. you have to start this hike between 5-7am or you will be forced to turn around before you reach the peak. there is also a place to buy kimbab at the base before you head up. its tastey too.  it is a gradual grade the whole way, so it is not too strenuous... All Though, you definately wanna wear the right shoes and bring your poles because 85 percent of the terrian is lava rock... big chunks of jagged uneven and slippery lava rock. be prepared to spend most of ur day looking down to watch your step. especially on the way down. i was so sick of the lava rock that i decided this was the least enjoyable hike i have ever done. i did however have a 2 yr old on my back which could have added the pressure to watch my steps so carefully. you do not get any views until the last 20-30 minutes of the hike. the view is nice but if i had it to do over. i would have skipped this hike and spent the day seeing other sights. I highly recommend Seongsan Ilchulbong for a similar view at the top. if you have lots of time to explore jeju and you are a determined hiker, dont let me stop you. however, if you only have a few days to explore the island, you can get a lot more bang for your buck elsewhere.

Arrived here on a group tour and was impressed with walking in the cave although important to note a few thing . Firstly there is a long walk inside the caves after initially going down some steep stairs. Once in the cave the ground is not even and majority of walking is done on the uneven rock surface itself, for this reason a good pair of water tight shoes are definitely required. There is constantly water dripping from the roof , certainly not raining , but does mean you spend a lot of time looking down being careful of your step avoiding puddles . Along the way the cave is well lit by lighting and also a number of stations with information describing the rock formations you are passing. Make sure you have time so as not to rush watch your step and enjoy .

Apparently, this is what happens when magma cools - it contracts and splits into pentagonal or hexagonal columns. Come here and see for yourself. It only costs 2,000 Won per head unless you are a member of the Korean armed forces (Sergeant or below) in which case you only pay 1,000 Won !We had picture postcard perfect weather during our visit so the photographs ought to look good. This place is along one of Jeju's Olle walking trails, so why not combine a visit here with a good walk ? Why not indeed ?

Another UNESCO World Heritage. It have a nice view from the top but you need to climb up the stairs. Perhaps is a good exercise.  :)  You may bring along the bottled water as it takes around 30 mins to the top. There have restaurants, coffee shops, food stalls, souvenir stalls at the bottom and free car park as well.

An UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and a World Heritage Site, the Hallasan National Park is loaded with walking trails and is home to South Korea?s highest mountain named the Shield Volcano Hallasan. You?ll find about 1800 different kinds of plants and a number of alpine animals along the way up. The park is a unique place for nature lovers. Settled right in the heart of Jeju island, this park with high density woods and blooming hillsides is concidered as a treat to be at. Transportation: start with chosing a right trail for you. There many different ways up to the mountain, but only one of them will bring you to the summit. To get to the entrance you?d probably need to take one of the public busses or rent a car. Both options are convenient. Equipment: You?d definitely need to be prepared for a long and tiring walk. All the trails are devided into segments, based on their difficulty. Some of the parts of the trail would be paved, some wouldn?t be equipped at all. You?d be grateful for those parts where you?d be able to walk and step on the wooden bridges and paths. But except those short and the easiest parts of the way, you?d need to climb on the steep and narrow rocks, hop along cobblestones and boulders. Timing: don?t rush, remember when you?re on the top, that was only a half of your journey. There is the same long way down the mountain when you?re on the summit. Tips: be prepared for considerable change of the temperature and other weather conditions. We started in a pleasant sunny day and finished when it was drizzling and the fog was literally embracing us. Add up some wind and decreased temperature and you?re almost in our shoes out there. You?d definetely need to wear tracking boots or something alike, protecting and supporting your feet well. Otherwise you  risk hurting your ankles and knees. (as us, cause we were not prepared)You?d also want to change your clothes after 6-7 hours tracking up and down this mountain. Believe me you?ll be sweating af.

Among all the interesting place in Jeju island, i personally love Udo the most. The sky really blue, sea really blue, sand really white, stone really unique, food taste nice...you have it all. I rent a car for the trip in Jeju, therefore i bring the car to Udo by ferry. There were three of us in the car, i feel it worth the ferry ticket. As in Udo, most of the   mini car   or special bike we saw are mostly two person, so unless you rent two, you cant fit in 3 persons. So if you are driving, you have more than 2, bring your car with you. Parking is very easy to find. But please go to the port earlier as buying ticket and finding entrance to board the ferry can be very confusing..so you will need more time.

Amazing cave carved by molten lava moving underground with many interesting features, however, you need to be prepaired for dim lighting, uneven floor with many tripping hazards as well as uneven steps/stairs.  Not suitable for young children or older folks who have trouble with sight or walking.

Although we know how the illusion works, it is still crazy to watch how the bottles or cars go up hill instead of going back. You don't need much time over there though. One mysterious road (according to our touri map there are two) is located right next to the Jeju Lovepark which is interesting and funny. You can go there for 9000 Won, spend about an hour watching love sculptures. :-)

Although the lava tubes are quite extensive and although there are several lava tubes, the section open to the public is only roughly 1 km in length. However, exploring even the limited stretch open to the public was an amazing experience. In the Manjanggul tube you can see a number of features that are characteristic of lava tubes such as lava shelves, lava stalactites, ropy lava, lava toes and plenty of lava flowlines. Being inside the tube where once hot lava poured through and imagining the force of the flow (which can be judged by the flowlines) was an amazing experience. This cave also boasts of the world?s biggest lava column, located at the very end of the tunnel. There?s a lot to see and experience as you walk through the tube. So make sure to take your time and carefully observe the various features that you?ll come across without rushing through it. The lighting inside the cave / tunnel is well orchestrated so that there?s just enough light to see where you?re going without marring the cave atmosphere with too much light. Sections of particular interest are highlighted by additional lighting and there are useful signboards all along the way. Bring a raincoat or umbrella though. Water continuously drips from the ceiling. Wearing shoes or sneakers might also be a good idea, preferably waterproof ones, since there are puddles on the ground (but this is not such a great deal ? you can walk with sandals if you?re careful and if you don?t mind the occasional feel of water against your feet!). This lava tube is highly recommended while on a trip to Jejudo. A note about transport ? Once you get off the bus (bus 701 from Jejushi / Seogwipo or anywhere inbetween on the East Coast of the island), the walk to the entrance will take you 30-40 minutes. There will be taxi drivers as you get off the bus who will insist that the walk will take one hour. If you do decide to take a taxi, they will charge you 5000 won for the ride (somewhat more than what it would actually cost if they run the meter). Even if you ask, they will refuse to use the meter. Bus 990 comes right up to the entrance and takes you back to the 701 bus stop (to a stop different from the one you got off). Unfortunately it does not run often.

Along with Seongsan Ilchulbong, Manjanggul Cave is one of the two must-see attractions in Jeju, IMHO.There is a small information center building available with some interesting facts about the cave.  The cave itself is quite fascinating.  It is only 1 km in length, but it requires a very slow pace to traverse the entire cave.  This is due to the very rough nature of the ground that one walks on.  The cave floor has not been smoothed by man - unlike Micheon cave, so the ground is extremely uneven, sharp, and at points quite dangerous!  You definitely would not want to take a fall on the ground.  The ground is also very wet in areas.  Finally, the cave is not very well illuminated.  This makes it quite difficult for people who are elderly, have physical disabilities, or if you want to carry a baby.  In fact, for these groups, I would strongly advise not to visit the cave.The cave itself is quite large in height and occupies a large volume of space.  However, it is quite dark inside the cave and there's nothing too overly unique (when compared to something like Cave of the Winds) within the cave - other than it's very big and somewhat creepy.   I only made it through one third of the cave before I had to turn back due to time constraints.  There are a few man-made displays of interest providing more information on the cave and how is was formed.

Along with Go Carts and a hot air balloon ride, the Maze Park has enough to keep everyone busy and happy! The Maze is fun to watch people navigate from the hot air balloon. A great view of World Cup Stadium too!! This was a fun day!

All the museums were great in jeju island if you're in and out within a hour or so.? But i think i stayed in this automobile museum for at least 3 hours.? My hobby and passion is cars back home jn the States so for any car lover,? this is the place.? From the model T,? old school Bentley and rolls royce to The original 300sl class Mercedes,? you see it all.? A must for car lovers...

review: After the Jeju Love Land, w/c is a X rated (for adults) theme park. Funny, unique, it's a theme park that you will never find in any other country... This is a must visit, if u wanna hve a fun, funny Xperience!Glass castle are full of creative art works made of Glass.. Good for picture taking... Colorful, artistic, imaginative pieces of art. You'll also find here the Glass Shoes of Cinderella & their carousel.

After reading quite a few reviews on lHallasan trails, I finally decided to have a go at it. I left early to start the hike on Gwaneumsa just before 7.00am. I actually got there by taxi from sunrise peak, seongsan as there is no bus arriving there. It costed me 35000won. On arrival, the place was deserted, so I started my walk. The first part is throught the forest so you don't get to see any scenery. Once you reach the last shelter then it opens up and the view is amazing. From there you have still a good climb to the top (the thoughest part actually). On the top you can see the crater and if it has been raining the lake inside. I went down the second trails called seongpanak which is said to be easier. This one is a bit boring in regards to scenery because you are always in the forest.All in all it took me 6h45 to get to the top and back which is around 18km. The up trail is pretty challenging and I would recommend people the be quite fit to take it the down trails is a challenge to your ankles and knees as the path is covered in huge stone so be careful not the twist anything. On the up trails you will find a water spring almost at the top, no food and no other water poitn apart from that. On the down trail the is a shelter serving pot noodle. On arriving down at seongpanak there was a few taxi waiting so I managed to get back to the hotel. There is also a shop that sells drink, food and rent shoes.My reco is to start early in the morning to avoid too many people. Get plenty of water (I got 1l and it wasn't enough). Good shoes are a must. And one moto : slowly but surly! Don't rush it as you will suffer on the way down. Appreciate the trail. Be careful though that at 12h30 they will stop you at the shelter from gwaneumsa so you need to go pass this before and you need to leave the top before 14h to make it down before closing time. I really enjoyed it as a challenge 1300m climb from 650m to 1950m.

After parking the rental car at Seongsan Harbor, we hopped on the ferry (KRW 1,500) to cross over to Udo. Upon alighting from the ferry at Cheonjinhang Harbor on Udo, we headed to the Udo Tour Bus counter and got ourselves a ticket each (KRW 5,000). The whole tour is conducted in Korean. Not a single hint of English but it was enjoyable. The bus driver was also the tour guide, telling us about the significance of each stop. He'd stop for 20 minutes at each place of interest and if you do not hop back on, fret not, you may hop on the other tour buses. Keep your ticket stub.The whole tour took about 2 hours. The village roads were really interesting. If I visit Jeju again, I would want to stay overnight at Udo. The atmosphere is good, the air is fresh, people are nice.

After a fulfilling breakfast, the first stop of our Jejueco tour was the Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) along Jeju's Jungmun Daepo coast, columnar joints (stone pillars piled up along the coast and is a designated cultural monument of Jeju island) which were formed from the volcanic lava from Hallasan mountain. The Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) are essentially rock pillars (columnar jointed rocks) shaped like cubes or hexagons of various sizes and almost seem as if they were carved by nature's stonemasons. The area where the Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) are located is part of an olle course: the path will lead you along the coast all the way to the Jungmun beach with spectacular views of the columnar jointed rocks. So if you want to exercise and take in the scenery at the same time, this is one scenic route you can take.Read more about my experience and photos at my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/jusangjeollidae-columnar-joints.html

Admission is 2000 won. Need to walk down a flight of stairs to reach the beach area. The beach is full of pebbles and rocks and you need to careful to balance your body as you walk or hop from one rock to another. It may be slippery at certain spots and do exercise some precaution when taking photographs. The cliff looks steep and this is the only unique waterfall in Asia where the water falls directly into the sea. While the waterfall was not as awesome as what I earlier saw in books, the sensation was relaxing and cooling with the thundery roar of the waterfall at the backdrop while you sat at the beach rocks gazing at the azure sea. It was an unique pristine natural scenery to appreciate and absorb. At Cheonjeyeon Falls, the attraction is secluded and one could not see the vast horizon of the ocean whereas here at Jeongbang Waterfall, the waterfall and the beach integrated into the ocean giving a wholesome broad vision effect. At Jusangjeolli Cliffs, one could only enjoy the serene sight of the torrential waves crashing against the blackish rock pillars from the elevated observation point and access to the beach area is prohibited. Jeongbang Waterfall gives us the convenient access to the beach area and so near to a gorgeous waterfall and a looming cliff. Like Yongduam Rock which is backed up by a dragon head legend, Jeongbang Waterfall also has a story of Seobul, a servant of the Chinese Emperor Jin  who was ordered by the Emperor to search for an elixir and he happened to by-pass this area during his search. An inscription written `Seobulgwacha' on the wall of the water fall was derived from this legend but I did not walk too near to the waterfall to see clearly that inscription. Jeju has quite a number of world class natural wonders and each wonder gives me a different perspective in appreciating nature.

Accessible by ferry. Udo is a tiny island so you wont get lost while wandering around this island. Filled with canola fields during spring, fresh breeze, peaceful atmosphere, sights of female divers, it is perfect for a daytrip. However if you plan to drive, just be extra careful as the roads are narrow.

A workout by renting bikes at port to ride around the whole island.  You get to see very different types of sand and beaches, you?ll better realize why they call it mini-jeju island.  The island?s famous peanuts have thin skin and not bitter as your typical peanut skins.  If you have elderly with you, there are golf carts for rent too!

A volcanic rock that looks like a dragon head looking up the sky,  NATURAL surrounding with lots of volcanic rocks formed by molten lava creating a scenic and spectacular view.  You can walk carefully along the volcanic rock to go as close to the dragon formation as you can for better photography.   Different time of the day, different view against the Sky. This place is beautiful , windy and cold even in spring.  No entrance fee! There is a man made mermaid, and 2 man made stone guardians of the land  There are 2 souvenir shops, grilled cuttlefish shop , ice cream and fruit stalls depending very much on tourists.  The Jeju airport is nearby and if you have the time, can count the planes landing and taking off at a busy airport.  Further away, there are motel and seafood restaurants.    We like the tasty green abalone porridge and the fresh and tasty seafood soup.All in all , I like this tourist place very much, I like earth natural formation very much.

A very short and busy road clogged by tourists, tour buses and cars trying to see and feel the uphill rolling effect. I personally did not see anything rolling uphill. Tour guides poured water and empty round mineral water bottles but it did not seem to give any credence to the anomaly. However I did see one car roll backwards (uphill) rather fast but couldn't tell if it was already in-gear, nevertheless the reverse lights weren't illuminated so I guess it wasn't rolling on it's own steam.

A unique must-do in my books to go where lava has gone before.   It is also a cave, so it dark, a little chilly with the occasional water drop.  The cave is left largely in its raw form (which was great) but it also meant an uneven and potholed path which requires a great deal of care walking it.

A stunning waterfall that one can get close to it. Can be crowded especially in the afternoon. A short 5 min walk from the car park. the rocks where people usually gather to take picture of the stunning waterfall can be slippery, not recommended for elderly visitors.

A short stretch of road that has vehicles rolling up a slope. Our driver even got out and place an empty bottle on the road and the bottle, like the car roll upwards.Amazing, got to see it to believe it.
A short distance of the road where it looks like uphill but when we put our car gear in neutral, the car moves !!! legends say it is because there are ghost pushing your car from behind !

A short 20 mins drive from the Jungmun resort area. Very easy to navigate and locate with the clear road signs available. Admission was just KRW 2,000 per adult. Very reasonable. The Waterfall is a short flight of stairs down from the main carpark. There were large groups of Korean high school students visiting during our time there so we just followed the crowd. Took us less than 15 mins to get down to the fall. Perhaps it's not the rainy season, the waterfall seemed tiny (compared to Niagara etc). The water flowed first into a stone pool before trickling into the sea. Not very impressive but a nice destination for our family with a toddler. He had a great time trying to balance on the big rocks by the fall. Next to the fall, there were 2 women divers selling abalone and sea squirts. I saw local tourists eating them as sashimi sitting right there on the rocks. Interesting.

A short 10 mins walk down down several flights of steps would lead u to the base of the fall. For the adventurous and nimble folks, you can navigate carefully across the rocks to get nearer to the waterfall. I was there on a crowded day and the task of leaping from rock to rock didn?t seem possible. It was still a nice view from the base. Do include this site in your itinerary. I think the volume of water was lesser since it was still winter when I visited.

A road seems to be uphill, but it is in fact a downhill. The driver shut off the engine at the 'downhill' but the car moves itself towards the 'uphill' without the help of anyone. Fun fact by tour guide: This mysterious incident was discovered by a taxi driver when he intend to take a leak at the roadside and found out the car moves itself towards the uphill after he stopped the car.

A relaxing trail with picturesque scenery. I went during autumn and the climate was just right. The leaves turning brown was a breathtaking sight and if you're lucky, you will be able to catch a glimpse of deers along the trails.Do be careful along the steep slopes during certain parts of the trail as a missed step could result in some pain. There are water points on the trail though located a substantial distance from each other. Do bring your own food or you can buy it from a store near the summit. Bear in mind that you will have to bring along your trash and don't leave it on the mountain! (Bring along extra trash bags!)
A nice break from the heat, it's nice and cool down there!You can walk 1km, I think we spent about an hour down there total.Really slippery, be careful!One of the coolest things I did in Jeju.

A 'must see' place when visiting the island. Lots of small shops around the entrance, a small fee (free if you work on the island), lots of stairs (a fairly tough climb) that lead to a variety of small temples and places to check out. Views are fantastic and on a clear day even better. You can get their by local bus although there is car parking but no 'wheel' access for baby strollers or wheelchairs. The golden Buddha and the drums give you an amazing feeling sitting so high above the surrounding area. Definitely worth it.

A must do in Jeju. We hired a taxi driver to take us and it was 2000won a person to enter. We wanted to go for sunrise but there was an extra fee to hire them that early. (If you want to rent a car, make sure you have an international license - it's about 1.5hr from Jeju city) The hike really isn't too bad. It is an incline, and yes there are lots of stairs, but it is do-able. There were plenty of elderly hiking up and lots of places to stop. Beautiful view from up top. Entrance also allows you to go down to the beach and see the women divers and eat fresh catch.
A magnetic hill. Interesting if you?ve never seen one before. Otherwise, just another hill where your car appears to roll uphill.

A little short distance adventure for about 2km round trip. Insides the lava tube, you can see different kind of volcanic stones formed by the lava last time. Be prepared with proper sports shoes as the pathway in the cave is a bit crooked. Be careful.

A great place to witness how the lava which was erupted centuries ago formed the cliffs. A great place to view sunset as well. The scenery is amazing. However, that's all to it. Will prob take less than 30 mins. Entrance fee cost 2k won per person. If you are driving, do not follow the directions given by GPS. It will bring you to a hotel instead. You should instead drive to the Jeju International Convention Center (ICC) and follow the signs there. The carpark is payable as well, albeit a small fee of 1-2k won, depending on the capacity of your vehicle.

A difficult one if you choose to do the longest one which takes 4.5 hrs up and 4 hrs down.We went up  the  Eorimok trail which took us 2 n half hours up..its not an easy trak with steps and rocky path but the track has been laid with a lot of effort.In autumn the trees start to turn their colours .We came down the yeongsil trail which took us one hour to come down with spectac views..its an easier way to climb down than to climb up the yongsil trail.Bus 240 goes and come back at both stops with the entrance name as the stop names.But while from Eiromok entrance it's just a 10 mins walk up to the start of the trail.....its 45 mins walk to walk to the yeongsil entrance bus stop to the start of the trail.There are no tkts entrance for the hikes,but if you have rented a car then there is a parking fees.Carry some food to eat and energy bars and water n juice.

A bit difficult to find, but a gorgeous location.   The waterfall flows into a small pool and then flows into the sea.  It was pretty crowded when we went, but still worth going.  The rocks are SLIPPERY.  Be careful when moving around on them as we saw a few people fall.  There are a few shops selling snacks and Jeju treats at the top and a proper coffee shop as well.

30 mins drive out from Jeju City.  My Wife and Daughter accompanied me on the first 2.5km of the 11.1km yellow route, then they took a short cut back (around 1.2km) to relax at the Korean style picnic tables and visit the carp pond.  I took another 1.5 hrs or so to complete the yellow route, which by the way is circular, not an up and back as reported sometimes previously. I came across plenty of deer, as well as some beautiful birds and flowers.  The first 5km or so has hessian Mats to walk on, which is very peasant, but then it gets a bit muddy and rocky, with a few steep sections.....walking boots or trail shoes are definitely best, although possible in Trainers.  Really enjoyed the hike.

2 things you must take with you for visiting Udo island - swimming suit and international driving licence. In case you want to rent ATV or scooter you should have international driving license, otherwise you will have to enjoy beauty of the island riding  bicycle. There are 2 sandy beaches available. Ferry can bring your car straight to the island.

1) The staff spoke limited English. When we got into the room, it appeared the A/C was not working. We told the staff and their response was that it was made such so as guests no need to turn on the A/C. A/C is only available during summer. They advised us to open the window / take a shower instead to feel fresher.1st night in the hotel, we couldn't sleep as the noise from the air (the hotel is near the airport) and road traffic entered our room as well as the dust.2) The casino opening hour was stated 10:00AM - 01:30AM. I tried to enter the casino at 11:00PM, got told that I would not be able to play (just seeing) as the casino is closing.3) Room is spacious and the bed is comfortable. However, the room and the hotel corridor have weird smell. It must be the carpet smell. The room has an old-looking room and most things in the room are payable (you only get the toiletries and 2 bottles of water)..In conclusion, very terrible experience staying in this hotel. I would not spend a single dollar to this hotel in future.

wow they have the most expensive teddy bear in the world!!! all the collection is exclusive and very very cute. heaven for me ^_^ love it very very much. I think this is the most interesting teddy museum i ever seen. 100% very highly recommended.
Worth a visit at least once. Pleasant walk round the folk village. Good collection. Could do better with more displays in English. But all in all thumbs-up for this place..

When I was a kid I would see Ripley's Believe it or Not on TV.? This is a great collection of bizarre everything from Elvis's hair to antique torture tools.? Our family had a great time there.? Bonus that there is a Starbucks next door.

Well  that's one I definitely wouldn't recommand. There are so many things to do in Jeju and many in a 5-km radius even (Sanbangguksa  Yongmeori Beach  Songaksan...) but the Hamel Ship exhibition center is a miss. It would have actually been interesting to have place dedicated to the historical significance of Hamel and Korea through foreigners' eyes  but this was just a small collection of cheap and run-down replicas of things you could see pretty much everywhere. Maybe kids would enjoy the pirate-looking ship  but that's the only good reason to go.

review: Visit this place even if you not interested or lover of sea shells at least to recognise the sheer efforts put in by Ms Myeong Yeon Sook  the director of this museum and owner of this place. This museum which has over 7 800 variety and accounting to more than millions of sea shells originating in Jeju and the world is the brain child of Ms Sook and master Metal craftsman Kwon Oh-Kyun.The beauty of these sea shells are to be seen to be believed. They have been arranged and displayed so artistically that one may easily mistake it as a painting.One may not see much of visitors around  but this really helps as we go around enjoying the magic of nature.Entrance fee is a bit high  but really worth it  considering the efforts put in to bring this huge collection of sea shells under one roof and creating the world's first seashell museum.
Very well put together with a fantastic collection of music which really compliments the art making it a fully immersive experience. Well worth a visit.
Very impressive bonsai tree collection. Interesting underground caves with both lava and lime. Not crowded.

This place is rather far from where stayed (it would take about an hour from Jeju city/Seogwipo) and if you have a car you can enjoy the scenic route passing by horse farms and ATV parks and occasionally some towns. Make sure your car has enough petrol/gas as we didn't note much stations during our drive.It is located at a bay by the sea which has a good view (after you are done with the aquarium). There is a parking lot available but we were there on a super busy day despite being a Monday (we just thought that maybe it was the school holidays?) and we were lucky to get a lot.Place is stroller friendly but be mindful if the place is quite full. Everyone can get mesmerised by the display and you may just knocked by a stroller or two.The displays are quite entertaining. There are some attractions such as otter/pelicans feeding. You can check the time of these attractions at their website and you can time your visit there. There is a underwater tunnel and the manta rays will just swim pass.There was a huge aquarium display and unfortunately for us we were not able to the see the whale shark they were housing as it had been released back into the sea for research purpose. At certain times there will be a feeding session by scuba divers. The penguin display had some fake penguins in between and for some reason they look pretty realistic beside a real one when the real ones don't move. Have fun figuring out which is which!There was a show featuring synchronized swimming diving from high places. The show was about pirates and fairies. Everyone enjoyed the show (all in Korean with English displayed on the screen) and we were just clapping without really understanding what's going on but you will sort of understand the story. After about 20 minutes or so there was a seal show followed by a dolphin show. Again in Korean and you just shout and clap whenever the locals do. (For the language: it is the same in all other countries. Just be don't care and enjoy the show!) The show was about 45 minutes long and there is a stand outside selling popcorn and peanut butter roasted squid (a must try!) so get some and enjoy the show.On another wing there is a small science museum and a 3D theater. You can skip the museum and head outdoors (as most are in Korean) but there is a holographic display of the whale shark inside that is really cool. Attraction is free. For the 3D theater not sure if we had to pay an additional sum but it was featuring a shark show and we reckoned the kids would be terrified.There is a cafeteria downstairs and the food is pretty good. You will need to pay at a counter which they will give you a device which beeps when the food is ready for collection. If can get quite crowded as there's limited space. During your walk there will be pop up stands selling food so you don't have worry about getting hungry while walking around.After it all head outside for the scenic view and some outdoor picture taking. We were there on a gloomy day and wind was pretty strong.

review: This museum is one of the most popular of the 50+ on Jeju Island and the carpark was packed with tour buses when we arrived. But if you can manage to get a slot on one of the formal tea ceremonies it really takes you out of the bustling tourist crowds and takes you to another place altogether. The time and care taken for all the preparations was amazing and could not have been more different to having a casual cuppa at home! I am not sure they do them in English - our host spoke in Korean but our little group had an interpreter to help us out. The venue used for this ceremony is also amazing. Beautiful minimal stone and wood shaped furniture in a sunlight-filled pavilion looking out onto the lawns of the museum. We also had a glimpse into the underground tea cellar area and a quick tour round the tourist shop. The collection of tea cups from different countries and eras was fascinating too in the area next to the shop.
This is not a museum. It's a collection of anything vaguely sex-related. It really seems like something a middle-schooler designed. Please save your money.

This is not a bias assessment. I would be glad if the establishment owner would take in advise from visitor feedback. This is my first time to rate an establishment with such a low rating. It is a total rip-off as entrance fee is collected before cafe and store. There nothing impressive with the collection and exhibit area is extremely small. There is another fees impose for DIY chocolate making session. No educational value  no entertainment value. I would not recommend it to anyone.
This is just a regular museum with a small collection of glass from different parts of the world. It is far away from everything and not worth the trip. I would skip it.
This is another product of Korean creativity. This is just a place where a Teddy Bear collections located and opened for public. The shape of the dolls were not so perfect and some were ugly.
This is an amazing collection of natural and men made stones in Jeju. In addition it has an outstanding water instillation and an indoor unique museum. Truly worth the visit

This is a contemporary art museum by the seafront in Jeju city showcasing a private collection in a disused cinema and an old bikeshop. There are many varied exhibits from China to Germany Korea to France.we especially liked a music and light show by French artist Pierre Huyghe (l'Exp챕dition scintillante).Entry is W12000 for adults and covers both buildings.

This collection of old houses and replication of villages was fascinating. One could really understand the way of living in the old times when getting up close to the stone construction and thatched roofs and garden plots. This is a perfect walking area for anyone and especially families. As an added bonus the little restaurant on site was reasonable for local dishes.

They ?쐒eborn??the dead and colorful insects to put them on displays as they are living the life of human with small scenes in the glass frames. We are amazed and especially impressed with the bugs playing football and the goalkeeper bug was catching it! There are also a huge collection of butterflies and other species in this museum.

There are so much to see in this museum. The whole day is enough to spend here if you want to read and appreciate all the displays. Good collections. I learned a lot from this museum. I regret doing four museum tours in one day for we had to rush this one. I would love to go back here.
The staff at the museum was lovely and welcoming  truly nice. The collection of seashell is quite impressive.

The park is definitely worth a visit for people who appreciate the beauty of nature. there's so much too see that one should reserve at least half a day for that park. The caves are also very impessive. there are restrooms and benches all over the park and everything's very clean. the collection of bonsai are impressive as well as the village of traditional jeju-houses.

The owner of the museum is an artist himself and one of the most important collectors in the world. I was totally taken away with many of the artworks and with the location itself(specially the Bike-Shop and the Cinema). One of my reasons for traveling South-Korea is discovering and enjoying modern art. This is the best collection I have seen in this country so far (out of around 30 museums and galleries). I was totally surprised to see this level of Art in Jeju and will definitely visit Arario in Space when I am back to Seoul.

The little museum has a simple collection of vintage tea cups from around the world. I am obsessive about tea cups so was very happy with the unplanned encounter. There was a small section on the history of tea but unfortunately for us it was mostly written in Korean. The place was buzzing even after its opening hours. Service was quick and friendly. Wide tea selection no lesser than the two O?셎ulloc stores in Insadong and Myeongdong. Above average tea beverages and desserts. (For green tea fan who is familiar with Japanese tea - this is the Tsujiri equivalent of Korea).As some reviewers has mentioned this is a tea shop+cafe+museum so don?셳 expect just a museum.

The Joanne Bear Museum is one of the stops in the package tour that we availed of. It is basically a collection of stuffed bears that Joanne Oh has created  each bear hand made. There are three buildings where all the bears are housed. We were there in winter and the place was well-heated. The pathway between the buildings were open air  though. The bears came in different sizes  colors and variations. There are some depict historical or cultural scenes  others depict pop culture. The bears are all finely crafted. Unfortunately though  many of the signage are in Korean only.There are several displays where guests can pose with the bears. One of those bears  a polar bear  was featured in a Korean drama  ?쏱aradise Ranch.??I especially loved the displays that feature the acronym of the place (JB) because it is my initial as well. There is a souvenir shop which sell?봸ou guessed it right?봲tuffed bears. I wanted to have one as a souvenir so I was settling for the least expensive keychain bear when I saw a much larger 8-inch plushie being sold at a discounted rate; it was only 2 000 won more expensive than the keychain so I got it instead. As with many of the Joanne bears  it an embroidery of Joanne Oh's signature.

The green tea flavour food collection is greatCan take a close look of green tea fieldA good place for souvenir as there are wide range of tea collection However it is not suggested to go on rainy day
The Dolhareubong (grandfather rock) collection on the grounds outside the building were my favorite part of the museum.

The aquarium is good and the penguins and sharks are worth watching. Huge collection of marine life you cant miss...The show seemed to be a bit dragging. Before the sealion and dolphin show there was a 'good pirate bad pirate ' show which for me was a bit boring. Dolphin show also wasted time showing videos. But towards last 5 mins it was good.

review: That is the first time I am rating a place terrible. To begin with there are only Korean introduction and description for all the items and collections displayed there. We all read Korean don't we?As stated in other reviews this place has zero content. I can easily find more chocolate related stuff in a convenience store that this so called chocolate land. Worse  the entry ticket is bundled with a purchase voucher of the chocolate items sold at the store in this place. Contradictory to the all Korean introductions and descriptions  the chocolate available in the store are all international brands. If you are looking for the experience of travelling to Korea to buy chocolate probably from your own country  there you go!

Seashell and coral art in their fascinating and natural colors. The seashells' mysterious world under the sea-- as designed by several artists. (is this a title. If not keep original sentence) With a collection of 7 800 species  hundreds of millions of beautiful shells and corals from all around the world joined by metal craft and copper  present the world's first 'Museum of Seashell Art'

Recommended place to visit for family with young children and teddy bear lovers as this museum holds a large collection of teddy bears with themes all over the world. Downside is that souvenirs are way too expensive.

O'Sulloc Tea Museum  is actually a shopping paradise for those who fancy for tea. O'Sulloc itself is famous for its Tea product. In front there's a collection of used cups that they arranged in such a way so it's picturesque.Since It's a green tea field expect for green tea product for sale including all side products (Cake Drinks etc). The shop available also allows us to test some of their products We let ourself went down to the greentea field and see what's actually a green tea look like when it's not harvested yet. We also have a little chat with the tea-picker ajumma. If you go to the upper floor you will be able to take picture of overall green tea field but don't expect too much.I recommend time of visit when the sun not in its brightest Enjoy!
Nothing much about the views but their tea collection is amazing and all of it nice. A bit expensive but definately worth it to buy the various tea from there!
Not that Jeju Museum of Art was a disappointment just that it was a small place to see limited collection.

My visit here with my family was superb for the world's most expensive teddy bear (in LV) was on display. The history and evolution of teddies on display was noteworthy. Huge collection. My daughter enjoyed the cuddly toys as well and could not resist to buy some souvenirs. I found it cute dressing up the teddies like the superstars especially Marilyn Monroe & Michael Jackson. Superb!

Exotic Jeju Island is known for many things: the majestic Hallasan--the massive shield volcano that formed the island and the highest point in South Korea; its mandarin groves; persimmon-dyed galot fashions; the sturdy Jeju ma horses  descended from the ponies of Mongol invaders; tasty black pork; and the iconic haenyeo women divers. But most visitors would not expect to find a Museum of African Art there. And  it's pretty darn good! Located in a massive structure modeled after the mud-brick Great Mosque of Djenne  the museum offers photo-ops galore in its Safari section  although the animals are of the stuffed variety. Very popular with children and couples. The upper floors house a respectable collection of African artifacts and photographs by Kim Jung Man. There is also a great gift shop. But  I have saved the best for last...the live performance of African folk music and dance. The group  Zalia from Senegal  featured lots of drumming  and audience members also got a drumming lesson and a chance to play along on one song. All in all  a quality experience...and a surprising one.
