Self-Drive Holiday in Jeju:Everyone loves going on holidays and I believe a great percentage of these do so on guided tours. Guided tours are fine where convenience is concerned; hotels, meals, itineraries, transport, flights, places of interests to visit, entrance fees etc. etc. are all taken care of by the tour company. As I had discovered decades ago, despite all the conveniences of a guided tour, there are drawbacks that would put one off such tours completely; not being able to sleep-in and wake up as and when you want, having limited time to enjoy the various places of interests or enjoy your lunch while taking in the magnificent scenery from a mountain top restaurant , having to put up with other travellers who simply cannot or are not bothered to be on time, not being able to visit or enjoy other interesting places that are rarely included in tour itineraries, to list a few. Ever since my first guided tour holiday overseas, I have opted for a self-drive holiday and I am very sure there are many out there who would love to do so too,  but refrained from doing so because of a lack of information and perhaps, apprehensive about what it would entail to do a self-drive holiday in a foreign land. This guide is to help dispel those apprehensions and provide the necessary information for you to successfully make that first self-drive holiday in the Honeymoon Island of Jeju, and hopefully, many more thereafter in other destinations of your dreams.Preparation:Many experts would advise, and rightly so, that you should first read up all the necessary information on driving at the destination that you will be holidaying in. However, in my opinion, what is more important is having the self-confidence to drive in a foreign land. Sometimes, things can go wrong, road and weather conditions can change to the extent that no pre-reading or preparation can help, but, with that very important self-confidence, it will see you through. You must also have a flexible mind set and be ready to accommodate changes when necessary ? only then will you be able to thoroughly enjoy your self-drive holiday. Having said that, I must say that driving in Jeju is a walk-in-the-park, quite unlike, for example, driving through the mountain pass between Sun Moon Lake and Hualien County in Taiwan ? that is a drive I would never recommend to the feint hearted.International Driving Permit ? you will need to obtain an International Driving Permit to be able to rent a car in Jeju, and for that matter, in most other countries. It can be easily obtained at AAS and it costs only $20.00 and is valid for one year. You would also want to search for information on all the places of interests and decide on which of those to visit during your stay in Jeju. This is to help you plan and minimize travelling time. These can be had at the Korea Tourism Centre at Samsung CentreChoice of Hotel ? There are many hotels catering to different needs and budgets to choose from. The one most often asked question is the location ? to stay in Jeju-si or Seogwipo-si? My experience tells me that it makes no difference ? it is just a matter of choice. If you are arriving in Jeju late at night, then, perhaps, you may wish to stay in a hotel that is near the airport, to minimize your night driving had you decided on a hotel in Seogwipo-si. We landed in Jeju at 2000 hrs, collected our car at 2100 hrs and drove to Seogwipo-si where our hotel was situated. It was a pleasant forty-five minute drive with guidance from the GPS unit.Car Rental Company:There are many car rental companies in Jeju, but you will most likely come across only a handful if you search the internet ? Kumho, AJ Rentals (AVIS), SIXT, Donga and Jeju Rent-a-Car. Do note, though, that there are more than a dozen of competing rental companies at the airport to choose from if you prefer to shop around for the best rates and cars upon your arrival. I book mine through AJ Rentals, not only because of the brand name, but it also provided the best rates among the others on the net and it did not require me to pay in advance upon confirmation of my reservation. To rent the car, you will need to have an International Driving Permit (obtain it from AAS), your local driving license and passport. You can pay either in cash or credit card. Type of Car:The type of car you choose is totally dependent on your preference and budget ? luxury or basic. However, do consider the available boot space that will be needed to accommodate your luggage. As a guide, the boot of a KIA K3 can accommodate only three large suitcases with no space for a smaller, fourth piece. In a situation where there are four adults, the smaller, fourth suitcase will have to share estate space in the back seat with two other passengers. The cost of rental is dependent on the type of car, number of days and the period of travel. As a guide, a KIA K3 cost approximately S$60.00 per day for 5 days during the holiday season in November. The rate includes insurance, CDW and the use of a English language GPS, with collection and return at the airport. The rates of the other rental companies that I surveyed were cheaper, however, I cannot vouch for their quality nor service support. You decide at your own risk. The overall condition of the car was good. The only ?defect? was the slight steering alignment problem but it was not something that would put us in danger at any time. Maps:Do you need a map when it is very likely that you will be relying on the GPS? YES! A map is necessary for planning your routes and selecting the places of interests to visit.You can easily obtain a detailed map of Jeju Island, with all the major highways and feeder routes from your local Korean Tourism office. You can also obtain these from the car-rental companies when you collect your car in Jeju. You can use it to plan your route, estimate the travel time and locate other possible places of interests that you don?t find on the standard tourist trail. You can use this same map to write down the telephone numbers of the places of interests that you plan to visit. You will need these numbers for keying into the GPS system to guide you to your destination. I made it a point to re-confirm that the telephone numbers are current by asking the hotel staff to extract the numbers from their computer system. This proved to be very useful. Collecting Your Car At The Airport:After clearing immigration and customs, proceed to gate 5 of the arrival terminal. Opposite the gate, there is a green, covered walk-way with a sign that says ?Car Rentals?; it will lead you to a building where there are a lot of car-rental companies. If you had pre-booked your car, look for the car-rental company in the building. However, do take note that this building houses the local car rental companies. For the international brands such as Avis, Hertz and the other bigger local companies, they are housed in another location outside the airport. You will need to check with them when you are doing the booking or email them for the information. If the collection centre of the car rental company that you booked with is located outside the airport, wait for their shuttle bus at Gate 5. You will recognize their shuttle bus by their brand name boldly emblazoned on the sides of the bus. Since I booked my car through Avis, I took the ?AJ? shuttle bus to their rental office on the outskirts of the airport. The shuttle bus runs on a regular schedule. Arriving at the front of the office, you take a queue ticket. If you had made reservations, it takes just a few seconds to call up your reservation after presenting your passport, driver's licence and International Driving Permit. You will be shown the rental agreement with all the details pertaining to the type, class, number of days of rental, total costs and any other relevant information. With Avis, the GPS is included in the rental, whereas for other rental companies that I had enquired with, the GPS is charged separately. After you have signed the rental agreement, you will be shown your car. You then drive it off to the inspection building where they will go through the car with you to identify any minor damages, scratches, dents etc. They will also have you verify that the fuel tank is full and instruct you on the use of the GPS before getting you to sign off the acknowledgement form. Do ensure that the GPS is an English language version. Keep the documents safely in the glove-compartment and be sure to get the telephone number of the station that you will return the car to. You will need this number to key into the GPS system to guide you back. You then proceed on your way, presumably, to your hotel for a much needed rest after the long flight to Jeju.When returning the car, you just need to drive back to the same depot from where you had collected it. Just key the given number into the GPS. Upon arrival, follow the sign, ?Car Return? and head for an available lot. The attendant there will check the car with you and when all is in order, he hands you a form to sign after you have returned the key to him. You then take the shuttle bus that will take you to the departure hall at the airport.The use of the GPS:Different makes and models operate slightly differently from one another, however, the common function that generalizes all of them is the use of the telephone number of a particular hotel, attraction or establishment to program the location into the GPS. For example, the telephone number of our hotel, Ocean Palace Hotel, Jeju, is 064 - 7305800. To navigate to the hotel from the airport, I just had to key in the number 7305800 and simply touch the 'Navigate' button and voila, it calculates the shortest route and starts the voice navigation system in a jiffy - it's as simple as that. From then on, just follow the voice navigation to get you to your hotel. If you make a wrong turn or pass a junction where you were supposed to turn, do not panic. Just relax and drive on ? it will re-direct you back to the planned route or at times, provide you with a new course. In fact, we had a lot of fun and discovered many new places of interest by intentionally turning off to smaller but interesting-looking roads just to see what lies ahead and where it will eventually lead us to ? that is the beauty of a self-drive holiday. Driving in Jeju:Jeju has a coastal ring road of approximately 181 km, not counting the connecting highways linking the North-South-East ?West regions. The coastal scene is a sight to behold! It is left-hand driving in Jeju.To those who have never driven on the left side of the road, it takes a little getting used to, physically as well as in your mind. It gets a little more confusing when turning at traffic junctions, especially when driving through ? stopping gives you an opportunity to orientate yourself and prepare in your mind the lane to take when turning. To minimize this confusion, always try to follow a car in front of you which is turning in the same direction as you. It is also helpful to remember that when turning, the roadside kerb will always be on the right of the driver. The roads, save for the highways, are slightly narrower than the roads we are used to in Singapore.Generally, the speed limits are:30 Km / hr within 100 m of school zones50 Km / hr in town areas60 Km / hr in the outskirts of town70 Km / hr along highwaysThe speed limits change quite frequently, so it is advisable to keep a look-out for the change in speed limits. There are speed-cameras practically everywhere, usually positioned up on traffic lights, lamp-posts and in some places, hidden behind 'boxes' manned by a policeman. So, if you wish to spend your money supporting the policemen, speed on at your own risk.The local drivers can, at times, be quite reckless. Just like we have hell-drivers here, there are hell-drivers in Jeju too, but not too many. Just stay alert and always be on the look-out using your wing and rearview mirrors all the time. Except for the main areas of Jeju-si and Seogwipo-si, most of the roads around the island are quite free of traffic.  To estimate the time needed to travel any distances, take an average speed of 45 km/hr.Parking:Generally free parking along kerb-sides and paid parking in some buildings and are generally available easily. Most hotels have free parking for their guests ? do check with the hotel management that you have booked with. Petrol cost: As at Nov 2014: Krw 1750 / ltrPlanning Your Routes:Planning your routes is totally at your own whim and fancy, depending on the places of interest as well as the available time you have on the island. If you have a few days ( I would recommend a minimum of five days), perhaps you may wish to consider the following suggestion:1. Day 1 ? Arrival and check into hotel. This sample itinerary is on the assumption that your hotel is in Seogwipo. 2. Day 2 ? Explore the west scenic coastal drive (Route 1132) of Sagye, Gosan-Ilwa, Hagwi-Aewol and visit the places of interest along this route ( Mt Sangkaksan / Songkaksan / Yongmeori). There are many cafes (especially along the Coastal Cafe Road) and bbq restaurants for stops of aromatic coffee and grilled black pig meat. Explore Jeju-si city (underground shopping mall) and return via highway 1131 where the famous ?Forest Tunnel? is located. After dinner, take a drive to the Lotte World Resort for some very beautiful night scenery of the giant windmills.3. Day 3 ? Go East this time along the Pyeoson, Sehwa-Jongdal and Gimyeong ? Haengwon coastal routes. Stopover at Seongsan Ilchubong (Sunrise Peak). Have dinner in Jeju-si before doing a night drive back to Seogwipo. 4. Day 4 ? Alternative 1Drive to Seongsan Port in the north-east via the eastern coastal route and park your car there. Purchase your ferry tickets to Udo Island and spend a very interesting day there. You can tour the island by buying the hop-off-on bus tickets or for the adventurers, you can hire the quad-bikes or scooters. Alternative 2 ? visit the popular tourist spots such as the Trick-art museum, teddy bear museum, waterfalls, submarine tours, Green Tea museum, Geomun Oreum, Citrus fruit farms, mysterious road, etc etc....5. Day 5 ? Check out of hotel for catch your flight back home.Have a safe and enjoyable holiday!Telephone Numbers of Attractions For GPS:Citrus Fruit Museum - 732 2114Geomun Oreum - 7108981Joongang Underground Mall - 723 1510Jusenggeolli Cliffs - 7381521Lotte Hotel - 731 1000Alive Museum - 805 0888Trick Art Museum - 787 8774Seongeup Folk Village - 787 1179Traditional 5 day market (Jeju-si) - 7435985Seongsan Harbour (Ferry to Udo Island) - 782 5671Seongsan Ilchubong - 783 0959Cheongyejeong Waterfall - 760 6331Cheongjiyeong Waterfall - 733 1528Jeongbang Waterfall - 733 1530Teddy Bear Museum - 738 7600Jeju Folk Village - 787 4501Jeju Sea-World - 784 2333Aqua Planet Jeju - 780 0900Manjanggul Cave - 710 7903Oedolgae - 760 3033

Hallim park is part botanical garden, mini zoo, and culture center. The majority of Hallim is mediocre, but the jewel of the park is its rich bonsai collection. There's an extensive range of bonsai trees at display, some of them are over 300 years old. To those unfamiliar with bonsai trees, they may just be miniature trees; but to those who know the value of these works of art, these bonsai trees are literally priceless. In fact, it's almost unbelievable how openly accessible these trees are to the guests, considering their value and need for extreme care.If you're planning on visiting, briefly study the artistry before your trip to enhance the enjoyment. This is a one-of-a-kind collection.

With Snoopy Garden’s steep entrance fee it initially didn’t make my itinerary. The indoor museum part was the highlight for me which had explanations about every main Peanuts character and several comic clips that span over Schulz’s 50 years of drawing them. The old newspaper clippings old toys and old books were also cool to look at. There are dozens of great photo spots which can create some major bottlenecks on crowded days. The garden had about half a dozen themed areas (including my favorite Charlie Brown’s baseball field) that are pretty vast and would have been a lot more pleasant to walk around in cooler weather. We skipped the cafe that charged a criminal 8500 won for a lemonade. I’m not sure that the high price of admission is justified but this is a well maintained attraction(which is refreshing considering the high number of run down museums and small theme parks in Jeju) and the quality of the displays are of superb quality. Adults and children both also fans and non-fans of Peanuts both would enjoy the visit here.

There were quite a few hands on displays like static balls  using bikes to light up a display  a few trick eye displays  plasma globes  and of course Tesla coils. Else you may wanna consider stay longer in the Believe it or not Museum or even the Alive Museum :)

Was fun taking photos at Alive museum we visited the museum at night and I guess because of that there were fewer tourists which meant what we could actually interact with the art more and did more funny shots with the art displayed.A great place for families young and old.

Visited the Park based on TA reviews. Extremely well done with extensive museums and stone displays. Allow at least 3-4 hours for the visit. Enormous work has gone into the development of the Park. Should be in the Top 5 attractions in Jeju outside the beaches.

Visited the museum just for the fun of it and was amused by some of the statues on display. Didn't think too much of it though so if this isn't on one of the must do's on your holiday list you can probably skip it and not miss much.

Visited on a friend's recommendation and it definitely didn't disappoint.  Upon entry to the building we walked through the historical display area before getting to the shop and cafe.  There were many different types of tea for sale and all beautifully packaged.  Again thanks to the friend who asked us to help buy stuff for her we knew to get the green tea milk spread.  For the tea they had samples for you to smell before purchasing.  We got the wedding tea green tea and green tea cold sticks. Can't wait to get home to try them.  Next we had the green tea roll green tea ice cream and green tea milk shake at the cafe.  All were exquisite.  On the outdoors there are great photo opportunities near the tea plantation.  As we walked there we discovered another building called Innisfree Jeju House.  It was a health food restaurant cum shop selling body oils and moisturiser.  We had lunch there and bought some beautiful smelling body lotion.  Again all fantastic.  The whole family enjoyed O'Sulloc!

Visited during a rainy day. Really not much to see but a large shop for purchasing chocolate with displays of chocolate from around the world. Lots of locally produced chocolate to purchase. It put in a half hour during the rain

review: Visit this place even if you not interested or lover of sea shells at least to recognise the sheer efforts put in by Ms Myeong Yeon Sook  the director of this museum and owner of this place. This museum which has over 7 800 variety and accounting to more than millions of sea shells originating in Jeju and the world is the brain child of Ms Sook and master Metal craftsman Kwon Oh-Kyun.The beauty of these sea shells are to be seen to be believed. They have been arranged and displayed so artistically that one may easily mistake it as a painting.One may not see much of visitors around  but this really helps as we go around enjoying the magic of nature.Entrance fee is a bit high  but really worth it  considering the efforts put in to bring this huge collection of sea shells under one roof and creating the world's first seashell museum.
Very informative but ofcourse the internet can tell us about those things. There are some display that scared me as im all alone when i visited the place. Overall i find it entertaining.

Very disappointing. There were a few panels in the entrance hall that had information about chocolate and very poorly kept display boxes  but everything was only in Korean. Downstairs  you can see chocolate packages from different countries  but mostly ordinary products that can be bought in Korean supermarkets. No effort was given to make a proper display with special chocolates. Plus  some chocolates were mislabeled under the wrong countries. There was a station where chocolates in bags could be squeezed into molds. I was not able to participate because the staff panicked when they saw a non-Korean face  despite the fact that I spoke Korean to them. Do yourself a favor and go in the convenience store across the road - there is a better display of chocolate there.
Very beautiful art work on display. Great for all types of groups! Amazing place for photos and for a different appreciation to art. Highly recommend!

Ultra modern building houses green tea related information and displays.But you really want to snack on green tea themed ice creams or others and walk in the garden of lush green tea shrubs.As garden is outdoors you want to avoid visiting during rain showers.

To fully enjoy cultural heritage it is recommended that you spent few hours reading and inspect all the objects that represents it.Even though it was raining during the time I visited I enjoyed the Folk village because they have a very interesting culture and history dated thousands of years.In each places represents how the Koreans house hold systems livelihood and government are highly organized.I also enjoyed the art exhibit and felt honored meeting the National artist.  He even gave me one of his works on display!After roaming around you might want to experience authentic Jeju cuisine by dropping at the Traditional Market inside the Folk village at reasonable price. Oh don't forget to try the Cactus candy!It's just unfortunate that we haven't witness any Korean traditional wedding ceremony that day due to rain.This is much better Folk Village to visit as it is bigger than the other nearby.

Thought it was gonna be some just rows and rows of teddy bear displays but was pleasantly surprised by the presentation and the whole set-up...the curators really have got a sense of humour!  :)was more like entering an art museum...

This place was way beyond my expectations.We visited most of aquariums in north east america since we have a little child and live near by new york city but this aquarium is one of the best compares to those in america.2yr old facility has lots of displays and shows.Very clean and up close displays so children can find interests.You should watch aqua aerobic and sea animal show. It is fun and amazing.The view from the building is spectacular.We found great deal with 20% off admission on internet so it was worthy for about $30.

review: This place is rather far from where stayed (it would take about an hour from Jeju city/Seogwipo) and if you have a car you can enjoy the scenic route passing by horse farms and ATV parks and occasionally some towns. Make sure your car has enough petrol/gas as we didn't note much stations during our drive.It is located at a bay by the sea which has a good view (after you are done with the aquarium). There is a parking lot available but we were there on a super busy day despite being a Monday (we just thought that maybe it was the school holidays?) and we were lucky to get a lot.Place is stroller friendly but be mindful if the place is quite full. Everyone can get mesmerised by the display and you may just knocked by a stroller or two.The displays are quite entertaining. There are some attractions such as otter/pelicans feeding. You can check the time of these attractions at their website and you can time your visit there. There is a underwater tunnel and the manta rays will just swim pass.There was a huge aquarium display and unfortunately for us we were not able to the see the whale shark they were housing as it had been released back into the sea for research purpose. At certain times there will be a feeding session by scuba divers. The penguin display had some fake penguins in between and for some reason they look pretty realistic beside a real one when the real ones don't move. Have fun figuring out which is which!There was a show featuring synchronized swimming diving from high places. The show was about pirates and fairies. Everyone enjoyed the show (all in Korean with English displayed on the screen) and we were just clapping without really understanding what's going on but you will sort of understand the story. After about 20 minutes or so there was a seal show followed by a dolphin show. Again in Korean and you just shout and clap whenever the locals do. (For the language: it is the same in all other countries. Just be don't care and enjoy the show!) The show was about 45 minutes long and there is a stand outside selling popcorn and peanut butter roasted squid (a must try!) so get some and enjoy the show.On another wing there is a small science museum and a 3D theater. You can skip the museum and head outdoors (as most are in Korean) but there is a holographic display of the whale shark inside that is really cool. Attraction is free. For the 3D theater not sure if we had to pay an additional sum but it was featuring a shark show and we reckoned the kids would be terrified.There is a cafeteria downstairs and the food is pretty good. You will need to pay at a counter which they will give you a device which beeps when the food is ready for collection. If can get quite crowded as there's limited space. During your walk there will be pop up stands selling food so you don't have worry about getting hungry while walking around.After it all head outside for the scenic view and some outdoor picture taking. We were there on a gloomy day and wind was pretty strong.

review: This place is copy of old Greek empire and the many gods of old times. It is beautiful replicated with many whites plaster statutes. The hall is big to indicate the structures and statues.The place will give the kids mystery of old times and the stars of God hopefully attracts their attention. The displays are huge.

This place is a must visit. We visited this place in late afternoon. The viewing deck was awesome as you really can view the rock clearly. There are  information display on the viewing deck explaining the rock formation...very informative. At the time of our visit the wave was high...and unexpected by us and the rest of the visitors who were busily taking photos.. the wave  splashes on the viewing deck...making those near the deck  wet...it was fun though :-). Though a bit wet we really enjoy the view and the amazing rock formation...It still amaze me how the rock can be form like that naturally...

This museum is eye opening and insightful. We visited this museum (do not bring children) and was amazed at how sex was on fl display. I did not know what to expect let your imagination run wild and you will probably see it.

This museum displays many clay artwork and handicrafted items from ages. The tour guide and the ticket booth employee cannot speak English anyway. However the souvenir shop in the museum sells many wonderful things that we could buy home as gifts.

This is the best show I've watched! We had front row seats and laughed out hearts out. The performance of Team Orange is superb and the energy displayed by each team member was just amazing. Nanta cooking show is a non-verbal show set around the kitchen. Actors use common cooking utensils as musical instruments and the creativity is just amazing. A very highly recommended show.

This is only a nice experience if it is not crowded. With us entered a family if four and they easily blocked 2-3 displays. The start of the tour is great. A lot of great photo opportunities. They gibe you examples and show how to pose. But suddenly this stops in the middle and you end up in a huge room with Aladdin Indiana Jones a volcano eruption? We had no clue what to do there.At the end there is a bug parking lot outside with even more displays. So if you are into instagram and pictures - this is yours. If not... well it is entertaining though. Unless there are tons of visitors.

this is one of must-seen attraction in jeju they displayed all about tea from jejuthe architecture of the meseum is really nice and awesome and the shop also sells many products range from tea you also must try the cafe dish such as ice cream roll cake etc..

This is more of a shop and cafe than a museum. The museum part is just a few display cabinets that leads to a cafe with goods displayed for sale. The tea plantation across the street is a flat moderately sized area that pales in comparison to the vast rolling and picturesque tea plantation of cameron highlands.This attraction is not worth the time unless one is a tea-lover.

This is an amazing place. The museum is absolutely first rate. All the exhibits have explanations in perfect English.  There are lots of interactive displays. If you are interested in the geology of Jeju you should come here first and expect to spend several hours. Outdoors there are 3 courses (walks) with exhibits of life in old Jeju. The exhibits are well done and English signs are excellent.  This place is huge and amazingly you will have it almost to yourself. It has an entry fee of about $5. That is the bargain of the century!   Don't skip any of it. It could easily take a full day if you are intellectually and esthetically inclined. It was the best thing I did on the island. I spent only about 4 hours. I would suggest you bring food and water with you. I had a few apples and tangerines.
This is a very lovely place. I really enjoy it! Especially all the outdoor display. Feels like being in a fairy tale story.

This is a beautiful destination. I would consider this a must do for all foreigners visiting Jeju Island. We did this stop as a part of our self drive 5 day holiday during the kids fall break. What I loved was the the design of the building and landscaping made the most of the site. It reminded me of visiting an upmarket winery. There is a fabulous view from the tower over the tea fields fabulous art displayed inside and precious tea cups to look at the amazing smell & sight of seeing tea roasting and demonstrations. The outside had sculptures. The kids loved airy ambiance of the cafe & wolfed down the Green Tea Swiss Roll. I loved my dacquoise! Plenty of parking bathroom facilities Well Done!

This area is a traditional village area with loads of space displays and things to see and do. A huge cultural complex created to show case all the various aspects of life in a Korean village. Working displays and demonstrations make the wandering around even more interesting as do the small shops that are spread throughout the complex. A really great couple of hours.

they have museum they have display how green tea is processed (but in korean only); they should have it in english as well. very nice place where you can sit and relax have a yummy green tea ice cream. but they do sell many kinds of green tea - blend with candy tutti fruity brown rice. the packaging is super cute but a bit expensive. you can buy lots of green tea as souvenirs for family and friends because these are special from jeju. worth visit!
They had French drawings and sculptures on display those which are masterpieces by Monet Rodin  Renior and many other great artists were displayed at the museum. Entrance fee is 10000??per person.

They ?쐒eborn??the dead and colorful insects to put them on displays as they are living the life of human with small scenes in the glass frames. We are amazed and especially impressed with the bugs playing football and the goalkeeper bug was catching it! There are also a huge collection of butterflies and other species in this museum.
There's quite a number of display to see if you are a teddy bear fanatic but really the place is not that big so you can finish touring within the hour.

There is nothing exciting with the Jeju Chilsung Fashion Street. It is a series of open-air pedestrian-only road lined with boutiques. The stores were familiar such as Starbucks New Balance Spyder MLB Tommy Hilfiger Crocs and Adidas although there are some designs that are available here that are not yet available in the Philippine market.The place was supposed to be part of the Jeju Winter Festival. Indeed there were a number of Christmas-themed displays although they were nothing compared to how lavish the Christmas displays in the Philippines are.I only strolled around the area then went to the Dongmun Market nearby. The Jungang Underground Shopping District is also close?봞s it was winter it was more comfortable shopping at the heated underground location of Jungang that it was in Chilsungro. Also the items sold at Chilsungro are from brands that are more known internationally (and thus are more expensive) than what is available at Jungang.
There is a large Buddha inside the temple and on the first floor a display of 8000 little Buddha statues. Good for a short visit but otherwise it's just like any other Buddhist temple.

There are so much to see in this museum. The whole day is enough to spend here if you want to read and appreciate all the displays. Good collections. I learned a lot from this museum. I regret doing four museum tours in one day for we had to rush this one. I would love to go back here.

There are 3 terry bear museums in Jeju. The one which we visited is Terry bear and safari. The lower floor is the safari and upper floor is the bear. Think this also to attract the kids to visit the place thus the safari.Take your time to see and enjoy the many characters of the terry bear. One corner of displays is a very expensive due to diamond crown.
The ticket is expensive for what you could see. Nothing special. Some displays could be humorous but that's about it.

The Tea Museum is situated on the south-west coast of the island in Seogwang. There is an interesting display of cups and teapots used in Korea under ancient dynasties. The museum provides an insight into the immense range of teas and derived products (especially cosmetics) and of course they can be purchased there too. Quite pricey.Learn about the history of tea and how to make it. The Jeju Samdayyeon Tangerine tea was being sampled as we were visiting. We also recommend trying the refreshing green tea ice-cream in the modern caf챕 attached.You can take a stroll across the well-landscaped gardens.Of course Osulloc Teas are available for purchase in Seoul too.

The staffs there were really nice. We were caught in a typhoon and hitch hiked in. They saw us drenched so they offered to send us back to our hotel after we finish our tour in the museum. How nice. Great hospitality. Plus  they have quite a bit to display.

The place was drizzling when we got there and managed to squeeze in one last parking lot beside the tea museum. eent straight to the tea museum and the place was really crowded. it showcase the tools used in tea productions and Got a few tastings of various type of tea and souvenirs. Went for the famous ice cream dessert and drink - good. Next walk over to Innisfree building where they have an open area for children to  play with the playdough and display of cosmetics product as well as a cafe with seating area. Outside tourist were busy taking pictures of tea plantations and themselves !
The only value here I think is let the kids make their own chocolates. It's a funny experience. Apart from that  the display is a joke. Anyway  the entrance fee is low and it doesn't matter much.

The museum is quite small and expensive....there are 2 floors with old teddy bears and teddy bear versions of famous painting and famous people. If you are nearby you can go but I would not specifically go there. My 3 years old son was little scared by the giant bears in display! Koreans seem to like it more

The museum is only a short walk from the Hyatt Regency hotel where we were staying.We went there to keep our daughter occupied but to tell the truth we all enjoyed the place. I enjoyed the way the displayed were made up from events in history.The only spoiler was the noise from Chinese tourists!

The museum has some interesting and sometimes humorous displays. The real attraction here is the outdoor sculpture park. A walk around it is  like no other outdoor display of art your have ever seen. Well worth the price of admission.This experience may not be for everyone. Obviously it is sexually oriented.

The land is big with many miniatures but I get tired of the figures real quickly. However there are some interesting photo worthy displays. Go if you have time to spare or if you are going with kids. Entrance fee is 8000won.
The kids and ladies will love this place. So many teddy bears on display and you can take picture with some of them.

The Joanne Bear Museum is one of the stops in the package tour that we availed of. It is basically a collection of stuffed bears that Joanne Oh has created  each bear hand made. There are three buildings where all the bears are housed. We were there in winter and the place was well-heated. The pathway between the buildings were open air  though. The bears came in different sizes  colors and variations. There are some depict historical or cultural scenes  others depict pop culture. The bears are all finely crafted. Unfortunately though  many of the signage are in Korean only.There are several displays where guests can pose with the bears. One of those bears  a polar bear  was featured in a Korean drama  ?쏱aradise Ranch.??I especially loved the displays that feature the acronym of the place (JB) because it is my initial as well. There is a souvenir shop which sell?봸ou guessed it right?봲tuffed bears. I wanted to have one as a souvenir so I was settling for the least expensive keychain bear when I saw a much larger 8-inch plushie being sold at a discounted rate; it was only 2 000 won more expensive than the keychain so I got it instead. As with many of the Joanne bears  it an embroidery of Joanne Oh's signature.

The green tea plantation of O'sulloc was my last stop prior to my flight for Seoul. My recommendation is to try the O'Sulloc green tea ice cream. There were also other green tea based products displayed like soap and beauty products. As for me I enjoyed my green tea ice cream under the flowering Cherry Blossom tree.

The government run museums in Jeju finally opened on a trial basis limiting a number of hourly visitors to 50 with online reservations being required (although it didn?셳 really seem like a must when we arrived).  Considering it's a large complex (which itself looks impressive) Jeju Museum of Art didn't have a whole lot in display other than a temporary exhibition consisting of mostly projected images.  Thorough explanations of the pieces were provided on pamphlets and the display although few in numbers  used the wide spaces well.
The entry tickets is too costly for what are displayed in the castle. I was not so impressive with the whole land.
The displays are nice and beautiful you can also have a personalized glass item with your name and picture which can be delivered to your hotel for free.

The chocolates there are not exactly cheap. We found cheaper ones on sale by the tourist attractions. Not exactly worth paying 3 000won to see some choco display. Nothing really that impressive too. The 3 000 won entrance ticket can be used to redeem for drinks or offset chocolate purchases within the museum too.

The best part of the tea musuem is the cafe which serve green tea latte ice cream cakes. i never get to try the green tea cheese tiramisu cake at the cafe so i headed to one of the O'sulloc in Myeongdong. It is really good. However the museum is just average. There are only cups and tea pots displayed. I think the BOH tea plantation museum in Malaysa is much better. Just my 2 cents.

The aquarium was actually nice and the range of species was adequate. The only issue was that that all the logos and banners of the place display a whale shark. However we didn't see any whale shark in the display. The price was rather high for a nothing special aquarium.

review: That is the first time I am rating a place terrible. To begin with there are only Korean introduction and description for all the items and collections displayed there. We all read Korean don't we?As stated in other reviews this place has zero content. I can easily find more chocolate related stuff in a convenience store that this so called chocolate land. Worse  the entry ticket is bundled with a purchase voucher of the chocolate items sold at the store in this place. Contradictory to the all Korean introductions and descriptions  the chocolate available in the store are all international brands. If you are looking for the experience of travelling to Korea to buy chocolate probably from your own country  there you go!

thank you very much for your revisit. we opened Elvis Theater newly  and changed display items regularly at extra gallery. anyway we are sorry for dissatisfation however  we are trying to give the satisfaction to all of our visitors.

Teddy bears were grouped and show case in different galleries. I love the way the bears were decorated  on the display especially the details in their attire. They looked beautiful and cute. Worth a visit if you like teddy bears.

Teddy bear museum was such a curious place ever. Many kinds of teddy bear are displayed on there and also great to take photos. Think takes 1~2 hours to look around here. I really liked it and also teddy bear souvenirs are pretty good to prepare as gifts but a little expensive to buy a lot. Anyway i would like to recommend to visit here. This museum is worth a visit:)

Tea Plantations are not my favourite places and this is not a museum as such. But the way the Koreans have done this makes it into a relaxing afternoon experience. The cherry blossoms just came out when we visited. There were scores of Korean students on a field trip but that's OK. It's spacious enough for everyone. A short display of tea cups from around the world lines the entrance of the building. Then it's tea shopping and testing. Try the buckwheat tea! Lots of chinese speaking staff (as with everywhere else in Seoul). Here I tasted the best green tea ice cream and cake. A walk in the surrounding garden and compound is nice. There is a glass building next to the main one by Korean brand Innisfree. In it there are soap making activities a cafe and skin care shopping.

Specility of S. Korean is to make a simple thing also most presentable and impressive with best possible aesthetic and respectful manner.Dinosaur land on Jeju Island is one of the attracting places for a family. More details of Dinosaur are displayed with 3D models of different types of Dinosaurs. All around nature was also so well prepared that things look more natural....In short I repeat my recommendation as given in one another review.....make your visit to Jeju at least once and have your own genuine experience which you might not get so well at other places.

So much to offer from beautiful botanic displays to a fabulous Bonsai area which was so peaceful and various specimens of fauna.... Plus several species of cacti. Caves to go down and lovely park area..... A lovely outing which was also very reasonably priced.

So much cuteness in one place. If you love teddy bears this is the place for you. And if you love Prince Hours (Goong) You will find the bears that they use on that korean drama displayed here. Place is located inside Jungmon Resort so it is pretty easy to find.
So many vintage cars on display good for car enthusiasts. Most were executive cars used by dignitaries.

review: Shows good selection of plants from various regions. Good organization of displays. Conveniently located near Hotel. Provided relaxed pace in touring the place. But limited information provided on plants.

Seriously stunning display of flowers at Camellia Hill; the biggest arboretum in Asia famous for its forest path and beautiful gardens of camellias. The arboretum is home to 6000 camellia trees of 500 different species including species that are known to produce the world?셲 largest and earliest blossoms. The place is drop-dead gorgeous and I would of spent a whole day adoring the different flowers if I wasn't rushing to maximise my day in Jeju.We were lucky to catch the early blooms of the Cherry Blossoms which was a major highlight of the trip for us. Towards the end of the trail is a small shop that should desserts coffee and souvenirs like postcards and cosmetics. I loved their postcard selection and went a little crazy on those souvenirs but no regrets. My brother enjoyed his homemade strawberry ice cream as it was packed full of flavour!
Pricey and most displays were in Korean. Very hokey. Recommend the Love Park outside Jeju city instead.

Pretty interesting theme park! All the sculptures displayed bluntly explain our sex life and culture. It is good to tAke photos with them and prohibited children from entering inside. Usually not crowded except special national holidays ir vacation season so whenever you could visit here freely.
playground filled with teddy bears. children are very happy to play there. All about teddy bears are very well displayed. the place is clean and comfortable for the kids. Very like it...
Part museum  part art gallery and totally worth a visit. The shells are wonderfully displayed in a variety of artistic designs that enhance the viewing experience. Absolutely worth a visit.

Our tour diverted to the tea museum because we were to visit dragon head rock but the tides were too high to take out the small boat.  Anyway would've been cold on the water with the very powerful windy day.  Building is in the midst of tea fields.  You are taken through an area with China from all over the world.  Most of the China on display was either from France or Germany.  Then you enter a room where you can buy souvenirs as teas makeup made with tea and then there is a counter to buy dessert and teas or tea lattes.  They are very pricey though about $6 for a hot cup of tea.  Then after leaving that room you enter a room where you can sample tea infused makeup.  This reminded me of when we toured Fragonard perfumery in France where everyone was trying on the lotions and perfumes.  There were even large vials filled with liquids which were identified by the plant or flower beside them.  Once again similar to the perfumery labs.  Then there was a counter to order same teas dessert and even cold tea drinks that were nonalcoholic versions of cocktails but with tea in them.  These looked like they might've been good.  We finally decided we were in need of a hot drink after the sea cliffs experience.  So we bought one of those overpriced tea lattes.

Our last destination for our first day in Jeju is this temple. Before arriving to the worship place near the parking area you will find vendors selling various souvenir items. Upon entrance we walk through the garden where we saw trees with oranges (mandarin in their place). It was last week of March when we visited this place we were lucky to see trees beautiful big oranges. Continuing the path we pass big rocks display with signage written in Korean which I don't understand. We then continue to walk farther and took the stairs until we reached the temple. Just like other places for workship you are not allowed to bring your shoes inside the place. Near the temple is a fountain they say if you drink water in the fountain it will bring good health and good luck to the person.

O'Sulloc Tea Museum is very small (there are not many displays to see) but there is a very large shop that sells tea products and a cafe that sells drinks and desserts.  There is a very brief tea tasting demonstration w/ narrative in Korean only.  In the cafe we had the best green tea ice cream and green tea roll cake we've ever tasted.  Prices for drinks & dessert was expensive ($4.50USD each for a small cup of ice cream and a slice of cake; $8.00USD for a large glass of orchid flavored iced green tea).  The tea products in the shop are also expensive.  If you are a tea connoisseur then this is the place for you.  Across the street from the museum there is an open field where the leaves are grown that you can walk around.  There is a viewing tower above the museum where you can also see the tea fields.  If you are exploring the west side of Jeju island O'Sulloc makes a great rest stop. I would not deliberately drive all the way out there just to visit this museum.

Osulloc tea is known as one of the more famous and reliable brand in Jeju...most of the tea is expensive too. Thus it is not uncommon for travel agencies to include the Osulloc green tea museum into its itinerary. A walk around the museum shows you a little background of tea in particular. You can also be able to see tea cups from different countries on display. I tried the green tea ice cream and it was yummy. We were told that if we spend more than 30000 won we can get a tax refund at the airport. So we really spent more than 30000 won on tea :) I wandered alone out of the tea museum and saw Innisfree!!! They were conducting some soap making lesson when I walked in. The deco is very different from what I saw in the malls. And of course I ended up buying stuffs....some facial masks that I wasn't able to find in Singapore.
Not to badmay go for a visit..Entrance fee is 8000Won for adult and 6000Won for children.There are old korean movie playing therealso korean 60's70's shops displayand etc

Nicely done up place very organise. Good stop for green tea ice cream and cake. Good range of tea pots and cups displayed. Well written history of tea drinking in Korea.Good for photo takings.Free sampling of tea and explanation (although mostly in Korean).
Nice walk through with lots of photo chances. All the descriptions were in korean but still was nice. The cave was nice and i liked it was self guided. The cactus display is worth visiting.

Nice place for a short stroll from the pier to the bridge and over to Saeseom Island. We took quite a number of photos of the sea  bridge  and looking inland to Seogwipo Port. We enjoyed the sea breeze  the view of the clear waters and the displays of acrobatic jumping fish in the port. Locals stroll the area and it is a picturesque place to relax for a while. If you're into nature walks you can follow the trail around the island  which is probably small enough for you to complete in an hour or so.You can also take the submarine tour nearby at Seogwipo Port - but do check the weather conditions  our guide told us that the currents and weather play a big part in whether you'll be able to see lots of marine life during your dive.

Nice museum with plenty of green tea variety product. Nice display with fresh tea selection for packaging. A huge bar like tea shop serving green tea base ice cream drinks and dessert. A short stroll bring us to innisfree workshop for DIY moulding your own soap bar and Innisfree natural oil for your own packaging to do. Overall nice experience and price is reasonable
Nexon Computer Museum - I went there with my buddy and we were so excited to see all those old computers on display... lol!

My wife wanted to visit this place since the last time we came.  This place is ideal for kids and couples.  Lots of history and old bears on display.  Good way to pass some time.   Located close to other museums...

My visit here with my family was superb for the world's most expensive teddy bear (in LV) was on display. The history and evolution of teddies on display was noteworthy. Huge collection. My daughter enjoyed the cuddly toys as well and could not resist to buy some souvenirs. I found it cute dressing up the teddies like the superstars especially Marilyn Monroe & Michael Jackson. Superb!

My friends and I decided to take a 2 day side trip in Jeju Island from Seoul. Our first stop is the famous O'Sulloc Tea Museum. We went there March of this year it was sunny and yet it was cold and very windy. When we were still on our way to the museum we were already awed to the beauty of this place. Everything was green and beautiful! I super love the place!!! We first went to the plantation itself from the parking lot. Walking on the pathway in the middle of the beautiful trees and shrubs was just a beautiful feeling and much more when we reach the plantation. We also went to the top of the building for  a bird's eye view of the plantation. Our last stop is their museum they have a great display of tea cups which illustrate the colorful history of tea plantation and tea making. After the museum is the store where they sell variety of green tea products. They also have free tasting of hot teas. Wonderful Jeju Island! Great opener for a tour:-)

My 5yr old loved it very much. Lots of dinosaurs on display outdoor. Several exhibitions on site such as fossils and seashells. Areas where you can interact with animals (feeding ponies and gerbils.) You also get to see parrots next to the gift shop. It's not a very big place. we spent about 2 hours there. We got a taxi there and the man at the ticket hut(speaks good English) was very kind to help us get a taxi back to hotel. A very enjoyable and pleasant place to visit if you like dinosaurs and animals.

museum is nothing to boast just a small section but tried the green tea roll latte & ice cream. roll cake quite nice but didn't taste much of green tea ice cream normal latte nice also but pity too many tourist when we went probably ran out of cups in their display that looks more appealing.
Lovely walk among the rows of tea. Very good concept to put Innisfree shop there. Interesting activities there like soap making. Attractive display

Loved it the various marine lives attraction there. Personally I liked most is the underwater aquarium where we could walk beneath the swimming fishes. Also the collection of various jellyfish and octopus on display. Stunning.

review: Located in the southern part of Jeju Island. It holds a lot of stuffed teddy bear displays. Entrance fee is cheap. Taxi fare from main city is around 30KRW one way.

Like most government run museums in Korea Jeju National Museum takes up some major square yardage despite having only about half hour worth of displays.  The displays were not the most engaging but there are good explanations in English Chinese and Japanese which provide a good overview of Jeju history.

Larger than anticipated with lots of interactive displays.  Bring a camera and be willing to be funny in a crowded space.  The indoor attractions were bettrr than the outdoor ones.  There is a coffee and snack bar with a lounge in the middle that made a very nice break point.  Easy to get to and staff was nice and helpful.  Staff spoke pretty good english and even called a cab for us.

Jeju has tonnes of 'museums' to draw in cash from tourists. Most of these are silly  man-made museums having no connection whatsoever to Jeju or even Korea. It is almost a sin to spend time in these museums while in Jeju  instead of enjoying the scenery outdoors.However I would reallly recommend a stop at the seashell museum if you have an hour to spare in the Seogwipo area. The labor of love of 1 woman  this place houses a staggering collection of shells from all over the world  crafted into stunning displays. Seashells so pretty  its hard to believe they are real..but they are.There's also a small shop to purchase souvenirs if you'd like but they don't pressure you. Also attached is a cafe.Close by to a bus stop.

Jeju Folk Village is not very big and not small as well but it effectively demonstrates the history of Jeju tradition from the 1890s. Different types of villages were located systematically. While walking through different houses and villages it feels like visiting a real movie shooting studio. Everything looks clean and real just like somebody still leaving there. The real animals and bird kept makes it even more alive village. Some of the life-size dummies kept there to display the old traditions and clothes were remarkable. The posters in from of few houses indicated that those were indeed used in making popular movies or TV dramas based on the old lifestyle.Besides there are various exhibition halls performance hall dram shooting sites poultry farms etc. which make it even more interesting. People can also even enjoy various folk games. It actually not only allow people to observe the traditional Jeju lifestyle during the 1890s but also allow people to get experience by playing folk games wearing traditional Korean dress etc. Thus it is recommended to visit this place during a visit to Jeju.

It's very much a market for locals but interesting to walk around. There are lots of colourful displays of fruit and vegetables. Dried fish stalls are also common  as are live shellfish and fish tanks where you can choose your purchase. It's a bit smelly in parts  particularly around the meat stalls.

Its three floors with aquariums but still not so big bu got pretty awesome one with big display where you can sit and enjoy the view. I also liked the show. They got 2 types of it one with humans and several with animals like dolphins and sea bear. Performance times are 11:10 13:00 15:00 and 17:00. There is also feeding times and female diver's diving. It opens from 10 to 19 so be sure you will see at least one of performance and have time to look around since performance lasts about 40-45 min each.

review: It's stated only those above age 18 are allowed in though am not sure if it's strictly enforced. There were plenty of tours consisting of local senior residents dropping in. Majority of the displays were outdoors so be prepared for plenty of walking. One of the buildings does not have elevator not escalator access to the upper floor hence it's inaccessible to those who can't use the stairs but they compensated by showing a brief video summary at the lower floor.

It was raining when we arrived and spent a fun afternoon at this museum posing with the different paintings photos and displays. Unfortunately the rain prevented us from taking photos with the various outdoor displays. Wheelchairs are available for loan and help make the experience more enjoyable for my mom who has difficulty walking. Entrance fee is KRW9000 per person. The Alive Museum covers a wider area and has more/different displays than the Trickeye Museum in Seoul.

It was pouring and we needed something to do.  Jeju has a lot of museums and this was our first stop.  As a person who studies sexual health I found the museum average.  Why?First the museum does a good job at giving a lot of different perspectives. Covering things like marriage history  homosexuality  maturity sti masturbation  bdsm etc. They have displays installations artefacts video and some interactivity. The biggest problem is that all the information is written in Korean. So it was impossible to actually learn. I would have liked to read all the information that was presented. Also the price was expensive 12000 won was a lot for what you got.If the information was in English I could see me giving 4 stars.

It was my first time ever to any of the ALIVE series and honestly it wasn't fantastic but I could be bias cause I hate crowded attractions and people hog and does not wait for their turn. My recommendation is to go during off peak season with at least a group of 3 as some of the displays can fit in a couple. I guess it will be more fun as well. Condition of displays are pretty good and one could easily spend at least 1.5 hours in there. There is also an outdoor park which features more abstract art which is pretty interesting. Overall worth the money? I'll say it's alright but it will be a place that I'll visit once.

It was a butterfly and insects theme park. Entry fee 9500 won. It doesn't display real butterflies and insects I think. There were just fake but they really did a great job by setting up for the exhibition. I really adored their creativeness to potray various human activities and historic scene by using insects and butterflies. The miniature were really nice. If you are expecting to see some real butterflies flying around you wouldn't see one :(We also went to mirror maze. This was superrr awesome! The maze was small but it really did made us feel excited to find our way out. Beware not to bump to those mirrors hehe.

It tells you the history of green tea and some other info on tea plantation in Jeju. Basically you enter the small room where they display some written history of tea in Jeju. You may need to read all the information and see some displays in about 10 mins before you come to their caf챕. Outside there is a small tea leave plantation where you could take some photos. There is a small lawn for children to run around. That is all about it.
it is super cute and i loved the teddies... also the LV one!!... my son loved all the displays.. and so did I.. it was a unique experience :)

It features Korean ancient village type of houses they stayed their work places their farms their lifestyle and others. It's a huge place so be prepared to walk a lot. The biggest draw here is the famous actress Lee her famous tv series was shot in one part of this village. It has a small exhibition house displaying things used in that tv series. Enjoy visiting this place if you are her fan otherwise you might just feel its just another garden. There was one thing interest me there were beams and beam holes in front of each village house by placing different number of beams it's actually telling others whether its widow's house or available or man at home. Be reminded it takes up a lot of the time for visiting this place may skip and visit other indoor museum.
Interesting to see historic chocolate packaging  however  amount  quality and selection of display have reflected on cost of admission fee.Great souvenir shop in the basement!

Interesting place. Lots of Tangerine in boxes as gifts and many stalls sell snacks and souveniors.Is also a wet market where you see fresh produce. Not forgetting display of pig heads can be found in serveral stalls. Can visit for the experience.
Interesting museum. Worth going. Summer time can be quite hot if viewing the outdoor displays. Gift shop is right under the greenhouse effect.

Initial feeling of uncertainty and doubt was quickly dispelled as we progressed through the front gates of this beautifully set and immaculately well thought of garden. Never would one imagine that from the exterior we would find such a warm and charming display of timeless and ancient art of bonsai and many other arts of nature. Definetely a thumbs up for this walk through time.

Indeed a disappointing experience. Yes  this is just an excuse to get you to the gift shop  but at least they could have made the trip there interesting. The story of chocolate is among the most fascinating in the histories of commodities  but they made it a torture. You will see some exhibits on the history of chocolate  a few displays of old boxes and cases of chocolates  and some needless toy sculptures  but mostly a forgettable experience. You do have to pay a small amount and get a coupon for your chocolate or drink purchase. So  if you are desperate to eat some chocolate  or it's raining heavily outside  or you need quickly some air-conditioning  then give it a try; otherwise  enjoy Jeju's natural scenery and wonders instead.

In Jeju we visited the O?셲ulloc tea fields and Museum. Inside the tea museum there is a tea gallery with a display of tea cups tea pots and the history of O?셲ulloc?셲 superior green tea which is harvested and roasted in Jeju Island. It is claimed that Jeju's volcanic soil weather and underground water are best for tea cultivation and there is some information on Korea?셲 traditional tea culture.We were shown a short demonstration on the pan-frying of tea leaves and had a sampling of their O?셲ulloc brand of roasted green tea. It has an acquired taste and may not be everyone?셲 cup of tea! Within the Tea Museum there is a caf챕 and we tried their green tea ice-cream which is quite good smooth and not too overpowering of green tea flavour. Their range of flavoured teas are sold in the retail section of the museum.

In Jeju  we had the opportunity to visit the Jeju Art Museum & Glass Castle  which is a theme park featuring an exhibition hall  garden and models made entirely of glass. One must spent at least two hours or more to walk around the indoor and outdoor areas. Nearby the entrance  there is a display ?쏥lass Worldwide??and the countries that produced glass are mentioned here - China  Italy  Czech Republic  Arab and Japan. Once you step indoor  a large glass beanstalk from the fairytale ?쏪ack & the Beanstalk??will greet visitors.The world's largest all-glass labyrinth  glass ball  glass diamond  a glass stonewall  mirror lake and a glass bridge are found in the model parks here. In one part of the outdoor theme park are Cinderella's glass slippers and a glass carriage. One will be held in awe at the marvellous pieces of art  all made entirely out of glass! Truly an eye opening experience!

If you`re a Zippo lover  this is a must visit spot. Museum locates in the ground floor of a modern seaside building with breathtaking pacific ocean view. There is 2 exhibition halls  one of those displays many special designed zippos in large size  and the other in fact is a zippo shop  you can see and buy different limited edition zippo there and many are designed by local designer.

If you wish to understand Korean culture better this is a must visit place as they have these display for better illustration for you understand. You can walk around the park nearby this Folk Village as we went there via Jeju City Tour Bus.

If you want to relieve your childhood and are fond of taking photos you must not miss this place.  It is a place where huge stuffed toys not only bears but all kinds of animals are displayed and you get a chance to take nice photos with these stuffed toys.  We really had fun here.

I wouldn't call this a museum as there are only a few tea cups and tea pots on display.Basically this a tourist stop for tea.The store has very expensive tea for sale and a cafe serving tea and desserts.The museum is surrounded by beautiful tea fields.It would have been nice if there had been info on the tea fields how it's grown  cultivated etc. Worth a stop if you have nothing else to do.

I would have not gone here if it were not recommended to me by a friend. It definitely exceeded all expectations. It is great fun for adults and kids. It has a number of interactive displays which are very intriguing. Would allow at least 90 minutes.

I visited Hallim Park confined in a wheelchair. Some ways are not appropiate for a wheelchair. I love gardens and seen a lot. This garden had beautiful displays although some were needing care. The park takes several hours to see. It has different plants from many parts of the word. The Bonsai collection was excellent and one of the best I seen in a botanical garden. Again this particular area was needing help with the trees. They have so many bonsais and only two workers to trim them. And the specimens available were very old.The caves are unique because I do not know any other part in the world you can see a volcanical and calcareal cave together and they have one in here. I had to use crutches to see them and I am not dissapointed of the effort.The local village moved into the park is nice and realistic (we visited a folk village the day before). The animal collection was above average. For kids they have an area to feed love birds and parakeets. Excellent fun. My youngest daughter is 25 and she was a child again in here.

I visited and stayed the night in a traditional village on the southern part of the mainland and this was still a great additional experience. It's a great deal with your ARC if you're a Jeju resident but not too expensive for non-locals. The village itself has really good English signage regular performances and lots of artists doing traditional work that is for sale and on display. Over-all it's much less hokey and more educational than expected. I'd definitely recommend it!

I think we would have gotten much more out of this if there was English on the first floor displays. On the second floor there is much more English to make it interesting.Some of the content is just weird and some what hilariousThe statues outside are also great to pose with!

I loved how not only did they have a lot of things on display but also that you could actually use and play with the majority of things they had on display. Time flied and staff was very helpful every time I needed any help. Would go again.

I lived on Jeju and took school groups 3 times and every visitor I had to learn about  the history of the island. There is a video (not recommended for children due to disturbing images and video) at the start which is in several different languages. Then the display hall (formerly a dusty collection of artifacts but now a shiny new display hall) then there is a trip through the oreum. Free guided tour too. Very interesting. Also for kids there is a tank to play in in the grounds (there used to be a plane I don't know where that's gone) and the oreum itself is well worth a climb. Great museum which is still developing. Well worth it.

I enjoyed touring the tea museum but I was a lil' disappointed because there were only a few exhibits displayed to the public. There is a caf챕. You gotta try their ice-cream. It is heavenly. There is also a store which you can purchase tea related items as souvenirs. This place is definitely worth the hype!

I am a sucker for green tea. I went there due to great reviews. But there is something I want to clarify. The display there for the museum i felt it is not consider a museum.this place is more like a place to enjoy the food made out from green tea from drinks to cakes and ice cream.Do make the trip worthwhile by visiting nearby attraction too.Note: 4 star because the food is really good.

I agree with the other reviewers in regards to the maintenance of the museum...but still fun to see all the models out in display. Theyre much largers than i had thought but some looked a little amateurish... great museum for pictures and history...

I actually really enjoyed this museum although for me I'd like a little more English to read the displays but there were a lot of different activities to do for people to see how stuff really works it was pretty cool!

Having been to the Monterey Aquarium I wasn't expecting that much from an aquarium on little Jeju Island. I was pleasantly surprised to find a modern well-done aquarium with really spectacular displays especially the female free-divers. A nice surprise.

review: Hallasan is the climax of our trip to Jeju. Jeju would be non existense if not because of Hallasan. So we made it a point to spend one day out of our limited time in Jeju hiking the tallest mountain in the country.We took Eorimok trail to ascend and descend via Yongsil trail. Both are beautiful in their own way. Eorimok's view started with tall shady trees and later an open space with mountains and oerums (parasite mountains) as far as the eyes can see. Yeongsil on the other hand displayed a canvas of rocky mountain with autumn leaves colouring the picture. The steps at Yeongsil trail were endless and steep - we were glad we took the trail to descend and not ascend.I enjoy being at Hallasan. Hopefully I'll get the chance to take the other trails leading up to the peak in the future.

Haha worst museum i have ever visited. For non-Korean speakers  95% of the displays are in Hangul  ?쒓?. The museum is comprised of 3-4 large rooms of tacky semi-chocolate related items  the chcolate displayed is random chocolate primarily bought from Korean supermarkets... some are just empty boxes. The owner seems to be a Liverpool F.C. fan and for some odd reason there was a compilation of Gerrard goals and a signed England shirt; easily the best part.

review: Great for Marvel fans and it has some cool displays. It only takes about 30 minutes to see everything which makes the 12 000 KRW ticket price quite steep.

Granted  we went during the off season  but i can't think that it would be much better in the peak season. Several of the displays did not work  and there was no place to get a real meal if you were hungry. The one redeeming feature was the greenhouse that contained the different citrus trees.
Got to see a lot of bears on displayed from day 1. Not a very big museum but can walk for around 1-2 hours. Got to buy a teddy bear there after the visit.
good display and knowledge of tea in korea. and at the end of the museum there was a cafe and a shop selling a variety of tea. cafe served really good tea and cakes.

Good day out with children and their Grandparents as we could all enjoy something in the museum.  Lots of interactive displays and activities.  Amazing to see how much computers and technology have changed!
Good collection of artefacts and little describing in details about the items on the display. Liked it.

Given the trials and tribulations faced by the Dutch crew all those centuries ago  I did find it irritating that the top deck of the boat was closed because the wind had risen to a slight breeze. I am unsure what sort of risk or danger the owners were trying to mitigate against  as I am sure the bridge would have been perfectly sate and noone was going to be blown overboard by a tiny puff of air. The display inside the boat tells an interesting story. The Covid temperature readers at the entrance were causing the staff member a bit of trouble (and they are inaccurate) and we almost got the impression that it was our fault for being foreign humans unable to work broken temperature readers. Hamel would have given up trying.

review: Free entrance.Good display and exhibition.Well arranged. You can see the history of Jeju... And typical display style. Not very big...

For a museum of tea I was disappointed to sample only one type of tea. I had more to taste when I went to a department store than the actual museum.It does have the green tea farm and displays that look beautiful but I found the whole experience disappointing...

for 6000won per a ticket for an adult  what you get is a coupon worthy of 3000won which u can use to buy chocolate at the shop...I still remember the first thing that the ticket officer told me was ... I could use the coupon to buy chocolate at the shop located at basement.What I feel so disappointed is that the so-called showroom only displays chocolates made in different shapes or figures. Also  what I can buy from the basement was chocolates from other countries. No Jeju features at all for both chocolates and display.This shop is a total disgrace to Korea.

For  tea lovers O'Sulloc Tea Museaum is a great place to visit.  There are different displays of varied teas and other beauty products derived from tea.  There is also a refreshment parlor serving anything made from tea.  Outside this museum is a big park where people may gather or just play.  Just in front of the museum is a tea plantation.

First my lower rating for this aquarium comes partly from expectations that were not met.  This aquarium used to have whale sharks but does NOT anymore.  They couldn't properly take care of them one died and they released the other back into the ocean.  Second this aquarium has been advertised as the largest in Asia which is not true.  It has the largest viewing window in East Asia.  Those misconceptions out of the way this is still a great aquarium.  Interesting sea life some of which I had never seen before.  Great displays and a show that is entertaining if you understand Korean at least somewhat.

review: Displays were fun and informative but not enough written in English.  There are some great photo opportunities with statues outside.  Entrance fee was a little more expensive than most other attractions.

Different display of teddy bear represent different culture of different country as well as history of Korea. There were 3 level however not attractive as i expected and I was finished the visit within 30 minutes.
Description of the various teddy bears on display are in korean. You can only take photos and look at it without understanding about it
collection of teddy bears in different ways and poses. some Individual and some in groups. Outside the museum there are also teddy bear display.

Calling this place a museum is absolute fraud. The entrance fee is 3000 won which is returned to you in the form of a coupon for the cafe or gift shop - both of which are insanely overpriced. The 'displays' are ridiculous - chocolate gold coins  chocolate Easter eggs  Guylian seashell-shaped chocolates  posters of the film 'Chocolat ' a statue of Willy Wonka. It's almost as if the museum is teasing the West for its chocolate traditions - if it can even be called that. There is really nothing of interest in this museum. There is  however  a pretty nice view of the ocean to the rear of the museum.

C1 ( 2016.07.14 ) I visited there for watching about Africa's culture  but the contents was not sufficient to me. The animal was made by doll  and the exhibits was just displayed without subject  I think. But the performance by Senegal's band was excellent. The music was very excited. If there was no performance  I could not award high marks.

Beautifully built facility to showcase all things aqua. It creatively displays sea creatures and even Jeju's hanyeo heritage. Truly impressive. Good restaurants to refuel and recharge. A wonderful place to bring the whole family: young and old.
