At first  i thought it was another museum but i was amazed by all the detail and display of all the artwork. Great for families  couples  and all. I recommend buying tickets in advance online as i have found all the museums in jeju island to be at least 2000 won cheaper.

As someone said earlier this one is really more of a store for green tea rather than a museum although certainly there are display cases of tea ware to make the museum claim credible. What it is without a doubt is a gorgeous tea store. Aesthetics-wise -- it's so excellently designed it can easily inspire anyone to spend about a hundred U.S. dollars or so just on green tea stuff.The tea you can buy even in Seoul so if you don't want to lug them you can buy O'Sulloc stuff in Seoul. But I don't think you can easily find a place elsewhere that serves the O'Sulloc food they were serving here. I tried the green tea cappuccino the green tea cake green tea cookies and green tea soft serve. They were reasonably yummy although nothing to rave about. It's really the novelty of it that makes the food purchase worth it. Great view of the tea fields from the rooftop.I recommend it to all green tea loving people.

As part of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour we were given some time to go around O'sulloc Green Tea's fields museum and cafe; as well as shop around in Innisfree's Jeju House.Queues tend to be long for both the O'sulloc Green Tea and Innisfree so it's best to prioritize one over the other if you're working with a limited amount of time. O'sulloc Green Tea displays its wide array of teas packaged in gorgeous boxes and tin cans. These are perfect as gifts for loved ones.They also house a cafe in the store where you eat and drink tea-infused items. Fortunately we were able to visit its branch in Seoul already (and bought our fare share of their tea boxes) so we focused our time in Innisfree instead.Innisfree has numerous branches in Seoul; however it's best to look out for the Jeju-exclusive items available in the Jeju house. Similar to O'sulloc Innisfree also has its own cafe which serves its own selection of drinks and food; for those not interested in its beauty products.

Aqua Planet was a last minute improvised of plans as the wind was exceptionally cold that day.However for the price we pay i am a tad disappointed. Yes the place is huge but the animals that were displayed weren't much. We've seen more and bigger arapaima sharks and stingray elsewhere.Theshow was half synchronized swimming and half animal show. The synchronized swimming wss just okay a bit too lengthy that it turned a little boring.Displays could have been more informative. It wasnt stated smaller shows like feeding times etc. We took our time wandering through the science part but overall there just isn't much.Not recommended.

review: An absolute must-see on a visit to Jeju. Walk a kilometre in an underground tunnel formed by lava flow. The display boards explain what you're seeing so the rocks are interesting even if you have no previous knowledge of geology. Included in most tours of the West side of the island.

Although most of the board and model displays are in Korean language some are in English. It stresses on different cultures of sex ranging from western SE asian chinese and japanese Peru and Indian societies. Different sculptures from ancient to modern ages show the impact of sex to human life. Some erotic sceneries are shown but good to our sex education of adults and even kids! It tells us the pyschology diseases economical values and romantic features of sex even the sex of the elderly people. It costs W12000 each for entry taking you about 1 to 2 hours walk in the 2-storey hall. It is easy to get there by taxi or Jungmun Express Bus (JEB)from Jeju intercity bus terminal (or from Jeju Grand Hotel in Yeon-dong) of Jeju-si. If taking JEB it costs W2500 for 45 minutes. You can take transit at Changcheon-ri and then take western round bus (towards Hwasun-ri direction away from Jungmun Resort). Only soft creams and drinks are provided. The lovers are welcome to enjoy the sex knowledge there.If the museum has translations into English or Chinese I'd give her 5 points!

Across the street from the museum is a green tea patch where people can take touristy pictures and just walk around. The day I was there it was way too hot to even attempt to take photos. Inside the building isn't really a museum but a tea shop that has a lot of variations of teas. There's also a little cafe that serves hot and cold tea drinks along with simple snacks to have with you tea. Out back there is a walkway for people so that they can see the open landscape. There is also a Innisfree Jeju Island shop that has make-up and it was interesting to see some of the main ingredients in their skincare line out on display. The Innisfree shop also had it's own separate cafe with beverages and food.

A wonderful recreation of traditional living in South Korea with working areas small demonstrations food and gift shop areas. Very informative displays and examples of traditional life. Very worth the time small entry fee and effort. Great day out.

A wonderful place to take children and adults can have a good time as well. There are many shows and interactive displays for children to use. They also have crafts for children. For adults they have very informative displays as well as guided tours
A small traditional village where you can see the way people used to live on the island. Many houses are still being lived in and the ones on display to the public are few but intriguing.
A good place to have some fun and laughter posing with the displays. It an optical illusion and 3-D museum that makes everything so real. You can take lots of fun photos here.

Wow! I'm glad I saw this before leaving! Jeju is full of surprises and this is one of them. We were extremely lucky this was a foggy day because seeing this place in fog was really special.  The amazing display of wood carvings etc at the wood exhibition place was amazing as we're all the large insects carved out of cedar wood. It's a 20 min drive from Jeju City. Apparently in summer you have to protect your lunch from the crows! A nice easy walk and an oreum (hill) trail if you want something a bit harder. There are lots of carved statues all along the way and one of those stone paths which you can walk on with your shoes off.  I manage about 2 feet, too hard for me! Haha!

When we arrived at Jeju, we took a taxi to Jejueco and left our luggage with time since check-in time was in the afternoon. From Jejueco we took a cab down to Glass Castle and managed to reach there before 5pm.As its name suggests, the Glass Castle is a glass art theme park that consists of an exhibition hall and garden with everything made out entirely out of glass! All in all, there are 6 themed model parks with over 250 models exhibited: they include the world?s largest glass ball and largest glass diamond, a glass stonewall, a mirror lake, and a glass bridge etc...The exhibition was definitely a breathtaking sight to behold: glass displays made of all kinds of shapes and sizes! We couldn't help but be amazed and ended up taking - pictures of all the art pieces. For more on the experience and photos, please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/glass-castle-jeju.html

When visiting other countries I realize the treatment of animal standards may differ, but I at least look for animals to be happy. This falconry “center”was bittersweet. Some of the animals had wonderful enclosures, but the birds of prey were treated very inhumanly. The same birds of prey/owls were tied to stands for the whole 3 hours we were there, with no food or water, in the blaring sun, with no supervision as people crowded and tried to touch them to the point they would flinch or try to fly away, only to be yanked by their chains. Their inhumane treatment brought tears to our eyes. At the far part of the center, we came upon their enclosures, cages about 5 x 5 x5 feet wide, where other birds of prey were chained, with little place to move and absolutely no enrichment toys.? This is unacceptable. There was a raccoon in a small enclosure with no enrichment toys, solely used for tourists to take selfies with. Last but not least, a pair of Coaty were also in a small enclosure. Their baby was on display in a small cage by the gift shop with no water. This “Center” does have some acceptable enclosures for fowl, rabbits, budgies, and the alpaca interaction was amazing, but surely they can treat all their animals with dignity. While we were there, a macaw flew away into the surrounding trees. Clearly the parrot did not have an attached handler nor proper training for flighted birds.

We're her during the off season. This was a great Museum for a cold day- on the inside. The outside was beautiful and would have been great to explore on a warmer day. Loved the lifestyle displays of ancient Korean life (kitchen, agriculture).

We were a little disappointed after walking all the way down the hill at Sunrise Peak to see the women divers, only to find out that because of the holiday, they wouldn't be diving today.So as a consolation, our tour guide took us to the Haenyeo Museum.  This museum was dedicated to the Haenyeo women divers of Jeju and Japan.  It's a very nice museum with excellent displays, and you will learn a lot about the divers.I recommend seeing the video show before you start wandering around.

We went to the Teddy Bear Museum only because it was right next door to the Lotte Hotel Jeju where we stayed.  At 10,000 won per adult and 8,000 won per child, it is a bit pricey.  You can be done with all the displays and the 5 minute teddy Elvis show in an hour.  If you like teddy bears then it is a museum for you as there are alot of cute displays and exhibits that memorialize past events in history.  Kinda cool but not my thing.  I enjoyed the outdoor park area more.  You can take pictures with cute bear statues and sit and enjoy the greenery.  There is a cafe that sells Taiwanese pearl drinks and a nice gift shop.

We went there by taxi from O'Sulloc Tea Museum. It's interesting when the displays are made of glass but nothing impressive. The entrance fee costs 9000 won but my friend and I got a discount thanks to the taxi driver uncle, and we end up paying 7000 won each.. The displays are mostly outside. On the 2nd floor, there is a gift shop..you can buy some gifts there and the cost is acceptable for some (e.g. accessories, keychain, etc) certain products (e.g. glass displays) are more expensive. It was raining when we visited the museum, but we just went around the museum and took some pictures. It is good to visit once but not more than that.

We went in, looked around the first 5 minutes and then left. I like teddy bears, I'm actually a bit of a big kid, but this was all a bit boring. Lots and lots of bears dressed in little outfits. Maybe good if it's raining but if the sun is shining outside I'd advise you to try other things. It was crowded too, so you couldn't easily see the displays anyway.

We went here on our way to south jeju.It was a nice place where we can see the various art forms possible with glass.A sculpture of a horse made with glass was displayed, which was really looking cool...

We went as a couple  not expecting much  but this place was really fun! Lots of little experiments to do with electricity  plasma  light. The   tesla coil music orchestra   was impressive... or did I just got high on the ozone? Even the arcade games upstairs were great.We ended up staying for more than 2 hours and left only because they were closing down.I only wish they put more effort into the English information/displays. There are little English summaries  but the Korean version always looked way more exhaustive.There also an   organic salad bar   and a black pork restaurant at the facility  but we didn't have time to visit.

We visited the museum a bit reluctantly and only because we had dragged our two children (10 and 15) round two scenic waterfalls and an archery practice place in the hours before. Our youngest daughter was definitely keen to do something that she chose. When we got there our suspicions seemed to be confirmed with a relatively high entrance fee (I think it was 6,000 won per adult) for what seemed to be a small place.However, once we got into the diorama room, both kids couldn't stop themselves from oohing and aahing the whole time. You really felt that somebody had fun putting it all together. It was in all the little touches (like adding little German flags to the 'storming of the Berlin wall' display) and the set ups such as the 'Bearacotta Army). As previous reviewers have mentioned, all of these are in glass cases so my husband (who is a very keen photographer with decent equipment) didn't deign to take any photos - our teenage daughter took over instead. Having just completed our photobook, I can only say that we had plenty of good shots, I could easily have filled 20 rather than 4 pages with good shots.We didn't miss any English explanations - the teddies really spoke for themselves. We also didn't approach it as a museum but rather as a fun place to look around. The re-enactments of historical events from the 20th century were also fairly self-explanatory.The shop was probably the only really boring bit since the selection was not particularly big and the prices, given the location, quite high.Overall, don't go if you want to learn anything about teddy bears but do go in with kids (or adults who appreciate the cuteness).

We visited the JAM (Jeju Aerospace Museum) and it was stunning, I love anything connected with planes or space so I was in heaven, the displays are well laid out and there were so many interactive displays for kids too that it shows that there was much thought in the museum.Not only was it about aircraft, but also about Korea's history of astronomy which was so fascinating that I could have spent all afternoon in this one section, Then we went into the space exhibition and again I was stunned at how much South Korea has achieved. We always think of? USA & Russia as being at the forefront, visit the JAM to have your eyes opened.Wonderful.

We travelled using the Jeju City tour bus and stopped here after visiting Jeomul Natural Recreation forest . There were other stops but we did not get down to visit the other places due to time constraints. Initially, we planned to only visit for an hour but the park was surprising large and interesting and we ended up spending over 2 hours here.  It was time well spent.  We saw lots of stone statues and products in all shapes and sizes. The displays of rocks and rock formations were scattered all over an extensive outdoor park as well as an indoor museum. You need to wear comfortable shoes, wear a hat and apply sun block. Toilets were clean and strategically located around the park and clean drinking water was available in many places.  You only need to pay a small entrance fee and it was well worth it. There was even an air-conditioned resting hut with hot/cold water and seats just outside the entrance.  In our opinion, we think this is the most interesting stop on the public tour bus circuit.  Highly recommended.

We stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal and took bus 110 from Jungang Rotary bus stop to Jungmun Tourist Complex. The bus journey about 30 minutes and cost less than 2000won one way. The bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly (Although I did not see Jungmun Tourist Complex on the TV screen, therefore I used GPS to locate instead. For my other bus trip, the stops were annoucne correctly and was reliable). You can press the bell to alight. Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. The Teddy bear museum is a small two storey museum. The famous personnel, movie and cartoon characters were dressed in bears to make those bears special. You can expected toy bears moving their limps as some bears were mechanically  wired. There is also a small outdoor park with some display of bears. There anShort 5 to 10 minutes elvis show at level 2 theatre. 30 minutes would be sufficient to finish the entire museum. The ground floor has a large souvenir shop where you can purchase teddy bear. A small palm size teddy key chain about SGD$15. A 10? bear cost about SGD$50. As I am not a bear fan, I rated 3 stars as I personally feel that SGD$12.50 for the entrance fee was a little pricy. However, I am sure the teddy bears fan would love this place and rated 4 stars and above. Anyway, the museum is close too many other attraction that is walking distance (Eg: Cheonjeyeon Falls). If not, you could also take a bus 702 to many other attractions like the Hyeopjae Beach. If not, you can take bus 782 or 110 back to seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal.

we saw a signage stating 'can speak mandarin' with some car parking space outside so we went down, apparently is a very small 'display village' which the 'guide' explained some of the history & activities. didn't manage to see live black pigs. the 'guide' saw we cannot enter the actual village as was occupied with people (which I am not sure how true it is). and they started selling us product in the end... however we manage to see folk village which we think should be the 'real / correct' one when we left and go straight down the road and see walls surrounding with flag & a big map (which too bad we can't understand)

We had an afternoon to kill and it was too hot for any outdoor activity so we decided to visit the museum. It had a fairly interesting display of teddy bears - displayed by era and themes. Highlight was the most expensive teddy bear in the world - the Louis Vutton teddy bear. If you had limited time on Jeju, this is not a must-see, but I'd like us you had an extra day, then, this is worth going on a hot or rainy day.

We got there early in the morning and the level of sea was low so that kids could play in shallow water and in the sand. Love the walk in the nearby park. Info that I found here were useful in finding transportation.  Love the bus system for having display in every bus with info on next station, temp...

We enjoyed a family visit ( 3 generations ) on a glorious sunny day. This is definitely a place to visit on a dry dayThere are some beautiful gardens and in one area a very impressive display of bonsai trees.The grandchildren particularly enjoyed the area displaying snakes, lizards , tortoises and parrotsThere is also a very good section of caves to walk through

We decided to pay a visit whilst we were on a weekend trip to Jeju as my wife loves flowers. She was not disappointed!The display of orchids, her favourite, were quite spectacular whilst we were there.

We chance upon this on our drive from Seogwipo to Hyeopjae.  The pink building is big and visible from the highway. They should have repainted it as it looks washout and faded pink. But once I step in, it?s totally new! Infact it is even newer than Sanrio Puroland which I visited in Tokyo and bigger than there! I am a true blue HK fan since 40 years ago. Once HK fan steps in, I am sure you will be transformed to a little princess at heart and you?ll be so excited again! There are a lot of Instagram worthy area to take photos. As others pointed out, it has a section that talks about the evolution of HK from 1970s till now.  There are HK rooms, dining room, bus, living room, wardrobe, dressing room etc. Even the toilets are so pretty! Level 2 offers some purikura area, a restaurant and some other HK displays.  There is a 3D dancing room too. On the 3rd floor, there is a open air rooftop HK small maze. On level 1, you go through the souvenirs shop to exit and a notice states that once u exit, u can?t go in again. So it?s best that u buy yr souvenirs when u are ready to leave. I swear I could stay there for 3 hours but as my husband is with me, it only took us about 1.5 hrs to complete our visit. Overall this place is small and not much for non Kitty fans. For us Kitty fans, it is definitely a must visit.

We came here for black pork and fried chicken. Aged fished and cuts of pork were on displayed. It was pretty smelly, but strangely I kinda liked it hahaha. Black pork was alright, but actually it tasted like normal pork?! Also, the fried chicken was good

We arrived in late autumn nearing winter so there were not many flowers on display. We still managed to see chrysanthemum in various colours!! We also managed to spot the peacocks and ostriches. There's a small enclosure for kids (and adults) to see the various birds they have there. We also visited the 2 caves within Hallim Park. There's also a big bonsai area in the park.The park is huge, so allocate about 2 hours to visit everything!

We are not HK fans, but it is still a sweet and pleasant visit. After-all nobody can say 'NO' to an innocent cute little kitty. It is actually a 3 (or 4) storey building, with many life size HK displays in different rooms, including the toilets. There are a small outdoor garden on 3rd flr, a cafe on 2nd flr, a small theatre, children playroom and a 'history' room on 1st flr. Plenty of photo opportunities. There is also a store at the Exit but we found the items much more expensive. Unlike a theme park, there is no ride here. The place was not crowded when we were there in the afternoon. We spent about an hr. Most suitable for children and serious HK fans :)

We agreed that visiting the Jeju Stone Park in the snow was one of the most enjoyable experiences we have had in Korea. The stones, sculptures, houses and other artefacts, as well as the lovely walks are beautiful in the snow. It also meant only a few people were visiting, so it was very peaceful and serene. The museum was excellent, very educational, and we really appreciated how the different lava types were displayed as sculptures. They are beautiful, nature?s art!

Was recommended to this place by a friend. Entry wasnt cheap at around 10k won. I was initially disappointed when inside the building. But upon stepping outside the building, i thought the displays were beautiful when the teddy bear displays are placed with nice scenery.

Walking the Dongmun Market is an experience that a visitor should not miss.  The local market has variety of daily food of the islanders.  Seeing the fresh fishes, seafoods, and other meats displayed in various forms for consumption was an eye opener.  We would love to buy and try some of the food if the merchant package them in ready-to-eat size.  On this entrepreneurs way, the Japanese market achieve high mark in its idea.  Visitors would love to try local food even to pay at a premium.

Visited this museum with my kids.  There were hundreds of Teddy bears displayed over 3 floors. We saw Teddy bears in all sizes,  different era and occasions, celebrity characters dress up, themes etc.   Kids were excited to watch the free performance theatre with teddy bears dressed up as Elvis and his supporting singers singing. Every floor has different group of bears on display.   Entrance also allowed visitors to venture out to the back garden which boosted more Teddy bear statues.   Garden was well maintained and worth a visit.  Near the main entrance,  it also had a 2 storey high wooden Teddy bear which is a real attraction for the kids. The entry ticket is not cheap,  unless you are a real Teddy bear fan,  in my view,  it is not a must see destination.

Visited Jeju Glass Castle on our second trip to the island visiting our son and daughter in law and our first grandchild. This attraction was not what I was expecting, it was very imaginative and well laid out, all displays were of glass, of course, some very talented glass blowers. Well worth a visit.

Very interesting inside and out. The first floor is mostly modern about sexual preference health and rights but it is 95% in Korean. I would recommend to bring a Korean friend who doesn't mind translating if you are interested in that part. There was also a big wall of history at the very front which was all in Korean that would be worth translating. It wasn't very busy and some of the   hands on   things that would show examples were broken so I started with a mediocre impression. The bigger and more impressive part though is the number of historic sexual things they have on the second and third floor. Lots of artifacts about sex in Eastern cultures with some in Western cultures but a lot of things have their English translation. This part is much more impressive and interesting to look at. A lot of phallic objects and   traditional   pieces but it's historic and that is how people viewed sex in history. The more modern section is more modernly-styled and was a bit confusing (a lot of sex dolls...? kind of weird) and included more fetish stuff than I expected. Not much on queer and non-hetero there was a small section (in Korean) on the ground floor and then one very gray area display on the top floor but not a whole lot can be expected of Korea (where homosexuality is still viewed very negatively). Overall it was worth the price and was pretty interesting to look at. Having a translator or understanding Korean would make it more memorable.

Very interesting display of modern and old teddy bears. Take the time to see the Elvis Presley gig in the theatre! A bit pricey and as most museums on Jeju is quite small, but worth it on a rainy day.

Very cute and tons of displays.  Many different themes and ages of bears.  Very good place for couples and children.  The lifelike bears were very sturdy so you dont need to worry about them falling on kids, even with posing with them.  They have an outdoor display section, but it was raining for our trip so we didn't get the full experience.  Nice store at the end but was a bit over priced as anticipated.  Very good for any rainy or sunny day.

Unlike Hello Kitty, I think most of us have cuddled or have in possession a toy teddy bear at a certain stage of our lives. So it is no wonder that the Teddy Bear Museum has such a wide appeal and which surely be included as a ?compulsory? destination on the itinerary of the independent travellers (especially those with children) and tour companies alike.Getting there and fees: We visited Teddy Bear Museum (GPS coordinate/code 7387600) on a rainy day, which was appropriate since the exhibits are predominantly indoor, except for the Teddy Bear Garden and Park where there?re a few teddy bear figurines outside and a park with great views of the sea.  The admission charges are 10,000 won for adults won, 9,000 won for teens and 8,000 won for children.The Museum/Attraction:  This Teddy Bear Museum is the first and largest teddy bear museum in South Korea. Once you enter, you are greeted by this huge teddy bear, who gives you a ?grand? welcome to further explore the five sections spread over 3 levels: The History Hall, The Art Hall and The Project Exhibition Hall, Gift Shop (all indoors) and an outdoor Teddy Bear Garden and Park. There?s also a caf챕/restaurant. Be prepared to spend at least 1 hour looking and taking photographs/selfies at all the interesting exhibits. The History Hall comprised of the history of bear manufacturing and some of the earliest toy bears, many of which are antique and rare. It also showcases milestones in human history, with the bears enacting several famous (human) historical scenes from different eras. This is indeed a refreshing concept for a museum! I particularly liked the teddy bears enacting the Titanic, landings on the moon and the iconic celebrities like the Beatles and Gandhi.In the Art Hall, you could see the world-famous artworks and designs in an art gallery form as well as animation characters beloved by children. I liked the Mona Lisa and two of the most expensive bears in the world - the Louis Vuitton teddy bear and the Diamond Bear. In the Project Exhibition Hall, you would meet teddy bears grouped to suit the theme of each exhibition. Not forgetting the large Gift Shop on the first level. While it offers plenty of gifts, these are nonetheless pricey. Nevertheless, you could take photos with Michael Jackson bear, Steve Jobs bear and a wedding couple bear amongst others. There?s also a mother panda with her baby pandas on display too.  We certainly enjoyed the wonderful experience of the Museum bringing out the child in each of us, and making us feel young again. Despite the pricey entrance fees, I still think the Teddy Bear Museum is worth visiting, and to me, once would be sufficient. But if you don?t like teddy bears at all, then it would be prudent to skip this attraction.

Unfortunately, many attractions in Jeju are man-made and not really worth your time.  However, I wish I had spent some more time at this location as it's one of the few natural, impressive landscapes that you will see in Jeju.  Sure, there's not much to see other than the cliffs and columns, but it is good to spend some time just taking it all in.  Another idea is listening to the sounds of the waves crashing the columns.  There is only a small area for you to take pictures, so I can imagine the place can get crowded during peak season and hours.  It also gets a little cold during the off-season in the fall, so beware.There is also a small park (if that's the best way of describing it) at the entrance of the cliffs that's worth a short look as well.  There are some vendors, small stone displays, and some assorted artistic pieces.
Two floors of teddy bears for display and one floor for selling them. Outdoor park is nice to walk around. But due to hot weather, we only go out for a short while and hide indoors.
This was worth the entry fee. There is a nice walking tour of the   museum  . It was interesting to see all the glass displays in the forest. We really enjoyed the walk through the exhibits

This was probably my favorite attraction - it wasn't a place where you go and just take pictures but also get to learn something. Throughout the cave, there are display boards highlightng the different lava formations. Plus, it's pretty awesome to be walking in a cave formed by lava flow. I felt like Indiana Jones! If you walk all the way to the end of the cave, you will see a pretty magnificent lava formation.Wear proper shoes as the cave floor is wet and being a jacket as it gets fairly cool underground.

This was a first time visit for us...and we found it to be cheesy with a capital 'C'. However, who would have thought that CHEESY could be so COOL!!!!Yup, we had fun here...the place was amazing. Nature in harmony with recycled glass and plastic. it's very well maintained, good to spend a few hours here taking pictures...as well as soaking in the various exhibits on display. I particularly enjoyed the walk in the Enchanted Forest, a bit creepy though...as it was secluded from the rest of the complex, and this added to the excitement of being in the forest...talk about a vivid imagination!They have a shop selling souvenirs as well, clean restrooms and a cafe. I would recommend those looking for some fun to drop by here, and just let your inner child run free!

This teddy bear museum is one of a few around the world.  Located in Jungmun tourist complex in Jeju, Korea, is this tiny museum for teddy bear fans alike.  For 8000 KRW you have unlimited day access to 3 floors of teddy bear exhibits and the outside grounds.  This museum carries interesting themed bears like the Mona Lisa bear, the Leonardo Da Vinci bear, a Marilyn Monroe bear, and so many others.  Currently they are displaying the Elvis bear.  On the ground floor there is even a really nice restaurant if you get hungry.  Not much choice in  terms of breakfast, they do offer mostly burgers and different types of coffees.  Also there is a gift shop if you are interested in taking home one of the really cute teddy bear souvenirs.Well worth the visit and few hours for both teddy bear fans and those with just a passing interest.  Remember to use the lockers next to the admission counter.  We didn't and carried all our jackets and bags for the entire exhibit,  It will make the visit a whole lot lighter and more fun.  Enjoy!

This place is just so amazing! All the displaying items were made by glass, the butterfly, the chairs, benches, pumpkin car, etc..... Not just clear colour and its colourful! I think they have done the check frequently because I can't find any defects, broken part from the displaying items. Best visit for lovers, family with elderly or kids...

This place is going to be boring if obviously you do not have an interest to look at teddy bears because this is what the place is all about, various themes of teddy bears on display. It also depends on some children, they may or may not like this place. My family love this place (including my parents) so it's not only for children if one have the interest. I even bought a teddy bear wearing a hanbok as a souvenir for myself. There was also a free Elvis teddy bear mini performance which is so cute. Only consider adding this location to your itinerary if you do have the interest, don't waste your time if you don't.

This place is amazing! I expected to find something of this quality in the US or Europe, not on a vacation island in Korea. The cars on display were absolutely amazing and gorgeous. Classic cars for me are better than modern machines as they have more unique designs and just invoke a more awe inspiring feeling within. Absolutely love it!
address: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관

review: This place is a must-see if you're a fan of teddy bears, but it's not just for the rabid fans.  I don't count myself as a particular fan one way or another, but I don't dislike them.  The bears here are displayed as various characters and in a variety of situations.  They're cute and can be interesting, but if you're not really into this kind of thing then you'd be bored.  I'm sure children would enjoy it.  For myself, I enjoyed it but I've seen it once and wouldn't go back.

This museum, like most of Jeju's other similar attractions, is but an excuse to get you to the gift shop. You can finish it in one hour, because they want to get you there fast! As opposed to most other museums in this resort island, this one is cute and amusing. It consists mostly of tableaus or displays with teddy bears re-enacting some important historical or popular culture event. Some may frown at the   Gandhi   teddy bear as perhaps not quite tasteful, but must surely enjoy the   Beatles   teddy bears, the   Chinatown   teddy bears, etc. You get the picture. Oh, yes the gift shop! It works; I bought a little cute bear as most everybody else seems to have done. Not that expensive and well-made. In other words, if you are going to see at least one of these museums that dot the south of the island, you may want to give this one a try. It's enjoyable.

This museum is all about Teddy Bear. All the display from old to the newest Teddy Bear is here. Teddy Bear in Louis Vuitton, Teddy Bear in Hong Kong and even MJ Teddy Bear will make you smile. You can also buy Teddy Bear for souvenirs.

This museum is about the dwindling women divers of Jeju who dive in the sea to collect Agar and shellfish as well as octopus. They are similar to their sisters in Japan and dive without the benefit of air tanks.This tradition is sadly dying out and it is to be hoped that this neatly laid out museum will attract members to the group and also increase worldwide awareness.It is a static museum with some electronic displays but later, if you are lucky, you might see them diving off the coast of U-Do island.Worth a visit!

This is the best stone exhibit on Jeju island.  And the best part of that is the museum itself.  There are many, many very interesting stones shapes, all collected from Jeju (I think).  If you like geology, there's a great explanation of lava types, stone formations, lava tubes, etc.  Also there is a nice drift-wood display with very unusual, artistic shapes.  Outside, there are many carved stone artifacts used by Jeju islanders from ages past.  The Obaek Jang-Goon Gallery has a nice drift-wood display in the basement.  Park is big, but except for the museums, just a walk-through is enough.  I spent 2 hours in the museums -- the best part!

This is NOT something to do on your own. Going with a small group is best because you will need someone to take photos of you/your friends interacting with all of the   art  . It's a silly good time with lots of themed rooms each one with loads of photos or interactive displays. Watch the floor for markers of where to stand to get the best angle for the optical illusions!

This is NOT really a museum. I mean having a teeny tiny collection and a small display of tea sets and tea cups and tea.... doesn't make a  museum. Honestly. Didn't help that it was drizzling and had a constant stream of tour buses... making it perpetually crowded. It's like 20 steps worth of   tea museum   followed by a cafe that sold some o'sulloc products. Stuff ranging from facial wash to flavoured tea and green tea milk spread. Since we were there we decided - oh hey let's try their apparently awesome green tea ice cream green tea latte & green tea roll. Meh. Nothing special. I've had better green tea food.Please just go buy a 2000 won green tea milk latte drink from any 7-11 or convenience store. A convenience store green tea latte is better than their caf챕's green tea latte. (Cost 6000 won)Their green tea ice cream(4500won) and roll(5000won) were equally disappointing. Nothing special. No harm dropping by this place if it's on the way - as it's free entry. BUT... Dont go out of your way to go here. It's nothing special and food's not worth it.

This is definitely a place for kids & ladies. Sorry guys. It is bear, bear, bear & more bear wherever you turn your head. Thank goodness photography is allowed in here. Most of the bears are small, about the height of your palm. I guess that makes them all the cuter. There is a giantic bear in front of the souvenir shop. Do take a few shots with it. Considering the number of bears on display, the number of teddy bear related memorabilia is quite limited,. I wonder why.

this is basically a tea house with a few displays related to   tea history   - only some random teaware from different places in the world. as a tea house the place is very nice. you can have some nice food and sweats based on tea... but its definitely not a museum.

This is a most unusual feature on the North-East coast of the island of Jeju, South Korea. Although there are a few around the world, these tubes are some of the best preserved ones and it is a Unesco World Heritage site. It is also accredited as a Global Geopark.You can walk 1km of the tube at Manjanggul (there are over 7 km but not open to the public)- it is damp and dark so go prepared with shoes that won't slip and also have an extra layer. The temperature drops quickly: it was 28C outside when we visited in late September but only 15C inside. However, they are very 'manageable'.The caves are well-preserved and present themselves as a long tunnel which displays various features. Though it is dark and so difficult to take photos, you can clearly see the lava flowlines and the lava shelves whilst the floor is ropy lava. At various points along the walk, you are directed to other features such as lava columns and lava stalacmites. Only one entrance of the 3 existing ones is used by the public.Well worth a visit, and especially so if interested in geography/ geology.

This is a great place to learn, displaying so much sort of Korean Traditional things. You will be able to learn lots of exciting Korean culture.. Try some Korean traditional food and learn how they used to stay. Must be there before leaving Korea.

This is a cute collection of teddybears and other stuffed animals in a variety of settings (a castle, a safari, etc.), but it's not what I was expecting with the name   Teseum   (teddy+museum).  There's a very small display of older teddybears (mostly photographs), but the main attraction is the displays you can see in the pictures.  There must be thousands here, ranging in size from one inch or shorter to probably eight feet tall. I imagine kids would be in hog heaven, but some of the older people in our tour group said it was a waste of time.  My favorites were the safari and the teddybear versions of old paintings.

This bridge connects Jeju Island with the islet of Saeseom and resembles an anchored taewoo, a traditional fishing boat of Jeju coming home with a boatful of fish and its wide net streatched.? The name Saeyeongyo means creation of new connections, as it connects uninhabited Saeseom with Jeju.? Come back when it is dark and see the amazing LED light display on the guardrail of the bridge.

They made the teddies to impersonate diffn celebrities: Elvis, Marilyn Monroe, Steve Jobs, Bruce Lee...whcih was quite funny...and there was a big garden at the back to have a nice stroll...the rest of the display was so so.

There's two Teddy Bear Museum in Jeju Island. One is Safari Theme that has an entrance fee of KRW 8,500 (Php 369) for adults. This has a safari theme great for pictures but on the second floor, there are more which has a variety of themes. The other Teddy Bear Museum where the most expensive Teddy Bear is on display wearing a Louis Vuitton outfit costs KRW 8,000 (Php 347). This one is better because it has so many display that you will be amazed, famous scene, characters, celebrities from different industries. Very nice! This is also the museum where Princess Hour was shot, a Korean novela. I will go back!

There's an entrance fee, that's one . It's very far away from where we stayed (Gujwa-eup), that's two . Transportation is quite a pain.... when you stay outside the city area ...we had to hire a cab everytime we go out and see places, although, they were very kind enough to ask and offer to wait for us until we finished our tour.I think the place is great for kids and teenagers and those who love modern art and colors. It's quite a huge place with lots of interesting collections... just follow the trails so you won't miss any of the displays. At the end of it, there is a shop wherein you can buy some souvenirs...i find it quite expensive though. ⓒ

There were many themes in this park, and even though I had thought this wouldn't be very interesting initially, my family and I ended up really enjoying the place.In particular, my mum liked the hydrangeas display, my kids liked the birds display (peacocks, especially), my wife liked the bonsai garden and I liked the caves! In all, we spent almost 4 hours there!!! And we didn't complete the park, because we were too hungry and wanted to go the Jeju-si for dinner :)

There is a lot more than meets the eye here. People first wonder but then realize they are glad to visit The Glass Castle. It is a museum and park of glass works by local artisans and crafts people and the collection is vast, so vast it takes a while to see everything. There is a diverse array of glass work in gardens, themes, and museum displays of varying quality and rarity around the park.This includes large outdoor sculptures such as the yellow submarine at the entrance or crystal skulls, and glass displays around the park. We were impressed by the size of the park and diverse collection of work. They also have workshops here and some hands on experiences.I would recommend this place as a worthy place to visit while on Jeju, near the O'Sulluc Tea Museum and Plantation which only 5 minutes away.

there are many kinds of artworks such as glass flowers,trees,music instrument,toilet,etcworld artist from japan,usa,italy, their works displayed.you can make something like glass cup if you want.it will be memorable while you are in jeju.

There are lots of teddy bears in different dressing inside the museum. It cost KRW10,000 per entry but my opinion is it doesn't worth this amount of money as this museum majors in displaying teddy bear collections in the display box, numerous of human size teddy bears satisfy your photo shooting desires. As compare to KRW10,000 spent in the Jeju Village Folk where cultural living of Jeju residents in the earlier century can be experienced, it's more worthy. Desire to enter this museum was due to the Korea drama series   若モ?, and I expected to have the display of the human size teddy bears in different room with different theme enable for photo session (something like Madame Tussaud's Wax museum) but it is not the way. All the theme teddy are inside the display box. You can just sight seeing it people collection.
there are display of recycle glasses. Glasses are recycled and made into flowers, fishes and others.

There are beautiful indoor and outdoor displays of blown glass in a variety of formats.  The indoor display includes masterpieces, many by the Italian master, Signoretto.  The outdoor displays make for a great walk about through a beautiful park-like area.

There are 2 teddy bear museums in Jeju. I don't have the address of the one that I went to, but it's not the one in Jungmun, which is the older one and where you'll only see teddy bears in glass cases. The newer teddy bear museum has teddy bears that are displayed according to themes, where you can pose together  with the teddy bears, and even touch and hug them. This is definitely more interactive than the ones in glass cases.

The whole way from the car park to the falls itself was scenic. At the start was a pond with mandarin ducks and a bridge. There were various representative statues of Jeju. There were also souvenir shops if you want to buy some snacks or souvenirs. I liked the different types of trees grown, even though it is not autumn, the maple trees still looked very pretty. All along the way is a river, you go to the falls on one side and you can return on the other side of the river. There were plenty of explanation signs on the falls, the mottled eels and the rock face etc. The falls themselves don?t look very impressive but I still like the whole place. On the way back there is a nice flower display and large sculpture as well a stone auditorium.

The weather was raining on the day I decided to do sightseeing on Jeju, so I was left with only a visit to the botanical gardens. You can reach it from the airport limousine bus route and behind the fast food shops near SK Energy shop.Luckily the garden exhibition was under glass roof, so it provided a good informative shelter from the rain.The botanical gardens are organised into themes, eg. Aquatic garden, cactus garden, etc. I guess this eliminates confusion for tourists and displays the plants in an educational fashion too. On a sunny day, there is more to do on the outside.There is a curio shop inside the gardens for some gifts but I did not see a coffee shop at the attraction.It will be educational for the kids!

The Teddy Bear museum is a fun stop. There are many displays of teddy bears in various historical, cinematic, and pop-culture type settings. Take your camera and visit each floor. The gift shop at the end is full of fun teddy bear treasures as well. Definitely a good stop for anyone. We went on a rainy day, but it would also be fun on a hot day if you are looking to get out of the heat. Fairly easy to find, it's located in a popular tourist area.

The place was rather quiet when we visited (it was on a Sunday morning) despite the heavy traffic from Seoul the day before. We were given pamphlets in English, while most of the displays were in Korean language. There are many teddy bears in display and most have been displayed/posed in accordance with certain themes (like Hollywood, Snow White, landing on the moon etc). It was interesting.There was an Elvis show, with teddy bears swaying their hips to Elvis's concert in Hawaii (if I'm correct) and that was entertaining for the kids.Outdoors is a small park with human size teddy figures, great for picture taking. Remember to take pictures with large teddy outside.There is also a cafe but we did not stop by since we had breakfast earlier. In the pamphlet, we saw a train ride but we couldn't locate it anywhere. May have missed it.There was one floor for shopping and there is a large selection of teddy bears to bring home. Maybe pricey but the quality is quite good.The place is convenient for families with small children (the kids were not terrified) and stroller friendly as there is an elevator available. There is also free parking outside.As usual, for Korean tourist attractions, there are discount vouchers available. Just have to know where to get it :)

The Peace Park is very spacious and beautifully laid out.  (Shouldn't compare but it reminded us of  a smaller version of the National Memorial Arboretum in Staffordshire, UK.)  They were still working on some landscaping while we were there.   We were lucky enough to catch the excellent art exhibition that is on at the moment and the museum display is very well laid out and informative - lots of English  so we learnt a lot about the Jeju's history around 1948.   We were there about 1.5 hours but could have stayed longer.

The park has a beautiful array of flowers and other well kept vegetation. The animal displays are somewhat of an after thought, but are ok. This is a good place to spend time outdoors with friends, family, or in a tour group.

The musueum is dedicated to the Haenyeo - female divers who traditionally fish for molluscs and octopuses etc. without using oxygen masks.  UNESCO has declared the Haenyeo part of humankind's intangible cultural heritage.  We visited the museum shortly after having seen a group of Haenyeo sing their traditional song before heading out into the sea to fish.  Having just witnessed the women fist hand added an extra element of interest.  The museum is well set out, informative and interesting.  Its models, life stories of individuals and displays of clothes and tools  really bring home how tough the life of the Haenyeo was in the past (and it's not easy today).  There is also a short movie explaining the history and traditions of the Haenyeo.  Well worth a visit!

The museum has many airplanes on display and also an outdoor area where you can walk into the planes. ? Very well done, lots of information and displays. ? Hands on activities instructions are only in Korean, but easy to figure out. ? A steal for the 10,000 WON entrance fee.

The museum has a lot of teddy bears (e.g.   Goong   or   Princess hours   teddy bears, etc) well protected in a glass boxes. A total of 3 levels in the building, displaying different kind of teddys and you can buy some souvenirs from the ground level. At the grond level, there are also teddys which you can take picture with (e.g. Steve Jobs, Psy, etc).Outside the building, there are some other teddys which you can also take pictures with. It would be fun if you love teddys but if you are not, it would be quite boring. Nothing much you can do, other than taking pictures and buying souvenirs. However, it still worth a go if you are curious about the variety of teddy bears being displayed inside. The admission fee is around 8,000 won (if i didn't remember wrongly).

The Jeju Glass Castle was part of the itinerary of the group tour that I was part of. We spent more than an hour in the premises. We visited at daytime?I noticed that there a good number of spotlights so the Jeju Glass Castle must have a different ambience at night.I have mixed feelings about the Jeju Glass Castle.THE GOODThe Jeju Glass Castle is picturesque and very instagrammable. There are numerous displays that one can pose with. Many of the displays are quite feminine, though?very floral and colorful?girly, even. Most of the displays are outdoors including a small glass maze. Our trip was in December so it was cold but manageable. I liked the international glass displays?the Murano glass, especially because it reminded me of my aunt who had a significant number of pieces of this type of glass. THE BADFirst and foremost, I expected to see a palace or at least a castle straight out of a fairy tale. The Jeju Glass Castle is nowhere near a castle or palace. The buildings were plain and very utilitarian. The gardens were manicured but not palatial. It was more of a museum and a park, rather than a castle. Secondly, aside from signage that are in Korean or that mention the name of the place, there is nothing in the museum that shouts, ?I am in Jeju!? or ?I am in Korea!? for that matter. There is nothing in the museum that is intrinsically exclusive to the Jeju Glass Castle.Lastly, I was looking forward to try the glass comfort but the lock inside was broken and the door won?t keep closed. THE VERDICTI was able to take good photos of the displays?like I said, they were very instagrammable. Nevertheless, I do not see myself going back here just for the sake of it. It gets boring eventually, with little to do except to look at beautiful glass.

The interior was nice with teddy bears as the main characters. The costumes the bear was wearing was splendid. Other than bears there?s a mini safari displaying animals such as lions, bears, tigers etc. Overall, for adults you can finish visiting the place within 20 mins.

The entrance fee was quite high, but it was a very fun family outing.  Our son loves teddy bears so this was great.  There were a lot of displays of bears in various famous places and dressed as famous people in history - cool.

The botanical garden is a place where a wide variety of plants are displayed for understanding how vast is our plant kingdom.it may also help to understand the geographical peculiarities of different countries all over the world. The best thing I have seen there was they provided each species scientific details along with the source country. It will be so exciting to see our country plant representing in a botanical garden situating in a foreign place. Furthermore botanical garden is situated in a very beautiful place with a wide variety of gardens and trees, as I said earlier all the plants and trees are named perfectly.

The benefit of this place is that it's open pretty late. So when you don't know what to do when everything is closed after 6:00 om check this out. Most of   Loveland   consists of lots of outside sculptures. There are a few small interior displays - including one with a history of sex toys and small dioramas of silly sex scenes. There are also a few shops - one with old dusty outdated sex toys; the other had funny souvenirs and modern sex toys. There was also a cute cafe that offered the dense penis and boob bread drinks and ice cream. There are lots of picture taking opportunities but after awhile it becomes repetitive. You get the picture.

The 5 day market is named because it opens every 5 days only. There are other 5 day markets in Jeju but this market is said to be the largest in Jeju with 1,000 over stalls. This market opens on the 17th and plus / minus 5 days before and after.Fret not if you missed the opening of this market. Because apparently the other 5 day markets are operate by the same stall owners. They rotate among the different markets and hence will be back to the same market after every 5 days.We went there on a morning and expected to spend the whole day there. But we were out in 2 hours.There are indeed many stalls in the market but many of them are carrying the same stuff. Clothings, household products, fruits and vegetables, kimchi, cooked food and of course Jeju mandarin oranges which are famous. Interestingly, pet dogs are sold alongside with fresh chickens. And ironically, there are stalls selling dog meat at the other end of the market.Same animal but different fate.We bought the famous mandarin oranges here although these are available at other places in Jeju as well. There are many similar-priced stalls selling this famous product in this market. We chose one of the varieties on display after sampling. It has a sweet aftertaste after the first tinge of sourness. The one we purchased is the 2nd most expensive type at $25,000 Won per 5 kg. There are other varieties at $30,000 Won per 5 kg and $15,000 Won per 10 kg etc.It?s a nice experience after all and I would say it?s worth a visit if you are in Jeju.

The   museum   is not too far from Jeju City so it's only a short ride in a taxi to this location.  You may want to tell the taxi driver to drive past the Jeju Mysterious Road if you are going this way as it is along the route.The museum itself attempts to shock you but you get over the shock in a few minutes and it does become a bit mundane after a while.  You do sense that the museum creators did have a good sense of humor though.  There are many many displays that feature sexual positions toys etc. but nothing that is too shocking.  The grounds are fairly immaculate too.  Many phallic symbols etc.  You know what to expect at this location.I guess it is worth the visit as there are not too many museums like this in the world but it really isn't worth an out of the way trip to this museum.

thank you for the visit. well , first of all we are so afraid of you were not so feel good at the teddy bear museum. however our museum consist of two main theme galleries. the history and the art.  and also there are extra gallery, Elvis concert theater and out door garden. we will take an effort to present visitor more exciting display and exhibition . thank you again and have a good day ^^

Spent about 3 hours here one afternoon and was very happy with the overall visit. A full display of buildings, traditional way of life, farm areas, gardens and other typical tourist information, shops and food areas give the whole village a unique attraction for everyone. A little pricey in the shops, but as you walk through the areas you get a real sense of tranquility with the how things were. Very enjoyable and if you are there - make sure you visit.

Spend an hour here to learn more about the background of the women divers. It gave me a new appreciation for the dedication of the women and I enjoyed seeing actual divers later, with a greater understanding of what they do and how they dive. I took a few moments to watch the video and then breezed through some of the other displays. Felt it was fairly priced for the value.
Some of the bears on display are quite old and dusty. Generally, give it a try if you have not been to other teddy bear museum.

So, perhaps this comparison is unfair, but if you have to choose between the two: the Teddy Bear Museum and this Teseum, I would personally choose this Teseum because the Teseum is slightly cheaper, closer to Jeju City, and way less pretentious (that may sound weird, but that's more or less what the difference was). Teseum was laid back, a bit more interactive, and generally understanding of that a visit to see Teddy bears would mean visiting the childish side on all of us. The Teddy Bear museum was more like an anthropological study of teddy bears or something, aka, less fun, a bit more uptight.For those in the group who were not as interested in the actual display, they could opt out and still purchase teddy bears. The gift shop was conveniently open to everyone visiting and there were a few convenience stores and such around.
Small museum. The displays were interesting- the Titanic, Normandy, and Berlin Wall to name a few ? Gift shop was pricey.

Since there is not much to see in Jeju City, I liked this the most. The rock itself looks nice, so if you happen to be in Jeju City and have free time, it worth to check and enjoy the view on the rocky seaside. easy to get here from Jeju Intercity Bus terminal, just take local bus #17, and tell the driver   Yongduam   he will show the right bus stop. From there only 5 mins walk. It is just a rock, so don't expect much, but it's good trip for 20-30mins. Before going to the rock, you should definitely check the bus schedule back to the city center (bus timetable is displayed not on the bus stop, but on the shopwindow just nearby where no one would ever search), as there's 1-2 bus in every hour.

Really enjoyed our visit, albeit we will be biased as we love & collect teddy bears. Creative display of teddies and awesome Teddy Wilson photos.Would have loved to be able o buy a Teddy Wilson replica at the shop
Really enjoy my time here at Bonte Museum, quiet, quaint with lots of funky modern art displays from indoor to outdoor, all my pictures taken there look fantastic from every angle.

Reading some previous reviews for this place, I was rather puzzled how this place could be rated 3 or more stars by others. It has a number of different glass creations presented in a museum-like setting. Quite a few of these items were from Italy, Venetian glass. There are a lot nicer ones in Venice. Also, they have quite limited displays and very few look special to us. We managed to see all displays in about 20 minutes! Overall, we were completely underwhelmed by this place. If you are interested taking photos, there are opportunities for some nice photos. For others, there is nothing to learn and experience anything new here. There are other nicer museums or sights to see in Jeju, so this can be safely avoided.

Our visit to Teseum was part of a tour package, and we had a lot of fun.  Photo opportunities were plentiful, even if there were a lot of other visitors.  We enjoyed posing with the huge bears, with different theme displays.  As well, the section on classical art was quite remarkable.

Our package tour brought us to upscale shopping centers and attractions that carry local and international brands. One of these was the Chilseongro Shopping Street. Fortunately, I had bookmarked Dongmun Market on Kakao map and it was a short walk from there. I had no plans to buy branded clothes (nor any clothes for that matter) so I ditched Chilseongro and headed to Dongmun.The Dongmun Market is a wet market, a traditional market. Pretty much everything in Jeju is available here?clothes, tangerines, chocolates, seafood, household items, food. The prices here were a lot lower than the chocolate stores and souvenir centers that our tour group operator brought us to.At Dongmun, you can haggle, especially if you buy plenty. I decided to buy chocolates to bring back home to our office staff. Since there were plenty of stalls selling chocolates, I compared prices first. I ended up buying from an elderly lady who offered the lowest price. I got more than 60 boxes and she gave me lots of freebies. There are stalls that had different types of food. Some even had live seafood available and they will cook it for you. I was too full to try out the local food, but I did miss having photos taken.There were a handful of stalls that sold kitsch souvenir items like keychains and magnets. There were two large stalls that had numerous items on display; their prices were high though. I ended up buying from the other stalls whose main items being sold were something else and just happened to have magnets and keychains on the side. Nevertheless, the prices at the souvenir shops in Seongsan IIchubong were lower; I wished I had bought there instead.

Our guide brought us here to understand the striking cultural lifestyle of the local folks of Jeju.  The unique and exquisite architectural design of the `primitive'' huts and cottages of the natives was impressive. The pair of well carved and exotic Jeju deities statues that were made from volcanic lava stood spiritually on guard at the entrance. The sculptures matched harmoniously with the decorative Kimchi clay vases left unattended in the manicured lush green lawn compound displaying a special cultural taste that reminded me of the unique Hindu traditions on the island of Bali. I always think that it is the vibrancy and dynamism of the native folk culture that made certain attractions so special. The unique Alisan native lifestyle in Taiwan is just remarkably outstanding and different from that of the Maori in New Zealand and again, distinctively unique from the Dayaks longhouse traditions. It is thus a pleasure and a must thing to do to visit a folk village in Jeju to look at how the culture of the natives and how it is being preserved here.  We were introduced to a guide speaker who showed us the many agricultural tools used by the local natives but the real commercialized promotion began when we were `lured' into a room with seats and the speaker started marketing a type of drinks made from `Wuweiji' traditional herb that grew in abundance in Jeju and is believed to strengthen and invigorates the mind and body. It looks like another `tourist trap' and on the pretext of going to the toilet, I escaped the aggressiveness of the marketing talk. I wandered around the cottage compound admiring the foliage and the surrounding native architectural designs until my group of friends came out from the promotion. One of my group members was anxious to purchase the `elixir' drinks to enhance her youthfulness and she shared the drinks with the rest in the group.   I came out from the cottage and saw there were many similar cottages around the village and there were many sales talk going on in the other cottages. The admission to this folk village was free but I am not sure if my guide earned any commission from the purchase of the herbal bottled drinks by my friend.Except for the commercialized promotion, it is interesting to visit a folk village in Jeju.

O'Sulloc Tea Museum is a small building set in a tea farm. It's a well designed lovely space with a display area about the history of tea and an exhibit wall of teacups and pots a shop where you can try some tea (only one kind though) and a restaurant featuring green tea beverages and sweets. You can also walk around outside there is a garden area in and around the building and also small rows of tea bushes just outside. There's no admission fee and it's not so much of a museum as a commercial venue for selling O'Sulloc products although items can be pricey for the budget traveller. I visited O'Sulloc with a few other backpackers (5 foreigners 1 Korean) and we all had a terrible experience of their customer service. The staff were sour faced and gave us the impression that we were not welcomed glaring at us and tidying their display in a huff when we looked at the product samples (these are samples ok - they're meant to be touched and looked at!). review: On our second day in Jeju, my parents and I went on a market blast in Jeju. We went to the following (1) Seogwipo Olle Market (2) Seogwipo 5-Day Market and (3) Dongmun Market.I highly recommend both Dongmun Market and Seogwipo Market. If you are living in Jeju City, visiting Dongmun would suffice. Fresh and relatively reasonable prices. Go to those stalls that display price tag to avoid paying a   premium  .

On entering through the entrance, one comes to the palm tree avenue. Different types of palm trees and cactuses greet you.  Next up is the wild grass and flowers garden. Felt relax walking along the path. Further ahead  are the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves. These 2 caves were formed by an eruption of Mt Halla many years ago. The temperature inside the caves is around 18 degrees celsius throughout the year so walking inside was cooling. Look out for the famed natural monuments, Pillar, Mother , the two dragons up on the roof, stalactites and stalagmites, and Dr. Jin and the fox girl.. Coming out to the cave,Jeju stones greet you gesturing Welcome . Next proceed to Jae-am folk village where one can see thatched  roof houses with stone walls. Do take a photo with the tall statue of Stone Grandfather, Dolharubang.  Next  will be the bird garden where you will see parrots, pheasants, ostriches and elegant peacocks walking around spreading their colourful stunning feathers. The following spot is Jae-am stone exhibit hall  where over 200 stones are displayed. We were amazed by the natural stone sculptures in the shape of  birds and waterfall. Walking on , following the signs, one comes to water garden where you can see 5 beautiful ponds, capped by the grand waterfall.. Finally you will reach the last section, subtropical botanic garden where  there are palm trees, foliage plants, herbs  alongside parrots, lizards, snakes and tortoises. After all the walking and photo taking, proceed to have lunch at Dolharubang restaurant  to try Jeju's traditional foods, like the delicious pork bulgogi. Or you can have freshly made seafood at Palm  Tree Restaurant. Or if you do not wish to lunch, you can enjoy fresh herb beverages at  Herb Cafe.

These are pretty creative and well made. Some even include music.There's also an   art   gallery, with some famous paintings or sculptures reenacted with teddy bears. This gallery extends into more dioramas such as the   runway   and a Korean wedding scene. Not always logical in where they put things, but fun anyway. There are a few honestly significant teddies in the museum - a Louis Voittan teddy that cost millions at auction, and a small side gallery of Teddies combined with historical memorabilia from Teddy Roosevelt, with some brief English descriptions of where the teddy bear came from.It's not a top attraction if you're here for a short visit, but if you're around a while and want something cute and fun, it's worth an hour or two!

review: My family and I visited this UNESCO World Heritage and South Korea National Monument cave on a late afternoon for 2 hours. There were not many visitors and we didn?t find any tour buses when we reached here.   Getting there & fees: Manjanggul Cave is located in the north western part of Jeju-do. To get (drive) to Manjanggul Cave, key in GPS coordinate 7834818. There is no parking fee at the huge car park. Entrance fee is 2,000 won for adults and 1,000 won for teenagers and children.Manjanggul Cave Museum: Upon climbing up the stairs from the car park, you will reach the Museum and a cafeteria/restaurant on its right. You could go in and have a look at the interesting exhibits, including how the Manjanggul Cave was formed from the volcanic activities.Manjanggul Cave: To get to the underground Cave, we followed the sign-posts ? it?s within 5 minutes? walk from the Manjanggul Cave Museum. Trek the entire 1 km stretch that?s opened to public and you will end with a colourful lit lava column - created from the dripping of lava from a hole in the ceiling ? which at about 8 meters high, is the tallest lava column on Earth. Nevertheless, there are a few things you have to take note while you are in the Cave:(1) The entrance to the Manjanggul Cave is also the exit ? there?s no exit at the end of the 1 km trail, which means you are walking 2 km return (2) Make sure you bring and wear a jacket or sweater with you because it?s freezing cold and chilly inside the cave. (3) Wear a cap or the jacket or sweater can be waterproof because you get water ocassioanlly dripping from the cave top onto you (4) The surface (floor) of the Cave is full of solidified lava flow terrain (i.e. extremely uneven surface) and water puddles, so you have to wear a pair of good walking shoes and walk carefully. Hold on to the railings of the stairs.(5) You probably don?t need a torchlight because the Cave is illuminated just enough by ground lightings. Some parts of the cave even have colourful lights shining at the dome shaped ceiling (cupola) (6) If you would like to take photographs inside the cave, you would need a tripod and switch to manual mode for long exposure (I used 4 seconds to 10 seconds exposure on my digital SLR).   There are displays at certain parts of the cave in English explaining the geology of the cave and the formation of the interesting structures (e.g. stalactites). In particular, there?s one structure ? ?Stone Turtle? ? in which the shape looks like Jeju-do Island, and which you could reach in about 30 minutes of one-way walking as it?s about 400m from the entrance. Along the Manjanggul Cave wall, we saw varied patterns of lava flow lines, some are straight while some are wavy. Really interesting! I have been to over 10 limestone caves around the world, but this is my first visit in a lava tunnel cave or lava tube cave (and Asia?s longest lava tube cave for that matter). You have to experience being transported to another world in this ?out of this world? cave for yourself ? don?t miss it!

My family and I spent about 45 minutes at this attraction on an early Monday afternoon, as our first stop of a Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliffs ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary. It is designated a Natural Monument and is part of the Global Geopark Network. Getting there & fees: When I keyed in GPS code of 7351000 and 7381521, it brought us confusingly to the Convention Centre and the car park of the Seaes Resort respectively. Thanks to the helpful staff of the Seaes resort, we followed the advice and drove past the Convention Centre and then looked out for a signage that indicated taking a right turn to a road that leads to the destination. Once there, we parked the car in the car park which charged a parking fee pf 1000 won. The entrance fee is 2000 won for adults & 1000 won for teenagers (youth) and children, and we used one of the lockers for free to keep our stuff.The Cliffs/Attraction: After paying the entrance fees, we walked past figurines of dolphins and a huge rock surrounded by the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac. We then took the pathway of wooden platform steps that brought us to the bird-eye view of the beautiful blue sea and the rocky cliffs containing the awesome columnar joints that are typically at the base of the cliff. The platform only showcases a section of the 2 km stretch of these rocky cliffs. Along the platform, there is a display in English and Korean that educate you about the origin of the rocks. It would be good if another display would be able to pictorially illustrate the geography and formation. According to the information, the columnar joints were formed from the lava flows from the Nokhajiak scoria cone from 140,000 to 250,000 years ago. During cooling of the molten lava, contraction occurred and split the basaltic rocks into polygonal columns. We saw mainly tetragonal (4 sided), pentagonal (5-sided) and hexagonal (6-sided) columns. Because the origin of the columnar joints and rocks is volcanic, these are black. Throughout the time, I stood there simply awestruck by what I saw ? it?s like a divine being had creatively sculptured these columnar joints to perfection. And why only at this 2km stretch and not at other coastal areas in Jeju since the volcanic molten lava flowed everywhere?  It?s a pity the waves that crashed onto the joints and rocks were not huge; otherwise I think it would be an even more awesome sight. There are several pointers to take note:(1) You could appreciate this attraction in less than 1 hour (including photo and selfie-taking)(2) As the attraction is outdoors, be prepared for what the weather will throw at you. Carry an umbrella or wear a cap or sunglasses or put on sunscreen on a sunny day(3) To see these rocks better, I suggest bringing along a pair of binoculars or zooming closer using your camera telephoto lens or your handphone(4) Take plenty of photographs but do not climb over or lean over too much the platform ?railings?We ranked Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff as one of the top 3 attractions in Jeju. For sure, this Nature?s awesome masterpiece is not to be missed!

Lee Jung-Seob Art Gallery, like most government run museums in Korea, had a low display items to museum area ratio.? It is dedicated to Lee who spent the last few years of his life in Seogwipo after being raised in present-day North Korea and spending a significant part of his life in Japan.? In a three floor building it was just one room with about 20 pieces of artifacts.? Fortunately the few artifacts which consisted of postcards Lee sent his wife, his earlier sketches, letters to his children, and his palette donated by his wife were all interesting to check out.

Korean women divers are called haenyeo. They dive in the ocean without any special tools to gather abalone, clams or seaweed. Wearing a lead weighted  vested and goggles, they plunge into 20 meter depths and stay underwater holding their breaths for two to three minutes.  Once they come up to the surface, they make a whistling sound, which is their unique way of breathing out carbon dioxide and breathing in fresh oxygen. The museum is in a four story building and housed many exhibits.  Gallery 1 on the first floor depicts the haenyeo's way of life. On the second floor at Gallery 2, you can see haenyeo's working life.  On the third floor at the observation area you can get a view overlooking the sea.  Gallery 3 displays exhibits of the sea around Jeju.  Outside the museum there is a lawn with statues, including one honoring the haenyeo. You can also admire the architecture of the museum. Further down, we chanced upon the haenyeo who were starting their show by singing a song. We were indeed lucky on that Tuesday afternoon as we managed to watch the show which started at 1.30.
