The museum has several floors and the lowest floor is the retail area. Very interesting stuff on display for sale. Be sure to go to the Elvis Presley theatre where you can catch a 4 minute show if the teddy bear Elvis doing a performance. It is held in 15 mins interval.

I couldn?t resist visiting this place on our way from Jeju city to Seogwipo. It made me giddy as a child. Entry fee is now 14,000 won per adult, and either 11,000 or 13,000 for children. This place has optional guided tours and accepts credit cards. Small room of Hello Kitty history and how her image has evolved since 1976. Original design merch on display. Lots of interactive rooms for kids and 3 floors to play. As an adult I still had fun and enjoyed a Hello Kitty hot chocolate (her face is in the cream), and Hello Kitty-shaped strawberry mousse cake in the cafe. You?re paying for the experience, here, so if you or your child is not a Hello Kitty fan, don?t waste your time. The maze on the roof is shaped like Hello Kitty from an aerial view and is strictly for children?the maze walls are only about 2 feet tall. My favorite part was the art exhibit (2nd floor) and all the small, unexpectedly perfect details (heart shaped straws, Hello Kitty toilet paper!). Souvenir shop: a mechanical pencil costs 7,700 won (more than $6)?I guess this is slightly more than American Sanrio store prices. But, if you?re willing to visit this museum, you?re probably also willing to pay for a momento of your experience.

I confess - I LOVED stuffed toys and teddy bears! So this museum where the cute teddies were all dressed up and re-enacting famous scenes just sent me into teddy heaven. Pros:- A lot of cute scenes of teddies- Some photo spots available - Large souvenir shop- Accessible for the disabled, as there?s lifts and wide aisles on every levelCons:- Many showcases were behind glass. Because of this, the photos I took weren?t nice due to the reflection. - Could have been more interactive. As this place is (probably?) targeted at kids, it would have been nice if more displays were interactive and engaging, rather than stuck behind a glass box.

I am not overly interested in much to with botany but if I were I think I would have enjoyed this park much more. (We were also there in late January so Im not sure how much the park differs in the warmer seasons)We had nothing planned for the day and happened upon Hallim Park when we were wondering around aimlessly so it filled its purpose to us as something to do/see for 1-2 hours time.The park displays plant (and some animal) species from Korea but mostly imported from other regions in a very touristy manner. It also provides easy access to some lava tubes/caves with a paved walkway through them that are somewhat interesting as well as some other themed areas.I wouldn't go out of your way to visit this park but if you in the area its an alright place to kill some time. (unless you a botanist then I'm sure you'd enjoy it much more)- there were some ostriches that were pecking out their/each others feathers which wasn't the most pleasant state to see them in but they were at least provided with decent space to roam9,000 won/pp in January 2012

I am not interested in plush toys, but I really was attracted by the teddy bear museum, and I love there. A full of fairy tale castle, real exist in the real world.  Because it is full of various style of teddy bear, kids will enjoy very much time in the amusement in the museum, and I as a youth, although is no longer a child, but still attracted by the relaxed happy atmosphere, and enjoyed all the items in the museum to visit.  The most impressive is one of the world's most expensive teddy bear, it is very beautiful, dress made of silk princess skirt, was decorated with swarovski crystals, France, and the biggest bright spot is her crown, made of platinum and diamond, very gorgeous, and value of this teddy bear is close to one hundred million won, but also as the exhibits on display only, not sales.  , of course, when the tourists are deeply attracted by all kinds of teddy bear, teddy bear museum shops can provide people with the teddy bear toy and its surrounding products, greatly satisfy the desire to tourists for a teddy bear.  Finally, I miss very much in the time to visit the museum. And look forward to the next trip to South Korea.

How silly is a museum of stuffed bears, if you don쨈t have kids or never had a Teddy bear?  We opted to forgo this museum for the Cheonjeyeon Falls which are amazing but when we got back on the tour bus, every person uniformly said they liked the Museum.So we went back another day and were mesmerized by the display of teddy bears dating from the 30쨈s and the overall cleverness and charm of the bears.  It finally got to me at the end when I could appreciate the bears in famous paintings like Laguna Beach쨈s Pageant of the Masters event with bears!A unique concept for a museum.

Heaven on Earth - volcanic stone sculptures abound - every tree a bonsai - cedar, pine, maple and more.  Azaleas were in full bloom and a delight in colour.  The birds, in particular the white peacock who posed displaying all his feathers fanned out.  Then onto the water garden with its lotus blooms, fish and waterfalls.  I would do anything to have a garden like this in which to spend my days.

Having been to the sex museum in China near Shanghai I was somewhat disappointed by this one mostly because I found it more biased and sexist than I would expect a museum to be.  It started out good with a fairly progressive and balanced presentation albeit almost entirely in Korean talking about sexual freedom and equity.  But the vast majority of displays were very...vanilla and heteronormative.  There was very little depiction or discussion of anything besides sex between one man and one woman.  Furthermore the depictions of women and closeups of vaginas far outnumbered depictions of the male form with many showing women in very submissive poses such as on all fours and wearing a leash!  There were even a few instances where the English text accompanying a display used rather judgmental language describing certain sex acts as   abnormal   or   depraved   which I found very shocking.  I think it's great that Korea which is typically very conservative has a museum about sex at all.  But to a more sexually progressive westerner it will probably seem outdated and disappointing.  It's also hard to get to if you don't have a car.

Hallim park is part botanical garden, mini zoo, and culture center. The majority of Hallim is mediocre, but the jewel of the park is its rich bonsai collection. There's an extensive range of bonsai trees at display, some of them are over 300 years old. To those unfamiliar with bonsai trees, they may just be miniature trees; but to those who know the value of these works of art, these bonsai trees are literally priceless. In fact, it's almost unbelievable how openly accessible these trees are to the guests, considering their value and need for extreme care.If you're planning on visiting, briefly study the artistry before your trip to enhance the enjoyment. This is a one-of-a-kind collection.

Hallim Park is huge and has many sub-theme parks inside, including subtropical garden, wild grass and flower, two lava caves, bonsai and Jeju stone garden, a Jeju folk village, a bird garden, a stone exhibit hall and a water garden.  Plan to spend 2-3 hours.  For me, the best was the bonsai display, many 200-300+ years old.  Most in plant containers, some growing in natural ground, well maintained.  I've never seen a bigger or better bonsai display (maybe you have to go Japan?)  Caves are nice, but if you really want to see lava caves and explanations, don't miss Manjungul Cave -- World Heritage stuff!  Stone exhibit is good, but I prefer the Jeju Stone Park.  Other sub-theme parts rate a 3 on my scale.

Haenyeo Museum which is dedicated to the female sea divers of Jeju was an excellent museum about the matriarchal culture of Jeju that used to exist.  Despite the large building that houses the museum, there isn?t that much on display.  However, visitors get an idea about the amount of responsibilities the typical haenyeos had, basically raising their children (some dived until the day before their children were born) and running the family finances while going out diving everyday.  The donated artifacts on displays were interesting but the information about the lives of haenyeos was fascinating.

Had read and heard about Ripley's Believe it or not before but this was our first time visiting.There were a lot of interesting and somewhat interactive exihbits on display. I didn't think these were the real thing though, but rather they were replicas. You could learn a lot of new facts here. One can tell that Mr Ripley really had a talent and knack for discovering and collecting quirky stuff.One thing to note is that some of the exibhits involved morbid subjects such as cannibalism, death and torture, etc. So might not be too suitable for little children.
Great New Year's Eve. There was a huge crowd of families there, entertainment, bonfire and a fantastic firework display. Very well organised  loved every minute.

From Segiowipo (Jangung rotary) the park can be reached in a little over an hour on the 231 bus which will drop you at the front of the park.   Fare 1200krw. Park admission is 5000krw. I spent 2.5 hrs here doing course 1 and 2. I think you might enjoy it more if you were an artist but I liked it all the same. The stone museum, which is the first stop on course 1 tells you all about how lava rocks are formed, their different types and would be a geologists dream. After that you'll walk around the park and see the different stone sculptures, most of which are natural,  some manmade. There are also a couple of replica traditional jeju houses and local pottery too. The Obaek gallery has some driftwood on display along with 1 hall of art but it is mostly empty. I thought there would be more info on the local traditions and how they lived but the park is still a work in progress. Its not due for completion until 2020. Rug up because it seems to be colder here than other areas of the island and you will be outside most of your visit. Recommend you go on a sunny day as this area gets very heavy fog too.

From historical event, paintings, to modern day moment, current dramas cast of all teddies. From teddy named Wilson on his journey around the world to Elvis and Queen Elizabeth in teddy version all in one place. Not to be missed, the most expensive LV and Swarovski teddy on display! Outside you can witness miniature teddies on some serious construction site of 9 meters height of huge gigantic Teddy in the making. There's a teddy souvenir shop, and also teddy cafe. The museum is not that big, just 2 floors of gallery and 1 floor cafe and shop. Some bears displayed outside in the park.

For the adventurous and those seeking a different experience. This place is located quite out of the way, however close enough to Halla arboretum as well. Quite challenging to find as Naver and googlemaps does not have this location up to date. If you are looking to find it, look for a bus that will take you to Halla arboretum stop and you could find it by following the street direction towards the arboretum. When you see a building with   playbox  , you've found it!There's an ice sculpture display area with an ice slide you can experience. Next level on is your VR experience that you could choose to experience (cost of entry varies depending on what experiences you would like to add on).As reference we chose the Basic A experience which provides us entry into the ice sculpture, Trick art area, 5D movie experience and 1 VR experience of our choice - cost 22000krw per person.You could spend at least an hour here and rest at the cafeteria before moving on.

For 11000krw entry per person, we expected an eye opener and an attraction different than most. Upon entering, we can see from the number of glass exhibits on display that this place would've been a great place to visit for couples or families.Beautiful display with intricacies that you will need to understand to appreciate. The displays look quite challenging to maintain as there are so many glass objects that could be dulled due to weather conditions. Aside from that, we appreciated the effort it would've taken to create this glass wonderland and enjoyed it extremely. Even in the wintry snowy condition we were experiencing, although this is an outdoor exhibition, we enjoyed it!Would recommend 1-2 hours at a slow walk pace with many photo opportunities.

First  there is nothing worth seeing in this place. The exhibits were not even interesting-think chocolates shaped after teddy bears and placed in display cabinets. Their ultimate objective is to lure you to their shop which sells chocolate that....can be bought all over Jeju island. They don't even make their own chocolate.Second  they are liars. The saleswoman introduced the jeju orange chocolates to me  gave me a sample to try and recommended the   best   tasting brand. I tried it and i did like it. She recommended getting the set of 5 small boxes (each box containing 8 pieces of chocolates) because it was more worth it than the bigger box which was going for the same price but had 2 pieces less. I bought the set of 5 small boxes. When I got back  i tried the chocolates. Guess what? They tasted like cheap imitation chocolates. Nothing like the sample she gave me. Worse  each box only had a MAXIMUM<- note  of 6 pieces of chocolates. In addition  the saleswoman had such a bad attitude after I said i would only get one set of 5 small boxes. This place is totally not worth the trip. You can get better chocolates even at the airport  at a cheaper price. Don't waste your time and money.?룷?렆

Feel cheated even to waste time in the museum, still don?t understand the concepts.  Some of the displays are actually quite spooky and some are lack of theme. It give the feeling that the place was put up without much thought.

Expected the place to be bigger. Only reason we went here was to kill some time before heading to the airport. Could have gone to the Ripley's museum instead which was just across the road. As expected, lots of teddy bears in the museum. Only interesting part was the history section. They had teddy bears from as old as 1905 on display. The bears were still kept in good condition.

Except for the tulips which do not bloom in Singapore and the caves which are special to Jeju, this park is not impressive. It does not have good landscaping on a whole. I understand that tried to grow flowers of all seasons so there are naturally trees and shrubs not in bloom. But still the landscaping could be improved so we don?t have to walk for such long periods with nothing much to see. I liked the statues and water feature, the tulips area which was very beautiful, the part of the park where some peacocks could roam around. However the enclosures could be done better for more visibility of the animals. I read some reviews that they were ill treated but I didn?t see any evidence of this. We have very good displays of succulents at Gardens by the Bay in Singapore and Yeomiji Botanical Gardens was also more impressive than Hallim park. For April, I would recommend to skip Hallim park and go for Yeomiji instead for a better visit in general unless you really like tulips. Have to admit the tulips display was very beautiful.

Everything about our favourite bear and its history. The museum has 3 floors, where you can see many different displays of teddy bears and animatronics, in a different setting. One floor is for displaying teddies from different times, another one shows teddy related artworks and finally there's a floor where you find a souvenir shop and some cafes. In the outside park you can view Jungmun sea while seeing human-sized teddy sculptures. The whole surrounding area is beautiful. Ideal for friends, couples and families as well!

DRAMA WORLD is consist of DRAMA STUDIO, TEDDY BEAR and WEDDING PHOTO ZONE. Drama studio is an indoor exhibition hall with a floor area of 5,000 square meters. Drama studio is actual TV drama studio and restored studio in KOREA, USA and EUROPE, in which the visitors can experience all costumes and accessories for free(except HANBOK, Wedding dress). Our exhibition is consist of town(street) studio and interior studio. Our exhibition is consist of Korean studio(K-DRAMA) and World studio(USA,EUROPE DRAMA). Visitors of all age groups can experience KOREA culture, Western(USA) culture and The Middle ages(EUROPE) culture through DRAMA STUDIO. We are the first experiment-type drama studio in Korea where the visitors wear the costumes and use the articles to be the main character in dramas. ※ Now, World Studio is consist of TEDDY BEAR EXHIBITION and WEDDING PHOTO ZONE with a background of Western and The Middle ages studio. Collaboration between DRAMA WORLD and TEDDY BEAR. TEDDY BEAR Exhibition Hall’s floor area is about 1,000 square meters. At DRAMA WORLD, visitors can see TEDDY BEAR, which produced scenes in drama of Korea, USA and Europe. Visitors can easily understand the scene of drama. Because the text(Chinese, English, Korean)is placed in each display of TEDDY BEAR. Visitors can take a picture with man-sized TEDDY BEAR using props and wearing costume for free. Visitors can learn about the Self-Wedding culture of Korea through the Wedding photo zone with a background of drama studio. Visitors can take a picture in wedding photo zone on studio of the Western Age in USA, the Middle Ages in Europe and Korea’s drama. In each Wedding photo zone, wedding accessories are placed. And they are available for free.

Don't miss this show if u are in Jeju. Only available & performing until October 2020....awesome immersive show.? @ 빛의 벙커 Bunker de Lumieres. The floors and walls become the canvas of this highly immersive digital art that come to life, as Van Gogh's art work are displayed all over and synchronised with beautiful clasical music. Definitely worth the more than an hour show.We enjoyed it tremendously!

Displays of glass, very touristy, not too impressive. Far out in the country. There was one point where we got to see a man blowing glass which wad quite cool, but other than that it very much like an ordinary glass museum.

Disclaimer: this review is written by my better half since I?m obviously not part of the Hello Kitty! target audience.Omg! Everything is in pink! Look at the displays! They are sooooo cuteeeeee! I want to take photos with everything! I?m an adult in Kittyland! Omg, the cafe is so nice! I don?t wanna leaveeeeeeeeee......Back to the lesser half: if you are a guy, just pay the entrance fee and make the Girlfriend/Wife/kids happy. They will love you even more when you cough up for the overpriced merchandise. Seriously, I?ve never seen the Wife happier, not even on our wedding day.
Definitely a lot of stones on this island! Discovered and are displayed and arranged beautifully. Thanks to Korean holiday week, our visit was free of charge.

Crowded with a good mix of locals and tourists; jostling along for something.But the items on offer are common, with lots of seasonal clothing on display. Snacks are plentiful, so you have lots of choice. It's an interesting market, with old hands working at street food corners.

Couldn't believe that a car museum of such excellence would be found on Jeju Island in South Korea.the large number of cars covered all makes, types and brands and we just loved all the old advertising posters around the museum.The displays outside were also a delight and the museum was not hard to get to by public transport.? We stopped off to watch some of the races on the way back and that is also worth a visit.? They use descendants of the Mongolian ponies, and with their colourful jockeys they made a wonderful display.? The extensive grounds have lots to entertain children as well as a mini golf course in the centre of the race track.? Would definately recommend both destinations.

review: Bunker de Lumieres is a bunker with the images of the works by the featured artist projected on all sides of the walls.? The display alternated between 30 minutes of Vincent Van Gogh works and 10 minutes of Paul Gaugain.? The images were absolutely stunning and it didn’t take long to get into an almost hypnotic state staring at the moving images.? The calm music playing enhanced the experience.? The Van Gogh part was definitely more entertaining because of the familiarity factor.? Other than the relatively remote location along with the steep entrance fee, it was a worthwhile visit and a unique way to appreciate some well known fine art.

Built on a reclaimed land-fill site, this vast area of pathways, statues, displays, museums and traditional villages is very worth a visit if on Jeju. From the impressive stone structures and flat basalt 'floor' at the entrance of the park, I was blown away by the vast array of statues that are displayed, explained and on show in this area. There is ample car parking that is only a short walk form the entry way. A small fee is required and then you are free to wander the area that included a massive and spectacular 2 store (below ground) museum that outlines the geographic development of Jeju along with many interactive displays, a short film with subtitles, examples and galleries of 'stone art'. A gift shop of course, provided a range of traditional and specific items and there are amenities spread throughout the part. Water features, a traditional village, an art gallery and a vast array of stone sculpture will give you hours of things to view and read as you wander through the park In my humble opinion, not to be missed!!!

Before traveling to Jeju I was unaware that there was a horse show.  Our guide asked us if we wanted to see a horse show and we said ?sure?.  We had no idea what to expect.  It appears that this show caters towards Korean tourists and the show is only in Korean.  However, there was a pamphlet available in English.  I didn?t see any other foreigners in the audience.  The show takes place in a large arena and lasted about an hour.  The seats are covered in case of rain.  The show is supposed to take place during the Mongol invasions of Korea during the 1200s.  They had mock battles, displayed archery skills, performed equestrian vaulting, and a variety of other skills.  I thought that the show was entertaining, well performed, and the Mongolian riders were very talented.  My 3 year old, was a bit scared by the battles.  The horses appeared to be well cared for and healthy.  At the beginning and end of the show you can purchase a carrot to feed to the horses.  I believe that the cost of the show was 18,000 won, but our guide was able to get us a discount.  Overall, I thought that it was fun and would go back.
Beautiful   Stone Grandpa   displays in multiple setting. A nice walk around the park and also learn about the local culture and history.

At the entrance of this huge garden layout is lush, green plants  there is a bonsai garden, herb gardens, an array of flowers, a subtropical garden, water garden and a stone display as you travel along a palm garden road. There is a fair amount of walking.This display of trees, plants and gardens is a wonderful experience although its the caves, limestone tube-shaped structures growing downward from the ceiling of the cave and stalagmites that grow from the floor up. Structures are formed  containing calcium-bicarbonate. Fossilized seashells, frozen lava, and numerous other structures which enhanced our walk through the caves.  Visit the stone exhibition hall, see the parrots and the various species of birds. A must see attraction.

At first  we thought this would just be a display of various seashells from around the world. But it was so much more than that! Just amazing and so artistic. This is more like a gallery of seashell and bronze art than a typical   museum  . The artist has a brilliant eye for unique creations with seashells  making some of the installations really come to life. The staff were friendly and there is something to see at every turn (even the bathrooms!). Adult entrance fee: 6 000 won (approx. $5) and well worth it. You will not be disappointed with this museum! A wonderful surprise on our rainy day of touring.

At ARARIO MUSEUM TAPDONG CINEMA unique art works of various artists (including Ugo Rondinone Kohei Nawa Andy Warhol and more) will be displayed all throughout the 1st to 5th floor. Super-sized arts which requires complicated installation such as   Hero No.2   by Zhang Huan and   What does the vessel contain that the river does not know   by Subodh Gupta will be premiered in Korea for the first time. In addition display of 4 large scale paintings by German Neo-expressionist Sigmar Polke will also contribute to create an overwhelming ambiance at the museum.

At 10000 KRW/entry (+ discounts, if you know where to find the coupons) it can be a bit pricey for some.But I personally liked the place. It was just full of beautiful glass sculptures. Almost everything on display was glass. It required a certain amount of walking, but it was definitely worth it exploring the compound. There was even a short pathway through a mini   jungle   that had a Dinosaur theme to it. Weather that day wasn't too good and it drizzled quite a bit, making it a rather gloomy day to go about, but there were so many pretty, sparkly glass sculptures to see, so I felt that this trip was worth it. Only the area was more open-space with very little cover, so we had to stay indoors for a bit.

As we didn't manage to watch the Haenyeo performance at Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak - we decided to visit the museum instead. The museum is quiet, probably because it's quite off the center.Fee: 1100 won per personStart with a short film on the history of haenyeo, the museum has 2 floors. Display of Haenyeo's life, their tools and equipment and other deep sea fishing and farming information.A particular section caught my attention - a digital map showing where the Haenyeo went to make a living, leaving behind their home town, to make more money like Hokkaido, Russia...There is also a section featuring the Haenyeo anti-Japanese campaign, which is very much inspiring.

As the Haenyeo is unique to Jeju, this museum is dedicated to them and their story. I found it very informative, interesting and of great value to understand the traditions of the island and the long association of these incredible women. Quality displays in Korean and English explain the history and feats of these remarkable women with several outside areas to explore as well. Certainly worth a visit.

Although the weather was uncomfortably hot and humid, we decided to check out the Spirited Garden based on its raving reviews.  The garden is a pleasant peaceful spot to relax for about an hour.  Although it?s not as picturesque as some of the famous Japanese gardens, the bonsai tree collection is quite impressive.  The display on how to observe the trees was especially interesting.  Few demerits here for the excessive amounts of signs with visitor comments saying how great their visits were at this place.  The ?history hall? was just photos of famous visitors with quotes about how great the garden was.  One almost felt an obligation to enjoy the visit because these photos and comments were plastered all over the place.

Along with Seongsan Ilchulbong, Manjanggul Cave is one of the two must-see attractions in Jeju, IMHO.There is a small information center building available with some interesting facts about the cave.  The cave itself is quite fascinating.  It is only 1 km in length, but it requires a very slow pace to traverse the entire cave.  This is due to the very rough nature of the ground that one walks on.  The cave floor has not been smoothed by man - unlike Micheon cave, so the ground is extremely uneven, sharp, and at points quite dangerous!  You definitely would not want to take a fall on the ground.  The ground is also very wet in areas.  Finally, the cave is not very well illuminated.  This makes it quite difficult for people who are elderly, have physical disabilities, or if you want to carry a baby.  In fact, for these groups, I would strongly advise not to visit the cave.The cave itself is quite large in height and occupies a large volume of space.  However, it is quite dark inside the cave and there's nothing too overly unique (when compared to something like Cave of the Winds) within the cave - other than it's very big and somewhat creepy.   I only made it through one third of the cave before I had to turn back due to time constraints.  There are a few man-made displays of interest providing more information on the cave and how is was formed.

All sorts of soft toy replicas of animals made according to their actual sizes. Lots of fun for the kids. You can pose for photos with the many displays, sit on some of the displays.  There are also displays of teddy bear replicas of famous artwork by the masters. There is a display of all the bears dressed in the national costumes of different parts of the world.
A very nicely laid our museum of teddy bears.  The have many displays show teddy bears in different well known situations.  The admission charge is fairly steep, but only go if you into teddy bears.

A unique theme park to visit. Just love the colorful displays of glass.  This theme park has an outdoor and indoor displays of everything made in glass.  What really caught my attention was the many shoes made in glass (for Cinderella). They are just so beautiful, makes me remember the Cinderella story all over again! Indoor displays are the many works of art made in glasses, so eye-pleasing too!.  They have workshops where you can make your own piece of glass art. Kids are welcome to join the workshops too.
A place when we find our childhood memories, interesting display of Teddy bears in various characters like snow white and the seven dwarfs, Elvis and Michael jordan etc.

A good place to go if you love Teddy Bear. For us, I had a good time having some history lessons with my 8 year old daughter. There's a display of historical events using Teddy Bears as characters, eg, opening of disney land, WW2, man landing on moon, return of Hong Kong to China in 1997 etc. the place isn't very big. spending 1 hour here would be sufficient. make sure you take photos with PSY as Teddy Bear, or Steve Jobs as Teddy Bear! There are 12 characters in total.

3D effects when taking photos. There is small guide on the wall besides the   painting   to help you to take photo to produce the effect you will display. Of course you can have your creative imagination position to take photo. To me is more on family bonding and a place to relax.

10,000won per adult. Two floors of teddy bears gallery. I was quite fascinated by the really old teddy bears. The Louis Vitton Teddy bear was also on display, which apparently went for $190,000 during a fund raising charity event. Saw Elvis bear, Marilyn Monroe bear, Steve Job bear etc. There is a massive gift shop at ground level, selling a variety of teddy bears. But quite overpriced 10,000won for a key chain teddy, 35,000won for a palm size teddy. I don't even dare to look at how much the larger bear cost.

While visiting a friend who works in Jeju my family drove around to visit places casually with a flexible schedule. We planned to visit the temple for half an hour but stayed more than an hour. The name of the temple means medical spring and the flowing water from a 3-dragon-head fountain next to the temple store tasted good and sweet. Although the temple was built for only around 20 years the buildings and layout followed the traditional design. The main building faces exact south that can view the sea. The bell tower is located in the east for sunrise and the drum tower is located in the west for sunset. The main building's first floor wooden windows are beautifully carved with inspiring stories covered by traditional white paper but not glass. There is a traditional Korean painting exhibition of Buddha of Compassion in the basement and it's gorgeous. The best part of our visit was that not many people around. We got the chance to enjoy the quietness and even used the mats inside the temple at the back of the first floor to meditate a short while. There are grapefruit trees in the yards along the way to bathroom.
While there are numerous exhibits and really very well kept the visitors are few.  The signs are not that great and there is a lot of walking required.

When in Jeju you can choose to go to Trick Art Museum or Alive Museum. Both are about the same you pose and take funny photos with the exhibits. The Alive Museum is divided into 5 sections Trick Art Object Art Digital Art Sculpture Art and Provence Art. If you follow the route after the first three you will get to the outdoor Sculpture Art. The last section Provence Art is basically a large room with a lot of large-sized stuff dogs in Provence village setting. The dogs are not as cute as the teddy bears at Teseum. I think Alive Museum is more suited for teenagers and youg adults visiting in groups it should be more fun for them.

When I was planning my trip to Jeju  I found this museum has got half positive and half negative comments from travelers. Well ??I decided to have a look by myself. When our car got near to the place  there was a strong smell. I was then told that there is a piggery farm nearby which stinks out the whole place. The ticket was not cheap but it included a cup of coffee plus a discount in the shop. The appearance of the building is interesting with an open courtyard. The first impression was not so bad.However when I got inside  it was quite disappointing. I think the management should consider a renovation  or at least a deep cleaning and some maintenance. I just felt I was in a dusty old weird mansion. Maybe those exhibits are precious and rare  but they are not well presented. For example  they put lots of chocolate boxes from all over the world in the same window display without proper descriptions. How can the people think that those boxes are precious when they are packed in a glass cabinet? The lighting on the second floor was horrible. The rooms were so dark adding horrific ambiance to the museum.

review: We've enjoyed looking at the exhibits tasting free samples of tea and bought delicious green tea ice cream (KRW4500). Then we walked over to Innisfree to make our own soap which was so much fun - KRW15000 for one kit that makes three soaps but two people can share the kit so it's a really fun experience! You get to gift-wrap them at the end so they'd make a lovely present. You can naturally buy soap much cheaper but the experience was great and you customise and prettify the soaps as much as you like.Both O'Sulloc and Innisfree can get quite busy - as we were leaving a massive coach party arrived. It's not super-easy to find a table in the O'Sulloc cafe so beware. I saw several couples cruising around desperate to find a table while their ice cream was melting rapidly.The only negative for us was the journey: from the intercity bus terminal in Jeju-Si it took over an hour: the traffic was awful both ways! According to our travel guide it should have been 40 minutes. If you're catching the bus from the bus terminal it's number 755 from platform 10 but beware as the bus leaves before the time stated on the board/your ticket and it's a 50 minute wait for the next one (we've learnt the hard way!)

Went there in May 2015 by jeju golden city bus tour (which sucked!) and totally enjoyed our 1 hour visit! The exhibitions were amazing and the atmosphere itself is beautiful there! Adm fee is good: just 1000 won as much as I remember. Though the prices at a coffee shop were pretty expensive.

Well  that's one I definitely wouldn't recommand. There are so many things to do in Jeju and many in a 5-km radius even (Sanbangguksa  Yongmeori Beach  Songaksan...) but the Hamel Ship exhibition center is a miss. It would have actually been interesting to have place dedicated to the historical significance of Hamel and Korea through foreigners' eyes  but this was just a small collection of cheap and run-down replicas of things you could see pretty much everywhere. Maybe kids would enjoy the pirate-looking ship  but that's the only good reason to go.

review: We were recommended Alive Museum by our guide who wasn't so sure what it was all about. The facade is not like any other museums we had visited in South Korea..more like an American building. It actually reminded me of the movie 'Night at the museum'! When we entered we realized that it was all about 'trick art'. We ended up marveling at and trying out almost all the paintings. My whole family really enjoyed the exhibits. The museum is quite big and divided into several sections. There is also a nice spacius cafe there which has fresh delicious egg tarts among other ood and drinks sold. Just outside the cafe is a garden with many interesting sculptures which await you to join in. The museum which I thought would be boring actually gave my family a couple of fun and exhilarating hours!

We were pleasantly surprised at the museum. The exhibits were very well displayed. There were 3 levels of exhibits. We even saw the most expensive teddy bear at the museum. There was a live performance by Elvis - the teddy bear.  The only  reason why it is not 5 stars is because most of the descriptions were in Korean only.

We were looking forward to this museum as a different experience. This museum is amusing but just so expensive in comparison to other museums in South Korea and particularly for the reduced number of exhibits.

We were expecting a tea museum explaining the origins of tea how it's made etc. However on arrival we realised it's really a showroom for o'sulloc products (tea plus innisfree facial products). And there is not one but two cafes on the premises. And the tea museum? It probably takes up 10% of the space and the only real exhibits we saw were porcelain ware for tea. The buildings and outdoor landscaping are nice but this is not a museum.

We went to the memorial hall to see the exhibition on Kim Manduk after we visited a recreation of her travellers' in that is about 150m away.I have always admired Korea's efforts to recreate buildings and scenes fron the past that are both infirmative and interesting.The exhibit at the hall added to what we had learnt at the inn.What comes across from the information cards and exhibits was a woman dedicated to the service of others.Profit was never her main motive. Nor self-aggrandizement.We need more people like her today.

We visited this place as we were told this folk village is a well maintained place compared to others. The entrance fee is KRW11000 per person. We came here around noon. We went to the restaurant to have lunch which is just a few minutes walknas you enter the village however we were told that they are closed for a private function. We end up having junk food from the convenient store near the entrance. I wish they would have informed us much earlier or put up proper notice on the matter. Anyway we went ahead to discover the village. The paths are clearly marked and easy to navigate using the map. At each exhibit there are signage but lack of the story for each place. Some of the buildings are not so well maintained. You can't enter most of the buildings. They is a cultural show which we managed to catch which ran for about 40minutes. You need to check the timing for it. Overall the place is nice but we wish we had a tour guide who is able to explain to us in detail sp we can appreciate the village and the history of it.

We visited the Manjanggul Cave on a very wet day.  The floor of the cave was wet and the stones slippery. Puddles of water lined the route. It would have been all right if the light was brighter but it was not. The lighting was dim and you can easily twist an ankle if you stepped into one of the many crevasses in the floor. The dim lighting did not make things any easier and you really have to watch where you are going. Wear proper walking shoes if you do not want to slip on the stones. I felt that the lava cone that was our destination was quite dazzling but I wish the authorities had spent a little more care in making the whole walk safer for those who are mobile but who are a little unsteady on their feet like the elderly. The video presentation that we saw after the walk was good. The exhibits were well curated and gave us an idea of other earth formations resulting from volcanic activity in the area.

We visited on a rainy weekend which made the aquarium a perfect place to visit.  It has a nice variety of exhibits and displays.  It was warmer inside than we expected...not heavily air conditioned.  Good entertainment for little kids plus teenagers.

review: We visited in April 2018 and were impressed by the quality and the size of the village. There is a lot of history and culture to be learned here. The exhibits are well maintained they have live gardens and animals to represent the life in the village as well as hands on exhibits for kids and adults to participate in. There are craftspeople and artisans that are making wood work and stoneware that you can purchase. It is very beautiful. Also there is a restaurant on premise near the front gates and gift shop. The living museum and village is wheelchair accessible and worth the price of admission. It will take 2 to 3 hours to see everything. It can easily be a half day experience. Get there early to avoid the crowds. It's popular for students and tourists along with all the major places you should visit while on Jeju.

We visited here as part of a ships tour. The 8 minute film was very interesting. There are three exhibit halls. The first two were the best. You can see the whole thing in less than an hour. I wouldn?t go out of my way to come here
We spent over 3 hours in the park and exhibition building.Gives you a perfect view on the history and evolution of mother earth. We really enjoyed and learned a lot.

We rented a car. We reached the Tea Museum just after 12 noon. The car park was already full and we had to park by the side road. The museum is more of an exhibition of tea cups with write-ups on a brief history of tea and the origins of the Osulloc tea. Easy reading for a morning activity. There is a tea merchandise section and a cafe.We ordered the green tea ice-cream and black tea ice-cream. Both were good. The tea was very intense on both the ice cream. The green tea roll was just passable for us. Drop by if you are on the way. I think at certain times of the day there maybe some demonstration on tea but nothing was written in English so not sure of the timing.

We invite you to 'Figure Museum Jeju'  full of fantastic movie figures and statues! There are tons of high quality exhibits! Action figures  movie statues  life size statues  upcycling arts  game statues  etc. Everybody can enjoy and have fun here with figures from movies and games and animations.

We didn?셳 spend much time here which was a pity but in any case there were too many tourists. Would be a better experience when less crowded. The buildings are stylish and there is a nice view of the tea gardens. You can try the tea and they explain the tea making process. The cafe looked good with desserts like green tea cake and ice cream but we didn?셳 try as the queue was too long. Nearby was the Innisfree building where many people were making handmade soap. There was also a cafe and exhibits of the different distilled essences of flowers and plants in Jeju.

We arrived at 10am and the place was delightfully empty. The downside was that there was no glassblowing display. However  the walks  the gardens and the exhibits are all interesting and enjoyable. Families of all ages can spend a good hour here.
Truly heartwarming to see how this cultural heritage is safeguarded and exhibited for us to see. This museum is very informative.
Totally worth it.  All of the exhibits have English translations so I was able to read up on all the animals that interested me.  It's a bit pricy but totally worth it.

review: To fully enjoy cultural heritage it is recommended that you spent few hours reading and inspect all the objects that represents it.Even though it was raining during the time I visited I enjoyed the Folk village because they have a very interesting culture and history dated thousands of years.In each places represents how the Koreans house hold systems livelihood and government are highly organized.I also enjoyed the art exhibit and felt honored meeting the National artist.  He even gave me one of his works on display!After roaming around you might want to experience authentic Jeju cuisine by dropping at the Traditional Market inside the Folk village at reasonable price. Oh don't forget to try the Cactus candy!It's just unfortunate that we haven't witness any Korean traditional wedding ceremony that day due to rain.This is much better Folk Village to visit as it is bigger than the other nearby.

This was suppose to be one of the 1st museum in the world to exhibit all sorts of teddy bears. Not a very big place but pack with tourists. For the really young at heart or the really young kids this may be a novelty.

This was my second trip to this museum.  The beautifully made exhibits address much about the history and lifestyle of the diving ladies. One exhibit also compares the Korean divers to the Japanese divers.  The viewpoints from the museum are lovely

This was a stop of a bus tour through the weestern part of the Island. The so called tea Museum is a building where they sell  tea in all kinds of packaging such as bags and boxes. The word Museum is barely justified by the few pots and cups that are exhibited. You certainly should not come here from Europe because of the tea Museum. For those that never have seen the harvest of tea leaves is worth a stop.

This venue offers quite a few exhibits for photo moment. Kids will surely like his place. The place can be done in an hour time unless you spend time explaining to the kids what each exhibit is about. The gift shop offer a good range of teddy bear to buy as a gift.

This site explains everything one needs to know about the island's historical past.  It has a long walkway leading one through outdoor exhibit areas each section with attendants who can give information.  There also was a traditional musical performance available to view.  It was chilly when we were there so we left earlier than desired but if we had known there was a cafe in which to warm up and perhaps have lunch we could have made a day of it.  One perk of going in February was that the crowds were very very small here and at other locations.

This museum isn't very large and in the winter you don't really want to go outside to admire the small amount of outdoor exhibits (which you can do from inside the windows anyway) but it's got enough interesting art to be worth 1000 KRW which is about USD $0.80. For one I enjoyed the Chang Ri Seok exhibit as his paintings are very earthy. The second floor exhibit was under renovation when I went but still for 1000 won I have no complaints about the first floor's contents. The gift shop is pretty underwhelming though.

This museum is located a short distance from the city center. However a taxi ride from our centrally located hotel only cost about 6000 Korean won. On the day that we went to the museum we were able to get free admittance because they had some special promotion though I think that the admission fee is very inexpensive anyway. We enjoyed the museum very much especially the special exhibit entitled ?쏞hoe Bu`s Diary: An Unexpected Encounter with China.??This exhibition will run from July 21 to October 4 2015. There is also a fascinating diorama of a Jeju village.If you like history and historical artifacts you will enjoy this museum. It?셲 well worth a visit.
This museum is in a remote location but it's quite easy to find. We totally enjoyed visit.  The exhibitions are very impressive.  Its a relatively small museum but it's the highlight of my day.

This museum is absolutely fun. From the moment I stepped in it was simply hilarious. I have always loved historical museums but I love these interactive ones even more. I was supposed to go to the Trick museum but the concierge at my hotel recommended ALIVE museum. It was a walking distance from my hotel in Jungmun so I walked over. At the beginning of the street where this museum is I saw a big sign but no museum. I had to walk a little bit before I saw the museum. I think they have to do better with the signs on the major street so visitors will be more informed on how to get there. It also looks like some wings are in still in construction. The road leading to the building looks like it needs finishing too.That being said once you get into the museum there are lots of interesting exhibitions and pictures. Most of them were famous painting s that we could interact with while taking pictures. It was fun watching other people interact with the pictures and sculptures as they took pictures. My favorites were the ALIVE Aquarium the coiled python that was squeezing the life out of me being a mermaid being dinner and fighting the leopard for my red suitcase. They are some sculptures in the museums grounds that are very interesting and interactive too. For just about $9 USD I had a very memorable day in Jeju. This is one of my favorite attractions in Jeju Island. I highly recommend visiting the ALIVE museum while on Jeju Island.

This is not a bias assessment. I would be glad if the establishment owner would take in advise from visitor feedback. This is my first time to rate an establishment with such a low rating. It is a total rip-off as entrance fee is collected before cafe and store. There nothing impressive with the collection and exhibit area is extremely small. There is another fees impose for DIY chocolate making session. No educational value  no entertainment value. I would not recommend it to anyone.

This is an amazing place. The museum is absolutely first rate. All the exhibits have explanations in perfect English.  There are lots of interactive displays. If you are interested in the geology of Jeju you should come here first and expect to spend several hours. Outdoors there are 3 courses (walks) with exhibits of life in old Jeju. The exhibits are well done and English signs are excellent.  This place is huge and amazingly you will have it almost to yourself. It has an entry fee of about $5. That is the bargain of the century!   Don't skip any of it. It could easily take a full day if you are intellectually and esthetically inclined. It was the best thing I did on the island. I spent only about 4 hours. I would suggest you bring food and water with you. I had a few apples and tangerines.

This is a well put together museum. It has all of the explanations in English. The museum includes an outside area as well as the inside. It covers the history of the island as well as the way of life of the islanders. There's a wildlife and fish exhibit.

This is a fun place for the family !  To enjoy this place to the max you must not be shy about lying on the floor or doing funny expressions to pose to achieve the photo effect .  We had great fun as a family n have a good laugh as we review the photos taken.  There's also a outdoor sculpture park which we enjoyed doing funny pose with the sculpture ! We were there on a Sunday about 1030am there wasn't a crowd that allow us to have more time at each exhibit to pose without worrying on holding up others.Go n have fun !

This is a cool place to take the family. It fun and easy way to walk through mazes. With stream for kids to play in. A amusing part for me was U given a picture of maze so can solve easily. The inside exhibition is worth a walk through with more puzzles and games.

This is a contemporary art museum by the seafront in Jeju city showcasing a private collection in a disused cinema and an old bikeshop. There are many varied exhibits from China to Germany Korea to France.we especially liked a music and light show by French artist Pierre Huyghe (l'Exp챕dition scintillante).Entry is W12000 for adults and covers both buildings.

This has to be the best museum on Jeju. I have lived here for over 5 years and I have been there at least 3 or 4 times. The exhibits are interesting and there is even a couple of places where you can play old video games for free. If you enjoy computers or video games at all this the place for you.

They have different exhibits some even showcase works of art by young local students. Do check out the time table for the exhibitions and they also have piano or musical performances also need to check the dates.

There is actually nothing much in this museum. Only Teddy Bears depicting some celebrities and events. I had expected more exhibition so I was disappointed with what I saw. I read that there is an outdoor museum but I didnt manage to find it. Recommended for kids only.

There is a big signage in Korean at the entrance next to the ticketing booth which we didn't apprehend  but the window of the ticketing booth was blocked with wood and when we moved to the back of the premises  we found back doors not closed and things which seemed to be exhibits were scattered on the backyard.
There are three connected mazes.  You can go through one or all.  A great way to spend a few hours.  There is also a museum/exhibit maze in the building.

There are several Alive Museums in Korea and Singapore.  Each features a series of themed scenes for trick-art photos.  You can pose as directed for each scene and create a funny memorable photoThis one is located in the Jungman Tourist Resort area on the southern side of Jeju Island.  We ended up going there on a rainy day when it was just too blustery to be on the beach.  Unfortunately everyone else had the same idea and it was too crowded.  We had to wait so long to take photos that we ended up not getting very many views for our memory book. I think we only took about a half-dozen.  It was so crowded in fact that it was even difficult to walk.  And it is a big place!  There are also interesting photo ops outside the building such as with various types of vehicles and statues.  I think the Alive Museums would offer a better service to visitors by following the system used by museums for special exhibits:  issue a limited number of tickets for a specific time period allowing one group to move through to a certain point before starting the next.  Really the best part about our visit is that we purchased a combo entrance ticket purchased there for 12000 Korean won  (about $10 USD) that allowed us to visit the nearby African Museum which was FANTASTIC and well worth the time spent there.  So if you go to the Alive Museum try to go early or pick a sunny day.  Or if you don't mind crowds and lots of jostling about it can be part of your rainy-day beach retreat.  Either way get the combo ticket!

There are quite a few of these in Jeju and Seoul. If you aren't the type to take photos at every painting then about an hour will be sufficient for the inside exhibits. It was raining so we didn't get to explore outdoors pity. The little Provence village at the end with the big stuffed dogs makes nice pictures too.

There are many glass exhibits in this park with indoor and outdoor sections. There is a myriad of colours once you step inside and it is sure to lift your mood. It is recommended for families and couples as there are many chances for memorable photos. You can try out glass blowing if you have the time and willing to pay.

The village was rather quiet and not as lively as in the pictures shown online. We were expecting to see interesting performance with some dancing. The actual performance was below par with just 2 ladies playing stringed instruments. There were no animals around except for 1 horse. Most of the houses were bare. The Dae Chang Geum theme park touted was actually just a small hut with some boring exhibits!

The place is quite far from the main town but it's worth it if you are a fan for green tea. There's a simple exhibition on history of green tea. Then there's the O'Sulloc shop and cafe which is full of green tea products and food. The green tea latte green tea ice cream and the green tea log cake are the 3 things must try in the cafe. The only bad thing is that the cafe is a bit too crowded and noisy to enjoy such nice tea.

The place is nice with exhibits of the tea culture and evolution. however the cafe is often crowded with visitors and finding a seat can be challenging. the exterior view is fantastic! visitors should also explore the area outside the museum!

The place is a bit run down and really short of foot traffic. We were accosted when we stepped into the museum shops. The entrance fee is relatively steep for Jeju - 12k for each adult.The exhibits are tasteful in my opinion but the rust is showing. For the entrance fee I expect to receive at least a small souvenir.

The park was probably pretty nice 4 or 5 years ago but now everything is falling apart and some exhibits aren't even open. My son is obsessed with going there but he is only 3 and anything dinosaur related makes him happy.

The Osulloc Tea Museum is just not a tea museum but I would rather say a tea complex which includes a Tea Cup Gallery various Tea Culture Rooms such as exhibition hall masters of tea vessels tea life center etc. tea caf챕 and tea gardens. Tea Museum also offers a premium tea class in which brewing our own green tea and sharing with friends during the premium tea class is one of the unique experiences so far in Jeju. In the class they not only explain tea and tea brewing methods but also demonstrate the use of various tea wares and their importance in making one good cup of tea. In the end it was a good memorable day to make and drink green tea. Besides museums souvenir shops and green tea caf챕 there are few tea gardens and resting areas where people can enjoy nature relax and take pictures to keep their memory forever.

The museum is located opposite of Jeju Korea Tourism Organisation and can be reached from Seogwipo or Airport on bus number 600. The entrance fees is 2000 won and there are 3 levels of teddy bears exhibition and the ground floor is where all sorts of teddy bears are being sold. There is a cafe within the museum and a theater showing Elvis Presley lookalike teddy bear singing Elvis's songs. It is about a 15 minutes session.
The museum is easy to navigate and move about and there are enough exhibits around. About 1 to 2 hours here would be enough. There is also a nice souvenir shop in the complex.
The museum has really cool exhibits and they were beautiful to see. It's easy to relax and forget about the outside world.
The main exhibition hall for the musuem is closed till the end of the year. They currently only have a small exhibition hall open to public

The indoor section of the teddies was not big and could be completed within an hour. There are teddy bears of different celebrities and famous events. There are also exhibits that shows the evolution of teddy bears over the century. There is also the world's most expensive teddy bear not to be missed.There is a short mechanical Elvis presley teddy bear show every quarter of an hour. I did not visit the outdoor section of the museum.

The government run museums in Jeju finally opened on a trial basis limiting a number of hourly visitors to 50 with online reservations being required (although it didn?셳 really seem like a must when we arrived).  Considering it's a large complex (which itself looks impressive) Jeju Museum of Art didn't have a whole lot in display other than a temporary exhibition consisting of mostly projected images.  Thorough explanations of the pieces were provided on pamphlets and the display although few in numbers  used the wide spaces well.

The exhibits here are very interesting and wacky with camera placement tricks. You can't see the illusions unless you take a photo. Effects came out rather cool on the photos. So do equip yourself with a camera and of course have someone with you to take photos for you. Many people it was hard to take pictures. Staff is unfriendly and did not smile.
the exhibits here are very interesting and wacky with camera placement tricks. but believe they can be updated with more new pictures and make it better!

The building itself is pretty cool  when we were there the tall grass was in in its full glory and towered over either side of the path into the building. We were given discounted admission because one of the exhibits inside was temporarily closed. It's interesting to walk around inside a bit (there are some nice clean bathrooms in there too) and see the several art exhibits inside. It's very peaceful and relaxing inside the building.
The architecture was beautiful. The stadium was opened to the public and you could enter the stands from one of the entrance beside a short exhibition on the world cup 2002.

The Alive Museum is an exhibit of life-sized optical illusions of which you can pose with for some really fun photos.  Admission was 10000 won ($10 USD) each.  It will take you between 60 and 90 minutes to get through the exhibits.  There are more than 100 photo opportunities.  Make sure you arrive with a charged camera or camera phone.  I would not recommend going alone as you would have nobody to take your photo.  An ice cream and coffee shop is located towards the end of the museum.Highly recommended.  We are glad we went.
thank you very much for your visit. and also appreciate your kind explanation about our museum. we believe everyone might be happy with lots of interesting exhibition in our museum.
thank you so much for the lovely reviewing. we are so happy to hear you have been impressed in our museum. we'll try to keep high quality of the exhibition and other facility conditions.

thank you so much for lovely detailed explanation of  Jungmun and our museum. If you were teddy bear lover you could stay much longer . we feel so sorry for that. however we exhibit very carefully selected world famous artist's masterpieces and antique bears which have historical value. thank you very much for your visit and have a nice weekend.

thank you for your visit. we exhibited carefully selected teddy bears by the world famous artist and historical value . and there is lovely teddy bear sculpture garden with nice view of Jungmun beach.normally most of people stays about an hour even more at the museum. it's too short 30 minutes  to taste our museum's genuine. have a nice day ^^
thank you for your visit. we exhibited carefully selected teddy bears by the world famous artist and historical value .

thank you for the visit and a comment. each of teddy bears exhibited at the galleries are carefully selected by the world famous artist and historical value etc. and also there is lovely teddy bear sculpture garden where you can take fresh air with nice view of Jungmun beach. please take a time with nice memories of childhood even if you are not a kid. have a nice day.. thank you

Seobok was born in 255 B.C. In what is now present day Yongkou city of Shandong province China. That is why there is Taesan square stone donated by people's government of Shandong Province  China. There is also a Seobok monument memorial.The story of his journey to the Far East as commanded by Emperor Qinshihuang can be seen from the stone frescos. You can also get more information from the Seobok Exhibition hall. After this  you can proceed to China Park  nice garden

Run by a tea company that touts itself to be a premium tea brand the tea museum is nothing more than a small exhibition of some historical earthern ware and the owner's/ company statement about bringing back Korean tea culture to modern society.It has a tea shop (their tangerine and Camellia teas are good) cafe (very crowded but has really good green tea sets  for two consisting of ice cream a drink and green tea Swiss roll) and a tea workshop area called the Tea Stone situated in a garden. There's also a tea plantation where you can score some good photos or just simply take a quiet peaceful stroll through the greenery.Nearby is the innisfree Jeju House which also has a cafe selling some of their beauty products. The selection isn't great and they don't  give you free samples though you could score some Jeju only products. I find going to Myeongdong for your K beauty haul much more satisfying and easier on the wallet. Or if you just wanna stop by for their DIY soap making activity (they also sell the kit at the store so you can do it on your own) it seems like a peaceful way to escape the hustle and bustle of the city.

read reviews on this place and thought should visit and ee all the hype. To start of with there is an entrance fee of 12000 KW its not worth it for the exhibits and it was all in Korean so really didn't get it at all. Anyways since I was already there just make the most of it. nothing so special so you can give this a miss if you have spare time enjoy the beach view is much better than wasting time here.

Personally I find this place to be one of the most undervalued sights in Jeju. Mokwana represents the historic administrative center in the oldest part of Jeju City. The place is not large yet has a lot to show with stories at every corner. It takes only about half an hour from the airport and it took us about an hour to get around once inside. They have nominal admission fee (~ 1.4USD) and it was worth. The only complaint is that some of the labels for exhibits were provided only in Korean.
Our tour only gave us 40mins here. We wasted our time at the front not realising the exhibits got much better further in.

On a 3 day trip to jeju we needed more indoor activities due to the daily snowy conditions and found Jeju National Museum. With low expectations and dampened spirits as we were expecting to visit more outdoor activities we were pleasantly happy with our choice.This museum was easily accessible from our hotel as it was only a 28 minutes bus ride (costs us 1150krw). The bus stop just outside the museum.The museum itself is quite out of the way from the city centre but so was all the other places we wanted to visit and therefore was not an issue for us.Highly recommend you taking your time to read and inspect each exhibit. It is quite amazing how history laid out the changes made due to advancement through discovery. Although for a quick browser it may only take you half an hour (it took us more than 1 hour).Entry was free and I'm not sure if this is the norm but surely worth a visit even if just as a time filler.

Okay this is pretty common on Jeju I guess. There are lots of museums that copy each other and it confuses tourists. This listing is an example of that. The reviews for this listing is a mix for the Museum of Sex and Health and for Loveland there is no actual listing on here for Loveland. We did our research first to decide which one to go to and Loveland looked like the more fun one - a lot of the pictures of outdoor sculptures on this listing are actually from Loveland not the Museum of Sex and Health). I'm not even if they both have the outdoor sculptures. Loveland is mostly outdoors but it does have an indoor section too with a shop and a diorama exhibit (if you're strapped for time you can probably skip the indoor part it's not very long and the exhibits inside are mostly in Korean so if you can't read it you have to extrapolate things for yourself). The park is fun a lot of it is very silly (they even designed the bathrooms in the spirit of the park - have a look at the door handles).
No doubt it is quite costly but there are a lot of teddy bear exhibits here which is quite worth the visit. Try it if you are nearby. Just pick one of the teddy bear museum in Korea would be enough.
Nicely designed with many exhibits and several shows.  Loved the 'fish ball.:  Adjacent to Sunrise Peak.

review: Nice museum with all the exhibitons. the deliberately explain bout the life of jeju women.plusThe children museum is just too cute.

My wife was bowled over when she saw the poster of the actress in the famous Korean drama - Jewel In The Palace.  Walking through the grounds we were told that the drama was filmed on site and visited the villages and houses.  It brought back nostalgic memories of the show capping the highlight visiting the exhibits.  But if you are not a fan of the drama the village is still a good place to visit to get a good idea of the traditional Korean homes during the Joseon era.

My wife and I thoroughly enjoyed our time at these gardens. The effort that has gone into creating different exhibits both indoor and outdoors in extraordinary. It has an extremely relaxing feel and a great view of the volcanic mountain.

My wife and I enjoyed taking in the detailed research and work that were put into this teddy bear exhibition. They have records and teddy bears from the 1900s alongside an outdoor teddy bear garden to soak in the teddy atmosphere.

My 5yr old loved it very much. Lots of dinosaurs on display outdoor. Several exhibitions on site such as fossils and seashells. Areas where you can interact with animals (feeding ponies and gerbils.) You also get to see parrots next to the gift shop. It's not a very big place. we spent about 2 hours there. We got a taxi there and the man at the ticket hut(speaks good English) was very kind to help us get a taxi back to hotel. A very enjoyable and pleasant place to visit if you like dinosaurs and animals.

Maybe I'm not the mini theme park type of person. It was poorly maintained and I did not enjoy it. There was a small area that showed how Korea was like in the 60s that I thought was different from the other outdoor exhibits. This is not a place I would recommend my friends to go. I think there are better places.

Loveland - the adult sex park.  I read about it before the trip and thought why not visit it.  Something different but we were disappointed.  The ticket was pricey @ 9000krw per person.  Inside the exhibits spread out over the park can be better sculptured and the themes in each exhibit area better managed.  Overall it was a disappointment.
Love the theme park.  It has exhibits of glass sculptures indoor and outdoor. The whole place is so colourful. You can enjoy all the glass work in this beautiful theme park.
Lots of greenery surrounds the museum with a small exhibition of tea cups. Cafe serves excellent green tea ice cream and dessert rolls.
Just like other museum.. its exhibit everything about Haenyoe. There are some festival on the day of my visit.

Jeju Museum of Contemporary Art is the main attraction in the few square kilometers of creative space in Hangyeong-eup area.  Without even entering the building there are a dozen or so cool sculptures in the garden area.  The exhibit consisted of works by local Jeju artists including a photography exhibit of the family members of the Jeju 4-3 Incident victims.  A satellite building had a nice exhibition of paintings of the mountains of Korea.

Jeju Folk Village Museum as it appears on map for Jeju is on the coast and is a must do for history and culture buffs. There are hands on exhibits that kids and adults can participate and use around the village. The park and museum is large and takes 2 to 3 hours at least. Perhaps longer to see everything without rush. We were quite impressed by the size the crafts people making products and the exhibits throughout. There are ample restrooms snack shops and Korean traditional products sold in the gift shop. There is also a restaurant on premise.The Jeju Folk Village attracts students from all over Korea as well as tourists from other countries. I highly recommend the park. There are beautiful floral blooms as well as animals photo opportunities and lots of traditional Korean history and culture to learn about. Well worth the price of admission. Plan to spend half a day here. Arrive early to avoid the crowds. There are some great gifts and candies to be found around the village including the traditional Korean taffy near the Hanbok photo place and the gift shop.

Jeju Folk Village is not very big and not small as well but it effectively demonstrates the history of Jeju tradition from the 1890s. Different types of villages were located systematically. While walking through different houses and villages it feels like visiting a real movie shooting studio. Everything looks clean and real just like somebody still leaving there. The real animals and bird kept makes it even more alive village. Some of the life-size dummies kept there to display the old traditions and clothes were remarkable. The posters in from of few houses indicated that those were indeed used in making popular movies or TV dramas based on the old lifestyle.Besides there are various exhibition halls performance hall dram shooting sites poultry farms etc. which make it even more interesting. People can also even enjoy various folk games. It actually not only allow people to observe the traditional Jeju lifestyle during the 1890s but also allow people to get experience by playing folk games wearing traditional Korean dress etc. Thus it is recommended to visit this place during a visit to Jeju.
Jeju April 3rd Peace Park  - really a peaceful place to visit. Walk through the small exhibitions to understand it better.

I've visited the original Da Vinci Museum in Florence in the middle of my school field trip many years ago. Since I visited fancy museums in that trip like the Louvre or Orsay  I never expected the Da Vinci Museum to be as good as those. However  it was one of the best places I've visited in the trip. Other museums only let people to look at the exhibits but those in Da Vinci was to be operated. I think touching was stronger feeling that looking. The memory is still clear.With the good memory from Florence  I also visited the one in Jeju and it was also great. I went there with my girlfriend and worried if she doesn't like it since it seems a bit for students and children. Anyway  turned out she liked its clean and pleasant facility. I think I like the one in Jeju little more since it is not in the middle of crowded city. Maybe because the one with me matters.

It's too far to make it worth your time. Suggest to skip and go to chocolate museums in Belgium or Germany  which are much much better. This doesn't cut it and exhibits feel a little neglected....The chocolates on sale are very expensive too. But I think the locals may find it an educational intro of chocolate for their children...

review: It's a teddy bear collector's dream to come here. Joanne Bear Museum have higher quality bears compared to the other bear museum in Jeju Island (which I forgotten the name). The beginning of the trip is a exhibition of teddy bears with theme clothing  which is very adorable! At the end of the trip  you can own one of the teddy bears there. Note that it's quite pricey  but the quality is there and it's said that it used organic material to make it.

It's a tea museum but there's very little exhibits so I was a little disappointed.However there's lush green fields of tea leaves to take photos with there's a Innisfree boutique store here and the food at the Ossuloc Cafe is really worth a try!

It's a exhibition place related to tea but very little to show. Just a room to show the history and some tea pots. Overall is a good place to sit down and enjoy the relaxationIf weather is good can go to the tea field for more photo....

It was unfortunate that the immersion tour group was delayed in setting out on a one hour journey to this natural heritage centre that we were not allowed to visit the 5 lava tubes. However the 4D film of a little boy 's adventure on this island more than made up for the disappointment of not visiting the lava tubes. It would have been a great trekking experience to the lava tubes from the museum exhibits & brochures ... perhaps it warrants another visit to this island?

It was a great experience! I was really amazed by the exhibits. They were made of glass and they came in different colours  shapes and sizes. I would definitely recommend this place. This place will also appeal to kids!P.S. There is an entrance fee  but I forgot the amount. If you come in a large group  I believe that there is a group discount.
It was a fun two hours in the museum especially for the children. They were excited seeing all the funny exhibits and posing for photos.

It was a butterfly and insects theme park. Entry fee 9500 won. It doesn't display real butterflies and insects I think. There were just fake but they really did a great job by setting up for the exhibition. I really adored their creativeness to potray various human activities and historic scene by using insects and butterflies. The miniature were really nice. If you are expecting to see some real butterflies flying around you wouldn't see one :(We also went to mirror maze. This was superrr awesome! The maze was small but it really did made us feel excited to find our way out. Beware not to bump to those mirrors hehe.

It is first time for me to write a review of a museum because it was much more beyond our expectations. You will love the exhibition even if you are not a big fun of cars. The best part for my 8 year-old son was the test driving for his first International Driving License.
