review: It features Korean ancient village type of houses they stayed their work places their farms their lifestyle and others. It's a huge place so be prepared to walk a lot. The biggest draw here is the famous actress Lee her famous tv series was shot in one part of this village. It has a small exhibition house displaying things used in that tv series. Enjoy visiting this place if you are her fan otherwise you might just feel its just another garden. There was one thing interest me there were beams and beam holes in front of each village house by placing different number of beams it's actually telling others whether its widow's house or available or man at home. Be reminded it takes up a lot of the time for visiting this place may skip and visit other indoor museum.

Is a quaint place with some very good drinks and desserts. But the crowd is overwhelming. I would skip this place altogether if I visit Jeju next. It?셲 got nice tea plantation front of the museum but I?셶e seen better ones in Taiwan. Truth is after a torturous hike up Hallasan mountain we needed to do something easy the following day so Osulloc Tea Museum was in the itinerary. Tea culture not very well exhibited and I think this is more of a shopping excursion. The staff not friendly or helpful but rather want to be done with your query. To sum it all if you want to shop you can come but otherwise this is a place you can skip.
Indoor and outdoor exhibits that are very colourful and unique. A mixture of local and foreign art glass sculptures and somewhat of a love theme surrounding the exhibits. Loved it..

Indeed a disappointing experience. Yes  this is just an excuse to get you to the gift shop  but at least they could have made the trip there interesting. The story of chocolate is among the most fascinating in the histories of commodities  but they made it a torture. You will see some exhibits on the history of chocolate  a few displays of old boxes and cases of chocolates  and some needless toy sculptures  but mostly a forgettable experience. You do have to pay a small amount and get a coupon for your chocolate or drink purchase. So  if you are desperate to eat some chocolate  or it's raining heavily outside  or you need quickly some air-conditioning  then give it a try; otherwise  enjoy Jeju's natural scenery and wonders instead.

Incredible work of art it was a great place to visit. The number of pictures were beyond my expectation; need more than 1 hour to see all exhibitions. Need a good camera for good quality. Sometimes need flash to get a brighter picture. ??0000 only.

In Jeju  we had the opportunity to visit the Jeju Art Museum & Glass Castle  which is a theme park featuring an exhibition hall  garden and models made entirely of glass. One must spent at least two hours or more to walk around the indoor and outdoor areas. Nearby the entrance  there is a display ?쏥lass Worldwide??and the countries that produced glass are mentioned here - China  Italy  Czech Republic  Arab and Japan. Once you step indoor  a large glass beanstalk from the fairytale ?쏪ack & the Beanstalk??will greet visitors.The world's largest all-glass labyrinth  glass ball  glass diamond  a glass stonewall  mirror lake and a glass bridge are found in the model parks here. In one part of the outdoor theme park are Cinderella's glass slippers and a glass carriage. One will be held in awe at the marvellous pieces of art  all made entirely out of glass! Truly an eye opening experience!

In five visits to South Korea in four years I have not come across a museum palace or historical building I did not like.They are all well-maintained offer good information in Englishoften have multilingual guides and free tours and are free or cheap to get in.The Jeju National Museum is no exception. Our hotel was about 4km away and we walked to and from there seeing many interesting sights on the way and eating lot of local food.I am an unabashed fan of the curating skills of the Koreans; they do a very good job.Here they provided a great overview from prehistoric to modern times offering interesting exhibits and information.There was also a special exhibition on Canopus a star of great significance to the people who lived here.Entry is free. There are buses from the city and taxi fares are reasonable. We like eating so we need to walk.

I'm traveling with a tour group and I think we stopped by this place because it's close to the O'sulloc Tea Museum. I'm not a fan of glass art and I feel that the glass art shown here were not that amazing.Another thing is that there's a lot of outdoor exhibition  so it is not a good place to visit if it's raining.

If you`re a Zippo lover  this is a must visit spot. Museum locates in the ground floor of a modern seaside building with breathtaking pacific ocean view. There is 2 exhibition halls  one of those displays many special designed zippos in large size  and the other in fact is a zippo shop  you can see and buy different limited edition zippo there and many are designed by local designer.

If you are looking for a cultural experience on Jeju then this is the place for you.  Lots of interesting exhibits all outside. It is a nice peaceful place to visit for the whole family. Needs more interaction with visitors to get 5 stars.

If this place wants to attract more foreign tourists they need to work hard on translating all their activities and signs to common international languages. The 4D show was mediocre. The projection film was in Korean only. The level 2 exhibits was a small area. The storyboard on the wall was all in Korean. We didn't enjoy this place at all. But if you still plan to go check the weather first. Note that you need to pay for the use of telescopes.
I was slightly surprised by the number of exhibits that the museum had.  It kept my tweens very entertained and they enjoyed their time here very much.  Recommended

I was not expecting a lot when I drove into the car park but I was very pleasantly surprised with it visit. It only cost 2000 won entry and I spent about 1.25 hours.Firstly the guide will set up the video for you and it is pretty gruesome with the brutality of war shown. Then you walk through the exhibition area which has good information about the tunnel system and how Jeju was included in Imperial Japan's last stand at the end of the Pacific War plus weapons and memorabilia. All with English explanations. Then you walk up the hill and go into the tunnel system. When you come out you can follow the less used path and go to the top of the hill for good views.  Lastly there is a tank you can climb into just before you leave. Absolutelyrecommended for all ages.
I was hoping to see more exhibits in here. I have been to a couple and this one wasn’t as intriguing. No theatre in this one. No professional photos here either.

I visited this place at night and really enjoyed it. You should definitely have your camera with you and ready to get lots and lots of dirty photos with the sculptures made for you to fit in. It also has a small sex shop and an exhibition. Within the park you will also find a casual gift shop.Fantastic place and definitely a must for couples!

I took my girlfriend here as she absolutely loves all things aquatic  especially shells  and she loves to go diving. A highlight of this museum is that the owner/operator collected all the exhibits herself  from oceans all around the world  and the museum represents literally a lifetime of work and passion for the sea.Taking that into consideration  if you love to dive  and love the sea  this place is simply amazing  my girlfriend was absolutely in awe  snapping picture after picture and commenting on the rarity and difficulty of finding she'll after shell in such amazing condition. The museum was an interesting oddity for myself  and I understand the reviews saying you could go through the whole thin g in 20-30 minutes  but for someone who is truly amazed by seashells  and the sea in general  you could easily spend more than an hour here (we were there somewhere around 2 hours) If you love seashells  an absolute must see  my girlfriend visibly lit up from the minute we walked in   all the way till we were back to our hotel in ?쒖＜??if you're not passionate about the shells  it's still worth a look at only 6$ (6 000?? per person. Some truly amazing art  especially if you consider it all came from the mind  hands  and worldwide dives of one very cool lady.

I personally found the museum to be rather over priced considering the exhibits are teddy bears dressed up as famous people in famous situations over the years. There were some moments which raised a smile but I think this attraction is more suited for children.

I participated in an event focusing on renewable energy and green growth at this superb convention centre. It is modern with meeting rooms upstairs having amazing almost panoramic view of the Jeju coastline. It has large exhibition floor  with large conference rooms on the three floors  but also bilateral meetings rooms that are convenient and centrally located. The catering and banquets were simply exquisite with great Korean cuisine and the banquet room and service were just incredible. I found it very convenient place for participating and networking.
I must to see in Jeju.  Its exhibits are better than the corning's glass factory in New York.Excellent place for picture taking.

I loved this museum so much! The seashells and paintings exhibited at this museum is awesome and seriously beautiful. Everything that you see in and around this museum is so artistic and shows so much of passion in it. The cafe within the vicinity is equally beautiful that offers good coffee and bread too!

I enjoyed touring the tea museum but I was a lil' disappointed because there were only a few exhibits displayed to the public. There is a caf챕. You gotta try their ice-cream. It is heavenly. There is also a store which you can purchase tea related items as souvenirs. This place is definitely worth the hype!

I don?셳 regret going but don?셳 have high expectations. All the rooms/ exhibitions are very differently themed. Some educational some just modern art one room has really good descriptions and English text another has no information in any language at all the next just used google translate and some rooms have lots and lots of educational texts but only in Korean. With that said I still had plenty good laughs saw lots of fun stuff learned some and had a few interesting conversations with my partner. Homosexuality and a few kinks are represented to some degree I wouldn?셳 bring grandma or anyone really you?셱e not perfectly comfortable seeing depictions of... well everything with. I  read about this peace park in Lonely Planet and asked to go there. Our local guide had never visited there before but said he would definitely take people there now. It took us a while to find the right way to go in- lower floor. On the first floor there was a beautiful photo exhibition but the museum is the real attraction. It tells the story of post World War 2 Jeju and  especially about the massacres by different sides of politics. While the museum focuses on Jeju it provides a real insight into the sources of the 1950s Korean war and the division of the country. The USA and its military commanders certainly contributed to the problems and the terrible suffering of the Jeju people.   I highly recommend Westerners to visit this place and the labelling in English is very good.

Having arrived in Jeju eager to see as much as possible in a short time frame - the art work was top on my hit list. I stumbled across the website for the Museum of Contemporary Art and was very excited to go (as there are so many museums to choose from!)I would recommend a whole morning to visit Jeoji as there is more than just this Museum there. The first Gallery I went to showed a lovely exhibiton on the Sound of Nature this gallery was on the left hand side of the road and was a free two floor exhibition. I then walked along the road to the Museum of Contemporary Art on the right. The Museum had 4 big rooms of Art - all of which had a meaningful message behind the artist's work in both Korean and English! The receptionists were very helpful when directing me as to where to go and I finished my self-guided tour with a visit to the Art shop which was outside in the sculpture garden. A lovely morning well spent taking in the delights of Korean art.

Great scenic spot with narrow shelf or rock at the base of cliffs which were part of an old volcano.  We visited on a day of high wind and rough seas and the site was closed as the path was too dangerous.  was able to visit the climate exhibition centre and see the model of the Dutch Ship De Sperwer  wrecked hundreds of years ago.  Also took the walk up the hill to the beacon tower.

Generally a fun and interesting exhibition due to the interactivity of the exhibits/3D photos. However if you are expecting a large variety of interaction you will be slightly disappointed. About halfway through the museum most exhibits start to feel similar. More enjoyable for teenagers-like crowds. Recommend about 1-1.5 hours for the whole museum.
Free entrance.Good display and exhibition.Well arranged. You can see the history of Jeju... And typical display style. Not very big...

Fabulous collection of contemporary art. Interesting installations and sculptures. Worth visiting. Some important artists shown. I love that Sth Korea has really good contemporary art to view. There are also other exhibition spaces included in the ticket. Amazing really.
Excellent place for picture taking. People who loves picture taking will enjoy here. I love the effects of each glass/sculpture/exhibit
Cute museum for families and teddy bear lovers. Two floors of exhibits plus more outside. A fun place for an hour stop over.

Chocolate land  is an interesting place to visit  it is close to Teddy Bear museum  they charge 3000 won for enterance  & give you coupon for the same amount  so when you buy chocolates the amount is deducted. It consists of 2 floors  the lower level has workshop where I saw people experimenting with chocolates  I did not because the did not know english.They have exhibition where chocolates from all parts of the world shown.They have samples on both levels to taste & then decide which flavor to buy. C1 ( 2016.07.13 ) I expected this museum because history and peace was this museum's theme. And I wanted know about Jeju's sad history in detail. C1 ( 2016.07.12 ) I visited there for seeing about Jeju's history but I disappointed. I've visited many museum in Korea and this local museum was small and a few exhibits. The exterior was big size but the exhibits was under my expectation. The staff was kind and the inside was well managed and clean.
Before I went there I expected there were many interesting exhibition for me to explore. Unfortunately there were nothing really surprise me.

Banglimwon is a large exhibition of plants. All the descriptions and signs are written in Korean maybe taking a pleisure walk was a good idea to us. We don’t think the tour guide want either being able to translate some thousands of plant names into Eng lish anyway. However this place is beautiful and worth to visit.

As the Chocolate Land is within 10 minutes??walk from the Teddy Bear Museum in the Jungmun Resort area ??just follow the direction on the sign-posts ??my family and I had no hesitation to visit it on a rainy Sunday.Getting there and fees: First and foremost  you have to note that Chocolate Land is different from Chocolate Museum. Chocolate Land is in the south central part of Jeju while Chocolate Museum is in the south west Jeju. We didn't need the GPS coordinate/code for Chocolate Land but it's 7381197 for anyone who's driving there directly. The entrance fee for adults is 3000 won and 2000 won for children. A voucher was given back for every purchased ticket which can be redeemed at the gift shop or the caf챕 or the Chocolate School.The Museum/Attraction: After going past the ticketing counter  you then turn right. The section on the left is a caf챕 and photograph/selfie stops of different types of Korean houses and benches with toy bears. There's even a figurine of Santa Claus in front of one house  which was interesting considering Christmas is still some 6 months away. The section on the right is the exhibits on the history of chocolates  with the words written only in Korean. We went down the stairways to the level below in which there's a Chocolate School which teaches chocolate making at 120 000 won with lessons starting every hour from 10am to 6pm (I think the children would be more interested than adults). We didn't go into the School; instead  we walked past M&M figurines and a Christmas tree (again interesting) and reached the chocolate shop where there are interesting exhibits of chocolates (behind glass) from America  Europe and Asia. The gift shop has an extensive selection of chocolates (I think slightly more than outside). The prices of the Jeju chocolates of the same brand at the gift shop were slightly more expensive compared to those selling outside Chocolate Land. However  the Chocolate Land chocolates became slightly cheaper than those outside when we utilised the discount vouchers. Unique local Jeju chocolates are those with pink cactus flowers  mandarin oranges and hallabong fillings. We couldn't wait till Christmas?쫤e ate some of the chocolates before we left Jeju  and these were yummy!There is a small observation area (Chocolate Garden) outside the building where the view looks towards the sea. There's also a statue of Willy Wonka from the 1971 movie ?쁗illy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory??where you could take a photograph and selfie with. But we couldn't go outside because it's raining.I recommend visiting the Chocolate Land if you have the time and if you have an appreciation of chocolates. Otherwise  I think you wouldn't miss much if you decide to skip it.

An aquarium with the typical fishes both salt and fresh water. What was interesting was the display of many species of frogs from the marshes. Also very very expensive tickets for a rather small exhibition. Would probably be more worth while if going with children as  there is an experiential exhibition which is kids-friendly.

Let?셲 be honest I didn?셳 have to buy this brand compared to all others available. The tea museum next door is also just a one room exhibition and place for shopping.

Admission to both main and special exhibits are free. The exhibition items and artifacts are well maintained and very informative. Easily accessible by numerous busses. A good place for children as well.

A great place to start off is the Women Divers exhibition center to see the old photos and explanation from the staff on the history of Women Divers. Than a slow walk up the peak for a great view ....  the wind was hallowing when we climb up and the local told us its a normal day ...   plenty of great eateries just a short walk from the entrance after the climb . You will learn the very interesting history of the Haenyeo, the female divers, no equipment, of Jeju. Well organized with good exhibits.

You have to walk on a ramp in order to get into the museum because car cannot drive into the area of exhibitions. The venue is separated into indoor and outdoor. For outdoor exhibitions, you should be aware of the weather. If it rains, the ramp would be slippery, so visitors are recommended to wear water-resistant shoes for unusual events. There are many limited-edition cars and some of them are even the only one in the world. There is also a shop located besides the entry of the museum, selling different car models and peripherals. review: you can skip it unless you really love glasses. the entrance fee is quite pricey for the content. we took quite fast to finish the exhibitions, there's indoors and outdoors, one with a punmpkin like carriage for Cinderella. there's also a park where glasses are scattered around purposefully. I like the quietness of the park rather than finding where are the glasses.

You can reach this place with Jeju tour bus - if you're going to the Roe Deer Observatory as well, I suggest you go there first and then walk downhill to the Peace Park (less than 10 mins). If you do it the other way round, you'll have to trek uphill. The admission for the Peace Park is free and everything is in English. The museum offers a comprehensive account of a controversial point in Korean history: some exhibits are quite chilling and upsetting but I think it's important to understand the history of this island: Jeju is not all about tangerines, erotic statues and kitschy teddy bears.

You can get here from Seogwipo on the 701 bus - costs 3,300 KRW each way and takes about 80 minutes.  After the bus drops you off, turn off one of the streets to the right and keep walking until you find the parking lot and entrance way.  There's a small exhibition before the ticket office, but there's not much in there, lots of photos and a little signage.  There's also a water drinking fountain just outside if you need to fill up.Note there are no garbage bins, so you will need to take all rubbish away with you.  Entrance fee is 2000 KRW.  All well signposted and lots of steps.  It will take about about 20 minutes to walk to the top.  There are lots of places to stop and sit and take photos and there are lookouts at the top for photos in all directions.  When you get to the top, all you can do it look around and come back down again.  You're not able to walk around inside the cone or around the edges.  (so yes we took our picnic back down again).When you walk back down, be sure to go to the small cove on the right hand side where you will see a (FREE) exhibition of women divers.    This happens at 130pm and 3pm.  Five older women divers took to the water, with their full old wetsuits on and 10 minutes later started coming back in with the octupus that they had caught. Only two caught some while we were there and came back out of the water clutching it, straight to the area where they sell the seafood that you can buy and take into the restaurant area to get it cooked for you.It's a pleasant way to spend an hour or so, but its a pain to make a specific trip here from Seogwipo (and longer from Jeju City), so plan something else around it.

Wow! I'm glad I saw this before leaving! Jeju is full of surprises and this is one of them. We were extremely lucky this was a foggy day because seeing this place in fog was really special.  The amazing display of wood carvings etc at the wood exhibition place was amazing as we're all the large insects carved out of cedar wood. It's a 20 min drive from Jeju City. Apparently in summer you have to protect your lunch from the crows! A nice easy walk and an oreum (hill) trail if you want something a bit harder. There are lots of carved statues all along the way and one of those stone paths which you can walk on with your shoes off.  I manage about 2 feet, too hard for me! Haha!

Whilst I'm giving the Teddy Bear Museum just 2 stars for quality, value for money, class of exhibits, and any actual worth as a proper   museum  , I have to admit that my visit made me laugh. I'm not sure though that derisive snorting sarcasm was what they were looking for.This museum is a pile of pants, masquerading as teddy bears.. The   attractions   are about 15 to 20 poor quality adult-human-sized bears, dressed in various outfits of clothing, with a challenge to guess   who   they are dressed as. Military uniform and two medals apparently is enough for a bear to resemble Prince William, for example - and a grey wig and   E=mc2   to represent Einstein.Then there are the bear portraits. Frames containing bears dressed to vaguely resemble famous portraits. Mona Lisa teddy bear, anyone?There's no   history   of the teddy bear, no collection of historical bears, no pictures / video clips of teddy bears being made, no maps showing where different types of teddy bears originated from - nothing educational whatsoever. There are no audio tours, no leaflets or signs to show the visitor around, and certainly no staff available to talk to about any   exhibits  , whether you are Korean, English, American or anything else.The gift shop on the lowest floor contained the largest number of bears - none of them particularly special, all just your usual cheap mass-produced bears, but at slightly hiked up prices.By far the worst part of the visit was the funniest. Your ticket includes entry to the   Elvis Stage Show  . Oh dear Lord, where on earth do I start? The show is on every 15 minutes. In a room with about 12 benches in it. There is a curtain at the far end, hiding the   stage  . On the quarter hour, the announcement is made -   The King of Rock and Roll, Elvis, is in the house!   The curtains open, and there it is. The Elvis Presley Show. Six, sad, lonely looking teddy bears, dressed in stage show outfits, rocking gently on their animatronic sticks. The three backing singers sway gently on the right, the drummer's arms flail up and down towards the drums, the guitarist's arm moves.Elvis meanwhile gyrate and swivels his hips, the crowd goes wild. Oh, no, sorry, that last sentence was a lie. Elvis sways and looks like he almost falls several times.Worst animatronic puppetry in the world. Hilarious. Hilariously BAD. Less than two minutes later, the curtains shut, and   Elvis has left the building   - until the next showing in approximately 12 or 13 minutes' time....Don't go to the Teddy Bear Museum thinking you'll have an interesting visit. Go to see the absolutely bizarre vision that South Koreans have of   entertainment  .

When we arrived at Jeju, we took a taxi to Jejueco and left our luggage with time since check-in time was in the afternoon. From Jejueco we took a cab down to Glass Castle and managed to reach there before 5pm.As its name suggests, the Glass Castle is a glass art theme park that consists of an exhibition hall and garden with everything made out entirely out of glass! All in all, there are 6 themed model parks with over 250 models exhibited: they include the world?s largest glass ball and largest glass diamond, a glass stonewall, a mirror lake, and a glass bridge etc...The exhibition was definitely a breathtaking sight to behold: glass displays made of all kinds of shapes and sizes! We couldn't help but be amazed and ended up taking - pictures of all the art pieces. For more on the experience and photos, please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/glass-castle-jeju.html

Went on a Friday afternoon at the suggestion of our hired taxi driver even though it was not in our planned itinerary as we happened to be in the area for lunch. There was no other visitor in there other then my friend and I. For 9000 won, there are many other attractions in Jeju to see. The place is small and just filled with colourful glass exhibits and decorations... we completed visiting in less than half an hour as it is a very small place.

We weren't planning on visiting this attraction, however wet and windy weather meant that our outdoor plans had to be postponed.Our children really enjoyed the exhibits and we found it interesting too. I would have rated it higher but the front door staff were so rude and unfriendly, it left a bad impression.

We went with high expectation, thinking that we could go into the larva tube. To our utmost disappointment, besides a 4-D movie, It was just a museum with some picture exhibits, and glassed up exhibits of a very small part of the larva tube. Admission was W3,000. It took us a long time to get there, as the bus was a 50 minute wait and it was extremely cold that day.

We went with friends to visit the museam and for all of us it was quite entertaining. Really nice recreation of historial moments and famous personalities   Teddy Bear Style  .Since I am a big fan of k drama Goong / Princess Hours, for me it was a must to visit the Museum and I was not dissapointed at all. There is an specific exhibition of this drama and it is amazing, showing the most memorable scenes as seen on TV and also there is a music video. Loved it.Finally, don't miss   Teddy Bear Elvis Music Show  .

We went to the Teddy Bear Museum only because it was right next door to the Lotte Hotel Jeju where we stayed.  At 10,000 won per adult and 8,000 won per child, it is a bit pricey.  You can be done with all the displays and the 5 minute teddy Elvis show in an hour.  If you like teddy bears then it is a museum for you as there are alot of cute displays and exhibits that memorialize past events in history.  Kinda cool but not my thing.  I enjoyed the outdoor park area more.  You can take pictures with cute bear statues and sit and enjoy the greenery.  There is a cafe that sells Taiwanese pearl drinks and a nice gift shop.

We visited the JAM (Jeju Aerospace Museum) and it was stunning, I love anything connected with planes or space so I was in heaven, the displays are well laid out and there were so many interactive displays for kids too that it shows that there was much thought in the museum.Not only was it about aircraft, but also about Korea's history of astronomy which was so fascinating that I could have spent all afternoon in this one section, Then we went into the space exhibition and again I was stunned at how much South Korea has achieved. We always think of? USA & Russia as being at the forefront, visit the JAM to have your eyes opened.Wonderful.

We stopped here on a whim to go zip lining which was pretty tame but a lovely way to view the green tea fields from above. The guides were good but very minimal English. We stopped and had some green tea ice cream at the cave cafe which is really unique. It's a true cave which gives you a break from the Jeju heat and humidity. The server here spoke English and was really nice even helping people take photos at the cave   photo spot.   We enjoyed the small tea museum too but would have appreciated translations for the exhibits. Overall a fun couple of hours.
address: 제주 제주시 조천읍 선교로 266-4 캐릭파크 내
입력주소: 제주 제주시 조천읍 선교로 266-4 캐릭파크 내

review: We love the story around the Innisfree Jeju House. It's organic and farm to table supply chain and mission is admirable. We had the the diver's special bento and it was delicious. My wife had the blue colored tea ade and I had fresh carrot juice and all of it was great. The have beautiful cakes in the shape of Halla mountain and tiramisu with delicate flower designs. The prices are in the higher end but well worth the refined quality and experience for those who like this sort of thing. My wife loved the purity of the food and calm views of the tea plantation.They also have products for sale as well as a tea extract exhibit. They have fun hands on tea soap making as well you can purchase and do there. Or they have other ones you can purchase and take home to do. Great place to calm down, re-energize, and enjoy.

We had only a metre of visibility when we went, it was cold, rainy and foggy. My review probably doesn’t do it justice, we were just super unlucky that day. Don’t visit on a rainy day. There is however a restaurant with an exhibition on top and there is a restroom too. We didn’t even bother with the walk as it looked gloomy and we couldn’t see much.

We book a tour on line from the cruise ship before we arrived at the port. The tour included a visit to Seongeup Folk Village.  There was an admission fee to the village.  There are several walkways around the village. The walkways are well maintained and there are no steps to climb.  There are exhibits our old building, farming and animals.  There are clean restrooms along the walkways.

Very worthwhile museum to visit on Jeju.  Gives an in depth view into Haenyeo culture, female free divers who gather shell fish.  Since the culture of the Haenyeo is beginning to die out, the museum is an important way to keep the knowledge alive.  Movie and exhibits, with beautiful walks through the village and surrounding farm fields.

Unlike Hello Kitty, I think most of us have cuddled or have in possession a toy teddy bear at a certain stage of our lives. So it is no wonder that the Teddy Bear Museum has such a wide appeal and which surely be included as a ?compulsory? destination on the itinerary of the independent travellers (especially those with children) and tour companies alike.Getting there and fees: We visited Teddy Bear Museum (GPS coordinate/code 7387600) on a rainy day, which was appropriate since the exhibits are predominantly indoor, except for the Teddy Bear Garden and Park where there?re a few teddy bear figurines outside and a park with great views of the sea.  The admission charges are 10,000 won for adults won, 9,000 won for teens and 8,000 won for children.The Museum/Attraction:  This Teddy Bear Museum is the first and largest teddy bear museum in South Korea. Once you enter, you are greeted by this huge teddy bear, who gives you a ?grand? welcome to further explore the five sections spread over 3 levels: The History Hall, The Art Hall and The Project Exhibition Hall, Gift Shop (all indoors) and an outdoor Teddy Bear Garden and Park. There?s also a caf챕/restaurant. Be prepared to spend at least 1 hour looking and taking photographs/selfies at all the interesting exhibits. The History Hall comprised of the history of bear manufacturing and some of the earliest toy bears, many of which are antique and rare. It also showcases milestones in human history, with the bears enacting several famous (human) historical scenes from different eras. This is indeed a refreshing concept for a museum! I particularly liked the teddy bears enacting the Titanic, landings on the moon and the iconic celebrities like the Beatles and Gandhi.In the Art Hall, you could see the world-famous artworks and designs in an art gallery form as well as animation characters beloved by children. I liked the Mona Lisa and two of the most expensive bears in the world - the Louis Vuitton teddy bear and the Diamond Bear. In the Project Exhibition Hall, you would meet teddy bears grouped to suit the theme of each exhibition. Not forgetting the large Gift Shop on the first level. While it offers plenty of gifts, these are nonetheless pricey. Nevertheless, you could take photos with Michael Jackson bear, Steve Jobs bear and a wedding couple bear amongst others. There?s also a mother panda with her baby pandas on display too.  We certainly enjoyed the wonderful experience of the Museum bringing out the child in each of us, and making us feel young again. Despite the pricey entrance fees, I still think the Teddy Bear Museum is worth visiting, and to me, once would be sufficient. But if you don?t like teddy bears at all, then it would be prudent to skip this attraction.

Too much of a tourist trap that has been boasting the same facilities/exhibits for several decades. Would have been more impressive to see a renovation of the space. The gift shop is great but is only accessible if you buy a ticket (adult tickets are 10,000 KRW). May be a better option if you're going with young children.
Too big n all along on yr own,Some exhibits are not well maintained. Video inside seems not working.  Unless you like stone, u may consider to skip and try others
This was worth the entry fee. There is a nice walking tour of the   museum  . It was interesting to see all the glass displays in the forest. We really enjoyed the walk through the exhibits

This was an amazing museum that I thoroughly enjoyed. A theater plays a documentary about the Haenyeo in several languages and the 3 exhibition halls show you how they lived, their equipment and how integral they are to the communities in which they live. The observatory lets you look out at the ocean, where if they are diving you'll be able to see the ladies in action. It's a shame that these amazing women free divers are declining in numbers, so if you get a chance to visit, do. PS There is a free diving school at Hallim (the west side of the island) if you're game.

This was a terrific little museum. Excellent, helpful staff. Fantastic introductory film that they played in English for us, and top class exhibits. We came away with a deep admiration for the women divers of Jeju, they are tough, proud and awesome achievers :)

This was a nice little excursion from the main island. Gotta take a ferry which means you need to head over to Udo early and be prepared to come back in the early evening as the ferry schedule will dictate your movement. There used to be a nice coffee shop halfway up at the base of the stairs to the lighthouse exhibits (October 2013). They had the cutest dog too but they were closed when we went back in December 2013. We took our car on the ferry. But you can also walk onto the ferry and then rent mopeds or four wheelers once you get to Udo so you can get around. I was thankful for the GPS in the car though because the roads are very winding, narrow, confusing, and I don't think are marked with names.

This was a first time visit for us...and we found it to be cheesy with a capital 'C'. However, who would have thought that CHEESY could be so COOL!!!!Yup, we had fun here...the place was amazing. Nature in harmony with recycled glass and plastic. it's very well maintained, good to spend a few hours here taking pictures...as well as soaking in the various exhibits on display. I particularly enjoyed the walk in the Enchanted Forest, a bit creepy though...as it was secluded from the rest of the complex, and this added to the excitement of being in the forest...talk about a vivid imagination!They have a shop selling souvenirs as well, clean restrooms and a cafe. I would recommend those looking for some fun to drop by here, and just let your inner child run free!

This teddy bear museum is one of a few around the world.  Located in Jungmun tourist complex in Jeju, Korea, is this tiny museum for teddy bear fans alike.  For 8000 KRW you have unlimited day access to 3 floors of teddy bear exhibits and the outside grounds.  This museum carries interesting themed bears like the Mona Lisa bear, the Leonardo Da Vinci bear, a Marilyn Monroe bear, and so many others.  Currently they are displaying the Elvis bear.  On the ground floor there is even a really nice restaurant if you get hungry.  Not much choice in  terms of breakfast, they do offer mostly burgers and different types of coffees.  Also there is a gift shop if you are interested in taking home one of the really cute teddy bear souvenirs.Well worth the visit and few hours for both teddy bear fans and those with just a passing interest.  Remember to use the lockers next to the admission counter.  We didn't and carried all our jackets and bags for the entire exhibit,  It will make the visit a whole lot lighter and more fun.  Enjoy!

This place was really unexpected. Through the Yeha Bus tour this was one of the stops and I am glad we visited this place. A lot of mini exhibits with bears dressed up according to the theme and the gift shop is great as well. For teddy bear lovers and lovers of all things cute, we recommend this place.

This place is huge!If you like nature, do visit Jeju Stone Park.  The English audio guide was excellent.  The exhibits were really interesting.  There were indoor and outdoor exhibits.  Do be selective if you have limited time.  One could easily spend up to half a day at this place.As we were a bit short on time, we browsed through the indoor museum rather quickly and still managed to pick up some interesting information.The outdoor areas were really nice and comfortable.  When we were there, the weather was cool and nice and we really had a good time walking around admiring the stones. It is a park that combines nature and art.  We like it a lot.

This museum is one of the attraction at Jungmun Resort. It consists of teddy bear exhibition from several country, the history, the art, life size teddy bear & of course souvenir store. If you're Princess Hours lovers (Kdrama) this place is perfect for you. You can't bring you belonging inside, so placed you belonging into a free locker on the entrance of the museum.

This museum boasts its huge variety of old computer related exhibitions to a new one. You may enjoy the old memories of punch card, MS-DOS, APPLE I~II, to VR, motion recognition, etc. The only point you should consider is entrance fee. I was ok because I can get Jeju resident discount. But most of visitors from outside of Jeju island should try to discount chances such as Naver booking, etc.

This is the best stone exhibit on Jeju island.  And the best part of that is the museum itself.  There are many, many very interesting stones shapes, all collected from Jeju (I think).  If you like geology, there's a great explanation of lava types, stone formations, lava tubes, etc.  Also there is a nice drift-wood display with very unusual, artistic shapes.  Outside, there are many carved stone artifacts used by Jeju islanders from ages past.  The Obaek Jang-Goon Gallery has a nice drift-wood display in the basement.  Park is big, but except for the museums, just a walk-through is enough.  I spent 2 hours in the museums -- the best part!

This is probably the wonderland of 90% of the female population. The place is not huge but if you are going to watch the 3D movie, you have to queue early coz they only have a certain number of 3D glasses. We only have less than 1.5 hours in Hello Kitty Island thus wasn't able to watch the movie. The toilet is cute!! I so love the mirror and of course the cleanliness of the place. Saw a lot of very cute exhibits in the museum. I especially like the bedroom. Wish it was mine. There is a caf챕 on the second floor. The deco is all pink and white. Didn't eat coz we were rushing for time and the snacks aren't really cheap. The gifts are expensive too. I can actually get them cheaper when I'm back in Singapore.

This is an in-door exhibits, with some out-door, but not during winter season. Probably 45-min visit will suffice.The in-doors exhibits were housed in glass, so not good for photo-takings, alot of reflections from the surrounding lightings. Some glass were dusty inside.

This is an excellent museum featuring contemporary art as well as traditional art. The buildings themselves, which were designed by Tadao Ando, were amazing. It was great just walking around inside while perusing the exhibits & or going for a stroll outside. My favorite part was the sculpture garden, which featured 3 pieces. You can go on the rooftop as well to see another sculpture as well as a great view of Jeju. I was also fortunate to have an opportunity to see Yayoi Kusama's Pumpkin & Infinity Mirrored Room. I don't know if it was because I went during off-season, but the museum wasn't crowded at all, so I was able to take my time. I would definitely come back here again if I had a chance

this is a very interesting park, they have at least 3 sections; a museum, 2 parks and smaller exhibits. If you like stones and interested in how they are formed and how they look like and appreciate by the people of the past and present, do visit. some stones have interesting tales like: Goddess and her 500 Sons. The whole park is pretty big, it can take up to more than 3 hours if you go through all the writings and descriptions. do go after a meal.

This is a lovely spot to visit. You can wander around the artists village enjoy the outdoor sculptures (kids will like the brightly coloured animals near the art shop/cafe) and then have a good look at the exhibitions inside.  There is a permanent one and a temporary one. The temporary one at present is about marine plastics and pollution. The work was really good especially the video work and created   man   by a young female Korean artist. Most impressive.The last Wednesday of the month entry is free but it's only 2000 won anyway I think. They have an English brochure and the lady at reception was very pleasant.

This is a glass art theme park featuring an exhibition hall, garden and models all made entirely out of glass. These are six themed model parks jn which over 250 models are exhibited. These include glass qrt masterpieces by international famous artist from Italy, the Czech Republic, Japan and more.At least one hour explore the entire exhibitation garden. Visit at night as the place is well litted and less tourist.

This is a fun place to stop and spend about a half hour or so.  The road in this section appears to defy gravity.  Not sure of the reason why, but is very interesting to see the car go backwards while facing downhill.  There are some interesting exhibits and statues, along with shops, nearby.

This attraction would be hard to describe. A huge park with magnificent exhibits of boulders and rocks. The park was so silent but the exhibits made their statements loud and clear.  An enjoyable afternoon just to immerse in the natural beauty of something as common as rocks, pebbles and such. Who would have imagined that such an outdoor exhibit could offer so much. There?s even a mothers? nursing room within the park itself.

There were bears of every color and design imaginable: there was an Elvis bear, Marilyn bear, Mona Lisa bear, Chinese bears, countryside bears and even Goong (the Korean drama) bears! It really was a bear wonderland. The only problem was that the commentary was all in Korean, it would have been better if there was English translation as well. The other problem was that most of the exhibits were housed in glass cases which made taking photos challenging as the reflections were very prominent. Besides viewing the bears, there is an in-store souvenir shop that has all sorts of bear items (e.g. keychains, stuffed bears, bags etc...). But if you love bears, than it should be worth a visit.For more on my experience and photos, please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/03/an-impromptu-visit-to-teddy-bear-museum.html

There is a secret bunker at on Jeju Island, which once housed old national communication facility and had remained unknown to the public for a long time. This large structure is covered with soil and trees, thus disguised to look like a mountain. This old national facility will be reborn as “Bunker de Lumieres”, a media art exhibition hall that will become Jeju's new landmark for culture and art.

There are some fictional characters that you and me adore and love during our childhood and yet still relish even though we have become adults. Hello Kitty is certainly one of them, and is a favourite of one of my children. However, the good part is not every visitor to Jeju and the locals are a fan of Hello Kitty, so the Hello Kitty Island Museum is not on the itinerary of most tour companies, and hence it?s not crowded.Getting there and fees: Hello Kitty Island Museum, opened in late 2013, is located in the south west part of Jeju (GPS code/coordinate 7926114).  Not to worry if you cannot find space in the small open-air car park outside the Museum because there?s another huge open air car park below the small one. Parking is free. Entrance fee to the Museum is 12,000 won for adult, 11,000 won for teenagers and 10,000Won for children. However, my family and I made use of the discount coupon for entrance fees from the Hertz car rental discount booklet.The Museum/Attraction: when we entered, we were immediately greeted by a large hall where there?s a circular cone of Hello Kitty toys, a photo-taking stop with the entire Hello Kitty family and Hello Kitty?s house where she?s standing at the balcony welcoming you and beckoning you to enter the door into the various exhibition halls. There are 3 levels with the exhibition halls on the first and second level, the gift shop on the first level, the Hello Kitty Caf챕 on the second level and the 3D theatre and an outdoor gallery on the third level. To cover everything, including a meal at the Hello Kitty Caf챕, would easily take about 2-3 hours. In the true sense, this Hello Kitty Museum is a museum ? there are exhibits of anything related to the adorable Hello Kitty. There are several themed exhibition halls on the first and second level e.g. History Hall, Art Education Hall, Music Education Hall, World Gallery Hall, Hello Kitty Room, Constellation Education Hall, amongst others.So we took plenty of photographs and selfies. I particularly like the exhibit of Hello Kitty represented by 26 countries (I found my own country) as well as the huge room containing the huge Hello Kitty bed where one of my children got the Hello Kitty toy snatched away by a toddler.At the Hello Kitty Caf챕 ? with Hello Kitty ribbon windows, Hello Kitty-themed sofas and Hello Kitty engraved tables ? you have to try the Hello Kitty Waffle Set, green tea latte, coffee or  hot chocolate (the 3 hot drinks have a profile of Hello Kitty on the surface), Hello Kitty Strawberry Cake and Cheesecake. Really yummy stuff!Whether you are a fan or not of Hello Kitty, I think this Museum is a fun attraction to visit and be acquainted with Hello Kitty. However, be prepared to ?share? the premises with many joyful and lively children and teenagers. But if you are not a fan and if you have limited time in Jeju, then I suppose you could spend that 2-3 hours elsewhere.

There are outdoor and indoor exhibits of glass sculptures and trinkets. There's a princessy area with giant diamond rings, a Cinderella glass carriage, showcase of glass slippers, etc. The girls liked this place. The adults found it boring. And overall, the place feels dated. Go only if you have young girls who might like the pretty glass exhibits.
There are a few places great for pics. although i should remind you that most of its exhibitions are in an open area like a park, so if you go here when the temperature is rather low, it is coldddd.

There are a few attractions within the same area. The teddy bear museum has 3 floors,with teddy bear exhibits and also it's history. There where some with themes and also resembles idols and famous people  and some that moves. There is also an elvis show with teddy bear on level 2 theatre. The outdoor photo taking area has a few exhibits too.

There are 2 major teddy bear themed attractions in Jeju, One is the Teddy Bear Museum and the other is Jeju Teseum. The Teddy Bear Museum is for mohair connoisseurs, but the bears there are all boxed up in glass exhibits. That is why given the limited amount of time we had in Jeju, we chose to visit Teseum. There are a lot of photo opportunities where we and especially our kids can pose with the many cuddly large-sized teddys at Teseum. The keyword here is interaction.

The weather was raining on the day I decided to do sightseeing on Jeju, so I was left with only a visit to the botanical gardens. You can reach it from the airport limousine bus route and behind the fast food shops near SK Energy shop.Luckily the garden exhibition was under glass roof, so it provided a good informative shelter from the rain.The botanical gardens are organised into themes, eg. Aquatic garden, cactus garden, etc. I guess this eliminates confusion for tourists and displays the plants in an educational fashion too. On a sunny day, there is more to do on the outside.There is a curio shop inside the gardens for some gifts but I did not see a coffee shop at the attraction.It will be educational for the kids!

The title summed it all up. Unlike a theme park, there is no ride here. there is only exhibition halls for you to look at. Don't expect much from it and you'll be okay. This was all a bit boring. There are too many people and it seems kind of noisy with the chatters.

The teddy bear museum is exactly what it's title states.  It's teddy bears in every shape and size.  The first area has historical teddy bears, dating back as far as the turn of the century (1900's).  The second section is works of art redone with teddy bears and finally, there is an outdoor exhibit including a 9 meter tall teddy bear that makes a showing every hour on the hour.  Young kids that like teddy bears and such will have a great time visiting here.  My daughter adored everything.  It is a little pricey, but if you rent a car to get around they often give you a book with coupons for the various attractions on the island or you can book in advance online at a discount price.

The Teddy Bear Museum is a pleasant surprise. The museum is very close to The Lotte Hotel and just across the street from Ripley?s Believe it or Not in Jungmun.  The exterior is nice. I wonder if the Louvre Museum was an inspiration for the conical architectural design of the museum.  The exhibitions consisted of many famous pictures and major events in human history. The difference is that in this museum, the teddy bears have taken over. So you will see Teddy Bear versions of Neil Armstrong on the moon, Michael Jordan dunking a basket ball, Elvis Presley rocking a guitar, Psy showing us Gangnam Style, and Marilyn Monroe, etc.  It is interesting, cute and amusing.  I am really glad I visited this museum and you should visit it too even if it is just for the laughs. It is adorable.

The Peace Park is very spacious and beautifully laid out.  (Shouldn't compare but it reminded us of  a smaller version of the National Memorial Arboretum in Staffordshire, UK.)  They were still working on some landscaping while we were there.   We were lucky enough to catch the excellent art exhibition that is on at the moment and the museum display is very well laid out and informative - lots of English  so we learnt a lot about the Jeju's history around 1948.   We were there about 1.5 hours but could have stayed longer.

The park is a great snapshot of what the island has to offer.  The gardens highlight a number of different plant species as well as shelter the lava tube which is both breathtaking and refreshing is the weather outside is toasty hot.  There are bonsai exhibits, traditional korean village exhibitions and even an aviary.  Very neat and pleasant way to spend an afternoon.

The museum has a vast collection of very cute and adorable exotic bears. Bears made to look like Van Gogh, Steve Jobs and even Michael Jackson. Entrance fee is reasonable and includes both the indoor and the outdoor portions of the museum. Outdoor has limited exhibits.
The kids enjoyed this place, lots for them to see and do.? Although, for smaller children some exhibits are a bit gruesome and scary. The shrunken heads were a fascination for them.

The history facts in this memorial hall recalled me of the one in Oswiecim, Poland... This memorial hall will help you to understand Jeju people's local history. Whenever I visit war related museum or places, we should stop fighting for nothing but losing the precious lives. I was even cried when I read 2 young men who could not enter the military school due to the wrong record of this tragic incident. I read all of explanation in Korean and English. I skipped some clips but I tried to watch 2 or 3 min's clips. Very well prepared in English and Korean. One of best museum. It is FREE. Only I concerned, there is no chairs to take a rest from time to time. And there was a decent with 15ish people, her voice was too much loud to make big echo in the hall area! I think they have to pay attention with other visitors who look into all scripts! I was a bit mad because she was too passionate to proceed her job. I think you do not need a docent because all of exhibits are perfectly translated in English. I feel very sorry for all deceased, and their family members who survived at the same time witnesses. I strongly recommend this museum if you are interested local history, and history buff. It is a must. In fact, there is no restaurant, there is a coffee shop only. If you rent a car, within 10 min's drive, there are some. The bus #343, or #344 go to 4.3 Peace Park. From this park, Jeju Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest is 5 min's drive away, and 20 min's walk on foot. This Forest is wonderful. I recommend to combine these 2 places to visit at once. The exhibits were pretty interesting actually but as mentioned in the title, it's a mainly outdoor venue! The glass sculptures look better in the day time or at night when the lights are on.. SO..! If the weather is not helpful, save it for another day! It's pretty far out, so if u are gonna go, do the O'sulluc tea museum and this together... Don't leave too late coz it's terribly difficult to get a cab, unless you have a pre-arranged driver. That said, the staff there really are very, very nice.. We were actually the last few patrons out and we were stranded without a cab, in the bloody freezing rain.. We had 3 ahjussis trying to help us call cabs and eventually one of em offered to drive us to the nearest bus stop instead coz no one was responding, and FYI the nearest bus stop is abt 10mins out too..

The collection of teddy bears is good and very nicely organized according to themes. I especially loved the collections of very old teddy bears and the stories behind them and their owners that really touched a soft spot in my heart. There were also very vintage Winnie the Pooh bears that were really an eye-opener, as well as bears wearing traditional korean costumes depicting scenes of ancient korean life that I liked. The outdoors section of the exhibits were however not very impressive and when my friend and I visited the museum in June, the museum was very warm indoors. We were sweating profusely as we looked at the exhibits and in fact found it a joy to go outdoors into the sun, which turned out to be cooler. This prevented me from giving the attraction a four star rating. However, the collection is really a must-see for teddy bear lovers and it will undoubtedly be a more enjoyable place to visit in other months of the year.

It was cute and a not so serious approach that would cater to the children.The museum consists of 2 Exhibition halls namely the hall of history and the hall of art.  This museum serves as the home for as many as 1,500 bears that includes the luxurious Louis Vuitton bear.

Sounds odd that it is actually my favourite attraction.. I love teddy bears. This place does not require much trekking like the sunrise peak, manjanggul cave, waterfall etc but it is a fantastic place to spend one or two hours just staring at the teddy bear exhibits with some even moving and each exhibit with a different theme. You get to see Elvis teddy bear performing   live   with his friends too. First time seeing teddy bear moving, wow experience for me. The souvenir shop is expensive though... nonetheless do give it a visit if you are a teddy lover! There is a Steve Jobs teddy, Einstein Teddy, quite creative and a twist to the usual brooding teddy we see.

Really really likes teddy bears a lot, so previously when friends go to Korea I will definitely get tagged in their teddy bear museum photos. But actually going there is quite a disappointment. Place for everyone - Solo, couple or with family.Garden has multiple theme garden build in. Botany students can spend days. Best one is Bonsai garden. There is exhibition on garden formation with pictures but everything is in Korean. Overall a clean, well laid-out museum at a very reasonable price at 9,000won each for adults.- Not as many exhibits as we’ve seen at the Smithsonian in DC or Naval Aviation Museum in Pensacola but still worth the visit to learn about Korea’s aviation history- Placards translated into multiple languages - Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese. - We don’t have kids but it seemed there were a large number of child friendly play and exhibit areas.- On the third floor was a go-cart type racing track and pizza cafe. It was about 30,000won a person so we didn’t try it but it looked cool.- From the 4F observatory you can see Hallasan Mt, the tea fields of O’Sulloc, and Shinwha Theme And Water Parks.We spent about an hour there in total.
Outstanding art gallery, with excellent exhibitions and buildings, nice cafe, an absolute must during your stay in Jeju!

O'Sulloc Tea Museum is a small building set in a tea farm. It's a well designed lovely space with a display area about the history of tea and an exhibit wall of teacups and pots a shop where you can try some tea (only one kind though) and a restaurant featuring green tea beverages and sweets. You can also walk around outside there is a garden area in and around the building and also small rows of tea bushes just outside. There's no admission fee and it's not so much of a museum as a commercial venue for selling O'Sulloc products although items can be pricey for the budget traveller. I visited O'Sulloc with a few other backpackers (5 foreigners 1 Korean) and we all had a terrible experience of their customer service. The staff were sour faced and gave us the impression that we were not welcomed glaring at us and tidying their display in a huff when we looked at the product samples (these are samples ok - they're meant to be touched and looked at!). The staff at the counter literally sneered in disdain at my Korean travel companion when he tried to make friendly small talk while we were purchasing our items. This was the worst experience I've had in my 3 weeks in Korea. All the other customer service staff I've encountered in Korea were either very polite and lovely or just neutral. I'm writing in formally to the management about this so hopefully by the time other TripAdvisor members visit they would have improved.In spite of that I did enjoy my visit (no point letting the staff spoil it) but I would recommend coming here only if you've done all your   must-do's   in Jeju or on a rainy day.

On entering through the entrance, one comes to the palm tree avenue. Different types of palm trees and cactuses greet you.  Next up is the wild grass and flowers garden. Felt relax walking along the path. Further ahead  are the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves. These 2 caves were formed by an eruption of Mt Halla many years ago. The temperature inside the caves is around 18 degrees celsius throughout the year so walking inside was cooling. Look out for the famed natural monuments, Pillar, Mother , the two dragons up on the roof, stalactites and stalagmites, and Dr. Jin and the fox girl.. Coming out to the cave,Jeju stones greet you gesturing Welcome . Next proceed to Jae-am folk village where one can see thatched  roof houses with stone walls. Do take a photo with the tall statue of Stone Grandfather, Dolharubang.  Next  will be the bird garden where you will see parrots, pheasants, ostriches and elegant peacocks walking around spreading their colourful stunning feathers. The following spot is Jae-am stone exhibit hall  where over 200 stones are displayed. We were amazed by the natural stone sculptures in the shape of  birds and waterfall. Walking on , following the signs, one comes to water garden where you can see 5 beautiful ponds, capped by the grand waterfall.. Finally you will reach the last section, subtropical botanic garden where  there are palm trees, foliage plants, herbs  alongside parrots, lizards, snakes and tortoises. After all the walking and photo taking, proceed to have lunch at Dolharubang restaurant  to try Jeju's traditional foods, like the delicious pork bulgogi. Or you can have freshly made seafood at Palm  Tree Restaurant. Or if you do not wish to lunch, you can enjoy fresh herb beverages at  Herb Cafe.

review: My family and I visited this UNESCO World Heritage and South Korea National Monument cave on a late afternoon for 2 hours. There were not many visitors and we didn?t find any tour buses when we reached here.   Getting there & fees: Manjanggul Cave is located in the north western part of Jeju-do. To get (drive) to Manjanggul Cave, key in GPS coordinate 7834818. There is no parking fee at the huge car park. Entrance fee is 2,000 won for adults and 1,000 won for teenagers and children.Manjanggul Cave Museum: Upon climbing up the stairs from the car park, you will reach the Museum and a cafeteria/restaurant on its right. You could go in and have a look at the interesting exhibits, including how the Manjanggul Cave was formed from the volcanic activities.Manjanggul Cave: To get to the underground Cave, we followed the sign-posts ? it?s within 5 minutes? walk from the Manjanggul Cave Museum. Trek the entire 1 km stretch that?s opened to public and you will end with a colourful lit lava column - created from the dripping of lava from a hole in the ceiling ? which at about 8 meters high, is the tallest lava column on Earth. Nevertheless, there are a few things you have to take note while you are in the Cave:(1) The entrance to the Manjanggul Cave is also the exit ? there?s no exit at the end of the 1 km trail, which means you are walking 2 km return (2) Make sure you bring and wear a jacket or sweater with you because it?s freezing cold and chilly inside the cave. (3) Wear a cap or the jacket or sweater can be waterproof because you get water ocassioanlly dripping from the cave top onto you (4) The surface (floor) of the Cave is full of solidified lava flow terrain (i.e. extremely uneven surface) and water puddles, so you have to wear a pair of good walking shoes and walk carefully. Hold on to the railings of the stairs.(5) You probably don?t need a torchlight because the Cave is illuminated just enough by ground lightings. Some parts of the cave even have colourful lights shining at the dome shaped ceiling (cupola) (6) If you would like to take photographs inside the cave, you would need a tripod and switch to manual mode for long exposure (I used 4 seconds to 10 seconds exposure on my digital SLR).   There are displays at certain parts of the cave in English explaining the geology of the cave and the formation of the interesting structures (e.g. stalactites). In particular, there?s one structure ? ?Stone Turtle? ? in which the shape looks like Jeju-do Island, and which you could reach in about 30 minutes of one-way walking as it?s about 400m from the entrance. Along the Manjanggul Cave wall, we saw varied patterns of lava flow lines, some are straight while some are wavy. Really interesting! I have been to over 10 limestone caves around the world, but this is my first visit in a lava tunnel cave or lava tube cave (and Asia?s longest lava tube cave for that matter). You have to experience being transported to another world in this ?out of this world? cave for yourself ? don?t miss it!

My daughter and I went to this place because my daughter very fond of Hello Kitty. The exhibition room quite good, but we really disappointed when we saw the park on the rooftop... It was not much to see and the Hello Kitty statue at the center of this park very dirty. Ticket price for this place quite high either.

Meet them, watch them and read about them here, at their own museum( which even has electric car charging points) Given there are so many museum to celebrate the dead and gone, this one for the living, is special with moving exhibits

Located next to   Loveland   this museum is small modern place with beautiful outdoor features such as a reflecting pool sculptures and a small surrounding forest. There was a little bit of everything from an exhibit about a famous national artist who lived for decades on Jeju to an interesting video and poetry collaboration of Korean rappers talking about social issues. The upstairs is currently showcasing drawings and sculptures made by Korean schoolchildren in a surprisingly cheeky cheerful exhibit. Much of the museum was in English but others were only in Korean. The price of admission was only 1000 won well worth it for the experience. There were several pieces that didn't wow me and some outdoor floorboards that need repairs but all in all this is a nice little museum. Make sure to drop by the cafe on the way out for a lovely view of the reflecting pool outside as you sip your coffee!

Located in the Jungmun Resort in Jeju, near some restaurants there. The palce is quite large, consisting of 12 galleries. They showed interesting exhibits collected by Ripley at reasonable price (10k won per person). Worth visiting if you want to have some indoor activity in Jeju.

Let's first get this out of the way: If you're not a teddy bear fan, if you're an over-serious person, or basically, if you had a fun-less childhood, don't bother visiting this place. Because then it would be pretty much a tourist ripoff kind of place, with nothing really worth seeing.But, if you do like bears, and regardless of how cheesy or a ripoff this place can be, you just want to have some fun, then by all means, check it out!Admittedly, I quite like teddy bears myself, and right from the moment I stepped in, I was constantly tickled by all the teddy bears modeled in the form of famous people, famous artworks, and even historical events. It can be sometimes strange to see the head of a bear in the place of what should've been a human one, but toss the strangeness aside and you'll realize there is so much to see and chuckle over. Having teddy bears in place of humans in the exhibits add a touch of innocent cuteness to everything.Do note that there's both an indoor and outdoor exhibit, so if you're on a schedule yet really want to see everything, make sure you plan your time well!

Korean women divers are called haenyeo. They dive in the ocean without any special tools to gather abalone, clams or seaweed. Wearing a lead weighted  vested and goggles, they plunge into 20 meter depths and stay underwater holding their breaths for two to three minutes.  Once they come up to the surface, they make a whistling sound, which is their unique way of breathing out carbon dioxide and breathing in fresh oxygen. The museum is in a four story building and housed many exhibits.  Gallery 1 on the first floor depicts the haenyeo's way of life. On the second floor at Gallery 2, you can see haenyeo's working life.  On the third floor at the observation area you can get a view overlooking the sea.  Gallery 3 displays exhibits of the sea around Jeju.  Outside the museum there is a lawn with statues, including one honoring the haenyeo. You can also admire the architecture of the museum. Further down, we chanced upon the haenyeo who were starting their show by singing a song. We were indeed lucky on that Tuesday afternoon as we managed to watch the show which started at 1.30.
Kids will love this museum but lesser for adults. There's around 3 levels of exhibition, but you can view them all pretty quick.
Jeju Stone Park is interesting. There are lots of great spots for photos and there are also lots of stone exhibits which infuses some aspects of history, culture and art.

Jeju Stone Park exceeded our expectations.  So much space and everything well laid out.  The museum was particularly interesting with some absolutely amazing pieces of lava, and microscopes set-up, which my 9-year old Daughter loved.  They also had an interesting photography exhibition (temporary).  If you are a geologist and/or simply interested in volcanoes and rocks, then you will probably spend all day here.  Appreciated the water machines everywhere but the restaurant was closed (just in case you are hungry).  We all enjoyed it immensely.  Children less than 12 are free and adults are KRW 5000 (very reasonable).

Jeju Hallim Park is a field of frontier spirit of a man who transformed a wasteland to a green paradise. Consisting nine different theme gardens and seasonal festivals, Hallim park is an international tourist attraction of Jeju island, South Korea exhibiting global species of plants and animals. It is 80 acre big and has nearly 1.2 million visitors every year. Visitor can also enjoy Jeju's traditional cuisine in our restaurants. (Gardens) 1. Subtropical botanic garden 2. Palm tree avenue 3. Wild grass and flower garden 4. Hyeopjae and Ssangyong cave 5. Jeju stone and bonsai garden 6. Jae-am folk village 7. Bird garden 8. Jeju stone exhibit hall 9. Water garden (Seasonal Festivals) Jan. - Daffodil Feb. - Ume flower Mar. - Tulip Apr. - Cherry blossoms May - Wild flower Jun. - Hydrangea Jul. thru Sep. - Water lily and lotus Oct. - Pumpkin Nov. - Chrysanthemum Dec. - Camelia (Restaurants and Cafe) - Palm tree restaurant - Dolharubang restaurant - Herb cafe

Jeju Glass Castle is a glass art theme park featuring an exhibition hall,garden and models all made entirely out of glass. These includes glass art masterpieces by international famous artists from Italy,The Czech Republic,Japan and many more. This theme park suitable for all ages. Very cold due to winter season,do put on more wear as you need to walk round the outdoor.

I've been very interested in the haenyeo ever since I first visited Jeju-do. This museum has some interesting exhibitions about the life and work of the haenyeo. Admission is very cheap, a bit over 1000 won for an adult. It's recommended to watch the short documentary about the haenyeo before visiting the exhibitions, to get the most out of your visit. It plays near the lobby. There's a gift shop on site with haenyeo-related items.
It's a showcase of animal dolls. The exhibit was made to look like a zoo with stuffed animals. It was boring for me though, but my daughter like it.

It's a mixed review.  The ticket price is 10,000KRW per adult and since other natural attractions are around 2,000KRW, this park should be well worth it.  Highs: The caves are really cool as well as the Bansai and Stone Garden. The park is easy to walk and has shops and toilets easily available.  Transportation is also easy as it's just the 702 bus from the Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal for 1 hour. Lows: The park is dated, like late 90s with its signage and information cards.  The bird exhibit, stone exhibit and flower garden are average at best.  While the park trail is easy to walk, you do walk through gift shops for the next exhibits (so a bit too tourist-y). Overall, it makes for a decent easy afternoon, especially with kids or elderly.  The park needs some updating to be worth the ticket price, but it is close to the beach (just 5 mins walking).

It's a large building but light on exhibits, or maybe it just seems that way with so much open space. Several historical and current type aircraft, mostly military, and several interactive exhibits for kids. Nice digital movies and a flight simulator section for kids and adults!

It wouldn't usually be my first choice to visit on an island filled with so many views but it was a rainy day so it seemed reasonable. Wasn't disappointed. The indoor exhibition is well arranged and themed: there was jungle, desert, and other sections. You can climb to the last floor of the tower in the middle for a nice view of the area. Can't go wrong in any way if you stop by. Didn't see the outdoor gardens since it was pouring rain but wasnt disappointed even with the indoor one alone

It was such a pain to get to but I loved the Stone Park. The main reason was to see the Dol hareubangs - the stone sculptures which represent Jeju. There was information about the mythology surrounding the formation of Jeju which was at times mind-boggling and contradictory. There are different routes around the park and there is an indoor exhibition which features the volcanic rocks and Jeju's origins as a volcanic island. I preferred the outdoor sections where the use of stone in Jeju was highlighted - used in things such as tombs/ shrines, walls, icons of spiritual beliefs etc. The largest sculptures are near the exit and the Dol hareubangs were awesome. They all had slightly different expressions and quirks which was cool. There are plans to expand the museum grounds and I would defo like to go back again in future. It was quite quiet when we were there and we only saw a few people except for a group on a guided tour at the end. Such a shame there are not more visitors but good for those who made the effort. Recommended visit in Jeju!

It was interesting how they recreated real-life historical events and famous works of art with teddy bears.  There are two main exhibit halls.   Of course there is a gift shop where you can purchase teddy bears.  My wife and I enjoyed it and took lots of pictures.  I think you will enjoy this place, even if you don't have a thing for teddy bears. Bonus:  there is a really nice Starbucks right across the street.

It is no wonder why Spirited Garden is one of the top-rated tourist attractions on Jeju Island. I found it one of the best garden I have visited so far. It is basically a Bonsai tree-themed Garden decorated with many waterfalls and beautiful ponds full of colorful koi carps. Hundreds of artistic bonsai trees can be seen planted on small to large flower pots and on the ground. The bonsai trees of fruits, especially Jeju mandarin (or orange), apples are very impressive. It has seven small gardens with beautiful exotic gates, one of which is called Secret Garden and exclusively use for national and international MICE events (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions). It appears that the garden is very famous in China and other neighboring countries. The information boards show that the garden has been visited by many honored public figures notably former premiers of China, Japan, Indonesia, and others. Also, the garden has been awarded many decorations such as ?KOREA Unique Venue?, ?Green MICE Venue?, etc.

is kind of pricey. there are only 2 levels of bears being exhibits and it is all behind the glass. The bears are just being display in different themes and costumes. we were impressed at the beginning but started to get bored a moment later. Overall, it is still worth a visit.

Innisfree Jeju House can be got to by taking a bus to the O'Sulloc tea museum stop. The tea museum is a very short walk away from Innisfree Jeju House.The place is quiet and peaceful, save for the calming music they play and the chatter of tourists and other visitors, but that wasn't too bad when I was there. There's an area devoted to DIY lessons/sessions where one can try making their own soap. There's a few pretty exhibits where one can smell various scents or read a little about the Innisfree brand and its products. There's a store area, with a few products that are exclusive to Innisfree Jeju House. And there's a cafe with various light food, drink and dessert options.Outside, there are tables and benches that overlook a nice view of the tea plantation, which you can go and take pictures in. Rows upon rows of tea leaves and a few windmills. It's all very pretty and is probably the biggest selling point of the whole compound containing both Innisfree Jeju House and the nearby tea museum. Note: I had to present my cert card.I was taken to a back area above the large exhibit where I was given a 5/7 wetsuit (the water was a little chilly) Meres booties a weight belt and weights mask regulator ScubaPro fins and BCD.There was a shower room for women with two open shower stalls. They do not allow you to wear anything under your wetsuit. I was given a small basket to store my clothes but it was difficult to keep them totally dry. I recommend giving them to someone or renting a locker out in the lobby for delicate items. After donning all my gear I got to check out the fish   hospital   above the aquarium where sick fish are kept separate until they are healthier. There was even a sea turtle!Each guest diver was assigned a guide but mine let me wander freely once he observed I could dive. There was only one other guest in the tank so that was nice. Otherwise it was just me and LOTS of sea life. In the tank there were lots of sharks: black tip nurse leopard small hammerheads. There were lots of large sting rays and schools of fish too. It was fun to interact with the guests too! I'd swim up to the glass and wave at the kids.
