The exhibits were very well done there was lots of food to eat while wondering around and great picture taking opportunities. Apparently they had two a few years ago but one died and they released the other one so they are no longer there.

Back in the days of yore --  how far back, no one can be certain --  three demigods came forth from three holes in the ground located near the northern coast of an island to the south of Korea.  These three demigods lived as hunter-gatherers until a ship arrived bearing three princesses, domesticated farm animals and seeds for growing grain. The princesses married with the demigods, and the Tamna Kingdom was born. Today, we know Tamna, which ended in 1404 with the coming of the Joseon Kings -- Korea's last imperial dynasty -- as Jejudo or Jeju Island.  We know that beloved and mystical site as Samseonghyeol (  sam   means three in Korean). It is a special place and, particularly for history buffs, a   must-see   in Jeju.  The holes, which likely were once active thermal vents on this volcanic isle, are surrounded by a protective Stonehenge-like ring and a mini-forest/park of lush and majestic, mature trees and flowers.  It is quite pleasant, and on a warm summer's day, a cool respite from the city that has grown around it.  There's a small museum showing a film about the founding of Tamna.  The film is in Korean, but if you look at the exhibits there before watching the film, you will understand it much better.  It is not readily possible to actually photograph the holes unless you have a ladder, a drone, a long selfie stick or happen to be about 8 feet tall...this would be my one disappointment about the site.  But there is an official photo mounted nearby.  If you have the time, plan to spend 1-1.5 hours there, to take in the walking trails, museum, movie and various historic buildings.  You will also be greeted by some of the original 18th century dolhareubangs (protective   stone grandfathers  ) remaining on the island.  It's a good outing for singles, couples, friends and families.  Even young children can enjoy the birds, flowers, stones and many benches located throughout the park.  Admission is quite nominal...2,500 KRW adults, 1,700 teens; 1,000 children 7-12.

As a big Hello Kitty fan, I was excited to visit Hello Kitty Island after hearing about it. Although the museum was quite fun, it was pretty run down with many of the exhibits being kind of dirty. The cafe in particular was not on par with the Hello Kitty cafes in Seoul. At those cafes, the cakes and drinks are very fresh but at Hello Kitty Island the cake we ordered tasted (and looked!) like it had been left on the shelf for a while. Similarly the gift shop didn't stock great souvenirs. Considering the price you pay to get in, I would have expected a bit more from this place. If you're a big Hello Kitty fan, I suggest one of the themed places in Seoul.

Appreciate the effort put in to do up the various exhibits. The fact that they were in closed exhibits surely help the maintenance of the whole place coz comparatively, the Teddy Bear Teseum/Safari was more run down.

An exhibit which tells you about the life of the women divers of Jeju.  Explains to you their gear, their daily life, their history and their future as a dying trade.  Small compound without any eatery or canteen.  Parking is free.  However, food (mainly seafood) can be found at a nearby wet market to the east of the exhibition.  Driving takes only about 5 mins.

Admission costs KRW 8,000. Unfortunately, the museum fell short of my expectations. Not conducive for photo taking and has 2 floors of teddy bear exhibits which I personally expected the museum to hold much more collection of teddy bears. Great for kids, not a must visit for adults unless you're a teddy bear lover.

A great museum well set out, very informative. Theres a short film, in English or Korean. Then a self directed tour of museum. Exhibits are well laid out with English translations. I would love to have had a translation of the interviews with the Haenyeo   women of the sea  . There is also a Haenyeo trail from the museum, taking in some of the traditional places the women divers used including the Bulteoks. You would need quite a lot of time to do both museum, park, and trail.

A great museum that is easily accessible.  A bus stop is located a block from the museum.  The ticket price is 1,100KRW during time of visit and well worth it.  The front desk also showed a special screening for me of the information video.  The exhibit is brilliant - informative, visual and interactive.  There's a observatory that oversees the water and the Sehwa area and a play area for small children.

A great museum in Jeju with all its collection of computers and video games. Pay around 8 USD and we can enjoy this museum along with playable exhibitions.Not only we can go back in time with old videogames and computers, we can even try to play the latest videogames (Xbox, Playstation etc) and just forget the time while you are inside!Basement is worth to visit if you really want to spend your day playing games.. quite a varsity of collection.Don't forget to try ordering the keyboard waffle... ^^

10,000 KRW per person. When you enter, pay for admission, and start in third floor, go down floors in order. In the basement, theres gift shop, cafe, and theres few more exhibits to see. Perfect for kids, fun for adults. Wish there could be more exhibitions of teddy bears. But if was nice!

World heritage Site. 13km long lava tube under Jeju Island. Formed by successive eruptions. The section that can be visited is about 1km long - first descending down two levels into the lava tube where the roof has collapsed and then walking up the tube under the mountain and ending at a lava pillar where the lave cascaded down from a parallel tube running above.  There is good lighting and regular interpretive signs.  Wear good footwear as it it wet underfoot even on hot and dry days.  It is also nice a cool on a summer day.

While visiting a friend who works in Jeju my family drove around to visit places casually with a flexible schedule. We planned to visit the temple for half an hour but stayed more than an hour. The name of the temple means medical spring and the flowing water from a 3-dragon-head fountain next to the temple store tasted good and sweet. Although the temple was built for only around 20 years the buildings and layout followed the traditional design. The main building faces exact south that can view the sea. The bell tower is located in the east for sunrise and the drum tower is located in the west for sunset. The main building's first floor wooden windows are beautifully carved with inspiring stories covered by traditional white paper but not glass. There is a traditional Korean painting exhibition of Buddha of Compassion in the basement and it's gorgeous. The best part of our visit was that not many people around. We got the chance to enjoy the quietness and even used the mats inside the temple at the back of the first floor to meditate a short while. There are grapefruit trees in the yards along the way to bathroom.

While learning about the life of Jeju folk village we enjoyed the gardens farms and orchards. They are beautiful and being taken care well. It was our first time that we saw cabbage with flowers.During our visit it was almost toward the end of closing time and probably that's the reason there're not many visitors.

When in Jeju you can choose to go to Trick Art Museum or Alive Museum. Both are about the same you pose and take funny photos with the exhibits. The Alive Museum is divided into 5 sections Trick Art Object Art Digital Art Sculpture Art and Provence Art. If you follow the route after the first three you will get to the outdoor Sculpture Art. The last section Provence Art is basically a large room with a lot of large-sized stuff dogs in Provence village setting. The dogs are not as cute as the teddy bears at Teseum. I think Alive Museum is more suited for teenagers and youg adults visiting in groups it should be more fun for them.

When I was planning my trip to Jeju  I found this museum has got half positive and half negative comments from travelers. Well ??I decided to have a look by myself. When our car got near to the place  there was a strong smell. I was then told that there is a piggery farm nearby which stinks out the whole place. The ticket was not cheap but it included a cup of coffee plus a discount in the shop. The appearance of the building is interesting with an open courtyard. The first impression was not so bad.However when I got inside  it was quite disappointing. I think the management should consider a renovation  or at least a deep cleaning and some maintenance. I just felt I was in a dusty old weird mansion. Maybe those exhibits are precious and rare  but they are not well presented. For example  they put lots of chocolate boxes from all over the world in the same window display without proper descriptions. How can the people think that those boxes are precious when they are packed in a glass cabinet? The lighting on the second floor was horrible. The rooms were so dark adding horrific ambiance to the museum.

review: What a quirky little place to visit! Just wish I had got my international drivers license before we left Australia though because then I would have been able to drive one of the fun little 3-wheel vehicles to get around the island. A short ferry trip from Jeju Island and then a bus trip around showed us the sights. A must-do is to get off the bus at the first stop and explore the 2 caves down on the beach - stunning and quite a spiritual experience. Absolutely loved our visit to this little island!

Went there with my other half but we didn't do a race. Spent about half an hour there to figure out the maze. its actually pretty obvious from the mini map they gave you but we took on the challenge of not using the map at all. Recommended to do a race and first to the bell tower wins! Its a little pricey for just half and hour of fun though. Paid about 4-5k won each. Cat lovers will love it there as they have free roaming cats around the entrance :)

Went in early Nov  the first time we went  it rained  so we went back the next day  and it was breathtaking. The view and the fact that there weren't a lot of people made it better. The oreum is quite a drive in  but it's worth it. Do note that there isn't a toilet there (as compared to the other oreum)

Went here during Easter. Overall experience was good. A bit too similar to Okinawa's Churaumi Aquarium which we visited a year ago. Not sure which one was established first.The main theatre show of diving and dolphins was a bit lame. Poor storyboard combined with several foreigners diving. A few of them did not look very happy probably from dull repetitive shows every day. The dolphin show was much better as far as I remember there wasn't any English subtitles.Probably the whole experience was better for kids or people who haven't been to large aquariums or the Okinawa Churaumi one. I would prefer the Okinawa Aquarium over this one for better location foreign tourist friendliness and overall comfort.

review: Went during the summer and its still pretty cold down there. Its a good rainy day itinerary as its entirely underground. Be warned that it can get really cold when  its raining though. Advised to wear good shoes are you wont be walking on flat ground and its quite wet and slippery. Its pretty interesting to learn  of the formation of the lava tube and a must go if its your first time in Jeju.

well. this fashion street was near with my hotel & i've walked here quite many times in a week. not so special for me as i don't do shopping but i ate 2times in this street that was impressivefirst time i reached here at 1st day no any breakfast shop near around*(they are opened at 9-10am at least) quite hungry & finally i stepped in one of traditional shop that only served 3 types of food all was hangover soup ha. seem that for drunken. price not so expensive(but not cheap) and quite many stuffs. tasty but full. lady boss also quite nice although she can't well communicate with meanother times with fds that was in a quiet corridor seem quite expensive restaurant with old & korean deco. however price was acceptable & serve sausage stew. well we ate traditional sausage stew in korean style house(boss always walk out from his room & overall style was house instead of restaurant). he was quite concern do we know how to eat & taking care of our table. maybe it has no many tourist but only korean or japanese while we having dinner moment.

We?re staying at the Lotte Hotel and this place is within walking distance.  First waterfall didn?t have any fall at this time due to a drought or off season maybe.  2nd fall was nice & it involved some walking down the stairs.  Overall the park is very pretty with its vibrant colors of the trees and the famous bridge you can walk across.

We were staying in Seogwipo and had an extra day with nothing to do. So decided to book tickets from Klook on the day of visit. From Days Hotel in Seogwipo we would have to take two buses 201 and then 295?. The first bus is 1 hr 10-15 mins and much more frequent than the second bus which is a 5 mins ride or a 25 mins 2 km walk. Taxis are cheap starting fare of 2800 krw will get you to Aqua Planet from the 201 bus stop but they are a needle in a sack - hard to come by! Other countries??hard to reach facility ir tourist site may provide some form of free shuttle/transport but not here. Once you enter the main facility it would take you a long time to find the toilets - certainly not tourist friendly. Live shows are also all in Korean  albeit with English & Chinese subtitles. The size of this Aquarium is about one third or one quarter of the Okinawa one so we were seriously disappointed with its size and varieties of fishes available. Visit if you have a car or join a local tour or book a taxi. If using public transport like us think twice about going as its 3-4 hrs to and fro Seogwipo.

review: We were quite surprised to see this place actually existed but then Jeju is meant to be a lovers island.  It was full of giggly groups of young girls and (separately) boys with the only couples being more mature tourists.I guess it can be seen as being quite educational.  Any shock you might find in the first 10 mins or so is soon negated as this place is just straight in your face.  On the whole very well done and an extra angle on your holiday.  So why isn't their one of these in Margate ?!

We went to the temple on the first day of our trip but we missed the vesak day celebration the day before.. The temple was decorated with lots of lanterns different colours..There are three buddha statues in the temple. Very inspiring!

We went on a rainy day and feared it would be too busy to enjoy but it was ok (the first section was the busiest but the crowds thin out the further you get in).  A lot of fun for kids and adults alike.  It took us longer than we thought to get through you could spend hours so would suggest bringing some snacks if you are travelling with kids like we did. There is a coffee shop on site but it only had sweets and ice cream.A fun outing if you've never been to a trick museum before.  Don't forget your camera!!!

We went here today for first time and love it?s it?s so beautiful and fun to walk around have good restaurants and coffee shop and good shop to buy thing make from jeju !! You can take bus or taxi too
We visited there in December first week and it was crowded. There were so many different colours of camellia flowers and we could take some awesome pictures there.

We visited the Hello Kitty Island to visit their cafe and also to have a look behind the history. The entrance for the cafe is not free so you have to buy a ticket first. Adults pay 12000 Wong. For this price the should maintain this area better. Outside it looks very used up also inside of the cafe. There were not much people and the tables were not clean. Also the location near a gas station is not the best one.

We visited here as part of a ships tour. The 8 minute film was very interesting. There are three exhibit halls. The first two were the best. You can see the whole thing in less than an hour. I wouldn?t go out of my way to come here

We visited for the night market. Nearby there is a multi storey public parking. The first stall butter fried rice with spicy pork is truly delicious and their orange juice (hallabong) freshly made is very nice though it is slightly expensive than the other stores. But it is freshly blend thus I love it and it taste good. Others stall look okay for me.

We took our 27 month old daughter here mostly because she was about to fall asleep on our bike ride and we didn't want to mess up her nap schedule. When you first walk in  they have a walk through of the animals of Africa. Our daughter had a ball naming the animals and learning new ones. We loved the learning experience she got while she stared bright eyed at all the big (and small) animals. She even loved the art and seeing all the different designs (although we admittedly had to go a bit faster than normal through the rest of the museum). For this being an unplanned stop  we were thrilled we did. What a nice addition to our vacation.

We took a cab and travel around Jeju. First: if you are intending to take a cab pls prepare your itinerary and let the driver know where you plan to go. 2nd: the driver will show you the mystery of the road. it seems that the bottle will roll to the steeper side of the road. bascially it is an eye illusion.

We like this maze a lot as it's not that easy as you can think of. Several times we went to an dead end and travel around similar corners!! Some kids running around to be the first ringing the bell at the finish point. It's a place full of laughter and we enjoyed it very much!!

We had heard about the tea plantation first on the television show Kimchi Chronicles on PBS (http://www.kimchichronicles.tv/). As an avid tea drinker I could hardly pass up the chance to check it out in person and it is amazing. We drank tea walked in the tea fields checked out the tea museum watched the roasting of tea bought tea tea soap tea lotion and tea ice cream. The museum and center are quite stunning and the drive out there interesting on some very well maintained roads. Don't miss this one if you are on Jeju Island.

We had alot of information to clarify & seek the tourists information centre assistance immediately on arrival in Jeju.It was about 20 minutes walk from our hotel. The Welcome Center houses the Jeju Tourists Information Centre & other offices as well.They got a young lady staff who speaks good English to attend to our queries.She was extremely helpful. We weren't very sure about certain places we wanted to go even after her guidance ( transport/directions wise) & she was so nice to give us an internet link for her to follow/communicate with us along our journey. Which she did.Certainly she went out of her way to help us poor tourists. Talk about great service and commitment. Wow!This is the first time in our travels that we experienced such a wonderful tourist centre staff. Many thanks.

We got so much help from the people to get here on the first day in Jeju. The view was really great and we felt released to enjoy the wind when walking through the trail. The horses and goats look so cozy around the trail.

We first went to this museum 7 years ago and wanted to visit this place again hoping there is some new attraction.  Sadly nothing has changed and lesser crowd.  Entrance fee is not cheap and I don't think its really worth to go unless you love teddy bear. We are out by 1 hour and kids wasn't very excited with the same display.

We came here early morning to take in the fresh air and scenic views of soesokkak estuary. There are water activities like the popular transparent kayak but it was closed when I went there. Just a note for those who wants to ride the transparent kayak do come here first thing in the morning and reserve a kayak for that day. There are nearby shops selling souvenirs and other eateries as well. I tried buying the hallabong ice cream from one of the stalls and it's really delicious.
Visited the place for the first time and really love their bears! Check out the Mona Lisa bear. Took a lot of photos.
Visited the Alice museum in a rainy day in Jeju was not sure of it at first but I must say we had a pretty fun time whoever put it together has a different sense of humor

Visited Sangumburi Crater as our first stop from Jeju city centre. It was in the morning and was rather cooling and relaxing. Not much visitors at the time. Sangumburi Crater was one of my favorite attractions of Jeju (the other being Udo-bong). It was a short stroll along the way and viewing of the greenery and flowers.

Visit this place even if you not interested or lover of sea shells at least to recognise the sheer efforts put in by Ms Myeong Yeon Sook  the director of this museum and owner of this place. This museum which has over 7 800 variety and accounting to more than millions of sea shells originating in Jeju and the world is the brain child of Ms Sook and master Metal craftsman Kwon Oh-Kyun.The beauty of these sea shells are to be seen to be believed. They have been arranged and displayed so artistically that one may easily mistake it as a painting.One may not see much of visitors around  but this really helps as we go around enjoying the magic of nature.Entrance fee is a bit high  but really worth it  considering the efforts put in to bring this huge collection of sea shells under one roof and creating the world's first seashell museum.

Very tasteful and informative. We were hesitant at first but figured we might as well take advantage of seeing what a sexually suppressed country could teach us :)The gift shop was a little lacking on museum related material and seemed to carry just local touristy items.

Very interesting maze. First 2 are fairly easy but the 3rd one gets a little tricky. Water mist kept getting in the way as you try to navigate so it gets a little more complicated. The kids and adults had a fun time. Should do it without the maps given so you just have to rely on sense of direction.
Truly Amazing view of the sunset. The climb up is not for the unfit but once up there I betcha your first word will be WOW.

Travelled by ferry from Seongsan habour (price 5500W two way). Upon reaching the island turn right to the carpark to purchase bus tickets (price 5000W). Bought the red tickets (you can only board the red buses with the red tickets and blue bus for the blue tickets). The bus is a hop on hop off bus (can only go forward not backward); you'll have to hold on to your ticket to board the bus for the next stop. Buses come every 20-30 mins. First stop was udobong peak - we had peanut ice cream (must try!!! Albeit a little sweet. Udo is known for the peanuts). The climb up is a little slippery so I won't recommend it on a rainy day. Requires some fitness to make it to the top but it is not too difficult. Otherwise a very relaxing climb that my family and I enjoyed very much! Stopped also at the Beacon mound (second stop on red bus) which was a nice selfie spot and then headed to the beaches before catching the ferry back to the mainland (last ferry back to jeju 5.30pm). The island is quite touristy though; expect things to be a bit more expensive.
This was the first time we hiked in the snow. We had to wear crampons in order to walk on the snow. The ascent was manageable and we saw kids around 10yrs old climbing as well.

This was our first stop for our south jeju trip and it was beautiful . One can just admire the natural beauty on how these columns and ckiffs would have formed due to molten lava . Must see destination in jeju
This was my first visit to a lava tube or cave.  It was a great little walk through a dark and amazing cave.

This was just like Legoland in California just on a much smaller scale (no pun intended). It looks like it was once a better place and has gone to the wayside. My first visit was around December then again in June. December was really rundown then June the grass and greenery covered up the poor parts from the winter. Kids will enjoy it you will be wondering why you gave KRW to see it!
This teddy bear museum was our first stop upon arrival in Jeju Island. Its more suited for kids and I was utterly bored.

This place was my must visit the first time I came to Jeju and I gladly returned back. You can participate in the tea class which is just another great activity to enjoy at this place. I love that there is both the tea museum and also the Innisfree house both having something different to offer. The only downside is the insane amount of visitors at all time so be ready to wait in line if you want something!
This peak offers a good view of the oreums and the sea but it did get very very crowded when we arrived there at about 9am. First time to Jeju? Must visit.

This museum isn't very large and in the winter you don't really want to go outside to admire the small amount of outdoor exhibits (which you can do from inside the windows anyway) but it's got enough interesting art to be worth 1000 KRW which is about USD $0.80. For one I enjoyed the Chang Ri Seok exhibit as his paintings are very earthy. The second floor exhibit was under renovation when I went but still for 1000 won I have no complaints about the first floor's contents. The gift shop is pretty underwhelming though.

This mountain is definitely worth a visit. I recommend a nice espresso and carrot juice at the bottom at Lazy Place Cafe - cool place with great views. It takes a little effort to get up to the cave with the water falling from the ceiling but well worth it especially if you?셱e a spiritual person. The other temples are serene. It is an UNESCO site of outstanding natural beauty with an historical layer at the coast below. A Dutchman was shipwrecked here in the C17th and wrote the first description of the Kingdom of Korea published in the West. I had a wonderful time with my girlfriend. Close place to stay is Mirabil.

This is the first time that my wife and I have visited a place like this. Honestly it exceeded our expectations and we were delighted with our visit. We recommend coming here if you have an hour or two to spare.

This is the first thing you should do if you visit Jeju. The tallest mountain in South Korea and you shouldn't miss it. Climb to the top if you can for awesome views of Jeju and its surrounding oreums. Locals recommend winter and spring but autumn is beautiful too especially along the Gwaneumsa trail.

this is one of the logest lava tube according to the information stated there. i loved it so much because that's my first lava tube visit. i went there during winter so it's cold inside. Bring your jacket along because it is cold and water dripping from top. Very good experince if you never try it. I think this is only 1/4 (1km) of the length open for public. It will take you 50mins if you would like to take pictures.

This is not only a museum but a cafe.  There is a main cafe in the first building where you can also purchase many tea products.  There is also another quieter cafe in the building up the hill where are can also take time to make soap.  The second cafe is not visited by most travelers and I would highly recommend it.

This is not a bias assessment. I would be glad if the establishment owner would take in advise from visitor feedback. This is my first time to rate an establishment with such a low rating. It is a total rip-off as entrance fee is collected before cafe and store. There nothing impressive with the collection and exhibit area is extremely small. There is another fees impose for DIY chocolate making session. No educational value  no entertainment value. I would not recommend it to anyone.
This is my first shooting but I enjoyed a lot. It?셲 a small shooting rage but well organized. 35000 Won must be not expensive.

This is first time we experienced a visit to a Green Tea plantation. Walking between the rows & rows of beautifully layed out fragrant tea leaves was just great.The cafe sells nice Green Tea ice creams & cakes plus tea leaves products obviously.An Innisfree shop sells the famous Korean cosmetics plus a small cafe included.Certainly this is an attraction that should not be missed when in Jeju.

This is an amazing place. The museum is absolutely first rate. All the exhibits have explanations in perfect English.  There are lots of interactive displays. If you are interested in the geology of Jeju you should come here first and expect to spend several hours. Outdoors there are 3 courses (walks) with exhibits of life in old Jeju. The exhibits are well done and English signs are excellent.  This place is huge and amazingly you will have it almost to yourself. It has an entry fee of about $5. That is the bargain of the century!   Don't skip any of it. It could easily take a full day if you are intellectually and esthetically inclined. It was the best thing I did on the island. I spent only about 4 hours. I would suggest you bring food and water with you. I had a few apples and tangerines.

This is a farm for Green Tea. First and foremost it is near the Glass park 5 mins drive away. So if you are planning to visit this place and have no budget constraints and have lots of time you can consider to spend 30mins at the glass park as well.The Tea farm sells tea (of course) and remember to try the green tea ice cream in the building. You can walk around the farm but be careful of the snakes. We seen one there.Nice place to visit whether alone in a group or with your family and kids.

This being my first time in Jeju Island it was an unforgettable experience riding around the circumference of the island. The view of the ocean was breathtaking and being on a bicycle allowed me to experience the island in a very tangible way. Honestly it was physically very challenging for me. The first day we were riding wasn’t so bad but on the second day the path was constantly switching between big uphills and big downhills. On the third day it was pouring rain and the winds were so strong! But even though it was hard this experience was very empowering.

There is so much going on with this place. Outrageous statues outside. A tittilating sign board but once you get passed the cheesy exterior and the quasi-porn first section this place is great.Fun educational sexy gross; this place has it all. But be warned. There are elements of hardcore. Unless you think your family can handle the naked pure unadulterated sexuality do not come in.I was with my wife and there is no one else I could have gone with. The best 2 hours ever. Just make sure you are not a prude.
There is a large Buddha inside the temple and on the first floor a display of 8000 little Buddha statues. Good for a short visit but otherwise it's just like any other Buddhist temple.

the way to this island is like my favorite of all the places in jeju... we took a 10 mints ferry from jeju city and the water was so beautiful and amazing... the ferry ride was also awesome. it was my first time on a ferry. we didnt stay on the island much but we rented a boat and saw around.. it was cool. we had a cool boat driver too.. we didnt have enough cash so he let us do it with half price. people in korea are too nice sometimes. if u have a licency you shld do ATV's too

The temple is super huge and well decorated. There are three layers the first layer is for the believers to worship the Buddha. Second floor is a place where you can talk to the Buddhist monks about your difficulties you faced in your life and have their spiritual purification. Of course some ?쁤oodwill??you have to forgive to this temple I saw one of the believer distribute a considerable fortune to that temple that believer must treats Buddha sincerely. In the entrance of the temple there was rice selling which is the accumulation of capital for the construction use. My mum bought one small pack of rice which costs 10K to support the running of the temple. There is also a water well besides the temple which brings lucky to the people who drink you shouldn?셳 miss that opportunity.Even though you are not a Buddha believer like me you are strongly recommended to go to that temple to have a look of the huge architecture and take pictures with the nice atmosphere.

The place is essentially a large botanical garden and cave in one attraction.First  botanical garden is quite large and can take quite a while to walk. The grounds are nicely manicured  with many plants  flowers  and trees. There are also some water fountains and small man made falls. There are also some statues and other stone objects in the park. There is also a greenhouse with various desert plants. It certainly isn't something you really need to see  but it is a pleasant walk through the area.However  the main attraction is Micheon cave. It is probably a naturally occurring cave. Nonetheless  the cave's ground has been leveled artifically to make it easy to walk on - compared to Manjanggul Cave which has a very uneven and dangerous floor. There is really not too much to see in the cave other than feel how cool it is and a few weird looking large figurines of cavemen...

The parking is free . Entrance fee was 2000W per Pax. You first descend about 5 minutes to a blue pond with the first waterfall . Beautiful and stunning . Then you proceed to the second waterfall about 10 walk . There was a third waterfall but it was about 40 minutes walk so we decided not to do that one . A five minute walk brought us to a bridge  which would bring you to another route . Overall expect to spend between 1-2 hours here .

The mountain's peak itself was covered with fog signaled rain will soon came pouring. I did not hike the mountain as the weather is somewhat not on my side. Just walk along the canola field in front of the mountain and snap some photos. There are paid field if you want to take photo with better view costs around KRW1000. I walked down heading to Yongmeori Coast but ended up in a small snack shop called Mongma Reukabuden. The shop owner is very nice person. While I had my Cheese Octopus Bread with Hallabong Juice the rain started to pour down. It was just drizzling at first as I finish my last bite of the octopus bread the drizzles turned to somewhat heavy downpour. The shop owner's wife generously gave me a new raincoat that never been used. Though they were speaking in local Korean and all I could understood bits and pieces of what she tried to convey in her effort to tell me to have this raincoat with no charge. I was solo traveling and generous shown by strangers really moved me ?졼뀪 For that piece of raincoat I humbly thanks them!
The maze is quite nice and little bit confusing if didn't use map as guide line. You guys can start a game with friend who finish first and it's exciting.

The lava tube was not claustrophobic at all. It was very comfortable and cool. The lighting is low but is still very visible and easy to navigate. Just did the first course but was glad we did! It was wet when we went and there was water dripping from the ceiling. It didn't bother me tho and didn't take away from the experience :)

The green tea cake is very very very delicious!!!! I am actually not really a fan of tea but that cake is just so tasty that I was grateful I went there.They sometimes provide demonstration and tester at certain hours so people who want to buy the tea can taste it first. However the employees speak in Korean so non Korean speakers can't understand the explanation.

The falls are really beautiful but extremely crowded. I would recommend taking the first bus you can to the area to be there as soon as it opens if you want to try to get decent pictures without hundreds of people in your photo.  We arrived around 11am and the sheer numbers of people detracted from the beauty of the falls.

the facilities are excellent  very spacious  and comfortable. staff great. out on it own with little to attract you and but great facility. not sure who supplied the food first night plenty to eat second night they ran out. end of our evenings there was no where to book/order a cab so thank goodness the BooYung hotel assisted.

The building is beautifully set into the landscape neither dominating nor subservient to it. Meticulously decorated with timber lattice this is a well designed building on the outside as well as the inside. You first enter into the gallery which brings you along a curve wall into the main sales area which looks out into the surrounding greenery and also into an enclosed courtyard. All in all a very well articulated building.

The architecture of this conference centre is the first exciting and majestic comment on the centre. It has big conference rooms with the best facilities to host big events. I attended the international mercury conference here and the logistics of the venue provided us with a flawless event. There are also several fast food restaurants at the bottom level of the centre  with a duty free shop on the other side. It is a local attraction and the visitors seem to enjoy it too  since it was constantly busy. On the second floor is a curio shop for some gifts from Jeju.The airport limousine bus no 600 stops outside entrance of the venue  but there are local taxis frequently available to take you anywhere.

That is the first time I am rating a place terrible. To begin with there are only Korean introduction and description for all the items and collections displayed there. We all read Korean don't we?As stated in other reviews this place has zero content. I can easily find more chocolate related stuff in a convenience store that this so called chocolate land. Worse  the entry ticket is bundled with a purchase voucher of the chocolate items sold at the store in this place. Contradictory to the all Korean introductions and descriptions  the chocolate available in the store are all international brands. If you are looking for the experience of travelling to Korea to buy chocolate probably from your own country  there you go!
thank you so much for your visit. your comment would be very helpful for us and we will serve anything at first for the visitor's convenience and satisfaction.

Spent half day on Udo Island walking around different spot by tourist bus! The bus tour is highly recommended to visitors without driving liscence since you can get on any bus of the same company with the ticket. Each stop has its uniqueness but still highly recommend the first stop! Simply stopby and enjoy Jimmy's Icecream along the seaside... guarentee this to be the most memorable part of the trip! The beach is also highly recommended since you feel like visiting Maldive with the clear water and blue sky. Try to arrive the ferry terminal to avoid overcrowding!

So the water level in South Korea is low right now due to an unusually dry rainy season so the falls were not as grand as they usually are however it was still an impressive sight and one I wont forget. BTW take a swim trunk with you and go swimming in the water at the bottom of the first falls its cold but amazing.

Shinhwa Theme Park is unique in many ways.  First it tries to make its own characters seems as popular as Mickey Mouse and Spider Man - it doesn’t work but it’s great fun just trying to figure out who is who.  Second everything seems brand new - so it’s spotless and at the same standards as a Disneyland or Universal Studios.  Third - the rides are small but oh so knock out fun.  And there is rarely anyone there.  I don’t know if they sell a fast pass but there is no need for one because i don’t ever imagine it getting that crowded.  The food was quite delicious too - great offerings at multiple locations.  You can easily do this park in a half day and not feel like your exhausted or missing anything.  Like everything in Jeju I think they think they are expanding but who knows..  and as i remember the entry price is super affordable.  So this is really a great time for anyone with kids or who enjoys theme parks.  Don’t go in thinking it’s Disneyland though and get picky - just enjoy it for what it is...a bold effort to start something special and first class and doing very well right from the start.  It was a great day for me and my daughter and her two cousins.  Enjoy!

Seashell and coral art in their fascinating and natural colors. The seashells' mysterious world under the sea-- as designed by several artists. (is this a title. If not keep original sentence) With a collection of 7 800 species  hundreds of millions of beautiful shells and corals from all around the world joined by metal craft and copper  present the world's first 'Museum of Seashell Art'

Really beautiful views from the peak of the tallest mountain in Korea! My friend and I are of above average fitness meaning we exercise with weights and cardio about five times a week. We made it up the mountain in three hours and down the mountain in three hours.  We took two separate 15 minute breaks on the way up and the way down.There will be a lot of people around nine and 10 AM! You should take the first bus in the morning to arrive before the crowds. We Took the 6:10 AM Bus from Jeju city intercity bus terminal and arrived at Seongpanak national park entrance at 6:40am to start our hike. The morning was a bit chilly but by 11:00am it was warm! We hiked in shorts with tshirts and a fleece. We had removed the fleece by 11. Bring water (2-3 bottles) and food as there isn't anyplace to but it once you leave the entrance to the park.If you don't make it to the final check point by 12:00 then they won't let you proceed to the peak. It would be really disappointing. There is an much to see for most of the hike as you're covered by trees but as you get close to the peak you can start getting the breathtaking views of Jeju.
Read online reviews is a must to come here. We went to the first shop 穩 for our dinner. We will be back again!

Pro: nice place as you will get free explanation of jeju. We were able to get first hand information about the traits of jeju woman and good history background of jeju.Cons: you will be exposed to v. long sales talk of made in jeju products. quite expensive and I was sitting through the talk half way i decided to leave.

Pretty big park with 2 caves that you can go through. Many school trips come here so don't be surprised to see flocks of students in the weekdays too. Nice peaceful area but there are quite a few other Jeju attractions I would see first if you're on a time limit.

Our two children loved this one. Easy to interact with and you leave with lots of funny pictures to bring home. Pizza at the restaurant was really yummy too. Nice break before you go out to the statue park in the back of the museum. Didn't seem to be well promoted - it's new and the first museum as you start on the road to the Jungmun Resort area. We took a cab from the Hyatt Regency (long uphill walk and potential rain) - less than 5000 won for the cab.

Our last destination for our first day in Jeju is this temple. Before arriving to the worship place near the parking area you will find vendors selling various souvenir items. Upon entrance we walk through the garden where we saw trees with oranges (mandarin in their place). It was last week of March when we visited this place we were lucky to see trees beautiful big oranges. Continuing the path we pass big rocks display with signage written in Korean which I don't understand. We then continue to walk farther and took the stairs until we reached the temple. Just like other places for workship you are not allowed to bring your shoes inside the place. Near the temple is a fountain they say if you drink water in the fountain it will bring good health and good luck to the person.

Our first time in Shinhwa World theme park visit in December 2017. One must come with the understanding that the theme park is not yet fully developed but it has some nice rides and you can spend a few hours there . My kids had a wonderful time . Since it is new  the park is not crowded. We had lunch at the food court and it was good Korean food . We were initially disappointed when the rides were suspended due to the snow. However the rides were resumed quickly after the snow stopped. We happened to have met the theme park Manager Mr Mason Kang when we ran into communication difficulty with one of the staff attending to the ride . He was very kind to explain to us that the rides would resume soon after they dry the area . His professionalism impressed us .  Our theme park experience was a great one . My kids tried the ice skating ring within the theme park compound . Everything is new and clean . We will come again ! They are going to have a Water theme park probably year after .
Our first stop on was this place. the driver took a couple of photos and then we entered into the cave. we were thrilled. we took 40 minute to cover the entire tube.

Our first stop in the Jeju trip was the Olloc Tea Museum.Here you can take a master class about how to make tea properly and try different kinds of teas.It was a very relaxing experience and the taste of the tea was very unique.If you like tea is definitely something you have to do if you travel to Jeju.Also you can visit the Innisfree shop right next to the museum and take beautiful pictures in the green tea fields around.
Only the first without the water falling is best for picture. The other two you will be on a platform far from the water.  The bridge is very big and allow you a good view.

Okay this is pretty common on Jeju I guess. There are lots of museums that copy each other and it confuses tourists. This listing is an example of that. The reviews for this listing is a mix for the Museum of Sex and Health and for Loveland there is no actual listing on here for Loveland. We did our research first to decide which one to go to and Loveland looked like the more fun one - a lot of the pictures of outdoor sculptures on this listing are actually from Loveland not the Museum of Sex and Health). I'm not even if they both have the outdoor sculptures. Loveland is mostly outdoors but it does have an indoor section too with a shop and a diorama exhibit (if you're strapped for time you can probably skip the indoor part it's not very long and the exhibits inside are mostly in Korean so if you can't read it you have to extrapolate things for yourself). The park is fun a lot of it is very silly (they even designed the bathrooms in the spirit of the park - have a look at the door handles).
My review was way too late.It was our first visit to seoul and went to jeju with our 1 year old daughter.Many people went here taking photos esp tourists.Nice scenery.

My girlfriend and I went for fun. It literally is like a museum. They have a bunch of statues outside and inside there is a lot of information to explain themes relating to sex. There is two floors. The first floor is about different positions amongst a lot of other stuff. The whole first floor is almost exclusively written in Korean. Unless you can read Korean I would skip it. The second floor does have English. I would only go if both floors have English. It is not for non-Korean speakers.

My friends and I decided to take a 2 day side trip in Jeju Island from Seoul. Our first stop is the famous O'Sulloc Tea Museum. We went there March of this year it was sunny and yet it was cold and very windy. When we were still on our way to the museum we were already awed to the beauty of this place. Everything was green and beautiful! I super love the place!!! We first went to the plantation itself from the parking lot. Walking on the pathway in the middle of the beautiful trees and shrubs was just a beautiful feeling and much more when we reach the plantation. We also went to the top of the building for  a bird's eye view of the plantation. Our last stop is their museum they have a great display of tea cups which illustrate the colorful history of tea plantation and tea making. After the museum is the store where they sell variety of green tea products. They also have free tasting of hot teas. Wonderful Jeju Island! Great opener for a tour:-)
Might not be worth the $2 entry fee. If you walk behind the first ticket counter you get one of the best views of the falls. There's another ticket booth that they punch your ticket at.

Long trail relatively easy.. specially the first 4 KM .. are flat basically The rest is a hit steepThey will give u a certificate if u take a picture up for 1000 wanBring ur own food.  And water.. In the winter wear ur gears as its super sleepery dont go with out gears i went in april. . And in the last 1/3 of the road i slipped and injured myself many times.. Fantastic hike.. Definitely recommend it

Located on the eastern part of Jeju lies Ilchul Land  a cultural spot that showcases Jeju's ecology which consists of the Micheon Cave  Subyeon Park  Folk Village  Wild Flower Bonsai Garden  and Cactus Greenhouse etc??For fans of Running Man (?곕떇留?  this is one place to visit as the team actually filmed here before: various signboards showcasing certain place scenes (at certain corners) that occurred during the filming of Running Man; bringing you a step closer to your favorite Running Man characters! The first stop was Micheon Cave  a cave that is a designated Natural Monument and one of the representative lava tubes of Jeju. Within this cave lie beautifully landscaped and manicured gardens which include a pond (Chumsung Dae).After we were done with the Micheon Cave  it was off to visit the Folk Village with a little yummy ice-cream of a snack on the way. The village was a replica of what would have been in the past with a millstone and buildings with commentary. There were even ?쁫ive??black pigs which were as long as my golden retriever! *Black pork is apparently a famous product of Jeju.For more on my experience and photos  please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/03/ilchul-land-micheon-cave-folk-village.html
just do the first route and get out unless you want to endless tombstones. dont miss the sky pond though.

Just a Stone throw away from  Seongsan Ilchulbong is located the Aqua Planet. It is easy to find and has generally enough parking place available. It is quite a big building and not to over look. Entrance fee is a bit pricy. We paid for 2 adults and one child over a 100k Won if I am not mistaken. Anyway a huge Aquarium costs probably a bit more efforts as other places in Jeju. The whole aquarium is made comfortable for stroller and wheel chair. We entered 20 minutes before 3pm and did a mistake. At the entrance they told us that we have to look the show first and then go through the Aquarium. It is what we did. So after the show we had to deal with a lot of People crawling through the aquarium at the same time. Don't do this. Instead do the other way around. Best case you enter the aquarium when the show starts. The aquarium itself is very nice and a lot to see not only for the juniors. A lot of species big and small and tall and tiny. Good place especially when it is either rainy or very hot outside. At the end as you may guess is a souvenir shop. LoL. Since then we have one Pingu more in our collection. Infrastructure wise (shops and 00) no issues. The show itself what shall i say. I thing you have to see it and judge. It is 40 minutes long and is divided by (20%) dolphin performance (20%) sea dog performance and some (60%) pirate story performance with humans only. Fair enough to say that over all the show was good and fascinating. Conclusion is that we visit the place again.

review: Just a museum  you will read a lot of stuffs about chocolate history and process of making. First I thought everything inside the house made of chocolate  but you don't expect that for a cheap entrance fee. One of the highlight is the workshop  if you are planning to attend with your kids  better check the timing. We bought some souvenir too and their chocolate are great. I didn't give a higher rating due to following... 1.) They provide free drink  but it is a coffee  I think it would be nice if its a chocolate drink 2.) Some interesting areas (Cocoa garden and kitchen) are not accessible when we visit (not sure if there is a special arrangement for it). Overall  it is not that scam and most likely I will visit it again when I'm with the kids.

review: I've been to Jeju twice. The first time I saw the Nanta show the second time I saw this one. And it's a good show. It's held in the local university which is conveniently close to the downtown of the northern part of the island. The show is creative and entertaining. It's just not quite as good as Nanta (although I believe it is cheaper?)

It's the first place we went on our first day in jeju.Had fun playing with mirror and it's interesting to see insects are decorated like human.. at first we don't understand what this park do but for me it's like an insects museum

It's supposed to be one of the seven winders of nature but not exactly my kind of travel destination. It's amazing for the sheer length of the cave (7km) although you are only allowed to go to the first km. We only managed to go 300 m since there wss not much to see except for molten rocks along the cave. There was not much to sustain interest in going further inside the cave so we decided to just go back. At least it was cool inside although the path was wet but nit muddy. Wear comfortable and non slippery shoes if you wish to see the cave.

It's my first stop after touching down in Jeju. It's quite an interesting place to enjoy the nice breeze and occasionally catching the view of the plane touching down at the nearby airport.. Steps are a bit uneven at some places where you can get a great photo of the rock
It's a shame that water is toooo cool because  the first reaction on a water fall like this is to go inside the water and don't come out ;-)

It was pouring and we needed something to do.  Jeju has a lot of museums and this was our first stop.  As a person who studies sexual health I found the museum average.  Why?First the museum does a good job at giving a lot of different perspectives. Covering things like marriage history  homosexuality  maturity sti masturbation  bdsm etc. They have displays installations artefacts video and some interactivity. The biggest problem is that all the information is written in Korean. So it was impossible to actually learn. I would have liked to read all the information that was presented. Also the price was expensive 12000 won was a lot for what you got.If the information was in English I could see me giving 4 stars.

It was our first time riding a horse.Strict instructions were given not to make sudden noises when riding as the frightened horses will go crazy & will cause serious injury to riders.All handphones/sling bags are not allowed too.Each rider gets to choose a hat & were matched to horses according to height.The horses walked unguided on a short (about 5 mins) fenced circuit. About 100 metres near the finish point the horses suddenly start galloping slowly.It was not easy to balance oneself on a horse holding just 2 grips on the saddle while it was galloping. We were concerned for that moment if we will fall off & was also wondering what happened to the horse. This was probably the scary part of uncertainty.It was a good experience though it was a short ride. At least now we know how it was to ride a horse.

It was my first time walking through a lava cave which was an enjoyable experience. I appreciated the natural formation of the tubes and to think that lava once flowed through was exciting. Others might think it's just a cave and the first few meters is the same throughout which is fair enough but I loved it.

It was my first time ever to any of the ALIVE series and honestly it wasn't fantastic but I could be bias cause I hate crowded attractions and people hog and does not wait for their turn. My recommendation is to go during off peak season with at least a group of 3 as some of the displays can fit in a couple. I guess it will be more fun as well. Condition of displays are pretty good and one could easily spend at least 1.5 hours in there. There is also an outdoor park which features more abstract art which is pretty interesting. Overall worth the money? I'll say it's alright but it will be a place that I'll visit once.

It takes entrance fee to enter the museum  but that's okay as there are three venues in total. With lots of different appearances bears  such as dressing up like students and wedding. The most memorial teddy bear is the president Obama  it is similar to the real Obama but in bear form. The top floor of the second venue is about wedding and relationships between lovers  so it is a great place for lovers to take pictures and have memories with the teddy bear couples. Although I am not a teddy bear fan  I took lots of photos in that first two venues. And in the third venue  bears are for sell  so please remember not to photo bears in the third venue as it is subjected to copy right. Finally  my father bought me a bear which I think is the cutest as a present of graduation. It takes about 40k-80k unequally per bear  but I think it is valuable as all bears are made in Jeju.So  if you think you don't have any way to spend your money  you can go to this teddy bear museum and buy your favorite bear as an emblem of stepping on Jeju.

It is relatively easy to drive to this location with ample parking lots. You will have to purchase yr tickets first before venturing further as the next booth only inspects the ticket. you probably need about 10 to 15mins walk before you reached the waterfall.  Do take your time to admire the nature during yr walk.  You can take the other path when you leave the waterfall. I enjoyed that moment with my family.
It is really an amazing and stunning cave. Only first 1km is opened to public and it takes about 40mins for the whole journey. Very worth to visit it.
It is one of a few place with optical illusion on the slop of the road. First time seen this kind of scene.If anyone had any experience at other country. I guess it is just the same.

It is my first time seeing a waterfall by the sea... The view was spectacular! Experience the breeze of the sea combined with the breeze from the waterfall. The majestic waterfall is already quite impressive itself...

It is first time for me to write a review of a museum because it was much more beyond our expectations. You will love the exhibition even if you are not a big fun of cars. The best part for my 8 year-old son was the test driving for his first International Driving License.
