Our first trip is a touch and go but our hext trip, we will focus on one  or two main areas. We could not do the hiking cos it takes time and better with an overnight stay near the base of the mountains.

We really enjoyed Udo. It's a small little island located about 30 minutes(ferry ride) off of Jeju. We got to the island with only about three hours before the last ferry was going to leave, so we wanted to pack in all that we could. First, we got some peanut ice cream. Then, we rented bicycles and tooled around the island's coast. It was beautiful and several times as I took in the sights, I kept thinking,   How cool is this? How many people I know will ever get to have this experience?   It was a neat feeling to be exploring a quaint and little-known spot in the world. We found a little beach and cooled off before heading back to the ferry.

We planned this for the kids but the adults had fun too. When we arrived, we bought the tickets while the kids were busy with the numerous cats around the area. It turns out that this is also a place for cat lovers, this place is a mini cat world too. You can get cat food from the ticket counter to feed the cats.In the maze, the kids formed a team and raced with us, the parents. Each team had to find the stamps hidden around the maze and stamp on the paper given. First team to collect all 6 stamps and ring the bell to exit the maze wins.Upon exiting the maze, as we passed thru the ticket counter again, the lady manning the counter asked us to visit the gift shop to claim a free postcard.

We hiked up the gwaneumsa trail (shorter, steeper but more scenic route). Really glad we chose this route as there was far less people and the views were spectacular.We arrived to the trail head at 7am and paid the 1800 krw fee for parking. The trail head is clearly marked and there's a nice washroom that you can use before beginning the trek. The trail is well marked (there's no way you can get lost) and also well maintained.You reach the first rest stop around 3km into the hike. There's a very smelly washroom there (there's a better one at the next rest stop). You must reach the last rest stop by a certain time or else you won't be able to proceed. The time posted today was 1300 although it looked like the only barrier was a small chain that you could walk around so I'm not sure how enforced that rule actually is. After the final rest stop the trail goes downhill a bit then the steepest climb begins. The stairs don't seem to end for the last 2.7km!! The views are spectacular though. Once we reached the top there was so many people! Where did they all come from? The seonpanak trail. So glad we chose this trail instead.In the end it took us 4.5 to climb to the top of hallasan (with many rest/photo/food breaks) and another 3.5 hours to descend. I had 2L of water although I only drank about 1L. There were many bugs but I didn't seem to get any bites. There doesn't seem to be any dangerous animals out there although there are signs warning about boars.

We hiked up Hallasan the first weekend in March 2012.  We brought coats, hats, gloves and scarfs, however we were not prepared for the amount of snow on the mountain.  Check the conditions ahead of time and be sure to bring walking sticks and spikes for your boots.  My family hiked for awhile but stopped about 1km from the top after we were in more than two feet of snow and freezing.

We hiked to the top of the volcano. The walk was pretty easy but long. Lots of information signs make it really easy to manage. The first part is in the wood, which means no view but shadows. The last quarter of the ascension is out of the woods but was really crowded what made the walk boring.The volcano is nice, but i think it may be overrated dut to the fact that it is the highest mountain of Korea.Anyway, it is a must do if you go to Jeju

We have visited this beach on our first day in Jeju island. As soon as we walked in we felt so happy to see this beautiful beach! It was beginning of September, it was hot but as soon as we went to beach we almost got frozen due to strong wind. Sand is white and when combined with clear sky water appears Caribbean blue :) it was difficult to find a place to sit as it was overcrowded. We asked a lady in a local shop to keep our belongings for us while we are swimming, she was very kind and didn't ask any money from us. We also met sunset on this beach. It was gorgeous.Tip. Take a windproof jacket with a hood of you cannot stand for wind for a long time.Renting a place on beach with umbrella costs 10,000KRW. Renting some inflatable toy (flamingo for example) is also 10,000. Life vest/goggles rent is also 10,000. And you won't see any price tags around, kind of weird.Food around. Chinese restaurant across the street serves nice jajamyun noodles for 6 or 7,000 KRW. I can recommend it. Drinks - cafe bene with gorgeous view. Average coffee. Good bagels with crab meat.

We had dinner there the first night.  I had bulgogi before, but never presented that way.  They didn't put any plate in frot of us.  We had to ask people next to us how to cook it and to eat it.We had the ime of our life there.  Unfortunately, I don't remember the name and cannot give a specific review for that restaurant.

We go in the end of June , basically it is hot outside, but inside the cave is cold and a bit freezing, take along taxi ride from Soegwipo area, cause we travel in 5, 1 senior over 75 , 1 teenager ,1 children of 7,  so we decide to book taxi for 8 hours to explore Jeju it is more convenient and save time  than using bus , but a little pricey 120.000 krw for whole day, After reaching the cave and go down to look inside , my wife and mother in law surrender, cause it is to exhaust to walk 2 kilometer ( in and out )for senior and a bit dim,   Cave is big , but there is no living creatures like bats or others, I my self do not really excited at first,  but my 7 years son and my teenagers daughter really like to explore the cave, so we are not prepared and just go. A bit chilling but still bearable, no toilet inside so prepared your self , the light is dim but still able to see around, there is water dropping from ceiling but not too often ,the water clean and no smell, the pathway is not level and bumpy ,watery here and there in a few area the but still manageable and walkable ,  don't have to worry,  if my 7 years old can do it so can others , at last this is a pleasant and unique experience, a bit exhausting walk , but worth a try

We found this museum in our travel guide and it sounded fun to visit. However, it was quite disappointing starting with the price which was much more expensive than all other museums. It only had a few rooms with teddy bear representations that got repetitive and monotonous after the first. On the other hand there was a nice outdoor park with fun sculptures to take pictures next to. Overall might be good for children but not so worth it for adults.

We engaged a Jeju Korean driver at 180,000 won per day for 2 full days to bring the 9 of us around for sightseeing in Jeju. On the first day, the guide headed to the attractions in the north and east of Jeju and on the second day, he covered attractions in the south and west of the island. Oedolgae was located at the southern part of Jeju at Seougwipo city. We came to view Oedolgae on the second day afternoon. It was free entrance. From the car park where we alighted from our van, there was a signboard that indicated Oedolgae was 250 m away from the car park. As we strolled our way to the cliff area, I noticed that this attraction was crowded with many tourists and everyone was trying to take good photos by standing at the barricaded area overlooking the azure seawater with the 20 m tall Oedolgae rock as the background. The scenery was amazing. Our guide spoke good Mandarin and he told us of the mystical tragic sorrowful legend of a saddened wife who feared the death of her beloved husband jumped into her death on seeing the body of her husband flushed to the coast. The Oedolgae rock was the embodiment of the wife who had committed suicide and the base of the rock represented the body of her husband. The sad story dampened my spirit momentarily but the awesome view of the stunning rock blended seamlessly with the azure sea and the clear blue sky. The fresh cooling sea breeze that caressed my face lifted my spirits and the next moment I found myself squeezing among the crowd to take good pictures with my group members against the picturesque backdrop. As we strolled along the weaving coastline, we viewed the Oedolgae from different perspective and each angle projected a captivating scenery. At one point was a big board depicting the picture of popular Korean drama show Dae Jang Geum (Jewel in the Palace) and of the famous Korean actress Lee Young-ae who acted as the great Palace female physician during the Joseon Dynasty. This place was the filming location of this popular traditional korean drama.  I really like this place. It is so picturesque and I was totally immersed in the magnificent scenery appreciating that rhythmic splashing of the seawater against the high cliff. That short juncture, the clock stood still and I just could not believe my eyes that I was standing and facing such a fairy like breathtaking natural attraction.

We didn't spent much time here as we are rushing. Overall is a nice place to visit. You can rent a bike or motor cars to go around the island or take the bus tour. At first we planned to drive car inside the island. However, due to many vehicles in the island and to avoid traffic jam, they have set the rules that only local island cars can drive into Udo island. I forgot the timeline but it took around one year period. For those who plan to drive car enter the island you may need to further check on it. When purchased the ferry ticket, you are required to fill in the two forms. Please bring along your passport as well. The counter personnel not many can speak English where we feel a bit challenge. Overall, is a nice place to visit. And if possible do spare around one day to enjoy the environment here.

We did this hike by end of March 2014. The first part is indeed a kind of forest walk. Half way we were indeed surprised to see some snow on the hills and later on lots of snow on the path, Since we did not have those clampons it was pretty tough. At the 2nd shelter we did indeed buy those clampons whereafter the hike was more easy to do. The view from top was not that good due to the upcoming mist. We were amazed though to see so many RAVENS waiting for food.

We did the Yeongsil trail.  The first kilometer in the forest was kind of random.  But once we got above the tree line, the scenery was beautiful.The path is very well maintained with boardwalks and handrails.  But it goes up 400 meters in the first 2.5 kilometers, so it is definitely steep, with entire sections of just stairs, a little bit like climbing up the Eiffel Tower.  This is not a relaxing stroll and you need to be in decent shape to enjoy it.  When we saw it was 7.4 kilometers round trip, we thought it would take us 2 hours, but it almost took us 3, with limited rest time.The last kilometer to the junction with the other trails is all flat, with boardwalks through the highlands.  We didn't try the restaurant on top.So all in all, lots of variety, beautiful bushes, beautiful flowers, lots of birds, nice rock formations.An absolute must if you go to Jeju Island.

We did the Seongpanak walk to the summit. I am of average fitness and found the first half relatively easy going, although the rocky path and stairs after the last rest station were a little harder. It took just under 2 hours up and about the same going down again, with a couple of very brief rest stops.The views from the top are pretty good if there are no clouds. There's not much to see on the way up though, as you're in the tree line and there is little variation.The track is well marked and easy to follow. Most of the track is volcanic rock, although there are sections of board walk as well and the last 1km is wooden stairs. I didn't think that the distance markers were that accurate.The paths get very crowded - most of the walkers are dressed and equipped like they are attempting to summit Everest, but realistically all you need is good shoes and plenty of water. Most people were using walking poles as well, which became extremely frustrating as they tended to block the paths. The only people I saw fall were using these poles, they really are not required.It would be difficult to do this track in the rain, as it would get quite slippery in places. My advice would be to go early to avoid the majority of the crowds - the car park fills with tour buses by mid-morning. We started at 0700 and it was still relatively busy then. You need to be at the last rest station by 1230 to be able to continue to the summit and leave the summit by 1430.Overall - I wouldn't do it again, but if you had a free day on Jeju, it's a good way to burn off a few calories.

We did the seongpanak trail. Check the weather the day before embarking, and make sure you have proper hiking shoes as the climb is rocky and some parts are pretty steep. Stretch your muscles before the climb or you'll end up sore the next day (or you can tote along some muscle rub)! Bug spray is also recommended, for those prone to mosquito bites. Try to get an early start if you can; as you have to pass the second rest stop before 1.00pm if you want to make it to the summit, otherwise the staff will not allow you to proceed. On average you would take 7-8 hours to hike to the summit and back, depending on the number of rest stops you make. There are 2 rest shelters along the way (one selling food like cup noodles and choco pie, pocari sweat and bottled water). There are toilets at both rest stops, but no water; no washing hands or flushing systems. Generally, the climb path is divided into thirds - beginning (relatively easy, mostly uneven but flat ground) - first rest stop - second leg (rocky ground, with some portions made up of many steps) - second rest stop - final leg (fair warning it gets really tough for beginners, as the terrain gets pretty rocky and steep) - summit!

We did the Seongpanak trail which is about 9.7km one way. The trek is pretty straightforward with clear markers. Not too difficult to summit at 1950m as the climb is gradual. Took us just under 6.5hrs to complete the 19.4km course including an hour for lunch and photos at the summit.  For the first 7km, you will be trekking under the forest canopy. The view will open up as you push for the final summit to the crater. Great view on a clear day. Path is very rocky so do have at least a sneaker on to have a good grip, especially after a rainfall, which is pretty frequent in Jeju. Buses plow the route so it's easy to get to start point from most part of Jeju. (Do take note that you have to reach the 2nd checkpoint by 1pm during summer or 12pm during winter to be allowed to continue to the summit.)

We did Olle Trail 1 (15kms) starting in Siheung and finishing in Gwanchiji Beach. Trail started next to Siheung elementary school and it was very well signposted all the way. The information center 1km up the road has no info in English and the gentleman didn't speak It either, although it's not really needed to follow the trail.The first 5-6kms are beautiful as you go up a hill, from where you can see the coast (including Seongsan Ilchulbong) on one side and the plains and Hallasan on the other, and you're surrounded by forest.Once down the hill, trail gets very boring for 8-9kms as it's on paved trails next to main roads. Final part from Seongsan to Gwanchiji is nice again as you walk next to the beach/sea.

We decided to go to Audi because of the 3 different beaches the were there (and for Haha Hoho Burgers). Getting there was more difficult than expected. We had a rental car which was nice to be able to retreat back to air conditioning. But the line for the ferry was so long that it took about 2 hours to get on the ferry. Once on the island our first stop was for lunch at Haha Hoho. We were lucky in that they didn't sell out of burgers by the time we got there at 1:50. Buy by the time our burgers were ready 2:40 they were sold out and not taking any more orders. So get there early for lunch. The drive around the island was nice  and picturesque. The first beach we stopped at was a disappointment. The water was green with algae and smelled. There was also quite a bit of trash. With the number of people there I would expect more maintenance. We stayed only briefly hoping for better beaches down the road. The next stop was a black sand beach nestled in a cool looking cove. But again there was trash everywhere. We didn't stay long. The first two beaches were a   bust.    The third was the   coral beach.   It was clean but the water still green with algae and seaweed. The beach was rough under our feet but the kids had fun. It was pretty crowded and the water became deep quickly so not much space to play for new swimmers. The views from the island were great, especially at sunset. Overall we were underwhelmed and felt we probably should have stayed on Jeju and just visited the northern beaches.

We chose the   short   hike up the mountain (volcano) and it was all up. We are Coloradoans and hike quite a bit and this one was a bit of a challenge. The first part was through an oak forest and it was hot and humid. We sweat like crazy and things got better once we got out of the oaks and into the pines. It took us 2+ hrs to get to the rest station and a bowl of noodles and a chocolate bar. The hike was amazing, though with strange vegetation and a miniature deer, the only wildlife we saw along with many butterflies. We did not go to the top since it was in the clouds and starting to rain, but the views of the ocean and Jeju-si were as advertised. This is a must see place and there is an easier hike than ours, but takes much longer we were told.

We caught the 7:30 am ferry from Seongshan Port to Udo.  The ferry left a bit early so we actually arrived at the island by 7:35.  The ferry ride should be about 15 minutes.  Cost was 17,000 kwr for 2 adults for round-trip tickets.  We struggled with whether we should have brought our car on board and immediately regretted not doing so once we landed.  Seems it is off season so not busy at all.  The first place we stopped at was the mango shop, where they also have a shop In the back for vehicle rentals.  Stopped there and tried to rent a mini-car/scooter but the staff said no rentals today because of the festival (seems it is the seashell festival).  Anyway, with no other option, we just took the hop-on and hop-off bus (5000 krw per person).  It?s about 21,000 krw round trip for a small car.  First stop was the lighthouse, got there at 7:45 and went back down to catch the next bus at 8:30.  The next stop after was the black sand beach.  Then to the other lighthouse on the northern tip of the island.  We concluded our trip at the stop after that which is the other ferry port.  We caught the 10 am ferry.  We skipped the white sand beach which is probably the most popular site as a lot of Korean dramas were shot there.  Some tips:- bring your car if you have one so you can visit the island on your own schedule - try the peanut ice cream at Jimmy?s Natural Ice Cream- most of the food places may be closed on a Sunday

We can't quite remember the order but my wife and I saw 3 waterfalls when we went looking for one. All the waterfalls were spell binding, gushing with water even in summer (April) However, 2 are fenced for safety reasons and the third one has a board warning you against swimming. You can, although, dip your feet in the cold water at the unfenced one. At the first one, you can make a wish and throw a coin into the shallow end of the fall. And if your schedule isn't packed, it's a great place to sit back and read a book.

We came here on 11 January 2015. We hiked up the Eorimok trail and came down on the Youngsil trail. According to the signs, the Eorimok trail are divided into three sections of differing difficulties - it begins difficult and gets easier as you hike up. I found the first half of Eorimok exhausting for a casual hiker because it is quite steep, and also slippery with snow. On the day it was also very foggy, resulting in low visibility. As we walked up to 1700m, we came across a store selling cup noodles. The cup noodles aren't very good and the environment of the eating area is poor; however, it is sensible to say that one shouldn't expect too much from a little mountain store. After eating you have to take the cabbage with you and bring it down to the mountain.Next, the Youngsil trail, which is THE BIGGEST NIGHTMARE. After walking for half an hour down we realised that most of the fences are covered in snow, meaning that we were walking in a mountain unfenced! Given the steep and slippery (snow) nature of the trail, it poses significant risks of fatal falls. In some situations we were (and also some other hikers) so scared that we had to sit down and slid slowly rather than walking. Sometimes it is so steep and slippery that it's not possible to stand up without tripping over, so we slid as though it's slippery dip. Make sure you wear crampon and bring trekking pole. Without them it is almost impossible to hike in Mt Halla in winter.

We came here for the sunset view, because that was the recommendation for this place. But we were disappointed.We reached Jeju via plane around 1pm and went to Hallim park (5min walk to Hyeopjae beach) after check in. After a walk around Hallim park we walk to Hyeopjae Beach for sunset watching. The weather is just nice, no rain, not too hot. The sand beach was covered with plastic material (?), I guess so tourist can walk on it. There was few garbage lying around the beach and it was a bit crowded with people, both local and tourists. The sunset view is not that nice.Again, to be fair, we come from the tropic. The Bornean sunset is probably the best sunset. So for people from the tropics, you can skip this place if you want to. But if you have nothing to do in Jeju, I guess you can come here to relax, after a walk at Hallim Park.To go here: Take bus #710 bound for Hyeopjae beach (or Hallim Park if you want to go there first. It's just 5min walk to Hyeopjae beach).

We booked one day tour, but had the best time with Andy so we decided to book one more day. We really think Andy is the best tour guide available in Jeju. Not only professional but he is very caring and very kind.He recommended the best destinations and kindly tried his best to find restaurants for us (we are vegans so it’s quite hard). It was our first time to Jeju and we felt safe traveling with him. You really want him to guide you for your Jeju trip!

We are a relatively fit family, but were not properly prepared for hiking Halla Mountain.  We made it as far as the Observatory (approx. 6 hours round trip). Since it rained days before, the summit was closed due to poor trail conditions.  Although some portions of the hiking trail are level & nicely paved (w/ wooden planks), the majority of the trail is very steep & rough (comprised of large, uneven volcanic rocks). Unfortunately, we wore Nike running shoes & Converse tennis shoes which did not provide adequate support & protection needed on the feet.  Since the incline & steps are uneven, you need to be careful where you step in order to prevent ankle or knee strains/sprains.  We saw some people fall on the jagged volcanic rocks & get scrapped pretty badly.  We found wood branches along the way to use as hiking sticks for balance.  This hike is alot tougher than the hike to the upper falls of Yosemite.  So we recommend that you come prepared:- sturdy hiking shoes and hiking poles- at least 2 bottles of water per person (there are 2 drinking wells w/ a communal drinking cup; we drank it & had no stomach probs)- bug repellent (we were there in the humid summer)- cooling scarf (to wet & wrap around neck)- energy food (power bars, fruit/nuts)- backpack (carry out your trash)- small first aid kitTip: There is a parking fee to park in front of the entrance.  All of the parking spots are usually taken very early.  Otherwise, if you park on the street or arrive by taxi/bus, there is no fee to enter the park.

We ( mostly) enjoyed our hike up Hallasan. It is a moderate climb despite being the highest peak in S. Korea. Important to note that you still need crampons to climb right now. Our hotel went and told us we didn?t need them as there was no snow left...well they were wrong! The steepest slopes on the trail are still sheer ice and it is quite treacherous without the crampons to help you grip! Other than that it was a good hike. Crater at the top is pretty cool. Also note that even on a clear day it was really hazy in the distance so the view from the top wasn?t as expected. Still worth it though. I recommend starting very early, get the first bus in the morning. The trail becomes quite crowded later on.

Was skeptical at first. But the park turns out to be pretty nice.  With amazing bonzai (some over 300 years old), flowers, lava caves and even peacocks!  We were lucky that we visited during cherry blossoms season, so it was an added bonus.  Only caution is don't go there hungry.  Food there is terrible and expensive.  Much better to eat elsewhere then visit the park for a good 3-4 hours.

Was here for dinner across two nights.  Managed to compare Dombedon (without knowing it's Michelin rated) and Hwaro Hyang (on our 1st night). Comparing the two restaurants, I'm wondering what's the big deal about Dombedon. For a start Dombedon seemed to be mass producing with the intent to get us through our meals asap while those at HH treated their meats with respect.  E.g. HH doesn't cook all their meats at one time while Dombedon just dumped all the meats at one time, resulting in charred meat, spoiling the experience.  I am not even sure if I was eating black pork, insignificant as it may be.  At HH, it was odd at first to see abalone being baked along with black pork, but it was a pleasure to see the shellfish curled up as it cooked.  In HH, they bothered to sprinkle salt on their pork to bring out the flavour, but Dombedon disappointedly didn't. Prices are really almost the  same anyway.  My recommendation would have been HH, though we haven't really tried the rest.(The 2nd pic is from HH and the 1st pic is from Dombedon.)

Visiting Hallasan was one of the best experience when we were in South Korea in July. Weather was absolutely gorgeous there! So we thought we well prepared for the one-day hiking event, wearing normal running trainners was a big NO, it was okay for the first few hours, then our feet were felt like being on those painful foot massage non-stop for the next 5 hours. So wear walking boots if you want to hike all the way up to the top! Tips: * If you get there by public transport (bus 781), be aware the bus back to the bus terminal is 782... it seems strange, but anyway bus 782 opposite the hallasan park entrance will take you back to the city centre.* Bring enough snacks and water, and take a proper rucksack with chest strip. you can get instant noodle at 2nd shelter, but its also your responsibility to bring the empty plastic noodle bowl and some left soup down, It could be a bit pain to carry the noodle bowl with some oily soup with you all the way back.* walking boots! !* For girls, take a pack of tissue/napkins with you

Visited over Thanksgiving weekend and were surprised by all the snow! We had a rental car (with chains and GPS) ... 1139 was blocked off first attempt so we took 1131 and viewed the snow from Seongpanak Rest Area and we knew we wanted to hike the next day but didn't have enough time for the long trek so we approached from the other side on 1139. Arrived to Yeongsil Hiking Trail at 7:50 a.m. and had no problem parking at the entrance. Hiked/walked the 1 hour of 2 we had and reached the temple and entrance to the next 40 minute hike which would have taken us to Witse Oreum - fellow hikers informed us crampons were required from there and I don't doubt it, wish we had hiking sticks too, definitely not to be done in the snow with anything other than proper boots. It was a more difficult walk than we thought it would be, fairly steep toward the end and we were all down to long sleeved shirts even though the temp was freezing. Kids (9, 12 & 15) loved it, lots of stops to throw snowballs, etc. As we headed back down at 9:00 we started passing big crowds ... so glad we got out early and enjoyed the tranquil quiet of the snow covered forest! The road was just about cleared when we were leaving so it seems you can drive and/or take a taxi to the temple then do the 40 min hike to the final stop on a day when the roads are clear. Cars were parked for over 1 mile toward the access road so again, hit it early!  Mt. Halla was visible when we approached the top - the first we had seen of the crater in 3 days there, absolutely gorgeous.

Visited Manjaggul Cave because it was a UNESCO Natural site, like Seongsan Ichulbong.  Unfortunately, beyond the concept of actually walking through lava tubes, the entire experience was rather disappointing.  It was dark, wet and cold. The ground was uneven and hence quite slippery with many puddles.  After the first few hundred metres, my older daughter lost interest but we insisted on walking further.  However, it was pretty much more of the same so we did not finish the entire course of 7.4 km (since it would actually be 14.8 if you consider you also have to walk back)!  So unless you are in the area and really into geography, I would give this a miss.

Visited Jeju Glass Castle on our second trip to the island visiting our son and daughter in law and our first grandchild. This attraction was not what I was expecting, it was very imaginative and well laid out, all displays were of glass, of course, some very talented glass blowers. Well worth a visit.

Very skilled young Mongolian horseriders, who perform a small Korean/Mongolian (horse)drama in an hour. Be aware of the showtimes, because I think they only have 4 shows a day. We were too late for the first show and while waiting for the next show we requested the taxidriver to bring and wait for us at Hallim park, which is only 10 minutes away. We also combined this with a short beach vsiit and local brunch at the beautifull Jeju-beach.

Very interesting inside and out. The first floor is mostly modern about sexual preference health and rights but it is 95% in Korean. I would recommend to bring a Korean friend who doesn't mind translating if you are interested in that part. There was also a big wall of history at the very front which was all in Korean that would be worth translating. It wasn't very busy and some of the   hands on   things that would show examples were broken so I started with a mediocre impression. The bigger and more impressive part though is the number of historic sexual things they have on the second and third floor. Lots of artifacts about sex in Eastern cultures with some in Western cultures but a lot of things have their English translation. This part is much more impressive and interesting to look at. A lot of phallic objects and   traditional   pieces but it's historic and that is how people viewed sex in history. The more modern section is more modernly-styled and was a bit confusing (a lot of sex dolls...? kind of weird) and included more fetish stuff than I expected. Not much on queer and non-hetero there was a small section (in Korean) on the ground floor and then one very gray area display on the top floor but not a whole lot can be expected of Korea (where homosexuality is still viewed very negatively). Overall it was worth the price and was pretty interesting to look at. Having a translator or understanding Korean would make it more memorable.

Very interesting for the first time. The local guide told us they name this road as   monster road   cos locals belive there is a invisible monster playing with the cars that's why the car move forward when uphill even stop engine. Great experience

Very commercialized tour spot in Jeju island. I visited this place a few days ago. I have been travel Jeju island tens of times but this is first time to visit this village and realized this place for selling someting to tourist. If you come to this village, just look around and don't enter the house. There are a lot of good spots you can see in Jeju island

Using Mr.Kang service for 2 days. He is very very nice and helpful. We gave our itinerary and he will drive for us. He is very nice and even gave us a bunch of orange.. my father love it very much. This is my first time in jeju. He even took good picture for my family too. He is very nice, i recomend you for using his service. Thank you Mr.Kang and see you again :)

Unlike Hello Kitty, I think most of us have cuddled or have in possession a toy teddy bear at a certain stage of our lives. So it is no wonder that the Teddy Bear Museum has such a wide appeal and which surely be included as a ?compulsory? destination on the itinerary of the independent travellers (especially those with children) and tour companies alike.Getting there and fees: We visited Teddy Bear Museum (GPS coordinate/code 7387600) on a rainy day, which was appropriate since the exhibits are predominantly indoor, except for the Teddy Bear Garden and Park where there?re a few teddy bear figurines outside and a park with great views of the sea.  The admission charges are 10,000 won for adults won, 9,000 won for teens and 8,000 won for children.The Museum/Attraction:  This Teddy Bear Museum is the first and largest teddy bear museum in South Korea. Once you enter, you are greeted by this huge teddy bear, who gives you a ?grand? welcome to further explore the five sections spread over 3 levels: The History Hall, The Art Hall and The Project Exhibition Hall, Gift Shop (all indoors) and an outdoor Teddy Bear Garden and Park. There?s also a caf챕/restaurant. Be prepared to spend at least 1 hour looking and taking photographs/selfies at all the interesting exhibits. The History Hall comprised of the history of bear manufacturing and some of the earliest toy bears, many of which are antique and rare. It also showcases milestones in human history, with the bears enacting several famous (human) historical scenes from different eras. This is indeed a refreshing concept for a museum! I particularly liked the teddy bears enacting the Titanic, landings on the moon and the iconic celebrities like the Beatles and Gandhi.In the Art Hall, you could see the world-famous artworks and designs in an art gallery form as well as animation characters beloved by children. I liked the Mona Lisa and two of the most expensive bears in the world - the Louis Vuitton teddy bear and the Diamond Bear. In the Project Exhibition Hall, you would meet teddy bears grouped to suit the theme of each exhibition. Not forgetting the large Gift Shop on the first level. While it offers plenty of gifts, these are nonetheless pricey. Nevertheless, you could take photos with Michael Jackson bear, Steve Jobs bear and a wedding couple bear amongst others. There?s also a mother panda with her baby pandas on display too.  We certainly enjoyed the wonderful experience of the Museum bringing out the child in each of us, and making us feel young again. Despite the pricey entrance fees, I still think the Teddy Bear Museum is worth visiting, and to me, once would be sufficient. But if you don?t like teddy bears at all, then it would be prudent to skip this attraction.

Udo or ?Cow Island? lies off the UNESCO World Heritage island of Jeju and is so named because its profile resembles a sleeping or resting ox. The fun begins with a 15 minute ferry ride from Seongsan Harbour, costing ??5,500 return trip. As the boat glides over the choppy waters, you can watch on deck the antics of Korean school students on excursion feeding the seagulls in mid-flight, with lots of shrieks and screams. Upon arrival at Cheonjin Port, shuttle buses will be waiting to take you around the island for a round (hop-on hop-off) trip ticket which you pay after the first stop. It?s a pity we could not understand the Korean commentary provided by the bus driver, as he had his captive audience in stitches along the journey. We enjoyed the rustic scenes of thatched farm houses and fields, surrounded by the azure blue seas. We made stops at Geommeolle Beach (black sands and cliff backdrop) and Seobin Baeksa Beach (white grains of rhodolith). The half day excursion to Udo was a joyful and unruffled experience!

Udo is like a big kids playground. You rent an electric scooter and scoot around this fun little island. We looped it in about an hour and a half, stopping for iced cream. The rental was 3 hours and so we explored the middle of the island off the beaten path. You cant really get lost and apple maps or navient works great (so does cell phone data). Some expert tips:Get the ?Harley Davidson? 2 man bike.Its rain covered, and you wont get too hot like the enclosed units. Adjust the seat forward (lever under your leg) to free up some space behind your seat for your bagOnce you get your scooter, scoot scoot! Everyone follows the same clockwise loop around the island. Open that throttle and pass those dottling tourists. Udo Awaits!Use your horn, and folks let you pass. Beep Beep!Skip the first two big pulloffs where everyone stops. Its way too crowded and you may have to pay to park! Watch for the big bus! It runs opposite motorcycle traffic and takes up most of the narrow roadway. So dont drive in the middle of the motorway. The bus driver is very safe and watches for confused motorcyclists. It was very safe.Otherwise, beep beep, scoot scoot, and enjoy the Electric Scooterland of Udo!

Udo is a very windy and beautiful island. The views from udo peak is breathtaking. There is a round trip udo tour bus for 5000won per pax which shuttle you to 5 attraction stops of the island. First stop is to the black sand beach where you can see the black sand beach and a cave (during low tide). If you want to go to the udo peak, you will need to walk a distance, climb up a hill to reach the udo peak. My first trip to udo was with my Jeju taxi guide and he drove us to udo and brought us up. My second time here was kinda cocked up because the udo tour bus driver only conveys in korean and our taxi guide this time did not accompany us to udo. Hence we did not made it to the peak. Nonetheless, we explored other stops (beaches and beaches). The sea and beaches are very beautiful. Udo is famous for their peanut and orange ice creams which I felt is a waste of money. Per cup of ice cream topped with some peanut or orange juice cost 5000won. Mcd ice cream taste nicer and bigger quantity. Oh yes, if you are willing to spend more you can rent bicycle and cycle around the island. And if you have international driving licence you can rent motorized vehicle to travel around. The roads are small and there's many tour buses shuttling people hence certain areas are abit congested.

Try to give yourself a little extra time to buy tickets as they day we travelled it was packed with tourists.The short ferry trip was wonderful, and offered great views of Udo as we approached. On reaching the island the first thing we observed were the amount of rental companies offering bikes, electric 2/3 seater buggies, scooters and tandem. In fact anything you can think of to explore the island. Ido is famous for peanuts and you will find many of these on sale in the quaint little cafes and shops dotted around main road. If you get the chance you should try the local    Udo peanut Makgeolli   The island is truly beautiful and if you do decide to join the hoards on electric vehicles shop around a bit as there are lots of rental companies eager to offer their wares. It is also important to ensure that you have an   international drivers licence  ,, as they appear to have tightened up since a number of accidents lately and wouldn't accept our UK credentials.All in all great trip with lots of ferries running bak and forward throughout the day.

True to the museum title, there?s quite a number of precious collections, including the first generation of Winnie the Pooh, Carebear and other well known bears. A number of bears dressed up as historical figures placed throughout the building provide good selfie opportunities. Worth it if you are a bear lover and in the Jungmun area.

Took the seongpanak trail up the mountain and must be at the last checkpoint before 1:00 pm or you'll not be allowed to the peak. from the information/parking space down to the station is about 5 km..? and from the station to the peak another 3-4 KM. approx 4-4.5 hrs (walking) from start to the peak. Trail is not very difficult, the first part is not so steep and you could run it if fit enough. but the last few Km is steep and knees gets tired climbing all that stairs. shelter at the last station do sell some drinks, chocolate bar, pie, hot coffee, ramen. Do not climb when it's raining as there's no view but you'll just get wet and cold, unless it's just the climb that's important, It's still relatively easy to go with proper weather suitable clothes.

Took bus 781 from City Hall in Jeju City about 30-40min bus ride for 1300KRW. Had some breakfast at the Seongpanak bus station (base camp), got a bottle of water and a snickers then started the hike. Read that it would take 8-9 hours roundtrip, got to the top in less than 3, a very slow and steady rising hike firstly through the forest and later up the mountain. Stunning views from about 1800m and up, saw some water also in the crater, quite crowded at the summit. Ate my chocolate bar, took a selfie and started walking down. Total time return trip to the bus station was 6 hours. Best tip is to not pause at the middle camp which you must reach before 12:00 if you want to get to the peak, but instead just walk on to the top and have some lunch or break up there, you will then skip most of the crowd, try to head back down before 13:00, as you need to leave the peak before 13:30 it does get crowded on the descent and will just increase your time spent by waiting for slow groups.The views are spectacular, do recommend, no fees.

To see the sunrise, one has to wake up early and hike along the stairs and some stone steps and must remember to bring along a torchlight or use our smartphone's torchlight as it can be still very dark during the hike. My husband & I took 30 min to reach the peak, while waiting for the sun to rise there were many people waiting and getting ready their cameras. At the crack of dawn, one will see the sun starts to peak out and see the first rays of the sun grace the Earth. During that moment, everyone started exclaiming with delight as I believe it is not easy for some of us who do not have strong stamina when comes to hiking but it was worth seeing such glorious sight. If I have the chance to visit Jeju, I would want to visit this place again.

To make sure hikers are able to return to base before sundown, you have to enter the trail no later than noon and must reach the final section of the approach by 12:30.  Gwaneumsa trail was about 8.7 km long taking about five hours at a leisurely pace.  Most of the hike was in a shaded area which would make it comfortable even during summer.   The first 3 kilometers were just a stroll with nicely laid out boardwalks for some stretches.  There are railings parallel to the trails in case an injured person needs to be transported from higher elevation, which made it extra reassuring for me.  Although steep, it was still a relatively easy hike and I made it through the last section without much problems.  From about 1600 m above and onwards, the trails were covered in ice and snow which slowed me down a bit as I didn?t even think about carrying crampons in late March.  As I got a late start the summit area was a little crowded with hikers having lunch or taking breaks.  Luckily, the Baekrokdam peak is a crater and there was a relatively wide area for people to sit around at the summit.  Unlike the Baekdusan Cheonji Lake, Baekrokdam is devoid of any water except a small patch of water that looks like a small puddle from the top.  While not particularly scenic, it is nice to stand at the highest point in the country.  Because of the strong winds, I didn?t stay long and started to head down the less steep Seongpanak Trail which was about 9.7 km to the parking lot.  Few kilometers from the summit was easy with boardwalk paths and steps.  There was a three kilometer stretch of snow covered trails that made the descent quite stressful though.  Once the snow covered area was cleared, it was a long but relatively flat walk rest of the way which my knees were thankful for.  The entire round trip took about nine hours total without much rest.  Having crampons would have shaved at least an hour off of that time.

To go there: take bus #710 bound for Sheongsan Ferry Terminal. You have to tell the driver where you're going before boarding the bus. Buy a ferry ticket from the ticket counter (5,500?? - round trip).We were there on 2nd May ~11am, the weather was windy but there was sunlight. We bought tickets for hop in and out bus from the ferry terminal. It will take you to 4 different attractions on the island, we only managed to enjoy the first 2 because it started raining (good thing we don't have an international licence, because u can rent a motorbike there too), and it was already windy, so the cold was too much for us. But I would recommend this place. Come once you're here, come at least once. I love the view. Too bad it was raining so we have to keep our trip short.

To be honest, I didn't expect much at first, but when I started walking up the stairs, OMG! I was really awed by the clear blue sky, silver grasses, wind, everything! The view of the crater was just   so-so   to me but the view of the other side with the silver grasses was just way too amazing! I would say, it's not something that's so special that you must go to see no matter what but still, it's something that you won't be able to see everyday or everywhere. First of all, you must go at the correct timing. I went during mid-October, the view was magnificent! You can even see Hallasan from afar (check out my photo). Thereafter, you can walk through a small road where you literally being surrounded by silver grasses. That's a perfect place to take photos as well (photo attached).This can be a romantic place, or it can also be a peaceful place where you go to relax your mind and to see something different.

Though pork is my least preferred meat option, I decided to try due to its popularity. I first headed to the Dombedon restaurant, but was told the minimum order is for 2 person. Not willing to eat and pay for double portions, I chose the restaurant just across the street.I ordered a set pork belly for 18,000 won. The waiter, a Vietnamese student, spoke great English. He demonstrated to me how to use the leaf to wrap the side dishes together with the pork. My pleasant surprise was the free cold noodles in soup.  Overall, it was a great experience for first time dining. As for the black pork, I felt it was over hyped as it tasted no better than the typical roast pork in Asia. Once is enough for me.

This well set out and very informative museum recounts the history of how many of the Jeju islanders were killed and repressed during the late 1940s and early 1950s.  The visitor passes through a series of rooms, each explaining in Korean and English a different stage in the tragic events.  Apart from the actual events themselves, two things shocked me most.  Firstly, that I had never before heard of the April 3 Uprising, although some 25-30,000 people were killed by Korean government forces and their supporters.  Secondly, that even well into South Korea's democracy the events continued to be hushed up and only relatively recently has the truth begun to be told.  Just a few years ago, mass graves were discovered near jeju airport.  The museum provides such a valuable insight into the island's past that I think no visit to Jeju would be complete without coming here and learning about the events and their aftermath.  Entry is free of charge.  The peace park around the museum provides a place for contemplation after visiting the museum.

This was the first time I'd ever been to a lava tube so it was a really new experience. It's basically a geology lesson on the impact of lava flows. It was interesting though perhaps a little too academic for non-geologists like me. It's dark though and you have to be careful where you step as this is, after all, a cave not a paved walkway. On the whole, it was a unique experience and it gave me a different view of the beauty of Jeju.

This was the first place to visit before we headed to other place in Jeju Island.O?셎ulloc Tea Museum is also located here and we just stopped by there for lunch and check out the products at Innisfree Jeju House. The lunch was not cheap , it's organic, There were also some visitors who were learning how to make soap, I think we need to pay for that course. I just bought a box of mini masks and move on to other places.Not too bad for a short lunch time and for photos maybe. To go about Jeju Island is best with to rent a car as it's more convenient to go for one places to another unlike in Seoul or Busan where subway are available.

This was our first visit to a lava tube, and we enjoyed it very much. The lava tube cave is maintained in natural state. Hence the floor is uneven and you need to watch your step. It is also very wet and little cold in side. Apart from that the walk is very enlightening. We learned many new things about lava tubes.The lava column at the end of the cave is a must see and is the highlight of the whole walk.Must visit.

This was our first stop during our weekend trip to Jeju. I had heard about these women before but didn't know much. First, they showed us a video (in English) all about the history. I was immediately hooked! The rest of the museum is so interesting. The pictures and artifacts tell a great story. I just wish I could have met the Haenyeo personally! Also, the women working at the museum were nice and helpful as we tried to get to our next stop.

This was our first attraction after arriving in Jeju-do. It was recommended by several locals including our taxi driver. We had a mixed aged group with us (4 year old active little boy to my 70 year mother) and everyone was able to enjoy what the park had to offer. My mom and aunts were amazed by the plants, especially the hundred year old bonsai trees. My two kids loved the caves. First time that I have ever seen white peacocks. The only thing I found rather odd was the petting zoo that requires another fee.

This was my best experience in Jeju. I went in October 2013 and we went up Yeongsil and down by Eorimok. The hike was not the most difficult, but can be quite crowded. We arrived by car around 8am and there was a queue to the carpark. Note that there are two carparks, one on the lower level (where buses drop you off) and one at the start of the trail. We waited about 45 mins to get into the first carpark, and when we saw that there was another queue to go up, we just parked at the lower carpark and started our hike from there. This is a good idea if you plan to go down by Eorimok - you won't have to climb up to get your car after taking to bus from Eorimok to Yeongsil.The hike in autumn was wonderful, the foliage was awesome and the weather was perfect. There is a rest area between both trails where you can buy cup noodles and chocolate bars. It took us around 4 hours to go up and down.

This was an interesting experience. I am usually ok in small spaces and felt this would be a great thing to do. But once I was in the middle of the first maze I felt a little uneasy. They provide a map and the maze itself is pretty easy to do. You also hear people walking around, but just something about the possibility of making a wrong turn made me not want to do the second and third maze. But there are really cool towers and a museum where you can take amazing pictures. the museum is free, they have trick art and a puzzle art. Getting here was a little bit difficult. Ask around your previous destination at the bus stop perhaps some people are willing to share taxi with you. Since the bus that goes around this area takes almost 45 minutes. And once you get to your destination you sometimes still have to walk a while to get to where you want to.

This was a nice walk up to the top. There's a lot of stairs, but it's not nearly as bad as I thought it was going to be. We went in Oct on a fairly sunny day (temp was probably in low-mid 20's) and you definitely want some water and sunscreen with you. I'd recommend going when it's more cloudy, if you can. There are a couple little shops along the way to the top (the first few levels of stairs, not all the way along) where you can also purchase water, and there is some tasty Jeju orange ice cream for sale too. The views are pretty, as is the temple, and it wasn't too busy when we were there in the middle of the afternoon.

This was a first time visit for us...and we found it to be cheesy with a capital 'C'. However, who would have thought that CHEESY could be so COOL!!!!Yup, we had fun here...the place was amazing. Nature in harmony with recycled glass and plastic. it's very well maintained, good to spend a few hours here taking pictures...as well as soaking in the various exhibits on display. I particularly enjoyed the walk in the Enchanted Forest, a bit creepy though...as it was secluded from the rest of the complex, and this added to the excitement of being in the forest...talk about a vivid imagination!They have a shop selling souvenirs as well, clean restrooms and a cafe. I would recommend those looking for some fun to drop by here, and just let your inner child run free!

This trail takes about 2 hours to get to the top, if you walk fast you could do it faster. It is uneventful and going to the top the first 70% you can only see trees. At the top there was too much fog/pollution so you could only see the crater, which had almost no water in it. There are stairs and wooden platforms so it is more like taking a simple stroll through the woods at a bit of an incline.

This top site in Jeju island is also known as Seongsan Sunrise Peak or 掠길ε뷴낡 It earns its reputation as Korea's first UNESCO World Natural Heritage site, and once you reached the top, you will see why. Be warned, it is a reasonable difficult climb that will easily take 20min to hike up. Wear comfortable shoes and bring water during hot weather. The uphill stairway will take you to a majestic dormant crater that offers spectacular view of the sunrise, hence the name. Be prepared for massive crowd of tourists throughout your climb, and get your vantage point to capture some of the majestic scenery throughout your climb.On your way down after enjoying the panoramic view of the UNESCO World Natural Heritage surrounding, make sure you allow enough energy to take the downhill path on the left to explore the Haenyo women diver performance at certain times. We were there after 3pm, so missed out on them unfortunately.

This review will be written from the point of view of a middle aged woman of average fitness, not someone for whom a 20 km trek is a walk in the park.Mount Hallasan is the highest peak in South Korea and if you are on Jeju island it's definitely worth visiting. We took the Seongpanak trail, a scenic , easy route which reaches the summit. Plan on one day for the trek up and down. Here are some tips:1. It goes like this - You take a bus or taxi to the Seongpanak trail, and start climbing. It's a mix of  some steps and an easy trail. After a while you reach the first stop - I forget the name - where you can use  the restroom. There's a small shelter where we had our packed sandwiches. After this, the trail becomes a little steeper, and you reach the next stage - the jindeballat rest stop.( Times by which you must reach the Jindeballat stop and when you must start your descent are posted on the trail). There are restrooms here - but inspie of information to the contrary , there was no food for sale. After this the climb becomes a little tricky , and you need around 2 hours to reach the summit . The views are amazing from the summit. The Koreans hiking the mountain were not only super fit, they were the sweetest people I've met. When I became tired near the summit, so many encouraged me with words like   Fighting!     Turn around and see how far you have come.  Tips :1. Wear good hiking shoes - at points , the trail is slippery, and good shoes with ankle support are helpful.2. Carry a stick. You can get your own hiking stick or buy one from the store at the bottom.3. Carry plenty of water and snacks.4. Take a selfie at the summit and you can get a certificate at the bottom stating you have completed the climb ( costs 1000 won)5. You do need a certain degree of cardiovascular fitness to make the climb comfortably. But apart from that, the uneven  rocks and boulders are a little tough to climb, so make sure you do some core and lower body exercises too. 6. If you climb down slowly, it gets a little dark by the time you reach the base. Carry a head lamp.

This post is about logistics and what to expect from the hike. My partner and I hit Hallasan around 6:45 in the morning on a Saturday to avoid the crowds. We drove to Seongpanak parking lot (free and was filling up quickly. A tour bus with dozens of hikers was already there) which was about a 30-minute drive from Seogwipo. From there we took a $15.00 taxi ride to the Gwaneumsa parking lot. As this was not a loop trail, we wanted to take the steeper/harder route in and have gentler descent (easier on our knees) back to our car. Turns out, doing it this way we avoided what felt like hundreds of people ascending when we were heading back later in the day. The Gwaneumsa parking lot has a fee. (Sorry TA fans, I didn't get the amount since we took a cab --- I am sure it is nominal, like all fees in RoK:) People are allowed to camp at the Gwaneumsa section of the park and I saw a few people starting their day as we marched to the trailhead. We were under tree cover and walked along a dry river bed for the first couple of miles. At this time of day, we only ran into seven other hikers on this trail. After you cross the river via bridge, the hike starts to get a little steeper. About two hours in, you hit a large, modern shelter and toilets. Good time to take a break and snack. Or keep carrying-on as you will get a chance to sit, eat and gaze at another resting place. After the shelter, you will cross a much larger, newer suspension bridge. Fresh water available here. The climb will get a bit harder for next half quarter mile. Continue past the foundation of the destroyed shelter. After you ascend the 18-22 inch tall stone steps, you will reach a ridge which is the other good stop.  No shelters (in fall you should opt for the shelter), but a nice wooden platform from which to gaze at how far you've come. Crows will land in search of scraps. At this point you are very near the top, only a couple more hundred feet to go.The crater was dry when we visited (first weekend in October), but still a wondrous site. The seasoned, local hikers brought burners and ramen and were happily chowing down near the crater. Darn! That would have been nice. The  t-shirt, fleece jacket and windbreaker I was wearing barely sustained me, so the hot ramen sounded freakin' great.The hike down Seongpanak was not nearly as enjoyable since we were bombarded by the late starters heading up. At one point, the hikers coming up were in a jam ? seriously, no one could move, there were so many people. There?s a large shelter a third of the way down. As another reviewer noted, be sure to wear supportive shoes with rigid shanks as you're constantly stepping on uneven rock.  I had on trail runners, which was fine going in, but heading down, my feet were pretty battered. The boardwalk was a nice breather when we could get it.*Seongpanak gentler ascent, (and descent) but be prepared to share the trail with dozens and dozens of other people.*Free parking at Seongpanak -- fills up quickly as early as 7am on weekends.*Toilets available on trail.*Take bimbimbap for a nutritious, affordable, and portable snack. Mandoo is another good one -- good balance of carbs and fat.*Listen and look Nuthatches, Wrens, Great T*ts, and other winter birds on the Gwaneumsa trail.*The park states you must hit the summit by noon. I think this is why so many people were rushing to hit the peak at the same time.

This place was the first on my list of place-to-go in Jeju. We were quite rushing as we don't want to miss the Haenyeo show (I totally adore them since years ago while watching documentary!). We would love to go for hiking to the peak, but we are pretty much time-constrained. Make sure to wear comfy shoes as there are lots of stairs. Go downstairs (it's really tiring to go upstairs later) to the Haenyeo house for the show and be there early as those ahjumma (auntie) in diver suit will perform their Haenyeo song and dance before going to the sea (this is so much fun!). There is boat service provided if you'd like a tour. You may enjoy fresh raw seafood (abalones, octopus etc.) from their catch, approx. from KRW10000 for a plate. If you love horse-riding, give it a try!The area is surrounded with souvenir shops. Try Hallabong (citrus fruit), one of Jeju specialities! The sight is way too gorgeous to be missed. MUST-GO-PLACE!Haenyeo (women diver) show: 1.30 pm & 3.00 pmAdmission fee for adult: KRW2000Boat ride: KRW10000Horse-riding: approx. KRW5000++Hallabong: KRW2000 each

This place was gorgeous! It is a Korean beach so it is crowded please keep that in mind. I am a Floridian and we have some of the best and most peaceful beaches on earth. But this, even for me, was truly an experience. One the amount of people was impressive but less crowded than Busan beach. Try to get here early and pay the money for the umbrella spot. They all cost the same, but you wanna be in the first row so you can see the water.The water is truly beautiful. The color is very different than floridan green blue waters. The ocean here is the deepest darkest blue I've ever seen, and the part that meets the beach is a light bright crystal blue. There are many families and watching the kids is really cute. We spent a lot of time floating around. Next time I would bring a float so we could inner tube around like the locals did.You can order food and the vendors or restaurants will bring them to your umbrella.Fried chicken is a must for Koreans on the beach. We actually were super hungry before going (next time we will do it differently) so we went to Korean food chain Mom's Touch that serves amazing crispy fried chicken in bbq glaze with pickled radishes. So on the beach we got ice cream and fresh fruits.Warning for travelers: more of a cultural heads up. There are showers- like beaches in America have...you do have to pay to use them, but there are no private changing rooms or showers it's all a show for anyone to see. Now it is gender separated, but don't be shocked to find you'll have to strip down in front of strangers. My husband is Korean and didn't warn me, but it was too late once I walked in, plus he already paid for my shower and I really needed a shower. But here's the thing you'll notice that no one cares about you, and no one looks at anyone. Just shower off, do your thing and you'll be outta there in no time. If this is too much for you to handle...then skip the shower and head back to your place to shower in your comfort level.

This museum is 90% in Korean but as they say some things are easier to understand. In the beginning the museum starts out with some interesting if broad sex-positive history. It's sex and HEALTH however so there's info about AIDS as well as misconceptions about sex and sexual health. Towards the middle of the museum it starts to go off the rails a little bit. The   Fantasy   section is a lot of chintzy garbage and mannequins in lewd/bizarre positions and tableaus. It doesn't add anything it moreso detracts from the legitimacy established in the first half. Only go if you're stuck with a rainy day. Otherwise you'd be better off enjoying Jeju's natural wonders.

This looks like any regular road.  However, due to an optical illusion, your car without any power will seemingly roll uphill.  This was discovered by a taxi driver by accident.  If you?re there, why not stop by.  It only takes a few minutes.  You?ll see other cars as well testing it out.  This was the first stop of our taxi tour that day and it only takes a few minutes.   There?s an English sign explaining the road.  If on the way, why not. A bit of fun!

This is the type of waterfall which discharges directly into the sea so coming here you will get two views - the waterfall and the sea. However the trick is in how near you want to get to it - first you got to navigate the deep steps, then the rocky and slippery ground to get as close to the waterfall as they allow you.  So it is very important to come with proper footwear. Then it?s a matter of how many shots you want to take. There is also a corner where some hawkers are selling fresh seafood. Not sure if it?s sashimi as we aren?t hungry.

This is the second time my family and I have visited Gapado Island since we had a good experience during our first visit back in November of last year. Unfortunately, our image of Gapado overall is now completely ruined due to an extremely unpleasant experience at the restaurant named “Gapado Yonggung House” (가파도 용궁정식&민박)?Upon arriving at the port at Gapado, we saw many restaurant advertisement posters. We found one restaurant poster with nice food images, so I called the restaurant to get directions. The owner (male) who answered the phone was quite unfriendly and told me bluntly to just look them up on naver map and find our way. He said that even if they give me directions, I wouldn’t know they are located. So my family and I found our own way to the restaurant after a 20 minute walk. It turned out that this restaurant was located furthest away in Gapado Island.?We ordered our meal and started to set our own plastic ware. Due to Covid-19 sensitive period, we always bring our own disposable chopsticks, spoon and paper cups to restaurants. The owner (lady) out of the blue bluntly asked us if we bought our own cups in a rather accusing manner. We said yes we brought these cups and asked “why do you ask?”, to which she said “Oh, we have some cups in our kitchen and wondered if you took them” I found this question to be rather offensive as I feel she was insinuating or implying that we just took (or stole) them from their kitchen without their knowledge. However, we overlooked her strange question and went about eating our meal.?We then wanted to order soft drinks. However, I could see that all staffs, owners included looked quite busy. Therefore, in my attempt to be helpful, I went to the fridge and removed two soft drinks from the fridge while at the same time informing the owners of my action of taking the 2 drinks, to which they acknowledged. To be perfectly clear, I was telling them to charge me for the 2 soft drinks I was taking.?However, only a few minutes after this action, I overhear the lady owner speak to her employee in a very loud voice to not stock up the fridge with so many soft drinks because people keep taking them from the fridge, while she herself was removing half the stock from the fridge and putting them away in the back storage. At that moment, I felt she was saying this intentionally to let me hear her, as her way of telling me that she was not pleased with the fact that I have removed the 2 soft drinks directly from the fridge. So at that point, I told the lady owner that I wanted to clarify that when I took the drinks from the fridge, I was telling her to charge me for it and that it didn’t feel nice to hear her make that comment so intentionally.?This is when we have experienced the most horrifying and unnatural turn of events. The lady owner got extremely angry at me and started yelling and shouting at me saying that she wasn’t talking about me, that she was talking about her other guests, etc. She could have very easily cleared up my mis-understanding in one nice sentence. Rather, she was ready to bite my head off and was talking (more like yelling, shouting) at me ten times louder than my voice.?I was so shocked by her behavior that I said I just wanted to clarify any potential mis-understanding about my taking the soft drinks, which I was telling them to charge me for, and that I actually did that as a gesture to be helpful since they looked so busy (obviously a huge mis-judgement on my part). ?The lady owner would not let this go and kept on yelling and arguing with me, her voice escalating louder and louder every second. I told the owner that we took the time to visit their restaurant and did not appreciate being treated like this. To this comment, the male owner jumped in and said that fact has nothing to do with this matter. Neither the lady nor the male owner offered one single word of apology nor made any attempts to provide explanation for their rude behavior, nor try to rectify this intense situation. The lady owner having her say just ran off and hid in her room after having her furious tantrum with us.?Although extremely disturbed by what just happened, as we have never experienced such rudeness ever in our entire lives, we still managed to complete the remainder of the meal in silence, all the while feeling ill at ease and uncomfortable. (FYI, my entire family and I suffered from indigestion later this same day due to this incident). After the meal, I paid for it at the counter and left the restaurant with my family, and not one single person at the restaurant acknowledged that we were leaving their restaurant, and no one (owners, staffs) even bothered to say a simple “thank you or goodbye”.?I am a firm believer that the most important part of any meal at any restaurant is quality of service. However, the level of horrible service we have experienced from this restaurant is completely unacceptable. From the many restaurants we could have chosen from at Gapado Island, I certainly feel choosing this restaurant is the one mistake I will live to regret. This unpleasant and rude encounter was bad enough to leave a bad image of the entire Gapado Island for us, while at the same time ruined a perfectly peaceful and happy family trip. All in all, it was a very unpleasant experience from beginning till the end at this restaurant, and I strongly do not recommend this restaurant to anyone visiting Gapado Island.
This is the place you can hug, kiss and take photos with teddy bear. Jeju Teseum is Korea's first and largest teddy bear museum. If you likes Teddy bear this is the place must visit in Jeju Island.

This is the first UNESCO world heritage that we visited in Korea. Walking distance about 1km, so be prepared to wear the comfort shoe. Some area a bit dark so be careful. Overall nice experience to visit this nature cave.

This is the first tourism that I visited during staying in Jeju Island. I went there around last October. At the same time  I went there since this island is one of the seven wonder. This lava tube actually make me very curious since it has so many education things. I went there with my mom which was 70 years old. Eventually we arrive in this place, this lava tube is wet and slippery so be careful when you go along with elderly. At the same time, you should wear proper shoes and mind your steps.So many interesting knowledge you will get inside this lava cave, beside you can visit museum close to this place.
This is the first spot we visited, we also tried the soap making program which is very interesting. The green tea fields are wonderful as well

This is probably my first 1-star review on TA. Much regretted visit and the only saving grace is that this place is right next to the Osulloc Tea Museum. We were drawn to this place after very good experience at the Innifree Green Cafe at Myongdong and we expected the same (if not better) at this concept store.Product - any Innisfree shops in myeongdong or duty free can offer you a better range at much better price. As Jeju was the last leg of my trip, I was planning to make most of my innisfree purchase in this store but they don?셳 carry much range here. I don?셳 remember there was onsite tourist refund as well (like how it is in Myeongdong) - another reason not to plan your shopping here.Food - I ordered a 18000krw main dish (named herdsman?) with some cold sausages, potato mash, rice balls and orange. The presentation was really pretty but it tasted nothing special. If you are looking for good looking food and great taste at the same time, you have better chance at Myongdong innisfree Green cafe. The other two pretty drinks we ordered were not worth a mention as well. Service - We were there at 450pm and all the soap making stations were occupied. We were told by a staff the soap making would only take 15mins and the place would close at 6pm. so we decided to wait at the cafe and return when the crowd lessen. At 525pm, a staff stopped me at the cashier when I tried to purchase the soap making set. She said that they have closed the soap making station at 520pm. And then another staff came by and said the station was closed at 5pm (?!). I am not sure exactly what time the station closed as there was no sign in the store and the staff were telling different things. The store closed at 6pm sharp and the staff can?셳 wait to have all the guests out by then - this I am sure. This place is a sad contrast to the Osulloc Tea Museum next door.

This is one of my favorite oreums (volcanic hills) on Jeju!!It is not exactly close to anything so be ready to travel quite a bit.  It is also a steep hike, but each step that takes your higher gives you more and more of a view. I am telling you the negative up first but I am also telling you...it is worth it.  *On the weekends (depending on the season) you will often find coffee trucks parked at the bottom parking lot.  You cannot count on this as they come and go...but if they are there, it will be a nice treat for you.*This oreum is also host to my favorite festival in Korea.  Jeju Fire Festival.  Thousands and thousands of people come to this oreum to say goodbye to the past memories and to welcome spring.  It is a seriously amazing event.  Fire, fireworks, food, beer, shopping tents, performances.....absolutely a fantastic event.

This is not really part of our tour in Jeju but since I researched on how to enjoy the tour with 30+ friends, I chanced upon this garden maze near Manjanggul lava tubes site (as in 500m away only).I really recommend this to friends and families who'd like to solve a mystery together and have fun doing it. The price in finishing the maze is a banner and the right to be the first to ring the bell.Please try the ice cream at the exit. You'll enjoy it after an exhilirating yet fun game (30 minutes estimated)

This is my second time I see this Nanta Show. The first time was in Seoul couples of years ago. Each time it never failed to amaze me. Very exciting and energetic show played by 5 showmasters. Located at Nanta Theatre about 10 kilometers away from Jeju City. Entrance fee normally 50,000 won but we managed to get only 30,000 won through our friend. Thanks to him. Really recommended.

This is my second time here. On my first trip, we can't get close to the cliff because of strong waves. This time round, I finally get to see the unique rock formations that made this a unesco site. A few photo spots in this area. I think 30mins viewing time is enough.

This is my first time visiting a cave and this is an extraordinary cave where this is actually a LAVE Tube which was formed 1million years ago. The open to public is only a section of its 5km length as a protection to its other natural environment and that is why it is labelled as the UNESCO Natural Heritage. The entrance to the 1km tube is a 100m long flight of stairs. Upon entering, the internal is wet and cold when visiting at this season (starting of spring). Other days would be still wet but temperature would be around 10-20degree C. The length of the tube excursion is just nice for family of elderly and young. My family (Mum, brother, wife and me) had a nice time inside the tube and although it is quite hard to take beautiful pictures, the experience is definitely immense.However, most of the time my mum is trying to avoid the water on the floor (do not worry it is not as slippery but it is on some areas), she did not notice much of the natural formation of the lava flow and lava stalagmites. The tube is well lit but it is recommend to bring torchlight to shone on areas above to see properly. Beware of the top water flowing down, that is why there is water on the floor. Overall, i feel that it is educational for the young and good walk for the elderly. To tour the place, i recommend to wear tracking shoe or covered shoe to prevent water or slipping. Else you will not enjoy the beauty of the tube. We had lunch at the nearby restaurant and it is a hearty meal. Lastly, i really enjoy the visit and definitely visit again in future, i hope you too!

This is my first ever hike and it was a real learning experience. Make sure to bring proper hiking shoes as the trail is VERY rocky and it can be easy to lose your footing and hurt your ankles. Walking stick is useful for the decent because it is MURDER on the knees. Coming down was much harder for me than going up. The view of Jeju at the top is amazing. But it was really crowded and I felt that the lake itself was a bit of a letdown looking like it was half drained... But overall, great hike and it's a good hike for first-timers! Bonus: I got to see a baby deer!

This is my favourite one of the three waterfalls i visited in Jeju! (April 2018)This place consist of three level waterfalls. The first level you will only see the waterfall if it has rained enough and the waterlevel is high enough to create the waterfall. The second one is the biggest of the three levels. It can be seen from two places. First is by the staircase and upclose. The second one is going over the bridge and after that (stone) stairs up on your rightside after crossing over the bridge. You can get a great view for the 2nd waterfall!The third and last level is the furtherst and the smallest one of all. If you are not fit enough or you can't walk very well, I advise to skip this one as there are a lot of stairs to go down and up afterwards.The first 2 levels are good enough to get a great view out of the place.

This is enormous highly worthwhile visiting. While I've visited caves around the world this is the first time I've seen lava tubes. They are huge you could drive a semi trailer through most of them. Defiantly worth seeing just for this aspect.It's quite wet on the floor of the cave, while you won't get wet, there are puddles of water. The ground is extremely uneven in places so good footwear is essential.There is heaps of signage in English on how they were formed.Highly worthwhile.
