This is an honest review which I?m only leaving because we weren?t allowed to leave the garden until we promised to give it a TripAdvisor review! Usually I?m much too lazy for such antics.First things first, I think it?s admirable what Bum-young Sung (the owner) has dreamt up and achieved over fifty odd years working here. I also think he has developed very sharp entrepreneurial acumen over this time - the entry fee is 12000 won and thousands of people (us included) seem to be happy to fork this out given the decent ratings Spirited Garden has achieved.Is it worth it? I?d have to say no for the following reasons:1) the garden is actually very small (you can wonder through it in 15-20 minutes).2) even though the trees are nice to look at (debatable given how some of the trees are shackled to metal frames), there are lots of signs imploring you to see the deeper meaning and philosophical undertones of the plants and stones, many of which didn?t really make a lot of sense.3) the owner will probably come to meet you at some point which seems superficially like a nice touch, but it did feel a bit mechanical - he would then get a phone call about some new guests coming into the park and suddenly have to dash off (probably to make sure they left a good TripAdvisor review)All in all, there?s a lot of great nature to see in Jeju, especially if you want to get away from the chaos and ponder the meaning of life, but why not climb up Mt Hallasan or do an Olle trail instead, and then go and spend your 12000 won on a present for yourself

This is an amazing market which sells almost everything you can think of. We went with the objective to enjoy some local snacks, get some hallabong tangerine and some jeju chocolate for our friends back home. Although the season for tangerine is over, there are still many available in the market. Prices for the tangerine are quite consistent so we just bought from the first few stalls we saw. There is not many brands for the jeju chocolate so we just picked one and we were told to compare prices with different stalls. For the same brand and quantity, I was quoted 7k, 8k and 10k korean won by 3 different stalls. We ended up buying from one of the biggest stalls in a corner. That said, I do encourage you to buy from the market. I found the same chocolate at the airport and it was selling at 15k korean won. We were too tired to get any local snack in the end but if I ever go back, I will try the seafood restaurant in the market. Was told they serve the cheapest and freshest sashimi in Jeju.

This is a weak but personal reason to visit this bridge, that is to say, it featured in the first Korean Drama series I ever watched. To put it in a nutshell, the guy followed the girl all the way to Jeju-do in order to convince her he was the one for her. The bridge scene featured just after they landed on the island, so it was just nice to see it in person as part of our stay here. There's not much more to say - I guess other people would have other reasons to visit. As a bonus we spotted women divers going out in their gear so that was some cultural aspect to the visit.

This is a fun place to visit. I wouldnt get out of my way to see it, but if you are in Jungmun and have an hour, its a fun place to see. The part I liked best are the Teddy Bears in   historical situations  . Like the first moon landing,  the discovery of the Terracotta Army, the fall of the Wall in Berlin etc.

This is a difficult review to write - the vegetation and environment at Hallim Park is great but my visit was ruined by seeing the way that the animals of the park were being treated.Firstly the Macaw House, an extra 1000krw to enter a large, hot greenhouse full of gorgeous birds in tiny wire cages with no vegetation or shade from the scorching heat.  There was a small black skinned pig in a cage less than 1m long.  Some animals were showing clear signs of distress and in two cases I was seriously concerned that animals were suffering severe heatstroke in a room that was exceedingly hot (34C outside and hotter in the house).The 'Beautiful Bird Garden' is a similar story - birds in cages with little shade, clear mite infections and stress related loss of plumage.  There were a few lucky peacocks able to roam freely but most were in tiny pens (10-15 per pen).  The facilities were not well maintained and the lack of shade is shocking given the heat of the Jeju summer.This was the most depressing experience I've had in a park - I've seen better cared for animals in developing nations.  The conditions at this park bring shame on Jeju and the nation when it appears that plants are treated better than animals.  To make any claims the Hallim Park is an ecological park is rubbish based upon this!If you care for the welfare of animals I would strongly urge you to avoid and express you anger to the local government.

This incredible cave flew with lava before. It is typical Jeju world heritage and must visit. The lava flew through all the tunnels and forms interesting geographic features. And another lava melted the roof of the channel and runs down to the first layer of lava. As usual, 2000 for an adult ticket.

This hike round trip, if stopping at the witseoreum shelter is about 5.8 miles round trip.  But a better way is to go up Eorimok trail (2.9 miles) and come back down via Yeongsil trail from Witseoreum Shelter (2.3 miles) Constant uphill to the top, good views of the mountains and the city below after halfway mark, and clean fresh air make this hike very worthwhile.  the hike up Eorimok trail consists alternating thick square studded steps, Boardwalk, and grave bedded large stones.    The first half is rather boring.  You hike up through the forest and have a recurring doubt about the trail you have chosen.  However, once you leave the trees, the view opens up and while it isn't majestic, it is a very pretty view to soak in during the remainder of the trail.    There is a lookout post that provides a sweeping view of the city below, and if there are low clouds you will be above it giving you an even more amazing view.   At the shelter you can use the restroom and buy cup noodle soup at around 11am and then start the descend down Yeongsil Trail.  This trail provides a view of the opposite side of the mountain and also has a lookout post that is rather awesome, especially when clouds are speeding past you.  Since we had friends drop us off at the Eorimok trail and pick us up at the Yeongsil trail, transportation wasn't a problem.  But at the Yeongsil trailhead we saw plenty of taxis waiting for business.

This high peak volcano is worth going for climbing... We went with my friend early march, the path was still snowyall the way!  Better to bring some equipement although it is possible to rent shoes at the convenient store down there.We were in march in a very low touristic season so it was quite nice to hike under the frozen pine trees with a beautiful blue sky. I think in high season on weekend, it could be crowdy! As it is a volcano, the walk is really sportive, meaning 6-10% continously during 2h. Get the first plane area, bring some candy bar or fruit, water of course, you will be enjoy this break on the roof of south Korea :=)

This Hallasan Fried Rice is a must have, must Go, must try, if you are in Udo Island. It is available at the 'Pungwon' restaurant. It is about 20mins walking from the harbour. If you are driving, key in the Tel no. 7841894 in your GPS device.First you will have to order either Black pork or cuttlefish according to your preference. There is a minimum number of portions to order based on the number of pax. There were 4 of us and we order 2 Pork and 1 Cuttlefish. We will begin by BBQ the meat. Until we are about halfway through, you can order the rice from the staff. The staff will put aside some meat and start by cooking the rice. The whole idea of Hallasan Fried Rice is that the staff will tell you the story about Mount Hallasan and the islands nearby; all these while making the rice into the shape of a mountain. He will then pour in the egg mixture and meat and cheese... and after numerous of flipping the rice, it's done. Fret not if you don't understand Korean, they have Chinese staff who can do the story telling in Mandarin. The process of hearing about the story is very interesting coupled with the visual of the staff cooking the rice. Not to mention, it tastes damn good too!

This beach was absolutely breathtaking! The sparkling fine sand, emerald clear water, and green hills all around made for a perfect beach day! Unlike what was stated in previous reviews from July 2019, we never had any problems with being able to swim freely and as far out as desired. There was also no line set out not to cross. This is the first beach I've been to with provided shading tents and umbrellas, but it was definitely nice for when we wanted a short break from the sun! We also never had to pay to use these, so I'm not sure if that is something only done during the busy season. The beach was not over crowded, especially at low tide, and it was easy to find little secluded areas if you wanted to be away from the majority of people. Locals were walking and swimming around to clean up trash, so it was honestly one of the cleanest beaches I have been to! Plenty of yummy restaurants to eat at, as well as bars for those wanting to stay out late and still have a view of the water. Be warned, there are no stores close by that sell towels, sunglasses, or other beach essentials, so make sure you are fully prepared! Definite   must see   while in JeJu!

This 6 KM (one-way) hike begins steeply, with nicely laid-out stairs climbing up through a beautiful, dense forest of oaks and maples.  It is very peaceful here, and our early (8 AM) start put us on the trail ahead of the crowds that showed up later in the day.  Most of the elevation gain -- total about 700M -- is accomplished in the first third of the hike.  The reward is a lovely stroll with some ups and downs through open meadows for the remainder of the hike to the Witse Oreum shelter.  Two springs are available if you need water on the way (but fill your water bottle directly:  I saw people drinking from the dippers hanging by one of the springs).  Views of the Halla crater wall and sweeping views downslope, of other parasitic cones and the sea, can be spectacular here on a clear day.  We went back down the Eorimok trail to our rental car, but other hikers we met recommended a one-way hike up the Yeongsil Trail (not so long) and then down the Eorimok (but then you have to take a bus or have two cars to do a shuttle).  Neither trail goes to the top of the crater, those areas being closed for extensive restoration.  However, the views were fantastic and I don't feel that I missed out on anything except a hard climb.

There's a lot to try and absorb in this open air museum. Maybe too much for your average tourist. I mean the somewhat authentic reproductions were cool for the first three or four structures. I enjoyed having a window into what life was like for peasants 100 - 300 years ago and/or the actors who currently play them in historical television dramas. However the minutia became simply overwhelming especially since there was a tendency to focus on the details as if everyone lived and breathed Korean archaeology. There was also a fairly obvious and persistent attempt to commercialize on cheesy trinkets. Some of the   traditional wares   were okay but I think you can get better quality at lower prices elsewhere. The same can be said for the food. The reenactments of wedding ceremonies and shaman rituals were entertaining and the kids could ride ponies. All in all I was glad to end my tour of this facility. It was a rather pricey way to spend an hour or two. If you were in the area or you have a passion for such things maybe give it a try. However I think there are far better ways to spend your time on Jeju. *You can catch bus 720 at the Bus Terminal for 3300 Won. The trip takes a little over an hour:http://www.rome2rio.com/s/Jeju-si/Jeju-Folk-Village-Museum*Here's a Jeju Weekly piece that might give you a better idea of what this place is all about:http://www.jejuweekly.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=4196

There were sooo many people  and the view was also not that great. I couldn't even take a proper picture. First i wasn't even sure if this is the right place, because it didn't look like the pictures i saw online.Go there if you want to have a walk at the cost (2000 won admission fee) and en passant you can look at the cliffs.Going there by bus is not really convenient. The bus station is a bit far and the bus comes about every hour (timetable not reliable).By the way this kind of view you can also have at the Phoenix island (near ilchulbong).

There is a stair to reach to top to this extinct volcano. It seems easy at first but you will need to be prepared to reach its top. They put places to sit through the course.Since I was there during summer time, I sweated a lot. But reaching the top pay all physical efforts!Then you can walked down in order to see (and get enjoyed by) the friendly ladies who dive! It was nice to see that they also served the seafood they've just captured! You need to see them because they are now just a few and how knows if there will be more of them in the future.Remember 1: the presentations of this ladies happen in specific times (I got their 13:30pm presentation, so I had to walk fast up and down the volcano in order to see them)Remember 2: you should pay a ticket to get inside the park.I truly recommend you to reach both the top of the volcano and see the women divers presentation.

There is a lot more than meets the eye here. People first wonder but then realize they are glad to visit The Glass Castle. It is a museum and park of glass works by local artisans and crafts people and the collection is vast, so vast it takes a while to see everything. There is a diverse array of glass work in gardens, themes, and museum displays of varying quality and rarity around the park.This includes large outdoor sculptures such as the yellow submarine at the entrance or crystal skulls, and glass displays around the park. We were impressed by the size of the park and diverse collection of work. They also have workshops here and some hands on experiences.I would recommend this place as a worthy place to visit while on Jeju, near the O'Sulluc Tea Museum and Plantation which only 5 minutes away.

There are three main waterfalls in the south of Jeju and this was the first one we saw, it is the only one by the sea and is about 15 minutes walk from downtown Seogwipo. There is a nice little park before the entrance to the waterfall.We went in the afternoon and it was crowded with many people taking pictures. Would suggest going early in the morning (they open at 8am), better for pictures with the sun shining on the waterfall and less people. Bring proper footwear or shoes you don't mind getting wet as it is very rocky and you can get wet from the spray. Entrance fee is 2000 won and it is a short walk down some stairs to the waterfall.

There are some fictional characters that you and me adore and love during our childhood and yet still relish even though we have become adults. Hello Kitty is certainly one of them, and is a favourite of one of my children. However, the good part is not every visitor to Jeju and the locals are a fan of Hello Kitty, so the Hello Kitty Island Museum is not on the itinerary of most tour companies, and hence it?s not crowded.Getting there and fees: Hello Kitty Island Museum, opened in late 2013, is located in the south west part of Jeju (GPS code/coordinate 7926114).  Not to worry if you cannot find space in the small open-air car park outside the Museum because there?s another huge open air car park below the small one. Parking is free. Entrance fee to the Museum is 12,000 won for adult, 11,000 won for teenagers and 10,000Won for children. However, my family and I made use of the discount coupon for entrance fees from the Hertz car rental discount booklet.The Museum/Attraction: when we entered, we were immediately greeted by a large hall where there?s a circular cone of Hello Kitty toys, a photo-taking stop with the entire Hello Kitty family and Hello Kitty?s house where she?s standing at the balcony welcoming you and beckoning you to enter the door into the various exhibition halls. There are 3 levels with the exhibition halls on the first and second level, the gift shop on the first level, the Hello Kitty Caf챕 on the second level and the 3D theatre and an outdoor gallery on the third level. To cover everything, including a meal at the Hello Kitty Caf챕, would easily take about 2-3 hours. In the true sense, this Hello Kitty Museum is a museum ? there are exhibits of anything related to the adorable Hello Kitty. There are several themed exhibition halls on the first and second level e.g. History Hall, Art Education Hall, Music Education Hall, World Gallery Hall, Hello Kitty Room, Constellation Education Hall, amongst others.So we took plenty of photographs and selfies. I particularly like the exhibit of Hello Kitty represented by 26 countries (I found my own country) as well as the huge room containing the huge Hello Kitty bed where one of my children got the Hello Kitty toy snatched away by a toddler.At the Hello Kitty Caf챕 ? with Hello Kitty ribbon windows, Hello Kitty-themed sofas and Hello Kitty engraved tables ? you have to try the Hello Kitty Waffle Set, green tea latte, coffee or  hot chocolate (the 3 hot drinks have a profile of Hello Kitty on the surface), Hello Kitty Strawberry Cake and Cheesecake. Really yummy stuff!Whether you are a fan or not of Hello Kitty, I think this Museum is a fun attraction to visit and be acquainted with Hello Kitty. However, be prepared to ?share? the premises with many joyful and lively children and teenagers. But if you are not a fan and if you have limited time in Jeju, then I suppose you could spend that 2-3 hours elsewhere.

There are 3 waterfalls near my guesthouse and I chose to visit Jeongbang Waterfall first; no special reason as I have a direct bus to there. Admission fee for adult is 2000 won, and youth will be 1000 won (the ticket ahjumma will ask for your birth year). So you will have to walk down a few stairs and cross over stones to reach the waterfall. It was cooling to just sit down here and enjoy the waterfall. But please remember to wear cover shoes in order to prevent falling. Not only you can take photos with the waterfall, there?s a connecting sea right beside and you can take beautiful picture. Solo travellers please remember to bring a selfie stick :)

There are 3 memorial towers, one of Kim Man Duk, civil uprising volunteers, and one of patriot at the end of Joseon dynasty. There is Kim Man Duk's grave stone, original one which moved here because of road construction in its original place. This is located in Sara-bong(hill) park. It is very low hi,, but you can enjoy beautiful sunrise on the top of hill. Even day time, I could enjoy nice view toward Jeju international port. I recommend walk around the hill first then visit Mochungsa afterwards, The Sarabong walk path is part of Olle #18. There are many locals who work out here. You can feel like a local!

There are 3 levels for the visitors to try. The first one is the easiest before you are engaged in a more challenging maze. It is fun if you have 2 groups of children/ people visiting this place. Not only that they can help their group members to find their way, the competition between the 2 groups makes it more exciting. Finally, the 3rd maze is the most difficult but you will have no problem. There is a clue/ help (you will see, it is a secret here) when you really need it. I think, the children managed all 3 maze puzzles in 1 hour.

The Yongmeori coastline was not on my list of places to see/go when I first planned my taxi tour itinerary, but I was persuaded to go by my guide, Mr Lee Hong Min. I am so glad that he brought us here as it turned out to be the highlight of the tour for me.There are 2 ways to access the coast - and you'll either begin or end up at the very impressive looking stone   stairway  . To walk the coastline, you don't need to be superfit as it's not a tough hike, but some might find the rocks to be uneven and slippery so do watch your step even as you take in the beautiful scenery. The round trip takes about 30 mins for the superfit and about an hour for families.The scenery of Yongmeori is breath-taking, especially for someone who's never seen such rocky formations before. Turning every corner drew exclamations of awe from us and we took dozens of pictures throughout. You can really see where the sea has eroded away the cliff, leaving craggy sights that vaguely remind me of the Grand Canyon. You can even see the inhabitants of the sea that were left 'stranded' at low tide, waiting for the high tide to return - small fish, oysters and mussels, and some weird cockroach like crustaceans scurry along the rocks. Haenyeo or women divers set up stall along the coast so if you fancy a fresh seafood snack, you can feast on the rocks for a unique experience unlike any other.Tip: There are no toilets once you pass the small stalls set-up before the attraction entrance as this is natural scenery attraction so do make sure all in your party go first before you enter.

The walking trail at Yongmeori Coast is just a few hundred meters (~700 m) long, but the layered sedimentary structures made from rocks and volcanic ashes, and dramatic shapes created by erosion from hard ocean-waves and wind make it breathtaking art of nature and truly resembles Geopark. It is known that the site is indeed designated as one of the nine Jeju sites certified by the Global Geopark Network in 2010. Personally, this is one of my best scenic places in Jeju in the view of both geology and photography lover.The part of these cliffs appeared stretched out from nearby Sanbangsan Mountain. The meaning of Yongmeori in Korean is Dragon Head. Interestingly, the rough surface of rocks and dramatic shapes formed by rocks due to erosions make it look like a dragon's head going underwater.This part of Jeju is also famous for women sea-drivers. During our visit, we have got an opportunity to try out a few fresh kinds of seafood sold by Korean grandmothers along the coastline. Another attraction near this cliff is the huge shipwreck which is actually a reproduction built as the Hamel Castaway Memorial to commemorate a Dutch sailor (Hendrick Hamel). It is said that he was drifted to the shore of Jeju by a typhoon in 1653. He then wrote a book providing the West some insights into Joseon Korea for the first time. All together this place is very impressive and must not be missed.

The walk in the cave is about 1km, which is pretty long. Please be careful as the cave is long, dark and slippery. In fact I think I spent more time looking on the ground than at the actual cave walls. But safety always comes first, and you can always stop at certain junctures to take a good look at the walls/ceilings.Nonetheless, the lava shelves and cave features were a wonderful sight to behold, especially for someone who appreciates geography/geology like me :) I have went to this attraction twice, and both times I have found the visit worthwhile.

The teddy bear museum is exactly what it's title states.  It's teddy bears in every shape and size.  The first area has historical teddy bears, dating back as far as the turn of the century (1900's).  The second section is works of art redone with teddy bears and finally, there is an outdoor exhibit including a 9 meter tall teddy bear that makes a showing every hour on the hour.  Young kids that like teddy bears and such will have a great time visiting here.  My daughter adored everything.  It is a little pricey, but if you rent a car to get around they often give you a book with coupons for the various attractions on the island or you can book in advance online at a discount price.

The tea museum is located on the western side of the island and represents the showpiece of the O'Sulloc tea   empire   in South Korea.  There are a number of O'Sulloc tea cafes all over South Korea which specialize in green tea and also sell sweets as well.  There is a large parking area to accommodate a number of cars and visitors.The tea museum consisted of four   features   from what I could surmise.  First you get a decent view of the western part of the island by walking up the stairs to the roof of the museum itself.  The views aren't that interesting but you do get a good view of the surrounding area.  Second the museum itself describes the tea growing/making/serving process.  Third the cafe/gift shop inside seems to attract the most number of visitors.  You can buy teas and other desserts like you would at any other O'Sulloc cafes.  However it does sell many other items - various teas and more.  Finally another attraction is the tea plantation itself.  O'Sulloc seemingly has a small portion of their plantation on-site that you can walk through (note there may be snakes in the plantation) to get a sense of how the green tea leaves are grown.There is also an Innisfree store right next to the tea museum but we did not visit it.The tea museum is worth a trip though I wouldn't go out of the way to visit it as you can always partake in O'Sulloc teas in various locations in South Korea.

The Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak has 2 main attractions. The first is obviously the climb to the peak itself. The second is the Woman Divers at the black sand beach at the bottom. We spent about 3 hours here and it was just barely enough. The climb is actually not that bad for the physically fit. The steps are steady and most are stone paved or have wooden stairs. There were quite a few elderly ladies/gents climbing too. Rest areas with benches are plentiful, so there really is no reason why you would not try for the top if you have the time. :-) Two thirds of the way up, you will see a big resting area with a marvelous view of the city below. Once you are up at the peak, you will also be able to see the city view AND into the crater. The climb back down is very safe with well made wooden staircases. Regarding the Woman Diver show at the bottom, I found the show to be a little underwhelming and a bit too touristy. However, it was still an interesting experience to see divers selling fresh seafood off the beach. If you have limited time, I would recommend that you focus on the hike/view, and just spend a couple of minutes to browse through the woman diver area. I think the Seongsan Iichulbong is a must-see in Jeju.

The Seongpanak trail that goes to the summit is curentlyclose, until July 31st. I went all the way to the start of Seongpanak  trail and had to take 2 buses to go Gwaneumsa trail.The hike was nice but difficult. The first part was nice, 3,1km of normal hiking, until we reached the hard part, very steep, with stairs and rock. The climb fromSamgakbong shelter to the summit was not too hard, but a bit warm because of the sun. It as very humid, so be sure to pack a lot of waterand food as there are no vendors on the trail. It easy to reachthe trail by bus, but we took a taxi back to our hotel as we were too tired. A very good exercice and a good hike. I would doit again! ;)

The rocks surrounded by the island have different size and have eroded for years. But the most interesting thing is that rocks are eroded into different levels of cylinders, so it is worth to spend a couple of minutes there taking photos and have a look. Moreover, there are paths for visitors to walk around the edges of the island to have different look of the rocks. It is the margin of Jeju, so when the wave flaps the cliffs, it creates a huge noise. At first, I thought it was something like weapons exposed, my heart pumped faster than normal. After I recognize it is only the wave hits the cliffs, I can clearly experience that how the level of power that the nature can be. It was an unforgettable experience.So, if you have an iPhone which contains the program of Live Photo, try to open it before you take photos. It is because you can record the energetic movement of wave in your photo.

The queue was long starting from midnight. The tag was given starting 2:30am. The limit was for 1300 first come first served. The waiting was in 2 celcius temperature. The trek up started at 5:30am in an orderly manner in a hushed procession like atmosphere. At the top of the plateau there were decks facing the direction of the sunrise. All was ready for the first sunrise of 2020. Unfortunately it did not happen. The clouds was too thick and we headed back an hour after the sunrise time. Was I disappointed? Not really. The whole experience was exhilarating, the wait, the trek, the anticipation of the sunrise. It was a memorable experience which I hope to repeat one day.

The moment I set my eyes on this island, I knew I was in heaven. The water looked extraordinary blue and the view was nothing short of a perfect dreamy scenery. We took a day trip on the ferry from jeju. On the island, we took the hop on hop off bus. Take any bus, doesn't really matter.. They will then tell you which color buses u can hop onto at the next destination along with a list of places they will stop at. I think it costs around 2200 won. The island was crowded specially with all the bikes but still it is not to be missed. The first stop was the udo peak. A hike of around 30 mins to a lighthouse from where you can see the entire islans. The view of the sunrise peak on jeju all along the hike was incredible! Then the bus took us to 2 beaches..one was a black sand beach which had a little cave but tides were high that day. We missed the 2nd beach and went to the last one with white sand. This beach was quite close to the port and we walked to the port from here along the coast. It was a beautiful walk and less crowded.There are lot of shops and cafes in front of the last beach.

The maze park is suitable for photo-shoots, the beautiful alley filled with green-leaves and also stone-walls. There are 3 maze available in this place. The first one is the easiest one, round shaped, and we can have a shortcut just by going to the side way. The side way also makes us easier to travel through the second maze. The third maze is the hardest, where it doesn't have a shortcut, and we have to go through the map by ourselves. Interesting if we are travelling with our little ones. On my last trip here at the end of September 2015, it was raining so bad, the wind was also very strong. So avoid to come here when the weather forecast predicts the weather to be raining.
the maze is not that big, a few turns here and there & u can practically memorize the route already. nevertheless, quite challenging for first timer like me. ^^

The marker for Routes 13, 14 and 14-1 are located in one spot. We got confused at first that we ended up completing abour 2-3km of Trail 14 until we got to another marker that we realized we were following the wrong path. We went back to the spot and started looking for the 14-1 trail. We spent the first half of the day doing Trail 14.When we headed to Trail 14-1 which was the intial plan, it was past noon already so the sun was up and it was hot (we did the trail on a summer day). It was a cool experience because the trail will bring you to the peak where you get a great 360 degree view of Jeju! It will take you inside a forest. You might even meet some horses along the way. By the time you'll get to the midpoint, which is the Osulloc Museum, you will realize how much you miss civilization and strangers. The trail will connect you to nature. You'll even find yourself in a dense forest! There are a lot of blue/orange ribbons so you won't be lost. This trail taught me to simply trust and find the blue/orange ribbons and enjoy/embrace nature wherever the trail (or life in general) may take you. Haha. This is definitely off the beaten path but it makes your Jeju tour even more special and truly your own. I would want to do more of the Olleh Trails in the future :)

The Manjanggul Lava Cave was a very large lava tube cave.  A 1km section in the middle of the 7.5km lava cave was open for groups to tour.  We found it an amazing place to visit, and an outstanding example of a lava cave, but since it is a lava tube cave, visitors should expect the following when visiting this attraction:1) unlike limestone caves, generally created by water over long periods of time, lava caves do not usually have the stunning formations (ie ? stalactites, stalagmites, etc).  They have their own unique, highlights, but are not as colorful.  Such is the case with this lava cave.2) the cave is very softly lit (not brightly lit) and has a very uneven floor, so walking takes attention and concentration.  Anyone with mobility problems should be very sure they can handle all the steps, uneven ground, and low lighting.3) the cave is cold and damp and the ceiling drips constantly.  The amount of dripping is directly related to the recent rain amounts received.  Since lava rock is very porous, the rain drips through the rock into the cave.4) the cave lists that it is ?restricted? access.  I don?t know what that means but I recommend finding out if you are trying to visit it on your own.  We were the first group to arrive that day and we had the cave to ourselves for about 30 min before other groups started showing up.  It made our experience even better, but it is possible that only groups with pre-purchased tickets have access?5) aside from the sheer size of the cave (again, huge for a lava tube cave), the coolest feature for us was the large lava column at the far end of the cave.  The dark hole in the ceiling, where the lava flowed into the cave and made the large column was quite impressive.We visited this cave as part of a cruise ship tour.  For those looking at things to do from a ship, there are 2 cruise ports on the island, one in the south port and one in the north port.  Where you port could determine your itinerary since various and impressive sights are available close to either town/port.  This lava tube cave is in the north-east part of the island, and is listed as   restricted   so, again, before you try to visit on your own, you might want to make sure you will be able to get into it.Jeju Island has so much to offer ? large lava tunnel caves, waterfalls, craters, mountains, cliffs, black sand beaches, incredible fresh seafood, and more but they are spread throughout the island, so it is impossible to see all of them in one area or in a short amount of time.  Also, some of the attractions are restricted, so they might require group access to enter.  We concentrated on the east end of the island during our visit and found it to be similar to Hawaii in many ways other than the temperature, which was quite a bit cooler than Hawaii during our visit at the end of March (55 deg F was our high temp).

The kids found this easier than we adults! At 3,300 for adults we found this good value.  The history behind this place was interesting.  Founded by an Aussie from WA who was the first foreigner to the area in the 80's.  He is still alive and has done much for the people of Jeju.  He obviously likes cats there's one lazing around every corner at the entrance!  It's a kids thing really but I'm glad I did it.  The guy on the door spoke quite good English and was very engaging.

The Jeju Glass Castle was part of the itinerary of the group tour that I was part of. We spent more than an hour in the premises. We visited at daytime?I noticed that there a good number of spotlights so the Jeju Glass Castle must have a different ambience at night.I have mixed feelings about the Jeju Glass Castle.THE GOODThe Jeju Glass Castle is picturesque and very instagrammable. There are numerous displays that one can pose with. Many of the displays are quite feminine, though?very floral and colorful?girly, even. Most of the displays are outdoors including a small glass maze. Our trip was in December so it was cold but manageable. I liked the international glass displays?the Murano glass, especially because it reminded me of my aunt who had a significant number of pieces of this type of glass. THE BADFirst and foremost, I expected to see a palace or at least a castle straight out of a fairy tale. The Jeju Glass Castle is nowhere near a castle or palace. The buildings were plain and very utilitarian. The gardens were manicured but not palatial. It was more of a museum and a park, rather than a castle. Secondly, aside from signage that are in Korean or that mention the name of the place, there is nothing in the museum that shouts, ?I am in Jeju!? or ?I am in Korea!? for that matter. There is nothing in the museum that is intrinsically exclusive to the Jeju Glass Castle.Lastly, I was looking forward to try the glass comfort but the lock inside was broken and the door won?t keep closed. THE VERDICTI was able to take good photos of the displays?like I said, they were very instagrammable. Nevertheless, I do not see myself going back here just for the sake of it. It gets boring eventually, with little to do except to look at beautiful glass.

The first impression and experience was good. After a while, everything else looked the same. The same sea, mountains and stones, albeit in a different formation. There are beach bikes for rent, which I think will be fun but we didn't enjoy that because we had hired a taxi for the Jeju trip.

The first 3 days were full of heavy rain and drizzles. Went here on the 3rd day, it took us more than an hour on the bus to get there. And it still rained. The hill is gorgeous but all I can say is try to pick a day without rain because it was quite slippery (figures since we wore flip flops to avoid our sneakers from getting wet). From here we went to Pyoseon Folk Village which took another hour. So from Seongsan Ilchulbong we took bus no. 295 to Pyoseon Community Centre then changed to bus no. 212 to Pyoseon Folk Village.
The entrance fee was quite expensive. Bear was so cute. I like the history of Teddy bear. And it was impressive to see the first teddy bear in the world !! Near this museum, it was Chocolate factory.

The Dragon Head Rock was rather disappointing since the shape was difficult to visualize as a dragon head no matter which ever way we looked at it.  However for a brief stop, it is worthwhile for first time visitors.

The cave is very big, stairs at the entrance is quite steep, you might be a little bit out of breath here, but once inside it is manageable. The cave is spacious and well maintained, there is clear line for people to walk, there isn't much to see, after walking around 1km you will reach the end of the accessible part of the cave, people take pictures here and then walk back to the entrance.  It is a great place to explore a cave for the first time, my children loved it here. The temperature drop inside the cave, so bring warm jacket

The bridge during night time was nice. I saw this on the plane from Seoul to Jeju. At first I came to see the sea next to it, but then I suddenly saw the bridge and thought it looked beautiful. It really brightens up the dark.

The attraction is not so exciting but still worth a visit if it is your first time in Jeju. This attraction is also pretty near Jeju's Loveland, an interesting and popular attraction that is not mentioned in TripAdvisor.

The 5 day market is named because it opens every 5 days only. There are other 5 day markets in Jeju but this market is said to be the largest in Jeju with 1,000 over stalls. This market opens on the 17th and plus / minus 5 days before and after.Fret not if you missed the opening of this market. Because apparently the other 5 day markets are operate by the same stall owners. They rotate among the different markets and hence will be back to the same market after every 5 days.We went there on a morning and expected to spend the whole day there. But we were out in 2 hours.There are indeed many stalls in the market but many of them are carrying the same stuff. Clothings, household products, fruits and vegetables, kimchi, cooked food and of course Jeju mandarin oranges which are famous. Interestingly, pet dogs are sold alongside with fresh chickens. And ironically, there are stalls selling dog meat at the other end of the market.Same animal but different fate.We bought the famous mandarin oranges here although these are available at other places in Jeju as well. There are many similar-priced stalls selling this famous product in this market. We chose one of the varieties on display after sampling. It has a sweet aftertaste after the first tinge of sourness. The one we purchased is the 2nd most expensive type at $25,000 Won per 5 kg. There are other varieties at $30,000 Won per 5 kg and $15,000 Won per 10 kg etc.It?s a nice experience after all and I would say it?s worth a visit if you are in Jeju.

That was the first place we visited after arriving at Jeju. Really enjoyed the chill atmosphere. In September, the weather was windy and a bit cool but still loved it. We also stopped by at Delmoondo cafe.

thank you so much for the visit . at first we are so wondering how you paid 39000won for the admission. it is 10,000won per adult. we suggest  you should check again the ticket price and if you could find some mistakes or serious problem, please let me know that.

thank you for the visit. well , first of all we are so afraid of you were not so feel good at the teddy bear museum. however our museum consist of two main theme galleries. the history and the art.  and also there are extra gallery, Elvis concert theater and out door garden. we will take an effort to present visitor more exciting display and exhibition . thank you again and have a good day ^^

Teddy Bear Safari is the world?s first exhibition theme park with various real life-sized wildlife and marine stuffed animals and teddy bears. Moreover, you will also meet our teddy bears dressed in traditional clothes of countries around the world and as gods from Greek mythology. Lastly, some of our teddy bears will be dressed up as Korean celebrities whom you may be well aware of.

TAKE NOTE: If you are not healthy and dont usually do cardio, the step up will be absolute hell for you. The only way you can circumvent the hellish experience is if you wake up extra early and take your own sweet time to traverse to the top.We woke up at 6am after checking sunrise at 7:20am, and was living in a hotel 2 minutes away. As we want to experience the whole sunrise, we rush up the rising path. Big mistake. By the time we're halfway up, I had visions of my 42km route march in 1.5 days during my army stint, and had to take frequent rest stops on the way up.Once you reach the top, you'll see nothing but the sea in front of you and while you're tired, you're also excited to witness the sunrise.Which you COULD... if it was a cloudless morning. The clouds will ruin your day. We didn't get to see anything in the end, as it was so cloudy and drizzling a bit, but after staying for an hour after sunrise, we did get to see a few peeks of sunrays.It only cost 2000 won so well worth the price, but definitely check the weather forecast first. It feels terrible to have almost burst your heart only to see nothing but clouds. I do imagine the sunrise is heavenly if you actually get to see it though.

Sunrise peak in English, this volcanic cone is 182 metres high. That works out to about 25 stories which is roughly how high you have to climb to get there.And to get there early enough to get a good position, you need to get up pretty early. We woke at 4am for a 4.30 start (this after a 60km bike ride the day before and another 60 to come on the day. We went up rather more briskly than we had planned (exuberance?) and were one of the first to arrive.First, let me acknowledge the impressive steps, in stone and wood, that have been built to help people get to the top (and the separate staircase that leads you down). Kudos to the engineers and builders. They even thought of rest stops which also work well as photo opportunity spots.The amphitheater-style seats at the top are well-thought out too and provide a good view.Sunrise was scheduled for about 5.30 and a fair crowd had gathered by then.Unfortunately, the sky was overcast and we could only glimpse the sun as it occasionally peeped through the clouds. But it was spectacular nonetheless.There was no admission charge as we were up and down before the ticket booth opened at 7am.It is still worthwhile visiting even if you don't want to watch the sunrise.

Staying in Seogwipo, I was advised to take bus 780, with the first bus leaving about 6:30am or 7am & getting to Seongpanak around 7:30 or 8am. I thought about taking a taxi to get there earlier, but I found later in the day it wasn't necessary. I believe it's the same bus from Jeju City.There's a small carpark at the entrance and a little store with a few drinks and snacks on sale. Apart from the lunch hut near the summit (which only offered noodles with hot water & bottles of cold water), this was the only place to buy anything. So carry some food and water with you, enough to last 4 hours or so.It's a fairly pleasant walk. Most of the time you will be walking on ground or planks of wood, and at times there will be nothing but big rocks, although most people were walking. I think I was the only person with hiking boots.Yes it can be very steep at times but is by no means difficult, nothing more than a series of steps. Just take lots of rest breaks and you'll be fine. It should take anywhere from 2.5 to 3 hours to reach the cut-off mark (see next paragraph) then another 1 hour to the top, so as long as you leave before 9am or 10am it should be alright.Coming down can take anywhere from 2.5 to 3.5 hours in total.I thought the cut-off point was strange, having a man in an office stopping people trying to reach the summit after 1pm, especially when the sun doesn't go down until about 7pm. I would've thought that was plenty of time to get up and back. That's just Korea and their over-sensitive rules...Not a lot of scenery along the way, but it's nice to enjoy being surrounded by trees for most of the way. For the most part it will be quiet, although some of the locals spoke loudly or even had their phones out playing music which I thought was weird.A lot of Koreans seem to be on a mission to get it done as quickly as possible, and they certainly have the stamina to do it, so keep in mind at times you may have to deal with people almost pushing you aside to get past.The view from the top is worth the hike. You'll be extremely lucky to see the bottom (climb Seongnam if you want a nice view), but you're here to see the crater lake, which is quite lovely to see when the cloud clears.

Stayed at a hotel close to the street, and so I stumbled here after a hike to Mt Hallasan peak. Our driver Mr. Kim Choong Kun (nytaxi5445@hanmail.net) was very pleasant, patient, spoke English, informative, and even took pictures of us.

Sounds odd that it is actually my favourite attraction.. I love teddy bears. This place does not require much trekking like the sunrise peak, manjanggul cave, waterfall etc but it is a fantastic place to spend one or two hours just staring at the teddy bear exhibits with some even moving and each exhibit with a different theme. You get to see Elvis teddy bear performing   live   with his friends too. First time seeing teddy bear moving, wow experience for me. So u conquered the first maze and thought ?this will be a piece of cake?. Wrong. That first maze lured you into a false sense of security and subsequent mazes are a lot harder to transverse. Small island off the Jeju coast makes for a nice day trip/excursion from the main Jeju island. We enjoyed the climb up the one and only peak for excellent views, as well as some stunning coastal caves and cliffs, lighthouse, crashing surf, and volcanic rock. Several things that I didn't like about this place. First they completely do not respect nature, eg. There are a few chairs on top with Celine dion's titanic music playing! I guess Koreans think that makes the place more romantic but it completely ruins the experience for me. Then the crater itself is impressive but the entrance fee was 6000w per person which is a total rip off. If these two objections don't deter you from going then at least go early (we went at 8:30 on a Monday) and literally had the crater to ourselves for 15 minutes.

Seongsan Ilchulbong is a tuff cone that has been formed from not so old (5000 years old) volcanic eruptions. It is 180-meter-high and one can walk to the top. Note that it has been well accommodated: there are stairs starting from the bottom to the top so that the walk is fairly easy. It takes about an hour for going to the top and come back, depending of course on how long one stays up-hill to enjoy the view. The view is the main thing here. It is just amazingly beautiful!First of all, one should pay attention to the different rock formations, some of them, featuring interesting shapes (see one of the two pictures I shared). Second, it is really great to stop all along the way up to enjoy the view from Jeju (see the second of the pictures I shared). On the top, one gets an amazing view on the other side (i.e. the sea). I was there in the middle of the day (there was no other way out in my case), but I can fairly well imagine the extra in being there at sunrise or sunset.Finally, note that there is an entrance fee, but it is very reasonable (about 2 USD).Overall, I strongly recommend this place and the walk. One moreover should definitely try to be there at sunrise/sunset. Please make sure to have enough water (it was really hot on the day I walked there) and be prepared: it could be crowded. The place is quite popular. There is a good reason for Seongsan Ilchulbong to be one of the top attractions of Jeju Island.

Seogpanak is an awesome hike, can def recommend it! It takes about 3.5-4h one way, without long stops. Bring enough water and food with you and there aren't any shops. You're walking on lava / stones most of the time so not really recommendable for people with weak ankles. Overall the hike is awesome and def worth a day's trip!

Self-Drive Holiday in Jeju:Everyone loves going on holidays and I believe a great percentage of these do so on guided tours. Guided tours are fine where convenience is concerned; hotels, meals, itineraries, transport, flights, places of interests to visit, entrance fees etc. etc. are all taken care of by the tour company. As I had discovered decades ago, despite all the conveniences of a guided tour, there are drawbacks that would put one off such tours completely; not being able to sleep-in and wake up as and when you want, having limited time to enjoy the various places of interests or enjoy your lunch while taking in the magnificent scenery from a mountain top restaurant , having to put up with other travellers who simply cannot or are not bothered to be on time, not being able to visit or enjoy other interesting places that are rarely included in tour itineraries, to list a few. Ever since my first guided tour holiday overseas, I have opted for a self-drive holiday and I am very sure there are many out there who would love to do so too,  but refrained from doing so because of a lack of information and perhaps, apprehensive about what it would entail to do a self-drive holiday in a foreign land. This guide is to help dispel those apprehensions and provide the necessary information for you to successfully make that first self-drive holiday in the Honeymoon Island of Jeju, and hopefully, many more thereafter in other destinations of your dreams.Preparation:Many experts would advise, and rightly so, that you should first read up all the necessary information on driving at the destination that you will be holidaying in. However, in my opinion, what is more important is having the self-confidence to drive in a foreign land. Sometimes, things can go wrong, road and weather conditions can change to the extent that no pre-reading or preparation can help, but, with that very important self-confidence, it will see you through. You must also have a flexible mind set and be ready to accommodate changes when necessary ? only then will you be able to thoroughly enjoy your self-drive holiday. Having said that, I must say that driving in Jeju is a walk-in-the-park, quite unlike, for example, driving through the mountain pass between Sun Moon Lake and Hualien County in Taiwan ? that is a drive I would never recommend to the feint hearted.International Driving Permit ? you will need to obtain an International Driving Permit to be able to rent a car in Jeju, and for that matter, in most other countries. It can be easily obtained at AAS and it costs only $20.00 and is valid for one year. You would also want to search for information on all the places of interests and decide on which of those to visit during your stay in Jeju. This is to help you plan and minimize travelling time. These can be had at the Korea Tourism Centre at Samsung CentreChoice of Hotel ? There are many hotels catering to different needs and budgets to choose from. The one most often asked question is the location ? to stay in Jeju-si or Seogwipo-si? My experience tells me that it makes no difference ? it is just a matter of choice. If you are arriving in Jeju late at night, then, perhaps, you may wish to stay in a hotel that is near the airport, to minimize your night driving had you decided on a hotel in Seogwipo-si. We landed in Jeju at 2000 hrs, collected our car at 2100 hrs and drove to Seogwipo-si where our hotel was situated. It was a pleasant forty-five minute drive with guidance from the GPS unit.Car Rental Company:There are many car rental companies in Jeju, but you will most likely come across only a handful if you search the internet ? Kumho, AJ Rentals (AVIS), SIXT, Donga and Jeju Rent-a-Car. Do note, though, that there are more than a dozen of competing rental companies at the airport to choose from if you prefer to shop around for the best rates and cars upon your arrival. I book mine through AJ Rentals, not only because of the brand name, but it also provided the best rates among the others on the net and it did not require me to pay in advance upon confirmation of my reservation. To rent the car, you will need to have an International Driving Permit (obtain it from AAS), your local driving license and passport. You can pay either in cash or credit card. Type of Car:The type of car you choose is totally dependent on your preference and budget ? luxury or basic. However, do consider the available boot space that will be needed to accommodate your luggage. As a guide, the boot of a KIA K3 can accommodate only three large suitcases with no space for a smaller, fourth piece. In a situation where there are four adults, the smaller, fourth suitcase will have to share estate space in the back seat with two other passengers. The cost of rental is dependent on the type of car, number of days and the period of travel. As a guide, a KIA K3 cost approximately S$60.00 per day for 5 days during the holiday season in November. The rate includes insurance, CDW and the use of a English language GPS, with collection and return at the airport. The rates of the other rental companies that I surveyed were cheaper, however, I cannot vouch for their quality nor service support. You decide at your own risk. The overall condition of the car was good. The only ?defect? was the slight steering alignment problem but it was not something that would put us in danger at any time. Maps:Do you need a map when it is very likely that you will be relying on the GPS? YES! A map is necessary for planning your routes and selecting the places of interests to visit.You can easily obtain a detailed map of Jeju Island, with all the major highways and feeder routes from your local Korean Tourism office. You can also obtain these from the car-rental companies when you collect your car in Jeju. You can use it to plan your route, estimate the travel time and locate other possible places of interests that you don?t find on the standard tourist trail. You can use this same map to write down the telephone numbers of the places of interests that you plan to visit. You will need these numbers for keying into the GPS system to guide you to your destination. I made it a point to re-confirm that the telephone numbers are current by asking the hotel staff to extract the numbers from their computer system. This proved to be very useful. Collecting Your Car At The Airport:After clearing immigration and customs, proceed to gate 5 of the arrival terminal. Opposite the gate, there is a green, covered walk-way with a sign that says ?Car Rentals?; it will lead you to a building where there are a lot of car-rental companies. If you had pre-booked your car, look for the car-rental company in the building. However, do take note that this building houses the local car rental companies. For the international brands such as Avis, Hertz and the other bigger local companies, they are housed in another location outside the airport. You will need to check with them when you are doing the booking or email them for the information. If the collection centre of the car rental company that you booked with is located outside the airport, wait for their shuttle bus at Gate 5. You will recognize their shuttle bus by their brand name boldly emblazoned on the sides of the bus. Since I booked my car through Avis, I took the ?AJ? shuttle bus to their rental office on the outskirts of the airport. The shuttle bus runs on a regular schedule. Arriving at the front of the office, you take a queue ticket. If you had made reservations, it takes just a few seconds to call up your reservation after presenting your passport, driver's licence and International Driving Permit. You will be shown the rental agreement with all the details pertaining to the type, class, number of days of rental, total costs and any other relevant information. With Avis, the GPS is included in the rental, whereas for other rental companies that I had enquired with, the GPS is charged separately. After you have signed the rental agreement, you will be shown your car. You then drive it off to the inspection building where they will go through the car with you to identify any minor damages, scratches, dents etc. They will also have you verify that the fuel tank is full and instruct you on the use of the GPS before getting you to sign off the acknowledgement form. Do ensure that the GPS is an English language version. Keep the documents safely in the glove-compartment and be sure to get the telephone number of the station that you will return the car to. You will need this number to key into the GPS system to guide you back. You then proceed on your way, presumably, to your hotel for a much needed rest after the long flight to Jeju.When returning the car, you just need to drive back to the same depot from where you had collected it. Just key the given number into the GPS. Upon arrival, follow the sign, ?Car Return? and head for an available lot. The attendant there will check the car with you and when all is in order, he hands you a form to sign after you have returned the key to him. You then take the shuttle bus that will take you to the departure hall at the airport.The use of the GPS:Different makes and models operate slightly differently from one another, however, the common function that generalizes all of them is the use of the telephone number of a particular hotel, attraction or establishment to program the location into the GPS. For example, the telephone number of our hotel, Ocean Palace Hotel, Jeju, is 064 - 7305800. To navigate to the hotel from the airport, I just had to key in the number 7305800 and simply touch the 'Navigate' button and voila, it calculates the shortest route and starts the voice navigation system in a jiffy - it's as simple as that. From then on, just follow the voice navigation to get you to your hotel. If you make a wrong turn or pass a junction where you were supposed to turn, do not panic. Just relax and drive on ? it will re-direct you back to the planned route or at times, provide you with a new course. In fact, we had a lot of fun and discovered many new places of interest by intentionally turning off to smaller but interesting-looking roads just to see what lies ahead and where it will eventually lead us to ? that is the beauty of a self-drive holiday. Driving in Jeju:Jeju has a coastal ring road of approximately 181 km, not counting the connecting highways linking the North-South-East ?West regions. The coastal scene is a sight to behold! It is left-hand driving in Jeju.To those who have never driven on the left side of the road, it takes a little getting used to, physically as well as in your mind. It gets a little more confusing when turning at traffic junctions, especially when driving through ? stopping gives you an opportunity to orientate yourself and prepare in your mind the lane to take when turning. To minimize this confusion, always try to follow a car in front of you which is turning in the same direction as you. It is also helpful to remember that when turning, the roadside kerb will always be on the right of the driver. The roads, save for the highways, are slightly narrower than the roads we are used to in Singapore.Generally, the speed limits are:30 Km / hr within 100 m of school zones50 Km / hr in town areas60 Km / hr in the outskirts of town70 Km / hr along highwaysThe speed limits change quite frequently, so it is advisable to keep a look-out for the change in speed limits. There are speed-cameras practically everywhere, usually positioned up on traffic lights, lamp-posts and in some places, hidden behind 'boxes' manned by a policeman. So, if you wish to spend your money supporting the policemen, speed on at your own risk.The local drivers can, at times, be quite reckless. Just like we have hell-drivers here, there are hell-drivers in Jeju too, but not too many. Just stay alert and always be on the look-out using your wing and rearview mirrors all the time. Except for the main areas of Jeju-si and Seogwipo-si, most of the roads around the island are quite free of traffic.  To estimate the time needed to travel any distances, take an average speed of 45 km/hr.Parking:Generally free parking along kerb-sides and paid parking in some buildings and are generally available easily. Most hotels have free parking for their guests ? do check with the hotel management that you have booked with. Petrol cost: As at Nov 2014: Krw 1750 / ltrPlanning Your Routes:Planning your routes is totally at your own whim and fancy, depending on the places of interest as well as the available time you have on the island. If you have a few days ( I would recommend a minimum of five days), perhaps you may wish to consider the following suggestion:1. Day 1 ? Arrival and check into hotel. This sample itinerary is on the assumption that your hotel is in Seogwipo. 2. Day 2 ? Explore the west scenic coastal drive (Route 1132) of Sagye, Gosan-Ilwa, Hagwi-Aewol and visit the places of interest along this route ( Mt Sangkaksan / Songkaksan / Yongmeori). There are many cafes (especially along the Coastal Cafe Road) and bbq restaurants for stops of aromatic coffee and grilled black pig meat. Explore Jeju-si city (underground shopping mall) and return via highway 1131 where the famous ?Forest Tunnel? is located. After dinner, take a drive to the Lotte World Resort for some very beautiful night scenery of the giant windmills.3. Day 3 ? Go East this time along the Pyeoson, Sehwa-Jongdal and Gimyeong ? Haengwon coastal routes. Stopover at Seongsan Ilchubong (Sunrise Peak). Have dinner in Jeju-si before doing a night drive back to Seogwipo. 4. Day 4 ? Alternative 1Drive to Seongsan Port in the north-east via the eastern coastal route and park your car there. Purchase your ferry tickets to Udo Island and spend a very interesting day there. You can tour the island by buying the hop-off-on bus tickets or for the adventurers, you can hire the quad-bikes or scooters. Alternative 2 ? visit the popular tourist spots such as the Trick-art museum, teddy bear museum, waterfalls, submarine tours, Green Tea museum, Geomun Oreum, Citrus fruit farms, mysterious road, etc etc....5. Day 5 ? Check out of hotel for catch your flight back home.Have a safe and enjoyable holiday!Telephone Numbers of Attractions For GPS:Citrus Fruit Museum - 732 2114Geomun Oreum - 7108981Joongang Underground Mall - 723 1510Jusenggeolli Cliffs - 7381521Lotte Hotel - 731 1000Alive Museum - 805 0888Trick Art Museum - 787 8774Seongeup Folk Village - 787 1179Traditional 5 day market (Jeju-si) - 7435985Seongsan Harbour (Ferry to Udo Island) - 782 5671Seongsan Ilchubong - 783 0959Cheongyejeong Waterfall - 760 6331Cheongjiyeong Waterfall - 733 1528Jeongbang Waterfall - 733 1530Teddy Bear Museum - 738 7600Jeju Folk Village - 787 4501Jeju Sea-World - 784 2333Aqua Planet Jeju - 780 0900Manjanggul Cave - 710 7903Oedolgae - 760 3033

Sammu Park is a destination not likely to appear on the typical package-tour’s itinerary for Jeju Island, but this downtown Sin-Jeju gem has some singularly unique features for the intrepid visitor.? First, the park was actually constructed on one of Jeju’s 368 oreums, local dialect for a small scoria (cinder) cone or parasitic/parallel volcano.? This one is Beduri oreum, surely one of the smaller ones, topping out at just 10 meters above its base with a circumference of 617 meters.? Beduri was transformed into the park in 1978 as part of an urban planning initiative. In addition to a large assortment of exercise equipment,? a children’s play area, badminton and basketball courts, and jogging/hiking trails, Beduri boasts a majestic, two-story octagonal pavilion, called Sammujeong. ? Constructed in the traditional Korean style and ringed by pine trees, the colorful wooden pavilion is almost like a giant tree-house.? It isn’t unusual to hear musicians and vocalists practicing there, taking advantage of the spot’s natural acoustics.? It’s a peaceful place to sip a beverage in any season.? Next, are you a train enthusiast or history buff?? Then you might want to visit Sammu for this feature alone:? the park is home to the last remaining steam locomotive for coal transportation in Korea.? MIKA Steam Locomotive No. 304 (registered Cultural Heritage No. 414) was manufactured in Japan in 1944, during Japanese colonial rule, and operated on Korean railroads until 1967. In 1978, President Park Chung Hee had it shipped to the park on Children’s Day, so that Jeju’s children could see a real train.? The train’s passenger car now contains a children’s library.? Finally, beginning in 2014, the park has been further renovated to be a sort of extension to the Bao Jian Street tourism and shopping district.? At the park’s south entrance, there is a giant clock surrounded by wildflowers and neon lampposts that match those on Bao Jian.? The clock has a Plexiglas dome that gives its neon face a trick-art, psychedelic look after dark.? Sammu Park is definitely worth a visit, particularly if you are staying at an area accommodation or if you will be going to Bao Jian…a chance for a little Jeju “nightlife.”
