quite big & locally, i reached here at 8am, just open 1 hour but seem that over 90% stalls already open & operating. same as the wooden brand said that was grandma's market so that many elder near around. they were selling & buying everything. many diff stuffs inside the market. maybe time was early, i don't see any tourist inside the market but local people to buy much stuffs. that also has movable breakfast service that was same as what i saw in most of market of southeast country. some selling by movable truck some just deliver by tray. busy job. besides, seafood stall also interesting as i saw a seller cut open the Devilfish, first time to see it as seem he was struggle with the fish skin. ha. impressiveanyway, good for visit here if you got time at day of 2,7,12,17,22&27.

Pretty unique place, well worth to visit! Dress up well as it doesn't seem chilling down there at first, but if you walk until the very end, then back, it may take an hour. Also, getting there not that easy:take #701 from jeju city intercity bus termal to the bus stop named   Entrance to the Manjanggul Lava Tubes  . This is quite far from the entrace though, and the bus #990 supposed to go there is extremely rare, so not much chance except to take a taxi (it should not cost more than 3000 won/ride).

Please visit this place only if you really love and in great passion to help preserve the nature. This attraction requires reservation as it only allow 400 hikers daily. There are 10 sessions and 3 different trails, a one-hr one, a 2.5-hr and a 3.5-hr one. All hikers will be lead by a center guide. Though the guide speaks only Korean and knows only limited English, there are signage and descriptions on each special location.We joined the first session and started at 9. We were required to arrive at least 10 minutes before 9, then bought the ticket (2000 won each) and showed the tickets to the Information Desk. Then we were given a badge which we needed to put on all the time and returned to the Desk after the hike. No food, including candies and gums, are allowed. Only water, without colours or tastes, is allowed to bring into the site. There is a water machine inside the Information Desk.The   Gotjawal   forests, grow in the center of the Geomunoreum crater, are very dense and luxuriant. While you can only look from the outlook points at Sangumburi 掠긷訝 and Seongsan Ilchulbong Tuff Cone 掠길ε뷴낡, this activity is an authentic encounter inside the crater, with the geological formation, vegetation and traits of lava activities

People who visiting Jeju island is to see its nature (except those to Casino), Hallasan is a must go to me.  Together with the family, we opted for the route of Yeongsil (shorter though not to the top and unable to see the crater), where we could easily accessed by self driving from Seogwipo city.  Along the hiking, we experienced the sub tropical environment in the bottom, then a much cooler environment after 1.5km of steep uphill.  The view is great though not fantastic, we spotted few wild deers having grass in the mountain.  The first 2-3 km was quite steep but mostly on boardwalk and constructed staircases, the last 1-2 km was rather flat.We ended in the point with toilet and food supply and then back down on the same route, due to the last section was closed.  An interesting hiking day to experience different climate, weather condition, meet locals, spot the wild animal, and do physical exercise.

Parking is free, next to Osulloc. The ajusshi will be there to direct you in the carpark. Lovely place. I love Innisfree products and im happy to be there. However, there are only skincare products, no makeup items. There is an area for soap-making but we didnt do it. During the time we visited, noone did it too, so i cant comment how interesting it is.There is also an area which you could do ink stamping on paper. If you like ink stamping, do remember to bring some paper along. Its free.The food is organic and took quite some time to prepare. So the best is to find a table first, order your food and then do your retail shopping. We ordered 4 drinks & 2 meals, it took about 20-30 mins to be done. Yes, its that long.There are also desserts and they are made beautifully. How i wish i still have the stomach space for them. I would just come back to have tea and dessert at the place. Dont forget to look at their   Jeju only   products. There is innisfree Hallabong jam and strawberry jam. Yup, jam for bread. So look closely at the retails. The price of the retail items are comparable to those in Seoul, so need not get them unless you desperately need it. Go for their   jeju only   items instead.There is a small tea planatation outside Innisfree, where most is seen taking OOTD. Toilets are behind Innisfree.

Parking is charged. I think we were there for about 1hr? They charged my SUV for 1,000 won, which is still pretty cheap in my opinion.The place is near Jeju International Airport, so this could be your first place in your itinerary or last.So there are two staircases down to see the Dragon Head rocks. One of them is closer to the rocks, which can be hard to see the Dragon Head formation. The place can be quite windy.There are stores selling Hallabong products as well. According to my friend, the souvenirs are priced almost the same everywhere.So rocks.. yea. Im not that keen actually. But if you like nature, you might probably like this.

Our visit was postponed for a day but it was worth the wait. There was a heavy snowstorm a couple of days prior and the roads to Hallasan National Park were closed. When access to the park was restored, a beautiful blanket of snow was awaiting.It was my first experience of snow and I loved it. I came from a tropical country (where the coldest temperature ever recorded was at 6 degrees Celsius) so experiencing snow is a surreal experience. Although we did not climb any trail to the summit, experiencing snow even just outside the Visitor Center was fun and pleasurable. The Jeju Snow Festival for 2018-2019 did not include the Visitor Center at Hallasan National Park, however, unlike the previous year so there were no attractions set up in the area.Because of this, I am going back to South Korea this coming December for another winter wonderland experience and to try out skiing.

Our stamina is not so good so it took us 5 hours round trip for Yeongsil Trail up to Witsae Oreum Shelter and back. There was no Ramen available at the shelter so if you plan to go, better bring lunch box, you will be tired and eat a lot anyway. There are plenty of hikers from old people to children so you wont get lost, even if you want. Yeongsil trail has 4 parts of itFirst part is wooden steps, you will pass some creeks and a lot of shade / trees.Second part is the most strenous part. Lots of rocks and steep climbs , so watch your step. There are some observation deck for you to take photos and rest. And more wooden steps with crazy inclination. After you pass the big rocks crossing,(third part) it will be open area with no shade and this has the best view. And the most leisure part because its flat with almost no inclination. There is water fountain where you can fill up your drink for free. Walk 10-15 minutes from the water fountain and you will reach Witsae Oreum Shelter. Tips : Use sunscreen all over your body, even if its windy and cold at the beginning of the trail, when it reach the open area with no shade, the sun ray will hit you so hard. Wear hat. My scalp got sunburnt. Even better go with long sleeve and long pants. Go very very early like 7 am because the parking lot will be full later.

Our package tour brought us to upscale shopping centers and attractions that carry local and international brands. One of these was the Chilseongro Shopping Street. Fortunately, I had bookmarked Dongmun Market on Kakao map and it was a short walk from there. I had no plans to buy branded clothes (nor any clothes for that matter) so I ditched Chilseongro and headed to Dongmun.The Dongmun Market is a wet market, a traditional market. Pretty much everything in Jeju is available here?clothes, tangerines, chocolates, seafood, household items, food. The prices here were a lot lower than the chocolate stores and souvenir centers that our tour group operator brought us to.At Dongmun, you can haggle, especially if you buy plenty. I decided to buy chocolates to bring back home to our office staff. Since there were plenty of stalls selling chocolates, I compared prices first. I ended up buying from an elderly lady who offered the lowest price. I got more than 60 boxes and she gave me lots of freebies. There are stalls that had different types of food. Some even had live seafood available and they will cook it for you. I was too full to try out the local food, but I did miss having photos taken.There were a handful of stalls that sold kitsch souvenir items like keychains and magnets. There were two large stalls that had numerous items on display; their prices were high though. I ended up buying from the other stalls whose main items being sold were something else and just happened to have magnets and keychains on the side. Nevertheless, the prices at the souvenir shops in Seongsan IIchubong were lower; I wished I had bought there instead.

Our initial plan is to visit museum then heading to the beach side to meet the divers to see how they work and that will bring us more understanding the history & culture behind. Unfortunately, we've no luck at all, we only manage to visit the museum.  Because the diver only work on some days which depend on the weather and sea condition. It is NOT every WEEKDAY! like most of the reviews in Tripadvisor and some other travel blogger who has been visited there before. I'm so so frustrated when I knew this from the locals. I don't understand why they put in their reviews or comment if they are unsure, its misleading and really let ppl down. So, if you plan to visit the divers, please check with the locals (people living nearby there or the restaurants nearby) on the first day you are in Jeju.

Our guide is June. On the first day, she’s a bit late on the pick up, then we have to go back to her place because she forgot her document for the trip which is unprofessional. Then as we started the tour on the car, she just silence which is weird for me, because normally a good tour guide will start speaking & add so much to a traveller's understanding about the landmark , history & culture of the country. But thats not happening on both of these tour. Even when i asked her some questions, she seems hesitate when answering. Later i found out that some of her answer about Jeju actually is wrong. This shown how she doesnt have much knowledge about the Island. It’s a shame because for being a tour guide ,thats one of the important skill to have.

Our guide dropped us at Seonimgyo Bridge at around 8am, and said he would pick us up around 11.30am.  3.5hrs for waterfalls?  I thought he must have made a mistake...Surprise surprise... We enjoyed the morning stroll across the park near Seonimgyo Bridge (with autumn leaves still visible in end Nov).  After a million selfies, we made our way to the 1st waterfall and was awestruck!  So beautiful!  Well strictly speaking, this is not a waterfall but a lake of some sort.  But who cares about the misnomer?To reach the 2nd falls, there is a well-marked trail.  A medium-distance walk with its fair share of up and down slopes.  Not arduous and I would definitely recommend it.  The waterfall is not Niagara, but I found it pretty in its subtlety.The 3rd falls has a warning - the trail may be difficult for children and elderly.  Since I am neither, I had assumed incorrectly that I would find it manageable.  Wrong!  It was a very very long way down (which was fine), and an equally long long way up (nearly killed me).  Was it worth it?  I am afraid not... for the 3rd falls. So my recommendation would be to visit the first 2 falls, but give the 3rd a miss (unless you want a workout).

Our guide brought us here to see the 10-inch snow... we came from tropical climate you see...So there is no climbing for us, but the snow was fun for the kids as it was their first experience...they were so happy making snowballs and we took some really great pictures here.
Our first visit to this magical island. Such a beautiful place, weather was great, people were friendly. Hope to return.

Our first place of visit on Jeju Island. Took a 40min cab ride from Jeju. Later learnt about how Jeju intercity bus worked and took the bus after. Taxi ride was reasonable about US$10, getting a cab was a little tricky. Took a short walk up the hill overlooking the bay. And enjoyed a nice pastry breakfast at the cafe and bakery.

Our FIRST meal in JEJU and we were just spoilt for choices. This is traditional market and we had so much fun walking in the market.The large boxes of tangerines greets you at the entrance and as you explore further, you see endless rows of fresh seafood. We randomly selected some food and they tasted delicious!

Our first lava tube cave experience ; feel like we are in a Indiana Jones movie exploring the dark and wet cave don?t know what?s ahead of you. Abit slippery and rocky , would recommend a pair of non slip shoes as I saw a few people fell .

Our family visited the Cheonjiyeon Falls on the first day of our trip. We came out quite late, around 5 pm and we decided to come here as this was one of the attractions that were opened at that time. The admission fee was reasonably cheap. The area was not that big as I imagined, you walk from the entrance to the waterfall and then back. The waterfall is quite nice to look at and I'm pretty sure it might look more majestic if you come here at night. Even though I came on a cloudy and rainy day, it didn't ruin the mood much, it makes the waterfall more mysterious and I liked the atmosphere.

Our family has visited quite a few aquariums but this is the first one where we've seen some adorable otters. Adorable! Facility is beautiful clean airy-feeling.Tanks are well-kept it appears so my guess is that the sea creatures are   happier.   The aquarium is just the right size for anyone to finish in less than two hours.  What's also nice is that it's right next to the ocean.

review: Our driver/tour guide took us here on the way back to the hotel. Actually, he said it was his first time there as well. My 17-year old son and I felt the uphill rolling and it was a weird feeling. Not sure why it was doing it, but we saw some tourists pouring water on the pavement and watching the water rolling uphill. Many years ago, I took my son to a similar   mystery road   in Manzanillo, Mexico. Back then, may be he was too young to feel it, or may be I was a terrible tour guide, but this time he finally got it. So, it was fun for us to take the quick detour and had some laughs.  Oh, and it was free and there are road signs tell you how to experience the   mystery  .

one of the many trick art museums in Korea. The first bit has the usual pose-with-renaissance-paintings stuff but if you don't have that much time skip that stuff and make your way through to the end where there's a pretty cool arabian nights themed room where you pretend to run from giants climb into the sky or escape over burning bridges. the station where you pretend to skydive while strapped to a backpack on the floor is quite special. warning : wear pants when visiting this museum if you wish to avoid inadvertently flashing other tourists. the sculpture garden is nothing fantastic and   little provence   is a bunch of stuffed dogs dressed in french peasant outfits in a lackluster room.

Nexon Computer Museum was surprisingly a fun visit.  Having grown up during the 1.44 MB floppy disk era, it was cool to see the now ancient artifacts from that era like the first Apple computers and the 8-bit graphic video game consoles (and of course the floppy disks themselves). The interactive zone with some of the classic video games like Galaga arranged in chronological order were a lot of fun.

Myself and wifey and our 2 boys aged 12 and 15, decided to walk this mountain, and arrived just after 9.30 in the morning. This trail is supposedly the easier of what are now 3 trails that take you to the summit. Because it wasn't the weekend, there were fewer people, and this was a big bonus, as the whole way up is sectioned off with guide rope, and is either wooden stairs or stones and rock. The few times we came across people, you were held up a bit until you came across a widening where you could overtake them. I can imagine this being very irritating on a weekend, and also you lose that feeling of being out in the wilderness.On the way up we met small groups of older Koreans, who offered us cucumbers and oranges, and we greeted all we met with    hello   or    how you doing ?   in Korean. This was mostly met with a smile and a happy reply.The downside with this trail, is that you are surrounded by trees the first 8 km up, and it is not until the last kilometre that you actually begin to get an appreciation of the views. In some ways it is quite beautiful, but like I said to our two boys, the bottom of the hill is nearly like the top, because you can only see the trees- okay different formations, but no view.At the top, you have the crater sectioned off, and you can peer down into it and take pictures. Because of the distance, we rate this quite a hard going trek,and there are many loose rocks that you could easily twist your ankle on, wifey did!!We used 3 hours up, a little more down, because we had to stop for a while, so wifey could swear at me when she twisted her ankle!!

My wife and I hiked the Seongpanak Trail up Hallasan in late May 2015. The trail starts relatively easy but gets more difficult after the first shelter. Make sure you have the rights shoes as the rocks can be pretty hard on your feet. This is a long climb, and for most of the trip you will be in a forest. Keep your eyes open and you may spot some of the elusive small native deer, we saw three on our trip. I am not in great shape, so it was a tough climb for me and took us 9 hrs. round trip. The rocks are really hard on your feet on the way down. Leave early since if you don't make it to the last shelter before 1 PM they will not allow you to ascend to the summit. The last shelter sells ramen and water and a few other items, but be aware you are expected to pack all of your own trash off of the mountain. There are some stores and shops in the parking lot at the entrance to the park, we bought some kimbop for lunch and packed it up with us. This is the tallest mountain in South Korea and the summit provides wonderful views at over 1900 meters high. Climbing Hallasan was a   bucket list   item for my wife, who was born in South Korea, and a memorable experience.

My wife and I hiked Hallasan last weekend, which was our first trip to Jeju Do. We've lived in Seoul for 5 years and finally made that trip south. We decided to take the Seongpanak Trail since it allows you to get to the top. Overall, the hike was great - beautiful scenery (although it was a hazy day for us so visibility was limited), challenging hike and it's something that will take up a whole day. We took a different trail down once we reached the top and the views were nicer on that one. I think there are only two trails that go all the way up. We're not hikers by any means so our legs were pretty tired on the way down the mountain. They estimate 8-9 hours total but we did it in 7! Be sure to pack some snacks and water as there's not much available on the hike. There's a small place at a checkpoint a couple hours into the Seongpanak trail where you can get some water, ramen and chocolate bars (along with some basic hiking gear) but don't expect much. We had only taken water with us (rookie mistake) and I was wishing for some extra snacks on the way down. There's also a store/small restaurant at the first entrance to the hike so you can stock up there. Overall, it's definitely worth doing as its one of the main attractions on Jeju.

review: My family and I visited this UNESCO World Heritage and South Korea National Monument cave on a late afternoon for 2 hours. There were not many visitors and we didn?t find any tour buses when we reached here.   Getting there & fees: Manjanggul Cave is located in the north western part of Jeju-do. To get (drive) to Manjanggul Cave, key in GPS coordinate 7834818. There is no parking fee at the huge car park. Entrance fee is 2,000 won for adults and 1,000 won for teenagers and children.Manjanggul Cave Museum: Upon climbing up the stairs from the car park, you will reach the Museum and a cafeteria/restaurant on its right. You could go in and have a look at the interesting exhibits, including how the Manjanggul Cave was formed from the volcanic activities.Manjanggul Cave: To get to the underground Cave, we followed the sign-posts ? it?s within 5 minutes? walk from the Manjanggul Cave Museum. Trek the entire 1 km stretch that?s opened to public and you will end with a colourful lit lava column - created from the dripping of lava from a hole in the ceiling ? which at about 8 meters high, is the tallest lava column on Earth. Nevertheless, there are a few things you have to take note while you are in the Cave:(1) The entrance to the Manjanggul Cave is also the exit ? there?s no exit at the end of the 1 km trail, which means you are walking 2 km return (2) Make sure you bring and wear a jacket or sweater with you because it?s freezing cold and chilly inside the cave. (3) Wear a cap or the jacket or sweater can be waterproof because you get water ocassioanlly dripping from the cave top onto you (4) The surface (floor) of the Cave is full of solidified lava flow terrain (i.e. extremely uneven surface) and water puddles, so you have to wear a pair of good walking shoes and walk carefully. Hold on to the railings of the stairs.(5) You probably don?t need a torchlight because the Cave is illuminated just enough by ground lightings. Some parts of the cave even have colourful lights shining at the dome shaped ceiling (cupola) (6) If you would like to take photographs inside the cave, you would need a tripod and switch to manual mode for long exposure (I used 4 seconds to 10 seconds exposure on my digital SLR).   There are displays at certain parts of the cave in English explaining the geology of the cave and the formation of the interesting structures (e.g. stalactites). In particular, there?s one structure ? ?Stone Turtle? ? in which the shape looks like Jeju-do Island, and which you could reach in about 30 minutes of one-way walking as it?s about 400m from the entrance. Along the Manjanggul Cave wall, we saw varied patterns of lava flow lines, some are straight while some are wavy. Really interesting! I have been to over 10 limestone caves around the world, but this is my first visit in a lava tunnel cave or lava tube cave (and Asia?s longest lava tube cave for that matter). You have to experience being transported to another world in this ?out of this world? cave for yourself ? don?t miss it!

My family and I spent about 45 minutes at this attraction on an early Monday afternoon, as our first stop of a Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliffs ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary. It is designated a Natural Monument and is part of the Global Geopark Network. Getting there & fees: When I keyed in GPS code of 7351000 and 7381521, it brought us confusingly to the Convention Centre and the car park of the Seaes Resort respectively. Thanks to the helpful staff of the Seaes resort, we followed the advice and drove past the Convention Centre and then looked out for a signage that indicated taking a right turn to a road that leads to the destination. Once there, we parked the car in the car park which charged a parking fee pf 1000 won. The entrance fee is 2000 won for adults & 1000 won for teenagers (youth) and children, and we used one of the lockers for free to keep our stuff.The Cliffs/Attraction: After paying the entrance fees, we walked past figurines of dolphins and a huge rock surrounded by the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac. We then took the pathway of wooden platform steps that brought us to the bird-eye view of the beautiful blue sea and the rocky cliffs containing the awesome columnar joints that are typically at the base of the cliff. The platform only showcases a section of the 2 km stretch of these rocky cliffs. Along the platform, there is a display in English and Korean that educate you about the origin of the rocks. It would be good if another display would be able to pictorially illustrate the geography and formation. According to the information, the columnar joints were formed from the lava flows from the Nokhajiak scoria cone from 140,000 to 250,000 years ago. During cooling of the molten lava, contraction occurred and split the basaltic rocks into polygonal columns. We saw mainly tetragonal (4 sided), pentagonal (5-sided) and hexagonal (6-sided) columns. Because the origin of the columnar joints and rocks is volcanic, these are black. Throughout the time, I stood there simply awestruck by what I saw ? it?s like a divine being had creatively sculptured these columnar joints to perfection. And why only at this 2km stretch and not at other coastal areas in Jeju since the volcanic molten lava flowed everywhere?  It?s a pity the waves that crashed onto the joints and rocks were not huge; otherwise I think it would be an even more awesome sight. There are several pointers to take note:(1) You could appreciate this attraction in less than 1 hour (including photo and selfie-taking)(2) As the attraction is outdoors, be prepared for what the weather will throw at you. Carry an umbrella or wear a cap or sunglasses or put on sunscreen on a sunny day(3) To see these rocks better, I suggest bringing along a pair of binoculars or zooming closer using your camera telephoto lens or your handphone(4) Take plenty of photographs but do not climb over or lean over too much the platform ?railings?We ranked Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff as one of the top 3 attractions in Jeju. For sure, this Nature?s awesome masterpiece is not to be missed!

My family and I liked this waterfall simply because of the coolness that sweeps away the afternoon heat. We visited this attraction on a Monday late afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary.Getting there & fees: The GPS coordinate/code for Jeongbang Waterfall is 7331530. It is located on the south central part of Jeju (Seogwipo). We parked our car for free at the car park. Entrance fee to the Waterfall is 1000 won for adults and 500 won for teenagers and children. The Waterfall/Attraction: Because the waterfall is so close to the sea, it gives the impression that the fresh water falls directly into the sea. The water actually falls 23 metres into a plunge-pool in a sheltered cove comprising of mainly black lava rocks and then flows to the sea. After the ticket booth, an approximately 5 minutes? descent on the sturdy steps of the wooden stairway took us to the bottom but still quite a distance from the waterfall. Even then, we were already ?bathed? by the cool water mist from the impact of the waterfall plunging onto the pond. We had to step on the rocks and boulders to get nearer to the base of the waterfall, and this was where we had to be very careful, very slow, very nimble and very sure-footed in negotiating the uneven rocks or boulders of different sizes and shapes as well as the slippery surface of the wet rocks. This is also where you have to wear good walking shoes and I don?t recommend slippers. Nevertheless, as more and more water mist and droplets landed onto our tired bodies as we approached closer and closer to the waterfall, we just felt refreshed and energised!  Because of the persistent mist and fine water droplets, it?s difficult to take selfies and photographs for that ?I was here at Jeongbang Waterfall? moment without these landing on your devices? lens and blurring the image. So you have to wipe off the water and be quick with the photograph taking.We spent about 30 minutes relaxing and soaking the ambience of the waterfall. During this time, we counted no less than 7 waterfall ?mini-streams? and only 20 visitors (not crowded). As the first 쩌 part of the descent path will not be walked again during the ascent, I would recommend taking photographs and selfies of the panorama during the initial stretch. In fact, the lookout point just after the ticket booth has this ?landmark? lone tree that faithfully watches over the waterfall, and you could include it to frame your photograph.If I could come again, I would do so in the cool morning with the sun shining on the waterfall. Anyway, this is one majestic waterfall that you wouldn?t want to miss!

Must visit this place if you are in Jeju.  This is the place where you can also watch women divers performance and taking the horse ride too. If you want to catch the Sunrise at the peak, start to climb at least 30 mins before the sunrise. Please check the weather first. If you are not that fit, start to climb 1 hour before the sunrise. Take note: Stairs all the way from the bottom to the top. A lot of resting area along the way.  Alternatively, from the entrance, walk towards the ocean on the left.  You can catch the sunrise from there too if you are too lazy to climb.  The view around the mountain is fantastic.  Many eateries, shops nearby.  It will be very crowded from 9am onwards with many tour buses.  Many parking lots nearby if you are unable to get any parking at the mountain carpark.

Mount Hallasan is the tallest mountain in South Korea, so expect this hike not to be an easy one. For the less trained hikers, you can go half way and stop at the first crater, which also offers beautiful views.
Miss this place one the first day, try again to drive to this place. Another scenic sight but when you seen the others, this is ordinary.

Mind your step! The cave is long, dark and slippery. This was the first time I'd ever been to a lava tube so it was a really new experience.The price is reasonable. A number of stations with information describing the rock formations you are passing.

Many of my friends recommended us to try Jeju black pork. However, it was definitely not a thing for me. Firstly, pricey. Secondly, nothing so special about. You can simply try any grill meat in Seoul and it tastes the same. Would recommend you to try something else in Jeju.

Manjanggul Cave is one of the top ten lava tubes to visit that was formed about 200,000-300,000 years ago. It is one of 7 Geomunoreum lava tubes of Jeju Island and located in the North East area.The visit can be done using either bus (another 30 mins or 2.7km walk to the entrance) or car. I'd suggest to rent a car while in Jeju because it will make it super easy to get around the island. If you drive, the number you want to input into the GPS is 7107903 :-).It was really windy and cold on the day we went to the cave. We walked for about 5 minutes from the free car park to the ticket booth but the temperature inside of the cave was very comfortable.The first lava related item that we saw was the lava column cascade. It would be there on the way to entrance, to greet everyone who came to visit the Manjanggul Cave.?The entrance started with two flights of stone stairs that might get a bit slippery during the rainy or winter period. Even though you wear non-slip shoes with you, it's definitely worthwhile to hold on to the railing when going down and up the stairs.The cave was definitely not wheelchair friendly since the stony surface is always wet, rocky and covered with puddles. Water will occasionally drop from the ceiling of the cave but it didn't really bother us. We saw that some people carried an umbrella with them or wore the plastic rain poncho but since you'll be walking a lot, it would be too warm if you wear the poncho. Another suggestion is just to wear a hat/ baseball cap in summer and stick to your winter jacket in the winter time.I tried to take some photos inside but it was pretty hard because the cave was quite dark. It was a really enjoyable walk and we got to learn about how the lava stream formed the lines on the cave, stalactites and stalagmites.There were a lot of rocks around our path and we learnt later on that big and fragmented rocks fell from the ceiling during or after the formation of the lava tubes! There were a lot of lava columns as well that was formed when lava flowed from the ceiling to the floor of the lava tube.Manjanggul Cave closes on the first Wednesday of each month. Their opening hours is from 9 AM to 6 PM with last admission at 5:10 PM.

Manjanggul cave is a 7.4km long lava tube, although it is only possible to walk for the first kilometer. It takes about an hour. Manjanggul cave is said to be one of the largest lava tube in the world. During the walk, one can really feel the size. There are open spaces here and there that are indeed pretty large and spacious. I appreciated the nice selection of several lava formations that was available, each of them being in general accompanied by few pieces of information. In particular, one should not miss the locally-famous 'turtle' rock (an accretion of lava around a fallen rock that has a turtle shape) and the tallest lava column in the world (7.6 meters high, see the picture I uploaded).There is an entrance fee, but it is very reasonable (about 2 USD).Overall, the visit is worthy but one must be ready about what Manjanggul Cave is: a dark and humid cave with a few stones and lava formations.

Loved this island off Jeju Island!  If you're staying in the Jungmun area, this requires about an hour taxi or car ride to the port where you catch a ferry (15 minute ride) the island. Best to buy a return ticket at the ticket office (the taxi driver helped us to do this, lucky for us as you need to show your ID or passport to buy tickets!).  The sun came out for us and the island was in all its glory - blue skies and blue sea - absolutely worth the trip.  Can easily spend half to one day here. Not sure how it works with the bus options though if you hire a cabin to stay along the bus route.When you arrive at U-Do, there are various bicycles/cars that you can hire (if you bring your driving licence), however, you can easily buy a hop on hop off bus ticket.  The bus driver talks for some of the way during the bus tour but if you don't understand what's going on, it's just as easy to enjoy the view from the window.  Nature is all around.Apart from the surrounding sea and boats, you can see horses and women divers (next to their orange buoys) in the sea.   We also enjoyed a black pork burger, mandarin juice at our first stop and also a peanut ice-cream from Jimmy's.This visit was another one of the many highlights to our trip and I would love to come again!  Pre-teen kids also enjoyed the beautiful breathtaking scenery.
Loved my first visit to a lava tube cave. Dark, lots of texture, educational information provided. Lots of fun and nice even on a rainy day!

Located in the north eastern part of the island.  Took us an hour from hotel.  The cave temperature is 5-10C lower than outside, so suggest to bring a jacket and don't wear your Jimmy Choos.  Is wet and slippery with uneven grounds.  (Not suggest for elderly)The open part in 2017 is the 2nd section.  which is about 1km from start to end. First you walk down a steep stairs 3 floors down and you start walking. When you reach the large platform at the end and see the huge lava rocks, take photo and then you walk back .Spent about 2 hours there.

Living in Hong Kong we're pretty used to tough hikes - this one is a little difficult but manageable for anyone who is reasonably fit or has some hiking experience. Whilst the incline on this hike is never that steep and the first part of the trail is easy with paved walkways, the terrain for the second half is pretty hard going with lots of rocks and boulders. We managed in trainers but hiking boots with a sturdy sole would probably be better, and some may feel more comfortable with poles. But it's ABSOLUTELY worth the effort for the view. The crater lake is quite impressive but more stunning is if you look back on Jeju from above the clouds. Took us about 6.5 hours up and down but bring plenty of snacks as there is only one point where you can buy water and some dubious looking packet noodles. Oh and there are no bins so bring a bag for your rubbish. If you are in Jeju and like hiking, you must do this as it's a great sense of achievement when you can say you've hiked S Korea's highest peak!

Like the name of the place, the first gallery show case a few very old teddy bears (over 100 years old). Some even come with old photo of children holding the same type of teddy bear. Hundreds of teddy bears are dressed up and some with animatronic to depict their human equivalent (eg. Elvis Presley singing in a concert).A great place for teddy bear or toy fans. But beyond the teddy bears, there isn't much to see here. So, it may not be everyone's cup-a-tea.Ample free parking is available infront of the museum.Tips: Visit the Elvis concert hall one floor above the cafe. It can be easily missed.If you know when you're going to visit the museum, purchase ticket online from sites such as Klook.com or Trazy.com to save some $$.

Let's first get this out of the way: If you're not a teddy bear fan, if you're an over-serious person, or basically, if you had a fun-less childhood, don't bother visiting this place. Because then it would be pretty much a tourist ripoff kind of place, with nothing really worth seeing.But, if you do like bears, and regardless of how cheesy or a ripoff this place can be, you just want to have some fun, then by all means, check it out!Admittedly, I quite like teddy bears myself, and right from the moment I stepped in, I was constantly tickled by all the teddy bears modeled in the form of famous people, famous artworks, and even historical events. It can be sometimes strange to see the head of a bear in the place of what should've been a human one, but toss the strangeness aside and you'll realize there is so much to see and chuckle over. Having teddy bears in place of humans in the exhibits add a touch of innocent cuteness to everything.Do note that there's both an indoor and outdoor exhibit, so if you're on a schedule yet really want to see everything, make sure you plan your time well!

Last weekend, I climbed up to the top of Hallsan Mountain and saw the crater on the top called Baerokdam. Hallasan is the highest mountain in Korea, 1,950m above sea level. It took 5 hours to go up to the to top, which means it took another 5 hours to climb down. Climbing was kind of fight with myself and I won! I'm really proud of it and the most unforgettable thing is Baerokdam itself. I can't express with a word. As it snowed for the first time this year, it was more beautiful.

Korea's first UNESCO World Natural Heritage site well-thronged by tourists. The uphill pathway leads to the majestic dormant crater and a path on the left of the ticket entrance brings you downwards to Haenyo women diver performance at 1.30 pm and 3 pm. Fresh catch of abalone, octopus, shells can be eaten sashimi style for about KRW50,000 per plate (pricey!).  At this spot, you're closest to the ocean for a spectacular view of the stratified cliffside and lava rock formations.  As you walk up the stairs, don't miss the platform for free binocular views of Udo Island. While the main goal of most tourists is to hike to the top of the crater,  do look back at  different vantage points for captivating views - azure sky, emerald sea, natural greens, black rocks and dotted by colourful buildings. Comfortable walking shoes recommended and beware of upskirting/fashion malfunction in the incredibly strong winds.  Jeju Weekly reported that from the 2H of 2017, hikers to Sunrise Peak will be required to book in advance via a reservation system for the route to the top of Sunrise Peak. The move comes after the Jeju Provincial Government took advice from 25 experts about how to protect the value of the island?s natural sites.

Korean women divers are called haenyeo. They dive in the ocean without any special tools to gather abalone, clams or seaweed. Wearing a lead weighted  vested and goggles, they plunge into 20 meter depths and stay underwater holding their breaths for two to three minutes.  Once they come up to the surface, they make a whistling sound, which is their unique way of breathing out carbon dioxide and breathing in fresh oxygen. The museum is in a four story building and housed many exhibits.  Gallery 1 on the first floor depicts the haenyeo's way of life. On the second floor at Gallery 2, you can see haenyeo's working life.  On the third floor at the observation area you can get a view overlooking the sea.  Gallery 3 displays exhibits of the sea around Jeju.  Outside the museum there is a lawn with statues, including one honoring the haenyeo. You can also admire the architecture of the museum. Further down, we chanced upon the haenyeo who were starting their show by singing a song. We were indeed lucky on that Tuesday afternoon as we managed to watch the show which started at 1.30.

Kim Mandeok Memorial.I really liked this place personally. I came to know of this woman, Kim Mandeok from this memorial museum. She was the first CEO woman in Chosun Dynasty, which was quite unusual especially as a woman. And when a famine came to Jeju, she helped people in Jeju. Because of the benevolent act, she was still remembered even now. Even a Korean drama dealt with her life. Her life is very exemplary and inspiring. You can find a fraction of Korean history here.

Just like everyone already mentioned, the road is indeed mysterious as the car would really move uphill on its own. However, it is only a very short stretch of the road. But I would still recommend it if you are self-driving and it's your first time in Jeju. Definitely, something you have to experience.You can also head to the museums that is nearby too after going to this road.

Jeongbang Waterfall was near our guesthouse and it was the first stop of our trip to the east of Jeju. You can climb through the rocks and take a photo in the middle the small pond, in front of the waterfall. The water spray catches the light and acts as a prism to scatter the light into rainbows..pretty

Jeju's teddy bear museum is one of the most iconic destinations. I first heard about it from watching the show Goong years ago, and decided I had to visit it if I ever went to Jeju island. It was a small museum, but nonetheless i'm glad I paid a visit. The museum is a short walk from The Shilla Jeju  , which is where we stayed.

Jeju-do best attraction, the Mysterious Road (Dokkaebi Road) or Goblin road as folk story say, it was the goblins who does the trick.. sound interesting. Young and old will find this place fun and mysterious. All you have to do is just stop your car at the designation point, on the double sign(emergency light), off the engine, release the hand brake and let the car move up the hill by itself, 'Yes.. roll up the hill'.The best is, this attraction is free of charge. Jeju Stone Park is a vast area with everything stone related.  With Jeju being a volcanic island, the lava stones are everywhere from the Harubang statues to the walls surrounding houses.  The park is divided into three courses which would take about an hour each at a leisurely pace.  The first course has mostly rock statues (including the Harubang statues) that most likely had some religious significance.  The second course shows how the rocks were used for more practical purposes (tombstones, tools, housing, etc) through the different eras of Korean history.  The third course specifically shows the different Jeju style housing made with mostly the volcanic rock walls.  It?s probably not the best place to be in the middle of heat in the summer but when the weather is nice, it?s a fantastic spot to spend a few hours.

I have seen pictures about Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff (?ъ＜ⓒ\由) and was amazed by the neat shapes of hexagon stone pillars formed by volcanic lava, i totally recommend tourist to spend time walking around the nicely design olle trail in the beautiful, as well as to visit Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff during your trip in Seogwipo or Chungmun area. you don't have to plan for a long stay, a good two hours should be more than enough, as it was just a viewing spot rather than you can actually walk-in and visit. Jeju is famous for hiking and its Olle walking routes, chosen to hike in Hallasan National Park as part of our itinerary. My first hiking experience in oversea and it is an unforgettable experience I ever had. Fantastic !

I've never done something like this before so it was a first time for me. We tried it in one direction but it didn't work, but when we tried it in the opposite direction (heading away from Loveland), it works and the car accelerated to 13 km/hr whilst on neutral. I've climbed Hallasan twice now, once in December and once in early March, and both times I took this route. This route is slightly longer than Gwaneumsa, but it's also a gradual incline with several easy portions. I took this route primarily because there is not a lot of public transportation available to/from the Gwaneumsa trail, plus I'm not sure I can do a steep incline the entire way up to the summit. For Seongpanak, you have about 5 km that are easy, 2.5 km that get harder, and then a pretty brutal last 2 km. Regardless, know that there are other hiking trails around the island and even around the volcano, but only the two mentioned above will lead you all the way up to the summit.Given some of the reviews I saw that are either inaccurate or not very helpful, I hope to compile a quick list to help you decide if this is something you want to do and if so, what you will need:1) It's definitely going to be an all-day kind of thing. You will be tired afterward, so you likely won't want to schedule too many other activities for the evening. Also, it's likely that you will be sore and tired the next day or two. 2) You need to start climbing no later than 8:30 AM. As several people have mentioned, you will not be allowed to access the last chunk of the way if you're not at the second shelter by 12:30 PM (this is winter time, so the schedule varies slightly from season to season... always check the Korean tourism sites).3) Even if it's sunny, there's a chance you might need crampons. In the winter months you will need them for sure, but even last weekend people were sliding down and falling repeatedly without them. I hear that it's even worse on the Gwaneumsa trail since it's a lot more shielded from the sunshine. 4) Bring food and water! The only place you can buy something is at the very beginning of the trail, and even then the options aren't fantastic. A little protein or fruit will go a long way whenever you're starting to feel tired, and it'll help you push through. Please make sure you do not leave any of your trash along the way; there are zero trashcans, so if you carry something particularly messy, you might want to pack a bag for the waste.5) Do not use the toilet in the first shelter! It's the worst smelling bathroom ever, which is rare for Korea since things are usually so clean... I suppose it's the septic system. I suggest using the toilets at the parking lot and at the last shelter (there are two). The first one is seriously a nightmare. 6) It's not an easy hike, but it's doable even for people who don't exercise strenuously. I've seen people carrying babies all the way to the top, and I've seen small children and old people make it, too. Definitely wear the right clothing, though, and especially the right shoes. If you're hiking at a time without snow, you will spend hours circumventing rocks of all sizes and ankle support will be extremely helpful for this. Anyway, thanks for reading, I hope you have a fantastic hike!

I've been very interested in the haenyeo ever since I first visited Jeju-do. This museum has some interesting exhibitions about the life and work of the haenyeo. Admission is very cheap, a bit over 1000 won for an adult. It's recommended to watch the short documentary about the haenyeo before visiting the exhibitions, to get the most out of your visit. It plays near the lobby. There's a gift shop on site with haenyeo-related items.

It's the first stop in our itinerary & we went to the Ssanyong cave where there are also lava tubes. It's not as big  as Manjang cave & it's better lighted. There's also a folk village in this park, a flower & bonsai garden & lots of lava stones formed into different figures. A bird sanctuary is also here.

It's my second visit to Jeju and since I am staying in Jungmun area, we decided to visit this nearby attraction. I can't remember the name of the teddy bear museum of my previous trip but it's definitely bigger than this. You will find this attraction amazing if you are visiting a teddy bear museum for the first time, but being my second visit to such attraction, I don't find anything particularly interesting.

its my first mountain hike, its a straightforward trail but tricky with rocky stone paths at some incline parts. not recommend for those with weak knees and ankles or just go slow n wear ur ankle guards. go up seongpanak (easier as more gradual)and down gwaneumsa (alot of steps, steeper) but gwaneumsa has valley view, creek view and there?s a tiny cave opening near the base with blast out icy wind even in summer.. pretty cool. there?s a bus to and from seongpanak and take taxi from gwaneunsa or prearranged pickup as there?s hardly a bus there.its a total of 9 hrs including rest stops though i rested longer at the peak and pressed on at rest stops. do pace yourself.. calves been killing me midway down the descent. needless to say its a painful walk for the next couple of days.. i slathered all the muscle aches cream..

Its just teddy bears, but they have it setup really well. They have even setup themes for bears eg. Moon landing theme with Neil Armstrong bear about to take first step, etc. nice souvenir shop selling decent stuff.
It's crowded but the view is amazing. If you're a first timer, I personally will recommend this than the other waterfalls in Jeju.

Its a very do-able climb up although at the first look it might look daunting. Even grannies reached the top! Once you slowly work your way up with plenty of pause in between, the reward at the end is amazing. Breathtaking views of the ocean and the crater.I'll do it again next time I go there!
It's a impressive waterfall in Jeju Island of historical significance.Should not miss this site, if it's your first trip to Jeju Island.

It's a 100m road whereby majority of the tourists are fascinated by this mysterious road. Beside the Mysterious Road, there are a few stall selling some snacks. You must go to the first stall which is near to the ending point of the mysterious road, and try their strawberries. It's the most fresh strawberry i have ever seen and eat! It's a must to try.

It wouldn't usually be my first choice to visit on an island filled with so many views but it was a rainy day so it seemed reasonable. Wasn't disappointed. Can't go wrong in any way if you stop by. Didn't see the outdoor gardens since it was pouring rain but wasnt disappointed even with the indoor one alone

It wasn't very clear from the guide books. The spot is basically a volcanic rock formation that is concave. I'm not sure that you can actually have a good view of the formation with its lush green centre from any walkable vantage point (like you get from travel books). So on nearing the spot, stop on the highway shoulder to get a distant photograph first.After you arrive, note that the car park is basically one way. Miss a turn and you have to exit the carpark and come back from the entrance. Be prepared to walk / hike as the areas open to public are quite steep. You can get a good open view of the city or the ocean. Refreshing scenery.
it was the first beach i went to korea. Although it is quite small. But not bad. Very clean and quite.....  Not so crowdy,,,

It was raining and our driver decided to start with this attraction first. Although before getting into the caves, we got a bit wet, but once inside we lost track of the rain. Just Nice.
