Go early i.e. 8.00am2. Get photo as much as you want3. Each season the waterfall will be different, if winter, you may get different panorama and landscape of the waterfall.Thank You.

It was my first time climbing. Being the unfit person I was, I was panting a little when we crossed the halfway mark. It was cold and windy in March, so I was all wrapped up, but with every break I took, I was busy taking my layers off! It's not that hard to climb up, just that I was not prepared for it. It's important to stay hydrated. It's worth the effort - the view is really stunning, even through the ascend. Enjoy!

It was my first hiking trip and I decided to take the Seongpanak trail (9.6km one way) so that I can reach the summit. The hike is long and steep at certain stages. Very rocky road and proper hiking shoe is strongly recommended. The hike starts from visitor center is at 750m. At 1500m, there's a Jindalrae shelter where you can take a break for hot instant noodle and refill your drinks. The hike is tough for me (someone who jog/cycle once or twice a week). Walking stick is my best friend to support me all the way. Reaching the submit at 1950m is breathtaking. You will see the beautiful Baengnokdam lake. On the way down, at 1324m we hike to see Saraoreum Lake too. The whole trail with break took me almost 10 hrs (9.15am till 7pm). It's seems to be an easy hike for the Koreans, including the elderly but to me is a lot of determination and perseverance. Will definately hike at the other trails if I have the chance to go back to Jeju. ** I saw deer **

It was kind of windy when I had my visit at Yeongmori cliff. At first, I thought it was another ordinary rock formation viewing after taking a few steps from the entrance...I was about to back out from the trek thinking I can see much of these in the Philippines, but as soon as my tour guide led me to the farther side of the cliff, I started to appreciate how unique the lava rock formation  was.  The best view to take a picture maybe is to include Mt, Sanbang in the back draft. You may also climb a few steps to the top or catch a good timing for huge strike of waves by the rocks.  Wear appropriate shoes as the pathways are always slippery and wet.

It was just perfect vacation for me & my friends. We always dream of cruises holidays amnd just had a blast on superstar gemini cruise. Hair and beauty treatment was the first thingwe went for. it was just awesome,. they made us feel us like superstars. One my friend spent all her time in the casino. Rooms were so comfy and i enjoed the food at every restaurant. busan and jeju are beautiful places and i wish to go there again!

It was an impressive sight. If you wear appropriate shoes/trainers and get close to the waterfall, you can get a bit wet. But you have to be prepared to walk on big and, sometimes, round rocks. Tip: Get there early. It was our first stop and we were glad. As we were leaving (around 10am), buses full of tourists were arriving. It would have been quite impossible to take good pictures without getting someone's head in them because the staircase is not that wide.

It was a very windy and rainy day... we could not climb to the summit but the experience was trilling! Recommended for trekking amateurs and pros! There are many coffee shops around the routes but bring your own food, comfortable clothing and decent equipment. It's totally equipped with stairs and view points but safety is always first!

It was a very hot day yesterday, July 31st 2018, and I got sunburn the day before so in 33 degree heat and me didn't match. I didn't go up to the top but I did go up to the first viewing platform, which i think most people would be able to manage slowly, not matter your age. It is well paved, and the views are incredible. It was a very windy day too, so there was no show by the women divers, Haenyo, but you could see where they went out and to be honest the roughness of the seas showed how tough the women must have always been. There are a few shops near the bottom and one part way up, so you can purchase drinks and trinkets if you wish. There is a Starbucks and a Dunkin' Donuts and i think a McDonald's near the car park, as well as multiple Korean restaurants. Well worth a visit, even if you can't ascend to the peak.

It took me 2 hours to reach the peak from the bottom. There are a lot of people saying 3-4 hours but that is because they take breaks every 10 minutes.The first 70% of the trail you are in trees and can't see anything. They have steps and wooden walkways so you don't need any equipment at all. When I arrived at the top you couldn't see much around you because of the fog/pollution or whatever. The crater itself was ok, I took some photos, but the water is very very small. If you have limited time I would not suggest coming here, there are much better mountains in the mainland of Korea. When I came the rocks were all wet, but they were not smooth so it wasn't slippery. There is a bus that will take you directly here if you search online from where you are. The bottom sells a few things like water, noodles, and Korean sushi.

It takes almost one and a half hour to arrive the Island from Jeju-si. But the view was stunning on the Island. There is a shuttle bus service which has 4 stops across the Island and 5000 won for each passager to have an unlimited ride. There is a famous icecream store at the first stop which sell peanut icecream which is very delicious. The beach at the third stop is so stunning with a beautiful ocean. However, the restaurant on the island are quite expensive, so better prepare your own food if you have a tight budget.
It is very sad history has in Korea.But, it is a been boarding.I like this place.Because I can know Korea's history and first time I feel said when I touring Jeju island.
It is the first lava cave I visit, easy to walk in and the temperature is not too cold or too humid.

It is really long cave. Pls wear sensible shoes and high heels are NO NO there.I think it is nice for the first 15 min but after 15min it all looks the same. So unless you really knows you rocks well, or else it will be just a walking trip

It is probably a bad idea to go round island with the 5000 KRW tour bus - all the 4 stopovers were swarmed with tourists, but with just 2-3 hours to spare, we did not have much choice. First stop was at Udo-bong leading towards the Udo Lighthouse. Next was the Geommeolle Beach with black sand and rocks. The other two were beaches. At the last stop it was a little confusing as to which tour bus to board (to end the tour) as there were apparently 2 ferry terminals, and each terminal would sell tour bus with different docket colours.If we were to come again, we might do the 1.1 Olle Trail, perhaps by bicycle. At some parts of the island it was really picturesque coastline and we saw the haenyeo divers.Sans the big turnout of tourists, Udo will get a better rating definitely.

It is my first hiking ever, I do feel some kind of relaxation after the experience. At first, I wonder how can those people climb up to reach the top, it takes more than a thousand stairs to be on the top, I was pretty scared. But when I was first stepping on the environment, I can feel the natural beauty of the nature. It enhances me to have a greater heart to finish the journey. There also some strangely shaped stones while I was climbing up the stairs, I learned the history behind the stones and took several selfies with the special stones. About 20 minutes, we reached the highest point of the mountain. The mountain was naturally a dead volcano, which build up with lots of grasses and trees, and is no longer a crater. The view is like a green-sea. I had never been such relaxed before. It is a great experience to me and is memorable.The overall journey took us about 1 hour, if you are a fan of hiking, you must enjoy it as the view is priceless. **Remember to buy a bottle of water before you go, there are shops for you to buy some snacks and drinks in the beginning of the path.

It is interesting but not quite a must-see in Jeju. If you miss it, it is still no grave regret unless you love geology. An extremely long volcanic lava tube but due to the number of tourists, I believe the condition of the cave is not as well preserved as the caverns in Europe. Careful walking in the first 100 metres... can easily twist one's ankles.

It is an archetypal tuff cone formed by hydrovolcanic eruptions upon a shallow seabed about five thousand years ago.  Situated on the eastern seaboard of Jeju Island and resembles a gigantic ancient castle, this tuff cone is 182 meters high, has a preserved bowl-like crater. There are two hiking trails to reach the peak , take the white path uphill and the orange path downhill. You just follow the crowd and the signages along the trail. During May and the coming summer, you do not need a jacket or pullover as it will be  hot and you will sweat a lot on the climb up. Wear covered sports shoes and  a cap / hat. The first part of the hike is the easiest and the least steep.  The rest of the path comprises steps of varying steepness. The final stretch gets very steep. Along the hiking trail, there are benches and pavilions to rest. Take a sip of water, rest your aching legs before proceeding . Toilets are available along the way. From the peak, you can see beautiful landscapes of Jeju island and do take a photo with the signage saying you are at Sunrise Peak. It took us 30 minutes to reach the top. The downhill walk was much easier, just follow the wooden stairs meandering its way down.  At the bottom, you can go for drinks at the cafetarias.

It is a small island. we took the boat from Jeju. In a lobby full of Korean people, speak no English or Chinese. It was a bit challenge for me. ;) helpful enough, when I tried to talk to the ticket officer, she spoke a little Chinese. The boat took around 15 min. it is a pretty simple boat, with both people, and cars. with 30 min. time interval.Landing on Udo, we chose the red bus tour. 4 stops. the first stop is the best place I should say. Brilliant view! sea with sea wind. And there are some bars and restraunts where you could take a seat and rest.The rest of the 2-3 stops, are normal. On the bus, the driver were saying in Korean languange, which we do not understand at all. But we heard laugh from time to time, which we believe everyone else enjoyed the drivers speech.It is a good short stay. sun shine is strong, get prepare with some protections.

It is a museum as well as an ecological park related to stone culture in the lives of Jeju people.  It is huge and you are required to walk a lot.  It is about 40-45 minutes drive either from Jeju Airport or Seogwipo area.  You need 1-2 hours to go around the complex and the museum.  Opening hours: 0900-1800 hrs.  Closed on first Monday of the month unless it is a holiday.  Entry fee: KRW 5,000.  It should be a MUST in your itinerary of Jeju Island.

Initially we had wanted to walk here from Seogwipo but gave up and took a taxi up the hill, the road was quite crowded with taxis and the car park filled with tour buses and cars. It is a very touristy place, there is ample reason. This is the place where Jewel of the Palace (Daejanggeum 鸚㏝룝) was filmed - one of the first Korean dramas popular all over asia. There is a cut-out of Janggeum where you can put your face and take a photo.More importantly, the scenery is lovely and dramatic. The rock column rises out of the beautiful blue sea. We left the path and tourists behind and walked around the rocks to the edge. We even came to a point where we could see Saeyeongyo Bridge in Seogwipo. We came across a blue rock thrush and a nice little coffee house before grabbing a cab on the main road. There is a bus running but we did not want to wait for it... it is about 6-8 min drive to seogwipo town

In my first visit there, it was very foggy and I couldn't see nothing; it was just an exercise (a not that hard one).But this time I was very lucky: it was a very fine day with little cloud and its view was fantastic. You should definitely climb it and see it for yourself, but check the local weather before and choose the day wisely.Climbing it wasn't that hard for my mother-in-law in her late 60s and my preteen daughter. But you should bring a bottle of drinking water or two with you as there's no stores that sell one near the peak (you can buy them at the CVS store in front of the gate).

In 2018, I went there with my friends. I don't plan on coming here at first. I'm so angry because of the hot weather. So we decided to enter a very nice building. And this was the building. Contrary to the expectation that teddy bears couldn't be so cute, teddy bears were so cute!! The teddy bear museum reminds me of the past when I really liked teddy bears when I was very young. It was good to take pictures because it was full of cute teddy bears. After returning home, the picture in the Teddy Bear Museum was the best among the other pictures.

Ilchulbong is a huge rock/volcano/crater on the North East of Jeju Island. At first it seems a little daunting when you pull into the carpark as it looks really huge and steep. Yes, there are a lot of steps, but there are plenty of places to pause or sit for a rest and once you get to the top there's a great sitting/viewing platform. The views are really spectacular in all directions and you can see all over the mountain. It's really worth a visit if ou are going to Jeju.

If you've never been to a Korean public bath then there are some things you should know. First go in and pay - currently it's 6000 Won for the baths (segregated by gender) and 8000 Won for both the bathes and the   jimjilbang   (which is a unisex area filled with different hot rooms to enjoy a sweat lodge style experience). You can stay as long as you want and even sleep there. I would never suggest doing so however since even though this is a standard option for most Korean baths and they are arguably the cheapest place to sleep in Korea they are also loud sometimes crowded and generally pretty damned uncomfortable for sleeping. You will be given a set of shorts and a shirt. If you are large like me you can expect to have to cram yourself into them. Use the key provided to find a locker in your respective undressing area. Don't worry even though it doesn't seem like you should be naked in this area it's okay.From here you will go into the showering/bathing area. DO NOT get into any of the pools without first scrubbing yourself down. Soap is provided as well as some abrasive washcloths but you will need your own shampoo which you can buy in the changing area. Once you are clean you can enjoy a variety of different temperature pools and sauna options ranging from the almost freezing to the almost boiling. After you are finished soaking you can either shower again and leave or put on the shorts provided and go to the jimjilbang common area. Here you will find several different hot rooms including a traditional mud hut style outside that looks like a giant wasps nest. Some of these rooms are intense so work your way up to the higher temperatures don't stay in for too long and remember to drink lots of water. Food and beverages will be available in the common area so remember to stash some cash in your shorts before going to the jimjilbang. You can also relax on the floors in the common area watching some bad TV or just snooze. There are a few other nooks and crannies you can explore but this is a basic sketch of what you can expect. Once you're done at the jimjilbang you can go back for another shower and soak dry off enjoy some complimentary personal hygiene products (although I urge caution with their aftershave) get dressed and go home.  Yongduamhaesu Land is a decent example of a Korean bath. It's fairly clean and has some nice facilities. It's also pretty busy so expect high volumes of people especially tourists. Oh and for all you   foreigners   out there of non-Asian decent please expect an awkward amount of interest in your body especially those regions that you'd rather not have a room full of Koreans staring at. I know this is weird and to be perfectly blunt I wish they could be more circumspect with their curiosity but they don't really mean any harm. It's an unspoken obsession amongst humans - particularly men and especially Korean men - to compare genitals. Koreans just tend to be more obvious about it in ways that might signal either sexual interest or a punch in the mouth in non-Korean cultures. Have patience.

If you're a fan of teddy bears, then you should visit this place. You can probably complete this in 1 - 2 hours time. There's a outdoor park with more pictures to capture. Didn't really change much as compared to the first visit few years ago.. You have to pay an admission fee to enter, which i can't really remember but it's not expensive.

If you have time along the way and want to stop for some black fur pig, you can learn about the history about the pigs from this village. It was great to learn and appreciate the culture first before we ate at a local black fur pork place nearby. Plus you get to taste some tasty tea where you can apparently taste all 5 different flavors, and horse placenta which makes a funny story to tell that it tastes like almonds.

If you have a chance to be there, try this... roll a filled water bottle down the slope (apply some force like bowling). It will move down first then the bottle began to   hestitate  , then it changes direction to move up the slope. It is really fun!

If you book a car to travel around, probably you can consider to drive pass this mysterious road which took less than 20min when you're on the way to other attraction. This mysterious road is quite interesting, it is about rolling up this   Down slope  .  You can try it, just by asking the driver to off the engine of your car, and let it roll freely. I also tested it out with my water bottle, it was quite funny, the bottle actually roll up. At first, i thought this was due to law of gravity, but i realize is just optical illusion caused by the surrounding that cause this illusion of   down looking slope  . Fun place with interesting facts.

If you are driving, I recommend you visit Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak first at around 7am to catch the sunrise at around 8:00am something.For me it's better seeing the Seongsan Ilchulbong in a far away place rather than hiking it for 30mins. So before reaching the gps route you would notice a lot of cars parked at the road side. Stop for a while and from there you would see a crowd of people waiting for the sunrise at the seashore and infront is the mountain touching the sun.If you like, you can still proceed with the peak 1km away from the stopover and hike a bit at the stairs to see the peak.After that a few kms away is the Seongsan Port going to Udo Island.Gps to Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak 710-7923Gps to Seongsan Port 7825671Upon reaching Udo island in a 15min ferry ride for 5500won, you can either walk, cycle or rent a scooter. You need an international drivers license to rent a scooter for 25000won for 2 hours, which i think is really short. Circling the whole island with a bit of stop over would already take you 2 hours. Not much to see in the island, a bit of flowery patches, mermaid statues and lighthouse and that's it.

If you are a teddy bear fanatic, you can give it a visit. I personally like teddy bear and was exciting to visit this place but after the first level, it was overall the same bear with different costume and theme showcase in the window and it's all in KOREAN! So U don't get to read the history of what being showcased. Only those with pictured like lady Diana's wedding, Roosevelt, Marilyn monroe are some examples. And the bear not that cute compare with some other bear I have seen before. It's very pricy too for you to get the bear. Paying for a premium but the quality is not that good. I ended buying a bear key chain as a remembrance n there is not hand carry bags for it. They charge KRW500.I was just wondering if I were to buy the bigger sized bear, so I still need to pay for the hand carry bag? After all, visitor pay for the entrance fees and it's much more than the KRW500.

If you are a Kpop fan and have an afternoon to spare, you shouldn't miss this. There were plethora of stations and   things to do   for me and my friends who were less knowledgable about kpop. Don't skip the gift shop on first floor!

If it's your first time visit, definitely take the path to Oedolgae. If you have time, from the main entrance, take a left and it will take you along a path along the ocean. Go about 1/2 mi walk along the path and you'll see off on your right a smaller path. Take this and it will take you down to the ocean. Many locals take this down and it's a small watering hole where locals go to swim and fish. Once you get to the bottom, the navigation along the rocky formations can be challenging but very much worth it. It's not a beach but you're right next to the waves as they come in. It's absolutely beautiful. Just for context, I took my 8 year old daughter and 6 year old son. They had to be careful navigating, but was able to do so with adult supervision. Many others have come to appreciate this but they have been leaving their trash behind and it's quite saddening to see such a beautiful place littered with garbage. If you do go down, please respect the beauty and take your garbage with you.

If it’s springtime?or even summer or fall-- that means it’s also time to think about visiting beautiful Gapado, or Gapa Island, which sits just off the southwestern tip of the Korean resort island of Jeju. ? Located some 5.5 km (3.42 mi.) offshore, Gapado is a quick ferry run from the port village of Moseulpo (maybe 20 min.)Gapado nearly got the distinction of being South Korea’s southern-most point, but that title went to nearby Marado.? Some tourists want to go there just to say they’ve been, but Gapado is noteworthy in its own right.? Gapada is home on its .84 sq. km? to about 250 residents.? The island has a picturesque school, a church and a Buddhist temple.? There are a couple Korean restaurants and small stores.? But, it’s a good idea to take bottled water and snacks with you, particularly if you plan to hike or bike all the way around the island.? You can bring your own bike, or perhaps rent one there.? Walking (Gapado has a 5k hiking trail that is part of Jeju’s famous Olle Course) or biking/electric scooter likely will be your only transportation choices, as there are no fossil-fueled vehicles on Gapado… But more about that in a bit.What makes it so special there?? Gapado offers spectacular views of the iconic mountain peaks or “sans” back to the north on Jeju, including Sanbangsan, Gunsan, Songaksan, Gogeunsan, Dansan and the Big Daddy of All Sans, Halla…the massive, central shield volcano that formed Jeju Island and the highest peak in South Korea.Equally impressive are Gapado’s golden-green barley fields, surrounded by traditional “batdam” stone agricultural walls.? The crop begins sprouting in late winter and reaches its full glory in late spring.? Gapado’s tradition of barley cultivation dates back to the 1840s and is celebrated annually with the Gapa Green Barley Festival. (Dates for 2015 are April 18- May 10.)Back to that transportation thing…well, barley is not the only thing green about Gapado.? Wind turbines, solar panels and other renewable, sustainable forms of energy are now being used on the island as part of a plan to make it one of the world’s first carbon-free islands, maybe THE first…. Summing up:? Good points:? outstanding natural beauty and photo ops in all directions; fresh air; clear aqua-hued seas that reveal black lava rocks; abundant hiking; colorful neighborhoods festooned with murals, recycled art and traditional Korean cultural artifacts;? site of annual Gapa Green Barley Festival? (April 18-May 10, 2015)Be sure to have on hand:? bottled water and small snacks; comfortable shoes; sunblock;? sunglasses; and a hat that won’t blow off easily; a stroller for very young children, layered clothing for coolish days.? There is little shade on the island, so be on guard against dehydration or sunburn on those hot or even excessively windy days.? Getting there:? Take an Intercity Bus from most points on Jeju Island to Seogwipo Main Terminal, and from there, a local bus to Moseulpo .? There is a short walk to the ferry from the busstop.? Ferries generally run twice a day, but as schedules and fares can change, it’s probably best to check for specifics through the Korean Travel Hotline: dial 1330 in country or outside Korea: +82-2-1330 or 1339 (Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese)

I woke up really early to get ready for this hike. I took the first bus 281 from the old bus terminal in Seogwipo leaving at 6am. We arrived at Seongpanak trail entrance about half an hour later. I did this trail mid January and you need crampon for this. Personally, I don?t like slippery surface so crampons really give me the confidence. But I saw people on the hike didn?t have crampons. Some other people hiked in their running shoes. Snow was thick but you basically walked on top so I guess You don?t necessarily need hiking boots. Unless you go off trail, the snow will be knee deep. It was such a nice feeling to see everybody get up and early to start the hike when it?s still dark out. The hike up was not very challenging and it took me about 4.5 hours. I?m an extremely slow walker. Keep in mind that there is cut off time. If you start too late and couldn?t get up to the last shelter on Seongpanak trail before 12pm, you are not allowed to go to the summit. The view at the top was so beautiful. It was very windy though. I took Gwaneumsa trail down since I wanted to change views. That was challenging. My knees hurt so bad even though I already wore knee braces. It?s shorter than Seongpanak trail but it took me almost the same amount of time. There was one part quite steep and I didn?t notice the rope which you can hold on to, I slid down and broke my trekking pole. Apart from being slippery, the trail is quite rocky and by the end of the day, after a beautiful sunny day, the snow started melting and made the trail very slushy. There was time I almost gave up, my whole body hurt and I started to get blister on my toes. When I got to the entrance of the trail, I took bus 475 for 10 mins to a university entrance station then changed to bus 281 to go back to Seogwipo. I guess you can take 281 directly from Gwaneumsa to Seogwipo but I didn?t know where it was so I followed the crowd. I totally recommend this hike.

I went with three friends to Geomunoreum on a Sunday in February 2016. The first thing I'd recommend is ensuring that your taxi driver takes you to the right place as ours dropped us off an hour's walk away from where we were supposed to be at an abandoned building.When we finally got to the Oreum we got in for free as Jeju English teachers. I think the prices were around 5KWon per person without Jeju residency.We had to join a tour group (obviously Korean-speaking guide) for the whole walk. The stops were far too regular and spoke for too long. This is why the route options are 1 hour/2.5hours/3.5hours (I think), because the guiding makes them so long! I guess it was our fault for not being able to understand, but it did mean the walk was interrupted and the experience ruined a little by travelling in a pack. We tried to pace ourselves between groups but kept getting trapped in them. I don't think you can do this walk without a guide.That said, the views were beautiful.

I went to this peak three times during my stay for a year on Jeju island! First time was in August when it was sweltering hot, so I never climbed it just took pictures from the bottom. The second time I went was in September when it was cooler and I climbed it and it only took the recommended time of 30 minutes. Such a beautiful view and the sign saying you reached the top is very nice. My last time climbing it was in December for the sunrise and my mom and I made it to the top just before sunrise but it was an overcast day so we only saw a tiny bit of pink under the clouds but still it was a nice view of Jeju from that height! Definitely recommend doing this while you are in Jeju :)

I went on a tour group to Jeju. The bus arrived at the Mysterious Road, all of us were waiting eagerly in anticipation of what's about to come (after hearing so much hype about it). Looking out the window, I saw a little kid on the street place a plastic bottle on the tarmac, and it looked like it was rolling up hill at first, but because of the way the bus was angled along the road, I was quick to discern that it was a mere optical illusion.As our bus reached the front of the 'queue', our driver switched off the engine, and slowly, but surely, our bus picked up speed. It was interesting as it was the first time I sat in a vehicle with it's engine switched off, THAT WAS IT. I looked out the front panel, and we were obviously going downhill, as I could not even see the sky (just trees whizzing by our bus).I'm guessing it only looks like you're going uphill from certain angles. Thankfully, we didn't spend too much time there, and off we went to our next destination!

I was thinking of skipping this attraction in favour of the natural attractions. Due to bad weather I visited this place on a whim but I enjoyed it better than expected. The building itself is quite pretty like a big greenhouse. The floral arrangement and landscaping is tasteful although not as good as Gardens by the Bay in Singapore. There are pretty sculptures dispersed through the compound. There are many different gardens to explore. We visited the indoor gardens first followed by taking the lift up to the top floor for a view of Seogwipo and lastly took the train for the outside gardens. It was too cold and windy to walk outside. There was some confusion about where to buy train tickets, the driver helped to walk to the counter and buy our tickets. Spring is probably a good time to visit since many flowers are in bloom. It would be good if they can stop the vandalism of the trees by the Koreans, many of them scratched their names on the branches.

I was slightly disappointed that we weren't able to see stalagmites and stalactites like I thought we could.A warning in advance, tourists are only allowed access to a fraction of the entire cave (it is still a long walk) and the walk isn't a loop, so you'll be seeing everything twice.TIP: Perhaps this is obvious, but it was quite cool and damp in the cave, so I recommend bringing an extra layer and wearing proper, closed shoes. The floor of the cave was quite puddle-ridden and it can be easy to trip as you stare at the inner walls. Also, bring a tripod or use the timer on your camera if you plan on taking photos.Overall, I really enjoyed my experience, though I should say that this is the first 'real' cave that I've ever visited. It's a good place to visit if you're on the island, but I wouldn't fly here all the way from Seoul just to visit.

I was on my wear the Toms until they literally fall off my feet, and this definitely got them about there. If you do anything before going to this cave, make sure you have the right waterproof, grippy-ish shoes for the job. But really, this was cool, literally.  I managed to be hot and sweaty almost everywhere we went while on the island, but in the cave he temp drops to a comfortable 50something degrees. Just glorious! Is it worth the walk? I'm not sure. It was nice enough, and definitely cool to say I have been inside a cave at least once. So I guess I would put this on the itinerary if you are visiting the island for he first time. Would I go again? Likely not, I think once was enough!

I was a little disappointed by the collection here, but then again this is a teddy bear museum and I'm not the biggest fan of teddies in the first place. It's a great attraction for younger children... They will have a great time. For adults, perhaps not so much.

I visited Seongeup Folk Village as part of the tour package to Jeju Island that was provided as free gift by a company that I need not mentioned here. As an Asian and having extensively travelled throughout Asia. I am familiar have experience all sorts of tricks and gimmicks. The first tip that this was another hard sell stop is that there is no time limit for the stop. Prior to this stop, we visited the famous Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak, they insisted that we returned to the bus by 1 hour which is not enough to really enjoy the place. However, we were told we can take all the time we need at Seongeup. Then a nice looking old lady who can speak Mandarin were waiting to greet us and give us a tour of the place. I was curios why no such tour guide were organised for Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak. The whole tour of the village was short 15 minutes, most of the info she provided I can easily find out from internet, then we were ushered into a room in one 'village building' where she proceed to let taste and test their natural products and tell us how miraculous is the products, the tea, the honey, horse bones and horse cream. The whole presentation took twice as long as the village tour. Then she went on and on and on about how healthy are the people and it is due to the miracles of horse bones. I mean come on. There are horses the world over. Surely if horse bones are the key to living longer and younger,.Someone other than the Jeju people would have known about it. Then next she talks about pricing which I almost fell out of my chair. Korean Won 190,000 or USD 185 for horse bones pellet? I am not sure how many fools are there in the world that bought into this ludicrous claims. Right there and then I wanted to leave. She then changes tack and describe how they money will help preserve the village, fund village children education healthcare etc etc. I heard that before in almost all my travel. Apparently, some of my fellow tour travellers are interested, so they stayed in the room while I explored the 'village'. The area is very small, most of the 'buildings' are similar to the one that I was in and there are various product demo sessions going on in other 'buldings'. In the end, we spend a total a 2 hour there and the organizer waited until everyone got onto the bus. It so different from the Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak stop where they chased back onto the bus and even went into the washroom to look for missing passengers. Just for non-asian travellers tour organiser gets sales commissions if the tour groups buy something. So they benefit if when they spend more types at such places rather then the actual sight that you wanted to see.

I visited Jeju Glass Castle last winter. I went there twice while I stayed in Jeju for a week. The first time I visited, the weather was good and so my family walked around the museum with joy. We were very glad to be there. The second time, I was very thrilled to visit again, but unluckily, it was raining. Our family struggled to see the sculptures that were placed outside. I recommend that you go to Jeju Glass Castle when the weather is good.

I visit Jeju at December 2015 and stayed near this museum. I have no plan to visit this museum, but from the outside looks interesting. I just made a couple of photos in the front. After that I intend to buy some souvenirs, but in fact visitors should buy ticket and enter the museum first. There is no souvenir shop available outside the ticketing gate

I took the eorimok trail which took about 2.5 hours to get to the top with the rest rooms, the first part of the trek is hard work and quite strenuous. After reaching the top I took the yeongsil trail back down which had some of the most stunning views along the way. As I came by bus the walk down from the yeongsil trail to the yeongsil ticket office where the bus stop is located takes another 40minuts or so depending on the pace. I Would highly recommend visiting this area and trying the trails.

i thought the museum sounded stupid but it was actually really cute!!! there were so many scenes set up with stuffed animals on the first floor.  they were so creative!  then you can you to the second floor and take pictures.  there's the rock band set up, the proposal bear, and many more.  there are also famous works of art re-done with teddy bears. finally there's the gift shop.  everything is over priced but you can't expect anything else...

I think this maze is one of the bigger maze land made famous by the   running man   Korean reality show. It's comprise by 3 mazes and I kind of enjoyed the the first or wind maze. If you're pressed for time and wants the easier path, take the 2 outer routes .

I think it was a great idea for them to have teddy bears pose for historical moments, people and scenes.  It may seem whimsical at first, but it is also a perfect platform for parents to explain certain moments in history and people to them.  E.g. having a bear bandaged with only one ear to portray u know who.  Perhaps one easily missed teddy bear is the actual world's most expensive teddy bear!There is also a gift shop at the end (with Michael and Audrey...) where they sell a variety of teddy bears.  Although the teddy bears look as normal as any teddy bears, mind u, u don't get those mass produced made-in-u-know-where quality.  Worth taking a look!This place will be more suitable for family with young children or people who just love teddy bears.

I stayed 4 night in Hamdeok Beach. If you are visiting Jeju for the very first time, you might want to move around because Jeju is quite big. Hamdeok is a great location to start your trip. It takes 20 mins by car, 30~40 mins by bus from Jeju International airport. It has many bus lines which offers you easy access to Airprot, Mountain Halla, Jeju city centre and even Seogwipo. I love the beach itself, but also there are lots of place to eat and chill. If you like to camp, there is a camping & caravan park at the end of beach. I loved it !!

I really enjoyed visiting this cave. It reminded me of the beauty of God's creation. I was expecting to explore the entire cave, but unfortunately, they only allow the public to explore the first 1 kilometer. Nevertheless, it was an eye-opening experience for me.Tips:-1. Wear comfortable clothes.2. Wear a good pair of shoes.3.Bring a cap.4. Bring a torchlight. You gotta visit this place if you are in Jeju Island!

I made the climb on 22.11.2013 but few days before my climb, I have been keeping my eye on the weather on the mountain. The first snowstorm hit the mountain top a few days earlier and I know that my hike will be much difficult with the snow along the path to the top of the mountain. I chose to ascend from Gwanuemsa trail and descend from Seogpanak trail and I know that I have made the right choice. Starting from Gwanuemsa trail was much tougher, with the rocky pathways in the beginning to the steep climb in the middle of the trail and snowy trail all the way up to the mountain top. Along the way, there is no food on sale but there is a shelter for people to fill up their water, at the Samgakbong Shelter. The total length of Gwanuemsa Trail is about 8.7km and Samgakbong shelter is about 6km from the starting point. To make it here will take about 2 hrs of normal walk. There is also a toilet available here but the you wouldn't want to spend more time at this toilet. The trail after Samgaokbong SHetlter has obviously been much tougher, with a lot of steep steps, or even no steps at all (all covered by thick snow) and at some point, the is a need to pull the rope along the trail to move upwards. The efforts are all worthwhile upon reaching the top of the mountain. It is good to come on a clear day because the view along Gwanuemsa trail especially upon approcahing the mountain top is spectacular.At the top of the mountain, the wind can be really strong. Be prepared with the chill and wear enough layer to prevent from getting cold. As mentioned, I descend from Seogpanak trail and this is somehow a boring trail. The total length is about 9.5km but all I can see is trees along the way. There is nothing much to see but it was quite a flat trail that make it the choice among many hikers. There are food on sale at the Samgakbong Shelter, and also a big toilet there. A good stop for hikers to build up their energy before continuing their hike. Crampon also on sale for 5000 won. Overall, it was a fresh and good place for first time traveller. If there is a chance to come back to Hallasan, I will sure try the other 2 trails on the western side of the mountain.

I loved my hike in Hallasan. We were a couple and we decided to take the 'most challenging trial' - Gwaneumsatrail (8.7 km).  There are four Hallasan trails on and around the mountain, but only two of these trails will take you all the way up to the volcano?s crater lip ? theGwaneneumsa trail is one of these, theSeongpanaktrail is the other one. It is important that you check beforehand which trial is open, because it depends on the weather forecast. In my case all the 4 trials were partially open which meant that the crater lip was not accessible unfortunately. There is a website you  check (in Korean) or you can simply do what I did and ask the staff at the reception of the hotel. Each trials is easily accessible by bus, however the buses are not that frequent - for example 1 every hour for the Gwaneneumsa train, so you might need a bit of planning. Our trail was accesible for 6 out of the 8.7 km and took us to the first shelter (1500m elevation) the hike took us.6 hours back/forth including a quick lunch break; the pace wasn't that high but we weren't that slow either. If you want to access the crater lip, one think that you need to bear in mind is that you need to make it to the first shelter by 12-13 depending on the season (November was 12.00pm).Another thing to remember is that there is no convenience store or food vendor available during the hike, so you want to pack some food (kimbap is a good option) and water. As the hike itself, I really enjoyed it, you will feel immerse in the nature and you will enjoy a nice variety of vegetation depending on the altitude.

I love flowers and tropical exotic plants, however we were there in July 2016 we don't find too many flowers around just a few species. We did find kiwi fruit tree in there with its fruits, our first time to see the tree. It was hot and humid, so umbrella and cold bottled water are recommended.

I hiked up Mt. Halla in the winter of 2007. It was my first hike up a mountain and relatively easy getting up to the first summit as a beginner. Unfortunately, I dont remember exactly what trail and how many hours it took but it was a day trip (up and returning down). The only downside with visiting during winter was that the snow and ice made it a bit challenging in some parts, since I didnt have proper footwear. My body ached a bit the next day, but spending the day at the spa made it all worth it!

I hiked up Hallasan during Spring March 2013. It was my first time scaling such mountains and i found it relatively tough. (20yo M) I would say its a very satisfying hike, as its really mind over body for my case. The mountain is roughly 1960m, and I started with the Seongpanak course at 700+m. It took roughly 4 hours to get up and slightly more to get down. Descend is more generally difficult as you have to take note of the ice and snow which gets very dangerous even with proper hiking equipment.Just some points to take note of.Hiking during Winter would provide very nice views but very dangerous.Remember to be well preparedIt takes around 10 hours round trip for a first time beginner

I have been to many caves but this is the first volcanic cave. There are explanations in both korean and English with pictures and the light shine on the park of the rocks to show you which part is mentioned. It is a 1km walk which is quite relaxing. I took bus 201 from the old bus terminal in Seogwipo City and it took about 2 hours to get to the Manjaggul cave entrance station. From the station, you?ll need to walk for 2 km to the park. During your walk to the cave, you will see a Maze Park. I didn?t visit this park but from what I observed from other people, they seem to have a lot of fun. The cave is quite straight forward. You pay the entrance ticket and get in and just walk and learn all the information along the way. When I left the park, I noticed there is a bus station so I checked it out and realized that I can take bus 711-1 to go back to the Main Street where the Manjaggul cave entrance bus stop is. From there, I can take 201 back to Seogwipo.

I had been to the Batu Caves and Sam Poh Kong caves in Malaysia but Manjanggul Cave in Jeju is different. Firstly, it is uniquely a long stretch of lava tube formed as a result of volcanic lava eruption and condensation unlike those limestone caves we found in Malaysia. Secondly, there is no religious worshipping in the caves unlike those in Malaysia where we found Hinduism and Taoism deities constructed in the interior accompanied along the many prayer ceremonies. The entrance fee is 2000KRW. As we proceeded down into the cave, I could feel the chilling cold wind brushed my face. It was dimly lit and at certain area it was completely darkness. Initially, I was not used to the coldness and the darkness but after walking for some time, I became used to it and became quite fun trying to avoid the wet area and listening to the echoes of those voices of our group. After our lava tunnel exploration, we had our lunch at a Korean restaurant near the entrance of the attraction. A wonderful restaurant and we had good taste of delicious Korean food.   We were in South Korea for 13 days and flew from Busan to Jeju via Jeju air. From Seoul to Busan, we traveled the whole east coast line stopping at Namiseon Island, Seoraksan, Donghae, Samseok, Gyeongju etc before we reached Busan. Our Korean coach driver `abandoned' us at Busan and returned to Seoul. At Jeju, we engaged another Korean driver who charged 180,000 KRW for one day full day tour. We engaged him for 2 days  which means the 9 of us paid about Sing $20/- each for a day tour. He spoke good Mandarin as well and he was very polite and cracked a lot of jokes while he brought us around. Manjanggul Cave was our first attraction we visited. The tour around Jeju Island was really amazing. There were so many natural scenic wonders so fascinating, so memorable and the scenery was so awesome and jaw-dropping. It was really a lovely island.

I found out about Love Land on Google during our cruise to Asia.  So when we landed my husband and I took a taxi cab there.  It was right next door to the Museum of Modern Art so we checked that out first.  And then we walked over to Love Land.  It could also be called   Happy Land   as we would every now and then hear an eruption of laughter from other visitors.  We were certainly laughing too.The sculptures in various poses of love were whimsical and clever.  It was a nice walk that took us about an hour and a half.  At the end we went into the shop where there were small dioramas and objects for sale.Volcanoes and waterfalls I have seen before.  But I had never seen a place like Love Land.  When we returned to our cruise ship fellow cruisers said   Why didn't you tell us?!  We would have gone.

I found much of Jeju island to be very commercialized and crowded with loud tour groups. This is a great place to enjoy the natural beaty of Jeju with smaller groups of people. There is a small entrance fee.  The first half mile is along a wide crushed rock road. It is lined with young   nutmeg   trees. The trees are in the yew family. They are Torreya nucifera and are native to Japan. I  visited in October when the small edible nuts ripen. The nuts are encased in a thin husk that has a wonderful aroma. You will see people collecting them under the large trees.  Eventually the road ends and then you follow a loop trail that is about 2 feet wide it is covered with a hemp rope mat that felt lovely to walk on with bare feet.  The crowds end at the beginning of the narrow trail so you can walk through this section in peace and really marvel at the enchanting colors and smells of the forest and hear the songs of the many birds.  There were signs to watch for snakes but I saw none. The yews are huge.  Make sure to investigate the tree bark it is fabric like and soft. Also many of the other plants have English name labels which is nice. The trail is flat and should take a leisurely couple of hours or less if you rush.  I noticed a lot of people sitting on benches in the first section enjoying picnic lunches.

I flow to Jeju just to walk up this mountain.  You have to apply to the  Hallasan National Park visitor management system for the QR code admission ticket. My ticket was for the Gwaneumsa Course, time slot 5-30am - 8-00am.   I started my walk at 7-50am,  It was perfect walking weather, overcased so not too warm.  There is a 500 hiker per day limit on this route to the top, on the other easier route there is a 1000 hiker per day limit. The first few kms is easy going and you think to yourself this walk is going to be a piece of cake.  After around 4 kms you reach the first of two public toilets on the route.  From there the walk becomes a uphill slot with countless wooden steps. On the way up there is two downhill's with maybe a couple of hundred steps to walk down before walking uphill again.  After the second public W.C.  the route is a never ending series of wooden staircases until at last it flattens  out and the top of the mountain.  When I did it there was maybe a hundred or more walkers queuing to get a photo next to the summit stone.    I just gave my phone to a person and asked them to take a photo with the stone in the background. Within minutes I was on my way back down.The reason why you need a photo with you and the summit stone (even if it over your shoulder in the distance) is to claim your Certificate of climbing Mt, Hallasan. On the Gwaneumsa Course you can self print your certificate at a booth just past the QR-cord booth at the trail head  If like me you are clueless with mobile phones you can go the manned QR code booth and them to do it for you.  There have a printer in the booth and was very happy to do it for me.   It costs 1000 won (around 1 us$) Facts and figures, I am a 73 year old Englishman on an extended holiday in Korea.  Start time 7-50am, summited at 11-05am.   Started down at 11-15 and back to the trailhead at 12-55pm. Yes I do class myself as a bit of a mountain walker so these times  are maybe a little faster then average, but mountain walking is about enjoying yourselves and not about how fast you can get up and down. I took a litre of liquid, in hindsight I should have taken more and I did finish it off when I was within sight of the carpark. There is a shop across the road from the carpark.   Food, I took no food just a few sweets and a couple of chocolate bars.  So the bottom line is you have to take all the food and drink with you.  It does say that you can get drinking water at the second WC (shelter) but I could not find any so don't depend on it. Getting back to Jeju City.   There was no buses so I started walking the 8 miles back to my hotel on the seafront. Pleased to say that  I did manage to flag down a taxi after around a mile.  All in all a very enjoyable day out on the mountain.

I first saw this falls on the local map I received. I investigated and stopped there using the airport limousine bus route no 600. It is a short walk from the main road and when you get closer, the sound of the water guides to its location. The water falls over a short (50-100 m) cliff, but it is beautiful and ideal to take some nature pictures. It runs into the sea immediately and provides a picturesque scene.Be careful when you visit, since the railing on the sea side was broken and seems quite a safety hazard for me.This spot does provide you with the opportunity to take some awesome pictures.

I first heard of Saebyeol Oreum when watching Hyori's Bed & Breakfast, and I really wanted to visit this famous oreum. The hike was insanely steep, and we huffed and puffed to get to the summit (520m above sea level). The view from the top was breathtaking, and the eoksae (flamegrass) covering the entire oreum was absolutely gorgeous. We were lucky to catch the magnificent sunset, and it was a great end to our Jeju trip. Highly recommended!

I expected a longer walk for this, given that this is what Mother Nature had blessed us with, but this cave is only opened for the first 1km to the public. Still, it was an amazing sight (with the turtle-like rock formation and the various lava formations). Wear comfortably with a cap or hoodie as the cave will be chilly and the water will drip from above! Also, bring flash lights as it can get quite dark!

I enjoyed the show very much. The young performers are skillful and must put a lot of effort for the show. It is totally beyond expectation. However  the horse riding experience was not worth to try. The staff was not friendly and official photo-taking costs too much. If it is not the first time to experience horse-riding  I would tell you   don't  .

I didn't reach the summit but hiking the Eorimok and Yeongsil trails didn't provide amazing views as far as I was concerned, but it's definitely worth doing.Take the 740 bus from City Bus Terminal to Eorimok (krw1800, 45 min) or Yeongsil Ticket Office (krw 2800, 60 min). Bus leaves CBT at 07:00, 08:00, 09:00, 10:00. You don?t want to set off after 10:00 as you won?t get back! Last returns are 17:36 (Yeongsil) and 17:55 (Eorimok) April through October.I took the Eorimok trail up (there?s an easy 1km walk from the bus stop to the trailhead) and reached the Witseoreum shelter in 2 hours, including stops. The first 2.4km are quite tough but it gets much easier the further you go. If you?re worried about your ankles then wear hiking boots but trail shoes are fine. The descent down via Yeongsil was a leisurely 90 mins but it feels like it would be a slightly tougher climb compared to Eorimok. There?s also a 2.5km downhill walk from the trailhead to the bus stop, so bear that in mind if you decide to start from Yeongsil. The scenery is much better on Yeongsil, although those with vertigo may find it tough, even with the very good safety barriers on the route. Eorimok doesn?t have those problems but the first 2km is under forest cover, with little scenery to admire for most of the climb.If you want to hike to the summit start very early, which probably means you'll need a car in case you miss the last bus back.There are clean, normal toilets at both entrances and at the Witseoreum stop. You will have to carry all trash back down as there are no bins anywhere on the mountain. You can buy hot instant noodles at the Witseoreum but you?ll have to carry it back down. I bought several buns and pastries at Paris Baguette for my hike.

I completed every single course over a period of a year so the following comments are just my opinions. If you are staying for a short period of time in Jeju courses 6 and 7 are the most popular and will probably get the most from. Both are very scenic and you will get to see some of the major sights. If you start at one of the information sites, you can pick up a Jeju Olle guide which has maps and information of the trails, guides for the Buses, to get to and from the starting points. Also I'd recommend downloading Kakao Maps app on your phone and you can zoom in and see the actual trail that you are following when you are on it. It comes in handy especially for me when I made a wrong turn on my trips. If your doing the entire course I'd recommend buying a jeju Olle Passport. Carry it with you and get it stamped at the starting points and halfway way points of the trails. I was living near jeju city and caught most of Buses from the Jeju inter city bus centre. The 101/201 express buses will take you to/ or near a lot of the starting points but I'd recommend picking up the Olle Guide first and the info in that is invaluable.Most of the Starting points are close to the roads unless you are going to one of the 3 islands. I used booking.com most of the time to book places to stay overnight as I don't speak Korean. Jeju has a lot of places to stay and there would be abundant places to stay except for maybe a couple of the more remote locations on the trail. There are offical Olle trail Hostels throughout the trails to which are very nice. If planning for no Korean speakers just check before hand that you are not traveling on a Jeju holiday as a lot of paces close down and might be harder to find a place to stay. Of course take plenty of water and there's usually 7/11 of CV's around the place where you can get snacks to eat.The trails themselves are very beautiful , Different scenes ranging from Black volcanic rock on the coastlines, Forest trails, Beautiful beaches, Hill sides, a lot of Oreums (Jeju extinct volcanoes) small towns with a chance to see wildlife and a lot of friendly people. For myself my favourite trails were routes 11, 18-1 Chuja-Do island), 1-1 (Udo island), 7. For me the stronger trails were on the southern eastern point of the island starting from route 6 through to 15.Getting to the supporting islands it you might take note you will need your Passport to catch the ferry to Udo. You must show it when buying a ticket. There are a lot of ferries going most of the day to Udo. They have a very nice Peanut ice cream there. The smaller island Gapado at the time I went there were only 2 ferries in the day and its not the most reliable service and the ferries can be cancelled due to bad weather can be cancelled due to bad weather so check beforehand if you can. Chuja-Do island was one of my favourites. When I done it they had 2 ferries a day and you can not do the whole trail in time to catch the next ferry back so be prepared to stay over night. I have heard of instances when the weather turned bad and people had to stay a couple of nights on the island because the ferries were cancelled so just plan for that just in case. it is a beautiful Island though and one of my favourites.I would also recommend going and joining the Olle Walkers Facebook group. They take guided walks along certain courses and have great information about weather and so forth. all you need to do is contribute to the group from time to time.

I come there first time.And I am very exciting when I see a bigest mountain and very cool on December 2014. There provide a lots of coffee shop such as Starbuck , Dunkin Donut and Coffee Bean. If you go down to the small beach then You meet Ajuma who sell seafood. Dont forget to try it!!!

I came here by chartered taxi, I got rate 130k KRW for 8 hrs use. Not sure how to come here with public transport though. For a first timer underground trip like me, it's quite interesting. The track is not very long, not suggested for Claustrophobic person (like my friend) as it's dark,wet and getting smaller inside. Suggested to bring a raincoat with you, if you forgot don't worry you can buy on convenience store in there.

I came here after visiting the nearby Jeju Loveland. This museum has 4 floors. First floor is the Welcome Stage, which traces the history of computers and hardwares. Second floor is Open Stage, which depicts the history and development of computer games. Third floor is Hidden Stage, which showcases how computers changed and expanded our everyday life. The Basement 1 is Special Stage, which is used for special exhibitions.Second and third floors allow visitors to play old computer and arcade games such as Space Invaders, Galaxy etc. Playing these games bring back fond memories of my younger days. Before leaving, I headed to the cafe at B1 and ordered the keyboard waffle for its novelty, not cheap at 12,000 won.Admission fees 8,000 won. Note it is closed on Monday. Worth a visit if you have half a day to spare. Suggest you combine this place with the nearby Jeju Loveland.

I call this the upside down mountain because that is basically what it is. I won't try to explain what geological forces were involved  in creating this unusual site, (mainly because I don't know :) but it I'll just say that I've never seen this sort of thing before.It is like looking at an upside down Halasan, only shorter or deeper or something.It was fun for the first five minutes of wondering while looking down at a hole in the ground but then its time to go.If you are going there I'd advise to take a picnic and sitting on the grass eating lunch. Because after staring at the hole there really isn't much to do and it takes a long time to get there. It is one of those places that you really should see but after five minutes you are wondering why you came.

I am not a teddy bear lover, but I found the collection very interesting. First of all, these were the collection of a Ms. Joanne Oh, a teddy bear artist. The bears date up to generations of collectibles. The design varies with time. The size of the bear are from tiny to bigger than man size. There were several hall showing different themes. Of course it will end with a souvenir shop showing many bear designs. In the international bear, there was even one of President Obama, with a letter of President Obama to Joanne Oh. The museum also has an advocacy of bear conservation. All in all, it was interesting with plenty of Photo opportunity for my wife who loved it so much. By the way, the materials used in Ms. Oh's bear were all made of ecological-friendly materials, another advocacy of this fantastic bear artist.

I absolutely recommend you to take a day trip and hike up Hallasan if you are in Jeju. Even though if it takes the whole day, since it is about 20km walking, it is worth it. If you are in okay shape I'd recommend you to go up on the Seongpanak trail. It is longer but easier than Gwaneumsa trail. The hike has a lot of stairs, so don't expect climbing. Once getting up, the most thing that shocked us what the loads and loads of bugs, since we never heard about that. They don't bite but they do get on you which is annoying. That said, the view is beautiful, to the island but also to the crater. Going down I'd recommend Gwaneumsa trail since it is a lot more beautiful and more to see. It is only the first third part that is the hardest, after that it gets okay. Remember to start climbing early since you have to reach the checkpoint before a certain time depending on the year. It takes about 3 hours to get to the checkpoint so try to check what time you have to be there before. The time is there because it takes a longer time to get down than you expect. Also bring water with you. There is only one point where you can buy going up, and only one point where you can fill your water bottle on both trails!

Hotel was right across this market so I stopped here on my first night for dinner. I was amazed by the selection of street food stalls, fresh produce and desserts. Most of the signs were in Korean but just follow the crowd and where there's a long line you'll never go wrong! I got a taste of the rice with fried black pork plus some fried octopus in batter, which were both great. Bought some boxes of cheap chocolate as well. Areas of the market selling fresh fish and vegetables are wet though so beware when walking through.

Hiked from the Yeongsil Hiking Trail Entrance (1280m) to Witseoreum Shelter (1700m). It was a total of 3.7km (one way) hike and took me 3.5 hours up.  Note that I do not exercise regularly and this was my first hiking experience.  I guess it is manageable for anyone as long you are determined to hike up regardless of your physical condition.  The trail was tricky involving a variety of tall rocks, wooden steps, pebbles and wooden planks, a tad steep at times.  My DSLR became cumbersome by midpoint that I've decided to use it at specific points for me to better soak in the sights and watch my steps at the same time.  The sights at various points are nothing but rewarding.A hiking stick and a good pair of shoes are definitely helpful.  Note that you have to bring your trash down after your hike!Bring more water and join the locals at various rest points with some snacks (eat what the Koreans do! Gimbap / tangerines / hard boiled eggs) and just immerse yourself in listening to their chatters while looking out far at the horizon!I would love to hike on the other trails of Hallasan again.

Hidden in the lush greens of Jeju is this hidden gem that impressed me and my friends when we visited in July. The huge lava cave is around 7KM long but for safety reasons, the public is only allowed to walk the first 1KM of the whole cave. However the sight you get from that 1 KM is breath taking already.Do not be tricked by the term   cave   and think that this place is going to be warm. Upon going down the flight of stairs to the entrance of the cave, there will be a sudden dip in temperature and it will get colder as you go deeper in. So do bring a jacket along if you are prone to feeling cold. However, if you are visiting in Summer, it's the perfect escape from the heat.Although the interior is dimly lit and the floor is very slippery and uneven, you are rewarded with an amazing sight for the trouble you go through. However, I would not recommend this place to elderly with walking difficulties as well as families with young children that need prams.

Hi guys, I decided to write a review for our Jeju driver Mr. Ko Suhong, (watsap +821099485005 ) because of his extraordinary service and he was so good toward us during our trip. Trust me, I only recommend something if it is good. This is my honest review n first long review. We visited Jeju for 4 days.Pro:1. You can book him without advanced payment but once u book him, he will be there for you2. He came to fetch us 15 mins earlier than schedule time .3. He bring us to the most beautiful places in Jeju. Of course you still have to do research where you want to go, at least u know about the places. I was doing my research for a month with details date-time, but by telling him those places that i want to go, he arranged the itinerary for me. Our trip went so smooth and Excellent. Having read positive & not so positive reviews about the caves, this is my 2 cents... firstly I love all things nature. Having been caving in Malaysia - both the tourists & caving adventure cave types - the lava tube here is definitely different and worth a visit. If you are interested to know about how the lava cave was formed, there are good informative write ups at the entrance & along the way providing information about the formations. Whether you are a fit or unfit person - it is still worth the entrance fees (KRW2,000 - approx USD2) to go in & have a look. If you enter & don?t like the environment, you can still climb back up & exit. If you love it, continue on the 1km track in. It is a little rocky in places due to the formation of the tube & slippery due to the high humidity. And also, it is much cooler in the cave - it was 14?C during early Oct. Having aching knees & calf muscles from the climb up My Hallasan 2 days prior to caving, I used a hiking stick to assist with balance, walked slowly & took my time climbing down & up the stairs. The sight inside the caves was worth the aches & pains of climbing the stairs. For me, this is a 5 star location. Well maintained & an experience not to be missed.

Hallasan was a good challenging climb, with the hike splits into 3 parts. The first 2 hour or so, we were hiking through mostly level ground, some rocks and little steps. As we reach the middle ground, the trail gets steeper, more rocky and almost half are made up of steps, mostly made of rocks. Using a hiking stick at this time really helps in making the climb easier. When it rains, which happened the entire day when we went, the ground gets covered with puddles and pools of water, so it was extra effort trying to choose the rocks to step on to avoid getting our feet wet. Towards the top, there are flights and flights of steps, followed by a trail made of rocks where u have to use a rope to climb up the steep rocky surface. It was challenging but overall, felt good.As it was raining, we didn't manage to get any view of the crater or lake at the summit. But the sense of accomplishment making it up was great!The way down was more challenging as after a day of rain, the trail became wetter and what used to be steps, some were submerged in water. Hence, even with a good waterproof shoes, ur feet could still get wet. Also, note that the sky turns dark at around 5pm in winter and there's no lighting in the reserve. Hence, make sure u buffer enough time to reach the foot of the mountain before that time. Otherwise, u would be hiking in the dark. Nevertheless, there would be a ranger moving down the rail lines in a cabin moving on a rail line, looking for stranded hikers. So no need to panic. However, I would still recommend planning well, checking the weather and choosing a clear day to climb. Start early so as to buffer enough time to reach the 3rd rest station by 12pm, as anytime after that, they do not allow hikers to go up to the top. Think it is for safety reason to buffer enough time for the ascend and descend. Also, to wear waterproof shoes and if available, bring a hiking stick along. Do standby a raincoat in case of light drizzle. Also bring some food along. Though they sell instant ramen and some bento at the resting stations, it closes by 2pm or so and you don't want to end up hungry.  Lastly, enjoy the climb!

Hallasan National Park is a fantastic place to explore. Firstly, the vegatation between Spring and Fall is beautiful. As you hike to higher elevations the landscape and plants slowly change. Numerous rare and even some endemic species are found here. Concerning wildlife, what visitors are most likely to see are the Roe Deer. These small deer are found throughout the park, and as I hiked quitely we came upon 5-10 throughout our 6 hour trek.In 2007 Hallasan became part of the Unesco World Heritage site calle   Jeju Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes  . This honor is only bestoyed on the most unique and important natural and cultural sites on Earth. Hallasan is a geolocial wonder, and is comparable to some of the most iconic national parks in the United States. The park probably deserves 2 days as visitors will want to hike to the crater lake on Hallasan peak, but the entirity of the park holds many exceptional sites. Many trips to Jeju island are scheduled around their trek at Hallasan. Make sure to bring plenty of water, and keep an eye on weather conditions. Hikers must start early if they want to hike to the peak, late arrivals will not be permitted to make the full trek as it takes anywhere from 6-10 hours depending on your pace.

Hallasan is Jeju?s massive mountain, and was once a volcano. It peaks at 2000 meters, and from 700 meters up, the only way up is by foot, and you?ll have to drop your car at a designated area to begin the climb. The best place to start the trek is Seongpanak, on the East side of the mountain. Going up takes about 4 hours, at a normal pace, this trek will take all day. There are two checkpoints that you much reach before a certain time of the day to be allowed to go all the way up (and come back down before sunset). This means that you absolutely have to go there early. I was at the foot of the mountain at 9am, and I wouldn?t advise anyone to start climbing after 9:30 if you don?t want to be turned down. Also, since this can be exhausting, pack beverages and food before going up. There is a small shop at Seongpanak and another one at the 1500 meter checkpoint, but they have very limited choice. Just stop at a convenience store in the city before going up and you should be good for the day. The climb is relatively uneventful for the first 2/3rd of the way, with fairly little to see because you?ll be surrounded by vegetation. But once you reach an altitude of about 1600 or 1700 meters, you?ll start getting a great look at the top of the mountain and more importantly at the rest of the island.  Once you reach the top, the view will be amazing. The volcano?s caldera feels like being on the moon, and you can also see Jeju?s coastline as well as its major cities, Jeju and Seogwipo. Absolutely breathtaking! Make sure to check the weather if you plan to go there, because the tall mountain tends to attract clouds, which could completely ruin the awesome view you?d get on a clear day.

From Segiowipo (Jangung rotary) the park can be reached in a little over an hour on the 231 bus which will drop you at the front of the park.   Fare 1200krw. Park admission is 5000krw. I spent 2.5 hrs here doing course 1 and 2. I think you might enjoy it more if you were an artist but I liked it all the same. The stone museum, which is the first stop on course 1 tells you all about how lava rocks are formed, their different types and would be a geologists dream. After that you'll walk around the park and see the different stone sculptures, most of which are natural,  some manmade. There are also a couple of replica traditional jeju houses and local pottery too. The Obaek gallery has some driftwood on display along with 1 hall of art but it is mostly empty. I thought there would be more info on the local traditions and how they lived but the park is still a work in progress. Its not due for completion until 2020. Rug up because it seems to be colder here than other areas of the island and you will be outside most of your visit. Recommend you go on a sunny day as this area gets very heavy fog too.

For the last day of our Jejueco tour, the first attraction we visited in the morning was Jeongbang waterfall. Situated on a high cliff by the sea, Jeongbang waterfall is the only waterfall in Asia to fall into the sea. Admission fee is 2,000 won for individuals and 1,600 won per person if you are in a group of 10 or more.When we finally reached our destination, to actually get up-close to Jeongbang waterfall, we had to walk down some (more) steep steps and make our way over a field of rocks/boulders. It was a pretty slippery (and uneven) walk, so make sure you wear footwear with good grip. But the walk was worth it: the sight of the waterfall emptying itself right into the sea which makes it a pretty unique and amazing (since we don?t really have such waterfalls in Singapore).For more photos and our Jeongbang Waterfall experience, do check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/jeongbang-waterfall.html :)

For a rather expensive entrance fee of KRW9,000, was somewhat disappointed with what it offered. Basically, the park is divided into 2 main areas, the inner garden and the outdoor garden. The inner garden is essentially the large glasshouse, with different sections of the glasshouse each housing a different theme, i.e. cactus garden, flower garden, aquatic garden, etc. In the centre of the glasshouse, you can take the lift / stairs to the top, where you can get a panoramic view of the entire estate. The sight was rather impressive, but the glasshouse did not seem to be maintained well. The outdoor garden is basically the land around the glasshouse. It is divided into various gardens with different themes (i.e. Korean, Japanese, etc.). In general, they were rather uninspiring and gimmicky. The French Garden was ok, but like the rest of the park, didn't seem to be maintained very well.There is a train that goes round the garden but when we tried to board it, we were told that we needed another ticket. Quite disappointing after having paid a hefty entrance fee. We decided to just walk instead.All in all, the park seems past its prime, and maintenance could have been better. I'd imagine that it was quite grand when it was first built.. especially the glasshouse.

The second stop is a kids play area, which if you are travelling with young kids they will love.  There are slides and swings and miniature buildings.  It was hard to get our kids to leave.  There are some unpleasant aspects to the train, getting a seat can be a hassle after the first loading.  The seats are also two sided benches, so if you have someone behind you that is inconsiderate, it can be quite uncomfortable.  Nonetheless, we had a great visit and really enjoyed Eco land.

Driving from the city to the Seongpanak trail is the most convenient way to do it, it's only 20 minutes away from the busy area of Jeju.I hiked the mountain at early morning January 01 and when i reached the Seongpanak trail the parking was crazy long that it goes as far as 1km from the side of the road. If you want to save time in walking you should be at the trail around 3am at Jan01. Anyway, the trail was relatively easy on the first 7km, it was cold around -1 to 5C that time, still manageable but the trail was slippery due to ice forming on rocks and the trail was covered with snow. So, to prevent accidents wear a mini crampons or a Yaktrak coil underneath your shoes.Don't worry hiking alone, you can do this without a guide, you probably are blind if you get lost out there. Also, the trail was properly maintained that hiking at the peak was a breeze except the last 2km of the hike. When you reached the final kilometers it starts to get steep, so take your time and avoid slippery rocks and you should be fine. Finally, the peak was amazing, you would be able to see sea of clouds if the weather permits. Overall not bad for a hike.

DRAMA WORLD is consist of DRAMA STUDIO, TEDDY BEAR and WEDDING PHOTO ZONE. Drama studio is an indoor exhibition hall with a floor area of 5,000 square meters. Drama studio is actual TV drama studio and restored studio in KOREA, USA and EUROPE, in which the visitors can experience all costumes and accessories for free(except HANBOK, Wedding dress). Our exhibition is consist of town(street) studio and interior studio. Our exhibition is consist of Korean studio(K-DRAMA) and World studio(USA,EUROPE DRAMA). Visitors of all age groups can experience KOREA culture, Western(USA) culture and The Middle ages(EUROPE) culture through DRAMA STUDIO. We are the first experiment-type drama studio in Korea where the visitors wear the costumes and use the articles to be the main character in dramas. ※ Now, World Studio is consist of TEDDY BEAR EXHIBITION and WEDDING PHOTO ZONE with a background of Western and The Middle ages studio. Collaboration between DRAMA WORLD and TEDDY BEAR. TEDDY BEAR Exhibition Hall’s floor area is about 1,000 square meters. At DRAMA WORLD, visitors can see TEDDY BEAR, which produced scenes in drama of Korea, USA and Europe. Visitors can easily understand the scene of drama. Because the text(Chinese, English, Korean)is placed in each display of TEDDY BEAR. Visitors can take a picture with man-sized TEDDY BEAR using props and wearing costume for free. Visitors can learn about the Self-Wedding culture of Korea through the Wedding photo zone with a background of drama studio. Visitors can take a picture in wedding photo zone on studio of the Western Age in USA, the Middle Ages in Europe and Korea’s drama. In each Wedding photo zone, wedding accessories are placed. And they are available for free.
