Nice views and steps on the ridge, then another transition to a boardwalk through a tundra like alpine area.  Go past WitseOreum to the 1700m. junction where there's a toilet and snack bar, hot cup noodles are the best.  You can go another 2 km closer to the crater but why bother? Pack out your garbage.  The man made plank trail is kind of artificial but keeps the humans on a defined path and generally keeps them out of trouble, all in all a good way to get the masses of all ages into the outdoors.

Climb was ok, first smooth hill roads, then mainly steps to the top. View wemhile climbing was nice. We did not manage to catch the sunrise due to cloudy skies. However, the view of jeju from pre dawn to dawn while climbing up was worth it. U literally see the city lights up before ur eyes.

Cheonjiyeon, Cheonjeyeon and Jeongbang Falls are all located around Seogwipo, the southern city of Jeju. The first two has very similar names so don't be confused. This one is located nearer to city while CheonjEyeon is located nearer to the Ripley's and Alive Museum to the west. Cheonjiyeon is less majestic than CheonjEyeon. You can actually see 3 falls within Cheonjeyeon. Confused? In other words, visit Cheonjeyeon instead of Cheonjiyeon if you have limited time!

Certainly my first experience entering a natural geological occurrence like this one. A nice walk on a seasoned path, although some parts were slippery, it was safe for most people. Senior citizens must take extra care as the uneven path were dimly lit. Here were many features to be amazed by and the information centre gave visitors a better understanding of the geological occurrence. Worthy visit.

Certainly a must-visit destination in Jeju! Soak yourself in the impressive view of this UNESCO heritage site. We came on the first Monday of the month, and unfortunately the paid trail to the peak is closed. Blessing in disguise is that portion of the trail is open free to the public though it only brings us to mid-way - perfect for those who find it too challenging to climb to the top. Don?t miss the women divers show which is on the left trail, at the foot of Seongsan Ilchulbong. Showtimes are 1.30 and 3pm. It?s complimentary. And you can choose to buy and eat fresh abalone at the little restaurant. Overall a truly relaxing and uplifting experience!

Came here during sunset time. The view is very beautiful and natural. Many tourist took photo over here. During your walking distance to Yongduam Rock, don?t buy any fruit from the first stores! Very rude and not friendly. Make sure those of you beware of them.

By the time we visit Ecoland, it's already 4pm so  time limited as it closes at 5 pm!We took a long train that stop at every 4 places of visiting.In the first stop, we went through attraction on beautiful scenery and artistic work and went to another second stops to wait for the train. Then the train took us to third stops and another attraction artwork of beautiful small houses and Christmas artwork and many others.  Then we went to last stop that is garden which grows lavender,green tea and many types of flowers. It's a beautiful garden on the whole. On whole, I'll come to again another time again on next visit!

Bought the tickets online to enjoy a discount. We arrived early to be amongst the first cars within the car park. Thus, we had a fuss free horse riding experience for the kids. The 50mins performance was also enjoyed by the kids. Unfortunately, the go karting wasn?t available due to rain a few hours before.

Book the jeju tour under Rakso travel from the Phillipines. Visited mt halla on dec.31,2015. We were lucky as snow during the week was scant but during our visit, snow is falling and everything transformed to a magical sight.This is the first time my children saw snow falling. However, i noticed that the falling snow are not flakes but more like 'dippin dots' unlike the one i experienced in switzerland.Nevertheless, the moment and the view were enchanting!. Highly recommended!!.

Beware for this is one of the tourist traps that you have to watch out for. First they will say that entrance fee is free of charge, then they will show you their tradition houses (which is okay, no offense) but at the end of the tour, they will bring you into a room and give you sample of the products that they sell in outrageous prices. Omija tea, horse oil lotion, and the list goes on. It was good that they didn't insist that we buy, we just said that we don't need them as we have already bought what we need.

Bet ya you have never seen this before! Its real touristy but well worth the walk. From the convention centre on the east side the first road down to the sea. You can't miss the busses. Taking pictures is best in the morning because of the sun. We went at 16:00 and the sun made it impossible to take good pictures. Got a crappy camera so that could also have something to do with it. Another tip is to follow the olle trail to the east from here after about a 1,5 hour walk (through beautifull orange plantations and up and down tracks paved / dirt) you'll get to the Yakcheonsa Temple. Get from there to the 600 airportbus back to where you came from.

Before you want to take a ferry to Udo island, please take note that you need to bring along your passport to purchase a ticket. You will be given 2 tickets, 1 for departure & 1 for arrival (you have to keep this and pass to the boatman at Udo when you want to return to main island). A tip is to get the korean map together with your language?s map because they have more details of the island as compared to other languages. The ferry comes every 15 minutes so you do not have to worry if you miss it. Inside the ferry, there are flooring with thermal and you have to take your shoes off before stepping into the resting platforms. Otherwise, you may choose to stand outside those rooms and there are some outdoor seats at the top of the ferry. Please also take note that there are 2 ports at Udo, so your ferry might stop at either one.Once you reach the island, you will be greeted by tons of shop assistants trying to get you to rent bikes to you. You will need an international driver license to be able to drive any motorise vehicles. Upon confirmation which is the vehicle you want, you have to leave your passport with the register counter. They will provide you with a map to go around the island. We were informed that the whole cycling trip takes an hour. However, here comes the challenging part. There were no proper division of the road for those driving trucks, buses, cars, motorcycles & bicycles. You can be riding your bicycle and have a full speed bus chasing behind you and pressing the horn at you. Cars and trucks from the opposite direction also travel at fast speed towards you, which we had to stop many times to give way to these fast moving vehicles. After getting to the first beach, which was really beautiful, the rest of the trip towards the next beach was tough as there were many upward slopes and split roads which have no proper signages to tell you which way to go. We had to go in to random houses and ask in broken korean for which way to go. However, when we reach the lighthouse area, we managed to locate Jimmy?s icecream shop as suggested by our Jeju driver. I tried the mandarin orange ice cream while my friend tried the apple mango ice cream. Everything tasted natural and yummy so I would recommend it to tourist who visit the place. However, from the road before this ice cream place onwards to the last 5 mins of the ride, it was all upwards riding.We took almost 3 hours to finish cycling around the whole island (We have done quite a few rides in Singapore so I don?t think we were slow in cycling around the island). So for those who have no license or feel that you?re not up to 2-3 hours of cycling, I would advise you to take the tour bus to get from places to places on the island.
Beautiful, peaceful, such an amazing experience. First time on jeju and it is def a place you must go and see. Mr. Sung is adorable and kind hearted

Beautiful scenery at the top with breathtaking surrounding views of Jeju. Well maintained stairs, although uneven at first because they use the volcanic rocks, Many resting places as you go up. There is a lady at the top who explains the origins of the peak in English, which was a pleasant surprise. Large carpark area, fast food stores and souvenir shops.

beautiful place & good for take 1day visit if you have time in jeju. we take off bus stop prior to entrance and take many picture at the outside of Seongsan Ilchulbong. it has a beautiful beach & flower and horses etc... after that, went inside the hill. we went to the end of cliff that has a show for haenyeo starting time was 1330 & 1530. that has a dance & sing a song before go inside the sea. first time to close view their hard duty as actually jeju still getting many haenyeo woman as i viewed that carrying the orange ball inside the sea. some near coastal and some in the middle of ocean. seem take a long time duty such a hard duty.after that we went to hill of Seongsan. good view but the summit just a half & not easy to identify. but overall view & trail was enjoyable. must see

At first, I doubt that this painters thing can amaze me. But then, the show begin. This four painters create many pictures with fun and hillarious process of making. Would like to see it again if they have a new show. Went there on 25th Dec 2017. Best Christmas performance.

At first, I did not see the point of going to a Teddy Bear Museum. I could not imaging myself checking all teddy bears dressed as popular celebrities and personalities. But I was suprised that I loved every minute of it and I was totally entertained. Me and my friend stayed in the museum for over an hour, longer than what we expected. Highly recommended.

At first, going through the green house,? we were a little disappointed until we walked the grounds outside.? The French? and Roman gardens were absolutely beautiful.? It was so peaceful and relaxing.

At first we didn't plan to visit the Cave as we had a tight schedule with so many other outdoor choices. Then I read something about the tube formed from volcanic lava activities so it is very unique compared to other limestone caves formed from soluble rocks.Overal the tube looked very smooth as you can imagine the hot lava flowing to make the tube. There are educational signs here and there to suggest you to look at the lava flow marks, the lava shelf marks and many others.I must say it was an eye opening hour and we learnt something new and be opened minded that it was not just another cave with so many stalagmites and stalactites that looked like different shapes in those unnatural colorful spotlights in some other countries.

At first one may feel very inquisitive and cannot picture logically why vehicles can still move uphill even with the engines turn off.  However after some observations,  you will realize that the road is actually going downhill.   But how it appears to look like uphill is a mystery, that's why call Mysterious Road!!!

At first it just looks like another small museum, but this small place packs in a lot of exciting stuff. From the history of Hello Kitty, to the awesome cafe with Kitty inspired desserts and coffee. From the maze on the terrace to the fun activity space for kids to draw and color, the museum packs wonderful experiences, experiences which will remain etched in my memories.

At first  we thought this would just be a display of various seashells from around the world. But it was so much more than that! Just amazing and so artistic. This is more like a gallery of seashell and bronze art than a typical   museum  . The artist has a brilliant eye for unique creations with seashells  making some of the installations really come to life. The staff were friendly and there is something to see at every turn (even the bathrooms!). Adult entrance fee: 6 000 won (approx. $5) and well worth it. You will not be disappointed with this museum! A wonderful surprise on our rainy day of touring.

At ARARIO MUSEUM TAPDONG CINEMA unique art works of various artists (including Ugo Rondinone Kohei Nawa Andy Warhol and more) will be displayed all throughout the 1st to 5th floor. Super-sized arts which requires complicated installation such as   Hero No.2   by Zhang Huan and   What does the vessel contain that the river does not know   by Subodh Gupta will be premiered in Korea for the first time. In addition display of 4 large scale paintings by German Neo-expressionist Sigmar Polke will also contribute to create an overwhelming ambiance at the museum.

As we stayed in Seogwipo, we followed part of Jeju Olle Route 6 and  7  from Chilshimni Poetry Park to Oedolgae. We started our personal trail from Saeyeongyo Bridge and went up to Chilshimni Poetry Park through a wooden stairway. The wooden stairway was located along the road where a lot of tourist buses parked (towards the end where there was a brown building beside) away from Saeyeongyo Bridge. When we reached Chilshimni Poetry Park (is just beside Park Sunshine hotel), we were lucky to catch a view of  the Cheonjiyeon Falls from the top. There was also a resting shelter with table and benches if you want to enjoy the view of the waterfall while having snacks or lunch. Afterwhich, we left the park to the main road (where Park Sunshine hotel was) and headed to Namseong-ro road which was indicated by the blue/orange ribbons for Oedolgae. Along the way, you will pass by몃媛?? Hostel (the hostel name is in Korean as I cannot find the English name online) before reaching Hwangwooji coast first (it is a very beautiful coast with a private emerald green pool. Then there was a trail to Oedolgae where was a cliff top that you can view the Saeyeongyo bridge. Oedolgae trail is  free 1 to 2 hours trail and it is not a difficult trail, it is pretty gentle with lots of benches for rest breaks as needed. It has pretty nice coast view. There were fruits and snack sold along the trail where you just need to place 1000won at the basket where you take the fruits/snacks from (there is not one attending to the store). It is based on trust. There were rest rooms outside the trails if needed with food stalls near the free public toilet with toilet paper provided. We need all the trail by foot and there is really no need for a car.

As soon as arrived at the airport, went there for the dinner. Well, there are many snacks, lots of street food but made in a restaurants. Lots of fresh local fruits, really fresh fish, raw fish sashimi, etc. Compare to Seoul, all fish are much more fresh and reasonable price. I ate some crab skewer, but after 10 steps from there found new ce local pork soup restaurant. So better to have a look first then decide which Korean light snack would be good for you. I am certain all kids will love this place to have some street food here!

As reviewed here, the first 10-15 minutes guests are taken on a tour to the various stations to see how traditional living in korea were. However the sales pitch on honey and several other product seems to have nothing really to do with the traditional farm life (or not obvious)... Do note the sales is not compulsory, but often, guests are 'pressured' into buying something by other guests..

As per suggestion of our taxi driver, we decided to climb up along the Eorimok trail as according to him, it was the easier of the two. The first 2km was upwards slope of big rocks stairs so it was a little tiring but after that, the course was breezy. Took us about 2h to the top. The day we went was super windy so it was really really cold and everyone took cover in the shelter at the top, but if the weather permits, you can sit outside and enjoy the view. The climb down by Yongsil trail was really beautiful and it's a very different kind of view than Eorimok. We understood why the driver said Eorimok was easier to climb up as Yongsil had more rocks that would have been a little difficult. I'm not an avid climber but both trails were doable and the views were worth it.

As I've mentioned on my review to Seongpanak Trail, I'd recommend it as the point of entry then exit through Gwaneumsa Trail. But, if you prefer a more challenging option, do the other way around. I went down from the summit through the Gwaneumsa Trail. It was the first week of April and the snow hasn't melted completely yet, making it slippery. It is very much recommended to have a walking stick, in my case, I used my tripod. The scenery in this trail was awesome. There are valleys in yellow and white. You can also find a spring water along the way. Hiking Hallasan in general solo is not a problem, regardless of which trail you take, because there are a lot of other hikers you meet along the way.

As its name, here is an idea to visit for Teddy Bear lovers and who interested in. Many zone that's quite interesting such as the first Winnie the Pooh, world's all time classic paintings x Teddy Bear, characters bear like Michael Jackson or Audrey Hepburn from Breakfast at Tiffany, and Steve Jobs. Entrance fees isn't cheap but still OK. For the exhibition of Bear dolls is good but for the shop, just soso nothing attractive.Parking available. Good for friends and family.

Arrived here on a group tour and was impressed with walking in the cave although important to note a few thing . Firstly there is a long walk inside the caves after initially going down some steep stairs. Once in the cave the ground is not even and majority of walking is done on the uneven rock surface itself, for this reason a good pair of water tight shoes are definitely required. There is constantly water dripping from the roof , certainly not raining , but does mean you spend a lot of time looking down being careful of your step avoiding puddles . Along the way the cave is well lit by lighting and also a number of stations with information describing the rock formations you are passing. Make sure you have time so as not to rush watch your step and enjoy .

Among the beaches in Korea, this is the one that most resembles Hawaii/Australia/Thailand.  White sands and turquoise waters, with striking black lava rock.  The water is warmer than on the mainland, and it's never been as crowded as Haeundae (in Busan) when I've gone. It's easy to go, even alone, and spend a relaxed afternoon swimming and sunbathing without feeling as though you're ruffling anyone's feathers.  This beach is always the first place on my checklist when I go to Jeju!

Am not much of an active person who trek but managed to finish the hike.  Pretty easy to find alternative transport instead of cab.   I took a cab to Jeju bus terminal and ask for the bus to seongpanak hallasan.  There are announcements and signboard to alert one for each stop and hence I manage to align at the seongpanak stop with no difficulty.  The trek was okay for the first leg (pre-rest stop) and got more challenging at the final leg.  Not knowing much, realised that most of the hikers have their hiking stick while I was on my own - then again I survive the hike abit limping for the long long hike :). In all, I enjoy the hike with not regrets

Although we went in the evening when some stalls are closed the place is quite vibrant nonetheless. If you hire a taxi for the day ask the driver to drop you off here. We kind of regretted we didn't as the taxi we hired went overtime and we were a bit tired. We took a bus at 1200 won from Jeju City (500) and it was a long and crowded trip as it had to pass through the airport first. Definitely worth a visit. Nothing much to buy other then tangerines (sold in bags of about 12 to 13) and jeju orange chocolates which you can find in Seoul. You can see the live seafood such as abalone, octopus, fishes etc. Also enjoy food such as gimbap, oden, tteoboki, fried stuff, blood sausages etc. There is also a stall selling orange jam filled cookie in the shape of the stone grandfather. Tastes good when eaten warm.

After reading quite a few reviews on lHallasan trails, I finally decided to have a go at it. I left early to start the hike on Gwaneumsa just before 7.00am. I actually got there by taxi from sunrise peak, seongsan as there is no bus arriving there. It costed me 35000won. On arrival, the place was deserted, so I started my walk. The first part is throught the forest so you don't get to see any scenery. Once you reach the last shelter then it opens up and the view is amazing. From there you have still a good climb to the top (the thoughest part actually). On the top you can see the crater and if it has been raining the lake inside. I went down the second trails called seongpanak which is said to be easier. This one is a bit boring in regards to scenery because you are always in the forest.All in all it took me 6h45 to get to the top and back which is around 18km. The up trail is pretty challenging and I would recommend people the be quite fit to take it the down trails is a challenge to your ankles and knees as the path is covered in huge stone so be careful not the twist anything. On the up trails you will find a water spring almost at the top, no food and no other water poitn apart from that. On the down trail the is a shelter serving pot noodle. On arriving down at seongpanak there was a few taxi waiting so I managed to get back to the hotel. There is also a shop that sells drink, food and rent shoes.My reco is to start early in the morning to avoid too many people. Get plenty of water (I got 1l and it wasn't enough). Good shoes are a must. And one moto : slowly but surly! Don't rush it as you will suffer on the way down. Appreciate the trail. Be careful though that at 12h30 they will stop you at the shelter from gwaneumsa so you need to go pass this before and you need to leave the top before 14h to make it down before closing time. I really enjoyed it as a challenge 1300m climb from 650m to 1950m.

After having been to quite a few of Jeju's museums...this has to be the most boring and way overpriced.  It should be charging 2000KRW entry. ..not the KRW11,000 each we paid!  All the extra stuff you can do inside costs extra, you can only see so many glass flowers and glass baubles before it becomes boring!  We went in the day time.  We had lunch there first.  I would suggest that people get lunch in the nearby restaurants .... much cheaper!  The food was good but not a great choice and double the price you'd pay locally.  Perhaps this place is better at night but even if it was the price is still too high.  I wouldn't bother taking kids here either.

After a fulfilling breakfast, the first stop of our Jejueco tour was the Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) along Jeju's Jungmun Daepo coast, columnar joints (stone pillars piled up along the coast and is a designated cultural monument of Jeju island) which were formed from the volcanic lava from Hallasan mountain. The Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) are essentially rock pillars (columnar jointed rocks) shaped like cubes or hexagons of various sizes and almost seem as if they were carved by nature's stonemasons. The area where the Jusangjeollidae (二쇱ⓒ\由щ?) are located is part of an olle course: the path will lead you along the coast all the way to the Jungmun beach with spectacular views of the columnar jointed rocks. So if you want to exercise and take in the scenery at the same time, this is one scenic route you can take.Read more about my experience and photos at my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/jusangjeollidae-columnar-joints.html

Actually like the other ones, I felt quite surprise at the my first visits since last year 2011. The guide showed me that I were in the bottom of the slope, she pointed to the tree lines along  the side of the road and truly, it has made me believe what she said. A few seconds later, the driver shut the engine and release the bus's brakes, the 45 seated bus was beginning move slowly then faster and faster.  Could you believe ? The huge bus was moving up to the top of the slope without working engine! A man of my group - an 50 ages supposed there were the natural magnetic power that dragged up the 2,5 tons iron bus to about 5-8 meter height during approximately 80 metes !!!It was happened about 10 mins then all of our group's participant disembarked the bus, they were starting to talk about what they saw during the past 10 minutes. Some one said it caused by a natural magnetic power (as above), other one assumed by the trick of the sun's lighting a man nearly lying face down to the road parallel to look forward to the starting point... others wisely poured the water to see the flows .... Of course, our guide has explained the cause but I really do not want to tell you, let's explore by yourself.Definitely, this places is quite appropriated for your family with kids. Aside the road, there are the Korean traditional food shops who sells fried fish ball, rice cake... but they are almost fried into the oil ...This places are really attracted a lot of people from Asia like Chinese, Vietnamese, Indian... I think you might found the similar road like the Jeju Mysterious Road of your own country but the Korean was wise to promote it via the drama film series currently expanding over the Asia.Totally, Jeju is an beautiful island and you should visit one time. With me, I could said   you could make the money by the very simple things

A short 20 mins drive from the Jungmun resort area. Very easy to navigate and locate with the clear road signs available. Admission was just KRW 2,000 per adult. Very reasonable. The Waterfall is a short flight of stairs down from the main carpark. There were large groups of Korean high school students visiting during our time there so we just followed the crowd. Took us less than 15 mins to get down to the fall. Perhaps it's not the rainy season, the waterfall seemed tiny (compared to Niagara etc). The water flowed first into a stone pool before trickling into the sea. Not very impressive but a nice destination for our family with a toddler. He had a great time trying to balance on the big rocks by the fall. Next to the fall, there were 2 women divers selling abalone and sea squirts. I saw local tourists eating them as sashimi sitting right there on the rocks. Interesting.

A really beautiful and picturesque waterfall! I was in awe when I first saw the waterfall and couldn't stop taking pictures of it from all angles. After passing the entrance, you can just follow the steps down and you can already catch an amazing view of the waterfall. Many people, including my family and I, took one step further and went down the rocks so that we could really catch the waterfall right in front of us. It was truly a spectacular view and the waterfall seemed so majestic. Definitely recommend to visit at least once when visiting Jeju!

A beautiful view on top of Seongsan IIchulbong. Plenty of parking. We did this twice in the same day. The first hike (approximately 30 minutes to get to the top, started at 1pm) was extremely foggy and we couldn't see anything. We hiked back down and spent some time on the shore. Once the sun came out we hiked back to the top. There are several stops on the way with spectacular views of Jeju. You can purchase drinks and trinkets from one small shop about half way up. Use the restroom before going up as there is not one on the way. For a family of three to include a 10 year old we took one large bottle of water and a small backpack with some snacks and additional items. Bring a camera as it is absolutely beautiful. On the way we saw several different species of birds and spiders. At the top there are several benches where you can sit and enjoy the view. At the bottom there is a Mcdonalds, an ice cream shop, a souvenir shop, and other small shops. I suggest you try the orange ice drinks...they are great! Overall cost, 5,000 won for two adults and one child. We paid cash. Enjoy!

30 mins drive out from Jeju City.  My Wife and Daughter accompanied me on the first 2.5km of the 11.1km yellow route, then they took a short cut back (around 1.2km) to relax at the Korean style picnic tables and visit the carp pond.  I took another 1.5 hrs or so to complete the yellow route, which by the way is circular, not an up and back as reported sometimes previously. I came across plenty of deer, as well as some beautiful birds and flowers.  The first 5km or so has hessian Mats to walk on, which is very peasant, but then it gets a bit muddy and rocky, with a few steep sections.....walking boots or trail shoes are definitely best, although possible in Trainers.  Really enjoyed the hike.

*Firstly, don't go here. Instead, go to the 5 Day Market (誘쇱ㅼ쇱 Minsok O-il Jang) in Jeju-si. It is open every day ending in 2 or 7: 2, 7, 12, 17, 22, 27th.*As for Dongmun, the best part is the 몃 (Hoddeok). Along one of the side alleys are these beautiful grandmas (癒몃 Halmeoni) who sell fried rice pastries filled with cinnamon, brown sugar, and nuts (Hoddeok). This is some of the best I've had in Korea. SO delicious. There are three of these stalls in this alley. The best, and oldest one, is furthest inside the market.The bad: vendors are rude and over priced. Their goods are not the highest quality and they know that the tourists don't know how to find better quality.

you should read the story of this museum.it comes to live cos there is a dream.it has a sharp appearance a vibrant red exterior in jeju when comparing with those surrounding buildings.the art pieces in the museum is nice but i do appreciate the way that the owner makes this museum as an art piece more.To renovate rather than destroy and rebuild keeping the scratches of time and inject the modern art atmosphere into this old building.although you may think the entry free maybe a bit high but it still worth to visit.the cafe and souvenir shop at top floor also nice to stay awhile.

You can go underground and experience the cold temperatures close to 12 degrees.. its like walking through an igloo.. Cold air everywhere and some parts are wet due to the precipitation though the soil. Reminder to bring a jacket and good shoes as floor is slippery and area is dark! Very good experience!

Yakcheonsa Temple is thought to be Asia?셲 largest Buddhist temple. The main temple has one storey below ground and five stories above with a floor area of  more than 175 sq m and a ceiling height of 29 metres. The Main Hall has 18000 Buddha statues and receives many worshippers for its medicinal waters. Monks were praying and chanting when we were there - I liked it very much.

Yakcheonsa Temple is a famous Buddhist Templet located in Jeju island south of mainland Korea. The temple was built in 1981 by a Buddhist monk . It has three floors  It has a large Buddhist prayer hall. It is also famous for housing 80000 Buddhas all located on the second floor encased in glass.  It also has smaller statue of Buddha surrounded by lotus flowers under a pair of intricately carved protective dragons. The view from the top floor is veryy beaytiful facing the sea

Wow... just wow. I certainly didn't expect that. Yakchunsa isn't considered one of the must-go in Jeju so I didn't expect all that much especially given that you have to take a small road to go there. But once I arrived I was in awe. The complex is big colorful and the main pagoda-like multi-floor temple is massive and beautiful. What's even better is that the inside is at least as good as the outside view. There are three floors each with its own atmosphere and ornaments (murals candlelights wooden structures...). Take some time to go outside towards the sea to get the full perspective of the temple complex.

While visiting a friend who works in Jeju my family drove around to visit places casually with a flexible schedule. We planned to visit the temple for half an hour but stayed more than an hour. The name of the temple means medical spring and the flowing water from a 3-dragon-head fountain next to the temple store tasted good and sweet. Although the temple was built for only around 20 years the buildings and layout followed the traditional design. The main building faces exact south that can view the sea. The bell tower is located in the east for sunrise and the drum tower is located in the west for sunset. The main building's first floor wooden windows are beautifully carved with inspiring stories covered by traditional white paper but not glass. There is a traditional Korean painting exhibition of Buddha of Compassion in the basement and it's gorgeous. The best part of our visit was that not many people around. We got the chance to enjoy the quietness and even used the mats inside the temple at the back of the first floor to meditate a short while. There are grapefruit trees in the yards along the way to bathroom.

When I was planning my trip to Jeju  I found this museum has got half positive and half negative comments from travelers. Well ??I decided to have a look by myself. When our car got near to the place  there was a strong smell. I was then told that there is a piggery farm nearby which stinks out the whole place. The ticket was not cheap but it included a cup of coffee plus a discount in the shop. The appearance of the building is interesting with an open courtyard. The first impression was not so bad.However when I got inside  it was quite disappointing. I think the management should consider a renovation  or at least a deep cleaning and some maintenance. I just felt I was in a dusty old weird mansion. Maybe those exhibits are precious and rare  but they are not well presented. For example  they put lots of chocolate boxes from all over the world in the same window display without proper descriptions. How can the people think that those boxes are precious when they are packed in a glass cabinet? The lighting on the second floor was horrible. The rooms were so dark adding horrific ambiance to the museum.

review: We went to DaHeeYeon for the self baths.In a large room of about 50 peoplewe sat on floor andunder direction of their instructorwe gave ourselves foot baths using products sold at their shop.The instructor spoke Korean but we were able to follow along.It was unusual and fun and soothing to our feet after days of sightseeing.

review: We visited Yakcheonsa Temple on our Jeju Olle Trail Route 8. This temple looks delightful because of its architecture and beautiful surrounding scenery. The views from the second floor were amazing! We even had a chance to ring the bell and make wishes here! A recommended place for photographers to get vivid pictures. You can also experience a temple stay activity in this Buddhist temple.

We visited the Manjanggul Cave on a very wet day.  The floor of the cave was wet and the stones slippery. Puddles of water lined the route. It would have been all right if the light was brighter but it was not. The lighting was dim and you can easily twist an ankle if you stepped into one of the many crevasses in the floor. The dim lighting did not make things any easier and you really have to watch where you are going. Wear proper walking shoes if you do not want to slip on the stones. I felt that the lava cone that was our destination was quite dazzling but I wish the authorities had spent a little more care in making the whole walk safer for those who are mobile but who are a little unsteady on their feet like the elderly. The video presentation that we saw after the walk was good. The exhibits were well curated and gave us an idea of other earth formations resulting from volcanic activity in the area.
We enjoyed our visit to this lovely temple. Don't miss climbing the upper floors and checking out the colorful lanterns.

Was quite doubtful if it is worth visiting after reading some of the reviews.  Went for it and it is quite worth a visit if you are interested in works of nature or with kids for education purpose.  The place isn't too difficult to walk if you are with the right shoes as the floor is wet and could be slippery.
Very nice and colorful with all HELLO Kitty history and toys and bag.Very delicious cafe on 2nd floor .3rd floor theater and nice view
Uneven staircase down. Uneven flooring in cave. This cave is pretty natural and includes unusual formations. It's worth seeing but take a flashlight as the lighting is very poor.
UNESCO recognised scenic spot! Most of the part looks more or less similar and the best part is at the last! Better save time for the last part and beware of the slippery floor.

Truly a unique lava cave that is open to public. Should not miss the opportunity. Very well managed with descriptive dual language (English and Korean) on all the unique naturally formed features along the long and winding 1.2 km long tube/cave. The 13 deg C temperature inside was a pleasant reprieve from the outside summer temp of 38 deg. Can be a little wet and the floor is not so flat and as such reasonably appropriate footwear is recommended.

This temple wasn't very busy when we were here and it was very pleasant to walk around for awhile. We probably spent a couple hours walking around the grounds and taking pictures inside. You can go up three floors inside the temple the paper lanterns hang down from the ceiling fairly far and you can get some neat pictures with them if you go upstairs.
This temple is a jewel of jeju island. Very nicely preserved with very good painting at the roof and also the wall on the second and third floor of the main temple.

This place will turn u from an adult back to a kid. Not a big place but plenty of Teddy bear and other cartoon figures for u to take pics with. All done up very nicely and photo friendly. But to take a photo is very challenging due to the crowd. About 2 floors and one and half hour is sufficient.

This museum isn't very large and in the winter you don't really want to go outside to admire the small amount of outdoor exhibits (which you can do from inside the windows anyway) but it's got enough interesting art to be worth 1000 KRW which is about USD $0.80. For one I enjoyed the Chang Ri Seok exhibit as his paintings are very earthy. The second floor exhibit was under renovation when I went but still for 1000 won I have no complaints about the first floor's contents. The gift shop is pretty underwhelming though.

This mountain is so tiring if you try and complete the ascent in 3 hours on a hot day but it's worth it for the view at the summit! The upward root that I took was a little bland because it was all under the cover of trees so you don't actually see anything new for most of the ascent. The crater on top still had some snow on it in April and you can see the full perimeter of the island from the top. I think this view would be even more spectacular in the summer. Make sure you bring plenty of water! There is nowhere to buy it on the way down if you take the alternative route. Also be prepared to use the horrible 'hole-in-the-floor toilets' if you need to go. Needed to take a taxi back to the hostel at the end because no buses stop there. A great day out though.
This is the must place to visit in Jeju island.Beautiful cave with very cold inside.The floor of this cave are total wet so when you walk please be careful

This is the most beautiful museum I have ever visited - absolutely packed with three floors of seashell art. When we visited there was no one else there at all! I have no idea why - but I probably wouldn't have enjoyed it as much if it was so busy. It was a bit more expensive than expected  probably because it doesn't get as many visitors  but it was well worth it and I got a free pair of earrings! Definitely go - they have a cafe too.

This is a natural cave and you have to walk down a stair at the entrance. It is dark inside the cave and be aware of your step as the stone on the floor are not plain. Better bring a jacket with you as the temperature inside is around 10-degree celsius only.

This is a large and well-kept temple by the water.There are 4 floors to visit and many murals and small statues to see. The large golden buddhas are impressive. You can take a mat and pray on the main floor or meditate in a second floor room.I spent a total of around 45 minutes at this site.

This is a fun place for the family !  To enjoy this place to the max you must not be shy about lying on the floor or doing funny expressions to pose to achieve the photo effect .  We had great fun as a family n have a good laugh as we review the photos taken.  There's also a outdoor sculpture park which we enjoyed doing funny pose with the sculpture ! We were there on a Sunday about 1030am there wasn't a crowd that allow us to have more time at each exhibit to pose without worrying on holding up others.Go n have fun !

This is a bit of a must see in Jeju. Its a walk underground in a lava tube obviously created by a volcano. The tunnel has some nice features but the payoff is at the end as there is a big lava colomn. Also if it's a hot day it's really refreshing as it is quite cold down there. A jacket or vest is recommended. The way is lit by lights but all in all a flashlight comes in handy but the one on your smartphone will do. The floor is very uneven so people who aren't that nimble might have problems. Finally there are bats in the cave who probably won't bother you but make the place a tad creepy as you sometimes see their shadow. Getting there with public transportation is hard drive or get a taxi. However the grey ones are cheaper than the black ones.
This beach was stunning. The sea floor was all sand and the water was very clear! The beach wasn't overly crowded for summer time. The water was warm and I felt like I was in Thailand

There's not really much museum. I thought I turned a wrong corner but had actually walked through the whole thing. Just one wall of tea cups and pots and basically no English signage. But it's free and you really go for the tea shop and cafe.Nice teas for sale (spendy but tasty!) and there are often free samples in the tea shop. Then move to the cafe for some green tea flavored sweets. I recommend the softserve ice cream twisted with yogurt. If you're here take time to climb to the 3rd floor observatory for some nice views. If you have a little extra time it's worth two other stops:1) just through the garden path walk up hill to the natural skin care center where you can smell local essences and make your own natural soap (for a fee). They have nice sandwiches and snacks for sale.2) Climb the oreum (small mountain) just north of O'Sulloc. Walk along the road past the tea fields until you see a concrete paved walk in toward the hill. Follow paths or bushwack until you see the path entrance. You can walk to the top in less than an hour from O'Sulloc. There's a nice viewing platform with views toward Seogwipo from the top.

There is nothing much here at the museum but the green tea ice cream and the green tea cake roll are fabulous! The green tea cake roll sold out in a very short period of time! We reached there at around noon time and we were so lucky that we took the second last roll! I guess the cake roll is pretty popular among the locals too as we saw a lot of locals stopping by at the cafe. I saw an O'Sulloc Cafe at Myeongdong too. We went in the morning and there were still quite a few of green tea cake rolls there. I wanted to get a cake roll the night before I flew back to Singapore (in order to maintain the freshness) but the staff told us that it has been sold out! The green tea cake roll tastes really good when it's eaten fresh. People who don't like the cream in the middle might not like the cake. Other than food you can go all the way to the third floor to take some photos. Personally I feel that the scenery outside of the building is much more nicer. There's a big park right in front of the tea museum there are people who lie down and chill on the grass. There's tea plantation located opposite of the tea museum. We are allowed to wander around there for more pretty photos.
There is a large Buddha inside the temple and on the first floor a display of 8000 little Buddha statues. Good for a short visit but otherwise it's just like any other Buddhist temple.

There are 3 terry bear museums in Jeju. The one which we visited is Terry bear and safari. The lower floor is the safari and upper floor is the bear. Think this also to attract the kids to visit the place thus the safari.Take your time to see and enjoy the many characters of the terry bear. One corner of displays is a very expensive due to diamond crown.

The temple itself is breathtaking. It is one of the largest temple I had visited. The architecture and scuplture of the temple is unique and beautiful. Climbed up to the third floor the view from the window toward the sea is just magnificant. Spend some time to admire the marvelous architecture especially during the evening.

The temple is super huge and well decorated. There are three layers the first layer is for the believers to worship the Buddha. Second floor is a place where you can talk to the Buddhist monks about your difficulties you faced in your life and have their spiritual purification. Of course some ?쁤oodwill??you have to forgive to this temple I saw one of the believer distribute a considerable fortune to that temple that believer must treats Buddha sincerely. In the entrance of the temple there was rice selling which is the accumulation of capital for the construction use. My mum bought one small pack of rice which costs 10K to support the running of the temple. There is also a water well besides the temple which brings lucky to the people who drink you shouldn?셳 miss that opportunity.Even though you are not a Buddha believer like me you are strongly recommended to go to that temple to have a look of the huge architecture and take pictures with the nice atmosphere.

The temple has a bus stop just in front of it (300 meters by foot) and it's quite spectacular.The main hall is beautiful and you can visit the upper floor too.Not to miss especially the 500 Buddhas shrine (where 500 different statues of Buddha are collected).

The temperature in the cave is at least 5 to 10C lower so please bring a jacket and wear proper shoes when going in. The entrance fee is cheap at 2K each for an adult.There are many locals visiting during the weekends so it's recommended you visit during weekdays if possible.The cave is dark and wet so we spent more time watching the floor as opposed to the cave.

The road to this temple is a single carriage way and you drive carefully.  Parking is free. Before I reached the temple I can hear the chanting and is was so soothing.  It just calm a city travellers. I didn't take any pictures inside the temple only the surrounding. It would be great to have a audio or a translator/guide to explain more of this historical and majestic temple.  The sea view from the temple is stunning. Do check out the temple second floor.

The place is essentially a large botanical garden and cave in one attraction.First  botanical garden is quite large and can take quite a while to walk. The grounds are nicely manicured  with many plants  flowers  and trees. There are also some water fountains and small man made falls. There are also some statues and other stone objects in the park. There is also a greenhouse with various desert plants. It certainly isn't something you really need to see  but it is a pleasant walk through the area.However  the main attraction is Micheon cave. It is probably a naturally occurring cave. Nonetheless  the cave's ground has been leveled artifically to make it easy to walk on - compared to Manjanggul Cave which has a very uneven and dangerous floor. There is really not too much to see in the cave other than feel how cool it is and a few weird looking large figurines of cavemen...

The performance itself is worth the price of admission. Make sure you arrive before one of the three showtimes during the day. They provide drums and you can jam along with the performers. I find this satisfying when you have so many museums in area feigning novelty. So again  If you can get your toddlers away from the stuffed animals  then there is a rewarding human element waiting on the bottom floor.

The museum is quite small and expensive....there are 2 floors with old teddy bears and teddy bear versions of famous painting and famous people. If you are nearby you can go but I would not specifically go there. My 3 years old son was little scared by the giant bears in display! Koreans seem to like it more

The museum is located opposite of Jeju Korea Tourism Organisation and can be reached from Seogwipo or Airport on bus number 600. The entrance fees is 2000 won and there are 3 levels of teddy bears exhibition and the ground floor is where all sorts of teddy bears are being sold. There is a cafe within the museum and a theater showing Elvis Presley lookalike teddy bear singing Elvis's songs. It is about a 15 minutes session.

The Manjanggul lava tubes caves are amazing and the walk is well worth it.  Dont forget to take your flash camera as you will not see sights like this again.The sides of the cave are smooth from the flowing hot lava and show striations along the sides from when the lava level was falling.  The size of the tune varies from small to very large.  Lighting has been set up to high-lite many of the features.  Wear good waterproof shoes as the floor is uneven  and there are many puddles from dripping water

The hedge maze is relatively small but really pretty. The atmosphere was relaxing and all the cats lazing around dozing are super cute. We took about 20 minutes to get out of the maze.Do watch out for HUGE spiders above your head. They spin their webs between the hedges. There are also huge ones in the toilets (saw one on the floor beside the seat). Eeks!!!
The cave is really huge and long. You have to be outfit ready when you go here. The floor is also somewhat slippery that's why wear good shoes. The cave is filled with facts about how it is formed.

The cave is cold and wet. It's not easy to walk on undulating floor filled with watery potholes. Certain section you have to bend your body as the ceiling is too low. The cave looks the same from the opening to the end.

The architecture of this conference centre is the first exciting and majestic comment on the centre. It has big conference rooms with the best facilities to host big events. I attended the international mercury conference here and the logistics of the venue provided us with a flawless event. There are also several fast food restaurants at the bottom level of the centre  with a duty free shop on the other side. It is a local attraction and the visitors seem to enjoy it too  since it was constantly busy. On the second floor is a curio shop for some gifts from Jeju.The airport limousine bus no 600 stops outside entrance of the venue  but there are local taxis frequently available to take you anywhere.

The 1k walk is really interesting and had good info in english. It's much cooler as soon as you walk down the steps and raincoats are useful as there are water drops and wear comfortable shoes for the rocky and wet floor. Most of it is quite dark but you can still get good photos. Definitely worth the visit
thank you for the visit and lovely explanation of our museum. as you mentioned you'd like to say again never miss Elvis concert at the second floor. have a nice day ^^
Super place for photo as the lightings make u a superstar. Many visitors and 3 floors to walk around. Very interactive. Must go

Suitable for anyone who can walk without aid as there were steep stairs leading in/out of cave. Floors were uneven as can be expected. We entered just after the rain so the place was literally dripping from the ceiling. One way in and out from the same entrance. Midpoint (the deepest part of the cave) was a formation that was supposedly the highlight. Lighting was sufficient to find your way around but not for taking pictures unless you are equipt with an SLR and a tripod. My 10yr old couldn't wait to get out as he was rather bored. No thanks to his father(me) who was busy taking pictures with long exposure :-)
So-so place which was also offered to us as part of the tour package. The place consisted of 3 floors but was pretty small to begin with. 1 hour should suffice at a casual pace.

Some sports brand but nothing exciting. We came twice but still we did not find any shops we like. Compared to shops in Seoul this is pale. Most shops selling winter coats. At end of this street turn left and just outside the wet market we find a shop bang bang. They have 2 floors lower for women and second for men. Managed to get some simple t shirts. Design was just very simple. Other than these nothing exciting here. The wet market is more exciting with tourists the korean snacks there were great! Here in this shopping street you get cafe. Very quiet cos winter. There is a shop selling desugner embroudery hackets and jeans gor guys but very expensive. The staff was speaking cantonese to the chinese customers so we assume Hong Kong shop. Nicer Jackets were $500 onwards.

Sitting prominently on a hillside there is no missing this huge Temple and it is one of the largest in the East.There is a bit of steep walk from the carpark to the Temple complex and we rewarded ourselves with a drink from the spring well on one side of the grounds.Consisting of a main hall with a Deities sculptured side walls of Buddha a large bell a separate Pagoda Monks quarters and three or four floors upstairs that can be accessed by visitors. These floors have many donations of precious metal statues and from up here there are excellent views of the main hall.It is prudent not to use the main entry into the big hall as there are clear warnings in many languages not to so out of respect. Also shoes must be taken off before using the side entries on either side of the main doors. A group of hapless visitors ignored these signs and were promptly told off and hustled out to use the side doors.Money donations are accepted either for the upkeep of the Temple or for incense and candles.While we were there we had three or four Monks chanting and offering up to Buddha and it was very serene to hear it from upstairs while overlooking the main hall.The grounds are well maintained with a couple of restrooms around the complex a cafeteria and Temple stays are available too.Enjoy your visit!
Peaceful place excellecent buildings. Photos cannot capture the real color of the tiles and ceilings decorations. You could go up to the 1st and 2nd floor of the template.

O'Sulloc Tea Museum  is actually a shopping paradise for those who fancy for tea. O'Sulloc itself is famous for its Tea product. In front there's a collection of used cups that they arranged in such a way so it's picturesque.Since It's a green tea field expect for green tea product for sale including all side products (Cake Drinks etc). The shop available also allows us to test some of their products We let ourself went down to the greentea field and see what's actually a green tea look like when it's not harvested yet. We also have a little chat with the tea-picker ajumma. If you go to the upper floor you will be able to take picture of overall green tea field but don't expect too much.I recommend time of visit when the sun not in its brightest Enjoy!

Opposite the museum is the tea field which you can walk across the road to take a photo and see how they grow the tea tree. There's parking space beside the museum. Besides there's the tea cafe and souvenir shop at the arrival floor. I would recommend the green tea smoothie top with soft cream green tea latte and green tea roll cake. It's very crowd with tourists and local people. So normally the seat are full. So if you go with friend I'd recommend one to fine the seat and one to queue up to get drink and desserts. Even its long queue to buy but it doesn't keep you wait too long. The green tea spread is the signature. There're also many selection of tea with nice packages and different aromas for your selection.

Not a bad way to fill in a couple of hours. The cave floor is very uneven as you are walking on solidified lava be sure to wear comfy shoes. Also can be quite damp so if you don't want to have water dripping on you maybe take an umbrella. Lots of information provided throughout the walk in several languages to keep you engaged also

Nice walk inside the huge lava cave since it's cool and you won't really feel the 1-km walk inside but wait until you realize that you have to walk another kilometer back! hehe... It was nice seeing the different lava rock formations but be careful since most of the floor is wet and ragged so you have to pay attention to where you are stepping.

Nice to take pictures of the tea gardens/have a walk around. Buy their different flavours of tea that they have and they always change their goods. You can try out their caf챕 as well as go up to the observatory area on a higher floor. It is extremely crowded though.

nice place to visit to see how nature works!!!....u can see how jeju was made thousands years ago.....beautiful cave!!!...but you must be fit to walk about 2km and walking in a slippery floor is not really easy in the dark....beautiful!!!!

Nice path all with light for evening walk all around the small island with places to sit here and there. An expensive suspended bridge with wood floor goes across  may be a lot for a 30 minutes walk.There is no fee to cross but next to the entry you can buy a trip in submarine. Well! Just nice walk when you stay close by.

My girlfriend and I went for fun. It literally is like a museum. They have a bunch of statues outside and inside there is a lot of information to explain themes relating to sex. There is two floors. The first floor is about different positions amongst a lot of other stuff. The whole first floor is almost exclusively written in Korean. Unless you can read Korean I would skip it. The second floor does have English. I would only go if both floors have English. It is not for non-Korean speakers.

Little walk down pathway along the cliff on the seaside.Something to see while in the area.May be difficult for elderly or those with weak walking abilities as walk to the waterfall from parking lot consist of lots of stairs and wet floors.

I've been to various Buddhist temples throughout South Korea and this by far has been the most breathtaking.  The monks were extremely welcoming and even pointed parts of the temple that I should go. The second floor of the main temple is best for pictures and found myself in that one spot for nearly 45 minutes.  Remember this is a holy place and be respectful especially for its monks who are so inviting.The best time to go is after 6:30 pm. The crowds are nearly gone and you'll be able to witness the ringing of the bells and 7 pm prayer by the monks.  The temple is lit and makes it more majestic than the day.Finally the giant golden Buddha statues were a sight to see. If you are in the Seogwipo area of Jeju- this is a must see!

It's well preserved but not good for people with disability. Inside is quite dark and has uneven flooring. Nothing to complain as it is made by nature and they also provided some trail/even flooring to follow.

Its true that its not much of a museum but really nice place to stop by and enjoy view from building. Its also free of charge. Not sure if you can come by bus probably yes. We used a rented car on island. Cafe is good and i personally like tea ice cream not so sweet as usual one and good for hot day. There is an open spot on the third floor to take a picture with nice view. There is also innisfree shop where you can buy DIY pack and make your own soap. Good place to relax on nearby grass.

Its three floors with aquariums but still not so big bu got pretty awesome one with big display where you can sit and enjoy the view. I also liked the show. They got 2 types of it one with humans and several with animals like dolphins and sea bear. Performance times are 11:10 13:00 15:00 and 17:00. There is also feeding times and female diver's diving. It opens from 10 to 19 so be sure you will see at least one of performance and have time to look around since performance lasts about 40-45 min each.
address: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 성산읍 섭지코지로 95 아쿠아플라넷 제주

review: It's stated only those above age 18 are allowed in though am not sure if it's strictly enforced. There were plenty of tours consisting of local senior residents dropping in. Majority of the displays were outdoors so be prepared for plenty of walking. One of the buildings does not have elevator not escalator access to the upper floor hence it's inaccessible to those who can't use the stairs but they compensated by showing a brief video summary at the lower floor.

It's part of our Jeju tour we stopped by.Beautiful collections spread throughout several floors. Lots of nice handiwork. Didn't have much time to view but for those who are interested in these kind of stuff it's a must see  otherwise half an hour visit would be plenty.There's also restroom and cafe on premise.

It?s like a walk in the dark. Watch your steps as the floor is uneven and could be slippery. Nothing much to see unless you are into geography. there are definitely nicer places in Jeju to visit than this cave.
It was an interesting visit but make sure you are able to walk two kilometers in dim lighting and on uneven flooring which can be wet and slippery. Wear comfortable shoes.

It takes entrance fee to enter the museum  but that's okay as there are three venues in total. With lots of different appearances bears  such as dressing up like students and wedding. The most memorial teddy bear is the president Obama  it is similar to the real Obama but in bear form. The top floor of the second venue is about wedding and relationships between lovers  so it is a great place for lovers to take pictures and have memories with the teddy bear couples. Although I am not a teddy bear fan  I took lots of photos in that first two venues. And in the third venue  bears are for sell  so please remember not to photo bears in the third venue as it is subjected to copy right. Finally  my father bought me a bear which I think is the cutest as a present of graduation. It takes about 40k-80k unequally per bear  but I think it is valuable as all bears are made in Jeju.So  if you think you don't have any way to spend your money  you can go to this teddy bear museum and buy your favorite bear as an emblem of stepping on Jeju.

It only costs about $2 to visit (separate from transportation costs).  Very well maintained site but still a rough surface that requires suitable footwear and it can be wet and slippery in some spots; also quite cool.  This is a very impressive channel to walk through and imagine the lava flowing and leaving the characteristic marks and artifacts along it path.  Dim lighting gives a neat eerieness that somehow makes it even more exciting to explore.  Various well constructed boardwalks with built in floor lights improve access.  The entire tour is about 1 km in each direction.  Very interesting experience.
It is dark and cooling walk and some part of the floor can be a bit rocky. Bring along a small torch light as some part can be quite dark.

It felt spooky from the fog as it was really cold inside. Do bring a jacket if you visit this place. You could see firsthand how the lava affected the rock formations in this cave and it is interesting to watch for first-timers. The floor is quite uneven due to the natural rock formations so do be careful and wear proper shoes. It is about 1km walk to the end and you have to u-turn back to exit as there's only one entrance which is also the exit.

If you're coming to Jeju the sex museums (at least three or four of them) are worth exploring. It might be a bit of a turnoff that the first floor is mostly in Korean but you probably didn't come here to read walls of text. Rated R to XXX in some places and definitely not for kids.

If you`re a Zippo lover  this is a must visit spot. Museum locates in the ground floor of a modern seaside building with breathtaking pacific ocean view. There is 2 exhibition halls  one of those displays many special designed zippos in large size  and the other in fact is a zippo shop  you can see and buy different limited edition zippo there and many are designed by local designer.

I'd like to do temple stay. but.. It was strange for me. No teacher or any guide just slept in the temple.But the temple was big and interesting.Big Budda was nice (look like) & comfortable.The main building organized around 3floors and long painting within philosophical story.

I went with a group of fellow Taekwondo practitioners. The cave is an amazing example of this type of geology. Need to be careful as floor a little uneven due to the natural rock formation but well worth a visit if your in the area. We all did a little Taekwondo practice whilst down there so it made the visit even more memorable.

I think we would have gotten much more out of this if there was English on the first floor displays. On the second floor there is much more English to make it interesting.Some of the content is just weird and some what hilariousThe statues outside are also great to pose with!

I participated in an event focusing on renewable energy and green growth at this superb convention centre. It is modern with meeting rooms upstairs having amazing almost panoramic view of the Jeju coastline. It has large exhibition floor  with large conference rooms on the three floors  but also bilateral meetings rooms that are convenient and centrally located. The catering and banquets were simply exquisite with great Korean cuisine and the banquet room and service were just incredible. I found it very convenient place for participating and networking.

I have visited a number of limestone caves before and this is the first lava tube cave I ever visited. I found it fascinating. Be warned that the floor is undulating and wet and one needs a pair of hiking shoes and a rain jacket to really enjoy this place.
i have been a hello kitty collector for over 25 years. this place is  like a walk down memory lane. it is 3 floors and filled with kitty trivia and memorabilia. there is also a gift store and cafe.

I  read about this peace park in Lonely Planet and asked to go there. Our local guide had never visited there before but said he would definitely take people there now. It took us a while to find the right way to go in- lower floor. On the first floor there was a beautiful photo exhibition but the museum is the real attraction. It tells the story of post World War 2 Jeju and  especially about the massacres by different sides of politics. While the museum focuses on Jeju it provides a real insight into the sources of the 1950s Korean war and the division of the country. The USA and its military commanders certainly contributed to the problems and the terrible suffering of the Jeju people.   I highly recommend Westerners to visit this place and the labelling in English is very good.

Having arrived in Jeju eager to see as much as possible in a short time frame - the art work was top on my hit list. I stumbled across the website for the Museum of Contemporary Art and was very excited to go (as there are so many museums to choose from!)I would recommend a whole morning to visit Jeoji as there is more than just this Museum there. The first Gallery I went to showed a lovely exhibiton on the Sound of Nature this gallery was on the left hand side of the road and was a free two floor exhibition. I then walked along the road to the Museum of Contemporary Art on the right. The Museum had 4 big rooms of Art - all of which had a meaningful message behind the artist's work in both Korean and English! The receptionists were very helpful when directing me as to where to go and I finished my self-guided tour with a visit to the Art shop which was outside in the sculpture garden. A lovely morning well spent taking in the delights of Korean art.

Have never fired a live round before so this was pretty exhilarating for me. There are about 7-8 pistols and revolvers to choose from and i settled with a Beretta. There are computer screens that can help you to view where your last shot was. And at the end you can keep your target paper. We ate at the buffet downstairs on the 3rd floor before coming up as there is a 35% discount on the shooting range price after. The original price for 12 rounds is 35k won. The staff are not able to speak english at all which was quite a bummer as they will usually guide you and teach you how to shoot the target properly.

Have been to other football and the Olympic stadiums like the AC Milan one and those in Beijing  however  this one in Jeju is nothing. Firstly the signages are lousy. We followed the sign to the tour assembly but it turned out to be hall with different consignments and room vividly for the mainland Chinese tours.The stairs and inside the Sex Museum which is located on the second floor is dark and primitive. Interesting it was accessible by a stair in the middle of the carpark. But seeing the lightings as well as the Admission Fee notice printed on a torn A4 paper put on the window of the counter  we had no mood at all to enter into the museum.There is a spa land and other shops in the premises  but the signage is not updated  still indicating shops that were already closed. The stadium has become a low-class event hall instead of holding information and the class of a worldwide event. The only good thing about this site is that it is free. We entered onto the seating area without seeing any guard or staff  but we got very disappointed especially compared with the AC Milan museum and stadium.

Had this on our itinerary as the photos by prior visitors seemed impressive. In truth there wasn?셳 a lot to see. We got there and after a quick wefie shot from the front of the temple we went up through the three floors of the temple?셲 interior which I find pleasant but nothing spectacular. We were done in 15-20mins.

Friend and I visited this museum on our first trip to Korea (while on the island of Jeju) and was pleasantly surprised by a great live performance of traditional African dances and drum beats/riddim. The artifacts are also very interesting and place was so big (3 floors) that we didn't have time to view everything.

For seashell lovers  this is a must visit museum with small entrance fee^^. They have the most exquisite collections of the world of seashells created into masterpieces of art collections. There are 2 storeys of them and a little cozy cafe on the ground floor to relax over a cup of coffee.

Exotic Jeju Island is known for many things: the majestic Hallasan--the massive shield volcano that formed the island and the highest point in South Korea; its mandarin groves; persimmon-dyed galot fashions; the sturdy Jeju ma horses  descended from the ponies of Mongol invaders; tasty black pork; and the iconic haenyeo women divers. But most visitors would not expect to find a Museum of African Art there. And  it's pretty darn good! Located in a massive structure modeled after the mud-brick Great Mosque of Djenne  the museum offers photo-ops galore in its Safari section  although the animals are of the stuffed variety. Very popular with children and couples. The upper floors house a respectable collection of African artifacts and photographs by Kim Jung Man. There is also a great gift shop. But  I have saved the best for last...the live performance of African folk music and dance. The group  Zalia from Senegal  featured lots of drumming  and audience members also got a drumming lesson and a chance to play along on one song. All in all  a quality experience...and a surprising one.

Entrance fee of KRW5 000 per adult which includes a huge cup of hot black coffee (I don't drink coffee and couldn't change it for a hot chocolate drink). The museum is located on one floor with various displays. Towards one end there's a glass concept kitchen where the various chocolates are made and a little further down  the chocolate shop. A box of 8-12 pieces could cost upwards of KRW13 000  and the lady was kind enough to let us try a dark chocolate which ended up quite yummy (not too sweet nor bitter  think it was a 60 or 70% one).

review: Don't expect to much. Lots of different cultural 'health' history. And watch out!
