I know this is weird and to be perfectly blunt I wish they could be more circumspect with their curiosity but they don't really mean any harm. It's an unspoken obsession amongst humans - particularly men and especially Korean men - to compare genitals. Koreans just tend to be more obvious about it in ways that might signal either sexual interest or a punch in the mouth in non-Korean cultures. Have patience.

If you're into exploration and discovering a destination's unique treasures, this is one place on Jeju Island, South Korea not to miss.  Located in a beautiful park-like setting, Manjanggul Cave permits you to descend hundreds of feet below the surface in a cave system that was created by lava flows from a now-extinct volcano.  The cave system constitutes the largest lava tube in the world and is accessible by foot.  Wear comfortable shoes that have good traction (like hikers or sneakers) and expect to get a little wet as the interior has water dripping from the ceilings in places that are unavoidable.  Nevertheless, this experience is a must-do for anyone who likes adventure.  The floor of the cave can be wet (necessitating the need for footwear with good traction) and the temperature in the cave is approximately 55* year-round.  Dress accordingly.  There are many interesting features to see and experience in Manjanggul Cave.  Allow about 90 minutes (minimum) to walk the entire length and be able to see all that it has to offer.  Although you don't get to experience total darkness as in some cave systems, this cave is more than intriguing with the lava formations that remain and the expansiveness of the interior areas.  You might also encounter some inhabitants of the cave.  Anyone who enjoys nature would find this place particularly appealing.

If you love nature, then you absolutely must visit this place. According to the booklet I took, there's an outdoor and an indoor garden. The latter one has 5 different sections: a flower garden, an aquatic garden, a cactus garden, a jungle garden and a tropical fruits? garden as well as an observatory on the 5th floor.The outdoor garden contains TEN different gardens including the herb garden and a french garden. It would take about 2.5 hours to see everything it offers.TRANSPORTATION:-from Jeju: take the Airport Limusine Shuttle (approx 50 mins)-from Seogwipo: take a public bus (approx 20 mins)

If you have an opportunity to visit these lava tubes, then make sure you do!   We have lava caves in New Zealand and I have seen the lava tubes on Hawaii, but these are giants in comparrison.  The grounds of Manjang Caves are well kept.From the carpark it is only a 3 or 4 minute walk along a concrete path to the entrance of the caves.   We were expecting big, but these caves are huge!There are a number of steps leading down into the mouth of the cave and then you are inside this amazing formation.   It was quite an eerie feeling as we ventured deeper and deeper inside the tube which measures approx 5meters wide and up to 10 meters high.   The temperature is quite pleasant inside the caves and it is a little damp.   Even though we all had good walking shoes on, we still had to be quite careful of where we walked on the uneven, slippery  floor.   It is true that there is not a lot of light inside the cave, but we felt that the dim lighting added to the atmosphere.   In hindsight, a torch might have been helpful.All in all, definitely well worth the visit and would highly recommend to all. I would recommend that this is probably not a safe place for the elderly and very young children.  My elderly parents waited for us at the main building where there was a restaurant, shop and toilets.

If you are there and have no place to visit, perhaps you may want to waste and hour or 2 to walk into the cave. There is no special attraction inside the cave that will give you a WOW factor. By end of the trail, you would just like saying...err...thats it? Its cold in winter and the floor are wet with water dripping from the cave ceiling. Its dark too.

If you are planning to visit the Hello Kitty Island, beware: there is a specific audience that his place caters to; it is not recommended for everyone. Our tour group went here in lieu of the Trick Eye Museum.Little girls and Hello Kitty fans would love this place. Hello Kitty merchandise are displayed everywhere. There is also a room that narrates the history of how Sanrio characters came about.  There is a Hello Kitty Caf챕 at the 2nd floor. On the 3rd floor, there is an auditorium that plays a Hello Kitty-themed show. Outside is an open-air Hello Kitty-themed miniature garden maze. The view of the landscape from here is wonderful. For me, it was meh. I am not among those that this place was built for.On the plus side, there a postcards available at the souvenir shop, which you pass through as you exit the building. I also liked the stamping stations spread around the place, which are reminiscent of postmarks.

If you are going with little kids, definitely go. But otherwise it's just OK though I would say worth a visit if you are bored. Pretty much all the information is in Korean, but then again doesn't take much to identify the teddy bear version of Steve Jobs or Albert Einstein ;) The place has two floors of teddy bears, and I must say after about 25 teddies they all start looking the same. This was close to our hotel and it was raining so we paid a visit. I would advise the museum to put more info in English as Jeju is becoming more internationlised in terms of tourists.

If you are a Kpop fan and have an afternoon to spare, you shouldn't miss this. There were plethora of stations and   things to do   for me and my friends who were less knowledgable about kpop. Don't skip the gift shop on first floor!

i wouldnt have rate poor until i went to   Teseum  . things in teddy bear museum all mini sizes in a box well protected. they have 3 floors, and only the ground floor have some bears for picture. For me kind of bored compare to Teseum, Teseum you can touch and picture closely with those teddys. Jeju has 2 or 3 teddy bear museum, i been to 2 one is teddy bear museum & another is Tesuem. more recommended to Teseum instead of this.   links: http://english.visitkorea.or.kr/enu/SI/SI_EN_3_1_1_1.jsp?cid=701764http://www.tripadvisor.com.my/Attraction_Review-g297885-d3805571-Reviews-Teseum_Jeju-Jeju_Jeju_do.html

I would recommend that you read the book ?The Island of Sea Women? by Lisa See before visiting the museum. I felt an emotional connection to the museum, the observatory and the grounds around the area, primarily because I had some background knowledge. The museum is well laid out and interesting. Do take the time to watch the video on the main floor before going through the exhibits. If you are there around 10:00 a.m. or 1:00 p.m. you may be able to see the women divers from the observatory on the 3rd floor.  Getting there: we were on a cruise ship and took a taxi from the ship terminal in Jeju City. It took about an hour and was a very scenic drive.  Our taxi driver gave us an hour to tour the museum and grounds and then dropped us off by the main market area in downtown Jeju City. It was under $100 for four people in a taxi.

I went there during the peak of summer, it was scorching hot outside, but once you step down about 10steps into the cave, the temperature dropped instantly about 10degree celcius. It was dark inside, the floor is uneven, it's basically the original form of the cave. There's water dropping from the ceiling, but that's just the natural way it is inside the cave. Despite all that though it is a safe place to walk to, and it's really quite amazing inside the cave. You can see the signs of the lava once flowing through inside. Quite a fun experience for me =)

I went their with my wife. I didn't find the place as interesting and exciting as other people claimed. My recommendation, unless you are a geologist this place has nothing substantial to offer. Take a warm cloth and comfortable shoes when you visit this place. The temperature in the cave is low(you feel cool even in summer) and the floor is wet and a little bit slippery.A person can have knowledge about lava tubes but personally I felt unsatisfied. The cave is very dark for anyone to figure out things inside. Information boards inside give information about the site. If a visitor has enough time to visit, you can drop by this place. But, if your schedule is tight you can skip this place.

I went here on Friday 31.05.2019. The front desk staff were very helpful, the museum is really easy as there's arrows on the floor directing you where to go. There is loads of information in English, it's easy to follow and very informative. The island has some really sad history, for anyone interested in history, and the impact of splitting Korea, this is a must do. The information does not make easy reading, but you will never forget this story, and it's an important one to remember. The gardens have lots of memorials, and outside is a nice space.It's not a pop in memorial/museum, it's bigger than expected. I'd recommend 2.5 hours to do the museum and outside. Unfortunately I had to rush as I got there late in the day and wish I'd had more time, but I'm pleased I went, and got most stuff done. It's accessible by bus. The museum closes at 6, last entry 5, but I'd suggest you get there no later than 3.30pm to do it properly.For clarity, this is the 4.3 peace park on the east side of the island, as there is one on the west side with a similar name, I've no idea what that one is like.

I went at July... quite a few steps down from entrance to cave and the floor is slippery with water...  You can feel the chill at entry, I suggest you remain in motion to avoid get cold..Walking around can be a challenge for some (especially for the elderly) since the floor is very rough and uneven, this is exacerbated by poor lighting in most parts throughout the cave.. a lot people used torches from phones to get around...It?s annoying for a inquisitive person as the half of the sign and info are Korean only... The interior of the space is pretty featureless... only two noticeable Lime stone caves are a lot more pretty, but it?s worth going if you are in the area and never been in a Lava Cave

I was thinking of skipping this attraction in favour of the natural attractions. Due to bad weather I visited this place on a whim but I enjoyed it better than expected. The building itself is quite pretty like a big greenhouse. The floral arrangement and landscaping is tasteful although not as good as Gardens by the Bay in Singapore. There are pretty sculptures dispersed through the compound. There are many different gardens to explore. We visited the indoor gardens first followed by taking the lift up to the top floor for a view of Seogwipo and lastly took the train for the outside gardens. It was too cold and windy to walk outside. There was some confusion about where to buy train tickets, the driver helped to walk to the counter and buy our tickets. Spring is probably a good time to visit since many flowers are in bloom. It would be good if they can stop the vandalism of the trees by the Koreans, many of them scratched their names on the branches.

I was slightly disappointed that we weren't able to see stalagmites and stalactites like I thought we could.A warning in advance, tourists are only allowed access to a fraction of the entire cave (it is still a long walk) and the walk isn't a loop, so you'll be seeing everything twice.TIP: Perhaps this is obvious, but it was quite cool and damp in the cave, so I recommend bringing an extra layer and wearing proper, closed shoes. The floor of the cave was quite puddle-ridden and it can be easy to trip as you stare at the inner walls. Also, bring a tripod or use the timer on your camera if you plan on taking photos.Overall, I really enjoyed my experience, though I should say that this is the first 'real' cave that I've ever visited. It's a good place to visit if you're on the island, but I wouldn't fly here all the way from Seoul just to visit.

I was excited to go see the Manjanggul caves, and had an image in my mind that unfortunately didn't fit what I saw. The whole experience is pretty cool, the floor is uneven, dodging water droplets becomes a game, the lava flow marks are beautiful, but lack of light, lack of stalactite formations, and a lot of areas that are fenced off let me down slightly. However, cheap entrance, and the atmosphere is actually quite lovely. If you get the chance to go, try and do it.

I visited this place with my family, my parents are seniors. Costs 2,000 won per person. The stairs were ok for me to climb, but will be more challenging for seniors. It?s approximately 40++ floor climb (based on my watch tracking) and takes around 20++ minutes of brisk climbing to reach the top. The uneven stone flooring in certain areas can be a little tricky to climb. The views were more beautiful halfway, rather than the top. Different paths for ascending and descending so the foot traffic is smooth. The view from the peak was slightly obscured by rocks and the fence, but there?s binoculars available for use for 500 won. We visited this location close to sunset, but the view was amazing nevertheless. Surrounding the area is a lot of eateries, and there?s washroom etc nearby (important in winter :) ). Ample FOC parking spots available.

i thought the museum sounded stupid but it was actually really cute!!! there were so many scenes set up with stuffed animals on the first floor.  they were so creative!  then you can you to the second floor and take pictures.  there's the rock band set up, the proposal bear, and many more.  there are also famous works of art re-done with teddy bears. finally there's the gift shop.  everything is over priced but you can't expect anything else...

I loved this place!!! Maybe because I love teddy bears and collect them. But objectively, I think they did a wonderful job to dress the bears up in adorable costumes and arrange them in all sorts of different themed settings. You start at the 3rd floor and walk down to the 1st. My favourite was the 2nd floor - even though the exhibits are encased in glass, I could put my own little bears (yes, I brought my own bears with me on this trip) on the glass and take pictures with them (no flash allowed). Some of the bears have even moving parts and some are life-sized. There is a scheduled musical and dance performance by Elvis bear and friends, which my parents enjoyed. At the outdoors area, you can take photos with life-sized bears in interesting poses and themed settings and there is even a clock that chimes hourly and is accompanied by bears dancing with the chimes. There is a cafe and a souvenir shop in the ground level and you can take pictures with panda bears (not real of course) and other cute bears, and buy a souvenir bear home (but price is quite ex).

I LOVE... this museum!!! I am a teddy bear fan so this museum feels like heaven to me aside from being a K-drama fan. Before visiting Jeju, I researched on the top sites recommended to be visited, i got fascinated with the reviews about Teddy Bear museum plus knowing that some of its Teddy Bears where featured in one my favorite Korean Drama of all time PRINCESS HOURS. The teddy bears are just so cute, you can see them perform different functions and dressed of different profession and famous personalities such as Marilyn Monroe, Steve Jobs, Madonna etc. Afetr visiting the exhibit halls, we then went to the lower ground floor area where tall Teddy Bears are on display alongside Teddy Bears items that are for sale.A must visit for Teddy Bear Lovers.

I had read some reviews that it was damp and dark and not worth a visit. So, I went with little expectation. When I stepped into the cave, I was amazed! It was definitely a place for people who love nature! As I walked through the tunnel, I tried to imagine the hot volcanic larva flowing through larva tube, leaving these marks and traces. I would highly recommend the place to people who really love the wonders of nature. Yes, the place was damp, with water dripping from the ceiling and very uneven floors and puddles of water everywhere.I still find it worth the 2.5km walk from the bus stop at the main road. To get there, we took bus 701 and got off at the Manjanggul Cave Bus Stop. Bus 990 could take us right to the entrance but the bus was so irregular. We had just missed one. Therefore we decided to walk in. It was an okay walk.

I didn't know what to expect in a lava tube, and I was totally amazed and intrigued. We decided to make the trip by public transport from Seogwipo for the adventure, and we enjoyed every moment. There are good facilities at the cave entrance - nice toilets, two food outlets and an information centre. Extremely impressive . It is nothing like a limestone cave, and does not have that enclosed feeling. It does require some stairs to be climbed, and the floor is a little uneven and dark, but more cavernous than cave like.

I didn't have any kind of expectation when I went to this museum. When we got in, I was pleasantly surprised. The teddy bears on display were interesting. The museum has several floors and the lowest floor is the retail area. Very interesting stuff on display for sale. Be sure to go to the Elvis Presley theatre where you can catch a 4 minute show if the teddy bear Elvis doing a performance. It is held in 15 mins interval.

I couldn?t resist visiting this place on our way from Jeju city to Seogwipo. It made me giddy as a child. Entry fee is now 14,000 won per adult, and either 11,000 or 13,000 for children. This place has optional guided tours and accepts credit cards. Small room of Hello Kitty history and how her image has evolved since 1976. Original design merch on display. Lots of interactive rooms for kids and 3 floors to play. As an adult I still had fun and enjoyed a Hello Kitty hot chocolate (her face is in the cream), and Hello Kitty-shaped strawberry mousse cake in the cafe. You?re paying for the experience, here, so if you or your child is not a Hello Kitty fan, don?t waste your time. The maze on the roof is shaped like Hello Kitty from an aerial view and is strictly for children?the maze walls are only about 2 feet tall. My favorite part was the art exhibit (2nd floor) and all the small, unexpectedly perfect details (heart shaped straws, Hello Kitty toilet paper!). Souvenir shop: a mechanical pencil costs 7,700 won (more than $6)?I guess this is slightly more than American Sanrio store prices. But, if you?re willing to visit this museum, you?re probably also willing to pay for a momento of your experience.

I came here after visiting the nearby Jeju Loveland. This museum has 4 floors. First floor is the Welcome Stage, which traces the history of computers and hardwares. Second floor is Open Stage, which depicts the history and development of computer games. Third floor is Hidden Stage, which showcases how computers changed and expanded our everyday life. The Basement 1 is Special Stage, which is used for special exhibitions.Second and third floors allow visitors to play old computer and arcade games such as Space Invaders, Galaxy etc. Playing these games bring back fond memories of my younger days. Before leaving, I headed to the cafe at B1 and ordered the keyboard waffle for its novelty, not cheap at 12,000 won.Admission fees 8,000 won. Note it is closed on Monday. Worth a visit if you have half a day to spare. Suggest you combine this place with the nearby Jeju Loveland.

I arrived that place on a sunny afternoon.When I entered the cave, I immediately felt very chilling and refreshing!I was really amazed, beautiful formation from the lava, 'elephant toes' 'cupola' etc.The floor is wet and uneven, so be careful.

I am sorry to say it but it was a boring place to visit. It would be interesting if we didn't have internet to get to know the world. By the way, my 8 year-old son was scared on the second floor to see all the torture instruments.

I am in the middle of living in Jeju for a year and visited the Haenyeo Museum with three friends a couple of months ago. It was a really great visit and showed really well the changes in Haenyeo lifestyle as time has gone on. The top floor has a beautiful picture gallery with gorgeous views. Highly recommend. I think you need about an hour - an hour and a half here.Also the gift shop is great for cute Jeju-y things. I put some   Jeju stockings   together for my cousin's kids for Christmas all with keyrings/books/purses/other stuff bought here.

Hidden in the lush greens of Jeju is this hidden gem that impressed me and my friends when we visited in July. The huge lava cave is around 7KM long but for safety reasons, the public is only allowed to walk the first 1KM of the whole cave. However the sight you get from that 1 KM is breath taking already.Do not be tricked by the term   cave   and think that this place is going to be warm. Upon going down the flight of stairs to the entrance of the cave, there will be a sudden dip in temperature and it will get colder as you go deeper in. So do bring a jacket along if you are prone to feeling cold. However, if you are visiting in Summer, it's the perfect escape from the heat.Although the interior is dimly lit and the floor is very slippery and uneven, you are rewarded with an amazing sight for the trouble you go through. However, I would not recommend this place to elderly with walking difficulties as well as families with young children that need prams.

Here you can find a lot of beautiful flowers and tropical flora. It is very suitable for green lover. Besides, you can find some tropical fruits over here with some information. After visited four themed garden park at the ground floor, you may proceed to the top floor using the lift at the center. You can see the beautiful view at the top floor. Also, you can take a train tour outside the building. :)

Having just visited the newly opened Teddy Bear Museum in Chengdu, Sichuan Province, China (by the same group), this original museum in Jeju was a little underwhelming, even for a solid teddy bear fan like me. Unlike those in Chengdu, I didn't appreciate the fact that all teddies in Jeju were enclosed in glass cases. Impossible to take a decent pic with them!There was a good collection of antique bears. Great for a collector like myself. Also there was the supposedly most expensive teddy bears in the world. The LV bear and the diamond bear.For sale of their Elvis bears I believe, there was a small theater on the second floor showing 4 mins Elvis teddy concert every quarter of the hour. Perhaps I went at a later hour (5pm), I was the only one in the theater. Appreciate that the museum is opened till 8pm in the evening, so it's great as a quick destination pre or post dinner, if you are staying or hanging around the Jungmum Resort Area. The museum was located right next to Lotte Hotel. There was a Lotteria on the ground floor but it was closed during my visit. An attractive and well stocked teddy store on the ground floor too, unlike its sad and sparse Chengdu cousin. Happy that there were some collector grade Korean handmade teddies for sale. Their house brand   so-called   limited edition replica made-in-China white Alfred bear (real limited edition would come with serial numbers) came in a nice copycat Steiff look alike gift box and a photo with a Korean prince. At only USD 35, it's great as a souvenir/gift!I like the outdoor park area. Great for kids to run around. Overall not a very big place. Whole place would take about an hour.

Great place to see local food sold by local people. There is plenty of Jeju products to choose from, as well as some farmers clothes, souvenirs, packed local food and of course a lot of oranges. When you hungry just eat some yummy ttoekpokki or mandoo. Cheap and great. Wear full shoes as floor is always wet from fish tanks.
Great place for kids, also for adults. There are alot of teddy bears, in second floor. This is standard place for tour. We enjoy this place.
Good experience to go into a lava cave. But floor in the cave is wet,slippery and uneven. Not meant for family with very young children and old people. Ok

From historical event, paintings, to modern day moment, current dramas cast of all teddies. From teddy named Wilson on his journey around the world to Elvis and Queen Elizabeth in teddy version all in one place. Not to be missed, the most expensive LV and Swarovski teddy on display! Outside you can witness miniature teddies on some serious construction site of 9 meters height of huge gigantic Teddy in the making. There's a teddy souvenir shop, and also teddy cafe. The museum is not that big, just 2 floors of gallery and 1 floor cafe and shop. Some bears displayed outside in the park.

Free carpark. There?s a replica fountain of the real lava column which is found at the end of the tunnel. Entrance costs 1000 won. Descent about 80 steep steps into the tunnel. Temp change can be felt immediately. Floors are damp from the rain and the water drippings from the ceilings. Best to have a hoodie and raincoat or an umbrella. The tunnels are very dark and damp. Go slowly and let the eyes adjust to the dim conditions.  There is a marking at 850metres which is great as it is difficult to gauge the distance while walking in the dark. Then you will have 150 metres more to go before reaching the end of the tunnel open to public. The world?s largest lava column, 7.6m in height is located at the end. Advise: wear sensible shoes with good grip as the floors are damp and slippery ; warm clothing; carry a torch- or use your phone?s flashlight. It makes the trek so much easier. Lastly, restrooms located at the surface level are decent though damp and a bit stinky.

For such a long bus ride and such great reviews, I was hoping for much more. We stayed on the Southwestern side of the island and took the nearly two hour bus trip to see this amazing cave that was rated near the top on TripAdvisor. However, we were sorely disappointed. If you've never been to a cave before, you should go. It's a unique type of cave, which is why I gave it a 3-point rating, but there is nothing that draws the attention. In most caves, there is at least one aspect that management (or whoever it is) chooses to make important, such as a really long stalactite that has a cool creation fact...but this cave had none of that. I think they only had around 3 or 4 sets of very cool lighting, illuminating barely anything. In a cave, lighting techniques are your best friends. The entire trek was actually incredibly dark, making viewing anything difficult. (I know that sounds funny if you've never been to a cave before, but those that have know that certain lighting highlights unique aspects but if there is minimal lighting, even walking is annoyingly difficult.) Finally, at the end of the cold, long trek through floors that you have to pay more attention to than the walls, we came to a column of something that almost reached the ceiling and could have been the highlight of the cave trip. The management simply didn't choose to beef this thing up. The lighting on the end piece was regular. There was no sign explaining what is was or how it came to be. It was simply the end of the road. And guess where the exit is? You have to walk back the exact way you came. So, we were bored twice. In short, I gave a 3 out of kindness for its unique type. The cave has potential. I simply wish whoever is in charge would utilize what they have to the fullest.

for me there is nothing special about this cave. the only thing we can do is just walking straight through the cave almost 1km (cmiww). and after we arrive to the end of the tunnel , we just see a small stage and some pic as i remembered. if you traveling with child , pls be carefull when you step the floor. because its really slipper..

For a start, if one is looking to purchase Innisfree products, it would probably be better to get them from their numerous stores on the island. Almost a quarter of the floor space here is set for people to try their hand at making (or shaping) Innisfree natural soap. The product selection is limited and they don't provide any free samples or special offers (like in their purpose built stores or counter in shopping malls). On the plus side, the store offer instant GST deduction for all items purchased here (min 30,000won).There is also a cafe here. But if one is looking for the famous Green Tea Latte or Green Tea ice cream and cake, those are only available from Ossulac Tea Museum Cafe next door.

For a first timer visiting this place as tourist, i can say that this place gives you the choices you need to bring back home. You need to do some haggling of price. Some of the salespersons are quite persistent. They would do the 'extra mile' to make you buy their merchandise. 3rd floor gift section also has good variety of choices. I ended up spending more than W100,000 there. No regrets !
Floor of cave dark, wet and uneven. Bring torch and must be able to walk on wet slippery uneven ground to enjoy this national heritage site.

Firstly, this is a tube and not a cave. Secondly, it is made of lava. So do not expect the majestic stalactites, stalagmites and other features associated with limestone caves.Although it is said to be 7 Km long, only a 1 Km length is open to the public. It is wide and not claustrophobic. Interesting features are marked and explained.It is dimly lit and you need a torch. The floor is uneven and wet.Having said that, it is a very unusual feature and worth a visit if you are in Jeju.

Fairly small place for a hefty KRW10,000 entrance fee; the most expensive Jeju attraction. Features 2 galleries of teddy bears from various countries and themes and a teddy souvenir shop.  Will appeal to ladies, children and couples keen on photo snaps with huggable teddies, especially the human-sized ones at the corner of each floor and in the gift shop. Be prepared to jostle with crowds on a busy day.  There is a 5 minute T-Elvis performance held at every 15 minute interval in the Elvis Presley theatre.  Can skip if you're not a teddy lover or been here before as exhibits hardly change.

Everything about our favourite bear and its history. The museum has 3 floors, where you can see many different displays of teddy bears and animatronics, in a different setting. One floor is for displaying teddies from different times, another one shows teddy related artworks and finally there's a floor where you find a souvenir shop and some cafes. In the outside park you can view Jungmun sea while seeing human-sized teddy sculptures. The whole surrounding area is beautiful. Ideal for friends, couples and families as well!

Even in March, Udo is beautiful--and in March, there are few visitors. When we were there, haenyo were out at low tide collecting seafood among the lava rocks, banging the rocks to bring them out. We stayed at a traditional hotel (thin mattresses on heated floor) near the lighthouse on the main road. Eat al fresco at the nearby restaurant across from the healing-stone throne is and check out their fresh   ginseng of the sea   (slices of a raw sea-cucumber-like animal). On the mainland, be sure to check out tiny Gangjeong Village, on the southern coast just west of Seogwipo, where villagers and Jeju priests are braving police, the navy, Hyundai, and Samsung 24/7 as they protest a huge naval base being foisted upon them. The mayor was jailed a few days ago for chaining himself around the neck to a rafter, when police rampaged and tore down protesters' headquarters, replacing it with boulders to prevent reconstruction. The protesters are very friendly, by the way. It's on the Ollie hiking trail, where it crosses over the Gangjeong River and passes the gates of the   destruction   site. A beautiful waterfall meets the sea and can be viewed by taking a path on either side of the bridge. Poonglim Resort is nearby, with full spa and small steam bath facilities.

DRAMA WORLD is consist of DRAMA STUDIO, TEDDY BEAR and WEDDING PHOTO ZONE. Drama studio is an indoor exhibition hall with a floor area of 5,000 square meters. Drama studio is actual TV drama studio and restored studio in KOREA, USA and EUROPE, in which the visitors can experience all costumes and accessories for free(except HANBOK, Wedding dress). Our exhibition is consist of town(street) studio and interior studio. Our exhibition is consist of Korean studio(K-DRAMA) and World studio(USA,EUROPE DRAMA). Visitors of all age groups can experience KOREA culture, Western(USA) culture and The Middle ages(EUROPE) culture through DRAMA STUDIO. We are the first experiment-type drama studio in Korea where the visitors wear the costumes and use the articles to be the main character in dramas. ※ Now, World Studio is consist of TEDDY BEAR EXHIBITION and WEDDING PHOTO ZONE with a background of Western and The Middle ages studio. Collaboration between DRAMA WORLD and TEDDY BEAR. TEDDY BEAR Exhibition Hall’s floor area is about 1,000 square meters. At DRAMA WORLD, visitors can see TEDDY BEAR, which produced scenes in drama of Korea, USA and Europe. Visitors can easily understand the scene of drama. Because the text(Chinese, English, Korean)is placed in each display of TEDDY BEAR. Visitors can take a picture with man-sized TEDDY BEAR using props and wearing costume for free. Visitors can learn about the Self-Wedding culture of Korea through the Wedding photo zone with a background of drama studio. Visitors can take a picture in wedding photo zone on studio of the Western Age in USA, the Middle Ages in Europe and Korea’s drama. In each Wedding photo zone, wedding accessories are placed. And they are available for free.

Don't miss this show if u are in Jeju. Only available & performing until October 2020....awesome immersive show.? @ 빛의 벙커 Bunker de Lumieres. The floors and walls become the canvas of this highly immersive digital art that come to life, as Van Gogh's art work are displayed all over and synchronised with beautiful clasical music. Definitely worth the more than an hour show.We enjoyed it tremendously!

Do you like cold, dark, dripping lava caves? Then this is for you! Just be warned - WEAR PROPER WATERPROOF SHOES! Or at least, bring an extra pair of shoes and socks cause your feet are going to get soaked in the many puddles. Better still, bring an umbrella or wear a poncho. The roof constantly drips, and there?s no way to avoid getting soaked. It would have been better if:- More lights could be installed. Some places were way too dim, and we had to use our handphone lights. - There was the option of tour guides. We wished someone could have walked us through and explained things a bit more!- Sone portions of the cave needed levelling. We were very worried about twisting our ankles at some points because the floor was VERY uneven! On the bright side:- Entrance fee is very cheap.- It?s a rare experience to walk around a lava tube. So just do it! :D (But be careful and walk slowly!)

Definitely worth a visit, even if you only have a few hours to spare. This attraction my husband and I completed in just over an hour, there is no audio guide but there are informative signs throughout the cave. You return to the start of the cave the same way you came in, so take your time reading the signs but if you are tight on time you can read some of it on the way back. Being a natural cave/tube the floor of the cave is pretty rocky, must wear comfortable shoes. If you are driving around Jeju, and using the rental GPS, the telephone number to type into the gps system is: 7834818

Definitely a special cave. As it is a lava tube, the floor is also made of solid lava, aka uneven flooring. Bring good hiking boots as it takes at least 40 minutes to reach the end. Advice to use a tripod for good photos.

Cuteness overload! They recreate the famous historical event, famous artpiece, famous public figure, which is starring the teddy bear itself! You can read about the teddy bear history, too. The museum is on the 1st & 2nd floor, while the ground floor is a merchandise store where you can buy some teddy bear dolls, etc.

Coming from a country where temples are famous for their stunning decoration I did not expect much from temples in East Asian countries. But Yakchunsa Temple was beyond my expectations. The temple is stunningly decorated. The Buddha statues are absolutely beautiful. I recommend you walk up to the second floor where you will see countless mini gold Buddha in different poses on the wall to your left and you can enjoy the view of the main hall and the main Buddha from high up. There is a small building to the left of the main hall with 500   heroes  . I think they are important monks or something. At least that's what it says in Chinese characters. All 500 of them have different facial expressions and poses. Some are very comical. Do take a quick look inside. And don't forget to drink the water from the water fountain before you leave the temple. The water there is refreshingly sweet.

Coat/mittens/warm clothing, good walking shoes, and at least a small flashlight are a must.  The entrance stairs are steep and can be wet/slippery.  The lighting inside varies in how well it is placed.  The floor surface is uneven and can be wet/slippery.This is a popular tourist destination on Jeju Island and so there will be waves of tourists and school groups pouring down into the lava tube cave as their tour buses arrive, but if you are patient and can take your time, there will be periods of quiet and peacefulness in between the groups during which you can enjoy the cave - but if you don't wear a coat and are chilled, it will make it hard to be patient and wait out the hordes of teenagers and other tourist groups!

Built on a reclaimed land-fill site, this vast area of pathways, statues, displays, museums and traditional villages is very worth a visit if on Jeju. From the impressive stone structures and flat basalt 'floor' at the entrance of the park, I was blown away by the vast array of statues that are displayed, explained and on show in this area. There is ample car parking that is only a short walk form the entry way. A small fee is required and then you are free to wander the area that included a massive and spectacular 2 store (below ground) museum that outlines the geographic development of Jeju along with many interactive displays, a short film with subtitles, examples and galleries of 'stone art'. A gift shop of course, provided a range of traditional and specific items and there are amenities spread throughout the part. Water features, a traditional village, an art gallery and a vast array of stone sculpture will give you hours of things to view and read as you wander through the park In my humble opinion, not to be missed!!!

Believed to be formed about 2,00,000 ? 3,00,000 years ago, this UNESCO protected heritage centre, the Manjjanggul Lava tube tunnels said to be one of the longest ( around 7.5 km) and well maintained Lava tube tunnels in the world. Though there would not be much to see around, the sheer excitement one experiences just walking into the dark ,rocky ,slippery tunnel is worth the money paid for.Important things to remember.-Those who are having difficulty in walking should avoid getting down the tunnel as the floor is rocky,slippery and uneven.-A good pair of shoes is a must. No high heeled footwear please.-Carry or wear warm clothes as the inside temperature would be much lower than outside.-Wearing a cap/hat would be also good as water would be dripping on your head as you walk.-The Tunnel is open for 1 KM for the Public and with minimal lighting. Carrying a low intensity torch would be best.

Before you want to take a ferry to Udo island, please take note that you need to bring along your passport to purchase a ticket. You will be given 2 tickets, 1 for departure & 1 for arrival (you have to keep this and pass to the boatman at Udo when you want to return to main island). A tip is to get the korean map together with your language?s map because they have more details of the island as compared to other languages. The ferry comes every 15 minutes so you do not have to worry if you miss it. Inside the ferry, there are flooring with thermal and you have to take your shoes off before stepping into the resting platforms. Otherwise, you may choose to stand outside those rooms and there are some outdoor seats at the top of the ferry. Please also take note that there are 2 ports at Udo, so your ferry might stop at either one.Once you reach the island, you will be greeted by tons of shop assistants trying to get you to rent bikes to you. You will need an international driver license to be able to drive any motorise vehicles. Upon confirmation which is the vehicle you want, you have to leave your passport with the register counter. They will provide you with a map to go around the island. We were informed that the whole cycling trip takes an hour. However, here comes the challenging part. There were no proper division of the road for those driving trucks, buses, cars, motorcycles & bicycles. You can be riding your bicycle and have a full speed bus chasing behind you and pressing the horn at you. Cars and trucks from the opposite direction also travel at fast speed towards you, which we had to stop many times to give way to these fast moving vehicles. After getting to the first beach, which was really beautiful, the rest of the trip towards the next beach was tough as there were many upward slopes and split roads which have no proper signages to tell you which way to go. We had to go in to random houses and ask in broken korean for which way to go. However, when we reach the lighthouse area, we managed to locate Jimmy?s icecream shop as suggested by our Jeju driver. I tried the mandarin orange ice cream while my friend tried the apple mango ice cream. Everything tasted natural and yummy so I would recommend it to tourist who visit the place. However, from the road before this ice cream place onwards to the last 5 mins of the ride, it was all upwards riding.We took almost 3 hours to finish cycling around the whole island (We have done quite a few rides in Singapore so I don?t think we were slow in cycling around the island). So for those who have no license or feel that you?re not up to 2-3 hours of cycling, I would advise you to take the tour bus to get from places to places on the island.

Be prepared to climb back up after going down the steps. Will need proper shoes as the floor is uneven, and does have small puddles of water  here and there.It was a nice walk in the cave, and getting a better understanding of nature involving volcanic lava flow.

At the entrance of this huge garden layout is lush, green plants  there is a bonsai garden, herb gardens, an array of flowers, a subtropical garden, water garden and a stone display as you travel along a palm garden road. There is a fair amount of walking.This display of trees, plants and gardens is a wonderful experience although its the caves, limestone tube-shaped structures growing downward from the ceiling of the cave and stalagmites that grow from the floor up. Structures are formed  containing calcium-bicarbonate. Fossilized seashells, frozen lava, and numerous other structures which enhanced our walk through the caves.  Visit the stone exhibition hall, see the parrots and the various species of birds. A must see attraction.

At ARARIO MUSEUM TAPDONG CINEMA unique art works of various artists (including Ugo Rondinone Kohei Nawa Andy Warhol and more) will be displayed all throughout the 1st to 5th floor. Super-sized arts which requires complicated installation such as   Hero No.2   by Zhang Huan and   What does the vessel contain that the river does not know   by Subodh Gupta will be premiered in Korea for the first time. In addition display of 4 large scale paintings by German Neo-expressionist Sigmar Polke will also contribute to create an overwhelming ambiance at the museum.

As we didn't manage to watch the Haenyeo performance at Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak - we decided to visit the museum instead. The museum is quiet, probably because it's quite off the center.Fee: 1100 won per personStart with a short film on the history of haenyeo, the museum has 2 floors. Display of Haenyeo's life, their tools and equipment and other deep sea fishing and farming information.A particular section caught my attention - a digital map showing where the Haenyeo went to make a living, leaving behind their home town, to make more money like Hokkaido, Russia...There is also a section featuring the Haenyeo anti-Japanese campaign, which is very much inspiring.

As a child I was a big Hello Kitty fan and thought it would be nice to visit this place, after seeing it at the airport. Getting here is really easy from the main bus terminal. I did not know what to expect when I got here. But when I got there I noticed it was $12,000 won to get in. But once you are inside there is nothing special about the place to be charging so much. Its just a bunch of halls with Hello Kitty pictures and some random facts. On the second floor there is a Cafe, that is also overpriced and over crowded. Almost impossible to get a good seat. Service is not great. They not only took forever to take my order, I was the only one in line, but also to give me what I had ordered. The gift shop is also an overpriced place with not a lot of options. Knowing what I know now I dont think I would have done this place.

Amazing cave carved by molten lava moving underground with many interesting features, however, you need to be prepaired for dim lighting, uneven floor with many tripping hazards as well as uneven steps/stairs.  Not suitable for young children or older folks who have trouble with sight or walking.

Amazed by the view inside the cave. Overall distance travel back and forth takes 1 hour to complete, approximately 2km. Advised to wear comfortable shoes (rocky slippery floor) and jacket as it can be very cold inside the cave. Bring an umbrella if you need it as there?s water droplets from the top of cave.

although it just open 1/3 of area for tourist but there was quite big & long cave actually. slipping & uneven floor sometimes. light setting not bad compared with other country. it was cold esp for you need to take walk over 1hour if you don't do fast pace to finish it. actually, it has 1km. the rock & lava also impressive. good to take time for it.and i reached here at 11am, maybe the sunlight with cool air. i saw some spot light before went inside the cave. that was beautiful.

Along with Seongsan Ilchulbong, Manjanggul Cave is one of the two must-see attractions in Jeju, IMHO.There is a small information center building available with some interesting facts about the cave.  The cave itself is quite fascinating.  It is only 1 km in length, but it requires a very slow pace to traverse the entire cave.  This is due to the very rough nature of the ground that one walks on.  The cave floor has not been smoothed by man - unlike Micheon cave, so the ground is extremely uneven, sharp, and at points quite dangerous!  You definitely would not want to take a fall on the ground.  The ground is also very wet in areas.  Finally, the cave is not very well illuminated.  This makes it quite difficult for people who are elderly, have physical disabilities, or if you want to carry a baby.  In fact, for these groups, I would strongly advise not to visit the cave.The cave itself is quite large in height and occupies a large volume of space.  However, it is quite dark inside the cave and there's nothing too overly unique (when compared to something like Cave of the Winds) within the cave - other than it's very big and somewhat creepy.   I only made it through one third of the cave before I had to turn back due to time constraints.  There are a few man-made displays of interest providing more information on the cave and how is was formed.

Admission costs KRW 8,000. Unfortunately, the museum fell short of my expectations. Not conducive for photo taking and has 2 floors of teddy bear exhibits which I personally expected the museum to hold much more collection of teddy bears. Great for kids, not a must visit for adults unless you're a teddy bear lover.

About 1 kilometer of the lava tube  is open to walk through. You descend a long staircase into the cave. You will be walking on the old lave flow, so the floor is uneven & pitted, and full of puddles. There is dim lighting, so you really need to bring your own flashlight to see where you are stepping. The wall are fairly smooth & rounded, you will only be seeing a few small formations. If you are a nature geek (like me) you will enjoy this. If you want  lots of stalactites & large formations, this is not for you.
A true hello kitty's fan dream come true, hello kitty is literally everywhere; on the walls, floors, pictures, in the bathroom, and there's even a cafe inside. It is beyond beautiful.

A terrific site that is well maintained and well explained. Points of interest are marked in 3 languages including English. Come prepared with proper footwear. Tourists are walking on uneven flooring. Also this tunnel can be damp.  Photographing is not permitted, but plenty of visitors were using their cell phones.
4 Floors of a journey in time from the 70s to the very much today technology.Experience interactive games and tasks, good for age 9+

3 floors of teddy bears, dressed in all forms.  Covered teddy bears from the 1900s to current, and they had bears of   famous   personalities such as Gandhi, Marilyn Monroe, The Beatles, Ab Lincoln and many more. The LV bear - supposedly most expensive bear in the world - was not so impressive. Loved the art themed bears - from   The Thinker   to   Mona Lisa   to   Michaelangelo's Creation  .

10,000won per adult. Two floors of teddy bears gallery. I was quite fascinated by the really old teddy bears. The Louis Vitton Teddy bear was also on display, which apparently went for $190,000 during a fund raising charity event. Saw Elvis bear, Marilyn Monroe bear, Steve Job bear etc. There is a massive gift shop at ground level, selling a variety of teddy bears. But quite overpriced 10,000won for a key chain teddy, 35,000won for a palm size teddy. I don't even dare to look at how much the larger bear cost.

10,000 KRW per person. When you enter, pay for admission, and start in third floor, go down floors in order. In the basement, theres gift shop, cafe, and theres few more exhibits to see. Perfect for kids, fun for adults. Wish there could be more exhibitions of teddy bears. But if was nice!

Would have been much fun if you visit this place during warm weather. I havent done any of their tea classes but if you want to take the class make sure to reserve the spot. They have pretty famous tea/souvenir store. Expensive but it will be a great gift for loved ones. If you like green tea flavor try their ice creams! Or they offer ice cream roll cake and other drinks. The museum part was very short where I thought it was bit disappointing. But worth the visit.
Worth visiting and spending a few hours enjoying many artifacts made of glass! Full of suggestions to bring back home for gifts!

We've enjoyed looking at the exhibits tasting free samples of tea and bought delicious green tea ice cream (KRW4500). Then we walked over to Innisfree to make our own soap which was so much fun - KRW15000 for one kit that makes three soaps but two people can share the kit so it's a really fun experience! You get to gift-wrap them at the end so they'd make a lovely present. You can naturally buy soap much cheaper but the experience was great and you customise and prettify the soaps as much as you like.Both O'Sulloc and Innisfree can get quite busy - as we were leaving a massive coach party arrived. It's not super-easy to find a table in the O'Sulloc cafe so beware. I saw several couples cruising around desperate to find a table while their ice cream was melting rapidly.The only negative for us was the journey: from the intercity bus terminal in Jeju-Si it took over an hour: the traffic was awful both ways! According to our travel guide it should have been 40 minutes. If you're catching the bus from the bus terminal it's number 755 from platform 10 but beware as the bus leaves before the time stated on the board/your ticket and it's a 50 minute wait for the next one (we've learnt the hard way!)

Went there with my friend.. We took a bus from Halla hospital (?쒕씪蹂묒썝) bus stop and took bus no. 755 and alighted at the bus stop right in front of O'Sulloc Tea Museum. The entrance is free and there is a gift shop and a cafe.. You can buy different types of teas and other products made from tea in the shop (e.g. tea packs skin care products etc). You can buy green tea ice cream green tea roll cake and beverages etc from the cafe.. The cost of the products are reasonable while some are more expensive.Opposite the road there is a big Tea farm of the tea museum. You can take pictures there but must beware of snakes (諭�議곗떖) as warned with a sign board on the tea plant.Beside the museum there is Innisfree Jejuhouse (just walking distance). There is a sign board showing the direction and the Innisfree Jejuhouse is on the left hand side of the Tea Museum. If you like Tea this is a must visit place.

Well this place was big. Need to prepare to walk if you're going at non-peak hours. Why? due to the train not moving. This place features Korean village cultural show donkey / house riding costume trying & a beautiful setting to get some nice pictures. We enjoyed solid 1-2hours walking. But having to travel with small kids its quite tiring. Anyway the replicas of houses & setting was great. Enjoyed buying some quality souvenir at the gift shops. My kids just love the small maze park. I don't op for a tour guide but a head set was just enough for us to make us understand the place.One thing for sure they're snakes wandering around the place. While walking we come across 2 snakes (small). My kids was terrified! So need to be extra careful for those who bring little kids. Another set back was the small shop selling fast food. I know there's a barrier problem in language but they seem to ignore foreign tourist due to the fact we cant communicate well with each other. Very hard to buy stuff. Water! walking makes you thirsty. Pro's :- The head set helps to understand the place even-though not so many point haves explanation. Perhaps its an area for improvement.Con's :- Snakes? YikesOverall the place was ok. But will not come again..
Well organised tour of Korean traditional village easy to navigate takes about an hour. Stop at the gift shops in between for gifts

Well if an already successful huge company invest in something new it can't go too wrong. I expected this place to be more authentic but what we got was a commercialized sugar-coated tea plantation experience. Nonetheless the place is very professional of course the quality is great and both the tea and desserts are yummy. The surroundings are beautiful the air is fresh and the scent of the plantation is amazing. It's a safe choice if you prefer a guaranteed good time over something unexpected and little bit more unique. It's a sophisticated modern place that reminds me more of a spa than a tea house. Regardless you can buy good quality tea here and some other gifts that comes in beautiful packages. All in all we had a good time!

We visited in April 2018 and were impressed by the quality and the size of the village. There is a lot of history and culture to be learned here. The exhibits are well maintained they have live gardens and animals to represent the life in the village as well as hands on exhibits for kids and adults to participate in. There are craftspeople and artisans that are making wood work and stoneware that you can purchase. It is very beautiful. Also there is a restaurant on premise near the front gates and gift shop. The living museum and village is wheelchair accessible and worth the price of admission. It will take 2 to 3 hours to see everything. It can easily be a half day experience. Get there early to avoid the crowds. It's popular for students and tourists along with all the major places you should visit while on Jeju.

We stopped by this place mainly to try tea but ended up buying so many gifts for our friends and families. Tea cosmetics and other souvenirs are pretty good here. Don't forget to check out the tea farm on the opposite site.

We loved looking at the shells collected from all over the world. They were artistically arranged. It was well worth the $6.00 entrance fee and I received pearl stud earrings for free. The gift shop was expensive and bordered on tacky. The few shells for sale were very expensive  $68.00 for a small shell.
We found great gifts at this market!  We like unique gifts so we were excited to find our Christmas gifts here to bring home.  I also enjoyed the best waffle at one of the food stands.

We didn't have to pay for admission so I guess it's a relaxing place to stop over a drink as there is Nothing much to see. we bought some tea leaves and cookies as gifts. The green tea cookies is good!

Visited this Museum in Dec 2017 with my family. Entrance ticket costs 34 000kwon for 2 adults and 2 children. The place basically is run-down  glasses broken  dirty and colour faded over the years. I didn't bother to check on the cafe inside and left the museum in 15mins. Nothing special in the gift shop as well. Total waste of my money and my time travelled to visit the so called museum. If you intend to visit this Jeju Glass Museum  don't bother!

Very tasteful and informative. We were hesitant at first but figured we might as well take advantage of seeing what a sexually suppressed country could teach us :)The gift shop was a little lacking on museum related material and seemed to carry just local touristy items.

Totally unexpected.A unique place where Bonsai trees are beautifully and elegantly presented.A big thank for Mr Sung for warm welcome and gift about this outstanding garden. Inspirational lessons from Mr Sung on how he has been developing the garden in last few decades against all obstacles. The garden seems his beautiful masterpieces?

To know how the teddy bear appears then visit it. Also knowing all the types of teddy bear and appreciate it. Also a garden walk for photo shoot plus Elvis teddy bear life show every 15minutes to listen to elvis.The gift shop is really something to buy to have visit this teddy bear museum

To be honest we had already sampled the green tea cake ice cream and tea at the O'Sulloc shop and cafe in Insadong Seoul. However this tea garden featured in 'the Kimchi Chronicles' so we had to make a kind of pilgrimage to see it. The overall experience in the shop and cafe was a bit stressful because there are many tourists here at any given time of the day. It is a bit of a shame because this made it difficult to look at the teas properly and then to decide what to purchase. The prices are not cheap - even more so than  eg Fortnum and Masons but the tea is quite unique as it is grown here on the island. I guess it is worth the premium especially if you are buying the tea as a gift.Next door there is the cosmetics side to this enterprise - Innisfree. Once again the products are quite unique eg Jeju volcanic clay pore mask. I think if you are visiting Seoul or any other big city as part of your trip it would be better buying the tea and facial products there but if you are in Jeju also then it is worth popping in to see where it all happens as part of your trip.The teas cake and ice creams at the cafe are really very good but be prepared to pay a lot for it. Just tell yourself you don't do this everyday...

This venue offers quite a few exhibits for photo moment. Kids will surely like his place. The place can be done in an hour time unless you spend time explaining to the kids what each exhibit is about. The gift shop offer a good range of teddy bear to buy as a gift.

This place is breathtakingly beautiful with especially kind staff. Every piece of art is a masterpiece. Nice (but expensive) giftshop and cute coffeeplace. Don't miss it if you are close by. I visited this place on the last day of a worktrip and it left a wonderful feeling about Jeju.

This museum isn't very large and in the winter you don't really want to go outside to admire the small amount of outdoor exhibits (which you can do from inside the windows anyway) but it's got enough interesting art to be worth 1000 KRW which is about USD $0.80. For one I enjoyed the Chang Ri Seok exhibit as his paintings are very earthy. The second floor exhibit was under renovation when I went but still for 1000 won I have no complaints about the first floor's contents. The gift shop is pretty underwhelming though.

This museum is not the easiest to find  located in an industrial type area. Upon entrance you receive a free sample of chocolate and a hot chocolate (not sure if this was offered due to the chilly  rainy weather  but it was definitely appreciated). Some interesting finds from around the world  historical facts  and treasures. There is an area where you may observe chocolate pieces being made for sale in the adjacent gift shop. Good stop for a rainy day on Jeju Island. Gift shop is a little pricey. Teenaged daughter loved it; teenaged son was bored.
address: 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 대정읍 일주서로3000번길 144 대정농공단지 내
입력주소: 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 대정읍 일주서로3000번길 144 대정농공단지 내

review: This museum displays many clay artwork and handicrafted items from ages. The tour guide and the ticket booth employee cannot speak English anyway. However the souvenir shop in the museum sells many wonderful things that we could buy home as gifts.

This little folk village was located right next to our hotel (Haevachi) so we figured we should check it out.  We were spoiled because we had just gone to the folk village and that is the bomb!It is only about $8 for admission and then we opted for the audio tours.  Most of the written signs are not in English so I'm glad we had the audio tours but they didn't work very well.  They are tripped by some sort of sensor when you go by but mine kept skipping back to the original message ugggg.It's a very large complex but somehow unauthentic feeling.  I thought the neatest part was the artisans that sell their crafts.  That was cool and they do have a nice gift shop.  It was very hot out so we went through fairly quickly.  If it hadn't been so hot we might have spent much longer just exploring.If this is your only opportunity to see such a thing then I would visit but if you have the chance to see the folk village in Seoul then I would wait for that one!

this is not a museum. This is a place surrounded by green tea plantations. It is also a place for you to get your tea fix. They have a plenty of teas to choose from and some are packaged so Nicely as gifts. I personally go back there for my green tea facial masks and powders. Its my third time there already. But be prepared the place is on most tourist groups itinerary so it can get a tad crowded. But for me its usually pick buy and lets go. So im totally fine w it. Stop by if youre a tea fan to pick up items to bring back.
This is a big temple with lots to see.  There are a couple of large budda statues and many small ones.  It also has a nice gift shop.It is far from downtown and a bit hard to get without a car.

There is nearly no advertisement for this museum in the city. I saw the sign at the traffic and wanted to give it a try. The building is so small that when i arrived I thought it will be a quick tiny event. But once you are inside you will be amazed by the beauty and the variety of seashells. Most of the explanations are in Korean but still nothing can stop you to enjoy this museum. At the roof  there is a giant shell  which you can go in and have a photo. There is also a small shop where you can buy gifts to your loved ones and something for yourself too.

There has a long line up food area even they only have simple menu. The food is good. Must try their mandarin drink. Lot of different kind of tea you can pick. I bought it for gift and its little bit pricey.
The view of the green tea field is really wonderful. And there are good things to give your parents and friends as gifts.
The scale and the scope of the museum itself is small but this is made up for by the caf챕 inside. The Innisfree JejuHouse is a better deal when it comes to diverse caf챕 faire and gift options.

The museum part of the building was only about 2 small rooms with a bit of history of tea-making.  Most of the rest was taken up by the gift shop and cafe.The green tea (Swiss) roll which is their iconic cake was sold out completely on the day we were there even though it was only about 11am.  Made do with green tea and tangerine soft serve ice-cream and tea.  The tangerine tea was beautifully presented in a stoneware cup and tasted better than the green tea.There are very limited food choices for a full meal and this is more a snack cafe.  The food at nearby Innisfree is much better with a wider range.  Eventually we had the green tea cake back in Seoul where it was easily available at the O Sulloc outlets in Myeongdong.

The green tea museum was nice.  They had tea sets from around the world from many different ages.  The gift shop had free green tea sampling which was quite delicious.  They also had a cafe where you can buy green tea roll cakes ice cream and lattes.

The glass museum is well presented and extremely pleasant environment!While the building seems modern and edgy the products are sweet rather than overly modern! If the gift shop is not making a huge profit it is because the gifts seem dated!

The architecture of this conference centre is the first exciting and majestic comment on the centre. It has big conference rooms with the best facilities to host big events. I attended the international mercury conference here and the logistics of the venue provided us with a flawless event. There are also several fast food restaurants at the bottom level of the centre  with a duty free shop on the other side. It is a local attraction and the visitors seem to enjoy it too  since it was constantly busy. On the second floor is a curio shop for some gifts from Jeju.The airport limousine bus no 600 stops outside entrance of the venue  but there are local taxis frequently available to take you anywhere.

The Alive Museum in Seogwipo is a pretty nice museum that is near a number of good restaurants and is definitely not hard to get to on foot. For 11000 won you can take photos with plenty of crazy cute and cool paintings all over the museum; this is definitely their specialty. I really enjoyed some of the paintings especially the ones near the picture of the wings that makes you look like an angel. The gift shop at the end and of course the mandatory photos taken of you upon coming in are really overpriced and we didn't go outside because it was so cold out but the inside was pretty worth it to get so many cool photo opportunities. If you're not into taking pictures though this museum probably isn't for you.

Teddy bear museum was such a curious place ever. Many kinds of teddy bear are displayed on there and also great to take photos. Think takes 1~2 hours to look around here. I really liked it and also teddy bear souvenirs are pretty good to prepare as gifts but a little expensive to buy a lot. Anyway i would like to recommend to visit here. This museum is worth a visit:)
Sls very nice tea. A must to try the matcha/ green tea icecream. Buy the season teas as gifts or for ur self! The green tea latte too!

Second time at O Sulloc and the grounds are beautiful and offers nice picture opportunities and a relaxing vibe. Spent a good amount of time at Innisfree House where you can buy packages of soap and customise them for friends. Good activity to engage the kids and also make gifts for friends :) Green tea ice cream was good and the tea leaves smelled really good as well.

Rows of organic tea plantations for cha lovers to scent savour and calm the senses.  A must-go on tourist itinerary so be prepared for crowds.  Long queues at the cafe for tea desserts.  Check out exquisite Samdayeon (?쇰떎??is a Korean post-fermented tea matured for a hundred days in barrels made out of cedar wood from Jeju Island) soft ice cream unique to Jeju shop only. Interesting tea blends and gifts at the tea shop. Don't miss the outdoor fields across from the museum for kettle and cup shaped plant sculptures and windmills for photo taking. A walking path connects to Innisfree Jeju House for more afternoon tea Innisfree products and craft making classes for young and old.
Pales in comparison to Osulloc Tea Museum but it's worth a look since they are side by side. The products in the gift shop are the widely available Innisfree facial products.

Our 4yo liked it well enough. We spent about 2hrs and spent more money at the gift shop than on admission (24000 won) and if it were nicer out we probably would have spent longer. Botanical garden a small garden maze Fossil museum animal feeding station bird attraction and the really TALL dinosaurs scattered throughout made for an enjoyable afternoon outing before nap time.

On our way back from Gahina Tea Pottery we were close-by the Tea Museum.  Many buses leave from there for Jeju and Seogwipo making this a convenient place to have a hot beverage.  Yes there is no entrance fee and that seems to be because it is mostly a gift shop and tea room.  That said the tea is lovely making for great gifts and the green tea ice cream quite tasty.  Clean bathrooms and a lovely building make this a nice place to pass through for a quick stop.

Not so much a museum as much as a gift shop on a tea field. I live right next door and it's always super busy (not sure why). The land is really beautiful with rolling tea fields but it is not a museum just an insanely overpriced gift shop. But if you're in the area it's definitely worth a visit.

My 5yr old loved it very much. Lots of dinosaurs on display outdoor. Several exhibitions on site such as fossils and seashells. Areas where you can interact with animals (feeding ponies and gerbils.) You also get to see parrots next to the gift shop. It's not a very big place. we spent about 2 hours there. We got a taxi there and the man at the ticket hut(speaks good English) was very kind to help us get a taxi back to hotel. A very enjoyable and pleasant place to visit if you like dinosaurs and animals.

Must visit for anyone who visits Jeju even though its more of an extended cafe/shop more than a museum. There is a small section dedicated to the history of tea and brewing/drinking techniques and apparatus but wouldn't call it a museum as such.There is also a nice area round the back to take photos and take in the scenery as well as an Innisfree attached to it.The cafe is the main attraction as it serves tea/cakes and ice cream to visitors and it is definitely up there with the best green tea ice cream I've had. After visiting a branch in Seoul we had to go to the origin of the tea. We tried the green tea tiramisu cake in Myeongdong which was excellent best green tea tiramisu cake I've had but opted for the green tea torte cake here as well as the ice cream. My opinion is the tiramisu was better but still very nice along with the ice cream.The gift shop was also good and we had members of staff brewing tea to allow you to sample the taste before buying. In hindsight we left without buying any tea but regretted as we left Jeju. If you're in limbo about whether to buy the tea or not my advice will be to just buy it regardless if the price is expensive since you'll probably regret it like we were. Only consolation is that the duty free inside Jeju international airport does stock some O'Sulloc products but not as much as here.Worth the visit but a bit out in the sticks. 8/10

Museum is fairly small but packed with tourists. Gift shop offer wide variety of gift ideas. Cafe was too packed for us to stay around for sampling snacks and drinks.Innisfree museum and green tea plantation are nearby

Made a quick stop here and found it mostly overrated and not that special. There were an abundance of tourists around. One thing I did enjoy is the green tea ice-cream. Also taste tested the Jeju mandarin flavoured tea which you can buy from the gift/tea shop. Overall a good place to stop at for a quick break if you are on the way to other attractions around the island.
Loved the desserts there but they can get pretty expensive (17~36k??for the dessert sets)I liked the tea I bought from the shop and they make great gifts~
Lots to see and eat. The black pork is absolutely delicious. Must try. Can get local food gifts and souvenirs here.

Jeju Folk Village Museum as it appears on map for Jeju is on the coast and is a must do for history and culture buffs. There are hands on exhibits that kids and adults can participate and use around the village. The park and museum is large and takes 2 to 3 hours at least. Perhaps longer to see everything without rush. We were quite impressed by the size the crafts people making products and the exhibits throughout. There are ample restrooms snack shops and Korean traditional products sold in the gift shop. There is also a restaurant on premise.The Jeju Folk Village attracts students from all over Korea as well as tourists from other countries. I highly recommend the park. There are beautiful floral blooms as well as animals photo opportunities and lots of traditional Korean history and culture to learn about. Well worth the price of admission. Plan to spend half a day here. Arrive early to avoid the crowds. There are some great gifts and candies to be found around the village including the traditional Korean taffy near the Hanbok photo place and the gift shop.

It's one of the best small museums on Jeju island. I went there twice and each time spent couple of hours in sheer amazement and delight. Almost each sea shell installation strikes with its beauty. The bronze things are also interesting and sometimes funny. Check the bathroom  by the way :)There is much stuff in the gift shop but quite expensive. Small cafe is cozy arranged with bronze installations and green plants. Try tea and bagels  they are tasty.
It's nice to walk around and see the different bears and the history of the bears. Admission is a good price but the gift shop is a bit pricey.

It's a wonderful botanical garden with many flowers and trees in natural jeju island atmosphere in Korea.Camellia flowers blooming in February are abundant throughout Camellia Hill garden. Its owner Mr. Yang has spent enormous amount time and financial resources to create build and improve the garden as one of the best attractions in Jeju Island.  There are many stone sculptures well maintained hiking trails green houses resting areas and a tea and gift shop the visitors can enjoy and take beautiful pictures.  It's located very near to Jeju Shinwha World Resort with many great hotels and restaurants.  It's a real gem place you should not miss along with Hanrim Botanical Park in Gumnung Beach area in Jeju Island.

It's 3000won for adults and 2000won for kids. They give you a gift voucher equivalent to the entrance fee which you can use to offset purchases or the DIY chocolate making session (12 000won). You get a box of 10 chocolates at the end of the 15 min session. You have to wait another 15 min for chocolates to solidify. Other than the DIY session  there's really nothing worth looking at here.

review: It looks like it has been abandoned for years  it has very nice artwork but it is also very dirty. The bathroom was disgusting. The gift shop smelled like cigarettes and had puddles of water every where. And the staff looked extremely bored and uninterested. I came at night so maybe the daytime is better. How ever I don't recommend it  definitely not worth the $8 per person day or night. (Got some nice pictures though)

It is really great how many things you can see on Jeju for less than $3 a person. We did not climb to the top but went into the park to the left to see the cliffs and get a closer look. You only have to walk a little to see a lot. Ample parking and coffee shops nearby. It was so beautiful despite the crowd. It was rainy and windy. Raincoats are sold in the gift shop.

It is not tourist attraction but great place for a conference  inside you have seven eleven and gift shop - I would advice this gift shop with nice sweets  tangerines and black garlic. Tangerines are the best from this Island!

It is hard to say anything good about this place. Basically  it is a small chocolate gift shop that charges $3 a person to enter. You receive a coupon good for $3 back on any purchase. I suppose it is their way to ensure that you buy something.The only interesting thing was that they had these cookie balls that you smashed with a hammer to eat.

It had rained heavily the night before our arrival which meant that it was very slippery inside the lava tunnel and water was dripping constantly which also formed puddles throughout the path.It is also very dark.  There are some lights but not enough to clearly see the terrain below you.  We got to the 300km marker and decided to turn back because we were trying to avoid twisting our ankles.  The lava flow creates interesting striations and grooves which does not result in an easy stroll through the tunnel.The walk may be less treacherous if the tunnel was dry but this is one attraction that should not be attempted by people with mobility issues.The one good thing is that there is a nice gift shop on the grounds which also serves snacks.  Clean bathrooms.

Interesting place. Lots of Tangerine in boxes as gifts and many stalls sell snacks and souveniors.Is also a wet market where you see fresh produce. Not forgetting display of pig heads can be found in serveral stalls. Can visit for the experience.
Interesting museum. Worth going. Summer time can be quite hot if viewing the outdoor displays. Gift shop is right under the greenhouse effect.
Innisfree cafe has lovely food. There is craft work in the cafe where you can make your own soap as a gift too. The plantation was amazing.

Indeed a disappointing experience. Yes  this is just an excuse to get you to the gift shop  but at least they could have made the trip there interesting. The story of chocolate is among the most fascinating in the histories of commodities  but they made it a torture. You will see some exhibits on the history of chocolate  a few displays of old boxes and cases of chocolates  and some needless toy sculptures  but mostly a forgettable experience. You do have to pay a small amount and get a coupon for your chocolate or drink purchase. So  if you are desperate to eat some chocolate  or it's raining heavily outside  or you need quickly some air-conditioning  then give it a try; otherwise  enjoy Jeju's natural scenery and wonders instead.
If you're in the area  check it out. It costs 4 000 Won to get in but they give you a coupon worth 3 000 Won to use in the gift shop.
