review: If your a fan of everything green tea like my daughter is this is a great place to visit extensive gift shop and resteraunt selling everything you can imagine from the company great background n pics of the history of the place and outside see tea fields and sculptures.

If you want to see a bunch of boxes of chocolate from all over the world  this is the place for you. The 3000 won you pay to enter gives you a discount to what you can buy there so if you want to buy chocolate you won't feel ripped off  but you can buy the same chocolate in any gift shop for the same price. There are a lot of great places on Jeju. I wouldn't go out of your way to visit here.

If you have the time it is a nice break but we were with a tour and time was limited. The gift area is near the museum which is very attractive but jam packed. Lots of product to buy that is pricey with little product education. The fields are just like the pictures but kind of underwhelming when you get there.

I was a little worried after reading some reviews but after going i am pleasantly surprised.  The entrance fee is a little high at 11000 won for an adult and if i had kids i might be worried they would get bored.  Seems perfect for couples and people who like taking pictures.  If you take your time and dont rush you can do the whole place in am hour.  Lots to look at.  Worth a stop.  Bonus...if your name is yoori you get free entrance and a free gift

I visited this place at night and really enjoyed it. You should definitely have your camera with you and ready to get lots and lots of dirty photos with the sculptures made for you to fit in. It also has a small sex shop and an exhibition. Within the park you will also find a casual gift shop.Fantastic place and definitely a must for couples!

I visited this as part of an inclusive tour.  This is really interesting.  there is the story of tea and you can walk among the tea bushes.  This is the best Korea tea there is and of course you can buy their products and sample green tea foods in the cafe. Their sister beauty products company Innesfree also has a cafe and gift shop.  Again these products have a hig reputation in S. Korea.  I would have liked more time to spend here.  The main cafe was packed and I would have like to have had green tea and green tea cake or green tea ice cream but I wouldn't have been able to see anything else in the time we had.  A pleasant place to visit for a few hours.
I like Dongmun market most. You could get gifts for your family and friends. They sell nice and big orange. There's a lot to sell and a lot to eat.
i have been a hello kitty collector for over 25 years. this place is  like a walk down memory lane. it is 3 floors and filled with kitty trivia and memorabilia. there is also a gift store and cafe.

I cant say this was a museum because majority of the building is dedicated to the gift shop and cafe.  They do have a small plantation across the street as well as an innisfree store next to it.  Apparently their green tea ice cream is a must try.  I thought transportation wise it was a little difficult to get to.

Exotic Jeju Island is known for many things: the majestic Hallasan--the massive shield volcano that formed the island and the highest point in South Korea; its mandarin groves; persimmon-dyed galot fashions; the sturdy Jeju ma horses  descended from the ponies of Mongol invaders; tasty black pork; and the iconic haenyeo women divers. But most visitors would not expect to find a Museum of African Art there. And  it's pretty darn good! Located in a massive structure modeled after the mud-brick Great Mosque of Djenne  the museum offers photo-ops galore in its Safari section  although the animals are of the stuffed variety. Very popular with children and couples. The upper floors house a respectable collection of African artifacts and photographs by Kim Jung Man. There is also a great gift shop. But  I have saved the best for last...the live performance of African folk music and dance. The group  Zalia from Senegal  featured lots of drumming  and audience members also got a drumming lesson and a chance to play along on one song. All in all  a quality experience...and a surprising one.

Enjoyed a couple of hours browsing thru the sea kingdom. Many varieties of fishes and huge aquarium of big fishes and string rays. Shop for souvenirs at the gift shop and some food and drinks at the caf챕. There are beautiful coast behind Aqua Planet which you might want to take stroll for some beautiful photos.

review: During our visit to Jeju Island I fell in love with the Hareubang statues.  They are all over the Island a unique distinguishing statue you will see everywhere you look.  I had many pictures taken while standing next to one of these great statutes!  The Dolharbang Park was full of ancient statues many dating back to the 20th century.Dol means stone and Hareubang means grandfather So Dolharbang means stone grandfather.  In gift shops you can even buy small Hareubang statues keychains chocolates perfume bottles...to take home for a happy memory

Came here just to try the tea but not visit the museum. The cafe offers a good variety of nice tea. I enjoy the cakes and ice cream too. There are gifts that you can buy for friends here. Things such as green tea chocolate biscuits and facial products. It?셲 quite a walk from the carpark for my tourist bus to the museum itself.

Calling this place a museum is absolute fraud. The entrance fee is 3000 won which is returned to you in the form of a coupon for the cafe or gift shop - both of which are insanely overpriced. The 'displays' are ridiculous - chocolate gold coins  chocolate Easter eggs  Guylian seashell-shaped chocolates  posters of the film 'Chocolat ' a statue of Willy Wonka. It's almost as if the museum is teasing the West for its chocolate traditions - if it can even be called that. There is really nothing of interest in this museum. There is  however  a pretty nice view of the ocean to the rear of the museum.

Awesome Museum! Has everything for singles and couples who want to visit! It was only 20 minutes from the hotel and the taxi service was great! Spend about 2 hours with the gift shops mini museums inside and looking at the statues. It was raining however the staff was prepared for the rain and had rain coats available for 2000 won! I would definitely recommend!

As the Chocolate Land is within 10 minutes??walk from the Teddy Bear Museum in the Jungmun Resort area ??just follow the direction on the sign-posts ??my family and I had no hesitation to visit it on a rainy Sunday.Getting there and fees: First and foremost  you have to note that Chocolate Land is different from Chocolate Museum. Chocolate Land is in the south central part of Jeju while Chocolate Museum is in the south west Jeju. We didn't need the GPS coordinate/code for Chocolate Land but it's 7381197 for anyone who's driving there directly. The entrance fee for adults is 3000 won and 2000 won for children. A voucher was given back for every purchased ticket which can be redeemed at the gift shop or the caf챕 or the Chocolate School.The Museum/Attraction: After going past the ticketing counter  you then turn right. The section on the left is a caf챕 and photograph/selfie stops of different types of Korean houses and benches with toy bears. There's even a figurine of Santa Claus in front of one house  which was interesting considering Christmas is still some 6 months away. The section on the right is the exhibits on the history of chocolates  with the words written only in Korean. We went down the stairways to the level below in which there's a Chocolate School which teaches chocolate making at 120 000 won with lessons starting every hour from 10am to 6pm (I think the children would be more interested than adults). We didn't go into the School; instead  we walked past M&M figurines and a Christmas tree (again interesting) and reached the chocolate shop where there are interesting exhibits of chocolates (behind glass) from America  Europe and Asia. The gift shop has an extensive selection of chocolates (I think slightly more than outside). The prices of the Jeju chocolates of the same brand at the gift shop were slightly more expensive compared to those selling outside Chocolate Land. However  the Chocolate Land chocolates became slightly cheaper than those outside when we utilised the discount vouchers. Unique local Jeju chocolates are those with pink cactus flowers  mandarin oranges and hallabong fillings. We couldn't wait till Christmas?쫤e ate some of the chocolates before we left Jeju  and these were yummy!There is a small observation area (Chocolate Garden) outside the building where the view looks towards the sea. There's also a statue of Willy Wonka from the 1971 movie ?쁗illy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory??where you could take a photograph and selfie with. But we couldn't go outside because it's raining.I recommend visiting the Chocolate Land if you have the time and if you have an appreciation of chocolates. Otherwise  I think you wouldn't miss much if you decide to skip it.

As part of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour we were given some time to go around O'sulloc Green Tea's fields museum and cafe; as well as shop around in Innisfree's Jeju House.Queues tend to be long for both the O'sulloc Green Tea and Innisfree so it's best to prioritize one over the other if you're working with a limited amount of time. O'sulloc Green Tea displays its wide array of teas packaged in gorgeous boxes and tin cans. These are perfect as gifts for loved ones.They also house a cafe in the store where you eat and drink tea-infused items. Fortunately we were able to visit its branch in Seoul already (and bought our fare share of their tea boxes) so we focused our time in Innisfree instead.Innisfree has numerous branches in Seoul; however it's best to look out for the Jeju-exclusive items available in the Jeju house. Similar to O'sulloc Innisfree also has its own cafe which serves its own selection of drinks and food; for those not interested in its beauty products.

Actually the taste of the tea is pretty good I like both hot and cold. Also recommend green tea roll (both flavor are good). Soft cream is great too.A little tip for people who looking for a gift this is the good place to grab something that look nice and actually nice. (And affordable)Another tip for you guys is if you go with your significant other or your friends just separate and look for the table first. The line up queue is very fast but it's a little bit hard to find the table.

A wonderful recreation of traditional living in South Korea with working areas small demonstrations food and gift shop areas. Very informative displays and examples of traditional life. Very worth the time small entry fee and effort. Great day out.
A crazy number of teddy bears in various sizes and various outfits. Great if you like teddy bears. Features a teddy bear themed gift shop at the lowest level.

Whilst I'm giving the Teddy Bear Museum just 2 stars for quality, value for money, class of exhibits, and any actual worth as a proper   museum  , I have to admit that my visit made me laugh. I'm not sure though that derisive snorting sarcasm was what they were looking for.This museum is a pile of pants, masquerading as teddy bears.. The   attractions   are about 15 to 20 poor quality adult-human-sized bears, dressed in various outfits of clothing, with a challenge to guess   who   they are dressed as. Military uniform and two medals apparently is enough for a bear to resemble Prince William, for example - and a grey wig and   E=mc2   to represent Einstein.Then there are the bear portraits. Frames containing bears dressed to vaguely resemble famous portraits. Mona Lisa teddy bear, anyone?There's no   history   of the teddy bear, no collection of historical bears, no pictures / video clips of teddy bears being made, no maps showing where different types of teddy bears originated from - nothing educational whatsoever. There are no audio tours, no leaflets or signs to show the visitor around, and certainly no staff available to talk to about any   exhibits  , whether you are Korean, English, American or anything else.The gift shop on the lowest floor contained the largest number of bears - none of them particularly special, all just your usual cheap mass-produced bears, but at slightly hiked up prices.By far the worst part of the visit was the funniest. Your ticket includes entry to the   Elvis Stage Show  . Oh dear Lord, where on earth do I start? The show is on every 15 minutes. In a room with about 12 benches in it. There is a curtain at the far end, hiding the   stage  . On the quarter hour, the announcement is made -   The King of Rock and Roll, Elvis, is in the house!   The curtains open, and there it is. The Elvis Presley Show. Six, sad, lonely looking teddy bears, dressed in stage show outfits, rocking gently on their animatronic sticks. The three backing singers sway gently on the right, the drummer's arms flail up and down towards the drums, the guitarist's arm moves.Elvis meanwhile gyrate and swivels his hips, the crowd goes wild. Oh, no, sorry, that last sentence was a lie. Elvis sways and looks like he almost falls several times.Worst animatronic puppetry in the world. Hilarious. Hilariously BAD. Less than two minutes later, the curtains shut, and   Elvis has left the building   - until the next showing in approximately 12 or 13 minutes' time....Don't go to the Teddy Bear Museum thinking you'll have an interesting visit. Go to see the absolutely bizarre vision that South Koreans have of   entertainment  .

When visiting other countries I realize the treatment of animal standards may differ, but I at least look for animals to be happy. This falconry “center”was bittersweet. Some of the animals had wonderful enclosures, but the birds of prey were treated very inhumanly. The same birds of prey/owls were tied to stands for the whole 3 hours we were there, with no food or water, in the blaring sun, with no supervision as people crowded and tried to touch them to the point they would flinch or try to fly away, only to be yanked by their chains. Their inhumane treatment brought tears to our eyes. At the far part of the center, we came upon their enclosures, cages about 5 x 5 x5 feet wide, where other birds of prey were chained, with little place to move and absolutely no enrichment toys.? This is unacceptable. There was a raccoon in a small enclosure with no enrichment toys, solely used for tourists to take selfies with. Last but not least, a pair of Coaty were also in a small enclosure. Their baby was on display in a small cage by the gift shop with no water. This “Center” does have some acceptable enclosures for fowl, rabbits, budgies, and the alpaca interaction was amazing, but surely they can treat all their animals with dignity. While we were there, a macaw flew away into the surrounding trees. Clearly the parrot did not have an attached handler nor proper training for flighted birds.

Went there with my friend, we took bus from Jungmun (at the bus stop nearby tourist information center, at the right hand side). We took bus no. 781 and alighted at Teddy valley golf and resort, from there turn left (after you alighted) and walk straight for 1 min, you will see the museum at your left hand side. The entrance ticket cost 12000 won per adult. There are gift shop, Kitty History Hall, Music Education Hall, Art Gallery, Hello Kitty Caf챕, 3D Theater and more.. The Hello Kitty Cafe is very big and is beautifully designed and decorated.. There are a lot of cute hello kitty inside the museum and there are also some outside the museum. If you are a hello kitty fan, this is a must visit place when you come to Jeju.The museum closes at 6pm, so you might want to go there earlier.

Well worth the trip! The museum is very well presented and organized. So cute! So pink! Lots of kids and laughter about. You can opt to pay for extras, like buttons, passport stamp collecting and heart shaped tag to write on and lock onto the balcony. Some furniture is a bit run down but overall it is really well cared for. The staff is very friendly and helpful. You can also get small food and drink from the cafe and there is a jungle gym are for children to play. They have a short movie and photo station on the roof at the end. The gift shop had lots to choose from and prices were pretty good compared to official merchandise sold elsewhere online. Spent almost the whole day there and I loved every second of it. The museum is incredibly interactive, it would be hard not to have fun. Brought my boyfriend and even he couldn't believe how fun it was :)

Welcome to the first Teddy Bear Museum in Korea. Here you will find everything you want to know about Teddy Bears. Teddy Bears have been loved and cherished since they were first introduced over 100 years ago. There are now millions of people who collect Teddy Bears. They seek out old, unique and valuable teddy bears for their personal collections. Our Teddy Bear Museum opened especially for the European collectors. The Teddy Bear Museum is more exciting than ever with   Teddy Bear   entertainment as never seen before. Jeju Teddy Bear Museum opened on April 24, 2001. It contains two galleries, a museum gift shop, and a museum cafe. Also, on site is a museum bar/restaurant, a wonderful place to meet friends, family, and lovers. From the outside garden, there is a view of Jung-Mun Beach.

We were received by a Chinese -speaking   Villager   upon entering the village. It is well set up, which gives a glimpse of the old life style of the local Jeju islanders. However, after a brief talk about the life of the local people, the guide was more interested to get us all seated inside a hut to sell her products, such as honey, Omija tea, and lo and behold...horse bone pellets (remedy for loss of calcium)! Her sales pitch was pushy and rather unfriendly, and we were not that interested by her goods (the price was exorbitant), we could sense her attitude turned from lukewarm to really cold. There is no doubt some local people really live here, as to keep the tradition alive, also supported by the government to do so. I think is better to keep the selling of local goods to another area (like setting up a gift shop), rather than incorporating it as some kind of compulsory lecture within the guide tour. I find that most off-putting. I give this place an average rating. The surrounding restaurants which serve the famous pork dishes from black pig were good.

We went to the Teddy Bear Museum only because it was right next door to the Lotte Hotel Jeju where we stayed.  At 10,000 won per adult and 8,000 won per child, it is a bit pricey.  You can be done with all the displays and the 5 minute teddy Elvis show in an hour.  If you like teddy bears then it is a museum for you as there are alot of cute displays and exhibits that memorialize past events in history.  Kinda cool but not my thing.  I enjoyed the outdoor park area more.  You can take pictures with cute bear statues and sit and enjoy the greenery.  There is a cafe that sells Taiwanese pearl drinks and a nice gift shop.

We went to the Glass Castle in spite of the 9000 Won entry fee simply because of all the hassle we had gone through to get there. Inside, it was really nothing more than a glass art museum, and a relatively small one at that. Admittedly, there were some very creative works of art, but there was a lot that wasn't that impressive as well. Over half of it is outside so, if you are there on a rainy day like we were, that will kill the experience even more. If you have young children forget it, there is almost nothing for them to do without spending additional money for them to make a glass craft. The crafts are neat but spendy. At the end of the museum, there is a gift store that, in my opinion, was really the only good reason to come here. Lots of cool trinkets to get for gifts and souvenirs - of special note are the hand painted, hollow, personalizeable, crystal balls. If you are up to the trip and willing to pay the cash to look at glass art go for it. Otherwise, there are other more interesting things around to do.

We went there by taxi from O'Sulloc Tea Museum. It's interesting when the displays are made of glass but nothing impressive. The entrance fee costs 9000 won but my friend and I got a discount thanks to the taxi driver uncle, and we end up paying 7000 won each.. The displays are mostly outside. On the 2nd floor, there is a gift shop..you can buy some gifts there and the cost is acceptable for some (e.g. accessories, keychain, etc) certain products (e.g. glass displays) are more expensive. It was raining when we visited the museum, but we just went around the museum and took some pictures. It is good to visit once but not more than that.

We visited here during our cruise day trip of the island. This is a very scenic place with gorgeous architecture and the   spring of life  . WARNING: Do not drink from that spring unless you want to risk some messy   internal issues  . The walk involves some climbing but not too bad with no steps just a gradual walk up an inclined path. They offer a gift shop and snack bar as you enter and exit.

We visited as part of a group/tour and arrived late in the day (about 5pm). Huge carpark just outside.Not at all busy. Our guide walked us around the village and gave informative information (in English) about the history of the island and the life styles of the people that would have/do live here.The few residents that we saw didn?t want photos taken, I thought a little strange since they live in a ?theme park? and must see tourists every day of the year.We were allowed to poke our heads into specified rooms/houses.There was a shop for gifts etc and a WC block for the use of behind the guest villa at the backWe spent about 40 mins here

We thought that since we are here in Jeju that we should visit Hello Kitty Island to buy our niece some gifts.  It turned out to be a big mistake.  First, there was this steep entry fee that you have to pay just to get into the building.  Then there was this lack of history on Hello Kitty.  Not educational for kids at all.  Finally, the stuff they sell at the gift shop were so expensive it put Japan to shame.  Not much of the products even have the trademark for specific sites.  Hello Kitty fans beware!!  You are better off going to Seoul to get gifts than here.

we stayed 3 nights in a hotel right near Black pork street, and it is rather close to Dongmun market, so we came here every afternoon when we finished our trip to famous attractions around the island. Lot of local eateries you can try, lot of candy/chocolate and mandarin shops those are specialties of Jeju that you can bring back home as gifts. From the Jeju bus terminal you can access here by bus #100 (takes around 10-15mins). bus stop is Dongmun rotary, right beside the entrance gate of the market.

We planned this for the kids but the adults had fun too. When we arrived, we bought the tickets while the kids were busy with the numerous cats around the area. It turns out that this is also a place for cat lovers, this place is a mini cat world too. You can get cat food from the ticket counter to feed the cats.In the maze, the kids formed a team and raced with us, the parents. Each team had to find the stamps hidden around the maze and stamp on the paper given. First team to collect all 6 stamps and ring the bell to exit the maze wins.Upon exiting the maze, as we passed thru the ticket counter again, the lady manning the counter asked us to visit the gift shop to claim a free postcard.

We drove ourselves and although a little hard to find, it was worth the effort. The area was quite well set out with information and small local restaurant and gift shop area. Entry is free to Jeju workers but about 5,000 won - the steps down are step but well made. We walked about 2 kms to the end of the tunnel - it was damp, cold and generally well lit. Wear sturdy shoes and a warm coat, take a water bottle.  Worth a look.

We didn't know what we could do with that one hour before sunset, so we decided to relive our childhood by going to this maze park. We completed the maze in slightly less than an hour. But boyfriend wanted to have some more fun by collecting all the ink stamps at various points in the maze, so he attempted the maze again and he got himself lost in the park while I waited for him at the elevated finishing point. It was fun. For children, if they managed to collect all the stamps, they will give a small gift from the park. We got a KimYoung Maze Park pen although we are not children :x The lady was nice. haha :)

We decided to visit one of JeJu?s famous attractions Hallim park. We took bus 100 from the Jeju intercity bus station and had a relaxing journey to the west side of the island passing through countryside and the coast line. The bus stops at the Hallim park bus stop and you still have a little walk along the road and through the car park until you come to the entrance.(entrance fee 10,000 won) we were lucky because the weather was good for June , sunny but not too hot as you do spend alot of time walking around. On entering you will see a large map of the park with all its attractions numbered, there is also a very good gift shop which has a large range of items from T.shirts to natural products made into soaps and teas. Then you start the walk of around 10 different attractions including water garden, bird garden, subtropical garden and ofcourse the attraction most people come to see the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves.Jeju is famous for its volcanic larva tubes and caves and if you haven?t visited any then this is a good time as its alot more convenient than doing another trip to the other caves. The park is actually quite big and you do need to spend a good 2 hours to see it all, so if your going to visit the nearby beaches allow yourself enough time.There are also some restaurants and washroom facilities.

We decided to include this in our tour after feeling a bit tired from all the hiking up mountains and paths. It's an easy couple of hours, especially if you have kids, whom seemed to be entertained with every variation of dressed up bear. There is also an extensive gift shop, with, you've guessed it, lots of bears and cuddlies. The prices aren't exactly cheap, but the quality seemed good. It's a good way to slow the pace down if you are in need of a rest.. Nice afternoon out.
Walk into a 3 storeys building. Gift shop, 3D theater, Hello Kitty Cafe and all sorts of Hello Kitty. Good fun place to explore, feeling happy and young again.

Very friendly and helpful to all of us, he is also very kind in recommending us the must-go attractions and even getting us discounted entrance fee around Jeju. He even brought us to the delicious restaurants, introduce us to all the different food around Jeju, gifted us some rice cakes. Would gladly recommend to my friends or anyone going to Jeju ?몟?뤍狩먲툘 狩먲툘 狩먲툘 狩먲툘 狩먲툘

Unlike Hello Kitty, I think most of us have cuddled or have in possession a toy teddy bear at a certain stage of our lives. So it is no wonder that the Teddy Bear Museum has such a wide appeal and which surely be included as a ?compulsory? destination on the itinerary of the independent travellers (especially those with children) and tour companies alike.Getting there and fees: We visited Teddy Bear Museum (GPS coordinate/code 7387600) on a rainy day, which was appropriate since the exhibits are predominantly indoor, except for the Teddy Bear Garden and Park where there?re a few teddy bear figurines outside and a park with great views of the sea.  The admission charges are 10,000 won for adults won, 9,000 won for teens and 8,000 won for children.The Museum/Attraction:  This Teddy Bear Museum is the first and largest teddy bear museum in South Korea. Once you enter, you are greeted by this huge teddy bear, who gives you a ?grand? welcome to further explore the five sections spread over 3 levels: The History Hall, The Art Hall and The Project Exhibition Hall, Gift Shop (all indoors) and an outdoor Teddy Bear Garden and Park. There?s also a caf챕/restaurant. Be prepared to spend at least 1 hour looking and taking photographs/selfies at all the interesting exhibits. The History Hall comprised of the history of bear manufacturing and some of the earliest toy bears, many of which are antique and rare. It also showcases milestones in human history, with the bears enacting several famous (human) historical scenes from different eras. This is indeed a refreshing concept for a museum! I particularly liked the teddy bears enacting the Titanic, landings on the moon and the iconic celebrities like the Beatles and Gandhi.In the Art Hall, you could see the world-famous artworks and designs in an art gallery form as well as animation characters beloved by children. I liked the Mona Lisa and two of the most expensive bears in the world - the Louis Vuitton teddy bear and the Diamond Bear. In the Project Exhibition Hall, you would meet teddy bears grouped to suit the theme of each exhibition. Not forgetting the large Gift Shop on the first level. While it offers plenty of gifts, these are nonetheless pricey. Nevertheless, you could take photos with Michael Jackson bear, Steve Jobs bear and a wedding couple bear amongst others. There?s also a mother panda with her baby pandas on display too.  We certainly enjoyed the wonderful experience of the Museum bringing out the child in each of us, and making us feel young again. Despite the pricey entrance fees, I still think the Teddy Bear Museum is worth visiting, and to me, once would be sufficient. But if you don?t like teddy bears at all, then it would be prudent to skip this attraction.

Unless you really really love Teddy Bears, this place is rather overpriced. At 8,000KRW per person, it gets expensive if you're in a group. And, they won't let you enter the gift shop without paying for a ticket. In the end, we found their gift shop not terribly different from the Safari Teseum (7,000KRW per person, but you can go directly to the gift shop). The Safari Teseum gift shop actually had more options (aka other animals for those who don't like stuffed bears).Still, if you really love Teddy Bears, you can make a day of it between the two places.

Too much of a tourist trap that has been boasting the same facilities/exhibits for several decades. Would have been more impressive to see a renovation of the space. The gift shop is great but is only accessible if you buy a ticket (adult tickets are 10,000 KRW). May be a better option if you're going with young children.

This was pretty entertaining. I had no idea what would be in a Teddy Bear museum... PLEASE go though. There are tons of bears from every period imaginable, wearing period and geographical clothing to match. Everyone is represented and it was actually a lot better than I thought when I hear   we are going to the Teddy Bear Museum  .... don't let that fool you! There is also an outside where you can walk around and see life-sized teddy bears. The gift shop is at the very end, and you WILL want something from it. Class Act, and a welcomed surprise!

This was an attraction I did not plan. But was in the area and decided to do. I did enjoy the climb. They have different levels of intensity and with this views are included. You can take stairs all the way to the top or you can slowly climb. Once up there the view was amazing. If you take a different way down you can even take pictures at a mini park with swings. They also had refreshments at the entrance and a small gift shop with over priced items. Definitely a must if in the area, but not necessarily worth to go out of your way to fit this place in. As its further away from other attractions and buses here can be difficult.

This teddy bear museum is one of a few around the world.  Located in Jungmun tourist complex in Jeju, Korea, is this tiny museum for teddy bear fans alike.  For 8000 KRW you have unlimited day access to 3 floors of teddy bear exhibits and the outside grounds.  This museum carries interesting themed bears like the Mona Lisa bear, the Leonardo Da Vinci bear, a Marilyn Monroe bear, and so many others.  Currently they are displaying the Elvis bear.  On the ground floor there is even a really nice restaurant if you get hungry.  Not much choice in  terms of breakfast, they do offer mostly burgers and different types of coffees.  Also there is a gift shop if you are interested in taking home one of the really cute teddy bear souvenirs.Well worth the visit and few hours for both teddy bear fans and those with just a passing interest.  Remember to use the lockers next to the admission counter.  We didn't and carried all our jackets and bags for the entire exhibit,  It will make the visit a whole lot lighter and more fun.  Enjoy!

This place was really unexpected. Through the Yeha Bus tour this was one of the stops and I am glad we visited this place. A lot of mini exhibits with bears dressed up according to the theme and the gift shop is great as well. For teddy bear lovers and lovers of all things cute, we recommend this place.

This museum, like most of Jeju's other similar attractions, is but an excuse to get you to the gift shop. You can finish it in one hour, because they want to get you there fast! As opposed to most other museums in this resort island, this one is cute and amusing. It consists mostly of tableaus or displays with teddy bears re-enacting some important historical or popular culture event. Some may frown at the   Gandhi   teddy bear as perhaps not quite tasteful, but must surely enjoy the   Beatles   teddy bears, the   Chinatown   teddy bears, etc. You get the picture. Oh, yes the gift shop! It works; I bought a little cute bear as most everybody else seems to have done. Not that expensive and well-made. In other words, if you are going to see at least one of these museums that dot the south of the island, you may want to give this one a try. It's enjoyable.

This is probably the wonderland of 90% of the female population. The place is not huge but if you are going to watch the 3D movie, you have to queue early coz they only have a certain number of 3D glasses. We only have less than 1.5 hours in Hello Kitty Island thus wasn't able to watch the movie. The toilet is cute!! I so love the mirror and of course the cleanliness of the place. Saw a lot of very cute exhibits in the museum. I especially like the bedroom. Wish it was mine. There is a caf챕 on the second floor. The deco is all pink and white. Didn't eat coz we were rushing for time and the snacks aren't really cheap. The gifts are expensive too. I can actually get them cheaper when I'm back in Singapore.

This is one of the many highlights of olle 7 hiking trail.  It is quite a scenic spot, and hence all the tourists here.  There are small gift shops and little unmanned fruit stands along the way (you just need to pick up the oranges or crackers you want anf then leave your money behind)

This is a traditional market where fresh produce and fish can be bought while another portion also sells gifts for travellers like souvenirs, chocolates, etc. We found the prices a bit cheaper than the other places.

This forest has a nutmeg tree that is over 826 years old.  We enjoyed walking on the paths that weave through the forest.  Beautiful trees, flowers and lovely singing birds.  We saw a snake and loved the fresh smelling air.  There is a small store selling drinks and snacks and a small coffee shop.  No gift shop.  The paths are well maintained and very easy to walk on.

This attraction consists of a beautiful and natural   sculpture by the sea  . This formation occurred long ago as part of volcanic activity in the area. You get to experience amazing scenery and photo ops at this very special place. As you enter, you walk through a gorgeously landscaped park and continue on with an easy walk to the observation platform overlooking the formations by the sea. You will not see anything like this anywhere else in the world. They also offer a nice snack bar and gift shop specializing in local fare. A really enjoyable way to spend a couple of hours!

There's basically nothing here except for the black rock that is sculpted by nature to look like a dragon head.  However, the sea view is pretty. Doesn't need to spend a lot of time here.  Maybe about 10 mins max. There's also a souvenir soup nearby which sells Korean gifts. The shop is not huge but you can find stuffs that typical souvenir shops will sell. eg. keychain, pen, towels, mugs, socks (yes, for some reasons, Koreans are really fond of cute socks with cartoons)..etc.Saw the Roll Hotto snack.  In Singapore, we call this flakey flour pastry as prata. In this case, they rolled the prata with egg and ham complete with vege. Kindda cool.The ice cream they are selling at this attraction is interesting.  I chose 2 flavors: Vanilla and Strawberry. Price is KRW3,000 or RMB20. It's kind of interesting to note that RMB is accepted in Korea as a form of payment. Nonetheless, the ice cream is yummy!More photos available onhttp://i-wanna-travel.blogspot.sg/2015/03/korea-jeju-17-mar-2014.html.

There is a reason that this place was packed.  The museum is located in a super modern building set amongst impeccably groomed grounds and a green tea plantation.  The   museum   part takes 5 minutes to get through but the caf챕 and market is buzzing with tourists enjoying an assortment of green tea treats.  I found lots more tea options at this store than any other in Korea (and there are many!)  But the bonus is the Innisfree store adjacent to the Museum on the same grounds.  Here you can make your own mask concoctions customize soap and find lots high quality unique gifts with Jeju logo on them.  I spent at least an hour here alone.  They also have a caf챕.  Definitely a must stop on Jeju!

There is a cafe at level 2 and a small gift shop selling Hallabong items after walking through their tangerines greenhouse. There is also a small museum where kids could learn about tangerines but they are mostly in Korean.Outside  the korean fans dedicated a small hectre of tangerine plantation to G-Dragon. There is even a Kwon Jiyong Tree. But since we were there in late March  the weather was still pretty chilly  so the leaves are not growing yet.You could ask the reception where it is  its just nearby. However do try asking them as   G-Dragon   forest. i tried saying as   GD    but they dont really get it. Lol.

There are some fictional characters that you and me adore and love during our childhood and yet still relish even though we have become adults. Hello Kitty is certainly one of them, and is a favourite of one of my children. However, the good part is not every visitor to Jeju and the locals are a fan of Hello Kitty, so the Hello Kitty Island Museum is not on the itinerary of most tour companies, and hence it?s not crowded.Getting there and fees: Hello Kitty Island Museum, opened in late 2013, is located in the south west part of Jeju (GPS code/coordinate 7926114).  Not to worry if you cannot find space in the small open-air car park outside the Museum because there?s another huge open air car park below the small one. Parking is free. Entrance fee to the Museum is 12,000 won for adult, 11,000 won for teenagers and 10,000Won for children. However, my family and I made use of the discount coupon for entrance fees from the Hertz car rental discount booklet.The Museum/Attraction: when we entered, we were immediately greeted by a large hall where there?s a circular cone of Hello Kitty toys, a photo-taking stop with the entire Hello Kitty family and Hello Kitty?s house where she?s standing at the balcony welcoming you and beckoning you to enter the door into the various exhibition halls. There are 3 levels with the exhibition halls on the first and second level, the gift shop on the first level, the Hello Kitty Caf챕 on the second level and the 3D theatre and an outdoor gallery on the third level. To cover everything, including a meal at the Hello Kitty Caf챕, would easily take about 2-3 hours. In the true sense, this Hello Kitty Museum is a museum ? there are exhibits of anything related to the adorable Hello Kitty. There are several themed exhibition halls on the first and second level e.g. History Hall, Art Education Hall, Music Education Hall, World Gallery Hall, Hello Kitty Room, Constellation Education Hall, amongst others.So we took plenty of photographs and selfies. I particularly like the exhibit of Hello Kitty represented by 26 countries (I found my own country) as well as the huge room containing the huge Hello Kitty bed where one of my children got the Hello Kitty toy snatched away by a toddler.At the Hello Kitty Caf챕 ? with Hello Kitty ribbon windows, Hello Kitty-themed sofas and Hello Kitty engraved tables ? you have to try the Hello Kitty Waffle Set, green tea latte, coffee or  hot chocolate (the 3 hot drinks have a profile of Hello Kitty on the surface), Hello Kitty Strawberry Cake and Cheesecake. Really yummy stuff!Whether you are a fan or not of Hello Kitty, I think this Museum is a fun attraction to visit and be acquainted with Hello Kitty. However, be prepared to ?share? the premises with many joyful and lively children and teenagers. But if you are not a fan and if you have limited time in Jeju, then I suppose you could spend that 2-3 hours elsewhere.

The weather was raining on the day I decided to do sightseeing on Jeju, so I was left with only a visit to the botanical gardens. You can reach it from the airport limousine bus route and behind the fast food shops near SK Energy shop.Luckily the garden exhibition was under glass roof, so it provided a good informative shelter from the rain.The botanical gardens are organised into themes, eg. Aquatic garden, cactus garden, etc. I guess this eliminates confusion for tourists and displays the plants in an educational fashion too. On a sunny day, there is more to do on the outside.There is a curio shop inside the gardens for some gifts but I did not see a coffee shop at the attraction.It will be educational for the kids!

The Teddy Bear museum is a fun stop. There are many displays of teddy bears in various historical, cinematic, and pop-culture type settings. Take your camera and visit each floor. The gift shop at the end is full of fun teddy bear treasures as well. Definitely a good stop for anyone. We went on a rainy day, but it would also be fun on a hot day if you are looking to get out of the heat. Fairly easy to find, it's located in a popular tourist area.

The tea museum is located on the western side of the island and represents the showpiece of the O'Sulloc tea   empire   in South Korea.  There are a number of O'Sulloc tea cafes all over South Korea which specialize in green tea and also sell sweets as well.  There is a large parking area to accommodate a number of cars and visitors.The tea museum consisted of four   features   from what I could surmise.  First you get a decent view of the western part of the island by walking up the stairs to the roof of the museum itself.  The views aren't that interesting but you do get a good view of the surrounding area.  Second the museum itself describes the tea growing/making/serving process.  Third the cafe/gift shop inside seems to attract the most number of visitors.  You can buy teas and other desserts like you would at any other O'Sulloc cafes.  However it does sell many other items - various teas and more.  Finally another attraction is the tea plantation itself.  O'Sulloc seemingly has a small portion of their plantation on-site that you can walk through (note there may be snakes in the plantation) to get a sense of how the green tea leaves are grown.There is also an Innisfree store right next to the tea museum but we did not visit it.The tea museum is worth a trip though I wouldn't go out of the way to visit it as you can always partake in O'Sulloc teas in various locations in South Korea.

The market mainly consists of two parts: a fruit market (mostly for visitors) and a fish market (mostly for local, as visitors basically can?t do anything with the raw fishes). In night time, there is also food stalls near Gate 8 but the number is limited (I think there?s about 20) so the queue is often long - mostly Korean youngsters. My Korean friend told me that Jeju is unique with its rice cake (similar to Japanese mochi) and orange that even Koreans ?have to? purchase as gifts when visiting Jeju thus their prices are not cheap.

The admission was 占2,000 per ticket, so not so bad.  96% of what you are walking on is just hardened lava and there are puddles, so bring good shoes.  This is also basically a cave, so it's quite chilly down there, so a jacket is nice to have.  From the bottom of the stairs to the lava column is just shy of a kilometer.  There are a variety of things to see along the way, such as the different types of formations and effects.Aside from the lava tube, there is only a small restaurant and a gift shop.  Not too far down the road is the mazeland.  There may be better times than others to go.  We got lucky and missed a huge crowd of young kids that had just arrived on a bus.

So, perhaps this comparison is unfair, but if you have to choose between the two: the Teddy Bear Museum and this Teseum, I would personally choose this Teseum because the Teseum is slightly cheaper, closer to Jeju City, and way less pretentious (that may sound weird, but that's more or less what the difference was). Teseum was laid back, a bit more interactive, and generally understanding of that a visit to see Teddy bears would mean visiting the childish side on all of us. The Teddy Bear museum was more like an anthropological study of teddy bears or something, aka, less fun, a bit more uptight.For those in the group who were not as interested in the actual display, they could opt out and still purchase teddy bears. The gift shop was conveniently open to everyone visiting and there were a few convenience stores and such around.
Small museum. The displays were interesting- the Titanic, Normandy, and Berlin Wall to name a few ? Gift shop was pricey.

Similar to other korean markets, there are lots of food and shops selling various stuff. There are many stalls selling snacks which you would buy home as gifts and you can get the jeju tangerines which was really delicious! Snacks in various boxes (chocolates, rice crackers etc) are still quite decently priced.Many variety too! I enjoyed a visit here!
Nice walk along the shore and take a few photos near the airport, tourist information, gift shops and casino.

My kids loved this place I was sort of disappointed in the gift store I wish that there were more of the things displayed that you could buy, but the actual displays were quite amazing lots of good photo ops.

review: Located in the middle of Jungmun Resort right across from a Ripley's Believe it or Not museum, I would only recommend this kitsch and cheese-tastic museum to visitors on a bleak and rainy day. The idea is cute, at best - history and art through the ages represented by teddy bears (My Fair Lady, Princess Diana and Prince Charles get married, the falling of the Berlin War, the Beatles, Mona Lisa, the Creation of Adam, etc.), but I would expect a museum in an expensive resort complex to at least have descriptions in English and other tourist languages (Japanese, Mandarin, Cantonese). The entrance fee of 8000 won is a little steep for what you are able to see. Not surprisingly, there is an entire floor dedicated to a pricey gift shop. The most impressive parts of the museum are the architecture of the glass pyramidal shaped building and the views from the garden to the rear. Overall, it's an alright way to kill an hour or so, but definitely not a must-see for me.

Just your run of the mill chocolate   factory   museum. They have all the info about the Cacao bean and how to make chocolate  a gift shop to buy chocolate  and that's it. They have a little chocolate workshop for kids. And kids only which was kind of disappointing.It's great if you have kids but if you are going to just to go or with your boy/girlfriend or spouse I wouldn't. It's mediocre and offers the same info about chocolate you could learn by googling it.
