review: Jeju is gifted by heaven with 3 famous waterfalls. This is the most awesome one that the mother nature embraces its beauty. From far, you could see rainbows.You probably will end up like me.. leaping and hoping from rocks & stones to get close to the waterfalls. I did fell down when I pursue a step of closeness to this natural beauty. But I could not resist its charm and finally I stood firm with the beauty. Don't envy, go for it!

I've been very interested in the haenyeo ever since I first visited Jeju-do. This museum has some interesting exhibitions about the life and work of the haenyeo. Admission is very cheap, a bit over 1000 won for an adult. It's recommended to watch the short documentary about the haenyeo before visiting the exhibitions, to get the most out of your visit. It plays near the lobby. There's a gift shop on site with haenyeo-related items.

Its fish market but have a lot of store sale a souvenir and gift item like small soju and jeju orange, jeju cohocolate and sama candies and friend...and at the end of dongmun market they have delicious street food....and yummy

It's a Safari Theme Teddy Bear Museum. There are all kinds of bears, including giraffe, zebras, sheeps, monkeys, pandas, etc. On the second level, there is even Egyptian theme bears decorated with crystals. Don't miss that. There are also international bears on displayed on level 2. Enjoy your visit. Don't miss out on purchasing the bears at the gift shop for souvenirs, you will be spoilt for choices. All the bears are made in Korea and worth buying for keepsake.

It's a mixed review.  The ticket price is 10,000KRW per adult and since other natural attractions are around 2,000KRW, this park should be well worth it.  Highs: The caves are really cool as well as the Bansai and Stone Garden. The park is easy to walk and has shops and toilets easily available.  Transportation is also easy as it's just the 702 bus from the Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal for 1 hour. Lows: The park is dated, like late 90s with its signage and information cards.  The bird exhibit, stone exhibit and flower garden are average at best.  While the park trail is easy to walk, you do walk through gift shops for the next exhibits (so a bit too tourist-y). Overall, it makes for a decent easy afternoon, especially with kids or elderly.  The park needs some updating to be worth the ticket price, but it is close to the beach (just 5 mins walking).

It was interesting how they recreated real-life historical events and famous works of art with teddy bears.  There are two main exhibit halls.   Of course there is a gift shop where you can purchase teddy bears.  My wife and I enjoyed it and took lots of pictures.  I think you will enjoy this place, even if you don't have a thing for teddy bears. Bonus:  there is a really nice Starbucks right across the street.

Innisfree is a well-known brand with numerous outlets throughout Korea and Asia. As it originated from Jeju, this is their main outlet in Korea. It was much smaller than expected, with only a single long building housing both the shop and cafe.The shop stocked quiet a good range of their toiletries and cosmetics, with an natural soap-making activity available. You can purchase a pack from the counter, choose the scent of soap you want, and there are stations with a screen to guide you through the soap-making process step-by-step. Shop staff are on hand for assistance as well. At the end of it, you can pack the soap into an eco-bag as a gift.The organic green cafe had ample seating and a good range of food, compared to the adjacent O Sulloc tea museum. Their drinks are served in funky bottles with interesting tastes, and make a pretty picture.If in the area, the soap-making is interesting and wouldn't take too long.

I'm not a big fan of Hello Kitty (my friend does), but it was fun to stroll around the place. It was filled with Hello Kitty goodness in pink and such a nice place to take pictures. There are so many rooms to be visited, and they even have a rooftop garden! Some of item showcased are very interactive and enjoyable. I believe it's worth the visit as every adult has their own inner-child side. Unravel your younger side out, and you'll enjoy the place lot more than you think. Recommended for families. Make sure to visit their cafe that serves nice choco drink (approx. KRW4000) & the gift shop!Admission fee for adult: approx. KRW10800++

If you love Hello Kitty, I think you will really like it. That being said, though, I think it is better for adult fans than for kids. For the most part, it is a Hello Kitty museum with displays for looking at. There's not really much for kids to do, other than look. The cafe was good, and cute. The gift shop had some cool stuff I hadn't seen elsewhere, but it is pricey. All in all, I would say that I am really glad I saw it, because it was super cute, but it wouldn't warrant a return visit.

If you don?t like teddy bears, don?t go. The gift shop is very nice. In the back outside there is the largest teddy bear I have ever seen. I found some nice items in there. I love how they made celebrity bears. The Elvis bear is s riot! They offer a show in the theatre. Nice cafe.

If you are not familiar with the Korean love of 'cute', you won't get what's going on at the Teddy Bear Museum. Don't expect a history of the teddy bear; expect teddy bears placed in historic events. It is cute. Kids love it. If you are searching for something serious, skip this one, but if you're looking for a bit of quirky fun that you will only find in Korea, check it out! *The gift shop is pricey.

If you are not a fan of BB, don't bother to go. Literally waste your entrance fee, if you want to get the gift, the gift shop is just rite at the entrance, no entrance fee requiredI think going to the GD Caf챕 is better than this KPop Museum. And the Teddy Bear museum next door worth 10 times more. I am not a huge fan of BB  but definitiely I know many KPOP stars.

If you are a Kpop fan and have an afternoon to spare, you shouldn't miss this. There were plethora of stations and   things to do   for me and my friends who were less knowledgable about kpop. Don't skip the gift shop on first floor!

If you are a Hello Kitty lover and an adult, it will be nice to see all of the different Hello Kitty items, but it will also be pretty boring for you as well.  This museum is definitely geared towards kids, though I think that there could be more activities for them. The gift shop at the end of everything is quite nice but rather expensive.

If this place was in Europe I am sure the entrance fee would be double or triple, and it would have a giant shop at the end. This place is full of hard to believe facts, artsy stuff and little experiments. To be honest, I would really like to see a little shop at the and, so that I could send a postcard or add a pencil to my collection if not buying a few sciencey gifts. Definitely spare some time for this place, you will enjoy!

I was looking forward to this attraction more than any other on Jeju and it didn't disappoint.  I wouldn't rate as #1 (more   touristy   than expected) but worth the stop.  If you can move past the gift stores selling trinkets, cheezy signage, animals in tiny cages and crowds, the attractions within the park are quite beautiful.  I especially liked the lava caves and the bonsai garden.  Those two areas alone were worth the stop.  If you have time, just past the park entrance is a stunning beach area.  Great for photos and possibly a toe dipped into the waters.

I visited Seongeup Folk Village as part of the tour package to Jeju Island that was provided as free gift by a company that I need not mentioned here. As an Asian and having extensively travelled throughout Asia. I am familiar have experience all sorts of tricks and gimmicks. The first tip that this was another hard sell stop is that there is no time limit for the stop. Prior to this stop, we visited the famous Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak, they insisted that we returned to the bus by 1 hour which is not enough to really enjoy the place. However, we were told we can take all the time we need at Seongeup. Then a nice looking old lady who can speak Mandarin were waiting to greet us and give us a tour of the place. I was curios why no such tour guide were organised for Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak. The whole tour of the village was short 15 minutes, most of the info she provided I can easily find out from internet, then we were ushered into a room in one 'village building' where she proceed to let taste and test their natural products and tell us how miraculous is the products, the tea, the honey, horse bones and horse cream. The whole presentation took twice as long as the village tour. Then she went on and on and on about how healthy are the people and it is due to the miracles of horse bones. I mean come on. There are horses the world over. Surely if horse bones are the key to living longer and younger,.Someone other than the Jeju people would have known about it. Then next she talks about pricing which I almost fell out of my chair. Korean Won 190,000 or USD 185 for horse bones pellet? I am not sure how many fools are there in the world that bought into this ludicrous claims. Right there and then I wanted to leave. She then changes tack and describe how they money will help preserve the village, fund village children education healthcare etc etc. I heard that before in almost all my travel. Apparently, some of my fellow tour travellers are interested, so they stayed in the room while I explored the 'village'. The area is very small, most of the 'buildings' are similar to the one that I was in and there are various product demo sessions going on in other 'buldings'. In the end, we spend a total a 2 hour there and the organizer waited until everyone got onto the bus. It so different from the Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak stop where they chased back onto the bus and even went into the washroom to look for missing passengers. Just for non-asian travellers tour organiser gets sales commissions if the tour groups buy something. So they benefit if when they spend more types at such places rather then the actual sight that you wanted to see.

i thought the museum sounded stupid but it was actually really cute!!! there were so many scenes set up with stuffed animals on the first floor.  they were so creative!  then you can you to the second floor and take pictures.  there's the rock band set up, the proposal bear, and many more.  there are also famous works of art re-done with teddy bears. finally there's the gift shop.  everything is over priced but you can't expect anything else...

I think it was a great idea for them to have teddy bears pose for historical moments, people and scenes.  It may seem whimsical at first, but it is also a perfect platform for parents to explain certain moments in history and people to them.  E.g. having a bear bandaged with only one ear to portray u know who.  Perhaps one easily missed teddy bear is the actual world's most expensive teddy bear!There is also a gift shop at the end (with Michael and Audrey...) where they sell a variety of teddy bears.  Although the teddy bears look as normal as any teddy bears, mind u, u don't get those mass produced made-in-u-know-where quality.  Worth taking a look!This place will be more suitable for family with young children or people who just love teddy bears.

I like to explore super markets in different cities and different countries. It's a good way to see what people are eating. Sometime when I have the courage, I will tried some of the local food. Dongmun Market is one of the popular traditional markets in Jeju. It is big, clean and colourful. They sell all kinds of stuff, like fruit, fresh or dry (some in gift boxes), vegetables, dry mushrooms, herbs, spices and fresh or dry sea food. There are some restaurants ready to serve you. They even sell clothing there. We walked around and took photos, but no one came to pressure us to buy stuff, I like that.Happy Travelling!

I have been wanting to visit the Teddy Bear Museum for the longest time but did not get to visit the one in Seoul 2 years ago. So, when we decided to plan a 2D1N trip to Jeju, this attraction is in my itinerary list. It is not located conveniently near the city centre and about an hour's bus ride to go to the attraction. I was so excited when I saw the museum when the bus passed by and alighted with much excitement. We were greeted with a huge bear at the entrance and it was like entering a wonderland. We walked around admiring the displays, the history of teddy bears etc. We also visited the outdoor park right behind the museum which are meant for visitors only. It was a fruitful visit and did not fail my expectation though. Love all the bears on sale at the gift shop but couldn't bring them all back so only got to admire them when I was there. If you are visiting Jeju, do drop by this museum to bring back childhood memories.

I have been here several times, I really do enjoy it.  It is just an easy and fun way to spend a day. Lots of photo opportunities.I see they occasionally offer glass blowing classes. I have never done this, but it is on my list of things to try!ProTip: There are 2 stores filled with glass items for sale.  Some tacky, but mostly rather reasonably priced gift ideas. Plus, lots of  cool looking jewelry.

I had heard about these women from NatGeo. Being able to see how important these women are to the local community was impressive. The museum provides a detailed panorama of these women's lives. From when they are children to when they give birth to late into their lives. It provides some real size replicas of boats, costumes, and even foods. A must see. A little out of the way if you are not staying in the area but well worth the drive or the bus ride(bus stop is named after the museum). Price is reasonable and the gift shop has some out of the normal options.

I guessed many have mentioned that this was a typical market and I do not think they were wrong. However, it really depends the reason for your visit. If you are here to try cheap and good raw and fresh seafood (eg: raw fish slices for 10000won only), OR to try a variety of local food (eg: Sundae aka blood sausage, traditional fishcake stick, Kimbap, fresh Jeju orange juices, different types of kimchi, korean rice cakes, croquette, Tteokbokki, hotba, Modeumjeon - where they eat during new year and jeons, OR to purchase souvenirs and snacks for your family and friends then you are at the right place! It was also cheaper to purchase dried goods like ikan bilis and kelp in the market than supermarkets.We were at Seogwipo Maeil Olleh Market before coming to this market and we found that stalls that sell Jeju's souvenirs and local snacks such as Jeju crunch chocolate were cheaper in this market. The shop owners also gave us a handful of other snacks to try after our purchase in hope that we would be back for more. In Summary, this was a good place to try many local food at a smaller amount and a place to purchase affordable snacks for gift at a cheaper price.

I got to visit this museum as part of an inclusive tour so I can't comment on the value of the entrance fee, but I loved this museum.  I haven't laughed so much in ages.  I am not sure if it is meant to be so delightfully funny!  It is famous in S Korea for a TV series   about a Princess that was filmed there.What you get is several galleries of teddy bears dressed up as historical figures, famous art works, and scenes from history or of S Korean culture.  There are several large bears around the place suitable for having your photo with eg Charlie Chaplin, Michael Jackson.  Outside there are several bears enjoying the gardens again suitable for being photographed with.  There is a cafe and a gift shop.  The cafe was closed when we visited late afternoon. There is a short running show of an automaton Elvis-Bear again hilarious!  I would definitely go back.  This museum is located in the Jungmun resort area on the Bus Route 600.  Get off at PlayKpop stop - its just next door.

I am in the middle of living in Jeju for a year and visited the Haenyeo Museum with three friends a couple of months ago. It was a really great visit and showed really well the changes in Haenyeo lifestyle as time has gone on. The top floor has a beautiful picture gallery with gorgeous views. Highly recommend. I think you need about an hour - an hour and a half here.Also the gift shop is great for cute Jeju-y things. I put some   Jeju stockings   together for my cousin's kids for Christmas all with keyrings/books/purses/other stuff bought here.

Horses are a big part of the Jeju culture  and Jeju Horse Park is a pretty cool place. Its museum includes many photographs  artifacts and a video telling the story of the Jeju   ma    or pony  which is descended from the ponies brought to the island by Mongol invaders. The island was considered a good place to raise horses  and the Mongols used it as such. At the park  you can also ride the horses. There is a great giftshop with lots of local handmade items. Children or even adults can make related crafts in an activity room. The building itself is round like a ger  the traditional nomadic tents used by the Mongols. The top deck includes a fabulous 360-degree view of the   oreums   (small cinder-cones or parasitic volcanoes) that literally ring the area of the park. Inside the railing  an artist has painted the oreums  along with their names. So  you can know exactly which oreums you are viewing. There are also some actual Mongolian gers (also known as yurts in other nomadic cultures). I believe tourists can actually spend the night in one of the gers. One thing to consider: If you want to visit  you must either have your own transportation or go with someone who does. It's kind of far from anywhere  and bus service may not operate in that area. Likewise  taxis don't just happen by. But  it is a beautiful area and interesting for the entire family We visited in the spring  and there were also lots of colorful wildflowers. Plan to spend a few hours there  especially if you will ride the horses.

Having just visited the newly opened Teddy Bear Museum in Chengdu, Sichuan Province, China (by the same group), this original museum in Jeju was a little underwhelming, even for a solid teddy bear fan like me. Unlike those in Chengdu, I didn't appreciate the fact that all teddies in Jeju were enclosed in glass cases. Impossible to take a decent pic with them!There was a good collection of antique bears. Great for a collector like myself. Also there was the supposedly most expensive teddy bears in the world. The LV bear and the diamond bear.For sale of their Elvis bears I believe, there was a small theater on the second floor showing 4 mins Elvis teddy concert every quarter of the hour. Perhaps I went at a later hour (5pm), I was the only one in the theater. Appreciate that the museum is opened till 8pm in the evening, so it's great as a quick destination pre or post dinner, if you are staying or hanging around the Jungmum Resort Area. The museum was located right next to Lotte Hotel. There was a Lotteria on the ground floor but it was closed during my visit. An attractive and well stocked teddy store on the ground floor too, unlike its sad and sparse Chengdu cousin. Happy that there were some collector grade Korean handmade teddies for sale. Their house brand   so-called   limited edition replica made-in-China white Alfred bear (real limited edition would come with serial numbers) came in a nice copycat Steiff look alike gift box and a photo with a Korean prince. At only USD 35, it's great as a souvenir/gift!I like the outdoor park area. Great for kids to run around. Overall not a very big place. Whole place would take about an hour.

Great food and local gifts such as sashimi, steamed pork, fresh fruit, and gifts.If you want to buy for yourself and friends, family, visit here to buy the things.You will love to visit for delicious local food.

For people who loves green tea, can check out the variety of green tea products they have; it's nice to 'chill-out' at the yard with hot beverage in hand.It will be good for the kids to try out their self made soap and they felt very good with their artwork. However, if you would to make your purchase at Innisfree, please do note that they DO NOT give out any free samples or gifts for your purchases (even thou I've purchased about KRW500,000 worth of products) unlike those in Seoul or Busan, they are very generous with their samples and gifts with purchase.

For only $10 (10,000 KW) you can spend an afternoon wandering around a carefully manicured small park that exhibits outdoor glass work. As you walk in there is a place to watch professional glass blowers blow bottles in the traditional way, and if you are taking a school group there, the kids can have ago at making something, and then return the next day to pick up their handiwork. After that you follow the path around the exhibits until you get to the other end.In this mainly outdoor museum, there are glass plants, flowers, and an eclectic collection of glass made curiosities that make a very pleasant way to spend a couple of hours. There is a small cafe in the middle of the exhibition, and the gift shop just before you exit. The bathrooms are at the entrance exit, so go before you start!

For a first timer visiting this place as tourist, i can say that this place gives you the choices you need to bring back home. You need to do some haggling of price. Some of the salespersons are quite persistent. They would do the 'extra mile' to make you buy their merchandise. 3rd floor gift section also has good variety of choices. I ended up spending more than W100,000 there. No regrets !

Fairly small place for a hefty KRW10,000 entrance fee; the most expensive Jeju attraction. Features 2 galleries of teddy bears from various countries and themes and a teddy souvenir shop.  Will appeal to ladies, children and couples keen on photo snaps with huggable teddies, especially the human-sized ones at the corner of each floor and in the gift shop. Be prepared to jostle with crowds on a busy day.  There is a 5 minute T-Elvis performance held at every 15 minute interval in the Elvis Presley theatre.  Can skip if you're not a teddy lover or been here before as exhibits hardly change.

Entrance is pretty expensive (9500??), but you get a comprehensive history of teddy bears. You can't really find that anywhere else,  I suppose. And some exhibits were moving. The gift shop stuffs were pretty darn expensive, the cheapest teddy was a small keychain teddy at 9500??. Highlight of the visit was the Teddy Elvis show at level 2. That was pretty cool. I also liked how there was a whole section dedicated to Pooh bear.

Dongmun Market is filled with every possible product that you can make out of tangerines.They grow tangerines on the island. There is tangerine chocolate, tangerine juice, tangerine cakes etc. There is also fish and food stalls. If you want to get your friends gifts or souvenirs from Jeju, you can buy them from here.
Depends on your agenda, there are stalls selling nice snacks like bbq octopus, fish cakes, etc. Many raw seafoods, oranges, chocolates and snacks for gifts.

Definitely the most fun I have in the island. Not that I didn't have fun in other attractions however I just love how everything they got in this attraction is an interactive one. I have the chance to watch GD's hologram concert as well here, they have one hologram concert every one hour. It's fun! Oh, and if you're a VIP this place is a must visit. Their gift shop offers some selection of VIP merchandises, from Krunk, snapback hats and VIP's light stick.The entry ticket is 15.000 won if I'm not wrong, but it is definitely worth every bucks you spend. There's a dancing room, a 360 degree 3D experience, you can even take pictures with your favorite Kpoppers using their hologram tech.

Built on a reclaimed land-fill site, this vast area of pathways, statues, displays, museums and traditional villages is very worth a visit if on Jeju. From the impressive stone structures and flat basalt 'floor' at the entrance of the park, I was blown away by the vast array of statues that are displayed, explained and on show in this area. There is ample car parking that is only a short walk form the entry way. A small fee is required and then you are free to wander the area that included a massive and spectacular 2 store (below ground) museum that outlines the geographic development of Jeju along with many interactive displays, a short film with subtitles, examples and galleries of 'stone art'. A gift shop of course, provided a range of traditional and specific items and there are amenities spread throughout the part. Water features, a traditional village, an art gallery and a vast array of stone sculpture will give you hours of things to view and read as you wander through the park In my humble opinion, not to be missed!!!

At Hallim park, there are a few lava caves that are interesting, and very cool (temperature).  The flower gardens are very nice.  The bonsai garden has trees that date to 300 years ago.  They are constantly trimmed to keep them small.  There is a restaurant at the entrance, and a rest area with a gift shop in the center of the park.

As a child I was a big Hello Kitty fan and thought it would be nice to visit this place, after seeing it at the airport. Getting here is really easy from the main bus terminal. I did not know what to expect when I got here. But when I got there I noticed it was $12,000 won to get in. But once you are inside there is nothing special about the place to be charging so much. Its just a bunch of halls with Hello Kitty pictures and some random facts. On the second floor there is a Cafe, that is also overpriced and over crowded. Almost impossible to get a good seat. Service is not great. They not only took forever to take my order, I was the only one in line, but also to give me what I had ordered. The gift shop is also an overpriced place with not a lot of options. Knowing what I know now I dont think I would have done this place.

As a big Hello Kitty fan, I was excited to visit Hello Kitty Island after hearing about it. Although the museum was quite fun, it was pretty run down with many of the exhibits being kind of dirty. The cafe in particular was not on par with the Hello Kitty cafes in Seoul. At those cafes, the cakes and drinks are very fresh but at Hello Kitty Island the cake we ordered tasted (and looked!) like it had been left on the shelf for a while. Similarly the gift shop didn't stock great souvenirs. Considering the price you pay to get in, I would have expected a bit more from this place. If you're a big Hello Kitty fan, I suggest one of the themed places in Seoul.

Amazing beachside for prewedding photos as there are this colorful chairs that are always available there as props. The beach was clean and there are cafes and the famous colorful candle gel gift shop. Great visit with family, couples or for photoshoots!
A must see if you are at Jungmun Resort Complex.  The teddy bears are very cute, would have loved to buy more at the gift store...too bad they didn't have tshirts with TBM and Jeju as a souvenir...
A lot of selection, different price ranges for all the price brackets. Clothes, some gifts and food. Worth coming to see.

A cute and cuddly experience at the Teddy Bear museum, this place is for kids and adults alike. It has an impressive collection of impressionistic teddy bears, from the 19th century to the major icons of today; a teddy bear version of Madame Tussaud's. Then there is a peaceful garden walk which is also adorned with teddy bear statues. The gift shop is irresistible, too.

10,000won per adult. Two floors of teddy bears gallery. I was quite fascinated by the really old teddy bears. The Louis Vitton Teddy bear was also on display, which apparently went for $190,000 during a fund raising charity event. Saw Elvis bear, Marilyn Monroe bear, Steve Job bear etc. There is a massive gift shop at ground level, selling a variety of teddy bears. But quite overpriced 10,000won for a key chain teddy, 35,000won for a palm size teddy. I don't even dare to look at how much the larger bear cost.

10,000 KRW per person. When you enter, pay for admission, and start in third floor, go down floors in order. In the basement, theres gift shop, cafe, and theres few more exhibits to see. Perfect for kids, fun for adults. Wish there could be more exhibitions of teddy bears. But if was nice!

Went there with my friend.. We took a bus from Halla hospital (?쒕씪蹂묒썝) bus stop and took bus no. 755 and alighted at the bus stop right in front of O'Sulloc Tea Museum. The entrance is free and there is a gift shop and a cafe.. You can buy different types of teas and other products made from tea in the shop (e.g. tea packs skin care products etc). You can buy green tea ice cream green tea roll cake and beverages etc from the cafe.. The cost of the products are reasonable while some are more expensive.Opposite the road there is a big Tea farm of the tea museum. You can take pictures there but must beware of snakes (諭�議곗떖) as warned with a sign board on the tea plant.Beside the museum there is Innisfree Jejuhouse (just walking distance). There is a sign board showing the direction and the Innisfree Jejuhouse is on the left hand side of the Tea Museum. If you like Tea this is a must visit place.

Well this place was big. Need to prepare to walk if you're going at non-peak hours. Why? due to the train not moving. This place features Korean village cultural show donkey / house riding costume trying & a beautiful setting to get some nice pictures. We enjoyed solid 1-2hours walking. But having to travel with small kids its quite tiring. Anyway the replicas of houses & setting was great. Enjoyed buying some quality souvenir at the gift shops. My kids just love the small maze park. I don't op for a tour guide but a head set was just enough for us to make us understand the place.One thing for sure they're snakes wandering around the place. While walking we come across 2 snakes (small). My kids was terrified! So need to be extra careful for those who bring little kids. Another set back was the small shop selling fast food. I know there's a barrier problem in language but they seem to ignore foreign tourist due to the fact we cant communicate well with each other. Very hard to buy stuff. Water! walking makes you thirsty. Pro's :- The head set helps to understand the place even-though not so many point haves explanation. Perhaps its an area for improvement.Con's :- Snakes? YikesOverall the place was ok. But will not come again..
Well organised tour of Korean traditional village easy to navigate takes about an hour. Stop at the gift shops in between for gifts

We visited in April 2018 and were impressed by the quality and the size of the village. There is a lot of history and culture to be learned here. The exhibits are well maintained they have live gardens and animals to represent the life in the village as well as hands on exhibits for kids and adults to participate in. There are craftspeople and artisans that are making wood work and stoneware that you can purchase. It is very beautiful. Also there is a restaurant on premise near the front gates and gift shop. The living museum and village is wheelchair accessible and worth the price of admission. It will take 2 to 3 hours to see everything. It can easily be a half day experience. Get there early to avoid the crowds. It's popular for students and tourists along with all the major places you should visit while on Jeju.

We loved looking at the shells collected from all over the world. They were artistically arranged. It was well worth the $6.00 entrance fee and I received pearl stud earrings for free. The gift shop was expensive and bordered on tacky. The few shells for sale were very expensive  $68.00 for a small shell.

Visited this Museum in Dec 2017 with my family. Entrance ticket costs 34 000kwon for 2 adults and 2 children. The place basically is run-down  glasses broken  dirty and colour faded over the years. I didn't bother to check on the cafe inside and left the museum in 15mins. Nothing special in the gift shop as well. Total waste of my money and my time travelled to visit the so called museum. If you intend to visit this Jeju Glass Museum  don't bother!

Very tasteful and informative. We were hesitant at first but figured we might as well take advantage of seeing what a sexually suppressed country could teach us :)The gift shop was a little lacking on museum related material and seemed to carry just local touristy items.

To know how the teddy bear appears then visit it. Also knowing all the types of teddy bear and appreciate it. Also a garden walk for photo shoot plus Elvis teddy bear life show every 15minutes to listen to elvis.The gift shop is really something to buy to have visit this teddy bear museum

This venue offers quite a few exhibits for photo moment. Kids will surely like his place. The place can be done in an hour time unless you spend time explaining to the kids what each exhibit is about. The gift shop offer a good range of teddy bear to buy as a gift.

This museum isn't very large and in the winter you don't really want to go outside to admire the small amount of outdoor exhibits (which you can do from inside the windows anyway) but it's got enough interesting art to be worth 1000 KRW which is about USD $0.80. For one I enjoyed the Chang Ri Seok exhibit as his paintings are very earthy. The second floor exhibit was under renovation when I went but still for 1000 won I have no complaints about the first floor's contents. The gift shop is pretty underwhelming though.

This museum is not the easiest to find  located in an industrial type area. Upon entrance you receive a free sample of chocolate and a hot chocolate (not sure if this was offered due to the chilly  rainy weather  but it was definitely appreciated). Some interesting finds from around the world  historical facts  and treasures. There is an area where you may observe chocolate pieces being made for sale in the adjacent gift shop. Good stop for a rainy day on Jeju Island. Gift shop is a little pricey. Teenaged daughter loved it; teenaged son was bored.

review: This little folk village was located right next to our hotel (Haevachi) so we figured we should check it out.  We were spoiled because we had just gone to the folk village and that is the bomb!It is only about $8 for admission and then we opted for the audio tours.  Most of the written signs are not in English so I'm glad we had the audio tours but they didn't work very well.  They are tripped by some sort of sensor when you go by but mine kept skipping back to the original message ugggg.It's a very large complex but somehow unauthentic feeling.  I thought the neatest part was the artisans that sell their crafts.  That was cool and they do have a nice gift shop.  It was very hot out so we went through fairly quickly.  If it hadn't been so hot we might have spent much longer just exploring.If this is your only opportunity to see such a thing then I would visit but if you have the chance to see the folk village in Seoul then I would wait for that one!
This is a big temple with lots to see.  There are a couple of large budda statues and many small ones.  It also has a nice gift shop.It is far from downtown and a bit hard to get without a car.

The museum part of the building was only about 2 small rooms with a bit of history of tea-making.  Most of the rest was taken up by the gift shop and cafe.The green tea (Swiss) roll which is their iconic cake was sold out completely on the day we were there even though it was only about 11am.  Made do with green tea and tangerine soft serve ice-cream and tea.  The tangerine tea was beautifully presented in a stoneware cup and tasted better than the green tea.There are very limited food choices for a full meal and this is more a snack cafe.  The food at nearby Innisfree is much better with a wider range.  Eventually we had the green tea cake back in Seoul where it was easily available at the O Sulloc outlets in Myeongdong.

The green tea museum was nice.  They had tea sets from around the world from many different ages.  The gift shop had free green tea sampling which was quite delicious.  They also had a cafe where you can buy green tea roll cakes ice cream and lattes.

The glass museum is well presented and extremely pleasant environment!While the building seems modern and edgy the products are sweet rather than overly modern! If the gift shop is not making a huge profit it is because the gifts seem dated!

The Alive Museum in Seogwipo is a pretty nice museum that is near a number of good restaurants and is definitely not hard to get to on foot. For 11000 won you can take photos with plenty of crazy cute and cool paintings all over the museum; this is definitely their specialty. I really enjoyed some of the paintings especially the ones near the picture of the wings that makes you look like an angel. The gift shop at the end and of course the mandatory photos taken of you upon coming in are really overpriced and we didn't go outside because it was so cold out but the inside was pretty worth it to get so many cool photo opportunities. If you're not into taking pictures though this museum probably isn't for you.
Pales in comparison to Osulloc Tea Museum but it's worth a look since they are side by side. The products in the gift shop are the widely available Innisfree facial products.

Our 4yo liked it well enough. We spent about 2hrs and spent more money at the gift shop than on admission (24000 won) and if it were nicer out we probably would have spent longer. Botanical garden a small garden maze Fossil museum animal feeding station bird attraction and the really TALL dinosaurs scattered throughout made for an enjoyable afternoon outing before nap time.

On our way back from Gahina Tea Pottery we were close-by the Tea Museum.  Many buses leave from there for Jeju and Seogwipo making this a convenient place to have a hot beverage.  Yes there is no entrance fee and that seems to be because it is mostly a gift shop and tea room.  That said the tea is lovely making for great gifts and the green tea ice cream quite tasty.  Clean bathrooms and a lovely building make this a nice place to pass through for a quick stop.

Not so much a museum as much as a gift shop on a tea field. I live right next door and it's always super busy (not sure why). The land is really beautiful with rolling tea fields but it is not a museum just an insanely overpriced gift shop. But if you're in the area it's definitely worth a visit.

My 5yr old loved it very much. Lots of dinosaurs on display outdoor. Several exhibitions on site such as fossils and seashells. Areas where you can interact with animals (feeding ponies and gerbils.) You also get to see parrots next to the gift shop. It's not a very big place. we spent about 2 hours there. We got a taxi there and the man at the ticket hut(speaks good English) was very kind to help us get a taxi back to hotel. A very enjoyable and pleasant place to visit if you like dinosaurs and animals.

Must visit for anyone who visits Jeju even though its more of an extended cafe/shop more than a museum. There is a small section dedicated to the history of tea and brewing/drinking techniques and apparatus but wouldn't call it a museum as such.There is also a nice area round the back to take photos and take in the scenery as well as an Innisfree attached to it.The cafe is the main attraction as it serves tea/cakes and ice cream to visitors and it is definitely up there with the best green tea ice cream I've had. After visiting a branch in Seoul we had to go to the origin of the tea. We tried the green tea tiramisu cake in Myeongdong which was excellent best green tea tiramisu cake I've had but opted for the green tea torte cake here as well as the ice cream. My opinion is the tiramisu was better but still very nice along with the ice cream.The gift shop was also good and we had members of staff brewing tea to allow you to sample the taste before buying. In hindsight we left without buying any tea but regretted as we left Jeju. If you're in limbo about whether to buy the tea or not my advice will be to just buy it regardless if the price is expensive since you'll probably regret it like we were. Only consolation is that the duty free inside Jeju international airport does stock some O'Sulloc products but not as much as here.Worth the visit but a bit out in the sticks. 8/10

Museum is fairly small but packed with tourists. Gift shop offer wide variety of gift ideas. Cafe was too packed for us to stay around for sampling snacks and drinks.Innisfree museum and green tea plantation are nearby

Jeju Folk Village Museum as it appears on map for Jeju is on the coast and is a must do for history and culture buffs. There are hands on exhibits that kids and adults can participate and use around the village. The park and museum is large and takes 2 to 3 hours at least. Perhaps longer to see everything without rush. We were quite impressed by the size the crafts people making products and the exhibits throughout. There are ample restrooms snack shops and Korean traditional products sold in the gift shop. There is also a restaurant on premise.The Jeju Folk Village attracts students from all over Korea as well as tourists from other countries. I highly recommend the park. There are beautiful floral blooms as well as animals photo opportunities and lots of traditional Korean history and culture to learn about. Well worth the price of admission. Plan to spend half a day here. Arrive early to avoid the crowds. There are some great gifts and candies to be found around the village including the traditional Korean taffy near the Hanbok photo place and the gift shop.

It's one of the best small museums on Jeju island. I went there twice and each time spent couple of hours in sheer amazement and delight. Almost each sea shell installation strikes with its beauty. The bronze things are also interesting and sometimes funny. Check the bathroom  by the way :)There is much stuff in the gift shop but quite expensive. Small cafe is cozy arranged with bronze installations and green plants. Try tea and bagels  they are tasty.
It's nice to walk around and see the different bears and the history of the bears. Admission is a good price but the gift shop is a bit pricey.

It's a wonderful botanical garden with many flowers and trees in natural jeju island atmosphere in Korea.Camellia flowers blooming in February are abundant throughout Camellia Hill garden. Its owner Mr. Yang has spent enormous amount time and financial resources to create build and improve the garden as one of the best attractions in Jeju Island.  There are many stone sculptures well maintained hiking trails green houses resting areas and a tea and gift shop the visitors can enjoy and take beautiful pictures.  It's located very near to Jeju Shinwha World Resort with many great hotels and restaurants.  It's a real gem place you should not miss along with Hanrim Botanical Park in Gumnung Beach area in Jeju Island.

It looks like it has been abandoned for years  it has very nice artwork but it is also very dirty. The bathroom was disgusting. The gift shop smelled like cigarettes and had puddles of water every where. And the staff looked extremely bored and uninterested. I came at night so maybe the daytime is better. How ever I don't recommend it  definitely not worth the $8 per person day or night. (Got some nice pictures though)

It is really great how many things you can see on Jeju for less than $3 a person. We did not climb to the top but went into the park to the left to see the cliffs and get a closer look. You only have to walk a little to see a lot. Ample parking and coffee shops nearby. It was so beautiful despite the crowd. It was rainy and windy. Raincoats are sold in the gift shop.

It is not tourist attraction but great place for a conference  inside you have seven eleven and gift shop - I would advice this gift shop with nice sweets  tangerines and black garlic. Tangerines are the best from this Island!

It is hard to say anything good about this place. Basically  it is a small chocolate gift shop that charges $3 a person to enter. You receive a coupon good for $3 back on any purchase. I suppose it is their way to ensure that you buy something.The only interesting thing was that they had these cookie balls that you smashed with a hammer to eat.

It had rained heavily the night before our arrival which meant that it was very slippery inside the lava tunnel and water was dripping constantly which also formed puddles throughout the path.It is also very dark.  There are some lights but not enough to clearly see the terrain below you.  We got to the 300km marker and decided to turn back because we were trying to avoid twisting our ankles.  The lava flow creates interesting striations and grooves which does not result in an easy stroll through the tunnel.The walk may be less treacherous if the tunnel was dry but this is one attraction that should not be attempted by people with mobility issues.The one good thing is that there is a nice gift shop on the grounds which also serves snacks.  Clean bathrooms.
Interesting museum. Worth going. Summer time can be quite hot if viewing the outdoor displays. Gift shop is right under the greenhouse effect.

Indeed a disappointing experience. Yes  this is just an excuse to get you to the gift shop  but at least they could have made the trip there interesting. The story of chocolate is among the most fascinating in the histories of commodities  but they made it a torture. You will see some exhibits on the history of chocolate  a few displays of old boxes and cases of chocolates  and some needless toy sculptures  but mostly a forgettable experience. You do have to pay a small amount and get a coupon for your chocolate or drink purchase. So  if you are desperate to eat some chocolate  or it's raining heavily outside  or you need quickly some air-conditioning  then give it a try; otherwise  enjoy Jeju's natural scenery and wonders instead.
If you're in the area  check it out. It costs 4 000 Won to get in but they give you a coupon worth 3 000 Won to use in the gift shop.

review: If your a fan of everything green tea like my daughter is this is a great place to visit extensive gift shop and resteraunt selling everything you can imagine from the company great background n pics of the history of the place and outside see tea fields and sculptures.

If you want to see a bunch of boxes of chocolate from all over the world  this is the place for you. The 3000 won you pay to enter gives you a discount to what you can buy there so if you want to buy chocolate you won't feel ripped off  but you can buy the same chocolate in any gift shop for the same price. There are a lot of great places on Jeju. I wouldn't go out of your way to visit here.

I visited this place at night and really enjoyed it. You should definitely have your camera with you and ready to get lots and lots of dirty photos with the sculptures made for you to fit in. It also has a small sex shop and an exhibition. Within the park you will also find a casual gift shop.Fantastic place and definitely a must for couples!

I visited this as part of an inclusive tour.  This is really interesting.  there is the story of tea and you can walk among the tea bushes.  This is the best Korea tea there is and of course you can buy their products and sample green tea foods in the cafe. Their sister beauty products company Innesfree also has a cafe and gift shop.  Again these products have a hig reputation in S. Korea.  I would have liked more time to spend here.  The main cafe was packed and I would have like to have had green tea and green tea cake or green tea ice cream but I wouldn't have been able to see anything else in the time we had.  A pleasant place to visit for a few hours.

I cant say this was a museum because majority of the building is dedicated to the gift shop and cafe.  They do have a small plantation across the street as well as an innisfree store next to it.  Apparently their green tea ice cream is a must try.  I thought transportation wise it was a little difficult to get to.

Exotic Jeju Island is known for many things: the majestic Hallasan--the massive shield volcano that formed the island and the highest point in South Korea; its mandarin groves; persimmon-dyed galot fashions; the sturdy Jeju ma horses  descended from the ponies of Mongol invaders; tasty black pork; and the iconic haenyeo women divers. But most visitors would not expect to find a Museum of African Art there. And  it's pretty darn good! Located in a massive structure modeled after the mud-brick Great Mosque of Djenne  the museum offers photo-ops galore in its Safari section  although the animals are of the stuffed variety. Very popular with children and couples. The upper floors house a respectable collection of African artifacts and photographs by Kim Jung Man. There is also a great gift shop. But  I have saved the best for last...the live performance of African folk music and dance. The group  Zalia from Senegal  featured lots of drumming  and audience members also got a drumming lesson and a chance to play along on one song. All in all  a quality experience...and a surprising one.

Enjoyed a couple of hours browsing thru the sea kingdom. Many varieties of fishes and huge aquarium of big fishes and string rays. Shop for souvenirs at the gift shop and some food and drinks at the caf챕. There are beautiful coast behind Aqua Planet which you might want to take stroll for some beautiful photos.
