we were definitely not prepared for this - in terms of experience and equipment!started off at about 9am on the Eorimok route. the entrance was a 10 min walk from the bus stop. then, it was off on the hike!initially the trail was straightforward. then it gradually went into a steep ascent. the path was quite rocky and unstable. but there were sufficient rest stops along the way. also people going in the same and opposite direction to you so you will not be alone (unless you hike in the middle of the night)there were also multiple signboards along the route providing interesting facts about Hallasan and also maps showing your current location and remaining distances to go to the next point.there was almost a natural portable water point where you can refill your bottles. remember to stay hydrated throughout and take breaks when needed.needless to say, the views along the route were truly breathtaking but the higher elevation you reach, the colder it becomes. also, the winds were very strong!we reached the Witseoreum shelter at about 12pm and had lunch there. The locals actually brought hot water in their thermos flasks and had cup ramen there!after lunch, we started our descent on the Yeongsil trail and reached the entrance of Yeongsil at about 2pm and there was a 2km walk out of the entrance to the bus stop.by then our legs were aching and heavy, but we pushed on. overall the hike took about 5 hrs.in summary, we should have worn more proper hiking footwear, wear thicker clothing (as higher you go, the colder it gets) and more food and snacks!we decided we will come back to attempt the summit next time.

We went up the Yeongsil side. Lots of parking cost was 1800 won. You drive about 2kms after paying.  Nice fairly easy walk. Still bits of remaining snow around. I could've done with putting my merino leggings on!  Still, forced me to walk faster!  Haha!

We went to see waterfall at 12PM, there were loads of people, nevertheless view was stunning, waterfall is huge. I'd say better go in day time as when sun is starting to set you'd get weird shadows on your pics and it just won't be the same. Bear in mind you'll have to walk on huge rocks so it's not very safe for toddlers and those carrying their babies, not suitable for those with walking difficulties. Better wear sports clothes which would cover legs in case you fall, to prevent scratches or whatever other injuries. It says no swimming but we took off our shoes and walked in shallow water. It was cold but fun. We also sat on rocks in close proximity to waterfall and splashes from it made us quite wet. But it was spectacular. Such a unique place! Tickets are 1,000 for 16-24 year olds, they require ID. For adults it's 2,000.

We went there on July 17, 2016. We asked the hotel front desk how to get there by public bus, 2 bus numbers to take to the destination. There are plenty of bus for the first leg, but the 2nd bus no. 990 there are only 2 or 3 available in a day and the next one for us like 2 hours away, so the few people/tourists that was there with us decided to walk to the destination for about 3 kilometers. When we got there sweaty and tired we pay the cheap fare of KW2,000 (mind you cheap attraction). The good thing is the cool breeze inside the cave, mind your steps because its wet and some puddle of waters in there. Many people in there, mostly Korean tourists. The few inside the dimly lighted cave is not impressive neither beautiful as I thought. When we got out at about 4:30 pm. we happened to catch the bus no. 990, to our surprise the bus driver told us to get out of the bus while he let the Korean passengers in. We asked why and he keep telling us taxi..taxi..taxi.. So apparently, he does not take foreigners to go to the next bus stop and forced us to take taxi, sure enough, a taxi driver in the area approached us. I felt so discriminated by the bus driver, we didn't even want to negotiate with the taxi driver (because, I believe they do this on purpose). We decided to walk back 3 km. to the next bus stop. It was a waste of almost a day of our time, definitely not recommended to visit this place, NOW I KNOW WHY IT'S CHEAP!

We walked up the Gwanmeusan Trail, only 20 minutes from downtown Jeju-si. It took us, going slowly with lots of rests about 9.5 hours. Good hiking shoes required. We witnessed multiple shoe failures. You have to hike back down shoeless if your shoes rip apart and they will due to the volcanic rocks used on the rrail. The rocks are cute until they aren't. They are murder on the feet, ankles, knees, and legs on the way down.We went in April 20 and it was warm... only one water stop about 3/4 way up.18+ miles round trip. Please ask questions if you have concerns. It is quite breathtaking but a strenuous hike. Many turn back early. Must make it to the Samgakbong shelter by 12:30. No support on the trail.... 2 bathrooms though about 1/4 and 3/4 way up. Must start return hike by 2PM... still took us 4 hours to down due to strenuous terrain and infinite number of stairs.

We walked the Eorimok Trail and it is a well maintained trail with signage all along the way that keeps you informed about how far you have gone, how far you have to go and categorizes the slope into three levels of difficulty (red=steep; yellow=moderate slope; green=gentle slope). It took us 2 hours to get to the tea house (Nambyrok Junction) from the parking lot at the base.  Even though we didn't go to the summit, there are beautiful views all along the trail. While this isn't a mountain climbers kind of trail, it is the tallest mountain in South Korea. My legs were sore for a week afterwards and I am in good shape. Be advised:  About 2/3s of the trail has big trees and good shade; there is no water along the trail; there are emergency phones every several hundred meters; and there is a single track 5-10m off the trail that looks like it would be used for emergency evacuation.
We visited the falls as a group accompanying my parents-in-law s this was one of the places they visited on their honeymoon 50 years ago, yes!It was a privilege to visit and share with them.

We like to hike.  Our idea of hiking is day trips and not super remote.  A 4-6 hour hike in a California Redwood state park is a good example.We took about 6 of the 20+ trails on the south and east coasts.  Every one was different and interesting in its own way.  We stayed in Jung-Mun on the south side.  Terrific little town with hole in wall places with tasty, healthy, cheap food and good bus transportation.These hikes were a little different from our standard in that they often took more than 6 hours. They also could dip in and out of populated areas. We liked that because we might trip across a restaurant run by old lady divers or an archery club doing target practice.  Most trails were not at all crowded. The worst was part of a trail where a Korean soap opera was filmed. It is hard to describe the Korean style of friendliness. They are very direct.  Example was a man at a bus stop who figured we were going to have difficulty getting to our destination. So he flagged a taxi, allegedly for himself, and invited us to hop on.  When we figured out what he was doing, we insisted on paying.  He refused. We got out, gave the driver money, he grabbed it and gave it back. We tossed the money into the window. He grabbed it again, tossed it back on the street and had the driver zip off.  There we were, picking up our money off the pavement. Anybody who has watched Koreans fight over who gets to pay the bill at a restaurant knows what I am saying. To Americans it looks like a hot argument when in fact it's best friends being best friends.  My advice is enjoy it but don't always loose the argument - sometimes you have to win and pay the bill.  This time we really tried but he was too clever for us;-)

We engaged a Jeju Korean driver at 180,000 won per day for 2 full days to bring the 9 of us around for sightseeing in Jeju. On the first day, the guide headed to the attractions in the north and east of Jeju and on the second day, he covered attractions in the south and west of the island. Oedolgae was located at the southern part of Jeju at Seougwipo city. We came to view Oedolgae on the second day afternoon. It was free entrance. From the car park where we alighted from our van, there was a signboard that indicated Oedolgae was 250 m away from the car park. As we strolled our way to the cliff area, I noticed that this attraction was crowded with many tourists and everyone was trying to take good photos by standing at the barricaded area overlooking the azure seawater with the 20 m tall Oedolgae rock as the background. The scenery was amazing. Our guide spoke good Mandarin and he told us of the mystical tragic sorrowful legend of a saddened wife who feared the death of her beloved husband jumped into her death on seeing the body of her husband flushed to the coast. The Oedolgae rock was the embodiment of the wife who had committed suicide and the base of the rock represented the body of her husband. The sad story dampened my spirit momentarily but the awesome view of the stunning rock blended seamlessly with the azure sea and the clear blue sky. The fresh cooling sea breeze that caressed my face lifted my spirits and the next moment I found myself squeezing among the crowd to take good pictures with my group members against the picturesque backdrop. As we strolled along the weaving coastline, we viewed the Oedolgae from different perspective and each angle projected a captivating scenery. At one point was a big board depicting the picture of popular Korean drama show Dae Jang Geum (Jewel in the Palace) and of the famous Korean actress Lee Young-ae who acted as the great Palace female physician during the Joseon Dynasty. This place was the filming location of this popular traditional korean drama.  I really like this place. It is so picturesque and I was totally immersed in the magnificent scenery appreciating that rhythmic splashing of the seawater against the high cliff. That short juncture, the clock stood still and I just could not believe my eyes that I was standing and facing such a fairy like breathtaking natural attraction.

We did the seongpanak trail. Check the weather the day before embarking, and make sure you have proper hiking shoes as the climb is rocky and some parts are pretty steep. Stretch your muscles before the climb or you'll end up sore the next day (or you can tote along some muscle rub)! Bug spray is also recommended, for those prone to mosquito bites. Try to get an early start if you can; as you have to pass the second rest stop before 1.00pm if you want to make it to the summit, otherwise the staff will not allow you to proceed. On average you would take 7-8 hours to hike to the summit and back, depending on the number of rest stops you make. There are 2 rest shelters along the way (one selling food like cup noodles and choco pie, pocari sweat and bottled water). There are toilets at both rest stops, but no water; no washing hands or flushing systems. Generally, the climb path is divided into thirds - beginning (relatively easy, mostly uneven but flat ground) - first rest stop - second leg (rocky ground, with some portions made up of many steps) - second rest stop - final leg (fair warning it gets really tough for beginners, as the terrain gets pretty rocky and steep) - summit!

We did the hike up the Summit via the 8.7km Gwaneumsa Trail and down via the 9.6km Seongpanak Trail. Though parts of the Trail are marked deceptively yellow and green (  easy  ), we couldn't feel our legs for 3 days thereafter. Very rocky/uneven terrain at most parts of the Trail - challenging without the aid of hiking poles. Good hiking boots is a definite must. Please note there is a specific cut-off time at each Trail checkpoint (which may differ depending on season) and also a specific cut-off time to descend from the Summit. Hence, it is recommended to start as early as possible. We started at 8am and completed around 7.30pm (which was getting really dark by then). Though tiring, the hike is still the highlight of our Jeju trip and memorable for many reasons. The feeling of walking above the clouds (at 1,950m) and having accomplished such a challenging hike is priceless.

We did the Gwaneumsa trail up Mount Hallasan to the peak and back is over 18 miles round trip, over 3500 feet of climbing and then descending it. But it's worth it. I offer only a few points of advice. It is tougher, 800m longer, but more scenic than the Seongpanak trail. To find the Gwanmeusa trail entrance parking lot, plug in the number for the Unesco Hallasa Gwaneumsa Office: +82-64-756-9950 (you only need the last 7 digits on Jeju GPS systems if driving).1) Be prepared with good hiking and walking shoes. We saw two shoes blow out, one about 2.5 hours in. The poor guy had to walk back. There is no rescue if this happens. Also, a girl's shoe blew out on the way down about 3/4 way down, it still nearly 1.5 hours to the end depending on how slow you go. I will discuss in #3 why good shoes are so important.2) Go early, and go slow if you are not in shape or do not do activities often. Hallasan is definitely attainable by nearly anyone but it is tough, very tough because of the steep steps. Unless you are in shape and do many physical activities all the time, I recommend starting at 6AM. You MUST be at Samgakbong shelter by 12:30PM otherwise they will turn you around. It is 3/4 way up the climb. From here it is another 2 hours to the peak of the Halla.3. The volcanic stone paths and the stairs will make your legs very very tired and your feet sore. I believe they made Gwanmeusa trail challenging with rocks on purpose. These are not small rocks, they are big ones that challenge each step. Walking sticks are highly recommended. The stones seem pretty and authentic until halfway up then they are tough. Then on the way down, each step seems like a sadistic joke played by the planners. Eventually you will be relieved to make it to the bottom to your car or bus.4. Be prepared for wind. We got lucky and it was warm the day we went... in fact low warm temperatures will seem even warmer due to humidity about 1/2 the time up the mountain and back. It is a little cooler and windier at the top. Wear light, polyester clothing in layers. long sleeve tech shirt, with light jacket and light rain cover. You should be OK. Gloves and hat or scarves during cooler time. Very light during summer due to heat and humidity.After you get down on Gwanmeusa trail, there is a small restaurant with Korean snacks like pajeon and gimbap, as well as a 7/11 next door. Drink some local mokkoli or soju with with the hot snacks/food! We had a great time. Only 20 minutes out Jeju City when there is no traffic. However with rush hour traffic, or busy time it takes about 45 minutes to get back into Jeju City.

We approximate the climb to be about 2,200 steps. So about an hour  to get up and down. The view while climbing to the top is breathtaking. You get a 360 degree view of Jeju. The stairs for climbing are easy for short legs like mine. They've got railings for you to hold on to and some rest points every so often. There are speakers located in certain areas as well to tell you the history of the place in Korean and Japanese. I'm pretty sure there's an English and Chinese version too. There's a person at the top too to give you some information regarding the place. There are some shops located at the foot of the place where you can eat and shop as well. The journey to the top was better than the view of what was on top.

Walking along the path (towards the Oedolgae Rock) was one of the highlights (since this was the final stop) of our Jejueco Tour. Being almost right next to the sea and surrounded by nature, it was a good place to take photos with its awesome coastal views, clear sea blue waters and ocean breeze in the background. There is no admission charge to see the Oedolgae Rock, which is located on the Seogwipo side of the island. However, I think if you purposely made an effort just to visit the Oedolgae Rock, you might be a little underwhelmed, because it is after all just a lone rock that stands at 20m high and surrounded by sea. What made the difference was the mystical legend that surrounds the Oedolgae Rock as well as the scenery that greets you when you walk along the path that weaves its way along the coast, allowing you to view the Oedolgae Rock, which is also known as the Lonely Rock, from different angles. The area that surrounds the Oedolgae Rock is apparently the filming location of the Korean drama series, Jewel in the Palace (鸚㏝룝).For more of my experience and photos, please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/03/oedolgae-rock-and-great-sea-view.html

Very beautiful place. Nice people, peaceful place. I want to come next time to visit it once more. We took photo with the founder of this garden. He is very nice person. In the garden you can see bansai trees and feed fishes, also there are some mini shops and cafe were you can drink coffee or the legendary rice wine.

Up & down of the mountain took us 9.5 hours including some short rest time during the hike. We started the hike around 9am (recommend to start early, we were late), and came down around 6:30pm. Our legs were like jelly legs after the hike, but is worth the hike. You can see nice view along the journey. Please do not forget to greet everyone you met with   anyeonghaseyo  , they are all very friendly people. Wear a pair of good hiking shoes, bring some snacks with you and also water. The stalls along the mountain are closed during our hike, luckily we have prepared enough snacks and water. The view at the peak is breathless. A lots of old korean aunties and uncles also managed to reach the peak, so I guess we all younger than them have no excuses of not fit to hike, right? haha...Wear sport attire, although some said it will be freezing cold at the peak (about 1950 meters height), but believe me, you wont feel cold as you have already all sweat during the hike. We spent about 30mins to 1 hour at the peak taking photos, resting and having our snacks before going down again. A pair of good hiking shoes is important so that you won't get blister on your feet. We will go back again in different season if we have the chance. We were travelling there in Oct 2018.

Unless one is interested in its history or legend about how the 3 holes came about, there is nothing much to explore. The compound is rather small and quiet, just a handful of visitors. In one pavilion is a 3D multimedia presentation, lasting 14 mins, which explains the legend behind these 3 holes. Unfortunately, visitors cannot get close to these holes, hence have to view from afar. 30 minutes is sufficient to cover this place, admission fees 2,500 won.Recommend to drop by only you have spare time to kill or already nearby. Else can skip this place.

Udo is like a big kids playground. You rent an electric scooter and scoot around this fun little island. We looped it in about an hour and a half, stopping for iced cream. The rental was 3 hours and so we explored the middle of the island off the beaten path. You cant really get lost and apple maps or navient works great (so does cell phone data). Some expert tips:Get the ?Harley Davidson? 2 man bike.Its rain covered, and you wont get too hot like the enclosed units. Adjust the seat forward (lever under your leg) to free up some space behind your seat for your bagOnce you get your scooter, scoot scoot! Everyone follows the same clockwise loop around the island. Open that throttle and pass those dottling tourists. Udo Awaits!Use your horn, and folks let you pass. Beep Beep!Skip the first two big pulloffs where everyone stops. Its way too crowded and you may have to pay to park! Watch for the big bus! It runs opposite motorcycle traffic and takes up most of the narrow roadway. So dont drive in the middle of the motorway. The bus driver is very safe and watches for confused motorcyclists. It was very safe.Otherwise, beep beep, scoot scoot, and enjoy the Electric Scooterland of Udo!

Took eight to nine hours to complete the hike via the gentler route. View at the top is really amazing you'll get to see a beautiful crater lake which sadly we're not allowed to go further down to. Terrain is mad crazy so make sure you're in good footwear made for hiking. Bring plenty of foot, water and a deep heat in case your aches/injuries act up (which most likely will). Be prepared as this hike will definitely take a toll on your legs which will hurt for days after the hike. Update boards can be seen along the way, the terrain is labelled and broken down into easy, normal and difficult segment. BUT, DO NOT BE FOOLED! The normal terrain is just as tough as the difficult terrain. Big boulder of rocks which are freakinggggg steeeeep! Trekking poles will definitely come in useful! If you intend to hike here, be prepared for an arduous journey, smelly puke-inducing restrooms at the two pitstops all in return for a spectacular view at the peak. A really good once in a lifetime experience, no regrets but I will defo not do it again. hahaha

To reach the waterfall from the parking area (free parking), you need to go down the stairs (not a lot of steps, but in my opinion, the steps could be quite steep). During my visit, there were a lot of school / college students, so the waterfall area were quite crowded. The view itself is actually quite spectacular, but as there were too many people that time, we decided to stay for around 15 minutes only.

To be honest, I wasn't quite sure what to expect before I saw this show. I knew generally it was about performers who drew and entertained the audience somehow on stage. BUT IT WAS AMAZING! We saw   Team Chaplin,   four   hunky   young men, all dressed in decidedly stylish paint-splattered black clothing, complete with Charlie Chaplin bowlers. It could best be described as a multi-media show in which the performers draw using charcoal, paint, LED touch screens (I think!) and other art mediums and techniques to create a wide variety of images from pop culture and the classics, most of it set to contemporary music. They dance plus do a little martial arts, mime and comedy, and they use audience participation very effectively. Among the images are Michael Jackson, the Little Mermaid, Bruce Lee, Beethoven and Jeju's own icon, Dolhareubang, or   Stone Grandfather.   Even after seeing the show, I am not sure how some of the effects were achieved. I'm not going to do any   spoilers   here of the action, because the element of surprise is important for this show. But trust me, you WILL be surprised. It has many entertaining moments. If you live in Jeju or plan to visit, you should make time for the show, which is performed on the campus of beautiful Cheju Halla College...you'll be treated there to one of the best views of Halla Mountain anywhere on the island...take your camera for that, and for the photo/autograph session at the end of the show.

TLDR:Long hike, not that easy if you're not fit. 8-9 hours, 19.6km in total.Bring at least 3L of water each. They do sell water at the checkpoint, though only in 600ml bottles.Wear shoes with good sole and ankle protectionConsider taking a small towel (or two) to wipe away sweatBring a warm jumper and possibly a clean, dry shirt. Even in summer it's cold at the topStart the hike before 8.30am if you want to reach the peak because if you don't make it past the checkpoint at around 7km in, before 12.30pm, you won't be allowed to go to the peak.Bring a plastic bag for your rubbish because there are no bins at all on the hikeFor those who want moreRemember that this hike is longer than an average work day and you will need to replace water lost through sweat. Pack around 3L of water per person. Also pack some protein and carbohydrate heavy snacks such as nuts and dried fruits to keep up your energy levels. If you sweat a lot, consider bringing an electrolyte drink sachet to use halfway (or buy a can of Pocari sweat at the checkpoint). At the checkpoint, you can buy instant noodles, 600mL water bottles and Pocari sweat. If you don't want noodles for lunch, bring lunch. But keep in mind it's cold at the top so some warm noodles can be perfect. The noodles are a bit spicy though, so if you don't like spicy food, maybe bring your own lunch. There are absolutely 0 facilities for heating or preparing food. They won't even give you hot water for any noodles you don't purchase from them. Also there are no rubbish bins on the entire hike so you'll need to bring a plastic bag to carry out your own rubbish. The toilets are pretty gross and may or may not have toilet paper so consider bringing tissues. Also the toilets generally have no sinks, so bring some hand sanitiser gel.A small towel or two to wipe away your sweat wouldn't go astray, and a warm coat/jacket and clean, dry shirt will make your time at the peak much more comfortable (addressed in a later section).We took the 781 bus from Jeju city hall at around 6.55am. We arrived at the Seongpanak stop around 7.25am.Make sure you give yourself enough time to get to the Jindallae Shelter (checkpoint around 7km into the hike) before 12.30pm. If you don't make it to the shelter before 12.30pm you will not be allowed to continue up to the peak. It's very disappointing, I'm sure, to hike for 7km, hoping to see the peak and then be told you can't go because you missed the 12.30 deadline. I can't stress this enough. At the shelter, we heard some Americans complaining that they had missed the deadline by 24 minutes (they had started the hike at 10.30am) and that there was no information available on the trail or online about this rule. They were wrong on two counts- there are at least 5 signs along the trail up to the shelter stating that you need to pass by 12.30pm (in English). Also there are a number of blogs about this hike online which also talk about the rule. Now we started at around 7.30am and made it to the shelter by 10am, but we didn't stop to rest at all before the shelter. The walk up to the shelter is 90% easy level with gentle slopes and a few short harsher sections. If you are fit enough to contemplate doing a 19.4km hike then this section should be fine for you. If you start the hike around 8.30am, you will have no issues making it to the checkpoint in time and you should make it back to the bottom by 6/6.30pm. Earlier if you don't rest too long and are relatively fit.Note: there are several places that you can stop to rest just after the shelter. If you are running close to the 12.30pm deadline, just get past the shelter and then stop to rest once you've gone past. Just make sure you don't rest too long because you've probably got another 5-6 hours before you get back to the end of the trail including the rest of the walk to the peak, and you don't want it to get dark or have to rush on the way down.The next section after the shelter is graded as 'normal' by the signs along the route. This section does have a few challenging sections but also some easier stretches as well. If you have regular short rests then it's manageable for people of minimal to moderate fitness with some huffing and puffing.The last 1-1.5km of the walk to the peak is where it starts to get difficult. By this stage you've already hiked uphill around 8km and for probably 3-3.5 hours. The way to the peak is hundreds and hundreds of stairs often with many oddly shaped rocks to navigate around whilst traversing increasingly steep steps. If you're not super fit then you will struggle on this section. At one point we were setting ourselves goals to make it up 3 sets of staircases before we would rest for 1 minute then start again. But the important point is you are so close to the top now, so just keep pushing.The top can be quite crowded. We made it by around 11.30am and hung around for about 30mins to take photos and admire the view. My next piece of advice is- bring a warm jumper because the wind is cold up there and if you're anything like me, you will be sweaty which makes the wind even colder. Another point: if you're a sweaty person, consider bringing an extra dry/warm shirt (or two) with you to change into at the top (and possibly on the way back down). If you're prone to sweat a lot, this can make a huge difference to your enjoyment at the peak because you will by dry and warm. Your photos won't look so sweaty either. Make sure you take a picture of all members of your party with the peak stone marker or the crater to prove that you reached the top.Keep in mind that the way back down can take longer than the way up because you are now passing many people on their way up and going down is very hard on your already exhausted legs and feet. It can take 4-5 hours to get back down from the peak. We started going down at 12pm and made it to the bottom by 4pm, but we stopped several times.The path is quite narrow so on your way down, you will have to stop to let people pass in the other direction many times (unless it's significantly past the 12.30pm deadline, in which case everyone will be going down). The section between the peak and the checkpoint is very hard on your feet and legs. It will feel like forever but just remember that the track gets gradually easier and gentler the closer you are to the end. Stop at the checkpoint for lunch if you haven't already had it, or you feel like some hot noodles to warm you up.Keep on all the way down, being very careful not to slip. There are many rocks and if they are slightly wet, they are very slippery. Eventually you'll make it to the bottom. Then you can take your photographic evidence of reaching the peak to the little tourist office and for 1000 won each, you'll get a certificate saying that you reached the 1950m summit of Mt Hallasan. Congratulations!Sore feet and legs and weary bodies, you can catch the 782 bus back to Jeju city for a well earned rest.

Tips & things to take note:- Bring LOTS of water. On average 2litres per pax.- Bring sufficient food - basically breakfast,lunch,dinner.- Got to reach the checkpoint by 1pm to be allowed to attempt summit- Got to start descent from summit by 2.30pm- Gets cold and windy at the peak so bring a windbreaker.- You have to carry your own trash down. No bins on the mountain at all.We took 11hours and took the Seongpanak trail up and Gwaneumsa trail down. Seongpanak is easiest as its gentler but its the longest trail. Gwaneumsa is much more scenic. We were beginner hikers and hence probably took longer. The tourist  centre told us it would take ~9hrs. Spotted a deer on our way down on the Gwaneumsa trail. It was pretty scary though, we walked for 1hr+ without spotting a single human. (probably cause we were slow)My legs ached for 4 days straight but I have no regrets. My knees and ankles were insanely sore by the end of the hike. If you've even the slightest knee/leg issues, please think THRICE before you attempt Hallasan.Also, toilets are only available at the bottom (before the hike) and at the checkpoint. The toilets are GROSS. I couldn't do it no matter how hard I tried. Toilet was damp and stinky and lots of flies. No water system & its a squat system for ladies. Basically peeing into a hole filled with other people's waste. Saw another lady peeing in the woods instead...Also, all the announcements are in Korean, though signboards are in English.Aim to start hiking by 7am-8am. Any later, you may not reach checkpoint/summit in time unless you have a good enough stamina.Hiking sticks and shoes would help tremedously. Though we did it with regular sneakers. LOTS OF BUGS. Bring insect repellent though again, we didn't have one.Overall, its worth it and wouldn't do it again but have no regrets.

This was defiantly a must do event for Jeju! We thought it would be easier than it was. Towards the top it gets very steep and with all the snow and ice it can be quite challenging, especially since we were only wearing regular footwear and no crampons or even hiking shoes!We made it and 3 days later our legs still hurt but was worth the struggle! It took us 3.5 hours each way including stops but not including the time at the very top, which was almost an hour. So 8 hours total!

This was a really enjoyable hike up the highest mountain in South Korea @ 1950m, and I recommend it as a great experience of the outdoors and physical activity.  However I saw a lot of people (both locals and foreigners) struggling with various aspects so please take note of the following points:WEATHER:  If you have the flexibility of several days from which to select, review the weather in advance and aim to choose the best day.....otherwise for example you may have no views when you emerge from the trees and at the summit.TIME, PACE & TIME-LIMITS:  This is a long hike, 19.2km round trip to be exact or about 12 miles, but is a relatively gentle incline.  The general consensus in many reviews is that it should take 10 hours total including breaks and lunch.  I would consider myself slightly above average fitness and took 6 hours total, however being solo it makes a difference because I could walk at my own brisk pace and take breaks (typically quite short 5-10 mins) when I wanted.  There are 2 shelters (with toilets) on the route located at approx 4km and 7km, and it's very important to note that for safety reasons they do not allow anyone past the second shelter (which is 2.3km from the summit) AFTER 13-00 HRS, no exceptions.  Furthermore everyone must depart the summit to start descending by 14-30 HRS latest.  I did come across quite people between the 2 shelters who appeared to be rushing to make the 13-00 deadline.  This is not recommended because either you could push yourself too hard and get exhausted, or get injured walking on the rocks, or simply miss the deadline.  FOOTWEAR:  At minimum bring sturdy training or trekking shoes, preferably hiking boots to provide ankle support. Some sections of the hike are on hessian mats and wooden walk ways which of course are very nice to walk on, however probably 30% or more is on large volcanic rocks which are not comfortable to walk on and requires some focus and concentration (especially descending when your legs are tired).  I was surprised to see some walking in sandals and they suffered.  A walking stick can be helpful but is not essential.DAYPACK:  Bring a small daypack to carry water, snacks, clothes etc and to keep your hands free.  Even in summer bring a light jacket or sweater because it can get cool at the top with the wind and elevation.  In Winter I'm sure it's really cold at the summit.PROTECTION:  Bring a hat for the higher elevations (when not in the forest), sun cream and lip balm.HYDRATION/SNACKS:  There is reportedly a source of mountain water half way up but personally I did not see it near the sign, and staff at one of the shelters advised me that no water is available.  Hence suggest that you bring at least 3-4 bottles of water or isotonic drink in your day pack per person (maybe 1.5 to 2 litres), and be sure to conserve it wisely because you'll need some on the way down.  I encountered some people on the way up who had no water left.  Muesli bars, chocolate and fruit are good sources of energy.  As well as fruit, the locals tend to pack rice & meat lunches and have communal picnics at the summit.TRANSPORT:  I used a rental car and got there early, before 8am.  The car park was already full and people started parking on both sides of the main road, which is allowed.  The bus stops are right there beside the car park for those using public transport.CERTIFICATE:   There is small office hidden away near the Seongpanak car park which will print your name on a nice certificate for 1000 Won. (US$1).IN SUMMARY: Please take the time to prepare properly and get there reasonably early so that you can enjoy the hike at your own pace.  During the walk I saw several deer, lots of beautiful butterflies and other insects and loved the great views ....Jeju is covered in 300+ volcanic cones so its amazing to see all of these.  HAVE A GREAT DAY ON HALLASAN!

This three tier waterfall is one of the three waterfalls in Jeju, the other two being Cheonjiveon and Jeongbang waterfalls. The forest surrounding the waterfall has been designated as a natural monument and as per Korean legend seven nymphs bath at the pond of this waterfall in the night.Located at a walkable distance from Seogwipo Harbour, the visit to this attraction calls for climbing of stairs. So avoid this place if you hate to climb steps. For others a good pair of shoes is a must.

This rock has the legend of a beautiful wife praying for a loving husband who has gone missing when fishing. When you look you may find the shape of a lady praying with a man on the bottom with a big tummy. Even more impressive is the walk around the coastal nature. It is considered to be number one walking trail in Jeju, Ollegil no. 7.

This place is big and we didn?t go through each inch of this place as both of us felt tired when came to this place. If you have time and the leg can support the walk, a good place to spend time with.

This museum is 90% in Korean but as they say some things are easier to understand. In the beginning the museum starts out with some interesting if broad sex-positive history. It's sex and HEALTH however so there's info about AIDS as well as misconceptions about sex and sexual health. Towards the middle of the museum it starts to go off the rails a little bit. The   Fantasy   section is a lot of chintzy garbage and mannequins in lewd/bizarre positions and tableaus. It doesn't add anything it moreso detracts from the legitimacy established in the first half. Only go if you're stuck with a rainy day. Otherwise you'd be better off enjoying Jeju's natural wonders.

This is probably my first 1-star review on TA. Much regretted visit and the only saving grace is that this place is right next to the Osulloc Tea Museum. We were drawn to this place after very good experience at the Innifree Green Cafe at Myongdong and we expected the same (if not better) at this concept store.Product - any Innisfree shops in myeongdong or duty free can offer you a better range at much better price. As Jeju was the last leg of my trip, I was planning to make most of my innisfree purchase in this store but they don?셳 carry much range here. I don?셳 remember there was onsite tourist refund as well (like how it is in Myeongdong) - another reason not to plan your shopping here.Food - I ordered a 18000krw main dish (named herdsman?) with some cold sausages, potato mash, rice balls and orange. The presentation was really pretty but it tasted nothing special. If you are looking for good looking food and great taste at the same time, you have better chance at Myongdong innisfree Green cafe. The other two pretty drinks we ordered were not worth a mention as well. Service - We were there at 450pm and all the soap making stations were occupied. We were told by a staff the soap making would only take 15mins and the place would close at 6pm. so we decided to wait at the cafe and return when the crowd lessen. At 525pm, a staff stopped me at the cashier when I tried to purchase the soap making set. She said that they have closed the soap making station at 520pm. And then another staff came by and said the station was closed at 5pm (?!). I am not sure exactly what time the station closed as there was no sign in the store and the staff were telling different things. The store closed at 6pm sharp and the staff can?셳 wait to have all the guests out by then - this I am sure. This place is a sad contrast to the Osulloc Tea Museum next door.

This amazing landscape is a must place to go when you visit Jeju. You have to climb up to see the creater and do not worries, just prepare you leg for a stairs (a lot of stairs hahaha). You better wear a comfortable shoes. when i came was sunny, temperature around 18C but the wind was strong, it makes my hair messy & runny nose (prepare face masker will help). The scenery along the way was refreshing & amazing, you will not disapointed.

There is not much to see on the way to the top. Remember it's a 19k hiking and you need to use your time wisely in a day. We went on a cloudy day. It wasn't too hot but the hiking was difficult with rocks covering most of the roads. So get yourself a real pair of hiking shoes! My feet got hurt and it was slippery after rain. Some parts have stairs, which are highly appreciated... The top view was great but maybe it was dry, we did not see water in the crate. Spring and Fall might have more to see. My friend and my legs have been hurting since we accomplished it...

There are only 2 trails that lead to the peak of Hallasan. Gwaneumsa and seongpanak trail. We took the seongpanak trail up and gwaneumsa trail down. It was no easy hike for sure. It took us 10 hours to hike up and back down ( late 20's, amateur!). We thought we give it a go and hike all the way to the peak since we were there. The scenery was breathtaking and definitely worth the hike. autumn foliage was amazing (but our leg muscles were aching real bad the next day). tons of people though. best to start the hike early about 6.30am if you wish to reach the top and if you are an amateur hiker with not-so-active lifestyle. be well prepared with adequate clothing, proper shoes and snacks

The waterfall is rather small, but it is almost in the middle of a city. When you arrive you will be on top of the cliff in which Jeongbang flows off of. Located near Seogwipo city, Jeongbang Waterfall is 23 meters high and is very close to the sea. This is why people tell that the water falls directly into the ocean. A legend says that servant of Emperor Jin of China, called as Seo Bul, sent to the area in order to search the magical herb of eternal youth in Mount Halla. People interested in seafood can taste fresh abalone sashimi with garlic slices & hot pepper paste as dipping. It is offered by ajummas, who collect them directly at this spot. Don쨈t forget to wear good shoes to avoid becoming a casualty.

The trails to the sight were well marked and easy to walk. There is no entrance fee and the view at the end is spectacular. It?s totally worthwhile. Be wary of the elderly gentlemen at the car park collecting a parking fee of 2000Won, it?s not legit because the sign at the carpark says it?s free parking. I wonder why the local authorities have not acted on this.

The park is the mystical legend of how three gods arrived in Jeju-do and started to develop the island. The place is a great escape from the busy city of Jeju, surrounded with trees and pavilion of traditional Korean architecture. You can also sit in for a 15 minutes long animation, available both in English and Korean  describing the origins of Jeju.

The park covers a vast area. One has to decide how far you wish to explore and watch your time. A map is given at the ticket counter and we did not expect it to be so big. We went according to the numbered stops. The view was spectacular for some parts of the park that we spent so much time on taking pictures. We tried to move quicker however, in the end, we did not even complete Course 1 (there are 3 different routes). It was enjoyable for some walk & laughter. There are scripts on stones to tell you about the legendary story of this stone park. You may decide, whether you want to keep walking and cover the whole park (I am not sure whether this is even possible in a day) or would you just want to have a feel of this peaceful and beautiful park.

The National Park is very peaceful by the time we reached in the afternoon. We tracked the shorter trail 9 stations point, as there is insufficient time for the longer trail. As we walked up the steped trail, enjoyed the woods, stones, freshness. Trail not recommended for those with weak legs - uneven steps. However,  you can still stay at the National Park to enjoy the serene park.

The museum is quite interesting if you're interested in geology.  It's nice to get a decent scientific understanding of how and why the other things you'll likely be seeing on Jeju (Hallasan, Seongsan Ilchulbong, etc.) are the way they are.  If geology bores the heck out of you, then skip the museum, but don't skip the park altogether.  It's really quite a beautiful place to walk around, especially if you're in the mood for something somewhat quiet and relaxing.  Major crowds can make some of the the other sites on Jeju quite the opposite of that, so it's nice to find a place that's legitimately peaceful.
the destination is built by legend about dragon who fall from the earth, as tourist object not much to see. it's nature rock, beach and on autum the weather is nice. no need much time
The cliff is good and legends about it - too :)But couldn't recommend it as   must see   (sorry, Oedolgae!)

The Cheonjeyeon Falls was a memorable last stop of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour. The size of the entire park the falls are situated in is generally small, but it's loaded with so many sights to see. In the entrance, you're immediately greeted with a beautiful pagoda and lush well-kept gardens. There's also a wishing fountain called the Fountain of Five Blessings that's worthy of your participation as the coins tossed inside the fountain are donated to Korea's underprivileged. Entering the site, one has to cross an intricately beautiful bridge which is elegant and regal in its own right. After that, the trek to the falls; sites begins. The entire trek is paved with concrete steps which make it more convenient and safer for visitors, especially as the trek requires ascend and decline quite a lot. Although, be prepared for a light workout as the number of steps do add up if you complete the entire trek (there are quick detours to the exit for those who don't wish to complete the entire trek or those grappling with a fear of heights).Shoutout to our amazing tour guide from Yeha Bus Tour for going the extra mile in making our entire tour enjoyable!

The bridge is beautiful to look at, and provides a nice walk to an island that provides more opportunity to stroll near the water.? Big tourist attraction, and if you prefer staying away from the crowds, you may not enjoy this.? Great picture taking venue, and it doesn't cost anything, except a little workout for your feet and legs.

Seonpanak is known to be the more difficult route, however both to the summit have their difficulties. Seonpanak definitely has nicer views than Gwaneumsa, thats why we chose to walk down this trail, as your back is facing the beauty on the way up. This route has TONS of rocks which make it hard to balance and hike without the proper shoes. There are 4 or 5 base camps, only one offering water, and one with (disgusting) squat toilets. It took about 3 1/2 hours to hike from the summit, to the bottom. My legs are KILLING ME. But, it was worth it!

Really....it is just another rock with a legend.  It seems that everyone turns into rock while waiting for someone....story line is always the same.  If you are a big fan of Korean drama - Daejeonggeum, then this is the place for you.  A lot of tourist stops here....maybe becos it has no admissions fees.  Try and come early in the morning as the tour buses start coming in late morning.

One of my objective in my Jeju trip is to climb Mt. Halla and I did it! Of course it was not an easy trek up and down. I took Seongpanak trail going up the peak which was abt  9.6 km. And took the Gwaneumsa trail on my way down, which was about 8.7 km. I was staying in Seogwipo and I took bus #780 and it dropped me exactly in front of Seongpanak. However, there was no bus at Gwaneumsa, but there were several taxi. You can asked them to dropped you the nearest bus stop going to Jeju. But I think you can walk going there. But as it was raining so hard that afternoon and my legs were about to give up, I took the taxi. But it was quite near and the driver asked me 5000 won (not sure if that was cheap ir not). Dont forget to bring a raincoat and chocolates and sweet for energy while trekking. And if you want some souvenir, you can get a certificate of yout climb (1000 won) at the office. You need a photo at the peak as evidence. But actually, they didnt asked me to show mine, but really I reached the summit! I got 5 pics! :) And mind you, it's better to be in proper trekking attire, because I was not, especially the shoes, so I slipped several times on the snowy parts. Happy trekking!

One of Jeju Island attraction, the rock formations that looks more like a horse head to me. Well, legendary it was a head of a dragon. We stop by for a photo stop on our way to airport.A good nice photographing platform for visitor to take picture. There is a stairway leading down to the rocky beach, down there you can see many locals selling fresh seafood.  It is not a wheelchair friendly place. Be there before sunset otherwise you will not able to take a clear photo.

On entering through the entrance, one comes to the palm tree avenue. Different types of palm trees and cactuses greet you.  Next up is the wild grass and flowers garden. Felt relax walking along the path. Further ahead  are the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves. These 2 caves were formed by an eruption of Mt Halla many years ago. The temperature inside the caves is around 18 degrees celsius throughout the year so walking inside was cooling. Look out for the famed natural monuments, Pillar, Mother , the two dragons up on the roof, stalactites and stalagmites, and Dr. Jin and the fox girl.. Coming out to the cave,Jeju stones greet you gesturing Welcome . Next proceed to Jae-am folk village where one can see thatched  roof houses with stone walls. Do take a photo with the tall statue of Stone Grandfather, Dolharubang.  Next  will be the bird garden where you will see parrots, pheasants, ostriches and elegant peacocks walking around spreading their colourful stunning feathers. The following spot is Jae-am stone exhibit hall  where over 200 stones are displayed. We were amazed by the natural stone sculptures in the shape of  birds and waterfall. Walking on , following the signs, one comes to water garden where you can see 5 beautiful ponds, capped by the grand waterfall.. Finally you will reach the last section, subtropical botanic garden where  there are palm trees, foliage plants, herbs  alongside parrots, lizards, snakes and tortoises. After all the walking and photo taking, proceed to have lunch at Dolharubang restaurant  to try Jeju's traditional foods, like the delicious pork bulgogi. Or you can have freshly made seafood at Palm  Tree Restaurant. Or if you do not wish to lunch, you can enjoy fresh herb beverages at  Herb Cafe.

On a recent vacation in Jeju, I decided to check out the Ramada Plaza Jeju Casino. My visit was in the mid-afternoon, and there were only a handful of casino patrons inside this small casino.When you enter the casino, they ask for your ID, and then they make a photocopy of it. I do not believe that there is a legal requirement for them to photocopy your passport (or in my case, Korean residency card) for their permanent records. Frankly speaking, I was offended by this requirement. To check a visitor’s identification, yes; permanent photocopied record, no.I had the intention of playing some blackjack, but as soon as I saw that they use continuous shuffling machines, I walked out. It is impossible for a blackjack player to gain the tiniest of advantages when such machines are used. My recommendation to blackjack players: don’t waste your time going to this casino.

review: Ok- this place was pretty cool...but here is the deal-- it says   Cave entrance   which makes you think that a   Cave exit   will at some point present itself. It does not. You go a km to the end then turn around. It is bumpy and not well-lit. I am (relatively) young and surefooted, as were my companions, and we all noted that this place could never exist in the US: they would get sued in a minute...someone would fall and break their leg and it would be all over. It was interesting, but for one thing: we had unfortunate timing. We went in with like 5 busloads of extremely loud Chinese teens (mostly male). It was insane, annoying and...after a while, slightly dangerous (they started running past us). There is NO ONE from the cave to be seen in the cave (only an occasional phone...maybe 2 in the entire kilometer distance), so no one was there to even say anything about this. Not horrible, but got old after a while. Once we got some distance between them and us, things improved.Oh and they don't tell you about the spiders until the visitors center afterwards...This is not a place for kids or old people or anyone with unsure footing. I am not exaggerating when I say the ground is totally uneven...and there are random stone blocks scattered about to cover holes or water..it was rather rough walking-- at times it took away from the coolness of the cave because you cannot walk without watching the ground...

Not a difficult climb, but if you haven't worked out in awhile, your legs will definitely feel like jelly on the way down. It took about 20 minutes to hike up the stairs to the top and another 20 minutes to get down. The volcanic cone and the view are totally worth visiting the top for.

No regrets coming here.   The climb up via slopes and steps is quite manageable with some stops in between.   Tho for inactive person like me, legs became a little wobbly as I came down 븝 Windy & cold at times, so better have jackets ready.     We took about 40 mins to ascend, stayed around for 30 mins.    Descend was slightly faster

My wife and I hiked Hallasan last weekend, which was our first trip to Jeju Do. We've lived in Seoul for 5 years and finally made that trip south. We decided to take the Seongpanak Trail since it allows you to get to the top. Overall, the hike was great - beautiful scenery (although it was a hazy day for us so visibility was limited), challenging hike and it's something that will take up a whole day. We took a different trail down once we reached the top and the views were nicer on that one. I think there are only two trails that go all the way up. We're not hikers by any means so our legs were pretty tired on the way down the mountain. They estimate 8-9 hours total but we did it in 7! Be sure to pack some snacks and water as there's not much available on the hike. There's a small place at a checkpoint a couple hours into the Seongpanak trail where you can get some water, ramen and chocolate bars (along with some basic hiking gear) but don't expect much. We had only taken water with us (rookie mistake) and I was wishing for some extra snacks on the way down. There's also a store/small restaurant at the first entrance to the hike so you can stock up there. Overall, it's definitely worth doing as its one of the main attractions on Jeju.

My husband and I consider ourselves pretty fit people, we regularly run and ski seasonally but we were impressed at the older Korean folks who visited the same track we did!We visited the Eorimok Trail which was advertised as a 3 hour walk one way. This time estimate is definitely accurate especially if it's consistent walking (which we did with very little breaks) if you take a 10 min breaks every so often, it would take you longer. Definitely allocate a full day for this walk and start early in winter as day time is shorter and sun sets early. We started around 10am and made it down by 4.30pm with about an 30-45 min break at the top of the trail. Remember to bring your rubbish down with you, there are no bins at the top!This trail is definitely not pram or wheelchair friendly. If you have had any leg or hip surgery recently I would also not recommend. Even though this is an 'easier' trail the walkway access is not well paved, there are large rocks and very uneven surfaces much of the way up the trail. Near the end of the day, my husband and I witnessed at least half a dozen people needing assistance down the mountain on their 'conveyor belt pulley' which was supposed to only be used for stock to be transported up and down the mountain, but in these cases of emergency some elderly and struggling walkers were transported two at a time, down the mountain. I also witnessed an old man cramping up on his way down, but lucky he was with a walking group, so they managed to organise for him to go down safely.Like many reviews say, there are consistent reminders around noon for walkers to start making their way down the mountain for your safety.This walk was beautiful and we definitely will be back to attempt another trail of this mountain! We were lucky with the weather and there was no cloud cover when we went up, but got really windy when we descended the mountain.If you are driving to Eorimok trail by rental car and are using their rental gps, the telephone number for Eorimok trail for input into the gps is: 7139950 or 7139953, definitely go early if you can, otherwise like us we arrived around 10am and had to park at the trail driveway entrance and hiked up to the full car park :)

My friends and I traveled to this scenic coast in year 2011. It was not part of my itinerary but it was introduced by our driver. I really impressed by the nature of this tourist spot. It is located along the Coast of South Western of Jeju Island. I can say it is the most Scenic spot of Jeju's Coastline. Yongmeori Coast looks as if a dragon?s head is going underwater. This area is made of Sa-am stacks, built up over millions of years.It is the place where the mountain dips into the sea at the Yongmeori Beach. Formed out of the natural piling of stacks of ?Sa-am? that have been occurring for millions of years, the locals equate the formation of the Yongmeori Cliffs in Jeju with the image of a dragon?s head going into the ocean for a dip.You may find more information through the website. In year 2011, there were less tourist as it was not as famous as other hot tourist spot like Seopjikoji that time. I cannot remember whether is there any entrance fee needed. However, please wear sport shoes as there are some climbing the rocks to tour this place. After the long entrance, our driver guided us and we walked in the circle of the shape of dragon's head rock. Our driver was a very good photographer who shown us to climb near the cliff just for the nice photograph position. Recall back, my legs were shaking and didn't dare to make a move for posting all those difficult photography position! I think I will never this again!      Along the road down to the coastline, there is the Hamel Castaway Memorial, in remembrance of Hamel who drifted to this place in 1653 where Korea in the history did not open their door to the World yet.

My friends and I pirposely went to this theme park as we are fans of the Bae Yong Jun drama- The Legend, when we planned this trip, we asked the tour agency to include this on our itinerary. The facade was like a fortress from the Joseon dynasty except for the cars in the parking lot, the ticket booth and te posters saying this place was the location for the drama    The Legend   with a big picture of BYJ. We feel like we travelled back in time, the entrance is the main village with the bridge and man-made lake, the houses are surreal as you can see inside its like 3D not only the facade of the house then as you turn right you will see the village for common people , its more hanok styles, there is a market place with plastic meats, beefs but lloked real and the center of the village has a big traditional bar , it has second fllor where you can go up and see the view of the rest of the village, there were chairs and tables with some traditional glasses and wine bottles where you can do some photoshoots, there were tradional rickshaw downstairs, and a well with water, then there's a big gambling house with tables, some traditional games, with a big wheel with numbers you can bet on it, then a high ranking official house where you can go inside, there were furnitures, a fire place, there's living room, bed rooms and a TV where the drama is being shown, they really used this for the drama, thenat the center if the whole theme park was the big palace, as there were big gates leading to the palace with the whole field with cobbled stones, the palace is just so surral, you can enter it, you can see receiving rooms for the royalties, the emperor's chair, the rooms for the royalties with huge bed, books made of bamboo so it looked like window blinds, then there' s a roomfilled with hanboks where you can wear them and take pictures with it, there were mannequins of the characters in the drama, there's a dungeon too where they filmed the slaves or criminals being? punished, there were other rooms as well like the dining room with huge and long dining table, ere's a garden too with waterfalls, whoa! its really like the whole Joseon dynasty vibe! We took a lot of time taking pictures of the whole place with every nook and cranny of this place, its really a place for those who are fans of the drama or BYJ or even if you are curious how they live during those times, its like we time travelled back to those kings, emperors, slaves, scholars. the entrance fee to the park is USD10 and you can stay as long as you like. We used a private car courtesy of our tour guide but its quite far from the city as I remember we travelled for at least an hour from our hotel Shilla,but its worth it.

My boyfriend and I just visited the Jeju Stone Park last weekend. The park is huge with lots to see! Plan to spend a couple hours here. The history and legends are so interesting and the sights are really gorgeous around the park. We took a taxi from Hamdeok Beach but were able to catch the bus very easily back to Jeju City for only 1,000 won. The only thing I'd suggest is making sure to eat before you get here or bringing food! They have a restaurant but it's closed and looks like it will be for a while. Other than that, really great park!

Manjang Cave is one of the finest lava tunnels in the world and it is a designated as a natural monument.Not an easy walk as lots of even walkway,  slippery and dark. Take a slow walk to enjoy the surrounding and was cooling as you walk. You will be able to see the trace of the lava that flow through the cave. I saw some who rush all their way in and out.With young children do note of their safety, for older people who having legs problem do not try. Partly, you need to walk down the stairs which is not easy and when you finished you need to walk up again.We really enjoyed the nature of this cave.

Located in Seogwipo. What makes this waterfall unique compared to the rest of waterfalls in Asia is ? this one falls directly into the ocean. The view is very dramatic and I can guarantee that you will say 'wow' the moment you see it from the distance.This waterfall is 23 meter / 75 feet high. It was written in a legend that a holy dragon lived underneath it. Due to it, it was said that the water can cure disease and bring rain during drought season.It costs KRW 10,000 to enter this area, same price as Cheonjiyeon waterfall entrance fee. The comparison that I can make between these two waterfalls is ? Cheonjiyeon has beautiful landscape compared to Jeongbang. But Jeongbang has the dramatic factor compared to relaxing, calming Cheonjiyeon waterfall.You will go through a simple, quaint little path before you reach the waterfall gate entrance. No man made sculptures or attempt to make this road appear to be more touristy. However, the pink wild flowers blooms along this little path captures my heart. If you pay very close attention, you will see spider (s) hanging in the bushes alongside the road too. And if you not scared of it, you can check it out and test your macro skill with your camera. Remember : look but don't touch!Note: There are lots of spiders in Jeju Island. They are every where.I was unable to get too close to the falls because 1) it was cold windy day 2) I easily suffocate with water mist 3) I don't have water protection cover for my camera. So, if you plan to come here, please make sure to bring water proof camera protection if you really care of your expensive camera.Ah, one more thing ? shoes. Please wear sensible, flat, good grip kind of shoes / sport shoes.

Like you back to your childhood where teddy bear is a must have for every child. You can sing with them, sleep, play, being weird or elegance. All can be done with teddy bear You can pose with them in many ways, no wonder it's called temuseum as teddy museum.

Legend said this stone is a woman who waited her man come back from sea. If ignore this kind of legend, this place is a good trail where you can capture a lot of good photos. Don't just look at this rock, follow the trail on the left, will guide you to a wooden bridge, there also a tiny stairs that can reach some rocks and seaside (look like ponds).

Jeju is full of great natural wonders - Seongsan IIchulbong Peak, Manjanggul Cave, Cheonjiyeon Falls, Hallasan Mountain, Jeongbang Falls, Yongduam Rock, Jungmun Beach, Oedolgae, Jusangjeoli Cliffs; each and every of these world class attractions is Nature's well-carved masterpiece. Jusangjeoli Cliffs is one of those gorgeous and stunning attractions that I favored. While it does not have the sentimental legend that back-up Oedolgae or the auspiciousness of the dragon like Yong-duam rock, the sight of the crashing torrential sea waves rhythmically crashing against the set of blackish, rock pillars and columns was so beautiful a sight that I was totally immersed in the picturesque scene. The turquoise azure sea water contrasted magnificently with the black cliffs and produced one of those awesome scenery that one could hardly imagine it existed on Earth. I was mesmerized by what I saw and my ears drowned by the thundering waves. For one short moment, my mind went into a meditative state despite the presence of the squeezing and noisy crowd. I like to thank our Korean guide, Mr Won, who drove us in his van around Jeju to visit all these beautiful nature's wonders.
It's good to work out your legs, but if the view over the dull crater really is reward enough has everyone decide for himself.

It's an extremely demanding 'hike' for most average people. We read about it but didnt expect it to be that difficult. We went up the Seongpanak trail, starting at 7.30am, did a short detour to see the lake and crater and eventually reaching the summit at around 1pm. We descended the gwaneumsa trail and only managed to reach the base at around 6.30pm. We aren't considered extremely fit and so the climb was considered challenging for us. Our legs hurt for the next few days. The view down was amazing, but the climb was also steeper. Many parts of the trail were rocks so that made it a little difficult to climb as well. There are many cabs waiting at the base of Gwaneumsa trail to take you back to Seongpanak where we parked our car. The cab fare was about 15000won and took about 15 minutes. Overall the hike was fulfilling albeit tiring. But the views were a good return for our efforts!
It was really windy when we went, but it was still fun! There were so many cats! Great place to stretch your legs and get some fresh air.

It was a nice hike, got really sore legs the day afterwards. You could even buy ramyeon noodles, water and snacks halfway. It is a trail all the way, more like a walk way made out of rocks than a hike. But still really nice!

It took everything in me to make this climb.  But at the end of the day, my legs wobbling, I could say,   I hiked Korea's tallest mountain  Make sure to bring your food as the only thing available for sail will be ramen noodle, a favorite among Koreans.One tip, push through till you get to the area set up for sitting and eating.  Doing this instead of many stops along the way will definitely save you some time.

It is an archetypal tuff cone formed by hydrovolcanic eruptions upon a shallow seabed about five thousand years ago.  Situated on the eastern seaboard of Jeju Island and resembles a gigantic ancient castle, this tuff cone is 182 meters high, has a preserved bowl-like crater. There are two hiking trails to reach the peak , take the white path uphill and the orange path downhill. You just follow the crowd and the signages along the trail. During May and the coming summer, you do not need a jacket or pullover as it will be  hot and you will sweat a lot on the climb up. Wear covered sports shoes and  a cap / hat. The first part of the hike is the easiest and the least steep.  The rest of the path comprises steps of varying steepness. The final stretch gets very steep. Along the hiking trail, there are benches and pavilions to rest. Take a sip of water, rest your aching legs before proceeding . Toilets are available along the way. From the peak, you can see beautiful landscapes of Jeju island and do take a photo with the signage saying you are at Sunrise Peak. It took us 30 minutes to reach the top. The downhill walk was much easier, just follow the wooden stairs meandering its way down.  At the bottom, you can go for drinks at the cafetarias.

It is a volcanic rock formation in the form of a dragon?s head, created by strong winds and waves over thousands of years. However, legend has it that a dragon stealing precious jade from Mt. Halla was shot down by an arrow from the mountain deity. When he fell down on Yongduam, his body immediately sank into the ocean and his head rapidly froze looking at the sky. Another legend has it that a white horse dreamt of being a dragon and ascending to the sky. On his ascent, he was caught by a soldier and froze into the rock. While admiring the dragon?s head, one can see how the black rocks contrast with the emerald blue ocean.

Information given in English about the legend of the rock.    You really have to use your imagination to see the woman.    While I didn?t think much of Oedolgae, there?s a lovely hike right along the coast, with pretty views.

If you want a good workout, take this adventure on. I'm in average shape and it took me just around two and 1/2 hours to climb the Seongpanak Trail (9.6KM) going non-stop. The trail is definitely steep in sections and please use caution on the way down. I learned the hard way that tired legs don't descend as well as normal legs and took a pretty good fall.  Fortunately I was able to careen into the bushes on the side of the trail much to the suprise of all the hikers around me. There are stairs...lots and lots of stairs. There is an trolley car too hidden off to the side that they use to resupply the shops at the two shelters and maybe for medical evacuation if needed.

If you come to Jeju island, Hala mountain tracking is No. 1 recommendation for you if you are health and have strong two legs. My recomendation is Yong-Sil course and it will take about 5 hours round tracking. It is totally different scene when you up to the mountain and never forget this memory.

If you are intending to go for the sunrise climb, please bring your own torchlight as lighting is minimal. About 2/3 of the climb comprise of a steep ascend. Not for the weak-hearted or those with circulation problems. It's physically challenging on the heart, not so much on the legs.Personally, a day climb (rather than a dawn climb) is better as you can see the view from the various heights. At the top, there are benches to sit and appreciate the view. Coming down was the easy bit as the stairs are well designed for the descend.

If there is nothing else you do go see this temple. It is a sprawling complex that goes all up to the base of the mountain. Along the way if you do hike all the way up to the top, there are signs to explain the legends behind the names of the places you walk and why there is a temple there. But even if you don't it is still an sight to see

I love this cave as it was calmy, a little bit wet but make you comfortable after a long walk from the bus stop. I had to walk 3km or more (I think) coz my legs felt so sore, but I love the walk inside the cave. If you take a public bus, don't finish up too late as you might miss the last bus.

I kindly suggest this trail!!! We started the hiking from Gwaneumsa Temple, probably the most challenging trail. The entire trail is organized and you can't choose the wrong street. It is not impossible to reach the top of the mountain but it is better to start early because after 1-2 pm they close the top of the mountain. We started at 8.30 and we reached the top in about 5 hours. Climbing down was more difficult due to the pain of knee and leg muscle but the environment and the mountain were wonderful. I have the dream to repeat the hiking again in another season, possibly easter or summer.

I hadn?t hiked in years, but thought I?d give it a try at a friend?s suggestion. I dressed in layers as the weather was still cold, but knew I?d get warm on the climb up. I didn?t use crampons and there was only a small amount of ice in some places, it was easy to avoid. I did use poles, which I?ve never used before, but was thankful to have them, especially on the way down. The terrain was rocky, but there are lots of stairs and ropes as you reach the summit. It was much colder at the summit and the view was clearer than I expected. The crater is impressive. I did see a deer and a couple red squirrels. The hike down was much more difficult. My legs were in so much pain by the end of the day. Bring lots of food and water. Many people have picnics at the summit. I arrived to the trailhead by taxi and found a taxi at the trailhead when finished. I had to wait around a bit for a taxi to show up.

I checked out Samseonghyeol not even knowing what it was exactly but went anyway because it was close to my hotel and it was some sort of a cultural sight.  Upon entering I learned it was basically three unimpressive holes where three demi-gods supposedly emerged from.  While the main sight isn?t impressive, it was still a nice park to walk around in during spring with the cherry blossoms.  It?s definitely not a sight worth going out of your way to see unless you?re interested in Korean legends.
Get your legs ready for lots of stairs! The hike was definitely worth it though, great views from the peak!

When we're going down to trail at about 10p.m., there are lots of people coming up the trail and it is quite packed with people.For person with knees or legs or ankle problems, must be really careful as I fell down several times due to rocky trails at certain places. However, the view along the trail were awesome and it feels really worth it! The warm ramyeon at the shelter was the climax!I went in April 2016. The wind is super strong on top. Before you visit this attraction, be sure to be appropriately dressed and have the essential gear.  Hiking boots are highly recommended as the ground is uneven and mostly rock.  Sun hat and shades will also be very useful when nearing the peak as the area there is more barren without much trees.  Trekking pole will also be useful for those with knee problems.You will have to start your day early as they will disallow entry to the final stretch (at the 2nd rest point).  There are 2 rest points, both with toilets.  The 2nd rest point (higher up) sells drinks and instant bowl noodles.  Rubbish will have to be brought down and thrown when you leave the park.  I climbed in early June and there were many many many bugs and wasps at the last leg and the peak.  For those climbing during spring, please prepare some bug balm.  These are the tips;1) Start early, reach the 2nd rest stop before 12pm.  2) Have the proper gear3) If possible, have your noodles etc after you finish the peak (if you're descending via the same trail), that way, you won't have to carry your trash up the peak4) If you're driving, reach there early (before 730).  Carpark fills up pretty quick5) A mineral spring can be found along the way for cool refreshing water!

Before we arrive, the tour guide told us the story of the dragon and how the mark of the dragon landed create all the cracks on ground. At night with spot lights, it added some mysteries of the legend and when we climb all the way down hill at the dragon head,. it complete the story itself. A good trip full of imagination

Am not much of an active person who trek but managed to finish the hike.  Pretty easy to find alternative transport instead of cab. The trek was okay for the first leg (pre-rest stop) and got more challenging at the final leg.  Not knowing much, realised that most of the hikers have their hiking stick while I was on my own - then again I survive the hike abit limping for the long long hike :). In all, I enjoy the hike with not regrets

Admission is 2000 won. Need to walk down a flight of stairs to reach the beach area. The beach is full of pebbles and rocks and you need to careful to balance your body as you walk or hop from one rock to another. It may be slippery at certain spots and do exercise some precaution when taking photographs. The cliff looks steep and this is the only unique waterfall in Asia where the water falls directly into the sea. While the waterfall was not as awesome as what I earlier saw in books, the sensation was relaxing and cooling with the thundery roar of the waterfall at the backdrop while you sat at the beach rocks gazing at the azure sea. It was an unique pristine natural scenery to appreciate and absorb. At Cheonjeyeon Falls, the attraction is secluded and one could not see the vast horizon of the ocean whereas here at Jeongbang Waterfall, the waterfall and the beach integrated into the ocean giving a wholesome broad vision effect. At Jusangjeolli Cliffs, one could only enjoy the serene sight of the torrential waves crashing against the blackish rock pillars from the elevated observation point and access to the beach area is prohibited. Jeongbang Waterfall gives us the convenient access to the beach area and so near to a gorgeous waterfall and a looming cliff. Like Yongduam Rock which is backed up by a dragon head legend, Jeongbang Waterfall also has a story of Seobul, a servant of the Chinese Emperor Jin  who was ordered by the Emperor to search for an elixir and he happened to by-pass this area during his search. An inscription written `Seobulgwacha' on the wall of the water fall was derived from this legend but I did not walk too near to the waterfall to see clearly that inscription. Jeju has quite a number of world class natural wonders and each wonder gives me a different perspective in appreciating nature.

According to legend, Samseung Hyeol is where three demigods emerged from the ground to become the founding fathers of Tamna. This is the basis of the legend, and it is well-known to most Jeju residents. The Tamna kingdom ended in 1404 when it was absorbed by the newly founded Joseon Dynasty. While this rather small shrine is undobutably not THAT ancient, it is a unique site. There is a small museum which shows a video that tells the full legend of Tamna's founding.One plus of this site is the original Dol hareubangs (Grandfather statues) located at the entrance. These statues are unique to Jeju island, with a similar variation in Korea's southern coast. There are only 48 remaining Dol hareubangs left on Jeju-do. These   grandfather   statues were made between 1763-65.

A beautiful garden to wander through. The museum played us an English 3D film introducing us to the legend of the three demigods who founded Jeju culture. Then we got to see the place where they sprang from the earth, infused with the spirit of the volcano.
