With Snoopy Garden’s steep entrance fee it initially didn’t make my itinerary. But the good reviews were consistent and friends also highly recommended the Charles Schulz’s Peanuts themed museum and garden. The indoor museum part was the highlight for me which had explanations about every main Peanuts character and several comic clips that span over Schulz’s 50 years of drawing them. The old newspaper clippings old toys and old books were also cool to look at. There are dozens of great photo spots which can create some major bottlenecks on crowded days. The garden had about half a dozen themed areas (including my favorite Charlie Brown’s baseball field) that are pretty vast and would have been a lot more pleasant to walk around in cooler weather. We skipped the cafe that charged a criminal 8500 won for a lemonade. I’m not sure that the high price of admission is justified but this is a well maintained attraction(which is refreshing considering the high number of run down museums and small theme parks in Jeju) and the quality of the displays are of superb quality. Adults and children both also fans and non-fans of Peanuts both would enjoy the visit here.

While I'm getting more and more tired of museums this was a huge surprise for me. It costs 9 dollars and it's in the middle of nowhere in the island like everything. But it is so funny I spent almost 2 hours there and it was totally worthy. The illusions they create are so real and so interesting.

Whether you are a dedicated tea aficionado or don't drink tea on a regular basis this museum's mix of educational material tea samples and even tea related products is unmatched. I have had green tea ice cream before but never as good as they make here! Also their assortment of dry tea tumblers and ceramics is quite nice.

When we were there they were having a special limited showing of the ancient art of making furniture jewelry boxes etc using shells.  The displays were beautiful and it was interesting to learn how involved the process is.  The museum was nice we went on a rainy day when we needed indoor activities. The last section Provence Art is basically a large room with a lot of large-sized stuff dogs in Provence village setting. The dogs are not as cute as the teddy bears at Teseum. I think Alive Museum is more suited for teenagers and youg adults visiting in groups it should be more fun for them.

When I was planning my trip to Jeju  I found this museum has got half positive and half negative comments from travelers. Well ??I decided to have a look by myself. When our car got near to the place  there was a strong smell. I was then told that there is a piggery farm nearby which stinks out the whole place. The ticket was not cheap but it included a cup of coffee plus a discount in the shop. The appearance of the building is interesting with an open courtyard. The first impression was not so bad.However when I got inside  it was quite disappointing. I think the management should consider a renovation  or at least a deep cleaning and some maintenance. For example  they put lots of chocolate boxes from all over the world in the same window display without proper descriptions. How can the people think that those boxes are precious when they are packed in a glass cabinet? The lighting on the second floor was horrible. The rooms were so dark adding horrific ambiance to the museum.

If you are already inside Jungmun Resort and are travelling in groups you can take a cab to this place since it would not cost much and you can save the hassle of walking. There are several sections in the museum and each sections has its own theme. Definitely worth a visit and we really didn't regret it. So do equip yourself with a camera and of course have someone with you to take photos for you.

We visited in April 2018 and were impressed by the quality and the size of the village. There is a lot of history and culture to be learned here. The exhibits are well maintained they have live gardens and animals to represent the life in the village as well as hands on exhibits for kids and adults to participate in. There are craftspeople and artisans that are making wood work and stoneware that you can purchase. It is very beautiful. Also there is a restaurant on premise near the front gates and gift shop. The living museum and village is wheelchair accessible and worth the price of admission. It will take 2 to 3 hours to see everything. It can easily be a half day experience. Get there early to avoid the crowds. It's popular for students and tourists along with all the major places you should visit while on Jeju.

We took our two year old daughter to the Teddy Bear Museum and she LOVED it. We enjoyed seeing the popular bears from our childhood. This is a good quick visit for the family. Don't forget to see the Elvis dancing and singing show before you leave. It is a hoot.

We took our 27 month old daughter here mostly because she was about to fall asleep on our bike ride and we didn't want to mess up her nap schedule. When you first walk in  they have a walk through of the animals of Africa. Our daughter had a ball naming the animals and learning new ones. We loved the learning experience she got while she stared bright eyed at all the big (and small) animals. She even loved the art and seeing all the different designs (although we admittedly had to go a bit faster than normal through the rest of the museum). For this being an unplanned stop  we were thrilled we did. What a nice addition to our vacation.

We took a short stroll in the tea plantation.  Somehow it did not evoke the same feelings of peaceful serenity I had expected.  Perhaps there were just too many people around hence the experience was vastly different from my previous Alishan (Taiwan) tea plantation visit.We tried the tangerine flavoured tea in the museum.  My husband loved the taste but it?셲 not for me.  Kids love the green tea ice cream.  Thumbs up.We found it hard to find a table with seats although we visited on a Monday.  It was that crowded!

We stopped by this museum at the end of a long day because my daughter  who loves science  was begging us to go. We were all pleasantly surprised. There were quite a few hands on displays like static balls  using bikes to light up a display  a few trick eye displays  plasma globes  and of course Tesla coils. The staff were incredibly friendly and although they didn't speak much English they went out of their way to show us around. The Tesla coil music show was quite cool - the coils were used to create different pitches and played both classical and modern music. It took about an hour to go through everything and cost ??0000 for 2 adults and 2 kids. My kids loved it! Great hands on science.

We spent some fun hours here luckily the weather was beautiful and I'd suggest to visit when it's sunny so the place can really shine. Could be better maintained but we liked it regardless. So what's to see here? Installations of famous landmarks and a tiny Korean village (which is more like few houses really). I wouldn't call this a theme park I'd say it's a park with an interesting and enjoyable theme without toys. I think most parks and museums in Jeju share one common problem: the staff seems to be nonpresent and there's a serious lack of catering service. No coffee shops restaurants or they're either closed. I think this place had something but I think it was closed. Either way I think it's worth visiting if you happen to be around and the surroundings are pretty too.

We spent like 3 hours in the museum took hundreds of funny photos! Although posing for the photos was like doing exercise quite tiring but still we had so much fun. Luckily it was not too crowded so we could take as many photos as we wanted at the same spot. There is also an outdoor space for photo-taking many creative sculptures. If you want to do something fun or if it is raining in Jeju this is the place you should visit!

We self-drive to this museum. Like everyone else we ate the green tea cake ice cream and hot green tea latte for lunch it was delicious especially for green tea lovers. It was crowded with bus loads of tourists but the cafe staff was very efficient and served quickly. Bought Jeju tangerine tea after trying the sample. We also went to the innisfree shop to buy cosmetics. And took photos of the garden that has beautiful cherry blossoms at this time. Great soothing weather and we also walked across the road to the tea plantation. Enjoyed ourselves.

We rented a car. We reached the Tea Museum just after 12 noon. The car park was already full and we had to park by the side road. The museum is more of an exhibition of tea cups with write-ups on a brief history of tea and the origins of the Osulloc tea. Easy reading for a morning activity. There is a tea merchandise section and a cafe.We ordered the green tea ice-cream and black tea ice-cream. Both were good. The tea was very intense on both the ice cream. The green tea roll was just passable for us. Drop by if you are on the way. I think at certain times of the day there maybe some demonstration on tea but nothing was written in English so not sure of the timing.

We rent a car in jeju and drove to this place.  We were pleasantly surprised and really enjoyed ourselves. If you're the sort who likes taking photos that stimulate the senses don't miss.  Quite a big museum and there are many fun and interesting spots to take photos.

We reached the cave 45 minutes before closing hour and had to walk really fast in order to reach the end of the cave to see the Lava tubes. Many friends told us it's a must visit in jeju.  But my Cousin and I were disappointed as we felt it's nothing fascinating. Better time could be spent in other attractions such as the sunrise peak and Teddy bear museum.
We passed a couple of hours here enjoyably.? It's a museum-lite type of experience. Very close to a few cafes/convenience stores and other attractions in the area.

We only went because it was raining and we needed some indoor attractions. We needed to occupy our young children (ages 9 and 4) so we decided to take a trip to the museum. It was much smaller than we had anticipated. Friendly staff who allowed us to trip some of the more unusual chocolates before we purchased them. We did find the same chocolates at E-Mart that was less expensive. The kids liked the chocolate school but we thought the kit was a bit overpriced as you could do the same thing in your kitchen.

review: We loved the Alive museum. It was so much fun!!!So many funny poses you could make and was a lovely way to spend the day out.
We love this museum with different teddy bears and so colourful. Great for kids and adults. While in Jeju is a place to visit. Visitors are crowded so go early.

We just visited the chocolate museum as a family and it was a bit of a let down. The tickets were 6000 for adults (tickets for children in elementary I think were 4500?) and they gave us free Americano. There really wasn't that much to see  and the place smelled funny. I think if you?셱e really interested in learning about the past of cacao and chocolate in Korea then this might be a fun place to visit  but if you don't have much interest in that  it might be a waste of money.However they do offer chocolate making classes every hour for little kids under 13. So there were a lot of children there when we went. Might be a fun place to visit with children :)They also sell chocolate  and we tried a sample and it was pretty good and rich in quality. We also bought 3 bars of 70% cacao for 30 000. The original price was 36 000  but with the entree ticket you get a 6 000 discount.

review: We invite you to 'Figure Museum Jeju'  full of fantastic movie figures and statues! There are tons of high quality exhibits! Action figures  movie statues  life size statues  upcycling arts  game statues  etc. Everybody can enjoy and have fun here with figures from movies and games and animations.
We have took a lot of photos and it amazed us a lot!! must go!!It will take up a good 1 - 1.5 hours to go around the whole museum.
We have fun at the Trickeye Museum. There are a great variety of backgrounds and they look really real.It should take about an hour to take 80% of the backgrounds on a non-peak period.

We had two rounds of tea tasting - the signature green tea and another caramile version. Both are good but not great. It's more of a Cafe than museum we had a great time buying tea for our family. The sales people speaks good English and is always ready to help.Cafe is a bit crowded but the turnover is fast and it did not take long to buy our drinks and get a seat. The back garden is connected to Innisfree Cafe so don't miss that too.Parking is a pain however so remember to be aggressive. Parking is not restricted to what's marked on the ground in Jeju.

We had some extra time so we thought we would check out Alive Museum thinking it would only take an hour. But it was actually very big. We probably spent 2 1/2 hours there and still didn't go to the outside part. But it was fun

We had heard about the tea plantation first on the television show Kimchi Chronicles on PBS (http://www.kimchichronicles.tv/). As an avid tea drinker I could hardly pass up the chance to check it out in person and it is amazing. We drank tea walked in the tea fields checked out the tea museum watched the roasting of tea bought tea tea soap tea lotion and tea ice cream. The museum and center are quite stunning and the drive out there interesting on some very well maintained roads. Don't miss this one if you are on Jeju Island.

We first went to this museum 7 years ago and wanted to visit this place again hoping there is some new attraction.  Sadly nothing has changed and lesser crowd.  Entrance fee is not cheap and I don't think its really worth to go unless you love teddy bear. We are out by 1 hour and kids wasn't very excited with the same display.

We felt a little cheated cause the castle wasn't so much of a castle. More like a small park and it was pricey for the entrance and there wasn't much to see at all. Realised that there are plenty of museums like these to cheat tourist money in Jeju so be selective on which ones you plan to visit. This is definitely not one of them that you should go.
We drove an hour to find this place. It was disappointing. There were tons of people and the museum was more like a store than a museum.

We didn't think our 11 year old and 7 year old boys would be interested in this museum at ll. Much to our surprise our oldest request to go. It was actually a lot of fun. It was a challenge for the boys to identify all the various moments in history that were depicted.

We didn't bother with the museum itself. Not my thing.But the Sunday Brunch at the cafe is legendary.Smoothies come in cute glass jars with thick straws and are so full of chunks of fruit that you almost have to chew them as you drink.The brunch itself is a mix of odd elements that I wouldn't normally put together - but they work..... creamy butternut squash soup scrambled eggs mustard coated potato wedges plus a ham/cheese/vegetable panini with salad leaves and balsamic vinegar on the side. Really good food.We sat outside the weather was lovely. Great view of the tea field (part of the museum) and the road. If I come back to Jeju on a trip sometime I'll definitely return for Sunday brunch!
We did sightseeing but gets dark early so we decided to check this museum out. We had seen several of the fliers. My daughter who is 10 really enjoyed it. We took a ton of pictures.

We did not plan to visit the museum originally but was brought here by accident by a taxi driver who couldn't speak much English (of which there are plenty in Jeju-do). We were pleasantly surprised and really enjoyed ourselves. If you're the sort who likes taking photos that stimulate the senses don't miss.

We decided to do this spontaneously and it was actually much funnier then I expected. The teddy bear through time stuff was really well done and the museum didn't feel like a drag despite its very limited options of showing teddy bears. Would recommend for pretty much all ages if you've got a day in Seogwipo.

We came to this museum based on the previous reviews and came away extremely disappointed. The displays are very average and there's really not too much to see inside the display hall. The tunnel with the dioramas (which looked to be the most interesting one) was locked while we were there. There were no signs to indicate why it was closed or when it would re-open.The other tunnels were OK but once you've seen one tunnel you've seen them all - and the fairy lighting in the tunnels did seem a little out of place considering their history. There is a lot of painful history in this area but the museum fails to capture and relay it.It would have been better to see more of the human history alluded to in the video display in the other displays.Note that a lot of the pictures for this Trip Advisor listing may not actually be of this museum - we were quite confused trying to find it based on these pictures and they make it seem a lot grander than it really is.Overall wouldn't recommend and wouldn't go back.

We came at night about 8pm after having dinner at a nearby noodles restaurant. And was the last to leave the museum. It takes about an hour plus to fully explore the huge facility. While it was really cool that we didn't have to worry about our silly poses and waiting in line (quiet at this time) we also realised that there was no one to help the both of us take couple shots for some poses. However we still enjoyed ourselves very much. Perhaps it'll be better to arrive 7pm for a better experience.
We are so glad that you have a great time in our museum. :)
We are glad that you have an amazing experience in our museum. :)
We are glad that you have a fun experience in our museum. :)
We are glad that you have a decent experience in our museum. We will try our best to add more creative elements in our museum.

We are glad that we have our wonderful tour guide was with us thus we were able to gain better understanding n knowledge about the green tea n it's plantation.The museum itself actually showcase the different type of green tea products (including facial products) so it's a shopping paradise for some.  There are free sampling of the green tea however we like the cafe most. Though a little pricey but the green tea yogurt ice cream n also the green tea milk ice cream is yummy (it has strong green tea taste).As it was crowded when we were there the cafe seemed to be under stocked for the crowd.  A friend managed to get herself green tea macaron n said it taste superb.A good stop over for some retail therapy n tea break n photo taking.

We also went to Jeju Stone Park. Easy to find and approach with car. Parking places are available but during peak season the earliy bird .....Entrance fee with 5000 Won for adult and 2000 Won for child. It is a nice walking area with a lot of big and small stones. Dont forget your camera to bring. Inside there is also a huge museum with history of vulcano eruptions and of course with history of Jeju. Mainly in Korean but it it is definetly worth to visit. It is a very nice place and we would come back again.

We already know its gonna rain the whole day based on the weather forecast that's why we were in this area as it is full of museum...So... We run into this Choc Land after visiting the 'believe it or not museum' & teddy bear museum. Ermm  how to say  you can use part of the entrance ticket to buy chocolate here  and there were many cute & special chocolate displayed... But  that was it  no more no less. So... Unless you don't mind  you may dropby to buy some chocolate & snap some nice picture  rest a bit as there is not much people here. Else you may wanna consider stay longer in the Believe it or not Museum or even the Alive Museum :)
We all really enjoyed this interactive museum.  It's so much fun to put yourself into the pictures.  They even show you where to stand to take the best pictures.  The variety was great.

We actually stayed at a hotel right on this beach.  The water is beautiful but there are signs saying no to swimming in some parts of it.  There is a cafe bene right next to it so you can grab a cup of coffee and go sit on the beach.  The only problem is that it is pretty far from anything else like all the museums and nature trails of jeju and it is kind of small which makes me think that in the summer it can get really crowded.

Was visit here coincidentally when asking taxi driver to dragon head but was allright place was beautiful and nice scenery view surround mountain and fresh air was nothing to complain. The park suit for kiddos wiyh some museum as well.

Was very crowded the day/time we were there.  There's a tiny museum which leads to shop and cafe.At the cafe we had the trio of  green tea cake/roll smoothie and ice cream which were very good.Then we headed next door to the Innisfree Jeju house.A nice way to spend a couple of hours.  There's a couple of very uncrowded O'sulloc cafes in Seoul too.

Was told that its the same operator as Trickart museum but this is larger & newer.  Alive Museum is near the Teseum teddy bear safari.  We did one after another. Lots of trickart to see & interact with to pose for funny photos. Even the adults are having fun. Better value than Teseum unless you're a teddy bear lover.

Was specially there to try their famous Matcha Roll and Matcha ice cream and it didn't disappoint. The cream within the Matcha roll was totally on point and delicious. The Matcha ice cream was rich and creamy. It went really well together with the matcha roll. There were too many tourist on the day we visited and was overly crowded. We were also disappointed with the innisfree shop beside the tea museum as we'd expected more product offerings. There are no cosmetics in the store. Only limited number of products. It is a 30-45mins drive from Jeju City.

Was fun taking photos at Alive museum we visited the museum at night and I guess because of that there were fewer tourists which meant what we could actually interact with the art more and did more funny shots with the art displayed.A great place for families young and old.

Was excited to see the tea museum but disappointed as it was only a 5 minute tour. We drove for about 1.5 hours to visit this museum from the other end of Jeju City.  The treats at the museum shop was a nice respite against the summer heat though. There is also the tea plantations just across the museum and Innisfree (Korean Skincare) beauty shop about 2 minutes walk away. I would recommend to go for the Stoner Tea museum tour to make this trip more worthwhile. However there are certain timings for it and we didnt manage to join.

Walking through this outdoor museum was fabulous.  There many interesting things to see and learn about the Korean history.The visit itself took about an hour and some of the things to purchase was quite interesting.  It was interesting to find out how the privilege and not so privilege lived.

Visited this place with a group of friends. The tea plantation wasn?셳 fantastic; don?셳 expect vast rolling hills of uninterrupted shrubbery. The museum was really small and led to a shop and restaurant which was much bigger than the museum itself. The place was milling with many tourists and it was uncomfortable to browse their merchandise or eat in peace. We tried the matcha ice cream and cake and there was nothing too special about it. I don?셳 think this place is worth a visit.

Visited this Museum in Dec 2017 with my family. Entrance ticket costs 34 000kwon for 2 adults and 2 children. The place basically is run-down  glasses broken  dirty and colour faded over the years. I didn't bother to check on the cafe inside and left the museum in 15mins. Nothing special in the gift shop as well. Total waste of my money and my time travelled to visit the so called museum. If you intend to visit this Jeju Glass Museum  don't bother!

Visited the tea museum as heard so much about it but there is nothing that special just some tea history and at the end of it  they sell the tea to visitors at touristy pricing. There is a caf챕 that serves green tea and ice cream too and that is ok to try out. There is an Innis free shop next door to tea factory but it was closed the day we visited. I would say its ok for a visit if you have spare time in your hands otherwise nothing really to shout about.

Visited the Park based on TA reviews. Extremely well done with extensive museums and stone displays. Allow at least 3-4 hours for the visit. Enormous work has gone into the development of the Park. Should be in the Top 5 attractions in Jeju outside the beaches.

Visited the Osulloc Tea Museum in the late afternoon. It was packed with visitors. Only few people really went to the museum. People just packed to shop for green tea or tea products. The cafe was crowded too and the seats/tables were not very clean because staff could not keep up with cleaning due to the huge crowds. Unless you want to purchase their products it is not the best place to visit.

Visited the museum just for the fun of it and was amused by some of the statues on display. Didn't think too much of it though so if this isn't on one of the must do's on your holiday list you can probably skip it and not miss much.

Visited the museum during a weekend and it was too crowded for me to have a close look at the teas. The queue for the cashier was too long with >20 pax queueing. Not sure how well rated was the taste of the tea but better to visit it on a less crowfed day if you plan to.
Visited the Alice museum in a rainy day in Jeju was not sure of it at first but I must say we had a pretty fun time whoever put it together has a different sense of humor

Visited on 7 June 2019 and found out it was closed for renovations (it was all fenced up...) till September 2019. Thankfully there was Osulloc Tea Museum right beside it so we didnt make awasted trip!

Visited in golden weekend so expected crowded with tourist and local. This place is big and nice. Environment is clean just not so tourist friendly cos the staffs barely speak English. But it?셲 doesn?셳 spoil our mood of visit cos I love ocean. This is a really good place to visit. Entrance is bit expensive compare others tourist attractions museum. It?셲 cover with 2 shows.  I got my discount ticket online via KLOOK. If visit on the day without buy online cost 39800won per person.

review: Visit to the modern tea museum is great. You can sample tea leaves and purchase them. Opposite the museum there is great vegetation scenery.

Visit this place even if you not interested or lover of sea shells at least to recognise the sheer efforts put in by Ms Myeong Yeon Sook  the director of this museum and owner of this place. This museum which has over 7 800 variety and accounting to more than millions of sea shells originating in Jeju and the world is the brain child of Ms Sook and master Metal craftsman Kwon Oh-Kyun.The beauty of these sea shells are to be seen to be believed. They have been arranged and displayed so artistically that one may easily mistake it as a painting.One may not see much of visitors around  but this really helps as we go around enjoying the magic of nature.Entrance fee is a bit high  but really worth it  considering the efforts put in to bring this huge collection of sea shells under one roof and creating the world's first seashell museum.

Viewpoint on the western end of Jeju Island.  Great place for sunset observation.  High on a cliff with good views all around.  There is a weather station here.Was here on a windy day - with field of swirling grass. To the north of the hill is a tail along the shore where it is possible to rent electric scooters.  There is also a small museum on the prehistoric settlement found in the area.

Very well manicured plantations and garden areas. Museum is professional and store was well laid out with all their delicious teas with samples in bottles for customers to smell.Limited parking space though. Could see people parking by the sides of roads all over the vicinity.Cashier staff was very helpful combining our global tax refund receipts when we made two purchases separately.Ice cream was good. Cream roll would prefer it like a Swiss roll where cream is well spread around the roll. Current style has too much dry cake at the sides.Beautiful packaging as always.

Very well managed green tea museum. They have a small museum to show the process of tea and how it has evolved over the years. Upon finishing the museum you can buy different green tea products from the shop. And there is also a cafe within the museum that sell excellent green tea ice cream and also green tea Swiss roll. If you have time you can walk further into the next building which is the innisfree shop within this building you will be able to make your own green tea soap under the supervision of the Innisfree staff. There is also a cafe that sell jam and cake in this building. Perfect to spend your afternoon in this place.

Very tasteful and informative. We were hesitant at first but figured we might as well take advantage of seeing what a sexually suppressed country could teach us :)The gift shop was a little lacking on museum related material and seemed to carry just local touristy items.
Very simple museum. I found the Haenyeo musuem more interesting but overall this museum is good. Beautiful architecture of the museum.

Very nice small museum. Not as boring as much of them. I found it interesting. I hate wandering for 8 hours in a museum with tons to read. That one is fesable in a normal amount of time. There was also a little show they did with movable boats showing how they worked in the days. Girls doing it were laughing the whole time as it was hilarious. My bf got picked to go help as cast along with others working the nets. I loved the whole scene with the chants. There are old boats outside you can go in and visit. Small souvenir shop with not much. Very helpful employees who offered to keep our luggages behind the counter as they did not fit in the lockers.
Very neat museum about female divers. The museum takes about 30 minutes. Don't forget to look around at the statues. Might be boring for small children.
Very interesting museum. It's just funny and fun. I don't think we can find  this kind of museum just anywhere. Definitely a laughing place to be.

Use your 3D imagination and spend a couple of fun hours. Where you can become part of each scenario from hungry dinosaurs to a VanGong painting from an explosive mine to be on a boat in Venice. Great museum best recommendation don't go alone to enjoy it more. Although other tourists are always kind to take some pic for you.

Unfortunately  I cannot say that this place is worth visiting. The surrounding area and sites (Sanbangsan and the temple  Yongmeori Coast) are worth the visit though  and I speculate that this is the only reason the museum has survived.The ship museum itself provides information about the Dutch sailor who landed on Jeju and was held captive and against his will for several years by Koreans (not sure why this is a source of pride as it seems to be made out). The story itself could be quite interesting  but to be honest  I would rather read about it in a well-written book than in a tacky and very cheesy museum using broken English. Children might enjoy walking through the ship replica so I suppose it could be worth visiting if you also visited the other nearby sites.I personally would never recommend this place to anyone.

review: Truly heartwarming to see how this cultural heritage is safeguarded and exhibited for us to see. This museum is very informative.

Transportation- You can take bus 755 to the museum takes half an hour from jeju downtown. Food- nothing nearby but you can get pretty decent coffee and jeju-special tea/drinks at the 'innisfree organic green cafe' at the same compound. The museum itself is not that exciting took us 15 mins finishing off everything including the teatree garden. The innisfree cafe/store nearby is so much more fun especially for the female fellow travellers.;)

Totally amusing day at Alive museum at Jeju. Great place for young kids adults and even senior citizen. Was there in mid Dec with 3 different age group all enjoyed taking photo & the place is well maintain.

Today is the last day in Jeju but since the plane is evening time so we went to Jeju folk village museum.It's worth visiting there! Every one of us really enjoyed ourselves going to learn their traditional style and ways of living! Furthermore the place is very beautifully designedmaking us just want to know what that's waiting ahead of us as we go along!I'll visit this place again if ever to go to Jeju again!

To know how the teddy bear appears then visit it. Also knowing all the types of teddy bear and appreciate it. Also a garden walk for photo shoot plus Elvis teddy bear life show every 15minutes to listen to elvis.The gift shop is really something to buy to have visit this teddy bear museum

To get the most from this attraction it would really help if you like green tea! Everything is based on it including the food and treats. I had the (very expensive) ice cream and it really wasn?셳 to my taste. The museum on tea equipment was very interesting. Don?셳 make this your day?셲 primary focus but if you are passing it?셲 worth popping in.

To enjoy a leisurely afternoon at the O'Sulloc Tea Museum slowly sipping hot green tea latte and savouring the famous green tea roll is true bliss. The green tea roll and green tea ice-cream are the best I've ever tried! :)
To be in a gigantic lava tube was something new and interesting. Recommended!  It's also near the Haenyo Museum which was very interesting as well.

Thought it was gonna be some just rows and rows of teddy bear displays but was pleasantly surprised by the presentation and the whole set-up...the curators really have got a sense of humour!  :)was more like entering an art museum...

This was suppose to be one of the 1st museum in the world to exhibit all sorts of teddy bears. Not a very big place but pack with tourists. For the really young at heart or the really young kids this may be a novelty.
This was not much of a museum. Thankfully it was free admission. I did like the building it was housed in as it was bright and airy. It's a nice place to stop for some tea and snacks.

This was my second trip to this museum.  The beautifully made exhibits address much about the history and lifestyle of the diving ladies. One exhibit also compares the Korean divers to the Japanese divers.  The viewpoints from the museum are lovely

This was actually my 2nd 3D museum that I'd been too. While it had different structures and art pieces it's also bigger than the 'trick eye museum' in Hongdae Seoul. This could be good or bad:Good: there's obviously more photo opportunities more of a day out and worth more for your moneyBad: you need to be in the mood to have lots of photos taken turns out multiple photo taking can actually be draining!Don't get me wrong though we had a great time! There's also a go-kart track round the back which you can use for extra money.

This was a tourist trap.No museum to me- just a bit of information about tea on the wall with a tea grousing machine- that?셲 it!Who calls this a museum?The rest of place was for cafe souvenir shop - some observatory deck where you could see the tea field.Honestly Amore Pacific did a great job to let people recognize that Jeju could produce tea that?셲 perfectly linked with their business. Very smart from business perspective- bravo in that sense.

This was a stop of a bus tour through the weestern part of the Island. The so called tea Museum is a building where they sell  tea in all kinds of packaging such as bags and boxes. The word Museum is barely justified by the few pots and cups that are exhibited. You certainly should not come here from Europe because of the tea Museum. For those that never have seen the harvest of tea leaves is worth a stop.

This was a great view. I was able to do it in less than an hour. Its a small descend( you will have to go up these same stairs to leave) to the actual waterfall. There were women selling seafood on the side. You can hear the waterfall when you get in the area. At the entrance there is food. And a 3 minute walk further there is an art museum. The waterfall itself was amazing. There was a lot of water coming down. And you can see it go directly to the ocean. Opposite the waterfall is the ocean.
This teddy bear museum was our first stop upon arrival in Jeju Island. Its more suited for kids and I was utterly bored.

This Teddy bear Museum is interesting however I would not recommend if there is no kids traveling with you.Giant Teddy in the back yard was fun to watch.Dolls in the store are little pricey.Kids perspective: 5/5Adults perspective: 3/5

This tea museum is very interesting.  It is a very knowledgeable museum that shows the tea making process right from the planting harvesting tea leaves and processing it into dried tea leaves. It also has a cafe attached where they serve green tea ice cream green tea swiss roll cake and green tea slurpee.
This tea museum is one of the coolest places to visit in west Jeju Island. Take your time to wefie with the giant milk tea or at the beautiful tea fields outside.
This tea museum has tea farm so can see the real green tea leaf. They also sell tea with reasonable price.

This so-called museum is really a sales outlet for O'Sulloc teas.  The grounds above the tea plantation is just beautiful to walk around.  The Innis Free Jeju House on the grounds is another sales outlet for Innis Free skin care products.  They offered a hands -on activity to make your own soap.  Lunch here was great.  They pride themselves in locally sources produce. I had the rice balls and soup.  We shared the mungwork steamed buns with red beans - not much to look at but very tasty. The shaved ices are a treat not to be missed

This sight is heavily crowded with many tours visiting but the ice cream and cakes are delicious and a must try if you visit. There is also a lot of tea on sale which you can also try. More of a store than a museum but not a bad place to spend an hour.

This place was my must visit the first time I came to Jeju and I gladly returned back. You can participate in the tea class which is just another great activity to enjoy at this place. I love that there is both the tea museum and also the Innisfree house both having something different to offer. The only downside is the insane amount of visitors at all time so be ready to wait in line if you want something!

This place was crowded when we arrived and had to wait a while before we could get seats in the cafe. The museum part was small and did not provide much information. The tea plantations are also open to visitors but the grounds were muddy due to the rain hence we didn't enter them. The variety and price of products are similar to those in their seoul busan branches hence I wouldn't recommend a special visit to this place if you have been to them before.

This place is worth visiting given it's nice environment and a lots of things to do. Food:  I highly recommend the green tea icecream and cake at the O'Sulloc tea museum which appears to be the focus of most visitors.  But I also want to take some time to remind you that there's another little gem inside the organic cafe of Innisfree that's also within the complex--DON'T MISS OUT THE TANGERINE SHAVED ICE! It comes in a big original size that can be sufficiently shared among 3 persons or there's a mini version if you only want a taste of it.  It's not cheap but worth trying because they use Jeju Tangerine which tasted somewhat more intense and flavourful.  Drinks:  They have free tea-demo which you can try their teas.  They also sell a selection of other drinks like tea latte.  Most of them tasted and smelled spectacular.  The teabags are also wrapped individually so they make good souvenirs as well. Soap making:  If you go early do try making your own soap at the Innisfree house it's a fun experience and make good souvenirs.View and/or pictures:  The environment around and within the museum is a great place for pictures with the open tea-farm and the delicate glass buildings or the colourful interior of the Innisfree house.  There's also a viewing deck in the O'sulloc Tea Museum which you can access by taking a lift.  The view up there is pretty amazing.  Tip:  1. Go on a sunny day if you want to take great pictures in the tea-farm2. Go early if you are worried that they sell out the cakes.  The tangerine shaved ice wasn't available after 5.30pm so we went to visit again on the next day.

This place is rather far from where stayed (it would take about an hour from Jeju city/Seogwipo) and if you have a car you can enjoy the scenic route passing by horse farms and ATV parks and occasionally some towns. Make sure your car has enough petrol/gas as we didn't note much stations during our drive.It is located at a bay by the sea which has a good view (after you are done with the aquarium). There is a parking lot available but we were there on a super busy day despite being a Monday (we just thought that maybe it was the school holidays?) and we were lucky to get a lot.Place is stroller friendly but be mindful if the place is quite full. Everyone can get mesmerised by the display and you may just knocked by a stroller or two.The displays are quite entertaining. There are some attractions such as otter/pelicans feeding. You can check the time of these attractions at their website and you can time your visit there. There is a underwater tunnel and the manta rays will just swim pass.There was a huge aquarium display and unfortunately for us we were not able to the see the whale shark they were housing as it had been released back into the sea for research purpose. At certain times there will be a feeding session by scuba divers. The penguin display had some fake penguins in between and for some reason they look pretty realistic beside a real one when the real ones don't move. Have fun figuring out which is which!There was a show featuring synchronized swimming diving from high places. The show was about pirates and fairies. Everyone enjoyed the show (all in Korean with English displayed on the screen) and we were just clapping without really understanding what's going on but you will sort of understand the story. After about 20 minutes or so there was a seal show followed by a dolphin show. Again in Korean and you just shout and clap whenever the locals do. (For the language: it is the same in all other countries. Just be don't care and enjoy the show!) The show was about 45 minutes long and there is a stand outside selling popcorn and peanut butter roasted squid (a must try!) so get some and enjoy the show.On another wing there is a small science museum and a 3D theater. You can skip the museum and head outdoors (as most are in Korean) but there is a holographic display of the whale shark inside that is really cool. Attraction is free. For the 3D theater not sure if we had to pay an additional sum but it was featuring a shark show and we reckoned the kids would be terrified.There is a cafeteria downstairs and the food is pretty good. You will need to pay at a counter which they will give you a device which beeps when the food is ready for collection. If can get quite crowded as there's limited space. During your walk there will be pop up stands selling food so you don't have worry about getting hungry while walking around.After it all head outside for the scenic view and some outdoor picture taking. We were there on a gloomy day and wind was pretty strong.

review: This place is nice. The museum tells you all you want to know about tea. Scent samples of tea are all over. There is a snack nook where you can try their signature desserts and beverages. This place is exactly as advertised. If you have never seen this type of art in person before then I guess it's worthwhile. But you must absolutely go with a sense of humor and at least one friend otherwise you will forever be asking strangers to take your photo which gets bothersome. And it's fairly crowded so you have to wait for people to clear out of your photoWithin walking distance of a few other notable museums and attractions in the jungmun area.

This place is an entertainment on its own. This place is a hit with the tourist. Famous for Jeju local tea. If you are driving parking is free of charge and there is someone manning the traffic when it gets busy. There is a small museum showcasing the tea history but don't expect to learn much. Then you will walk into the tea shop which is quite huge followed by the cafe. We tried the green tea ice cream green tea swiss roll and jeju orange drink. Mind you the queue is very long but fast moving. I like their green tea ice cream and the swiss roll. There are few corners inside and outside of this place which is IG worthy. Nice place for the environment but it's not really museum per say. They have a branch in Seoul in case you are wondering.

This O'Sulloc Tea Museum locate at jeju and here we can find many things made from Green Tea.  For example we can find tea cake ice cream lotion soap and many others thing make from Green Tea.  Very Nice Place to visit or a good place to enjoy the good atmosphere.

This museum shows the history of teddy bears and put them in different scenes depicting their eras.There is also an Elvis Presley show at the level 2 theatre at every 15 mins. Do catch the show!This place would be fantastic for teddy bear lovers and the children.

This museum provided so much variety and information from around the globe. Kids would get bored but if you enjoy art and seeing the natural beauty of the ocean than this is a good place to come. There are also an abundance of decently priced souvenirs and a cute Cafe! My wife also received free silver pearl earrings upon entry!

This museum isn't very large and in the winter you don't really want to go outside to admire the small amount of outdoor exhibits (which you can do from inside the windows anyway) but it's got enough interesting art to be worth 1000 KRW which is about USD $0.80. For one I enjoyed the Chang Ri Seok exhibit as his paintings are very earthy. The second floor exhibit was under renovation when I went but still for 1000 won I have no complaints about the first floor's contents. The gift shop is pretty underwhelming though.

This museum is well worth the trip and it's FREE to the public. Very informative and emotional. This museum will not disappoint. I was so impressed with the honest representation of Jeju history. This museum incorporates works of local artists to help tell the stories and are very well done and effective. The staff was very kind and helpful. You also get a great book for free when you visit. My visit here was very moving and I would recommend it to everyone. Very impressive!
This museum is really nice and beautiful. The air conditioning is also a nice break from the heat. It is a free museum and often extremely crowded. The ice cream and tea were wonderful.

This museum is one of the most popular of the 50+ on Jeju Island and the carpark was packed with tour buses when we arrived. But if you can manage to get a slot on one of the formal tea ceremonies it really takes you out of the bustling tourist crowds and takes you to another place altogether. The time and care taken for all the preparations was amazing and could not have been more different to having a casual cuppa at home! I am not sure they do them in English - our host spoke in Korean but our little group had an interpreter to help us out. The venue used for this ceremony is also amazing. Beautiful minimal stone and wood shaped furniture in a sunlight-filled pavilion looking out onto the lawns of the museum. We also had a glimpse into the underground tea cellar area and a quick tour round the tourist shop. The collection of tea cups from different countries and eras was fascinating too in the area next to the shop.

This museum is not the easiest to find  located in an industrial type area. Upon entrance you receive a free sample of chocolate and a hot chocolate (not sure if this was offered due to the chilly  rainy weather  but it was definitely appreciated). Some interesting finds from around the world  historical facts  and treasures. There is an area where you may observe chocolate pieces being made for sale in the adjacent gift shop. Good stop for a rainy day on Jeju Island. Gift shop is a little pricey. Teenaged daughter loved it; teenaged son was bored.

review: This museum is located a short distance from the city center. However a taxi ride from our centrally located hotel only cost about 6000 Korean won. On the day that we went to the museum we were able to get free admittance because they had some special promotion though I think that the admission fee is very inexpensive anyway. We enjoyed the museum very much especially the special exhibit entitled ?쏞hoe Bu`s Diary: An Unexpected Encounter with China.??This exhibition will run from July 21 to October 4 2015. There is also a fascinating diorama of a Jeju village.If you like history and historical artifacts you will enjoy this museum. It?셲 well worth a visit.
This museum is in a remote location but it's quite easy to find. We totally enjoyed visit.  The exhibitions are very impressive.  Its a relatively small museum but it's the highlight of my day.

This museum is eye opening and insightful. We visited this museum (do not bring children) and was amazed at how sex was on fl display. I did not know what to expect let your imagination run wild and you will probably see it.

This museum is EXTREMELY well put together.  It is not often in Korea where you will find proper English translations.  This place does not disappoint. There is a wealth of knowledge to be found here for those interested in the sad history Jeju people have had to endure.  ProTip:  Make sure you take time to explore the outside part (the lands and the memorial wall). ProTip:  You do not want to rush thru this.  Make sure you give yourself enough time to really walk around and read about the history.  The museum covers almost 6 years worth of events and details!
This museum is basically just one whimsical photo op after another.  Great filler for your facebook album.  Fun for the whole family.

This museum is absolutely fun. From the moment I stepped in it was simply hilarious. I have always loved historical museums but I love these interactive ones even more. I was supposed to go to the Trick museum but the concierge at my hotel recommended ALIVE museum. It was a walking distance from my hotel in Jungmun so I walked over. At the beginning of the street where this museum is I saw a big sign but no museum. I had to walk a little bit before I saw the museum. I think they have to do better with the signs on the major street so visitors will be more informed on how to get there. It also looks like some wings are in still in construction. The road leading to the building looks like it needs finishing too.That being said once you get into the museum there are lots of interesting exhibitions and pictures. Most of them were famous painting s that we could interact with while taking pictures. It was fun watching other people interact with the pictures and sculptures as they took pictures. My favorites were the ALIVE Aquarium the coiled python that was squeezing the life out of me being a mermaid being dinner and fighting the leopard for my red suitcase. They are some sculptures in the museums grounds that are very interesting and interactive too. For just about $9 USD I had a very memorable day in Jeju. This is one of my favorite attractions in Jeju Island. I highly recommend visiting the ALIVE museum while on Jeju Island.
This museum have a lot of teddy bear. You must visit this museum if u go to jeju. For me teddy bear museum is fun to visit with family like your son or your daughter.
This museum has been done so well and with a great tribute to the women divers. We learnt a lot about these women and have a great admiration for them. Well worth a visit

This museum features the history of tea in Jeju as well as you can view the tea plantation from the observation deck. You also can taste the green tea ice cream and cake at the cafe besides a good place to buy green tea. This area also features innisfree shop where you can make your own soap besides a lot of innisfree products on sale.

This museum displays many clay artwork and handicrafted items from ages. The tour guide and the ticket booth employee cannot speak English anyway. However the souvenir shop in the museum sells many wonderful things that we could buy home as gifts.

This is THE place if you crave green tea desserts!! Tried both the green tea soft ice cream and green tea roll cake with cream cheese...absolutely delightful! Small museum with history of tea culture lots of tea types for purchase...even green tea based chocolates and jam! The rooftop offers a good view of the surrounding areas! Place can be packed with visitors so ensure sufficient time to spend!
This is the most boring museum ever. They have some stuff made with chocolate but it's nothing nice. Also if you want to take the chocolate class you have to pay more.

This is the most beautiful museum I have ever visited - absolutely packed with three floors of seashell art. When we visited there was no one else there at all! I have no idea why - but I probably wouldn't have enjoyed it as much if it was so busy. It was a bit more expensive than expected  probably because it doesn't get as many visitors  but it was well worth it and I got a free pair of earrings! Definitely go - they have a cafe too.
This is open air museum with so many statue in the garden.  Here we can find so many statue represent Man and Women.  So Many interesting statue to take picture with.

This is not only a museum but a cafe.  There is a main cafe in the first building where you can also purchase many tea products.  There is also another quieter cafe in the building up the hill where are can also take time to make soap.  The second cafe is not visited by most travelers and I would highly recommend it.

This is not exactly a museum  but a shop impersonating as museum  that sells teddy bear. Uses gimmick of hand make teddy bear that resembled Obama and some other celebrities  but really nothing interest unless one is crazy over teddy bear.

this is not a museum. This is a place surrounded by green tea plantations. It is also a place for you to get your tea fix. They have a plenty of teas to choose from and some are packaged so Nicely as gifts. I personally go back there for my green tea facial masks and powders. Its my third time there already. But be prepared the place is on most tourist groups itinerary so it can get a tad crowded. But for me its usually pick buy and lets go. So im totally fine w it. Stop by if youre a tea fan to pick up items to bring back.
This is not a museum. It's a collection of anything vaguely sex-related. It really seems like something a middle-schooler designed. Please save your money.

This is more of a shop and cafe than a museum. The museum part is just a few display cabinets that leads to a cafe with goods displayed for sale. The tea plantation across the street is a flat moderately sized area that pales in comparison to the vast rolling and picturesque tea plantation of cameron highlands.This attraction is not worth the time unless one is a tea-lover.

This is located in the southwest quadrant of the island and can be a chore to get to without a car. The highlight of the building is the tea drinking experience that you need to make a reservation for(I'm pretty sure) that is entirely in Korean though so bear that in mind. There are tea fields in different directions for quite a ways the ones next to the museum are setup for visitors and picture but the further away fields aren't meant for tourists. We arrived around 10:30 and it wasnt busy at all but when we were getting ready to leave at 12:30 it was quite full.
This is just a regular museum with a small collection of glass from different parts of the world. It is far away from everything and not worth the trip. I would skip it.

This is better known as Jeju Love Land Park and I thought it was hilarious! Everything that could be penis shaped is penis shaped it is full of sculptures pictures dioramas. I wouldn't call it educational or a museum but a sex themed amusement park and indeed I was amused!
This is an unexpected indoor/outdoor museum. To be visited on sunny day. This museum depicts the stone culture of Jeju island with lots of interesting structures. It is entertaining for the kids.

This is an amazing place. The museum is absolutely first rate. All the exhibits have explanations in perfect English.  There are lots of interactive displays. If you are interested in the geology of Jeju you should come here first and expect to spend several hours. Outdoors there are 3 courses (walks) with exhibits of life in old Jeju. The exhibits are well done and English signs are excellent.  This place is huge and amazingly you will have it almost to yourself. It has an entry fee of about $5. That is the bargain of the century!   Don't skip any of it. It could easily take a full day if you are intellectually and esthetically inclined. It was the best thing I did on the island. I spent only about 4 hours. I would suggest you bring food and water with you. I had a few apples and tangerines.
This is an amazing collection of natural and men made stones in Jeju. In addition it has an outstanding water instillation and an indoor unique museum. Truly worth the visit

This is a well put together museum. It has all of the explanations in English. The museum includes an outside area as well as the inside. It covers the history of the island as well as the way of life of the islanders. There's a wildlife and fish exhibit.

This is a very expensive museum that is not worth visiting.  Although they have a lot of antique teddy bear and nice gallery but most of the explaination are in korea that make us difficult to understand their history.  The staff are not good in speaking English or Chinese.  The only good things is their surrounding scenery are nice for photographer to take photo.
This is a smallish 3D museum and only worth going if you are going to the Greek Mytholody Museum and mini maze next door. Combined ticket 12k Won.
This is a nicely designed artistic museum for tea lovers. It also has a cafe serving tea related desserts.
This is a museum depicting life in a traditional Korean village. Great place to explore and appreciate the scenery as there are flower gardens as well. Great place for photography.
This is a great museum and I highly recommend you visit this museum. With a bit of imagination lots of photos to be taken.
This is a funny museum in Jeju-si. It describes life in Jeju back in the day pretty well. Have a go if you've time.

This is a cool teddy bear museum for all the teddy lovers out there. Even non-teddy lovers will be converted :) There are interesting celebrity teddies such as Elvis and Einstein. Lots of good pictures to be taken!

This is a contemporary art museum by the seafront in Jeju city showcasing a private collection in a disused cinema and an old bikeshop. This has to be the best museum on Jeju. I have lived here for over 5 years and I have been there at least 3 or 4 times. The exhibits are interesting and there is even a couple of places where you can play old video games for free. If you enjoy computers or video games at all this the place for you.

This can hardly be called a museum. The museum part takes 5 maybe 10 minutes to see. After that it is nothing more than a very expensive tea shop. That being said if tea is your cup of tea you would probably enjoy trying their many different tea creations.

they have museum they have display how green tea is processed (but in korean only); they should have it in english as well. very nice place where you can sit and relax have a yummy green tea ice cream. but they do sell many kinds of green tea - blend with candy tutti fruity brown rice. the packaging is super cute but a bit expensive. you can buy lots of green tea as souvenirs for family and friends because these are special from jeju. worth visit!
They had French drawings and sculptures on display those which are masterpieces by Monet Rodin  Renior and many other great artists were displayed at the museum. Entrance fee is 10000??per person.

There's really nothing much to see for a museum but the cafe is good for a tea break and the green tea plantation is a nice backdrop for photo taking if the weather is good
There's probably other attractions that are better than the Alive Museum. It was just not that good nor was it bad.

There's not really much museum. I thought I turned a wrong corner but had actually walked through the whole thing. Just one wall of tea cups and pots and basically no English signage. But it's free and you really go for the tea shop and cafe.Nice teas for sale (spendy but tasty!) and there are often free samples in the tea shop. Then move to the cafe for some green tea flavored sweets. I recommend the softserve ice cream twisted with yogurt. If you're here take time to climb to the 3rd floor observatory for some nice views. If you have a little extra time it's worth two other stops:1) just through the garden path walk up hill to the natural skin care center where you can smell local essences and make your own natural soap (for a fee).
