There is nothing much here at the museum but the green tea ice cream and the green tea cake roll are fabulous! The green tea cake roll sold out in a very short period of time! We reached there at around noon time and we were so lucky that we took the second last roll! I guess the cake roll is pretty popular among the locals too as we saw a lot of locals stopping by at the cafe. I saw an O'Sulloc Cafe at Myeongdong too. We went in the morning and there were still quite a few of green tea cake rolls there. I wanted to get a cake roll the night before I flew back to Singapore (in order to maintain the freshness) but the staff told us that it has been sold out! The green tea cake roll tastes really good when it's eaten fresh. People who don't like the cream in the middle might not like the cake. Other than food you can go all the way to the third floor to take some photos. Personally I feel that the scenery outside of the building is much more nicer. There's a big park right in front of the tea museum there are people who lie down and chill on the grass. There's tea plantation located opposite of the tea museum. We are allowed to wander around there for more pretty photos.
There is no English wordings in this museum. There is a store and restaurant here. You can give it a missed if you want to know more about the tea history.
There is no chocolate model  just Chocolate shop  don't think to go there. its poorest chocolate museum in the world.

There is nearly no advertisement for this museum in the city. I saw the sign at the traffic and wanted to give it a try. The building is so small that when i arrived I thought it will be a quick tiny event. But once you are inside you will be amazed by the beauty and the variety of seashells. Most of the explanations are in Korean but still nothing can stop you to enjoy this museum. At the roof  there is a giant shell  which you can go in and have a photo. There is also a small shop where you can buy gifts to your loved ones and something for yourself too.

There is actually nothing much in this museum. Only Teddy Bears depicting some celebrities and events. I had expected more exhibition so I was disappointed with what I saw. I read that there is an outdoor museum but I didnt manage to find it. Recommended for kids only.

There is a very small museum-ish area which shows a variety of teas. But basically its a shop for their products and the cafe.  You can try their signature green tea products which are also available in all their cafes around the country.  They have a nice viewing deck area where you can look out onto the tea fields.  The tea fields are also accessible so that you can stand amongst them to take photos.  Watch out for the spiders.

There is a cafe and merchandise shop in the tea museum which seems like it is the main attraction of the museum. So go early to beat the tour groups. If you are not a sweet tooth skip the green tea latte. Go for the soft serve ice cream. Do not miss the plantations. Plenty of photo opportunities if you venture into the green tea plantations
There are three connected mazes.  You can go through one or all.  A great way to spend a few hours.  There is also a museum/exhibit maze in the building.

There are so much to see in this museum. The whole day is enough to spend here if you want to read and appreciate all the displays. Good collections. I learned a lot from this museum. I regret doing four museum tours in one day for we had to rush this one. I would love to go back here.

There are several museum of sex & health in Jeju islands.  Jeju Loveland is one of them located a short drive from Jeju Town or Jeju Airport.  It is also a stop of Jeju Golden Bus City Tour.  There are hundreds of sexy and comic sculptures which are placed outside in a well maintained park.  There is also a soft core art galleries and adult toy stores where things are quite expensive. The entry fee: Won 12000 Timing: 0900 to 2300 hrs. Entry allowed for adults above 20 years of age.  It is something different.

There are several Alive Museums in Korea and Singapore.  Each features a series of themed scenes for trick-art photos.  You can pose as directed for each scene and create a funny memorable photoThis one is located in the Jungman Tourist Resort area on the southern side of Jeju Island.  We ended up going there on a rainy day when it was just too blustery to be on the beach.  Unfortunately everyone else had the same idea and it was too crowded.  We had to wait so long to take photos that we ended up not getting very many views for our memory book. I think we only took about a half-dozen.  It was so crowded in fact that it was even difficult to walk.  And it is a big place!  There are also interesting photo ops outside the building such as with various types of vehicles and statues.  I think the Alive Museums would offer a better service to visitors by following the system used by museums for special exhibits:  issue a limited number of tickets for a specific time period allowing one group to move through to a certain point before starting the next.  Really the best part about our visit is that we purchased a combo entrance ticket purchased there for 12000 Korean won  (about $10 USD) that allowed us to visit the nearby African Museum which was FANTASTIC and well worth the time spent there.  So if you go to the Alive Museum try to go early or pick a sunny day.  Or if you don't mind crowds and lots of jostling about it can be part of your rainy-day beach retreat.  Either way get the combo ticket!

There are many interesting places to visit in jeju. Limited range of products. Disappointing. That is why I am giving it low rating. Soap making? All stations are full.. You don?셳 see products flying off the shelves. And neither do you see people walking out of store with lots of shopping. Telling signs! Go next door. Osulloc Tea Museum. Eat and spend there...

There are lot of naturally formed stones from volcano eruption. There is also a museum where they teach and share about volcano eruption and a nice place to take pictures with the stones where they have arranged it nicely.

There are 3 terry bear museums in Jeju. The one which we visited is Terry bear and safari. The lower floor is the safari and upper floor is the bear. Think this also to attract the kids to visit the place thus the safari.Take your time to see and enjoy the many characters of the terry bear. One corner of displays is a very expensive due to diamond crown.

The teddy bears are so cute and the child can learn a lot knowlege via knowing the different style teddy bears. We learn more about the historic story. All my family members love the Teddy Bear Museum!

The tea museum isn?셳 the highlight. It?셲 the cafe after. Super crowded but the staff does a great job making orders and moving people through. The garden outside is nice to walk through and the tea field makes for nice photos. Parking was free.

The Tea Museum is situated on the south-west coast of the island in Seogwang. There is an interesting display of cups and teapots used in Korea under ancient dynasties. The museum provides an insight into the immense range of teas and derived products (especially cosmetics) and of course they can be purchased there too. Quite pricey.Learn about the history of tea and how to make it. The Jeju Samdayyeon Tangerine tea was being sampled as we were visiting. We also recommend trying the refreshing green tea ice-cream in the modern caf챕 attached.You can take a stroll across the well-landscaped gardens.Of course Osulloc Teas are available for purchase in Seoul too.

The tea museum is not a muesum at all but instead a huge store selling tea. Other then that the tea fields are nice to look it. You can make some green tea soup and eat green tea ice cream. Be warned this place is always packed with tourists.
The tea museum is just two shelves. The place makes money from expensive drinks and cakes and other souvenirs like tea leaves and mugs.
The tea fields are lovely - a photographic opportunity. On a clear day Hall Mountain is visible in your photographs. Aerospace museum is next door for those interested.

The tea caf챕 and museum were extremely crowded so we headed for the Innisfree Jeju House.  It was a delightful oasis of calm comprising an organic food caf챕 a large space for making your own soap and a smallish retail space dedicated to bath and arotherapy products as well as a small selection of exclusive souvenirs.  We had the house special bingsoo (the Korean ice kachang) and it was so refreshing.  Not only was the shaven ice powdery soft the red beans were tasty the selection of healthy nuts crunchy and various Korean rice cakes both soft and crispy were delicious - all in a great dessert.  Being starved of clean fresh air for a while during the haze season back in Singapore it was very refreshing to sit outside enjoying the cool clean air and view the miles of tea bushes.We were so entranced by the place that we returned for lunch the next day.  I had the rice balls with soba & oden soup while my sis had a mini hot dog with the same soup.  We then proceeded to relax with a cup of coffee.  What utter bliss!Besides enjoying the F&B we picked up body scrub facial wash and some soft drinking bottles.  The staff was friendly and fluent enough in English which made our buying experience very smooth indeed.  We will definitely return when we are next in Jeju.

The staffs there were really nice. We were caught in a typhoon and hitch hiked in. They saw us drenched so they offered to send us back to our hotel after we finish our tour in the museum. How nice. Great hospitality. Plus  they have quite a bit to display.
The staff at the museum was lovely and welcoming  truly nice. The collection of seashell is quite impressive.
The scale and the scope of the museum itself is small but this is made up for by the caf챕 inside. The Innisfree JejuHouse is a better deal when it comes to diverse caf챕 faire and gift options.
The rolls and green tea lattes are a must.  Museum has a lovely ambience to it. Cafe closes early at 6pm.

The place was drizzling when we got there and managed to squeeze in one last parking lot beside the tea museum. eent straight to the tea museum and the place was really crowded. it showcase the tools used in tea productions and Got a few tastings of various type of tea and souvenirs. Went for the famous ice cream dessert and drink - good. Next walk over to Innisfree building where they have an open area for children to  play with the playdough and display of cosmetics product as well as a cafe with seating area. Outside tourist were busy taking pictures of tea plantations and themselves !

The place was crowded with tourist when we were there The Cafe was full Did not have a chance to sit sample the tea and cake. Museum explaining the history of tea. Unless you are into tea can skip if you do not have time. Don't need much time there 30 mins.

The place is small but there are a lot different section and concept bears in the museum from drama series to fashion...and my favorite Elvis Presley!! I wish they have more bears soon. Good place for adults and kids to visit!

The place is not well-maintained  to say the least. It felt like a haunted theme park experience rather than a nice museum. The place was empty from visitors  basically there were hardly any staff present. The installations are rusty  the cafe and the restaurant were closed down. All in all  it felt haunted therefore we left with some bizarre feelings. I'm sure once it was beautiful but neglect made its damage.

The place is nice with exhibits of the tea culture and evolution. however the cafe is often crowded with visitors and finding a seat can be challenging. the exterior view is fantastic! visitors should also explore the area outside the museum!

The place is a bit run down and really short of foot traffic. We were accosted when we stepped into the museum shops. The entrance fee is relatively steep for Jeju - 12k for each adult.The exhibits are tasteful in my opinion but the rust is showing. For the entrance fee I expect to receive at least a small souvenir.

The performance itself is worth the price of admission. Make sure you arrive before one of the three showtimes during the day. They provide drums and you can jam along with the performers. I find this satisfying when you have so many museums in area feigning novelty. So again  If you can get your toddlers away from the stuffed animals  then there is a rewarding human element waiting on the bottom floor.

The O쨈Sulloc Tea Museum and tea field is a treat!  It쨈s easy to get to by the airport bus we got to it by taking the Yeha West Tour.Be prepared for crowds in the cafe.  However if you go across the road to the tea fields it쨈s easy to walk along the tea plants and be alone in a field of green tea.The museum is interesting and explains the tea picking and fermentation process.The real fun is the cafe and shopping for tea!  It쨈s a bit overwhelming but fascinating to think that so many types of tea can be produced with one leaf!O쨈Sulloc also sells a cosmetic line I haven쨈t tried any of those products so I can쨈t comment on their cosmetics versus all the other great stuff that Korea has for skin care. The cafe offers the most delicious green tea ice cream.  I쨈m dying to try the cakes but can쨈t get pass the ice cream.  There is also a brown roasted tea ice cream but I prefer the green tea one.  It isn쨈t sweet and has a distinctive green tea flavor left on your palate as you get ready for the next bite.Recommendation--I got the Cold Green Sticks which are perfect for a bottle of water.  The other teas you definitely need a strainer otherwise get the tea in teabags.Oh and O짢Sulloc has a cafe in the Nampo area in Busan if you need your green tea ice cream fix. Other cafes have green tea ice cream but OSulloc is yummy and my favorite.O쨈Sulloc seems to be branding itself as a high end tea so you just can쨈t purchase it in a grocery store nor do the hotels have it as complimentary tea a shame since it is a Korean brand. So stock up and enjoy.

The owner of the museum is an artist himself and one of the most important collectors in the world. I was totally taken away with many of the artworks and with the location itself(specially the Bike-Shop and the Cinema). One of my reasons for traveling South-Korea is discovering and enjoying modern art. This is the best collection I have seen in this country so far (out of around 30 museums and galleries). I was totally surprised to see this level of Art in Jeju and will definitely visit Arario in Space when I am back to Seoul.

The Osulloc Tea Museum is located around 30 mins from Seogwipo and 35 mins from Jeju city.This pleasant venue is comprised of the Tea Museum a shop a coffee place a cosmetics shop and the tea fields.We didn't visit the museum as we are familiar with the processes. Instead we visited the coffee shop where we had a Sejak green tea an ice cream and a slice of roll cake. Everything was good!We also bought some tea cosmetics and hung around the tea plantation.

The Osulloc Tea Museum is just not a tea museum but I would rather say a tea complex which includes a Tea Cup Gallery various Tea Culture Rooms such as exhibition hall masters of tea vessels tea life center etc. tea caf챕 and tea gardens. Tea Museum also offers a premium tea class in which brewing our own green tea and sharing with friends during the premium tea class is one of the unique experiences so far in Jeju. In the class they not only explain tea and tea brewing methods but also demonstrate the use of various tea wares and their importance in making one good cup of tea. In the end it was a good memorable day to make and drink green tea. Besides museums souvenir shops and green tea caf챕 there are few tea gardens and resting areas where people can enjoy nature relax and take pictures to keep their memory forever.
The museum part was interesting a bit crowded at the food area but the queue was fast and quite a lot of tables. Purchase 30000won to get tax refund. Lots of tea selection.

The museum part of the building was only about 2 small rooms with a bit of history of tea-making.  Most of the rest was taken up by the gift shop and cafe.The green tea (Swiss) roll which is their iconic cake was sold out completely on the day we were there even though it was only about 11am.  Made do with green tea and tangerine soft serve ice-cream and tea.  The tangerine tea was beautifully presented in a stoneware cup and tasted better than the green tea.There are very limited food choices for a full meal and this is more a snack cafe.  The food at nearby Innisfree is much better with a wider range.  Eventually we had the green tea cake back in Seoul where it was easily available at the O Sulloc outlets in Myeongdong.

The museum is very small. The main attraction seems to be the cafe next to it. The tangerine smoothies at the cafe taste very good. Its matcha ice cream and desserts are pretty ordinary  Japan still has the best matcha in the world.
The museum is very small. Find it very weird not any form of art but just like kamasutra book on the face. Ticket is pricey for what you see.

The museum is small but tastefully decorated and designed. The tea products are great and the presentation on how to drink/pour tea was an experience in itself. Go and enjoy! It is truly worth your visit.

The museum is really made for kids.  The museum is filled with endless pieces of slightly altered art that enhances optical illusions.  Kids would probably love the museum and the endless optical illusions.  If you are adult you will be amused by the paintings for approximately two minutes and then you'll be quite bored after a while.The middle of the museum also contains some sort of self playing organ or set of instruments which was not very impressive.There is also a karting facility on-site but I did not try it.  The karts did look a bit slow though and it didn't look too fun.If you do decide to spend the 10000 won per person then keep your expectations low and don't try to over-analyze the paintings.  Just don't think too much and you'll enjoy your time there then...

The museum is quite small and expensive....there are 2 floors with old teddy bears and teddy bear versions of famous painting and famous people. If you are nearby you can go but I would not specifically go there. My 3 years old son was little scared by the giant bears in display! Koreans seem to like it more

The museum is only a short walk from the Hyatt Regency hotel where we were staying.We went there to keep our daughter occupied but to tell the truth we all enjoyed the place. I enjoyed the way the displayed were made up from events in history.The only spoiler was the noise from Chinese tourists!

The museum is mostly outdoors and everything is made of glass. However  the garden it self is not looked after very well. We also thought you were able to make your own glass  but thats not what happened. Instead we had to choose one glass and paint it and fill it with color sand.. Not worth 38000 for enter and this piece of glass.. The museum should be renovated..

The museum is located opposite of Jeju Korea Tourism Organisation and can be reached from Seogwipo or Airport on bus number 600. The entrance fees is 2000 won and there are 3 levels of teddy bears exhibition and the ground floor is where all sorts of teddy bears are being sold. There is a cafe within the museum and a theater showing Elvis Presley lookalike teddy bear singing Elvis's songs. It is about a 15 minutes session.

The museum is located in the middle of the tea garden and the air around the place is so fresh. The museum explains to you quite in detail about the tea history and next to the museum there is a shop and cafe selling product from osulloc. Very very nice place to visit especially the garden area. However this is a very touristy place too and quite far to access.

The museum is limited in size but the fantastic shop and cafe make up for that. The history is interesting but the ability to smell and taste teas is awesome!  Highly recommend the Hallabong Fredo!  The green tea was great too. Pretty views of the landscape.
The museum is excellent. you get to understand how Jeju island is formed and the geothermal activities.The ground itself is hugh. It takes about 1-2 hours stroll.It is cold and windy in Dec.
The museum is easy to navigate and move about and there are enough exhibits around. About 1 to 2 hours here would be enough. There is also a nice souvenir shop in the complex.
The museum is big enough but boring. They should have more interesting stuffs. Especially more aircrafts.

The museum has some interesting and sometimes humorous displays. The real attraction here is the outdoor sculpture park. A walk around it is  like no other outdoor display of art your have ever seen. Well worth the price of admission.This experience may not be for everyone. Obviously it is sexually oriented.
The museum has really cool exhibits and they were beautiful to see. It's easy to relax and forget about the outside world.
The museum has nothing much in it it is more like a cafe with overcrowding issue. The tea plantation is of decent size and good view for photo spot.

The museum has a wonderful shop where you can buy amazing varieties of tea. All of them wonderful flavors. If you like tea this is the best place to visit and to spend a lot of money in high quality products.Also they have a coffee shop with the best green tea ice cream and green tea roll cake.
The museum has a bunch of pictures and areas that one could pose in to make it seem like they are part of the painting. This became one of our families favorites on a rainy day.

The museum had some very nice glass art pieces  even with a flower garden made entirely of glass. Nice and fun place for the young and old. However the maintenance of the place could be better and some areas looked a little under-maintained.

The museum doesn't offer so much there is a miniature showing about making tea leaves process starting from the plantation to end product. But I did enjoy the scenery so much a wide green tea plantation you can purchase a cup of green tea ice cream which tastes really good (you will buy the second cup as soon as you finish! enjoy the scenery and feel the wind cool breeze in Spring.

The museum can be improved with more English explanation. Go to the open air top for the best 360 view of the area and plantation. There are signs at the plantation warning of snakes but none spotted during our visit. There is a crowd at the cafe and shop but the turnover is quick as most of them followed a group tour and hence can't linger that long. You can get a seat if you are not in a rush. The stuff are expensive but it won't deter a green tea fan. Do be extra careful when crossing the roads to the opposite car parks. The cars and trucks are speed demons.

The Museum caffe offers very delicious tea and I recommend the very fragrance green tea latte and creamy Osulloc milk tea. There are other types of tea offer too such as red papaya milk tea. The tea must go with the green tea cake roll and green tea ice cream or green tea O fredo. The cake roll is soft and like the green tea ice cream it's just melt in your mouth with great green tea taste and scents . All the food is not too sweet. On top of this the free wet tissues that offer in the cafe provides extra cooling effect probably it has added some green tea extract just the company cosmetic brand  Innisfree green tea mask.

The museum becomes busier as the day goes on really busy late in the day so going early is the best plan to be stress free and see everything with little to no people there for best photo experiences.The museum is really cool and covers Korean tea history. It leads to the tea shop where you can sample some good tea cakes and teas. You can also purchase teas here as well as other tea confections.Next to the museum short 5 minute walk is the Innisfree Jeju House which I cover in another review. You can get lunch and some fresh teas to enjoy here. There is also great tea and Jeju House related products as well as fun tea soap making kits. Ones you can do there and others that you can take home.Before lunch at Innishouse but after tea and snack at the Tea Museum you should walk the plantation. Great photos in the fields next to the tea museum but across the street are two areas one with a big tree that is old an beautiful but also a tree with deep red blossom that makes for a great photo with Hallasan in the background.The Stone House was closed for renovations when we visited in April 2018.

The museum and park are both really engaging. We learned a lot and enjoyed a family discussion on history and human nature. The park is really gorgeous and the entire experiences as moving. A highlight of our trip.

The little museum has a simple collection of vintage tea cups from around the world. I am obsessive about tea cups so was very happy with the unplanned encounter. There was a small section on the history of tea but unfortunately for us it was mostly written in Korean. The place was buzzing even after its opening hours. Service was quick and friendly. Wide tea selection no lesser than the two O?셎ulloc stores in Insadong and Myeongdong. Above average tea beverages and desserts. (For green tea fan who is familiar with Japanese tea - this is the Tsujiri equivalent of Korea).As some reviewers has mentioned this is a tea shop+cafe+museum so don?셳 expect just a museum.

The Lee Jung-Seob Street near the museum is where more time can be spent (than the Lee Jung-Seob Museum) with some good restaurants and cafes lining the street that is decorated with art influenced by him or replicas of his work. Visitors can also take a look at his old home located on this street.

The last time when i was visiting the glass museum was in the night time and this time round was in the day timeI have see the difference between the day and night and i personally like the night time as all the light are lighted up and it is so beautiful and romantic.

The Joanne Bear Museum is one of the stops in the package tour that we availed of. It is basically a collection of stuffed bears that Joanne Oh has created  each bear hand made. There are three buildings where all the bears are housed. We were there in winter and the place was well-heated. The pathway between the buildings were open air  though. The bears came in different sizes  colors and variations. There are some depict historical or cultural scenes  others depict pop culture. The bears are all finely crafted. Unfortunately though  many of the signage are in Korean only.There are several displays where guests can pose with the bears. One of those bears  a polar bear  was featured in a Korean drama  ?쏱aradise Ranch.??I especially loved the displays that feature the acronym of the place (JB) because it is my initial as well. There is a souvenir shop which sell?봸ou guessed it right?봲tuffed bears. I wanted to have one as a souvenir so I was settling for the least expensive keychain bear when I saw a much larger 8-inch plushie being sold at a discounted rate; it was only 2 000 won more expensive than the keychain so I got it instead. As with many of the Joanne bears  it an embroidery of Joanne Oh's signature.

The Jeju Areospace Museum is located SSW of Jeju at road 1121. It is a huge and obvious building which you can not miss. Lot of parking places are available. Entrance fee is quite reasonable. 2 adults and one child for 28k Won. Good and accessible for stroller and wheel chair. Inside there are a so many things to see. The museum is clearly structured and you have enough room and peace. We went there in the late afternoon and only 3 tour busses were waiting outside. So the museum was quite empty which was simply perfect. Very interesting and nice to see and study was the science? room where especially Bernoulli was explained practically very well. Further you have a huge hall with plenty of planes and units/turbines. Other areas showing other planets and space ships and so on and so on. The good thing is you have plenty of room and feel not like in an anthill. Our three years old boy had so many fun and was so interested. Me too of course and even my wife was quite impressed. Outside a couple of more planes and helicopters. Some of them accessible and we had a lot of fun. There is only one minus: mostly missing English explanations. The value vs. money is worse to stop a second time.

The indoor section of the teddies was not big and could be completed within an hour. There are teddy bears of different celebrities and famous events. There are also exhibits that shows the evolution of teddy bears over the century. There is also the world's most expensive teddy bear not to be missed.There is a short mechanical Elvis presley teddy bear show every quarter of an hour. I did not visit the outdoor section of the museum.

The green tea museum was nice.  They had tea sets from around the world from many different ages.  The gift shop had free green tea sampling which was quite delicious.  They also had a cafe where you can buy green tea roll cakes ice cream and lattes.

The green tea museum is a must see for all travelers. You can walk the grounds learn about the benefits of green tea on health and enjoy numerous teas and pastries. In addition they are connected with many other health and beauty attractions

The government run museums in Jeju finally opened on a trial basis limiting a number of hourly visitors to 50 with online reservations being required (although it didn?셳 really seem like a must when we arrived).  Considering it's a large complex (which itself looks impressive) Jeju Museum of Art didn't have a whole lot in display other than a temporary exhibition consisting of mostly projected images.  Thorough explanations of the pieces were provided on pamphlets and the display although few in numbers  used the wide spaces well.
the Glass museum was very nice.We were amazed how they showed us the process of making a glass bottle.We have bought souvenirs from there..

The glass museum is well presented and extremely pleasant environment!While the building seems modern and edgy the products are sweet rather than overly modern! If the gift shop is not making a huge profit it is because the gifts seem dated!

The folk museum is a huge cultural town-like place located at the south-east portion of Jeju Island. It is easily accessible by car. For those who are self-driving like I did fear not there is an abundant number of parking lots to park your car and it's completely free.The admission fee for an adult cost around 10000 won. Considering the size of the museum it's a rather reasonable price. The museum is divided into many different sections showcasing different cultural aspects of Korea's rich history.If you get tired from walking or can bear the scorching sun the museum provides a tram service that brings you around the museum stopping at different attractions. There are also many different restaurants and snack booths selling traditional Korean meals as well as snacks. If you have never been to Jeju before do take the opportunity to visit this place at least once! Ideal for all ages.

The erotic and exotic art sculptures are interesting and daring but a bit dated.I think the museum has already operated since 20 over years ago based on our driver's comments. It sure is time to undergo an overhaul to spice up the place with digital technology 3D virtual arts and robots.

The entire place is quite nicely run by Amore Pacific who owns large green tea fields and cosmetic brands such as Innisfree. The tea museum is a small setup which links directly to the retail section. Don't expect much from the museum but the retail section is a heaven for tea fans! Adjacent to the tea museum is the local specialty shop of Innisfree. Checkout the Jeju specials such as green tea essential oil. Surrounding these 2 building are endless stretches of green tea farms.
The Dolhareubong (grandfather rock) collection on the grounds outside the building were my favorite part of the museum.

The chocolates there are not exactly cheap. We found cheaper ones on sale by the tourist attractions. Not exactly worth paying 3 000won to see some choco display. Nothing really that impressive too. The 3 000 won entrance ticket can be used to redeem for drinks or offset chocolate purchases within the museum too.

The chocolate museum was a highlight of our Jeju trip in 2020  the fresh chocolate made by the resident chocolatier is a real treat. Be aware that not only the quality  but also the price of the chocolate is on an international level  with a decent-sized box going for some 30 dollars. But for buying three boxes  we got three tickets for a chocolate making workshop  which was greatly enjoyed by the kids.We will come again  if only to get some memorable treats. The museum itself is informative  but don't expect too much.

review: The cafe is pretty good with green tea drinks of all kind and dessert! We tried the green tea ice cream which was really good. However almost EVERYONE comes here so it will take some time to find a table. Be patient and enjoy the outdoor fields. I personally thought the outdoor fields had more to see than the so called museum. They also have a variety of green tea for you to buy as souvenirs too. Really easy to find with a huge free parking lot.

The butterfly museum is interesting showcasing many species of insects but the information are all in Korean. Walk out of the building there is an outdoor park with a maze. The mirror maze is not to be missed the kids had so much fun finding their way out!

The building looks altogether too expensive aggressive on the outside. The garden is much more welcoming. The oriental poetic flavour of tea culture is missing in spite of the half hearted follies in the garden and the half moon shaped enclosed courtyard. Koreans' wholesale acceptance of western contemporary architecture does not work too well for tea museum. Still not bad for photo taking. We did not find too many affordable items in the store. We were also told by locals that they are not organic and spray herbicide.

The building has a good shape good exterior and interior. For the museum itself it is not that special. The interesting part is that you will be explained some kind of tea and they will give you a tester for you to drink. The tea is so good it is worth to buy. And in its cafe they have green tea ice cream and hot gren tea latte which is surprisingly taste really good! Don't forget to buy some :)

The brochure states that is a glass castle. This is definitely not a glass castle but a fun museum  so if you have kids and they are expecting to see a Cinderella kind of environment  well  this is not .What you find though it's the explanation on how glass in made and transformed in different shapes (entrance) to different kind of finished product. If you want  you can also have a go (helped by professionals)!It's a good  small scale museum and it's quite entertaining and educational. A mention of honor goes to the ticket guy at the entrance. On our way out we asked him to help us out to get a taxi. He was the sweetest and hard-core-customer orientated guy I saw in action in Jeju (and  I must admit they are all very good). He tried to get a taxi for us  getting the price  helping us (mind you  his English was limited  so he struggled a lot but nonetheless worked hard to explain us everything he could) and even giving us for free a cold bottle of water whilst waiting outside (for the taxi). You could see he was really trying his best and I hope someone from the Museum will read this feed-back and rewarding him.One thing I would avoid is the Coffee Shop inside the museum. You will find a girl with a grudge (promise you...the whole time)  doing nothing but playing with her mobile and almost being upset by you interrupting her during her game. I think this is the only person in Jeju I have found soooooooo..... unhappy and customer unfriendly? Maybe the ticket guy could teach her?Another note: you can get a 30% reduction ticket for the submarine a few kilometers away.

The best part of the tea musuem is the cafe which serve green tea latte ice cream cakes. i never get to try the green tea cheese tiramisu cake at the cafe so i headed to one of the O'sulloc in Myeongdong. It is really good. However the museum is just average. There are only cups and tea pots displayed. I think the BOH tea plantation museum in Malaysa is much better. Just my 2 cents.
The bar in the museum offer very nice tea with cakes and it also have a beautiful scene outside of the museum.

The attraction consists of a tea museum a cafe and a tea field. If you have been to Seoul you will notice that there are other O'Sulloc Tea houses in Seoul minus the tea field. We had the green tea ice cream here and it was good but pricey. The tea field itself was great for photos but it is not all that different from other tea fields you see across Asia. I don't think this is a must-see attraction but it is great as a pit stop if you are passing through the area.

The art is so real and creativity is the most appreciated from this museum. Long walk through the hall with many art picture along side you. At the end there's cozy cafe and beautiful garden. Unfortunately when we visited there it was raining so we can't play and took photo at the garden.

The ambience is good with green being the dominant colour . You are literally welcomed by the green tea fields. The museum has history about tea i loved it. Then the tea they sell at the store within the museum its crazy.i thought we kenyans are crazy about tea but these guys took it a notch higher. Flavours from cherry to rose to caramel and they are pocket friendly. I loved the tea ice cream personally. Visit again please

the alive museum is quite big and fun ... lots of different sections for photo taking . and the place for taking photos is quite spacious . no much tourists when we are there so we can take our time for each photos  there a outdoor place for photo taking too.
The Alive Museum is huge compared to similar museums in Seoul. There are so many paintings to take goofy pictures with! My parents (in their 60s) enjoyed it too.

The Alive Museum is an exhibit of life-sized optical illusions of which you can pose with for some really fun photos.  Admission was 10000 won ($10 USD) each.  It will take you between 60 and 90 minutes to get through the exhibits.  There are more than 100 photo opportunities.  Make sure you arrive with a charged camera or camera phone.  I would not recommend going alone as you would have nobody to take your photo.  An ice cream and coffee shop is located towards the end of the museum.Highly recommended.  We are glad we went.

The Alive Museum in Seogwipo is a pretty nice museum that is near a number of good restaurants and is definitely not hard to get to on foot. For 11000 won you can take photos with plenty of crazy cute and cool paintings all over the museum; this is definitely their specialty. I really enjoyed some of the paintings especially the ones near the picture of the wings that makes you look like an angel. The gift shop at the end and of course the mandatory photos taken of you upon coming in are really overpriced and we didn't go outside because it was so cold out but the inside was pretty worth it to get so many cool photo opportunities. If you're not into taking pictures though this museum probably isn't for you.

The admission fee for trickeye museum in Jeju is cheaper than other branch in Hongdae and Busan. I dont know if there's different inside the museum of every branch or not but the Jeju branch is relatively small. But its not too crowded so you can take the picture freely without long queue with other visitors.

thank you very much for your visit. we're so glad to hear you were happy with Elvis show even though you were not quite interested in other teddy bears. however we believe you had felt delightful childhood's memories while in the museum
thank you very much for your visit. and also appreciate your kind explanation about our museum. we believe everyone might be happy with lots of interesting exhibition in our museum.
thank you very much for the visit. we hopefully believe you had a wonderful time with your kids at the teddy bear museum
thank you very much for the visit. lots of adult visitors loves our museum while they are in the museum they could think happy childhood memories. ^^
thank you so much for your visit and indicate the correct original teddy bear museum
thank you so much for your visit and a lovely good suggestion come to our museum.

Temple is nice design and along our walk we found many tangerines tree which I believe during the spring season the temple view will be good. Since It's FOC do drop by if you have time. It's along the way to Teddy Bear Museum and Cheonjeyon Fall Yeomiji Botanical Garden
Teddy bear museum! I think is all the children favourites!  I have brought home a little brown bear ??Just for fun  There are a lot of theme bears u can see in the museum  so just enjoyed it.

Teddy bear museum was such a curious place ever. Many kinds of teddy bear are displayed on there and also great to take photos. Think takes 1~2 hours to look around here. I really liked it and also teddy bear souvenirs are pretty good to prepare as gifts but a little expensive to buy a lot. Anyway i would like to recommend to visit here. This museum is worth a visit:)
Teady bear musuem in Jeji island is another touris spot for bear lover. 2 hours walk in the museum is a good walking tour whr en travel in Jeji.

Tea Plantations are not my favourite places and this is not a museum as such. But the way the Koreans have done this makes it into a relaxing afternoon experience. The cherry blossoms just came out when we visited. There were scores of Korean students on a field trip but that's OK. It's spacious enough for everyone. A short display of tea cups from around the world lines the entrance of the building. Then it's tea shopping and testing. Try the buckwheat tea! Lots of chinese speaking staff (as with everywhere else in Seoul). Here I tasted the best green tea ice cream and cake. A walk in the surrounding garden and compound is nice. There is a glass building next to the main one by Korean brand Innisfree. In it there are soap making activities a cafe and skin care shopping.

Tea plantation near the city center with a tea museum containing a few old tes pots (you will probably have wider assortment in a flea market). I will probably enjoy visiting an actual farm with fruit trees and greenhouses planted to vegetables than spending time at the tea plantation. There is no entrance fee but there is also no tour guide or someone or something to explain what there is to see.

Tea house you can find all variation of tea from osulloc brand. High quality of tea in korea. And there are cafe inside you can order drinks and food that contains of green tea really unique. Dont forget to take a picture at the tea garden in front of their museum.

strictly for those above 18.but beware that buses come here ends early.after 10pm i only see taxis and cars.Interesting stone sculptures of male and female organs.sex positions..a shop selling interesting condoms and penis keychains vibrators etc..super cold at night..open until midnight..there is a indoor museum and show clay figurines..

Strictly for adults this open air museum has many stone sculptures of male and female in various positions. There is also an indoor museum with miniature clay figurines a souvenir shop and a food stall within the compound. Admission fee 12.000 won. Suggest you combine this place with the nearby Nexon Computer Museum.Transport tip: From the airport take bus 331 332 465 466 at airport bus stand 6 between gates 4 & 5. Alight at Jeju Museum of Art walk 400m. Bus fare is 1150 won journey about 30 mins.

Stopped here on the way to Segwipo from Jeju City. Had an incredible lunch at Innisfree House walked the gardens and then had dessert and tea at the tea museum. Highly suggest this site to anyone who enjoys serene landscapes and healthy/energizing food!

Stop by Alive museum on the way to visit other places spend an hour inside the optical illusion museum and play kart outside.  Karing part is fun with the two seater. (Kids can sit next to parent) and it is 4 times faster than the ones in Disney.

Sports fans will probably enjoy this the most. Not really sure what to do here beyond appreciate the cool design for a couple of minutes and then go into the stadium for two more minutes. It's stunning  but likely best enjoyed during an actual game. The structure houses a sex museum (wasn't that interesting) and a paper doll museum (didn't try that one). Unless you're a soccer enthusiast or an architect  youll be fine enjoying its striking design as you drive by.

Spent a few hours at the museum along with many many others! Small building with some good information but crowds crammed the shop which leads into the cafe. This caused overcrowding and did not make for the most enjoyable afternoon. Outdoors area is worth wandering through and the gardens and fields are worth looking at. The Innisfree Jeju House across the way is probably more interesting.
Spent a couple of hours at this museum. It was a fun attraction to visit with friends and got a lot of hilarious photos.
Spend about 30mins. Nice view of black valcanoes columns. Impressed with the natural view of it. 5 mins drive from Play Kpop and Alive Museum.
Spend 1.5hours there. Autumn weather and view is amazing. 11000won per adult is quite pricey. Theres real animal in that museum

So this is more a shop than a museum to me. But the cafe there is highly recommended!! You need to try the green tea cakes and the cookies as well! Wish i could've tried the ice cream but i was afraid i get sick. It's literally the best roll cake. The garden was nice and you can make your own shop at innisfree didnt have enough time though.. Remember to take pictures at the cup made of plants across the street..
So much history saved at Jeju Museum of War History & Peace. As they say sometime war is necessary for the peace to follow!

Small museum which showcases lots of green tea cups from around the world. As it was raining at the time of visit I spent more time indoors and at the cafe. As this is a tourist hotspot the cafe is always full and finding a table is quite a challenge (I was lucky though). I recommend ordering the green tea ice cream and the cold drip tea which is only sold at the Jeju outlet.Will probably visit again next time to see the green tea plantations which I missed out on.This museum is a stone's throw away from Innisfree Jeju House - barely 90 seconds walk which is worth a visit as well.
Since you are at Osulloc Tea Museum already

since it was raining heavily with winds we decided to visit this top rated museum in jeju. its similar to trick-eye museum in seoul so if you have visited that then you might not find this so exciting. There are many trick potrait where you can stand and take some nice 3d pics. Even though we didnt take much pics we were happy to see many ppl posing around. some of them are quite funny too.

Seriously the number of people that were there on a sunny afternoon stressed us out. It almost seemed like a one drop shop rather than a museum. There was very little to see in terms of the museum the shop and the cafe were f***ing noisy and busy we couldn't even walk through. We had set B which included a green tea roll cake a hallabong drink and a green tea ice cream. Very average. SKIP!

Seashell and coral art in their fascinating and natural colors. The seashells' mysterious world under the sea-- as designed by several artists. (is this a title. If not keep original sentence) With a collection of 7 800 species  hundreds of millions of beautiful shells and corals from all around the world joined by metal craft and copper  present the world's first 'Museum of Seashell Art'

Run by a tea company that touts itself to be a premium tea brand the tea museum is nothing more than a small exhibition of some historical earthern ware and the owner's/ company statement about bringing back Korean tea culture to modern society.It has a tea shop (their tangerine and Camellia teas are good) cafe (very crowded but has really good green tea sets  for two consisting of ice cream a drink and green tea Swiss roll) and a tea workshop area called the Tea Stone situated in a garden. There's also a tea plantation where you can score some good photos or just simply take a quiet peaceful stroll through the greenery.Nearby is the innisfree Jeju House which also has a cafe selling some of their beauty products. The selection isn't great and they don't  give you free samples though you could score some Jeju only products. I find going to Myeongdong for your K beauty haul much more satisfying and easier on the wallet. Or if you just wanna stop by for their DIY soap making activity (they also sell the kit at the store so you can do it on your own) it seems like a peaceful way to escape the hustle and bustle of the city.

Rows of organic tea plantations for cha lovers to scent savour and calm the senses.  A must-go on tourist itinerary so be prepared for crowds.  Long queues at the cafe for tea desserts.  Check out exquisite Samdayeon (?쇰떎??is a Korean post-fermented tea matured for a hundred days in barrels made out of cedar wood from Jeju Island) soft ice cream unique to Jeju shop only. Interesting tea blends and gifts at the tea shop. Don't miss the outdoor fields across from the museum for kettle and cup shaped plant sculptures and windmills for photo taking. A walking path connects to Innisfree Jeju House for more afternoon tea Innisfree products and craft making classes for young and old.
Relaxing museum with great visuals

Recommended place to visit for family with young children and teddy bear lovers as this museum holds a large collection of teddy bears with themes all over the world. Downside is that souvenirs are way too expensive.

Really enjoyed our visit but would say it is more of a shopping venue than museum but we really enjoyed trying different types of green tea and also green tea icecream!!!We would have enjoyed more if more of the history had been shared

really didn't expect in such conservative country seeing this museum but making money is not easy so they made it . if u looking for fun experience and some kind of new pictures which probably can not share any where so go for it . when i visited place i met many old grand ma than young :D

Quite frankly I am not sure how to describe the tea museum and its surrounding. I had high expectations that were disappointed. The museum is fairly small and not really that informative or wow the adjacent souvenir area and caf챕 doesn't look too appealing either. There is a small tower that offers a nice view when on top. Nearby then the Innisfree Caf챕 which was already closed when we arrived and then the tea plantation where lots of people take selfies with tea bushes in the background.And that was it. I would say good for a quick stopover but not really a destination in itself 30-60 min there more than enough.

Quite a big museum and there are many fun and interesting spots to take photos. Entrance fee is around 9000 krw per person but you can spend a good 40mins to 1hr in the museum walking around and taking photos. Very good place to visit. Not too sure how accessible it is by public transport as I booked a driver for the day.

Purchased both museum & go karting which provided a fun morning. More fun pictures than I expected & certainly took many photos!! Make sure have plenty of battery as think get better with photos as you go.

Probably because it was still cold but i wasnt a big fan of the field or the museum. Im sure during the summer it is much better greener and the weather would be ok for enjoying a green tea ice scream.
plus: the concept about 3D art is very good me and my wife very excited. if you like art and like to take a photo. you must visit this museum.minus: nothing

Plenty of interesting glass installations in the park and museum. Really worth to see. Very nice and friendly owner. Many beautiful things and funny toys in the shop. The best way to get there is by taxi  it's about $15 from Seogwipo city center.

Place is breathtakingly beautiful. There are mountains and the sea. Great place to stopover and enjoy the view. Take a short stroll about 20mins downhill where the ship museum would be. Didnt go in but the exterior looks great enough for photos. Occasionally there will be a small carnival at the foot of the hilll and also a small group of barn animals.

Perfect for a rainy day and this island has a ton of them!When we pulled up we weren't sure if it was the right way place. The exterior is huge! Doesn't look like a trick eye museum type of place. But once inside there is a ticket booth. It was 10000 won per adult and 7000 won for your children. It was well worth the price. Once inside you will see pictures that you interact with and take pictures from specific angles. With the right pose it looks like you are in the action. Took us about 1 hour to make our way through and we had a blast. Only down side is that if it is crowded people are waiting to take pictures and shoving infront of you.
Parts were cute but pretty lame. I only went because they were open later than other museums around.
Part museum  part art gallery and totally worth a visit. The shells are wonderfully displayed in a variety of artistic designs that enhance the viewing experience. Absolutely worth a visit.
Pales in comparison to Osulloc Tea Museum but it's worth a look since they are side by side. The products in the gift shop are the widely available Innisfree facial products.
Overall..this museum is good if we go with family due to my visit this time is for business tour..so just enjoy take photo and buy some souvenir for my kids.

Out of our surprise no entrance fees needed when you visit Jeju Folk museum. There was a guide that told us about their culture and was a nice experience for us and even the kids. The village was small but a nice encounter. An hour is more than enough.

Our two children loved this one. Easy to interact with and you leave with lots of funny pictures to bring home. Pizza at the restaurant was really yummy too. Nice break before you go out to the statue park in the back of the museum. Didn't seem to be well promoted - it's new and the first museum as you start on the road to the Jungmun Resort area. We took a cab from the Hyatt Regency (long uphill walk and potential rain) - less than 5000 won for the cab.

Our tour diverted to the tea museum because we were to visit dragon head rock but the tides were too high to take out the small boat.  Anyway would've been cold on the water with the very powerful windy day.  Building is in the midst of tea fields.  You are taken through an area with China from all over the world.  Most of the China on display was either from France or Germany.  Then you enter a room where you can buy souvenirs as teas makeup made with tea and then there is a counter to buy dessert and teas or tea lattes.  They are very pricey though about $6 for a hot cup of tea.  Then after leaving that room you enter a room where you can sample tea infused makeup.  This reminded me of when we toured Fragonard perfumery in France where everyone was trying on the lotions and perfumes.  There were even large vials filled with liquids which were identified by the plant or flower beside them.  Once again similar to the perfumery labs.  Then there was a counter to order same teas dessert and even cold tea drinks that were nonalcoholic versions of cocktails but with tea in them.  These looked like they might've been good.  We finally decided we were in need of a hot drink after the sea cliffs experience.  So we bought one of those overpriced tea lattes.

Our first stop in the Jeju trip was the Olloc Tea Museum.Here you can take a master class about how to make tea properly and try different kinds of teas.It was a very relaxing experience and the taste of the tea was very unique.If you like tea is definitely something you have to do if you travel to Jeju.Also you can visit the Innisfree shop right next to the museum and take beautiful pictures in the green tea fields around.

Our 4yo liked it well enough. We spent about 2hrs and spent more money at the gift shop than on admission (24000 won) and if it were nicer out we probably would have spent longer. Botanical garden a small garden maze Fossil museum animal feeding station bird attraction and the really TALL dinosaurs scattered throughout made for an enjoyable afternoon outing before nap time.

O'Sulloc Tea Museum is very small (there are not many displays to see) but there is a very large shop that sells tea products and a cafe that sells drinks and desserts.  There is a very brief tea tasting demonstration w/ narrative in Korean only.  In the cafe we had the best green tea ice cream and green tea roll cake we've ever tasted.  Prices for drinks & dessert was expensive ($4.50USD each for a small cup of ice cream and a slice of cake; $8.00USD for a large glass of orchid flavored iced green tea).  The tea products in the shop are also expensive.  If you are a tea connoisseur then this is the place for you.  Across the street from the museum there is an open field where the leaves are grown that you can walk around.  There is a viewing tower above the museum where you can also see the tea fields.  If you are exploring the west side of Jeju island O'Sulloc makes a great rest stop. I would not deliberately drive all the way out there just to visit this museum.

O'Sulloc Tea Museum  is actually a shopping paradise for those who fancy for tea. O'Sulloc itself is famous for its Tea product. In front there's a collection of used cups that they arranged in such a way so it's picturesque.Since It's a green tea field expect for green tea product for sale including all side products (Cake Drinks etc). The shop available also allows us to test some of their products We let ourself went down to the greentea field and see what's actually a green tea look like when it's not harvested yet. We also have a little chat with the tea-picker ajumma. If you go to the upper floor you will be able to take picture of overall green tea field but don't expect too much.I recommend time of visit when the sun not in its brightest Enjoy!

Osulloc tea is known as one of the more famous and reliable brand in Jeju...most of the tea is expensive too. Thus it is not uncommon for travel agencies to include the Osulloc green tea museum into its itinerary. A walk around the museum shows you a little background of tea in particular. You can also be able to see tea cups from different countries on display. I tried the green tea ice cream and it was yummy. We were told that if we spend more than 30000 won we can get a tax refund at the airport. So we really spent more than 30000 won on tea :) I wandered alone out of the tea museum and saw Innisfree!!! They were conducting some soap making lesson when I walked in. The deco is very different from what I saw in the malls. And of course I ended up buying stuffs....some facial masks that I wasn't able to find in Singapore.

O'sulloc plantation and museum was one of the most memorable places in Jeju.It's really unique and cool place.Even though museum is not that big but you can see and try a lot.They also sell some products in Green tea flavor but they are bit expensive..We tried Green Tea coctail and ice cream. Both were good and we don't regret spending money on it!~Also if you go to O'sulloc don't miss the Innisfree house.For males it might be a bit boring though..But if you are female this place is deffinetely amazing!

Osulloc is famous for their teas. They have a green tea field right outside the museum/cafe. Recommended things to try are their green tea ice cream green tea cake and green tea latte! Great location for picture taking in the green tea field; Bring a wide angle lens! right next door is the innisfree jeju house. Estimated time spent at osculloc is 30-45 minutes tops.

O'sulloc is a green tea museum if you like green tea is a must come or visit place. Please trust me you will like it and also there is an innisfree outlet that has more limited edition products.For more information and insight visit my youtube channel (search by title) - EN CHANNEL: #3 TRAVEL BLOG DAY 2 JEJU - NATURE - GD CAFE - TEDDY BEAR - O'SULLOC

Opposite the museum is the tea field which you can walk across the road to take a photo and see how they grow the tea tree. There's parking space beside the museum. Besides there's the tea cafe and souvenir shop at the arrival floor. I would recommend the green tea smoothie top with soft cream green tea latte and green tea roll cake. It's very crowd with tourists and local people. So normally the seat are full. So if you go with friend I'd recommend one to fine the seat and one to queue up to get drink and desserts. Even its long queue to buy but it doesn't keep you wait too long. The green tea spread is the signature. There're also many selection of tea with nice packages and different aromas for your selection.

Open air museum that hosts a plethora of weird statues that are lewd and sometimes bizarre. It is really more of a photo-taking venue than one that is educational. Even so I felt embarrassed posting any of the photos I took here on Facebook as some of the sculptures were just too sexually explicit. Great if you are going with a group of good friends for a good laugh. Don't go if you are easily offended by sexual content.
One of the many unusual museums on Jeju island. Same format and content as the american ones - but worth the trip nonetheless. Lots of great photo ops.

One of the highlight of our trip as we wanted to visit tea plantation and try the green tea products. Plantation is ok and is a good spot to take pictures. Observatory facing the plantation and museum is so so only. We tried their happy green tea green tea swiss roll and green tea ice cream. Happy green tea with a citrus taste was refreshing. Swiss roll was yummy (a must try!) and my partner loved her green tea ice cream. A great place to have our afternoon teabreak!

one of my destinations in Jeju recommended for green tea lovers. Green tea ice-cream is excellent can spend 3 hours there to deeply understand the cultivation processing and taste of green tea.  More you can find Innisfree house in the Museum.  Feel relax feel the nature there~~

One of my all time favourite brand of tea! Great to finally step foot into the museum. There are specialty teas that is only available at the museum eg the freshly roasted green tea and the herbal tea lines coupled with a few award winning teas!There are set options at the cafe and the weather was beautiful so we took our order outside and it was great sitting amongst the trees and enjoying a fine cup of tea and dessert! Highly recommend the green tea roll and green tea cheesecake! Do bring your passport along so that you can do the tax rebate once you spend 30000 won and above! Right across the street you can also take photos amongst the rows of luscious greens!

On our way back from Gahina Tea Pottery we were close-by the Tea Museum.  Many buses leave from there for Jeju and Seogwipo making this a convenient place to have a hot beverage.  Yes there is no entrance fee and that seems to be because it is mostly a gift shop and tea room.  That said the tea is lovely making for great gifts and the green tea ice cream quite tasty.  Clean bathrooms and a lovely building make this a nice place to pass through for a quick stop.

On a 3 day trip to jeju we needed more indoor activities due to the daily snowy conditions and found Jeju National Museum. With low expectations and dampened spirits as we were expecting to visit more outdoor activities we were pleasantly happy with our choice.This museum was easily accessible from our hotel as it was only a 28 minutes bus ride (costs us 1150krw). The bus stop just outside the museum.The museum itself is quite out of the way from the city centre but so was all the other places we wanted to visit and therefore was not an issue for us.Highly recommend you taking your time to read and inspect each exhibit. It is quite amazing how history laid out the changes made due to advancement through discovery. Although for a quick browser it may only take you half an hour (it took us more than 1 hour).Entry was free and I'm not sure if this is the norm but surely worth a visit even if just as a time filler.

Okay this is pretty common on Jeju I guess. There are lots of museums that copy each other and it confuses tourists. This listing is an example of that. The reviews for this listing is a mix for the Museum of Sex and Health and for Loveland there is no actual listing on here for Loveland. We did our research first to decide which one to go to and Loveland looked like the more fun one - a lot of the pictures of outdoor sculptures on this listing are actually from Loveland not the Museum of Sex and Health). I'm not even if they both have the outdoor sculptures. Loveland is mostly outdoors but it does have an indoor section too with a shop and a diorama exhibit (if you're strapped for time you can probably skip the indoor part it's not very long and the exhibits inside are mostly in Korean so if you can't read it you have to extrapolate things for yourself). The park is fun a lot of it is very silly (they even designed the bathrooms in the spirit of the park - have a look at the door handles).

Okay if visitor is kind of tea lover. Like being here for shopping which is not that extraordinary or the must spot. Just okay for the museum zone and cafe easy and relaxing tea field or area to walk but not that wow anyway. For food and drinks good but for cake and desserts I personally feel soso. For the shop and products' variety are good. Free parking on site.

Obviously this type of museum won't be interesting for everyone but we had a blast taking pictures with all the images on the wall. Just something a little different if you're looking for it. Something simple and fun to do with the family. I think kids would love it!
Nothing much in the museum but you can take photo at the green tea plantation around it and buy some freshly fried tea leaves
Not too much impressive but quite good with Jeju House Innis. The museum doesnt have too much information about tea.
Not that Jeju Museum of Art was a disappointment just that it was a small place to see limited collection.

Not so much a museum as much as a gift shop on a tea field. I live right next door and it's always super busy (not sure why). The land is really beautiful with rolling tea fields but it is not a museum just an insanely overpriced gift shop. But if you're in the area it's definitely worth a visit.
no special inside the museum but tea field is ok also getting quite many beautiful flowers near around. good for strolling & taking picture

No fee to enter but honestly not a museum! Just a place to eat green tea ice cream and other yummy green tea products. Plus buying Tea. There is a tea farm behind it which is pretty cool to see. I went when it was raining so beware the slippery. Innisfree next door has better food and drinks in my opinion.
No doubt it is quite costly but there are a lot of teddy bear exhibits here which is quite worth the visit. Try it if you are nearby. Just pick one of the teddy bear museum in Korea would be enough.

Nice spot for photo taking as there is a tea plantation whereby tourist pose for photos...Across the plantation sits the Tea Museum whereby you can shop for tea related products and have a drink/bite in the cafe to chill.Next to the Tea Museum is the innisfree shop whereby they conduct hands-on soap making class if one is keen.

nice place to walk around and see the korean culture. Since it is an open museum it is very hot during summer prepare your cap or umbrella even sun glass if you dont want to get burn. But if you like to take cultural pictures and natural flower this is the place. the location is quite far from downtown. I was with a group tour and i dont really recommend for a solo visitor to visit unless you have other purpose to come i.e to learn korean culture etc. Also perhaps it would be more fun if you visit with a guide that could explain what is behind the miniatures.

Nice place to stop over for a snack! Not much in the museum but was nice to have a cup of tea and some green tea soft serve.  A very clean and minimalistic decor. The main highlight of the visit for me was the innisfree store at the back with some limited edition products only available in Jeju. Worth checking out! The osulloc store also has various amenities for sale including skin care products.

Nice museum with plenty of green tea variety product. Nice display with fresh tea selection for packaging. A huge bar like tea shop serving green tea base ice cream drinks and dessert. A short stroll bring us to innisfree workshop for DIY moulding your own soap bar and Innisfree natural oil for your own packaging to do. Overall nice experience and price is reasonable
Nice museum with all the exhibitons. the deliberately explain bout the life of jeju women.plusThe children museum is just too cute.
Nexon Computer Museum - I went there with my buddy and we were so excited to see all those old computers on display... lol!
Never been to such museum before so it was a very fun experience. Spent about 2 hours here taking tonnes of pictures. Feel like i'm 15 yrs old again. A must visit for the young at heart!

Need something to do with your family and don't want to break the bank? This is the place for you. For $10 per person you can go into the Trick Eye museum which is designed for you to take some amazing pictures using some perceptive and trick camera angle techniques. The first floor is about different positions amongst a lot of other stuff. The whole first floor is almost exclusively written in Korean. Unless you can read Korean I would skip it. The second floor does have English. I would only go if both floors have English. It is not for non-Korean speakers.

My friends and I decided to take a 2 day side trip in Jeju Island from Seoul. Our first stop is the famous O'Sulloc Tea Museum. We went there March of this year it was sunny and yet it was cold and very windy. When we were still on our way to the museum we were already awed to the beauty of this place. Everything was green and beautiful! I super love the place!!! We first went to the plantation itself from the parking lot. Walking on the pathway in the middle of the beautiful trees and shrubs was just a beautiful feeling and much more when we reach the plantation. We also went to the top of the building for  a bird's eye view of the plantation. Our last stop is their museum they have a great display of tea cups which illustrate the colorful history of tea plantation and tea making. After the museum is the store where they sell variety of green tea products. They also have free tasting of hot teas. Wonderful Jeju Island! Great opener for a tour:-)

My family and I chose the Alive Museum over the Trick Eye Museum because the former is larger and has more art pieces. Furthermore we chose to go in the evening after dinner so that we don?셳 have to jostle with the daytime crowd. However the disadvantage of the night visit is that the karting (carting) activities were already closed at 5 pm. Moreover it was too dark to take any photographs with the outdoor sculptures in the French themed garden. But it?셲 okay because our primary objective was to have a good time inside the Museum which we did. Getting there and Fees: We drove to the Alive Museum (GPS coordinate/code 8050888) and reached there at about 7pm 2.5 hours before Museum closing time of 9:30pm. Parking is free at the huge car park. Entrance fees to the Alive Museum is 10000 won for adults 9000 won for teenagers and 8000 won for children. If you rent a car check whether there are available discounts on the entrance fees and karting on the discount booklet (we used those from the Hertz discount book).The Museum:  Depending on your time spent at each art piece and the number of visitors present (who would jostle with you for the right to pose and take photos) you would need at least 2 hours to ?쐏articipate??in all the art pieces inside the Museum. It is very easy to become so engross that you lose track of time! And don?셳 worry about how to pose because there?셱e instructions and explanations written in Korean Mandarin (Chinese) English and Japanese on how to pose. If you are going by yourself I recommend you bring a tripod along or you could take selfies (although most photos have to be taken beyond the selfie distance) or you could keep asking other visitors to take your photos.We leisurely spent a lively 2.5 hours (7-9:30 pm) inside the Alive Museum which was just enough to view and take photographs and selfies of most of the art pieces. I say ?쐌ost??because there are a few paintings of adult themes which are not suitable for my children. Anyway we almost had the entire museum to ourselves except for 6 other visitors! So we unreservedly and hilariously pose at most of the 3-D art and paintings without feeling shy and without anyone looking at us. As a result we were among the last to leave the Museum.Of the 4 categories of art inside the museum ??trick art digital art objet art and Provence art (sculpture art is outside the museum) ??my favourite are those in the trick art section. Trick art is a perspective technique which makes use of optical illusions so as to enable visitors to interactively ?쐃nter??as the main character into seemingly three-dimensional realistic paintings and artworks with the visitors eventually having a good laugh at their ?쏿dventure??  I particularly liked the 3-D illusions of the parachute standing on the bridge over the molten lava and the hanging onto a nail at the side of the building. We also enjoyed the Provence art section which is a pastel-coloured fairy tale village with bears and dogs donning period costumes.We had a truly unforgettable experience with plenty of amazing photographs and fun with optical illusions. So could you!

Jeju Museum of War History and Peace is a must-see place if you visit Jeju. Most tourists just hang out at the beaches restaurants golf courses etc or walk on the Olle. Walking on the Olle is nice--a great pilgrimage for healing. If you really want to know about the unique history of Jeju and the Korean Peninsula however you must visit this museum. Although it's hard to get there by public transportation it's worth visiting. The museum shows how Jeju Islanders were persecuted by Japanese colonialists and then by Korean and U.S. soldiers after Korea's independence. The museum's free-guided tour takes the visitors to the harsh realities of islanders' historical suffering and the division of political ideologies between two Koreas. The highlight of this museum is its peace garden. This huge garden made me pray for peace in the Korean peninsula.

Jeju Museum of Contemporary Art is the main attraction in the few square kilometers of creative space in Hangyeong-eup area.  Without even entering the building there are a dozen or so cool sculptures in the garden area.  The exhibit consisted of works by local Jeju artists including a photography exhibit of the family members of the Jeju 4-3 Incident victims.  A satellite building had a nice exhibition of paintings of the mountains of Korea.

Jeju has tonnes of 'museums' to draw in cash from tourists. Most of these are silly  man-made museums having no connection whatsoever to Jeju or even Korea. It is almost a sin to spend time in these museums while in Jeju  instead of enjoying the scenery outdoors.However I would reallly recommend a stop at the seashell museum if you have an hour to spare in the Seogwipo area. The labor of love of 1 woman  this place houses a staggering collection of shells from all over the world  crafted into stunning displays. Seashells so pretty  its hard to believe they are real..but they are.There's also a small shop to purchase souvenirs if you'd like but they don't pressure you. Also attached is a cafe.Close by to a bus stop.

Jeju Folk Village Museum as it appears on map for Jeju is on the coast and is a must do for history and culture buffs. There are hands on exhibits that kids and adults can participate and use around the village. The park and museum is large and takes 2 to 3 hours at least. Perhaps longer to see everything without rush. We were quite impressed by the size the crafts people making products and the exhibits throughout. There are ample restrooms snack shops and Korean traditional products sold in the gift shop. There is also a restaurant on premise.The Jeju Folk Village attracts students from all over Korea as well as tourists from other countries. I highly recommend the park. There are beautiful floral blooms as well as animals photo opportunities and lots of traditional Korean history and culture to learn about. Well worth the price of admission. Plan to spend half a day here. Arrive early to avoid the crowds. There are some great gifts and candies to be found around the village including the traditional Korean taffy near the Hanbok photo place and the gift shop.

Exotic Jeju Island is known for many things: the majestic Hallasan--the massive shield volcano that formed the island and the highest point in South Korea; its mandarin groves; persimmon-dyed galot fashions; the sturdy Jeju ma horses  descended from the ponies of Mongol invaders; tasty black pork; and the iconic haenyeo women divers. But most visitors would not expect to find a Museum of African Art there. And  it's pretty darn good! Located in a massive structure modeled after the mud-brick Great Mosque of Djenne  the museum offers photo-ops galore in its Safari section  although the animals are of the stuffed variety. Very popular with children and couples. The upper floors house a respectable collection of African artifacts and photographs by Kim Jung Man. There is also a great gift shop. But  I have saved the best for last...the live performance of African folk music and dance. The group  Zalia from Senegal  featured lots of drumming  and audience members also got a drumming lesson and a chance to play along on one song. All in all  a quality experience...and a surprising one.
