As the Chocolate Land is within 10 minutes??walk from the Teddy Bear Museum in the Jungmun Resort area ??just follow the direction on the sign-posts ??my family and I had no hesitation to visit it on a rainy Sunday.Getting there and fees: First and foremost  you have to note that Chocolate Land is different from Chocolate Museum. Chocolate Land is in the south central part of Jeju while Chocolate Museum is in the south west Jeju. We didn't need the GPS coordinate/code for Chocolate Land but it's 7381197 for anyone who's driving there directly. The entrance fee for adults is 3000 won and 2000 won for children. A voucher was given back for every purchased ticket which can be redeemed at the gift shop or the caf챕 or the Chocolate School.The Museum/Attraction: After going past the ticketing counter  you then turn right. The section on the left is a caf챕 and photograph/selfie stops of different types of Korean houses and benches with toy bears. There's even a figurine of Santa Claus in front of one house  which was interesting considering Christmas is still some 6 months away. The section on the right is the exhibits on the history of chocolates  with the words written only in Korean. We went down the stairways to the level below in which there's a Chocolate School which teaches chocolate making at 120 000 won with lessons starting every hour from 10am to 6pm (I think the children would be more interested than adults). We didn't go into the School; instead  we walked past M&M figurines and a Christmas tree (again interesting) and reached the chocolate shop where there are interesting exhibits of chocolates (behind glass) from America  Europe and Asia. The gift shop has an extensive selection of chocolates (I think slightly more than outside). The prices of the Jeju chocolates of the same brand at the gift shop were slightly more expensive compared to those selling outside Chocolate Land. However  the Chocolate Land chocolates became slightly cheaper than those outside when we utilised the discount vouchers. Unique local Jeju chocolates are those with pink cactus flowers  mandarin oranges and hallabong fillings. We couldn't wait till Christmas?쫤e ate some of the chocolates before we left Jeju  and these were yummy!There is a small observation area (Chocolate Garden) outside the building where the view looks towards the sea. There's also a statue of Willy Wonka from the 1971 movie ?쁗illy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory??where you could take a photograph and selfie with. But we couldn't go outside because it's raining.I recommend visiting the Chocolate Land if you have the time and if you have an appreciation of chocolates. Otherwise  I think you wouldn't miss much if you decide to skip it.

As someone said earlier this one is really more of a store for green tea rather than a museum although certainly there are display cases of tea ware to make the museum claim credible. What it is without a doubt is a gorgeous tea store. Aesthetics-wise -- it's so excellently designed it can easily inspire anyone to spend about a hundred U.S. dollars or so just on green tea stuff.The tea you can buy even in Seoul so if you don't want to lug them you can buy O'Sulloc stuff in Seoul. But I don't think you can easily find a place elsewhere that serves the O'Sulloc food they were serving here. I tried the green tea cappuccino the green tea cake green tea cookies and green tea soft serve. They were reasonably yummy although nothing to rave about. O'sulloc Green Tea displays its wide array of teas packaged in gorgeous boxes and tin cans. These are perfect as gifts for loved ones.They also house a cafe in the store where you eat and drink tea-infused items. Fortunately we were able to visit its branch in Seoul already (and bought our fare share of their tea boxes) so we focused our time in Innisfree instead.Innisfree has numerous branches in Seoul; however it's best to look out for the Jeju-exclusive items available in the Jeju house. Similar to O'sulloc Innisfree also has its own cafe which serves its own selection of drinks and food; for those not interested in its beauty products.

As noted by other reviewers there are indeed large crowds to beat on a weekend visit but the tea museum is definitely worth a visit. Good to note that here is English subtitling on most of the signs in the small museum. The biggest draw for me was the beautiful architecture of the building. Local volcanic stone is used in combination with brick glass and steel. The result is beautiful and the building has featured in quite a few design magazines for good reason.

As it was raining on the day we visited we could only have tea in the cave caf챕 and look at the souvenir shop. I managed to get an olive coloured leather bracelet with a sterling silver magnetic catch for my niece for a good price.  Whatever we could see of the grounds looked very promising.We will consider returning here on a fine day on our next trip to Jeju.

A worth to visit this museum quite similiar to TrickEye Museum (imo). Many interesting poses and the place is big.

A large variety of tea and tea sets. Nice litle store where they sell the tea's and set together. Too many groups and very crowded but interesting enough to spend a short time inside the tea museum.

A great place to learn about history and culture of Jeju. Stone museum is a must-see for those who are interested in geology. Views of the Sky Pond reflecting nearby mountain are fascinating. There is a small traditional village. You can borrow an audio guide at the ticket office for free.

A good place if you love tea.They have a tea plantation that you have access to and take pictures. Not bad but when we went it was pretty hot. So we opt out of that. The museum itself was alright. Your Eyes will tell you one thing. Your experience will tell you another. All in less than 10 minutes.An this is not part of 'Alive' or 'Trick Art Museum'.Although this peculiar stretch of road in Jeju is only about 100 metres long, it really does draw in the crowds.  I arrived there as a skeptic. My wife have read the brochures and blogs about that place. But I was persuaded to be there. Following the instructions:1. drive car to start point, indicated by a stone pillar on the side of the road.2. engage Neutral Gear3. switch off engine4. disengage all brakes (foot and hand brakes)5. sit and relax as you feel your car roll UPHILL!Outside you you will see tour-leaders and other disbelievers coming out with all kinds of theories and proofs. They have their   spirit-levels   (as contactors carry) and cans of soft drinks to, without external force, roll uphill.All this in 5-10 mins.  Figure out HOW for yourself.

You want to know about volcanoes? This is the place. The museum is interactive and informative. And not to mention it houses some of the most beautiful natural volcanic sculptures around. There are three courses to follow in order to see what the park has to offer - taking things at a leisurely pace, this can easily take 3 hours to complete. It is well worth it though - with the some of the paths in course two taking on an enchanted forest appeal. The entrance is 5000 won, and you can get to the park on the Jeju City Tour Bus. The stops are just outside the park. A good poncho will serve better during rainy weather than an umbrella here, as there are parts of the course with low lying foliage (and the wind can be a little ferocious at times too).

You must pay for 2000KWR/ adult for entrance. It has natural beautiful. Comparing with Ghenh Da Dia in Phu Yen, Vietnam, It 's not as good as Genh Da Dia. But i think it's still a good place to experience in Jeju. It nears KPOP Play, TeddyBear Museum and so on

You have to walk on a ramp in order to get into the museum because car cannot drive into the area of exhibitions. The venue is separated into indoor and outdoor. For outdoor exhibitions, you should be aware of the weather. If it rains, the ramp would be slippery, so visitors are recommended to wear water-resistant shoes for unusual events. There are plenty of cars exhibited, including antique cars and modern cars. There are descriptions beside every single car including where they produce, which car firm belongs to and when it is first produced. There are many limited-edition cars and some of them are even the only one in the world. There is also a shop located besides the entry of the museum, selling different car models and peripherals. I bought a wheel like key chain, it costs 10k KWD, which is relatively cheap compare to the models of cars.So, if you are a car fan or you want to have some souvenirs about cars, you are recommended to go to the car museum to buy your favorites.

review: you can view the teddy bears from different countries,enjoy yourself at the museum shop, caf챕, restaurant or the outdoor park where you can view the spectacular Jungmun Sea. At the museum garden, you can meet the teddy bear sculptures and models. The garden decorated with various themes such as the Korean Black bear family and the magical pond. Children under are free. Lots of free parking.

You can start the trail downhill from Story Ville villas and end at Oedolgae. On that Ole trail there is a museum and a coffee shop on the way. If you drive there, there is plenty of parking and small restaurants, etc. people come here to watch the sunset.

You can reach this place with Jeju tour bus - if you're going to the Roe Deer Observatory as well, I suggest you go there first and then walk downhill to the Peace Park (less than 10 mins). If you do it the other way round, you'll have to trek uphill. The admission for the Peace Park is free and everything is in English. The museum offers a comprehensive account of a controversial point in Korean history: some exhibits are quite chilling and upsetting but I think it's important to understand the history of this island: Jeju is not all about tangerines, erotic statues and kitschy teddy bears.

You can find all kinds of teddy bears in the museum and the   cosplay  is simply amazing. I was impressed by how creative they are. There is a garden behind the museum for which you can have a short walk with a couple of photos.

You can easily spend 2 or 3 hours walking around the stones and getting to know the  past lifestyle of the island population as well as the geological history of Jeju. Volcanic rocks are exposed as real art pieces in a museum, allowing you to have a different look at them and admire the work of nature.

You can discover your favourite teddy or safari animal here. With 3 floors of huggable and adorable animals there is much posing, hugging and choosing. You can even get a teddy to propose marriage to you.Teseum should not be confused with Teddy Bear Museum located in Seogwipo (near Alive Museum), a more 'serious' museum.

Yongmeori is a rough and dramatic coastline shaped from lava eruptions. Walking along the spectacular rock formations is an experience that only Jeju-do can offer. Firstly, some of the water pockets with bright turquoise water are striking in their uniqueness. Secondly, the sometimes bizarre rock formation are nothing if not eye-catching. Lastly, the strange (slightly grotesque) insects that scurry along some of the rocks are strangely interesting. They never touch or climb on you, every footfall makes them scurry in all direction. Yongmeori is a bit off the   classic   tourist itinerary. Most visitors enjoy a beach or two, maybe a hike at Hallasan or the Seongsan Ilchulbong, and perhaps they fit in a waterfall and museum. Jeju has so much to offer that is often overlooked. Yongmerori Coast is one of these places.

Without considering visitors could visit and shop at this museum, they charged the highest entrance fee among all other natural sites we visited in Jeju. If it were not for the kids, it was certainly not worthwhile to pay 4 times the entrance fees to other UNESCO sites.

Whilst I'm giving the Teddy Bear Museum just 2 stars for quality, value for money, class of exhibits, and any actual worth as a proper   museum  , I have to admit that my visit made me laugh. I'm not sure though that derisive snorting sarcasm was what they were looking for.This museum is a pile of pants, masquerading as teddy bears.. The   attractions   are about 15 to 20 poor quality adult-human-sized bears, dressed in various outfits of clothing, with a challenge to guess   who   they are dressed as. Military uniform and two medals apparently is enough for a bear to resemble Prince William, for example - and a grey wig and   E=mc2   to represent Einstein.Then there are the bear portraits. Frames containing bears dressed to vaguely resemble famous portraits. Mona Lisa teddy bear, anyone?There's no   history   of the teddy bear, no collection of historical bears, no pictures / video clips of teddy bears being made, no maps showing where different types of teddy bears originated from - nothing educational whatsoever. There are no audio tours, no leaflets or signs to show the visitor around, and certainly no staff available to talk to about any   exhibits  , whether you are Korean, English, American or anything else.The gift shop on the lowest floor contained the largest number of bears - none of them particularly special, all just your usual cheap mass-produced bears, but at slightly hiked up prices.By far the worst part of the visit was the funniest. Your ticket includes entry to the   Elvis Stage Show  . Oh dear Lord, where on earth do I start? The show is on every 15 minutes. In a room with about 12 benches in it. There is a curtain at the far end, hiding the   stage  . On the quarter hour, the announcement is made -   The King of Rock and Roll, Elvis, is in the house!   The curtains open, and there it is. The Elvis Presley Show. Six, sad, lonely looking teddy bears, dressed in stage show outfits, rocking gently on their animatronic sticks. The three backing singers sway gently on the right, the drummer's arms flail up and down towards the drums, the guitarist's arm moves.Elvis meanwhile gyrate and swivels his hips, the crowd goes wild. Oh, no, sorry, that last sentence was a lie. Elvis sways and looks like he almost falls several times.Worst animatronic puppetry in the world. Hilarious. Hilariously BAD. Less than two minutes later, the curtains shut, and   Elvis has left the building   - until the next showing in approximately 12 or 13 minutes' time....Don't go to the Teddy Bear Museum thinking you'll have an interesting visit. Go to see the absolutely bizarre vision that South Koreans have of   entertainment  .

We went to Udo island on 27th May 2016. Weather was pretty good and sunny. Udo island is a full one day trip. We took a taxi from our hotel in jeju city to intercity bus terminal. Booked our tickets to Seongsan ferry terminal bus#710. It runs on an interval of 20 minutes. We took our bus at 9.40am. It took us approximately 1hr 30min to reach the terminal. From there, we booked our return tickets for the ferry which takes you to Udo island. Return ticket is valid for the entire day and no specific return time is mentioned on it. So you can spend the day in Udo and take any ferry from Udo back to the terminal. To book ferry tickets first you will need to fill some form lying there on the tables. Then show the filled form at the ticket counter and they will give you the ticket. Ferry runs every 30 mins from the terminal. And it takes 15 mins to reach Udo by ferry. Upon arrival to Udo island, you need to walk for 2 minutes and you will see various vendors for renting bike and bicycles. For renting a bike, you need to have driving license and for foreigners international driving license. We didn't have it, so we booked a hop on hop off tour bus. There were two vendors for the bus tour - red buses and blue buses. Red bus tour vendor offered 5 destinations and blue one offered 4 both at the cost of 5,500KRW per person. We booked the red one as we wanted to cover 5 destinations. Also, red buses were available in abundance and blue buses seemed to be pretty less. Once you book the bus ticket, you need to keep the ticket safely with you for the entire trip as whenever you'll board the bus you need to show it to the driver. So DO NOT lose the ticket. Hop on the bus for your first attraction and on the way you will get to see beautiful Udo island with small and tiny roads and farming everywhere. For going to the next attraction, you can hop on any of the bus as the bus service is really good and arrives every 20 minutes at the attraction point. We loved all the attractions except for the museum which I guess was our 4th attraction on the list. You may also skip any of the attractions by not getting off the bus. We also tried peanut ice cream there which was really good and refreshing. Also, you can take a speed boat ride on one of the attractions. In our list, it was the first attraction point to the beach. They charge 10,000KRW for speed boat per person and take you to eight scenic views. We also located so many dophins in the sea which was so exciting. After all the attractions are covered, bus will drop you back to the ferry terminal and while boarding the bus driver will finally collect your ticket.All in all, a memorable and a pleasant trip for us. Just avoid going there on a rainy day. Good luck!!! :)

We went to the Teddy Bear Museum only because it was right next door to the Lotte Hotel Jeju where we stayed.  At 10,000 won per adult and 8,000 won per child, it is a bit pricey.  You can be done with all the displays and the 5 minute teddy Elvis show in an hour.  If you like teddy bears then it is a museum for you as there are alot of cute displays and exhibits that memorialize past events in history.  Kinda cool but not my thing.  I enjoyed the outdoor park area more.  You can take pictures with cute bear statues and sit and enjoy the greenery.  There is a cafe that sells Taiwanese pearl drinks and a nice gift shop.

We went to the Glass Castle in spite of the 9000 Won entry fee simply because of all the hassle we had gone through to get there. Inside, it was really nothing more than a glass art museum, and a relatively small one at that. Admittedly, there were some very creative works of art, but there was a lot that wasn't that impressive as well. Over half of it is outside so, if you are there on a rainy day like we were, that will kill the experience even more. If you have young children forget it, there is almost nothing for them to do without spending additional money for them to make a glass craft. The crafts are neat but spendy. At the end of the museum, there is a gift store that, in my opinion, was really the only good reason to come here. Lots of cool trinkets to get for gifts and souvenirs - of special note are the hand painted, hollow, personalizeable, crystal balls. If you are up to the trip and willing to pay the cash to look at glass art go for it. Otherwise, there are other more interesting things around to do.

We went to eorimok trail to enjoy the winter festival. Great outdoor fun for children. Best part its free (except for 1,000krw parking fees). My kid loves d slide!! There?s even a museum to learn how hallasan mountain was formed. In my opinion this is the best place to visit in jeju.

We went there for lunch. It is next to O  Sulloc Tea Museum. There is a car park next to it, if it's is full, can park opposite next to the tea plantation. They serve Bing su (shaved ice) as well. Tried the tangerine shave ice. Average, don't waste your money. Menu limited an pricey. Can purchase Innisfree products as well. Price same as Seoul. Nice place to relax. There is soap making class, where by one cAn purchase the ingredients and make a personalize soap. There is a tea plantation next to it.

We went there by taxi from O'Sulloc Tea Museum. It's interesting when the displays are made of glass but nothing impressive. The entrance fee costs 9000 won but my friend and I got a discount thanks to the taxi driver uncle, and we end up paying 7000 won each.. The displays are mostly outside. On the 2nd floor, there is a gift shop..you can buy some gifts there and the cost is acceptable for some (e.g. accessories, keychain, etc) certain products (e.g. glass displays) are more expensive. It was raining when we visited the museum, but we just went around the museum and took some pictures. It is good to visit once but not more than that.

We went there after 5hrs cycling under the Sun at Udo Island.  The feeling was like, from oven jump into the fridge - it's definitely have a great cooling effect! It is very much different from Batu Cave @ Malaysia or Silver Cave @ China, Guilin.  As this is a Lava Tube.  Its long and not much of stalactite or stalagmite.  It is a long cooling lava tube.  I am very impressed by the way they develop and maintain it.  It is clean and 'safe' to walk (you'll need around 1 hour to walk in and out, and it is pretty dark and quiet inside) about, instruction & illustration are clear.  I would say it will be more fun if you imagine how this tube has been formed and even picture yourself in the movie :)  Wear sport shoes for a comfort walk.  If you have time then it is good to experience this. Note:1)  I bump into a group of backpackers from Hong Kong where they took public transport to this cave, and I was told that they need to walk quite a distance from the bus stop to this place.  So check properly if you were to go with kids & elderly that you might want to avoid such a long walk. 2) Next to the entrance there is a museum, there is a fun digital photo service there where you can choose the sightseeing background and snap the picture of yourself, then amend it, you can pay and print it out if you are happy with it or you can just re take as many times as you wish! It's all self services and I had fun here! It's not expensive tho, try it out if you happens to be here. 3) Nearby Manjang Cave there is this Kimyeong Maze park, just about 5-10mins walk away, don't miss this if you are around this area too.

We visited this Innisfree flagship store after visiting the tea museum just besides it. This shop had a cafe with very nice looking desserts and staff were friendly and helpful. However, was sorely disappointed that a flagship store only sold skincare items and no makeup items at all :(

We visited the museum a bit reluctantly and only because we had dragged our two children (10 and 15) round two scenic waterfalls and an archery practice place in the hours before. Our youngest daughter was definitely keen to do something that she chose. When we got there our suspicions seemed to be confirmed with a relatively high entrance fee (I think it was 6,000 won per adult) for what seemed to be a small place.However, once we got into the diorama room, both kids couldn't stop themselves from oohing and aahing the whole time. You really felt that somebody had fun putting it all together. It was in all the little touches (like adding little German flags to the 'storming of the Berlin wall' display) and the set ups such as the 'Bearacotta Army). As previous reviewers have mentioned, all of these are in glass cases so my husband (who is a very keen photographer with decent equipment) didn't deign to take any photos - our teenage daughter took over instead. Having just completed our photobook, I can only say that we had plenty of good shots, I could easily have filled 20 rather than 4 pages with good shots.We didn't miss any English explanations - the teddies really spoke for themselves. We also didn't approach it as a museum but rather as a fun place to look around. The re-enactments of historical events from the 20th century were also fairly self-explanatory.The shop was probably the only really boring bit since the selection was not particularly big and the prices, given the location, quite high.Overall, don't go if you want to learn anything about teddy bears but do go in with kids (or adults who appreciate the cuteness).

We visited the JAM (Jeju Aerospace Museum) and it was stunning, I love anything connected with planes or space so I was in heaven, the displays are well laid out and there were so many interactive displays for kids too that it shows that there was much thought in the museum.Not only was it about aircraft, but also about Korea's history of astronomy which was so fascinating that I could have spent all afternoon in this one section, Then we went into the space exhibition and again I was stunned at how much South Korea has achieved. We always think of? USA & Russia as being at the forefront, visit the JAM to have your eyes opened.Wonderful.

We visited in the Teddy Bear Museum in Jeju around late Nov 2017, and it was quite empty when we visited.  The entry charges was pricey considering the only activity was to look at teddy bears in glass casings.  The glass casings made it difficult to take nice photos, as there were lots of reflections.  However, the kids enjoyed the place very much.  There is also an outdoor area (don't miss it, very nice place to take photos).  Overall, an above-average place to visit, but it is indoors so if the weather is bad, this is a place you can drop by.

We travelled using the Jeju City tour bus and stopped here after visiting Jeomul Natural Recreation forest . There were other stops but we did not get down to visit the other places due to time constraints. Initially, we planned to only visit for an hour but the park was surprising large and interesting and we ended up spending over 2 hours here.  It was time well spent.  We saw lots of stone statues and products in all shapes and sizes. The displays of rocks and rock formations were scattered all over an extensive outdoor park as well as an indoor museum. You need to wear comfortable shoes, wear a hat and apply sun block. Toilets were clean and strategically located around the park and clean drinking water was available in many places.  You only need to pay a small entrance fee and it was well worth it. There was even an air-conditioned resting hut with hot/cold water and seats just outside the entrance.  In our opinion, we think this is the most interesting stop on the public tour bus circuit.  Highly recommended.

We took ride on bus no. 282 from Arang Joeul Street to visit Teddy Bear Museum jeju which is nearby to Jungmun  tourist resort. Bus fare cost us only KRW 1150 per pax. The visit to Teddy bear museum was fantastic especially for my sister, teddy bear lover. It was amazing to see many collection of teddy bears from all over the world with different themes and events globally.  There were three sections of the teddy bear museum; starting from the history, artwork and forest of teddy bear. There was a garden outside of the museum with the construction of enormous teddy bear. We can get a glimpse of the LV and Swarvosky teddy bear. The most nostalgic teddy bear was the Princess Hour theme teddy bear. The most great thing to watch was the Elvis Presley show. However, the teddy bear sold there was expensive. It was worth to visit this place.

We stopped here on a whim to go zip lining which was pretty tame but a lovely way to view the green tea fields from above. The guides were good but very minimal English. We stopped and had some green tea ice cream at the cave cafe which is really unique. It's a true cave which gives you a break from the Jeju heat and humidity. The server here spoke English and was really nice even helping people take photos at the cave   photo spot.   We enjoyed the small tea museum too but would have appreciated translations for the exhibits. Overall a fun couple of hours.

Do not confuse this waterfall with Cheonjiyeon waterfall. The admission fee was KRW2,000 per pax. You can kill two birds with one stone. You get to see two attractions the famous Seonimgyo bridge with seven nymphs carves (fairy bridge) and the three-tiered waterfall. We did not go for the third waterfall as the trail was quite steep. We only went to the pond of fairy and the second waterfall.

We stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal and took bus 110 from Jungang Rotary bus stop to Jungmun Tourist Complex. The bus journey about 30 minutes and cost less than 2000won one way. The bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly (Although I did not see Jungmun Tourist Complex on the TV screen, therefore I used GPS to locate instead. You can press the bell to alight. For my other bus trip, the stops were announced correctly and was reliable). We actually stopped that Jungmun Tourist Complex to go the the Teddy bear museum and Cheonjeyeon Falls before proceeding to the beach. Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. The journey on the bus we great as you will pass by paddy field, wind mills and wild flower fields. You will see a beautiful beach 1st ( I think it is Geumneung Beach) but don?t get down, get down at Hyeopjae beach as the view is nicer (about 2 stops away). You can walk down the stretch later (There is a public toilet down the stretch if you need). The weather then (April 26) was 12 to 17 degree Celcius and remember to buy a jacket and windbreaker as it was very windy when we were there. We so blessed that the sky cleared up to reveal one of the most beautiful turquoise beaches I have been. The beach was wide and the colours of the water clear and blue. There are many caf챕 where you can buy a hot drink from. Noted that the caf챕 only allow you to use the toilet if you buy a drink (the receipt will print the password to get into the toilet). You can always use the public toilet. We decide to walk along the orange and blue ribbon trail (Jeju Olle Route 14) and it was one of the best trail for me. We complete only part of the the trail where we walk through the villages to the fishing port. The route will bring you to a serene path with light house and the wind mills. The the path became rocky nearing the windmills, and we decided to walk out through the rocky back alley of a shellfish place (away from the orange/blue ribbon) and landed at a bus stop. We took bus 702 back to seogwipo. It was a must go beach but only on a clear blue day where the magnificent of the beach will show up.

We happened upon this place along the drive to Jeju Folk Village Museum (which is a must do). The walk around the park only takes about 1 to 1.5 hours. There are some nice views and the crater is cool.

We had the best time at the 3D Alive Museum.  As you walk through there are pictures on the walls and floors that you pose in certain ways to make it appear the picture is   alive  .  You can be sky diving riding on a magic carpet in King Kongs grip etc.  We edited our pictures once home and they are wonderful!  Highly recommend this museum!!

We had an afternoon to kill and it was too hot for any outdoor activity so we decided to visit the museum. It had a fairly interesting display of teddy bears - displayed by era and themes. Highlight was the most expensive teddy bear in the world - the Louis Vutton teddy bear. If you had limited time on Jeju, this is not a must-see, but I'd like us you had an extra day, then, this is worth going on a hot or rainy day.
We had a taxi tour and this just happened to be on the way to a museum. It was neat to experience and see, but I wouldn't stop by if it was out of the way.

We got there by bus. It was a rainy day and the walk was like 2-3 km so we took a taxi. 5 min drive for 4$ was a very good option vs getting all wet. This was one of the highlights of my jeju trip. Walking down those amazing lava tubes. You feel so small. It's midly cold and water drips from the ceiling so bring an overcoat. The ground is uneven but you can walk easily still. Saw old people with walking sticks along the way. Very cheap ticket entry for the marvel this is. At the end, there is a beautiful stalactite that makes a great pic. There are dim lights along the way but my headlamp made walking easier for me and people walking in front of me... You guys are welcome lol There is a restaurant at the entrance. Pretty expensive one. But if you cross to the joined convenient souvenir shop, they make fast korean food for a thenth of the price. They have soup, gimbap, mandoo and they are very good. Not the greatest place for souvenirs since that store is the only one around and does not have much. We enjoyed this museum thoroughly.  Thousands of teddy bears with a multitude of poses, extremely creative. Very good history of teddy bears.

We enjoyed our time in Innisfree Jeju House very much and will definitely return if we ever visit Jeju Island again! It links to Osulloc Tea Museum. We did 3 Jeju Olle Route 1, 6 & 7 and 14-1. We did not complete all the Olle route but every one of the route was breath-taking and worth the walk. All the route were doable by public transport and car rental was not needed.Jeju Olle Route 1We did not do the entire route 1 as we wanted to visit seongsan 1st plus we started late. As we stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal, we took bus 701 to Seongsan ilchulbong. The bus journey took more than 1.5hours and cost about 3300won one way and the bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly.  The TV screen will flash seongsan-ri entrance and you can press the bell to alight (photo attached). Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. I have car sickness but it was still bearable for me. We alighted and headed to the black beach along Seongsan. It was called the black beach as the sand was black. Not sure why we need not need to pay for the entrance fee to Seongsan that day (25th April) but we were happy as the temperature was about 17 degree Celsius. We wore T-shirt with a windbreaker only as the sun kept us warm. A windbreaker will be good as it can be quite windy especially if you walk along the beach. There were 2 track at Seongsan. One track led to the peak of Seongsan which consist about 10 flights of stairs (Pretty doable even with poor fitness ? just take as many rest breaks as needed). At the peak, you will be able to have a panoramic view of the city and the surrounding water bodies. The other track is along the coast area with pretty wild purple (I think is Lunaria annua)  and yellow canola wild flower and volcanic stacked rocks.After Seongsan, you can continue to the Jeju Olle Route 1 to Al Oreum along the ocean area. The Jeju Olle Route 1 will pass by canola flower patches for photo taking, a nice ocean view with beaches for scenic viewing, a new hotel named as The Cloud, the ferry terminal, along many beautiful seashore. We stopped at one of the seashore where we witness locals harvesting gastropod, sword razor clams and cockles using simple equipment. We were friendly and allowed us to take photo of how they harvest sword razor clams. If you are interesting in harvesting, remember to bring a good jacket as the wind was strong in April. Putting on waterproof boots will be good too. We continued to walk along the coast where cuttlefish were being dried along the coast. There were many restaurants along the way too. As we continued the walk, we noted that there was no bus stop along the walk after the fish port/market (there was a Ojo Haenyeo House bus stop). The next bus stop was at Jongdal Elementary school which was quite a distance away.After walking through the coastal area, you will walk through a village for a short period before reaching the expressway. The walk towards Al Oreum required you to cross an expressway and the route up the Al Oreum seemed alittle deserted with trees but there was still a road up. You will contine to see the orange/blue ribbons that were well spaced. However, we started the walk at 1pm and took too many stops for picture taking. Therefore, we were unable to finish the walk to Al Oreum.We decided to back track  and took bus 701 from the Jongdal Elementary school stop at about 5.30 pm back to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal (we take on the side nearer to the expressway, not the opposite). Therefore, make sure you start the Olle route earlier if you want to reach the top of Al Oreum where you will have a bird-eye view of the paddy field and coastal area. The bus journey took about 2 hours to reach Seogwipo-si.Jeju Olle Route 6 & 7 We did not do the entire 6 & 7 trail but we visited Chilshimni Poetry Park, Hwangwooji coast, Oedolgae observatory and Oedolgae. This was a scenic trail and I highly recommend. We stayed at a hotel along Jungang-ro road, that was near the Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market. From our hotel, it was a 10 minutes walk to Geolmae Eco Park. The park led us along Seohong-ro road to Taepyeong-to road (where we passed by Hotel Yeon) where we were able to see the Saeyeong Bridge. After the bridge was in sight, we followed our instinct to the Bridge. There was an ice-cream stall that serve grape soft-serve that was delicious. We made our way onto the bridge to view the pristine bluish-green coastline and headed to Saeseom Island. Saeseom Island was a short 20 to 30 minutes trail that brought us to a rocky coastline where you can view two lighthouses (red and white). You could walk to the white lighthouse on the rocks but at your own risk. There were many locals fishing along the rocky areas too. In short, the trail along the Saeyeongyo Bridge was fairly easy yet scenic enough. We were there on the 22nd of April and the weather was about 15 degree Celsius in the day. A light jacket with windbreak will be sufficient. Afterwhich we headed to Chilshimni Poetry Park (which you can view Cheonjiyeon Falls for free) as there was a stairway along the left side of main exit road (where all the tour buses parked, pedestrian walkway path with brown wood). The stairway seemed to indicate going up a temple. However, we landed in Chilshimni Poetry Park. We took pictures of the waterfall and left Chilshimni Poetry Park to follow the orange/blue Jeju Olle ribbon to Hwangwooji coast and Oedolgae. The orange/blue Jeju Olle ribbon were along the park main road (Namseongjung-ro road where Park Sunshine hotel was). Then, You need to turn in to Namseong-ro road and you will see a brick wall painted dark blue with pinnochio seated on a bench (photo attached) you will passed by a ?hip?몃媛?? Hostel (the hostel name is in Korean as I cannot find the English name online - photo attached). u will then past by Poong Gyung Hotel in Jeju (not the one u can find online - photo attached) before arriving at Hwangwooji coast. I love Hwangwooji coast bcos it was like a private pool. There were only a few Korean that day, playing, swimming and hunting of sea creatures in the private pool. It also has a good view of the Saeyeongyo Bridge from a far.  After-which we head to Oedolgae and walked till Dombenang-gil Road. We decided to head back as I needed the toilet. At the entrance to Oedolgae, there was a public toilet acorss the road. The toilet were will keep with toilet paper provided. You can watch the sunset if you have time. Visited this museum with my kids.  There were hundreds of Teddy bears displayed over 3 floors. Movie and exhibits, with beautiful walks through the village and surrounding farm fields.
