Unlike Hello Kitty, I think most of us have cuddled or have in possession a toy teddy bear at a certain stage of our lives. So it is no wonder that the Teddy Bear Museum has such a wide appeal and which surely be included as a ?compulsory? destination on the itinerary of the independent travellers (especially those with children) and tour companies alike.Getting there and fees: We visited Teddy Bear Museum (GPS coordinate/code 7387600) on a rainy day, which was appropriate since the exhibits are predominantly indoor, except for the Teddy Bear Garden and Park where there?re a few teddy bear figurines outside and a park with great views of the sea.  The admission charges are 10,000 won for adults won, 9,000 won for teens and 8,000 won for children.The Museum/Attraction:  This Teddy Bear Museum is the first and largest teddy bear museum in South Korea. Once you enter, you are greeted by this huge teddy bear, who gives you a ?grand? welcome to further explore the five sections spread over 3 levels: The History Hall, The Art Hall and The Project Exhibition Hall, Gift Shop (all indoors) and an outdoor Teddy Bear Garden and Park. There?s also a caf챕/restaurant. Be prepared to spend at least 1 hour looking and taking photographs/selfies at all the interesting exhibits. The History Hall comprised of the history of bear manufacturing and some of the earliest toy bears, many of which are antique and rare. It also showcases milestones in human history, with the bears enacting several famous (human) historical scenes from different eras. This is indeed a refreshing concept for a museum! I particularly liked the teddy bears enacting the Titanic, landings on the moon and the iconic celebrities like the Beatles and Gandhi.In the Art Hall, you could see the world-famous artworks and designs in an art gallery form as well as animation characters beloved by children. I liked the Mona Lisa and two of the most expensive bears in the world - the Louis Vuitton teddy bear and the Diamond Bear. In the Project Exhibition Hall, you would meet teddy bears grouped to suit the theme of each exhibition. Not forgetting the large Gift Shop on the first level. While it offers plenty of gifts, these are nonetheless pricey. Nevertheless, you could take photos with Michael Jackson bear, Steve Jobs bear and a wedding couple bear amongst others. There?s also a mother panda with her baby pandas on display too.  We certainly enjoyed the wonderful experience of the Museum bringing out the child in each of us, and making us feel young again. Despite the pricey entrance fees, I still think the Teddy Bear Museum is worth visiting, and to me, once would be sufficient. But if you don?t like teddy bears at all, then it would be prudent to skip this attraction.

Udo was formed by an volcanic eruption in the 12th century. We took the ferry boat then signed up for a on/off bus tour and it was worthwhile. The bus stopped at 6 different locations to include three beaches (black sand, gold sand and white sand), near the large volcanic mountain that is the hump that makes up Udo (you can walk up  to the top but given the limited visibility, we  didn't), the Udo Museum (free if you are taking the on/off bus), and Biyang-dong (a small island off of Udo). Because of the weather we did not swim at the beaches but the other attractions were worthwhile, especially Biyang-dong. We were told that because of the rain there weren't the crowds that you normally have on Udo. There are plenty of good restaurants as well. If the weather had permitted, we would have rented bicycles and  ridden around the island (apx 14 KM). I would plan for just over a half day.Costs: Ferry apx 10,000 won per person round tripBus tour: apx 6,000 won per per person (one complete circuit)

True to the museum title, there?s quite a number of precious collections, including the first generation of Winnie the Pooh, Carebear and other well known bears. A number of bears dressed up as historical figures placed throughout the building provide good selfie opportunities. Worth it if you are a bear lover and in the Jungmun area.

Transportation: There are several buses that make stops at this destination, but just like everything in Jeju, rental car is the recommended mode of travel. Food: the lava tubes does have a restaurant colocated but I did not eat. There are also some snacks you can purchase here but you are not allowed to bring them down into the lava tubes. Attraction: The scale of the lava tube really surprised me. We descended roughly 30 feet into the lava tube after we purchased our tickets ($4 pp). The stairs were slippery, so be cautious when descending. Don?t worry if you have claustrophobia, The tube is about 25ft across and 20 feet high! There are no tour guides, so you won?t have anybody explaining the history or the geology of the tubes, but there are educational signs posted about every 100 feet. There was also a great museum on sit I recommend visiting prior to going into the lava tubes. Great place to visit, and it took us about 1 hour and 15 minutes.

Though am not craving for Teddy Bear, still find it ok to stop by if you have time.  You may know the history of teddy bear via this museum.  Only too bad, we can't find Mr. Bean best friend, Teddy in it.  However, you will find Elvis Presley, The Beatles & many others.

Thoroughly enjoyed the visit to the Museum. Awesome show featuring the Elvis Presley bear. So many bears with such exquisite costume designs, special thematic showcases. From celebrity bears to Disney bears. You name it, they have it. I was completely mesmerized. Don't miss the bear shows.

This well set out and very informative museum recounts the history of how many of the Jeju islanders were killed and repressed during the late 1940s and early 1950s.  The visitor passes through a series of rooms, each explaining in Korean and English a different stage in the tragic events.  Apart from the actual events themselves, two things shocked me most.  Firstly, that I had never before heard of the April 3 Uprising, although some 25-30,000 people were killed by Korean government forces and their supporters.  Secondly, that even well into South Korea's democracy the events continued to be hushed up and only relatively recently has the truth begun to be told.  Just a few years ago, mass graves were discovered near jeju airport.  The museum provides such a valuable insight into the island's past that I think no visit to Jeju would be complete without coming here and learning about the events and their aftermath.  Entry is free of charge.  The peace park around the museum provides a place for contemplation after visiting the museum.
This was worth the entry fee. There is a nice walking tour of the   museum  . It was interesting to see all the glass displays in the forest. We really enjoyed the walk through the exhibits

This was the first place to visit before we headed to other place in Jeju Island.O?셎ulloc Tea Museum is also located here and we just stopped by there for lunch and check out the products at Innisfree Jeju House. The lunch was not cheap , it's organic, There were also some visitors who were learning how to make soap, I think we need to pay for that course. I just bought a box of mini masks and move on to other places.Not too bad for a short lunch time and for photos maybe. To go about Jeju Island is best with to rent a car as it's more convenient to go for one places to another unlike in Seoul or Busan where subway are available.

This was pretty entertaining. I had no idea what would be in a Teddy Bear museum... PLEASE go though. There are tons of bears from every period imaginable, wearing period and geographical clothing to match. Everyone is represented and it was actually a lot better than I thought when I hear   we are going to the Teddy Bear Museum  .... don't let that fool you! There is also an outside where you can walk around and see life-sized teddy bears. The gift shop is at the very end, and you WILL want something from it. Class Act, and a welcomed surprise!

This was our first stop during our weekend trip to Jeju. I had heard about these women before but didn't know much. First, they showed us a video (in English) all about the history. I was immediately hooked! The rest of the museum is so interesting. The pictures and artifacts tell a great story. I just wish I could have met the Haenyeo personally! Also, the women working at the museum were nice and helpful as we tried to get to our next stop.

This was an interesting experience. I am usually ok in small spaces and felt this would be a great thing to do. But once I was in the middle of the first maze I felt a little uneasy. They provide a map and the maze itself is pretty easy to do. You also hear people walking around, but just something about the possibility of making a wrong turn made me not want to do the second and third maze. But there are really cool towers and a museum where you can take amazing pictures. the museum is free, they have trick art and a puzzle art. Getting here was a little bit difficult. Ask around your previous destination at the bus stop perhaps some people are willing to share taxi with you. Since the bus that goes around this area takes almost 45 minutes. And once you get to your destination you sometimes still have to walk a while to get to where you want to.

This was an amazing museum that I thoroughly enjoyed. A theater plays a documentary about the Haenyeo in several languages and the 3 exhibition halls show you how they lived, their equipment and how integral they are to the communities in which they live. The observatory lets you look out at the ocean, where if they are diving you'll be able to see the ladies in action. It's a shame that these amazing women free divers are declining in numbers, so if you get a chance to visit, do. PS There is a free diving school at Hallim (the west side of the island) if you're game.

This was a terrific little museum. Excellent, helpful staff. Fantastic introductory film that they played in English for us, and top class exhibits. We came away with a deep admiration for the women divers of Jeju, they are tough, proud and awesome achievers :)

This teddy bear museum is one of a few around the world.  Located in Jungmun tourist complex in Jeju, Korea, is this tiny museum for teddy bear fans alike.  For 8000 KRW you have unlimited day access to 3 floors of teddy bear exhibits and the outside grounds.  This museum carries interesting themed bears like the Mona Lisa bear, the Leonardo Da Vinci bear, a Marilyn Monroe bear, and so many others.  Currently they are displaying the Elvis bear.  On the ground floor there is even a really nice restaurant if you get hungry.  Not much choice in  terms of breakfast, they do offer mostly burgers and different types of coffees.  Also there is a gift shop if you are interested in taking home one of the really cute teddy bear souvenirs.Well worth the visit and few hours for both teddy bear fans and those with just a passing interest.  Remember to use the lockers next to the admission counter.  We didn't and carried all our jackets and bags for the entire exhibit,  It will make the visit a whole lot lighter and more fun.  Enjoy!

This place is huge!If you like nature, do visit Jeju Stone Park.  The English audio guide was excellent.  The exhibits were really interesting.  There were indoor and outdoor exhibits.  Do be selective if you have limited time.  One could easily spend up to half a day at this place.As we were a bit short on time, we browsed through the indoor museum rather quickly and still managed to pick up some interesting information.The outdoor areas were really nice and comfortable.  When we were there, the weather was cool and nice and we really had a good time walking around admiring the stones. It is a park that combines nature and art.  We like it a lot.

This place is easily accessible by bus, next to O'Sulloc tea museum. Makes me feel very cosy the moment I stepped in. It's a cafe as well as a place for soap making workshop. It also sells own products (limited).I love the healthy breakfast which is organic and surprisingly very tasty. However, it is on the pricey side.

This museum, which focuses on the women divers of Jeju, is well designed and well laid out. It offers a fascinating look into the lives (past and present) of these divers, who spend up to 2 minutes underwater at a time without any breathing apparatus to catch abalone and other sea life. Our guide told us that the divers' current age range is 55 to 85. Younger women have no interest incontinuing this cultural tradition, which is an incredibly difficult way to earn a living and to help support a family.Nicely curated, the museum offers an excellent film about the divers and shows various aspects of their lives, including past and current swim wear. the tools that have been used, models of fishing villages and the Jeju traditional fishing boat. I thoroughly enjoyed this close look at a rare way of life that likely won't be around much longer.

This museum, like most of Jeju's other similar attractions, is but an excuse to get you to the gift shop. You can finish it in one hour, because they want to get you there fast! As opposed to most other museums in this resort island, this one is cute and amusing. It consists mostly of tableaus or displays with teddy bears re-enacting some important historical or popular culture event. Some may frown at the   Gandhi   teddy bear as perhaps not quite tasteful, but must surely enjoy the   Beatles   teddy bears, the   Chinatown   teddy bears, etc. You get the picture. Oh, yes the gift shop! It works; I bought a little cute bear as most everybody else seems to have done. Not that expensive and well-made. In other words, if you are going to see at least one of these museums that dot the south of the island, you may want to give this one a try. It's enjoyable.

This museum is one of the attraction at Jungmun Resort. It consists of teddy bear exhibition from several country, the history, the art, life size teddy bear & of course souvenir store. If you're Princess Hours lovers (Kdrama) this place is perfect for you. You can't bring you belonging inside, so placed you belonging into a free locker on the entrance of the museum.

This museum is interesting if you have the keen interest in geology & history of jeju volcanic past. The entire park is very well maintained and its advisable to bring an umbrella if you're those who can't really take the sunlight.For couples who would just want to take a quiet stroll, this place is strongly recommended as crowds here are lesser as compare to other tourist attraction in jeju.

This museum is intended for tourists who love to take photos. Most of the artworks housed in the museum are modified versions of original paintings so that you can integrate with the painting. Hence bringing a camera or a smartphone is a must! A companion is also a must since taking a   selfie   to achieve the desired effect might prove to be impossible.This is one of the two 3D interactive museums in Jeju Island. The other one Trick Art Museum is located farther in the eastern part of the island. We went to this place as it is nearer to the Jungmun Area where most hotels (Hyatt Regency Shilla Hotel Lotte Hotel etc.) are located.Aside from the in-house artworks there is also a park with sculptures and play sets that will be appreciated by kids. Tips: avoid flash photography to get the desired effect; bring a jacket w/ hoodie (can be used in some of the artworks); and black pants make people blend better with the background.Admission costs KRW 8000 per person. The entire area is air-conditioned and wifi access is offered for free. Other extras include lockers to deposit your bags as this may hamper your experience.This is a fun destination for couples families or small groups.

This museum is all about Teddy Bear. All the display from old to the newest Teddy Bear is here. Teddy Bear in Louis Vuitton, Teddy Bear in Hong Kong and even MJ Teddy Bear will make you smile. You can also buy Teddy Bear for souvenirs.

This museum is about the dwindling women divers of Jeju who dive in the sea to collect Agar and shellfish as well as octopus. They are similar to their sisters in Japan and dive without the benefit of air tanks.This tradition is sadly dying out and it is to be hoped that this neatly laid out museum will attract members to the group and also increase worldwide awareness.It is a static museum with some electronic displays but later, if you are lucky, you might see them diving off the coast of U-Do island.Worth a visit!

This museum is a lot bigger than expected, and housed so many different teddy bears in fun settings that it made even adults excited. Would highly recommend if you have little kids, as they would love being able to touch the bears and taking photos with them.

This museum is 90% in Korean but as they say some things are easier to understand. In the beginning the museum starts out with some interesting if broad sex-positive history. It's sex and HEALTH however so there's info about AIDS as well as misconceptions about sex and sexual health. Towards the middle of the museum it starts to go off the rails a little bit. The   Fantasy   section is a lot of chintzy garbage and mannequins in lewd/bizarre positions and tableaus. It doesn't add anything it moreso detracts from the legitimacy established in the first half. Only go if you're stuck with a rainy day. Otherwise you'd be better off enjoying Jeju's natural wonders.

This museum boasts its huge variety of old computer related exhibitions to a new one. You may enjoy the old memories of punch card, MS-DOS, APPLE I~II, to VR, motion recognition, etc. The only point you should consider is entrance fee. I was ok because I can get Jeju resident discount. But most of visitors from outside of Jeju island should try to discount chances such as Naver booking, etc.
This landmark is very well maintained with beautiful structures. Very instagram friendly. Location is also pretty near many places like teddy bear museum, several waterfalls and casino resorts.
This is the place you can hug, kiss and take photos with teddy bear. Jeju Teseum is Korea's first and largest teddy bear museum. If you likes Teddy bear this is the place must visit in Jeju Island.

This is the first tourism that I visited during staying in Jeju Island. I went there around last October. At the same time  I went there since this island is one of the seven wonder. This lava tube actually make me very curious since it has so many education things. I went there with my mom which was 70 years old. Eventually we arrive in this place, this lava tube is wet and slippery so be careful when you go along with elderly. At the same time, you should wear proper shoes and mind your steps.So many interesting knowledge you will get inside this lava cave, beside you can visit museum close to this place.

This is the best stone exhibit on Jeju island.  And the best part of that is the museum itself.  There are many, many very interesting stones shapes, all collected from Jeju (I think).  If you like geology, there's a great explanation of lava types, stone formations, lava tubes, etc.  Also there is a nice drift-wood display with very unusual, artistic shapes.  Outside, there are many carved stone artifacts used by Jeju islanders from ages past.  The Obaek Jang-Goon Gallery has a nice drift-wood display in the basement.  Park is big, but except for the museums, just a walk-through is enough.  I spent 2 hours in the museums -- the best part!
This is really the heaven for antique car fans like us. Grandpa was enjoying the old days by seeing these old pals, and kids enjoyed the fun ride of kiddy kart surrounding the museum.
address: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관

review: This is probably the wonderland of 90% of the female population. The place is not huge but if you are going to watch the 3D movie, you have to queue early coz they only have a certain number of 3D glasses. We only have less than 1.5 hours in Hello Kitty Island thus wasn't able to watch the movie. The toilet is cute!! I so love the mirror and of course the cleanliness of the place. Saw a lot of very cute exhibits in the museum. I especially like the bedroom. Wish it was mine. There is a caf챕 on the second floor. The deco is all pink and white. Didn't eat coz we were rushing for time and the snacks aren't really cheap. The gifts are expensive too. I can actually get them cheaper when I'm back in Singapore.

This is probably my first 1-star review on TA. Much regretted visit and the only saving grace is that this place is right next to the Osulloc Tea Museum. We were drawn to this place after very good experience at the Innifree Green Cafe at Myongdong and we expected the same (if not better) at this concept store.Product - any Innisfree shops in myeongdong or duty free can offer you a better range at much better price. As Jeju was the last leg of my trip, I was planning to make most of my innisfree purchase in this store but they don?셳 carry much range here. I don?셳 remember there was onsite tourist refund as well (like how it is in Myeongdong) - another reason not to plan your shopping here.Food - I ordered a 18000krw main dish (named herdsman?) with some cold sausages, potato mash, rice balls and orange. The presentation was really pretty but it tasted nothing special. If you are looking for good looking food and great taste at the same time, you have better chance at Myongdong innisfree Green cafe. The other two pretty drinks we ordered were not worth a mention as well. Service - We were there at 450pm and all the soap making stations were occupied. We were told by a staff the soap making would only take 15mins and the place would close at 6pm. so we decided to wait at the cafe and return when the crowd lessen. At 525pm, a staff stopped me at the cashier when I tried to purchase the soap making set. She said that they have closed the soap making station at 520pm. And then another staff came by and said the station was closed at 5pm (?!). I am not sure exactly what time the station closed as there was no sign in the store and the staff were telling different things. The store closed at 6pm sharp and the staff can?셳 wait to have all the guests out by then - this I am sure. This place is a sad contrast to the Osulloc Tea Museum next door.

This is one of the most remarkable scenic attractions of Jeju. Our Korean driver brought us here. We told him we are not interested in arts museums or teddy bear or maze park. We only wanted to see the natural sites and wonders in Jeju and he brought us here and we thanked him for that. There was a Buddha Park directly at the car park where we alighted. I could see the golden face of the Buddha from the highland opposite the park. From the car park,  the panoramic view of the beach was amazing; the lush green vegetation studded with autumn foliage with long stretch of gorgeous coastline and natural cliff view and the azure sea horizon. It was nature's master-piece presented in so marvelous and harmonious form that I could not find better words to describe this stunning, breathtaking and jaw dropping scenery. For a moment, a sensation of joy and happiness flooded and filled my heart. As the gentle sea breeze blew on my face, I found tranquility, calmness and serenity in this beautiful land. I immediately dashed down the flight of stairs to embrace this beautiful and spectacular piece of natural wonder. I roamed and wandered around the scenic landscape and found myself singing the Happy Wanderer lyrics: `I like to go a wandering up the mountain track  And as I go, I love to sing, My knapsack on my back. Val-deri,Val-dera, Val-deri,..'  There was the Hamel Castaway Memorial and the vessel Hamel that drifted to this place in 1653. I stood near the replicated Hamel vessel to admire the European naval architectural of that time and I saw the rangers tendered to the horses in the range. From the coast, I could see the majestic Mt Sanbangsan loomed at the site of the Buddha Park and I could vividly see some of my group members were resting and relaxing at a pavilion below the car park enjoying the gentle sea breeze.You must pardon me for my excitement and exhilaration as I came from a city with urbanized concrete jungle with little natural scenery. Jeju is full of natural wonders and Mt Sanbangsan and Yongmeori beach are exceptionally gorgeous gems that deserved a good lengthy exploration.

This is NOT really a museum. I mean having a teeny tiny collection and a small display of tea sets and tea cups and tea.... doesn't make a  museum. Honestly. Didn't help that it was drizzling and had a constant stream of tour buses... making it perpetually crowded. It's like 20 steps worth of   tea museum   followed by a cafe that sold some o'sulloc products. Stuff ranging from facial wash to flavoured tea and green tea milk spread. Since we were there we decided - oh hey let's try their apparently awesome green tea ice cream green tea latte & green tea roll. Meh. Nothing special. I've had better green tea food.Please just go buy a 2000 won green tea milk latte drink from any 7-11 or convenience store. A convenience store green tea latte is better than their caf챕's green tea latte. (Cost 6000 won)Their green tea ice cream(4500won) and roll(5000won) were equally disappointing. Nothing special. No harm dropping by this place if it's on the way - as it's free entry. BUT... Dont go out of your way to go here. It's nothing special and food's not worth it.

This is for the female Merchant who saved people in Jeju island 17,18 Century, Joseon dynasty. Very carefully and beautifully made. However, it is limited for 3rd floor. 2nd floor is for kids' experience museum. 1st floor is for some special exposition from time to time. It is FREE, worth to visit for an hour. It is located near by Jeju coastal international port and Dongmun traditional market. Actually from this market, exit/entrance #3, it is just 500 m away. In those times, people in Jeju island could not get out of the island, however, since she saved whole population in the island, The King Jungjo wanted to give a awards but she refused. Instead, she asked him she would love to visit the peninsular once, and wanted to travel in Diamond mountain(located in North Korea now). So she could get the chance to meet the King and travel inland. Under the Patriarchal system, it must be very hard for her to work as a merchant, but became the most rich person in Jeju, then when there was big famine, she released whole rice and food for free to Jeju people. Any way, it was great fun to enjoy each section from her birth to death. All explanation are in English and in Korean both.

this is basically a tea house with a few displays related to   tea history   - only some random teaware from different places in the world. as a tea house the place is very nice. you can have some nice food and sweats based on tea... but its definitely not a museum.

This is an excellent museum featuring contemporary art as well as traditional art. The buildings themselves, which were designed by Tadao Ando, were amazing. It was great just walking around inside while perusing the exhibits & or going for a stroll outside. My favorite part was the sculpture garden, which featured 3 pieces. You can go on the rooftop as well to see another sculpture as well as a great view of Jeju. I was also fortunate to have an opportunity to see Yayoi Kusama's Pumpkin & Infinity Mirrored Room. I don't know if it was because I went during off-season, but the museum wasn't crowded at all, so I was able to take my time. I would definitely come back here again if I had a chance

this is a very interesting park, they have at least 3 sections; a museum, 2 parks and smaller exhibits. If you like stones and interested in how they are formed and how they look like and appreciate by the people of the past and present, do visit. some stones have interesting tales like: Goddess and her 500 Sons. The whole park is pretty big, it can take up to more than 3 hours if you go through all the writings and descriptions. do go after a meal.

This is a Teddy Bear Museum that all inside about the Teddy Bear.  They have so many Theme of Teddy Bear.  Near the exit they also have many stuff for us to buy and bring home, such as doll, key chain, cloth, jacket, sweater, etc..  This Museum is more suitable for the children, but for adult if you are bored you can wait near the exit there are some coffe shop.

This is a shop and cafe on the grounds of the AmorePacific Osulloc tea museum. The shop selection is a bit small. But there is a section of goods that can only be bought at this location. There is a large area where you can make your own soap, and then lay for it. The other half of the building is the cafe, which while not cheap was surprisingly good. The staff was perfectly fine but not amazing either.

This is a real village with households living inside, opposite from folk villages built in museums. In fact, the people live there are mainly the haenyeo (women divers) - there is a museum for them in the east coast of Jeju. There is no entrance fee, so the village depends on the sale of souvenirs, basically the blueberries fermented drink and the organic skin creams. A volunteer will assist you to walk around the town, which is very helpful. A site note is that it is often used as a movie set, for example for the movie entitled Dae Jang Gum.

This is a nice and cute museum especially for small girl.  Here They have Theatre, they have explanation about hello kitty, they have restaurant with hello kitty image on the dishes, they have souvenir shop

This is a greatt museum and more traditional compared to most of the Jeju ones which can be rather quirky. The Haenyeo museum is well resourced in English, has some lovely photos and details a really important part of Jeju's history. Definitely worth a visit

This is a great find for me. The museum is full of interesting things. Live hologram concert, G-Dragon, is super-duper:) The staff is awesome! very nice and friendly.I would highly recommend. Playkpop is not comparable with other Museum!!!

This is a facility that houses multiple attractions  and they are all basically geared toward separating the tourist from his or her money. Notwithstanding this  our family had a great time spending a couple of hours here. The main attraction appears to be the indoor cart racing track. It's not cheap  around KRW 40 000 for a package that includes 10 minutes on the track and a ticket to the   unique objects   museum. We actually found the items in the museum quite entertaining - objects that trick your eye  weird inventions. The go cart driving was a bit disconcerting (no helmets  no apparent real concern for safety) but in the end it was fun. I was glad I was on the track with just another father-son pair. On the way out  my kid bought carrots for horses that were in a corral  and the guy there was nice enough to take my kid around a lap on the horse (again  no safety gear). My kid was fine but I was glad when both the go cart ride and the horseride finished without any problems.If you are desperate to kill a couple of ours and the weather is bad  this may be a good place to go with tweens or teens. They also offered a   Survival Game   attraction which looked like it was done with laser-tag type guns (not paintball).

This is a cute collection of teddybears and other stuffed animals in a variety of settings (a castle, a safari, etc.), but it's not what I was expecting with the name   Teseum   (teddy+museum).  There's a very small display of older teddybears (mostly photographs), but the main attraction is the displays you can see in the pictures.  There must be thousands here, ranging in size from one inch or shorter to probably eight feet tall. I imagine kids would be in hog heaven, but some of the older people in our tour group said it was a waste of time.  My favorites were the safari and the teddybear versions of old paintings.

This is a cave formed by molten lava melting the rock layers away over a very very long time. So expect a huge dimly-lit tunnel with uneven walking surface. The small museum does a good job of explaining the geological aspect of the cave. The 2 km round trip into the cave is not difficult but wear a pair good walking shoes and if you need, bring a small torch. This cave is located on the eastern part of the island so best to visit nearby attractions like the Ichulbong, Phoenix Island etc.Another tip: if you hated Geography in school, give this place a miss. LOL!

This is a big park where you get to sample the attractions seen in Jeju . We enjoyed visiting the folk museum, flower and bonsai garden, Jeju stone park as well as the place where they have big palm trees. Our time was limited so we didn't really stay here for long.

This is a big area in the outskirts of Jeju city, need to car to get there. There are many stone formations around the park and there is story of an old grandmother who had 500 kids and was finally cooked in the porridge and the kids ate her as they didnt know. There is a nice stone museum that explains how rock formation on Jeju is formed and all about volcanic activities and some weird looking rocks. Educational place for kids!

There's two Teddy Bear Museum in Jeju Island. One is Safari Theme that has an entrance fee of KRW 8,500 (Php 369) for adults. This has a safari theme great for pictures but on the second floor, there are more which has a variety of themes. The other Teddy Bear Museum where the most expensive Teddy Bear is on display wearing a Louis Vuitton outfit costs KRW 8,000 (Php 347). This one is better because it has so many display that you will be amazed, famous scene, characters, celebrities from different industries. Very nice! This is also the museum where Princess Hour was shot, a Korean novela. I will go back!

There's a lot to try and absorb in this open air museum. Maybe too much for your average tourist. I mean the somewhat authentic reproductions were cool for the first three or four structures. I enjoyed having a window into what life was like for peasants 100 - 300 years ago and/or the actors who currently play them in historical television dramas. However the minutia became simply overwhelming especially since there was a tendency to focus on the details as if everyone lived and breathed Korean archaeology. There was also a fairly obvious and persistent attempt to commercialize on cheesy trinkets. Some of the   traditional wares   were okay but I think you can get better quality at lower prices elsewhere. The same can be said for the food. The reenactments of wedding ceremonies and shaman rituals were entertaining and the kids could ride ponies. All in all I was glad to end my tour of this facility. It was a rather pricey way to spend an hour or two. If you were in the area or you have a passion for such things maybe give it a try. However I think there are far better ways to spend your time on Jeju. *You can catch bus 720 at the Bus Terminal for 3300 Won. The trip takes a little over an hour:http://www.rome2rio.com/s/Jeju-si/Jeju-Folk-Village-Museum*Here's a Jeju Weekly piece that might give you a better idea of what this place is all about:http://www.jejuweekly.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=4196

There were bears of every color and design imaginable: there was an Elvis bear, Marilyn bear, Mona Lisa bear, Chinese bears, countryside bears and even Goong (the Korean drama) bears! It really was a bear wonderland. The only problem was that the commentary was all in Korean, it would have been better if there was English translation as well. The other problem was that most of the exhibits were housed in glass cases which made taking photos challenging as the reflections were very prominent. Besides viewing the bears, there is an in-store souvenir shop that has all sorts of bear items (e.g. keychains, stuffed bears, bags etc...). But if you love bears, than it should be worth a visit.For more on my experience and photos, please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/03/an-impromptu-visit-to-teddy-bear-museum.html

There is a reason that this place was packed.  The museum is located in a super modern building set amongst impeccably groomed grounds and a green tea plantation.  The   museum   part takes 5 minutes to get through but the caf챕 and market is buzzing with tourists enjoying an assortment of green tea treats.  I found lots more tea options at this store than any other in Korea (and there are many!)  But the bonus is the Innisfree store adjacent to the Museum on the same grounds.  Here you can make your own mask concoctions customize soap and find lots high quality unique gifts with Jeju logo on them.  I spent at least an hour here alone.  They also have a caf챕.  Definitely a must stop on Jeju!

There is a lot more than meets the eye here. People first wonder but then realize they are glad to visit The Glass Castle. It is a museum and park of glass works by local artisans and crafts people and the collection is vast, so vast it takes a while to see everything. There is a diverse array of glass work in gardens, themes, and museum displays of varying quality and rarity around the park.This includes large outdoor sculptures such as the yellow submarine at the entrance or crystal skulls, and glass displays around the park. We were impressed by the size of the park and diverse collection of work. They also have workshops here and some hands on experiences.I would recommend this place as a worthy place to visit while on Jeju, near the O'Sulluc Tea Museum and Plantation which only 5 minutes away.

There is a cafe at level 2 and a small gift shop selling Hallabong items after walking through their tangerines greenhouse. There is also a small museum where kids could learn about tangerines but they are mostly in Korean.Outside  the korean fans dedicated a small hectre of tangerine plantation to G-Dragon. There is even a Kwon Jiyong Tree. But since we were there in late March  the weather was still pretty chilly  so the leaves are not growing yet.You could ask the reception where it is  its just nearby. However do try asking them as   G-Dragon   forest. i tried saying as   GD    but they dont really get it. Lol.

There are some fictional characters that you and me adore and love during our childhood and yet still relish even though we have become adults. Hello Kitty is certainly one of them, and is a favourite of one of my children. However, the good part is not every visitor to Jeju and the locals are a fan of Hello Kitty, so the Hello Kitty Island Museum is not on the itinerary of most tour companies, and hence it?s not crowded.Getting there and fees: Hello Kitty Island Museum, opened in late 2013, is located in the south west part of Jeju (GPS code/coordinate 7926114).  Not to worry if you cannot find space in the small open-air car park outside the Museum because there?s another huge open air car park below the small one. Parking is free. Entrance fee to the Museum is 12,000 won for adult, 11,000 won for teenagers and 10,000Won for children. However, my family and I made use of the discount coupon for entrance fees from the Hertz car rental discount booklet.The Museum/Attraction: when we entered, we were immediately greeted by a large hall where there?s a circular cone of Hello Kitty toys, a photo-taking stop with the entire Hello Kitty family and Hello Kitty?s house where she?s standing at the balcony welcoming you and beckoning you to enter the door into the various exhibition halls. There are 3 levels with the exhibition halls on the first and second level, the gift shop on the first level, the Hello Kitty Caf챕 on the second level and the 3D theatre and an outdoor gallery on the third level. To cover everything, including a meal at the Hello Kitty Caf챕, would easily take about 2-3 hours. In the true sense, this Hello Kitty Museum is a museum ? there are exhibits of anything related to the adorable Hello Kitty. There are several themed exhibition halls on the first and second level e.g. History Hall, Art Education Hall, Music Education Hall, World Gallery Hall, Hello Kitty Room, Constellation Education Hall, amongst others.So we took plenty of photographs and selfies. I particularly like the exhibit of Hello Kitty represented by 26 countries (I found my own country) as well as the huge room containing the huge Hello Kitty bed where one of my children got the Hello Kitty toy snatched away by a toddler.At the Hello Kitty Caf챕 ? with Hello Kitty ribbon windows, Hello Kitty-themed sofas and Hello Kitty engraved tables ? you have to try the Hello Kitty Waffle Set, green tea latte, coffee or  hot chocolate (the 3 hot drinks have a profile of Hello Kitty on the surface), Hello Kitty Strawberry Cake and Cheesecake. Really yummy stuff!Whether you are a fan or not of Hello Kitty, I think this Museum is a fun attraction to visit and be acquainted with Hello Kitty. However, be prepared to ?share? the premises with many joyful and lively children and teenagers. But if you are not a fan and if you have limited time in Jeju, then I suppose you could spend that 2-3 hours elsewhere.

There are lots of teddy bears in different dressing inside the museum. It cost KRW10,000 per entry but my opinion is it doesn't worth this amount of money as this museum majors in displaying teddy bear collections in the display box, numerous of human size teddy bears satisfy your photo shooting desires. As compare to KRW10,000 spent in the Jeju Village Folk where cultural living of Jeju residents in the earlier century can be experienced, it's more worthy. Desire to enter this museum was due to the Korea drama series   若モ?, and I expected to have the display of the human size teddy bears in different room with different theme enable for photo session (something like Madame Tussaud's Wax museum) but it is not the way. All the theme teddy are inside the display box. You can just sight seeing it people collection.

There are a few spots that feature the renowned Jeju women divers. However, this museum is a good place for one to be more acquainted on this tradition and the dwindling of this important part of Jeju history.

There are a few attractions within the same area. The teddy bear museum has 3 floors,with teddy bear exhibits and also it's history. There where some with themes and also resembles idols and famous people  and some that moves. There is also an elvis show with teddy bear on level 2 theatre. The outdoor photo taking area has a few exhibits too.

There are 3 teddy bear museums in Jeju Island, but this is the only one you could touch and hug, that?s why it?s called safari, while the teddy bears in the other two are kept in the glass box. Although I am not a big fans of soft toys, it?s still cute to see them.

There are 2 teddy bear museums in Jeju. I don't have the address of the one that I went to, but it's not the one in Jungmun, which is the older one and where you'll only see teddy bears in glass cases. The newer teddy bear museum has teddy bears that are displayed according to themes, where you can pose together  with the teddy bears, and even touch and hug them. This is definitely more interactive than the ones in glass cases.

There are 2 major teddy bear themed attractions in Jeju, One is the Teddy Bear Museum and the other is Jeju Teseum. The Teddy Bear Museum is for mohair connoisseurs, but the bears there are all boxed up in glass exhibits. That is why given the limited amount of time we had in Jeju, we chose to visit Teseum. There are a lot of photo opportunities where we and especially our kids can pose with the many cuddly large-sized teddys at Teseum. The keyword here is interaction.

The women divers of jeju are famous for their free diving culture of gathering food from the bottom of the sea such as sea cucumber, sea weed, and various shellfish. They are so dedicated to this that It is said that they will start their diving three days after giving birth. They also form unions to govern their way of life and culture. The purpose of this museum also serves to preserve their culture as less and less women are taking up this trade.

The Teddy Bear Museum is quite a fun attraction to visit if you like teddy bears! There's soooo many teddy bears around! With different themes, different era and even teddy bears of very popular characters! (something like the teddy bear version of Madame Tussauds)Full review: http://wanderer.summeree.com/travel/korea/jeju/teddy-bear-museum/

The Teddy Bear museum is near other attractions in Seogwipo.  Opposite is the Believe it or Not Museum.  If you have watched the korean drama Goong (The Palace or Princess Hours) , this place place is probably something you would like to visit.  I like teddy bears and it's fun to look into all those dressed up teddy bears.

The teddy bear museum is exactly what it's title states.  It's teddy bears in every shape and size.  The first area has historical teddy bears, dating back as far as the turn of the century (1900's).  The second section is works of art redone with teddy bears and finally, there is an outdoor exhibit including a 9 meter tall teddy bear that makes a showing every hour on the hour.  Young kids that like teddy bears and such will have a great time visiting here.  My daughter adored everything.  It is a little pricey, but if you rent a car to get around they often give you a book with coupons for the various attractions on the island or you can book in advance online at a discount price.

The Teddy Bear Museum is a pleasant surprise. The museum is very close to The Lotte Hotel and just across the street from Ripley?s Believe it or Not in Jungmun.  The exterior is nice. I wonder if the Louvre Museum was an inspiration for the conical architectural design of the museum.  The exhibitions consisted of many famous pictures and major events in human history. The difference is that in this museum, the teddy bears have taken over. So you will see Teddy Bear versions of Neil Armstrong on the moon, Michael Jordan dunking a basket ball, Elvis Presley rocking a guitar, Psy showing us Gangnam Style, and Marilyn Monroe, etc.  It is interesting, cute and amusing.  I am really glad I visited this museum and you should visit it too even if it is just for the laughs. It is adorable.

The Teddy Bear museum is a fun stop. There are many displays of teddy bears in various historical, cinematic, and pop-culture type settings. Take your camera and visit each floor. The gift shop at the end is full of fun teddy bear treasures as well. Definitely a good stop for anyone. We went on a rainy day, but it would also be fun on a hot day if you are looking to get out of the heat. Fairly easy to find, it's located in a popular tourist area.
The Teddy bear museum has pictures of different famous arts and history. Examples (the mona lesa, WWII, THE KISS)
The teddies in the museum are all so adorable!!! My family and I enjoyed every minute in the museum, taking photos with the teddies indoors and outdoors! Must-visit!!!

The tea museum is located on the western side of the island and represents the showpiece of the O'Sulloc tea   empire   in South Korea.  There are a number of O'Sulloc tea cafes all over South Korea which specialize in green tea and also sell sweets as well.  There is a large parking area to accommodate a number of cars and visitors.The tea museum consisted of four   features   from what I could surmise.  First you get a decent view of the western part of the island by walking up the stairs to the roof of the museum itself.  The views aren't that interesting but you do get a good view of the surrounding area.  Second the museum itself describes the tea growing/making/serving process.  Third the cafe/gift shop inside seems to attract the most number of visitors.  You can buy teas and other desserts like you would at any other O'Sulloc cafes.  However it does sell many other items - various teas and more.  Finally another attraction is the tea plantation itself.  O'Sulloc seemingly has a small portion of their plantation on-site that you can walk through (note there may be snakes in the plantation) to get a sense of how the green tea leaves are grown.There is also an Innisfree store right next to the tea museum but we did not visit it.The tea museum is worth a trip though I wouldn't go out of the way to visit it as you can always partake in O'Sulloc teas in various locations in South Korea.

The products they sell are overpriced compared to the innisfree stores in Busan, Daegu and Seoul so don't bother buying from them. There really isn't much to see apart from the fact that it is rather close to the O?셲ulloc Tea Museum.TLDR: Not worth your time, Jeju is so beautiful go somewhere else!

the play KPOP museum has a ?live concert? segment where GD will perform as if it?s a live concert. The other levels has standees of KPOP idols as well as interactive game booths such as photo booths, dress up booths etc. Good place to visit if you are a big fan of KPOP groups from JYP entertainment.

The place itself is huge. We went before lunch and it was a good time because the sun was up. Being a glass museum, most of the art are made of glass and having the sun at its brightest made the art look even more amazing. It's nice to look at the reflections made. There are different signs in Korean, Japanese, and English. They also have shop where they sell little glass artwork. You can bargain with the sellers too. They're nice and friendly.

The Peace park serves both as a memorial to the victims of the April 3 uprising as well as the long period of persecution of islanders that followed. The museum shows the background of the conflict, connected to the division of Korea, in great detail. It could benefit from more signs in other languages. But it does give a detailed and balanced look at the period and also mentions reconciliation in the future, in contrast to many other memorials in Korea, which only look at the suffering in the past. Well worth to get to the out-of-the-way Peace Park.

The Peace Park is very spacious and beautifully laid out.  (Shouldn't compare but it reminded us of  a smaller version of the National Memorial Arboretum in Staffordshire, UK.)  They were still working on some landscaping while we were there.   We were lucky enough to catch the excellent art exhibition that is on at the moment and the museum display is very well laid out and informative - lots of English  so we learnt a lot about the Jeju's history around 1948.   We were there about 1.5 hours but could have stayed longer.

The Park is quite a distance away from other major sights but it is different in that the star attraction are those   grandfather stone sculptures  .Be prepared for lots of walking on easy trails.  There are small pebbles everywhere so do watch the kids and carefully navigate those wheelchairs and baby strollers.The underground museum near next to the water reservoir/water sculpture is definitely for those interested in geology.  It is a good place to take a break and use the restrooms as there is another set of lavatories near the car park.
The O'sulloc   Museum   is in reality a big store where they sell you Tea (can be really expensive) and attached to the store there is a big coffee shop.

The musueum is dedicated to the Haenyeo - female divers who traditionally fish for molluscs and octopuses etc. without using oxygen masks.  UNESCO has declared the Haenyeo part of humankind's intangible cultural heritage.  We visited the museum shortly after having seen a group of Haenyeo sing their traditional song before heading out into the sea to fish.  Having just witnessed the women fist hand added an extra element of interest.  The museum is well set out, informative and interesting.  Its models, life stories of individuals and displays of clothes and tools  really bring home how tough the life of the Haenyeo was in the past (and it's not easy today).  There is also a short movie explaining the history and traditions of the Haenyeo.  Well worth a visit!

The museum was very very hard to find. The employees were rude and unpleasant. The glass   art   is just a pile of glorified junk. I regeret wasting my time there with my boyfriend. The entrance fee is a joke  please Do NOT go there

The museum was so awful and pathetic, smell dust and you can meet creepy and gloomy teddybear inside. We had lots of fun with my friends because we decided to laugh at the situation instead of being angry for spending 9000 wons at this place... Please note that if you want to wear drama disguise you'll be charge 5000 wons more...

The museum was ok, computers and computer games are not my kind of thing but it was interactive so really kept me engaged.The keyboard-shaped waffles in the cafe with four side sauces/cream/ice-cream in the cafe in the basement are awesome. Go for them!Walkable from Nohyung Lotte Mart.

The museum is quite interesting if you're interested in geology.  It's nice to get a decent scientific understanding of how and why the other things you'll likely be seeing on Jeju (Hallasan, Seongsan Ilchulbong, etc.) are the way they are.  If geology bores the heck out of you, then skip the museum, but don't skip the park altogether.  It's really quite a beautiful place to walk around, especially if you're in the mood for something somewhat quiet and relaxing.  Major crowds can make some of the the other sites on Jeju quite the opposite of that, so it's nice to find a place that's legitimately peaceful.
the museum is ok, but not what is in there you can find it elsewhere in the world, nothing amazing making worth the journey.

The museum is not too big, you'll be finished around 30min.  The teddy bears collections are awesome, and for kdrama mania, there is a spot dedicated to the famous Princess Hours drama.  There are other museums nearby so you can plan the visit together with other nearby attractions,  most of the attractions close by 18.00 so plan accordingly

The museum is located next to a please area of town with multiple artists in various media as well as tea/coffee shops - which is how we found the location.? There is a small entrance fee (1000 Won per adult at the time).? In addition to the small, but nice collection of paintings and sculpture, there is a great view of the city and see from the 3rd floor.? If art is your thing, then definitely go.? Otherwise go only as weather or your schedule dictates.

The museum is interesting and probably really fun with children. It is a little strange as there are bears dressed up as princesses, maybe even British royalty and whole safaris. It was interesting to say the least, but I would rather spend my time outside.

The museum is full of teddies of all sizes created from all the Korean dramas begining with the classic   Winter Sonata   till the American President Obama. On the rooftop, you can view the whole valley of Jejudo as well as the scenic Hallasan. There are some cookies for sampling and plenty of teddies for sale in the shop at the end of the tour^^~

The museum has many airplanes on display and also an outdoor area where you can walk into the planes. ? Very well done, lots of information and displays. ? Hands on activities instructions are only in Korean, but easy to figure out. ? A steal for the 10,000 WON entrance fee.

The museum has a vast collection of very cute and adorable exotic bears. Bears made to look like Van Gogh, Steve Jobs and even Michael Jackson. Entrance fee is reasonable and includes both the indoor and the outdoor portions of the museum. Outdoor has limited exhibits.

The museum has a lot of teddy bears (e.g.   Goong   or   Princess hours   teddy bears, etc) well protected in a glass boxes. A total of 3 levels in the building, displaying different kind of teddys and you can buy some souvenirs from the ground level. At the grond level, there are also teddys which you can take picture with (e.g. Steve Jobs, Psy, etc).Outside the building, there are some other teddys which you can also take pictures with. It would be fun if you love teddys but if you are not, it would be quite boring. Nothing much you can do, other than taking pictures and buying souvenirs. However, it still worth a go if you are curious about the variety of teddy bears being displayed inside. The admission fee is around 8,000 won (if i didn't remember wrongly).

The marker for Routes 13, 14 and 14-1 are located in one spot. We got confused at first that we ended up completing abour 2-3km of Trail 14 until we got to another marker that we realized we were following the wrong path. We went back to the spot and started looking for the 14-1 trail. We spent the first half of the day doing Trail 14.When we headed to Trail 14-1 which was the intial plan, it was past noon already so the sun was up and it was hot (we did the trail on a summer day). It was a cool experience because the trail will bring you to the peak where you get a great 360 degree view of Jeju! It will take you inside a forest. You might even meet some horses along the way. By the time you'll get to the midpoint, which is the Osulloc Museum, you will realize how much you miss civilization and strangers. The trail will connect you to nature. You'll even find yourself in a dense forest! There are a lot of blue/orange ribbons so you won't be lost. This trail taught me to simply trust and find the blue/orange ribbons and enjoy/embrace nature wherever the trail (or life in general) may take you. Haha. This is definitely off the beaten path but it makes your Jeju tour even more special and truly your own. I would want to do more of the Olleh Trails in the future :)

The Manjanggul cave was worth going to see, but there really isn't much to actually see in there. As one of the longest lava tubes in the world, it's sheer size is impressive, and the information boards about the particular features of the cave are informative (albeit in strange English translations) and interesting. Once you've reached the end of the tunnel, there's not much to actually see except the lava column (largest known in the world apparently), and then you just walk back the way you came. The horrible coloured lighting makes it all look a bit tacky though, and the museum on site is geared towards younger school children. Worth popping in for a quick visit on your way to somewhere else though.

The Jeju Uprising/Massacre (or simply 4.3), with up to 80,000 villagers killed by the military, took place just prior to the Korean War but is relevant today as South Korea re-militarizes the Island of Peace. Go to the museum, then witness the current hot protests against a naval base being constructed in the fishing/farming village of Gangjeong (between Seogwipo and Jungmun), along the Ollie Trail.

The Jeju Glass Castle was part of the itinerary of the group tour that I was part of. We spent more than an hour in the premises. We visited at daytime?I noticed that there a good number of spotlights so the Jeju Glass Castle must have a different ambience at night.I have mixed feelings about the Jeju Glass Castle.THE GOODThe Jeju Glass Castle is picturesque and very instagrammable. There are numerous displays that one can pose with. Many of the displays are quite feminine, though?very floral and colorful?girly, even. Most of the displays are outdoors including a small glass maze. Our trip was in December so it was cold but manageable. I liked the international glass displays?the Murano glass, especially because it reminded me of my aunt who had a significant number of pieces of this type of glass. THE BADFirst and foremost, I expected to see a palace or at least a castle straight out of a fairy tale. The Jeju Glass Castle is nowhere near a castle or palace. The buildings were plain and very utilitarian. The gardens were manicured but not palatial. It was more of a museum and a park, rather than a castle. Secondly, aside from signage that are in Korean or that mention the name of the place, there is nothing in the museum that shouts, ?I am in Jeju!? or ?I am in Korea!? for that matter. There is nothing in the museum that is intrinsically exclusive to the Jeju Glass Castle.Lastly, I was looking forward to try the glass comfort but the lock inside was broken and the door won?t keep closed. THE VERDICTI was able to take good photos of the displays?like I said, they were very instagrammable. Nevertheless, I do not see myself going back here just for the sake of it. It gets boring eventually, with little to do except to look at beautiful glass.

The history facts in this memorial hall recalled me of the one in Oswiecim, Poland... This memorial hall will help you to understand Jeju people's local history. Whenever I visit war related museum or places, we should stop fighting for nothing but losing the precious lives. I was even cried when I read 2 young men who could not enter the military school due to the wrong record of this tragic incident. I read all of explanation in Korean and English. I skipped some clips but I tried to watch 2 or 3 min's clips. Very well prepared in English and Korean. One of best museum. It is FREE. Only I concerned, there is no chairs to take a rest from time to time. And there was a decent with 15ish people, her voice was too much loud to make big echo in the hall area! I think they have to pay attention with other visitors who look into all scripts! I was a bit mad because she was too passionate to proceed her job. I think you do not need a docent because all of exhibits are perfectly translated in English. There are many heart breaking stories, but when I entered into the cave Darangshi(?), I could keep saying   oh my god..   I feel very sorry for all deceased, and their family members who survived at the same time witnesses. I strongly recommend this museum if you are interested local history, and history buff. It is a must. In fact, there is no restaurant, there is a coffee shop only. If you rent a car, within 10 min's drive, there are some. The bus #343, or #344 go to 4.3 Peace Park. From this park, Jeju Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest is 5 min's drive away, and 20 min's walk on foot. This Forest is wonderful. I recommend to combine these 2 places to visit at once. History and Nature are very good combination! The last stop of 343 &344 is this forest.

The Halla Arboretum is a sort of giant tree garden/park spread out over a mountain with innumerable trails that span the mountain side, leading to the top.  Key trees are labeled in museum fashion though the information provided is minimal.  Think of the arboretum as a park on a hillside with paths leading to a summit with views of the peak and city.  It's quietly beautiful with the cool air gently perfumed by the trees and soil.  If you are traveling on Jeju and are looking for a place to spend d1-2 hours, the Halla Arboreteum is a good call.

The exhibits were pretty interesting actually but as mentioned in the title, it's a mainly outdoor venue! The glass sculptures look better in the day time or at night when the lights are on.. SO..! If the weather is not helpful, save it for another day! It's pretty far out, so if u are gonna go, do the O'sulluc tea museum and this together... Don't leave too late coz it's terribly difficult to get a cab, unless you have a pre-arranged driver. That said, the staff there really are very, very nice.. We were actually the last few patrons out and we were stranded without a cab, in the bloody freezing rain.. We had 3 ahjussis trying to help us call cabs and eventually one of em offered to drive us to the nearest bus stop instead coz no one was responding, and FYI the nearest bus stop is abt 10mins out too..
The entrance fee was quite expensive. Bear was so cute. I like the history of Teddy bear. And it was impressive to see the first teddy bear in the world !! Near this museum, it was Chocolate factory.

The description at each stop was brief brief brief. I wonder why we came here...What took the longest amount of time??? The darn sales pitch conducted by a Korean auntie who claimed to be a BIG star just because she acted once in a local drama. The sales pitch was held inside a shabby shack. As it was winter the stuffiness was still bearable. Can you imagine if you came in summer??? With her broken Chinese (she turned to our tour guide for any sentences containing slightly more complex grammar) she enthusiastically tried to sell us this & that especially her biggest profit spinner - honey. She did not let her lack of fluency in Chinese stop her from making big bucks out of tourists. Not only that she even tried to sell us the many   benefits   of her empty honey glass bottle! Namely what we could do with it after we had finished eating the honey - Coin bank kitchen container blah blah blah & blah blah blah. Yakkity yakkity yak. She gave those who wanted to try a tiny teaspoon of her honey. And at the end of her sales pitch instead of letting tourists approached her if they were interested in buying she walked to each & every one of us while we were still seated (!) to ask if we wanted to buy. I think this must be because she knew that we would all walk out without buying anything if she just stand there & wait for people to come to her. So she took the more aggressive approach. Unfortunately I fell for her aggressive sales tactic & had to fork out a hefty sum for her   unique   honey. I say 'hefty' sum because when we were at the airport waiting to transfer for our flight to Seoul we saw a souvenir shop selling the SAME honey at a price which was 10000 won LESSER than what the darn old woman sold us!!! Oh man we were all so pissed! We had been cheated!!! Warning to tourists: Do NOT buy honey at this village museum!!!

The collection of teddy bears is good and very nicely organized according to themes. I especially loved the collections of very old teddy bears and the stories behind them and their owners that really touched a soft spot in my heart. There were also very vintage Winnie the Pooh bears that were really an eye-opener, as well as bears wearing traditional korean costumes depicting scenes of ancient korean life that I liked. The outdoors section of the exhibits were however not very impressive and when my friend and I visited the museum in June, the museum was very warm indoors. We were sweating profusely as we looked at the exhibits and in fact found it a joy to go outdoors into the sun, which turned out to be cooler. This prevented me from giving the attraction a four star rating. However, the collection is really a must-see for teddy bear lovers and it will undoubtedly be a more enjoyable place to visit in other months of the year.

The building is attached to the   jeju tourism   board (or something like that). It costs about 4 or 5 000 won to get in  then handed a coupon for a discount at the cafe or any of the products. The children enjoyed it as they got to make chocolate for 10 000 which included a take home mold. The museum isn't much to look at but just enough to make your mouth water. It is close enough to all the other activities in the area  if traveling with kids  this is a good   trade off   point to let them have some fun.
The bears are adorable! It is also a 10 min walk from the cheonjeyeon waterfalls, alive museum and 3100w away from the cliffs!

The   museum   is not too far from Jeju City so it's only a short ride in a taxi to this location.  You may want to tell the taxi driver to drive past the Jeju Mysterious Road if you are going this way as it is along the route.The museum itself attempts to shock you but you get over the shock in a few minutes and it does become a bit mundane after a while.  You do sense that the museum creators did have a good sense of humor though.  There are many many displays that feature sexual positions toys etc. but nothing that is too shocking.  The grounds are fairly immaculate too.  Many phallic symbols etc.  You know what to expect at this location.I guess it is worth the visit as there are not too many museums like this in the world but it really isn't worth an out of the way trip to this museum.

Teddy Bears dressed up in art and history, what's not to love? Museum isn't big, exhibition are on two levels. Elvis show is entertaining.

Teddy bear museum located at Jungmun resort at Jeju. It's easy to reach the resort by Airport Limousine 600 from Grace hotel bus stop or others. So many teddy bear with different characters and customs. We can take a photo with big Teddy bear like Einstein, Steve Jobs, Van Gogh etc.There's a garden with many teddy bear statues. So cute!

Teddy Bear Museum in Jeju opened in 2001 and boasts for owning the largest collection of teddy bears.  What differentiates this museum from the rest is that Korea's history was told using the bears.  It was cute and a not so serious approach that would cater to the children.The museum consists of 2 Exhibition halls namely the hall of history and the hall of art.  This museum serves as the home for as many as 1,500 bears that includes the luxurious Louis Vuitton bear.

Spent an hour exploring the cave first thing in the morning - very beautiful, unique and wasn't crowded.
