Nonetheless, we explored other stops (beaches and beaches). The sea and beaches are very beautiful. Udo is famous for their peanut and orange ice creams which I felt is a waste of money. Per cup of ice cream topped with some peanut or orange juice cost 5000won. Mcd ice cream taste nicer and bigger quantity. Oh yes, if you are willing to spend more you can rent bicycle and cycle around the island. And if you have international driving licence you can rent motorized vehicle to travel around. The roads are small and there's many tour buses shuttling people hence certain areas are abit congested.

Udo is a small island to the east of Jeju Island - about 1 hour bus from the Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal to Cheng Shan Port and take another 15 mins on a ferry to Udo.  Udo offers a beachside road around the island.  If you have an international driving license, you can rent a small electri car to drive around the island, if not, you can still rent a eletri bicycle or use local bus.  There are many restaurant and cafes along the beachside road.  Sometime you can see a small white sand beach between those dark volcano rocks.

Udo is a really small island, you can go around by bicycle in several hours. Udo is a volcanic island, so it has several nice beaches with white and black sand, impressing lava rock formations, caves etc. We went there several times, every time for 2-3 days, and every time it was just wonderful. You should go and spend a few days there if you want to relax in a quite and peaceful atmosphere with no nightlife, co crowds, no big attractions but with beautiful nature. Still, if you want to get in touch with the rest of the world - no problem here, our Korean mobiles were working fine, Internet was available right in the   arrival hall   of the port and in many   minbaks   (small Korean-style hotels).You can get there easily from Seongsan port  (＿?깆??고) of Jeju island by ferry in just 10-15 minutes. Ferries depart every hour from 08.00 till 17.30 or 18.00 depending on season. Most accommodations are found on on the White Coral Beach (Seo-bin-baek-sa, ＿?鍮諛깆?? or  Sanhosa, ??고몄?? ), 10 minutes walk from the port. They are all small 1-2 floor buildings located directly on the beach with seaview (Pensions, Minbaks). We never booked anything in advance, but found a room on site, but we went in May and October - not highest season. The rooms were always nice and big, also with kitchen and all the necessary kitchenware. Also there are small shops with snacks and some Korean restaurants.So, what to do in there?- swim in the pure emerald water of White coral beach, see the special kind of sand, it really feels like you are in tropics ^^- rent a bike and go around the islandThe road goes nicely along the shore, there were almost no cars except on the busier Jeju-facing side, and we enjoyed the scenery very much!  - Geommeolle Beach (寃?硫?)This is a black sand beach with very beautiful and unusual rock formations and caves, and we spent a very good time there. You can go in caves and see small rocks piled up on each other. And once a year they have a symphony concert in the caves!!Also, if you are a diver with a certificate, there is a diver center there. We tried to do it, but we did not have a PADI certificate so they refused, they do not do fun dives.And  we took a motor boat (10 000W/person) to see farther caves with a spectacular view of Udo cliffs (Hu-hae-seok-byeok, ＿?댁＿?踰). If you are lucky, you can also see a peculiar site called Ju-gan-myeong-weol - sun reflecting at the ceiling of a cave giving a   moon shape  . We also went up the hill, nice view of both Udo and Jeju!!What problems you can encounter in Udo?- languageLocal people are friendly and try to help, but they do not understand English!!So if you do not speak Korean, print out Korean names of what you want to visit and some basic Korean phrases (preferably in Korean, not transcriptions, because pronunciation may be tricky). BUT! the owner of the LOG-house speaks English very good!- foodThere is no Western restaurants on the island, only Korean!! The shops on the beach only sell snacks like Ramen, but there is a bigger mart inland called Hana-ro Mart with fruits, vegetables, milk, etc. (??濡 留, try to ask locals for directions and go there by bike, you will find it, there is no place to get lost ^^). And it could be a good idea to bring some food with you from Jeju, especially if you want something like cheese, wine etc.

Try to give yourself a little extra time to buy tickets as they day we travelled it was packed with tourists.The short ferry trip was wonderful, and offered great views of Udo as we approached. On reaching the island the first thing we observed were the amount of rental companies offering bikes, electric 2/3 seater buggies, scooters and tandem. In fact anything you can think of to explore the island. Ido is famous for peanuts and you will find many of these on sale in the quaint little cafes and shops dotted around main road. If you get the chance you should try the local    Udo peanut Makgeolli   The island is truly beautiful and if you do decide to join the hoards on electric vehicles shop around a bit as there are lots of rental companies eager to offer their wares. It is also important to ensure that you have an   international drivers licence  ,, as they appear to have tightened up since a number of accidents lately and wouldn't accept our UK credentials.All in all great trip with lots of ferries running bak and forward throughout the day.

This was a really enjoyable hike up the highest mountain in South Korea @ 1950m, and I recommend it as a great experience of the outdoors and physical activity.  However I saw a lot of people (both locals and foreigners) struggling with various aspects so please take note of the following points:WEATHER:  If you have the flexibility of several days from which to select, review the weather in advance and aim to choose the best day.....otherwise for example you may have no views when you emerge from the trees and at the summit.TIME, PACE & TIME-LIMITS:  This is a long hike, 19.2km round trip to be exact or about 12 miles, but is a relatively gentle incline.  The general consensus in many reviews is that it should take 10 hours total including breaks and lunch.  I would consider myself slightly above average fitness and took 6 hours total, however being solo it makes a difference because I could walk at my own brisk pace and take breaks (typically quite short 5-10 mins) when I wanted.  There are 2 shelters (with toilets) on the route located at approx 4km and 7km, and it's very important to note that for safety reasons they do not allow anyone past the second shelter (which is 2.3km from the summit) AFTER 13-00 HRS, no exceptions.  Furthermore everyone must depart the summit to start descending by 14-30 HRS latest.  I did come across quite people between the 2 shelters who appeared to be rushing to make the 13-00 deadline.  This is not recommended because either you could push yourself too hard and get exhausted, or get injured walking on the rocks, or simply miss the deadline.  FOOTWEAR:  At minimum bring sturdy training or trekking shoes, preferably hiking boots to provide ankle support. Some sections of the hike are on hessian mats and wooden walk ways which of course are very nice to walk on, however probably 30% or more is on large volcanic rocks which are not comfortable to walk on and requires some focus and concentration (especially descending when your legs are tired).  I was surprised to see some walking in sandals and they suffered.  A walking stick can be helpful but is not essential.DAYPACK:  Bring a small daypack to carry water, snacks, clothes etc and to keep your hands free.  Even in summer bring a light jacket or sweater because it can get cool at the top with the wind and elevation.  In Winter I'm sure it's really cold at the summit.PROTECTION:  Bring a hat for the higher elevations (when not in the forest), sun cream and lip balm.HYDRATION/SNACKS:  There is reportedly a source of mountain water half way up but personally I did not see it near the sign, and staff at one of the shelters advised me that no water is available.  Hence suggest that you bring at least 3-4 bottles of water or isotonic drink in your day pack per person (maybe 1.5 to 2 litres), and be sure to conserve it wisely because you'll need some on the way down.  I encountered some people on the way up who had no water left.  Muesli bars, chocolate and fruit are good sources of energy.  As well as fruit, the locals tend to pack rice & meat lunches and have communal picnics at the summit.TRANSPORT:  I used a rental car and got there early, before 8am.  The car park was already full and people started parking on both sides of the main road, which is allowed.  The bus stops are right there beside the car park for those using public transport.CERTIFICATE:   There is small office hidden away near the Seongpanak car park which will print your name on a nice certificate for 1000 Won. (US$1).IN SUMMARY: Please take the time to prepare properly and get there reasonably early so that you can enjoy the hike at your own pace.  During the walk I saw several deer, lots of beautiful butterflies and other insects and loved the great views ....Jeju is covered in 300+ volcanic cones so its amazing to see all of these.  HAVE A GREAT DAY ON HALLASAN!

At the start sign, set gear to neutral and off the brakes and watch your car go uphill. It is quite fun because of the optical illusion. No fun if you don't drive.

This is a national park in the true sense.  There are long walking trails to see amazing sites, and you must be prepared to spend time and be in good shape for the walks.  Also, bring plenty of water for the walks.  The park has awesome views and long and winding roads.

This is a fun place to stop and spend about a half hour or so.  The road in this section appears to defy gravity.  Not sure of the reason why, but is very interesting to see the car go backwards while facing downhill.  There are some interesting exhibits and statues, along with shops, nearby.

This hill looks rather spectacular from a distance and the approach to its foot is thru a pretty green field. The pathway is well maintained and it's an easy hike up to the top, at only 180 meters. It's mostly a broad stairway to the top and makes for a pleasant evening walk. At the peak it would be a great place to watch the stars on a clear moonless night. Admission is free after   closing time   -- there's no gate.

This forest of nutmeg trees are easily accessible and very easy and nice to take a walk - 2 easy trails which are around 1 to 2.2 km long - all easy terrain, just some stretches of little gravel roads. We enjoyed an hour's walk in the sunset and loved it. While travelling there, keep looking out for the road which is flanked by giant nutmeg trees, said to be filming location for several Korean romantic drama.

There's a starting point and ending point, that shows this mysterious road's gravitational force. Many went with tour buses but it's best to experience this in your own rented car! Switch to neutral and let the mystery begin!

There were many tour groups at the place and many people were walking on the road. Anyway, there was nothing exciting about the place. It is just a short (around 50 metres) stretch of road and things roll upslope instead of downslope. Give this a miss if you have not enough time.

There is not much to see on the way to the top. Remember it's a 19k hiking and you need to use your time wisely in a day. We went on a cloudy day. It wasn't too hot but the hiking was difficult with rocks covering most of the roads. So get yourself a real pair of hiking shoes! My feet got hurt and it was slippery after rain. Some parts have stairs, which are highly appreciated... The top view was great but maybe it was dry, we did not see water in the crate. Spring and Fall might have more to see. My friend and my legs have been hurting since we accomplished it...

There is a start point specified on the road. I stopped my car, put car to neutral and released the brakes - the car started to move slowly forward and up slope! From inside the car, the road is up slope, yet the car is like rolling down slope on neutral gear. Fascinating! A must try if you are self-driving.

There are two kinds of people in the world: those who like their beaches to be overrun with screaming, writhing masses of tourists, and those who think being happy is important. And sure, this could be just another one of those jaded reviews written by a bitter old troll who has no other outlet for his vitriol than to misinform random strangers on the Internet, but it's not. I'm here to vehemently disabuse anyone who is thinking of having a quiet day at Hyeopjae beach out of a sense of civic duty. Yes, the beach itself is a soft sand frame for spectacular sunsets punctuated by occasionally clear blue-green waters, but it's also a growing epicenter for the worst kind of overbooked tourism. Pros: The beach itself is broad, and the area in front of the main beach lends itself to a safe experience for attended children: there is a large, open region of sand at low tide and shallow water at high tide for kids to play in.  The view is nice, and the sunsets are extravagant. There is camping nearby with good tree cover, adequate facilities for showering, stores for trinkets and swimming paraphernalia, and places to buy food and drink. There is also a small but growing night life near the beach that has a distinctly island feel, far from the thumping of your standard Korean club scene. Cons: The swimming area is unbelievably small, so not only does everyone get to experience a sardine style of   swimming   in water that rarely goes past the hips of an adult, the water is also full of sand and debris due to the high person-per-square-meter ratio. Visibility underwater is often zero, so don't expect to see fish on a busy day - which is pretty much the entire high season. There is garbage everywhere, both in the water, and in large, reeking piles near the parking lot. The noise is unbelievable (just like the parking) and the local restaurants - with only one or two exceptions - cater to the lowest common denominator for quality.  Hyeopjae is being targeted by packaged family tours, and yet there is a laughably inadequate infrastructure in place to ensure a safe, organized experience for children. The beautiful volcanic rocks along the sides of the beach and in some parts of the water are playgrounds of minor and major injury. The often unattended children that race up and down the beach are in no way warned about or protected from these hazards. The forest of beach umbrellas tightly packed on the   main beach   is both uncomfortably crowded and poorly organized for parents to keep an eye on their kids, and for kids to find their parents when they get lost. The lifeguards are simultaneously overworked and overzealous. They are simply too busy whistling at people to keep them safe from the dangers of hip-deep water (a strange and annoying tradition amongst Jeju lifeguards) to effectively keep an eye out for people - especially children - who are may be in real trouble.Bottom Line: If you've never had the chance to explore Jeju, you won?t know just how bad Hyeopjae is. Moreover, as I said in the beginning, some people actually enjoy the mass market appeal of tourist traps, and I don't begrudge them their tastes. All I'm saying is Jeju has an embarrassment of better beaches with better food and better facilities. In fact, you only have to travel up or down the road for 15 minutes in either direction to find beautiful, secluded areas where you lavish on an empty beach and swim in truly pristine waters. Q.E.D.

There are sign posts to mark the start and end of the 100 metres stretch of the Mysterious Road.  Pretty fun to play   magic   with family and friends. Put your car to neutral gear, release your foot off the accelerator and notice the car moving   uphill   on the road.  Recreate the same effect with a bottle or ball rolling uphill.  The Mysterious Road is actually a gravity hill i.e. a place where a slight downhill slope appears to be an uphill slope due to higher surroundings, creating the natural illusion that water flows uphill or that a car left out of gear rolls uphill.  Worth a fun stop if you self-drive!

There are number of buses that go to this market, 500, 37, 502 & etc. Make sure to alight at Jungang junction stop & walk into a side road about 5mins. The market sell plenty of seafood, meat, fruit & snack at reasonable price. We enjoy dinner there.
there are many things to enjoy including Eco Bridge, Hovercraft, Eco Windmill, Picnic Garden, Kid?s Town, Eco Road, Bare Foot Scoria, Lavender Garden (season) & etc

There are 3 memorial towers, one of Kim Man Duk, civil uprising volunteers, and one of patriot at the end of Joseon dynasty. There is Kim Man Duk's grave stone, original one which moved here because of road construction in its original place. This is located in Sara-bong(hill) park. It is very low hi,, but you can enjoy beautiful sunrise on the top of hill. Even day time, I could enjoy nice view toward Jeju international port. I recommend walk around the hill first then visit Mochungsa afterwards, The Sarabong walk path is part of Olle #18. There are many locals who work out here. You can feel like a local!

The water is a beautiful emerald color but the beach is too crowded. Too many parasols, shops, and small hotels. Go to the beach down the road if you want a more relaxing day at the beach.Tip: There are some decent beach style restaurants on the main road. There is nice a pizza cafe with covered outside seating. Also there is a Mom's Touch that servers fast food (chicken sandwiches).This beach is ranked as one of the top beaches in Jeju by Koreans. I was disappointed but I realized that the standards are different. Hey if you want simple food, people, and shade then this is the place to go.

The trail system in Jeju is quite extensive and well mapped out. Our hotel was right on Olle 7 so one day we went tracking. What started on a normal surface road became a rough surface hiking trail through bushes, up and down a rocky coastline. The trail is indicated by ribbons, from what I understand different colors for different olles. when in Jeju hiking should definitely be on the to do list.

The sea in Jeju Island was very clean and a good place to enjoy the natural scenery. There were many kinds of cafes and long coastal roads. Also, the cafes had unique personalities and were good places to take pictures and the taste of coffee was good. I went there for 2 nights and 3 days, and I could see the beautiful sea when the sun was bright, and there was a dark atmosphere of the sea when the weather was cloudy. However, unlike in the past, the whole atmosphere of the sea seemed to disappear as many buildings were built. There was a wish for a return to the old sea. Nevertheless, if I visited Jeju Island again, I wanted to go to Woljeongri Beach again. Viewers of this review also recommend going to Woljeongri beach where I went.

The road was called mysterious road as it seem to be a up slope but your vehicle can move slowly up like going down slope. The area is less crowded at around 7-9am until the tour bus came, where many people actually went down to crowd around this road. The tour bus would stop at the start of the slope and off its Engine and slowly moved up to the end and turn into the car park where the tourists would come down and see cars moving up. Some of them would pour water to show that the water went up instead of down. It is quite mind boggling. But actual fact that this road is due to the surrounding which makes you have the perception thinking it is a up slope but actually it is down.Way to get there is by Car or Bus. It is close to Jeju LoveLand and it is down the same road, so it is not too difficult to find.

The road brings you to an altitude of 1100 m close to e Mt. Hallasan which with 1900 m is the highest mountain in South Korea. They have built a walk with wooden planks that brings you to nice trees without getting wet feet. The walk takes about one hour when taking Pictures, if you rush it is only 20 minutes.

The place is good only for families with little children.Kids will be excited about the fact that a  car(or bottle) seems to go up on downhill. However, for adults? Not really...If u have plenty of time to spend on the road.

The Mysterious road is really mysterious to me! As my friend and I booked a taxi for the day, we still had time on our hands before the day ends, so the taxi driver took us to this road and off his engine. Next thing we know, the car was moving on its on up the slope. Talk about creepy. Can't know what scientific explanation there could be behind this. If you are travelling by car and will pass by here, by all means, experience the wonder.

The Mysterious Road is one where the road appears to go uphill, but it's actually downhill.  So cars go there, turn off their motors and   coast uphill.    It's actually more fun to watch the faces of the tourists than to watch the vehicles.  My advice: take a long lens, and quietly record the looks of awe.  Makes for some great shots.

The Mysterious Road is an interesting to visit while in Jeju and don't need to pay. The Bus Driver show that even with the engine stopped, the bus still able to move forward. The visit won't take too much of the time, just interestingly an eye illumination.

The Mysterious Road is a little bit overrated I guess. Its just a road that has an optical illusion. You cannot really see the different it makes also. So, I would say it's just average place to visit here if you have extra time.

The Jeju Mysterious Road, also known as Dokkaebi Road, lies on a hill at the foot of a mountain, and connects two major highways on Jejudo Island. It has earned its name, as objects and liquid appear to roll and flow up the hill instead of down, when, in fact, such image of gravity defiance is an optical illusion rendered by the seemingly high surroundings.

The hotel owner drove us there in a morning. It took 1 hour for the round trip. The road was paved with concrete and so it was good for children or elder. When we arrived the summit, many people are waiting there for the sunrise. It was windy and cloudy and the sunrise was not beautiful as we expected. Nevertheless,  you could enjoy the full city view on the top of IIchulbong. On return trip, you could ate abalone slices in the Sea Woman house located in foot of the mountain. Overall, this Unesco Heritage worth a visit!

The guard told me I should've called to the office before heading for there. The snow made cars are stuck in the road. I could clearly see with my bare eyes. Even if today's weather was so perfect and wonderful, it is a forest under tremendously tall trees so lots of shadow made them ice. Maybe next week might be OK to visit inside but please call beforehand if it is allowed to get in. Even at the entrance, I could see beautiful scenery from a distance.

The ferry to Udo island is fairly close to the Seongsan Ilchulbong peak, close to a 15 mins walk. The ferry ride is 15 mins only, and you get to see some amazing views all through. In the island, there are many beautiful beaches and cafes. We rented bikes (do remember to ask them for a map if you do!), and rode all around the island. A complete round on the ocean road took like 3+ hours, but was loads of fun. Cos we could stop by at beaches to relax, or cafes for a quick bite or drink. We took lots of incredible pictures. A perfect day spent in gorgeous weather!

The experience is new and the music is nice. However, I go bored after some time because I am not a art person and do not quite grasp what the artists are trying to express. Driving through narrow road to get there.

The drive there was pleasant as you passed through many scenic places. Saw some homes with unique design.As we were at the start of Mysterious Road, our taxi driver switch off the engine and let the car just roll ?up the road?. Was wondering how could this happen!!! We witness some other vehicles doing the same. Our taxi driver took a bottle of waterAnd pour it in the middle of the road, the water didn?t flow backward. A group of Chinese tourist ,were doing the same thing, the guide say it?s a scam.  But the truth is ?Optic Illusion ?Nice backdrop of mount hallasan

The dragon head rock is a good place to visit, if your wanting to stay close to jeju si. It doesnt take long to look at the rock and there are many tourists but the costal road is a nice relaxing walk.
The bus was on the road with engine off. Instead of reverse it moves forward (the road is on uphill). Water was pour on the road and it flow upwards, against the gravity of the road.

The bus driver has completely stopped the engine at the starting point of Jeju Mysterious road and once he release the break the bus moves eventhough it is an upward slope...Why? The answer we got from the tour guide is that, it is an optical illusion - that actually it is a downward slope. Well it doesnt look like that at the time and even now I couldnt believe it is a downward instead of an upward slope - believe it or not!!

The best parts about this tour were the walk from the main road where you can admire the cherry blossom on both sides of the road and the newly opened Angel-In-Us coffee house. If not for the springtime cherry blossoms, there doesn't seem to be much else to see.

The admission was 占2,000 per ticket, so not so bad.  96% of what you are walking on is just hardened lava and there are puddles, so bring good shoes.  This is also basically a cave, so it's quite chilly down there, so a jacket is nice to have.  From the bottom of the stairs to the lava column is just shy of a kilometer.  There are a variety of things to see along the way, such as the different types of formations and effects.Aside from the lava tube, there is only a small restaurant and a gift shop.  Not too far down the road is the mazeland.  There may be better times than others to go.  We got lucky and missed a huge crowd of young kids that had just arrived on a bus.

The   museum   is not too far from Jeju City so it's only a short ride in a taxi to this location.  You may want to tell the taxi driver to drive past the Jeju Mysterious Road if you are going this way as it is along the route.The museum itself attempts to shock you but you get over the shock in a few minutes and it does become a bit mundane after a while.  You do sense that the museum creators did have a good sense of humor though.  There are many many displays that feature sexual positions toys etc. but nothing that is too shocking.  The grounds are fairly immaculate too.  Many phallic symbols etc.  You know what to expect at this location.I guess it is worth the visit as there are not too many museums like this in the world but it really isn't worth an out of the way trip to this museum.

Take a boat is convenient from Jeju to Udo (we were driving , the boat is able to carry the car) only 30 minutes boat, then arrive at Udo. We drive along the coste road, stopped by the hill, it is a 30 mins climbing, once reach the top you can have a overview of this Island  We literally turned around the island by car. Tried sea food abalone and some shellfish. It was very good experience. We star at 11.30am boat to Udo and finished at 4pm to take boat back to Jeju main land. It can be a 3-4 hours visit.

Stumble upon it when wanting to cross the road. There's mainly women's stuff, plenty of cosmetics, very few man's stuffs and some restaurants. Looks like a typical China zhuhai gong pei type of underground mall, but smaller. The ships above ground sells higher quality stuffs.

Someone told me Udo is beautiful, so it's in my wish list when I visit Jejudo. I went there on Saturday (7.5.2016). At the harbour, there are many different type of transportation vehicles for rent to travel Udo, so, basically the narrow road at Udo is full of vehicles, no matter is two wheel, three wheel or four wheel. I did the Olle trail 1.1, travel on foot, it was frustrated and irritating when need to walk together with so many types of vehicles, noisy and crowded. But, luckily the trail does divert some part of the trekking route which is away from the vehicle road, hiking up to the light house hill and also farm house and farming area.

some people say this road again the earth gravitation, but some said it's cause the magnet field is big at that area. if see with eyes the street look uphill but the car stop and  engine stop can forward till some point.

So we are sat in the car, put on neutral mode and the car actually moved! This is a really cool experience and it only takes a minute to do- I have seen mysterious roads on the travel channel before but this was my first time doing it- if you find yourself on Jeju island check it out!

So i understand that the optical illusion was interesting, but there is literally nothing here. If you go here, you should only spend not more than 10 minutes. Take a pic in the road sign, buy a snack if you want, and be done with it..

Small local old village. There are several old huts for tourist to visit.Shops sell honey, traditional juice and facial cream inside those houses.Sales are very helpful to show direction of road. They speak fluent Mandarin.

Small island off the Jeju coast makes for a nice day trip/excursion from the main Jeju island. We enjoyed the climb up the one and only peak for excellent views, as well as some stunning coastal caves and cliffs, lighthouse, crashing surf, and volcanic rock. At first blush it may not seem too nice but Udo kind of grows on you. I'd recommend renting a moped or bicycle and bopping around the backroads; that would be the best way to see and enjoy Udo.

Small island - the main road that goes around the island is around 13,8 km. A good way to explore is to rent a vehicle - electric scooter, electric motor cycle, electric bike, or bike - and go as you like. But all the electric is required international driving license.

Slapstick, cheesy humour so just relax into it and join in the fun of the show. It's entertaining as the predictable story unfolds - beware, there is a little bit of audience participation - just go with it! The performers are professional and their drumming is excellent. The story is told with very few words but is very easy to follow. There are strobe lights at one point. The theatre is out in the middle of nowhere so eat before going or book into the NANTA hotel next door to eat. The planetarium is across the road so you could go to an early NANTA performance the on to do some star gazing.

Skip this and head for Dodubong Peak, especially if you're on the Jeju Golden Bus day tour. This place is unremarkable and is honestly one of the dirtiest parts of the area; I attempted to have my photo taken and a rat scurried out from between the rocks. If you walk up the road (away from the site) about a half mile, maybe less, the photo ops are much nicer. The area near Dodubong Peak is also nicer and you can see great views of of Jeju from the summit.

Since Jeju is best travelled by car, the mysterious road (it's actual name) is definitely worth checking out. Putting the car on the apparent downslope in neutral gear will make the car move backwards and vice-versa...freaked us out until we discovered the optical illusion behind it. Be careful of all the other cars trying it out as well as pedestrians attempting something similar by pouring water onto the road surface.

Seongsan Ilchulbong/Sunrise Peak (＿?깆??곗쇱遊). Seongsan Ilchulbong, as with all natural formations on Jeju, was formed by hydrovolcanic eruptions about 5,000 years ago. Its volcanic cone is 600-meters wide and 90 meters tall, and its crated lined with 99 rocky spires that resemble a crown. In addition to its appearance, or rather, because of its appearance, it was name as one of the 7 wonders of nature in the world in 2011 (UNESCO Natural World Heritage). So needless to say, it would not be a surprise to see busloads of tourists at the carpark planning to make their way up to the peak.There are 2 suggested paths to reach the peak, where the view is said to be magnificent. I can?t remember which path we took, but the trail leading up to the peak was well maintained and quite manageable with proper steps to lead us along our way.However, despite there being steps, they were still steep, but at least the path was one of the most even paths that we had walked that day (e.g. no rocky paths nor muddy roads). The path uphill to Seongsan Ilchulbong comprises steps of varying steepness.For more photos and about my experience, please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/seongsan-ilchulbongsunrise-peak.html

Self-Drive Holiday in Jeju:Everyone loves going on holidays and I believe a great percentage of these do so on guided tours. Guided tours are fine where convenience is concerned; hotels, meals, itineraries, transport, flights, places of interests to visit, entrance fees etc. etc. are all taken care of by the tour company. As I had discovered decades ago, despite all the conveniences of a guided tour, there are drawbacks that would put one off such tours completely; not being able to sleep-in and wake up as and when you want, having limited time to enjoy the various places of interests or enjoy your lunch while taking in the magnificent scenery from a mountain top restaurant , having to put up with other travellers who simply cannot or are not bothered to be on time, not being able to visit or enjoy other interesting places that are rarely included in tour itineraries, to list a few. Ever since my first guided tour holiday overseas, I have opted for a self-drive holiday and I am very sure there are many out there who would love to do so too,  but refrained from doing so because of a lack of information and perhaps, apprehensive about what it would entail to do a self-drive holiday in a foreign land. This guide is to help dispel those apprehensions and provide the necessary information for you to successfully make that first self-drive holiday in the Honeymoon Island of Jeju, and hopefully, many more thereafter in other destinations of your dreams.Preparation:Many experts would advise, and rightly so, that you should first read up all the necessary information on driving at the destination that you will be holidaying in. However, in my opinion, what is more important is having the self-confidence to drive in a foreign land. Sometimes, things can go wrong, road and weather conditions can change to the extent that no pre-reading or preparation can help, but, with that very important self-confidence, it will see you through. You must also have a flexible mind set and be ready to accommodate changes when necessary ? only then will you be able to thoroughly enjoy your self-drive holiday. Having said that, I must say that driving in Jeju is a walk-in-the-park, quite unlike, for example, driving through the mountain pass between Sun Moon Lake and Hualien County in Taiwan ? that is a drive I would never recommend to the feint hearted.International Driving Permit ? you will need to obtain an International Driving Permit to be able to rent a car in Jeju, and for that matter, in most other countries. It can be easily obtained at AAS and it costs only $20.00 and is valid for one year. You would also want to search for information on all the places of interests and decide on which of those to visit during your stay in Jeju. This is to help you plan and minimize travelling time. These can be had at the Korea Tourism Centre at Samsung CentreChoice of Hotel ? There are many hotels catering to different needs and budgets to choose from. The one most often asked question is the location ? to stay in Jeju-si or Seogwipo-si? My experience tells me that it makes no difference ? it is just a matter of choice. If you are arriving in Jeju late at night, then, perhaps, you may wish to stay in a hotel that is near the airport, to minimize your night driving had you decided on a hotel in Seogwipo-si. We landed in Jeju at 2000 hrs, collected our car at 2100 hrs and drove to Seogwipo-si where our hotel was situated. It was a pleasant forty-five minute drive with guidance from the GPS unit.Car Rental Company:There are many car rental companies in Jeju, but you will most likely come across only a handful if you search the internet ? Kumho, AJ Rentals (AVIS), SIXT, Donga and Jeju Rent-a-Car. Do note, though, that there are more than a dozen of competing rental companies at the airport to choose from if you prefer to shop around for the best rates and cars upon your arrival. I book mine through AJ Rentals, not only because of the brand name, but it also provided the best rates among the others on the net and it did not require me to pay in advance upon confirmation of my reservation. To rent the car, you will need to have an International Driving Permit (obtain it from AAS), your local driving license and passport. You can pay either in cash or credit card. Type of Car:The type of car you choose is totally dependent on your preference and budget ? luxury or basic. However, do consider the available boot space that will be needed to accommodate your luggage. As a guide, the boot of a KIA K3 can accommodate only three large suitcases with no space for a smaller, fourth piece. In a situation where there are four adults, the smaller, fourth suitcase will have to share estate space in the back seat with two other passengers. The cost of rental is dependent on the type of car, number of days and the period of travel. As a guide, a KIA K3 cost approximately S$60.00 per day for 5 days during the holiday season in November. The rate includes insurance, CDW and the use of a English language GPS, with collection and return at the airport. The rates of the other rental companies that I surveyed were cheaper, however, I cannot vouch for their quality nor service support. You decide at your own risk. The overall condition of the car was good. The only ?defect? was the slight steering alignment problem but it was not something that would put us in danger at any time. Maps:Do you need a map when it is very likely that you will be relying on the GPS? YES! A map is necessary for planning your routes and selecting the places of interests to visit.You can easily obtain a detailed map of Jeju Island, with all the major highways and feeder routes from your local Korean Tourism office. You can also obtain these from the car-rental companies when you collect your car in Jeju. You can use it to plan your route, estimate the travel time and locate other possible places of interests that you don?t find on the standard tourist trail. You can use this same map to write down the telephone numbers of the places of interests that you plan to visit. You will need these numbers for keying into the GPS system to guide you to your destination. I made it a point to re-confirm that the telephone numbers are current by asking the hotel staff to extract the numbers from their computer system. This proved to be very useful. Collecting Your Car At The Airport:After clearing immigration and customs, proceed to gate 5 of the arrival terminal. Opposite the gate, there is a green, covered walk-way with a sign that says ?Car Rentals?; it will lead you to a building where there are a lot of car-rental companies. If you had pre-booked your car, look for the car-rental company in the building. However, do take note that this building houses the local car rental companies. For the international brands such as Avis, Hertz and the other bigger local companies, they are housed in another location outside the airport. You will need to check with them when you are doing the booking or email them for the information. If the collection centre of the car rental company that you booked with is located outside the airport, wait for their shuttle bus at Gate 5. You will recognize their shuttle bus by their brand name boldly emblazoned on the sides of the bus. Since I booked my car through Avis, I took the ?AJ? shuttle bus to their rental office on the outskirts of the airport. The shuttle bus runs on a regular schedule. Arriving at the front of the office, you take a queue ticket. If you had made reservations, it takes just a few seconds to call up your reservation after presenting your passport, driver's licence and International Driving Permit. You will be shown the rental agreement with all the details pertaining to the type, class, number of days of rental, total costs and any other relevant information. With Avis, the GPS is included in the rental, whereas for other rental companies that I had enquired with, the GPS is charged separately. After you have signed the rental agreement, you will be shown your car. You then drive it off to the inspection building where they will go through the car with you to identify any minor damages, scratches, dents etc. They will also have you verify that the fuel tank is full and instruct you on the use of the GPS before getting you to sign off the acknowledgement form. Do ensure that the GPS is an English language version. Keep the documents safely in the glove-compartment and be sure to get the telephone number of the station that you will return the car to. You will need this number to key into the GPS system to guide you back. You then proceed on your way, presumably, to your hotel for a much needed rest after the long flight to Jeju.When returning the car, you just need to drive back to the same depot from where you had collected it. Just key the given number into the GPS. Upon arrival, follow the sign, ?Car Return? and head for an available lot. The attendant there will check the car with you and when all is in order, he hands you a form to sign after you have returned the key to him. You then take the shuttle bus that will take you to the departure hall at the airport.The use of the GPS:Different makes and models operate slightly differently from one another, however, the common function that generalizes all of them is the use of the telephone number of a particular hotel, attraction or establishment to program the location into the GPS. For example, the telephone number of our hotel, Ocean Palace Hotel, Jeju, is 064 - 7305800. To navigate to the hotel from the airport, I just had to key in the number 7305800 and simply touch the 'Navigate' button and voila, it calculates the shortest route and starts the voice navigation system in a jiffy - it's as simple as that. From then on, just follow the voice navigation to get you to your hotel. If you make a wrong turn or pass a junction where you were supposed to turn, do not panic. Just relax and drive on ? it will re-direct you back to the planned route or at times, provide you with a new course. In fact, we had a lot of fun and discovered many new places of interest by intentionally turning off to smaller but interesting-looking roads just to see what lies ahead and where it will eventually lead us to ? that is the beauty of a self-drive holiday. Driving in Jeju:Jeju has a coastal ring road of approximately 181 km, not counting the connecting highways linking the North-South-East ?West regions. The coastal scene is a sight to behold! It is left-hand driving in Jeju.To those who have never driven on the left side of the road, it takes a little getting used to, physically as well as in your mind. It gets a little more confusing when turning at traffic junctions, especially when driving through ? stopping gives you an opportunity to orientate yourself and prepare in your mind the lane to take when turning. To minimize this confusion, always try to follow a car in front of you which is turning in the same direction as you. It is also helpful to remember that when turning, the roadside kerb will always be on the right of the driver. The roads, save for the highways, are slightly narrower than the roads we are used to in Singapore.Generally, the speed limits are:30 Km / hr within 100 m of school zones50 Km / hr in town areas60 Km / hr in the outskirts of town70 Km / hr along highwaysThe speed limits change quite frequently, so it is advisable to keep a look-out for the change in speed limits. There are speed-cameras practically everywhere, usually positioned up on traffic lights, lamp-posts and in some places, hidden behind 'boxes' manned by a policeman. So, if you wish to spend your money supporting the policemen, speed on at your own risk.The local drivers can, at times, be quite reckless. Just like we have hell-drivers here, there are hell-drivers in Jeju too, but not too many. Just stay alert and always be on the look-out using your wing and rearview mirrors all the time. Except for the main areas of Jeju-si and Seogwipo-si, most of the roads around the island are quite free of traffic.  To estimate the time needed to travel any distances, take an average speed of 45 km/hr.Parking:Generally free parking along kerb-sides and paid parking in some buildings and are generally available easily. Most hotels have free parking for their guests ? do check with the hotel management that you have booked with. Petrol cost: As at Nov 2014: Krw 1750 / ltrPlanning Your Routes:Planning your routes is totally at your own whim and fancy, depending on the places of interest as well as the available time you have on the island. If you have a few days ( I would recommend a minimum of five days), perhaps you may wish to consider the following suggestion:1. Day 1 ? Arrival and check into hotel. This sample itinerary is on the assumption that your hotel is in Seogwipo. 2. Day 2 ? Explore the west scenic coastal drive (Route 1132) of Sagye, Gosan-Ilwa, Hagwi-Aewol and visit the places of interest along this route ( Mt Sangkaksan / Songkaksan / Yongmeori). There are many cafes (especially along the Coastal Cafe Road) and bbq restaurants for stops of aromatic coffee and grilled black pig meat. Explore Jeju-si city (underground shopping mall) and return via highway 1131 where the famous ?Forest Tunnel? is located. After dinner, take a drive to the Lotte World Resort for some very beautiful night scenery of the giant windmills.3. Day 3 ? Go East this time along the Pyeoson, Sehwa-Jongdal and Gimyeong ? Haengwon coastal routes. Stopover at Seongsan Ilchubong (Sunrise Peak). Have dinner in Jeju-si before doing a night drive back to Seogwipo. 4. Day 4 ? Alternative 1Drive to Seongsan Port in the north-east via the eastern coastal route and park your car there. Purchase your ferry tickets to Udo Island and spend a very interesting day there. You can tour the island by buying the hop-off-on bus tickets or for the adventurers, you can hire the quad-bikes or scooters. Alternative 2 ? visit the popular tourist spots such as the Trick-art museum, teddy bear museum, waterfalls, submarine tours, Green Tea museum, Geomun Oreum, Citrus fruit farms, mysterious road, etc etc....5. Day 5 ? Sammu Park is a destination not likely to appear on the typical package-tour’s itinerary for Jeju Island, but this downtown Sin-Jeju gem has some singularly unique features for the intrepid visitor.? First, the park was actually constructed on one of Jeju’s 368 oreums, local dialect for a small scoria (cinder) cone or parasitic/parallel volcano.? This one is Beduri oreum, surely one of the smaller ones, topping out at just 10 meters above its base with a circumference of 617 meters.? Beduri was transformed into the park in 1978 as part of an urban planning initiative. In addition to a large assortment of exercise equipment,? a children’s play area, badminton and basketball courts, and jogging/hiking trails, Beduri boasts a majestic, two-story octagonal pavilion, called Sammujeong. ? Constructed in the traditional Korean style and ringed by pine trees, the colorful wooden pavilion is almost like a giant tree-house.? It isn’t unusual to hear musicians and vocalists practicing there, taking advantage of the spot’s natural acoustics.? It’s a peaceful place to sip a beverage in any season.? Next, are you a train enthusiast or history buff?? Then you might want to visit Sammu for this feature alone:? the park is home to the last remaining steam locomotive for coal transportation in Korea.? MIKA Steam Locomotive No. 304 (registered Cultural Heritage No. 414) was manufactured in Japan in 1944, during Japanese colonial rule, and operated on Korean railroads until 1967. In 1978, President Park Chung Hee had it shipped to the park on Children’s Day, so that Jeju’s children could see a real train.? The train’s passenger car now contains a children’s library.? Finally, beginning in 2014, the park has been further renovated to be a sort of extension to the Bao Jian Street tourism and shopping district.? At the park’s south entrance, there is a giant clock surrounded by wildflowers and neon lampposts that match those on Bao Jian.? The clock has a Plexiglas dome that gives its neon face a trick-art, psychedelic look after dark.? Sammu Park is definitely worth a visit, particularly if you are staying at an area accommodation or if you will be going to Bao Jian…a chance for a little Jeju “nightlife.”

Right here, at this strange mysterious road in Jeju, I was also trying to observe if the trees growing around the vicinity of the mysterious road bend towards and focused at the core center where the strange phenomenon occurred but I could not see what I saw at Song Qingling's mausoleum. One of the Olle-gil trails (trail 10-1 to be exact) goes through and around most of the island although two or three hours are enough to walk on every single path on the island.? Handful of Harubang statues and some rapeseed flower fields make some good photo spots.? Other than the few dozen houses, the small elementary school is the only notable building.? As it only takes a couple of hours to walk around the entire island, eating a meal is about the only other thing to do.? Few seafood restaurants serve up some raw fish but the Gapado Haemul Jjajang restaurant was the most popular spot during my trip serving up Koreanized Chinese food with plentiful seafood toppings on the jjampong (spicy broth noodles) and jjajangmyeon (black bean noodles).

One of the benefits of being an island is all the beaches. One of the drawbacks is that beaches usually draw tourists, and where there are tourists, the shallow villainy of tourist industries inevitably follows. Sehwa has not yet been targeted for development. As of this writing, the long, open expanse of Sehwa beach is still a beach in its rawest form. When the tide goes out, the volcanic rock formations nearer to the road are exposed, leaving tidal pools to explore, thriving with an over abundance of flora and fauna. The beach at low tide is enormous, and rarely crowded. There are no lifeguards. No music. No lights. Just a beautiful beach, minor waves, clean sand, and decent swimming. When the tide comes in, you can continue swimming, or you can visit some of the restaurants in the area that cater to the locals rather than skimp for the tourists. I had some shabu shabu (??\대＿?) very near Sehwa which was like a kick to the pleasure center of my brain.  Sometimes there's even a local crafts market right next to Sehwa beach, but you have to get lucky to catch it.   Basically, Sehwa is a beach that is still Jeju. It's part of a local community, part of a local ecosystem, as yet only mildly disturbed by ideas of profitability or development.

On Jeju Island's Halla Mountain--at 1,950 meters, South Korea's tallest-- can be found Korea’s highest paved roadway, known as 1100 Meter Road or the 1100 Highland Rest Area.? There, you can take a self-paced nature hike on an elevated wooden walkway through a “volcanic” wetland; with its many lava rocks, trees and wildflowers, this place has an otherworldly beauty that you and your camera will love.? You’ll likely see lots of ravens, magpies and maybe some roe deer (be sure to stay alert for them along the highway if you are driving). Across the road, there’s a colorful cafe and shop, offering local beverage favorites and snacks, as well as souvenirs.? (They carry a good selection of galot clothing, made locally using persimmon-dyed fabrics.)? From the cafe’s observation deck, enjoy a perfect view of some of Halla’s most famous landmarks, including Yeongsil Folding Screen Rocks and the 500 Generals Rocks.This area takes on a very different character with each season, and locals often drive up to see the magnificent ice formations that form on the trees and rocks in the winter and spring, when Halla’s higher-elevation trails may be closed to hikers.? But it’s also a good choice for visitors who have limited time to climb, even when the higher trails are open, because it is possible to experience these incredible scenes at the 1100 Meter Road area.Not only is this a beautiful area, these days the 1100 Meter Highland is part of the Jeju Biosphere Reserve, a UNESCO and World Natural Heritage Site.A couple of points:? this attraction is actually located on Highway 1139, which will also take you past Eorimok, Yeongshil and Mysterious Road. You can drive or take an intercity-bus from either the Jeju City (north) or Jungman Resort area (south) side.? If you take a taxi, you should make a roundtrip reservation, allowing 1-2 hours there.? It’s a good idea to take at least a light jacket, even on a summer day, and for late fall to late spring, have a heavier coat, gloves and even a hat.? And don’t forget your shades and skin protection; even in winter, the sunlight can be strong on Hallasan.

But, don't be afraid of Gwaneumsa! Bus from there to Jeju is 1200W. A long and tiring day but definitely worth it.

review: My family and I spent about 45 minutes at this attraction on an early Monday afternoon, as our first stop of a Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliffs ? Jeongbang Waterfall ? Oedolgae ? Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary. It is designated a Natural Monument and is part of the Global Geopark Network. Getting there & fees: When I keyed in GPS code of 7351000 and 7381521, it brought us confusingly to the Convention Centre and the car park of the Seaes Resort respectively. Thanks to the helpful staff of the Seaes resort, we followed the advice and drove past the Convention Centre and then looked out for a signage that indicated taking a right turn to a road that leads to the destination. Once there, we parked the car in the car park which charged a parking fee pf 1000 won. The entrance fee is 2000 won for adults & 1000 won for teenagers (youth) and children, and we used one of the lockers for free to keep our stuff.The Cliffs/Attraction: After paying the entrance fees, we walked past figurines of dolphins and a huge rock surrounded by the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac. We then took the pathway of wooden platform steps that brought us to the bird-eye view of the beautiful blue sea and the rocky cliffs containing the awesome columnar joints that are typically at the base of the cliff. The platform only showcases a section of the 2 km stretch of these rocky cliffs. Along the platform, there is a display in English and Korean that educate you about the origin of the rocks. It would be good if another display would be able to pictorially illustrate the geography and formation. According to the information, the columnar joints were formed from the lava flows from the Nokhajiak scoria cone from 140,000 to 250,000 years ago. During cooling of the molten lava, contraction occurred and split the basaltic rocks into polygonal columns. We saw mainly tetragonal (4 sided), pentagonal (5-sided) and hexagonal (6-sided) columns. Because the origin of the columnar joints and rocks is volcanic, these are black. Throughout the time, I stood there simply awestruck by what I saw ? it?s like a divine being had creatively sculptured these columnar joints to perfection. And why only at this 2km stretch and not at other coastal areas in Jeju since the volcanic molten lava flowed everywhere?  It?s a pity the waves that crashed onto the joints and rocks were not huge; otherwise I think it would be an even more awesome sight. There are several pointers to take note:(1) You could appreciate this attraction in less than 1 hour (including photo and selfie-taking)(2) As the attraction is outdoors, be prepared for what the weather will throw at you. Carry an umbrella or wear a cap or sunglasses or put on sunscreen on a sunny day(3) To see these rocks better, I suggest bringing along a pair of binoculars or zooming closer using your camera telephoto lens or your handphone(4) Take plenty of photographs but do not climb over or lean over too much the platform ?railings?We ranked Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff as one of the top 3 attractions in Jeju. For sure, this Nature?s awesome masterpiece is not to be missed!

My family and I drove to this awesome natural attraction and walked along the layered rocks and cliffs produced as a result of a volcanic eruption on a beautiful non-windy and sunny morning. Safety concerns: Yeongmeori (Dragon's Head) Coast is opened from 8 am to 6:30 pm from May to September. It will be closed when the weather changes in a way that impacts people?s safety (e.g. high tidal waves, strong winds), so it is better to call to check before going. Also a rainy day means that the rocks and coast will become slippery and you may have problems taking photographs. in any case, you definitely need a good pair of walking shoes.2 walking trails: You have to take note that there are 2 trails and entrances to Yeongmeori Coast. Both trails meet each other but are not connected due to safety issue, which means you have to pay separate entrance fees. However, I saw a white bridge is presently being constructed that links the 2 trails, but it remains unclear as to when it will be opened. Between the 2 trails ? Trail 1 and Trail 2 (described below) ? I found Trail 2 to be  safer for walking and has more spectacular sandstone rock formations and cliffs, and because of that my family and I spent about 3 hours admiring the attraction and taking photographs.  Trail 1: This trail is where the tourists go, and starts after the Hamel Castaway Memorial and the Hamel vessel. You park your car (along with the tour coaches) at a car park that?s next to a mini theme park (with the Viking amongst others). You then walk along the seaside promenade next to sandstone layered rocks along the sea, which takes about 1.5 to 3 hours return after the ticket booth (1,000 won for adults & 500 won for teenagers & children). Since certain stretches of the promenade are narrow, you have to walk carefully so as not to fall into the sea and onto the rocks.Trail 2:  This is a shorter trail that in theory should only take about 30-60 minutes return after the ticket booth. You park your car just beneath the temple. Parking is free. Cross the road and look for 3 bronze circular structures with inscriptions of ?Jeju Island Geopark?, ?Global Geopark Networks? and ?New 7 Wonders of Nature? and a green signage ?Yongmeori Coast Entrance -> 300m? From there, you just walk down the steps and follow the path which will take you past several shops. After about 10 minutes? walk, you will reach a ticket booth. After buying the tickets (1,000 won for adults & 500 won for teenagers & children), turn left and you would come to the top of a narrow and steep passageway to the coast. Take your time to carefully choose the big rocks as your steps for your descent (and then I realised what the term ?stepping stone? means). There are no handrails. Once you reached the bottom after about 6 minutes (longer when there are many people), turn around and look up at the challenging and difficult passageway and appreciate your achievement! Looking across the sea, we saw Mount Hallasan. Instead of going left, I recommend you go to the right and once through a archway or hole in a rock wall, and you will soon encounter the spectacular irregular layered and wavy sandstone cliffs that often contain ?pot-holes?. The rock formation at certain places was carved out by  a blade that cut itself into the layered rocks, creating v-shaped clefts. And when the waves crashed into the rocks, it sounds like roaring thunder ? awesome!  There?s a short cement bridge where standing on it allows you to take a superb photograph of the rock formation and the narrow stretch of turquoise-coloured sea. It is also around this same spot that you can take another superb photograph of the cliffs with Mount Sanbangsan in the background. There were 2 ladies (I didn?t think they were the famed ?Haenyeo? sea-divers) at the shoreline with 3 basins of sea animals - sea snail (sora), sea squirt (myeonggye) and sea cucumber (haesam) ? who would be happy to enable you  to experience Korean culture of eating raw seafood by the shoreline. I didn?t like to eat raw seafood so I didn?t try.Overall, my family and I think that Yeongmeori Coast is one attraction in Jeju that ranks it as among the top 3 attractions in Jeju. Don?t miss it! It will blow your mind away!

My family (including 1 years old and 4 years old kid) visited this place. The experience is very good.If you plan to stay 2 nights at Seogwipo, i suggest you to arrange to go on the 1st day itself, cause the weather is very difficult to predict.Get the help of your hotel reception to 760-6321 and confirm the opening time (might close due to high tide or bad weather)Free parking space available. My 4 year old found the road very fascinating and he kept mentioning mysterious road throughout the day. It was probably just an average experience for adults but if you are travelling with the little ones, it may be worthwhile to spend some time to bring your kids to view this road.
Much to see, places to stop and   smell the roses.   Traffic a bit chaotic but go slow and expect everyone else to disregard the rules of the road AS WE KNOW THEM :) Be flexible and open-minded :)

Mountain HallasanIt was a fanatic walk ever, friendly people all around. Unfortunate in Jeju island, English is not a common language, road signs, information boards are all in Korean, mainly people speak Korean, surprisingly, you might find people speak Japanese and mandarin. There are a few entrances from around the Moutain, make sure you do your research.I believe there are more than 4 entrances. Due to limited time, I have chosen the easiest and fastest trail (Eorimok). You could take public transport or driving. There is parking 17mins walk, and payable parking 1000won, save your time. Be prepared below- Go toilet, do the necessity before you start - Go to visitor centre get a map and find out more. ( e.g. if the convenient store is open?) - 2-3 hours walk one way, the washroom only available in the destination. Choose the hiking shoes. (Bad experience, my sport shoes are ruined) - Best to start your journey at 8 or 9 in the morning, as early as you could. If you are doing other trails, allow more than 8 hours. Eorimok entrance, it took me 5hours, I took a slow walk. - Be warned after certain time (14:30, not certain), you may not be allowed to go in. - Bring a lot of water, or bring enough cash (drinkable water is not enough to supply to public), bring your own food if you don't want to end up eating spicy instant noodle.- Store only sell, instant noodle(super spicy), and spring water. (Limited to 2 portions of instant noodle per person) price: 1000won for instant noodle, 1000won for a bottle of water- Bring extra clothe to change, bring a light weight jacket. (It is a bit chilling on top)- Bring insects repellent spray or lotion- Bring wet tissue and normal tissue- Bring a bag for rubbish, smoking and littering are not allowed.The place is well protected, please respect :)  Voila! Happy Journey!
Maybe we travel in morning with foggy weather, the illusion of the slope of the road make it mysterious. Not very interested.

Marado Island is remote, largely barren, and is   nearly   empty. There is a small population of island residents. There is a small oddly shaped church, a Buddhist temple, and a lighthouse. As far as buildings go, there is little of interest. The primary feature of Marado is the rugged coastline, typical of Jeju-do. Doesn't sound that appealing? Yet, I did enjoy my visit here because it is nice to see a part of Jeju that is largely unaffected by tourism, small museums, resorts, golf, or honeymooners. The ferry does not depart too frequently. Once you arrive on Marado, you really can only do one thing, walk around the entire island, which only takes 2 hours. If the weather is nice (May-August), you should be able to get some pretty pictures of the rugged coast, bright green grass, and some of the lonely buildings on the island.Some of these small island communities are such a contrast to our (foreigners) perception of Korea, that a visit in itself helps creates a more broad image of the country. A worthy experience, that I would recommend if you have plenty of time on Jeju Island.

Many tours include this spot for tourists.  I personally find it over-rated.  It is an illusionary experience where the environs surrounding the particular stretch of road gives one the impression that it is not what it is supposed to be.  Some guides would even spill water on the road to experiment.  Interesting - yes, but I would not include it as part of a tour itinerary.

Manjanggul is a must see when in Jeju. It is easy to get (near) there from the main bus terminal in Jeju City, just take bus 701. It drops at the highway at the crossroad (there is an audible announcement in English on the bus as well as written on the screen) in about an hour's time, or just under. From there you can walk (under two KM) or take a cab (about 1000 Won per person). There is also a large parking lot if you have your own car or take a taxi.The entrance fee is 2000 Won and once you have your entrance ticket you follow the crowds of people down the steep set of stairs (be careful - it can be a bit slippery) and into the cave itself. The floor of the lava tube can be difficult for some (elderly, disabled, children) as it is rather uneven and tends to be rather wet. With proper shoes one should be able to navigate the 1 kilometer tube with no issues. It isn't very lighted inside so take care and watch your step.It's a pretty cool (in every sense of the word) experience and definitely looks very different from a   normal cave   in that it is one long tube with high ceilings and lacking the traditional stalagmites/stalactites.if you have a tendency to get chilly, do take a sweater or light jacket as the temperature inside is cooler than the outside, regardless of the time of year.

Manjanggul Cave came to me as a surprise. To walk in a lava tube is an enchanting experience. There are steep stairs and long walk so be prepared. Don't bring heavy bags. Wear jacket because its cold inside the cave. Bring good camera. As you enter the cave, you will see the limestone that looks like lava flow (see picture attached). The path is dim that completes the enchanting atmosphere. By the end of the road, you can see the lava column.

Lots of people, but it's expected.  Climb was not too bad but my wife did need a rest in the middle.  Provides great view on a clear day.  Take some pics of it when you are far away if you are driving.  There are places on the side of the road where you can park and take a few pictures of the entire thing.
Looks just like a normal road, except that due to the slant of the trees it appears like things are going uphill. A trick of the eye, and a cute experience.

Located in Seogwipo. What makes this waterfall unique compared to the rest of waterfalls in Asia is ? this one falls directly into the ocean. The view is very dramatic and I can guarantee that you will say 'wow' the moment you see it from the distance.This waterfall is 23 meter / 75 feet high. It was written in a legend that a holy dragon lived underneath it. Due to it, it was said that the water can cure disease and bring rain during drought season.It costs KRW 10,000 to enter this area, same price as Cheonjiyeon waterfall entrance fee. The comparison that I can make between these two waterfalls is ? Cheonjiyeon has beautiful landscape compared to Jeongbang. But Jeongbang has the dramatic factor compared to relaxing, calming Cheonjiyeon waterfall.You will go through a simple, quaint little path before you reach the waterfall gate entrance. No man made sculptures or attempt to make this road appear to be more touristy. However, the pink wild flowers blooms along this little path captures my heart. If you pay very close attention, you will see spider (s) hanging in the bushes alongside the road too. And if you not scared of it, you can check it out and test your macro skill with your camera. Remember : look but don't touch!Note: There are lots of spiders in Jeju Island. They are every where.I was unable to get too close to the falls because 1) it was cold windy day 2) I easily suffocate with water mist 3) I don't have water protection cover for my camera. So, if you plan to come here, please make sure to bring water proof camera protection if you really care of your expensive camera.Ah, one more thing ? shoes. Please wear sensible, flat, good grip kind of shoes / sport shoes.

Just like everyone already mentioned, the road is indeed mysterious as the car would really move uphill on its own. However, it is only a very short stretch of the road. But I would still recommend it if you are self-driving and it's your first time in Jeju. Definitely, something you have to experience.You can also head to the museums that is nearby too after going to this road.

Just another market but in a different city. Similar in most ways.However, a distinct difference here is the huge amount of Jeju oranges (tangerines) on sale. Not just here but in other markets in Jeju too.Also it is common to see roadside trucks & makeshift stalls selling oranges - everywhere.Jeju is well known for its oranges , probably it's the season now. But they aren't exactly cheap despite the abundance of supply.We went to a nice Tangerine Orchard Farm right here in Jeju, where we paid 5,000?? admission fee per pax. And one can eat as much oranges as you want for unlimited time while at the Orchard.After which, every pax is entitled to pick/bring back 1kg free. Great experience & deal.

Just an ordinary road but countless of tourist buses and vans parked along it. Explore the mystery personally to appreciate the magical side of it. We'd done all tricks - stopped the car engine and let it roll uphill, poured water on road and see the trail running upward, closed our eyes and walked both ways where we found the gravity is totally against us !! Great fun ~!
Just a short stretch of road where it   appears   to defy gravity. Kill the engine where the START signs indicate and feel the car moving uphill on its own.

Jeju-do best attraction, the Mysterious Road (Dokkaebi Road) or Goblin road as folk story say, it was the goblins who does the trick.. sound interesting. Young and old will find this place fun and mysterious. All you have to do is just stop your car at the designation point, on the double sign(emergency light), off the engine, release the hand brake and let the car move up the hill by itself, 'Yes.. roll up the hill'.The best is, this attraction is free of charge. Along the Mysterious Road, have a few food stall, try out the grilled black pork sausage and many delicious food. For those driving, key in the number 7126988 (yup.. heading to Loveland, you will reach Mysterious Road first), most people stop by here on the way to airport.

Jeju is know for horses and mandarins. I'd say, this is a must see for those who visit Jeju for the first time.Tickets can be bought online in Trazy.com. You should receive your e-tickets within 24hrs. Then exchange this at The Ma park's ticket booth. To get there, we took a taxi from Hyeojae Beach (costs KRW9,000). It's a must that you buy ticket in advance due to limited seats. A lot of private tour bus go here. Public transportation is very seldom in this area. If you can arrange a round trip transpo, please do so. As for us, we walked 2 KM to the main road. But again, the 1Hr show is worth seeing. =)

Jeju had a volcano that erupted long time ago, its lava flowed thru the Manjang cave leaving a lava tube that is about 4 kilometers long, The part open to public is about 1 kilometer with three entrances. Although lighted, it is still dark, wet and cold inside. Although it is an experience to go in, but be careful as it is wet and dark, the floor are not level, especially in the inner portion where there is almost no road. For the adventurous, bring along flashlight and wear rubber shoes. As for me, I just walk part of the way to feel it, as it's not worth the risk to go thru the whole cave. Again, it may help if there are better lighting showing important landmark within the cave like other caves in asia. Underground cave of Palawan, stalagtite cave in Halong Bay for example.
It's very near to Loveland. Interesting to see the car roll forward upslope. Start on the south, towards Jeju city. Length of the road is quite short, maybe 50m?

Its totally waste my time going up here, but its okey .... Just want to know how mysterious the road is, but for me the road it self is not going up, its only trick your eye .... The location, is only 50 meter road that has end sign and start sign, thats it nothing more.
it's only an eye perspective view. when we see the car slowly run up while the machine off, the road actually go down. Nothing special
Its just something like a less than 50 meter road with   strange   situation. Not worthed if you intentionally go there.

It's just a stadium with some architectural appeal but the shape tells a story  which is interesting. Try telling any football aficionado that it just a stadium and you will get howls of protest!From the 2002 FIFA World Cup it is designed around   the mouth of a volcano    and its roof in the shape of nets of traditional fishing boats in Jeju.So looking at it in that respect makes it more interesting.It was not open when we visited as of course there are no games here at the moment (although open during the summer months) so it was like looking into a fish bowl without the fish.Outside the stadium are many stone crafted 'dol hareubangs ' carved from porous basalt (volcanic rock).The statues' faces feature grinning expressions and bulging eyes without pupils  a long  broad nose  and slight smile and their hands rest on their bellies.These are quite common throughout Jeju and can be quite comic and a little suggestive!Have a peek here if in the area just to have at look at the stadium design and also the rock statues.Enjoy your visit!

It's just a road, but if you want to make it interesting, do some experiment on it. Get out of your vehicle, and try walking down/up the road. Or test the road by pouring water/ walk inversely. We enjoyed it!

It's definitely mysterious, that much I can say. You see vehicle after vehicle with their engines dead, and rolling UP the road. My guide tried to explain it's a trick of the eye, and that the road only appears to be going upwards when it's really otherwise. But no matter how I tried, I just don't see it. The road just goes upward to my eyes, and things simply go against the law of gravity here. It was really puzzling to see, and worth a tickle of one's brains.

It's basically an optical illusion, where it appears to be upslope, but it's actually going downhill. All the drivers there will switch off the engine an let the car run down the road by itself. It's only worth seeing if you so happen to pass by this road.

It's an optical illusion where the road appears to slopes downhill when in fact, it slopes uphill.  You will need to try it with a bottle on its side to understand.  It is impossible to describe but the experience will warrant it.
It's amazing how illusion can make an up slope looking road,in actual fact downward sloped. Try it out with a water bottle and watch it roll up hill!

It's amazing how enterprising the locals (or promoters of tourism) have been! Without spoiling for others, and if you are into 'problem solving' give it a go! Our coach drove pass the road and we were asked to solve the mystery!!! Bit of fun.

It's actually quite interesting as the road seems like an uphill slope but vehicles will move forward (slowly) without turning on their engine. It?s some sort of an optical illusion i suppose. But you can?t really see it from the side actually. It just.. seems like a normal road lolIf you are around the area, you can drop by to take a look.For full review: http://wanderer.summeree.com/travel/korea/jeju/the-mysterious-road/

It's actually just one short stretch of the road but interesting. The road gives you an impression that its going up hill instead it's actually going down the hill. The surrounding including the plants, trees, field and fencing are giving you that up hill impression. So when you switch off the vehicle engine that you are in, the vehicle will continue to move forward. Same goes to the test where they will show you by rolling a water bottle. Try walking backward and you can feel it. You might feel a bit disappointed as there is nothing else over there

It's a waterfall that goes directly to the see. Not many like that so you should visited it at least once. The road after the stairs was rocky, so you have to be careful. There's a woman diver, so there' s some people that ate her catch near the waterfall.

It's a hedge maze straight out of the movies, except with nothing popping up to scare you. It is only the hedge.  It takes about 20 minutes to find your way out and costs 3,300 for an adult. It's 500m down the road from Manjanggul cave, so if you're going to the cave you could stop by, but not worth the trip otherwise.

It's a 100m road whereby majority of the tourists are fascinated by this mysterious road. All the drivers will put it on neutral gear on the   starting point   and you find the car moving up but the road looks like incline. A short stop is given and you can have a good photo shoot over there. Most of the tour guide will tell you the truth behind this mysterious road and you will realise that    Things really cannot be judge by it's appearance.   Beside the Mysterious Road, there are a few stall selling some snacks. You must go to the first stall which is near to the ending point of the mysterious road, and try their strawberries. It's the most fresh strawberry i have ever seen and eat! It's a must to try.
It was very weired and interesting. If you are going there, try to turn off your car and test it if the road tricks you! You will be very surprised!

It was ur eyes who played trick! Discovered in the 70s, there are 4 such places in the whole of Jeju island. Your tour guide will reveal to you the   secret   of the road, so I won;t be here to soil your surprise. It's fun to try to walk backward (uphill) and fell more easier than downhill.

It was nice experience when suddenly u find these kinds of roads... Some kind of mysterious nature behaviour that able to control your vehicles to suddenly runs on its own...
