I took a nice picture here with my travel friends, used a large stone (its carved with korean words) as background... Interesting experience... ;)

It was my first hiking trip and I decided to take the Seongpanak trail (9.6km one way) so that I can reach the summit. The hike is long and steep at certain stages. Very rocky road and proper hiking shoe is strongly recommended. The hike starts from visitor center is at 750m. At 1500m, there's a Jindalrae shelter where you can take a break for hot instant noodle and refill your drinks. The hike is tough for me (someone who jog/cycle once or twice a week). Walking stick is my best friend to support me all the way. Reaching the submit at 1950m is breathtaking. You will see the beautiful Baengnokdam lake. On the way down, at 1324m we hike to see Saraoreum Lake too. The whole trail with break took me almost 10 hrs (9.15am till 7pm). It's seems to be an easy hike for the Koreans, including the elderly but to me is a lot of determination and perseverance. Will definately hike at the other trails if I have the chance to go back to Jeju. ** I saw deer **

It was like being in another world! The cave is enormous and there are interesting rock formations, along with information about them along the way. It's very cold (10-15C), which is a welcome break from the Jeju heat! But maybe bring a sweater. The only problem is that it's very hard to get to if you don't have a car. From the main road, only a special bus goes to the cave entrance, and it comes once an hour. There are no taxis in the area. It's a 20 minute walk with no buildings/trees to shelter from the heat. So keep this in mind when going, as you may want to arrange for a taxi beforehand.

It was great to see the vehicle moving while turned off. I recommend whoever visiting this place to read the scientific explanation to add a benefit to enjoyment. On the other hand, I was told that there are other mysterious roads in other countries that make the cars move faster and harder. If it is near to a place you're already going then I think you should have a look, it won't take much time.

It was a really wonderful experience to cycle around the island, although a little tiring. You can rent a motorcycle or trike as well. It is really busy and sometimes a little crowded on the roads. There are many restaurants and a few beaches. Excellent food to be had

It this is on the way to your other destination, then no harm dropping by. We just drove past by the road, then came down to take some picture. A 10 min pit stop. Nothing fanciful. Not a big deal to give this a miss.

It takes 15 min to get to Udo by ferry from Jeju, which schedule every 60 min.When you reach the island you have many shops that will offer you to rent small electric vehicles for 2 hours, it will be enough for browsing around all the beautiful circle road of the island. if you're planning to have lunch or some other activity, take 3 hours. 2 hours cost around 20,000 KRW for an electric scooter (1 person).Important Tip: 1. Take detailed pictures of the rental as they will sometimes try to blame you on some scratches they found when you return.2. Can't be miss is the   Rise Mango   100% that sell all over the Island.

It probably takes <1 min on this road as not much time is needed at this place. The vehicle will appear to be moving up slope when the engine is offed, should only visit when you are just nice passing by the area, purposely detour just to see this road is not needed to me.

It isn't very hard to locate this stretch of road, since you'll see numerous other tourists conducting their own experiments along the road, be it with the help of a rented vehicle, an empty beverage can, or simply water.Is the stretch of road as mysterious as it claims to be? It depends. If you're the kind of person who couldn't be bothered with science, optical illusions and whatnot, you'd be better off checking out the snack shops nearby, observing the other tourists and their interesting behavior, or skipping this place altogether.However, if you've always been interested in physics and seemingly unexplainable phenomenons which you know are actually explainable, give yourself an hour or more to thoroughly check this place out. Photography lovers may also deem this place worth their time.The bottom line? If you're heading to another tourist attraction (e.g. Hallasan) and it's on the way, and you have time to spare, feel free to check this place out. Otherwise, don't bother.

It is smaller than I expected. Basically, it is a long walking path under the ground and it is about 15-20 degree celcius. It leads you to see different kinds of lava formation. And lastly it brings you to the iconic lava stack. It takes about 40 minutes by walking under the tunnel (to and fro) to end your visit.I walked about 25 minutes from Bus station ( Manjanggul Entrance) to the cave. The bus doesn't get you directly to the cave, but only the main road connecting to the cave. Plug your ears to headphone and listen to some good musics while walking to the cave. Scenery on both sides of the road is good. :)
It is really a mysterious road!!! It is a upslope. However when u off engine, the car will move dwn by itself

It is only mildly interesting as part of a tour package which include this as a drive-through attraction.Plenty of cars & coaches stop & have their engines turned off to experience the   rolling uphill   mysterious effect.It is quite interesting to see how this phenomenon and the perception of the surrounding environment to the naked eyes has come so far to give birth to a tourist attraction. It could also double as a quick pit-stop to grab some snacks & skewers at the food store along the road.Hint: Get there, spend 5-10min walking one way forward, and then walking backward, or lay a half filled water bottle on the road, to crack this mystery.

It is just a vision trick. The road appears going up when it is really going down, so cars and buses can glide down when put in neutral. The way the trees at the side of the road is planted tricks your vision. Coming from Canada, we have seen it similar to the one in Moncton, New Brunswick.

It is indeed mysterious as to why this spot is named as mysterious road and promoted as such (there are road signs giving directions to the spot in the city).  I think the road is not steep enough so that when the car is put to neutral, it goes too slow to create an impressive illusion.

It is definitely an important piece of gem showing the massive power of lava flow.We were excited to see the marks on the wall, the tall lava column and the Stalactites in the forming.  However, I echo the other reviewers their caution:1. It is poorly lite to protect the rock formation.  Bring a torch so that you can appreciate the mark of the flow.2. Ground is uneven and slippery (worst than the cobble road of medieval towns).  Old people and children have to take care.3. It is cooler than ground level and there is water dropping from above.  Recommend to bring along water jacket with hood.4. Its a fairly long walk (exit point is same as entrance).  Total walking time is more than an hour if you want to see the lava column.If you are not big fan of rock formation, you can pass.
It is an interesting road and we had a car so we can do it a few times. I would say that if you are not going in that direction, there is no need to drive there specially for it.

It is a good experience to be there and see how mystery the road was. We were with our kind tour guide that gave us an experiment to test the road. Pour water and see where it flows, true enough it was a mystery (still need not to be solved).

It has always been something i try to do everytime i go for a holiday, is to go trekking in the mountains or forest. I went in late December and took a cab up to the start of yeongsil trail, and went down Eorimok trail. It was near a six hours journey, with a 20 mins lunch break. As i went during late december, the drive up the mountain area was really foggy and the visibility is only like 5 metres in front of us which is kinda scary because there were many windy roads. but as soon as we are nearing the trail, the fog seems to have been lifted due to the heights. Good info to know: Yeongsil trail have many flights of steps. Depending on what you prefer, manmade steps means relatively safe walkway but it is up most of the time.Eorimok trail has more stones steps and is more natural. But it could mean that it is more tedious, really depends on your preference.Lunch is ramen noodle at the shelter, they sell small snacks and drinks too. PS: As i went during the winter, the timing to enter certain trail is really strict because the sun sets really early like 5ish in the afternoon. So it is definitely a thing to take note of especially if you are not fast paced. Also during winter, along the trail, there will be snow left from the night before, and it IS really Slippery!! I nearly slipped many times because i was wearing a normal sneaker and not trekking shoe. And a really helpful thing to have is a walking stick! Other than that, enjoy your time with nature there!

Island best explored by driving, ATV or bike rental. Ferry across from mainland Jeju also carries vehicles. Road kinda narrow so one need to be careful, I blew a tyre when my right wheel rammed into a rock or kerb :-(  Lots of climbing if you really wanna explore in-depth. Many small eateries on the island. Very scenic island with lots of photo opportunity. Be wary of last ferry back or you would be stuck there overnight

Interesting road... My bus was shifted to neutral gear and went up th hill by itself....Had saw this before in Taiwan and china... It was actually an optical illusion .. Nonetheless quite amaze by it. Other than this generally speaking the attraction has no depth... Can go if visiting some other attraction in the area, but not worth it if travelling long distance for it .

Interesting experience  as we we pull to neutral gear, release the accerator, the car just go forward, upwards. The mysterious road is short, we made a few rounds. There is a car park where you turn in to go a few rounds if you wanted to. We tried the  same stretch to road after the end point. The car just go backward on the upward facing slope.

Initially, we were only planning on staying here for a few minutes to take some pictures because the reviews were so mediocre. We rented a car and drove to the entrance our GPS took us to (FYI if you rent a car and don't read Korean, make sure you get a GPS with it, Google maps/Apple maps/etc doesn't work in Korea, only Naver). I think it was some kind kind of back entrance, off the road, because no buses or anything were parked there. There wasn't even really a parking lot. When we walked through the village, to the other side, we saw the big parking lot and all the cheesy buildings and shops and stuff. But from the back side, it was just lots of nice little houses (some I think still had people living there) and pretty, walled-off yards. We were there in the morning and the are we were in had almost no one around, except for a few Chinese ladies who had decided to leave their tour and were having fun (we saw them rejoin with their tour later, so I didn't pull that out of thin air, lol). The main front entrance area is way more touristy and that's probably all people getting off the bus see, hence the bad reviews. If you keep walking through the whole town and take your time (if you can), it's actually pretty and peaceful. I think we spent a couple hours here.

Initially we had wanted to walk here from Seogwipo but gave up and took a taxi up the hill, the road was quite crowded with taxis and the car park filled with tour buses and cars. It is a very touristy place, there is ample reason. This is the place where Jewel of the Palace (Daejanggeum 鸚㏝룝) was filmed - one of the first Korean dramas popular all over asia. There is a cut-out of Janggeum where you can put your face and take a photo.More importantly, the scenery is lovely and dramatic. The rock column rises out of the beautiful blue sea. We left the path and tourists behind and walked around the rocks to the edge. We even came to a point where we could see Saeyeongyo Bridge in Seogwipo. We came across a blue rock thrush and a nice little coffee house before grabbing a cab on the main road. There is a bus running but we did not want to wait for it... it is about 6-8 min drive to seogwipo town

In April, the waters are not warm yet, so sitting here is quite beautiful and not crowded. A sense of both oceanic drive close by at the coastal road, a coffee deck behind and an almost cove like open white sand isolation which will probably disappear in peak summer

I'm sure this is a beautiful place when the flowers are in bloom but there weren't many when we went in late July.  There were still some hydrangeas and a few other flowers around but I think they could plant more varieties so that the park is pretty in different seasons.  The worst part though was the signage and map.  We got lost 3-4 times in one hour!  The map is mostly pictures without words in any language and it's hard to tell where you are.  The only way we figured it out was that there are a couple of   you are here   signs (in Korean).  They've put up some   This way please   signs but then there will be a fork in the road and there's not another   this way   sign.

If you've read my post about my 14 hours hike, you'd understand why I didn't go up this peak lol. Anyway, I strolled around the area and had dinner so it's still nice to watch the sceneries around it. If you're sick of Korean food, there's McDonald's, Starbucks and Dunkin' Donuts. Not to mention a fish and chips shop (on the two-way main road) , but I'm not sure if it's good. If you're not sick of Korean facial and body products shopping, Innisfree and Nature Republic are around there.
If you're a free and easy traveller, I'll totally not recommend you to travel to see this mysterious road. If you're on a tour bus, this is an interesting experience.

If you?re driving around Jeju Island, this place is a must. It took me a while to figure out what was the big deal (mysterious) about this road but after I figured out the way it was described to be, it was definitely cool and somewhat mysterious. So here it goes: you drive upto the starting point of mysterious road and put the car in neutral gear. The road certainly looks like and uphill, however the car drives forward until 100m to the end of the mysterious road. Anti-gravity huh? I?m not sure of the scientific explanation for this phenomenon, but I recommend you experience this if you?re driving around Jeju Island. Takes only 15 minutes and certainly worth the time and experience!
If you never get the chance to come to Jeju and experience the road for yourself, at least You Tube it! This was completely crazy to see. Everything in the videos is real in case you were wondering!

If you have some time to spare, it is recommended to check out this place. However if you are in a really short trip, IMO i dont think its worth to drive here as its just a road, unless you are on your way to love land.

If you book a car to travel around, probably you can consider to drive pass this mysterious road which took less than 20min when you're on the way to other attraction. This mysterious road is quite interesting, it is about rolling up this   Down slope  .  You can try it, just by asking the driver to off the engine of your car, and let it roll freely. I also tested it out with my water bottle, it was quite funny, the bottle actually roll up. At first, i thought this was due to law of gravity, but i realize is just optical illusion caused by the surrounding that cause this illusion of   down looking slope  . Fun place with interesting facts.
If you are in jeju island of course you have to go there. A great ride, with some mysterious road,..may be some ghost... Up there get a jacket it s could be cold....

If you are expecting something out of the ordinary, this case just isn't for you. No, there isn't any sign of life (bats) in it. It's just a natural cave formed, with tracks at it's natural state. Dark ambience, only with some help provided through man-made lights. But don't worry, the road before you is still visible.

If you are driving, I recommend you visit Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak first at around 7am to catch the sunrise at around 8:00am something.For me it's better seeing the Seongsan Ilchulbong in a far away place rather than hiking it for 30mins. So before reaching the gps route you would notice a lot of cars parked at the road side. Stop for a while and from there you would see a crowd of people waiting for the sunrise at the seashore and infront is the mountain touching the sun.If you like, you can still proceed with the peak 1km away from the stopover and hike a bit at the stairs to see the peak.After that a few kms away is the Seongsan Port going to Udo Island.Gps to Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak 710-7923Gps to Seongsan Port 7825671Upon reaching Udo island in a 15min ferry ride for 5500won, you can either walk, cycle or rent a scooter. You need an international drivers license to rent a scooter for 25000won for 2 hours, which i think is really short. Circling the whole island with a bit of stop over would already take you 2 hours. Not much to see in the island, a bit of flowery patches, mermaid statues and lighthouse and that's it.
If you are a hello kitty fans, this is a must-visit-place in jeju, accessible by public transport, is along a main road. You get to experience colouring, 3D short movie clips.
If you are a car enthusiast, this is a great place to visit. They have a broad range of cars and an area where kids can drive a car around a track.
address: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관

review: I would say that this waterfall is higher and have better view than cheonjaeyeon waterfall althought cheonjaeyeon waterfall is close by from teddy bear museum, we take taxi in the afternoon from teddy bear museum to jeongbang waterfall and it cost around 25-30 usd, and the street is almost empty. The road down to the waterfall is much nearer and easier than cheonjaeyeon waterfall. When you take pictures, off course you would like to get closer to the waterfall, but be carefull of the rocks, they were quite slippery, we spend an hour to take pictures and sitting in the rock. The admission fee on nov 2014 is still 2,000 won per adult about $2. On winter it opens from 08.00 to 18.00
I wondering how their built the road and the environment to make it so mysterious! The taxi driver stopped the engine for us to feel the different, it was amazing!

I went on a tour group to Jeju. The bus arrived at the Mysterious Road, all of us were waiting eagerly in anticipation of what's about to come (after hearing so much hype about it). Looking out the window, I saw a little kid on the street place a plastic bottle on the tarmac, and it looked like it was rolling up hill at first, but because of the way the bus was angled along the road, I was quick to discern that it was a mere optical illusion.As our bus reached the front of the 'queue', our driver switched off the engine, and slowly, but surely, our bus picked up speed. It was interesting as it was the first time I sat in a vehicle with it's engine switched off, THAT WAS IT. I looked out the front panel, and we were obviously going downhill, as I could not even see the sky (just trees whizzing by our bus).I'm guessing it only looks like you're going uphill from certain angles. Thankfully, we didn't spend too much time there, and off we went to our next destination!
I was very excited to see that road, but when you are in the car the feeling is not as obvious as you may imagine. Worth visiting but nothing spectacular

I was traveling solo via public transportation, I arrived there 30 mins early before it opened for public that day. For it's 1st month of Spring (April), most of natural attractions were free admission. Good thing it was free, though I appreciate it, it's not really astounding as I though (well, as per my perspective).From downtown of Jeju, take bus 701 (East Route). You can ask your hotel reception of the bus stop. It would be easier if you have private car (especially for group traveler). Alight at Manjanggul Entrance, walk about 25mins, you'll pass by Gimnyeong Maze Park (roughly 15mins walk from bus stop). Not for a person who's kinda frightened to walk alone in a road of unknown :) You can wait for bus 990 the only bus that passes through Manjanggul Cave yet it isn't frequent.Just follow your path way back, if you're lucky enough, a taxi would offer you a ride for a certain price roughly KW3,000. You can negotiate the cost. In my case, I negotiated for KW2,000 which I think is reasonable enough. Yet when I'm about to pay, I only have KW50,000, the driver doesn't have any loose change, so he asked only KW1,000, I still have none, instead he just took the last coins I have, KW700.

I was here with my family. Thinking what is so mysterious about this road? Its just a road, with nature on the sides. It?s just another ?normal? road. Sigh, a total waste of time.Until I reach the place, I was blown away! Not because of the strong wind (I was there when it was raining heavily with strong winds), but the mysterious part of this road. I was told to stay in the car, to witness the mystery of this road. The engine got turned off, hand brake was let gone, brakes were let gone too, the car automatically went up the slope by itself!It is a new experience here for me in Jeju, a totally worth of time to visit!

I walked Routes 6 and 7 on 23rd-24th Oct 2017. The distance was 15km and 18km respectively.The weather was perfect - sunshine and cool breezes. These 2 routes are reputed to be the more beautiful ones. There are a couple of picture-perfect waterfalls and breath-taking shorelines along the way. 2,000Won per entry is charged for the waterfall. Along the way are small fishing ports where one can get to taste local seafood. There are small cafe along the way too, where one can sit, relax and taking in the beautiful scenery. Coffee is +/-4,000won. As I was staying at the starting point, from the finishing point I took taxi back It costs about 8kWon. Oh yes, there are clean restrooms every 5km or so. Just a little minus point, the blue & red ribbon is not easy to be found in urban area. So try looking for the blue line on the tar road.

I visited here with my family, so we drived our rental car. But if you don't have an international license, then rent a bike or motorcycle.You can rent it in a reasonable price.There are 5 bus stations here and those are nice sights.There is a beach in two sights and one of them is a popular site for jet boat.And the other one is popular for water leports.And whole Island is a heaven for riders.If you love mountian bike or road bike, then take your bike to this island.This is a perfect place for cycling.And there are many nice restaurant and dessert cafe, so enjoy yourself here.

I thought it was a long winding road but the distance is short an it gave optical illusion of our bus going uphill. Well when you got down the bus to see yourself, it makes no differences. Just a road filled with curious people.

I studied the seoqwipo bus route and decided to bring my family for a day trip to Udo Island. I stayed in Jungmun Resort vicinity. It was easy to catch bus 282 from here and made a transfer for direct bus to Udo Passenger Terminal. Upon arrival, after filling up the necessary details and proof of passports竊we went to the cruise Departure point. Luckily we chosen a weekday for this trip. The queue was short. In the cruise ship, we could find seats. A 15 min ride and we were greeted by several e-scooters and shop houses. Here, you could settle for lunch. But if it was too early for you, several sightseeing spots come with line of restaurants. We took the circular bus (white color van) which we thought was the best choice. Every stop you were  required to queue to abroad. This bus went to most attractions including black sand & Udo lighthouse. The bus route was also the route for E-scooters /car. Do be careful for safety sake. Returning from Udo Island was amazing : we could not find a bus stop that for the same bus number  supposed to bring us back to Seoqwipo! Nevertheless, luckily we had alternative plan ! we took a bus that brought us to Gimpo Airport. Got a decent dinner and then took limo bus 600 directly to our accomodation, alighting at bus stop named Jungmun Resort Entrance. This DIY by public transport comes in cheap!This trip you need a whole day.

I still enjoyed checking out the bear museum but I must say that the entrance fee is too much and unreasonable considering the bear museum is not that big.You can visit this place in less than 30 minutes because nothing much to see, they have small collection.This is just across the road from Ripleys Believe it or Not Museum. You better skip bear museum and just spend more time in Ripleys as it is more collection of interesting items and reasonable entrance price.

I specifically spend half a day here during my trip at Jeju and has no regret. We rented a electric scooter with KRW30k for 2 hrs, do note that you need International Driving License to rent it. We had burger at HahaHoho cafe and the Pork burger is delicious. The landscape and view is so pretty. The road is narrow so I don't recommend you to drive rented car there. Udo island trip is definitely one of the highlight of our trip to Jeju!

I saw the review and decided to give it a try if I ever manage to find this location from the Korea GPS (we rent a car).Lucky enough we discover this road when we were heading to Love Lands. It's just right after it! So we drove to the starting point and off the engine and yes, it is moving! (Even the road is up hill a bit).Then we park the car aside and walk towards Love Land, but we saw many people were trying to walk in a backward manner up the road (which you suppose to feel hard/difficult bcos it is up hill), and backward manner down the road (which then strangely you felt like something is pulling you back even you are walking down hill) So I would say this is a very good experience and I'm glad that I experience this! But my friend didn't really feels anything when she tried the walk, so I guess it also depends on individual's physical sensitivity towards this mysterious road...

I really loved this waterfall. Just the way you can chill on the rocks and look out to the ocean or the waterfall itself. You can also get close to it also which is nice (unlike Cheonjiyeon Waterfall which in my opinion pales in comparison). It costs 2,000 KRW to get in and my advice is set aside a few hours to just chill. It's really wonderful. There is also wifi so you can video call your mates and show them how much their lives suck compared to yours. I got the 781 bus from Jeju bus terminal (3,000 KRW and 50 mins) and got off just as you get into Seogwipo (best use an offline map with gps). I wandered towards it and it's actually not that easy to find. The waterfall is on the west side but you want to get to the east side to view it. If you can't find it, there's a Buddhist arch/gate thing you can see from the main road. This marks the correct path and takes you in front of Seobok temple (Seobok temple should now be on your right and some well kept walled gardens on your left). Keep walking and you'll see the entrance. Note: as you walk on this path you'll be on a bridge at some point. If you carefully tread over the side garden you can look over the wall and see the top of the waterfall, it's not that spectacular but might as well grab a look.

I read many negative review about this place from other travellers but for me, it was quite an interesting place with strange phenomena going on. My taxi driver brought me here on the way to Seongsan and he show me what is so mysterious about this road and it was indeed very strange. He stop the car at one end of the road and the car will automatically move up towards the slope (even when the car engine is not on). It was just an experience and one will not spend more than 10 minutes here. A good short trip before going to other places.

I have quite mixed feelings about the NANTA show, but the criticism is not with the show itself but with the overall experience. This review is for the show in Jeju-do.Positives:It was very easy to book tickets on line even from abroad. Once you create an account and log in, you are able to see ticket availability, choose your seats and pay for them. An online confirmation serves as your ticket until you turn up at the theatre on the day and get physical tickets. They send you a reminder via email before the show, and you can cancel up to a day before the show.The show is very funny and our whole family laughed a lot.My dad commented that the seats are more comfortable than the theatre seats in London.There is a parking lot if you are driving in.Negatives:The location in Jeju-si means that if you are staying in Seogwipo-si (as we were) then it takes over an hour to get to the theatre. And over an hour to get back home to your hotel after that.The show is catered to tourists as it doesn't use any Korean language to communicate its humour. As such, you will be surrounded by people who talk throughout the show. There's nothing you can do about this, they are really having a fun time, but you need to be aware about it. Or you can just join in and make loud comments too.There are no catering facilities at the venue so if you are driving in you need to think about where you are eating before or after the show. Fortunately just opposite the car park, across the road, there is a row of restaurants - just pick the one that you like.The toilets were filthy on the day we visited, and this was even before the show started. Since we were there for the early session at 5pm, I just don't know how the toilets can be be in such a disgusting state, unless they were not cleaned from the night before.Finally:If you are visiting Seoul, you can watch the NANTA show there too at several locations in the city. That might be a better option if you are not staying in Jeju-si itself, as the driving was just too tiring from Seogwipo-si.

I have just come back from Udo and i am happy i decided to go there.originaly it was  not in my plan. Based in Jeju-si I took bus710 (3300짜) to Seogsan port,1h20min drive. Then ferry (return ticket 5500짜) 20min. I rent bicycle (8000짜/3hours) and start Udo tour around the cost. It is 18km around island so if you are in hurry it is possible to make it much faster 1.5h enough. I also made a couple of detours inside island to see how people live. Everything is small and cute there:roads,houses,fields,fences made of stones.I recommend to climb Udo hill -nice view from there and climb is easy. It was sunny day and i get sunburned so please do not forget sunblock cream. It is windy island and one doesn't  feel is being sunburned.

I had read some reviews that it was damp and dark and not worth a visit. So, I went with little expectation. When I stepped into the cave, I was amazed! It was definitely a place for people who love nature! As I walked through the tunnel, I tried to imagine the hot volcanic larva flowing through larva tube, leaving these marks and traces. I would highly recommend the place to people who really love the wonders of nature. Yes, the place was damp, with water dripping from the ceiling and very uneven floors and puddles of water everywhere.I still find it worth the 2.5km walk from the bus stop at the main road. To get there, we took bus 701 and got off at the Manjanggul Cave Bus Stop. Bus 990 could take us right to the entrance but the bus was so irregular. We had just missed one. Therefore we decided to walk in. It was an okay walk.

I had high hopes for this spot, but it is hard to recommend it.  What was once a pretty island is now circled by identical seafood restaurants, cafes, burger joints and other tourist shops.   Biking a loop around the island is nice enough, but the road is jammed with little electric   rickshaw   things and noisy scooters.  Honestly, this place would be a perfect case study of bad development for a tourism management class.

I found much of Jeju island to be very commercialized and crowded with loud tour groups. This is a great place to enjoy the natural beaty of Jeju with smaller groups of people. There is a small entrance fee.  The first half mile is along a wide crushed rock road. It is lined with young   nutmeg   trees. The trees are in the yew family. They are Torreya nucifera and are native to Japan. I  visited in October when the small edible nuts ripen. The nuts are encased in a thin husk that has a wonderful aroma. You will see people collecting them under the large trees.  Eventually the road ends and then you follow a loop trail that is about 2 feet wide it is covered with a hemp rope mat that felt lovely to walk on with bare feet.  The crowds end at the beginning of the narrow trail so you can walk through this section in peace and really marvel at the enchanting colors and smells of the forest and hear the songs of the many birds.  There were signs to watch for snakes but I saw none. The yews are huge.  Make sure to investigate the tree bark it is fabric like and soft. Also many of the other plants have English name labels which is nice. The trail is flat and should take a leisurely couple of hours or less if you rush.  I noticed a lot of people sitting on benches in the first section enjoying picnic lunches.

I found it well boring to be honest. I prefer stuff like the lava caves and waterfalls - I guess I just like to be wowed. However it was a peaceful place and it was surrounded by lovely countryside. Maybe a place for a stroll with your loved one. Still if you want to get there from Jeju - you can get a bus 710-1 from the bus terminal. Note there are two 710's (assume the other one is 710-2).  It costs about 3,000 KRW (40 minute ride) and there is a designated stop about 3 or 4 stops after Gyorae Entrance (not junction which is 2 stops away). Note: Gyorae Entrance is a good stop to know about as it on the north - south road (Jeju-seogwipo) which is the 781/782 bus route.... just in case you want to go anywhere else after or get bored like me :)How helpful am I!

I flow to Jeju just to walk up this mountain.  You have to apply to the  Hallasan National Park visitor management system for the QR code admission ticket. My ticket was for the Gwaneumsa Course, time slot 5-30am - 8-00am.   I started my walk at 7-50am,  It was perfect walking weather, overcased so not too warm.  There is a 500 hiker per day limit on this route to the top, on the other easier route there is a 1000 hiker per day limit. The first few kms is easy going and you think to yourself this walk is going to be a piece of cake.  After around 4 kms you reach the first of two public toilets on the route.  From there the walk becomes a uphill slot with countless wooden steps. On the way up there is two downhill's with maybe a couple of hundred steps to walk down before walking uphill again.  After the second public W.C.  the route is a never ending series of wooden staircases until at last it flattens  out and the top of the mountain.  When I did it there was maybe a hundred or more walkers queuing to get a photo next to the summit stone.    I just gave my phone to a person and asked them to take a photo with the stone in the background. Within minutes I was on my way back down.The reason why you need a photo with you and the summit stone (even if it over your shoulder in the distance) is to claim your Certificate of climbing Mt, Hallasan. On the Gwaneumsa Course you can self print your certificate at a booth just past the QR-cord booth at the trail head  If like me you are clueless with mobile phones you can go the manned QR code booth and them to do it for you.  There have a printer in the booth and was very happy to do it for me.   It costs 1000 won (around 1 us$) Facts and figures, I am a 73 year old Englishman on an extended holiday in Korea.  Start time 7-50am, summited at 11-05am.   Started down at 11-15 and back to the trailhead at 12-55pm. Yes I do class myself as a bit of a mountain walker so these times  are maybe a little faster then average, but mountain walking is about enjoying yourselves and not about how fast you can get up and down. I took a litre of liquid, in hindsight I should have taken more and I did finish it off when I was within sight of the carpark. There is a shop across the road from the carpark.   Food, I took no food just a few sweets and a couple of chocolate bars.  So the bottom line is you have to take all the food and drink with you.  It does say that you can get drinking water at the second WC (shelter) but I could not find any so don't depend on it. Getting back to Jeju City.   There was no buses so I started walking the 8 miles back to my hotel on the seafront. Pleased to say that  I did manage to flag down a taxi after around a mile.  All in all a very enjoyable day out on the mountain.

I first saw this falls on the local map I received. I investigated and stopped there using the airport limousine bus route no 600. I completed every single course over a period of a year so the following comments are just my opinions. If you are staying for a short period of time in Jeju courses 6 and 7 are the most popular and will probably get the most from. Both are very scenic and you will get to see some of the major sights. If you start at one of the information sites, you can pick up a Jeju Olle guide which has maps and information of the trails, guides for the Buses, to get to and from the starting points. Also I'd recommend downloading Kakao Maps app on your phone and you can zoom in and see the actual trail that you are following when you are on it. It comes in handy especially for me when I made a wrong turn on my trips. If your doing the entire course I'd recommend buying a jeju Olle Passport. Carry it with you and get it stamped at the starting points and halfway way points of the trails. I was living near jeju city and caught most of Buses from the Jeju inter city bus centre. The 101/201 express buses will take you to/ or near a lot of the starting points but I'd recommend picking up the Olle Guide first and the info in that is invaluable.Most of the Starting points are close to the roads unless you are going to one of the 3 islands. I used booking.com most of the time to book places to stay overnight as I don't speak Korean. Jeju has a lot of places to stay and there would be abundant places to stay except for maybe a couple of the more remote locations on the trail. There are offical Olle trail Hostels throughout the trails to which are very nice. If planning for no Korean speakers just check before hand that you are not traveling on a Jeju holiday as a lot of paces close down and might be harder to find a place to stay. Of course take plenty of water and there's usually 7/11 of CV's around the place where you can get snacks to eat.The trails themselves are very beautiful , Different scenes ranging from Black volcanic rock on the coastlines, Forest trails, Beautiful beaches, Hill sides, a lot of Oreums (Jeju extinct volcanoes) small towns with a chance to see wildlife and a lot of friendly people. For myself my favourite trails were routes 11, 18-1 Chuja-Do island), 1-1 (Udo island), 7. For me the stronger trails were on the southern eastern point of the island starting from route 6 through to 15.Getting to the supporting islands it you might take note you will need your Passport to catch the ferry to Udo. You must show it when buying a ticket. There are a lot of ferries going most of the day to Udo. They have a very nice Peanut ice cream there. The smaller island Gapado at the time I went there were only 2 ferries in the day and its not the most reliable service and the ferries can be cancelled due to bad weather can be cancelled due to bad weather so check beforehand if you can. Chuja-Do island was one of my favourites. When I done it they had 2 ferries a day and you can not do the whole trail in time to catch the next ferry back so be prepared to stay over night. I have heard of instances when the weather turned bad and people had to stay a couple of nights on the island because the ferries were cancelled so just plan for that just in case. it is a beautiful Island though and one of my favourites.I would also recommend going and joining the Olle Walkers Facebook group. They take guided walks along certain courses and have great information about weather and so forth. all you need to do is contribute to the group from time to time.

I chanced upon this wonderful beach along Ilchul-ro Road while my family and I were on our way to Breeze Bay Hotel. I returned to the beach in the late afternoon and my family and I went to the same spot again the next day early afternoon. On both occasions, I parked our car at a car park that’s got just a few cars. Gwangchigi Beach is very long and the spot that I was at was near to a erected stone put up by the Rotary International. The good part was that there were very few people on this secluded beach. The better part was that Gwangchigi Beach is a black sand beach (yes, we finally experienced a black sand beach). The best part was the beach offers a marvellous view of the south-western face of Seongsan Ilchulbong. Using a pair of binoculars or a telephoto camera lens, you could see visitors climbing the stairways as well as the summit of Seongsan Ilchulbong.Moreover, walk along the beach and you will find unusual rocks and rock terrain just beyond the black sand. I believe the rocks arose from the explosion of an underwater volcano long time again that created the Seongsan Ilchulbong. During the late afternoon or sunset, the sunlight produced a beautiful array of black, brown, orange and green (algae-covered) colours of these rocks. Because late afternoon is where low tide occurs, the sea water was trapped within the rocks as ‘ponds’ ? and there were beautiful reflections of Seongsan Ilchulbong on the still water. Alternatively, you could walk on the rough brown ‘mat’ (not sure what’s the material) that was laid on the grass. It was along this mat path that I saw a horse that was tied to a pole. I guessed the horse was used for horse-riding but I didn’t see such activity as it was already past 5 o’clock in the afternoon.Gwangchigi Beach is one beach in Jeju that is under-rated and not well known. It warrants being among the top 10 beaches in Jeju. Anyway, I recommend visiting it as part of the Seongsan Ilchulbong experience.

It took us 3-4 hours to round the island due to time for camera and lunch.  Back to the electrical bike, which could power to assist you, but battery did not last long, it usually fails in the last up slope (the last check point with a cave and cliff) - and it is tough for rider to move uphill without gear.  So I suggest you rent a normal bike, it is cheaper, more reliable, and rider can wear hat but not the heavy helmet.  I will say if you want to visit Udo, visit in low season, not summer, which is really crowded and extremely hot - no tree, no shelter along the road.

For such a long bus ride and such great reviews, I was hoping for much more. We stayed on the Southwestern side of the island and took the nearly two hour bus trip to see this amazing cave that was rated near the top on TripAdvisor. However, we were sorely disappointed. If you've never been to a cave before, you should go. It's a unique type of cave, which is why I gave it a 3-point rating, but there is nothing that draws the attention. In most caves, there is at least one aspect that management (or whoever it is) chooses to make important, such as a really long stalactite that has a cool creation fact...but this cave had none of that. I think they only had around 3 or 4 sets of very cool lighting, illuminating barely anything. In a cave, lighting techniques are your best friends. The entire trek was actually incredibly dark, making viewing anything difficult. (I know that sounds funny if you've never been to a cave before, but those that have know that certain lighting highlights unique aspects but if there is minimal lighting, even walking is annoyingly difficult.) Finally, at the end of the cold, long trek through floors that you have to pay more attention to than the walls, we came to a column of something that almost reached the ceiling and could have been the highlight of the cave trip. The management simply didn't choose to beef this thing up. The lighting on the end piece was regular. There was no sign explaining what is was or how it came to be. It was simply the end of the road. And guess where the exit is? You have to walk back the exact way you came. So, we were bored twice. In short, I gave a 3 out of kindness for its unique type. The cave has potential. I simply wish whoever is in charge would utilize what they have to the fullest.

The mayor was jailed a few days ago for chaining himself around the neck to a rafter, when police rampaged and tore down protesters' headquarters, replacing it with boulders to prevent reconstruction. The protesters are very friendly, by the way. It's on the Ollie hiking trail, where it crosses over the Gangjeong River and passes the gates of the   destruction   site. Driving from the city to the Seongpanak trail is the most convenient way to do it, it's only 20 minutes away from the busy area of Jeju.I hiked the mountain at early morning January 01 and when i reached the Seongpanak trail the parking was crazy long that it goes as far as 1km from the side of the road. If you want to save time in walking you should be at the trail around 3am at Jan01. Anyway, the trail was relatively easy on the first 7km, it was cold around -1 to 5C that time, still manageable but the trail was slippery due to ice forming on rocks and the trail was covered with snow. So, to prevent accidents wear a mini crampons or a Yaktrak coil underneath your shoes.Don't worry hiking alone, you can do this without a guide, you probably are blind if you get lost out there. Also, the trail was properly maintained that hiking at the peak was a breeze except the last 2km of the hike. When you reached the final kilometers it starts to get steep, so take your time and avoid slippery rocks and you should be fine. Finally, the peak was amazing, you would be able to see sea of clouds if the weather permits. Overall not bad for a hike.

Drive yourself to the 100m stretch of road. When see the   start   marker, put your gear to neutral and you will notice that the car is moving forward even as you are going uphill without engaging any gear. Pretty interesting short experience.

Don't make a special trip to see this place,  Only interesting if you pass by.  I mean, it's only a piece of road where you turn off the engine on the incline and watch the car roll for a few yards.  We've got more interesting mystery spot in Santa Cruz, Calif.

Wear layers as it gets cool up high.  First part is through bush trail, we had a roe deer come across 10 m. away.  Then trails steepens to get to ridgeline, a little tough.  Nice views and steps on the ridge, then another transition to a boardwalk through a tundra like alpine area. Disclaimer: Everyone has their own tastes, and just because I may not like something, it doesn't mean you won't like it. And even though I might be dismissive and even sarcastic about this attraction, I am not attempting to insult anyone who thought that Jeju's   Mysterious Road   was fun. The fact is, this road would be amazing IF it wasn't swarming with tourists and IF you just happened to find it one day when you were driving around on the stunning back roads of Jeju. Jeju has Korea's best scenic driving, hands down. But this...Here's the deal. Yes, your brain will lie to you about the incline of this road and it will appear as if you are not rolling downhill, which you are. And that's a fun fact about human neurology and perception. My brain also tried to lie to me in order to convince me that the illusion was worth the large, obnoxious crowds of people that clogged the road, the busloads of hyperactive tourists on a conveyor belt from the airport, and the shops set up on either side of the road in order to overcharge them for very average products. Basically, it's a tourist trap. Sure, it has its appeal, but of all the things you could do on Jeju, why would you spend your time doing this?
Definitely a tourist trap, not a lot to do here. The illusion of the car rolling uphill isn't that big of a deal. Plenty of other pretty roads to drive along that are worth more of your time.

Curious a lot but not much time belong the legend story about this road is looking down n the cover of seems getting up by tree for side of this road. We tried to engine off and its moving forward, nice its like magic.

Climbing Mt Hallasan was absolutely amazing, and I would recommend anyone going to Jeju to attempt a climb. If you?re a bit unsure, make sure to research the trails before-hand and start walking in the morning ? many trails close at 2-3pm.Bring lots of water and snacks (although in typical Korean fashion, there is a 'restaurant' at the 'top', where all the lower trails intersect. Do your research, take a car or taxi to the start of the trail (buses will drop you off much further down the mountain, and you'll have to spend time and energy walking up along a road before you can even start the trail). The views must usually be stunning, but on the day we went, it was covered in cloud/fog. Even so, I would 100% recommend it and I would definitely go again if I went back to Jeju.

Climb was ok, first smooth hill roads, then mainly steps to the top. View wemhile climbing was nice. We did not manage to catch the sunrise due to cloudy skies. However, the view of jeju from pre dawn to dawn while climbing up was worth it. U literally see the city lights up before ur eyes.

Chilshimni Poetry Park is part of Jeju Olle Route 6 that was easy to located as it was along the main road, Namseongjung-ro road where Park sunshine hotel or Poong Gyung Hotel were. It was a free general park with playground where the locals hang out and it can be finish in 30 minutes for less. However, the highlight of the park was the ability to have a clear view Cheonjiyeon waterfalls from a height for free! We spent some time chilling at the table and benches to appreciate the falls. There was also a stairway down to Saeyeongyo bridge. As the park was part of Jeju Olle Route 6, we went out to the main road, Namseongjung-ro road, and followed the orange/blue ribbons to Oedolgae. I have rated this park a 4 stars for the beautiful view of the Cheonjiyeon waterfalls.

Cheonjeyeon Falls are very near to the Booyoung hotel and the ICC (International Convention Center), an easy 5 minutes walk takes you to the bottom of a very steep flight of wooden steps. If you chance to go up there (no English signs, and as far as I could judge, they do not mention the fall even in Korean) you will find the falls, only to climb down - and then up again. I found it very exhaustive. The falls had very little water, so were somewhat disappointing. Optical illusion is what it is.

C1 ( 2016.07.14 ) This park was larger than I think. There was consist of several area, and had various theme. I saw many plants, animals, folk village, cave, etc in this park. I felt good in walking road with various ecology system. All was good to me, but reptile in small transparent box was pitiful. If had time, I want to feel natural feelings in this park keeping my composure. Excellent place to enjoy reserve.

C1 ( 2016.07.14 ) This columnar joint was located in South Jeju, and had beautiful sight. This place was good to enjoy view made by wave and sight and sound made by wave and cliff. I didn't expect this area, but there was excellent, And had walking road was good with exotic atmosphere. Very beatutiful place to me.

But too overcrowded by visitors even at September! :)Possible to rent bicycle or scooter (electric or usual) or quadro-unit and make your trip around the island (but you need actual international driver license with correct category!).It's big enough for walkers.Very small and narrow road all around island - be very, very, very careful as main part of drivers are young people with very little experience of driving and winds in their heads (sorry, but true!) :)

Bring your swimming gear along, it has a sea swimming pool during low tides, basically daytime. Seeing ppl drives and swimming. There is life-jacket rental available for snorkelling. No entrance ticket required. But the carpark attendance charged us W2K which seem only W1K per hour. No proper carpark control. See ppl park along road side.

Bring your own food or you can buy from the cafe nearby and sit by the stairs watching the locals fishing or enjoying the sea breeze. Beautiful red and white horse light-houses that stood out from far. We took a cab there and for return trip, just walked 5~10mins to grab a cab from the main road.

Bet ya you have never seen this before! Its real touristy but well worth the walk. From the convention centre on the east side the first road down to the sea. You can't miss the busses. Taking pictures is best in the morning because of the sun. We went at 16:00 and the sun made it impossible to take good pictures. Got a crappy camera so that could also have something to do with it. Another tip is to follow the olle trail to the east from here after about a 1,5 hour walk (through beautifull orange plantations and up and down tracks paved / dirt) you'll get to the Yakcheonsa Temple. Get from there to the 600 airportbus back to where you came from.

Before you want to take a ferry to Udo island, please take note that you need to bring along your passport to purchase a ticket. You will be given 2 tickets, 1 for departure & 1 for arrival (you have to keep this and pass to the boatman at Udo when you want to return to main island). A tip is to get the korean map together with your language?s map because they have more details of the island as compared to other languages. The ferry comes every 15 minutes so you do not have to worry if you miss it. Inside the ferry, there are flooring with thermal and you have to take your shoes off before stepping into the resting platforms. Otherwise, you may choose to stand outside those rooms and there are some outdoor seats at the top of the ferry. Please also take note that there are 2 ports at Udo, so your ferry might stop at either one.Once you reach the island, you will be greeted by tons of shop assistants trying to get you to rent bikes to you. You will need an international driver license to be able to drive any motorise vehicles. Upon confirmation which is the vehicle you want, you have to leave your passport with the register counter. They will provide you with a map to go around the island. We were informed that the whole cycling trip takes an hour. However, here comes the challenging part. There were no proper division of the road for those driving trucks, buses, cars, motorcycles & bicycles. You can be riding your bicycle and have a full speed bus chasing behind you and pressing the horn at you. Cars and trucks from the opposite direction also travel at fast speed towards you, which we had to stop many times to give way to these fast moving vehicles. After getting to the first beach, which was really beautiful, the rest of the trip towards the next beach was tough as there were many upward slopes and split roads which have no proper signages to tell you which way to go. We had to go in to random houses and ask in broken korean for which way to go. However, when we reach the lighthouse area, we managed to locate Jimmy?s icecream shop as suggested by our Jeju driver. I tried the mandarin orange ice cream while my friend tried the apple mango ice cream. Everything tasted natural and yummy so I would recommend it to tourist who visit the place. However, from the road before this ice cream place onwards to the last 5 mins of the ride, it was all upwards riding.We took almost 3 hours to finish cycling around the whole island (We have done quite a few rides in Singapore so I don?t think we were slow in cycling around the island). So for those who have no license or feel that you?re not up to 2-3 hours of cycling, I would advise you to take the tour bus to get from places to places on the island.

Been there and seen the bus going slightly 'up slope' when engine is off.Could be explained by gravity at this part of the road, although the up slope was not too obvoius, hence my title - not so amazing.If u are going there by yourself it might not be worthwhile, really

Be sure to visit even if you come to Jeju by only 3-4 days. Climbing is better to start early in the morning. At the beginning, some steep, climb to 1/3 after it enjoyed, leisurely walk along the gentle slope, wooded, narrow mountain road is very cool. Slightly sweating, big mouth breathing, anxious to put lung wash. I think is better shoes for climbing than sneakers because the rocks often.

Basically, this is just an eye illumination. You see a uphill road but actually it's a downhill road and vice versa. What you have to do is just let your car in N mode, then you will see the magic. Or you can get down from your car, and put a bottle on the road in a laying position. It's quite interesting because you can hardly find this kind of natural eye illumination.

Basically nothing much here. The road seemed to be uphill and when the engine of the vehicle is switched off, it will   roll uphill  . However, it is a natural optical illusion, and the road is actually downhill. Spend not more than 15mins here if you drive as the road is just about 50 metres. Also, the   rolling down   phenomenon only works on large vehicles like buses or truck. Small saloon cars will not encounter the   rolling uphill   effect.

At the entrance of this huge garden layout is lush, green plants  there is a bonsai garden, herb gardens, an array of flowers, a subtropical garden, water garden and a stone display as you travel along a palm garden road. There is a fair amount of walking.This display of trees, plants and gardens is a wonderful experience although its the caves, limestone tube-shaped structures growing downward from the ceiling of the cave and stalagmites that grow from the floor up. Structures are formed  containing calcium-bicarbonate. Fossilized seashells, frozen lava, and numerous other structures which enhanced our walk through the caves.  Visit the stone exhibition hall, see the parrots and the various species of birds. A must see attraction.

At first one may feel very inquisitive and cannot picture logically why vehicles can still move uphill even with the engines turn off.  However after some observations,  you will realize that the road is actually going downhill.   But how it appears to look like uphill is a mystery, that's why call Mysterious Road!!!

At eye level, the short stretch looked like an upward sloping road, but it was actually a 3 degrees downhill slant. A bit out of the way, would not recommend making a trip there unless you're from Jeju-si enroute to Hallasan National Park. Many of the 'mysterious bottle rolling uphill' videos have been posted on youtube in case you want to see the mystery! The real attraction here was the huge iconic black pig family statue. It was detailed and incredible. LOL

As with many cars that went there, my taxi stopped, turned off the engine, switched to Neutral gear and yes, the car started rolling uphill......But interestingly, the road is also called the demon road there. Look around the place, and you will see some cute little   devils   around the place.Nothing much there else, expect that you need to be there and say you done that.

As we stayed in Seogwipo, we followed part of Jeju Olle Route 6 and  7  from Chilshimni Poetry Park to Oedolgae. We started our personal trail from Saeyeongyo Bridge and went up to Chilshimni Poetry Park through a wooden stairway. The wooden stairway was located along the road where a lot of tourist buses parked (towards the end where there was a brown building beside) away from Saeyeongyo Bridge. When we reached Chilshimni Poetry Park (is just beside Park Sunshine hotel), we were lucky to catch a view of  the Cheonjiyeon Falls from the top. There was also a resting shelter with table and benches if you want to enjoy the view of the waterfall while having snacks or lunch. Afterwhich, we left the park to the main road (where Park Sunshine hotel was) and headed to Namseong-ro road which was indicated by the blue/orange ribbons for Oedolgae. Along the way, you will pass by몃媛?? Hostel (the hostel name is in Korean as I cannot find the English name online) before reaching Hwangwooji coast first (it is a very beautiful coast with a private emerald green pool. Then there was a trail to Oedolgae where was a cliff top that you can view the Saeyeongyo bridge. Oedolgae trail is  free 1 to 2 hours trail and it is not a difficult trail, it is pretty gentle with lots of benches for rest breaks as needed. It has pretty nice coast view. There were fruits and snack sold along the trail where you just need to place 1000won at the basket where you take the fruits/snacks from (there is not one attending to the store). It is based on trust. There were rest rooms outside the trails if needed with food stalls near the free public toilet with toilet paper provided. We need all the trail by foot and there is really no need for a car.

As we stayed in Seogwipo, we followed Jeju Olle Route 6 from Chilshimni Poetry Park (to see the Cheonjiyeon Falls from the top) to Oedolgae and happened to see this Hwangwooji coast (probably part of olle route 6) which was my favourite spot of the day. You will walk along Namseong-ro road and passed by 외돌개나라 Hostel (the hostel name is in Korean as I cannot find the English name online). I love the place bcos it was like a private pool and it is free. There were only a few Korean that day, playing, swimming and hunting of sea creatures in the private pool. It also has a good view of the Saeyeongyo Bridge from a far.? After-which we head to Oedolgae.You can walk there and you do not need a car. Probably a 15 minutes walk from the main road (Namseongjung-ro road where Poong Gyung Hotel or Park sunshine hotel jeju is) and walk in to Namseong-ro road where? 외돌개나라 Hostel is.

As the name implies, this street is a street of restaurants & dining. There are so many   nice   appetizing looking? restaurants as we explored the place.A very helpful   road map   at the main road entrance shows the restaurants names & types of food & exactly its location within the street.This street is nearby Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market. Seogwipo main town is quite small, so most of these   attractions   are quite close by.

As I rented a car to explore Jeju (highly recommended), we came here a couple of times to enjoy the experience putting the gear at N position and realizing how the car went up the hill.We also tried on the road with a can of beer that also was rolling hill up apparently. It is maybe an optical illusion but when you are there it looks clearly and without any doubt that cars and things go up the road. The kids were amazed and really enjoyed as we also did.Try to avoid the afternoons, as most of the guided tours are here at that time with many buses horning in hurry to repeat the experience several times and many pedestrians around. In the morning the day after it was almost empty !

As a tour stop, the bus with engine shut off rolls up the road, this includes water and bottle, how mysterious? I say its average because I have seen this. Short vision is the road seem to be going up, but its real orientation is that of downward slope.  Therefore, it is still following the law of gravity. Conclusion, enjoy the moment and do not share your secret.

As a part of our school's field trip program, we went to the one of the known attraction in Jeju-do which is the Jeju mysterious road. While inside of the bus, our tour guide asked the driver to turn the engine off. Our tour guide pointed out that even though the engine is turned off, the bus still continues to move   way up  . But in reality, our bus moved downwards. It was like an optical illusion. For me, this attraction is not that amazing, just a normal road. On a positive note, if you have a lot of time to spend in the island, give it a try and experience the illusion.

An hour is okay, but if you have the time it might be better to make this 1,5 hour. We combined this with waiting for the Mongolian horse show, which you should not miss and close to this location. You \can also enjoy the beautifull Jeju-beach on the other side of the road.This park is very well maintained. Enjoy the beautifull Bonsai trees, the waterfalls, the flowers, the cave and the statues. The cave was the least exciting to us, but the bonsai trees from over 150 years old were most impressive.

Always wanted to see a lava cave and I finally did. It was quite chilly in there so do bring a jacket. And the ceiling is always dripping, so bring an umbrella or raincoat as well. The whole lava tube is about 2.5km long. Pleasant walk on slightly uneven ground. Took bus 701 from Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal to Manjanggul Cave. Remember to always press the bus bell for the stop you want to get off! We had a crazy bus driver that just kept on driving until we told him to stop (he didn't even stop to pick up the couple who were waving at the bus stop, bizarre!). Anyway the bus only stop out on the main road, there is still a 2.5km walk to the cave entrance. You can flag down a taxi and it cost 2800 won to the entrance.

Although we know how the illusion works, it is still crazy to watch how the bottles or cars go up hill instead of going back. You don't need much time over there though. One mysterious road (according to our touri map there are two) is located right next to the Jeju Lovepark which is interesting and funny. You can go there for 9000 Won, spend about an hour watching love sculptures. :-)

After parking the rental car at Seongsan Harbor, we hopped on the ferry (KRW 1,500) to cross over to Udo. Upon alighting from the ferry at Cheonjinhang Harbor on Udo, we headed to the Udo Tour Bus counter and got ourselves a ticket each (KRW 5,000). The whole tour is conducted in Korean. Not a single hint of English but it was enjoyable. The bus driver was also the tour guide, telling us about the significance of each stop. He'd stop for 20 minutes at each place of interest and if you do not hop back on, fret not, you may hop on the other tour buses. Keep your ticket stub.The whole tour took about 2 hours. The village roads were really interesting. If I visit Jeju again, I would want to stay overnight at Udo. The atmosphere is good, the air is fresh, people are nice.

Admission is 2000 won. Need to walk down a flight of stairs to reach the beach area. The beach is full of pebbles and rocks and you need to careful to balance your body as you walk or hop from one rock to another. It may be slippery at certain spots and do exercise some precaution when taking photographs. The cliff looks steep and this is the only unique waterfall in Asia where the water falls directly into the sea. While the waterfall was not as awesome as what I earlier saw in books, the sensation was relaxing and cooling with the thundery roar of the waterfall at the backdrop while you sat at the beach rocks gazing at the azure sea. It was an unique pristine natural scenery to appreciate and absorb. At Cheonjeyeon Falls, the attraction is secluded and one could not see the vast horizon of the ocean whereas here at Jeongbang Waterfall, the waterfall and the beach integrated into the ocean giving a wholesome broad vision effect. At Jusangjeolli Cliffs, one could only enjoy the serene sight of the torrential waves crashing against the blackish rock pillars from the elevated observation point and access to the beach area is prohibited. Jeongbang Waterfall gives us the convenient access to the beach area and so near to a gorgeous waterfall and a looming cliff. Like Yongduam Rock which is backed up by a dragon head legend, Jeongbang Waterfall also has a story of Seobul, a servant of the Chinese Emperor Jin  who was ordered by the Emperor to search for an elixir and he happened to by-pass this area during his search. An inscription written `Seobulgwacha' on the wall of the water fall was derived from this legend but I did not walk too near to the waterfall to see clearly that inscription. Jeju has quite a number of world class natural wonders and each wonder gives me a different perspective in appreciating nature.

Actually originally didn't think to visit this place. But coincidence have the chance, me and my travel partners was shock to see with our own eyes for the water and bottle both run to the upfront road which its was suppose to be opposite way....Make youself drop by to see this amazing effect while you around in Jeju. This place is just very nearby the Sex Museum which we didn't go but passby~

Actually like the other ones, I felt quite surprise at the my first visits since last year 2011. The guide showed me that I were in the bottom of the slope, she pointed to the tree lines along  the side of the road and truly, it has made me believe what she said. A few seconds later, the driver shut the engine and release the bus's brakes, the 45 seated bus was beginning move slowly then faster and faster.  Could you believe ? The huge bus was moving up to the top of the slope without working engine! A man of my group - an 50 ages supposed there were the natural magnetic power that dragged up the 2,5 tons iron bus to about 5-8 meter height during approximately 80 metes !!!It was happened about 10 mins then all of our group's participant disembarked the bus, they were starting to talk about what they saw during the past 10 minutes. Some one said it caused by a natural magnetic power (as above), other one assumed by the trick of the sun's lighting a man nearly lying face down to the road parallel to look forward to the starting point... others wisely poured the water to see the flows .... Of course, our guide has explained the cause but I really do not want to tell you, let's explore by yourself.Definitely, this places is quite appropriated for your family with kids. Aside the road, there are the Korean traditional food shops who sells fried fish ball, rice cake... but they are almost fried into the oil ...This places are really attracted a lot of people from Asia like Chinese, Vietnamese, Indian... I think you might found the similar road like the Jeju Mysterious Road of your own country but the Korean was wise to promote it via the drama film series currently expanding over the Asia.Totally, Jeju is an beautiful island and you should visit one time. With me, I could said   you could make the money by the very simple things

Accessible by ferry. Udo is a tiny island so you wont get lost while wandering around this island. Filled with canola fields during spring, fresh breeze, peaceful atmosphere, sights of female divers, it is perfect for a daytrip. However if you plan to drive, just be extra careful as the roads are narrow.

A way to escape from daily hectic life. You can walk at your own pace and choose the route and scenery you like (coastal road, hiking). I completed Route 1, 1-1, 20, part of route 6 & 7. Just choose the route and follow the olle sign, relax and enjoy the view Olle wanna show you. Is quite safe, I am a girl and I walked alone.

A very short and busy road clogged by tourists, tour buses and cars trying to see and feel the uphill rolling effect. I personally did not see anything rolling uphill. Tour guides poured water and empty round mineral water bottles but it did not seem to give any credence to the anomaly. However I did see one car roll backwards (uphill) rather fast but couldn't tell if it was already in-gear, nevertheless the reverse lights weren't illuminated so I guess it wasn't rolling on it's own steam.

A short stretch of road that has vehicles rolling up a slope. Our driver even got out and place an empty bottle on the road and the bottle, like the car roll upwards.Amazing, got to see it to believe it.
A short distance of the road where it looks like uphill but when we put our car gear in neutral, the car moves !!! legends say it is because there are ghost pushing your car from behind !

A short 20 mins drive from the Jungmun resort area. Very easy to navigate and locate with the clear road signs available. Admission was just KRW 2,000 per adult. Very reasonable. The Waterfall is a short flight of stairs down from the main carpark. There were large groups of Korean high school students visiting during our time there so we just followed the crowd. Took us less than 15 mins to get down to the fall. Perhaps it's not the rainy season, the waterfall seemed tiny (compared to Niagara etc). The water flowed first into a stone pool before trickling into the sea. Not very impressive but a nice destination for our family with a toddler. He had a great time trying to balance on the big rocks by the fall. Next to the fall, there were 2 women divers selling abalone and sea squirts. I saw local tourists eating them as sashimi sitting right there on the rocks. Interesting.

A road seems to be uphill, but it is in fact a downhill. The driver shut off the engine at the 'downhill' but the car moves itself towards the 'uphill' without the help of anyone. Fun fact by tour guide: This mysterious incident was discovered by a taxi driver when he intend to take a leak at the roadside and found out the car moves itself towards the uphill after he stopped the car.

A nice beach with fine sand and lots of facilities such as parasols for hire, cocktails and food stalls. There are showers and toilets close by too. On the downside, it's incredibly busy and parking is a nightmare. Once all the parasols and tables are out there's very little sand left! The amount of space available for swimming is small. We preferred to go to the less popular beach along the road. It's more spacious and more relaxed.

1) The staff spoke limited English. When we got into the room, it appeared the A/C was not working. We told the staff and their response was that it was made such so as guests no need to turn on the A/C. A/C is only available during summer. They advised us to open the window / take a shower instead to feel fresher.1st night in the hotel, we couldn't sleep as the noise from the air (the hotel is near the airport) and road traffic entered our room as well as the dust.2) The casino opening hour was stated 10:00AM - 01:30AM. I tried to enter the casino at 11:00PM, got told that I would not be able to play (just seeing) as the casino is closing.3) Room is spacious and the bed is comfortable. However, the room and the hotel corridor have weird smell. It must be the carpet smell. The room has an old-looking room and most things in the room are payable (you only get the toiletries and 2 bottles of water)..In conclusion, very terrible experience staying in this hotel. I would not spend a single dollar to this hotel in future.

You will find endless tea leaves! A very refreshing sight. There is a cafe where you can sit and enjoy your greentea cake roll greentea ice cream & a pot of hot greentea! It is also beside Innisfree shop where you will enjoy shopping for cosmetics and fragrances!

You will enjoy this place depends on how u spend your time :1. Take photo in the tea garden & entrance2. Order you green tea/ green tea ice cream or drinks and bring it outside the cafe (depend on weather) 3.Walk around4. visit the innisfree museum & shop for some innisfree product.

you should read the story of this museum.it comes to live cos there is a dream.it has a sharp appearance a vibrant red exterior in jeju when comparing with those surrounding buildings.the art pieces in the museum is nice but i do appreciate the way that the owner makes this museum as an art piece more.To renovate rather than destroy and rebuild keeping the scratches of time and inject the modern art atmosphere into this old building.although you may think the entry free maybe a bit high but it still worth to visit.the cafe and souvenir shop at top floor also nice to stay awhile.
You may find a lot of Korean bbq pork restaurants on this street. Some shops open till 2-3pm and some closes early for lunch. They serve almost the same menu in every shop on this street!
You don't have to spend a lot of time here but the displays are well done and interesting.  There is a small shop at the end from which you can purchase a bear

You could park and walk to the falls. Entrance was 2000w. Opens at 0900 not crowded. You?re able to walk right up to the edge of the falls for great photos. Some available shops for souvenirs and snacks.

You can see the history of tea in Korea and world in general you can eat green tea ice cream and shop from a variety of products (face creams etc.) which are all made from green tea. There are tea farms outside also so that you can enjoy a short nice walk in these tea farms.
Who does not like teddy bears - bears everywhere; great views and of course - the essential shop! Good for children and families

Whether you are a tea fan or just want to see a nice view of the area this is a nice place to visit. The ?쐌useum??is quite small. The bigger draw is the store (with a sample) and tea/ice cream shop. It was very busy very touristy!

When we arrived there it was already flooded by numbers of tourists so we had a hard time to find a seat and taste the tea sample. Maybe to avoid the bad traffic and buses of tourists you should go early in the morning before the tour buses arrived.Very futuristic design building with the tea plantation across the road perfect for photo session. Don't forget to shop O'sulloc products particularly the green tea.

When I was planning my trip to Jeju  I found this museum has got half positive and half negative comments from travelers. Well ??I decided to have a look by myself. When our car got near to the place  there was a strong smell. I was then told that there is a piggery farm nearby which stinks out the whole place. The ticket was not cheap but it included a cup of coffee plus a discount in the shop. The appearance of the building is interesting with an open courtyard. The first impression was not so bad.However when I got inside  it was quite disappointing. I think the management should consider a renovation  or at least a deep cleaning and some maintenance. I just felt I was in a dusty old weird mansion. Maybe those exhibits are precious and rare  but they are not well presented. For example  they put lots of chocolate boxes from all over the world in the same window display without proper descriptions. How can the people think that those boxes are precious when they are packed in a glass cabinet? The lighting on the second floor was horrible. The rooms were so dark adding horrific ambiance to the museum.
