review: Went with two boys that dislike shopping. Good thing they hv soap or bubble bath craft to keep both busy while I shop. Surprisingly it took them longer to finish their craft then my shopping! A win-win place for me!

Went to the tea museum. The place was busy with loads of tourists. The area was very well maintained with a lot of Instagram potential shots. The Innisfree flagship store is just next to the museum. Ended up going to the innisfree store to look for potential buys. This shop has some products which are exclusive only to it. It also had diy packs where one can make bath bombs (shaped like leaf or horse) or regular soaps. Once bought you can either spend some time nsking it on site (needs any half hour) or you could take home to make it. There's also a lovely cafe attached to this shop.Had a lovely time here.?몟

Went there with my friend.. We took a bus from Halla hospital (?쒕씪蹂묒썝) bus stop and took bus no. 755 and alighted at the bus stop right in front of O'Sulloc Tea Museum. The entrance is free and there is a gift shop and a cafe.. You can buy different types of teas and other products made from tea in the shop (e.g. tea packs skin care products etc). You can buy green tea ice cream green tea roll cake and beverages etc from the cafe.. The cost of the products are reasonable while some are more expensive.Opposite the road there is a big Tea farm of the tea museum. You can take pictures there but must beware of snakes (諭�議곗떖) as warned with a sign board on the tea plant.Beside the museum there is Innisfree Jejuhouse (just walking distance). There is a sign board showing the direction and the Innisfree Jejuhouse is on the left hand side of the Tea Museum. If you like Tea this is a must visit place.

Went there last week on my trip to Jeju. Its a local market where you can find shopkeepers selling almost everything. From souvenirs to sea food. And stuff is pretty cheap too. Visit once to experience the local flavour and to collect some stuff to take back

Went there in May 2015 by jeju golden city bus tour (which sucked!) and totally enjoyed our 1 hour visit! The exhibitions were amazing and the atmosphere itself is beautiful there! Adm fee is good: just 1000 won as much as I remember. Though the prices at a coffee shop were pretty expensive.

Went there as part of a cruise ship itinerary. It is a great walk and views. Avoid if raining or cloudy. The walk to the top of what is known in English as Sunrise Peak is quite strenuous and involves a lot of stairs. There are rest stops along the way. There are no lifts. It can get quite windy so jackets are required. There is a town centre area at the base with restaurants and shops.

Went around with a friend and the place is huge. I think we managed to walk from gate 8 to gate 4 before we realized we cane there looking to eat and ended up just window shopping because there?s lots to feast your eyes on. There?s mostly food and fresh produce and seafood and food products made from Jeju oranges.

well. this fashion street was near with my hotel & i've walked here quite many times in a week. not so special for me as i don't do shopping but i ate 2times in this street that was impressivefirst time i reached here at 1st day no any breakfast shop near around*(they are opened at 9-10am at least) quite hungry & finally i stepped in one of traditional shop that only served 3 types of food all was hangover soup ha. seem that for drunken. price not so expensive(but not cheap) and quite many stuffs. tasty but full. lady boss also quite nice although she can't well communicate with meanother times with fds that was in a quiet corridor seem quite expensive restaurant with old & korean deco. however price was acceptable & serve sausage stew. well we ate traditional sausage stew in korean style house(boss always walk out from his room & overall style was house instead of restaurant). he was quite concern do we know how to eat & taking care of our table. maybe it has no many tourist but only korean or japanese while we having dinner moment.

Well this place was big. Need to prepare to walk if you're going at non-peak hours. Why? due to the train not moving. This place features Korean village cultural show donkey / house riding costume trying & a beautiful setting to get some nice pictures. We enjoyed solid 1-2hours walking. But having to travel with small kids its quite tiring. Anyway the replicas of houses & setting was great. Enjoyed buying some quality souvenir at the gift shops. My kids just love the small maze park. I don't op for a tour guide but a head set was just enough for us to make us understand the place.One thing for sure they're snakes wandering around the place. While walking we come across 2 snakes (small). My kids was terrified! So need to be extra careful for those who bring little kids. Another set back was the small shop selling fast food. I know there's a barrier problem in language but they seem to ignore foreign tourist due to the fact we cant communicate well with each other. Very hard to buy stuff. Water! walking makes you thirsty. Pro's :- The head set helps to understand the place even-though not so many point haves explanation. Perhaps its an area for improvement.Con's :- Snakes? YikesOverall the place was ok. But will not come again..
Well organised tour of Korean traditional village easy to navigate takes about an hour. Stop at the gift shops in between for gifts
We were there just for the sunset. Loved it. It was a weekday and there were not many people at the beach.There are shops in the area too.

We were mesmerized with the glass art. Such detailed work! The route made it easier to walk and enjoy all the glass art. Admission fee is 11 000 won. There were also one part of the park that showed glass palace  but we end up walking about 10minutes and no castle was in our sight  quite disappointed. P/S: you can find cute fridge magnet of jeju at the end of the souvenir shop. There were only 1 000 won for one. Very cheap for a fridge magnet I think.

We were glad we could catch this show in Jeju as time in Seoul were simply too precious for shopping. It's funny and you don't need to understand Korean to enjoy it. All 3 of us including our 4 yr old enjoyed it. It' a plus to have that cute lady in the show as well. Show time is 90 mins but not a dull moment. We got our taxi guide to reserve the tickets on the same day and only manage to get the VIP seats at w60k each. It would be better if you can reserve the ticket days in advance.

We went to visit this Dragon Rock and it put a bleak end to our Jeju trip. The rock is a beautiful artwork of nature but people seem to be taking too much advantages of it. The town nearby is full of hotel and other shops for travelers just down the street from the rock. We just couldn?t walk very near to it because the way down there is dangerous and blocked with the fence.

We went to the Teddy Bear Museum with my young kid. The museum has lots of teddy bears and would probably interest those who are teddy bear lovers. They do have a shop that sell  lots of teddy bear merchandise. We finish the tour in about 20 minutes.
We went to the 1st shop at black pork street. Expensive black pork but it is worth the price. Even my kids love it. We end up ordering 1 more set although expensive

We went to DaHeeYeon for the self baths.In a large room of about 50 peoplewe sat on floor andunder direction of their instructorwe gave ourselves foot baths using products sold at their shop.The instructor spoke Korean but we were able to follow along.It was unusual and fun and soothing to our feet after days of sightseeing.

review: We went on a rainy day and feared it would be too busy to enjoy but it was ok (the first section was the busiest but the crowds thin out the further you get in).  A lot of fun for kids and adults alike.  It took us longer than we thought to get through you could spend hours so would suggest bringing some snacks if you are travelling with kids like we did. There is a coffee shop on site but it only had sweets and ice cream.A fun outing if you've never been to a trick museum before.  Don't forget your camera!!!

We went here today for first time and love it?s it?s so beautiful and fun to walk around have good restaurants and coffee shop and good shop to buy thing make from jeju !! You can take bus or taxi too

We went here on a rainy day as we really wanted to see how the famous O'Sulloc tea was made. The museum is nothing more than a room (unfortunately not all texts are translated info english) and the majority of the space is taken up by the shop and the cafe which seems like the main focus of this location.Two things were nice getting a look of the tea plantations and having a quick tea tasting.I would recommend this only if you are a true O'Sulloc fan or if you have spare time not visiting all the other sights at Jeju island.

We went here as part of a shops tour. It was cloudy and rainy so you couldn?t really see anything. Our guide wasn?t very good so he didn?t explain much. I wouldn?t go here again unless it was a clear day

We visited the Tea Museum in a rainy windy day. The place was very crowded with tourists especially the cafe and shop. There were some history and artefacts displayed which I guess was why it's called a museum. I actually expected more from a 'museum'.The goods sold in cafe and shop were the same with other branches in Seoul maybe with a few 'only in Jeju' specials. They were quite pricey but tasted great.

We visited the Dongmum market in March . It is quite a large market selling all kinds of food items so you can try the local delicacies. Their is a separate fish and seafood area that is quite extensive with a wide variety of local seafood . The is a variety of clothing and souvenir items . It is in the heart of the city around many shopping areas that surround the market . Their is also a Starbucks not too far from the market .
We visited on a Monday morning and there are so many tourists and koreans at both the green tea cafe and shop and Innisfree Jeju House and cafe. Good green tea drink and desserts though.

We visited in April 2018 and were impressed by the quality and the size of the village. There is a lot of history and culture to be learned here. The exhibits are well maintained they have live gardens and animals to represent the life in the village as well as hands on exhibits for kids and adults to participate in. There are craftspeople and artisans that are making wood work and stoneware that you can purchase. It is very beautiful. Also there is a restaurant on premise near the front gates and gift shop. The living museum and village is wheelchair accessible and worth the price of admission. It will take 2 to 3 hours to see everything. It can easily be a half day experience. Get there early to avoid the crowds. It's popular for students and tourists along with all the major places you should visit while on Jeju.

We visited at the beginning of May and it was cold. It also rained when we were on the beach. So could not enjoy the water.However beach is very nice and clean. We had coffee in the coffee shop on beach which gives you nice view of the beach.Its just opposite Hallim park so can be combined.Would nice to spend a warm and sunny day on this beach.

We visited and there were about 20 buses in the parking lot. The shop where you get the tea or ice cream was very full so we went out to the tea bushes and enjoyed our tea there. We did learn about how tea is made and seeing the actual plant was interesting to me. Wish it was less crowded.

We took city tour bus and stopped at this famous black pork street for dinner at the shop with long queue.   Minimum order is KWR 54000 for 600g pork for 2 pax ie roughly 300g per pax.  It seemed so meaty but the helper grilled the pork just nice and we finished all.

We spent some fun hours here luckily the weather was beautiful and I'd suggest to visit when it's sunny so the place can really shine. Could be better maintained but we liked it regardless. So what's to see here? Installations of famous landmarks and a tiny Korean village (which is more like few houses really). I wouldn't call this a theme park I'd say it's a park with an interesting and enjoyable theme without toys. I think most parks and museums in Jeju share one common problem: the staff seems to be nonpresent and there's a serious lack of catering service. No coffee shops restaurants or they're either closed. I think this place had something but I think it was closed. Either way I think it's worth visiting if you happen to be around and the surroundings are pretty too.

We self-drive to this museum. Like everyone else we ate the green tea cake ice cream and hot green tea latte for lunch it was delicious especially for green tea lovers. It was crowded with bus loads of tourists but the cafe staff was very efficient and served quickly. Bought Jeju tangerine tea after trying the sample. We also went to the innisfree shop to buy cosmetics. And took photos of the garden that has beautiful cherry blossoms at this time. Great soothing weather and we also walked across the road to the tea plantation. Enjoyed ourselves.

We read some blogs that showed amazing blue-green water kayaks and paddleboards and lots of places to jump in and swim.  When we got there we found some pretty views (including a pretty violent whirlpool that formed in the river as the tide came in) but ZERO activities. So it was a bit disappointing on that level.....but still a pretty place for a stroll and lots of cafes/shops/trinket-sellers around.

We paid for our tickets and got past the entrance when it started pouring. We waited it out for maybe an hour or more  but it didn't stop  only got harder. The lady at the ice cream shop must have felt sorry for us because she gave us chairs to sit on while we waited and even some free chocolates. We asked the ticket counter if we can get a refund since we didn't actually see anything except for the sign  but unfortunately they said no. It seemed like it would have a been a great place if we actually got to go past the front hahaha! At least they made a lot of money selling umbrellas that day.

We order 4 drinks and all we are like the ice-coffee rather than hot coffee the green tea cake is yummy. I bought two boxes tea bag form the shop its regret so bought two boxes tea bag. Its really nice smell and good taste too.

We made a stop there for lunch as recommended by our B&B owner. There are now 2 coffee shops. We had lunch in the new one. The steamed bun with sausage was nice. The brunch set menu was a bit bland. The best thing in the brunch set is the homemade yoghurt with marmalade. We enjoyed the view while having lunch. Quite relaxing. More Korean day-trippers and foreigners. We had green tea ice cream from the old coffee shop afterwards. Really good green tea ice cream. Better than some that we had in Japan. If you want a quick lunch and want something non-local this is the place to go.

We loved looking at the shells collected from all over the world. They were artistically arranged. It was well worth the $6.00 entrance fee and I received pearl stud earrings for free. The gift shop was expensive and bordered on tacky. The few shells for sale were very expensive  $68.00 for a small shell.

We love caverns and Manjanggul did not dissapoint. It is a good length and the world's tallest lava column at the end. They send students from Korea on field trips to learn about it so it is important to local history.There is a store and restaurant onsite  as well as a visitor center.  You can get coffee and snacks at the shop too. Well worth the buck to visit. It was 1000won or 2000won which is $1 or $2.

We finally got a good clear day.Yesterday at Sunrise Mountain we had been in the clouds.  Some nice views down the coast. Not a terrible tough or long hike to get to the end of the trail with a small temple cave. Number of mostly coffee shops at the bottom and bathroom facilities.

We enjoy the visit. The place looks magical. We couple enjoy it and so thus our young adult kid and 9 year kid. Each of the stop is worth the visit. There are coffee shop and snacks in each of the stop.The best stop is the last stop wherein there are so many beautiful flowers fully landscape and so good to take pictures. We visited autumn. The place is clean the restrooms are clean. I love their coffee its worth the visit.

We came here on a sunny morning primarily since we had never seen any tea plantations and it seemed like a sufficiently different thing to do on holiday.There is no entrance fee to the actual plantation and parking is plentiful. We started off at the viewing terrace (with a sign halfway up the stairs informing us: 'What a great view') where there were tea plants in view as far as the eye could see. I was a bit disappointed since they really don't look dissimilar from any other bush (not being a gardener myself).The main attraction for us came a bit afterwards when we went into the Innisfree shop. In there you can buy sets for making cosmetic items. We chose to buy two sets of soap making equipment which cost us 10000 won each. You then take the equipment to the craft benches in the shop each of which was equipped with an I-pad showing us in English what we had to do. Our kids (10 and 15 - both girls) just loved it and spent a good 45 minutes happily occupied. We thought it was great - I even borrowed some of their stuff and joined in (very soothing). We thus ended up with some happily entertained girls and two presents to take home to grandparents to accompany the video my husband made of the whole event.After this we ordered some green tea food and drink from the caf챕. Again the atmosphere was lovely - bright and airy. Prices as mentioned elsewhere are quite high but taken in conjunction with the atmosphere felt ok. The food was lovely.Overall we spent a lovely morning here and all came away very pleasantly surprised.

We came here early morning to take in the fresh air and scenic views of soesokkak estuary. There are water activities like the popular transparent kayak but it was closed when I went there. Just a note for those who wants to ride the transparent kayak do come here first thing in the morning and reserve a kayak for that day. There are nearby shops selling souvenirs and other eateries as well. I tried buying the hallabong ice cream from one of the stalls and it's really delicious.

We are glad that we have our wonderful tour guide was with us thus we were able to gain better understanding n knowledge about the green tea n it's plantation.The museum itself actually showcase the different type of green tea products (including facial products) so it's a shopping paradise for some.  There are free sampling of the green tea however we like the cafe most. Though a little pricey but the green tea yogurt ice cream n also the green tea milk ice cream is yummy (it has strong green tea taste).As it was crowded when we were there the cafe seemed to be under stocked for the crowd.  A friend managed to get herself green tea macaron n said it taste superb.A good stop over for some retail therapy n tea break n photo taking.

Was? a great refuge from a rainy day. Only one English sign so hard to know what it was all about. Artwork didn't appeal to me- seemed quite juvenile in style. Surrounding area is quite nice- coffee shops and stores.

Was very crowded the day/time we were there.  There's a tiny museum which leads to shop and cafe.At the cafe we had the trio of  green tea cake/roll smoothie and ice cream which were very good.Then we headed next door to the Innisfree Jeju house.A nice way to spend a couple of hours.  There's a couple of very uncrowded O'sulloc cafes in Seoul too.

Was specially there to try their famous Matcha Roll and Matcha ice cream and it didn't disappoint. The cream within the Matcha roll was totally on point and delicious. The Matcha ice cream was rich and creamy. It went really well together with the matcha roll. There were too many tourist on the day we visited and was overly crowded. We were also disappointed with the innisfree shop beside the tea museum as we'd expected more product offerings. There are no cosmetics in the store. Only limited number of products. It is a 30-45mins drive from Jeju City.

Was excited to see the tea museum but disappointed as it was only a 5 minute tour. We drove for about 1.5 hours to visit this museum from the other end of Jeju City.  The treats at the museum shop was a nice respite against the summer heat though. There is also the tea plantations just across the museum and Innisfree (Korean Skincare) beauty shop about 2 minutes walk away. I would recommend to go for the Stoner Tea museum tour to make this trip more worthwhile. However there are certain timings for it and we didnt manage to join.

Visited this place with a group of friends. The tea plantation wasn?셳 fantastic; don?셳 expect vast rolling hills of uninterrupted shrubbery. The museum was really small and led to a shop and restaurant which was much bigger than the museum itself. The place was milling with many tourists and it was uncomfortable to browse their merchandise or eat in peace. We tried the matcha ice cream and cake and there was nothing too special about it. I don?셳 think this place is worth a visit.

Visited this Museum in Dec 2017 with my family. Entrance ticket costs 34 000kwon for 2 adults and 2 children. The place basically is run-down  glasses broken  dirty and colour faded over the years. I didn't bother to check on the cafe inside and left the museum in 15mins. Nothing special in the gift shop as well. Total waste of my money and my time travelled to visit the so called museum. If you intend to visit this Jeju Glass Museum  don't bother!

Visited the tea museum as heard so much about it but there is nothing that special just some tea history and at the end of it  they sell the tea to visitors at touristy pricing. There is a caf챕 that serves green tea and ice cream too and that is ok to try out. There is an Innis free shop next door to tea factory but it was closed the day we visited. I would say its ok for a visit if you have spare time in your hands otherwise nothing really to shout about.

Visited the Osulloc Tea Museum in the late afternoon. It was packed with visitors. Only few people really went to the museum. People just packed to shop for green tea or tea products. The cafe was crowded too and the seats/tables were not very clean because staff could not keep up with cleaning due to the huge crowds. Unless you want to purchase their products it is not the best place to visit.

Visited on a rainy day.  Limited parking - so had to park along the road and take a muddy path through the team garden.  Tea shop was very crowded to went to the Innisfree jeju House about 60 m away - great food and can make your own soap.

Visited on a friend's recommendation and it definitely didn't disappoint.  Upon entry to the building we walked through the historical display area before getting to the shop and cafe.  There were many different types of tea for sale and all beautifully packaged.  Again thanks to the friend who asked us to help buy stuff for her we knew to get the green tea milk spread.  For the tea they had samples for you to smell before purchasing.  We got the wedding tea green tea and green tea cold sticks. Can't wait to get home to try them.  Next we had the green tea roll green tea ice cream and green tea milk shake at the cafe.  All were exquisite.  On the outdoors there are great photo opportunities near the tea plantation.  As we walked there we discovered another building called Innisfree Jeju House.  It was a health food restaurant cum shop selling body oils and moisturiser.  We had lunch there and bought some beautiful smelling body lotion.  Again all fantastic.  The whole family enjoyed O'Sulloc!

Visited in the evening.  It is a local market selling Jeju specialities as well as a wet market section selling the fresh & live seafood.  Good to visit if you are into shopping for foods and want jeju local foods and street food.

Visited during a rainy day. Really not much to see but a large shop for purchasing chocolate with displays of chocolate from around the world. Lots of locally produced chocolate to purchase. It put in a half hour during the rain

review: Visit if you are a fan of teddy bears. Not much to do besides taking pictures and you might have to queue to take pictures. There is a souvenir shop at the entrance/exit.There is also a small stall selling snacks to the left of the entrance and down some step of stairs.

Very well managed green tea museum. They have a small museum to show the process of tea and how it has evolved over the years. Upon finishing the museum you can buy different green tea products from the shop. And there is also a cafe within the museum that sell excellent green tea ice cream and also green tea Swiss roll. If you have time you can walk further into the next building which is the innisfree shop within this building you will be able to make your own green tea soap under the supervision of the Innisfree staff. There is also a cafe that sell jam and cake in this building. Perfect to spend your afternoon in this place.

Very tasteful and informative. We were hesitant at first but figured we might as well take advantage of seeing what a sexually suppressed country could teach us :)The gift shop was a little lacking on museum related material and seemed to carry just local touristy items.

Very pretty and not too taxing walk to add to any outings on Jeju. Our day was a little foggy but the view was still amazing with the Spring growth just starting to show. Lots of other attractions in the near vicinity makes it a good spot to include in a day out. The short but steep hike up to the 'temple in a cave' provides some lovely views on a good day and there are several other attractions at the base of the walk including the Big Golden Buddha temples tea shops the Dutch ship and rock walks. Enjoyable.

Very nice small museum. Not as boring as much of them. I found it interesting. I hate wandering for 8 hours in a museum with tons to read. That one is fesable in a normal amount of time. There was also a little show they did with movable boats showing how they worked in the days. Girls doing it were laughing the whole time as it was hilarious. My bf got picked to go help as cast along with others working the nets. I loved the whole scene with the chants. There are old boats outside you can go in and visit. Small souvenir shop with not much. Very helpful employees who offered to keep our luggages behind the counter as they did not fit in the lockers.
Very nice place different quircky a bit cheese but really nice. Go on sunset see the lights. Shops are not the best. But the waffles are very good :) Pay attention to the names of the sculptures
Very beautiful beach with azure sea. Lots of coffee shops and restaurants on the shoreline to grab a snack and enjoy the view.
Underground shops over around 2 blocks. Nothing really interesting. You can skip it if you run out of time. Some clothing shops. Better save your money and time for Seoul.

Udo is a beautiful place that we have no regret to visit and spent 3 hours to round the island with rental electric car for KRW35000. Most shop offer KRW20000 for 2 hours and we find it will be a rush that you can?t really enjoy the scenic view of the island. Returned ferry ticket cost KRW8500/person. Rental car is currently not allowed to enter the island as a one year control started Aug 2017 so we parked it at covered parking near the port before we depart to Udo.

Total waste of money (6000 for adults). Tragically outdated  tacky  uninteresting. Not much focus on actual chocolate - we were expecting samples  exciting cafe  lots of choice to buy from. There is none of this. Shop super overpriced. Don't waste your time.

review: To know how the teddy bear appears then visit it. Also knowing all the types of teddy bear and appreciate it. Also a garden walk for photo shoot plus Elvis teddy bear life show every 15minutes to listen to elvis.The gift shop is really something to buy to have visit this teddy bear museum

To be honest we had already sampled the green tea cake ice cream and tea at the O'Sulloc shop and cafe in Insadong Seoul. However this tea garden featured in 'the Kimchi Chronicles' so we had to make a kind of pilgrimage to see it. The overall experience in the shop and cafe was a bit stressful because there are many tourists here at any given time of the day. It is a bit of a shame because this made it difficult to look at the teas properly and then to decide what to purchase. The prices are not cheap - even more so than  eg Fortnum and Masons but the tea is quite unique as it is grown here on the island. I guess it is worth the premium especially if you are buying the tea as a gift.Next door there is the cosmetics side to this enterprise - Innisfree. Once again the products are quite unique eg Jeju volcanic clay pore mask. I think if you are visiting Seoul or any other big city as part of your trip it would be better buying the tea and facial products there but if you are in Jeju also then it is worth popping in to see where it all happens as part of your trip.The teas cake and ice creams at the cafe are really very good but be prepared to pay a lot for it. Just tell yourself you don't do this everyday...

This would be my fav market so far at Jeju. You can buy lots of local products and local delicacies to eat as well. The market was so packed with locals and tourists so you kinda need to walk slowly and try not to block the road. LOLThere are lots of exit / entrance here but rest assured that it is interconnected and you won't get lost. Most shops are selling the same products but if you really wish to buy then you need to scout for the best price!

This was a tourist trap.No museum to me- just a bit of information about tea on the wall with a tea grousing machine- that?셲 it!Who calls this a museum?The rest of place was for cafe souvenir shop - some observatory deck where you could see the tea field.Honestly Amore Pacific did a great job to let people recognize that Jeju could produce tea that?셲 perfectly linked with their business. Very smart from business perspective- bravo in that sense.

This venue offers quite a few exhibits for photo moment. Kids will surely like his place. The place can be done in an hour time unless you spend time explaining to the kids what each exhibit is about. The gift shop offer a good range of teddy bear to buy as a gift.
this ug shopping mall has a lot of entrance one of them was located near dongmun market.mostly sell clothes and food.
This short walking street has many shops selling cosmetics sport apparel youngster fashion etc. It is bit quiet for the walking street may be due to the drop in the Chinese tourists.
This place isn't worth the visit. There isn't much to see except for the rock & beach. There are better beaches out there. More of a tourist trap with all the souvenir shops along the stretch.

This place is just outside the love land . There is a huge parking lot just behind this row of shops. In front of these shops selling sausages and fruits is the road . You can borrow a bottle of water and row it down the road and miraculously it will come to a stop and row backwards! Opposite the road is a grazing field where you can see cows . Ok a visit if you are in the area.

This place is huge with lotsa huts garden with lovely flowers and even souvenir shop! Best place to experience and learn olden Korean living. We are too lucky to bump into a group of actor and actress filming new movie there.

This place is breathtakingly beautiful with especially kind staff. Every piece of art is a masterpiece. Nice (but expensive) giftshop and cute coffeeplace. Don't miss it if you are close by. I visited this place on the last day of a worktrip and it left a wonderful feeling about Jeju.

This place is a hit with the tourist. Famous for Jeju local tea. If you are driving parking is free of charge and there is someone manning the traffic when it gets busy. There is a small museum showcasing the tea history but don't expect to learn much. Then you will walk into the tea shop which is quite huge followed by the cafe. We tried the green tea ice cream green tea swiss roll and jeju orange drink. Mind you the queue is very long but fast moving. I like their green tea ice cream and the swiss roll. There are few corners inside and outside of this place which is IG worthy. Nice place for the environment but it's not really museum per say. They have a branch in Seoul in case you are wondering.
This park is a whole bunch of Korean fun with a little bit of history mixed in with stuff for kids. The surrounds are peaceful and the coffee shop is a great place to finish off.

This museum isn't very large and in the winter you don't really want to go outside to admire the small amount of outdoor exhibits (which you can do from inside the windows anyway) but it's got enough interesting art to be worth 1000 KRW which is about USD $0.80. For one I enjoyed the Chang Ri Seok exhibit as his paintings are very earthy. The second floor exhibit was under renovation when I went but still for 1000 won I have no complaints about the first floor's contents. The gift shop is pretty underwhelming though.

This museum is one of the most popular of the 50+ on Jeju Island and the carpark was packed with tour buses when we arrived. But if you can manage to get a slot on one of the formal tea ceremonies it really takes you out of the bustling tourist crowds and takes you to another place altogether. The time and care taken for all the preparations was amazing and could not have been more different to having a casual cuppa at home! I am not sure they do them in English - our host spoke in Korean but our little group had an interpreter to help us out. The venue used for this ceremony is also amazing. Beautiful minimal stone and wood shaped furniture in a sunlight-filled pavilion looking out onto the lawns of the museum. We also had a glimpse into the underground tea cellar area and a quick tour round the tourist shop. The collection of tea cups from different countries and eras was fascinating too in the area next to the shop.

This museum is not the easiest to find  located in an industrial type area. Upon entrance you receive a free sample of chocolate and a hot chocolate (not sure if this was offered due to the chilly  rainy weather  but it was definitely appreciated). Some interesting finds from around the world  historical facts  and treasures. There is an area where you may observe chocolate pieces being made for sale in the adjacent gift shop. Good stop for a rainy day on Jeju Island. Gift shop is a little pricey. Teenaged daughter loved it; teenaged son was bored.

review: This museum features the history of tea in Jeju as well as you can view the tea plantation from the observation deck. You also can taste the green tea ice cream and cake at the cafe besides a good place to buy green tea. This area also features innisfree shop where you can make your own soap besides a lot of innisfree products on sale.

This museum displays many clay artwork and handicrafted items from ages. The tour guide and the ticket booth employee cannot speak English anyway. However the souvenir shop in the museum sells many wonderful things that we could buy home as gifts.

This market sell all sort of things from fresh seafood to chocolate. We bought those chocolate souvenier from here. There are many shops selling similar item.One can also buy various ready to eat food (street food kind) and there are restaurants too. One thing to take note is that dustbin is rare  so you may want to bring a plastic bag to throw your litter.
This market offer variety products from raw to ready to eat. Many stalls and shop offer local menu here. Jeju orange can be easily found here. Open till night.
This market has various souvenir shops and they are quite cheap. But make sure that you visit at least three shops for price checking.

This little folk village was located right next to our hotel (Haevachi) so we figured we should check it out.  We were spoiled because we had just gone to the folk village and that is the bomb!It is only about $8 for admission and then we opted for the audio tours.  Most of the written signs are not in English so I'm glad we had the audio tours but they didn't work very well.  They are tripped by some sort of sensor when you go by but mine kept skipping back to the original message ugggg.It's a very large complex but somehow unauthentic feeling.  I thought the neatest part was the artisans that sell their crafts.  That was cool and they do have a nice gift shop.  It was very hot out so we went through fairly quickly.  If it hadn't been so hot we might have spent much longer just exploring.If this is your only opportunity to see such a thing then I would visit but if you have the chance to see the folk village in Seoul then I would wait for that one!

This large market is located on the East side of the island. You'll find a variety of places to eats  souvenirs  fresh produces  meats  seafood and variety of other things. It's where the locals to their shopping  as the super markets are small  so it's one stop shopping. After taking a tour on that side of the island  its worth a visit to grab some fresh items if you're tired of eating out all the times  just make sure to bargain with the stall vendors.

this is the place to go for food and shopping when at Seogwipo. The market is pretty huge to walk  see and experience the everyday routines of those worked there as well as the regular stream of tourists that makes the place crowded and noisy. if you stay around Seogwipo  chances is you will be there at least once or every evening for did or to pass time. take time to go around the entire interior with multiple lanes with as well as the outside shops. You might just find interesting things to see and get something you like.

this is one of must-seen attraction in jeju they displayed all about tea from jejuthe architecture of the meseum is really nice and awesome and the shop also sells many products range from tea you also must try the cafe dish such as ice cream roll cake etc..

This is not exactly a museum  but a shop impersonating as museum  that sells teddy bear. Uses gimmick of hand make teddy bear that resembled Obama and some other celebrities  but really nothing interest unless one is crazy over teddy bear.

This is more of a shop and cafe than a museum. The museum part is just a few display cabinets that leads to a cafe with goods displayed for sale. The tea plantation across the street is a flat moderately sized area that pales in comparison to the vast rolling and picturesque tea plantation of cameron highlands.This attraction is not worth the time unless one is a tea-lover.

This is like any other market in Korea. Cheap shopping for clothes  bags  food and souvenirs. If haven't visited one of these markets  then I would go just to have the experience. Otherwise not a must see.

This is first time we experienced a visit to a Green Tea plantation. Walking between the rows & rows of beautifully layed out fragrant tea leaves was just great.The cafe sells nice Green Tea ice creams & cakes plus tea leaves products obviously.An Innisfree shop sells the famous Korean cosmetics plus a small cafe included.Certainly this is an attraction that should not be missed when in Jeju.

This is a very popular tourist destination there are a wide variety of teas for purchase and well as a little cafe to stop and chat over the famous green tea ice cream. Innesfree has a little shop in location where you can make your own soap. The only problem is to wash your hands afterwards you need to go to the bathrooms (outside) so I?셝 recommend taking some hand wipes unless you want soap everywhere. The property has a perfect spot to take photos with the tea plants and take a small stroll. This place can get very busy do either early morning or a little later in the afternoon are better times

This is a must-do! You get to the peak using staircases which allows any age group to do this activity also. There are also toilets along the way. The view of the peak as well as Jeju Island is amazing.There are shops where you can buy souvenirs. You should try the tangerine ice cream 'cuz it's yummy!
This is a great one stop shop to get souvenirs from jejuLots of korean street food available if you arekeen to try

This is a contemporary art museum by the seafront in Jeju city showcasing a private collection in a disused cinema and an old bikeshop. There are many varied exhibits from China to Germany Korea to France.we especially liked a music and light show by French artist Pierre Huyghe (l'Exp챕dition scintillante).Entry is W12000 for adults and covers both buildings.
This is a big temple with lots to see.  There are a couple of large budda statues and many small ones.  It also has a nice gift shop.It is far from downtown and a bit hard to get without a car.

This canyon was created by lava flows.When it rains water can flow down from the mountain in to the estuary. We were there during a rainy period and saw water cascading down. Our guide said in a week or two the upper area might be completely dry and sea water would fill in much of the now being filled by fresh water. Alongside the ?쐒iver??and parallel road are a number of shops particularly close to the sea. The beach at the end is black sand. Really a beautiful unique area.

This can hardly be called a museum. The museum part takes 5 maybe 10 minutes to see. After that it is nothing more than a very expensive tea shop. That being said if tea is your cup of tea you would probably enjoy trying their many different tea creations.

This area is a traditional village area with loads of space displays and things to see and do. A huge cultural complex created to show case all the various aspects of life in a Korean village. Working displays and demonstrations make the wandering around even more interesting as do the small shops that are spread throughout the complex. A really great couple of hours.

They mostly sell clothes and cosmetics here. This place is equivalent to those underground shopping centres in Seoul. It is a large space and you can try  bargaining too. Close proximity to Dongmun Market and a gem of a historical area called Gwandeokjeong.

There's not really much museum. I thought I turned a wrong corner but had actually walked through the whole thing. Just one wall of tea cups and pots and basically no English signage. But it's free and you really go for the tea shop and cafe.Nice teas for sale (spendy but tasty!) and there are often free samples in the tea shop. Then move to the cafe for some green tea flavored sweets. I recommend the softserve ice cream twisted with yogurt. If you're here take time to climb to the 3rd floor observatory for some nice views. If you have a little extra time it's worth two other stops:1) just through the garden path walk up hill to the natural skin care center where you can smell local essences and make your own natural soap (for a fee). They have nice sandwiches and snacks for sale.2) Climb the oreum (small mountain) just north of O'Sulloc. Walk along the road past the tea fields until you see a concrete paved walk in toward the hill. Follow paths or bushwack until you see the path entrance. You can walk to the top in less than an hour from O'Sulloc. There's a nice viewing platform with views toward Seogwipo from the top.

There is one shop that is in the corner and it is a MUST to go there. Its the busiest shop and you wont missed it. We tried a few black pork shops and you can tell the difference between good and great.  YUMMM!

There is nothing exciting with the Jeju Chilsung Fashion Street. It is a series of open-air pedestrian-only road lined with boutiques. The stores were familiar such as Starbucks New Balance Spyder MLB Tommy Hilfiger Crocs and Adidas although there are some designs that are available here that are not yet available in the Philippine market.The place was supposed to be part of the Jeju Winter Festival. Indeed there were a number of Christmas-themed displays although they were nothing compared to how lavish the Christmas displays in the Philippines are.I only strolled around the area then went to the Dongmun Market nearby. The Jungang Underground Shopping District is also close?봞s it was winter it was more comfortable shopping at the heated underground location of Jungang that it was in Chilsungro. Also the items sold at Chilsungro are from brands that are more known internationally (and thus are more expensive) than what is available at Jungang.
There is no chocolate model  just Chocolate shop  don't think to go there. its poorest chocolate museum in the world.

There is nearly no advertisement for this museum in the city. I saw the sign at the traffic and wanted to give it a try. The building is so small that when i arrived I thought it will be a quick tiny event. But once you are inside you will be amazed by the beauty and the variety of seashells. Most of the explanations are in Korean but still nothing can stop you to enjoy this museum. At the roof  there is a giant shell  which you can go in and have a photo. There is also a small shop where you can buy gifts to your loved ones and something for yourself too.

There is a very small museum-ish area which shows a variety of teas. But basically its a shop for their products and the cafe.  You can try their signature green tea products which are also available in all their cafes around the country.  They have a nice viewing deck area where you can look out onto the tea fields.  The tea fields are also accessible so that you can stand amongst them to take photos.  Watch out for the spiders.

There is a cafe and merchandise shop in the tea museum which seems like it is the main attraction of the museum. So go early to beat the tour groups. If you are not a sweet tooth skip the green tea latte. Go for the soft serve ice cream. Do not miss the plantations. Plenty of photo opportunities if you venture into the green tea plantations

There aren't a lot of stuff you can do here unless you join the chocolate making class which costs around 20 000won including the kit. The good thing is that the entry fee (3 000 won) may be used to purchase anything here. There's a small shop that sells ice cream here so it's a good place to rest.
There are workshops and cafe in it along with sculptures showing the tea making process. Must try their samdayeon ice cream in their cafe.

There are many interesting places to visit in jeju. Limited range of products. Disappointing. That is why I am giving it low rating. Soap making? All stations are full.. You don?셳 see products flying off the shelves. And neither do you see people walking out of store with lots of shopping. Telling signs! Go next door. Osulloc Tea Museum. Eat and spend there...

There are a lot of food choices in the market  especially a lot of shops selling the Jeju oranges and Jeju orange juice. You can easily get souvenirs from the market. Most of the shop keepers can speak English/Mandarin. There is a free car park just 1 min on foot from the market  another one with charge right inside the market.
The world cup stadium from 2002 is now the home of jeju united.Nice stadion with some shopping around. If you're in the area nice to see but not worth an extra trip.

The village is huge explaining about the cultures of jeju folks. Plenty of photo shooting corners beautiful flowers farm.There is also a shop renting korean traditional clothes (hanbok renting) where you can wear the clothes and walk around the village for photo shooting. the price is reasonable (comparable to those hanbok renting shop in jeju city)estimate to spend 3 hours there.youth and kids got discount for the entrance fee (do bring passport along)is a must visit spot if you come to jeju.

The usual suspects (green tea roll matcha soft serve etc) are good of course but I also had a delicious cup of Houjicha Latte. It was perfect for a cool spring day sitting out in the O'sulloc back garden. Definitely deserves a repeat order.The O'sulloc shop here has many varieties of tea as well as skincare. Bought a pack of jeju green tea bags - when I opened the packet a most delicious aroma of roasted tea leaves greeted me.
The tea fields covers a large area green and pleasant.  The shops offer many special green tea items.  We had green tea ice cream and it?셲 soooo delicious.

The Stadium is closed almost all the week long except when a match is there  no visits are allowed inside  may be because that was in winter. The nice thing is that you can picture it from outside inside in  and a nearby small shops community & large e-Market place to shop & eat in their food-court. Nice play ground area around to check & may be to practice for free  you can see the local folks play around with some apparatuses  and machines to fit up
The place is well kept and there was a lovely souvenir shop on site. There is not much to see in this part of Jeju so climbing up this rock was definitely an uplifting experience.
The place is very nice. However during weekends and holidays the lines for the tea shop are very long. So make sure to line up early on the visit to ensure you get to taste their tea!

The place is quite far from the main town but it's worth it if you are a fan for green tea. There's a simple exhibition on history of green tea. Then there's the O'Sulloc shop and cafe which is full of green tea products and food. The green tea latte green tea ice cream and the green tea log cake are the 3 things must try in the cafe. The only bad thing is that the cafe is a bit too crowded and noisy to enjoy such nice tea.

The place is a bit run down and really short of foot traffic. We were accosted when we stepped into the museum shops. The entrance fee is relatively steep for Jeju - 12k for each adult.The exhibits are tasteful in my opinion but the rust is showing. For the entrance fee I expect to receive at least a small souvenir.

The O쨈Sulloc Tea Museum and tea field is a treat!  It쨈s easy to get to by the airport bus we got to it by taking the Yeha West Tour.Be prepared for crowds in the cafe.  However if you go across the road to the tea fields it쨈s easy to walk along the tea plants and be alone in a field of green tea.The museum is interesting and explains the tea picking and fermentation process.The real fun is the cafe and shopping for tea!  It쨈s a bit overwhelming but fascinating to think that so many types of tea can be produced with one leaf!O쨈Sulloc also sells a cosmetic line I haven쨈t tried any of those products so I can쨈t comment on their cosmetics versus all the other great stuff that Korea has for skin care. The cafe offers the most delicious green tea ice cream.  I쨈m dying to try the cakes but can쨈t get pass the ice cream.  There is also a brown roasted tea ice cream but I prefer the green tea one.  It isn쨈t sweet and has a distinctive green tea flavor left on your palate as you get ready for the next bite.Recommendation--I got the Cold Green Sticks which are perfect for a bottle of water.  The other teas you definitely need a strainer otherwise get the tea in teabags.Oh and O짢Sulloc has a cafe in the Nampo area in Busan if you need your green tea ice cream fix. Other cafes have green tea ice cream but OSulloc is yummy and my favorite.O쨈Sulloc seems to be branding itself as a high end tea so you just can쨈t purchase it in a grocery store nor do the hotels have it as complimentary tea a shame since it is a Korean brand. So stock up and enjoy.

The owner of the museum is an artist himself and one of the most important collectors in the world. I was totally taken away with many of the artworks and with the location itself(specially the Bike-Shop and the Cinema). One of my reasons for traveling South-Korea is discovering and enjoying modern art. This is the best collection I have seen in this country so far (out of around 30 museums and galleries). I was totally surprised to see this level of Art in Jeju and will definitely visit Arario in Space when I am back to Seoul.

The Osulloc Tea Museum is located around 30 mins from Seogwipo and 35 mins from Jeju city.This pleasant venue is comprised of the Tea Museum a shop a coffee place a cosmetics shop and the tea fields.We didn't visit the museum as we are familiar with the processes. Instead we visited the coffee shop where we had a Sejak green tea an ice cream and a slice of roll cake. Everything was good!We also bought some tea cosmetics and hung around the tea plantation.

The Osulloc Tea Museum is just not a tea museum but I would rather say a tea complex which includes a Tea Cup Gallery various Tea Culture Rooms such as exhibition hall masters of tea vessels tea life center etc. tea caf챕 and tea gardens. Tea Museum also offers a premium tea class in which brewing our own green tea and sharing with friends during the premium tea class is one of the unique experiences so far in Jeju. In the class they not only explain tea and tea brewing methods but also demonstrate the use of various tea wares and their importance in making one good cup of tea. In the end it was a good memorable day to make and drink green tea. Besides museums souvenir shops and green tea caf챕 there are few tea gardens and resting areas where people can enjoy nature relax and take pictures to keep their memory forever.

The museum part of the building was only about 2 small rooms with a bit of history of tea-making.  Most of the rest was taken up by the gift shop and cafe.The green tea (Swiss) roll which is their iconic cake was sold out completely on the day we were there even though it was only about 11am.  Made do with green tea and tangerine soft serve ice-cream and tea.  The tangerine tea was beautifully presented in a stoneware cup and tasted better than the green tea.There are very limited food choices for a full meal and this is more a snack cafe.  The food at nearby Innisfree is much better with a wider range.  Eventually we had the green tea cake back in Seoul where it was easily available at the O Sulloc outlets in Myeongdong.

The museum is located in the middle of the tea garden and the air around the place is so fresh. The museum explains to you quite in detail about the tea history and next to the museum there is a shop and cafe selling product from osulloc. Very very nice place to visit especially the garden area. However this is a very touristy place too and quite far to access.

The museum is limited in size but the fantastic shop and cafe make up for that. The history is interesting but the ability to smell and taste teas is awesome!  Highly recommend the Hallabong Fredo!  The green tea was great too. Pretty views of the landscape.
The museum is easy to navigate and move about and there are enough exhibits around. About 1 to 2 hours here would be enough. There is also a nice souvenir shop in the complex.

The museum has a wonderful shop where you can buy amazing varieties of tea. All of them wonderful flavors. If you like tea this is the best place to visit and to spend a lot of money in high quality products.Also they have a coffee shop with the best green tea ice cream and green tea roll cake.

The museum can be improved with more English explanation. Go to the open air top for the best 360 view of the area and plantation. There are signs at the plantation warning of snakes but none spotted during our visit. There is a crowd at the cafe and shop but the turnover is quick as most of them followed a group tour and hence can't linger that long. You can get a seat if you are not in a rush. The stuff are expensive but it won't deter a green tea fan. Do be extra careful when crossing the roads to the opposite car parks. The cars and trucks are speed demons.

The museum becomes busier as the day goes on really busy late in the day so going early is the best plan to be stress free and see everything with little to no people there for best photo experiences.The museum is really cool and covers Korean tea history. It leads to the tea shop where you can sample some good tea cakes and teas. You can also purchase teas here as well as other tea confections.Next to the museum short 5 minute walk is the Innisfree Jeju House which I cover in another review. You can get lunch and some fresh teas to enjoy here. There is also great tea and Jeju House related products as well as fun tea soap making kits. Ones you can do there and others that you can take home.Before lunch at Innishouse but after tea and snack at the Tea Museum you should walk the plantation. Great photos in the fields next to the tea museum but across the street are two areas one with a big tree that is old an beautiful but also a tree with deep red blossom that makes for a great photo with Hallasan in the background.The Stone House was closed for renovations when we visited in April 2018.

The mountain's peak itself was covered with fog signaled rain will soon came pouring. I did not hike the mountain as the weather is somewhat not on my side. Just walk along the canola field in front of the mountain and snap some photos. There are paid field if you want to take photo with better view costs around KRW1000. I walked down heading to Yongmeori Coast but ended up in a small snack shop called Mongma Reukabuden. The shop owner is very nice person. While I had my Cheese Octopus Bread with Hallabong Juice the rain started to pour down. It was just drizzling at first as I finish my last bite of the octopus bread the drizzles turned to somewhat heavy downpour. The shop owner's wife generously gave me a new raincoat that never been used. Though they were speaking in local Korean and all I could understood bits and pieces of what she tried to convey in her effort to tell me to have this raincoat with no charge. I was solo traveling and generous shown by strangers really moved me ?졼뀪 For that piece of raincoat I humbly thanks them!

The little museum has a simple collection of vintage tea cups from around the world. I am obsessive about tea cups so was very happy with the unplanned encounter. There was a small section on the history of tea but unfortunately for us it was mostly written in Korean. The place was buzzing even after its opening hours. Service was quick and friendly. Wide tea selection no lesser than the two O?셎ulloc stores in Insadong and Myeongdong. Above average tea beverages and desserts. (For green tea fan who is familiar with Japanese tea - this is the Tsujiri equivalent of Korea).As some reviewers has mentioned this is a tea shop+cafe+museum so don?셳 expect just a museum.

The Koreans we were traveling with said that this was the largest folk village they had ever been to.  It is very large with many many huts buildings and gardening examples.  Sunscreen and good walking shoes are a must.  This is not a quick in/out place.  There are several restaurants inside.  There is a Jeju cactus fruit taffy shop inside that will give you free samples - so yummy we had to buy a few bags to bring home!This is also a popular tourist destination but the place is so big that it never felt overcrowded anywhere we were except the entrance.  There are waterfalls a maze flower gardens and many little shops tucked in here and there all over the place.  There are restrooms near the main entrance.If you want to experience an almost overwhelmingly large example of Korean folk history this is your place!

The Joanne Bear Museum is one of the stops in the package tour that we availed of. It is basically a collection of stuffed bears that Joanne Oh has created  each bear hand made. There are three buildings where all the bears are housed. We were there in winter and the place was well-heated. The pathway between the buildings were open air  though. The bears came in different sizes  colors and variations. There are some depict historical or cultural scenes  others depict pop culture. The bears are all finely crafted. Unfortunately though  many of the signage are in Korean only.There are several displays where guests can pose with the bears. One of those bears  a polar bear  was featured in a Korean drama  ?쏱aradise Ranch.??I especially loved the displays that feature the acronym of the place (JB) because it is my initial as well. There is a souvenir shop which sell?봸ou guessed it right?봲tuffed bears. I wanted to have one as a souvenir so I was settling for the least expensive keychain bear when I saw a much larger 8-inch plushie being sold at a discounted rate; it was only 2 000 won more expensive than the keychain so I got it instead. As with many of the Joanne bears  it an embroidery of Joanne Oh's signature.

The highest mountain in South Korea.  Several paths and some are easily accessible by public bus.  I chose the one to the summit up and down.  Clear sign and a small shop before going up the summit.  Good view.  Can get a certificate to the summit in the park office.

The green tea museum was nice.  They had tea sets from around the world from many different ages.  The gift shop had free green tea sampling which was quite delicious.  They also had a cafe where you can buy green tea roll cakes ice cream and lattes.
The green tea latte is nice ! Not too sweet for me ! Just nice !  Went over to Innisfree shop ! Taxi fare from Jeju SkyPark hotel till there  cost me around won 32000!
The green tea ice cream is good and I enjoyed the hallabong O tea ice that the top not cream but ice cream. Delicious. A good place to shop for authentic tea in Jeju .

The glass museum is well presented and extremely pleasant environment!While the building seems modern and edgy the products are sweet rather than overly modern! If the gift shop is not making a huge profit it is because the gifts seem dated!

The entrance is an orange frame which juts our of the ground so it will be really hard to miss. But If you go for flashy shopping centre then this place is not for you. There?s a lot on sale if you take the time to browse through. Unfortunately I am the type who goes for flashy shopping centre so we just came in and breeze through.

The entire place is quite nicely run by Amore Pacific who owns large green tea fields and cosmetic brands such as Innisfree. The tea museum is a small setup which links directly to the retail section. Don't expect much from the museum but the retail section is a heaven for tea fans! Adjacent to the tea museum is the local specialty shop of Innisfree. Checkout the Jeju specials such as green tea essential oil. Surrounding these 2 building are endless stretches of green tea farms.

The chocolate museum was a highlight of our Jeju trip in 2020  the fresh chocolate made by the resident chocolatier is a real treat. Be aware that not only the quality  but also the price of the chocolate is on an international level  with a decent-sized box going for some 30 dollars. But for buying three boxes  we got three tickets for a chocolate making workshop  which was greatly enjoyed by the kids.We will come again  if only to get some memorable treats. The museum itself is informative  but don't expect too much.

review: The car drives  up the road by itself! Great fun. ( visual effect)It only works one way. You need to drive in neutral towards the shops. If you arrived from Jejusi do a U turn after the shops to experience the effect. The effect is quite spectacular with a water bottle placed in the middle of the road. You will see clearly the bottle rolling up.

The brochure states that is a glass castle. This is definitely not a glass castle but a fun museum  so if you have kids and they are expecting to see a Cinderella kind of environment  well  this is not .What you find though it's the explanation on how glass in made and transformed in different shapes (entrance) to different kind of finished product. If you want  you can also have a go (helped by professionals)!It's a good  small scale museum and it's quite entertaining and educational. A mention of honor goes to the ticket guy at the entrance. On our way out we asked him to help us out to get a taxi. He was the sweetest and hard-core-customer orientated guy I saw in action in Jeju (and  I must admit they are all very good). He tried to get a taxi for us  getting the price  helping us (mind you  his English was limited  so he struggled a lot but nonetheless worked hard to explain us everything he could) and even giving us for free a cold bottle of water whilst waiting outside (for the taxi). You could see he was really trying his best and I hope someone from the Museum will read this feed-back and rewarding him.One thing I would avoid is the Coffee Shop inside the museum. You will find a girl with a grudge (promise you...the whole time)  doing nothing but playing with her mobile and almost being upset by you interrupting her during her game. I think this is the only person in Jeju I have found soooooooo..... unhappy and customer unfriendly? Maybe the ticket guy could teach her?Another note: you can get a 30% reduction ticket for the submarine a few kilometers away.

The beach area as well as the water are looking clean. The sand is white. We did not go in since it was late October. The view is nice and the neighbourhood has shops and restaurants available. There is a coffee shop directly at the beach where you can rest if you find a place to rest. Usually the shop is quite crowded. At night time some fireworks ongoing. We had the Golden Tulip hotel and we were enjoying the view to the beach every morning.
The area is littered with shops and restaurants and an underground shopping mall.Discovering this gem was truly a delight. Area is a bit small but admission fee is only 1500\ for adults.

The architecture of this conference centre is the first exciting and majestic comment on the centre. It has big conference rooms with the best facilities to host big events. I attended the international mercury conference here and the logistics of the venue provided us with a flawless event. There are also several fast food restaurants at the bottom level of the centre  with a duty free shop on the other side. It is a local attraction and the visitors seem to enjoy it too  since it was constantly busy. On the second floor is a curio shop for some gifts from Jeju.The airport limousine bus no 600 stops outside entrance of the venue  but there are local taxis frequently available to take you anywhere.

The aquarium is spacious.  You can see a lot of sea animals no matter how hot cold or rainy the outdoor is.  Taking a leaflet at the entrance is a must because the show time is up-dated.  It is so funny to see the penguins line up to eat food and jump up the stairs.  The otters are also interesting when you see them playing through the tunnels and on the swinging bed.  The 'stars' of the aquarium can be seen at the theatre which is attractive and interesting. My family stayed there for more than three hours.  The soft toys sold there are in good quality and my daughter bought a penguin as a souvenir.  There are food shops for people to enjoy but we didn't try any.
