review: The Alive Museum is an exhibit of life-sized optical illusions of which you can pose with for some really fun photos.  Admission was 10000 won ($10 USD) each.  It will take you between 60 and 90 minutes to get through the exhibits.  There are more than 100 photo opportunities.  Make sure you arrive with a charged camera or camera phone.  I would not recommend going alone as you would have nobody to take your photo.  An ice cream and coffee shop is located towards the end of the museum.Highly recommended.  We are glad we went.

The Alive Museum in Seogwipo is a pretty nice museum that is near a number of good restaurants and is definitely not hard to get to on foot. For 11000 won you can take photos with plenty of crazy cute and cool paintings all over the museum; this is definitely their specialty. I really enjoyed some of the paintings especially the ones near the picture of the wings that makes you look like an angel. The gift shop at the end and of course the mandatory photos taken of you upon coming in are really overpriced and we didn't go outside because it was so cold out but the inside was pretty worth it to get so many cool photo opportunities. If you're not into taking pictures though this museum probably isn't for you.
That?셲 all you see for acres and acres. Don?셳 expect to shop for their products here. You are better off purchasing Innisfree products from their retail outlets all over Seogwipo or Jeju City.

Tea Plantations are not my favourite places and this is not a museum as such. But the way the Koreans have done this makes it into a relaxing afternoon experience. The cherry blossoms just came out when we visited. There were scores of Korean students on a field trip but that's OK. It's spacious enough for everyone. A short display of tea cups from around the world lines the entrance of the building. Then it's tea shopping and testing. Try the buckwheat tea! Lots of chinese speaking staff (as with everywhere else in Seoul). Here I tasted the best green tea ice cream and cake. A walk in the surrounding garden and compound is nice. There is a glass building next to the main one by Korean brand Innisfree. In it there are soap making activities a cafe and skin care shopping.
Take your time to explore the surroundings you feel the inspiration more and BTW the shop over there is reasonably priced

Sunrise Peak. Sunset PeakWe travelled as part of a tour and on arriving were given the usual coach departure time. 1hour in this instance! Not sure of the entrance fee as it was included in our tourNot hanging around we set off immediately for the top with several good rests in between. The pathway is steep in places but in good order with plenty of resting/passing places. Separate paths up and down. Quite a climb but well worth it. Half way up is a little stall/shop for soft drinks and snacks (they have to manhandle everything up!)Once at the top there are plenty of viewing spots. Really worth the climb. We witnessed a superb sunset over the island and took some wonderful photosOn the path down there is a WC.We made the round journey just about in time with 15mins at the peak and a wander around the cliff edge on the way downFrom what I?ve heard the sunset is equally as breathtaking as the sunrise but not as crowded. Sunset was at approx 7.30 and on the way down the path is fairly well lit

strictly for those above 18.but beware that buses come here ends early.after 10pm i only see taxis and cars.Interesting stone sculptures of male and female organs.sex positions..a shop selling interesting condoms and penis keychains vibrators etc..super cold at night..open until midnight..there is a indoor museum and show clay figurines..

Strictly for adults this open air museum has many stone sculptures of male and female in various positions. There is also an indoor museum with miniature clay figurines a souvenir shop and a food stall within the compound. Admission fee 12.000 won. Suggest you combine this place with the nearby Nexon Computer Museum.Transport tip: From the airport take bus 331 332 465 466 at airport bus stand 6 between gates 4 & 5. Alight at Jeju Museum of Art walk 400m. Bus fare is 1150 won journey about 30 mins.

Steep climb up the hill but the view worth every step. The stair halfway up is quite steep and a bit of a challenge if u have a bad knee. The best time to go is either for sunset or sunrise. There is only 1 shop to buy water up there. Make sure you have your water with you for the climb.

Spent a few hours at the museum along with many many others! Small building with some good information but crowds crammed the shop which leads into the cafe. This caused overcrowding and did not make for the most enjoyable afternoon. Outdoors area is worth wandering through and the gardens and fields are worth looking at. The Innisfree Jeju House across the way is probably more interesting.

Songaksan was one of the places that had actually a very small crowd of tourists so it make the hike a bit more enjoyable. At the foot of the mountain is a large parking lot with some coffee shops and restaurants from there it is a light hike up the mountain. Lots of greenery and nice views along the way. The center which I believe is a crate is closed right now I think for recovery from too many tourists. it is still a good destination to visit the hike is easy and relaxing peaceful and enjoyable.

Some sports brand but nothing exciting. We came twice but still we did not find any shops we like. Compared to shops in Seoul this is pale. Most shops selling winter coats. At end of this street turn left and just outside the wet market we find a shop bang bang. They have 2 floors lower for women and second for men. Managed to get some simple t shirts. Design was just very simple. Other than these nothing exciting here. The wet market is more exciting with tourists the korean snacks there were great! Here in this shopping street you get cafe. Very quiet cos winter. There is a shop selling desugner embroudery hackets and jeans gor guys but very expensive. The staff was speaking cantonese to the chinese customers so we assume Hong Kong shop. Nicer Jackets were $500 onwards.

So you get to this place and will be faced with mountains of oranges  pork knuckles and fish. Bet its the place to be if your mission is to get groceries or some local snacks.But if you want to buy souvenior  this place isn't really ideal as most stuff 竊늨ranges you can't take overseas  fishe neither;packed snacks are like what you can see all over the island 竊뎤eems a bit mass produced.The interesting to observe is that most shops are ran by one solo lady  only. They took a lot of hardship to get the business running .

So this is more a shop than a museum to me. But the cafe there is highly recommended!! You need to try the green tea cakes and the cookies as well! Wish i could've tried the ice cream but i was afraid i get sick. It's literally the best roll cake. The garden was nice and you can make your own shop at innisfree didnt have enough time though.. Remember to take pictures at the cup made of plants across the street..

Small tea plantation in front of cafe and Innisfree shop. Must try the latte tea and the cake. Innisfree shop is nothing extra-ordinary. Worth a short visit. You can also enjoy the tea and cake back in town at Myeondong.

Slow and sleepy village. Hardly see any activities from the people living here. Where have they gone to?Saw some shops selling food and stuff.The village is preserved in the traditional way of the early generations. Good for educational purpose but you need a guide who is able to explain the meaning of their livelihood.

Since Chinese-Korean relationship became worse there is huge decrease in tourists from china which resulted in many shops shutting down. Half a street is empty now so there's not much choice of shopping. However big shops are still good (new balance and such). You'll see almost no people there.

Seriously the number of people that were there on a sunny afternoon stressed us out. It almost seemed like a one drop shop rather than a museum. There was very little to see in terms of the museum the shop and the cafe were f***ing noisy and busy we couldn't even walk through. We had set B which included a green tea roll cake a hallabong drink and a green tea ice cream. Very average. SKIP!

Seriously stunning display of flowers at Camellia Hill; the biggest arboretum in Asia famous for its forest path and beautiful gardens of camellias. The arboretum is home to 6000 camellia trees of 500 different species including species that are known to produce the world?셲 largest and earliest blossoms. The place is drop-dead gorgeous and I would of spent a whole day adoring the different flowers if I wasn't rushing to maximise my day in Jeju.We were lucky to catch the early blooms of the Cherry Blossoms which was a major highlight of the trip for us. Towards the end of the trail is a small shop that should desserts coffee and souvenirs like postcards and cosmetics. I loved their postcard selection and went a little crazy on those souvenirs but no regrets. My brother enjoyed his homemade strawberry ice cream as it was packed full of flavour!

Run by a tea company that touts itself to be a premium tea brand the tea museum is nothing more than a small exhibition of some historical earthern ware and the owner's/ company statement about bringing back Korean tea culture to modern society.It has a tea shop (their tangerine and Camellia teas are good) cafe (very crowded but has really good green tea sets  for two consisting of ice cream a drink and green tea Swiss roll) and a tea workshop area called the Tea Stone situated in a garden. There's also a tea plantation where you can score some good photos or just simply take a quiet peaceful stroll through the greenery.Nearby is the innisfree Jeju House which also has a cafe selling some of their beauty products. The selection isn't great and they don't  give you free samples though you could score some Jeju only products. I find going to Myeongdong for your K beauty haul much more satisfying and easier on the wallet. Or if you just wanna stop by for their DIY soap making activity (they also sell the kit at the store so you can do it on your own) it seems like a peaceful way to escape the hustle and bustle of the city.

Rows of organic tea plantations for cha lovers to scent savour and calm the senses.  A must-go on tourist itinerary so be prepared for crowds.  Long queues at the cafe for tea desserts.  Check out exquisite Samdayeon (?쇰떎??is a Korean post-fermented tea matured for a hundred days in barrels made out of cedar wood from Jeju Island) soft ice cream unique to Jeju shop only. Interesting tea blends and gifts at the tea shop. Don't miss the outdoor fields across from the museum for kettle and cup shaped plant sculptures and windmills for photo taking. A walking path connects to Innisfree Jeju House for more afternoon tea Innisfree products and craft making classes for young and old.

Rented a driver for 9hrs for KR150K look for an english speaking driver that can act as a tour guide as well. Have to provide for driver's meal as well.There is an Inisfree shop onsite however there are many Inisfree in Myeongdong so if you are visiting Seoul can simply skip the shop and visit other tourist spots.The green tea ice-cream is nice but for KR5000 it is abit over-priced.Nice place to visit while visiting the West Coast side in Jeju.
Relaxing ambience & fun workshop

Really enjoyed our visit but would say it is more of a shopping venue than museum but we really enjoyed trying different types of green tea and also green tea icecream!!!We would have enjoyed more if more of the history had been shared
Read online reviews is a must to come here. We went to the first shop 穩 for our dinner. We will be back again!

Plenty of interesting glass installations in the park and museum. Really worth to see. Very nice and friendly owner. Many beautiful things and funny toys in the shop. The best way to get there is by taxi  it's about $15 from Seogwipo city center.
Perfect place for renting a bike and it takes about 1.5 to 2 hours to paddle around the island. Coffee shops and attranctions along the way.
Pales in comparison to Osulloc Tea Museum but it's worth a look since they are side by side. The products in the gift shop are the widely available Innisfree facial products.

Our first stop in the Jeju trip was the Olloc Tea Museum.Here you can take a master class about how to make tea properly and try different kinds of teas.It was a very relaxing experience and the taste of the tea was very unique.If you like tea is definitely something you have to do if you travel to Jeju.Also you can visit the Innisfree shop right next to the museum and take beautiful pictures in the green tea fields around.

Our 4yo liked it well enough. We spent about 2hrs and spent more money at the gift shop than on admission (24000 won) and if it were nicer out we probably would have spent longer. Botanical garden a small garden maze Fossil museum animal feeding station bird attraction and the really TALL dinosaurs scattered throughout made for an enjoyable afternoon outing before nap time.

O'Sulloc Tea Museum is very small (there are not many displays to see) but there is a very large shop that sells tea products and a cafe that sells drinks and desserts.  There is a very brief tea tasting demonstration w/ narrative in Korean only.  In the cafe we had the best green tea ice cream and green tea roll cake we've ever tasted.  Prices for drinks & dessert was expensive ($4.50USD each for a small cup of ice cream and a slice of cake; $8.00USD for a large glass of orchid flavored iced green tea).  The tea products in the shop are also expensive.  If you are a tea connoisseur then this is the place for you.  Across the street from the museum there is an open field where the leaves are grown that you can walk around.  There is a viewing tower above the museum where you can also see the tea fields.  If you are exploring the west side of Jeju island O'Sulloc makes a great rest stop. I would not deliberately drive all the way out there just to visit this museum.

O'Sulloc Tea Museum  is actually a shopping paradise for those who fancy for tea. O'Sulloc itself is famous for its Tea product. In front there's a collection of used cups that they arranged in such a way so it's picturesque.Since It's a green tea field expect for green tea product for sale including all side products (Cake Drinks etc). The shop available also allows us to test some of their products We let ourself went down to the greentea field and see what's actually a green tea look like when it's not harvested yet. We also have a little chat with the tea-picker ajumma. If you go to the upper floor you will be able to take picture of overall green tea field but don't expect too much.I recommend time of visit when the sun not in its brightest Enjoy!

O'sulloc is famous for its green tea plantation. It attracts plenty of tourists who frequent the place. In one building it shows all types of green tea with tea demos. Many people comes here to buy excellent tea quality for personal use. You can also eat in its tea shop with green tea latte and green tea ice cream for taste. On another building they sell tea as a cosmetics or other uses of green tea. All in all it is very informative and zen in design. Price are very reasonable.
Ossuloc is a very popular brand in Korea. However when we got here there's a project day occured so the shop is closed for public. But we still can take a photo in tea farm located across the shop.
Organic soap making workshop and green tea snacks

Opposite the museum is the tea field which you can walk across the road to take a photo and see how they grow the tea tree. There's parking space beside the museum. Besides there's the tea cafe and souvenir shop at the arrival floor. I would recommend the green tea smoothie top with soft cream green tea latte and green tea roll cake. It's very crowd with tourists and local people. So normally the seat are full. So if you go with friend I'd recommend one to fine the seat and one to queue up to get drink and desserts. Even its long queue to buy but it doesn't keep you wait too long. The green tea spread is the signature. There're also many selection of tea with nice packages and different aromas for your selection.
one of Main tourist object. You must use your image to get the head. A lot shop on the way which attract tourist to spend more time than the main object.

On our way back from Gahina Tea Pottery we were close-by the Tea Museum.  Many buses leave from there for Jeju and Seogwipo making this a convenient place to have a hot beverage.  Yes there is no entrance fee and that seems to be because it is mostly a gift shop and tea room.  That said the tea is lovely making for great gifts and the green tea ice cream quite tasty.  Clean bathrooms and a lovely building make this a nice place to pass through for a quick stop.

On February 2019 I visit Jeju Island I go to O?셲ulloc Tea Shop This shop store provide tea product Tea  Ice cream green tea bakery mix with Green Tea all very yummy. All decorations in shop very good have outside and inside  all staff is good service.

Okay this is pretty common on Jeju I guess. There are lots of museums that copy each other and it confuses tourists. This listing is an example of that. The reviews for this listing is a mix for the Museum of Sex and Health and for Loveland there is no actual listing on here for Loveland. We did our research first to decide which one to go to and Loveland looked like the more fun one - a lot of the pictures of outdoor sculptures on this listing are actually from Loveland not the Museum of Sex and Health). I'm not even if they both have the outdoor sculptures. Loveland is mostly outdoors but it does have an indoor section too with a shop and a diorama exhibit (if you're strapped for time you can probably skip the indoor part it's not very long and the exhibits inside are mostly in Korean so if you can't read it you have to extrapolate things for yourself). The park is fun a lot of it is very silly (they even designed the bathrooms in the spirit of the park - have a look at the door handles).

Okay if visitor is kind of tea lover. Like being here for shopping which is not that extraordinary or the must spot. Just okay for the museum zone and cafe easy and relaxing tea field or area to walk but not that wow anyway. For food and drinks good but for cake and desserts I personally feel soso. For the shop and products' variety are good. Free parking on site.

Nothing much to shop as underground complex is quite small. Had Doni burger which was not bad (near exit 5). Other than that it's not really worth a visit as there are better stuff to do at jeju. Spent 6d5n in jeju and didn't finish what we set out for.

Nothing much here if you are not a tea people or if you are not the type who takes selfies. This is a great place for instagram pictures and selfie with the tea plantation in the background. After all the selfies there is inmisfree shop and cafe but i would reccommend to drink at O'Sullic Cafe itself as the cakes and tea are very nice. Its quite sad that they close at 6pm! Didnt get to enjoy much at the cafe but we did enjoy and took lots of selfie at the tea plantation area!
Not to badmay go for a visit..Entrance fee is 8000Won for adult and 6000Won for children.There are old korean movie playing therealso korean 60's70's shops displayand etc

Not so much a museum as much as a gift shop on a tea field. I live right next door and it's always super busy (not sure why). The land is really beautiful with rolling tea fields but it is not a museum just an insanely overpriced gift shop. But if you're in the area it's definitely worth a visit.
Not so great but for a small place like Jeju .....good to go if you have a day to spare. Lots of eateries around & cosmetic shops as well.
Not all the shops are open when we arrived at 12pm. Do try the fried doughnut (500-1000won)!! There's a multi story carpark beside.

Normally as everyone is aware that the aquarium always be busy and crowd with people. Here also crowd but it's not too tight since the space is very big. Once we get into the aquarium you can buy the ticket at the lobby and the restroom is in the left. The lobby is very large so you won't get stuck with people.They will give the wristband tag and you get into aquarium on the right. You will experience sea animals like other aquarium separated into sections and time zone. The difference that I found its better is there have the seating at like the stadium in front of grand aquarium so we can sit and relax there.If you come at the right timeYou will see the special diving show by the local lady whom dive deep and find the seafood stuffs. So you will see the way of local people living as well.There's also the show available but the ticket would be different. At the end of tunnel you will see the souvenir shop which I think the items are not too expensive.I think it's better than other place I have been since some places you may see people more than sea animals.At the exit of aquarium you can see the nice scenic view of Hallasan Mountain

Nice spot for photo taking as there is a tea plantation whereby tourist pose for photos...Across the plantation sits the Tea Museum whereby you can shop for tea related products and have a drink/bite in the cafe to chill.Next to the Tea Museum is the innisfree shop whereby they conduct hands-on soap making class if one is keen.
Nice place to shop top quality teas. But usually very crowded. Innisfree store is less crowded than tea shop so go there to eat dessert.

Nice museum with plenty of green tea variety product. Nice display with fresh tea selection for packaging. A huge bar like tea shop serving green tea base ice cream drinks and dessert. A short stroll bring us to innisfree workshop for DIY moulding your own soap bar and Innisfree natural oil for your own packaging to do. Overall nice experience and price is reasonable
Nice but you should also check out the underground shopping it's great. For souvenirs clothes cosmetics etc...

Next to Innisfree is O'Sulloc Tea House. Other than information on the history of O'Sulloc and Korea Tea Culture the most attractive feature for tourist is the cafe and the shop. I did not compare the price of tea so I can't provide much information on that. However in my opinion (no offense) the tea there is not that great. It may smell nice but the taste is not rich and complex enough. But the green tea powder is worth the price if you love green tea. Move on to the cafe. It seems like there are no much varieties compare to the branch at Myeongdong so if you are going to Seoul too may as well visit the O'Sulloc house at Myeongdong. The green tea ice cream is rich and smooth. The cake roll available in Jeju is  onlywith vanila cream filling which is not nice at all compare to the green tea filling at Myeongdong.

Never would have guessed but there's shopping  eating  a water park and movie theater at the world stadium. Jeju triathlon was headquartered here so I did that business. You can put on Hanboks (Korean clothing) and take pictures as well  that's all free.

My review is a little late but it's better late than never. We've visited this place when I was four months pregnant and I was able to hike up to the summit. This place is serene. It's breathtaking to see the wonderful view when you've reach the top. The kids love the lush greens at the hilly part of this place. It's very well-maintained. There are souvenir shops located at the entrance of the park.

My friend and I enjoyed the hike up the stairs to the top and the view of Jejudo was worth the hike up. Took roughly 10-15 minutes to get up. There are rest stops on the way to the top. There are shops on the bottom if you need some energy before or after the walk :)

My 5yr old loved it very much. Lots of dinosaurs on display outdoor. Several exhibitions on site such as fossils and seashells. Areas where you can interact with animals (feeding ponies and gerbils.) You also get to see parrots next to the gift shop. It's not a very big place. we spent about 2 hours there. We got a taxi there and the man at the ticket hut(speaks good English) was very kind to help us get a taxi back to hotel. A very enjoyable and pleasant place to visit if you like dinosaurs and animals.

My 10 yo daughter and I have really enjoyed seeing the waterfall. It was a quick 20 minute walk up a scenic paved path with some other small falls. It was definitely worth a visit. Cost couple won to get in. There are several shops right outside and along the way to buy souvenirs and snacks.

Must visit for anyone who visits Jeju even though its more of an extended cafe/shop more than a museum. There is a small section dedicated to the history of tea and brewing/drinking techniques and apparatus but wouldn't call it a museum as such.There is also a nice area round the back to take photos and take in the scenery as well as an Innisfree attached to it.The cafe is the main attraction as it serves tea/cakes and ice cream to visitors and it is definitely up there with the best green tea ice cream I've had. After visiting a branch in Seoul we had to go to the origin of the tea. We tried the green tea tiramisu cake in Myeongdong which was excellent best green tea tiramisu cake I've had but opted for the green tea torte cake here as well as the ice cream. My opinion is the tiramisu was better but still very nice along with the ice cream.The gift shop was also good and we had members of staff brewing tea to allow you to sample the taste before buying. In hindsight we left without buying any tea but regretted as we left Jeju. If you're in limbo about whether to buy the tea or not my advice will be to just buy it regardless if the price is expensive since you'll probably regret it like we were. Only consolation is that the duty free inside Jeju international airport does stock some O'Sulloc products but not as much as here.Worth the visit but a bit out in the sticks. 8/10

Museum is fairly small but packed with tourists. Gift shop offer wide variety of gift ideas. Cafe was too packed for us to stay around for sampling snacks and drinks.Innisfree museum and green tea plantation are nearby
More of a stylish tea shop and a cafe. They have a wide selection of high quality flavoured tea for sale.

Max 1 and half hour. The human figures in the park shows the erotic part of the human being in different sex positions but done in an very artistic fashion. There's also shops inside selling sex toys accessories. Try not to bring underage in not sure if they restrict.
Many small shops mainly selling clothes.The best is if it's raining you can have a dry walk below the streets...
Mainly a large shop and cafe selling tea based products.  still worth a visit if only for the ice cream and cakes

Made a quick stop here and found it mostly overrated and not that special. There were an abundance of tourists around. One thing I did enjoy is the green tea ice-cream. Also taste tested the Jeju mandarin flavoured tea which you can buy from the gift/tea shop. Overall a good place to stop at for a quick break if you are on the way to other attractions around the island.
Lovely walk among the rows of tea. Very good concept to put Innisfree shop there. Interesting activities there like soap making. Attractive display
Loved the desserts there but they can get pretty expensive (17~36k??for the dessert sets)I liked the tea I bought from the shop and they make great gifts~

Love the amenities at the place. Clean and functional. The view is breathtaking and there is ample area for picture taking etc. before the serious business of hiking.Make sure wear and bring proper gear and supplies as there are limited item at the sole shop at the base.

Love Land is the place i visit and having so much fun in jeju! entrance fee w9000 per person but seriously worth it cos place is huge with indoor and outdoor. outdoor with all the sex pose statues very embarrassing while walking around the park. but i really do enjoy! its cute and some sexual knowledge >///< visit during January spend about 2 hours plus in the park. i believe can be more but due to weather is super cold we couldn't stand the windy cold we left right after round the whole park. basically is 80% outdoor and 10% indoor + 10% indoor souvenir shop.

lots of different types of bears to satisfy the history buffs and also people who just want to see cute bears.  Souvenir shop was great.  The best part was the teddy bear garden in the back..spent close to an hour there just strolling and taking pictures through the well manicured grounds..

Location is bit difficult if you get there by Bus I'd recommend taxi or rent a car.Tea Museum however it's more like mini shopping place where they sell green tea stuffs and cosmetic stuffs as well.Also their restaurants is quite nice and tasteful.Must visit there when the weather is good since it is very nice to take picture outside.

Located next to dongmun and jungang underground market so you can combine all three in one go. Not much to see and shop. You will probably eat in dongmun. We took dinner at the end of the street in a Japanese restaurant and was really good food. Jeju has a small population and do not really expect much shopping I could not find a memory card for my camera :-(

Located in Seogwipo area. Beautiful waterfall that easy to access as only reached 5-10 minutes walking their path. Mostly is stairs. Entrance Fee KRW2000. Have some small shops near the entrance selling local souvenir.

Located by Gate 11 (or 13) of Jeju Central Underground Shopping Center.  Inexpensive admission to visit and discounted for a group of 10 people.  Oldest Dol hareubangs in the island are reserved by the platform outside the entrance.  Staffs are friendly and willing to help tourists.  If you love history you must visit this place.

Like the beaches that surround beautiful Jeju Island this pedestrian-friendly shopping zone is constantly evolving?쫉ifferent almost with each new day.Once frequented by students the area was reborn in 2011 as Bao Jian Street to mark the arrival of nearly 12000 Chinese tourists who were given a vacation trip to Jeju Island by their employer.  The street?셲 new checkerboard pattern now showcases fountains with colored lights outdoor seating areas Korean-style bonsai landscaping statues brightly colored neon street lights and oh yes  a TROVE of shops.  Specialties include cosmetics trekking shoes and clothes golf-specialty shops hair and nail salons jewelry (including a Korean jade store) local souvenirs a handmade-leather-goods shop restaurants cafes bars and boutique hotels.  Just off the main street one can find bakeries more restaurants bars (including the locally brewed Jespi Beer) and more shops?쫛ne could spend an entire evening or longer just checking everything out.While most of the coffee shops and some stores are open during the day this is a place that really comes to life in the evening. All the colored lights sort of draw you in and along.  And note that while most of the street is closed to vehicles there are a couple of active cross streets so do look both ways before entering those intersections.Depending on when you visit you may get treated to an outdoor concert.  In 2014 the local Culture and Art Division sponsored a street music fest during late summer and early fall.  (For information about future festivals or events call 82-064-728-2714).  Although it can?셳 compare with say the night markets of Taipei or other larger cities Bao Jian Street does provide a bit of balance to all the hiking and climbing many tourists do during the day.  You can definitely find some dinner and a few brews there so check it out.  Interesting photo ops.

Just over the road from the Jeju Folk Village  the area has some lovely sandy areas to play around; cool memorial area of the women divers of Jeju and several snack shops (a little expensive). Toilets available and some very nice views. Worth a quick visit when in the area.
just more of an optical illusion thing. it seems i am more interested with the souvenir shops and the stalls offering classy street food. several photos to take can be more like it

Just a Stone throw away from  Seongsan Ilchulbong is located the Aqua Planet. It is easy to find and has generally enough parking place available. It is quite a big building and not to over look. Entrance fee is a bit pricy. We paid for 2 adults and one child over a 100k Won if I am not mistaken. Anyway a huge Aquarium costs probably a bit more efforts as other places in Jeju. The whole aquarium is made comfortable for stroller and wheel chair. We entered 20 minutes before 3pm and did a mistake. At the entrance they told us that we have to look the show first and then go through the Aquarium. It is what we did. So after the show we had to deal with a lot of People crawling through the aquarium at the same time. Don't do this. Instead do the other way around. Best case you enter the aquarium when the show starts. The aquarium itself is very nice and a lot to see not only for the juniors. A lot of species big and small and tall and tiny. Good place especially when it is either rainy or very hot outside. At the end as you may guess is a souvenir shop. LoL. Since then we have one Pingu more in our collection. Infrastructure wise (shops and 00) no issues. The show itself what shall i say. I thing you have to see it and judge. It is 40 minutes long and is divided by (20%) dolphin performance (20%) sea dog performance and some (60%) pirate story performance with humans only. Fair enough to say that over all the show was good and fascinating. Conclusion is that we visit the place again.

review: JTO Duty Free is situated at the southern city of Seogwipo. 50 minutes from Jeju city. Worth to go if you are nearby if you have limited time. The duty free shop at Jeju city and airport is better. This place has limited selections and occupy only a relatively small area in the ICC conference center.

Jeju has tonnes of 'museums' to draw in cash from tourists. Most of these are silly  man-made museums having no connection whatsoever to Jeju or even Korea. It is almost a sin to spend time in these museums while in Jeju  instead of enjoying the scenery outdoors.However I would reallly recommend a stop at the seashell museum if you have an hour to spare in the Seogwipo area. The labor of love of 1 woman  this place houses a staggering collection of shells from all over the world  crafted into stunning displays. Seashells so pretty  its hard to believe they are real..but they are.There's also a small shop to purchase souvenirs if you'd like but they don't pressure you. Also attached is a cafe.Close by to a bus stop.

Jeju Folk Village Museum as it appears on map for Jeju is on the coast and is a must do for history and culture buffs. There are hands on exhibits that kids and adults can participate and use around the village. The park and museum is large and takes 2 to 3 hours at least. Perhaps longer to see everything without rush. We were quite impressed by the size the crafts people making products and the exhibits throughout. There are ample restrooms snack shops and Korean traditional products sold in the gift shop. There is also a restaurant on premise.The Jeju Folk Village attracts students from all over Korea as well as tourists from other countries. I highly recommend the park. There are beautiful floral blooms as well as animals photo opportunities and lots of traditional Korean history and culture to learn about. Well worth the price of admission. Plan to spend half a day here. Arrive early to avoid the crowds. There are some great gifts and candies to be found around the village including the traditional Korean taffy near the Hanbok photo place and the gift shop.

Its true that its not much of a museum but really nice place to stop by and enjoy view from building. Its also free of charge. Not sure if you can come by bus probably yes. We used a rented car on island. Cafe is good and i personally like tea ice cream not so sweet as usual one and good for hot day. There is an open spot on the third floor to take a picture with nice view. There is also innisfree shop where you can buy DIY pack and make your own soap. Good place to relax on nearby grass.

It's one street away from the seafood street and walking distance to the shopping street too. Quite a number of korean bbq & restaurant. We went in to one that's filled with locals and it turned out to be a wise choice.

It's one of the best small museums on Jeju island. I went there twice and each time spent couple of hours in sheer amazement and delight. Almost each sea shell installation strikes with its beauty. The bronze things are also interesting and sometimes funny. Check the bathroom  by the way :)There is much stuff in the gift shop but quite expensive. Small cafe is cozy arranged with bronze installations and green plants. Try tea and bagels  they are tasty.

Its not a green tea museum there are some ancient and modern tea pots and cups leading to tea skin care and food outlet.But worst part was most items on sale were cheaper at Insadong or other outlets.Tea field is good Intagrammerable photo location but try to skip this place. We had better time and food at Innisfree shop about 50 meters away.
It's nice to walk around and see the different bears and the history of the bears. Admission is a good price but the gift shop is a bit pricey.
It's near to junggang underground shopping street  most of the shop I realized it's not open or not vacant  rather dim the lights and deserted street here .

Its good place to get to know how Korean people lived on Jeju do island. There are houses of all kind of people like craftsmen usual habitants prisoners and etc. Also some photos of women divers from Jeju. Its probably better to use a guide since all information is in Korean and  there are several traditional korean games on the ground that need to be explained. There are several shops inside: some craftsmen shops like wooden crafts and caligraphy and also souvenirs and some local candy. We enjoyed our walk here. Its nice park that also got some ponds and small waterfalls. Its quite big one also. fee amount is 10000 krw per person.

It's a wonderful botanical garden with many flowers and trees in natural jeju island atmosphere in Korea.Camellia flowers blooming in February are abundant throughout Camellia Hill garden. Its owner Mr. Yang has spent enormous amount time and financial resources to create build and improve the garden as one of the best attractions in Jeju Island.  There are many stone sculptures well maintained hiking trails green houses resting areas and a tea and gift shop the visitors can enjoy and take beautiful pictures.  It's located very near to Jeju Shinwha World Resort with many great hotels and restaurants.  It's a real gem place you should not miss along with Hanrim Botanical Park in Gumnung Beach area in Jeju Island.

It's a very touristy place. There is nothing special about this place. The product that you purchase here is with tax even though Jeju island is a tax free country. You may do your shopping in the airpot.

It's a nice shopping street that is about 5 min walk from Dongmun Market and beside Jungang underground shopping place that is closed till August 2016. There is Tommy Hilfiger interesting souvenir store The Islander local designer and mid-range fashion shops shoes and stationery stores and cafes as well. Nearby at one end is the attraction Gwandeokjeong Pavilion. At the other end of the street there is also a black pork street.

It's 3000 Won to enter and it is mostly just a chocolate shop. They do chocolate making classes  if you are interested  but that costs an additional 10 000 - 12 000 won (sorry  I am not sure about the exact price. We asked  but I don't remember). You can use your entrance fee to purchase chocolate  but way not just buy chocolate somewhere else?

It?셲 not much of a museum really but more like a short glorification and summary of the history of O?셲ulloc. I would?셶e actually been interested in finding out more about how tea is grown tea types production etc. the tea fields surrounding the actual museum are more interesting. Following the (very small) museum (which is also free of entry to be fair) one is led to the tea shop/ cafe in what I can only describe as a controlled stampede! I didn?셳 find any way to actually sample some tea or at least smell it before buying; I kinda wanted to get a better idea of a bag of tea that costs up to 100$ before buying it. At Twinings in London they understand that and offer free samples. In other places you can at least smell the tea. At O?셲ulloc you get what you see on the shelf (if you can reach it that is). It was raining when we went (but had no other choice to fit it into our packed itinerary) so we bought raincoats at the tiny souvenir shop before entering. Because of the rain there weren't alot of other tourists but we also could not fully enjoy the place since it was basically like an open air museum with buildings that mimic the traditional houses. There were some traditional games and tools lying around for tourists to play with too. It was still very interesting though and we enjoyed reading a little bit of history of jeju at each area.

It was much nicer when I visited here 4 years ago. Now there are too many people waiting to buy and eat everything the shop have. Museum part hasn't improved as well nothing much to look at. To be honest Insadong branch is nicer than here..one good thing was it was nice to sit down and look over the green yard. To make your experience more fun; 1. You can try tea tasting sessions (only 4 sessions a day please book in advance) 2. Innisfree has some soap making area (it's for kids but I enjoyed making and decorating my own soap)

It was located behind the mbc k-pop. The place was quite deserted. Nothing much to see.. you are given ??000 voucher each for a ??000 admission fee. Literally  this place is just encouraging you to shop at their shop.

It was a small park with a maze inside. We were lucky to find the exit on the bridge in 8 minutes and we enjoyed some ice-cream in the small souvenir shop while waiting the rest of group to come out.  This maze would be fun for children.

It was a relaxing short walk to the falls. We went during the evening and it was quite touristy. It's a great site to take pictures before the waterfall if there isn't too much people. The entry was only 2000 won and there are shops and restaurants near the entrance

It takes 45-60 minutes to hike around the whole trail. The trail is diverse in the scenes that it presents along different coastal views. Brace yourself for high wind speeds during the colder months. There are a lot of inclines/declines on the trail so be wary of that on the way. There are a couple of restaurants/eateries spotted along mid-trail but I have no comment on those establishments. Before the trail officially begins there is a little rest-stop with coffee shops convenience stores and restrooms so I would recommend using the facilities before you embark on your hike.

It looks like it has been abandoned for years  it has very nice artwork but it is also very dirty. The bathroom was disgusting. The gift shop smelled like cigarettes and had puddles of water every where. And the staff looked extremely bored and uninterested. I came at night so maybe the daytime is better. How ever I don't recommend it  definitely not worth the $8 per person day or night. (Got some nice pictures though)

It is really great how many things you can see on Jeju for less than $3 a person. We did not climb to the top but went into the park to the left to see the cliffs and get a closer look. You only have to walk a little to see a lot. Ample parking and coffee shops nearby. It was so beautiful despite the crowd. It was rainy and windy. Raincoats are sold in the gift shop.

It is not tourist attraction but great place for a conference  inside you have seven eleven and gift shop - I would advice this gift shop with nice sweets  tangerines and black garlic. Tangerines are the best from this Island!

It is listed as a Unesco World Heritage and definetly a place to stop. Highway 1132 will bring you there and you cannot miss it. Be prepared that parking might not be easy and you may have to spend some time. The place is quite busy and many tourist buses are coming too. We had a cloudy day and it was very windy. Entrance fee is 2000 adult and 1000 child. Couple of shops at the entrance where you can buy each and everything. Please keep in mind that waste management is terrible as everywhere in Korea. If you buy something keep in mind that no any trash beans are available. The way up and down is quite crowded and loud. Obviously many tourists are rushing on top to get the selfies done to rush down again. The walk is definetly nothing for stroller or wheel chair. We went up slowly enjoying the view and getting some pictures. On top it is quite nice to look into the volvano and rest. Sure some pictures not to forget. But again very busy place and loud. Again our day was cloudy and windy but as long as it is not raining worth to visit the peak. So conclusion would be to visit the place very early.
It is interesting to walk around the shops and see the food and souvenirs they sell.The vendors are very friendly!

It is hard to say anything good about this place. Basically  it is a small chocolate gift shop that charges $3 a person to enter. You receive a coupon good for $3 back on any purchase. I suppose it is their way to ensure that you buy something.The only interesting thing was that they had these cookie balls that you smashed with a hammer to eat.

It is easy to find and has a few parking places. No entrance fee. Restroom availabe at the parking lot. You walk alonxg the coast line and dont forget your camera. It is a nice spot for taking pictures. Has couple of small shops for water and fuits. Its worth to stop. Not easy for whell chair and stroller.
It is a very big market. Sell all kinds of things. From fresh seafood to clothes.Should visit when in jeju.There is a underground shopping centre nearby.

It is a hilly place with rows of eateries and shops. There are interesting street performances that are usually held in the evening. Look out for the shops where the local visit as they offer authentic Korean food. Do visit Gambit Gallery an unassuming shop that stocks hand-dyed clothes.
It is a great place to quickly pass by. It isn't a big place and doesn't require much time.The place consist of the tea leaves garden a small museum small shop and cafe.

It had rained heavily the night before our arrival which meant that it was very slippery inside the lava tunnel and water was dripping constantly which also formed puddles throughout the path.It is also very dark.  There are some lights but not enough to clearly see the terrain below you.  We got to the 300km marker and decided to turn back because we were trying to avoid twisting our ankles.  The lava flow creates interesting striations and grooves which does not result in an easy stroll through the tunnel.The walk may be less treacherous if the tunnel was dry but this is one attraction that should not be attempted by people with mobility issues.The one good thing is that there is a nice gift shop on the grounds which also serves snacks.  Clean bathrooms.
It basically looks like a shopping mall in Shenzhen. There are a few cosmetic shops but most of the shops sell old-fashioned clothes. Not worth a visit at all.

Is a quaint place with some very good drinks and desserts. But the crowd is overwhelming. I would skip this place altogether if I visit Jeju next. It?셲 got nice tea plantation front of the museum but I?셶e seen better ones in Taiwan. Truth is after a torturous hike up Hallasan mountain we needed to do something easy the following day so Osulloc Tea Museum was in the itinerary. Tea culture not very well exhibited and I think this is more of a shopping excursion. The staff not friendly or helpful but rather want to be done with your query. To sum it all if you want to shop you can come but otherwise this is a place you can skip.
Interesting to see historic chocolate packaging  however  amount  quality and selection of display have reflected on cost of admission fee.Great souvenir shop in the basement!
Interesting museum. Worth going. Summer time can be quite hot if viewing the outdoor displays. Gift shop is right under the greenhouse effect.
Interesting museum with lots of teddy bears. Amusing time for adults and kids alike.  Lots of photo opportunities and there's an Elvis concert as well as shop/cafe for further amusement!

Innisfree is a Korean cosmetics brand known for its natural ingredients sourced directly from Jeju in Korea...think of it as a Korean Body Shop. The Innisfree House in Jeju is a combined shop and cafe located inside the Osulloc Green Tea Museum complex. You can buy products and make your own soaps as well as sit and chill with some Korean and Western fusion drinks and cafe style food. Good stop for lunch or afternoon tea and to pick up souvenirs. Recommend spending only 1 hour (combined with the green tea plantation photo op)

Indeed a disappointing experience. Yes  this is just an excuse to get you to the gift shop  but at least they could have made the trip there interesting. The story of chocolate is among the most fascinating in the histories of commodities  but they made it a torture. You will see some exhibits on the history of chocolate  a few displays of old boxes and cases of chocolates  and some needless toy sculptures  but mostly a forgettable experience. You do have to pay a small amount and get a coupon for your chocolate or drink purchase. So  if you are desperate to eat some chocolate  or it's raining heavily outside  or you need quickly some air-conditioning  then give it a try; otherwise  enjoy Jeju's natural scenery and wonders instead.

In the 'Tea Stone' building you can try their tea workshops. They explained the history of Tea in Jeju and how all the elements in nature affect the taste.During the class we were not allowed to take pictures which made us focus on the experience and just relax smell the aroma of the wet tea and even make tea for our friends! The desserts they served were also very nice! I drink tea a lot but this workshop proved there is much more to enjoy when you brew and prepare the tea!Personally I devour a cup of tea in seconds but this class made me realize the pleasure I can get if I put effort into making it.There was also a decent cafe with various options all using green tea.If you like makeup and skin-care the famous Korean brand Innisfree also has a branch there which is quite different from the shops in Seoul.

Impressive aquarium great facility with restaurants souvenir shops and some more. Aqua Planet is right next to the sea shore that makes it a beautiful sight day and night. Too bad the staff were rude and unreasonable. It's also a bit pricey but it's definitely worth the visit. The ticket can be cheaper if you pre-order it and skip the show.

If you`re a Zippo lover  this is a must visit spot. Museum locates in the ground floor of a modern seaside building with breathtaking pacific ocean view. There is 2 exhibition halls  one of those displays many special designed zippos in large size  and the other in fact is a zippo shop  you can see and buy different limited edition zippo there and many are designed by local designer.

If you want to see a bunch of boxes of chocolate from all over the world  this is the place for you. The 3000 won you pay to enter gives you a discount to what you can buy there so if you want to buy chocolate you won't feel ripped off  but you can buy the same chocolate in any gift shop for the same price. There are a lot of great places on Jeju. I wouldn't go out of your way to visit here.

If you want to buy or get your fix of osulloc green tea goodies you don?셳 really need to come all the way to Jeju. Shopping in seoul for osulloc goods is a better option. Aside from the view and the shop nothing else to do here. I?셫 not sure why they even call this a museum. I wish they have a proper green tea tour as part of their program. I don?셳 mind spending for a quality experience.

If you love green tea it's nice to stop by and have their desserts here. We ordered the ice cream the cake roll and they latte. Innisfree store is also at this faciity where you can buy their products too. Good stop for shopping a green tea snack!

If you go for brands (local and international) this short street is probably the place to go to on this part of the island. The street is closed to traffic so you could spend a while walking in comfort. The street is on the way to dongmun market and the underground shopping centre. Along the way it also branches off into some kind of roofed shopping arcade which we did not visit.

If you go for brands (international or local) this short street is probably the place to visit on this side of the island. It leads to the dongmun market and the underground shopping centre. Along the way this branches off into a covered shopping arcade which we did not visit.

If you are the fan of Korean tea you should go to this place and try yourself. They offer some tester so you can before you buy. Besides tea there are some products such as green tea milk spread cosmetic skin care etc that the main ingredient is tea are also available here. Besides the indoor museum or shop you can walk around at the tea plantation outside and take a nice camera shot.

If you are a fan of green tea you should pass by here if it's on the way of where you are going. The museum itself doesn't offer too much information. There is a green tea field and they serve green tea green tea drinks green tea ice cream and all things related to green tea (ok maybe not all but you know what I mean). My time here was not too bad just too many tourists and it may be hard for you to find a seat. There is an innisfree shop right next to the museum and there are some limited products you can find there.

if you appreciate football games  this can be a memorable place for you to go. basically there's nothing much you can do there because the stadium gates are closed so you wont get to enter the stadium. But still  you can camwhoring around there and once you are done  maybe you can consider to go shopping at E-Mart which located just across the street from the stadium

If I had time to visit just one traditional market I will choose Dongmun to Seogwipo. The bonus in visiting Dongmun is that there's an underground shopping centre and shopping streets nearby with food outlets.

I wouldn't go out of my way to see it but it is fun walking through the place. There are still some shops and a small waterpark/spa that only opens fully in the summer. Very quiet almost ghost town type of feel. Go karts are near by to if your into that
i went yesterday . this place was great. i really like it .and shop in the museum there are many art product.i bought one . good price and good design.i recomend this place.

I went traveling to Jeju from Shanghai and my friend helped me booked the Discovery diving trip at good diver. We chose this dive shop because it's PADI certified and the location is convenient. And they have English website with very useful information compared with many local dive shops with information only in Korean. It was such an amazing experience doing discovery dive with them and it went beyond what I expected. I felt I was in good hand because the instructor was very experienced and he knew how to make beginner at ease with a good sense of humor. His calm and caring presence also helped a lot. Traveling and diving at Mun island which is a small island to the south of Jeju in the morning is a very refreshing experience. The scenery is beautiful and we saw a good amount of soft coral and school of fishes. Jen another instructor is also very helpful and it was fun chatting with her along the way. She gave me a ride and dropped me off at a local restaurant for lunch and the pork noodle she recommended was very delicious.

I went to Jeju after spending 6 days in Seoul. After Namdaemun  Myeondong  Hongdae and many undergeound shopping malls naturally Maeil Oleh Oleh did not excite me. Mainly targeting tourist business and restaurants amd stuff is not cheap there.

I went here a couple of times during my stay on Jeju Island. I loved the Innisfree shop where you could buy packs of soap that you then made with either green tea tangerine or volcanic rock ash. It was so cool and they made lovely souvenirs for when I came home. Also the green tea roll cake there is delicious! And the gardens are great for taking photos. 10/10 would recommend.

I was working in a school really near there so i visited quite a few times; but It was basically just a tea shop which had a cafe which sold tea green tea ice cream and other ice creams. However the outside area is really peaceful and quiet and there is a path which leads to another cafe in an outer building where they have sodas and food and shakes which tasted amazing my fav one was the Oreo milkshake!!! I would Go there just for the shake but stay for the peace and quiet.

I was on a group day tour so unfortunately didn't have as much time here. Walked through the museum very quickly ordered the ice cream and cake and quickly rushed to buy a few products at the shop. The view of the green tea fields provided a great photo op but was surprised to see 'beware of snake' signs walking through the garden fortunately didn't encounter any snakes though but they should take more precaution on this as I see a lot of small kids walking and running through the areas. There's an Innisfree house for buying the famous Korean brand cosmetic next door but quite frankly this was a bit disappointing for an Innisfree loyalist like me. The selections were limited compared to the shops in town all over Korea. One woman  in my tour group bought a bunch of products but was not offered any free samples which is common in other shops. I would suggest skipping this part and spend all the time in the O'Sulloc cafe and tea museum.

I visited this place at night and really enjoyed it. You should definitely have your camera with you and ready to get lots and lots of dirty photos with the sculptures made for you to fit in. It also has a small sex shop and an exhibition. Within the park you will also find a casual gift shop.Fantastic place and definitely a must for couples!

I visited this as part of an inclusive tour.  This is really interesting.  there is the story of tea and you can walk among the tea bushes.  This is the best Korea tea there is and of course you can buy their products and sample green tea foods in the cafe. Their sister beauty products company Innesfree also has a cafe and gift shop.  Again these products have a hig reputation in S. Korea.  I would have liked more time to spend here.  The main cafe was packed and I would have like to have had green tea and green tea cake or green tea ice cream but I wouldn't have been able to see anything else in the time we had.  A pleasant place to visit for a few hours.
I visited here for searching Halla tangerines. There was no souvenirs sold at this place. Need to have a shoplot selling souvenirs here in the future.
I visited about a year ago and I had amazing deals on tea there is also a lovely shop up a little hill that was lovely. All around and a beautiful landscape and garden

I thought I will see a museum but it was a cafe and a shop. I don't think it deserve the visit. If you have time and you love the green tea you might like it.Next to it Innisfree it is also a shop and a cafe and you can make your own soap there.

I recently visited this beach with a group of friends and it was definitely worth it.  We were staying in Jeju City so it was about an hour bus ride to get to the beach.  There isn't any space to lay down a blanket so you have to rent an umbrella.  The water is crystal is clear and the tide is very low.  I had to walk about 300 meter in order to get water that was waist high. There are all kinds of coffee shops and restaurants located along the strip of the beach so you can eat and hang for  as long as you like.  The water is beautiful and makes it worth it.

I really love this place just that there are too many people. Everything green tea is amazing here. we had the icecream and it was so strongly flavored. I loved it. I have seen many Korean Markets in the course of my 18 days in korea. To be honest  no market have truly captured my attention. You can go to any traditional market in any state of S.K and you wouldn't be missing out. My advice for any Korean Traditional Market in general:- Go to any market that is decently sized that is convenient to travel to from your accomodation. - Take note that they do not have rubbish bins there most of the time and you'd have to return your trash to the store which you have bought the food from. - Be very clear in the number of portions you order as I had a rather awful experience ordering one portion and receiving three person quantity since I had three people.- Go in the morning/day time since most markets will be closing shop by 6pm- The fishcake skewers and the broth are great to enjoy on a cold day. You grab a cup from the stall to get the broth and start eating the oden. Payment will come after you return the sticks to the owner.Lastly  enjoy yourselves in Korea. Learn some basic Korean before you come as you will definitely elevate your experience in Korea. Koreans will always treat you better if they see you making an effort to speak some Korean as all other countries.

Exotic Jeju Island is known for many things: the majestic Hallasan--the massive shield volcano that formed the island and the highest point in South Korea; its mandarin groves; persimmon-dyed galot fashions; the sturdy Jeju ma horses  descended from the ponies of Mongol invaders; tasty black pork; and the iconic haenyeo women divers. But most visitors would not expect to find a Museum of African Art there. And  it's pretty darn good! Located in a massive structure modeled after the mud-brick Great Mosque of Djenne  the museum offers photo-ops galore in its Safari section  although the animals are of the stuffed variety. Very popular with children and couples. The upper floors house a respectable collection of African artifacts and photographs by Kim Jung Man. There is also a great gift shop. But  I have saved the best for last...the live performance of African folk music and dance. The group  Zalia from Senegal  featured lots of drumming  and audience members also got a drumming lesson and a chance to play along on one song. All in all  a quality experience...and a surprising one.

Entrance fee of KRW5 000 per adult which includes a huge cup of hot black coffee (I don't drink coffee and couldn't change it for a hot chocolate drink). The museum is located on one floor with various displays. Towards one end there's a glass concept kitchen where the various chocolates are made and a little further down  the chocolate shop. A box of 8-12 pieces could cost upwards of KRW13 000  and the lady was kind enough to let us try a dark chocolate which ended up quite yummy (not too sweet nor bitter  think it was a 60 or 70% one).

Considered one of the ten best view points of Jeju this attraction is not to be missed One can enjoy this visit if you like to soak yourself or would like to find yourself among the clouds. On a foggy day one can easily miss the existence of this mountain.If you are visiting during winter or rainy season better to plan the visit during afternoon as one can have a magnificent view from the top without much clouds around.This mountain believed to be formed by the volcanic lava houses the Sanbang-gulsa Temple and the Bomunsa Temple.It also has other attractions as Golden Bhuddha Tea Shops etc. Once on the top one can see the ridge called the Dragon Head where a memorial has been built for Hendrick Hamel the first westerner who was the first to introduce Korea to the western world after his ship got wrecked. This mountain is believed to be used as a watch tower and smoke used to be sent out during the day or fire was lit during the night if any urgent message was needed to be conveyed.Climbing the steps would be a little tough for those who are not regular walkers and for the old.

As the Chocolate Land is within 10 minutes??walk from the Teddy Bear Museum in the Jungmun Resort area ??just follow the direction on the sign-posts ??my family and I had no hesitation to visit it on a rainy Sunday.Getting there and fees: First and foremost  you have to note that Chocolate Land is different from Chocolate Museum. Chocolate Land is in the south central part of Jeju while Chocolate Museum is in the south west Jeju. We didn't need the GPS coordinate/code for Chocolate Land but it's 7381197 for anyone who's driving there directly. The entrance fee for adults is 3000 won and 2000 won for children. A voucher was given back for every purchased ticket which can be redeemed at the gift shop or the caf챕 or the Chocolate School.The Museum/Attraction: After going past the ticketing counter  you then turn right. The section on the left is a caf챕 and photograph/selfie stops of different types of Korean houses and benches with toy bears. There's even a figurine of Santa Claus in front of one house  which was interesting considering Christmas is still some 6 months away. The section on the right is the exhibits on the history of chocolates  with the words written only in Korean. We went down the stairways to the level below in which there's a Chocolate School which teaches chocolate making at 120 000 won with lessons starting every hour from 10am to 6pm (I think the children would be more interested than adults). We didn't go into the School; instead  we walked past M&M figurines and a Christmas tree (again interesting) and reached the chocolate shop where there are interesting exhibits of chocolates (behind glass) from America  Europe and Asia. The gift shop has an extensive selection of chocolates (I think slightly more than outside). The prices of the Jeju chocolates of the same brand at the gift shop were slightly more expensive compared to those selling outside Chocolate Land. However  the Chocolate Land chocolates became slightly cheaper than those outside when we utilised the discount vouchers. Unique local Jeju chocolates are those with pink cactus flowers  mandarin oranges and hallabong fillings. We couldn't wait till Christmas?쫤e ate some of the chocolates before we left Jeju  and these were yummy!There is a small observation area (Chocolate Garden) outside the building where the view looks towards the sea. There's also a statue of Willy Wonka from the 1971 movie ?쁗illy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory??where you could take a photograph and selfie with. But we couldn't go outside because it's raining.I recommend visiting the Chocolate Land if you have the time and if you have an appreciation of chocolates. Otherwise  I think you wouldn't miss much if you decide to skip it.

As part of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour we were given some time to go around O'sulloc Green Tea's fields museum and cafe; as well as shop around in Innisfree's Jeju House.Queues tend to be long for both the O'sulloc Green Tea and Innisfree so it's best to prioritize one over the other if you're working with a limited amount of time. O'sulloc Green Tea displays its wide array of teas packaged in gorgeous boxes and tin cans. Fortunately we were able to visit its branch in Seoul already (and bought our fare share of their tea boxes) so we focused our time in Innisfree instead.Innisfree has numerous branches in Seoul; however it's best to look out for the Jeju-exclusive items available in the Jeju house. Similar to O'sulloc Innisfree also has its own cafe which serves its own selection of drinks and food; for those not interested in its beauty products.

Whatever we could see of the grounds looked very promising.We will consider returning here on a fine day on our next trip to Jeju.

A 50 min good show! Though we do not understand their language. The intro a bit nagging  but overall the show still okay for us! It started with some introduction  monkey show  sealion and dolphin. After the show we can take photo with the dolphin but subjected to the availability of the photo ticket which cost 10k won. I personally think that is reasonable as you can take photo with the dolphin very near unfortunately  we are not able to grab the photo ticket due to language constraint. If we have known this  we will immediately buy it over the counter. There is a souvenir shop outside and plenty of restaurant/caf챕 outside. Entrance ticket will be adult 15k and child 10k.

2000krw to get in.    Walk down stairs to get to a very rocky area with the waterfall coming down right next to the sea.  There was not a huge amount of water flowing down.     Some souvenir/food shops around.
+18 enjoy your time there Interesting sculptures of male and female organs sex positions all over the place and a shop
You will need good shoes and ~20 min, and water, the rout is amazing, clean, safe and view is breathtaking, on the way back you can buy tangerine juice form the shops - delicious!

You might go in the market which is partially underground and think you?re in this. You?re not. This is about 100 little shops with similar wares. About 3 places to eat including don burger. One neat thing about this is that they say it is the largest in the world. It?s one block but in the middle flares out to several aisles. I don?t know if anybody reads trip advisor unless you click HELPFUL. If you do this, it sends me an email and it makes me smile :-)

You know that line movie critics love to use when it comes to B-grade chick flicks?   Have low expectations, then you'll enjoy it.   The same can be said of Manjang Cave.The lava tube was not as spectacular as I expected it to be, but it did offer a few interesting sights here and there. Walking all the way to the end of the trail and back took about an hour, but if you walk quickly, you can complete the journey within thirty minutes.Take note that the ground is wet and rocky, so be sure to wear your walking shoes. Also, it can get quite cold, so a jacket would most certainly come in handy. For photography lovers, you may not fancy the fact that it's a bit dark in the cave, but there's nothing a few adjustments here and there can't do!Facilities include, but are not limited to, souvenir shops, toilets and lockers. Bear in mind though that there are no toilets in the cave itself. Tickets are cheaper for children, but you'll need passports for proof!If you're spending more than a day in Jeju, you may want to consider checking this place out. If not, you're better off exploring other places such as the Hallasan National Park.

You have to walk on a ramp in order to get into the museum because car cannot drive into the area of exhibitions. The venue is separated into indoor and outdoor. For outdoor exhibitions, you should be aware of the weather. If it rains, the ramp would be slippery, so visitors are recommended to wear water-resistant shoes for unusual events. There are plenty of cars exhibited, including antique cars and modern cars. There are descriptions beside every single car including where they produce, which car firm belongs to and when it is first produced. There are many limited-edition cars and some of them are even the only one in the world. There is also a shop located besides the entry of the museum, selling different car models and peripherals. I bought a wheel like key chain, it costs 10k KWD, which is relatively cheap compare to the models of cars.So, if you are a car fan or you want to have some souvenirs about cars, you are recommended to go to the car museum to buy your favorites.
address: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관
입력주소: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관

review: you can view the teddy bears from different countries,enjoy yourself at the museum shop, caf챕, restaurant or the outdoor park where you can view the spectacular Jungmun Sea. At the museum garden, you can meet the teddy bear sculptures and models. The garden decorated with various themes such as the Korean Black bear family and the magical pond. Children under are free. Lots of free parking.

You can start the trail downhill from Story Ville villas and end at Oedolgae. On that Ole trail there is a museum and a coffee shop on the way. If you drive there, there is plenty of parking and small restaurants, etc. people come here to watch the sunset.
You can see windmill and it was lovely to take a picture. There are shops nearby and convenient store. Relaxing, windy and nice white sand beach.
You can see it from a deck, and it does require imagination to see it as a dragon head. Nothing else here, but there are some snack shops.. Worth roughly 15minutes.

You can imagine: blue sky, strong wind and black shore.  Lots of shops and restaurants around the small island.  Locals can hire a small motorcar but for foreigners without local driving licence, bicycles seem to be the only choice.  It takes about 3 hours to finish the round-island cycling with adequate sightseeing.
You can find everything and anything there, local fruits andveggies are excellent and cheap and you'll see an authentic Jeju market where Locals go to shop.

You can easily spend a half or full day sightseeing around the island. They have tour buses which will take you around to the major sights but I'd recommend renting a bike. There are heaps of places to rent bikes from after you get off the ferry. You'll need an international license to rent a scooter or ATV. But there are no serious hills in the island so (if you're there in fall/spring with fair weather) I'd really recommend a bicycle. It was so lovely cycling around the island and easily jumping on and off my bike to snap pictures.The bike rental was 4 hours for 10,000 won. They shop will give you a map of the island with tours and sightseeing locations on it. Although you don't really need it as you basically just cycle the seaside road. Don't forget your camera or to eat the famous peanut ice cream!

Yes , it's slightly expensive. Not meant for daily meal, but it's not killer expensive. The first shop in the left is awesome. Seems like they got Michelin award or something. 48,000 krw for a delicious mealworms 2  is okay. Something about the meal. Beautiful.

Wow-this place is huge, gorgeous and meticulously maintained. Spent 3 hours there wandering aimlessly, just loved it and the calming vibe. Just wish the shops and vendors stayed until 7 pm close as I missed the chance to try cactus ice cream. Don't drive past this place if u have an hour or a few to spend.

Worth a visit if you are a beach person - lots of people. Plenty of food booths and shops close by, lots of gimmicks to buy to include in your day. Water was okay - typical sand in the pants type of thing!!

Without considering visitors could visit and shop at this museum, they charged the highest entrance fee among all other natural sites we visited in Jeju. If it were not for the kids, it was certainly not worthwhile to pay 4 times the entrance fees to other UNESCO sites.

Wide variety of shops: clothes shoes restaurant etc.  Nice place to get some shopping done.  I went here last week to go for last shopping i noticed that the street is less crowd maybe due to the   virus   spreading arpund the world and also the weather is very cold. FILA BRAND IS WAY CHEAPER here.

Whilst I'm giving the Teddy Bear Museum just 2 stars for quality, value for money, class of exhibits, and any actual worth as a proper   museum  , I have to admit that my visit made me laugh. I'm not sure though that derisive snorting sarcasm was what they were looking for.This museum is a pile of pants, masquerading as teddy bears.. The   attractions   are about 15 to 20 poor quality adult-human-sized bears, dressed in various outfits of clothing, with a challenge to guess   who   they are dressed as. Military uniform and two medals apparently is enough for a bear to resemble Prince William, for example - and a grey wig and   E=mc2   to represent Einstein.Then there are the bear portraits. Frames containing bears dressed to vaguely resemble famous portraits. Mona Lisa teddy bear, anyone?There's no   history   of the teddy bear, no collection of historical bears, no pictures / video clips of teddy bears being made, no maps showing where different types of teddy bears originated from - nothing educational whatsoever. There are no audio tours, no leaflets or signs to show the visitor around, and certainly no staff available to talk to about any   exhibits  , whether you are Korean, English, American or anything else.The gift shop on the lowest floor contained the largest number of bears - none of them particularly special, all just your usual cheap mass-produced bears, but at slightly hiked up prices.By far the worst part of the visit was the funniest. Your ticket includes entry to the   Elvis Stage Show  . Oh dear Lord, where on earth do I start? The show is on every 15 minutes. In a room with about 12 benches in it. There is a curtain at the far end, hiding the   stage  . On the quarter hour, the announcement is made -   The King of Rock and Roll, Elvis, is in the house!   The curtains open, and there it is. The Elvis Presley Show. Six, sad, lonely looking teddy bears, dressed in stage show outfits, rocking gently on their animatronic sticks. The three backing singers sway gently on the right, the drummer's arms flail up and down towards the drums, the guitarist's arm moves.Elvis meanwhile gyrate and swivels his hips, the crowd goes wild. Oh, no, sorry, that last sentence was a lie. Elvis sways and looks like he almost falls several times.Worst animatronic puppetry in the world. Hilarious. Hilariously BAD. Less than two minutes later, the curtains shut, and   Elvis has left the building   - until the next showing in approximately 12 or 13 minutes' time....Don't go to the Teddy Bear Museum thinking you'll have an interesting visit. Go to see the absolutely bizarre vision that South Koreans have of   entertainment  .

While in Jeju, another worth seeing place is Daepo Jusangjeollidae, where stone pillars (columnar joints) are formed like cubes or hexagons of various sizes due to volcanic lava and are piled up along the coast. One can walk down to the special platform to take pictures of the stone formations, but it was crowded with tourists when we were there. The view of the sea was breathtaking and one can see the waves hitting against the stone pillars. Truly a unique and wonderful experience!While we were there, we saw a local man ordering fresh sea cucumber from the lady seller. The sea cucumber was sliced and then eaten raw with chilly sauce. It seems like it is a common practice among the locals to eat raw sea-food such as sea cucumber, abalones, shell fish and sea snails in Jeju.  There is also an information counter inside a building near the park and one can request for a Tour Map of Jeju (Jeju at a glance) with information on tourists attractions, shopping in Seogwipo Olle Market, the Intercity Bus Routes and contact numbers for tourism information and transport information.
