When you vivit Jeju Island,  it is very easy for you to find cosmetic center in jugang underground shopping center. There are many kind of korean cosmetic product. Such as soothing gel, sheet mask, lipt tint, and facial wash. From airport you can go to jugang underground shopping center by bus or by taxi. You can ask tourist information in airport about bus number that can bring you there

When you said about Jeju, this Ilchubung will appear in the advertisement and you will know that is Jeju. But for sure, you will not able to snap a photo like in the adver since that only can be done if you take a photo from the helicopter and etc.For family, it is a bit tough if you bring small kids below 10 yrs old since you need to walk to the peak via stair and for adults people also a tiring activity but worth it since you can see the good view of the city and sea around that area. For photography also it will a nice thing to have.They said, the best thing during sunrise to be at the peak, but we are not make it during the sunrise so could not provide any comments on that. Also there is free show of diverwoman at the beach area just that area, they showing the activity of catching octopus with diving and selling the octopus to the audience. Most of the korea people eat it raw with Korean Sauce, i'm yet try the tast.Souvenir shop also available at the entrance of the Ilchubung peak.Thank You.

When visiting other countries I realize the treatment of animal standards may differ, but I at least look for animals to be happy. This falconry “center”was bittersweet. Some of the animals had wonderful enclosures, but the birds of prey were treated very inhumanly. The same birds of prey/owls were tied to stands for the whole 3 hours we were there, with no food or water, in the blaring sun, with no supervision as people crowded and tried to touch them to the point they would flinch or try to fly away, only to be yanked by their chains. Their inhumane treatment brought tears to our eyes. At the far part of the center, we came upon their enclosures, cages about 5 x 5 x5 feet wide, where other birds of prey were chained, with little place to move and absolutely no enrichment toys.? This is unacceptable. There was a raccoon in a small enclosure with no enrichment toys, solely used for tourists to take selfies with. Last but not least, a pair of Coaty were also in a small enclosure. Their baby was on display in a small cage by the gift shop with no water. This “Center” does have some acceptable enclosures for fowl, rabbits, budgies, and the alpaca interaction was amazing, but surely they can treat all their animals with dignity. While we were there, a macaw flew away into the surrounding trees. Clearly the parrot did not have an attached handler nor proper training for flighted birds.

What's there to see here? There's the rocks, the sea, and a few souvenir shops, but really, the place is, quite frankly, overrated. The rock doesn't even resemble a dragon's head!This may be one of my shortest reviews ever, but it's only because the place is not very interesting. Yes, there's a great sea view (the reason why I didn't give this attraction a   terrible   rating), but other than that, there's really no reason to visit this place.Only give this attraction a go if you really fancy posing with the rock, or if you really love the sea. My humble opinion is that Jeju definitely has more places worthy of your precious time.

What WERE they thinking of! The   museum   is a few glass cases with examples of bars/boxes of chocolates. The   factory   is a table where you can buy cooking chocolate and make your own. The only good news is that your (HUGE) entrance fee is refunded in the way of a coupon to use at the (VERY OVERPRICED) chocolate shop. There is NOTHING here. It's AWFUL.Buy your choccies in the supermarket and give this place a wide berth.

Went with my friend and it was really a rare experience and rare sight for us. There are a lot of sculptures in the park and all of them come in different poses. It was a good chance to take some funny photos but we found it not so appropriate to take such pictures and so we didn't take much pictures of the sculptures.We walked across the park and saw different sculptures which have different funny messages (and we had a good laugh about some of the messages). After that we went in to their indoor shop where they sell   adults toys   and some chocolates (with pictures of different poses). There are also some shops outside which sell handmade stuffs and chocolates. Overall if you are in Jeju and you are not shy take a visit here once. However the way here is not so convenient. We took a taxi from our hotel since it is near (it took about 15 mins by taxi).

Went via a taxi tour in Early Feb 2014. Admission for each person: 2000 won.Hordes and hordes of tourists but you can still try to take some nice and pretty pictures while waiting for those tour groups passing by. Divers performance (if I am not wrong) is at 11am and 3pm. We did not went during that time so we did not manage to see it.Without going up to the peak, you can also see a nice view of the ocean and surroundings. There are also several souvenirs and food shops at the foot of the sunrise peak. It is a UNESCO site and it is a must to visit if you are in Jeju! Still awesome despite in winter.Don't forget that there are stairs and stairs up to the peak :P

Went today - very clear day. Reminded me of Falcor from the Never Ending Story. Hahahha!  We took the southern trail to the lookout. Was a great place to stop and see the local female divers gather fresh mussels, clams, abalone, squid and sea cucumbers. They quickly set up shop with a few kids stools and rock formations (ready made table top). They brought out a few bottles of soju (I think they hid it in the ocean to keep it cool. Luv the grapefruit flava) and they were ready for customers.  Freshest seafood I've ever tasted- Anthony Bordain would've been proud.

Went there without much training as I envisage that winter time is more pleasant to climb. We reached the base around 7.30am as we try to take the first bus. As we envisage there are snow, I have a pair of crampons bought before arriving in Jeju. Fortunately I did as the crampon sold at the shop is rather expensive. Then it was a relax 2 hours climb, I did not want to rush, but took time to appreciate the environments and snow. The crampons came in useful as you climb further up, it gets slippery. Good to have walking sticks too. At about the 1000+ meter stop, there is shop where you could buys hot noodles and drinks. I bought another set of crampons there as it is reasonable compared to the shop at the base of the mountain.After a short rest, the final climb to the top. Here there is a series of steps and staircase that leads to the top. At some point it was rather steep so have to climb up slowly, catching my breaths as the higher altitude and cold tends to slow you down. There is a timing to get down from the mountain per regulations, hence the need to get to the top early to enjoy the view and triumph. Finally reaching the top, was rewarded with a gorgeous scenery. It was kind of crowded and there was a queue of climbers taking turns to take picture with the summit monument.  After taking lots of pictures, hiking down was relatively easily, reaching the base in half the time. Took the bus back to town to enjoy a beer and fried chickens. A trip not to be missed.

Went there with my friend, we took bus from Jungmun (at the bus stop nearby tourist information center, at the right hand side). We took bus no. 781 and alighted at Teddy valley golf and resort, from there turn left (after you alighted) and walk straight for 1 min, you will see the museum at your left hand side. The entrance ticket cost 12000 won per adult. There are gift shop, Kitty History Hall, Music Education Hall, Art Gallery, Hello Kitty Caf챕, 3D Theater and more.. The Hello Kitty Cafe is very big and is beautifully designed and decorated.. There are a lot of cute hello kitty inside the museum and there are also some outside the museum. If you are a hello kitty fan, this is a must visit place when you come to Jeju.The museum closes at 6pm, so you might want to go there earlier.

Went there and hike up the hill for less than 20 minutes. Not suitable for elderly people to hike up the hill. Toilets at the hillside currently under construction. So there is no toilet at the peak. View was spectacular at the peak. Upon leaving, purchase a huge long foot sausage nearby GS shop. The pair of old couple was indeed very friendly ><

Went in the evening, the wind was very strong as we climb to the top. Amazing sceneries, worthy to climb up. The climb is fun, not difficult. There are many shops  nearby the entrance, prices varies for the same product so it's better to compare prices before buying.

Well, it was just a rock, nothing special as we come from a place full of strangely-shaped rocks and mountains (Guilin)! We tried the alive octopus at the restaurant near the rock, it was FUN!!! The shop owner caught and cut the octopus into small pieces. The poor thing was still stuck on the plate while we tried to get it into our mouth.  Tasted great with some mustard and soybean sauce!

Well worth the trip! The museum is very well presented and organized. So cute! So pink! Lots of kids and laughter about. You can opt to pay for extras, like buttons, passport stamp collecting and heart shaped tag to write on and lock onto the balcony. Some furniture is a bit run down but overall it is really well cared for. The staff is very friendly and helpful. You can also get small food and drink from the cafe and there is a jungle gym are for children to play. They have a short movie and photo station on the roof at the end. The gift shop had lots to choose from and prices were pretty good compared to official merchandise sold elsewhere online. Spent almost the whole day there and I loved every second of it. The museum is incredibly interactive, it would be hard not to have fun. Brought my boyfriend and even he couldn't believe how fun it was :)

Welcome to the first Teddy Bear Museum in Korea. Here you will find everything you want to know about Teddy Bears. Teddy Bears have been loved and cherished since they were first introduced over 100 years ago. There are now millions of people who collect Teddy Bears. They seek out old, unique and valuable teddy bears for their personal collections. Our Teddy Bear Museum opened especially for the European collectors. The Teddy Bear Museum is more exciting than ever with   Teddy Bear   entertainment as never seen before. Jeju Teddy Bear Museum opened on April 24, 2001. It contains two galleries, a museum gift shop, and a museum cafe. Also, on site is a museum bar/restaurant, a wonderful place to meet friends, family, and lovers. From the outside garden, there is a view of Jung-Mun Beach.

Wear sunscreen because this maze can take quite awhile to conquer!  I wouldn't advise trying to complete it during the middle of the day when there will be very little shade, because it can be quite hot while you are in the direct sunlight.There are restrooms, free parking, a small convenience store style snack shop, and a small picnic area under the trees near the parking area.  A fun stop.

We were there with a tour group and this itinary was compulsory.  Interesting to understand the history and a better understanding of the culture.  The guide of the village was obviously a Chinese but they spin it to say she is Korean (didn't see any)!  Sold products after the talk and items were not cheap.  360,000 Won for the Horse Bone Powder.  50,000 Won for the Horse Oil.  Saw at other shops away from the village, selling at 30,000 Won for the Horse oil.  Bought the Horse Bone powder and realized everything was in Korean!  If this is a State product and only sold in the village, pamplets of it should be in multi - languages as it is targeted at tourists.

We were received by a Chinese -speaking   Villager   upon entering the village. It is well set up, which gives a glimpse of the old life style of the local Jeju islanders. However, after a brief talk about the life of the local people, the guide was more interested to get us all seated inside a hut to sell her products, such as honey, Omija tea, and lo and behold...horse bone pellets (remedy for loss of calcium)! Her sales pitch was pushy and rather unfriendly, and we were not that interested by her goods (the price was exorbitant), we could sense her attitude turned from lukewarm to really cold. There is no doubt some local people really live here, as to keep the tradition alive, also supported by the government to do so. I think is better to keep the selling of local goods to another area (like setting up a gift shop), rather than incorporating it as some kind of compulsory lecture within the guide tour. I find that most off-putting. I give this place an average rating. The surrounding restaurants which serve the famous pork dishes from black pig were good.

We were looking for Dombaedon Restaurant in the black pork street.  We couldn't find it.  We went into a nearby shop to ask for info and were told that the restaurant at the corner - Dombedon Restaurant was good.The Dombedon Restaurant is a michelin starred restaurant.  It was quite crowded, we waited 30 minutes for our table.There were four of us, thought of ordering 3 portions to share (do not want to waste food).  We were told to order at least 4 portions.  So instead of ordering 4 portions of the black pork meat set, we ordered 2 portions of black pork set and 2 black pork bulgogi instead.The black pork bbq set came with steamed egg custard and kimchi stew.  The black pork was tender but a little fat though.  The meat was tasty and good to wrap and eat with perilla leaf.The black pork bulgogi was well marinated and juicy.  The black pork set 450g was KRW43,000 for two persons.  The bulgogi 180g was KRW18,000 for one person.  Though the price of this restaurant is higher compared to the other nearby restaurants, it's worth every cent of it.

We were looking for a good place to shop and buy souvenirs and we found this place in Jungang area. Lot of cheap items from clothes, bags, shoes and beauty products.Tips:- GPS: 752-8776- There is a public parking in front of Jeju Bank along Ohyeon-gil. 3-4 hours cost us 3700Krw.- Jejumok Gwana is just on the West exit (exit 11). You might want to drop by if you got time.- There are Korean food in the middle section. Cheap but taste good.

We were fortunate to catch a not-as-crowded ferry at around 2plus and stayed till 530pm and got back around 6pm. Ferry ride takes around 15mins but get up early and start walking towards the exit if u don't want to be Squashed w the main crowd! Upon arrival on the island, we decided to take the bus tour (costs 5000KRW/pax) which stops at 2 locations- the lighthouse peak as well as the beach.I must say Udo is very very windy so make sure u gear up and tie your hair if necessary!Hiking up to the lighthouse took us around 15mins up(lots of stairs, but after that it's v scenic). We had a good view of the whole island, despite being drizzly throughout the day. Dennis Cafe is really nice, cozy and affordable peanut ice cream as compared to the crowded 'Running man' ice cream shop which wasn't actually good. If I could go back, I would definitely bring my international driving license and rent an E bike!

We went to three or four different beaches on the island and this one hands down is the best. We didn't swim as it was in September already but spent a couple of hours strolling on the boardwalk. There are plenty of eateries across the street from the beach and some were on the beach side as well. The view was fantastic and definitely worth a visit. Also, parking was quite easy as well. We stopped for coffee (of course) and sweets at the nice coffee shop right on the beach before leaving and sitting there drinking coffee and watching sunset was a real treat.

we went to this place, but we didn't went up the park/hill/rock, as it will require lots of walking, which we didn't want to do :)you will still be able to have an impressive view at the entrance, and amazed by this natural creation. you can see the people walking up to the peak, enjoy the strong wind, as it is located by the sea, do a little shopping around the entrance area, or even find a nice cafe that is facing the spot to enjoy a hot coffee!

We went to this folks village on tour. For me, this village is very nice and i learn a lot of their culture. For example, as a Chinese, we celebrate Chinese New Year. The elderly will give red packets to us as a sign of good fortune. Everything comes in red during Chinese New Year. But in Korea, they will use White packets and everything comes in Black and White during Chinese New Year. This is because in old era of Korea, when they have wars, the man will be wearing white colour war costume and when they come back to their own house, their clothes is full of Red Colour Blood, that's the reason why they thinks that Red Colour is not a fortunate colour to them. More and more stories you can learn from this place, especially from the statue, you can see usually man is eating always and woman is the one who always do everything. That's their culture. This place is really worth a visit, and by the way, we are not being brought to those shop which sells local specialty. Hence, i felt that this place is nice to visit and nice place to take photos.

We went to the Teddy Bear Museum only because it was right next door to the Lotte Hotel Jeju where we stayed.  At 10,000 won per adult and 8,000 won per child, it is a bit pricey.  You can be done with all the displays and the 5 minute teddy Elvis show in an hour.  If you like teddy bears then it is a museum for you as there are alot of cute displays and exhibits that memorialize past events in history.  Kinda cool but not my thing.  I enjoyed the outdoor park area more.  You can take pictures with cute bear statues and sit and enjoy the greenery.  There is a cafe that sells Taiwanese pearl drinks and a nice gift shop.

We went to Dongmun Market on the last day of our tour in Jeju. There are many local produce here, especially seafood and tangerines. We sampled their street food and snacks as we strolled through the rows of stalls and shops, soaking up the local atmosphere. Our taxi tour guide, Mr Lee would help us to talk to the stallkeepers, and also ensure that we did not pay any extra. We did not have enough time to thoroughly check out the market because we had to catch a flight. This is one of the places I would visit again if I return to Jeju.

We went there for the DIY soap workshop. Fun and easy, just follow the steps in the video showed at the computer in front of you. You can then make a unique soap of your own. There is also a cafe for light lunch. And many Innisfree product to buy ad well ! A nice place to spend an hour or so during the raining day.

We went there by taxi from O'Sulloc Tea Museum. It's interesting when the displays are made of glass but nothing impressive. The entrance fee costs 9000 won but my friend and I got a discount thanks to the taxi driver uncle, and we end up paying 7000 won each.. The displays are mostly outside. On the 2nd floor, there is a gift shop..you can buy some gifts there and the cost is acceptable for some (e.g. accessories, keychain, etc) certain products (e.g. glass displays) are more expensive. It was raining when we visited the museum, but we just went around the museum and took some pictures. It is good to visit once but not more than that.

We went sometime March so the weather was a bit cold and the wind was strong since the mountain is near the ocean. Suggest to wear something warm and put on comfortable shoes for the hike. There are also cafes (Starbucks, etc.) and shops (Faceshop, local souvenir shops, etc.) by the entrance.

We went on the first Monday of the month, and the mountaineering trail was closed, so do take note when planning. However, the first portion of the trail was still available for free, which was still amazing and less of an exercise. The view from all spots were breathtaking, making this spot a must-see when you?re in Jeju.Do catch the woman?s diver show at 1.30pm and 3pm, located down the trail. It was an interesting experience to see the elderly women dive down to retrieve the seafood in the ocean, and you can buy and eat some of their fresh catches at the shop nearby.Highly recommend for a magnificent sightseeing experience in Jeju!

We went on a very rainy day so there weren?t many people.     The white seafoam crashing against the rock was amazing.     The formations were breathtaking.     Information given in English about how they were formed.      It doesn?t take very long to walk the trail, no more than 30 minutes.     There are toilet facilities and a couple shops with limited food and other items for purchase.   On a nicer day, there would probably be a lot more vendors.

We wanted to visit an orange, (tangerine) farm in Jeju, where the famous Jeju oranges are grown.Through the tourists information centre, we found this farm nearest from the city centre. We had to take a bus.It is a very nice orange farm. Fee is 5,000\ per pax- with unlimited time, eat as much oranges as you want while in the orchard & get to bring back 1kg of oranges at the end of it.Great deal considering 1 small tray of oranges in the markets are selling for same price or higher.The young lady in charge was very friendly & helpful although she don't speak English ( Google Translate comes in handy everytime ).The shop was very nice too. Products made at the farm using their fresh oranges includes jams, confectionery & oranges as well. The small production factory could be seen from the shop.Free tasting of their orange jam plus few pieces biscuits included. The jam was very good, made of real oranges.

We walked past Yongdu-am rock when we were trying to find the jimjilbang that we were staying at for the night. If we had made any effort to go and see it I would have been bummed but since it was in passing it was interesting in its own manner. I can understand how it looks like a dragon and you don't need TOO much of an imagination to be able to see it but unless your interested in folklore/'the dragon' means anything to you, you won't be overly excited/impressed.If it didn't have reams of tourists and tour buses or the tourist shops all around it Im not sure I would have even stopped to take a picture.(the ladies working in the tour information centre right outside of this area speak good english and are very kind and helpful if you need directions)

We visited this Innisfree flagship store after visiting the tea museum just besides it. This shop had a cafe with very nice looking desserts and staff were friendly and helpful. However, was sorely disappointed that a flagship store only sold skincare items and no makeup items at all :(

We visited the museum a bit reluctantly and only because we had dragged our two children (10 and 15) round two scenic waterfalls and an archery practice place in the hours before. Our youngest daughter was definitely keen to do something that she chose. When we got there our suspicions seemed to be confirmed with a relatively high entrance fee (I think it was 6,000 won per adult) for what seemed to be a small place.However, once we got into the diorama room, both kids couldn't stop themselves from oohing and aahing the whole time. You really felt that somebody had fun putting it all together. It was in all the little touches (like adding little German flags to the 'storming of the Berlin wall' display) and the set ups such as the 'Bearacotta Army). As previous reviewers have mentioned, all of these are in glass cases so my husband (who is a very keen photographer with decent equipment) didn't deign to take any photos - our teenage daughter took over instead. Having just completed our photobook, I can only say that we had plenty of good shots, I could easily have filled 20 rather than 4 pages with good shots.We didn't miss any English explanations - the teddies really spoke for themselves. We also didn't approach it as a museum but rather as a fun place to look around. The re-enactments of historical events from the 20th century were also fairly self-explanatory.The shop was probably the only really boring bit since the selection was not particularly big and the prices, given the location, quite high.Overall, don't go if you want to learn anything about teddy bears but do go in with kids (or adults who appreciate the cuteness).

We visited here in the fall during the annual Peanut Festival...yes, peanuts are grown on this island off the east coast of Jeju Island.  Autumn was a good time to visit there because it was cooler and not so crowded.  Our pension owner, Mr. Lee, picked us up at the ferry and drove us to our accommodation, right across the coast road from the famous white coral beach, the only one of its kind in Korea.  The coral beach was beautiful but much smaller than I'd expected and impossible to walk on without closed shoes.  The pension, called The Log House, is not only close to the beach, it is close to a cluster of restaurants and coffeeshops.  It is possible to do a lot of hiking and go up to the lighthouse for a 360 view and to catch the first glimpse of sunrise...which can be spectacular.  Because it was during the Peanut Festival, we could sample peanut wine and other local products, including several types of peanut icecream. We had a great room at the pension, on the corner with great views of the fishing boats and the famous Sunrise Peak crater across the channel.  The pension owner, Mr. Lee, spoke enough English to take care of all our needs.  At other pensions, little to no English is spoken by the staff/owners.  The owner also drove us to the ferry the next day.  Although bikes and ATVs are available for rent, the roads are a bit curvy and narrow for my comfort level.  If you like adventure, go for it!  Be sure to bring your international drivers license.  Enjoy!

We visited here during our cruise day trip of the island. This is a very scenic place with gorgeous architecture and the   spring of life  . WARNING: Do not drink from that spring unless you want to risk some messy   internal issues  . The walk involves some climbing but not too bad with no steps just a gradual walk up an inclined path. They offer a gift shop and snack bar as you enter and exit.

We visited as part of a group/tour and arrived late in the day (about 5pm). Huge carpark just outside.Not at all busy. Our guide walked us around the village and gave informative information (in English) about the history of the island and the life styles of the people that would have/do live here.The few residents that we saw didn?t want photos taken, I thought a little strange since they live in a ?theme park? and must see tourists every day of the year.We were allowed to poke our heads into specified rooms/houses.There was a shop for gifts etc and a WC block for the use of behind the guest villa at the backWe spent about 40 mins here

We thought that since we are here in Jeju that we should visit Hello Kitty Island to buy our niece some gifts.  It turned out to be a big mistake.  First, there was this steep entry fee that you have to pay just to get into the building.  Then there was this lack of history on Hello Kitty.  Not educational for kids at all.  Finally, the stuff they sell at the gift shop were so expensive it put Japan to shame.  Not much of the products even have the trademark for specific sites.  Hello Kitty fans beware!!  You are better off going to Seoul to get gifts than here.

We stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal as we knew that we needed to take an early bus to Hallasan. We noted that we needed to reach a certain point on Hallasan by 12.30pm as they would not allow people to continue to hike up after 12.30pm due to foreseen danger. We took bus 782 at 6.00am sharp from seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal and alight at Seongpanak bus stop to start our hike at Hallasan. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly.  The ride took about 30 minutes. The cost of the ride was less than 2000won and the bus driver could provide change if needed. We alighted at Seongpanak bus stop on the side with a hiking track. That track was not the track up to Hallasan. We needed to cross to the opposite side and pass the souvenir and rest stop place to the correct Hallasan track (free entrance). In the beginning the track was gentle and doable. We managed to spot birds and deer grazing around. However, the rest of the track up was pretty boring as there was nothing much to see. After 1-2km, the hike started to be more steep (as in more elevated with steps) as there were many rocky steps to hike up. There were two rest stops before the summit that provided fairly clean and well-maintained toilet with toilet paper. However, there would not be any tap to wash hands. Therefore, remember to buy wet wipes to clean your hands. At the second rest stop, raman, drinks and crampons were sold. Get all the supplies you need before hiking up as there is no shops at the summit. It will be good to bring tomatoes or fruit for the hike as those provide fluid as well as sugar (instead of salty food item with msg ? this will make you feel sick). Anyway, you are not suppose to cook at the summit. Remember to bring trash bag to clear your trash too. From the second rest stop onwards, the steep rocky steps continued with harsher windy condition as you progress to the top. Therefore, remember to bring windbreaker and windproof pants as the wind was rather strong 1 to 2km before reaching the summit. We hike on 24 April with a summit temperature of 6 to 12 degree Celsius. We were blessed as there were no rain snow during the hike. The 1 to 2km up the summit consist of wooden steps that I found difficulty tracking up due to the wind and my lack of motivation (as I kept on looking at the summit and felt that it was so far away). Therefore, it would be better to just look at the steps in front of you and conquer those instead. When we finally reach the summit, we had a view of Baengnokdam crater and the surroundings. I was feeling nausea partly due to the fatigue as I did not exercise for 2 month prior to this hike. However, we managed to hike up to the summit in 3.5 hours. The wind continued to be harsh on us. Therefore we stayed for 15 minutes and decide to just hike down. Take pics even if you feel unwell. You will feel better as you ascend down. We hike down from the other hard track, the Gwaneumsa Trail although I was super tired. I did not regret that choice as it was much more scenic in comparison with the Seongpanak track. I thought that descending would not be a toll on me but I was wrong. As the track consist of many rocky steps, it was hard on my knees and I had to work on my balance too. The ajumma (they were over 50 years old) were able to hike way faster than me (in my early thirties). There was one rest stop only and we stop for the toilet. It was again clean with toilet paper provided. Generally, it was a descending hike with minimal ascending (with only a few flights of stairs up). We took 4.30 hours to hike down and I was totally shacked. The rest area at the bottom was also much more beautiful as compared to the Seongpanak rest stop. We wanted to take a bus back but we were told that there were no buses on Monday. There were buses back to Jeju city on other day from Gwaneumsa. (we noted that one of the bus come around 4pm towards Jeju city). We took a cab back to Jeju Dongmun Traditional Market for 20, 000 won. From the traditional market, we took a taxi for 3200 won to the bus terminal (bought bus ticket from the counter) to take bus 781 back to seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal (the journey was more than 1.5 hours).Personally, I find the hike difficult and I would suggest some stamina training to enjoy the hike better. I would suggest to hike when there is good weather as I find the hike difficult even in good weather (due to the rocky steps). Having said these, I would still recommend the hike as I love the challenge.

We stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal and took bus 110 from Jungang Rotary bus stop to Jungmun Tourist Complex. The bus journey about 30 minutes and cost less than 2000won one way. The bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly (Although I did not see Jungmun Tourist Complex on the TV screen, therefore I used GPS to locate instead. For my other bus trip, the stops were annoucne correctly and was reliable). You can press the bell to alight. Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. The Teddy bear museum is a small two storey museum. The famous personnel, movie and cartoon characters were dressed in bears to make those bears special. You can expected toy bears moving their limps as some bears were mechanically  wired. There is also a small outdoor park with some display of bears. There anShort 5 to 10 minutes elvis show at level 2 theatre. 30 minutes would be sufficient to finish the entire museum. The ground floor has a large souvenir shop where you can purchase teddy bear. A small palm size teddy key chain about SGD$15. A 10? bear cost about SGD$50. As I am not a bear fan, I rated 3 stars as I personally feel that SGD$12.50 for the entrance fee was a little pricy. However, I am sure the teddy bears fan would love this place and rated 4 stars and above. Anyway, the museum is close too many other attraction that is walking distance (Eg: Cheonjeyeon Falls). If not, you could also take a bus 702 to many other attractions like the Hyeopjae Beach. If not, you can take bus 782 or 110 back to seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal.

we stayed 3 nights in a hotel right near Black pork street, and it is rather close to Dongmun market, so we came here every afternoon when we finished our trip to famous attractions around the island. Lot of local eateries you can try, lot of candy/chocolate and mandarin shops those are specialties of Jeju that you can bring back home as gifts. From the Jeju bus terminal you can access here by bus #100 (takes around 10-15mins). bus stop is Dongmun rotary, right beside the entrance gate of the market.

We spent a nice & easy day on the island.  The island is small enough to complete within a day and yet big enough for you to do/see.  The ferry ride to the island was a short and easy one.  We didn't drive there which was good since we already pre-planned to ride around the island.  There were many rental shops to choose from.  There were many different types of vehicle you could choose from, e.g. manual bike, ebike, mini-car (not sure what you call them), etc. Do note that some will require international license.  We opted for the ebike which was in good use for the uphills. The route around the island was scenic and very instagrammable.  Many caf챕s to choose from. It is a good place to roam in your own pace and taking your own time to absorb the pretty views.Definitely a place worth going.

We selected yeongsil trail since we rarely hike in own country and it is recommended for beginner. We started our hike at 9:30am and it took us 3 hours to reach the shelter while 2 hours to come down. We used back same route to come down since we drove there. The cup noodle shop was closed when we reached the shelter, grateful we brought some biscuit and roti else we will starving after long hike hours. We didn?t expect still having ice on mountain since it is turning spring. This get bit challenging especially to me as my shoes a bit tough to walk on the ice. But luckily a korean lady offered her stick to me and hold my hand to cross the ice path. It really make a different with the stick support. It is really recommended to get prepare self well with good hiking shoes, enough water and food.

We rented bikes, very old bikes... and toured the island.  It is easy to do so and there is lots to see.  We arrived at 11am and saw the Udo women divers out collecting seaweed and shellfish.  By afternoon they had seaweed drying all over the island.  There were lots of picnic spots, coffe shops, and other forms of getting around.  This is a great day trip from Jeju or you can stay on island.Not alot of English spoken but did run into a couple of people in coffee shops that spoke English.  We didn't mind.  All signage is in English so it is still easy to get around.

We really enjoyed this hike with our family. It is steep, as the reviews noted, but it is very fast. Our five-year-old and seven-year-old had no problem doing it on their own. It has nice views, isn?t very difficult, and it?s right next to an interesting coffee shop (you can see it from the parking lot) that has been converted from an old horseback riding resort. The coffee shop also has a bakery with some delicious treats for after the hike.  Easy to find and plenty of parking.  Overall a great little outing.

We planned this for the kids but the adults had fun too. When we arrived, we bought the tickets while the kids were busy with the numerous cats around the area. It turns out that this is also a place for cat lovers, this place is a mini cat world too. You can get cat food from the ticket counter to feed the cats.In the maze, the kids formed a team and raced with us, the parents. Each team had to find the stamps hidden around the maze and stamp on the paper given. First team to collect all 6 stamps and ring the bell to exit the maze wins.Upon exiting the maze, as we passed thru the ticket counter again, the lady manning the counter asked us to visit the gift shop to claim a free postcard.

We originally got the bus here to go to hallim park. we noticed this beautiful beach and decided to check it out. anyway we ended up staying here all day. Was so nice to be on such soft, yellow sand with clear waters. There was quite a few families with young children which was nice to see all the children playing. Unfortunately there was a digger truck digging the sand while we were there for a few hours and a man kept blowing his whistle at everyone walking near the truck. if it wasnt for this it would have been excellent. Theres shops and restaurants close by and toilet blocks that provide flowing water to wash off but this is cut off around 5 or 6 pm. Sunset here was amazing.

We learnt about the folklore, daily life and local people in the village, worthy the 1-hour drive! The local guide (an old woman) taught us some dialect and showed us some daily-used tools back in the past. At last she led us to a shopping room for some honey and medicine. It would have been perfect if we had more time and spent less in the shop.

We hired bicycles at a shop adjacent the pier and cycled around the whole island. Along country roods, there were many scenic spots, mostly adjacent to the sea,  where we could take pictures. Besides, there were many cafes and kiosks where we could dine and rest.  Cycling around the island in a relaxing pace took about 3 to 4 hours. It was a very good experience.

We hiked up the Seongpanak  trail in Early September. From Seogwipo City, it is quite remote and we took a long taxi ride to get there. The wy up was beautiful, rising through the forest, befor emerging into stunning views up the peak, trails along gorges and n awesome suspension bridge. Trail was populated but not too busy, the peak was busy but the view was spectacular - you could see clear out to sea on both sides of the island. We took the shallower and busier gwaneumsa trail down, this was a less exciting walk, but has shops and bus stops at the trail head. This is definitely a must do hike if you are able to manage it.

We hiked this in December in the snow.  We started from the Yeongsil entrance, and just went up to the Shelter as we started pretty late.  The hike is tough for those who are out of shape but perfectly doable for regular hikers.  It took us about 2 hours up and about 1.5 hours down - the snow making it much slower than we would normally take (and more scenic, but very slippery in places).I would recommend good hiking shoes as the rocks are tough and slippery in places - I saw some people wearing what I would consider to be bedroom slippers and they were really struggling!  Those mini-crampons were also a godsend in the snow (the shop at the bottom sells them).Great views on the way up and from the top.  As we had a car, we had to go back the way we came but next time we will come when the plants are green and do a loop hike.  Can't wait.

We heard from travelers and locals that this street are famous because of their native black pork.in our 3 days stay in jeju, we have tried 3 black pork restaurants in this street. The people working in the restaurant are very accomodating, service are great! Specially the black pork itself. I must say im addicted toIt. I keep coming back when i have a chance. And the next to the street are shopping stores where you can find a lot of choices

We have visited this beach on our first day in Jeju island. As soon as we walked in we felt so happy to see this beautiful beach! It was beginning of September, it was hot but as soon as we went to beach we almost got frozen due to strong wind. Sand is white and when combined with clear sky water appears Caribbean blue :) it was difficult to find a place to sit as it was overcrowded. We asked a lady in a local shop to keep our belongings for us while we are swimming, she was very kind and didn't ask any money from us. We also met sunset on this beach. It was gorgeous.Tip. Take a windproof jacket with a hood of you cannot stand for wind for a long time.Renting a place on beach with umbrella costs 10,000KRW. Renting some inflatable toy (flamingo for example) is also 10,000. Life vest/goggles rent is also 10,000. And you won't see any price tags around, kind of weird.Food around. Chinese restaurant across the street serves nice jajamyun noodles for 6 or 7,000 KRW. I can recommend it. Drinks - cafe bene with gorgeous view. Average coffee. Good bagels with crab meat.

We had dinner at a resto in Blackpork street in Jejusi which locates opposite Dongmun market. The price was 14.000w/200gr (normal pork) and 18.000w/200gr (black pork). Our meal was so delicious, it costed nearly 40.000w for two of us. You are highly recommended to have a try with this once you visit Jeju, as black pork bbq is one of the island?s specialties. Near the Blackpork street is the shopping street and underground shopping area where you could have a walk after a heavy meal.

We got there by bus. It was a rainy day and the walk was like 2-3 km so we took a taxi. 5 min drive for 4$ was a very good option vs getting all wet. This was one of the highlights of my jeju trip. Walking down those amazing lava tubes. You feel so small. It's midly cold and water drips from the ceiling so bring an overcoat. The ground is uneven but you can walk easily still. Saw old people with walking sticks along the way. Very cheap ticket entry for the marvel this is. At the end, there is a beautiful stalactite that makes a great pic. There are dim lights along the way but my headlamp made walking easier for me and people walking in front of me... You guys are welcome lol There is a restaurant at the entrance. Pretty expensive one. But if you cross to the joined convenient souvenir shop, they make fast korean food for a thenth of the price. They have soup, gimbap, mandoo and they are very good. Not the greatest place for souvenirs since that store is the only one around and does not have much. In between those 2 places, there is a small museum that takes around 10 min to cross and it explains the formation of the lava tube. Very interesting. A must do!

We followed Trip Advisor's map and was brought to a small hotel garden area. We were iniatially confused but the hotel staff pointed the way to us. It wasn't very far already. We took our time walking, and to tell you the truth, I was glad we came the way we came. We found a way down to the rocky beach and climbed a little right to where the waves break. At that point the rocks aren't geometrical, just normal. Afters we walked thru a garden, which was a good distraction, and finally arrived at the cliffs. To my disappointment we can't actually go down to the rocks. And then there were a few shops selling fresh seafood, postcards, ice cream, mandarin oranges and to my surprise, some hallabong oranges. I got it pretty cheap too, compared to other places that I went after that

We finally found this street on our second attempt. Google map failed to function well in Korea, don't know why. Maps.me as suggested by other blogger was good for car travellers. It is not stable for pedestrians. Anyway, it's just opposite the jeju dongmun traditional market, cross the main road and the street is at the inner side. You may show the entrance arch to shop keepers nearby, they will indicate the direction. To me, the black pork is not anything spectacular, just common bbq as can be found elsewhere. I am not a food critic, hence I couldn't actually tell the difference. You can try any of the restaurants in this street. I guess they are the same. Enjoy!

We enjoyed our time in Innisfree Jeju House very much and will definitely return if we ever visit Jeju Island again! It links to Osulloc Tea Museum. Just a few steps away and you will arrive at Innisfree Jeju House. The retail area was crowded. While ladies shop for their skincare, we had some really unique desserts, coffee and tea in the cafe. You can also purchase the hand soap making kit and make your own soap there. Not to forget to enjoy the tea field view before you leave the place!

We enjoy shopping underground. We were able walk from one end to another. Just remember where you enter. There is a number so you will not get lost.There were beauty products, children clothing, adult clothing, bags, shoes, restaurants, etc. They are not your designer stuff but cheap items. Since winter, they sell winter wear. We bought some face masks, cleanser for less than $10. We also bought bags for $15. The lady said made in korea so we think ok. The backpack is great cos very spacous. Good for traveling. Quality is just ok. Then at one exit near to the wet market, we found a shop called bang bang. It belongs to a friend of the korean actor who starred in the famous korean drama   my love from the star   we were able to buy simple T shirts, socks. They are less than $10. Socks about $3. We actually shop here 2 times when we were staying in ocean suites hotel. It was just 10 to 15 minutes walk to this underground shopping area.There are restaurants here too. We found a good korean restaurant here. It was good food and affordable.

We drove over to Sunrise Peak on a rainy, windy day in October and knew that we would be back the following day when the rain was supposed to be gone. Thank goodness, we came back, it would have been a miserable and somewhat dangerous hike in the rain. The ticket for the hike was less than $4 USD for two adults. The hike is full of stone stairs, and if you follow the signs (please follow the signs, don't be that person) there are plenty of places to stop, rest, and enjoy the view. At the halfway point, there is even a small shop with drinks and a souvenir stand that will char a wood sign for you with your name. When we got to the top, and enjoyed the clear, clean skies (so different from Seoul) we could watch the fishing boats and could even see some of the Women Divers of Jeju at the bottom. My suggestion is to get there early, the trails opened at 0730 and enjoy your hike. The bus tours and most other Korean tourists won't be out that early. Wear good shoes and comfortable clothing and bring your camera. It was a lovely sight in October. By the time we came back down after enjoying the views and watching the divers, the parking lot was starting to fill up with many bus tours. This place would still be gorgeous, but not as fun, if we would have had to share the stone stairs with 3,000 of our closest tourists.

We drove ourselves and although a little hard to find, it was worth the effort. The area was quite well set out with information and small local restaurant and gift shop area. Entry is free to Jeju workers but about 5,000 won - the steps down are step but well made. We walked about 2 kms to the end of the tunnel - it was damp, cold and generally well lit. Wear sturdy shoes and a warm coat, take a water bottle.  Worth a look.

We drove our rented car onto the ferry which took us to Udo in 15 minutes. If the weather hadnt been so cold, we would have tried the fun looking electric scooters. We stumbled into a seafood restaurant to the left of the ferry terminal and enjoyed a sumptuous seafood kimchi hotpot. Ordering was not a problem as the service staff spoke mandarin. The place was an obvious favourite with locals. We spent 4 hours exploring various sites and even got lost. A friendly local policeman kindly pointed us the right way. We stopped by quaint coffeeshops and hugged their cute puppies. We were reluctant to leave this idyllic tiny island.

We decided to visit one of JeJu?s famous attractions Hallim park. We took bus 100 from the Jeju intercity bus station and had a relaxing journey to the west side of the island passing through countryside and the coast line. The bus stops at the Hallim park bus stop and you still have a little walk along the road and through the car park until you come to the entrance.(entrance fee 10,000 won) we were lucky because the weather was good for June , sunny but not too hot as you do spend alot of time walking around. On entering you will see a large map of the park with all its attractions numbered, there is also a very good gift shop which has a large range of items from T.shirts to natural products made into soaps and teas. Then you start the walk of around 10 different attractions including water garden, bird garden, subtropical garden and ofcourse the attraction most people come to see the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves.Jeju is famous for its volcanic larva tubes and caves and if you haven?t visited any then this is a good time as its alot more convenient than doing another trip to the other caves. The park is actually quite big and you do need to spend a good 2 hours to see it all, so if your going to visit the nearby beaches allow yourself enough time.There are also some restaurants and washroom facilities.

We decided to visit one of Je Ju Islands  popular beaches on the north of the Island. As we were staying in the north of Je Ju city we decided to take a taxi to the Inter-city bus terminal ( taxis are cheap compared to most cities) we boarded bus no. 10 and used our Emoney card to pay, you can get them from most convevience stores (saves you worrying about the fare and right money)The bus journey was pleasant and took you pass some natural sites and small villages.All the bus stops are named in English and there is a video screen on the bus telling you the next stop. On arrival of the beach bus stop it seems quiet with only a few shops and a good size supermarket , as you proceed along you will see the main entrance of the beach but still have a little walk until you come to it. The beach is spectacular just as shown on most tourist advertisements , one thing you will notice in JeJu is that the people respect the nature and surroundings. The beach is spotless with clean white sand and as you look to the right you will see the ever familiar black volcanic rock, it makes a nice contrast with the crystal clear blue sea.As we visited the beach at the end of June it was less crowded and the beach season hadn?t officially began.However the toilet and shower facilities were still open, the main beach is a good size and as the tide was out when we got there you can still paddle around and search for fish or crabs in the rock areas. We then went to the second beach which is just a little walk away , it is next to Seoubong peak and a bit smaller but just as nice. All in all the beach at this time of the year is good to visit and relax , the water was a little cold but there were people swimming.

We decided to include this in our tour after feeling a bit tired from all the hiking up mountains and paths. It's an easy couple of hours, especially if you have kids, whom seemed to be entertained with every variation of dressed up bear. There is also an extensive gift shop, with, you've guessed it, lots of bears and cuddlies. The prices aren't exactly cheap, but the quality seemed good. It's a good way to slow the pace down if you are in need of a rest.. Nice afternoon out.

We chance upon this on our drive from Seogwipo to Hyeopjae.  The pink building is big and visible from the highway. They should have repainted it as it looks washout and faded pink. But once I step in, it?s totally new! Infact it is even newer than Sanrio Puroland which I visited in Tokyo and bigger than there! I am a true blue HK fan since 40 years ago. Once HK fan steps in, I am sure you will be transformed to a little princess at heart and you?ll be so excited again! There are a lot of Instagram worthy area to take photos. As others pointed out, it has a section that talks about the evolution of HK from 1970s till now.  There are HK rooms, dining room, bus, living room, wardrobe, dressing room etc. Even the toilets are so pretty! Level 2 offers some purikura area, a restaurant and some other HK displays.  There is a 3D dancing room too. On the 3rd floor, there is a open air rooftop HK small maze. On level 1, you go through the souvenirs shop to exit and a notice states that once u exit, u can?t go in again. So it?s best that u buy yr souvenirs when u are ready to leave. I swear I could stay there for 3 hours but as my husband is with me, it only took us about 1.5 hrs to complete our visit. Overall this place is small and not much for non Kitty fans. For us Kitty fans, it is definitely a must visit.

We caught the 7:30 am ferry from Seongshan Port to Udo.  The ferry left a bit early so we actually arrived at the island by 7:35.  The ferry ride should be about 15 minutes.  Cost was 17,000 kwr for 2 adults for round-trip tickets.  We struggled with whether we should have brought our car on board and immediately regretted not doing so once we landed.  Seems it is off season so not busy at all.  The first place we stopped at was the mango shop, where they also have a shop In the back for vehicle rentals.  Stopped there and tried to rent a mini-car/scooter but the staff said no rentals today because of the festival (seems it is the seashell festival).  Anyway, with no other option, we just took the hop-on and hop-off bus (5000 krw per person).  It?s about 21,000 krw round trip for a small car.  First stop was the lighthouse, got there at 7:45 and went back down to catch the next bus at 8:30.  The next stop after was the black sand beach.  Then to the other lighthouse on the northern tip of the island.  We concluded our trip at the stop after that which is the other ferry port.  We caught the 10 am ferry.  We skipped the white sand beach which is probably the most popular site as a lot of Korean dramas were shot there.  Some tips:- bring your car if you have one so you can visit the island on your own schedule - try the peanut ice cream at Jimmy?s Natural Ice Cream- most of the food places may be closed on a Sunday

We arrived here by bus from our Jeju hotel on a Friday night.  It took approximately 35-40 minutes because of the traffic and the nondirect route our bus took.  The front of the market (across the street) has a small open square area where they would have live music for the night.  We also noticed a few drunks sitting around in the area, but they seemed harmless.The market itself is quite large.  The market seemed to specialize in selling tangerines.  There were stall after stall selling local tangerines.  There is a larger variety of items offered for sale as you walk into the market some more.  We tried some food that was being sold - in this case, some pork at around 9000 won.  There is also seafood and other vegetables and meats sold.  The market seemed to extend to other areas - it's quite close to the Black Pork Street, some other more upscale shops and restaurants.  It's definitely worth a 1-2 hour walk within the market to explore.

We approximate the climb to be about 2,200 steps. So about an hour  to get up and down. The view while climbing to the top is breathtaking. You get a 360 degree view of Jeju. The stairs for climbing are easy for short legs like mine. They've got railings for you to hold on to and some rest points every so often. There are speakers located in certain areas as well to tell you the history of the place in Korean and Japanese. I'm pretty sure there's an English and Chinese version too. There's a person at the top too to give you some information regarding the place. There are some shops located at the foot of the place where you can eat and shop as well. The journey to the top was better than the view of what was on top.

Water was very clear and sand was clean. There are some shops on the beach, and toilet facilities close by. Plenty of eating places around the area too. A nice beach to spent a day or just a little while. There are people firing fireworks at night. So if you happen to be there when that happen, you are in for some light show.

Was recommended to find dinner on this street so we decided to check it out but ended up having the best dinner in jeju. Was gonna go into a famous corner shop but the wait was too long so we went to the one beside it (2nd shop, sorry don't know the name). Ordered a mixed grill so we had black pork and abalone (famous in jeju too) with the other dishes too. Great selection of side dishes as well. But it was really expensive, maybe around 70AU$ but felt that it was worth it.
walking in the local dongmun market, I was impressed with a lots of fresh fish shops. I can observe how local people work and enjoy their normal life.Seafood is fresh and at reasonable price!
Walk into a 3 storeys building. Gift shop, 3D theater, Hello Kitty Cafe and all sorts of Hello Kitty. Good fun place to explore, feeling happy and young again.

Visited this place on 4 June but was closed for renovations. Luckily beside it, there is the O?셲ulloc Tea shop and museum. However this place is over crowded and the washroom is the most smelly I?셶e ever been in the whole of Jeju. Skip it and buy yr Innisfree elsewhere in Korea.

Visited this hello kitty island with my young children and family. Its like a museum of hello kitty, with a lay area for kids on level 2 and also a cafe. On level 3, there is a small theatre area for a short 8 minutes show. The food in the cafe are all hello kitty themed. And not forgetting a hello kitty souvenir shop. Spent around 1 1/2 hours here.

Visited Hamdeok Beach (⑤댁) with my boyfriend. We took a walk around the beach. It was really windy and cold. The wind was strong. The beach is very clean and beautiful. The waters are clear. We took some pictures there and we happened to see couple having wedding photoshoot (with the beautiful scenery).Many people from various age groups visited this beach. It is a nice place to take a walk and chill out. There are hotels, shops, convenience stores, cafes and restaurants nearby the beach. There is also public toilet nearby the beach (near the carpark). We drove there. It is very convenient and we can get some snacks while chilling out there.

Visit to Udo has to be the best bet on my trip to Jeju! It was not on my itinerary until I reached Jeju - initially put off by a journey over because I don't drive and I was afraid I will lose my way, miss ferries etc. Glad I went Udo!It wasn't difficult to reach the port to catch my ferry as I got guidance from the staff where I was staying (December Hotel Jeju). I took bus and watched the scenery along the way till I reached the terminal stop. Bought my ferry tickets and was quickly onboard (there seems to be more ferries than I thought and read). Watched others feed the seagulls food on the ferry ride and in a short while, I arrived at the island! There were many options on how you want to travel around the island and so I took the most rustic and simple way --- bicycle! It was not difficult and I got to choose a cute pink bicycle as my companion for the day. I took the clockwise path and followed the many other visitors on the road.Udo brought me many surprises - many people but not rowdy, beautiful beautiful waters and beaches (see my photos), cool yet warm, quiet along some paths but not totally deserted. I liked the fact there are many photo stops, and the food I tried there were delicious! I love the Hallasan Fried Rice at the shop I chanced upon randomly - stopped cos I felt hungry. And it was one of the greatest food deal I had!I would choose to come here, earlier, again next time. There were some other areas I didn't manage to explore as I wanted to catch the ferry back. I could have also spend some time chilling at the cafe for a snack or drink. I find this the best way to enjoy Udo, away from all the hype of Jeju itself. Love it.

Very underwhelmed. Arrived by ship & took free port shuttle into Jeju-si (capital) & dropped by the Jungang underground shopping street & Guandeokjeong. Walked past Yongyeon Bridge & past park to Dongduam rock. Pleasant walk. Then back to find Black Pork St, but didn't try it as we had heard it was nothing special. Enough to fill in a day (about 6 hours ashore.) Friends who went on a trip round the island said it wasn't terribly interesting & worth the cost. Do pick up a map from the tourist info kiosk, not far from where you arrive, then you can walk round sights described

Very nice island. You take a ferry from Jeju Island to Udo in 5-10 minutes you get there. I rented a quadricycle and it was fun to discover the island by this transportation mode. The ocean is clean and warm; pretty nice to bathe!The shops however don't speak English normally. If in Jeju, I totally recommend Udo as a spot to visit.
Very near the Dongmun market, just like any ordinary underground shopping center. Nothing new, nothing different. Many entrances and exits too.
Very easy to walk to. Eating places nearby. Very beautiful.  We had breakfast at Dunkin Doughnuts nearby. Cost is 2,000 won to see. Unique shopping near location.

Very big market. Combination of a wet and dry market. Interesting cos they sell many live seafood, vegetables, fruits, sourvenir.The seafood seems expensive when i convert but it could be cos more for tourists. A fish can be $50. We enjoy eating the local food like cuttle fish, fish cake, fish ball, crab stick. About $4 to $7. Just immerse in local culture. The colouful array of oranges and by oroducts. 15 boxes orange chocolate for 10k won. Looks alot but one box only 8 pcs candies so bulky to carry.There is a store sells korean sourvenir like keychain, clipper, magnet, etc $3 to 5 a piece.Bought a sweatpants 5k won so less than $10.Did not dare buy hallabong oranges cos too heavy to carry home. More for local tourists.Overall we do enjoy this market. Near to the underground shopping and fashion street too.

Very beautiful place. Nice people, peaceful place. I want to come next time to visit it once more. We took photo with the founder of this garden. He is very nice person. In the garden you can see bansai trees and feed fishes, also there are some mini shops and cafe were you can drink coffee or the legendary rice wine.

Unlike Hello Kitty, I think most of us have cuddled or have in possession a toy teddy bear at a certain stage of our lives. So it is no wonder that the Teddy Bear Museum has such a wide appeal and which surely be included as a ?compulsory? destination on the itinerary of the independent travellers (especially those with children) and tour companies alike.Getting there and fees: We visited Teddy Bear Museum (GPS coordinate/code 7387600) on a rainy day, which was appropriate since the exhibits are predominantly indoor, except for the Teddy Bear Garden and Park where there?re a few teddy bear figurines outside and a park with great views of the sea.  The admission charges are 10,000 won for adults won, 9,000 won for teens and 8,000 won for children.The Museum/Attraction:  This Teddy Bear Museum is the first and largest teddy bear museum in South Korea. Once you enter, you are greeted by this huge teddy bear, who gives you a ?grand? welcome to further explore the five sections spread over 3 levels: The History Hall, The Art Hall and The Project Exhibition Hall, Gift Shop (all indoors) and an outdoor Teddy Bear Garden and Park. There?s also a caf챕/restaurant. Be prepared to spend at least 1 hour looking and taking photographs/selfies at all the interesting exhibits. The History Hall comprised of the history of bear manufacturing and some of the earliest toy bears, many of which are antique and rare. It also showcases milestones in human history, with the bears enacting several famous (human) historical scenes from different eras. This is indeed a refreshing concept for a museum! I particularly liked the teddy bears enacting the Titanic, landings on the moon and the iconic celebrities like the Beatles and Gandhi.In the Art Hall, you could see the world-famous artworks and designs in an art gallery form as well as animation characters beloved by children. I liked the Mona Lisa and two of the most expensive bears in the world - the Louis Vuitton teddy bear and the Diamond Bear. In the Project Exhibition Hall, you would meet teddy bears grouped to suit the theme of each exhibition. Not forgetting the large Gift Shop on the first level. While it offers plenty of gifts, these are nonetheless pricey. Nevertheless, you could take photos with Michael Jackson bear, Steve Jobs bear and a wedding couple bear amongst others. There?s also a mother panda with her baby pandas on display too.  We certainly enjoyed the wonderful experience of the Museum bringing out the child in each of us, and making us feel young again. Despite the pricey entrance fees, I still think the Teddy Bear Museum is worth visiting, and to me, once would be sufficient. But if you don?t like teddy bears at all, then it would be prudent to skip this attraction.

Unless you really really love Teddy Bears, this place is rather overpriced. At 8,000KRW per person, it gets expensive if you're in a group. And, they won't let you enter the gift shop without paying for a ticket. In the end, we found their gift shop not terribly different from the Safari Teseum (7,000KRW per person, but you can go directly to the gift shop). The Safari Teseum gift shop actually had more options (aka other animals for those who don't like stuffed bears).Still, if you really love Teddy Bears, you can make a day of it between the two places.
Underwhelming. We needed a stop and there were some interesting shops nearby (persimmons and mushrooms, I think) so it wasn't a total loss, but not worth the detour.

Udo- we went early, were there before 9am. Spent roughly 3 hours on the key spots.1. Ferry to Udo- Our jumbo taxi driver drove us over. Needed to fill out all personal details plus showing our passports when purchasing tickets. Return trip for 5 of us plus driver plus jumbo taxi return was KRW70,000. No queues, not crowded. We went there on 2 Jun 2017 Friday. Just a 15-min ride, need to leave the car diring the trip. Have a good view of Sunrise Peak from the ferry.2. Peak- For a good view of Jeju and Udo, walk up to the peak. Be alert that the track along the coastline uphill is not an easy one for people who don't exercise a lot.  Useful to have hiking stick with you for this short track.3. Geommeollae Beach- Absolutely gorgeous scenery.  A must go place. That's where the famous peanut icecream shops are. There are two.  We tried one and it tasted well.4. Beaches- We went to two. Unforgettable colour and tranquility.  Must go as well.

Udo Island is a small island located in the east side of Jeju. We visited there due the great reviews given below in TripAdvisor. It cost about 5,500 won for the ferry ride to and fro. My friend and I wanted to ride the ATV while we were there however the rental shops were strict on the rental without international driving license so in the end we took a tour bus that stops at 4 different locations and cost 5,000won per person. The bus comes at an interval of 30 minutes so once you get down in one location, you can stay at the location for 30 minutes before moving on to another place. As we went there in Spring, the canola flowers are blooming beautifully. We also went to the Black Sand Beach and also the Hyopje Beach. Quite a good worth of money if you are looking at short tours around the island.

Udo island is a small island at east of Jeju Island. It is named after cow because of its cow alike shape. Once you reached the island, you are able to find few bike rental shop. You can rent a electrical scooter with roof or normal scooter to tour around the island. Bare in mind the speed limit is 30 km/h. Most of the rental shop offer two hours rental only. Generally, it should be sufficient if you don't linger at each place too long. Do try the peanut ice-cream as the island is famous for peanut plantation. Get your camera ready as there are many beautiful scenaries to take photos.

Udo is a really small island, you can go around by bicycle in several hours. Udo is a volcanic island, so it has several nice beaches with white and black sand, impressing lava rock formations, caves etc. We went there several times, every time for 2-3 days, and every time it was just wonderful. You should go and spend a few days there if you want to relax in a quite and peaceful atmosphere with no nightlife, co crowds, no big attractions but with beautiful nature. Still, if you want to get in touch with the rest of the world - no problem here, our Korean mobiles were working fine, Internet was available right in the   arrival hall   of the port and in many   minbaks   (small Korean-style hotels).You can get there easily from Seongsan port  (＿?깆??고) of Jeju island by ferry in just 10-15 minutes. Ferries depart every hour from 08.00 till 17.30 or 18.00 depending on season. Most accommodations are found on on the White Coral Beach (Seo-bin-baek-sa, ＿?鍮諛깆?? or  Sanhosa, ??고몄?? ), 10 minutes walk from the port. They are all small 1-2 floor buildings located directly on the beach with seaview (Pensions, Minbaks). We never booked anything in advance, but found a room on site, but we went in May and October - not highest season. The rooms were always nice and big, also with kitchen and all the necessary kitchenware. Also there are small shops with snacks and some Korean restaurants.So, what to do in there?- swim in the pure emerald water of White coral beach, see the special kind of sand, it really feels like you are in tropics ^^- rent a bike and go around the islandThe road goes nicely along the shore, there were almost no cars except on the busier Jeju-facing side, and we enjoyed the scenery very much!  - Geommeolle Beach (寃?硫?)This is a black sand beach with very beautiful and unusual rock formations and caves, and we spent a very good time there. You can go in caves and see small rocks piled up on each other. And once a year they have a symphony concert in the caves!!Also, if you are a diver with a certificate, there is a diver center there. We tried to do it, but we did not have a PADI certificate so they refused, they do not do fun dives.And  we took a motor boat (10 000W/person) to see farther caves with a spectacular view of Udo cliffs (Hu-hae-seok-byeok, ＿?댁＿?踰). If you are lucky, you can also see a peculiar site called Ju-gan-myeong-weol - sun reflecting at the ceiling of a cave giving a   moon shape  . We also went up the hill, nice view of both Udo and Jeju!!What problems you can encounter in Udo?- languageLocal people are friendly and try to help, but they do not understand English!!So if you do not speak Korean, print out Korean names of what you want to visit and some basic Korean phrases (preferably in Korean, not transcriptions, because pronunciation may be tricky). BUT! the owner of the LOG-house speaks English very good!- foodThere is no Western restaurants on the island, only Korean!! The shops on the beach only sell snacks like Ramen, but there is a bigger mart inland called Hana-ro Mart with fruits, vegetables, milk, etc. (??濡 留, try to ask locals for directions and go there by bike, you will find it, there is no place to get lost ^^). And it could be a good idea to bring some food with you from Jeju, especially if you want something like cheese, wine etc.

Udo is a mini-Jeju, with traditional elements such as stone walls, farms, female divers and ocean cliffs all compressed into a much more manageable area. I rented a bicycle with a basket from an old ahjussi for 4000krw (3 hours). His stall, or rather tent, was located just at the ferry terminal. There are shops across the street that rent out bicycles, scooters and motorcycles.Cycling around Udo was a breeze. It was mainly flat terrain with some gentle slopes here and there. You will ride past white sandy beaches, rocky pools, farms, stone walls, female divers, cute puppies and cafes. Remember to grab some peanut ice cream, the island?s specialty.For more information and pictures on Udo, visit my travel blog https://honjatravel.wordpress.com/2015/07/24/top-5-favourite-places-in-jeju/

Try to give yourself a little extra time to buy tickets as they day we travelled it was packed with tourists.The short ferry trip was wonderful, and offered great views of Udo as we approached. On reaching the island the first thing we observed were the amount of rental companies offering bikes, electric 2/3 seater buggies, scooters and tandem. In fact anything you can think of to explore the island. Ido is famous for peanuts and you will find many of these on sale in the quaint little cafes and shops dotted around main road. If you get the chance you should try the local    Udo peanut Makgeolli   The island is truly beautiful and if you do decide to join the hoards on electric vehicles shop around a bit as there are lots of rental companies eager to offer their wares. It is also important to ensure that you have an   international drivers licence  ,, as they appear to have tightened up since a number of accidents lately and wouldn't accept our UK credentials.All in all great trip with lots of ferries running bak and forward throughout the day.
