Took around 6 hours up and 4-5hours down the volcano. Really pretty with all the snow around, but on the way down snow started to melt and the ground is slightly muddy. traveled there in the winter period from December to January. You should go and reserve an entire day for this winter hike!If you choose not to climb to the peak, at around half way mark there is a crater which is around 3 hours up and another 3 hours down. The crater is filled with water but is frozen in winter. But i would recommend heading to the peak for the best views! There is a rest station at 2/3 hours mark with toliets and 2nd rest station at the 4/5hours mark near to summit. The 2nd rest station has a small shop that sells coffee, instant noodles, gloves, small tidbits. But best if you bring along some gimbap along to fill your stomach.

Too much of a tourist trap that has been boasting the same facilities/exhibits for several decades. Would have been more impressive to see a renovation of the space. The gift shop is great but is only accessible if you buy a ticket (adult tickets are 10,000 KRW). May be a better option if you're going with young children.

To be full of cosmetics and fashion items. If you're shopaholic you shouldn't miss an opportunity for shopping. Quite Cheap. If it's rainy days and can't go for climb mountains, you can go jungang instead.

this was the tallest waterfalls i visited ever. multiple waterfalls nearby, nice pictures to take there, a lot of shops. there's as well a small waterfall nearby that you can take a lot of nice pictures there on the bridge & down in the waterfall itself. Overall it was fantastic

This was pretty entertaining. I had no idea what would be in a Teddy Bear museum... PLEASE go though. There are tons of bears from every period imaginable, wearing period and geographical clothing to match. Everyone is represented and it was actually a lot better than I thought when I hear   we are going to the Teddy Bear Museum  .... don't let that fool you! There is also an outside where you can walk around and see life-sized teddy bears. The gift shop is at the very end, and you WILL want something from it. Class Act, and a welcomed surprise!

This was one of the stops for the Jeju Golden Bus Tour. Since we were hungry, we got off this stop and wandered into the Dongmun market. There were lots of seafood and stalls selling Korean food; we had grilled mackerel and fish soup. With rice and lots of side dishes, the meal came to 15000 won. Though the sellers couldn't speak English, they had menus in English. Get your hallabong chocolate here too. So many other flavors to choose from as well and with so many shops competing here, you are spoilt for choice. Unfortunately, we didn't buy and regretted when we realised when other tourist places in Jeju city didn't have the the range offered in Dongmun market.

This was one of the only attractions that was open the day after Typhoon Bolaven moved away from Jeju this summer. On the day after there was still some strong wind and it was overcast, but people were out clearing debris off the roadways and sidewalks. Our hotel called ahead to this Botanical Garden and they said they were open, so we took the bus over and sure enough it was! It was a huge greenhouse building with an observation area at the top you can climb stairs to and see all over the area including the ocean. There were different climate areas inside with plants from that part of the world (jungle, dessert, local climate, flowers, etc), a small cafe with coffee and ice cream, some shops, and restrooms inside. Outside there were nice grounds with a big grassy area where people could sit, and other themed gardens (Korean, Japanese, French, Italian). Very pretty. Signs inside in English and Korean and Chinese describe some of the plants.? There were lockers inside for rent with coins. They weren't huge but we saw some backpackers taking a medium sized pack out of one.They were renovating part of the building but we didn't smell or hear anything bothersome. All in all it was a nice place to visit if it's raining or just post-typhoon outside, if you love plants, or have some extra time to see sights on Jeju.

This was covered under our west course jeju tour.This is a large park with good bonsy trees ,lava caves and plants and animals and a old jeju village huts to show jeju culture.We can enjoy photography.If localite a good picnic spot.food shops available.

This was an attraction I did not plan. But was in the area and decided to do. I did enjoy the climb. They have different levels of intensity and with this views are included. You can take stairs all the way to the top or you can slowly climb. Once up there the view was amazing. If you take a different way down you can even take pictures at a mini park with swings. They also had refreshments at the entrance and a small gift shop with over priced items. Definitely a must if in the area, but not necessarily worth to go out of your way to fit this place in. As its further away from other attractions and buses here can be difficult.

This was a nice walk up to the top. There's a lot of stairs, but it's not nearly as bad as I thought it was going to be. We went in Oct on a fairly sunny day (temp was probably in low-mid 20's) and you definitely want some water and sunscreen with you. I'd recommend going when it's more cloudy, if you can. There are a couple little shops along the way to the top (the first few levels of stairs, not all the way along) where you can also purchase water, and there is some tasty Jeju orange ice cream for sale too. The views are pretty, as is the temple, and it wasn't too busy when we were there in the middle of the afternoon.

This was a nice little excursion from the main island. Gotta take a ferry which means you need to head over to Udo early and be prepared to come back in the early evening as the ferry schedule will dictate your movement. There used to be a nice coffee shop halfway up at the base of the stairs to the lighthouse exhibits (October 2013). They had the cutest dog too but they were closed when we went back in December 2013. We took our car on the ferry. But you can also walk onto the ferry and then rent mopeds or four wheelers once you get to Udo so you can get around. I was thankful for the GPS in the car though because the roads are very winding, narrow, confusing, and I don't think are marked with names.

This was a first time visit for us...and we found it to be cheesy with a capital 'C'. However, who would have thought that CHEESY could be so COOL!!!!Yup, we had fun here...the place was amazing. Nature in harmony with recycled glass and plastic. it's very well maintained, good to spend a few hours here taking pictures...as well as soaking in the various exhibits on display. I particularly enjoyed the walk in the Enchanted Forest, a bit creepy though...as it was secluded from the rest of the complex, and this added to the excitement of being in the forest...talk about a vivid imagination!They have a shop selling souvenirs as well, clean restrooms and a cafe. I would recommend those looking for some fun to drop by here, and just let your inner child run free!

This underground shopping street is kinda cool. It has clothes, beauty products, a large number of children's stall, and no doubt impresses the many thousands of tourists that come through Jeju City every day. However, if you have ever been to Singapore, and experienced the underground warren of the connected malls on Orchard road, this will not in any way tantalize you. At best it will make you smile at the 1970's feel of it all ;-)

This Underground Shopping Mall is again beside one of the walking street.  It also has many entrance/exit.  Basically, the shops are selling more for women and not for youngsters. It really make use of the space on the island, and place to hide during down pour.

This teddy bear museum is one of a few around the world.  Located in Jungmun tourist complex in Jeju, Korea, is this tiny museum for teddy bear fans alike.  For 8000 KRW you have unlimited day access to 3 floors of teddy bear exhibits and the outside grounds.  This museum carries interesting themed bears like the Mona Lisa bear, the Leonardo Da Vinci bear, a Marilyn Monroe bear, and so many others.  Currently they are displaying the Elvis bear.  On the ground floor there is even a really nice restaurant if you get hungry.  Not much choice in  terms of breakfast, they do offer mostly burgers and different types of coffees.  Also there is a gift shop if you are interested in taking home one of the really cute teddy bear souvenirs.Well worth the visit and few hours for both teddy bear fans and those with just a passing interest.  Remember to use the lockers next to the admission counter.  We didn't and carried all our jackets and bags for the entire exhibit,  It will make the visit a whole lot lighter and more fun.  Enjoy!

This site consists of a large network of staircases that you climb to see a crater as well as a beach where the woman divers do a demonstration.The walk up the stairs is very long. It is not impossible and there are many places to take breaks without holding up the line. The spot is very busy so there will be an unbroken line of people going up and down. I would suggest taking water with you. The view from the top is quite nice. Allow 1 hour to do the climb at a leisurely pace.At the beach the woman divers do demonstrations on a set schedule. Check the times when you arrive. They will suit up for the dive, sing a song and then go into the water looking for seafood. When we were there a lady came back with an octopus. It does not take long for them to find something so it is worth it to wait to see the catch.There are bathrooms and snack shops there as well.

This shopping centre is huge, full of goods like cosmetics, clothes, shoes, small electronics and mobile accessories. And people of course. Not different from underground shopping in Seoul or Incheon.

This shop is located along Chilsung Fashion Street, just a short 5 min walk from Dongmun Market. There is a range of souvenirs that are affordable and not found at the typical tourist shops, e.g. scented candles, dolls, organic socks, brooches, postcards, handmade key chains of fabric horse, notebooks, tote bags and posters. The quality of products are better here.

This Rock is believe as a Snake want to be a Dragon, so according to the local story there are God who live a the Sea.  And the Snake should have the Jade from the God and Snake steal the jade while the God is sleeping but before the snake escape the God Woke up and put an Arrow to the snake.  Half Body (Upper Part) already come out from the sea at it's become a dragon but the lower part is still below the sea and become the rock.  That's why the upper part that we can see looks like Dragon Head Rock.  This area is very near from the Parking area, here we can find Orange Seller, Snack seller, restaurant also, souvenir shop.  Nice place to see and near from Jeju Airport.. 10 Minutes from the airport.

This place was the first on my list of place-to-go in Jeju. We were quite rushing as we don't want to miss the Haenyeo show (I totally adore them since years ago while watching documentary!). We would love to go for hiking to the peak, but we are pretty much time-constrained. Make sure to wear comfy shoes as there are lots of stairs. Go downstairs (it's really tiring to go upstairs later) to the Haenyeo house for the show and be there early as those ahjumma (auntie) in diver suit will perform their Haenyeo song and dance before going to the sea (this is so much fun!). There is boat service provided if you'd like a tour. You may enjoy fresh raw seafood (abalones, octopus etc.) from their catch, approx. from KRW10000 for a plate. If you love horse-riding, give it a try!The area is surrounded with souvenir shops. Try Hallabong (citrus fruit), one of Jeju specialities! The sight is way too gorgeous to be missed. MUST-GO-PLACE!Haenyeo (women diver) show: 1.30 pm & 3.00 pmAdmission fee for adult: KRW2000Boat ride: KRW10000Horse-riding: approx. KRW5000++Hallabong: KRW2000 each

This place was really unexpected. Through the Yeha Bus tour this was one of the stops and I am glad we visited this place. A lot of mini exhibits with bears dressed up according to the theme and the gift shop is great as well. For teddy bear lovers and lovers of all things cute, we recommend this place.

This place is the signature sightseeing here. So every tourists would be here. It's crowd with people. There're many shops, kiosk, snack bar and food shops at the front of the sightseeing. So there are large space for parking. You need to buy ticket to get in there. Once you get ticket, you walk straight on the walk way till you see the junction. There's the highlight signage for photo shooting. And you need to choose either way to go. If you go to the right, you need to walk up to the hill and you will see the good view from there. The way to go up the mountain is fine, not too rough. But not recommend during rainy day.If you go to the left, you will see fisherman Village, sea sand sun and fresh seafood from local people. The highlight is the lady from the village dive deep into sea to get the seafood stuffs.

This place is quite overrated when the cliffs aren't as majestic and huge as can be seen in pictures. These are lava columns that hardened upon meeting the sea and formed into pillar-like structures. Going into the platforms was easy, not too much hiking but after seeing it, there's not much to see or do. Beware of the shops nearby and try to haggle before buying.

This place is perfect for culinary, searching for snack with cheaper price, and mall (called Jungang Shopping Mall). I find small authentic teokbokki stall here and seafood restaurant. It will a little quiet at night, so you can walks freely here. The market will be closed around 7 pm so come here before closing time.

This place is great for shopping with reasonable and cheaper prices compared to other places. Also, it is underground and covered, so u need not worry about the weather. U could take your meals at the big market on the  street level, get your fix of souvenirs such as jeju chocolates, crunch, tangerines and such, then head downstairs to shop. Most store ladies there could speak Mandarine and a little English so communication is not a big issue. Definitely a must come for shopping in Jeju!

This place is easily accessible by bus, next to O'Sulloc tea museum. Makes me feel very cosy the moment I stepped in. It's a cafe as well as a place for soap making workshop. It also sells own products (limited).I love the healthy breakfast which is organic and surprisingly very tasty. However, it is on the pricey side.

This place is a definite must see on my list. The market is huge and includes shops that sell about everything you can imagine (clothes, kitchen appliances, souvenirs, meat, fish, ice cream, pancakes, desserts, traditional street food, oranges, oranges and more oranges). The fruit is expensive, but that's normal for Korea. The street food is cheap and absolutely delicious. It is definitely a good way to kill a couple hours and try some of Jeju's famous treats.

This place has great vibes and energy of a beautiful beach town. Many cafes offer good views. I spent about 2 hours in one of the cafes and totally enjoyed the views. There?s a very good seafood ramen and pancake restaurant nearby : Sogob-E 怨깆 ? Seafood Ramen ShopAddress: 565 Woljeong-ri, Gujwa-eup, Cheju, Jeju-do, South Korea

This museum, like most of Jeju's other similar attractions, is but an excuse to get you to the gift shop. You can finish it in one hour, because they want to get you there fast! As opposed to most other museums in this resort island, this one is cute and amusing. It consists mostly of tableaus or displays with teddy bears re-enacting some important historical or popular culture event. Some may frown at the   Gandhi   teddy bear as perhaps not quite tasteful, but must surely enjoy the   Beatles   teddy bears, the   Chinatown   teddy bears, etc. You get the picture. Oh, yes the gift shop! It works; I bought a little cute bear as most everybody else seems to have done. Not that expensive and well-made. In other words, if you are going to see at least one of these museums that dot the south of the island, you may want to give this one a try. It's enjoyable.

This market sells many products either fashionable clothes and branded cosmetics. There're many food shops available with reasonable place too. If you are seeking for sport shoes or toys.You can also find here. Some shops will give you the tax refund and some not.You need to check carefully. The famous cosmetic shops like ETUDE and skin food, some of famous items may not available. There're 11 gates which the even gate no. will locate on the right whereas the odd ones are on the left. It's not complicated and easy to walk. There's restroom available too.If you don't buy the well known brand, you will also find the local Korean cosmetic brand which is very cheap. I buy 12 hand creams with 10,000 won prize and can get the complimentary mask for 10 sheets. It's very good price. The souvenir shop also available here.I would also recommend to come as the choice of your shopping since it's not too crowded like duty free building and you don't need to buy a lot of same items in pack like duty free. As most of Korean cosmetics in duty free would be sold in pack of more than 2 pieces which sometimes you don't need that much.

This market sells many goods. I would recommend it for buying souvenirs from Jeju, like chocolate crunch and chocolate. There were also shoes and clothes for sale but not so fashionable. There are many shops selling dry and wet goods, mandarin oranges and other Jeju products. It is really large and you can spend quite a few hours there. Good for wet weather as it is covered.

This market is really big, there is fish market, street food corner and the souvenir shops corners where you can buy jeju chocolates,... Anyways, I'm addicted to the street food corners here. The food marrket is at the gate 8. There are so many kind of street food with good price.

This market is popular amongst the locals and tourists, hence expect this place to be crowded. Majority of shops are selling oranges and fresh seafood. Besides these, there are other sections selling meat, vegetables, spices, snacks etc. I bought 1 stick of crab and seafood balls for 4,000 won. Recommend to try their famous peanut ice cream for 1,500 won. Yummy.

This is your typically local market where you can get fresh product here.  I will NOT say this place offers the cheapest price but rather there are varieties for you to choose from.  The market has many entrance and each entrance leads to you to a particular section where they sell the same stuff ranging from clothes, fruits and to live seafood.  We picked up some Jeju tangerines and sweets here which were pretty good.  Discount?  Most shops are priced the same so its hard to get discount. Best time to come is about 2pm where there are lesser crowd.  Its also a short walk to the underground shopping mall so if you are here, do take the chance to visit the underground mall altogether.

This is your typical open air market. In the west we call it a Farmers Market. It has just about everything you might need. You will be exposed to the Korean Culture there.  The shop keepers are usually older so there isn't a lot of English spoken but, if you  want to buy something they will understand and act accordantly. Don't be afraid to barter a little.It is crowed  most the time so I shy away from going there but, if you like to rub butts with the general public and need to pick up something for the home, garden, something new to wear or something special for dinner this is the place for you.
this is the nice beach evervi seen, all water us so clean.beside have lots of resturant , hotel.. mini shop

This is such a great place!Even if you don't have enough time, you can see a lot.There are few stages and different   yards   to go to.Really peacefull place if you climb few stages up.After going up you can see beautiful view of the coast as well.And the helpful thing is that they have a small shop in front of the temple (downstairs) so after climbing all mountains and the temple place you can get nice drink or ice cream. Also, they have a car parking place.

This is probably one of my favourite beaches of all time. Do not be put up by busy pictures... The water is shallow, for about 200m or more out to sea so the area for children to play and people to swim or snorkel is huge. We set up towels on the short and put up our own umbrellas and it really didn't feel crowded at all. There are loads of shops and restaurants around, as well as loads of places to rent rubber rings etc. I also saw lots of water sports happening outside of the safe swim zone. Truly a great day or so out!! And sunset is beautiful too.

This is probably my first 1-star review on TA. Much regretted visit and the only saving grace is that this place is right next to the Osulloc Tea Museum. We were drawn to this place after very good experience at the Innifree Green Cafe at Myongdong and we expected the same (if not better) at this concept store.Product - any Innisfree shops in myeongdong or duty free can offer you a better range at much better price. As Jeju was the last leg of my trip, I was planning to make most of my innisfree purchase in this store but they don?셳 carry much range here. I don?셳 remember there was onsite tourist refund as well (like how it is in Myeongdong) - another reason not to plan your shopping here.Food - I ordered a 18000krw main dish (named herdsman?) with some cold sausages, potato mash, rice balls and orange. The presentation was really pretty but it tasted nothing special. If you are looking for good looking food and great taste at the same time, you have better chance at Myongdong innisfree Green cafe. The other two pretty drinks we ordered were not worth a mention as well. Service - We were there at 450pm and all the soap making stations were occupied. We were told by a staff the soap making would only take 15mins and the place would close at 6pm. so we decided to wait at the cafe and return when the crowd lessen. At 525pm, a staff stopped me at the cashier when I tried to purchase the soap making set. She said that they have closed the soap making station at 520pm. And then another staff came by and said the station was closed at 5pm (?!). I am not sure exactly what time the station closed as there was no sign in the store and the staff were telling different things. The store closed at 6pm sharp and the staff can?셳 wait to have all the guests out by then - this I am sure. This place is a sad contrast to the Osulloc Tea Museum next door.

This is perfect for solo and family travelers that are vacationing in Jeju. Adult admission is 5,000 KW and is well worth it. The hike takes about 30 minutes to an hour and can be  fairly steep in some areas. There are many shops, cafes, and restaurants around the area once you are done with the hike to the top. If you time it right, you will be able to see the famous Women Divers of JeJu who perform at 1:30 PM. The heritage behind it is very unique since it has been carried one for generations.

This is one road which really left my puzzled. The bus driver did turn off his enjoy but the bus still managed to roll on, to my eyes, the path was an up-sloping one. So how did the bus manage to move on its own? Does it mean the path is actually downwards sloping?This is just any other road along Jeju Island which after completion, people found out about this weird phenomenon. Well, the locals will explain to you the whole reason to this phenomenon. Don't worry, expect a crowd there with tour buses pulling over, but don't expect a fee to be paid unless you patronize the little snack shops there.

This is one of the world heritage in Jeju Island. When i visit Jeju, i stayed in a hotel nearby, so i can see the sunrise from the top of seonsan Ilchulbong. To see the beautiful sunrise, i walk from my hotel at 4.30 am. You need to buy an entrance ticket to this place.You need to walk the stair path, uphill, and soon you arrive on top, you'll find so many people already setting up the camera to capture the sunrise. after enjoying the beautiful scene from top, on our way down, my eyes can't stop admiring the beauty scene of Jeju City. Everything is taking your breath away in this place.You also can ride a horse or watch the mermaid show (lady divers). If you want to buy some goods for your family from Jeju (orange, souvenirs, cake, snacks), you have to buy it in Jeju, because you can't find any of these goods in Seoul. If you want to give a second thought on it, your last chance to shop is in the Jeju International airport (price is the same everywhere in Jeju).This is a very highly recommended place to visit in Jeju Island!

This is one of the many highlights of olle 7 hiking trail.  It is quite a scenic spot, and hence all the tourists here.  There are small gift shops and little unmanned fruit stands along the way (you just need to pick up the oranges or crackers you want anf then leave your money behind)

This is one of my favorite oreums (volcanic hills) on Jeju!!It is not exactly close to anything so be ready to travel quite a bit.  It is also a steep hike, but each step that takes your higher gives you more and more of a view. I am telling you the negative up first but I am also telling you...it is worth it.  *On the weekends (depending on the season) you will often find coffee trucks parked at the bottom parking lot.  You cannot count on this as they come and go...but if they are there, it will be a nice treat for you.*This oreum is also host to my favorite festival in Korea.  Jeju Fire Festival.  Thousands and thousands of people come to this oreum to say goodbye to the past memories and to welcome spring.  It is a seriously amazing event.  Fire, fireworks, food, beer, shopping tents, performances.....absolutely a fantastic event.

This is one of my favorite beaches on Jeju.  As someone who lives here, this is mainly because the beach is big enough to hold the droves of tourists who come here every summer.  During off season it is even more spectacular.  Wide stretches of sand with very few people filling it.Around the beach areas there are enough cafes, restaurants, shops to keep a person full and happy throughout the day.  ProTip: Midway down the beach (there is another set of bathrooms up the stairs.  Save yourself the trip of trying to make it to the main ones!

This is definitely a place for kids & ladies. Sorry guys. It is bear, bear, bear & more bear wherever you turn your head. Thank goodness photography is allowed in here. Most of the bears are small, about the height of your palm. I guess that makes them all the cuter. There is a giantic bear in front of the souvenir shop. Do take a few shots with it. Considering the number of bears on display, the number of teddy bear related memorabilia is quite limited,. I wonder why.

This is definitely a must do on Jeju Island.  Climb early in the morning to avoid the throngs of people.  If the pollution is low, you'll have a great view.  Beware, even if you climb early in the morning, it may not be peaceful.  There will be many selfie sticks! I was expecting lush green grass and canola flowers -- it became very apparent that the online images have been Photoshopped.  It is still well worth it to visit - just don't expect the view to be as stellar as what you see online.

This is an underground shopping center which is just around the corner of Orange Tree  Cafe & Hotel. This is just the normal shopping center which you would see in most of the subways thru out Seoul, however, the good thing about this underground shopping mall is that each of the exits leads to different streets which has more shops....eg. Uniqlo, ABC Mart, Daiso, and also various cafes.....and also to the Dongmun Market and also to the Black Pork Street.

This is a Teddy Bear Museum that all inside about the Teddy Bear.  They have so many Theme of Teddy Bear.  Near the exit they also have many stuff for us to buy and bring home, such as doll, key chain, cloth, jacket, sweater, etc..  This Museum is more suitable for the children, but for adult if you are bored you can wait near the exit there are some coffe shop.

This is a shop and cafe on the grounds of the AmorePacific Osulloc tea museum. The shop selection is a bit small. But there is a section of goods that can only be bought at this location. There is a large area where you can make your own soap, and then lay for it. The other half of the building is the cafe, which while not cheap was surprisingly good. The staff was perfectly fine but not amazing either.

This is a nice and cute museum especially for small girl.  Here They have Theatre, they have explanation about hello kitty, they have restaurant with hello kitty image on the dishes, they have souvenir shop

This is a must-see in Jeju city. It is a local market where they offer souvenirs, food, food, and more food. It is very different to anything I know from central Europe (not the market itself, but the offered food). Note: strong smell to spices and seafood. We bought a stone grandfather in one of the shops, which was offered for two to four (!!) times the price at touristic spots. Here, we found the cheapest price. No idea if tourists still pay a higher price, but we were fine with it (20000 KRW for a ~30cm stone grandfather).

This is a must go in Jeju if you are into hiking and scenary. The paths are manageable, but I would recommend proper boots and even crampons during winter season for the snow. It gets really cold, so proper clothing is advised. Just make sure you can take them off when your body heats up during the climb. We managed the climb without crampons (as the shop at the bottom was trying to rip us off), but we took the cheap option at the 2nd check-point of Seongpanak Trail.

This is a lovely spot to visit. You can wander around the artists village enjoy the outdoor sculptures (kids will like the brightly coloured animals near the art shop/cafe) and then have a good look at the exhibitions inside.  There is a permanent one and a temporary one. The temporary one at present is about marine plastics and pollution. The work was really good especially the video work and created   man   by a young female Korean artist. Most impressive.The last Wednesday of the month entry is free but it's only 2000 won anyway I think. They have an English brochure and the lady at reception was very pleasant.

This is a fun place to stop and spend about a half hour or so.  The road in this section appears to defy gravity.  Not sure of the reason why, but is very interesting to see the car go backwards while facing downhill.  There are some interesting exhibits and statues, along with shops, nearby.

This is a fun and interactive show that would be great for families with members of all ages.The VIP seats are more expensive, but you have the chance of being picked to participate in segments of the show. If this is not important to you, choose the regular seats as the theater is not very large anyway. You can get a 5,000 won discount if you reserve tickets through YEHA Tours. Then pick up the tickets on the day of the show.Instead of an intermission in the middle, a cast member does some interactive clapping and stomping with the audience.The City Hall downtown area is a 15-minute walk away from the theater. You can find restaurants and shops there.

This huge place has many shops and stalls selling household items, fish and seafood.   And there is also the food street selling all kinds of local food.   Just be careful and remember which gate/entrance you enter or else you may find yourself lost and spend time trying to find your way out.

This forest has a nutmeg tree that is over 826 years old.  We enjoyed walking on the paths that weave through the forest.  Beautiful trees, flowers and lovely singing birds.  We saw a snake and loved the fresh smelling air.  There is a small store selling drinks and snacks and a small coffee shop.  No gift shop.  The paths are well maintained and very easy to walk on.

This excellent beach has a lil' bit of everything.  Located not far away from Jeju City/Airport, Hamdeok provides great atmosphere filled with Restaurants, Coffee Shops, waterfronts and one of the most beautiful sunsets in Korea! We sat down in the beachfront walk, cracked open a couple of beers and enjoy the evening breeze.  It was so cool watching people prepping their dinner and drinkin' some Soju while the sound of the waves and live music was heard across the darkness of the night.  We follow the music and found this young talented musician playing guitar and singing on front of a young crowd.  That was the Cherry on top of the Cake!  Stroll & Enjoy!

This bridge in Seogwipo harbour goes across to a small island which takes about 20 minutes to walk around.? It is a nice place to go at sunset, there are nice views and many birds in the trees.? Also nearby are the Cheoniyeon waterfalls, and a few shops and cafes.
This beach is one of the most beariful beaches in Jeju, with its white sand and really good restaurants and coffeeshops nearby. Really recomendable to go!

This beach is adjecent to GeumNeung Beach - you can walk between them. Hallim Park is also next to it - all are walkable from each other. There are plenty of shops and umbrella rentals, etc. Camping is avaiable at the next door beach. Some areas are not for swimming due to strong currents. Lovely view of a nearby island. You can take the 202 bus from the 5 day market near the airport. Takes about an hour.

This beach is a good one.  The sand is soft and powdery and the clear water very gradually gets deep which allows us to comfortably walk unusually far into the ocean.  The other special characteristic is that there is a big change from low tide to high tide.  The high tide, which occurred around 10 pm when we were there, completely covers up a pretty large beach area.  It's pretty fascinating.  The food and drink shops near the beach were a bit of a letdown for us because they were overpriced.

This attraction consists of a beautiful and natural   sculpture by the sea  . This formation occurred long ago as part of volcanic activity in the area. You get to experience amazing scenery and photo ops at this very special place. As you enter, you walk through a gorgeously landscaped park and continue on with an easy walk to the observation platform overlooking the formations by the sea. You will not see anything like this anywhere else in the world. They also offer a nice snack bar and gift shop specializing in local fare. A really enjoyable way to spend a couple of hours!
They sell mostly food, fruit and fish. Some other stuff like clothing and typical market style stuff is available. Just right next to the underground shopping street if you want to buy stuff.

There's basically nothing here except for the black rock that is sculpted by nature to look like a dragon head.  However, the sea view is pretty. Doesn't need to spend a lot of time here.  Maybe about 10 mins max. There's also a souvenir soup nearby which sells Korean gifts. The shop is not huge but you can find stuffs that typical souvenir shops will sell. eg. keychain, pen, towels, mugs, socks (yes, for some reasons, Koreans are really fond of cute socks with cartoons)..etc.Saw the Roll Hotto snack.  In Singapore, we call this flakey flour pastry as prata. In this case, they rolled the prata with egg and ham complete with vege. Kindda cool.The ice cream they are selling at this attraction is interesting.  I chose 2 flavors: Vanilla and Strawberry. Price is KRW3,000 or RMB20. It's kind of interesting to note that RMB is accepted in Korea as a form of payment. Nonetheless, the ice cream is yummy!More photos available onhttp://i-wanna-travel.blogspot.sg/2015/03/korea-jeju-17-mar-2014.html.

There's an entrance fee, that's one . It's very far away from where we stayed (Gujwa-eup), that's two . Transportation is quite a pain.... when you stay outside the city area ...we had to hire a cab everytime we go out and see places, although, they were very kind enough to ask and offer to wait for us until we finished our tour.I think the place is great for kids and teenagers and those who love modern art and colors. It's quite a huge place with lots of interesting collections... just follow the trails so you won't miss any of the displays. At the end of it, there is a shop wherein you can buy some souvenirs...i find it quite expensive though. ⓒ

There were bears of every color and design imaginable: there was an Elvis bear, Marilyn bear, Mona Lisa bear, Chinese bears, countryside bears and even Goong (the Korean drama) bears! It really was a bear wonderland. The only problem was that the commentary was all in Korean, it would have been better if there was English translation as well. The other problem was that most of the exhibits were housed in glass cases which made taking photos challenging as the reflections were very prominent. Besides viewing the bears, there is an in-store souvenir shop that has all sorts of bear items (e.g. keychains, stuffed bears, bags etc...). But if you love bears, than it should be worth a visit.For more on my experience and photos, please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/03/an-impromptu-visit-to-teddy-bear-museum.html

There is walk along the  nice promenade to get to this rock. It is hard to make out the dragon in the rock but Asians love strangely shaped rocks. In my opinion it was not so spectacular but the walk along the promenade is very nice, over nice bridge and coffee shops along the way.

There is a start sign & stop sign. Upon reaching the start sign, switch to neutral gear, on hazard light, and keep your car engine on. It will start to move forward on a uphill slope. Very slowly. Of course, do be alert and keep your eye infront and foot hover on brake if necessary.It is a one lane traffic, so not all cars are stopping to be wow by this nature forces, you might be honked by other drivers for slowing down and doing this anti-gravity act. Well... just ignore them. They will move on by cutting your lane.There is a convenient shop next to it and car park. You can park your car there and come down to try it with a half-filled water bottle. It will perform the same too, rolling up on a up-slope.However, beware of cars. There is still on-coming traffic.

There is a place for hand-made soap. If you buy a pack of raw material for making soap, you are able to sit down and design your own soap right away. The package is ~15,000 won which includes the material of making 3 pieces of soap and the final product wrapping stuff as well. It is a very good experience for ladies apart from shopping.

There is a lot more than meets the eye here. People first wonder but then realize they are glad to visit The Glass Castle. It is a museum and park of glass works by local artisans and crafts people and the collection is vast, so vast it takes a while to see everything. There is a diverse array of glass work in gardens, themes, and museum displays of varying quality and rarity around the park.This includes large outdoor sculptures such as the yellow submarine at the entrance or crystal skulls, and glass displays around the park. We were impressed by the size of the park and diverse collection of work. They also have workshops here and some hands on experiences.I would recommend this place as a worthy place to visit while on Jeju, near the O'Sulluc Tea Museum and Plantation which only 5 minutes away.

There is a huge greenhouse with 7 separate areas of different plants including desert, aquatic, floral, jungle, and tropical fruit. ? The tropical fruit area had platters (examples)? of many different types of the fruit of the nearby trees. ? There are a couple small shops in the greenhouse selling different items as well as food and drink.? ? There is also an elevator going up to a 5th floor observatory. ? We went on a very rainy day.? ? Couldn’t see a thing. ? The greenhouse was extremely busy, I’m sure moreso due to the bad weather.? ? ? 10,000 won to enter.

There is a cafe at level 2 and a small gift shop selling Hallabong items after walking through their tangerines greenhouse. There is also a small museum where kids could learn about tangerines but they are mostly in Korean.Outside  the korean fans dedicated a small hectre of tangerine plantation to G-Dragon. There is even a Kwon Jiyong Tree. But since we were there in late March  the weather was still pretty chilly  so the leaves are not growing yet.You could ask the reception where it is  its just nearby. However do try asking them as   G-Dragon   forest. i tried saying as   GD    but they dont really get it. Lol.

There are some fictional characters that you and me adore and love during our childhood and yet still relish even though we have become adults. Hello Kitty is certainly one of them, and is a favourite of one of my children. However, the good part is not every visitor to Jeju and the locals are a fan of Hello Kitty, so the Hello Kitty Island Museum is not on the itinerary of most tour companies, and hence it?s not crowded.Getting there and fees: Hello Kitty Island Museum, opened in late 2013, is located in the south west part of Jeju (GPS code/coordinate 7926114).  Not to worry if you cannot find space in the small open-air car park outside the Museum because there?s another huge open air car park below the small one. Parking is free. Entrance fee to the Museum is 12,000 won for adult, 11,000 won for teenagers and 10,000Won for children. However, my family and I made use of the discount coupon for entrance fees from the Hertz car rental discount booklet.The Museum/Attraction: when we entered, we were immediately greeted by a large hall where there?s a circular cone of Hello Kitty toys, a photo-taking stop with the entire Hello Kitty family and Hello Kitty?s house where she?s standing at the balcony welcoming you and beckoning you to enter the door into the various exhibition halls. There are 3 levels with the exhibition halls on the first and second level, the gift shop on the first level, the Hello Kitty Caf챕 on the second level and the 3D theatre and an outdoor gallery on the third level. To cover everything, including a meal at the Hello Kitty Caf챕, would easily take about 2-3 hours. In the true sense, this Hello Kitty Museum is a museum ? there are exhibits of anything related to the adorable Hello Kitty. There are several themed exhibition halls on the first and second level e.g. History Hall, Art Education Hall, Music Education Hall, World Gallery Hall, Hello Kitty Room, Constellation Education Hall, amongst others.So we took plenty of photographs and selfies. I particularly like the exhibit of Hello Kitty represented by 26 countries (I found my own country) as well as the huge room containing the huge Hello Kitty bed where one of my children got the Hello Kitty toy snatched away by a toddler.At the Hello Kitty Caf챕 ? with Hello Kitty ribbon windows, Hello Kitty-themed sofas and Hello Kitty engraved tables ? you have to try the Hello Kitty Waffle Set, green tea latte, coffee or  hot chocolate (the 3 hot drinks have a profile of Hello Kitty on the surface), Hello Kitty Strawberry Cake and Cheesecake. Really yummy stuff!Whether you are a fan or not of Hello Kitty, I think this Museum is a fun attraction to visit and be acquainted with Hello Kitty. However, be prepared to ?share? the premises with many joyful and lively children and teenagers. But if you are not a fan and if you have limited time in Jeju, then I suppose you could spend that 2-3 hours elsewhere.

There are many waterfalls in Jeju, we decided to have a look at Cheonjiyeon. There is a large parking lot, eateries and a couple of souvenir shops, 7eleven etc when you arrive. To walk to the waterfall is about 10-15 min along a small tree lined river. Many tourists and tourists groups are visiting the waterfall so it will be quite crowded. The waterfall as such is nice, but not too tall or spectacular. everybody takes a few selfies and then heads back to the parking lot pretty much. If nearby it makes to stop by and visit but it is not worth a long journey just to see this waterfall.

There are a lot of shops and many things to buy, but they are repeated a lot of the time. There are a lot of fish and a lot of fruit. Then you also find some other goods as well. Very nice experience and one can buy a lot of souvenirs

There are 3 levels to the place. All 3 levels showcase bears of different ages and make. Many are modelled after heroes of the present and future, there's Disney bears, Korean culture bears, Moon bears etc. There's even a Steve Jobs bear on level 1 (within the shopping area). There's quite a fair bit of 100+ year old bears and i find these more fascinating than the rest. Sadly, the most crowded place is the shopping area on level 1 where tourist buys all sorts of momento bears.

The whole way from the car park to the falls itself was scenic. At the start was a pond with mandarin ducks and a bridge. There were various representative statues of Jeju. There were also souvenir shops if you want to buy some snacks or souvenirs. I liked the different types of trees grown, even though it is not autumn, the maple trees still looked very pretty. All along the way is a river, you go to the falls on one side and you can return on the other side of the river. There were plenty of explanation signs on the falls, the mottled eels and the rock face etc. The falls themselves don?t look very impressive but I still like the whole place. On the way back there is a nice flower display and large sculpture as well a stone auditorium.

The weather was raining on the day I decided to do sightseeing on Jeju, so I was left with only a visit to the botanical gardens. You can reach it from the airport limousine bus route and behind the fast food shops near SK Energy shop.Luckily the garden exhibition was under glass roof, so it provided a good informative shelter from the rain.The botanical gardens are organised into themes, eg. Aquatic garden, cactus garden, etc. I guess this eliminates confusion for tourists and displays the plants in an educational fashion too. On a sunny day, there is more to do on the outside.There is a curio shop inside the gardens for some gifts but I did not see a coffee shop at the attraction.It will be educational for the kids!

The water is a beautiful emerald color but the beach is too crowded. Too many parasols, shops, and small hotels. Go to the beach down the road if you want a more relaxing day at the beach.Tip: There are some decent beach style restaurants on the main road. There is nice a pizza cafe with covered outside seating. Also there is a Mom's Touch that servers fast food (chicken sandwiches).This beach is ranked as one of the top beaches in Jeju by Koreans. I was disappointed but I realized that the standards are different. Hey if you want simple food, people, and shade then this is the place to go.

The walk up the mountain provided beautiful views!  The mild spring weather and breeze allowed for an easier ascend for a   not so in shape   person. Did not go for sunrise but pretty regardless. Easy to locate parking lot and shops near by to accept your money;).

The Teddy Bear museum is a fun stop. There are many displays of teddy bears in various historical, cinematic, and pop-culture type settings. Take your camera and visit each floor. The gift shop at the end is full of fun teddy bear treasures as well. Definitely a good stop for anyone. We went on a rainy day, but it would also be fun on a hot day if you are looking to get out of the heat. Fairly easy to find, it's located in a popular tourist area.

The tea museum is located on the western side of the island and represents the showpiece of the O'Sulloc tea   empire   in South Korea.  There are a number of O'Sulloc tea cafes all over South Korea which specialize in green tea and also sell sweets as well.  There is a large parking area to accommodate a number of cars and visitors.The tea museum consisted of four   features   from what I could surmise.  First you get a decent view of the western part of the island by walking up the stairs to the roof of the museum itself.  The views aren't that interesting but you do get a good view of the surrounding area.  Second the museum itself describes the tea growing/making/serving process.  Third the cafe/gift shop inside seems to attract the most number of visitors.  You can buy teas and other desserts like you would at any other O'Sulloc cafes.  However it does sell many other items - various teas and more.  Finally another attraction is the tea plantation itself.  O'Sulloc seemingly has a small portion of their plantation on-site that you can walk through (note there may be snakes in the plantation) to get a sense of how the green tea leaves are grown.There is also an Innisfree store right next to the tea museum but we did not visit it.The tea museum is worth a trip though I wouldn't go out of the way to visit it as you can always partake in O'Sulloc teas in various locations in South Korea.

The soap making workshop is fun and interesting for kids and couples. Innisfree Jeju House is next to the famous O'Sulloc Green tea, you can spend at least 2 to 3 hours in these two placesfor soap making workshop, tea break and photograhping in the tea plantation.

The Seongsan Sunrise Peak is a crater with views from the overlook at the top edge of the crater, and a paved stairway/walkway up to the crater's edge.  A ticket is required to hike up the hundreds of steps to the overlook on the ridge of the crater, but if you are up to it, the view from the top is wonderful.  The crater is accessible from a causeway connected to the main island, but is itself surrounded by water everywhere except along the causeway, which adds to the view of the clear water below.  Parking is available at the crater, along with rest rooms at numerous places near the parking lot and shops, and one more restroom on the path, near where the uphill and downhill paths cross.  I always recommend carrying some toilet paper and hand towelettes in case they restrooms don't have them.The women abalone divers perform a couple of times in the afternoon on most days, so that might help determine your schedule.  Also, the smog was fairly thick the day we were there, so it limited a lot of the view of the island from the top of the crater.  The view nearby was still beautiful.  On a side note, we visited on a tour from a cruise ship.  There are 2 cruise ports on the island, one in the south port and one in the north port.  Where you port could determine your itinerary since various and impressive sights are available close to either town/port.The island has so much to offer ? large lava tunnel caves, waterfalls, craters, mountains, cliffs, black sand beaches, incredible fresh seafood, and more but they are spread throughout the island, so it is  impossible to see all of them in one area or in a short amount of time.  Also, some of the attractions are restricted, so they might require group access, or have other requirements to enter.  This attraction had a ticket kiosk near the entrance, so it didn't look like it had any restrictions for individuals to either enter or buy tickets.  We concentrated on the east end of the island during our visit and found it to be similar to Hawaii in many ways other than the temperature, which was quite a bit cooler than Hawaii during our visit at the end of March (55 deg F was our high temp).  Even this crater reminded us of Diamond Head, in Honolulu.

The Seongeup Folk Village was a walled-in village in the southeast of the island where stone homes showed the construction, culture and lifestyle of the island?s people long ago.Obviously, Jeju wants to maintain some type of historical reference to the old lifestyle.  Our tour guide made it interesting by talking about some practical aspects of the design of the huts (how it was heated, how it was built, etc), but this just wasn't my thing.  In fact, several families that help with the upkeep of the huts actually live in other huts in the community.  That said, those huts have modern adjustments like windows, electric power, etc so even they have moved beyond the   old ways  .  The village had a few shops and a restroom and outside the village was a convenience store with drinks available and another restroom. For me, the bottom line was - I would have preferred to spend the time at a natural landmark (waterfall, cave, hiking trail, etc) instead of doing this, but it was part of an all day tour.  There are simply too many other options to see in Jeju for this to make it to the top of the list, unless it is your   thing  .

The Seongeup Folk Village is huge.  The main entrance has a big car park and a side entrance where you can drive your car in.  Besides the car park, there are many restaurants, two public toilets and a few shops.From the main entrance, you can take a stroll and check out some of the conserved buildings which are open to public.  Information is available in English and you can learn about the earlier settlers and buildings of Jeju Island.  There are also some shops and restaurants inside the folk village.You can easily spend 1-2 hours inside the village and having lunch either in the restaurants inside or besides the car park.  We had delicious black pork bbq at Nammun restaurant (787 2432) located in the area besides the car park.Tip:There are other entrances to the village as well.  I was at one of these prior to finding the main entrance, and there are sales people trying to get us to into houses outside the gate and market horse oil cream and other products.  Avoid these.  While I can't verify whether the products are authentic, it definitely felt like a scam.  Seemed that some reviewers thought this is part of the folk village.

The previous review states that the climb was in 20 minutes but for a relatively unfit person like myself, it took me 30 to 40 minutes with numerous stops beginning from halfway till the top. Much to your agitation, we see older citizens and children alike happily and easily climbing the steps and overtook you to the top. Nevertheless, the view on the top was well worth the tough climb (according to my unfit status). Managed to take some photo shots of the surrounding and the crater itself. As it was just beginning spring, the crater floor was covered with brownish grass and vegetation, not the greenish color you would expect in summer. What I most remembered was the real cold buffeting wind of 2 Degrees Celsius blowing and you could really feel it even with winter jackets and caps worn while climbing the steps. But it was most memorable. Wife did not want to climb the steps but decided to go shopping for the famous Jeju orange chocolates in the shops at the foot of the park.

The place was rather quiet when we visited (it was on a Sunday morning) despite the heavy traffic from Seoul the day before. We were given pamphlets in English, while most of the displays were in Korean language. There are many teddy bears in display and most have been displayed/posed in accordance with certain themes (like Hollywood, Snow White, landing on the moon etc). It was interesting.There was an Elvis show, with teddy bears swaying their hips to Elvis's concert in Hawaii (if I'm correct) and that was entertaining for the kids.Outdoors is a small park with human size teddy figures, great for picture taking. Remember to take pictures with large teddy outside.There is also a cafe but we did not stop by since we had breakfast earlier. In the pamphlet, we saw a train ride but we couldn't locate it anywhere. May have missed it.There was one floor for shopping and there is a large selection of teddy bears to bring home. Maybe pricey but the quality is quite good.The place is convenient for families with small children (the kids were not terrified) and stroller friendly as there is an elevator available. There is also free parking outside.As usual, for Korean tourist attractions, there are discount vouchers available. Just have to know where to get it :)

The place itself is huge. We went before lunch and it was a good time because the sun was up. Being a glass museum, most of the art are made of glass and having the sun at its brightest made the art look even more amazing. It's nice to look at the reflections made. There are different signs in Korean, Japanese, and English. They also have shop where they sell little glass artwork. You can bargain with the sellers too. They're nice and friendly.

the pinky building and all kitty stuffs! Very interesting and nice place for pictures. they have cafe & shop for kitty stuffs, Kitty fans this is the place do not be missed. things slightly expensive because of   Sanrio   brand. but not so tourist friendly cos its not a walking distance from town, either by bus or taxi. We took bus to Kitty island (but missed one station cos we dont understand Korean language, we only stop the bus driver when we passed kitty island), for return in convenient we pick taxi (black color), cost us 60USD back to town (like 10mins distance only)
The O'sulloc   Museum   is in reality a big store where they sell you Tea (can be really expensive) and attached to the store there is a big coffee shop.

The museum is located next to a please area of town with multiple artists in various media as well as tea/coffee shops - which is how we found the location.? There is a small entrance fee (1000 Won per adult at the time).? In addition to the small, but nice collection of paintings and sculpture, there is a great view of the city and see from the 3rd floor.? If art is your thing, then definitely go.? Otherwise go only as weather or your schedule dictates.

The museum is full of teddies of all sizes created from all the Korean dramas begining with the classic   Winter Sonata   till the American President Obama. On the rooftop, you can view the whole valley of Jejudo as well as the scenic Hallasan. There are some cookies for sampling and plenty of teddies for sale in the shop at the end of the tour^^~

The moment I set my eyes on this island, I knew I was in heaven. The water looked extraordinary blue and the view was nothing short of a perfect dreamy scenery. We took a day trip on the ferry from jeju. On the island, we took the hop on hop off bus. Take any bus, doesn't really matter.. They will then tell you which color buses u can hop onto at the next destination along with a list of places they will stop at. I think it costs around 2200 won. The island was crowded specially with all the bikes but still it is not to be missed. The first stop was the udo peak. A hike of around 30 mins to a lighthouse from where you can see the entire islans. The view of the sunrise peak on jeju all along the hike was incredible! Then the bus took us to 2 beaches..one was a black sand beach which had a little cave but tides were high that day. We missed the 2nd beach and went to the last one with white sand. This beach was quite close to the port and we walked to the port from here along the coast. It was a beautiful walk and less crowded.There are lot of shops and cafes in front of the last beach.

The market is full of local appeal with fresh fruits, vegetables, and local snacks to seafood and various sundries. A great way to spend a few hours walking around, doing some souvenir shopping, and eating local treats. The market is full of warm and friendly people who are interested and appreciative of the tourist that venture to visit the attraction. I would recommend to any one who appreciates the local things about traveling.

The market is basically divided into 3 sections, 1 for fresh seafood, 1 for fruits and 1 for dry sundries. One can buy fresh seafood from the stalls and have them cooked in any of the restaurants there - which are mostly located at the upper level of the shops there.

The market is 60% local 40% tailored to tourist, hence depending on what you are after you can choose the part that suits your expectation.It is the local fresh meat , fish and vegetable market--fresh goodies are sold at a very reasonable price and exceptional quality. The touristic part is nice also-- lot of old aunties promoting the snacks, personally i dont think that's the most authentic souvenir so we decided to go to the pottery shop and ending up buying soup copper pot and stone pot back (though it's heavy) as it did remind us a lot more about the trip.The fresh snack stands are very busy and people are elbow to elbows. Food was yum but probably you don't wonna spend more than 2 hours there. Btw, there is a night food market outside after 5 pm and it's worth grabbing a snack or two.

The Jungang Undergroung Shopping Center was among the shopping stops that we had for our Jeju tour package. The area is sizeable. There are 12 gates conveniently marked?I had to remember Gate 5 since this is where our tour bus was scheduled to pick us up.  There were beauty products, clothes, cosmetics, more clothes, more beauty products?did I already mention clothes and cosmetics? The clothes and bags sold here are not your designer stuff but cheaper items. The cosmetics sold here are similar to what you have at every corner in Korea. If you are looking for really inexpensive items, it is better going to the Dongmun Market. If you want branded items, head to the Chilseongro Fashion Street. Both these locations are nearby, at Gates 2 and 3 respectively. The only redeeming factor that the Jungang Underground Shopping Center is that it is indoors and has climate control, which is useful for a cold winter day.

The island is beautiful, yet very cold especially in winter time. We aimed for halla rice and peanut ice cream. Just the shop near the port has peanut ice cream (not just putting nuts on that!). We used the sightseeing bus and by foot to travel around the island.

The history facts in this memorial hall recalled me of the one in Oswiecim, Poland... This memorial hall will help you to understand Jeju people's local history. Whenever I visit war related museum or places, we should stop fighting for nothing but losing the precious lives. I was even cried when I read 2 young men who could not enter the military school due to the wrong record of this tragic incident. I read all of explanation in Korean and English. I skipped some clips but I tried to watch 2 or 3 min's clips. Very well prepared in English and Korean. One of best museum. It is FREE. Only I concerned, there is no chairs to take a rest from time to time. And there was a decent with 15ish people, her voice was too much loud to make big echo in the hall area! I think they have to pay attention with other visitors who look into all scripts! I was a bit mad because she was too passionate to proceed her job. I think you do not need a docent because all of exhibits are perfectly translated in English. There are many heart breaking stories, but when I entered into the cave Darangshi(?), I could keep saying   oh my god..   I feel very sorry for all deceased, and their family members who survived at the same time witnesses. I strongly recommend this museum if you are interested local history, and history buff. It is a must. In fact, there is no restaurant, there is a coffee shop only. If you rent a car, within 10 min's drive, there are some. The bus #343, or #344 go to 4.3 Peace Park. From this park, Jeju Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest is 5 min's drive away, and 20 min's walk on foot. This Forest is wonderful. I recommend to combine these 2 places to visit at once. History and Nature are very good combination! The last stop of 343 &344 is this forest.

The hike was awesome. Very scenic and nature at its best. There are a few different routes to the top. ( summit is out of bounds though) At the top, you can find a shelter with washroom and a small shop selling cup noodles. We drove there, so had to take the same route down. There are taxis waiting at the start points when we finished our walk(around noon time)

The hike was an easy one with stairs. Less than one hour slow pace hiking up. My brother brought his baby as well in baby carrier. There are a lot of souvenir shops nearby. In my experience, the souvenir sold there is much cheaper than the one in Jeju City.

The highlight of my trip to Jeju was visiting Udo, which is small enough to be traversed by bike in a matter of hours. My girlfriend and I were glad to chose the pedal-bikes over the motorbikes and car tours because, with all the different little coffee shops and sites to explore, you'll want to take your time. While you may not find much in the way of   impressive historical sites   compared to other places in Korea or the rest of Asia, this is a beautiful place if you're just looking to relax, meandering the coast with friends or a loved one, and enjoying some local treats. It's also very scenic, so super easy to capture scenic photos. The people were also super-friendly in helping you get around, even despite the language barrier. I'd love to return again.
The great place to hangout..i like the view.. have many shop,cafe to chill outAnd if you lucky you can see the women looking for a seafood , also can enjoy the fresh seafood

The gardens are peaceful and pleasant to stroll around. There is a lot of emphasis on Confucian lore, which is a tad overplayed. Also overplayed is the constant homage to whatever Chinese Premier visited to dig a hole and plant a bonsai. The shop and restaurants are in beautiful buildings and of high quality. The use of local lava rock to surround the gardens makes for a sombre effect, but I guess that is the intent. This is not the sort of place the teens are going to rave about, but older folk and gardeners will very much enjoy
The entrance was a bit expensive but since we had the time we went for it, saw lots of colorful flowers and trees, they also had a souvenir shop and lots of benches around the park for resting.

The dragon head rock makes for an interesting photo souvenir. It is a nice place to visit, but probably would not count as one of the must-see places in Korea. Shops selling grilled octopus and other snacks line the route to the attraction, but the food is nothing spectacular as well. Allocate 30 minutes for the place.

The description at each stop was brief brief brief. I wonder why we came here...What took the longest amount of time??? The darn sales pitch conducted by a Korean auntie who claimed to be a BIG star just because she acted once in a local drama. The sales pitch was held inside a shabby shack. As it was winter the stuffiness was still bearable. Can you imagine if you came in summer??? With her broken Chinese (she turned to our tour guide for any sentences containing slightly more complex grammar) she enthusiastically tried to sell us this & that especially her biggest profit spinner - honey. She did not let her lack of fluency in Chinese stop her from making big bucks out of tourists. Not only that she even tried to sell us the many   benefits   of her empty honey glass bottle! Namely what we could do with it after we had finished eating the honey - Coin bank kitchen container blah blah blah & blah blah blah. Yakkity yakkity yak. She gave those who wanted to try a tiny teaspoon of her honey. And at the end of her sales pitch instead of letting tourists approached her if they were interested in buying she walked to each & every one of us while we were still seated (!) to ask if we wanted to buy. I think this must be because she knew that we would all walk out without buying anything if she just stand there & wait for people to come to her. So she took the more aggressive approach. Unfortunately I fell for her aggressive sales tactic & had to fork out a hefty sum for her   unique   honey. I say 'hefty' sum because when we were at the airport waiting to transfer for our flight to Seoul we saw a souvenir shop selling the SAME honey at a price which was 10000 won LESSER than what the darn old woman sold us!!! Oh man we were all so pissed! We had been cheated!!! Warning to tourists: Do NOT buy honey at this village museum!!!

The cruise ship docked in Jeju South Koren for a few hours. We didn?t plan anything, just walked around downtown.  We saw a flight of stairs, looks like it leads to some metro station, so we went down to take a look. It is a huge underground shopping center. They sell clothing, accessories, shoes and cosmetics. This is a shopper?s haven. They also have free Wi-Fi that you can connect with family and friends. Although we don?t know their language, but the people are very friendly and helpful. I don?t mind to visit Jeju again.Happy Travelling!
The cliff is amazing with a nice park to walk around. After the stroll, we visited to ICC duty free shop for shopping.

The bus ride from the bus terminal is near an hour and the bus stop you alight at looks like a bus stop in the middle of a highway. From the bus stop, walk 2km to Manjanggul cave. It's a very long walk and not if you are on a solo trip (my mistake as i thought there would be shops and things to see along the way!) as it can get quite scary. Cave is very dark, not well-lit, cold and vey wet. The floor and stairs/steps are very uneven with puddles of water so will suggest covered shoes. Will need a jacket or shawl as the cave gets colder as you walk further in. The lava/cave formation is amazing but I couldn't properly enjoy the sights as I have to keep watching out for puddles of water and the uneven floor to avoid tripping.Will only suggest this if you like to see lava formations, have a group of friends to go with and have transportation to bring you to and fro.

The building looks a bit old. There re space for parking. Inside the castle, there's hello kitty tree at the middle for photo shooting. When you walk inside, there're few theme of hello kitty for photo shooting and walk up the stair to the 2nd floor you will see a few rooms theme of hello kitty including the kitty cafe which sell drinks,Desserts and cakes. The restroom also there. The price is not high. The restaurant decorated in cute seating with hello kitty design. On the way back on ground floor you need to pass the souvenir shop. The price is not cheap for stuffs but if you are hello kitty fan it may worth.

The benefit of this place is that it's open pretty late. So when you don't know what to do when everything is closed after 6:00 om check this out. Most of   Loveland   consists of lots of outside sculptures. There are a few small interior displays - including one with a history of sex toys and small dioramas of silly sex scenes. There are also a few shops - one with old dusty outdated sex toys; the other had funny souvenirs and modern sex toys. There was also a cute cafe that offered the dense penis and boob bread drinks and ice cream. There are lots of picture taking opportunities but after awhile it becomes repetitive. You get the picture.
The beach itself is quite small, however, viewing it from the windows of one coffee shops along the beach is a very nice feeling

The BBQ pork restaurant open till midnight and our plane landed on 8 pm and after settle in hotel, still have time to enjoy, Nearby there were 24 hours store which can do a bit of late night shopping.

The admission was 占2,000 per ticket, so not so bad.  96% of what you are walking on is just hardened lava and there are puddles, so bring good shoes.  This is also basically a cave, so it's quite chilly down there, so a jacket is nice to have.  From the bottom of the stairs to the lava column is just shy of a kilometer.  There are a variety of things to see along the way, such as the different types of formations and effects.Aside from the lava tube, there is only a small restaurant and a gift shop.  Not too far down the road is the mazeland.  There may be better times than others to go.  We got lucky and missed a huge crowd of young kids that had just arrived on a bus.

The admission fee is 10000 won per pax, so it's probably the most expensive admission ticket you'll pay in Jeju.If you're a fan of bears, though, this is photo heaven =](And maybe shopping heaven! The prices of the bears are really exorbitant though.)

thank you so much for visiting.At the museum, there are two main galleries, gallery extra, souvenir shop, cafe, Elvis theater and outdoor garden. you might had wonderful time with lovely teddy bears at the museum, we believe. thank for the review and have a good day ^^

thank you so much for the visit and the review. well, i am so afraid there is no teddy Wilson replica at the shop. i will let you know when teddy Wilson replica is birth as a selling product. have a nice day ^^
Stumbled on this shop while hiding from the rain. Very   girly   and cutesy style things for sale. Great place if you like to buy postcards or items with the travel location name though!

Steps down to the waterfall are well constructed and have seats along the way. It is mostly shaded on the way down if it is hot like when I went. You can see women selling abalone on the rock shore, I have tried it, because when in Rome, but I don't like the texture.There are little shops selling souvenirs, and drinks etc. There is also a tourist information point near the car park exit, and they are very helpful. You can walk to the harbour, or to the other waterfalls in the area in around 30 minutes along the seashore and there are a few gardens along the route.

Spent the sun rose moment at Seongsang Ilchulbong, which was a wonderful sight it self. After,  we say in the cafe waiting for the ferry stated to operate. Walk from Seongsan to the Udo ferry terminal for about 20 to 30 mins.Fillup a form with names and contact number, purchased round ticket (do not loose it) and get board, straight forward. Ferry travel the channel for only 15 mins.On Udo island terminal, immediately you find a shop for transport rental: bike,  motor bike, trike, ATV and others.We choose hop on hop off bus. Any bus will drop you to four different spot ONCE,  in the island which was near to an attraction. If you decided to skip the spot you'll still need to wait for the next bus which is another 30 mins. At the last spot you need to showed the bus driver your ferry ticket also.

Spent about 3 hours here one afternoon and was very happy with the overall visit. A full display of buildings, traditional way of life, farm areas, gardens and other typical tourist information, shops and food areas give the whole village a unique attraction for everyone. A little pricey in the shops, but as you walk through the areas you get a real sense of tranquility with the how things were. Very enjoyable and if you are there - make sure you visit.

Sounds odd that it is actually my favourite attraction.. I love teddy bears. This place does not require much trekking like the sunrise peak, manjanggul cave, waterfall etc but it is a fantastic place to spend one or two hours just staring at the teddy bear exhibits with some even moving and each exhibit with a different theme. You get to see Elvis teddy bear performing   live   with his friends too. First time seeing teddy bear moving, wow experience for me. The souvenir shop is expensive though... nonetheless do give it a visit if you are a teddy lover! There is a Steve Jobs teddy, Einstein Teddy, quite creative and a twist to the usual brooding teddy we see.

Sort of worth visiting if you like green tea.  The   museum   is dwarfed by more commercial stuff including a massive cosmetics shop and a restaurant serving tea-related products.  Note that the tea fields are actually bigger than they first look so you can escape the crowds quite easily for photo opportunities.

So, perhaps this comparison is unfair, but if you have to choose between the two: the Teddy Bear Museum and this Teseum, I would personally choose this Teseum because the Teseum is slightly cheaper, closer to Jeju City, and way less pretentious (that may sound weird, but that's more or less what the difference was). Teseum was laid back, a bit more interactive, and generally understanding of that a visit to see Teddy bears would mean visiting the childish side on all of us. The Teddy Bear museum was more like an anthropological study of teddy bears or something, aka, less fun, a bit more uptight.For those in the group who were not as interested in the actual display, they could opt out and still purchase teddy bears. The gift shop was conveniently open to everyone visiting and there were a few convenience stores and such around.
Small museum. The displays were interesting- the Titanic, Normandy, and Berlin Wall to name a few ? Gift shop was pricey.

Small local old village. There are several old huts for tourist to visit.Shops sell honey, traditional juice and facial cream inside those houses.Sales are very helpful to show direction of road. They speak fluent Mandarin.

Seongsan Ilchulbong, also called ?Sunrise Peak? is located on the eastern end of Jeju island and is an ideal spot for watching sunrise. Hiking up Seongsan Ilchulbong is quite manageable for us as it takes about 30 minutes to reach the top with stops to take photographs and admire the view. There are proper steps leading to the top and it is very well maintained and well marked with signages but is quite steep at some spots of the trail. There are two hiking trails to reach the peak of the Seongsan Ilchulbong. On the way up to the Seongsan Ilchulbong?s peak, one can enjoy the scenery of the surrounding coastal landscape of Jeju and the unique rocks along the way. On that day when we were there, the place was thronged by bus loads of tourists and going up the peak may be time consuming, if one is not fit. So be prepared to spend at least 1.5 hours here. At the base, there are shops selling dried seaweeds, local delicacies, drinks, ice-cream and local handicrafts. Once you have seen this place, you will know why it is UNESCO?s heritage site - the 7 New Wonders of the World!

Seongsan Ilchulbong provides a great view of the city, and ocean especially if you reach the peak.It's 180m up, and steep, so if you don't have the right condition it may be hard for you to climb up.The place is also famous for the women divers performance. It starts at 1:30pm and 3:00pm if I am not mistaken.There are also nearby shops in the area you won't get hungry or thirsty.If you collect city Starbucks mugs, there's a Starbucks nearby that offer Jeju mugs, cups and tumblers.
