My elderly parents waited for us at the main building where there was a restaurant, shop and toilets.

If you go to Jeju Island, this is a good place to go. There is a Kitty Cafe inside, it is the same as those in Seoul. Apart from the Cafe, there is also an souvenir shop, you can buy those limited edition products there. If you drive there, you may need to wait for the parking space during peak hours.

If you don?t like teddy bears, don?t go. The gift shop is very nice. In the back outside there is the largest teddy bear I have ever seen. I found some nice items in there. I love how they made celebrity bears. The Elvis bear is s riot! They offer a show in the theatre. Nice cafe.

If you are planning to visit the Hello Kitty Island, beware: there is a specific audience that his place caters to; it is not recommended for everyone. Our tour group went here in lieu of the Trick Eye Museum.Little girls and Hello Kitty fans would love this place. Hello Kitty merchandise are displayed everywhere. There is also a room that narrates the history of how Sanrio characters came about.  There is a Hello Kitty Caf챕 at the 2nd floor. On the 3rd floor, there is an auditorium that plays a Hello Kitty-themed show. Outside is an open-air Hello Kitty-themed miniature garden maze. The view of the landscape from here is wonderful. For me, it was meh. I am not among those that this place was built for.On the plus side, there a postcards available at the souvenir shop, which you pass through as you exit the building. I also liked the stamping stations spread around the place, which are reminiscent of postmarks.

If you are not familiar with the Korean love of 'cute', you won't get what's going on at the Teddy Bear Museum. Don't expect a history of the teddy bear; expect teddy bears placed in historic events. It is cute. Kids love it. If you are searching for something serious, skip this one, but if you're looking for a bit of quirky fun that you will only find in Korea, check it out! *The gift shop is pricey.

If you are not a fan of BB, don't bother to go. Literally waste your entrance fee, if you want to get the gift, the gift shop is just rite at the entrance, no entrance fee requiredI think going to the GD Caf챕 is better than this KPop Museum. And the Teddy Bear museum next door worth 10 times more. I am not a huge fan of BB  but definitiely I know many KPOP stars.

If you are in the Seogwipo-city area and only a short time in Je-Ju this is a great find. A traditional house, a story of a great S. Korean artist, a nicely designed park and a street of small arty shops.

If you are a Kpop fan and have an afternoon to spare, you shouldn't miss this. There were plethora of stations and   things to do   for me and my friends who were less knowledgable about kpop. Don't skip the gift shop on first floor!

If you are a Hello Kitty lover and an adult, it will be nice to see all of the different Hello Kitty items, but it will also be pretty boring for you as well.  This museum is definitely geared towards kids, though I think that there could be more activities for them. The gift shop at the end of everything is quite nice but rather expensive.

If u like striking out poses with friends using the lifesize teddy bears in different costumes and characters, this is the place for u. There's also an outdoor gardens with bear exhibits, fountain and lake and a blooming grapefruit tree. Looks really good and I think it would be a nice feeling sitting around in the outdoor garden having ur lunch. That's provided it does rain. Get your tickets cheaper via taobao, the China online shopping site. They have almost 50% discount for foreigners, which we tapped on. Just need to print our confirmation and entry was a breeze. Also, this place is accessible via a bus from Jeju intercity bus terminal. Stop at jungmun resort. Nearby are alive musuem, yeomiji botanical gardens and cheonjiyeon waterfalls, good for a self planned one day trip.

If this place was in Europe I am sure the entrance fee would be double or triple, and it would have a giant shop at the end. This place is full of hard to believe facts, artsy stuff and little experiments. To be honest, I would really like to see a little shop at the and, so that I could send a postcard or add a pencil to my collection if not buying a few sciencey gifts. Definitely spare some time for this place, you will enjoy!

If staying in or visitng Seogwipo, this is a must. It's no Niagra Falls, but the quality-to-price ratio of this georgeous waterfall is difficult to overstate, as it costs only 2000 won (less than 2USD). A short walk down several staircases, passing shops along the way, will lead you to a stoney beach and the nearby waterfall. You're free to get as close as you wish, but, as many other reviewers have pointed out, the myst created by the falls makes the rocks slippery. So, wear shoes with decent treading and proceed with caution!

I went to Udo with the ferry, the queues were super long to buy the tickets but it was quite fast. The island was very crowded. I got a normal bike for 10000 won. Go to the shop on your far right. the shop straight ahead when you inboard the ferry is super crowded with Korean tourists who look for a 3 wheel scooter. These scooters are everywhere. You need to be super careful as no-one really knows how to drive them. The island is super popular among locals. Thousands of scooters and selfie-hungry teenagers looking for the best pose next to the lighthouses. Moreover prices are high and the island is full of plastic rubbish (bottles, cups, bags). I would only recommend to go during low season. But most probably the rubbish will still be there as some piles looked already quite old. The peanut ice cream is nice but not worth the money.

I went to there to have late breakfast and shopping. They mainly sell local produce of Jeju which is tangerine. It is selling almost everything with tangerine. Other than that, can go there for local food like blood sausage, dteokboki and all..Outside of the market area, there is other shopping place as well.

I went to see the crater in middle day. Was a long bus ride to get there for a 10 min visit in all. Not what I expected. It is a very rare formed crater in the world and the explanations are on a board but kind of deceiving to look at for me. All full of lush green trees and very wide, it does not give great pics and you don't see it that well either. Not as impressive as I expected. Would tell you to prioritize other stuff if you have a tight schedule. Souvenir shop has not much to buy and there is a small restaurant for snacks or ice cream.

I went to Hallassan Park to hike to the peak but unfortunately there was too much snow and I went up to Jindallaabat Shelter.  Reaching the park was very easy, you take bus 780 from the bus station 1800 Won).  Park is free.  The trail is well laid out and it is full of people of all ages trekking.  There is cell coverage in the trail and free WiFi in the shelter.  The trail is narrow so it is always hectic when passing people by.  It takes about 2 1/2 hours to get to the shelter and an hour and a half to get down.  At the enterance, there is a shop a resturant. They also sell hiking supplies if you forgot to bring your own.  Bathrooms were closed in Sokbat shelter.

I was staying last week at the Shilla in Seogwigpo, and this was just a short cab ride away. Despite the slight morning drizzle, it held the attention of my 20 year old son! There were enough wow moments - spider web, Jack's beanstalk, mushrooms, football, dinosaur eggs, slippers... all made of glass, of course. I'm sure they would have looked even more impressive at night with the lights on. The cafe was worth a stopover -- you must have the freshly squeezed tangerine juice there. The souvenir shop sells some nice pieces of glass jewelry and ornaments.

I was on tour with my parents thus the title. The art itself is pretty good. You have different artists interpreting sex in different ways. Just like a typical museum with labels this has one too. Don't miss out on reading what their art are called. It's pretty hilarious. There's a shop where you can buy   stuff   as well. The whole place is open to 18 year olds and above only.

I wanted to do this at sunrise but never woke up. So I went around 11h. Lots of tourists. It's all stairs to the top but not that hard. Takes 20 min in all. Beautiful view and scenery on top. There are some souvenirs and food shops at the bottom (Dunkin Donuts, Starbucks and cie).There is also a souvenir shop at half the moutain with beautiful engraved wood done by a woman there. I bought my most beautiful souvenir to her. She engraved Jeju, the date on it and wrapped it good for me. It's a short must do thing! You will get great pics there.

I visit Jeju at December 2015 and stayed near this museum. I have no plan to visit this museum, but from the outside looks interesting. I just made a couple of photos in the front. After that I intend to buy some souvenirs, but in fact visitors should buy ticket and enter the museum first. There is no souvenir shop available outside the ticketing gate

i thought the museum sounded stupid but it was actually really cute!!! there were so many scenes set up with stuffed animals on the first floor.  they were so creative!  then you can you to the second floor and take pictures.  there's the rock band set up, the proposal bear, and many more.  there are also famous works of art re-done with teddy bears. finally there's the gift shop.  everything is over priced but you can't expect anything else...

I think it was a great idea for them to have teddy bears pose for historical moments, people and scenes.  It may seem whimsical at first, but it is also a perfect platform for parents to explain certain moments in history and people to them.  E.g. having a bear bandaged with only one ear to portray u know who.  Perhaps one easily missed teddy bear is the actual world's most expensive teddy bear!There is also a gift shop at the end (with Michael and Audrey...) where they sell a variety of teddy bears.  Although the teddy bears look as normal as any teddy bears, mind u, u don't get those mass produced made-in-u-know-where quality.  Worth taking a look!This place will be more suitable for family with young children or people who just love teddy bears.

I studied the seoqwipo bus route and decided to bring my family for a day trip to Udo Island. I stayed in Jungmun Resort vicinity. It was easy to catch bus 282 from here and made a transfer for direct bus to Udo Passenger Terminal. Upon arrival, after filling up the necessary details and proof of passports竊we went to the cruise Departure point. Luckily we chosen a weekday for this trip. The queue was short. In the cruise ship, we could find seats. A 15 min ride and we were greeted by several e-scooters and shop houses. Here, you could settle for lunch. But if it was too early for you, several sightseeing spots come with line of restaurants. We took the circular bus (white color van) which we thought was the best choice. Every stop you were  required to queue to abroad. This bus went to most attractions including black sand & Udo lighthouse. The bus route was also the route for E-scooters /car. Do be careful for safety sake. Returning from Udo Island was amazing : we could not find a bus stop that for the same bus number  supposed to bring us back to Seoqwipo! Nevertheless, luckily we had alternative plan ! we took a bus that brought us to Gimpo Airport. Got a decent dinner and then took limo bus 600 directly to our accomodation, alighting at bus stop named Jungmun Resort Entrance. This DIY by public transport comes in cheap!This trip you need a whole day.

I spent few hours at the museum, I had jet lag  because of 6 hours difference in my biological hour, & it is near Hana Hotel where I stayed. It is a nice walk to the museum. I thought it is a happy place, because most of the visitors were happy especially those with children. I took my time looking at the museum & the shop. I enjoyed my time. The museum have stairs & elevator. I took lunch at the resturant , it is fast food, with reasonable price.Bathrooms at each level & they are clean. The view from outside the resturant is nice & relaxing, & the outside garden is beautiful.I watched the Elvis show,it is nice & professional work. I think to enjoy & appreciate the museum you have to spend few hours, not a quick visit.I thought it is a delightful happy place.

I really love this place, sooo much. You can reach this place by bus number 710 from Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal directly, trip around 90 minutes & pay for bus fare by T-Money. This bus route passing some attraction in Jeju, so please stop at the attraction you wants to visit. You can rent a car too. From bus stop at Seongsan Ilchulbong, you must walking around 300 meters. What i loved about this place is, so many seafood restaurants (because it really close with ocean) & some Korean cosmetics shop too. Don't forget to bring jacket, umbrella and of course mineral water. If you have strength, you can climbs the hill (around 500 meters). But so much fog when i'm there, i can't see clearly the basin. You will met some elderly people here, at the peak. Fresh air & green vegetation will makes your eyes & breath feels relieve. You can buy some souvenirs when you get back to the foothills.

I really liked this part of the trip. We hiked up to the top, and I am a five month pregnant lady so you can do it too! The view of the city below is the most interesting view you are going to get from the top of the crater. The top of the crater itself isn't that spectacular. It was very pretty and fun! Also we happened to be there around the same time as the lady divers so we watched that and it was pretty interesting. When we were there in December they were doing shows around 1:30 and 3:30. You should definitely come here. There are also little restaurants and shops at the bottom if you are hungry!

I loved this place!!! Maybe because I love teddy bears and collect them. But objectively, I think they did a wonderful job to dress the bears up in adorable costumes and arrange them in all sorts of different themed settings. You start at the 3rd floor and walk down to the 1st. My favourite was the 2nd floor - even though the exhibits are encased in glass, I could put my own little bears (yes, I brought my own bears with me on this trip) on the glass and take pictures with them (no flash allowed). Some of the bears have even moving parts and some are life-sized. There is a scheduled musical and dance performance by Elvis bear and friends, which my parents enjoyed. At the outdoors area, you can take photos with life-sized bears in interesting poses and themed settings and there is even a clock that chimes hourly and is accompanied by bears dancing with the chimes. There is a cafe and a souvenir shop in the ground level and you can take pictures with panda bears (not real of course) and other cute bears, and buy a souvenir bear home (but price is quite ex).

I loved this place! My kids found the raw seafood smell a bit overbearing but they managed. I loved all the fresh seafood, vegetables & fruit along with all the kimchi & spices! This is a place to come to for locals & an experience for visitors. I wish our community had such a place as this. I would be shopping here all the time!

I love this place so much. Everyone can easily climb this mountain because they provide stairs which is well built, not too steep and not slippery. Although it made me tired to climb to the top but the scenery up there is very beautiful. I took so many photographs. The combination of land and sea scenery is very good.There is also many souvenir shops and food stall on the rest area with cheap souvenirs which is a good place to buy jeju souvenirs.Must visit.

I hiked up Hallasan via Seongpanak trail and went down the Gwaneumsa trail. The hiking was almost torturous, for a person who does only some jogging as preparation to hike Halla, but it indeed worth every step towards the peak because of the heavenly view of Jeju from there. Expect rocky trails, crazy steep staircases and trails. Bring at least 2 litres of water (you can refill your bottles at fresh water springs along Seongpanak and after the bridge in Gwaneumsa trail). There's a small shop selling hot noodles, drinking water and hot coffee at Jindallae Bat shelter. Toilets are available at Sokbat and Jindallabaet and a few more somewhere along Gwaneumsa. Start early to complete the hike early. Be sure to bring your camera. Get walking sticks too if you can, I didn't but I could still do the hike :D I went to Jeju on a solo trip and did the hike alone, but a lot of other hikers were very kind giving me words of encouragement and even waited for me along Gwaneumsa trail. A must do if you get to Jeju! No entrance fee! :D

I have to say, when we reached the summit of Seongsan Ilchulbong we were a bit underwhelmed. It's impressive if you haven't yet seen the summit of Hallasan, but if you have it really doesn't compare. The crater of Seongsan Ilchulbong is porous, so it doesn't hold water like Hallasan. And it only takes you about 20-30 mins to reach the top viewing deck. It does make for a good photo, but so do the views of Seongsan village and the coastline nearby. The view on the pathway walking towards the base of it is also impressive in itself.It's definitely worth visiting, and there are plenty of little shops/stalls selling food as well as cheap souvenirs. Nearby is Ilchulbong beach, with black sand. Haenyeo female divers are famous here, and there is a restaurant at the far end of the beach serving fresh seafood caught by the divers, but we didn't have time to eat there.
I have driven pass this place coincidentally It's quite unique place, worth a visit. A few shops, restaurants, caf챕, and street food markets.

I have climbed Mt Bogong in Australia, Mt Kinabalu in Malaysia, which were both taller than Mt Hallasan, but I find climbing Hallasan most challenging! We took the bus to Seongpanak. The path is all uneven as it was paved with lava rocks, all the way to the top! My poor feet were quite sore the next day. Make sure you have proper hiking shoes. Definitely not recommended for children or people with knee problems. It was raining and quite foggy when we reached the top, so we couldn't see the crater unfortunately. We were pleasantly surprised at the half way mark where that is a little shop selling instant noodles for 1500won. You can also buy mineral water for 1000won, which is the same price as in the shop in the city. I would have thought they would sell it for twice the price! They are strict about the timing of your climb. It was summer, so the cut off time at the halfway mark was 13.30hrs. If you couldn't make it there by that time, they would not allow you to further climb up to the peak, which is fair enough. We wanted to hike down Gwaneumsa but it closed due to falling rocks, so we had to hike down the same way we came up. Before you leave, you can always pay 1000won for a certificate with your name printed on it (at the foot of the mountain, there is an office near the toilet areas, where they usually collect payments for climbers that come by cars. If you take the bus, you do not need to pay any parking fees). You'll have to show a selfie photo at the top of Hallasan, in order to have the certificate. The person manning the office is not very good with computer. He took forever to type out names. Overall, it was an interesting experience.

I have been wanting to visit the Teddy Bear Museum for the longest time but did not get to visit the one in Seoul 2 years ago. So, when we decided to plan a 2D1N trip to Jeju, this attraction is in my itinerary list. It is not located conveniently near the city centre and about an hour's bus ride to go to the attraction. I was so excited when I saw the museum when the bus passed by and alighted with much excitement. We were greeted with a huge bear at the entrance and it was like entering a wonderland. We walked around admiring the displays, the history of teddy bears etc. We also visited the outdoor park right behind the museum which are meant for visitors only. It was a fruitful visit and did not fail my expectation though. Love all the bears on sale at the gift shop but couldn't bring them all back so only got to admire them when I was there. If you are visiting Jeju, do drop by this museum to bring back childhood memories.

I hadn't heard all that much about this beach and I was really pleasantly surprised, in a big way. The beach itself is fairly wide, and the sand is great. Moreover, the water is crystal clear, and the water is warm, so if you actually want to go swimming, it's a great spot (unfortunately I didn't have enough time). But this place is more than just a beach. Right behind the beach is a nice little town so it is lively and you have shops and dining options there. On the beach you have a nice fancy  coffeeshop that is perfectly located, directly overlooking the sea. Add to that the rocks on each side of the beaches, as well as the small mountain to the East, so this place is not only perfect for relaxing, but also for taking pictures.

I had to high an expectation for this shop unfortunately. It isn't anything very special, and it's selection is quite small compared to the other Jeju shops I jage been to. The prices are fair though, I think it is a fine option if you are staying within Jeju city.

I had high hopes for this spot, but it is hard to recommend it.  What was once a pretty island is now circled by identical seafood restaurants, cafes, burger joints and other tourist shops.   Biking a loop around the island is nice enough, but the road is jammed with little electric   rickshaw   things and noisy scooters.  Honestly, this place would be a perfect case study of bad development for a tourism management class.

I had heard about these women from NatGeo. Being able to see how important these women are to the local community was impressive. The museum provides a detailed panorama of these women's lives. From when they are children to when they give birth to late into their lives. It provides some real size replicas of boats, costumes, and even foods. A must see. A little out of the way if you are not staying in the area but well worth the drive or the bus ride(bus stop is named after the museum). Price is reasonable and the gift shop has some out of the normal options.

I guessed many have mentioned that this was a typical market and I do not think they were wrong. However, it really depends the reason for your visit. If you are here to try cheap and good raw and fresh seafood (eg: raw fish slices for 10000won only), OR to try a variety of local food (eg: Sundae aka blood sausage, traditional fishcake stick, Kimbap, fresh Jeju orange juices, different types of kimchi, korean rice cakes, croquette, Tteokbokki, hotba, Modeumjeon - where they eat during new year and jeons, OR to purchase souvenirs and snacks for your family and friends then you are at the right place! It was also cheaper to purchase dried goods like ikan bilis and kelp in the market than supermarkets.We were at Seogwipo Maeil Olleh Market before coming to this market and we found that stalls that sell Jeju's souvenirs and local snacks such as Jeju crunch chocolate were cheaper in this market. The shop owners also gave us a handful of other snacks to try after our purchase in hope that we would be back for more. In Summary, this was a good place to try many local food at a smaller amount and a place to purchase affordable snacks for gift at a cheaper price.

I got to visit this museum as part of an inclusive tour so I can't comment on the value of the entrance fee, but I loved this museum.  I haven't laughed so much in ages.  I am not sure if it is meant to be so delightfully funny!  It is famous in S Korea for a TV series   about a Princess that was filmed there.What you get is several galleries of teddy bears dressed up as historical figures, famous art works, and scenes from history or of S Korean culture.  There are several large bears around the place suitable for having your photo with eg Charlie Chaplin, Michael Jackson.  Outside there are several bears enjoying the gardens again suitable for being photographed with.  There is a cafe and a gift shop.  The cafe was closed when we visited late afternoon. There is a short running show of an automaton Elvis-Bear again hilarious!  I would definitely go back.  This museum is located in the Jungmun resort area on the Bus Route 600.  Get off at PlayKpop stop - its just next door.

I got a public bus from the Inter-city Bus Terminal at Jeju-si to this park at only Won 2000. 1 hour required.  This is the last activity of my trip and upon leaving, luckily I met an American man at the bus stop who agreed to share a taxi with me heading to the airport, otherwise I may be late.Time is rather limited for me and I took a quick and rough walk in the park after taking a 45 min lunch of seafood pot at the restaurant at the entrance.  Yummy!  Seafood is to die for in Jeju.  I like this park as it's well gardened, clean, cozy with some souvenirs shops and two restaurants inside.  And I did not meet groups of tourists which is a PLUS.  Visitors decent. Next time when I come to Jeju, I should spend plenty of time in this park.There is a famous beach opposite to the park entrance so you can have a walk there as well after leaving here.

I got 28 hour spare time before my flight to Dhaka in my last visit to Korea. When I got this break at the very last moment, I searched Jeju air ticket and hotel booking online without any delay. As I purchased it at the last moment, I had to spend USD 125 more for air ticket and hotel booking. Jeju is a rush destination in summer. It's is a fairly large island to cover within 24 hours. Thanks to TripAdvisor and reviewers for helping me to select Seongsan Ilchulbong and Hamdaeok beach from many other attractions.Tourists have time, usually visit Seongsan Ilchulbong before dawn to observe Sunrise. That why it is also known as Sunrise peak. As I did?t had that option in hand, I climbed it at afternoon. I took a taxi from my hotel at Hamdaeok beach and it costs around USD 28. Bus is always cheaper but I had only 20 hours left in my hand to catch my return flight. Sunrise peak entry ticket costs USD 2 for adults and USD1 for child. Most of the review I read earlier suggests it takes 20 minutes to climb on the peak but as an amateur I took roughly 40 to 45 minutes to climb. There are two wide and convenient stairway to climb on the peak. I selected the left side stairway and eventually it was a right decision. Because there is a small grocery in the midway selling soft drinks and water for those who didn't buy it from the base. As usual they charge double for each drinks but it was a life saver for me. When I came down from the other way I didn't find any shop like this. There are also a  midway station if you are tired want get refreshed for a while. When I reached on the peak I was almost exhausted. The view is literally breathtaking. I was sitting there more than one hour and a half as it is so charming that made for  forget everything else of life. I came down from the other stair way. The surrounding is so calm and comfortable that I stayed their until it?s dark. Tips: Try to book air ticket and hotel upfront to save cost. Rely more in internet than locals advise because there is a high chance of misleading information due to language barrier. I lost twice in the island for relying on them and lost around 3 hours of my precious time. There are halal restaurant ( Bagdad and Rajmahal) in Jeju island. 4 days are fairly enough to cover most of the attraction of Jeju. It costs total USD 400 all inclusive  for me for a quick tour , however if you are two them many cost will be shared within you. If I could catch the early morning flight from Gimpo airport at 7:30 am and save three more hours to arrive Jeju island then I could go to Udo island as well. I couldn't do that because I had to come from Suwon city. So if you stay at Seoul, you can catch 7:30 morning flight comfortably.

I found this to be the best attraction in Jeju. It really is a lot of stairs, so if you are not good in health condition, this might be very tiresome. But there are rest points a long the way, so you can take your time. There are little shops and restaurants around after you finish your hike. Beautiful views to take pictures both going up and down.

I found this place by accident. One afternoon as I was shopping at Seogwipo market area, I happen to see the sea at a distant. I thought I'd just take a walk towards there. It was a lovely surprise, as I managed to get to this very much talked about waterfalls. The water actually drains directly into the sea, and not another freshwater reservoir as more commonly seen.There is an entrance fee and plenty of souvenir shops and eateries here. It's a beautiful sight and even better sound.... the sound of the water gushing down into the ocean. The mist from the pounding of the water is so refreshing. Be prepared to walk along some steep steps...not many but quite steep.

I found pretty disappointing this 1 block Street where several pork cuisine restaurants are located, mostly for tourists, thats why the prices raises up from others in the city. Only if you go to shop nearby and want to taste Jeju pork in well decorated restaurants

I found out about Love Land on Google during our cruise to Asia.  So when we landed my husband and I took a taxi cab there.  It was right next door to the Museum of Modern Art so we checked that out first.  And then we walked over to Love Land.  It could also be called   Happy Land   as we would every now and then hear an eruption of laughter from other visitors.  We were certainly laughing too.The sculptures in various poses of love were whimsical and clever.  It was a nice walk that took us about an hour and a half.  At the end we went into the shop where there were small dioramas and objects for sale.Volcanoes and waterfalls I have seen before.  But I had never seen a place like Love Land.  When we returned to our cruise ship fellow cruisers said   Why didn't you tell us?!  We would have gone.

I flow to Jeju just to walk up this mountain.  You have to apply to the  Hallasan National Park visitor management system for the QR code admission ticket. My ticket was for the Gwaneumsa Course, time slot 5-30am - 8-00am.   I started my walk at 7-50am,  It was perfect walking weather, overcased so not too warm.  There is a 500 hiker per day limit on this route to the top, on the other easier route there is a 1000 hiker per day limit. The first few kms is easy going and you think to yourself this walk is going to be a piece of cake.  After around 4 kms you reach the first of two public toilets on the route.  From there the walk becomes a uphill slot with countless wooden steps. On the way up there is two downhill's with maybe a couple of hundred steps to walk down before walking uphill again.  After the second public W.C.  the route is a never ending series of wooden staircases until at last it flattens  out and the top of the mountain.  When I did it there was maybe a hundred or more walkers queuing to get a photo next to the summit stone.    I just gave my phone to a person and asked them to take a photo with the stone in the background. Within minutes I was on my way back down.The reason why you need a photo with you and the summit stone (even if it over your shoulder in the distance) is to claim your Certificate of climbing Mt, Hallasan. On the Gwaneumsa Course you can self print your certificate at a booth just past the QR-cord booth at the trail head  If like me you are clueless with mobile phones you can go the manned QR code booth and them to do it for you.  There have a printer in the booth and was very happy to do it for me.   It costs 1000 won (around 1 us$) Facts and figures, I am a 73 year old Englishman on an extended holiday in Korea.  Start time 7-50am, summited at 11-05am.   Started down at 11-15 and back to the trailhead at 12-55pm. Yes I do class myself as a bit of a mountain walker so these times  are maybe a little faster then average, but mountain walking is about enjoying yourselves and not about how fast you can get up and down. I took a litre of liquid, in hindsight I should have taken more and I did finish it off when I was within sight of the carpark. There is a shop across the road from the carpark.   Food, I took no food just a few sweets and a couple of chocolate bars.  So the bottom line is you have to take all the food and drink with you.  It does say that you can get drinking water at the second WC (shelter) but I could not find any so don't depend on it. Getting back to Jeju City.   There was no buses so I started walking the 8 miles back to my hotel on the seafront. Pleased to say that  I did manage to flag down a taxi after around a mile.  All in all a very enjoyable day out on the mountain.

I don't understand the hype of this place. Maybe it's because I went on a Sunday and no one was around, but I walked around for about an hour and there wasn't much to see. The small houses are cute and it's interesting to read how durable they are when taking into account that they are basically made from mud and straw. But the town was absolutely dead quiet, we felt like we weren't even supposed to speak. I wouldn't recommend this 'village'. (There was a small coffee shop near the car park that sold incredibly expensive coffee).

I didn't know I was looking at this famous peak when we approached in a taxi (looking for a lunch spot that our kids would approve of). I was saying   Wow, look at that   as we drove towards it. Then our driver explained it was the famous peak. I can see why, even on a cloudy rainy day it was such a beautiful scene. We couldn't climb to the peak because it was closed to the public due to an impending typhoon. I was disappointed we couldnt climb but so glad that we got to see it, even from the base. Absolutely beautiful area. I want to come back to Jeju just to climb that peak and see the beauty from above.Incidentally there were plenty of restaurants and cafes and shops in the small town at the base. Even an American Embassy (i.e. Mcdonalds)

I couldn?t resist visiting this place on our way from Jeju city to Seogwipo. It made me giddy as a child. Entry fee is now 14,000 won per adult, and either 11,000 or 13,000 for children. This place has optional guided tours and accepts credit cards. Small room of Hello Kitty history and how her image has evolved since 1976. Original design merch on display. Lots of interactive rooms for kids and 3 floors to play. As an adult I still had fun and enjoyed a Hello Kitty hot chocolate (her face is in the cream), and Hello Kitty-shaped strawberry mousse cake in the cafe. You?re paying for the experience, here, so if you or your child is not a Hello Kitty fan, don?t waste your time. The maze on the roof is shaped like Hello Kitty from an aerial view and is strictly for children?the maze walls are only about 2 feet tall. My favorite part was the art exhibit (2nd floor) and all the small, unexpectedly perfect details (heart shaped straws, Hello Kitty toilet paper!). Souvenir shop: a mechanical pencil costs 7,700 won (more than $6)?I guess this is slightly more than American Sanrio store prices. But, if you?re willing to visit this museum, you?re probably also willing to pay for a momento of your experience.

I confess - I LOVED stuffed toys and teddy bears! So this museum where the cute teddies were all dressed up and re-enacting famous scenes just sent me into teddy heaven. Pros:- A lot of cute scenes of teddies- Some photo spots available - Large souvenir shop- Accessible for the disabled, as there?s lifts and wide aisles on every levelCons:- Many showcases were behind glass. Because of this, the photos I took weren?t nice due to the reflection. - Could have been more interactive. As this place is (probably?) targeted at kids, it would have been nice if more displays were interactive and engaging, rather than stuck behind a glass box.

I come there first time.And I am very exciting when I see a bigest mountain and very cool on December 2014. There provide a lots of coffee shop such as Starbuck , Dunkin Donut and Coffee Bean. If you go down to the small beach then You meet Ajuma who sell seafood. Dont forget to try it!!!

I am super Hello Kitty fans and for sure go there when I was in Jeju.  Frankly, it is a place for kids rather than fans.  Not many specialty items available in the shop.  It is a good experience to have a coffee at the cafe.

I am not interested in plush toys, but I really was attracted by the teddy bear museum, and I love there. A full of fairy tale castle, real exist in the real world.  Because it is full of various style of teddy bear, kids will enjoy very much time in the amusement in the museum, and I as a youth, although is no longer a child, but still attracted by the relaxed happy atmosphere, and enjoyed all the items in the museum to visit.  The most impressive is one of the world's most expensive teddy bear, it is very beautiful, dress made of silk princess skirt, was decorated with swarovski crystals, France, and the biggest bright spot is her crown, made of platinum and diamond, very gorgeous, and value of this teddy bear is close to one hundred million won, but also as the exhibits on display only, not sales.  , of course, when the tourists are deeply attracted by all kinds of teddy bear, teddy bear museum shops can provide people with the teddy bear toy and its surrounding products, greatly satisfy the desire to tourists for a teddy bear.  Finally, I miss very much in the time to visit the museum. And look forward to the next trip to South Korea.

I am not a teddy bear lover, but I found the collection very interesting. First of all, these were the collection of a Ms. Joanne Oh, a teddy bear artist. The bears date up to generations of collectibles. The design varies with time. The size of the bear are from tiny to bigger than man size. There were several hall showing different themes. Of course it will end with a souvenir shop showing many bear designs. In the international bear, there was even one of President Obama, with a letter of President Obama to Joanne Oh. The museum also has an advocacy of bear conservation. All in all, it was interesting with plenty of Photo opportunity for my wife who loved it so much. By the way, the materials used in Ms. Oh's bear were all made of ecological-friendly materials, another advocacy of this fantastic bear artist.

I am in the middle of living in Jeju for a year and visited the Haenyeo Museum with three friends a couple of months ago. It was a really great visit and showed really well the changes in Haenyeo lifestyle as time has gone on. The top floor has a beautiful picture gallery with gorgeous views. Highly recommend. I think you need about an hour - an hour and a half here.Also the gift shop is great for cute Jeju-y things. I put some   Jeju stockings   together for my cousin's kids for Christmas all with keyrings/books/purses/other stuff bought here.

I am a huge fan of Udo.  I have been numerous times and I never get tired of exploring a new road or a new cafe.At times it is soooo overrun by tourists that it can be a little overwhelming, but if you are smart and plan your trip during quiet times of the year, it is really rewarding.  The roads are quieter, the stores less busy.  There are numerous ways you can tour the island:I usually take my car.  I have heard that NO rental cars are allowed on Udo anymore.  so be aware of that.But once off the ferry there are so many scooter and electric bike shops* around.  *Foriegners be aware that you do need a license to rent these!ProTip:  I absolutely recommend you get off the beaten path and go explore the inner part of the island. So many cute cafes and splendid views!

Huge, lots to see and easy to get lost in the maze of stalls. For a glimpse into local life with products ranging from clothes, fabrics, sundries, cooked/fresh food, seafood, dried goods and everything in between. Local souvenirs definitely cheaper here than duty free shops and touristy spots. Check out fresh tangerines, Jeju chocolates, hallabong jam/honey vitamins; even dried anchovies (great as Korean soup base) and ginseng roots for DIY ginseng chicken at home. Do compare prices at a few stalls and bargain with the kind ahjummas when buying several items. Souvenir hunters, moms and senior relatives will definitely love exploring the colourful atmosphere of Dongmun market. The covered market is good activity during rainy or hot days. Nearby attractions: Jungang underground shopping street, E-martNote:Street parking just outside the market can be difficult at peak hours, suggest self-drivers park around Black Pork Street or nearby hotels and walk to the market.

Horses are a big part of the Jeju culture  and Jeju Horse Park is a pretty cool place. Its museum includes many photographs  artifacts and a video telling the story of the Jeju   ma    or pony  which is descended from the ponies brought to the island by Mongol invaders. The island was considered a good place to raise horses  and the Mongols used it as such. At the park  you can also ride the horses. There is a great giftshop with lots of local handmade items. Children or even adults can make related crafts in an activity room. The building itself is round like a ger  the traditional nomadic tents used by the Mongols. The top deck includes a fabulous 360-degree view of the   oreums   (small cinder-cones or parasitic volcanoes) that literally ring the area of the park. Inside the railing  an artist has painted the oreums  along with their names. So  you can know exactly which oreums you are viewing. There are also some actual Mongolian gers (also known as yurts in other nomadic cultures). I believe tourists can actually spend the night in one of the gers. One thing to consider: If you want to visit  you must either have your own transportation or go with someone who does. It's kind of far from anywhere  and bus service may not operate in that area. Likewise  taxis don't just happen by. But  it is a beautiful area and interesting for the entire family We visited in the spring  and there were also lots of colorful wildflowers. Plan to spend a few hours there  especially if you will ride the horses.

Hiking Hallasan is the number one experience to do on Jeju. You have to be reasonably fit but it's fairly easy to complete as a day hike and no guides are needed. The trails are well maintained and easy to follow and there are great views. If you climb in winter, it's well worth getting small instep crampons for about 10 dollars from the shop at the bottom of either the Seongpanak or Gwameumsa trails. I recommend walking up the steeper Gwaneumsa trail, and down the Seongpanak trail. I've been up four times now, different routes, and this is definitely my preferred approach. The views are much better and Seongpanak is much easier on the knees coming down.

Have you taken a trip recently? If you have not, go to Jeju Island in South Korea right now. There are two towns there with hotels of good reputation. Also, Jeju has a beautiful hiking trail called the ?Olle Road?. You can see a variety of sea creatures and birds there.   Olle Road takes you to the amazingly nice ?Hanra Mountain?. Hanra Mountain is a dormant volcano. Climbing to the top is a little challenging because the mountain?s altitude is about 2000meters.  Also, Don't forget to go the big shopping centers for foreigners. The exchange rates are better in Korea than in your home country. So change your currency at the Jeju International Airport, or withdraw cash from the banks.    This place gives beautiful views. Visit Jeju Isalnd. You will have very fun time!

Hallasan is Jeju?s massive mountain, and was once a volcano. It peaks at 2000 meters, and from 700 meters up, the only way up is by foot, and you?ll have to drop your car at a designated area to begin the climb. The best place to start the trek is Seongpanak, on the East side of the mountain. Going up takes about 4 hours, at a normal pace, this trek will take all day. There are two checkpoints that you much reach before a certain time of the day to be allowed to go all the way up (and come back down before sunset). This means that you absolutely have to go there early. I was at the foot of the mountain at 9am, and I wouldn?t advise anyone to start climbing after 9:30 if you don?t want to be turned down. Also, since this can be exhausting, pack beverages and food before going up. There is a small shop at Seongpanak and another one at the 1500 meter checkpoint, but they have very limited choice. Just stop at a convenience store in the city before going up and you should be good for the day. The climb is relatively uneventful for the first 2/3rd of the way, with fairly little to see because you?ll be surrounded by vegetation. But once you reach an altitude of about 1600 or 1700 meters, you?ll start getting a great look at the top of the mountain and more importantly at the rest of the island.  Once you reach the top, the view will be amazing. The volcano?s caldera feels like being on the moon, and you can also see Jeju?s coastline as well as its major cities, Jeju and Seogwipo. Absolutely breathtaking! Make sure to check the weather if you plan to go there, because the tall mountain tends to attract clouds, which could completely ruin the awesome view you?d get on a clear day.

Great place, good food and a bit crowded... You can find a lot of shops that selling chocolate, jeju mageoli, jeju oranges... If you want to bring some to your country, better you buy it here... It's cheaper than at the airport lor (obviously!!!)... The prices are same at all shops... You can get 6/12/15 boxes of choc for 10.000 won here (diff by size n type)... The prices will be 3x at the airport...

Good show for young and old. No need any knowledge of Korean. Theater is located in the middle of nowhere so make sure you have your meals before going. There is a convenient shop (GS25) in the hotel nearby but limited food selection. There is also a restaurant within the hotel but only opens at 7pm (our show was 8pm) when we were there. Be punctual, the show starts on time.
Good for rainy day. Lots of little cosmetic shops to get last minute purchases, interesting clothing and shoe shops.
good facility,many store and warm when winter season its the best place for shopping at Jeju.nearby to dongmun market and its easy to go by bus

Going to Hallasan by bus #701 from our hotel in Hamdeok area, through Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal, change to bus #740 departing every 1 hour.  Stop at Eurimok Trail point. Walking from bus stop to the gate for about 5 minutes. There was a nice facilities at the gate: clean toilet, small convenient store with drinks vending machines, and police station too.Please be aware that   sleepers   are not allowed to be use for trekking due to heavy terrain. Including our son's crocs shoes. Unfortunately, the shop run out shoes stock so He can't join us.Eurimok trail quite heavy for untrained persons, we just only reached 1.300 meters before deciding to turn back to base.The bus #740 was picking us up at 15:35 back to Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal.

Getting here was tricky, as you must take a bus from either Jeju or Segowipo and even then the bus stop is 2km from the entrance so usually taxis cruise past and you can do them a deal. It is pricey to reach and has an entrance fee (half price for youths under 25 with valid passport) but has full facilities such as restaurant, shop, toilets, lockers etc, It is a little cold underground so recommended to bring a jumper or warm clothing. It is incredible to be underground in a volcanoe and there are numerous info signs in various languages along the route as you walk underground to the cone. It's a little dark for photos but if your camera can be adjusted there can be some great shots. You must walk quiet far and it can be wet on the ground so proper shoes recommended and flip-flops/sandals avoided. I saw plenty of kids but obviously it is dark so may be a little scary, plus it's quite a fair walk so think through if you want to walk about a mile to the cone or just have a quick look. An interesting trip for sure!

Generally, a great place to shop for mask, body care, face care products with great prices. Do beware of some shops do actually give a kind of face/attitude if you touch or even asked for prices ( please note that, most shops dont include a price tag) after you  decided not to buy.

From the Jejusi bus terminal we took bus 201 to Udo. It took about 1 1/2 hours. Definitely download the app Naver to navigate your way around the island, as Google Maps does not have any results for public transportation. We spent 4 hours on the island. Ferry ride from the port is only about 15 minutes each way. Buying a ticket can be a little chaotic as there are no signs in English but we just held up 2 fingers for two passengers and were given 2 round-trip tickets. Upon arrival in Udo expect to be bombarded with shop owners yelling at you to rent bicycles, ebikes, motorcycles, or 3-wheeled cars (for 2 people). 2 people renting 2 ebikes for 4 hours cost us 40,000 won. Need int?l drivers license for the latter 2. I definitely recommend the ebike over the bicycle unless you really want to get strenuous exercise. Lots of hills and 11.4 km of trail to follow. Lots of little mini-towns where you can buy food, have coffee or peanut ice cream (recommend). Tons of photo opps so take your time. We finished in 3 hours, 40 mins (and my hubby wanted to stop A. LOT. Last ferry back to Jeju is at at 5 pm this time of year. Plan accordingly.

From Jeju City Local Bus Terminal, take bus #701, stop at Seongsan Port. It takes 90mins, 3300won.Fill up the boarding form for the ferry, before you proceed to buy the ferry ticket at the counter. Round trip charges 5500won, which takes 10mins per trip. Expect a lot of visitors during weekends or public holidays.At Udo, there are shops offer rental of bicycles, ATV, automatic scooter, etc. which can accommodate every one either youths, elders or children.You could enjoy cycling around the island the best during a windy chilling day.When I think of Udo, I will remember the kindness of restaurant owner of щ 대Ъ珥. When I was eating, I accidentally hit my dental braces with the spoon, and I was rubbing to ensure it was alright. The ajumma approached me and asked me what happened, I showed her my braces, and she was quick-witted to get scissor to cut banchan into smaller pieces, while cutting, she repeatedly saying   ottoke ottoke  .. I was really grateful to her, and I enjoyed the lunch well.

From historical event, paintings, to modern day moment, current dramas cast of all teddies. From teddy named Wilson on his journey around the world to Elvis and Queen Elizabeth in teddy version all in one place. Not to be missed, the most expensive LV and Swarovski teddy on display! Outside you can witness miniature teddies on some serious construction site of 9 meters height of huge gigantic Teddy in the making. There's a teddy souvenir shop, and also teddy cafe. The museum is not that big, just 2 floors of gallery and 1 floor cafe and shop. Some bears displayed outside in the park.

Free access.  We knew more about the history, living and status of haenyeo.  The exhibits are well decorated with nominal English descriptions.  The souvenir shop is a good place to buy souvenirs about haenyeo.
Forget Lotte Duty Free, You can find almost every Korean Skin Care Brand here, TheFaceShop, Etude, Isoi, Banilla , Nature Republic, etc, all with cheap price and lots of bonus.

For us - it was a last 'must see' on Jeju Island.  Our tour books featured it as a top site, so we went.  We didn't have much time, and it worked (since it's near the airport) for a quick stop off.  I didn't hate it - it was crowded though.  Lots of tour groups, teens, etc.  There were several shops nearby that were handy for our last bit of shopping.  You don't need to spend a lot of time here, but the rock formation is neat and the myth behind it is interesting.

For those that love fish, this market is a place to visit. Very interesting but not for me. You can also shop for shoes, clothes, chocolate, souvenirs and fruit. I found it a little on the dirty side but it might be because I don't care for fish much.

For the ones who believe they are in good shape:Why struggle, why do it the hard way? because it is much more scenic and maybe only one tenth of climbers going that way. Taxi from town to starting point (approx 20 min) was 11.000 won on taximeter from my hotel in Nohyung-dong (near the int. airport) or take the bus but only on sat and sundays). Bus stop at Seongpanak when you come down from the mountain on the road. Check schedule and bus no. Taxi back 20.000 won (not on meter..)This is by far the most important place to look before you set out. THE WEATHER! http://www.mountain-forecast.com/peaks/Hallasan/forecasts/1950 I wouldn't call my self an experienced climber but I did it in 3h10min up and 2h down. This is in a pace where I overtook and was not overtaken, and very short breaks, maybe only 2 min in total 5 times. The track is changes between rocks or stairs, I think it's well kept. Two toilet stations up and two down. None at the top. Bring 3-4L of liquids minimum, no passport nor entry is needed for the mountain (aug 2013). A windbreaker for the summit can be nice to have. The weather can change every minute so rain is likely. I did it in old worn-out runners. Bring food and nutrition - no shops. Good luck and enjoy

For only $10 (10,000 KW) you can spend an afternoon wandering around a carefully manicured small park that exhibits outdoor glass work. As you walk in there is a place to watch professional glass blowers blow bottles in the traditional way, and if you are taking a school group there, the kids can have ago at making something, and then return the next day to pick up their handiwork. After that you follow the path around the exhibits until you get to the other end.In this mainly outdoor museum, there are glass plants, flowers, and an eclectic collection of glass made curiosities that make a very pleasant way to spend a couple of hours. There is a small cafe in the middle of the exhibition, and the gift shop just before you exit. The bathrooms are at the entrance exit, so go before you start!

For a start, if one is looking to purchase Innisfree products, it would probably be better to get them from their numerous stores on the island. Almost a quarter of the floor space here is set for people to try their hand at making (or shaping) Innisfree natural soap. The product selection is limited and they don't provide any free samples or special offers (like in their purpose built stores or counter in shopping malls). On the plus side, the store offer instant GST deduction for all items purchased here (min 30,000won).There is also a cafe here. But if one is looking for the famous Green Tea Latte or Green Tea ice cream and cake, those are only available from Ossulac Tea Museum Cafe next door.
Fish and chip shop with Aussie beers, wines and S. African Savanna cider :) Many other eateries nearby.

First thing we've noticed is how civilized this beach is - loads of restaurants, shops , cafes nearby. We were lucky enough to visit it in September, when holiday season is over for majority of Korean guys - so, it was not that crowded. Water was very clean and the only downside, that it was already a little bit cold. If you walk few hundred meters in a right hand direction from the main beach (towards the hill), you would see a camping ground with even smaller strip of sand - and we were absolutely alone there.

First of all, this place is huge.Formed through volcanic activity which resulted in 46 'small volcanoes' in the park itself. From what i saw, they ain't 'small'!There are a few entrances and trails. I took the Eulrimok Trail. It was pretty easy as compared to other mountains i hiked. First third, about 2.4km is quite difficult. Lots of stones and steps. Then it gradually became easier. The view is definitely awesome the moment you clear the forest area.There is a reststop at about 5km. Be sure to bring your own food. There is no cafe or shop there. The locals actually even cooked their own ramyeon by bringing them and hot water too. Some used the army-styled ration. There are no trash cans. You have to bring your trash back.You can take a public bus to this trail (gotta walk in opposite the bus stop. A good almoat 2km gentle upslope).Only bus 240 brings hikers here. You might want to check.Reminder, it is super cold in winter.

First  there is nothing worth seeing in this place. The exhibits were not even interesting-think chocolates shaped after teddy bears and placed in display cabinets. Their ultimate objective is to lure you to their shop which sells chocolate that....can be bought all over Jeju island. They don't even make their own chocolate.Second  they are liars. The saleswoman introduced the jeju orange chocolates to me  gave me a sample to try and recommended the   best   tasting brand. I tried it and i did like it. She recommended getting the set of 5 small boxes (each box containing 8 pieces of chocolates) because it was more worth it than the bigger box which was going for the same price but had 2 pieces less. I bought the set of 5 small boxes. When I got back  i tried the chocolates. Guess what? They tasted like cheap imitation chocolates. Nothing like the sample she gave me. Worse  each box only had a MAXIMUM<- note  of 6 pieces of chocolates. In addition  the saleswoman had such a bad attitude after I said i would only get one set of 5 small boxes. This place is totally not worth the trip. You can get better chocolates even at the airport  at a cheaper price. Don't waste your time and money.?룷?렆

Fairly small place for a hefty KRW10,000 entrance fee; the most expensive Jeju attraction. Features 2 galleries of teddy bears from various countries and themes and a teddy souvenir shop.  Will appeal to ladies, children and couples keen on photo snaps with huggable teddies, especially the human-sized ones at the corner of each floor and in the gift shop. Be prepared to jostle with crowds on a busy day.  There is a 5 minute T-Elvis performance held at every 15 minute interval in the Elvis Presley theatre.  Can skip if you're not a teddy lover or been here before as exhibits hardly change.

Everything about our favourite bear and its history. The museum has 3 floors, where you can see many different displays of teddy bears and animatronics, in a different setting. One floor is for displaying teddies from different times, another one shows teddy related artworks and finally there's a floor where you find a souvenir shop and some cafes. In the outside park you can view Jungmun sea while seeing human-sized teddy sculptures. The whole surrounding area is beautiful. Ideal for friends, couples and families as well!

Eorimok trail ends at Witse Oreum, at about 1700m up Hallasan. From carpark to the hut and back, including half an hour for noodles at the top is close to 4.5 hours. This includes photo times. Like everything on Jeju, this is a tourist walk, for pretty much anyone who can put one foot in front of the other up a very well marked or board-walked track. That notwithstanding, the walk is pleasant and the area itself is nice. In early Feb you will still likely have snow (we had snow from carpark to hut) and will require some small walking crampons to ensure grip. These are 5000W from the small shop at the carpark, beside the toilets and are pretty good actually. If you have some full mountaineering fangs it would almost be worth taking them for a laugh. We were the only westerners on the trail from perhaps 3-400 people and it would have only added to everyone's curiosity. Taxi from Jeju city will set you back about 20 000W and you can easily get a cab from the carpark taxi stand for your return trip. Hallasan is definitely the best, and some would say only real, attraction on Jeju and if you have half a day, then this is the track for you.

Entry for family of two adults and two kids under (3 and 1): $28. We were done with the museum in about 15 mins. The best part of the museum is the tea shop in the basement. Unless you have a strange obsession with teddy bears, save your money!

Entrance is pretty expensive (9500??), but you get a comprehensive history of teddy bears. You can't really find that anywhere else,  I suppose. And some exhibits were moving. The gift shop stuffs were pretty darn expensive, the cheapest teddy was a small keychain teddy at 9500??. Highlight of the visit was the Teddy Elvis show at level 2. That was pretty cool. I also liked how there was a whole section dedicated to Pooh bear.

Eco land has big landscape. Inside there are 4 trains station. A small train that drops people in all station, after reaching a station, people can look around and get into next train. One part is good for children, since there are kids house, kids coffee shop(miniature), fire station (miniature), bank(miniature), movie theatre(miniature) . This whole place is good for natural lovers, people in all ages, Photographers and videographer. Near this place, miniature park, Sangumburi Crater  and stone land are there. All these 3 places can be seen in one day.   So book a taxi for these 3 places.  My Taxi driver charged me 90,000 KRW for 11 AM to 6 PM.  Bus doesn't come frequently to these places. Usually if you taxi for using between 9 AM to 5 PM, you will have to pay 120,000 KRW.
Easy visit - gps to car park, down steps and the rock's there.   Its pretty enough for a quick visit.  Some shops, snack places in the area.  Parking was free for a short stay

Easily accessible via 15min ferry from Jeju Seongsanpo harbour, Udo is ideal for a short day trip or sorta those places in Korean dramas whereby couples miss the last ferry and have to wing it for the night). Anyways we made sure to check the ferry schedule. We had 2 hours and decided to walk instead of renting motorised vehicles (didn't have IDL), bicycles (too hot) or tourist hop-on-hop-off bus (too rushed). Other than tourists nearly running down pedestrians and into other vehicles, it's a nice place to explore & hike for nature lovers. Ferry return is a little pricey at ??8500 but should be ok if staying over. We tried the peanut icecream but didn't think it was that great. Basically vanilla soft serve with sprinkled peanuts. Perhaps the wrong shop.

During my travel to Jeju on the second day I decided to relax a bit and to visit aqua planet next to sunrise pick. As most of the main attraction on Jeju island it is very clean and well organised with food court gif shop and smilling staff. I have paid 39500 won but if you understand Korean there is site where you can get discounted tariffs. The visit is in 3 part the aquariums the science part and the theatre. The science part wasn't much. the aquariums are huge and the main one has a   screen   8 m high by 15 m long it is like a giant tv screen where you see lot of different fishes. The Theatre has representation about 3 or 4 times a day which last 45 minutes. 30 minutes with swimmers and 20 minutes with dolphins and seals. Overall it was a good experience very good if you have kids. Bear in mind that apart from a few writing in English everything is in Korean.I went on Sunday morning and it was pretty busy with lots of kids... but beareable. I recommend after the visit that should take about 2 h to exit towards the seaside and walk along the coast to the light house and the church. There is also the Zippo museum along the way.
