review: Dongmun wet and dry market show lots of fish and seafood. One shop inside provides local korean food even Running man visited before. Jeji mandarin can be purchased by box. Small souvenirs are sold. If you want local experience, 2 to 3 hours walk can be arranged.

dongmun si chang is a place for traditional item shopping. They sell seafood, fruits, chocolate souvenirs, meat and vege. I have no idea about the pricing as i didn't ask much. Just manage to get some orange chocolate as souvenirs because it close at 8pm korea time. Then i visit Junggak underground shopping centre which will close at 10pm.

Dongmun market is a must visit in Jeju. Its a market where you can get almost any local products here. In the AM, there are plenty of shops selling dry food supplies, fruits, seafood, local snacks and few small restaurants. At night, you can grab some local food here at the stalls. Prices at the stalls are quite standard, ranging from KRW1000. We tried few food here which was good.

Do not bother spending your time going here unless there is some specific item or shopping you need to do. Come on, you are on Jeju, a small slice of paradise on Earth, go see funny statues or climb a mountain.

Dived back to those nostalgic childhood moments when teddy bears once played as friends in your life. This Teddy Bear Museum has a wide array of collection of teddy bears, dressed beautifully in different costumes. The most popular bear will probably be the one dressed in Louis Vuitton clothes.What particularly caught my attention was the exhibition which actually used famous paintings such as the Mona Lisa, and the Teddy Bear was dressed to depict her. A creative way to carry out this exhibition. However, those expect to see a wide range of   depiction  .Overall, I felt that this was only an average stop-over, but will be good for families traveling with their young children. There's a souvenir shop on site too, where I'll be expecting young children to be bugging their parents to get them a teddy bear each!

Disclaimer: Everyone has their own tastes, and just because I may not like something, it doesn't mean you won't like it. And even though I might be dismissive and even sarcastic about this attraction, I am not attempting to insult anyone who thought that Jeju's   Mysterious Road   was fun. The fact is, this road would be amazing IF it wasn't swarming with tourists and IF you just happened to find it one day when you were driving around on the stunning back roads of Jeju. Jeju has Korea's best scenic driving, hands down. But this...Here's the deal. Yes, your brain will lie to you about the incline of this road and it will appear as if you are not rolling downhill, which you are. And that's a fun fact about human neurology and perception. My brain also tried to lie to me in order to convince me that the illusion was worth the large, obnoxious crowds of people that clogged the road, the busloads of hyperactive tourists on a conveyor belt from the airport, and the shops set up on either side of the road in order to overcharge them for very average products. Basically, it's a tourist trap. Sure, it has its appeal, but of all the things you could do on Jeju, why would you spend your time doing this?

Despite the temperature being around 17 degrees Celsius Springtime end of March, we were nearly blown away the minute we got out of our car. It was super windy & cold at the base! Had to put on extra layers, wind breakers etc. However the climb up is via long, steep stairs (my nemesis!!) so had to take off some layers halfway as I wheezed & panted my way up! View from top was just okay, wasn't as green as the photos we saw. Maybe because it was early spring. On the way down, we took a detour to the Diving Women's museum / hut / restaurant just by the rocky beach. Owing to the weather, no diving woman worth her salt, was going to do a performance in the sea. We had to contend with a couple of squirmy sea creatures in tanks, which the diving women chopped up with precision & served to us with soya sauce. The abalone, octopus & shell-fish were as fresh as you could get and tough as erasers. But we did it more for the experience than the cuisine or taste. You can pick up more tasty fare at the shops near the carpark if you're hungry.

Definitely the most fun I have in the island. Not that I didn't have fun in other attractions however I just love how everything they got in this attraction is an interactive one. I have the chance to watch GD's hologram concert as well here, they have one hologram concert every one hour. It's fun! Oh, and if you're a VIP this place is a must visit. Their gift shop offers some selection of VIP merchandises, from Krunk, snapback hats and VIP's light stick.The entry ticket is 15.000 won if I'm not wrong, but it is definitely worth every bucks you spend. There's a dancing room, a 360 degree 3D experience, you can even take pictures with your favorite Kpoppers using their hologram tech.
Cool Place, great mountain rock formation. Ilchulbong Peak is an hour travel via InterCity Bus #701 from Jeju City Hall cost around 2,050won. There are eateries and souvenir shops nearby.

Communication barrier is not a problem for us to shop here. Yes, they don't really speak English. But, we still had a good time to shop and bargain. If you want to shop korean fashion (but not the designer label or branded one), clothing, accessories, bags, cosmetic, skin care, this is the place. One place for everything so that you don't have to walk more. Innisfree, Nature Republic, The Saem, Skin Food, you name it. All are here.

Close to dongmun market - could ask for direction from nearby local shops. I took a look at menu of two restaurants and they are quite the same regarding price and menu options (set price for 2 is around 50k won). i must admit that although taste of black pork is more delicious, it is not exceptional if considering the price nearly double normal porks

Circumnavigated this little island on a bike in an afternoon, and it was a lovely excursion. The older culture is still somewhat alive (weeding through the tourist stops), but even the bitsy coffee shops are endearing. Bicycle is the way to see this place, for sure!

Came here after lunch nearby , ample parking space , restaurant, cafe , beauty shops near the parking area . Need to buy tickets to enter , it was a cold & windy day . No haenyo show on that day , the view was breathtaking. Huffing & puffing all the way up the stairs .

Came here after having our dinner nearby , stroll along this underground shopping which was not that long , bought some Korean brand cosmetic here that's all, not crowded , free filter water with paper cups for drinks , clean toilet to use , heated on a cold weather . If it's raining outside would be nice to spend some time here .

Built on a reclaimed land-fill site, this vast area of pathways, statues, displays, museums and traditional villages is very worth a visit if on Jeju. From the impressive stone structures and flat basalt 'floor' at the entrance of the park, I was blown away by the vast array of statues that are displayed, explained and on show in this area. There is ample car parking that is only a short walk form the entry way. A small fee is required and then you are free to wander the area that included a massive and spectacular 2 store (below ground) museum that outlines the geographic development of Jeju along with many interactive displays, a short film with subtitles, examples and galleries of 'stone art'. A gift shop of course, provided a range of traditional and specific items and there are amenities spread throughout the part. Water features, a traditional village, an art gallery and a vast array of stone sculpture will give you hours of things to view and read as you wander through the park In my humble opinion, not to be missed!!!

Brought by our taxi driver/guide to this place since it was were the Korean drama Jewel in the Palace was filmed supposedly. The lady owner gave us a tour of her property with the pigpen where we saw the famous Jeju black pig, the old kitchen and the living/bedroom quarters which was all good but at the end she brought us to a room where we sampled the nice tea and the sales talk began. It was uncomfortable since we specifically told our driver that we don't want to go to any shopping place. Another thing I didn't know that we were supposed to give a donation for the tour and I'm not sure if the 5 dollars I gave for 2 people was enough.
Breathtaking view. Very breezy at the summit. It takes a bit of exercise, but not too difficult to climb. Well surrounded by cafe, restaurants and shops. Toilets are quite clean.
Blowholes were small as compared to New Zealand?s Pancake rocks. But view is beautiful, a small park outside with shops around. Many attractions like Teddy bear museum are just a walking distance.
Black Pork Street! Every shop sells black port, one person MUST get one portion. It's nice and smooth. Do not mixed the black pork with any other stuff else the taste is damaged.

Before you want to take a ferry to Udo island, please take note that you need to bring along your passport to purchase a ticket. You will be given 2 tickets, 1 for departure & 1 for arrival (you have to keep this and pass to the boatman at Udo when you want to return to main island). A tip is to get the korean map together with your language?s map because they have more details of the island as compared to other languages. The ferry comes every 15 minutes so you do not have to worry if you miss it. Inside the ferry, there are flooring with thermal and you have to take your shoes off before stepping into the resting platforms. Otherwise, you may choose to stand outside those rooms and there are some outdoor seats at the top of the ferry. Please also take note that there are 2 ports at Udo, so your ferry might stop at either one.Once you reach the island, you will be greeted by tons of shop assistants trying to get you to rent bikes to you. You will need an international driver license to be able to drive any motorise vehicles. Upon confirmation which is the vehicle you want, you have to leave your passport with the register counter. They will provide you with a map to go around the island. We were informed that the whole cycling trip takes an hour. However, here comes the challenging part. There were no proper division of the road for those driving trucks, buses, cars, motorcycles & bicycles. You can be riding your bicycle and have a full speed bus chasing behind you and pressing the horn at you. Cars and trucks from the opposite direction also travel at fast speed towards you, which we had to stop many times to give way to these fast moving vehicles. After getting to the first beach, which was really beautiful, the rest of the trip towards the next beach was tough as there were many upward slopes and split roads which have no proper signages to tell you which way to go. We had to go in to random houses and ask in broken korean for which way to go. However, when we reach the lighthouse area, we managed to locate Jimmy?s icecream shop as suggested by our Jeju driver. I tried the mandarin orange ice cream while my friend tried the apple mango ice cream. Everything tasted natural and yummy so I would recommend it to tourist who visit the place. However, from the road before this ice cream place onwards to the last 5 mins of the ride, it was all upwards riding.We took almost 3 hours to finish cycling around the whole island (We have done quite a few rides in Singapore so I don?t think we were slow in cycling around the island). So for those who have no license or feel that you?re not up to 2-3 hours of cycling, I would advise you to take the tour bus to get from places to places on the island.

Beautiful scenery at the top with breathtaking surrounding views of Jeju. Well maintained stairs, although uneven at first because they use the volcanic rocks, Many resting places as you go up. There is a lady at the top who explains the origins of the peak in English, which was a pleasant surprise. Large carpark area, fast food stores and souvenir shops.

Be prepared to climb a long flight of steps to reach the top. Once you are at the top, the view is breathtaking. I love the view and the climbing is worth all the effort. There are a lot of restaurants and shops below and you can catch live performance of women divers are the bottom at certain time.

Basically, this is a museum of teddy bears.Teddy bears are made in many shapes, sizes & images of many famous personalities or characters.As usual, there is a souvenir shop. And also a small theatre showing musical teddy bears singing & dancing eg to Elvis Presley songs.Probably the kids may enjoy it better.Frankly, it is quite boring. If time is tight, suggest give this place a miss & go to better attractions. You won't miss much not coming here.

Basically this place is formed when lava flows through the land on its way to the ocean. Understand that this cave (or tube)!is 6.4m long but only 1m is accessible as the rest are closed for various reasons. It?s about 11degrees at the deepest end so for those who are not used to this, please bring along your sweaters. Also the path is uneven and wet so don?t come in your shopping shoes. Otherwise it?s a very educational tour. Signages are posted at strategic points to explain the event. Oh yes. The steps down to the cave is very high so hold on to the railing tight or be very careful where you plant your feet.

Based on a Malaysian blogger's review, we went over to one of the shops there to savour this renown dish.It was a BAD experience, the black pork sold there tough like wild boar and did not have any distinct tastes.Later on when we met some locals, they advise that locals don't eat there, only tourist who are attracted by the hype of the place.Fortunately, there are many other shops around Jeju City which served better Black Pork., In fact, we had a very good one at Halla Pork Restaurant in nearby Sehwa-ri.

At the back or Osulloc Tea Museum is Innisfree house. This is a much more peaceful place to have a drink and small eats but unfortunately, we were not aware hence and our drinks at the Osulloc. But we had another drink here just because it was peaceful and we needed the calm. Is cute that we walked the 30 steps from Osulloc to Innisfree we see a sign that there are snakes... we would think with the amount of crowd and noise, the snakes would have been gone. Lol This place is about clean eating and is peaceful. Some light shopping and not crowded at all.

At Hallim park, there are a few lava caves that are interesting, and very cool (temperature).  The flower gardens are very nice.  The bonsai garden has trees that date to 300 years ago.  They are constantly trimmed to keep them small.  There is a restaurant at the entrance, and a rest area with a gift shop in the center of the park.

As with typical tourist attraction markets, you?ll find plenty of vendors hawking various wares....Food probably is the worst rip off considering prices.Only if you are time constrained should you make any purchases here; especially food, as the quality is very shoddy and expensive compared to local brick & mortar shops.

As lava caves go, this one is pretty good. It is approximately 2 kms long, wet, cold and dark although well lite for the tourists. Car parking is available and you can also take a local bus close to the area - you ned to walk the final distance. Payment is made at the booth prior to the entry stairs and from there the path is pretty well developed. Having visited many lava tunnels/caves in other countries, this one was basically what I expected but had its own unique sights. The path is rough and rocky in places and you need to wear sensible walking shoes and have a coat - visit in winter and you need o really rug up. Signage is both Korean and English and prior to the cave entry there is a selection of Korean restaurants and food shops. Some pretty park areas are also worth a look.

As its name, here is an idea to visit for Teddy Bear lovers and who interested in. Many zone that's quite interesting such as the first Winnie the Pooh, world's all time classic paintings x Teddy Bear, characters bear like Michael Jackson or Audrey Hepburn from Breakfast at Tiffany, and Steve Jobs. Entrance fees isn't cheap but still OK. For the exhibition of Bear dolls is good but for the shop, just soso nothing attractive.Parking available. Good for friends and family.

As a child I was a big Hello Kitty fan and thought it would be nice to visit this place, after seeing it at the airport. Getting here is really easy from the main bus terminal. I did not know what to expect when I got here. But when I got there I noticed it was $12,000 won to get in. But once you are inside there is nothing special about the place to be charging so much. Its just a bunch of halls with Hello Kitty pictures and some random facts. On the second floor there is a Cafe, that is also overpriced and over crowded. Almost impossible to get a good seat. Service is not great. They not only took forever to take my order, I was the only one in line, but also to give me what I had ordered. The gift shop is also an overpriced place with not a lot of options. Knowing what I know now I dont think I would have done this place.

As a big Hello Kitty fan, I was excited to visit Hello Kitty Island after hearing about it. Although the museum was quite fun, it was pretty run down with many of the exhibits being kind of dirty. The cafe in particular was not on par with the Hello Kitty cafes in Seoul. At those cafes, the cakes and drinks are very fresh but at Hello Kitty Island the cake we ordered tasted (and looked!) like it had been left on the shelf for a while. Similarly the gift shop didn't stock great souvenirs. Considering the price you pay to get in, I would have expected a bit more from this place. If you're a big Hello Kitty fan, I suggest one of the themed places in Seoul.

Armed with a Jeju Travel Guide map for cruise tourists, on 9 October we walked in the short distance from the Mariner of the Seas to Dongmun Market and the adjoining Jungang underground shopping street.Wandering through both of these sites provides the contrasting opportunity to encounter local culture with its unique produce, sights and smells  as well as standard internationally branded shopping in a bazaar environment.As a short term tourist visitors we 'soaked up' what we saw and, of course, the market with its variety from fruit, vegetables, meat, seafood and food stalls came out on top.It was a rewarding morning off the boat, very easy to undertake.

Another UNESCO World Heritage. It have a nice view from the top but you need to climb up the stairs. Perhaps is a good exercise.  :)  You may bring along the bottled water as it takes around 30 mins to the top. There have restaurants, coffee shops, food stalls, souvenir stalls at the bottom and free car park as well.

Amazing beachside for prewedding photos as there are this colorful chairs that are always available there as props. The beach was clean and there are cafes and the famous colorful candle gel gift shop. Great visit with family, couples or for photoshoots!

Although there are many small vendors and shops during the day, the best part is at night when the food stalls appear. There are many (mostly Korean) options. From burgers, to tempura and ice cream burritos, you will not go hungry! On average, the food costs around 7,000 krw per meal. Smaller items like gimbap and individual tempura is cheaper. I would not recommend this market for any type of clothing shopping. The interior is mainly dried fish, nuts, juices, souvenirs, some bbq, and a couple sit down restaurants.

Although I heard it is a best place for shopping in cheap price, but am found it bit expensive. Moreover, the condition should be improved for more visitor to come especially tourist from all over the world.

After Shopping in Chilsungro Shopping Streer. We go ahead here to find good and delicious food. There is a lot of choices. Fresh orange juice, grilled squids, pork and chickens. A lot pf variety of good food.

After reading quite a few reviews on lHallasan trails, I finally decided to have a go at it. I left early to start the hike on Gwaneumsa just before 7.00am. I actually got there by taxi from sunrise peak, seongsan as there is no bus arriving there. It costed me 35000won. On arrival, the place was deserted, so I started my walk. The first part is throught the forest so you don't get to see any scenery. Once you reach the last shelter then it opens up and the view is amazing. From there you have still a good climb to the top (the thoughest part actually). On the top you can see the crater and if it has been raining the lake inside. I went down the second trails called seongpanak which is said to be easier. This one is a bit boring in regards to scenery because you are always in the forest.All in all it took me 6h45 to get to the top and back which is around 18km. The up trail is pretty challenging and I would recommend people the be quite fit to take it the down trails is a challenge to your ankles and knees as the path is covered in huge stone so be careful not the twist anything. On the up trails you will find a water spring almost at the top, no food and no other water poitn apart from that. On the down trail the is a shelter serving pot noodle. On arriving down at seongpanak there was a few taxi waiting so I managed to get back to the hotel. There is also a shop that sells drink, food and rent shoes.My reco is to start early in the morning to avoid too many people. Get plenty of water (I got 1l and it wasn't enough). Good shoes are a must. And one moto : slowly but surly! Don't rush it as you will suffer on the way down. Appreciate the trail. Be careful though that at 12h30 they will stop you at the shelter from gwaneumsa so you need to go pass this before and you need to leave the top before 14h to make it down before closing time. I really enjoyed it as a challenge 1300m climb from 650m to 1950m.

Actually like the other ones, I felt quite surprise at the my first visits since last year 2011. The guide showed me that I were in the bottom of the slope, she pointed to the tree lines along  the side of the road and truly, it has made me believe what she said. A few seconds later, the driver shut the engine and release the bus's brakes, the 45 seated bus was beginning move slowly then faster and faster.  Could you believe ? The huge bus was moving up to the top of the slope without working engine! A man of my group - an 50 ages supposed there were the natural magnetic power that dragged up the 2,5 tons iron bus to about 5-8 meter height during approximately 80 metes !!!It was happened about 10 mins then all of our group's participant disembarked the bus, they were starting to talk about what they saw during the past 10 minutes. Some one said it caused by a natural magnetic power (as above), other one assumed by the trick of the sun's lighting a man nearly lying face down to the road parallel to look forward to the starting point... others wisely poured the water to see the flows .... Of course, our guide has explained the cause but I really do not want to tell you, let's explore by yourself.Definitely, this places is quite appropriated for your family with kids. Aside the road, there are the Korean traditional food shops who sells fried fish ball, rice cake... but they are almost fried into the oil ...This places are really attracted a lot of people from Asia like Chinese, Vietnamese, Indian... I think you might found the similar road like the Jeju Mysterious Road of your own country but the Korean was wise to promote it via the drama film series currently expanding over the Asia.Totally, Jeju is an beautiful island and you should visit one time. With me, I could said   you could make the money by the very simple things

Absolutely hike Oedolgae, it's a beautiful coastal walk that is part of an Olle trail. You wind all around a part of the southern coast of Jeju, and can walk as long as you please. Lots of shops and restaurants along the way. The Jeju trails are my favorite attraction on Jeju, definitely walk one! And they're free!
absolutely beautiful cliffs, great views of lava cliffs. a must see for anyone traveling to Jeju Island!only quirk is the small shops selling touristy things.

A volcanic rock that looks like a dragon head looking up the sky,  NATURAL surrounding with lots of volcanic rocks formed by molten lava creating a scenic and spectacular view.  You can walk carefully along the volcanic rock to go as close to the dragon formation as you can for better photography.   Different time of the day, different view against the Sky. This place is beautiful , windy and cold even in spring.  No entrance fee! There is a man made mermaid, and 2 man made stone guardians of the land  There are 2 souvenir shops, grilled cuttlefish shop , ice cream and fruit stalls depending very much on tourists.  The Jeju airport is nearby and if you have the time, can count the planes landing and taking off at a busy airport.  Further away, there are motel and seafood restaurants.    We like the tasty green abalone porridge and the fresh and tasty seafood soup.All in all , I like this tourist place very much, I like earth natural formation very much.

A unique theme park to visit. Just love the colorful displays of glass.  This theme park has an outdoor and indoor displays of everything made in glass.  What really caught my attention was the many shoes made in glass (for Cinderella). They are just so beautiful, makes me remember the Cinderella story all over again! Indoor displays are the many works of art made in glasses, so eye-pleasing too!.  They have workshops where you can make your own piece of glass art. Kids are welcome to join the workshops too.

A traditional market which sells a lot of Jeju Oranges, jeju chocolates, seafoods (e.g. Fish, abalone, etc), pork, orange juices and many more.. the price of the chocolates is the same as any other stores outside. The price of the other products are also reasonable.You can visit this market and have a feel of their largest traditional market in Jeju. I went there with my friend before 8pm but some of the stores had started cleaning and preparing to close the shop. The market is open till 9pm (if I am not wrong).

A traditional market situated in Jeju City that gives you a real and authentic taste of the local lifestyle in Jeju. It sells a wide range of local produce and goods. Buy all your local souvenirs such as hallabong orange, jeju chocolates and snacks here! The shopkeepers will toss in freebies (they call it   service  ) as well! It is near the black pork street which is also worth the visit.

A 'must see' place when visiting the island. Lots of small shops around the entrance, a small fee (free if you work on the island), lots of stairs (a fairly tough climb) that lead to a variety of small temples and places to check out. Views are fantastic and on a clear day even better. You can get their by local bus although there is car parking but no 'wheel' access for baby strollers or wheelchairs. The golden Buddha and the drums give you an amazing feeling sitting so high above the surrounding area. Definitely worth it.

A must for visitors tot he island. An area of beauty, amazing geographical formations, haenyeo (diving women), shops and foods. A very steep climb to the top but the steps are well developed and there are small seats along the climb to take a break. Great views fro the top, but if the day is windy be prepared for some discomfort. Take a water bottle, camera and coat! Worth every step!

A museum showcases a huge collection of Teddy Bears with various themes and events.Kids will definitely love this place and if you are a Teddy Bear fan, then never miss it.They have maintained a beautiful garden outside the museum, while there is also a Caf챕 and a Souvenir shop.My younger daughter enjoyed every bit of it.
A museum for adults only. There were unusual art designs of male and female organs. There is also a shop inside where you can buy   for adults   stuff.

A hike to the top is quite challenging especially for the elderly and family with young children as there are heaps of steps. Make sure to bring something to hydrate you as there were no drinking fountains available on your way to the top. Enjoy the views of the sea and cityscape once you're at the top. Also, there are a number of restaurants, coffee shops and food stalls at the bottom of the peak.

A good place to go shopping and grab something to eat. You can find from cheap street food to fine dining Jeju traditional restaurant! Also, if you are a fruit lover like me, you can find all kinds of fruits in a reasonable price!
A fun beach, with lots of shallows for swimming and playing in the water.  The park is well kept, there are great coffee shops and restaurants. A very nice sandy beach which is hard to find in Jeju.

A cute and cuddly experience at the Teddy Bear museum, this place is for kids and adults alike. It has an impressive collection of impressionistic teddy bears, from the 19th century to the major icons of today; a teddy bear version of Madame Tussaud's. Then there is a peaceful garden walk which is also adorned with teddy bear statues. The gift shop is irresistible, too.

A bit difficult to find, but a gorgeous location.   The waterfall flows into a small pool and then flows into the sea.  It was pretty crowded when we went, but still worth going.  The rocks are SLIPPERY.  Be careful when moving around on them as we saw a few people fall.  There are a few shops selling snacks and Jeju treats at the top and a proper coffee shop as well.

A beautiful view on top of Seongsan IIchulbong. Plenty of parking. We did this twice in the same day. The first hike (approximately 30 minutes to get to the top, started at 1pm) was extremely foggy and we couldn't see anything. We hiked back down and spent some time on the shore. Once the sun came out we hiked back to the top. There are several stops on the way with spectacular views of Jeju. You can purchase drinks and trinkets from one small shop about half way up. Use the restroom before going up as there is not one on the way. For a family of three to include a 10 year old we took one large bottle of water and a small backpack with some snacks and additional items. Bring a camera as it is absolutely beautiful. On the way we saw several different species of birds and spiders. At the top there are several benches where you can sit and enjoy the view. At the bottom there is a Mcdonalds, an ice cream shop, a souvenir shop, and other small shops. I suggest you try the orange ice drinks...they are great! Overall cost, 5,000 won for two adults and one child. We paid cash. Enjoy!

2000krw entry.    Just beyond the ticket booth are pictures and descriptions of some of the highlights of the area along with bathroom facilities.    Further on, are some small shops and food stalls.      It?s a beautiful walk with lovely plants to get to the waterfall.   There are supposed to be 2 meter long, 20 kilo eels in the pool by the waterfall.   We couldn?t see any.    Waterfall was nice but nothing particularly special.

10,000won per adult. Two floors of teddy bears gallery. I was quite fascinated by the really old teddy bears. The Louis Vitton Teddy bear was also on display, which apparently went for $190,000 during a fund raising charity event. Saw Elvis bear, Marilyn Monroe bear, Steve Job bear etc. There is a massive gift shop at ground level, selling a variety of teddy bears. But quite overpriced 10,000won for a key chain teddy, 35,000won for a palm size teddy. I don't even dare to look at how much the larger bear cost.

10,000 KRW per person. When you enter, pay for admission, and start in third floor, go down floors in order. In the basement, theres gift shop, cafe, and theres few more exhibits to see. Perfect for kids, fun for adults. Wish there could be more exhibitions of teddy bears. But if was nice!

- Jeju is also known for it's high quality green tea. you can view the teddy bears from different countries,enjoy yourself at the museum shop, caf챕, restaurant or the outdoor park where you can view the spectacular Jungmun Sea. At the museum garden, you can meet the teddy bear sculptures and models. The garden decorated with various themes such as the Korean Black bear family and the magical pond. Children under are free. Lots of free parking.

You can see teddy bears in a lot of human like professions and daily situations. They are really beautifully made.It's really attractive, so go for it when you have plenty of time.I was there in 2011.

You can reach this place with Jeju tour bus - if you're going to the Roe Deer Observatory as well, I suggest you go there first and then walk downhill to the Peace Park (less than 10 mins). If you do it the other way round, you'll have to trek uphill. The admission for the Peace Park is free and everything is in English. The museum offers a comprehensive account of a controversial point in Korean history: some exhibits are quite chilling and upsetting but I think it's important to understand the history of this island: Jeju is not all about tangerines, erotic statues and kitschy teddy bears.

You can find all kinds of teddy bears in the museum and the   cosplay  is simply amazing. I was impressed by how creative they are. There is a garden behind the museum for which you can have a short walk with a couple of photos.

You can discover your favourite teddy or safari animal here. With 3 floors of huggable and adorable animals there is much posing, hugging and choosing. You can even get a teddy to propose marriage to you.Teseum should not be confused with Teddy Bear Museum located in Seogwipo (near Alive Museum), a more 'serious' museum.

Worth paying for. There are so many teddies in various costumes and postures. There are elvis, the paddington bear, bear at the markets. For those who loves teddy bears, you can also see the evolution of teddy bears . My personal favourite is the teddy bears as featured in Princess Hours and also few diorama of korean culture; the women's diver, korean traditional wedding. Dont forget to take the picture at the park too! My take on the souveniers, as expected is a bit pricey, but if you want to have a momento, maybe you should buy the postcards.

Whilst I'm giving the Teddy Bear Museum just 2 stars for quality, value for money, class of exhibits, and any actual worth as a proper   museum  , I have to admit that my visit made me laugh. I'm not sure though that derisive snorting sarcasm was what they were looking for.This museum is a pile of pants, masquerading as teddy bears.. The   attractions   are about 15 to 20 poor quality adult-human-sized bears, dressed in various outfits of clothing, with a challenge to guess   who   they are dressed as. Military uniform and two medals apparently is enough for a bear to resemble Prince William, for example - and a grey wig and   E=mc2   to represent Einstein.Then there are the bear portraits. Frames containing bears dressed to vaguely resemble famous portraits. Mona Lisa teddy bear, anyone?There's no   history   of the teddy bear, no collection of historical bears, no pictures / video clips of teddy bears being made, no maps showing where different types of teddy bears originated from - nothing educational whatsoever. There are no audio tours, no leaflets or signs to show the visitor around, and certainly no staff available to talk to about any   exhibits  , whether you are Korean, English, American or anything else.The gift shop on the lowest floor contained the largest number of bears - none of them particularly special, all just your usual cheap mass-produced bears, but at slightly hiked up prices.By far the worst part of the visit was the funniest. Your ticket includes entry to the   Elvis Stage Show  . Oh dear Lord, where on earth do I start? The show is on every 15 minutes. In a room with about 12 benches in it. There is a curtain at the far end, hiding the   stage  . On the quarter hour, the announcement is made -   The King of Rock and Roll, Elvis, is in the house!   The curtains open, and there it is. The Elvis Presley Show. Six, sad, lonely looking teddy bears, dressed in stage show outfits, rocking gently on their animatronic sticks. The three backing singers sway gently on the right, the drummer's arms flail up and down towards the drums, the guitarist's arm moves.Elvis meanwhile gyrate and swivels his hips, the crowd goes wild. Oh, no, sorry, that last sentence was a lie. Elvis sways and looks like he almost falls several times.Worst animatronic puppetry in the world. Hilarious. Hilariously BAD. Less than two minutes later, the curtains shut, and   Elvis has left the building   - until the next showing in approximately 12 or 13 minutes' time....Don't go to the Teddy Bear Museum thinking you'll have an interesting visit. Go to see the absolutely bizarre vision that South Koreans have of   entertainment  .

While searching online, it says that the museum is closed, but turns out it is still open! Everything was fantastic about the museum because we love teddy bears, but the huge teddy outside of the museum could not perform because of bad weather. It can also get pretty warm and stuffy indoors during autumn and winter since the heater is switched on and there was barely any air ventilation as well. The store has a lot of teddies for sale as well.

When I first heard about the Teddy Bear museum, I said, Really?  Well, it was interesting, and I suppose if you had young children, the kids would love it.  I don't have a need to visit that museum ever again.  If you're a teddy bear lover than this is the museum for you.  While visiting, I did learn something new.  The teddy bear is named after Teddy Roosevelt.

Went there with my friend, we took bus from Jungmun (at the bus stop nearby tourist information center, at the right hand side). We took bus no. 781 and alighted at Teddy valley golf and resort, from there turn left (after you alighted) and walk straight for 1 min, you will see the museum at your left hand side. The entrance ticket cost 12000 won per adult. There are gift shop, Kitty History Hall, Music Education Hall, Art Gallery, Hello Kitty Caf챕, 3D Theater and more.. The Hello Kitty Cafe is very big and is beautifully designed and decorated.. There are a lot of cute hello kitty inside the museum and there are also some outside the museum. If you are a hello kitty fan, this is a must visit place when you come to Jeju.The museum closes at 6pm, so you might want to go there earlier.

Went there on 25th Dec 2017. I thought the museum will make me amazed by having a written history about how they created a teddy bear doll from scratch. But then, it wasn't really a museum. It should be called Teddy Bear Collection. It only consist of lots of teddy bear from small size to giant size with different clothes on. That is all.

Went in Feb 14. Admission fee: 9000 won eachIt is located near to Alive Museum and Believe it or Not Musuem. The Seogwipo tourist center is also nearby.The whole touring of the museum took us about 1hr. It was quite small but filled with loads and loads of teddy!Worth a visit if you love teddy bears, else you can forget about going there since the admission fee is not that cheap.

Well, if you like teddy bears, drop by this place to see their collection.  Honestly, I get more excited browsing teddy bears at a departmental store.  This place is probably losing its charm as it is mainly visited by tourists sent here by tour buses and very little koreans or free-n-easy tourists.

Welcome to the first Teddy Bear Museum in Korea. Here you will find everything you want to know about Teddy Bears. Teddy Bears have been loved and cherished since they were first introduced over 100 years ago. There are now millions of people who collect Teddy Bears. They seek out old, unique and valuable teddy bears for their personal collections. Our Teddy Bear Museum opened especially for the European collectors. The Teddy Bear Museum is more exciting than ever with   Teddy Bear   entertainment as never seen before. Jeju Teddy Bear Museum opened on April 24, 2001. It contains two galleries, a museum gift shop, and a museum cafe. Also, on site is a museum bar/restaurant, a wonderful place to meet friends, family, and lovers. From the outside garden, there is a view of Jung-Mun Beach.

We would have never imagined that you can make so much out of a teddy bear. We thoroughly enjoyed the experience and I would suggest it for any bear lover but especially for families with young kids. As for the Alive Museum, I would strongly advice to go there either in the morning or early in the afternoon. We visited it in the morning and it was a bliss, but my guts' feeling tells me the crowds in the afternoon must be a little bit more stressful to deal with.PS: Don't forget the Elvis Presley Show. Yes, it is kind of tacky but really cute anyway!
We will meet, hug, touch, take picture or even kiss the teddy bears. Cute background for taking picture.

We went with friends to visit the museam and for all of us it was quite entertaining. Really nice recreation of historial moments and famous personalities   Teddy Bear Style  .Since I am a big fan of k drama Goong / Princess Hours, for me it was a must to visit the Museum and I was not dissapointed at all. There is an specific exhibition of this drama and it is amazing, showing the most memorable scenes as seen on TV and also there is a music video. Loved it.Finally, don't miss   Teddy Bear Elvis Music Show  .

We went to the Teddy Bear Museum only because it was right next door to the Lotte Hotel Jeju where we stayed.  At 10,000 won per adult and 8,000 won per child, it is a bit pricey.  You can be done with all the displays and the 5 minute teddy Elvis show in an hour.  If you like teddy bears then it is a museum for you as there are alot of cute displays and exhibits that memorialize past events in history.  Kinda cool but not my thing.  I enjoyed the outdoor park area more.  You can take pictures with cute bear statues and sit and enjoy the greenery.  There is a cafe that sells Taiwanese pearl drinks and a nice gift shop.

We went in, looked around the first 5 minutes and then left. I like teddy bears, I'm actually a bit of a big kid, but this was all a bit boring. Lots and lots of bears dressed in little outfits. Maybe good if it's raining but if the sun is shining outside I'd advise you to try other things. It was crowded too, so you couldn't easily see the displays anyway.

We visited this just because it was rainy, and realized that it would be great to visit otherwise.  It was interesting because of the theme-based teddy bears in thousands, spread across 3 floors.  Loved the Gandhi bear, Times square scene, Mother teresa bears, Charlie Chaplin bears, most expensive teddy bears (Louis Vuitton) and so on.Do visit if you can fit it in your schedule!

We visited the museum a bit reluctantly and only because we had dragged our two children (10 and 15) round two scenic waterfalls and an archery practice place in the hours before. Our youngest daughter was definitely keen to do something that she chose. When we got there our suspicions seemed to be confirmed with a relatively high entrance fee (I think it was 6,000 won per adult) for what seemed to be a small place.However, once we got into the diorama room, both kids couldn't stop themselves from oohing and aahing the whole time. You really felt that somebody had fun putting it all together. It was in all the little touches (like adding little German flags to the 'storming of the Berlin wall' display) and the set ups such as the 'Bearacotta Army). As previous reviewers have mentioned, all of these are in glass cases so my husband (who is a very keen photographer with decent equipment) didn't deign to take any photos - our teenage daughter took over instead. Having just completed our photobook, I can only say that we had plenty of good shots, I could easily have filled 20 rather than 4 pages with good shots.We didn't miss any English explanations - the teddies really spoke for themselves. We also didn't approach it as a museum but rather as a fun place to look around. The re-enactments of historical events from the 20th century were also fairly self-explanatory.The shop was probably the only really boring bit since the selection was not particularly big and the prices, given the location, quite high.Overall, don't go if you want to learn anything about teddy bears but do go in with kids (or adults who appreciate the cuteness).

We visited in the Teddy Bear Museum in Jeju around late Nov 2017, and it was quite empty when we visited.  The entry charges was pricey considering the only activity was to look at teddy bears in glass casings.  The glass casings made it difficult to take nice photos, as there were lots of reflections.  However, the kids enjoyed the place very much.  There is also an outdoor area (don't miss it, very nice place to take photos).  Overall, an above-average place to visit, but it is indoors so if the weather is bad, this is a place you can drop by.

We took ride on bus no. 282 from Arang Joeul Street to visit Teddy Bear Museum jeju which is nearby to Jungmun  tourist resort. Bus fare cost us only KRW 1150 per pax. The visit to Teddy bear museum was fantastic especially for my sister, teddy bear lover. It was amazing to see many collection of teddy bears from all over the world with different themes and events globally.  There were three sections of the teddy bear museum; starting from the history, artwork and forest of teddy bear. There was a garden outside of the museum with the construction of enormous teddy bear. We can get a glimpse of the LV and Swarvosky teddy bear. The most nostalgic teddy bear was the Princess Hour theme teddy bear. The most great thing to watch was the Elvis Presley show. However, the teddy bear sold there was expensive. It was worth to visit this place.

We stopped at Jungmun tourist complex to visit teddy bear museum by taking bus no. 282 from Arang Joeul Street in Seogwipo.  It was 6 minutes walk to Cheonjeyeon waterfall. Do not confuse this waterfall with Cheonjiyeon waterfall. The admission fee was KRW2,000 per pax. You can kill two birds with one stone. You get to see two attractions the famous Seonimgyo bridge with seven nymphs carves (fairy bridge) and the three-tiered waterfall. We did not go for the third waterfall as the trail was quite steep. We only went to the pond of fairy and the second waterfall.

We stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal and took bus 110 from Jungang Rotary bus stop to Jungmun Tourist Complex. The bus journey about 30 minutes and cost less than 2000won one way. The bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly (Although I did not see Jungmun Tourist Complex on the TV screen, therefore I used GPS to locate instead. You can press the bell to alight. For my other bus trip, the stops were announced correctly and was reliable). We actually stopped that Jungmun Tourist Complex to go the the Teddy bear museum and Cheonjeyeon Falls before proceeding to the beach. Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. We needed to change bus 702 (opposite the tourist infrmation counter) to Hyeojae beach. It cost 3300 won. The journey on the bus we great as you will pass by paddy field, wind mills and wild flower fields. You will see a beautiful beach 1st ( I think it is Geumneung Beach) but don?t get down, get down at Hyeopjae beach as the view is nicer (about 2 stops away). You can walk down the stretch later (There is a public toilet down the stretch if you need). The weather then (April 26) was 12 to 17 degree Celcius and remember to buy a jacket and windbreaker as it was very windy when we were there. We so blessed that the sky cleared up to reveal one of the most beautiful turquoise beaches I have been. The beach was wide and the colours of the water clear and blue. There are many caf챕 where you can buy a hot drink from. Noted that the caf챕 only allow you to use the toilet if you buy a drink (the receipt will print the password to get into the toilet). You can always use the public toilet. We decide to walk along the orange and blue ribbon trail (Jeju Olle Route 14) and it was one of the best trail for me. We complete only part of the the trail where we walk through the villages to the fishing port. The route will bring you to a serene path with light house and the wind mills. The the path became rocky nearing the windmills, and we decided to walk out through the rocky back alley of a shellfish place (away from the orange/blue ribbon) and landed at a bus stop. We took bus 702 back to seogwipo. It was a must go beach but only on a clear blue day where the magnificent of the beach will show up.

We had an afternoon to kill and it was too hot for any outdoor activity so we decided to visit the museum. It had a fairly interesting display of teddy bears - displayed by era and themes. Highlight was the most expensive teddy bear in the world - the Louis Vutton teddy bear. If you had limited time on Jeju, this is not a must-see, but I'd like us you had an extra day, then, this is worth going on a hot or rainy day.

We found this museum in our travel guide and it sounded fun to visit. However, it was quite disappointing starting with the price which was much more expensive than all other museums. It only had a few rooms with teddy bear representations that got repetitive and monotonous after the first. On the other hand there was a nice outdoor park with fun sculptures to take pictures next to. Overall might be good for children but not so worth it for adults.
We enjoyed this museum thoroughly.  Thousands of teddy bears with a multitude of poses, extremely creative. Very good history of teddy bears.

The bus journey took more than 1.5hours and cost about 3300won one way and the bus driver could provide change if needed. The TV screen will flash seongsan-ri entrance and you can press the bell to alight (photo attached). We alighted and headed to the black beach along Seongsan. It was called the black beach as the sand was black. Not sure why we need not need to pay for the entrance fee to Seongsan that day (25th April) but we were happy as the temperature was about 17 degree Celsius. We wore T-shirt with a windbreaker only as the sun kept us warm. A windbreaker will be good as it can be quite windy especially if you walk along the beach. There were 2 track at Seongsan. One track led to the peak of Seongsan which consist about 10 flights of stairs (Pretty doable even with poor fitness ? just take as many rest breaks as needed). At the peak, you will be able to have a panoramic view of the city and the surrounding water bodies. The other track is along the coast area with pretty wild purple (I think is Lunaria annua)  and yellow canola wild flower and volcanic stacked rocks.After Seongsan, you can continue to the Jeju Olle Route 1 to Al Oreum along the ocean area. The Jeju Olle Route 1 will pass by canola flower patches for photo taking, a nice ocean view with beaches for scenic viewing, a new hotel named as The Cloud, the ferry terminal, along many beautiful seashore. We stopped at one of the seashore where we witness locals harvesting gastropod, sword razor clams and cockles using simple equipment. We were friendly and allowed us to take photo of how they harvest sword razor clams. If you are interesting in harvesting, remember to bring a good jacket as the wind was strong in April. Putting on waterproof boots will be good too. We continued to walk along the coast where cuttlefish were being dried along the coast. There were many restaurants along the way too. As we continued the walk, we noted that there was no bus stop along the walk after the fish port/market (there was a Ojo Haenyeo House bus stop). The next bus stop was at Jongdal Elementary school which was quite a distance away.After walking through the coastal area, you will walk through a village for a short period before reaching the expressway. The walk towards Al Oreum required you to cross an expressway and the route up the Al Oreum seemed alittle deserted with trees but there was still a road up. You will contine to see the orange/blue ribbons that were well spaced. However, we started the walk at 1pm and took too many stops for picture taking. Therefore, we were unable to finish the walk to Al Oreum.We decided to back track  and took bus 701 from the Jongdal Elementary school stop at about 5.30 pm back to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal (we take on the side nearer to the expressway, not the opposite). Therefore, make sure you start the Olle route earlier if you want to reach the top of Al Oreum where you will have a bird-eye view of the paddy field and coastal area. The bus journey took about 2 hours to reach Seogwipo-si.Jeju Olle Route 6 & 7 We did not do the entire 6 & 7 trail but we visited Chilshimni Poetry Park, Hwangwooji coast, Oedolgae observatory and Oedolgae. This was a scenic trail and I highly recommend. We stayed at a hotel along Jungang-ro road, that was near the Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market. From our hotel, it was a 10 minutes walk to Geolmae Eco Park. The park led us along Seohong-ro road to Taepyeong-to road (where we passed by Hotel Yeon) where we were able to see the Saeyeong Bridge. After the bridge was in sight, we followed our instinct to the Bridge. There was an ice-cream stall that serve grape soft-serve that was delicious. We made our way onto the bridge to view the pristine bluish-green coastline and headed to Saeseom Island. Saeseom Island was a short 20 to 30 minutes trail that brought us to a rocky coastline where you can view two lighthouses (red and white). You could walk to the white lighthouse on the rocks but at your own risk. There were many locals fishing along the rocky areas too. In short, the trail along the Saeyeongyo Bridge was fairly easy yet scenic enough. We were there on the 22nd of April and the weather was about 15 degree Celsius in the day. A light jacket with windbreak will be sufficient. Afterwhich we headed to Chilshimni Poetry Park (which you can view Cheonjiyeon Falls for free) as there was a stairway along the left side of main exit road (where all the tour buses parked, pedestrian walkway path with brown wood). The stairway seemed to indicate going up a temple. However, we landed in Chilshimni Poetry Park. We took pictures of the waterfall and left Chilshimni Poetry Park to follow the orange/blue Jeju Olle ribbon to Hwangwooji coast and Oedolgae. The orange/blue Jeju Olle ribbon were along the park main road (Namseongjung-ro road where Park Sunshine hotel was). Then, You need to turn in to Namseong-ro road and you will see a brick wall painted dark blue with pinnochio seated on a bench (photo attached) you will passed by a ?hip?몃媛?? Hostel (the hostel name is in Korean as I cannot find the English name online - photo attached). u will then past by Poong Gyung Hotel in Jeju (not the one u can find online - photo attached) before arriving at Hwangwooji coast. I love Hwangwooji coast bcos it was like a private pool. There were only a few Korean that day, playing, swimming and hunting of sea creatures in the private pool. It also has a good view of the Saeyeongyo Bridge from a far.  After-which we head to Oedolgae and walked till Dombenang-gil Road. We decided to head back as I needed the toilet. At the entrance to Oedolgae, there was a public toilet acorss the road. The toilet were will keep with toilet paper provided. You can watch the sunset if you have time. However, we decided to walk back to our hotel as we were tire. Jeju Olle Route 14 ? 1If you love beaches, this is a must walk route (at least it was really breathe-taking for me).
